## 1. System Overview

### 1.1 What the product is

**All-in-One Workspace** (shipped under the names `Nekotic Workspace` / NexDrop —
`src/config/app.ts:3-4`) is a single navigation surface over seven things that are normally seven
products. The PRD states the constraint plainly in `WS-OVW-01`: one surface over
Project / Folder / File / Task / QA / API Doc / Config / Discussion, where *a write to one source is
visible to every related tool immediately*. Everything below is that sentence made into a schema.

Six subsystems, and they are not independent — each one is addressed through the one before it:

| # | Subsystem | What it is | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Drive tree** | One self-referential tree of *nodes*. Five kinds — `project`, `folder`, `document`, `board`, `file` — sharing one id space, one slug-based URL, one owner, one archive/trash lifecycle and one access chain. Every other subsystem hangs off a node. | `src/types/node.ts:24` `DriveNodeType`; `src/types/node.ts:48-78` `DriveNodeBase`; canon T-06 |
| 2 | **Block documents** | A page is an ordered array of typed blocks — 14 `BlockType` values collapsing into 9 interfaces — with autosave, pin, lock, duplicate, move, archive, delete, and full version history. Config documents and secret documents are the same node lifecycle with a different editor. | `src/types/document.ts:4-18`; PRD `WS-DOC-05`; canon T-18, T-20, T-22 |
| 3 | **Board engine, four views** | One board owns one schema (7 `ColumnType`s) and one record set. Table, Kanban, Calendar and Gantt are **projections of the same rows, never copies**. Saved views carry filters, sorts, grouping and column presentation. | `src/types/board.ts:7-14`, `:270` `BoardViewType`, `:331-380` `SavedView`; PRD `BD-COR-07` — "Table / Kanban / Calendar / Timeline are projections, never copies" |
| 4 | **Config and secret documents** | A config document is raw text in one of 15 `ConfigFormat`s with versioned history. A secret document is a list of keys whose values are encrypted at rest, masked in every listing, and revealable only by a privileged role — with every reveal and copy written to the workspace audit trail. | `src/types/devtools.ts:22-37`, `:97`; PRD `DV-CFG-22`, `DV-SEC-23`; canon T-20 – T-25 |
| 5 | **Collaboration** | Threaded comments (two levels, mentions encoded `@[Name](usr_id)`), watches on rows / documents / boards, a per-recipient notification inbox, My Work, global search, favourites and recent. | `src/types/collab.ts`; `docs/COLLABORATION.md`; canon T-33 – T-35 |
| 6 | **Governance** | Four cumulative roles, 39 permission keys, access rules that flow down the tree with per-node overrides, three narrowing layers (trashed / frozen / locked) that can only ever *take away*, and an append-only audit log. | `src/types/permission.ts:8`, `:30-77`; `src/lib/permissions/`; PRD `SY-RBC-42`, `SY-INH-43`, `SY-AUD-41`; canon §2.10 |

The scope boundary is itself a requirement. `SY-POS-45`: every feature must serve **Organize /
Connect / View**, and Workflow Automation, API Gateway and Email Client are *explicitly out of
scope*. That is why §1.4 stops where it does.

### 1.2 The current state: a complete frontend against a modelled server

There is a finished Next.js 16 App Router frontend — 470 TypeScript files under `src/`, 764 unit
tests, coverage thresholds enforced at 80 % (`vitest.config.mts`) — and **there is no server at
all**. `next.config.ts:6` sets `output: "export"`, so the application compiles to static HTML and
JavaScript and is currently published to GitHub Pages under `basePath: "/Nekotic-Workspace"`
(`src/config/base-path.ts:8`).

Everything the backend will own is presently an **in-process mock** under `src/services/` — 17
files, 4 455 lines, module-level `Map`s that die with the browser tab. A hard refresh loses every
change.

**This mock is not a stub. It is a model, and it was written to be one.** The frontend's own words:

> In-memory board backend. It is deliberately shaped like the HTTP API that replaces it: reads and
> writes are async, every write returns the authoritative record, and the row id sequence lives
> *here* — the client never invents a `TASK-00n`.
> — `src/services/board-service.ts:55-61`

> The honest caveat: there is no server here. This module reads the same process's stores, so it is
> a faithful *model* of the check a real API must make, not a substitute for it.
> — `src/services/authz.ts:29-33`

#### 1.2.1 What "a faithful model" buys the backend developer

This is the single most useful fact in this document, so it is spelled out. The mock already
imposes, on itself, six properties that a real API must have. **They are not aspirations; they are
enforced by the shipped tests.** A backend that reproduces them needs no negotiation with the
frontend team.

| Property the mock already has | Where it lives | What it means for you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Every call is async and takes an `AbortSignal`.** Aborting rejects with `cancelled`, never a network error. | `src/services/backend.ts:13-32`; C-12 | The cancellation contract is settled. A disconnected client is not an error to log. |
| **Every write returns the authoritative record**, and the stores replace optimistic state with the response. | `src/services/board-service.ts:55-61`; `src/hooks/use-async-resource.ts:86-89` `setData`; C-10 | No `204` where an object is expected. No "refetch after write" round trip. |
| **The row-id sequence lives on the server side of the seam.** The optimistic placeholder is literally `` `${prefix}-…` `` with an ellipsis. | `src/store/board-store.ts:363-366`; `src/types/board.ts:239-240` — "assigned by the backend, never derived on the client" | `custom_id` is a per-board counter you own, monotonic, never reissued (C-02, `BD-RID-10`). |
| **The caller is resolved, never declared.** The permission model refuses to take a role as an argument. | `src/services/authz.ts:24-28` — "A role the client sends is a claim, not a fact" | Identity, role, IP and clock come from the session and the socket. Delete `userId`, `role`, `actor`, `owner`, `grantedBy` from every request body (C-09). |
| **One error shape, and the code is load-bearing.** Eight `AppErrorCode` values; `use-embedded-board.ts:140` branches on `error.code === "not_found"`, `errors.ts:31` derives `isRetryable` from the code. | `src/types/async.ts:2-20`; `src/services/errors.ts` | The error envelope in §7.4 is not a proposal. Changing it breaks shipped branches. |
| **Partial success is reported, never silent.** `requested === applied.length + skipped.length` is asserted by test. | `src/services/board-service.ts:958-965` | Bulk and import are `200` responses carrying a report, not `4xx`. |

#### 1.2.2 What the frontend fakes, and therefore what you own outright

| Faked today | Where | Becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The current user — a hardcoded constant imported by **33 files** | `src/mock/users.ts:3-9` | A session. **See §8: authentication is greenfield.** |
| The whole drive tree, workspaces, membership, trash, access rules | `src/mock/tree.ts`, `src/mock/workspaces.ts`, `src/mock/access.ts`, seeded at module load | `nodes`, `workspaces`, `workspace_members`, `trash_entries`, `access_rules` |
| Ids: `nextId(prefix)` — one process-global base-36 counter | `src/services/backend.ts:4-10` | `UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` (C-01) |
| The clock: a frozen `MOCK_NOW` used as a *written* value | `src/config/app.ts:10` | `now()`, `TIMESTAMPTZ` (C-03) |
| The audit log, written **by the client** | `src/store/permission-store.ts:71`, `:99` | Rows written by the endpoint that performs the action, inside its transaction (canon §3.23) |
| Attachment bytes and file blobs — `Map<assetId, Blob>` handing out object URLs that die with the tab | `src/services/file-service.ts:35-37`; `src/services/comment-service.ts:209-219` | S3-compatible object storage + short-lived signed URLs (OQ-75) |
| Link unfurling — a title synthesised from the URL slug | `src/services/link-service.ts:15` | A server-side, SSRF-guarded fetch (E-118) |
| Notification fan-out, done inside `commentService.add` | `src/services/comment-service.ts:223` | The same fan-out, in the same transaction as the comment insert (E-120) |
| Realtime — an in-process bus, because `REALTIME_ENDPOINT` is `null` | `src/config/app.ts:65-69` | One WebSocket per workspace, Redis pub/sub for fan-out (E-138) |

The `REALTIME_ENDPOINT: string | null = null` line is worth pausing on: the socket seam is already
cut. Setting that constant to a URL is the whole client-side change.

### 1.3 The target stack, and why it is deliberately small

**Four moving parts. No more.**

| Part | Role | Why it is here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **PostgreSQL** | The single source of truth. 39 tables (canon §1.1). JSONB for the two structures that are always read whole — `board_rows.cells` and `board_columns.config` — with generated columns and GIN indexes for the lenses that are actually queried. `tsvector` + GIN for search rather than a separate index store. | Every hard question in this product is a foreign-key question: cascade on row delete, cascade on comment delete, quota accounting, orphan collection (canon §1.3.4). Postgres answers all of them in one engine. |
| **One backend service** | Sixteen **modules** inside one deployable: `identity`, `workspace`, `drive`, `boards`, `views`, `templates`, `documents`, `devtools`, `files`, `relations`, `collab`, `search`, `insights`, `system`, `governance`, `realtime` (C-14). | The frontend's own layering is already this: `services/` is one seam, and a permission check crosses drive + board + document + governance in a single call (`src/services/authz.ts:36-53`). Splitting that across network boundaries would turn one `authorize()` into a distributed transaction. |
| **Redis** | Pub/sub fan-out for the WebSocket across service instances; short-lived cache (permission resolution, `/config`); rate-limit token buckets; idempotency-key records. **No queue, no job broker, no primary data.** | Realtime needs cross-instance fan-out and nothing else does. Redis losing its whole dataset must cost a reconnect, never a record. |
| **S3-compatible object storage** | File bytes only, addressed by `file_assets.storage_key`. Uploads go **directly** to the store through a presigned `PUT`; downloads and thumbnails are short-lived signed URLs minted per response. | `WS-FIL-06` says object storage explicitly. Bytes never traverse the API service, so a 100 MB upload does not occupy a request worker. |

**Plus one dependency that is not a moving part.** A **KMS** (the cloud provider's, or a Vault
transit engine) holds one master key that wraps the per-workspace data key for secret encryption
(canon OQ-65: envelope encryption, AES-256-GCM, ciphertext + IV + tag in the row). It is not listed
above because it stores no application state and is on no read path but `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/{secretId}/reveal`
(E-103). It appears in the topology diagram for completeness.

**And what is deliberately absent** — this is a decision, not an omission (canon scope statement,
ground rule 8):

> No Kafka. No microservices. No CQRS. No event sourcing. No GraphQL. No API gateway.

The reasoning is the product's own shape. There are 140 endpoints over 39 tables serving one
frontend. The heaviest write in the system is a cross-board bulk move touching two boards in one
transaction (E-077); the heaviest read is one board's snapshot (E-047). Neither is a scale problem
that a message bus solves, and both are correctness problems that a single ACID transaction solves.
`SY-POS-45` puts "API Gateway" on the explicit out-of-scope list for the *product*; the same
judgement applies to its infrastructure.

### 1.4 Runtime topology

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph browser["Browser"]
    spa["SPA bundle<br/>Next.js 16 static export<br/>next.config.ts:6-8"]
    rt["RealtimeTransport seam<br/>src/lib/realtime/transport.ts"]
    ls["localStorage<br/>recent · comment drafts · theme<br/>NEVER a token"]
  end

  cdn["Static host / CDN<br/>serves HTML, JS, 404.html"]

  subgraph service["Backend service — one deployable, 16 modules"]
    http["HTTP API<br/>/api/v1"]
    authz["authorize · 5 gates<br/>membership → visibility → role → matrix → narrowing"]
    ws["WebSocket hub<br/>GET /api/v1/realtime"]
    sweep["Scheduled sweeps<br/>trash purge · upload reaper · export jobs"]
  end

  pg[("PostgreSQL<br/>39 tables · JSONB cells<br/>tsvector search")]
  redis[("Redis<br/>pub/sub · cache<br/>rate limits · idempotency")]
  s3[("S3-compatible store<br/>file bytes only")]
  kms["KMS<br/>wraps the per-workspace<br/>secret data key"]

  spa -->|"loads once"| cdn
  spa -->|"HTTPS · JSON · Bearer access token"| http
  spa -->|"presigned PUT · bytes bypass the API"| s3
  spa -->|"GET signed URL, then fetch"| s3
  rt <-->|"WSS · one socket per workspace"| ws
  spa --- ls

  http --> authz
  authz --> pg
  http --> pg
  http --> redis
  http -->|"mint presigned URL"| s3
  http -->|"unwrap data key"| kms
  ws --> redis
  http -->|"publish frame"| redis
  sweep --> pg
  sweep --> s3
```

Four things the diagram is asserting, each of which is a decision:

1. **The SPA talks to exactly one API origin.** It is a static bundle; it has no server-render path
   and therefore no server-side session. §8 is written against that fact.
2. **File bytes never pass through the API service.** Upload is a presigned `PUT` straight to the
   object store (E-110/E-111); download is a signed URL (E-116/E-117). The API mints URLs and
   accounts for quota; it does not proxy bytes.
3. **Redis is between the API and the socket, not between the API and the database.** A frame is
   published to Redis and delivered by whichever instance holds the subscriber's socket. Nothing
   reads its primary state from Redis.
4. **The permission decision is one function, called first.** `authorize()` runs five gates in
   order — membership, visibility, effective role, matrix/ownership, then the trashed/frozen/locked
   narrowing — before any state is read or written. The frontend models exactly this and names the
   three gates its model omits (`src/services/authz.ts:36-53`, and OQ-16 – OQ-22).

### 1.5 What the backend inherits as already-decided

A backend developer should not re-open any of these. Each is either shipped frontend behaviour or a
canon decision made on top of it.

| Decision | Where it is settled |
| --- | --- |
| UUID primary keys; `TASK-001` is a separate `custom_id` column | C-01, C-02 |
| `TIMESTAMPTZ` + ISO 8601 for instants; `DATE` + `YYYY-MM-DD` for date-only, **never converted through UTC** | C-03, C-04, `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-16`. See §7.12. |
| No `any` in any contract; every dynamic value is a discriminated union | C-05, and `src/types/` contains none |
| Every JSONB column has a named TypeScript interface documenting its structure | C-06 |
| Optional (`x?: T`) and nullable (`x: T \| null`) are different and are not collapsed | C-08, `src/types/board.ts:76-79` vs `:223` |
| Enum members on the wire are the exact frontend string literal, casing included — `longText`, `permission_denied`, `into-self`, `my-work` | C-13, canon §2.0 |
| One `nodes` table with a `kind` discriminant and five 1:1 side tables | canon §1.3.1 |
| `cells` as JSONB on the row, not an EAV `cell_values` table | canon §1.3.2 |
| Select options inside `board_columns.config`, not a `select_options` table | canon §1.3.3 |
| One `file_assets` table plus four typed join tables — **not** a polymorphic owner pair | canon §1.3.4 |
| Task / Bug / QA / API-catalogue are **board templates**, not tables. No chapter may introduce one. | canon §1.3.5 |
| Success responses carry no envelope; errors are `{ "error": AppError }` | canon §6.2, §7.3–7.4 below |
| Cursor pagination everywhere it paginates; no `page` or `offset` parameter exists in this API | canon §6.3, §7.6 below |

## 2. Backend Scope

### 2.1 In scope

The backend owns every piece of state that must survive a browser refresh, be seen by a second
person, or be refused to a third. Concretely, the sixteen modules of C-14, serving the 140 endpoints
of canon §3 over the 39 tables of canon §1.1, plus four cross-cutting obligations that belong to no
single module:

| Cross-cutting obligation | Why it is the backend's | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Every permission decision, re-checked server-side.** The frontend gate is UX. | "Frontend permissions are UX only — a hidden button says 'this is not for you' before a request is refused; it is not a boundary, and the backend still has to re-check every key." | `README.md` § Governance; `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:24-25`; P-09 |
| **Identity, role, IP and the clock.** Resolved from the session and the socket, never read from a request body. | "A role the client sends is a claim, not a fact." | `src/services/authz.ts:24-28`; C-09; OQ-16 – OQ-21 |
| **Every server-assigned identifier**: node ids, row ids, `custom_id`/`displayId`, column ids, option ids, view ids, comment ids, asset ids, audit ids. | The client mints `tmp_`/`new_`/`acl_` placeholders and swaps them for the response. | `src/store/board-store.ts:360-366`; canon C-01, C-02 |
| **Every audit row.** Written by the endpoint that performs the action, inside its transaction. There is no audit write endpoint and no chapter may add one. | "The service exposes `record` and `list`, and nothing else… so no screen can grow an Edit button that quietly works." | `src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20`; canon §3.23 |

### 2.2 Explicitly NOT in scope — the frontend-only concerns

The frontend audit found seven categories of state and behaviour that live in the browser **and must
stay there**. Each is listed with the exact module that owns it, so nobody builds an endpoint for
it by accident.

| # | Concern | Lives in | Why it is not backend state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Grid selection** — the cell cursor `range`, `editing` cell, `drawerRowId`, `isDragSelecting`, `selectedRowIds`, the shift-click anchor `lastSelectedRowId`, `renamingColumnId`, `detailCell` | `src/store/grid-store.ts:45-81` | Every field is ephemeral interaction state. `reset()` is called on **every board change** (`src/hooks/use-board.ts:23-28`), and `useBulkActions` filters stale ids out before any write (`use-bulk-actions.ts:54`). Persisting a selection would mean persisting a cursor position that is already gone by the time it lands. |
| 2 | **Drag state** — `draggingNodeId`, `isFileDrag` | `src/store/dnd-store.ts:5-25` | Kept out of the workspace store deliberately: "it changes on every drag gesture and no data component should re-render because of it" (`:15-18`). The *result* of a drag is a `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/move` (E-026); the gesture is not. |
| 3 | **Virtualisation** — the visible row window, overscan band, measured row offsets, scroll position | `src/hooks/use-virtual-rows.ts:35-78`; `src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx:58`; `src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx:49` | It is a rendering strategy over a page of rows the API already returned. The API's unit is a cursor page (§7.6), not a viewport. |
| 4 | **Theme** | `src/lib/theme.ts:11-27`; `localStorage["nexdrop-theme"]` | Applied by a pre-hydration boot script so the first paint is correct; `<html class="dark">` is the source of truth, **not the stored value** (`:19-24`). A server round trip cannot happen before first paint in a static export, so a server-stored theme would flash. |
| 5 | **Sidebar collapse** | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:140`, `:254`, `:914-916`; driven by `useResponsiveSidebar` below `SIDEBAR_COLLAPSE_BREAKPOINT = 1024` (`src/config/app.ts:20-24`) | It is set by the **viewport**, not by a click, whenever the window is narrow. A server-held value would be overwritten by the next resize. See the carve-out in §2.2.1. |
| 6 | **Client-side presentational formatting** — byte sizes (`formatBytes`), relative time (`12m ago`), the `en-GB` date rendering, cell display truncation, calendar grid construction | `src/lib/format.ts:7`, `:29`; `src/lib/cell-display.ts`; `src/lib/calendar.ts:283-364` | These are locale and viewport decisions. `Intl` formatters are cached per locale (`calendar.ts:283-293`) precisely because the locale is a *parameter*, not a stored value. **See the boundary in §2.2.2 — some prose genuinely is the server's.** |
| 7 | **Client-side spreadsheet and document generation** — XLSX read/write, CSV/TSV parsing, ZIP, PDF writing | `src/lib/xlsx.ts:1-12`, `src/lib/csv.ts:1-6`, `src/lib/zip.ts`, `src/lib/pdf.ts` | Import parses the file **in the browser** and posts a parsed `ImportSource` as JSON (`src/types/system.ts:67-74`); export builds the bytes entirely client-side and never calls a service (`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:20-27`). The API therefore accepts and returns JSON, never `multipart/form-data`, for import and view/selection export (§7.11). |

Also not backend state, and grouped here so the list is exhaustive:

| Concern | Where | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tree expansion (`expandedIds`), node multi-select, `previewNodeId` | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:112-120` | Navigation state. |
| Intent hand-offs: `rowRequest`, `renameRequestId`, `titleFocusNodeId` | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:118-140` | "Create → land the caret in the name" is a UI hand-off between two components, not a record. |
| Feedback toasts (`Feedback`, `pushFeedback`) | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:100-104` | Rendered from the response the API already returned. |
| **Role preview** (`previewAs`) | `src/store/permission-store.ts:47-51` | *"Role preview is not a session switch. It narrows what the interface offers; it does not re-authenticate, and a reload clears it"* (`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:359-360`). **Do not build a server-side impersonation mode** — see OQ-21. If a role is ever declared on the wire, the server applies `min(serverResolvedRole, declaredRole)` and never `max`. |
| The simulation panel — forced network / permission / empty / upload / save failures and latency profiles | `src/services/simulation.ts:9-73` | Exists so every error branch in the UI is reachable. **None of it ships and the API needs no equivalent.** |
| Eight UI-only enums that never cross the wire: `ViewMode`, `SortKey`, `ImportStep`, `DocumentActionId`, `SaveStatus`, `NotificationTab`, `BodySegmentKind`, `SmartViewId` | canon §2.10, closing note | In particular the API filters notifications by `reason`, **never by tab name** (OQ-90). |
| `Recent` — an LRU of 10 `EntityRef`s | `localStorage["nexdrop-recent"]`, `src/store/recent-store.ts:9-18` | "kept in this browser only". Canon's position: it stays there (OQ-96). |
| Comment drafts | `localStorage["nexdrop-comment-draft:<key>"]`, `src/hooks/use-comment-draft.ts:5-17` | Same. Canon's position: it stays there (OQ-97). |

**One invariant worth stating in a security review:** nothing else is persisted in the browser. No
auth token, no user id, no board data, no draft document content, and — stated as a design
invariant in two places — **no secret plaintext** (`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:48-55`,
`src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:92-105`). §8 is designed not to break that.

#### 2.2.1 The carve-out: preferences whose *value* persists even though the *interaction* does not

Three of the concerns above have a persisted-value half that canon has already reserved a table for.
Read this before concluding "the backend stores nothing about the UI".

| Value | Table | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-viewer column widths and collapsed-group state on a board view | `board_view_preferences` (T-16) | **RECOMMENDATION**, OQ-46. Filters and sorts stay **shared** — they are what a named view *is*. Widths and collapse are per viewer. |
| Sidebar collapse, drive view mode (`grid`/`list`), drive sort key and direction | `user_ui_preferences` (T-37) | **RECOMMENDATION**, OQ-98. Not built until OQ-98 is answered; until then the client keeps them and nothing breaks. |
| Recent, comment drafts | *no table* | Canon's position under OQ-96 / OQ-97 is that both stay in `localStorage`. |

The distinction is the useful one: **the grid's cursor is never persisted; a column the user
widened is.** `collapsedByView` and `collapsedParentsByView` are keyed by view id so collapsed
groups survive a view switch (`src/store/grid-store.ts:50-56`) — that is exactly the shape T-16
would take.

#### 2.2.2 The boundary inside "formatting": what the server *does* render

Item 6 above is the easiest one to get wrong in both directions. The rule:

**The client renders values. The server renders sentences about history.**

| Server-rendered — a stored string | Grounding |
| --- | --- |
| `AuditEvent.detail` — "One sentence. The UI never renders a raw audit payload" | `src/types/audit.ts:37-38` |
| `AuditEvent.target` — "Human label of the thing acted on — never an id, never a payload" | `src/types/audit.ts:35-36` |
| `ActivityEntry.summary` — "Human sentence fragment: `changed Status`, `created TASK-001`" | `src/types/board.ts:501-502` |
| `AppNotification` pre-rendered title and body, frozen at creation because a notification is a historical statement | canon T-35, OQ-79 |
| `UserSummary.initials` and `accentColor` — served fields, not derived | `src/types/user.ts:8-11`; `src/mock/users.ts:3-17` |

| Client-rendered — never sent as a string | Grounding |
| --- | --- |
| `1.4 MB` from `sizeBytes` | `src/lib/format.ts:7-19` |
| `12m ago` from an ISO instant | `src/lib/format.ts:29` |
| `27 Aug 2026` from a `YYYY-MM-DD` day key, in `en-GB` | `src/lib/calendar.ts:57`, `:300-317` |
| Cell truncation under `compact` / `wrap` / `full` | `src/types/board.ts:316-326`; `src/lib/cell-display.ts` |

Sending a formatted byte count or a relative time would freeze a viewport decision into a record and
would go stale the moment the tab stayed open.

### 2.3 Module priority

**How the bands are defined.**

- **P0** — the shell does not boot, or boots into a refusal, without it. `AppShell` mounts
  `WorkspaceGuard` and nothing inside a workspace renders until membership is settled
  (`src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx:49-52`, `src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:10-27`).
- **P1** — the shell boots and P0 surfaces work, but a numbered PRD feature is dead.
- **P2** — the feature degrades gracefully into behaviour the frontend already handles, or it is a
  `RECOMMENDATION` whose OQ is still open.

| Module | Band | Owns | What breaks without it | Endpoints (canon §3) | Tables |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | **P0** | Authentication, session, the caller. Directory reads. | **Everything.** 33 files import a hardcoded user (`src/mock/users.ts:3`); no request can name an actor. See §8. | E-001 – E-006 | T-01, T-02, T-37 |
| `workspace` | **P0** | Tenancy, membership, roles, storage quota, invitations. | `WorkspaceGuard` renders the refusal screen for everyone. "Not a member" is not "viewer" (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`). | E-007 – E-019 | T-03, T-04, T-05 |
| `drive` | **P0** | The node tree, slugs, path resolution, move/duplicate/rename, favourites, archive, soft delete. | Every route resolves a slug chain against the tree (`src/app/(workspace)/drive/[[...path]]/page.tsx`). Boards, pages, config and secret documents all render **inside** `/drive/<path>`. | E-020 – E-035 | T-06, T-07 |
| `governance` | **P0** | `authorize()`, access rules, capability sets, the permission catalogue, the audit log. | Not "no permissions" — **no safe read at all**. The tree endpoint is pruned by visibility before it is returned (E-020, `src/lib/tree.ts:297-320`). | E-040 – E-046, E-136, E-137 | T-08, T-36 |
| `boards` | **P0** | Board aggregate, columns, rows, cells, `custom_id` counter, row activity. | `BD-COR-07`, the product's centre. Table view is the default surface of every board node. | E-047 – E-073 | T-10 – T-12, T-14 |
| `views` | **P0** | Saved views: type, filters, sorts, grouping, column presentation. | A board must have **at least one view** — E-081 refuses the delete that would leave zero (`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`). A board with no views cannot render. | E-078 – E-083 | T-15, T-16 |
| `documents` | **P0** | Block pages, autosave, pin, lock. | `WS-DOC-05`. Document nodes exist in the seeded tree from the first frame; opening one without this module is a 404 on a node the sidebar is showing. | E-091 – E-094 | T-18, T-19 |
| `templates` | **P0** *(built-ins)* / **P2** *(user-authored)* | The four built-in blueprints as seed rows; instantiation. | Board creation takes a `templateId` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts` `createBoard`), so the four seeds are P0. Saving a board **as** a template (E-089/E-090) is `RECOMMENDATION` under OQ-47 → P2. | E-087, E-088 *(P0)*; E-089, E-090 *(P2)* | T-17 |
| `files` | **P1** | Presigned uploads, quota accounting, previews, text/spreadsheet save, downloads, signed URLs, link unfurl. | `WS-FIL-06` and the whole `/files` route. File **nodes** still list from `drive`, so the tree is intact; their bytes are not. | E-110 – E-118 | T-27 – T-32 |
| `collab` | **P1** | Comments, mentions, watches, notifications — and the transactional fan-out. | `CO-CMT-26`, `CO-MEN-27`, `CO-WAT-28`, `CO-NOT-29`. The bell renders zero; the drawer's comment tab is empty. | E-119 – E-132 | T-33 – T-35 |
| `system` | **P1** | Trash console, bulk actions, import/export, version history across pages/config/secrets. | `SY-BLK-34` … `SY-VER-39`. `/trash` and `/archive` render empty; multi-select loses its action bar. Node soft-delete itself is `drive` (E-032), so nothing is lost, only unrecoverable through the UI. | E-036 – E-039, E-074 – E-077, E-084 – E-086, E-095 – E-098 | T-09, T-38, T-39 |
| `devtools` | **P1** | Config documents, secret documents, encryption, reveal/copy/rotate, the secret access trail, environments. | `DV-CFG-22`, `DV-SEC-23`, `DV-ENV-21`. **Ship it complete or not at all**: a half-built secret store with an unaudited reveal is worse than no secret store. | E-099 – E-109 | T-20 – T-26 |
| `search` | **P1** | Global full-text search across 8 result kinds, permission-funnelled before scanning. | `CO-SCH-31`. `⌘K` opens an empty dialog. The cheap drive quick-find (E-035) is a separate `drive` endpoint and survives (OQ-94). | E-133 | *(tsvector columns on existing tables; no table of its own)* |
| `insights` | **P1** — *land it first among P1* | Dashboard aggregates and My Work. | `SY-DSH-44`, `CO-MYW-30`. **`/` redirects to `/dashboard`**, so this is the app's landing screen; without it the first thing a user sees is an error panel rather than the onboarding state. | E-134, E-135 | *(projections; canon §1.2 — no tables)* |
| `realtime` | **P1** — *with one P0 frame* | The WebSocket hub and Redis fan-out. | **RT-05 `permission.changed` is not optional**: without it a revoked user keeps a loaded board on screen until they reload (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:74-83`; canon §7.1). The other frames are convergence, not correctness. The seam already exists — `REALTIME_ENDPOINT` is `null` (`src/config/app.ts:65-69`) and unknown frame types are ignored by the client (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`), so frames can ship one at a time. | E-138 | *(none — Redis pub/sub)* |
| `relations` | **P2** | The `board_row_relations` projection, the bulk relation resolver, backlinks. | `DV-REL-24`. A relation cell renders its stored id and a deleted target renders `[Deleted Item]` with an unlink action, so the degradation is already designed. The `task` built-in template ships a "Blocked by" relation column, which would render empty. | E-071, E-072 | T-13 |

**A delivery note that follows from the table, not an opinion.** The eight P0 entries are not eight
milestones — they are one. `authorize()` needs membership (`workspace`), the ancestor chain
(`drive`) and the node's lock state (`documents`) in a single read; the drive tree endpoint is
pruned by `governance` before it returns; a board node without `views` cannot render. The smallest
shippable slice is: **sign in → list workspaces → read the pruned tree → open one board with one
view → edit one cell → see it after a refresh.** Everything in P1 hangs off that slice, and every
P1 module can be added without a client release except `realtime`, which needs one constant changed.

### 2.4 Two scope questions the frontend does not settle

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-42) — are import parsing and export generation client-side by design, or by
absence of a server?**
**Evidence** — the frontend parses `.xlsx`/`.csv`/`.tsv` in the browser
(`src/lib/xlsx.ts:1-12`, `src/lib/csv.ts:1-6`) and posts an already-parsed `ImportSource`
(`src/types/system.ts:67-74`); export builds XLSX, CSV and PDF bytes entirely client-side and never
calls a service (`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:20-27`, `src/lib/pdf.ts`). `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5 000`
(`src/config/app.ts:48`) is a ceiling a browser can hold; `SY-EXP-36` asks for 5 000 rows to Excel
in under 2 s, which a browser meets.
**Recommendation** — keep parsing and small-scope generation in the browser. The API accepts JSON
for `POST /boards/{boardId}/import/plan` and `/import` (E-084, E-085) and returns `ExportOutcome`
for `view` and `selection` scope; only **whole-board export** (E-086, `board` scope) becomes an
async `ExportJob` writing to object storage with a signed URL, because that is the only case where
the row count is unbounded.
**Impact if wrong** — if the server must parse, `POST /import/plan` gains a `multipart/form-data`
variant and the whole §7.11 "JSON only" rule gains an exception. Contained, but it changes the
content-type contract.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-29) — `ExportOutcome.omittedColumns` implies column-level permissions that
exist nowhere.**
**Evidence** — export drops columns the viewer may not read *before* any writer sees them
(`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:20-27`, `selectExportColumns(..., { canViewSensitive })`), and
`SY-EXP-36` states "a column the caller may not read is removed from the exported file". But the
39-key catalogue has **no column-scoped key** (`src/types/permission.ts:30-77`), and `canViewSensitive`
is derived in the client from a name heuristic.
**Recommendation** — do not introduce column-level ACLs. Treat "sensitive" as a board-schema
property the backend can evaluate, and resolve it with OQ-48 (column roles are name heuristics, not
schema) rather than by extending the permission catalogue.
**Impact if wrong** — if real column-level permissions are required, `access_rules` gains a
`column_id` scope and every board read grows a per-column filter. That is a schema change in the
hottest read path in the product.

---

---

## 3. Domain Model

### 3.0 How to read this section

This section names the aggregates, draws their boundaries and states their invariants. It does not
draw the schema — §5 does that, and the schema chapter carries the columns. Every claim here is
either an **EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (the frontend at `/Users/chikarin/Projects/NexDrop/Gen fe` or the
PRD settles it, cited `path:line`) or a **RECOMMENDATION** carrying the canon **OQ id** that reserves
the decision. Table names, enum members and endpoint ids are canon's (`spec/canon.md` §1, §2, §3) and
are not re-litigated here.

---

### 3.1 The single most important idea in this system

> **A board owns one schema and one set of records. A view owns nothing but presentation.**

This is not a design preference. It is already how the frontend is built, and building the backend
any other way breaks it.

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** There is exactly one record store per board and exactly one query over it.
`src/lib/board-view.ts:15-21` states the rule in the file header:

> *"A view never owns records — it describes how to read the board's. Schema (name, type, config)
> lives on the column and is shared by every view. Presentation (order, width, visibility) is per
> view, so hiding a column in the table cannot change what Kanban or Calendar show."*

and `src/lib/board-view.ts:190-193` states the mechanism:

> *"The single query the whole board runs: filters, then search, then sort. Table, Kanban, Calendar
> and Timeline all consume the row ids it returns."*

`queryRowIds` (`src/lib/board-view.ts:194-236`) is that one query. It takes `rowsById`, `rowOrder`,
the active `SavedView` and a search string, and returns `readonly string[]` — row ids. Table, Kanban,
Calendar and Gantt are **projection functions over those ids**, not stores:

| Surface | Component | What it projects the same ids through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table | `src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx` | `resolveColumns` order + width + visibility |
| Kanban | `src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx` | `groupByColumnId` buckets over the select column's options |
| Calendar | `src/components/board/views/calendar-board.tsx` | `dateColumnId` → a day key per row (`src/lib/board-calendar.ts`) |
| Gantt | `src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx` | `dateColumnId` + `endDateColumnId` → a bar (`src/lib/board-gantt.ts`) |

**What this settles for the backend, permanently.**

1. There is **no per-view record table**. No `kanban_cards`, no `calendar_events`, no `gantt_tasks`,
   no `timeline_bars`. A view is a row in `board_views` (T-15) and nothing else.
2. Switching a view is a **client-side re-projection of rows already loaded**. It issues no write and
   needs no endpoint. E-078…E-082 write view *configuration*; they never touch `board_rows`.
3. A schema write (`board_columns`) is visible to **every** view of the board. A presentation write
   (`board_views`) is visible to **that view only**. The split is exactly:

   | Operation | Writes | Visible to | Endpoint |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Rename column, change type, change config, add/delete/reorder column | `board_columns` | every view | E-052…E-060 |
   | Resize, hide/show, reorder, sort, filter, group, row height, display mode, Gantt zoom | one `board_views` row | that view only | E-080 |
   | Per-viewer width and collapse state | `board_view_preferences` | that viewer only | E-083 (RECO, OQ-46) |

4. Deleting a column must **prune every view of the board in the same transaction** (E-054). The
   frontend's `pruneView` (`src/lib/board-view.ts:288-334`) drops filters, sorts, `columnOrder`,
   `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnDisplay`, `columnWidths`, `groupByColumnId`, `dateColumnId` and
   `endDateColumnId` that name a column the schema no longer has. The backend performs the same
   pruning server-side; a view carrying a dead reference is a spec defect.
5. Realtime follows the same shape. `board.schema.changed` (RT-10) carries `{ boardId }` and nothing
   else; the client refetches the whole schema, which is C-11 ("a schema response is a **complete
   array**, never a delta", `src/store/board-store.ts:698`).

#### 3.1.1 The corollary: QA, Task, Bug and API Catalogue are board *templates*, not domains

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `src/lib/board-templates.ts:12-18`:

> *"A template is inert data: `instantiateTemplate` deep-copies everything it hands out, so a board
> can add, rename or delete columns without the template it came from ever changing — the acceptance
> criterion for DV-TMP-19."*

There is **no `tasks` table, no `bugs` table, no `qa_cases` table and no `api_endpoints` table**
(canon §1.2, §1.3.5). `task`, `bug`, `qa` and `apiDocs` are four seed rows in `board_templates`
(T-17). A board created from one is an ordinary board from the moment it exists.

The evidence that this is a hard rule and not a convenience:

- **The product reads a board by what it became, not by what it was made from.** `isQaBoard`
  (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:92-99`) does not look at `templateId`. It asks whether the board's status
  column offers an option labelled `passed` or `failed`. The comment at
  `src/lib/dashboard.ts:87-91` is explicit: *"Template id is not enough: a board created from the QA
  template and then reshaped should follow what it became, not what it was made from."*
- **Cross-template queries address columns by *role*, never by id.** `lensesFor`
  (`src/lib/my-work.ts:59-68`) picks the assignee / due / status columns by matching the column
  *name* against `/assign|owner|tester|responsible/i`, `/due|deadline/i` and `/status|result|state/i`.
  A board with no column for a role *contributes nothing* to the widget that needs it rather than
  guessing (`src/lib/my-work.ts:14-21`).
- **`SearchResultKind`'s `api` / `bug` / `qa` buckets are a read-time projection.**
  `src/services/search-service.ts:39-43` is a three-entry map from template id to result kind. It is
  a lens on `boards.template_id`, not a schema.
- **`BoardNode.templateId` is a bare `string`, "for reference only"** (`src/types/node.ts:110-111`,
  `src/types/board.ts:414-415`).
- **A template-specific rule is a warning, never a constraint.** The API-documentation board's
  duplicate-endpoint check (`DV-API-20`, `src/components/board/api-duplicate-banner.tsx`) is *"warned
  in amber, never blocked"* — a validation a dedicated `api_endpoints` table would be forced to make
  an error.

**A writer who feels the pull toward a typed table for one of these four is looking at a template
column list.** Document the template row, not a table.

---

### 3.2 The aggregate hierarchy

Six aggregates. Indentation is containment; a `→` marks a reference that crosses an aggregate
boundary and is therefore an id, never an embedded object.

- **Workspace** — the tenant boundary. `workspaces` (T-03)
  - `plan`, `badge`, `color`, `slug`, `used_bytes` counter
  - **Member** — `workspace_members` (T-04), `(workspace_id, user_id)` → `WorkspaceRole` + `joined_at`
    - → `users` (T-01) — soft-deactivated, never hard-deleted
    - `workspace_invitations` (T-05) — pending email invite → role, token hash, expiry *(RECO, OQ-04)*
  - `environments` (T-26) — the shared deployment label list, `SelectOption`-shaped (DV-ENV-21)
  - `board_templates` (T-17) — four built-in seed rows plus this workspace's own
  - **Node tree** — `nodes` (T-06). One table, discriminated by `kind`. The drive.
    - `project` — `status`, `color`, `description`
    - `folder` — `color`
    - `document` — `document_kind` ∈ `page | config | secret`, `icon`, pin and lock state
      - `page` → **Document** content: `documents` (T-18) + `document_versions` (T-19)
      - `config` → **Config** content: `config_documents` (T-20) + `config_versions` (T-21)
      - `secret` → **Secret** container: `secret_documents` (T-22)
        - `secrets` (T-23) — one key per row, `value_encrypted BYTEA`
        - `secret_rotations` (T-24) — *that* a key rotated. **No value column, ever.**
        - `secret_access_events` (T-25) — per-secret reveal / copy / rotate trail
    - `board` — `board_kind`, `template_id`
      - → **Board** content: `boards` (T-10)
    - `file` — `file_kind`, `extension`, `mime_type`, `size_bytes`
      - → `file_nodes` (T-28) → `file_assets` (T-27)
    - `node_favorites` (T-07) — per user, not a flag on the node *(OQ-07)*
    - `trash_entries` (T-09) — restore metadata for a deleted subtree
    - `access_rules` (T-08) — see **Governance**
  - **Board** — `boards` (T-10). The single source of truth for records.
    - **Columns** — `board_columns` (T-11): `type`, `position`, `width`, `hidden`, `is_primary`,
      `config` JSONB
      - **Options** — `SelectConfig.options[]` **inside** `board_columns.config`, not a table *(canon §1.3.3)*
        - `availability` — a `ConditionGroup` tree per option
        - `transitionRules.transitions` — keyed by option id, reserved key `"__empty__"`
        - `completedOptionIds` — which options mean "finished"
    - **Rows** — `board_rows` (T-12): `custom_id`, `sequence`, `parent_row_id`, `position`, `revision`
      - **Cells** — `board_rows.cells` JSONB, `Record<columnId, CellValue>` *(canon §1.3.2)*
      - subtask containment — `parent_row_id`, self-referential, same board *(OQ-33)*
    - **Relations** — `board_row_relations` (T-13): a projection of relation cells so backlinks are
      an indexed query. Written in the same transaction as the cell.
    - **Views** — `board_views` (T-15): `type`, filters, sorts, grouping, column presentation
      - `board_view_preferences` (T-16) — per-viewer overrides *(RECO, OQ-46)*
    - **Activity** — `row_activity` (T-14): one entry per write, however many fields it touched
    - `import_jobs` (T-38), `export_jobs` (T-39) *(RECO, OQ-41 / OQ-42)*
  - **Collaboration**
    - **Comments** — `comments` (T-33): body, decomposed target, `parent_id`, resolve and tombstone
      columns
      - **Mentions** — `comments.mentioned_user_ids`, parsed server-side from `@[Name](usr_id)`.
        **Not a table.**
      - `comment_attachments` (T-30) → `file_assets`
    - **Watches** — `watches` (T-34): `(user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)` + `since`
    - **Notifications** — `notifications` (T-35): one row **per recipient**, fan-out on write
    - **Favourites** — `node_favorites` (T-07), listed under the node tree because it keys a node
    - **Recents** — *not a table.* `localStorage` under `nexdrop-recent` *(OQ-96)*
    - **Activity** — `row_activity` (T-14), listed under Board because it keys a row
  - **Governance**
    - **Roles** — `WorkspaceRole`, four members, cumulative. Not a table: the matrix is code
      (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:77-96`).
    - **Permissions** — the 39-key `PermissionKey` catalogue. **Not a table**: static config served
      from E-045 so both sides agree (canon §1.2).
    - **Access grants** — `access_rules` (T-08): one grant, on one node, for one subject
    - **Audit** — `audit_events` (T-36): append-only. **No write endpoint exists and no chapter may
      add one** (canon §3.23).
  - `user_sessions` (T-02), `user_ui_preferences` (T-37) — keyed by user, not by workspace

---

### 3.3 Aggregate by aggregate

#### 3.3.1 Workspace — the tenant boundary

**Root.** `workspaces` (T-03). **Contents.** `workspace_members`, `workspace_invitations`,
`environments`, `board_templates` (the workspace's own), and — transitively — every `nodes` row.

**Boundary.** A workspace is the outermost gate. Crossing it is not a permission question, it is an
existence question.

**Invariants.**

| # | Invariant | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W-1 | **"Not a member" is not "viewer".** A workspace the caller is not a member of answers identically to one that does not exist: `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, `404`, `not_found`. | `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`; canon §4.3 |
| W-2 | **The workspace never loses its last admin.** `isLastAdmin` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:85-88`) guards leave (`:106-119`), remove (`:122-138`) and demote. E-014/E-015/E-016 all refuse with `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN`, `409`. | `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157` |
| W-3 | **The creator becomes admin in the same write.** E-008 inserts `workspaces` and `workspace_members` in one transaction. There is no window in which a workspace has no administrator. | `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:212-238` |
| W-4 | `workspaces.slug` is globally unique. Single tenant; there is no tenant table. | *(OQ-02, position taken in canon §8.8)* |
| W-5 | `workspaces.used_bytes` is maintained **transactionally** with every `file_assets` insert and delete, with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. It is never recomputed by aggregate on read. An upload that would exceed `StorageQuota.totalBytes` is refused with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `507`. | canon §1.4, §8.8 (OQ-05); `src/types/workspace.ts:5-10` |
| W-6 | `StorageQuota.totalBytes` comes from static per-plan service config, not a `plans` table. Three tiers with fixed quotas cannot drift if they are not rows. | canon §1.2 *(OQ-06)* |
| W-7 | Leaving the workspace you are standing in switches you out in the same write (E-016). | `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:106-119` |

**Transaction rule.** Workspace creation, membership change and workspace deletion each land as one
transaction. A membership change additionally emits `permission.changed` (RT-05) with
`nodeId: null` — because a role change re-resolves access on **every** node in the workspace.

#### 3.3.2 Member — the person inside the tenant

**Root.** `workspace_members` (T-04). It is a join row with state, not a link table: it carries
`role` and `joined_at`, and `WorkspaceMember` is the shape the API returns (`src/types/user.ts:22-25`).

**Boundary.** `users` (T-01) lives *outside* the workspace aggregate. One person may hold membership
in many workspaces with a different role in each. `workspace_members` is the only place a role is
stored.

**Invariants.**

| # | Invariant | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M-1 | **A user is soft-deactivated, never hard-deleted.** `users.is_active = false`. The directory endpoint (E-006) returns deactivated members flagged `isActive: false` so an old assignment still renders a name. | `src/types/user.ts:14-20`; `src/mock/users.ts:41-58` |
| M-2 | Role comes from `workspace_members`, resolved from the **session**. A role in a request body is a claim, not a fact. | C-09; `src/services/authz.ts:24-27` |
| M-3 | `WorkspaceRole` order **is** the rank, ascending: `viewer < member < manager < admin`. `roleRank` is `WORKSPACE_ROLES.indexOf(role)`. | `src/types/permission.ts:10-20` |
| M-4 | Roles are **cumulative**: each role is the one below it plus what it adds. Viewer holds **zero** keys by construction, not by omission. | `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:16, 84-96` |
| M-5 | Ownership is a **separate axis**, not a fifth role. It escalates five keys (`node.rename`, `node.delete`, `node.archive`, `file.delete`, `document.lock`) on the things you made, and only from `member` upward. | `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:99-108`; `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:71-74` |

**RECOMMENDATION.** `workspace_invitations` (T-05) models the flow implied by
`WorkspaceMember.joinedAt`, which the frontend carries but never produces *(OQ-04)*. E-013 creates
one; E-019 consumes it and inserts the `workspace_members` row in the same transaction.

#### 3.3.3 Node tree — the drive

**Root.** `nodes` (T-06). **One table, discriminated by `kind`**, with the shared column set as real
columns and the per-kind extras as nullable columns (canon §1.3.1). Content lives in five 1:1 side
tables keyed by `node_id`: `boards`, `documents`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents`,
`file_nodes`.

**Boundary.** The node is the **unit of addressing, routing, permission and lifecycle**. Content is
entered through its node and then addressed by its own id (P-04): `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board`
returns the snapshot including `board.id`, and every board sub-resource then hangs off
`/boards/{boardId}`.

**Invariants.**

| # | Invariant | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N-1 | `children` is **DERIVED** from `parent_id` and is never stored. | `src/types/node.ts:149-151` |
| N-2 | `slug` is unique among **live siblings, across kinds**. A trashed row is excluded so a restore never collides. Minted once at creation, re-uniquified only on **move**, never re-minted on rename. | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:472-490`; canon §8.8 *(OQ-09 / OQ-10)* |
| N-3 | Only `project` and `folder` are containers. `isContainer` (`src/types/node.ts:146-147`) is the whole rule. A document or board under a leaf is refused: `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER`, `409` — *"Pages can only live inside folders."* | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:748-753` |
| N-4 | **Move rejects four ways**, and they are distinct outcomes, not one error: `same-parent`, `into-self`, `into-descendant`, `invalid-target`. `same-parent` is a no-op the caller should treat as success. | `src/lib/tree.ts:170-197` |
| N-5 | **Archiving is inherited and is not the same as being archived.** A node under an archived ancestor is *frozen*: every write is refused and it **cannot be thawed on its own**. A node archived in its own right is read-only but still offers Restore. `inheritedArchiveOf` looks at `path.slice(0, -1)` — the own flag is deliberately not read. | `src/lib/archive.ts:30-45`; `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:56-62, 79-85` |
| N-6 | `archiveSourceOf` walks **root-first** so the **outermost** archived ancestor is the one reported and the one whose Restore ends the freeze. E-034 therefore lists only the outermost archived node per subtree. | `src/lib/archive.ts:19-28` |
| N-7 | Delete is soft: `deleted_at` + `deleted_by`, never a boolean. `isTrashed` on the wire is `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`. Deleting **detaches the whole subtree**, so permanently deleting a folder cannot take an already-deleted child with it. | canon §1.4; `src/types/system.ts:164-169` |
| N-8 | A trashed node accepts **nothing but `node.delete`**. `can()` returns false for every other key. | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-81` |
| N-9 | Restore walks `originalAncestorIds` root-first for the deepest surviving container and reports `isRelocated` when the original parent is gone. This is a `200` outcome, never an error. | `src/types/system.ts:171-188`; canon §4.3 |
| N-10 | **Visibility pruning is subtree-wide.** `collectAllowed` skips a node *and its whole subtree* when the predicate fails: *"a file inside a folder the viewer cannot open must not surface in search results just because the file itself carries no restriction of its own."* | `src/lib/tree.ts:296-320` |
| N-11 | `is_shared` is **DERIVED**: true when any `access_rules` row exists on the node. | canon §1.3.1 |
| N-12 | `blockCount`, `excerpt`, `itemCount`, `openCount` are **DERIVED** projections kept in sync by the owning module. `summarize()` is the exact payload for a page. | `src/services/document-service.ts:148-171` |
| N-13 | `is_favorite` is **per user**, resolved from `node_favorites` for the caller — not a column on the node. | canon §8.8 *(OQ-07)* |

**Why one table and not five.** Every node variant shares one column set (`DriveNodeBase`,
`src/types/node.ts:48-78`), one routing key, one permission chain and one archive/trash lifecycle;
`resolvePath`, `collectAllowed`, `moveNode`, `cloneNode` and `effectiveAccess` all take `DriveNode`
without narrowing (`src/lib/tree.ts:15-320`, `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`); and
`UNIQUE (parent_id, slug)` must hold **across kinds**, which a split schema cannot express.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-56)** — three copies of `isArchived`
**What is unclear.** `DriveNodeBase.isArchived?` (`src/types/node.ts:66`), `DocumentNode.isArchived`
(required, `:103`) and `WorkspaceDocument.isArchived` (`src/types/document.ts:129`) are three fields
holding the same fact, and `summarize()` copies the document's value onto the node
(`src/services/document-service.ts:168`). Nothing declares which one is canonical.
**Evidence.** The freeze resolver reads the **node** chain and only the node chain
(`src/lib/archive.ts:37-45` → `findPathToId` over `DriveNode[]`). `documentCapabilities`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:135-141`) reads the **document** copy. The two never disagree in
the mock only because `summarize` runs on every save.
**Recommendation.** **The node owns it.** One column, `nodes.archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`.
`WorkspaceDocument.isArchived` and `DocumentNode.isArchived` are both projections of
`nodes.archived_at IS NOT NULL`, computed on read. `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/archive` (E-030) is the only
writer.
**Impact if wrong.** Two writable copies drift; a page that is archived on one surface and editable
on another is a data-integrity bug that only shows up as "the lock didn't take".

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-12)** — duplicating a container
**What is unclear.** E-027 duplicates recursively. `cloneNode` (`src/lib/tree.ts:200-230`) mints a
fresh id for every descendant but copies **tree metadata only** — it never reaches into `boards`,
`documents`, `config_documents` or `secret_documents`. Whether a duplicated project carries its
boards' rows, its pages' blocks, or its secrets' values is undecided.
**Evidence.** `documentService.duplicate` exists and copies blocks
(`src/services/document-service.ts:313`), so per-node content duplication is already modelled for
one kind. Nothing equivalent exists for boards or secrets. `SecretEntry` deliberately has no `value`
field at all (`src/types/devtools.ts:68-73`).
**Recommendation.** Duplicate content for `project`, `folder`, `document(page)`, `board` and `file`
(the asset is referenced, not re-uploaded — one `file_assets` row, two `file_nodes` rows).
**Refuse to duplicate a `secret` node**, and refuse the whole operation if the subtree contains one,
with `409` `PERMISSION_DENIED`-adjacent copy. Copying ciphertext silently doubles the blast radius of
a leak and produces a second rotation history that no audit trail explains.
**Impact if wrong.** Either duplicating a project silently produces empty boards, or it silently
clones every production secret in it.

#### 3.3.4 Board — records, schema, views

**Root.** `boards` (T-10), keyed to exactly one `nodes` row (`node_id UNIQUE NOT NULL`).

**Contents.** `board_columns`, `board_rows`, `board_views`, `board_view_preferences`,
`board_row_relations`, `row_activity`, `import_jobs`, `export_jobs`.

**Boundary.** The board is a **consistency boundary for the record set and its schema**. A column
write and the cell rewrites it causes are one transaction. A row write and its `row_activity` entry
and its `board_row_relations` projection are one transaction. Two boards are two boundaries — the
one operation that spans both, `bulkMove` (E-077), is explicitly *"one transaction over **both**
boards"* and needs `row.delete` on the source **and** `row.create` on the target *(OQ-17)*.

**Invariants.**

| # | Invariant | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B-1 | **`displayId` is minted by the backend, never derived on the client.** `boards.next_sequence` is monotonic and only increases: deleting `TASK-005` never re-issues `005`. `formatRowId(prefix, sequence)` pads to 3 and grows past it. | `src/types/board.ts:240-243`; `src/lib/row-id.ts:1-15`; `src/services/board-service.ts:65-68` |
| B-2 | `row_id_prefix` matches `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` — upper-case letters only, capped at six. | `src/lib/row-id.ts:9-20`; `ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID` |
| B-3 | **The cell's `kind` may legitimately disagree with its column's `type`.** A conversion preserves an unparseable value as `CellValue.text` rather than dropping it. The API must not normalise the tag away. | `src/types/board.ts:214-218`; canon §2.5 |
| B-4 | The frontend writes an **explicit empty `CellValue` of the column's kind**, never `null` or an absent key. Rows are dense by construction. | `src/lib/cell-values.ts:20-36` `emptyCellFor` |
| B-5 | **One write bumps `revision` once, however many cells it touched.** `updateCells` builds a `touched` map keyed by row id and increments once per row. | `src/services/board-service.ts:500-520` |
| B-6 | **Cell writes are last-write-wins plus a `ConflictNotice`. Never `409`.** Three exact properties: a missing `baseRevisions[rowId]` never conflicts; `base < current.revision` conflicts while equal-or-greater does not; **at most one notice per row per call**, raised by the first edit that touches it. | `src/services/board-service.ts:504-512` |
| B-7 | The **primary column** titles every record. It can never be hidden and never be deleted. `hidden` is *silently ignored* on it, not rejected. | `src/types/board.ts:178-179`; `src/lib/board-schema.ts:98-99` |
| B-8 | Column names de-duplicate silently: `Notes`, `Notes 2`, `Notes 3`. Two names collide when they differ only in case and punctuation. | `src/lib/board-schema.ts:150-179` |
| B-9 | Column `width` is clamped, never rejected: `[MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH, MAX_COLUMN_WIDTH]`, rounded. | `src/lib/board-schema.ts:70-72` |
| B-10 | Column `position` is **densely renumbered `0..n-1`** on reorder. View order is a separate array on `board_views.column_order`. | `src/lib/board-schema.ts:163-167`; `src/lib/board-view.ts:263-280` |
| B-11 | **Select options live inside `board_columns.config`.** Three sibling structures reference option ids by value — `completedOptionIds`, `transitionRules.transitions`, and each option's `availability` tree — so splitting them out puts one atomic configuration across two tables with no FK able to protect any reference. | canon §1.3.3; `src/types/board.ts:120-138` |
| B-12 | `"__empty__"` is a **reserved option id** standing for the empty bucket on both sides of a transition. It must be rejected as a user-authored id: `OPTION_ID_RESERVED`, `400`. | `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:27-32` |
| B-13 | Creating an option **dedupes by trimmed, case-folded label and returns the existing option with `200`** — never `409`. Colour is chosen client-side by cycling the eight-colour palette and sent in the request. | canon §3.7 E-058; `src/store/board-store.ts:844-851` |
| B-14 | Deleting an option leaves the orphaned id in `cells`. The frontend renders it as unknown, not deleted, so the backend **must not prune cells silently**. | canon §1.3.3 |
| B-15 | **Transition rules are not permission.** *"Permission answers 'may this person edit Status at all'; a transition rule answers 'may Status go from here to there'. Both are checked, separately, before a drop is written."* | `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:22-25` |
| B-16 | **Containment is not Relation.** `parentRowId` is containment; a "blocked by" dependency is a *relation column* holding row ids. *"The two live side by side and never read each other's data."* | `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:12-16` |
| B-17 | Deleting a parent row **lifts its children to top level**; it never cascades. E-065 returns the lifted children so the client reconciles. | canon §3.8 E-065 |
| B-18 | **Backlinks are derived, never stored.** *"Nothing is stored for a backlink: it is derived by asking which rows point here, so the two directions can never disagree."* `board_row_relations` is an index over the cells, written in the same transaction as the cell — not a second copy of the truth. | `src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:14-18` |
| B-19 | **Archived records are frozen, not deleted.** They are excluded from every view by default and are read-only until restored. `includeArchived` is the one switch. `bulkArchive` (E-075) is the only call that may target an archived row; `bulkDelete` (E-076) may too. | `src/lib/board-view.ts:183-187`; `src/lib/archive.ts:52-53` |
| B-20 | **A bulk response accounts for every id sent**: `requested === applied.length + skipped.length`. *"A bulk write that silently drops a record is worse than one that refuses."* Partial success is a `200`, never an error body. | `src/services/board-service.ts:957-965` |
| B-21 | One activity entry per write, however many fields it touched — *"'changed Status and Due Date' is one line in the timeline with two changes under it rather than two competing lines at the same second."* | `src/types/board.ts:489-495`; `src/services/board-service.ts:526-531` |
| B-22 | A view carries **at least one** per board: E-081 refuses the delete that would leave zero (`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`, `409`). | canon §3.10 |
| B-23 | `id` and `boardId` are **forcibly preserved** against a view patch (E-080). | canon §3.10 |
| B-24 | Listing boards is **derived from the tree and must never seed or read a board's rows** — *"a 5.000-record board is not built just to name it."* | `src/services/board-service.ts:1232-1245` |
| B-25 | A date-only cell is a `YYYY-MM-DD` day key and **must never be converted through UTC**. *"A due date is a square on a calendar, not a moment."* | `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24`; C-04 |

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-48)** — the board's column *roles* are name heuristics, and canon's generated
columns depend on them
**What is unclear.** Canon §1.3.2 requires four generated columns on `board_rows` — `due_date DATE`,
`due_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `status_option_id TEXT`, `assignee_ids UUID[]` — *"each derived from the column
the board designates for that role"*. **Nothing in the frontend stores such a designation.**
**Evidence.** `lensesFor` (`src/lib/my-work.ts:59-68`) resolves the three roles at read time by
regex over the column *name* (`/assign|owner|tester|responsible/i`, `/due|deadline/i`,
`/status|result|state/i`), with `fallbackToFirst` true for assignee and status and **false** for due
(*"'Found on' and 'Executed on' are history, not work that is due"*, `:63-64`). `Board` carries
`primaryColumnId` and nothing else role-shaped (`src/types/board.ts:412-427`).
**Recommendation.** Add three nullable columns to `boards`: `assignee_column_id`, `due_column_id`,
`status_column_id`, each `UUID NULL REFERENCES board_columns(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`. Populate them
at board creation from the template, and **seed them by running the existing regex once at
migration**, so no board changes behaviour on the day the backend lands. `PATCH /boards/{boardId}`
(E-050) gains them. The generated columns then read a designated id instead of a name. Keep the
regex as the *fallback* when a designation is null, so a board created before the field existed
still contributes to My Work.
**Impact if wrong.** If the roles stay name-based, the generated columns cannot exist (a generated
column may not depend on another table), so My Work, the deadline dashboard and every date filter
become a full scan of `cells` JSONB across every board the caller can see. If the roles become
*only* schema-based with no fallback, every board whose column is called "Owner" silently drops out
of My Work on the day of the cutover.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-15)** — rows are deleted permanently while nodes get a 30-day trash
**What is unclear.** `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}` (E-032) soft-deletes into `trash_entries` with a 30-day
retention. `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` (E-065) and `bulkDelete` (E-076) are permanent.
Whether that asymmetry is intended is not stated anywhere.
**Evidence.** `board_rows` carries `archived_at` (`src/types/board.ts:250-254`) but no `deleted_at`;
canon §1.4 lists `deleted_at` on `nodes`, `comments` and `board_rows` — so canon expects the column
to exist even though no endpoint sets it. Archive is presented to the user as the reversible
operation and Delete as the terminal one (`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx`).
**Recommendation.** Keep the asymmetry and make it explicit: `board_rows.deleted_at` exists and
E-065 sets it, but rows are **not** surfaced in `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/trash` and are swept on
the same nightly job at the same 30-day horizon. This gives support a recovery path without adding a
"Record trash" surface the product does not have.
**Impact if wrong.** If rows really are hard-deleted, `row_activity`, `comments`, `watches`,
`notifications` and `board_row_relations` all need cascade semantics decided at once, and a
mis-clicked bulk delete of 200 records is unrecoverable.

#### 3.3.5 Collaboration

**Root.** There is no single root. Comments, watches and notifications are three peer aggregates
that all address their target through one shape, `EntityRef` (`src/types/collab.ts:16-26`).

**The shared address.** `refKey` (`src/lib/entity-ref.ts:21-23`) is the only place in the codebase
that knows the format:

| `kind` | `targetKey` grammar | Segments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `row:<boardId>:<rowId>` | 3 |
| `document` / `board` / `project` / `folder` / `file` | `<kind>:<nodeId>` | 2 |

**RECOMMENDATION.** Store the target **decomposed** — `target_kind`, `target_node_id`,
`target_board_id`, `target_row_id`, `target_label` — and *serialise* `targetKey` on the way out
exactly as `refKey` does. A single opaque text key makes `ON DELETE CASCADE`, permission joins and
every My Work / search query a `LIKE`.

**Invariants.**

| # | Invariant | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C-1 | **Replies never nest past one level.** A reply to a reply re-parents to the root. `parent_id` therefore always points at a root comment or is null. | `src/types/collab.ts:60-64`; canon §3.19 E-125 |
| C-2 | **`mentionedUserIds` is parsed server-side** from `@[Name](usr_id)` in the body. A client-supplied list is ignored. | canon §3.19 E-120; `src/lib/mentions.ts` |
| C-3 | **Posting a comment is one transaction**: the comment + auto-watch the author + mention notifications + watcher notifications + the `row_activity` entry + the realtime frame. *"Posting is also the only place a notification is created for collaboration, which is what keeps the inbox consistent with what was actually said."* | `src/services/comment-service.ts:15-22` |
| C-4 | Delete is a **tombstone**, not a row removal, so replies do not orphan. Own comment at `member`, anyone else's at `manager`. | canon §3.19 E-122 *(OQ-24)* |
| C-5 | **Resolution is a thread property.** `is_resolved` / `resolved_by` / `resolved_at` live on the **root** comment only; resolving a reply is `COMMENT_RESOLVE_NOT_ROOT`, `409`. | canon §8.8 *(OQ-80)* |
| C-6 | **Only `row`, `document` and `board` are watchable** — *"a file or folder has no activity stream"*. Anything else is refused with `validation`. | `src/types/collab.ts:85-86`; `src/lib/entity-ref.ts:64-69` |
| C-7 | **A notification is one row per recipient**, fanned out on write. `list()` only ever returns the signed-in user's inbox; `notification.created` (RT-03) is delivered **only** to its `recipientId`. | `src/types/collab.ts:101-105`; `src/store/notification-store.ts:112` |
| C-8 | **Tabs are a projection of `reason`, not a second field** — *"one notification can never disagree with the tab it lands in."* The API filters by `reason`; the four-to-five mapping (`following` → `watch` + `comment`) stays in the frontend. | `src/lib/notifications.ts:3-13` *(OQ-90)* |
| C-9 | **`EntityRef.label` is frozen on `notifications` and resolved live everywhere else.** A notification is a historical statement; a comment target is not. The label is **untrusted display text, never an authorisation input** — visibility is re-resolved server-side before any list is returned. | canon §1.4, §8.8 *(OQ-79)*; `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:252-268` |
| C-10 | The unread badge is **server-computed** (E-132), so it is not "unread among the ones we loaded". | canon §3.21 *(OQ-91)* |
| C-11 | `markRead` **silently ignores ids outside the caller's own inbox** — it does not error. | canon §3.21 E-130 |
| C-12 | **Recent is not server state.** Per-device by nature; stays in `localStorage` under `nexdrop-recent`. Comment drafts likewise, under `nexdrop-comment-draft:<key>`. | `src/store/recent-store.ts:9-18`; `src/hooks/use-comment-draft.ts:5-17` *(OQ-96 / OQ-97)* |
| C-13 | **Favourites are per user**, a row in `node_favorites`, not a flag on the node. | canon §8.8 *(OQ-07)* |
| C-14 | Row activity stores **both** the rendered `changes` (returned to the client) and an internal `raw_changes` (never returned). *"The timeline reads these — it never sees, and never renders, a raw payload."* | `src/types/board.ts:479-482`; canon §8.8 *(OQ-51)* |

#### 3.3.6 Governance

**Root.** None — governance is a *cross-cutting* aggregate: `access_rules` keys a node,
`audit_events` keys a workspace, and roles and permissions are code, not rows.

**The two axes, never merged.**

- **ACCESS** answers *"may this person see this node at all"*. Resolved through the tree by
  `effectiveAccess` (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`).
- **CAPABILITY** answers *"what may they do with it"*. Resolved by `can`
  (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:69-87`) from the effective role plus the key.

**Invariants.**

| # | Invariant | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G-1 | **Access flows down the tree; the deepest rule wins.** `matchIn` walks the chain root→node and keeps the last match, so the most specific node wins. At one node a **user-scoped rule beats a role-scoped rule**. The workspace role is the floor. | `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:55-79, 91-120`; canon §8.8 *(OQ-22)* |
| G-2 | `explicit` vs `override` is one question: **does the rule written here agree with what would have flowed down**. | `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:114-119` |
| G-3 | **At most one rule per `(node, subject)`.** Writing replaces. A duplicate would make resolution order-dependent. | canon §3.5 E-042 |
| G-4 | Clearing the last rule on a node makes it **inherit again**. | canon §3.5 E-043 |
| G-5 | Three modes and no more: `inherit`, `workspace`, `restricted`. *"The point is that an ordinary person can look at a folder and say what it does. Anything finer belongs in the role matrix."* | `src/types/node.ts:3-15` |
| G-6 | **Three narrowing layers only ever take away**: trashed, frozen, locked. `READ_ONLY_KEYS = { board.export, workspace.audit.view, secret.reveal }` pass through all three. | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:29-33, 69-87` |
| G-7 | **A lock stops content writes and never the unlock itself.** `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS` is the twelve-key set a lock closes; `document.lock` is not in it. | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:36-49, 84` |
| G-8 | **`CapabilitySet` is a projection of the catalogue, not a parallel truth** — *"so `capabilities.edit` and `can('row.update')` can never disagree."* `edit` resolves to a *different key per node kind*. | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:108-132` |
| G-9 | **The frontend gate is not security.** *"It decides what the UI offers; the backend decides what actually happens, and must re-check every one of these keys."* | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:24-26` |
| G-10 | **A refusal names nothing.** *"A refusal that reads 'Finance is restricted' hands the name of a private folder to the one person who was told they may not have it."* `not_found` and "you may not see it" answer identically. | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-163`; canon §4.2 |
| G-11 | **`previewAs` may only narrow.** A preview role that outranks the caller's real role is `PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES`, `400`. | canon §4.3 *(OQ-21)* |
| G-12 | **Moving a node is a permission change.** It relocates the node under a different access chain, so E-026 emits `permission.changed` (RT-05). | canon §7.1 |
| G-13 | **The audit log is append-only by construction.** *"The service exposes `record` and `list`, and nothing else. There is no update path and no delete path, so no surface can offer one."* No write endpoint exists and no chapter may add one. | `src/types/audit.ts:4-10`; canon §3.23 |
| G-14 | `audit_events.ip` is **stamped by the backend off the socket. The client never sends one.** Same for `secret_access_events.ip`. | `src/types/audit.ts:32-33`; `src/types/devtools.ts:106-107` |
| G-15 | `audit_events.target` is the **human label** of the thing acted on — never an id, never a payload. `detail` is one sentence **written by the service** (SY-ACT-40). The structured payload goes to a separate, never-returned `context` column. | `src/types/audit.ts:35-38`; canon §5.3 `AuditContext` *(OQ-25)* |
| G-16 | **Refusals are recorded as carefully as successes.** A denied secret reveal writes its audit rows **before** the refusal is returned. Severity defaults to `error` on a denial, `info` otherwise. | `src/services/devtools-service.ts:342-345, 370-396` |
| G-17 | `copy` has **no permission key of its own** — it is gated by `secret.reveal` and audited as a reveal. *"Copying is a read of plaintext, so it files under reveal. Only an actual write to the stored value is a rotation."* | `src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-387` |
| G-18 | The 39-key catalogue is **static config served from the backend** (E-045), not a table. `PermissionModule` is **derived from the key's first segment, never declared beside it** — *"a key can therefore never be filed under a module it does not belong to."* | `src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:8-14`; canon §1.2 |
| G-19 | `audit_events.action` is *"the permission key wherever one governs it"*, but the field is typed `string`, not `PermissionKey` — some actions have no key. | `src/types/audit.ts:26-30` |

---

### 3.4 Derived, never stored

These are read-time projections. A chapter that adds a column for one of them has introduced a
second truth that will drift.

| Field | Derived from | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DriveNode.children` | `nodes.parent_id` | `src/types/node.ts:149-151` |
| `DriveNode.isTrashed` | `nodes.deleted_at IS NOT NULL` | canon §1.4 |
| `DriveNode.isArchived` | `nodes.archived_at IS NOT NULL` | *(OQ-56 above)* |
| `DriveNode.isShared` | `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM access_rules WHERE node_id = …)` | canon §1.3.1 |
| `DriveNode.isFavorite` | `node_favorites` for the calling user | *(OQ-07)* |
| `NodeState` | `deleted_at` → ancestor `archived_at` → own `archived_at` → active | canon §2.4 *(OQ-11)* |
| `DocumentNode.blockCount`, `.excerpt` | `documents.blocks` | `src/services/document-service.ts:160-171` |
| `BoardNode.itemCount`, `.openCount` | `board_rows` | canon §1.3.1 |
| `WorkspaceDocument.isLocked` | `documents.locked_by IS NOT NULL` | `src/services/document-service.ts:229-234` |
| `Board.name`, `Document.title`, `ConfigDocument.name`, `SecretDocument.name` | `nodes.name` | canon §8.8 *(OQ-30)* |
| `Backlink[]` | indexed query over `board_row_relations` | `backlinks-panel.tsx:14-18` |
| `SearchResultKind` ∈ `api\|bug\|qa` | `boards.template_id` at read time | `src/services/search-service.ts:39-43` |
| `MyWorkWidget[]`, `DashboardSummary` | scans over `board_rows` the caller may see | `src/services/my-work-service.ts:18-25` |
| `CellAttachment.url`, `.thumbnailUrl`, `FileNode.previewUrl` | short-lived signed URLs minted per response, **never accepted on write** | `src/types/board.ts:206-207`; canon §8.8 *(OQ-75)* |
| `ResolvedAccess.source`, `.inheritedRole`, `.inheritedFrom` | the ancestor chain | `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:127-167` |
| `CapabilitySet` | `can()` over the catalogue | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:121-132` |
| `AuditPage.total`, `.bySeverity` | facets over the **whole filtered set**, not the page | `src/types/audit.ts:50-55` |

### 3.5 Transaction boundaries

One statement per boundary. A chapter specifying one of these operations must reproduce the list.

| Operation | Must land atomically | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create workspace | `workspaces` + `workspace_members` (creator as admin) | E-008 |
| Delete node | `nodes.deleted_at` on the whole subtree + `trash_entries` row with the resolved ancestor chain and human path | E-032 |
| Restore | `trash_entries` delete + `nodes.deleted_at = NULL` on the subtree + slug re-uniquification | E-037 |
| Delete column | `board_columns` delete + `cells` key prune on every row + `pruneView` on every `board_views` row of the board | E-054 |
| Convert column | `board_columns.type` + `board_columns.config` + a rewrite of that key on every row | E-057 |
| Write cells | `board_rows.cells` + `revision + 1` + one `row_activity` entry per row + `board_row_relations` upsert for relation cells | E-066 |
| Delete row | `board_rows` + lift children to `parent_row_id = NULL` + `board_row_relations` prune | E-065 |
| Bulk move | source `board_rows` delete + target `board_rows` insert, **one transaction over both boards** | E-077 |
| Import | column creation + column removal + every row insert — *"all land or none do"* | E-085 |
| Post comment | `comments` + author auto-watch + mention `notifications` + watcher `notifications` + `row_activity` + realtime frame | E-120 |
| Reveal / copy secret | `secret_access_events` row **and** `audit_events` row, **before** the response — allowed or denied alike | E-103, E-104 |
| Rotate secrets | whole-list replace of `secrets` in the given order + one `secret_rotations` row per key touched + audit | E-102 |
| Complete upload | `file_assets` insert + `workspaces.used_bytes` increment (`FOR UPDATE`) + optional `nodes` + `file_nodes` insert | E-111 |
| Any access write | `access_rules` write + `audit_events` row + `permission.changed` frame | E-041, E-042, E-043 |

## 4. Database Schema

One PostgreSQL database, 39 tables (canon §1.1). This part documents the core of it: the six tables
that every other table hangs off — `users`, `user_sessions`, `workspaces`, `workspace_members`,
`workspace_invitations` — and the two that make the drive a drive: `nodes` and `access_rules`.
