Everything else in the registry either points at a node, points at a workspace member, or is
content keyed by `node_id`.

**Conventions that bind every table in the specification.**

*Primary keys.* Every table has `id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`. No exceptions, no
composite primary keys, no serial integers (canon C-01). A join table like `workspace_members` still
gets a surrogate `id`; its `(workspace_id, user_id)` pair becomes a `UNIQUE` constraint, not the key.
This is not decoration: `AccessRule.id` is a wire field the frontend addresses
(`DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules/{ruleId}`, E-043) and `src/store/permission-store.ts:63` mints
one for every grant, so surrogate keys are already in the contract.

*Business identifiers.* A human-facing identifier — `TASK-001`, a workspace slug, a node slug — is a
separate column and never the primary key (canon C-02). `board_rows.custom_id` is the canonical
example: `src/types/board.ts:240` records that it is *"assigned by the BACKEND, never derived on the
client"*, and `BD-RID-10` requires that deleting `TASK-005` never re-issues `005`. A `custom_id` is
therefore a value the server owns, unique within its scope, and independently mutable — a slug can be
re-uniquified on a move (E-026) while the row's `id` never moves. In this part the `custom_id`
pattern appears twice, both times under a different name because the frontend named them:
`workspaces.slug` (globally unique) and `nodes.slug` (unique among live siblings).

*Time.* Every instant is `TIMESTAMPTZ` in the database and ISO 8601 on the wire — `nowIso()` at
`src/services/backend.ts:64-66` produces `2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z` and nothing in `src/types/`
carries any other instant format (canon C-03). A date-only value is `DATE` in the database and
`YYYY-MM-DD` on the wire, and **must never be converted through UTC** (canon C-04) — the frontend
maintains an entire date-key layer for exactly this reason (`src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24`, *"A due date
is a square on a calendar, not a moment"*). No table in this part holds a date-only value; every
timestamp here is a real instant.

*Naming.* Tables are `snake_case` plural. Columns are `snake_case`. The API converts to `camelCase`
at the boundary, because the frontend is uniformly `camelCase` — `parent_id` ships as `parentId`,
`is_active` as `isActive`. Enum types are `snake_case` (`workspace_role`, `node_access_mode`) but
their **values are the frontend string literals verbatim, casing included** (canon C-13, §2.0):
`CREATE TYPE node_kind AS ENUM ('project','folder','document','board','file')`. Nothing normalises
`longText` to `long_text` anywhere in the schema, so no mapping layer exists that could drift.

*Soft delete.* Soft deletion is `deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL` plus `deleted_by UUID NULL`, never a
boolean (canon §1.4). It applies to exactly three tables in the whole schema: `nodes`, `comments` and
`board_rows`. `isTrashed` on the wire is `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`. Everything else is hard-deleted,
and the hard deletes are deliberate: a `workspace_members` row that is soft-deleted is a membership
that half exists, and `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14` is explicit that *"not a member" is not
"viewer"* — a half-membership is precisely the fallback that file exists to prevent. Archiving uses
the same shape one level up: `archived_at` / `archived_by`, never `is_archived BOOLEAN`, so the
Archive listing (E-034) can order by when the freeze happened and the audit trail knows who did it.

*Actor columns.* Every mutable table carries `created_at` and `updated_at`. Where a human actor
exists, it also carries `created_by` and `updated_by` referencing `users(id)`. These are resolved
**from the session, never from the request body** (canon C-09): `src/services/authz.ts:24-27` states
the rule — *"A role the client sends is a claim, not a fact, and an endpoint that trusts one is not
enforcing anything."* `users` itself has no `created_by` (a person is not created by another person
in any flow the frontend models), and `user_sessions` has none for the same reason.

*Users are never hard-deleted.* `src/types/user.ts:14-17` — *"Members removed from the workspace
stay resolvable so their name still renders — flagged inactive, never dropped"* — and
`src/mock/users.ts:41-58` ships two fixtures (`usr_former_thanh`, `usr_former_quyen`) that exist only
to exercise it. Consequently **every foreign key to `users(id)` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`**. The
deletion path is `users.is_active = false`, which is a normal `UPDATE`. Declaring `CASCADE` on a user
FK would be declaring an outcome the product has decided never to produce.

*JSONB.* Every JSONB column in the specification ships with its structure as a named TypeScript
interface in the same chapter (canon C-06). **No table in this part has a JSONB column.** Every
per-kind extra on `nodes` is a real, typed, nullable column, so it can carry a `CHECK`, be indexed,
and be validated by the database rather than by hope. That is a deliberate choice and it is defended
under `nodes` below.

*No `any`.* Every wire contract in this part is a closed discriminated union or a concrete scalar
(canon C-05).

**The shape of this part.**

```mermaid
erDiagram
    users ||--o{ user_sessions : "has"
    users ||--o{ workspace_members : "holds"
    workspaces ||--o{ workspace_members : "grants"
    workspaces ||--o{ workspace_invitations : "offers"
    workspaces ||--o{ nodes : "contains"
    users ||--o{ nodes : "owns"
    nodes ||--o{ nodes : "parent_id"
    nodes ||--o{ access_rules : "restricted by"
    users ||--o{ access_rules : "subject / granted_by"
```

Two axes run through every one of these tables and are never merged
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:15-33`):

- **ACCESS** — *may this person see this node at all.* Decided by `nodes.access_mode` walked root →
  node, with `access_rules` supplying the grants and `nodes.owner_id` as the standing safety net.
- **CAPABILITY** — *what may they do once they are looking.* Decided by `workspace_members.role`
  through the role matrix, narrowed by `access_rules` on the chain, then narrowed again by trashed /
  frozen / locked state.

*"a Viewer who is granted a restricted folder **sees it** and edits nothing, a Manager who is not
granted it **does not see it**, whatever their role"* (`visibility.ts:20-27`). Merging the two would
make "high enough role" a way into a folder somebody deliberately shut. No table in this part may be
read as if it answered both questions at once.

---

### Table: `users`

**Purpose** — One person, once, for the whole installation. Every name, avatar and initial rendered
anywhere in the product resolves here: a node's owner, a cell's assignee, a comment's author, an
audit event's actor. It is deliberately global rather than per-workspace, because one person is in
several workspaces and their identity must not fork.

**Who creates a record** — Sign-up (`POST /auth/login`'s registration sibling) or acceptance of a
workspace invitation (E-019). Both are **RECOMMENDATION** territory: the frontend has no
authentication surface at all — `src/mock/users.ts:3-9` hardcodes `CURRENT_USER` and every store
reads it directly (canon OQ-01, severity *blocking*). No other path creates a user; in particular
E-013 (`POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members`) creates a `workspace_invitations` row, not a user.

**Lifetime** — Permanent. A user is **never hard-deleted**. Removal from a workspace deletes the
`workspace_members` row; leaving the product sets `is_active = false` and `deactivated_at`, and every
projection keeps rendering the name flagged inactive (`DirectoryUser.isActive`,
`src/types/user.ts:18-20`). E-006 (`GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/directory`) **includes deactivated
members on purpose**, so a board cell assigned to somebody who left still renders a person instead of
an id.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Surrogate key. Ships as `UserSummary.id`. |
| `email` | `CITEXT` | no | — | yes | Login identity and the address an invitation is sent to. `CITEXT` because `Khanh@x.io` and `khanh@x.io` are one person; `src/mock/users.ts:6` stores it lowercase but nothing enforces case anywhere. |
| `name` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Display name. `UserSummary.name`. |
| `avatar_url` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `UserSummary.avatarUrl`. **Optional, not nullable, on the wire** (canon C-08): omit the key when the column is `NULL`, never send `null` — `src/types/user.ts:10` declares `avatarUrl?: string`. |
| `accent_color` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `UserSummary.accentColor`. A CSS custom-property reference such as `var(--kind-image)` (`src/mock/users.ts:13-16`). Assigned once at creation from the palette and then stable, because a person's colour changing under them is a bug, not a feature. Optional on the wire. |
| `password_hash` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | **RECOMMENDATION** (OQ-01). Argon2id. `NULL` for a user who has only ever authenticated through a future SSO path, so the column can never be read as "no password means any password". |
| `timezone` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | **RECOMMENDATION** (OQ-92). IANA zone name. Nothing in this part reads it; it is declared here because "today" and "overdue" have to be computed against *somebody's* midnight and the My Work / dashboard chapter owns that decision. |
| `is_active` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `true` | no | `DirectoryUser.isActive`. False means deactivated, and every projection keeps resolving the row. |
| `deactivated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | When `is_active` went false. Paired with the flag so the two cannot disagree (see the check constraint). |
| `last_login_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | **RECOMMENDATION** (OQ-01). Updated by E-001. Not on the wire. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Touched by E-005. |

`initials` is **not a column.** `UserSummary.initials` (`src/types/user.ts:9`) is a two-letter
fallback rendered when `avatarUrl` is absent, and it is a pure function of `name`. Storing it creates
a second copy that a rename can leave stale; deriving it server-side on the projection cannot. Derive
it with the same two-word rule `badgeFor` uses for workspace badges
(`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:167-177`): first letters of the first two words, upper-cased, falling
back to the first two characters of a single word.

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TABLE users (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email           CITEXT      NOT NULL,
  name            TEXT        NOT NULL,
  avatar_url      TEXT,
  accent_color    TEXT,
  password_hash   TEXT,
  timezone        TEXT,
  is_active       BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  deactivated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_login_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys** — none. `users` is a root table; it is the thing everything else points at.

**Unique Constraints**

| Constraint | Columns | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users_email_uniq` | `(email)` | One account per address. `CITEXT` makes it case-insensitive without a functional index. Violated → `MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` on invite acceptance, or the registration equivalent. |

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users_pkey` | `(id)` | Every join from `nodes.owner_id`, `workspace_members.user_id`, `access_rules.subject_user_id`, `comments.author_id`, `audit_events.actor_id`. |
| `users_email_uniq` | `UNIQUE (email)` | E-001 login by address; E-013 invite by address (`invite-member-dialog.tsx` filters candidates by `person.isActive && !isWorkspaceMember(...)`). |

No index on `name` and none on `is_active`. There is no server-side query that filters users by
either: the directory (E-006) is workspace-scoped and driven from `workspace_members`, and every
name filter in the product — the mention picker, the invite combobox, the access dialog's candidate
list — runs client-side over the already-loaded directory
(`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:99-115`). An index with no query behind it is a
write cost with no reader.

**Check Constraints**

| Constraint | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users_name_not_blank` | `char_length(btrim(name)) > 0` | A blank name renders as an empty avatar with no fallback. |
| `users_deactivation_consistent` | `(is_active = true AND deactivated_at IS NULL) OR (is_active = false AND deactivated_at IS NOT NULL)` | The flag and its timestamp are one fact. Two columns that can disagree eventually do. |

**Relationships**

| Cardinality | To | Through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1-N | `user_sessions` | `user_sessions.user_id` |
| N-N | `workspaces` | `workspace_members` (join carries `role`, `joined_at`) |
| 1-N | `nodes` | `nodes.owner_id`, plus `created_by` / `updated_by` / `archived_by` / `deleted_by` / `locked_by` |
| 1-N | `access_rules` | `access_rules.subject_user_id` and `access_rules.granted_by` |
| 1-N | everything with an actor | `comments.author_id`, `audit_events.actor_id`, `board_rows.created_by`, `secret_rotations.rotated_by`, … |

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Reads / writes | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-001 | `POST /auth/login` | reads `email`, `password_hash`; writes `last_login_at` | — (RECO, OQ-01) |
| E-004 | `GET /me` | reads the session's user | session |
| E-005 | `PATCH /me` | writes `name`, `avatar_url`, `accent_color`, `timezone`; returns `UserSummary` | session |
| E-006 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/directory` | joins `workspace_members` → `users`, returns `DirectoryUser[]` **including `isActive: false` rows** | membership |
| E-015 | `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}` | does **not** touch `users`; deletes the membership only | `workspace.member.manage` |

Every write returns the authoritative record — no `204` where the frontend expects an object
(canon C-10), because the stores replace optimistic state with the response.

**Errors**

`AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (401 / `permission_denied`) — the same message for a wrong address and a
wrong password, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts. `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`
(429 / `validation`, `isRetryable: true`, carries `retryAfterSeconds`).

---

### Table: `user_sessions`

**Purpose** — One refresh-token family per device, so a session can be revoked without revoking every
other device, and so a stolen refresh token is detectable. Access tokens are short-lived and are not
stored; only the refresh family is a row.

**Who creates a record** — E-001 (`POST /auth/login`). E-003 (`POST /auth/refresh`) rotates the
family: it marks the presented row `revoked_at` and inserts its successor with the same `family_id`.

**Lifetime** — Until `expires_at`, until E-002 revokes it, or until a replay revokes the whole family.
A nightly sweep hard-deletes rows past `expires_at + 30 days`; the grace window exists so a support
question about "why was I logged out" is answerable.

**RECOMMENDATION** (canon OQ-01, severity *blocking*) — **the entire table.** *"There is no
authentication, session or token model anywhere in the frontend."* `src/types/` contains no
credential, session, token, refresh token, OAuth identity or login-audit type. Canon §8.8 takes the
position: session-cookie auth against `users`, short-lived access token plus a rotating refresh
family here, identity resolved from the session and never from a request body.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | One issued refresh token. |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Who it authenticates. |
| `family_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Constant across every rotation on one device. Revoking a family logs out that device and nothing else. |
| `refresh_token_hash` | `BYTEA` | no | — | yes | SHA-256 of the token. The token itself is never stored, so a database dump is not a set of live sessions. |
| `issued_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |
| `expires_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | — | no | Absolute expiry of this token. |
| `revoked_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | Set on rotation, on logout, and on replay detection. |
| `replaced_by_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | The successor row. Present exactly when the row was retired by a normal rotation. |
| `user_agent` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | Recorded for the "your devices" surface a future release will want. Never returned to anyone but the owner. |
| `ip_address` | `INET` | yes | `NULL` | no | Taken from the socket, never from a header the client controls (canon C-09). |
| `last_used_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | Updated on each successful refresh. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are never hard-deleted; `RESTRICT` makes an accidental one fail loudly instead of silently destroying the only record of which devices held a session. Deactivation revokes sessions explicitly, in the same transaction, which is a write the audit log can see. |
| `replaced_by_id` | `user_sessions(id)` | `SET NULL` | The successor may be swept before its predecessor's grace window closes. Losing the pointer is harmless; blocking the sweep is not. |

**Unique Constraints**

| Constraint | Columns | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_sessions_token_uniq` | `(refresh_token_hash)` | Two rows with one token hash would make replay detection ambiguous. |

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_sessions_token_uniq` | `UNIQUE (refresh_token_hash)` | E-003: look up the presented token in one probe. |
| `user_sessions_family_idx` | `(family_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL` | Replay response: revoke every live row in the family in one statement. |
| `user_sessions_user_idx` | `(user_id, revoked_at)` | E-002 logout-everywhere; deactivating a user. |
| `user_sessions_expiry_idx` | `(expires_at)` | The nightly sweep. |

**Check Constraints**

| Constraint | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_sessions_window_valid` | `expires_at > issued_at` | A session that expires before it is issued is a clock bug the database can catch. |
| `user_sessions_no_self_replace` | `replaced_by_id IS NULL OR replaced_by_id <> id` | — |

**Relationships** — N-1 to `users`. Self-referential 1-1 chain through `replaced_by_id` within a
`family_id`.

**APIs that use it** — E-001 (insert), E-002 (revoke the presented family), E-003 (rotate).
E-003 is the security-critical one: if the presented `refresh_token_hash` resolves to a row whose
`revoked_at IS NOT NULL`, that is a replay — **revoke the entire `family_id`** and answer
`AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` (401 / `permission_denied`). This runs in one transaction with
`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the matched row, so two concurrent refreshes cannot both succeed.

**Errors** — `AUTH_REQUIRED` (401), `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` (401), `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` (401), all
mapping to `AppErrorCode` `permission_denied` per canon §4.2.

**Realtime** — none. A revocation reaches an open tab as a `401` on its next call, which the frontend
already maps through `toAppError` (`src/services/errors.ts:52-64`).

---

### Table: `user_ui_preferences`

Canon T-37. **RECOMMENDATION, deferred — OQ-98.** Do not build this until OQ-98 is
answered; nothing breaks while it does not exist.

**Purpose** — the handful of settings that describe how one person likes to look at the
product, as opposed to what the product contains. Today they live in the zustand store and
nowhere else: `isSidebarCollapsed` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:226`, `:916`), the drive's
`viewMode` of `grid` or `list` (`:118`, `:247`, `:451`) and the drive's sort key and
direction. Because the store is memory-only, every one of them resets on reload — which is
the whole argument for the table, and also the reason its absence is survivable.

**Who creates a record** — upsert on first write, by the owner and nobody else. There is no
create endpoint; E-141 `PUT /me/preferences/{scope}` writes the row or makes it.

**How long it lives** — as long as the user. Cascades on user delete. Never expires, never
archives; a stale preference is simply the last thing that person chose.

**How it is deleted** — only with the user row. There is deliberately no "reset my
preferences" endpoint: the client already knows every default, so a reset is a `PUT` of the
defaults, not a `DELETE`.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | Who this is for. |
| `scope` | `TEXT` | no | — | composite | Which surface: `sidebar`, `drive`. Deliberately not an enum — a new surface must not need a migration to be remembered. |
| `preferences` | `JSONB` | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | no | The values. Structure documented below, per scope. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |

**`preferences` JSONB — the complete contract, one variant per `scope`**

```ts
/** scope = "sidebar" */
interface SidebarPreferences {
  readonly isCollapsed: boolean;
}

/** scope = "drive" */
interface DrivePreferences {
  readonly viewMode: "grid" | "list";
  readonly sortKey: "name" | "updatedAt" | "createdAt" | "size";
  readonly sortDirection: "asc" | "desc";
}
```

Every field is optional on read: an unknown key is ignored and a missing key falls back to
the client's own default, so shipping a new preference never requires a backfill and never
breaks an older client.

**Primary Key** — `(user_id, scope)`. A natural composite rather than a surrogate `id`: the
pair *is* the identity, and a surrogate would permit two rows to disagree about one scope.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | `users(id)` | `CASCADE` | A preference about how to render a workspace is meaningless without the person whose preference it is. |

**Unique Constraints** — the primary key covers it.

**Indexes** — the primary key only. Every read is `WHERE user_id = $1`, bounded to a handful
of rows.

**Checks** — `CHECK (jsonb_typeof(preferences) = 'object')`, so a scalar or an array cannot
be written where the client will index by key.

**Delete Behavior** — hard delete with the user. Not soft-deleted: there is no audit
interest in what somebody's sidebar used to look like.

**Relationships** — N-1 to `users`. Deliberately **not** workspace-scoped: the sidebar is
collapsed or it is not, whichever workspace is open, and scoping it per workspace would make
one person's sidebar flicker between two states as they switch.

**APIs that use it** — E-140 `GET /me/preferences` returns every scope as one map (one
round trip at boot, before first paint). E-141 `PUT /me/preferences/{scope}` replaces one
scope. Both are session-scoped; neither takes a `userId`, because reading or writing
somebody else's preferences is not a thing this API can express.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-98)** — whether these should be server state at all. The cost is one
write per sidebar toggle; the benefit is that a second device opens the way the first was
left. The recommendation is yes for `drive` and yes for `sidebar`, and no for anything that
changes as fast as a scroll position.

---

### Table: `workspaces`

**Purpose** — The tenant boundary. Everything else in the schema is scoped to exactly one workspace,
and membership of a workspace is the outermost gate in the permission model
(`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`). It also carries the switcher's presentation — badge and colour —
and the storage counter the quota is checked against.

**Who creates a record** — E-008 (`POST /workspaces`). **The creator becomes an admin in the same
write**, not in a follow-up: `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:212-238` states why — *"a workspace whose
creator has to be added afterwards has a moment where nobody can administer it, and a failure in
between leaves one that nobody can ever administer."* The `workspaces` insert and the
`workspace_members` insert are one transaction or the endpoint has a failure mode that produces an
unadministrable tenant.

**Lifetime** — Until E-011 (`DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}`), which is a **hard delete** and takes
the whole tenant with it through `ON DELETE CASCADE`: nodes, members, invitations, access rules,
boards, documents, secrets, environments, audit events. There is no workspace trash. This matches the
frontend, which drops the tree and the bin outright (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:338-360`).

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | — |
| `name` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `Workspace.name`. 1–60 characters (`WORKSPACE_NAME_MAX = 60`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:196`). |
| `description` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `Workspace.description?`. ≤ 280 characters (`WORKSPACE_DESCRIPTION_MAX`, `:197`). **Optional on the wire** — omit the key when `NULL`. |
| `slug` | `TEXT` | no | — | yes | `Workspace.slug`, *"URL-safe identifier, unique across the tenant"* (`src/types/workspace.ts:17`). Minted by `uniqueSlug(slugify(name), taken)` (`:234`). **Globally unique** — canon OQ-02 position: single tenant, no tenant table above the workspace. |
| `plan` | `workspace_plan` | no | `'free'` | no | `free` \| `team` \| `enterprise` (`src/types/workspace.ts:3`). A new workspace starts `free` (`:235`). |
| `badge` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | 1–2 characters shown on the switcher tile. Derived from the name by `badgeFor` when the caller supplies none, else the caller's value upper-cased and truncated to 2 (`:236`). |
| `color` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | CSS colour for the tile. Cycles the `TILE_COLORS` palette when unspecified (`:180-187, :237`). |
| `used_bytes` | `BIGINT` | no | `0` | no | `StorageQuota.usedBytes`. **A transactionally maintained counter, never an aggregate computed on read** (canon §1.4). Incremented by E-111 in the same transaction as the `file_assets` insert; decremented when an asset is destroyed. |
| `storage_limit_bytes` | `BIGINT` | yes | `NULL` | no | Per-workspace override of the plan quota. `NULL` means "use the plan's quota from service config" — canon §1.2 is explicit that there is **no `plans` table**: three tiers with fixed quotas, static service config, *"not a row that can drift"*. `StorageQuota.totalBytes` on the wire is `COALESCE(storage_limit_bytes, quota_for(plan))` (OQ-06). |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | **RECOMMENDATION** — `Workspace` carries no timestamps (canon OQ-02 position: add them). |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Touched by E-010. |
| `created_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | The creator. Not a fifth role and not an ownership grant — canon OQ-03 position: **four roles**, and creator-ness is an attribute. It exists so "who made this tenant" is answerable. |

`members` and `storage` are **not columns.** `Workspace.members: readonly WorkspaceMember[]` and
`Workspace.storage: StorageQuota` (`src/types/workspace.ts:24-25`) are composed by the API: `members`
from `workspace_members ⋈ users`, `storage` from `used_bytes` and the plan quota. E-009 returns them
embedded because that is the frontend's shape; they are not stored embedded.

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TYPE workspace_plan AS ENUM ('free', 'team', 'enterprise');

CREATE TABLE workspaces (
  id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name                TEXT           NOT NULL,
  description         TEXT,
  slug                TEXT           NOT NULL,
  plan                workspace_plan NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',
  badge               TEXT           NOT NULL,
  color               TEXT           NOT NULL,
  used_bytes          BIGINT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  storage_limit_bytes BIGINT,
  created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by          UUID           NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
);
```

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `created_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are never hard-deleted. `RESTRICT` states the invariant in the schema rather than trusting every future code path to remember it. |

**Unique Constraints**

| Constraint | Columns | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaces_slug_uniq` | `(slug)` | The slug addresses the workspace. Two workspaces sharing one makes a URL ambiguous. Violated → `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` (409 / `conflict`). The API should not race for it: mint with `uniqueSlug` semantics inside the insert transaction and retry once on conflict. |

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaces_pkey` | `(id)` | Every scoped read in the product. |
| `workspaces_slug_uniq` | `UNIQUE (slug)` | Resolving a workspace from a URL segment; the uniqueness check on E-008 / E-010. |

E-007 (`GET /workspaces`) does **not** scan this table. It is driven from
`workspace_members (user_id)` — see that table's indexes. `visibleWorkspaces`
(`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:45-50`) is explicit that filtering a full list in the component would
leave *"every other consumer — a URL, a keyboard shortcut, a stale link — reading the full one"*, so
the server-side read starts at membership and joins outward.

**Check Constraints**

| Constraint | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaces_name_length` | `char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 60` | `validateWorkspaceName` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:200-207`). |
| `workspaces_description_length` | `description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 280` | `WORKSPACE_DESCRIPTION_MAX`. |
| `workspaces_badge_length` | `char_length(badge) BETWEEN 1 AND 2` | *"Short mark rendered in the switcher tile (1–2 chars)"* (`src/types/workspace.ts:20`). |
| `workspaces_slug_shape` | `slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$'` | Matches `slugify` output (`src/lib/utils.ts:60-70`). |
| `workspaces_used_bytes_non_negative` | `used_bytes >= 0` | A negative counter means a double decrement; catch it at the write. |
| `workspaces_storage_limit_positive` | `storage_limit_bytes IS NULL OR storage_limit_bytes > 0` | — |

**Relationships**

| Cardinality | To | Through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N-N | `users` | `workspace_members` |
| 1-N | `workspace_members`, `workspace_invitations`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `environments`, `board_templates` (user-authored), `audit_events`, `trash_entries` | each table's `workspace_id`, all `ON DELETE CASCADE` |

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Behaviour | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-007 | `GET /workspaces` | Only workspaces the caller is a member of. Never the full list. | session |
| E-008 | `POST /workspaces` | Insert + creator's admin membership in **one transaction** | session |
| E-009 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}` | Returns `Workspace` with `members` and `storage` composed | membership |
| E-010 | `PATCH /workspaces/{workspaceId}` | `name`, `description`, `badge`, `color`, `plan` | `workspace.manage` |
| E-011 | `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}` | Hard delete, cascade | `workspace.delete` |
| E-017 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/storage` | `{ usedBytes, totalBytes }` from `used_bytes` + plan quota | membership |
| E-110 | `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/uploads` | Reads `used_bytes` and the quota **before** issuing a presigned URL | `file.upload` |
| E-111 | `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` | `UPDATE workspaces SET used_bytes = used_bytes + $n` under `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, in the same transaction as the asset insert | `file.upload` |

**Transaction rule for `used_bytes`** (canon §1.4, OQ-05 position): every mutation of the counter
takes `SELECT used_bytes FROM workspaces WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` first. Two concurrent uploads that
each read the pre-increment value would both pass the quota check and both write, and the workspace
would end up over its limit with no error anywhere. Over quota → `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`
(507 / `upload_failed`).

**Errors** — `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404 / `not_found`) covers both an unknown workspace **and one the
caller is not a member of**; they answer identically so a URL cannot be used to learn which
workspaces exist (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:60-66`). `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` (409),
`QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (507).

**Realtime** — E-010 and E-011 emit no dedicated frame. A membership change emits `permission.changed`
(RT-05) with `nodeId: null`; see `workspace_members`.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-02) — destructive-delete confirmation.**
**What is unclear** — whether E-011 must require the caller to re-type the workspace name.
**Evidence** — PRD `WS-ARC-02` (`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:12`) requires exactly
that for a **project** with active members: *"Xóa Project đang có thành viên làm việc: Bắt buộc nhập
lại tên Project để xác nhận."* It says nothing about a workspace. The frontend's
`deleteWorkspace` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:338-360`) takes no confirmation argument at all.
**Recommendation** — treat the PRD rule as a client-side gate for projects (E-032 on a node of kind
`project`) and add nothing to the wire for it, since the backend cannot verify that a human typed
anything. For E-011, which destroys a tenant, require `workspace.delete` — already Admin-only — and
audit it at `error` severity. Do not invent a `confirmName` body field: it is theatre the server
cannot enforce.
**Impact if wrong** — if the confirmation is meant to be server-verified, a scripted call can destroy
a workspace that the UI would have made somebody type a name to destroy.

---

### Table: `workspace_members`

**Purpose** — The join between a person and a tenant, carrying the role that person holds there. It is
**the outermost gate**: before any question about a folder, a board or an access rule, there is *are
you in this workspace at all* (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`). The absence of a row is not a
`viewer` row — *"'Not a member' is not 'viewer'"* — and the schema must never be read as if a missing
row had a default.

**Who creates a record** — E-008 (the creator, as `admin`, in the workspace's own transaction) and
E-019 (`POST /invitations/{token}/accept`). E-013 does **not** create one; it creates a
`workspace_invitations` row. E-014 (`PATCH .../members/{userId}`) updates `role` on an existing row.

**Lifetime** — Until E-015 (removed by an admin) or E-016 (`DELETE .../members/me`, leaving). Both are
**hard deletes**. There is no soft-deleted membership, because a soft-deleted membership is exactly
the "somebody who holds no role but is not absent" state the module exists to make impossible. The
person survives in `users` with `is_active` untouched, so every cell, comment and audit row that
names them still renders.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Surrogate key per canon C-01, even though the natural key is the pair below. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | (composite) | — |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | no | — | (composite) | — |
| `role` | `workspace_role` | no | `'member'` | no | `viewer` \| `member` \| `manager` \| `admin` — **the declaration order is the rank** (`src/types/permission.ts:8-20`; `roleRank` is `WORKSPACE_ROLES.indexOf(role)`). Ship the enum values in that order so `roleRank` is reproducible server-side. |
| `joined_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `WorkspaceMember.joinedAt` (`src/types/user.ts:24`). |
| `invited_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Who invited them. `NULL` for the workspace creator, who invited nobody. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Equal to `joined_at` in practice; kept for uniformity with every other mutable table. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Touched by a role change. |
| `updated_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Who last changed the role, from the session (canon C-09). `NULL` until the first change. |

`WorkspaceMember` on the wire extends `UserSummary` — the API composes
`users ⋈ workspace_members` and flattens. Note it carries **no `workspaceId`**
(`src/types/user.ts:22-25`): it is always read in the context of one workspace, as `Workspace.members`
or as the body of E-012.

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TYPE workspace_role AS ENUM ('viewer', 'member', 'manager', 'admin');

CREATE TABLE workspace_members (
  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  workspace_id UUID           NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id      UUID           NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)      ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  role         workspace_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
  joined_at    TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  invited_by   UUID           REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by   UUID           REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  CONSTRAINT workspace_members_pair_uniq UNIQUE (workspace_id, user_id)
);
```

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | A membership of a workspace that no longer exists is not a fact about anything. E-011 is intended to take the tenant and everything scoped to it. |
| `user_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are never hard-deleted (`src/types/user.ts:14-17`). `RESTRICT` turns an accidental hard delete into a failed statement instead of a silent mass un-membering. |
| `invited_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Same reason; this is history. |
| `updated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Same reason. |

**Unique Constraints**

| Constraint | Columns | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members_pair_uniq` | `(workspace_id, user_id)` | One membership per person per workspace. The frontend's `withMember` already treats a repeat add as a role change rather than a second row (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:244-259`); the constraint is what lets the API implement that as `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (workspace_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET role = …`. It is also the target of a composite FK from `access_rules` — see that table. |

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members_pair_uniq` | `UNIQUE (workspace_id, user_id)` | **Gate 1 on every single request**: "is this caller a member of this workspace, and with what role". This is the hottest index in the schema — `SY-RBC-42` budgets p99 < 10 ms at the middleware. One probe, covering, no heap fetch if `role` is included. |
| `workspace_members_user_idx` | `(user_id)` | E-007 (`GET /workspaces`) — the workspaces this person is in. |
| `workspace_members_admin_idx` | `(workspace_id) WHERE role = 'admin'` | The last-admin check (below). Partial, because it is only ever asked about admins. |

Recommended covering form: `UNIQUE (workspace_id, user_id) INCLUDE (role)` so gate 1 is an
index-only scan.

**Check Constraints** — none beyond the enum and the FKs. The last-admin rule is **not** a check
constraint: it is a cross-row invariant over a filtered set, which `CHECK` cannot express, and it has
to be enforced transactionally anyway.

**The last-admin invariant** — **EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-162` defines
it once and reads it from three directions, and the API must refuse all three:

| Endpoint | Refusal | Frontend rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E-014 demoting the last admin | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` (409 / `conflict`) | `canChangeRole` (`:149-162`) |
| E-015 removing the last admin | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` | `canRemoveMember` (`:122-146`) |
| E-016 the last admin leaving | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` | `canLeaveWorkspace` (`:106-119`) |

*"A workspace with no administrator cannot be repaired from inside it — the members who are left can
neither invite anyone nor promote anyone, which is a shape the product should never be able to reach
by accident"* (`:98-105`).

**Transaction.** The check and the write are one transaction, and the check must lock:

```
BEGIN;
  SELECT user_id FROM workspace_members
    WHERE workspace_id = $ws AND role = 'admin'
    FOR UPDATE;                       -- locks the admin set, not just one row
  IF the result is exactly [$target] THEN raise WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN;
  <the demotion / removal / departure>
COMMIT;
```

Without `FOR UPDATE` over the admin set, two concurrent demotions of the two remaining admins each
see one other admin, each pass, and the workspace ends with none. This is the one place in this part
where a race produces an unrecoverable state, so it is worth the lock.

`canRemoveMember` also refuses `actorId === targetId` with *"Use Leave workspace to take yourself out
— removing is for other people."* (`:122-132`) — E-015 must reject a self-target and point at E-016,
because E-016 does something extra that E-015 does not (below).

**E-016 does two things in one write.** `removeMember` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:388-408`):
when the person leaving is the caller *and* the workspace they are leaving is the one they are
standing in, the response also switches them to another workspace they hold — *"there is no frame in
which the app is showing a tree they no longer hold."* The API expresses this by returning `204` and
letting the client re-read E-007, but the server-side obligation is the same: publish
`permission.changed` before the response returns.

**Relationships**

| Cardinality | To | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N-1 | `workspaces` | — |
| N-1 | `users` | — |
| — | `access_rules` | A user-scoped rule *should* name a member, but there is deliberately **no FK** enforcing it. See `access_rules` → Foreign Keys. |

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Behaviour | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-007 | `GET /workspaces` | Drives the whole read | session |
| E-012 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members` | `WorkspaceMember[]`, `users ⋈ workspace_members` | membership |
| E-013 | `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members` | Creates a `workspace_invitations` row, returns `WorkspaceInvitation`. Does **not** insert here. | `workspace.member.manage` |
| E-014 | `PATCH /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}` | Role change; last-admin guarded | `workspace.member.manage` |
| E-015 | `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}` | Removal; last-admin guarded; self-target refused | `workspace.member.manage` |
| E-016 | `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/me` | Leaving; last-admin guarded | membership |
| E-019 | `POST /invitations/{token}/accept` | Inserts the row and consumes the invitation, one transaction | authenticated |
| — | *every request* | Gate 1: membership + role, before any node is touched | — |

**Errors** — `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` (409 / `conflict`), `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` (404 / `not_found`),
`MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` (409 / `conflict`), `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404) for a caller who is not a
member.

**Realtime** — every write here publishes **RT-05 `permission.changed`** with
`{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds }` (canon §7.1). `nodeId` is `null` precisely because the change
is workspace membership rather than one node. The frame carries **ids only**: *"a frame announcing a
revocation must not be the thing that leaks what was revoked"* (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`).
Without it, a demoted user keeps a loaded board on screen until they reload
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`), and RT-05 is therefore not optional. The same event must bust any
server-side authorization cache keyed by `(workspaceId, userId)`.

**Audit** — every write here is an `audit_events` row in the same transaction:
module `workspace`, action `workspace.member.manage`, severity `warn`.

---

### Table: `workspace_invitations`

**Purpose** — A pending offer of membership to an email address that may not yet have a `users` row.
It exists because E-013 has to be able to invite somebody who has never signed in, and because
`WorkspaceMember.joinedAt` implies a moment of joining that nothing in the frontend models.

**Who creates a record** — E-013 (`POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members`), which returns
`WorkspaceInvitation`, not `WorkspaceMember`.

**Lifetime** — Until accepted (E-019 sets `accepted_at` and inserts the membership in one
transaction), revoked, or expired. Rows are kept after acceptance as evidence of who invited whom; a
sweep hard-deletes rows more than 90 days past `expires_at` that were never accepted.

**RECOMMENDATION** — the whole table (canon OQ-04). *"The invitation flow implied by
`WorkspaceMember.joinedAt` is unmodelled."* The frontend's invite dialog adds an existing directory
user straight into `Workspace.members` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:244-259`); there is no pending
state anywhere in `src/`. The interface `WorkspaceInvitation`
`{ id, workspaceId, email, role, invitedBy, expiresAt, acceptedAt }` is added by canon §5.3.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | — |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | (composite) | — |
| `email` | `CITEXT` | no | — | (composite) | Address invited. Deliberately not an FK to `users`: the invitee may not exist yet. |
| `role` | `workspace_role` | no | `'member'` | no | The role the membership will be created with. |
| `token_hash` | `BYTEA` | no | — | yes | SHA-256 of the invitation token. The token is emailed and never stored, exactly as with refresh tokens. |
| `invited_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | From the session. |
| `expires_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | — | no | **RECOMMENDATION**: 14 days. Served to the client from `GET /config` (E-139) so the two sides cannot disagree. |
| `accepted_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | Set by E-019. Non-null means consumed. |
| `accepted_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | The `users` row that accepted — which may have been created by the acceptance itself. |
| `revoked_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | An admin withdrawing the invitation. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | An invitation to a destroyed workspace cannot be accepted and has no meaning. |
| `invited_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | History. |
| `accepted_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | History. |

**Unique Constraints**

| Constraint | Columns | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_invitations_token_uniq` | `(token_hash)` | One token, one invitation. |
| `workspace_invitations_pending_uniq` | `(workspace_id, email) WHERE accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL` | At most one live invitation per address per workspace. A second invite to the same address is `MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` (409), matching *"Already a member or already invited"* in canon §4.3. Partial, so re-inviting somebody whose earlier invitation expired is allowed. |

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_invitations_token_uniq` | `UNIQUE (token_hash)` | E-019: resolve a token in one probe. |
| `workspace_invitations_pending_uniq` | partial unique, above | E-018 (`GET .../invitations`) filtered to live rows; the duplicate-invite check on E-013. |
| `workspace_invitations_expiry_idx` | `(expires_at) WHERE accepted_at IS NULL` | The sweep. |

**Check Constraints**

| Constraint | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_invitations_not_both_terminal` | `NOT (accepted_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_at IS NOT NULL)` | An invitation cannot be both accepted and withdrawn. |
| `workspace_invitations_accepted_pair` | `(accepted_at IS NULL) = (accepted_by IS NULL)` | The two are one fact. |
| `workspace_invitations_window` | `expires_at > created_at` | — |

**Relationships** — N-1 to `workspaces`; N-1 to `users` twice (`invited_by`, `accepted_by`); 1-1 with
the `workspace_members` row it produces, though the link is not stored — the membership's
`invited_by` carries the same person and that is sufficient.

**APIs that use it** — E-013 (insert), E-018 (`GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations`, gated on
`workspace.member.manage`), E-019 (`POST /invitations/{token}/accept`, authenticated).

E-019 is one transaction: resolve the token, assert `accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND
expires_at > now()`, create or find the `users` row, insert `workspace_members`, set `accepted_at` /
`accepted_by`, write the audit row, publish RT-05. Any failure rolls all of it back — a consumed
invitation with no membership behind it is unrecoverable from the UI.

**Errors** — `INVITATION_INVALID` (404 / `not_found`) for a token that is unknown, consumed, revoked
**or expired**; all four answer identically so a token cannot be probed for its state.
`MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` (409) on a duplicate invite.

**Realtime** — E-019 publishes RT-05 (`permission.changed`, `nodeId: null`), because a new member's
visible tree just changed from nothing to something.

---

### Table: `nodes`

**Purpose** — The drive tree, and the spine of the whole product. Every addressable thing lives here
as one row: a project, a folder, a block page, a config document, a secret document, a board, a file.
Routing resolves against it (`resolvePath`), permissions resolve against it (`visibleTree`,
`effectiveAccess`), archiving and trashing are lifecycle states on it, and the five content tables —
`boards`, `documents`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents`, `file_nodes` — are 1:1 side tables
keyed by `node_id`.

**Who creates a record** — E-024 (`POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes`, one endpoint with `kind` in
the body), E-027 (`POST /nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate`, recursively), E-111 (`POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete`
when `createDriveNode` is true — canon OQ-74 position: default `true` for drive and document-block
uploads, `false` for board cells and comments).

**Lifetime** — Three states and a purge. Active → archived (`archived_at`, reversible via E-031) →
trashed (`deleted_at`, E-032, which **detaches the whole subtree**) → hard-deleted by E-038, E-039 or
the 30-day retention sweep (canon OQ-14 position; `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`,
`src/config/app.ts:42`). Restoring walks the recorded ancestor chain for the deepest surviving
container (E-037), which is why deletion is soft and detaching rather than a cascade.

#### Why one table

**DECIDED (canon §1.3.1): a single `nodes` table**, discriminated by `kind`, with the shared column
set as real columns and the per-kind extras as nullable columns.

Every node variant already shares one column set (`DriveNodeBase`, `src/types/node.ts:48-78`), one
routing key, one permission chain and one archive/trash lifecycle, and `parent_id` is
**self-referential across kinds** — a board sits inside a folder sits inside a project. Five tables
would mean a five-way `UNION` on every tree walk, every ancestor chain, every access resolution and
every breadcrumb. `resolvePath`, `collectAllowed`, `moveNode`, `cloneNode` and `effectiveAccess` all
take `DriveNode` without narrowing (`src/lib/tree.ts:15-320`,
`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`). And `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug)` must hold **across
kinds** — a folder and a board cannot both be `payment` under the same parent — which a split schema
cannot express at all.

**And no JSONB for the extras.** The per-kind fields are eleven typed scalars, not an open bag:
`color`, `description`, `project_status`, `document_kind`, `icon`, `board_kind`, plus the four derived
counters and `excerpt`. As real columns they carry `CHECK` constraints that make an invalid shape
impossible (a project with no status, a board with no `board_kind`), and `project_status` is a
Postgres enum rather than a string somebody can typo. As JSONB none of that is available and the
whole benefit — one row per node — is unchanged. Canon C-06 would also require an interface per
variant, which is five interfaces describing columns that could simply be columns.

#### Columns

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `DriveNode.id`. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | (composite) | `DriveNode.workspaceId`. Denormalised onto every node — it is on the frontend type too (`src/types/node.ts:54`) — because every listing, search and quota query is workspace-scoped and none of them should have to walk to the root to find out where they are. Kept honest by a composite FK (below). |
| `parent_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | (composite) | `DriveNode.parentId`. `NULL` means the workspace root. Self-referential. |
| `kind` | `node_kind` | no | — | no | `project` \| `folder` \| `document` \| `board` \| `file`. Ships as `node.kind`. **This is canon's one rename**: the frontend calls the type `DriveNodeType` and the field `type` (`src/types/node.ts:24`); the wire field is `kind` on a table called `nodes`, and the five members are unchanged (canon §2.1). |
| `name` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `DriveNode.name`. |
| `slug` | `TEXT` | no | — | (composite) | `DriveNode.slug` — *"URL-safe segment, unique among siblings — the routing key"* (`src/types/node.ts:51-52`). Minted once at creation by `uniqueSlug(slugify(name), siblingSlugs)`; **not re-minted on rename**, re-uniquified **only on move** (canon OQ-09 / OQ-10 position). |
| `owner_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `DriveNode.owner` (a `UserSummary`, joined on read). Ownership is a **separate axis from role** (`src/types/permission.ts:3-7`): it escalates five keys on your own things and it always admits you to a restricted node (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:76-93`). |
| `access_mode` | `node_access_mode` | no | `'inherit'` | no | `inherit` \| `workspace` \| `restricted`. On the wire it is `accessMode?`, and **absent means `inherit`** (`src/types/node.ts:77`, `accessModeOf` at `visibility.ts:47-50`) — so the API omits the key when the column is `'inherit'`. Applies to **every kind**, files included, not only containers. |
| `archived_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | `isArchived` on the wire is `archived_at IS NOT NULL`. A timestamp rather than a boolean so E-034 can order the archive listing and the audit trail knows when. |
| `archived_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | From the session. |
| `deleted_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | `isTrashed` on the wire is `deleted_at IS NOT NULL` (canon §1.4). |
| `deleted_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | From the session. Feeds `TrashEntry.deletedBy`. |
| `color` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | Required for `project` (`ProjectNode.color: string`), optional for `folder` (`FolderNode.color?`), and must be `NULL` for the other three. The asymmetry is real and is in the type (`src/types/node.ts:84` vs `:91`). |
| `description` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `ProjectNode.description?`. Projects only. |
| `project_status` | `project_status` | yes | `NULL` | no | `active` \| `paused` \| `archived` (`src/types/node.ts:46`). Required for `project`, `NULL` otherwise. See the open question below — it overlaps `archived_at`. |
| `document_kind` | `document_kind` | yes | `NULL` | no | `page` \| `config` \| `secret`. **Absent means `page`** (`documentKindOf`, `src/types/node.ts:144`), so the API omits the key when the column is `'page'`, exactly as the mock factory does (`src/mock/factory.ts:169-172`). Documents only. It selects which side table holds the content: `documents`, `config_documents` or `secret_documents`. |
| `icon` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `DocumentNode.icon` — an emoji. Required for `document`. |
| `board_kind` | `board_kind` | yes | `NULL` | no | `kanban` \| `table` \| `timeline` \| `doc`. Required for `board`. **A presentation hint, stored as given and never validated against `BoardViewType`** — the two vocabularies genuinely differ and canon OQ-31 takes the position that they stay apart. |
| `is_pinned` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `false` | no | `DocumentNode.isPinned`. Canon OQ-30 position: **the node owns it**, and `documents` projects it rather than duplicating it. |
| `locked_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | `isLocked` is `locked_at IS NOT NULL`. A lock closes the content-write key set and nothing else (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:36-49, 84`). |
| `locked_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | `WorkspaceDocument.lockedBy` (`src/types/document.ts:128`). **From the session, never from the request body** (canon OQ-60). Kept beside `locked_at` so the two cannot drift. |
| `block_count` | `INTEGER` | yes | `NULL` | no | `DocumentNode.blockCount`. **Derived, denormalised, maintained by the `documents` module** in the same transaction as a save — `DocumentSummaryPatch` (`src/services/document-service.ts:148-170`) is exactly this projection. |
| `excerpt` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `DocumentNode.excerpt` (first ~120 characters of the blocks) and `FileNode.excerpt?` (plain-text head of a text-like file). One column, two producers, same meaning: the body text search and the listing subtitle both read it (`src/services/search-service.ts:145-146`). |
| `item_count` | `INTEGER` | yes | `NULL` | no | `BoardNode.itemCount`. Denormalised counter, maintained by the `boards` module. |
| `open_count` | `INTEGER` | yes | `NULL` | no | `BoardNode.openCount`. Same. |
| `search_vector` | `tsvector` | no | generated | no | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(name,'') \|\| ' ' \|\| coalesce(excerpt,''))) STORED`. Canon §1.2: there is deliberately **no separate `search_index` table**; `tsvector` columns with GIN indexes live on `documents`, `board_rows`, `comments` and `nodes`. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `DriveNode.createdAt`. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `DriveNode.updatedAt`. Touched by rename, move, content save, archive, restore. |
| `created_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Equal to `owner_id` at creation; they diverge if ownership is ever transferred. |
| `updated_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | From the session. |

**Five wire fields that are NOT columns**, and must not become columns:

| Wire field | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `children` | **Derived** from `parent_id` (canon §1.3.1; `childrenOf`, `src/types/node.ts:150-151`). Storing it is storing the tree twice. |
| `isFavorite` | **Per user**, from `node_favorites (user_id, node_id)` (T-07, canon OQ-07 position). The frontend models it as a plain boolean on the node (`src/types/node.ts:58`), which is wrong for a multi-user server: two people starring the same board would fight over one column. Documented in a later part. |
| `isShared` | **Derived**: true when any `access_rules` row exists on the node (canon §1.3.1). |
| `isTrashed` / `isArchived` | Derived from `deleted_at` / `archived_at`. Both stay on the wire because the frontend reads them (`src/types/node.ts:56-70`). |
| `templateId` (boards) | Projected from `boards.template_id` by the 1:1 join. `BoardNode.templateId` is a bare `string`, *"for reference only"* (`src/types/node.ts:110-111`), and one source of truth beats two. The join is cheap — `boards.node_id` is unique-indexed — and it does not read a board's rows, which is what E-048 forbids. |
| `previewUrl` / `thumbnailUrl` (files) | **Minted per response** as short-lived signed URLs, never stored and never accepted on write (canon OQ-75 position). The frontend's values are session object URLs that die with the tab. |
| `kind`, `extension`, `mimeType`, `sizeBytes`, `version` (files) | From `file_nodes` → `file_assets` (T-27/T-28), not from `nodes`. |
| `state` | `NodeState`, derived on read, never stored. See below. |

**`NodeState`** (canon §2.4) — a derived, read-only, additive field. It is not a column; it is
computed per node per request, and its precedence is exactly the frontend's:

```ts
/** Derived on read. Never a stored column. Precedence is top to bottom. */
type NodeState =
  | "trashed"    // deleted_at IS NOT NULL — accepts nothing but node.delete
  | "frozen"     // an ANCESTOR is archived — every write refused, and the node
                 // cannot be thawed on its own
  | "archived"   // this node's own archived_at — read-only, but Restore is offered
  | "active";
```

`frozen` reads the **ancestors only** and deliberately not the node's own flag
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:57-62`, `src/lib/archive.ts:30-45`): *"you can always restore the
thing you are standing on, but a page inside an archived project cannot be thawed on its own."*
E-031 must refuse a restore on a node with an archived ancestor — `NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED`
(409 / `conflict`).

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TYPE node_kind        AS ENUM ('project', 'folder', 'document', 'board', 'file');
CREATE TYPE node_access_mode AS ENUM ('inherit', 'workspace', 'restricted');
CREATE TYPE document_kind    AS ENUM ('page', 'config', 'secret');
CREATE TYPE board_kind       AS ENUM ('kanban', 'table', 'timeline', 'doc');
CREATE TYPE project_status   AS ENUM ('active', 'paused', 'archived');

CREATE TABLE nodes (
  id             UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  workspace_id   UUID             NOT NULL,
  parent_id      UUID,
  kind           node_kind        NOT NULL,
  name           TEXT             NOT NULL,
  slug           TEXT             NOT NULL,
  owner_id       UUID             NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  access_mode    node_access_mode NOT NULL DEFAULT 'inherit',

  archived_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  archived_by    UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  deleted_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
  deleted_by     UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  color          TEXT,
  description    TEXT,
  project_status project_status,
  document_kind  document_kind,
  icon           TEXT,
  board_kind     board_kind,
  is_pinned      BOOLEAN          NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  locked_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  locked_by      UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  block_count    INTEGER,
  excerpt        TEXT,
  item_count     INTEGER,
  open_count     INTEGER,

  search_vector  tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
                   to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(name, '') || ' ' || coalesce(excerpt, ''))
                 ) STORED,

  created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  updated_by     UUID          REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  CONSTRAINT nodes_id_workspace_uniq UNIQUE (id, workspace_id),
  CONSTRAINT nodes_workspace_fk FOREIGN KEY (workspace_id)
    REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT nodes_parent_fk FOREIGN KEY (parent_id, workspace_id)
    REFERENCES nodes(id, workspace_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column(s) | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | E-011 destroys the tenant and everything scoped to it. A node whose workspace is gone is unreachable by every endpoint in the API — there is no route to it that does not start at a workspace. |
| `(parent_id, workspace_id)` | `nodes(id, workspace_id)` | `CASCADE` | Two jobs in one constraint. (a) **A child can never be in a different workspace from its parent** — a plain `parent_id → nodes(id)` FK permits it, and one cross-tenant node makes `visibleTree` return another tenant's subtree. The composite form makes it impossible, which is why `nodes_id_workspace_uniq` exists. (b) The cascade is what makes a purge one statement. The three endpoints that hard-delete a node — E-038 (purge one trash entry), E-039 (empty trash), E-011 (delete workspace) — all intend the whole subtree to go, and all three compute reclaimed bytes and write their audit row **before** issuing the delete. **No other code path may issue `DELETE FROM nodes`.** Everything else is `UPDATE … SET deleted_at = now()`. |
| `owner_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | The owner is the standing safety net into a restricted node (`visibility.ts:87-93`): *"Somebody has to be able to get back into a folder they shut."* Losing the owner silently would strand the node behind the admin recovery console. Users are deactivated, never deleted, so this never fires — which is the point of declaring it. |
| `archived_by`, `deleted_by`, `locked_by`, `created_by`, `updated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | History. Every one of these appears in a `TrashEntry`, a banner or an audit row. |

**Unique Constraints**

Slug uniqueness is **per sibling set, scoped by workspace at the root, and excludes trashed rows**
(canon §1.3.1). It needs two partial unique indexes rather than one constraint, because in Postgres
`NULL` parent ids are all distinct from one another and would not collide:

| Index | Definition | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes_slug_child_uniq` | `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug) WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL` | `resolvePath` walks the chain and takes the **first** match (`src/lib/tree.ts:48-57`), so two siblings sharing a slug makes the loser permanently unreachable and every link to it silently opens the other. `src/store/workspace-store.ts:472-480` documents exactly this: *"the loser becomes unreachable and every link to it silently opens the other."* |
| `nodes_slug_root_uniq` | `UNIQUE (workspace_id, slug) WHERE parent_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL` | Root-level siblings are scoped by workspace, not by a parent that does not exist. |
| `nodes_id_workspace_uniq` | `UNIQUE (id, workspace_id)` | Not a business rule — the target of the composite parent FK above. Zero extra cost: `id` is already unique. |

`deleted_at IS NULL` in both predicates is load-bearing. A trashed node is **detached** from the tree
(`src/lib/trash.ts:6-13`, *"Deleting detaches"*), so it is not a sibling of anything any more, and if
it kept its slug reserved a restore into a parent that has since gained a node with the same name
would deadlock: the restore has nowhere legal to land. Excluding trashed rows means E-037 must
**re-uniquify the slug on restore** against the live siblings of the target parent, exactly as E-026
does on move.

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes_pkey` | `(id)` | Every `GET /nodes/{nodeId}` (E-022) and every ancestor-chain step. |
| `nodes_parent_idx` | `(parent_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | E-023 `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/children`; the downward subtree CTE for archive/move/delete impact. |
| `nodes_workspace_kind_idx` | `(workspace_id, kind) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | E-020 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/tree` — one flat scan of the workspace, nested in memory, no CTE. Also E-048 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/boards`, which filters `kind = 'board'` and **must never seed or read a board's rows** (`src/services/board-service.ts:1234-1246`). |
| `nodes_owner_idx` | `(workspace_id, owner_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | "Things I own" — the owner-escalation path and any future ownership-transfer console. |
| `nodes_archived_idx` | `(workspace_id, archived_at DESC) WHERE archived_at IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL` | E-034 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/archive`, which returns **only the outermost archived node per subtree** — the index finds the candidates, the ancestor walk filters them. |
| `nodes_trash_idx` | `(workspace_id, deleted_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL` | E-036 trash listing, newest-deleted first (`sortTrash`, `src/lib/trash.ts:140-143`), and the nightly retention sweep on `deleted_at < now() - interval '30 days'`. |
| `nodes_restricted_idx` | `(workspace_id) WHERE access_mode = 'restricted' AND deleted_at IS NULL` | E-046 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/restricted-nodes`, the admin recovery console (`restrictedNodesOf`, `visibility.ts:270-291`). Partial and tiny — most workspaces have a handful of restricted nodes. **This read is itself audited at `warn`** (canon OQ-26). |
| `nodes_search_idx` | `GIN (search_vector)` | E-133 global search, which produces the `document`, `file` and `place` buckets from node `name` and `excerpt` (`src/services/search-service.ts:137-161`). |
| `nodes_name_trgm_idx` | `GIN (lower(name) gin_trgm_ops) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | E-035 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/search?q=` — drive quick-find. Its semantics are **substring**, not full-text: `searchNodes` does `name.toLowerCase().includes(needle)` (`src/lib/tree.ts:278-295`), which `tsvector` cannot answer. `pg_trgm` can. |

**Check Constraints**

| Constraint | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes_no_self_parent` | `parent_id IS NULL OR parent_id <> id` | The trivial cycle. The non-trivial one cannot be a check constraint — see below. |
| `nodes_name_not_blank` | `char_length(btrim(name)) > 0` | `renameNode` refuses an empty name (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:484-485`); the database refuses it too. |
| `nodes_slug_shape` | `slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$' AND char_length(slug) BETWEEN 1 AND 72` | Matches `slugify` (`src/lib/utils.ts:53-70`: lowercase, diacritics stripped, `đ`→`d`, non-alphanumerics collapsed to `-`, edges trimmed, capped at 60) plus room for `uniqueSlug`'s `-2`… suffix (`:73-80`). |
| `nodes_project_shape` | `kind <> 'project' OR (color IS NOT NULL AND project_status IS NOT NULL)` | `ProjectNode.color: string` and `status: ProjectStatus` are both required (`src/types/node.ts:80-86`). |
| `nodes_document_shape` | `kind <> 'document' OR icon IS NOT NULL` | `DocumentNode.icon: string` is required (`:99`). |
| `nodes_board_shape` | `kind <> 'board' OR board_kind IS NOT NULL` | `BoardNode.boardKind: BoardKind` is required (`:109`). |
| `nodes_extras_confined` | `(kind = 'project' OR description IS NULL AND project_status IS NULL) AND (kind IN ('project','folder') OR color IS NULL) AND (kind = 'document' OR (document_kind IS NULL AND icon IS NULL AND is_pinned = false AND locked_at IS NULL)) AND (kind = 'board' OR (board_kind IS NULL AND item_count IS NULL AND open_count IS NULL)) AND (kind = 'document' OR block_count IS NULL)` | A file with a `board_kind` is data that no reader knows how to interpret; the single-table decision is only safe if the discriminant is actually enforced. |
| `nodes_lock_pair` | `(locked_at IS NULL) = (locked_by IS NULL)` | One fact, two columns. |
| `nodes_archive_pair` | `(archived_at IS NULL) = (archived_by IS NULL)` | Same. |
| `nodes_delete_pair` | `(deleted_at IS NULL) = (deleted_by IS NULL)` | Same. |
| `nodes_counts_non_negative` | `coalesce(block_count, 0) >= 0 AND coalesce(item_count, 0) >= 0 AND coalesce(open_count, 0) >= 0 AND coalesce(open_count, 0) <= coalesce(item_count, 0)` | A board with more open records than records is a counter that has drifted; fail the write that caused it rather than rendering it. |

#### Containment: which kinds may hold children

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `isContainer(node)` is `kind IN ('project','folder')`
(`src/types/node.ts:146-147`), and it is the only definition — `childrenOf` returns `[]` for
everything else (`:150-151`). The frontend refuses a document under a leaf with *"Pages can only live
inside folders"* (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:752`) and a board with *"Boards can only live inside
folders"* (`:803`); `moveNode` refuses a drop on a non-container with `invalid-target`
(`src/lib/tree.ts:182-186`).

The backend enforces the same rule on **E-024** and **E-026**:

```
parent must be NULL (workspace root) OR a live node with kind IN ('project','folder')
otherwise → NODE_NOT_CONTAINER (409 / conflict)  on create
         → NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET (409 / conflict) on move
```

PRD `WS-FLD-03` confirms the content set: *"Folder có thể chứa: Folder con, Document, Board, File,
Config Document, Secret Document"* — and config and secret documents are `document_kind` values, not
new kinds. This is **not** a check constraint, because it is a rule about the *parent's* row, which
`CHECK` cannot reach. It is a guard inside the same transaction as the write, under the same lock as
the cycle check.

#### Cycle prevention on move

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** PRD `WS-FLD-03` edge case: *"Kéo Folder cha vào chính Folder con của nó:
Chặn thao tác và báo lỗi cấu trúc vòng lặp"* — dragging a parent folder into one of its own
descendants is blocked and reported as a cycle error. The frontend implements it in `moveNode`
(`src/lib/tree.ts:170-197`) and the rejections are a closed enum,
`MoveRejection = "same-parent" | "into-self" | "into-descendant" | "invalid-target"`
(**kebab-case**, canon §2.3). The client's rejection is UX only; the backend must re-check.

Each rejection maps to one error reason (canon §4.3):

| `MoveRejection` | Reason | HTTP / code | Frontend message (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:977-988`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `same-parent` | `NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT` | 409 / `conflict` | "Item is already in that folder" — *a no-op the caller should treat as success* |
| `into-self` | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF` | 409 / `conflict` | "A folder cannot be moved into itself" |
| `into-descendant` | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT` | 409 / `conflict` | "A folder cannot be moved into one of its own subfolders" |
| `invalid-target` | `NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET` | 409 / `conflict` | "That destination cannot hold items" |

**The check the backend must perform.** Note the direction: the frontend walks **down** from the node
(`isDescendantOf`, `src/lib/tree.ts:147-156`) because it already holds the whole tree in memory. The
backend must walk **up** from the target — the answer is identical and the cost is bounded by depth
(≤ 10 in practice) instead of by subtree size.

```
FUNCTION moveNode(actor, nodeId, targetParentId):

  # 0. Serialise structural writes for this workspace. Two moves that each pass
  #    their own check can still produce a cycle: A→B and B→A, concurrently,
  #    both legal in isolation, both illegal together. There is no constraint
  #    that can catch this after the fact, so it must not be allowed to happen.
  BEGIN TRANSACTION
  pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(node.workspace_id))

  node := SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE id = nodeId FOR UPDATE
  IF node IS NULL OR node.deleted_at IS NOT NULL:
      REJECT NODE_NOT_FOUND

  # 1. Gate 1 and gate 2 before anything structural is considered.
  REQUIRE membership(actor, node.workspace_id)
  REQUIRE visible(actor, nodeId)              AND visible(actor, targetParentId)
  REQUIRE capability(actor, nodeId, "node.move")
  REQUIRE node.deleted_at IS NULL             ELSE NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY
  REQUIRE no archived ancestor of nodeId      ELSE NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR

  # 2. The trivial cases, in the frontend's order.
  IF targetParentId == nodeId:            REJECT NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF
  IF node.parent_id  == targetParentId:   REJECT NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT

  # 3. The target must be able to hold children, and be in the same workspace.
  IF targetParentId IS NOT NULL:
      target := SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE id = targetParentId FOR UPDATE
      IF target IS NULL
         OR target.deleted_at IS NOT NULL
         OR target.workspace_id <> node.workspace_id
         OR target.kind NOT IN ('project', 'folder'):
              REJECT NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET

      # 4. THE CYCLE CHECK. Walk root-ward from the target. If the node being
      #    moved appears anywhere on that chain, the target is inside the node,
      #    and the move would detach a subtree into itself: the rows survive,
      #    every walk from the root stops finding them, and the whole branch is
      #    silently orphaned. Bounded by depth, so it cannot be expensive.
      ancestors := ancestorChainOf(targetParentId)     # [target, parent, …, root]
      IF nodeId IN ancestors:
              REJECT NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT

      # 5. Depth guard — see below. Never a product limit; a runaway stop.
      IF depthOf(targetParentId) + 1 + heightOf(nodeId) > MAX_TREE_DEPTH:
              REJECT NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET

  # 6. Re-uniquify the slug against the NEW siblings (canon OQ-10). The slug is
  #    minted once at creation and never re-minted on rename, but a move can
  #    land it beside a sibling that already holds it, and the partial unique
  #    index would refuse the write.
  newSlug := uniqueSlug(node.slug, liveSiblingSlugsOf(targetParentId))

  # 7. Compute who loses sight of it BEFORE the write, so the response can say
  #    so (moveVisibilityImpact, src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:313-333).
  impact := visibilityImpact(node, targetParentId)

  UPDATE nodes
     SET parent_id = targetParentId, slug = newSlug,
         updated_at = now(), updated_by = actor.id
   WHERE id = nodeId

  writeAuditEvent(module: "node", action: "node.move", severity: "info", actor)
  COMMIT

  publish RT-11 node.changed { workspaceId, nodeId, change: "moved" }
  publish RT-05 permission.changed { workspaceId, nodeId, userIds: impact.losing ∪ impact.gaining }
  RETURN MoveNodeResponse
```

The ancestor chain, as documentation SQL:

```sql
-- documentation only. Root-ward from :target_id, cycle-safe, depth-bounded.
WITH RECURSIVE chain(id, parent_id, depth) AS (
    SELECT n.id, n.parent_id, 0
      FROM nodes n
     WHERE n.id = :target_id
  UNION ALL
    SELECT n.id, n.parent_id, chain.depth + 1
      FROM nodes n
      JOIN chain ON n.id = chain.parent_id
     WHERE chain.depth < 64            -- runaway stop, not a product rule
)
SELECT id FROM chain;
```

`UNION ALL` with an explicit `depth` bound rather than bare recursion: if the data ever *did* contain
a cycle, an unbounded CTE would spin until the statement timeout, and the bound turns that into a
fast, diagnosable failure. On PostgreSQL 14+, `CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path` expresses the same
protection declaratively; either is acceptable, neither is optional.

**Why `pg_advisory_xact_lock` and not a constraint.** A cycle is a property of a *set* of rows, and
PostgreSQL has no constraint that can express one — no `CHECK`, no `EXCLUDE`, no trigger that is
race-free without a lock. The alternatives are `SERIALIZABLE` isolation for the whole endpoint (which
makes every move retryable and every unrelated concurrent write a potential serialisation failure) or
a per-workspace advisory lock held for the length of the transaction. Moves are rare, human-paced,
and PRD `WS-FLD-03` budgets 300 ms for one, so a workspace-wide lock costs nothing real. Take the
same lock in E-024 (create), E-032 (trash) and E-037 (restore) — every write that changes the shape
of the tree — so the invariant holds across all of them and not only against other moves.

**Depth.** **EXISTING REQUIREMENT** — PRD `WS-FLD-03`: *"Hỗ trợ độ sâu cây thư mục tối thiểu 10 cấp
không giới hạn node"* — at least 10 levels, **unbounded node count**. The frontend imposes no depth
limit anywhere: `findNodeById`, `findPathToId`, `flattenTree` and `visibleTree` all recurse without a
bound (`src/lib/tree.ts`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:211-237`). **RECOMMENDATION** —
