```ts
  /** Stable within the tree. Used by the editor to patch and remove. */
  readonly id: string;
  /** A `board_columns.id` on THIS board. */
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly operator: ConditionOperator;
  /**
   * Read the way the target column reads it:
   *   select   → a SelectOption.id      (never a label)
   *   user     → a users.id
   *   date     → `YYYY-MM-DD`           (a calendar day, never an instant — C-04)
   *   relation → a board_rows.id
   *   text     → free text
   * Empty string when the operator's arity is "none".
   */
  readonly value: string;
  /** The list for `isAnyOf` / `isNoneOf`. Single-value operators ignore it. */
  readonly values?: readonly string[];
}

type ConditionConjunction = "and" | "or";

/** Conditions plus nested groups, combined by one conjunction.
 *  Nesting is what makes `A and (B or C)` expressible without a second shape. */
interface ConditionGroup {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly conjunction: ConditionConjunction;
  readonly conditions: readonly Condition[];
  readonly groups: readonly ConditionGroup[];
}
```

**`ConditionOperator` is NOT a superset of `FilterOperator`**, despite the comment at
`src/types/board.ts:20-23`. `FilterOperator` uniquely has `onOrBefore` and `onOrAfter`;
`ConditionOperator` uniquely has `isAnyOf`, `isNoneOf` and `on`. Two enums ship, as the code has them
(canon §2.5, OQ-37).

**Operators offered per column type** (`OPERATORS_BY_TYPE`, `src/lib/conditions.ts:65-73`). A
condition naming an operator its column does not offer is rejected with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

| Column type | Legal operators |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `longText` | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `notContains`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `select` | `is`, `isNot`, `isAnyOf`, `isNoneOf`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `user` | `is`, `isNot`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `date` | `before`, `after`, `on`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `attachment` | `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `relation` | `contains`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |

**Value arity** (`valueArityFor`, `src/lib/conditions.ts:82-86`): `isEmpty` / `isNotEmpty` → none;
`isAnyOf` / `isNoneOf` → list, read from `values` and falling back to `[value]` when `values` is
absent or empty (`needlesOf`, `:135-138`); everything else → single.

**Evaluation semantics — the backend must reproduce all six** (`evaluateCondition`,
`src/lib/conditions.ts:196-250`; `evaluateConditionGroup`, `:258-273`):

1. **A condition pointing at a deleted column returns `true`** — it is ignored, not failed closed
   (`:196-198`). This is load-bearing: "a deleted column must not silently lock every option."
2. **An empty group is satisfied.** Nested empty groups are filtered out before combining, and a
   group whose every child filtered out is also satisfied (`:262, 271`).
3. `date` comparisons are **calendar days**, computed from `iso.slice(0, 10)`
   (`dayNumber`, `:129-132`). An unparsable bound returns `true` (permissive); a `null` cell value
   returns `false`. **No UTC conversion ever happens** (C-04).
4. Identity cells (`select`, `user`, `relation`) match the **stored id first, the rendered label
   second**, both case-folded (`matchesIdentity`, `:145-158`). A rule written by the builder (an id)
   and one written by hand (a name) therefore agree.
5. Everything else compares `cellText(...).toLowerCase()`.
6. `or` → `results.some`; anything else → `results.every`.

**The refusal string.** `describeConditionGroup` renders the tree to one human line — `QA Status is
Passed and Reviewer is not empty` — resolving option ids to labels and user ids to names, and
wrapping nested groups in parentheses (`src/lib/conditions.ts:278-321`). The explanation the API
returns is `` `Requires ${describeConditionGroup(...)}` ``
(`src/lib/select-availability.ts:92-101`). Error → `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` (409 / `conflict`).

**The three gates, in order** (`resolveOptionAvailability`, `src/lib/select-availability.ts:69-117`).
The backend runs the same three, in the same order, on every write path listed in §4.14:

| # | Gate | `reason` | Explanation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `option.isDisabled` | `disabled` | `"Turned off in column settings"` |
| 2 | `availability` does not hold for this record | `condition` | `` `Requires ${describeConditionGroup(...)}` `` |
| 3 | a transition rule forbids arriving here from the record's current option | `transition` | the verdict sentence from §4.14 |

`unavailableBehavior` decides only what the *dropdown* does with a failed option — `"disabled"`
(default) keeps it greyed, `"hidden"` drops it (`visibleOptions`, `:127-131`). It never affects
whether a write is accepted.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-38) — how deep may a `ConditionGroup` nest, and how large may a `config` be?**
**Evidence** — `ConditionGroup.groups` is unbounded recursion (`src/types/board.ts:59-64`);
`evaluateConditionGroup`, `cloneConditionGroup` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:474-483`) and
`describeConditionGroup` all recurse without a depth guard; nothing in `src/config/app.ts` caps a
column config.
**Recommendation** — cap at **depth 5**, **50 conditions across the whole tree**, and a **64 KB**
serialised `board_columns.config`. Validate on write, before the shallow merge, and refuse with
`CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` (400 / `validation`) or `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` (413). Depth 5 comfortably
exceeds every tree any template or UI produces — the built-in `task` rule is depth 1 with one
condition (`whenEmpty`, `src/lib/board-templates.ts:118-125`).
**Impact if wrong** — a hand-crafted `config` write becomes a stack-overflow and a CPU denial of
service against every reader of the board, because the tree is evaluated once per option per record
per render.

---

### 4.16 Table: `board_rows`

**Purpose** — one record on one board. It carries its own business identifier (`TASK-042`), its
place in the board's order, its parent when it is a subtask, its optimistic-concurrency token, its
archive state, and all of its cell values as one JSONB document.

**Who creates a record** — `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows` (E-062), `POST
/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/duplicate` (E-064), `POST /boards/{boardId}/import` (E-085) and the
destination half of `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/move` (E-077). Every one of them allocates
`sequence` from `boards.next_sequence` (§4.11.1); the client never invents an id.

**Lifetime** — soft delete, per canon §1.4 (`deleted_at` + `deleted_by` on `nodes`, `comments` and
`board_rows`). `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` (E-065) and `POST …/rows/bulk/delete` (E-076)
set `deleted_at`; the retention sweep hard-deletes afterwards. **Deleting a parent never cascades to
its children** — they are lifted to the top level (`parent_row_id → NULL`, `revision + 1`) and the
response carries them so the client reconciles. Rows also cascade away with their board when the
board's node is purged.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `uuid` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Record identity. Wire field `row.id`. |
| `board_id` | `uuid` | no | — | no | Owning board. |
| `sequence` | `bigint` | no | — | no (composite) | The numeric part of the business id. Monotonic per board, **never reused** (§4.11.1). Wire field `row.sequence`. |
| `custom_id` | `text` | no | — | no (composite) | `TASK-042`. Written by the service as `` `${board.row_id_prefix}-${lpad(sequence, 3, '0')}` ``; numbers past the padding simply grow (`formatRowId`, `src/lib/row-id.ts:13-15`). **Never the primary key** (C-02). Wire field `row.displayId`. |
| `parent_row_id` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | Parent record in the subtask hierarchy. A subtask is a full record — its own id, status, assignee, attachments, comments and history — so the parent stores a pointer, never a nested copy (`src/types/board.ts:255-263`). |
| `position` | `numeric` | no | — | no | Fractional index giving the board its order (canon OQ-34). See §4.16.3. |
| `cells` | `jsonb` | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | no | `Record<columnId, CellValue>`. The whole of §4.17. |
| `revision` | `bigint` | no | `1` | no | Optimistic-concurrency token. **One bump per write, however many cells that write touched** (`src/services/board-service.ts:514-519`). Wire field `row.revision`. |
| `archived_at` | `timestamptz` | yes | `NULL` | no | SY-ARC-37. Non-null means frozen: readable, keeps its history, refuses edits until restored. Wire field `row.archivedAt`. |
| `deleted_at` | `timestamptz` | yes | `NULL` | no | Soft delete (canon §1.4). Absent from the wire; a deleted row is simply not returned. |
| `deleted_by` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | From the session. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `updated_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `created_by` | `uuid` | no | — | no | Wire field `row.createdBy`. There is deliberately no `updated_by` — the frontend has none (OQ-35); the actor of the last write is in `row_activity`. |
| `due_date` | `date` | yes | `NULL` | no | Indexed projection. §4.16.4. |
| `due_at` | `timestamptz` | yes | `NULL` | no | Indexed projection. **A separate column from `due_date`, never a widening of it** (C-04, OQ-32). |
| `status_option_id` | `text` | yes | `NULL` | no | Indexed projection. |
| `assignee_ids` | `uuid[]` | no | `'{}'` | no | Indexed projection. |
| `search_vector` | `tsvector` | yes | `NULL` | no | GIN-indexed full text over the record's textual cells; canon §1.2 puts the index on the row rather than in a `search_index` table. |

`isPending` (`src/types/board.ts:265`) is client-only and is never stored or accepted.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | A record has no life outside its board. |
| `(parent_row_id, board_id)` | `board_rows(id, board_id)` | `SET NULL (parent_row_id)` | Two behaviours in one constraint. **`SET NULL` implements "children are lifted to the top level, never cascade-deleted"** exactly (`detachOrphans`, `src/services/board-service.ts:460-470`; E-065's `DeleteRowResponse` carries the lifted children so the client reconciles). **The composite target makes `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD` a database guarantee** rather than a service check: with `UNIQUE (id, board_id)` on this table, a parent on another board simply has no matching row. Requires PostgreSQL 15+ for the column-scoped `SET NULL`. |
| `created_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are never hard-deleted (T-01), so old assignments still render a name. |
| `deleted_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Same. |

**Unique Constraints**

- `UNIQUE (board_id, sequence)` — the counter's guarantee, written down.
- `UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)` — `TASK-042` is unique per board. Two different boards may both
  hold `TASK-001`; canon does not make display ids globally unique (OQ-95).
- `UNIQUE (id, board_id)` — carries no information of its own; it exists **only** so the composite
  parent FK above can target it.

Both `(board_id, sequence)` and `(board_id, custom_id)` include soft-deleted rows on purpose: a
number that has been issued is spent, deleted or not.

**Indexes**

| Index | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `board_rows_pkey (id)` | E-063, E-064, E-065, E-067, E-070, E-072, E-073. |
| `(board_id, position, id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND archived_at IS NULL` | E-047 and E-061 — the default read. Keyset pagination is on `(position, id)` (canon §6.3), and archived records are hidden from every view by default (`src/types/board.ts:251-254`). |
| `(board_id, position, id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | E-061 with `includeArchived=true`; E-075 `bulk/archive`, the one call that may target archived rows. |
| `(parent_row_id) WHERE parent_row_id IS NOT NULL` | E-068 `GET …/rows/{rowId}/subtasks`; the cycle-check recursive CTE on E-067; the lift-to-top-level update on E-065. |
| `UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)` | E-069 row search — `TASK 7` and `task-7` both resolve to `TASK-007` (`matchesRowId`, `src/lib/row-id.ts:46-62`); inline `TASK-001` references in comment bodies (OQ-95). |
| `GIN (cells jsonb_path_ops)` | Reaching inside `cells` for a server-side filter that no projection column covers. |
| `GIN (search_vector)` | E-069 primary-column substring search; E-133 global search over records. |
| `(board_id, due_date) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND archived_at IS NULL` | E-134 My Work (`dueToday`, `overdue`), E-135 the deadline dashboard. |
| `(board_id, status_option_id)` | E-135 the task and QA dashboards. |
| `GIN (assignee_ids)` | E-134 "assigned to me" across every board in the workspace. |

**Check Constraints**

- `sequence > 0`.
- `custom_id ~ '^[A-Z]{1,6}-[0-9]+$'` — the shape `formatRowId` produces.
- `parent_row_id IS DISTINCT FROM id` — self-parenting. The service refuses first with
  `ROW_PARENT_SELF` ("A record cannot be its own parent", `src/services/board-service.ts:384`); the
  constraint is the backstop.
- `jsonb_typeof(cells) = 'object'`.
- `position` is not constrained; it is a dense-ordered `numeric` with no meaningful bounds.

**Cycles are not expressible as a check constraint.** `PUT /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/parent`
(E-067) must walk the chain with a recursive CTE inside the write transaction and refuse with
`ROW_PARENT_CYCLE` — message `` `${parent.displayId} is already under ${row.displayId}` ``
(`src/services/board-service.ts:389-391`). The same walk enforces the depth cap
(`ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP`); canon's position on OQ-33 is **depth 5**, which the frontend does not
enforce ("no depth limit", `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:6-12`) and which the API therefore owns alone.

**Relationships**

- N-1 `boards`.
- 1-N self, through `parent_row_id` (containment). Adjacency list, not nested sets: every helper in
  `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts` walks `parentRowId` alone.
- 1-N `board_row_relations` as source and as target (dependency). **Containment and relation "live
  side by side and never read each other's data"** (`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:14-18`).
- 1-N `row_activity` (T-14), `comments` (T-33), `cell_attachments` (T-29), `watches` (T-34).

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Realtime | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-047 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` → `BoardSnapshot` | visibility | read-only | — | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-061 | `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows?cursor=&limit=&includeArchived=` → `RowPage` | visibility | read-only | — | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-062 | `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows` → `BoardRow` | `row.create` | One: bump `next_sequence`, insert, index relations, write activity | RT-06 `row.created` | `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND`, `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` |
| E-063 | `GET …/rows/{rowId}` → `BoardRow` | visibility | read-only | — | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-064 | `POST …/rows/{rowId}/duplicate` → `BoardRow` | `row.create` | One | RT-06 | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-065 | `DELETE …/rows/{rowId}` → `DeleteRowResponse` | `row.delete` | One: soft-delete + lift children + drop relation edges | RT-09 `row.deleted`, RT-07 per lifted child | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-066 | `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` → `UpdateCellsResponse` | `row.update` | One over every touched row. **Always `200`; last-write-wins plus `ConflictNotice[]`; never `409`** | RT-07 per row | `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY`, `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID`, `DATE_VALUE_INVALID`, `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED`, `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` |
| E-067 | `PUT …/rows/{rowId}/parent` → `BoardRow` | `row.move` | One + recursive CTE | RT-07 | `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND`, `ROW_PARENT_SELF`, `ROW_PARENT_CYCLE`, `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD`, `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` |
| E-068 | `GET …/rows/{rowId}/subtasks` → `BoardRow[]` | visibility | read-only | — | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-069 | `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/search?q=&limit=` → `BoardRow[]` | visibility | read-only | — | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-073 | `PATCH …/rows/{rowId}/position` → `BoardRow` | `row.move` | One | RT-07 | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-074 – E-077 | bulk update / archive / delete / move | `row.update` / `row.archive` / `row.delete` / both | One each; E-077 spans **both** boards | RT-07 / RT-08 / RT-09 / RT-09 + RT-06 | `BULK_TARGET_BOARD_SAME`, `BULK_TARGET_NOT_A_BOARD` |
| E-085 | `POST /boards/{boardId}/import` → `ImportOutcome` | `board.import` | **One**: column creation, column removal and row inserts all land or none do | RT-06 batched, RT-10 | `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED` |

**Frontend callers** — `useBoardStore.addRow` / `editCells` / `setRowParent` / `removeRow` /
`bulkUpdate` (`src/store/board-store.ts`); `boardService.*` (`src/services/board-service.ts:1383-1415`);
`useSubtasks` and `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx` for the hierarchy;
`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:127` for E-069.

#### 4.16.1 The concurrency contract

`revision` is the token, and it is **never used to refuse a cell write**. Canon §6.4 and
`src/services/board-service.ts:484-535` settle the policy: last-write-wins plus a notice.

`PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` takes `baseRevisions: Record<rowId, number>` and reproduces
three properties exactly (`:504-512`):

1. A missing `baseRevisions[rowId]` **never** conflicts.
2. `base < current.revision` conflicts; equal or greater does not.
3. **At most one notice per row per call**, raised by the first edit that touches that row.

The stale write is *applied*, `revision` is bumped once, and the collision is reported as
`ConflictNotice { id, rowId, columnId, message }` with
`` message = `${displayId} changed elsewhere — your edit was kept` ``. The response carries the
authoritative rows so the client reconciles rather than guesses
(`reconcileRows`, `src/lib/board-records.ts:109-116`). `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` exists in the error
registry and is explicitly **never** used for cell writes.

#### 4.16.2 Archive

`archived_at` is a timestamp, not a boolean (`isRowArchived` tests for a non-empty string,
`src/lib/archive.ts:52-53`). Archived means frozen, not hidden away: the record stays readable and
keeps its history, and every write path is closed until it is restored
(`ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY`, 409).

- Archived rows are excluded from every view by default and from every dashboard tally (E-135).
- `POST …/rows/bulk/archive` (E-075) is **the one call that may target archived rows**; `bulk/delete`
  (E-076) may too, because "archiving freezes edits, not removal"
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:1058`).
- `bulkUpdate` (E-074) skips them, reporting each as `BulkSkip { reason: "archived" }`.
- Archiving a parent does **not** cascade to its subtasks (canon OQ-33 position).
- Re-archiving something already archived is a no-op that writes no activity entry
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:1034-1043`).

#### 4.16.3 Ordering — `position numeric`

**RECOMMENDATION (OQ-34), position taken by canon §8.8.** `rowOrder` in the frontend is "the array
the server sent" (`docs/BOARD.md:295-298`); an explicit key is needed for manual reordering and for
concurrent inserts.

- Append: `COALESCE(MAX(position), 0) + 1` within the board.
- Insert after row *R*: the midpoint of *R*'s position and the next row's, or `R + 1` at the end.
- **A new subtask is filed directly after its parent's last descendant**, so the board's own order
  already reads as the tree even before a view nests it (`lastDescendantOf`,
  `src/services/board-service.ts:322-352`). That is an ordering rule and it needs a fractional index
  to be expressible at all.
- `numeric` is arbitrary-precision, so midpoints never run out. Renormalise the board to dense
  integers when any denominator exceeds ~40 digits; the operation is a single ordered `UPDATE` and
  emits one RT-10.

Keyset pagination sorts on `(position, id)`; `id` breaks the tie so the cursor is total.

#### 4.16.4 The indexed projections — `due_date`, `due_at`, `status_option_id`, `assignee_ids`

Canon §1.3.2 requires these four columns so that filtering, My Work and the dashboard do not have to
reach into `cells`. Each is derived from the column the board designates for that role.

`due_date` and `due_at` are **two columns, not one**. Which one is written is decided by the due
column's `DateConfig.includesTime`: `false` → the calendar day goes to `due_date` and `due_at` stays
`NULL`; `true` → the instant goes to `due_at` and `due_date` stays `NULL`. **A date-only value is
never widened into an instant** (C-04, canon OQ-32 position; `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24` — "A due date
is a square on a calendar, not a moment").

`status_option_id` is the record's **first** option id in the status column, or `NULL` — the same
value `currentKey` uses as the transition source (`src/lib/select-availability.ts:56-62`) and the
same one `statusOf` reads for My Work (`src/lib/my-work.ts:127-137`).

`assignee_ids` is the assignee column's `userIds`, in order.

They are maintained by the service **inside the same statement that writes `cells`** — the one
`UPDATE` on E-066 sets `cells`, `revision`, `updated_at` and all four projections together, so they
can never lag. They are also rewritten by E-053 (a `DateConfig.includesTime` flip moves a value
between `due_date` and `due_at`), E-057 (conversion), E-054 (the role column deleted → `NULL`) and
E-050 (a role reassignment rewrites the whole board's projections in one pass).

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-48) — which column plays which role?**
**Evidence** — the frontend picks by **name heuristic**, not schema: `ASSIGNEE_NAMES =
/assign|owner|tester|responsible/i`, `DUE_NAMES = /due|deadline/i`, `STATUS_NAMES =
/status|result|state/i` (`src/lib/my-work.ts:82-84`), with a deliberate asymmetry — assignee and
status fall back to the first column of that type, the due date does **not**, "because 'Found on' and
'Executed on' are history, not work that is due" (`src/lib/my-work.ts:120-123`). A second, competing
definition of "done" exists as a hard-coded English label table, `DONE_LABELS`
(`src/lib/my-work.ts:87-100`), beside the configured `completedOptionIds` (OQ-49).
**Recommendation** — store the three role pointers explicitly on `boards`
(`assignee_column_id`, `due_column_id`, `status_column_id`, all `NULL`-able, `ON DELETE SET NULL`),
default them at board creation by running the existing heuristic once, and expose them on E-050 so a
board owner can correct a guess. A board with a `NULL` role contributes nothing to the widgets that
need it — exactly what the heuristic already does when it finds no match.
**Impact if wrong** — the projections are indexed on a column the product did not mean, and My Work
silently shows the wrong records; worse, renaming a column ("Due date" → "Target") would today change
which records are overdue, with no write and no audit entry to explain it.

---

### 4.17 Cell values — `board_rows.cells JSONB`

**DECIDED (canon §1.3.2): `cells jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` holding `Record<columnId, CellValue>`.
There is no `cell_values` table.** This section reproduces the trade-off in full, as canon requires,
and then specifies the JSONB shape of every variant.

#### 4.17.1 The trade-off, reproduced

| Axis | `cells JSONB` on the row (**CHOSEN**) | `cell_values` row-per-cell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Read one board** | One row per record. `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` returns the whole set (`src/services/board-service.ts:229-241`). | N×M rows to fetch and pivot in the application. |
| **A 5 000-row read** | 5 000 rows, each ~1–3 KB — one index scan on `(board_id, position, id)`. | A 5 000-row × 12-column board is **60 000 rows per page load**, plus the pivot. |
| **Partial updates** | One `UPDATE` per row. N edits on one row = **one** `revision + 1`, which is the documented contract (`src/services/board-service.ts:500-520`). | N upserts. The "one revision per write, not per cell" rule needs a row-level lock on `board_rows` anyway, so the table buys nothing and costs a round of upserts. |
| **Type safety** | Native. The tagged union is stored as written, and a cell's `kind` may legitimately disagree with its column's `type` after a conversion — the `text` escape hatch survives (`src/types/board.ts:214-218`). | Needs a `kind` column beside the column's `type` **and** a nullable value column per branch — seven of them — or a JSONB value column, which is the same problem one join further away. |
| **Column delete / duplicate / convert** | Rewrites `cells` on every row: one statement per row, already the frontend's model (`src/services/board-service.ts:691-756`). | `DELETE WHERE column_id = …` is genuinely cheaper. **This is the one axis EAV wins.** |
| **Query-ability: filter / sort on a column** | GIN `jsonb_path_ops` on `cells`, plus the four projection columns of §4.16.4 for the lenses the product actually queries. Filtering and sorting are client-side today (`docs/BOARD.md:301-306`). | Native btree per column. Better for ad-hoc server-side query — the axis to revisit if OQ-36 lands as a full query DSL. |
| **Indexing** | One GIN index covers every key; four btree/GIN indexes cover the hot paths. | One btree per `(column_id, value)` — more indexes, each narrower. |
| **Sparse boards** | An absent key is an absent cell. But the frontend writes an explicit **empty `CellValue` of the column's kind**, never `null` (`emptyCellFor`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:24-36`; used on every insert, `src/services/board-service.ts:537-539`), so rows are dense by construction and the sparsity advantage is theoretical. | Genuinely sparse. |
| **Referential integrity on `column_id`** | None. Orphaned keys must be pruned by the same transaction that drops a column (E-054). | A real FK to `board_columns`. |
| **Row size** | A 12-column record is ~1–3 KB. The TOAST threshold is 2 KB, so wide boards will TOAST — fine for whole-row reads, bad for single-cell reads, and **there are no single-cell reads** (canon P-03 forbids the route). | n/a |
| **Migration cost if we are wrong** | `jsonb_each` → insert. Mechanical, one pass. | The reverse is a pivot, also mechanical. |

The decisive fact is the access pattern: the row is always read whole and always written whole.
`BoardSnapshot` ships every row; `reconcileRows` overwrites by id
(`src/lib/board-records.ts:109-116`). An EAV table would be normalising data that is never queried
one cell at a time.

#### 4.17.2 The stored shape of every variant

```ts
/**
 * Cell values are tagged with their own kind rather than inferred from the
 * column. A converted column can therefore keep the text it could not parse
 * instead of dropping the user's data.  src/types/board.ts:219-230
 */
type CellValue =
  | { readonly kind: "text";       readonly value: string }
  | { readonly kind: "longText";   readonly value: string }
  | { readonly kind: "select";     readonly optionIds: readonly string[];        readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "date";       readonly iso: string | null;                  readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "user";       readonly userIds: readonly string[];          readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "attachment"; readonly attachments: readonly CellAttachment[]; readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "relation";   readonly rowIds: readonly string[];           readonly text?: string };

/** A file attached to a record. Metadata only — the board never holds bytes. */
interface CellAttachment {
  readonly id: string;              // = file_assets.id (T-27)
  readonly name: string;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  /** Minted per response as a short-lived signed URL. NEVER accepted on write. */
  readonly url: string | null;
  readonly thumbnailUrl: string | null;
  readonly uploadedBy?: string;     // users.id
  readonly createdAt?: string;      // ISO 8601
}

/** The whole cells document. Keys are board_columns.id values. */
type BoardRowCells = Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
```

| `kind` | Stored JSON | Empty value written on insert | Empty test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `{"kind":"text","value":"…"}` | `{"kind":"text","value":""}` | `value.trim().length === 0` |
| `longText` | `{"kind":"longText","value":"…"}` — newlines preserved | `{"kind":"longText","value":""}` | `value.trim().length === 0` |
| `select` | `{"kind":"select","optionIds":["status_4"]}` — **ids, never labels** | `{"kind":"select","optionIds":[]}` | `optionIds.length === 0 && !text` |
| `date` | `{"kind":"date","iso":"2026-08-27"}` or a full instant | `{"kind":"date","iso":null}` | `iso === null && !text` |
| `user` | `{"kind":"user","userIds":["usr_…"]}` | `{"kind":"user","userIds":[]}` | `userIds.length === 0 && !text` |
| `attachment` | `{"kind":"attachment","attachments":[…]}` | `{"kind":"attachment","attachments":[]}` | `attachments.length === 0` — **`text` is deliberately not consulted** |
| `relation` | `{"kind":"relation","rowIds":["…uuid…"]}` — target row ids | `{"kind":"relation","rowIds":[]}` | `rowIds.length === 0 && !text` |

(`emptyCellFor` / `isCellEmpty`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:24-64`.)

#### 4.17.3 Five rules the backend must not break

1. **A cell's `kind` may legitimately disagree with its column's `type`, and the API must not
   normalise it away** (canon §2.5). `cellOf` reads a mismatched value as *empty* rather than
   erroring (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:43-46`), so a schema change racing an edit can never crash a
   reader. Validate only that `kind` is a `ColumnType` member — `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` (400)
   otherwise.
2. **`text` is opaque payload. Do not strip it, do not normalise it, do not re-parse it
   server-side.** It holds the original string the target type could not parse, so a conversion, an
   import or a paste never destroys the user's data
   (`parseTextIntoCell`, `src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:25-82`). It is cleared only when the cell is
   written with a value that parses. `cellEquals` compares `text` as part of structural identity
   (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:167-193`), and optimistic rollback is guarded on exact equality — so a
   server-side rewrite of `text` would break rollback, not just tidiness.
3. **`date.iso` is stored as the string the client sent.** Do not coerce it inside the JSONB. A date
   column may or may not carry a time (`DateConfig.includesTime`), and `withDayKey` deliberately
   preserves the time component when only the day changes (`src/lib/calendar.ts:143-148`). The
   indexed form lives in `due_date` / `due_at` (§4.16.4), never in the document. Malformed →
   `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` (400).
4. **Only `assetId` is persisted for an attachment.** `url` and `thumbnailUrl` are minted per
   response as short-lived signed URLs and are **never accepted on write** (canon OQ-75;
   `src/types/board.ts:206-207` — "session URL; null once the session ends"). The authoritative
   attachment record is `cell_attachments` (T-29); the JSONB carries the ordered reference.
5. **Cells are dense.** Every insert writes an explicit empty value for every column
   (`emptyCells`, `src/services/board-service.ts:537-539`), and E-054 deletes the key rather than
   nulling it. Never write `null` as a cell value.

---

### 4.18 Table: `board_row_relations`

**Purpose** — the indexed projection of every relation cell, so a backlink is one indexed query
rather than a scan of every board. The authoritative, ordered list stays in
`board_rows.cells[columnId].rowIds`; this table is written in the same transaction and never read as
the source of truth.

**Who creates a record** — the same transaction as any write that touches a relation cell: E-066,
E-074, E-062, E-064, E-077, E-085 and E-057 (a conversion into or out of `relation`). Never a
client; there is no endpoint that writes this table directly.

**Lifetime** — bound to its three referents. Deleting the source row, the source column or the
target row deletes the edge by cascade. It is never soft-deleted: a projection with a tombstone
would be two states to keep in step.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `uuid` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Edge identity. Not exposed on the wire. |
| `source_row_id` | `uuid` | no | — | no (composite) | The record whose cell holds the link. |
| `source_column_id` | `uuid` | no | — | no (composite) | The relation column the link was written in. **This column is the relation's "type"** — see below. |
| `target_row_id` | `uuid` | no | — | no (composite) | The record pointed at. |
| `target_board_id` | `uuid` | no | — | no | Denormalised from the target row so a cross-board permission filter does not need a join back to `board_rows`. |
| `position` | `int` | no | — | no | The link's index inside `rowIds`. The frontend reads `rowIds` **in order** and renders chips in that order. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |

**There is no `type` column, and no chapter may add one.** Canon §2.9 reserves `RelationType` and
deliberately does not define it: the frontend has no such enum, and inventing one would violate
ground rule 3. **A relation's meaning is its source column.** "Blocked by" is a relation *column*
named "Blocked by", shipped by the `task` template (`col_blocks`,
`src/lib/board-templates.ts:188`); `bug` and `apiDocs` ship "Related task" (`col_task`); `qa` ships
"Related bug". `source_column_id` therefore carries exactly the information a `type` column would,
with a foreign key protecting it and with the user free to add a fourth kind of link by adding a
fourth column. Introducing a typed edge kind requires resolving **OQ-45** first.

Equally: **containment is not relation.** `board_rows.parent_row_id` is the subtask hierarchy and
never appears here. "TASK-003 blocked by TASK-002 is a dependency, TASK-001 containing TASK-002 is
containment. The two live side by side and never read each other's data"
(`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:14-18`, restated for Gantt at `src/lib/board-gantt.ts:29-32`).

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source_row_id` | `board_rows(id)` | `CASCADE` | The projection has no meaning without the cell it projects. |
| `source_column_id` | `board_columns(id)` | `CASCADE` | E-054 removes the column's key from every record's `cells`; the edges must go in the same transaction or the backlink panel keeps showing a column that no longer exists. |
| `target_row_id` | `board_rows(id)` | `CASCADE` | **The edge dies; the id in the JSONB cell does not.** Canon OQ-44's position: leave the dangling id in `cells.rowIds` so `[Deleted Item]` keeps rendering and the record's history stays honest (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:22, 117-122`). A "clean up dangling links" maintenance action is the right fix, never a silent rewrite. |
| `target_board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | Redundant with the target row's cascade; present so the denormalised column cannot outlive its board. |

**Unique Constraints**

- `UNIQUE (source_row_id, source_column_id, target_row_id)` — one edge per link. A cell that lists
  the same target twice collapses to one edge; the JSONB keeps the duplicate, because the JSONB is
  what the user wrote.

**Indexes**

| Index | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `board_row_relations_pkey (id)` | Maintenance only. |
| `(source_row_id, source_column_id, position)` | Rewriting one cell's edges: delete-by-source then insert, in `position` order. |
| `(target_row_id)` | **E-072 `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/backlinks`** — "an indexed query, never a scan". This index is the entire reason the table exists. |
| `(target_board_id, target_row_id)` | E-071 `GET /boards/{boardId}/relation-index?ids=` — one request per target board, never one per cell, filtered by read access on the target board's node. |

**Check Constraints**

- `position >= 0`.
- `source_row_id <> target_row_id` is **not** constrained: a record legitimately may reference itself
  in a relation column, and nothing in the frontend forbids it.

**Relationships**

- N-1 `board_rows` twice (source and target) — an N-N join table between records, **cross-board by
  design**: `RelationConfig.boardId` names the target board and `null` means "this board"
  (`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:104-106`).
- N-1 `board_columns` (source column).

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Realtime | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-072 | `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/backlinks` → `Backlink[]` | visibility | read-only | — | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-071 | `GET /boards/{boardId}/relation-index?ids=` → `RelationTarget[]` | visibility **on the target board's node** | read-only | — | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-066, E-074, E-062, E-064, E-077, E-085, E-057, E-054 | writers | as per the owning endpoint | the edge rewrite is part of the owning transaction | the owning frame | — |

**Backlinks are derived, never stored twice.** There is no mirrored value on the target record:
"Nothing is stored for a backlink: it is derived by asking which rows point here, so the two
directions can never disagree" (`src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:14-19`). Canon's
position on OQ-44 confirms it — no mirroring, dangling ids preserved.

`Backlink` and `RelationTarget` are the two read shapes (canon §5.3):

```ts
interface RelationTarget {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly title: string;        // the target board's primary column, as text
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly boardName: string;
}

interface Backlink {
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly boardNodeId: string;
  readonly boardName: string;
  readonly columnName: string;   // the relation column the link was written in
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly title: string;
}
```

E-071 must filter its results by the caller's read access on the **target** board's node and return
the surviving subset. The frontend degrades gracefully: until every referenced board has answered,
`relationResolved` is false and an unresolved id renders as *unknown*, never as `[Deleted Item]`
(`src/lib/cell-values.ts:14-22, 117-122`; `src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts:21-24`). A filtered-out
row therefore leaks nothing.

**Frontend callers** — `src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:21`
(`boardService.listBacklinks`); `src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts:51`
(`boardService.relationIndex`, one call per distinct target board).

---

### 4.19 Table: `board_views`

**Purpose** — a saved way of reading the board: type, filters, sorts, grouping, date anchors and
column presentation. A view never owns records — "switching views never copies data; a view just
describes how to read it" (`src/types/board.ts:330-333`). Views are **shared per board**, and their
order is the board's, not the reader's (canon E-082).

**Who creates a record** — `POST /boards/{boardId}/views` (E-079), where `from` copies an existing
view — that is how "duplicate" works; and the board-creation transaction, which turns each
`TemplateView` into a full `SavedView` (§4.20).

**Lifetime** — hard delete through `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}` (E-081), **refused when
it would leave the board with zero views** (`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`, 409 — "A board needs at least one
view", `src/services/board-service.ts:887-892`). Cascades away with the board.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `uuid` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | View identity. **Forcibly preserved against a patch** (E-080). |
| `board_id` | `uuid` | no | — | no | Owning board. **Also forcibly preserved against a patch** (`src/services/board-service.ts:800-802`). |
| `name` | `text` | no | — | no | Tab label. Not unique — duplicating names the copy `` `${source.name} copy` `` (`src/store/board-store.ts:967-975`) and nothing enforces more. |
| `type` | `board_view_type` | no | — | no | Enum: `table`, `kanban`, `calendar`, `gantt`. |
| `position` | `int` | no | — | no | Tab-strip order, dense `0..n-1`, rewritten by E-082. |
| `filters` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | `ViewFilter[]`. §4.19.1. |
| `filter_conjunction` | `text` | no | `'and'` | no | `and` \| `or` — "all of" / "any of". |
| `sorts` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | `ViewSort[]`, multi-level: earlier entries win, later ones break ties. |
| `hidden_column_ids` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | `string[]` of `board_columns.id`. |
| `column_order` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | `string[]`. Ids missing from it fall back to schema `position` — appended after every explicitly ordered column (`src/lib/board-view.ts:40`). |
| `column_widths` | `jsonb` | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | no | `Record<columnId, number>`. The shared default; a viewer may override it (T-16). |
| `column_display` | `jsonb` | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | no | `Record<columnId, CellDisplayMode>`. **A column missing from the map is `compact`.** §4.19.2. |
| `row_height` | `text` | no | `'medium'` | no | `short` \| `medium` \| `tall`. Table only. |
| `group_by_column_id` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | Grouping column for the table and Kanban. Kanban *is* grouping, so it is required there. |
| `hide_empty_groups` | `boolean` | no | `false` | no | Forced `false` for Kanban on read — Kanban always shows empty buckets (`src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:136-160`). |
| `date_column_id` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | Calendar's anchor; the Gantt's start anchor. |
| `end_date_column_id` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | The Gantt's end anchor. |
| `subtask_display` | `text` | no | `'nested'` | no | `nested` \| `flat` \| `hidden`. Per view, so one view can nest subtasks while another lists every record flat. |
| `gantt_zoom` | `text` | no | `'week'` | no | `week` \| `month` \| `quarter` — **plus the legacy `day`**. See below. |
| `show_dependencies` | `boolean` | no | `true` | no | Draw the "blocked by" connectors. Off is a legitimate way to read a plan. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `updated_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `created_by` | `uuid` | no | — | no | |

**`gantt_zoom` and the legacy `"day"` — mandatory** (canon §2.6). A saved view may still hold
`"day"`, a per-day scale that was removed (`src/types/board.ts:272-281`). The API **accepts `"day"`
on write and on read and coerces it to `"week"`**; it never rejects it. Store it as `text` with
`CHECK (gantt_zoom IN ('week','month','quarter','day'))` — **not** as a Postgres enum that refuses
`'day'`, which would need a data migration first.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | A view has no meaning without its board. |
| `group_by_column_id` | `board_columns(id)` | `SET NULL` | This *is* `pruneView` for this field: "the view survives the deletion instead of rendering against a column that is gone" (`src/lib/board-view.ts:282-287`). A Kanban view whose grouping column was deleted must still open. |
| `date_column_id` | `board_columns(id)` | `SET NULL` | Same. |
| `end_date_column_id` | `board_columns(id)` | `SET NULL` | Same. |
| `created_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are never hard-deleted. |

The six JSONB payloads that also hold column ids — `filters`, `sorts`, `column_order`,
`hidden_column_ids`, `column_widths`, `column_display` — **cannot** be protected by a foreign key.
E-054 must prune all six in its own transaction, reproducing `pruneView`
(`src/lib/board-view.ts:288-334`) exactly. A view persisted holding a dead column id is a spec
defect.

**Unique Constraints**

- `UNIQUE (board_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` — dense tab order; deferred because
  E-082 rewrites the whole strip in one statement.

**Indexes**

| Index | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `board_views_pkey (id)` | E-080, E-081, E-083. |
| `(board_id, position)` | E-078 `GET /boards/{boardId}/views`; the `views` array inside every `Board` (E-047, E-049). |
| `(group_by_column_id)`, `(date_column_id)`, `(end_date_column_id)` | Required by the three FKs so E-054's `SET NULL` does not sequential-scan every view in the workspace. |

**Check Constraints**

- `position >= 0`.
- `filter_conjunction IN ('and','or')`.
- `row_height IN ('short','medium','tall')`.
- `subtask_display IN ('nested','flat','hidden')`.
- `gantt_zoom IN ('week','month','quarter','day')`.
- `jsonb_typeof(filters) = 'array'` and the same for `sorts`, `hidden_column_ids`, `column_order`;
  `jsonb_typeof(column_widths) = 'object'` and the same for `column_display`.

**`VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` is a write-time validation, not a check constraint.** Kanban needs
`group_by_column_id` and calendar needs `date_column_id` (canon §4.3), but E-054's `SET NULL` can
null either of them *after* the view was validly written, and the view must survive that. So: refuse
the write that would create or patch a view into that state (400 / `validation`); tolerate the state
when a column delete produced it, and let the view render its empty-state.

**Relationships**

- N-1 `boards`.
- N-1 `board_columns` three times, and by reference through six JSONB payloads.
- 1-N `board_view_preferences` (T-16) — the per-viewer companion, below.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Realtime | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-078 | `GET /boards/{boardId}/views` → `SavedView[]` | visibility | read-only | — | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-079 | `POST /boards/{boardId}/views` → `SavedView` | `board.view.manage` | One | RT-10 | `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN`, `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-080 | `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}` → `SavedView` | `board.view.manage` | One | RT-10 | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` |
| E-081 | `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}` → `SavedView[]` | `board.view.manage` | One: delete + renumber | RT-10 | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `VIEW_LAST_REMAINING` |
| E-082 | `POST /boards/{boardId}/views/reorder` → `SavedView[]` | `board.view.manage` | One: dense renumber | RT-10 | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-083 | `PUT /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}/preferences` → `ViewPreferences` | visibility | One (writes T-16, not this table) | — | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-054 | `DELETE …/columns/{columnId}` | `board.column.delete` | Prunes every view in the same transaction | RT-10 | — |

**Frontend callers** — `boardService.createView` / `updateView` / `reorderView` / `deleteView`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:790-898`) behind `useBoardStore.createView`, `patchView`,
`reorderView`, `deleteView`, `setColumnWidth`, `setColumnDisplay`, `setColumnHidden`,
`setColumnOrder` (`src/store/board-store.ts:229-257, 943-1120`);
`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx` and `view-config-bar.tsx` for the controls;
`resolveColumns` (`src/lib/board-view.ts:24-41`) for the merge.

#### 4.19.1 `SavedViewConfig` — the full JSONB interface

The six JSONB columns above are one logical document. `SavedViewConfig` names it, so a chapter
reading `filters jsonb` never has to guess:

```ts
type BoardViewType   = "table" | "kanban" | "calendar" | "gantt";
type FilterConjunction = "and" | "or";
type SortDirection   = "asc" | "desc";
type CellDisplayMode = "compact" | "wrap" | "full";
type RowHeight       = "short" | "medium" | "tall";
type SubtaskDisplay  = "nested" | "flat" | "hidden";
type GanttZoom       = "week" | "month" | "quarter";     // "day" accepted on the wire, coerced

type FilterOperator =
  | "isNotEmpty" | "isEmpty" | "contains" | "notContains"
  | "is" | "isNot" | "before" | "after" | "onOrBefore" | "onOrAfter";

/** board_views.filters — one element per condition. */
interface ViewFilter {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly columnId: string;      // board_columns.id on THIS board
  readonly operator: FilterOperator;
  /** Interpreted by the column's type: an option id OR label for select, a
   *  user id OR name for user, `YYYY-MM-DD` for date, free text otherwise. */
  readonly value: string;
}

/** board_views.sorts — multi-level; earlier entries win, later ones break ties. */
interface ViewSort {
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly direction: SortDirection;
}

/**
 * The complete presentation payload of a saved view. Every member maps to one
 * `board_views` column; the six marked JSONB are stored as documents, the rest
 * as scalars. This interface is the contract for all of them together.
 */
interface SavedViewConfig {
  readonly filters: readonly ViewFilter[];                            // jsonb
  readonly filterConjunction: FilterConjunction;
  readonly sorts: readonly ViewSort[];                                // jsonb
  readonly hiddenColumnIds: readonly string[];                        // jsonb
  readonly columnOrder: readonly string[];                            // jsonb
  readonly columnWidths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;            // jsonb
  /** Absent key = "compact". Only text/longText columns are flexible. */
  readonly columnDisplay?: Readonly<Record<string, CellDisplayMode>>; // jsonb
  readonly rowHeight: RowHeight;
  readonly groupByColumnId: string | null;
  readonly hideEmptyGroups: boolean;
  readonly dateColumnId: string | null;
  readonly endDateColumnId: string | null;
  readonly subtaskDisplay?: SubtaskDisplay;                           // default "nested"
  readonly ganttZoom?: GanttZoom;                                     // default "week"
  readonly showDependencies?: boolean;                                // default true
}

/** The wire shape: identity + config. `id` and `boardId` are forcibly preserved
 *  against any patch (src/services/board-service.ts:800-802). */
interface SavedView extends SavedViewConfig {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
}
```

**Defaults a fresh view is created with** (`src/services/board-service.ts:827-843`) — the service
writes these, the client sends only `name`, `type` and optionally `from`:
`filters: []`, `filterConjunction: "and"`, `sorts: []`, `hiddenColumnIds: []`, `columnOrder: []`,
`columnWidths: {}`, `rowHeight: "medium"`, `groupByColumnId: null`, `hideEmptyGroups: false`,
`dateColumnId: null`, `endDateColumnId: null`.

**Which view type consumes which field** — the backend validates against this and nothing else:

| Field | table | kanban | calendar | gantt |
| --- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| `filters`, `filterConjunction`, `sorts` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnOrder` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| `columnWidths`, `columnDisplay`, `rowHeight` | ✔ | — | — | — |
| `groupByColumnId` | ✔ | **required** | — | — |
| `hideEmptyGroups` | ✔ | forced `false` | — | — |
| `dateColumnId` | — | — | **required** | start anchor |
| `endDateColumnId` | — | — | — | end anchor |
| `subtaskDisplay` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| `ganttZoom`, `showDependencies` | — | — | — | ✔ |

(`src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:126-160`; `src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:82-136`;
`src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx:82-83`. The Gantt's task-panel width is local component
state, not `columnWidths` — `gantt-board.tsx:73`.)

**Companion table (owned by the views chapter): `board_view_preferences` (T-16, OQ-46, E-083).**
`(view_id, user_id)` → per-viewer overrides for column widths and collapse state, with the shared
view providing the defaults. Canon's position on OQ-46: `board_views` is shared and governed by
`board.view.manage`; **filters and sorts stay shared — they are what a named view *is*.** The merge
point is already a single function on the client (`resolveColumns`), so the split is contained. The
problem it solves is real and named in the source: column widths currently live on the shared view,
so one person's resize reaches everyone (`docs/BOARD.md:378-382`).

#### 4.19.2 Why column display modes live on the saved view, not on the column

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — the frontend decided this, and the schema follows it.**

`CellDisplayMode` (`compact` | `wrap` | `full`) is stored in `board_views.column_display`, a
`Record<columnId, CellDisplayMode>`. There is deliberately **no `display_mode` column on
`board_columns`**. The reason is written into the type itself:

> "Per-column display mode. Presentation, so it sits beside `columnWidths` rather than on the schema:
> one saved view can read Step in full while another keeps it to a line, without either changing what
> the column *is*. A column missing from the map is `compact`."
> — `src/types/board.ts:347-353`

The concrete case is a QA board. "Steps to reproduce" is a paragraph. The **Triage** view wants one
line per record so a hundred defects fit on a screen; the **Execution** view wants the whole step
text in place so a tester can read it without opening a drawer. Both are reading the same column of
the same board at the same moment. A mode stored on the column would force one of those two readers
to lose, and the loser's only recourse would be to edit shared schema — a change that would reach
everyone on the board.

Four supporting facts make this the schema-correct split, not just a UI preference:

1. **The split is already codified.** `resolveColumns(board, view)` is the one merge point:
   effective width is `view.columnWidths[id] ?? column.width` (clamped), effective hidden is
   `!isPrimary && (view.hiddenColumnIds.has(id) || column.hidden)` — the view can only *add* hiding
   on top of the schema's, never remove it (`src/lib/board-view.ts:24-41`). `columnDisplay` joins
   `columnWidths`, `columnOrder` and `hiddenColumnIds` on the per-view side of exactly that line.
2. **It is read only through the view.** `table-grid.tsx:132` reads
   `view?.columnDisplay ?? EMPTY_DISPLAY` and nothing else in the codebase reads it; it is written
   only by `useBoardStore.setColumnDisplay`, which patches the view
   (`src/store/board-store.ts:1062-1073`). There is no code path in which a column would supply one.
3. **It has no effect on most types.** Only `text` and `longText` are flexible; chips, dates, avatars
   and file thumbnails are laid out rather than flowed, so a second line would show nothing more
   (`isFlexibleColumn`, `src/lib/cell-display.ts:60-69`). A schema field that is meaningless for five
   of seven column types is not schema.
4. **It is table-only.** Kanban, calendar and Gantt never consult it. A field on `board_columns`
   would be a schema property that three of four view types ignore.

The same argument settles `columnWidths`, `columnOrder`, `hiddenColumnIds`, `rowHeight` and
`subtaskDisplay` — all per view. `board_columns.width` and `board_columns.hidden` remain as the
*schema defaults* a view starts from, which is why both exist in both places and why the merge is
directional.

**Consequence for E-054.** Because `column_display` is keyed by column id inside a JSONB document, a
column delete must strip its key in the same transaction — "a view that still names a deleted column
is a view carrying a dead reference" (`src/lib/board-view.ts:298-303`).

---

### 4.19.3 Table: `board_view_preferences`

Canon T-16. **RECOMMENDATION, deferred — OQ-46.**

**Purpose** — the part of a saved view that is one person's, split out from the part that is
everybody's. Today `SavedViewConfig` holds `columnWidths` and `columnDisplay` alongside
`filters` and `sorts` on the same shared row (`src/types/board.ts:346-353`), which means
dragging a column edge edits a view your colleagues are reading. This table is the
recommended fix, and the split it draws is the whole of the recommendation:

| Stays on `board_views` (shared) | Moves here (per viewer) |
| --- | --- |
| `filters`, `filterConjunction`, `sorts`, `groupByColumnId`, `hideEmptyGroups`, `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnOrder`, `dateColumnId`, `endDateColumnId`, `rowHeight` | `columnWidths`, `columnDisplay`, collapsed-group state |

Filters and sorts stay shared because they are **what a named view is** — "Open bugs, newest
first" stops meaning anything if each viewer's copy filters differently. A column's width is
not part of that meaning.

**Who creates a record** — upsert by the viewer, on their first width drag or group collapse
in that view. Never created eagerly: a person who never resizes anything never gets a row.

**How long it lives** — until the view or the user goes. No expiry.

**How it is deleted** — cascaded from either side. There is no explicit delete endpoint;
writing an empty `preferences` object is the reset, and the row may then be reaped or left,
indifferently.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `view_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | |
| `preferences` | `JSONB` | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | no | Structure below. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |

**`preferences` JSONB — the complete contract**

```ts
interface BoardViewPreferences {
  /** Column id → pixel width. A column absent from the map uses the view's own. */
  readonly columnWidths?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  /** Column id → display mode. Absent means `compact`, as on the shared view. */
  readonly columnDisplay?: Readonly<Record<string, CellDisplayMode>>;
  /** Group keys the viewer has folded shut. Never persisted shared. */
  readonly collapsedGroupKeys?: readonly string[];
}
```

Every key is optional and every unknown key is ignored, so the client resolves a column's
width as *viewer override → view value → schema `width`* and always finds an answer. A
column id that no longer exists is dropped on read rather than erroring: schema changes must
not make somebody's view unreadable.

**Primary Key** — `(view_id, user_id)`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `view_id` | `board_views(id)` | `CASCADE` | An override of a deleted view is not an override. |
| `user_id` | `users(id)` | `CASCADE` | |

**Unique Constraints** — the primary key.

**Indexes** — the primary key. Reads are always `(view_id, user_id)`; nothing lists this
table.

**Checks** — `CHECK (jsonb_typeof(preferences) = 'object')`.

**Delete Behavior** — hard delete, cascaded from both parents.

**Relationships** — N-1 to `board_views`, N-1 to `users`. Because it is keyed on the **view**
and not on the board, a person who has widened a column in "All bugs" has not widened it in
"My bugs" — which matches how the two views already differ in every other respect.

**APIs that use it** — E-083 `PUT /views/{viewId}/preferences` writes it; the values ride out
on the view read (E-080/E-081) already merged, so the client never has to make two calls or
know the merge rule. **This endpoint does not require `board.view.manage`** — that is the
point of the split. Membership plus read access on the board is enough to move your own
column edge, where editing the shared view is not.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-46)** — whether to make the split at all, or to leave widths shared and
accept that resizing edits everyone's view. The recommendation is to split, and to ship the
merge on the read side first so the client never learns about two sources.

---

### 4.20 Table: `board_templates`

**Purpose** — a board blueprint: the columns and views a new board starts with, plus its record-id
prefix. The four built-ins (`task`, `bug`, `qa`, `apiDocs`) are **seed rows in this table**, not
constants in backend source. `columns` and `views` are JSONB because a template is inert data that is
deep-copied at instantiation and never queried per column.

**Who creates a record** — the four built-ins by seed migration with `is_builtin = true` and
`workspace_id = NULL`. User-authored templates by `POST
/workspaces/{workspaceId}/board-templates` (E-089, `board.template.manage`, **RECOMMENDATION**,
OQ-47) — "save a board as a template".

**Lifetime** — `DELETE /board-templates/{templateId}` (E-090), **refused on a built-in**. Deleting a
user template nulls `boards.template_id` on every board made from it (`SET NULL`) and changes nothing
else about those boards. Built-ins are never deleted; a workspace's own templates cascade away with
the workspace.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `uuid` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Template identity (C-01). |
| `builtin_id` | `text` | yes | `NULL` | yes | `task` \| `bug` \| `qa` \| `apiDocs` for the four seeds, `NULL` otherwise. **This is what the wire's `templateId` carries for a built-in**, so `board.templateId === "apiDocs"` keeps working (`src/lib/api-catalog.ts:28-40`, `src/services/search-service.ts:39-43`). |
| `workspace_id` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | `NULL` for the built-ins, which every workspace sees. Set for user-authored templates. |
| `is_builtin` | `boolean` | no | `false` | no | Guards E-090 and marks the seed rows. |
| `name` | `text` | no | — | no | `Task board`, `Bug board`, `QA / QC board`, `API documentation`. |
| `description` | `text` | no | `''` | no | One line, shown in the template picker. |
| `row_id_prefix` | `text` | no | — | no | `TASK`, `BUG`, `QA`, `API`. Copied to `boards.row_id_prefix` at instantiation. |
| `primary_column_id` | `text` | no | — | no | A **template-local** column id (`col_title`, `col_endpoint`), not a UUID and not a foreign key — template column ids are remapped at instantiation. |
| `columns` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | `BoardTemplateColumn[]`. Below. |
| `views` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | `TemplateView[]`. Below. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `updated_at` | `timestamptz` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `created_by` | `uuid` | yes | `NULL` | no | `NULL` for the seeds. |

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | A workspace's own templates go with it. `NULL` (built-in) is never affected. |
| `created_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are never hard-deleted. |

**Unique Constraints**

- `UNIQUE (builtin_id)` — one row per built-in.
- `UNIQUE (workspace_id, lower(name)) WHERE workspace_id IS NOT NULL` — **RECOMMENDATION**: two
  templates with the same name in one workspace are a picker the user cannot read. The frontend has
  no user-template UI, so this rule is proposed, not observed (OQ-47).

**Indexes**

| Index | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `board_templates_pkey (id)` | E-088, E-090; the `boards.template_id` join. |
| `UNIQUE (builtin_id)` | Resolving the wire value `"apiDocs"` back to a row. |
| `(workspace_id) WHERE workspace_id IS NOT NULL` | E-087 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/board-templates` — built-ins plus this workspace's own. |

**Check Constraints**

- `row_id_prefix ~ '^[A-Z]{1,6}$'`.
- `is_builtin = (builtin_id IS NOT NULL)` — the two flags cannot disagree.
- `NOT (is_builtin AND workspace_id IS NOT NULL)` — a built-in belongs to no workspace.
- `jsonb_typeof(columns) = 'array' AND jsonb_typeof(views) = 'array'`.

**Relationships**

- 1-N `boards` through `boards.template_id` (`SET NULL`).
- N-1 `workspaces`, nullable.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Realtime | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-087 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/board-templates` → `BoardTemplate[]` | membership | read-only | — | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-088 | `GET /board-templates/{templateId}` → `BoardTemplate` | membership | read-only | — | `not_found` |
| E-089 | `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/board-templates` → `BoardTemplate` | `board.template.manage` | One | — | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`, `VALIDATION_FAILED` |
| E-090 | `DELETE /board-templates/{templateId}` | `board.template.manage` | One | — | `not_found`, `conflict` on a built-in |
| E-024 | `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` (`kind: "board"`, `templateId`) | `node.create` + `board.create` | One: node + board + every column + every view | RT-11 | `not_found` |

**Frontend callers** — `templateById` / `BOARD_TEMPLATES` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:408-419`)
behind the template picker; `useCreateBoard` (`src/hooks/use-create-board.ts:22-35`);
`prefixForBoard` (`src/mock/board.ts:69-71`).

#### 4.20.1 The two JSONB payloads

```ts
/**
 * A column as a template declares it. Identical to `BoardColumn` except that
 * `id` is a template-local string (`col_status`), not a UUID: real ids are
 * minted at instantiation. `config` is the same discriminated union as
 * `board_columns.config` (§4.12.1), option ids included.
 */
type BoardTemplateColumn = {
  readonly id: string;                       // template-local, e.g. "col_status"
  readonly name: string;
  readonly position: number;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly hidden: boolean;
  readonly isPrimary: boolean;
} & {
  [T in ColumnType]: { readonly type: T; readonly config: ColumnConfigByType[T] };
}[ColumnType];

/** A view as a template declares it — ids are minted when it is instantiated.
 *  Every optional field is defaulted at instantiation, not stored. */
interface TemplateView {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
  readonly groupByColumnId?: string;         // template-local column id
  readonly dateColumnId?: string;
  readonly endDateColumnId?: string;
  readonly hiddenColumnIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly sorts?: readonly ViewSort[];
  readonly filters?: readonly ViewFilter[];
}
```

#### 4.20.2 Instantiation — the exact contract

**A template is inert data. Instantiating one deep-copies its schema, so editing the board it
produced can never reach back** (`src/types/board.ts:396-399`; the catalogue is deep-`Object.freeze`d
at module load, `src/lib/board-templates.ts:459-471`, so an accidental in-place write fails loudly).
Canon §1.3.5 makes this a hard rule: the board a template produced is an ordinary board that can add,
rename, retype and delete columns and must never be constrained by the template it came from.

Inside the E-024 transaction:

1. **Mint a fresh UUID for every template column.** Insert them into `board_columns` with `position`
   taken from the template, `width` / `hidden` / `is_primary` copied, and `config` deep-copied.
2. **Keep every select option id verbatim** — `status_0 … status_4`, `env_0 … env_2`,
   `method_0 …`. `instantiateColumns` copies option objects without re-minting their ids
   (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:434-441`), and three sibling structures inside the same `config`
   reference them: `completedOptionIds`, `transitionRules.transitions` (keys **and** target arrays)
   and each option's `availability` conditions. Re-minting would mean rewriting all three; keeping
   them costs nothing, because an option id is a column-scoped string inside a JSONB document, not a
   database row, and C-01 does not reach it.
3. **Remap every template-local *column* id to the new UUID**, in all seven places it can appear:
   `boards.primary_column_id`; each view's `groupByColumnId`, `dateColumnId`, `endDateColumnId` and
   `hiddenColumnIds`; each view's `sorts[].columnId` and `filters[].columnId`; and — easy to miss —
   **`Condition.columnId` inside every option's `availability` tree**. The `task` template's "Done"
   option is gated on `col_blocks` being empty (`whenEmpty("status_4_rule", "col_blocks")`,
   `src/lib/board-templates.ts:118-125, 148-157`), and a missed remap there silently disables the
   rule, because a condition pointing at an unknown column evaluates to `true` (§4.15, rule 1).
4. **Deep-copy every nested structure**: each option object, each `availability` `ConditionGroup`
   recursively including `Condition.values` arrays (`cloneConditionGroup`,
   `src/lib/board-templates.ts:474-483`), `completedOptionIds`, and the `transitions` map with each
   target array copied.
5. **Turn each `TemplateView` into a full `board_views` row**, defaulting everything the template
   omits: `filterConjunction: "and"`, `columnOrder: []`, `columnWidths: {}`, `columnDisplay: {}`,
   `rowHeight: "medium"`, `hideEmptyGroups: false`, `subtaskDisplay: "nested"`,
   `ganttZoom: "week"`, `showDependencies: true`, and `null` for any unset anchor
   (`src/mock/board.ts:73-96`).
6. **Order the views so the node's `boardKind` opens first.** The matching view is hoisted to
   `position 0` (`src/mock/board.ts:98-99`), and the tree's legacy `timeline` kind maps onto the
   `gantt` view type (`VIEW_TYPE_BY_BOARD_KIND`, `src/services/board-service.ts:76-81`).
7. **Copy `row_id_prefix`** to `boards.row_id_prefix`, and set `boards.template_id` — for reference
   only.

#### 4.20.3 The four built-ins, as seed data

| `builtin_id` | `name` | `row_id_prefix` | primary column | Notable config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `task` | Task board | `TASK` | `col_title` (text) | Status with 5 options; `completedOptionIds: ["status_4"]`; a seeded, **disabled** transition table; **"Done" gated on `Blocked by` being empty** via `availability`. Views: All records (table), Board (kanban on `col_status`), Schedule (calendar on `col_due`), Roadmap (gantt `col_start` → `col_due`). |
| `bug` | Bug board | `BUG` | `col_title` "Summary" | Severity; Status with 6 options and `completedOptionIds: ["status_4","status_5"]`; a seeded ladder — nothing jumps from New straight to Verified; Environment from the shared list. |
| `qa` | QA / QC board | `QA` | `col_title` "Test case" | Result with `completedOptionIds: ["result_1"]` (Passed); Suite; Environment; evidence attachment. |
| `apiDocs` | API documentation | `API` | `col_endpoint` (text) | Method with a colour per verb (`METHOD_OPTIONS`); Domain; Auth; Environment. |

(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:129-406`.) Two vocabularies are defined **once** and shared:
`ENVIRONMENT_OPTIONS` = Development / Staging / Production with ids `env_0 … env_2` and
`PRODUCTION_OPTION_ID = "env_2"` (`:26-36`); `METHOD_OPTIONS` = GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE
(`:39-49`). The environment list is also a workspace table (T-26, DV-ENV-21, OQ-63); the template's
copy is a snapshot taken at instantiation and diverges freely afterwards, like every other part of a
template.

All four ship their transition tables with `enabled: false` — "a board should behave exactly as it
always has until someone opts into the rules" (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:103-113`).

**No typed tables for the four.** There is no `tasks`, `bugs`, `qa_cases` or `api_endpoints` table,
and canon §1.3.5 forbids adding one. The evidence that this is a hard rule rather than a convenience:
the dashboard reads a board as QA **by what it became** — its status column offering a `passed` or
`failed` option — and explicitly not by template id, because "a board created from the QA template
and then reshaped should follow what it became" (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:86-96`). And the API board's
duplicate-endpoint rule is "warned in amber, **never blocked**" (`DV-API-20`) — a validation a
dedicated table would have to make an error.
