### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

Four places where I followed canon over my own reading, plus one place where canon disagrees with
itself. None of them changed what I wrote; all of them are worth a pass before the document ships.

1. **Table names.** My brief named `row_relations`, `saved_views` and `board_column_options`. Canon's
   registry names them `board_row_relations` (T-13), `board_views` (T-15) and — for the third — no
   table at all, because canon §1.3.3 decides select options live in `board_columns.config`. I
   followed canon in all three cases. §4.13 documents the option as a fully specified JSONB object so
   the brief's content requirement (id, label, colour, position, disabled flag, availability rule) is
   still answered in full; the answer to "position" is that the array index *is* the position, and
   that this is load-bearing in three places.

2. **`board_rows.version` vs `revision`.** My brief said `version`; the frontend field is `revision`
   (`src/types/board.ts:249`) and canon T-12 says `revision`. I used `revision` everywhere.

3. **Canon contradicts itself about `boards.name`.** Canon T-10 lists `name` as a column on `boards`;
   canon §8.8's position on OQ-30 says the node owns `name` and that it is "**projected**, not
   duplicated". I followed §8.8, because it is the explicit decision and T-10 is a one-line summary.
   Consequence worth confirming: E-050 `PATCH /boards/{boardId}` lists `name` as patchable, so that
   field writes through to `nodes.name` inside the board's transaction and needs `node.rename` in
   addition to `board.manage`. If the editor prefers a duplicated `boards.name`, §4.11 and E-050's
   permission line both need changing.

4. **Canon says the four projection columns on `board_rows` are "generated columns … maintained by
   Postgres" (§1.3.2).** They cannot be literal `GENERATED ALWAYS AS` columns: the expression would
   have to know *which* column id plays the due-date role on *this* board, and that is per-board row
   data, not a constant, so the expression is not immutable. I documented them as projections
   maintained by the service inside the same statement that writes `cells` (§4.16.4), which produces
   the same guarantee — they can never lag a cell write — without requiring an impossible DDL. A
   `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger reading `boards` is the equivalent alternative if the editor
   prefers the invariant enforced below the service.

5. **`board_rows` soft delete.** Canon §1.4 puts `deleted_at` / `deleted_by` on `board_rows`, so I
   included them. The frontend hard-deletes records — "records have no trash of their own"
   (`src/services/board-service.ts:1049`) — and canon's own OQ-15 asks whether that asymmetry with
   the 30-day node trash is intended, taking no position. If OQ-15 resolves as "records really are
   permanent", the two columns come out of §4.16 and E-065/E-076 become hard deletes; nothing else in
   this chapter changes, because the composite parent FK's `SET NULL` already produces the
   lift-to-top-level behaviour either way.

### Shared preface — the decomposed target, used by three tables

`comments` (T-33), `watches` (T-34) and `notifications` (T-35) all point at the same
thing through the same five columns. It is written once here and referenced from each
table rather than re-explained three times.

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** The frontend addresses every collaboration target through one
shape, `EntityRef` (`src/types/collab.ts:16-26`), and identifies it with one string,
`refKey` (`src/lib/entity-ref.ts:21-23`) — the only place in the codebase that knows the
format:

```ts
export function refKey(ref: EntityRef): string {
  return ref.kind === "row"
    ? `row:${ref.boardId ?? ref.nodeId}:${ref.rowId}`
    : `${ref.kind}:${ref.nodeId}`;
}
```

| `kind` | `targetKey` grammar | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `row:<boardId>:<rowId>` | `row:brd_nd_bug_tracker:brd_nd_bug_tracker_row_7` |
| `document` / `board` / `project` / `folder` / `file` | `<kind>:<nodeId>` | `document:nd_engineering_handbook` |

**DECISION — store it decomposed, generate the string.** `targetKey` is never a column
and never a primary key. Five real columns carry it:

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target_kind` | `entity_kind` | `EntityKind` (§2.3): `project`, `folder`, `board`, `document`, `file`, `row` |
| `target_node_id` | `UUID` | The drive node that addresses the target — the routing anchor |
| `target_board_id` | `UUID` | Non-null only when `target_kind = 'row'` |
| `target_row_id` | `UUID` | Non-null only when `target_kind = 'row'` |
| `target_label` | `TEXT` | Display snapshot of the target's name at write time |

Reason, in one sentence: `ON DELETE CASCADE`, the permission funnel, the My Work
`mentioned` query and the global search join are all foreign-key questions, and a single
opaque text key turns every one of them into a `LIKE`.

The API serialises `targetKey` back into every response exactly as `refKey` does, so the
frontend's React keys, its `Map<targetKey, …>` stores and its realtime routing
(`src/store/watch-store.ts:21`, `src/hooks/use-comments.ts:59`) keep working unchanged.

**Two check constraints hold on every table that carries these columns:**

```sql
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_row_id   IS NOT NULL))
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_board_id IS NOT NULL))
```

**`target_label` is untrusted display text, never an authorisation input.** It is a copy
of the target's name taken at write time, and the frontend already treats a stale label
as a disclosure risk: it re-resolves every notification against the tree the reader can
see *now* and drops items whose node is gone or no longer visible
(`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:58-64` → `keepVisibleRefs`,
`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:252-268` — *"the resource is gone, and its name is
still on screen"*). **The backend must apply that filter server-side and never rely on
the client dropping them.**

Per canon §1.4, the label is **resolved live on read** on `comments` and `watches`, and
**frozen at creation** on `notifications` — a notification is a historical statement
(OQ-79).

---

### Table: `comments`

**Purpose** — One comment or reply on one target, for every target kind the workspace
has. A record and a page share the same thread model, the same reply rules and the same
mention fan-out, so there is one table and not one per surface
(`src/services/comment-service.ts:15-22`). It is also the only place a collaboration
notification is created, which is what keeps the inbox consistent with what was actually
said.

**Who creates a record** — `POST /comments` (E-120), called by the record drawer
(`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:266`) and the document page
(`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:139-143`) through
`useComments().post` (`src/hooks/use-comments.ts:78-107`). The actor is the session
user; `author_id` is never read from the body (C-09).

**Lifetime** — **Soft delete.** `deleted_at` / `deleted_by` are set by E-122 and the row
stays, because `buildThreads` promotes an orphan reply to a root
(`src/lib/comments.ts:67-87`) — a hard delete of a root would silently restructure a live
thread into what reads as data corruption. A soft-deleted comment is returned as a
tombstone when it has replies and omitted when it has none. Hard deletion happens only by
cascade: purging the target node from trash, hard-deleting the target row (E-065), or
deleting the workspace.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | C-01. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Tenant scope. Every search and every list is workspace-scoped before it is node-scoped. |
| `target_kind` | `entity_kind` | no | — | no | See the shared preface. |
| `target_node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Routing anchor and the permission join key. |
| `target_board_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Non-null iff `target_kind = 'row'`. |
| `target_row_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Non-null iff `target_kind = 'row'`. |
| `target_label` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Display snapshot. Re-resolved live on read; kept for forensics when the target is gone. |
| `parent_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | The **root** this replies to. `NULL` on a root. Never points at a reply. |
| `author_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Session user at post time. |
| `body` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Raw body, mentions encoded as `@[Name](usr_id)`. Stored exactly as sent, trimmed. |
| `body_plain` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `plainBody(body)` — mention tokens flattened to `@Name` (`src/lib/mentions.ts:133-135`). Written by the service in the same statement; the search index and the notification preview both read it. |
| `mentioned_user_ids` | `UUID[]` | no | `'{}'` | no | Parsed **server-side** from `body` by the regex at `src/lib/mentions.ts:13`; de-duplicated, first-appearance order. A client-supplied list is ignored (E-120). |
| `search_tsv` | `tsvector` | no | generated | no | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', body_plain)) STORED`. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | C-03. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Any write to the row. On the wire as `updatedAt`. |
| `edited_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | Set the first time the **body** changes after posting, and refreshed on every later edit. `isEdited` on the wire is `edited_at IS NOT NULL`. |
| `resolved_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | Thread resolution. Only ever set where `parent_id IS NULL` (OQ-80). |
| `resolved_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Session user who resolved it. |
| `deleted_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | Soft delete (canon §1.4 — never a boolean). |
| `deleted_by` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Session user who deleted it. |

There is **no** `is_edited BOOLEAN` and **no** `is_resolved BOOLEAN` column: canon §1.4
forbids a boolean where a timestamp answers both "whether" and "when". Both booleans are
derived on read, so the frontend contract (`Comment.isEdited`,
`src/types/collab.ts:54-55`) is unchanged.

**No JSONB column.** The target is decomposed into typed columns precisely so it can be
joined, cascaded and permission-filtered; the body is prose, not structure.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | A deleted tenant leaves nothing behind. |
| `target_node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | A node purged from trash takes its threads. A thread whose `refKey` no longer routes anywhere is unreachable by construction, so keeping it only preserves the target's name (a leak surface, §preface). |
| `target_board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same, one level down. Redundant with the node cascade in practice; kept so the constraint, not a convention, guarantees it. |
| `target_row_id` | `board_rows(id)` | `CASCADE` | Rows are hard-deleted (E-065), and a comment on a record that no longer exists has no drawer to render in. **Note the asymmetry with nodes, which get a 30-day trash — OQ-15.** |
| `parent_id` | `comments(id)` | `SET NULL` | Matches the frontend exactly: `buildThreads` promotes an orphan reply to a root rather than dropping it (`src/lib/comments.ts:72-84`). Because delete is soft, this only ever fires on a purge. `CASCADE` here would delete a colleague's reply as a side effect of removing the root. |
| `author_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are soft-deactivated, never hard-deleted (T-01), so the author always renders. `RESTRICT` makes a future hard delete fail loudly instead of erasing authorship. |
| `resolved_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Same. |
| `deleted_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Same. |

**Unique Constraints** — none. Two identical bodies posted twice by the same author are
two comments; idempotency is the client's `upsertComment` by id
(`src/lib/comments.ts:23-39`), not a database constraint.

**Check Constraints**

```sql
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_row_id   IS NOT NULL))
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_board_id IS NOT NULL))
CHECK (parent_id IS DISTINCT FROM id)                              -- no self-parent
CHECK (resolved_at IS NULL OR parent_id IS NULL)                   -- resolution is a thread property
CHECK ((resolved_at IS NULL) = (resolved_by IS NULL))
CHECK ((deleted_at  IS NULL) = (deleted_by  IS NULL))
CHECK (edited_at IS NULL OR edited_at >= created_at)
```

Two rules that a `CHECK` cannot express and the service must therefore enforce:

1. **`parent_id` must reference a root.** A `CHECK` cannot subquery. The service reproduces
   `rootIdFor` (`src/services/comment-service.ts:149-156`) verbatim: an unknown parent is
   `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND` (404); a parent that is itself a reply **silently re-parents to
   that reply's root** and is not an error (E-125 — "a reply to a reply re-parents to the
   root"). The result is that `parent_id` is always null or a root.
2. **A comment needs a body or an attachment.** `length(btrim(body)) > 0` OR at least one
   `comment_attachments` row — a cross-table condition. Enforced at E-120 and E-121 with
   `COMMENT_EMPTY` (400 / `validation`): *"A comment needs a message or an attachment"* on
   create, *"A comment cannot be emptied"* on edit
   (`src/services/comment-service.ts:106-111`, `:178-183`).

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `comments_thread_idx (target_node_id, target_kind, target_row_id, created_at ASC, id ASC)` | E-119 — one thread, oldest-first, keyset-paged on `(created_at, id)` (§6.3). Also the drawer's comment-count badge (`commentService.countFor`, `:60-62`). |
| `comments_replies_idx (parent_id, created_at ASC, id ASC) WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL` | E-125 — replies of one root, and the per-root reply count on `CommentPage`. |
| `comments_mentions_idx GIN (mentioned_user_ids)` | E-134 My Work `mentioned` widget — `WHERE mentioned_user_ids @> ARRAY[$me]`, replacing the frontend's full-catalogue scan (`src/services/comment-service.ts:65-75`). |
| `comments_search_idx GIN (search_tsv)` | E-133 global search, `comment` group. The permission funnel runs first and yields a visible node-id set, so the scan is `target_node_id = ANY($visible) AND search_tsv @@ …` (`src/services/search-service.ts:116-131`). |
| `comments_target_row_idx (target_row_id) WHERE target_row_id IS NOT NULL` | Backs the `board_rows` cascade so a bulk row delete (E-076) does not sequential-scan `comments` once per row. |

**Relationships**

- **N-1** to `users` (`author_id`, `resolved_by`, `deleted_by`).
- **N-1** to `nodes`, `boards`, `board_rows` — the decomposed target.
- **1-N** self-referential, exactly **two levels deep**: a root has many replies; a reply
  has none. Enforced at write time, not at render time.
- **1-N** to `comment_attachments`.
- **N-1** to `workspaces`.
- **No** foreign key from `notifications` to `comments`. A notification is a historical
  statement with a frozen title and body (OQ-79); deleting the comment must not delete or
  rewrite the notification that announced it.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-119 | `GET /comments?targetKind=&targetNodeId=&targetBoardId=&targetRowId=&cursor=&limit=` | visibility on the target | `CommentPage`, roots first, each with a reply count (OQ-83). |
| E-120 | `POST /comments` | `comment.create` | One transaction — see below. |
| E-121 | `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` | author only | Sets `edited_at`, recomputes `mentioned_user_ids` and `body_plain`. |
| E-122 | `DELETE /comments/{commentId}` | `comment.delete` | Own comment at `member`, anyone else's at `manager` (OQ-24). Returns the tombstone. |
| E-123 | `POST /comments/{commentId}/resolve` | `comment.resolve` | Root comments only (OQ-80). |
| E-124 | `DELETE /comments/{commentId}/resolve` | `comment.resolve` | |
| E-125 | `GET /comments/{commentId}/replies?cursor=&limit=` | visibility on the target | |
| E-133 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/search` | membership | `comment` group; snippet from `body_plain`. |
| E-134 | `GET /me/work` | session | `mentioned` widget. |

**Page shape (RECOMMENDATION — canon §5.5 names `CommentPage` without defining it):**

```ts
/** E-119, E-125. Oldest-first, keyset on (created_at ASC, id ASC) — §6.3. */
interface CommentPage {
  readonly items: readonly Comment[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
  /** Root comment id → number of non-deleted replies. Roots only. */
  readonly replyCounts: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
}
```

**Transaction — E-120 is one transaction, in this order** (mirroring
`src/services/comment-service.ts:100-146`):

1. Validate: trimmed body non-empty **or** at least one attachment, else `COMMENT_EMPTY`.
2. Resolve `parent_id` through `rootIdFor`.
3. `INSERT` the comment; `INSERT` its `comment_attachments` rows.
4. **Auto-watch the author** — upsert into `watches` (§`watches`). This runs *before* the
   fan-out so the author is already a watcher and is then excluded from the `comment`
   notification by `exceptUserId`.
5. Fan out notifications (§`notifications`).
6. `INSERT` a `row_activity` entry with `kind = 'commented'` when the target is a row.
7. `COMMIT`, then publish **RT-01 `comment.created`** to every subscriber with that
   `targetKey` open.

The realtime frame is published **after commit**, never inside it: a frame for a write
that rolls back is a phantom the client dedups by id but cannot un-render.

**Errors** — `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND` (404), `COMMENT_EMPTY` (400), `COMMENT_NOT_AUTHOR` (403,
*"You can only edit your own comments"* / *"Reply instead to add to the thread."*),
`COMMENT_ALREADY_RESOLVED` (409), `COMMENT_RESOLVE_NOT_ROOT` (409), `NODE_NOT_FOUND` /
`ROW_NOT_FOUND` (404), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403).

**Realtime** — RT-01 `comment.created` on E-120; RT-02 `comment.updated` on E-121, E-122,
E-123 and E-124. Both carry `{ targetKey, comment }`, which is the one place canon lets a
frame carry content — the receiver already holds visibility on that `targetKey` to be
subscribed at all (OQ-100).

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-81) — does the PRD's "keep the edit history" require a
> `comment_revisions` table?**
> **Evidence** — the PRD edge case for `CO-CMT-26` says *"Gắn nhãn '(đã chỉnh sửa)' và
> lưu lại lịch sử sửa"*. The frontend keeps only `updatedAt` + `isEdited`
> (`src/types/collab.ts:52-55`) and exposes no way to read prior revisions;
> `commentService.edit` overwrites the body in place
> (`src/services/comment-service.ts:189-195`). Canon's 39-table registry has no such table.
> **Recommendation** — follow canon and do **not** add a table now. If the requirement is
> confirmed, it is one append-only child table (`comment_id`, `body`, `edited_by`,
> `edited_at`) and one `INSERT` on the existing E-121 transaction; nothing in this chapter
> changes.
> **Impact if wrong** — the history is unrecoverable, because it was never written. It
> cannot be back-filled from data that does not exist.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-84) — does editing a comment notify people newly mentioned in the edit?**
> **Evidence** — `edit` recomputes `mentionedUserIds`
> (`src/services/comment-service.ts:192`) but only `add` calls `fanOut` (`:141`). A person
> named for the first time in an edit is never notified today.
> **Recommendation** — on E-121, diff `mentioned_user_ids` before and after and emit a
> `mention` notification only for ids that are **newly** present. Never re-notify someone
> already named, and never emit a `comment` notification on an edit.
> **Impact if wrong** — either people are pulled into threads silently, or every typo fix
> re-pings the thread.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-85) — mentioning somebody who cannot see the target.**
> **Evidence** — the PRD for `CO-MEN-27` requires the system to prompt for an access
> grant. The frontend does none of it: `mentionCandidates` filters on `isActive` only
> (`src/lib/mentions.ts:80`) and `fanOut` notifies every mentioned id unconditionally
> (`:224-235`) — the recipient's inbox then drops the item
> (`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:58-64`), so they are pinged into a void.
> **Recommendation** — on E-120, resolve each mentioned user's visibility of
> `target_node_id`. Still create the comment and still store the id in
> `mentioned_user_ids`, but **do not create a notification the recipient cannot act on**,
> and return `unreachableMentions: UserSummary[]` on the response so the UI can offer to
> grant access. Do **not** filter the mention picker by node access — that turns the
> picker into an access-mapping oracle.
> **Impact if wrong** — the PRD requirement is unmet and mentions silently fail; or the
> picker leaks who can see what.

---

### Not a table: `comment_mentions`

**Canon settles this and it is not re-litigated here.** The 39-table registry (§1.1) has
no `comment_mentions` and no generic `mentions` table, and §1.2 does not list one among
the tables that deliberately do not exist either — it simply is not in the schema. A
mention is a **projection of the comment body**, stored on the comment itself.

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — the storage format.** A mention lives *inside* the body as
`@[Display Name](user_id)`. The regex source is `src/lib/mentions.ts:13`:

```
@\[([^\]]{1,64})\]\(([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64})\)
```

Group 1 is the label (1–64 characters, anything but `]`), group 2 the user id (1–64
characters, `A-Za-z0-9_-` only). `extractMentionIds` (`:94-103`) de-duplicates through a
`Set` and preserves first-appearance order; `plainBody` (`:133-135`) flattens the token to
`@Name` for previews and search.

**What replaces the table:** `comments.mentioned_user_ids UUID[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`
with a `GIN` index.

**Why an array column and not a join table** — the honest trade-off:

| Axis | `mentioned_user_ids UUID[]` (CHOSEN) | `comment_mentions (comment_id, user_id)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Write cost | Zero extra statements. The array is computed in the same `INSERT`/`UPDATE` that writes the body. | One `DELETE` + N `INSERT`s per edit, because an edit rewrites the whole set. |
| "Comments mentioning me" (E-134) | `WHERE mentioned_user_ids @> ARRAY[$me]`, one GIN probe. | A join, marginally better selectivity. |
| Referential integrity on the user id | **None.** A mention id that never was a user, or was one and is now hard-deleted, stays in the array. | An FK to `users`. **This is the one axis the join table wins.** |
| Consistency with the body | Guaranteed: both are written by the same statement from the same parse. | Two writes that can disagree if one fails. |
| Deriving the set | Always re-derivable from `body` — the array is a cache, never the source of truth. | Same, but the cache is a table. |

The integrity gap is bounded in practice: `users` rows are soft-deactivated and never
hard-deleted (T-01), so a dangling id can only arise from a body that was never a real
mention — and the fan-out already resolves each id against the directory before creating a
notification, dropping anything unknown. That is cheaper than a join table whose only job
is to re-state what the body already says.

**Consequences a writer must honour:**

- `mentioned_user_ids` is **derived server-side on every write** (E-120, E-121). A
  client-supplied list is ignored — canon E-120 states this explicitly. A client that
  could name recipients could notify anyone in the workspace about a comment they cannot
  read.
- The mention picker (`GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/directory`, E-006) returns
  `DirectoryUser[]` **including deactivated members flagged `isActive: false`**, and the
  composer filters them out client-side (`src/lib/mentions.ts:80`) — *"former members are
  resolvable but not mentionable"*. The backend must not remove deactivated members from
  the directory; old mentions still have to render a name.
- Rendering is `parseBody` (`src/lib/mentions.ts:109-130`), which tokenises mentions and
  `TASK-001`-style record references **in one pass, in document order**. The backend never
  renders a body; it stores the raw string and the flattened `body_plain`.

---

### Table: `watches`

Canon T-34. The brief calls this `resource_watches`; the canonical name is `watches`, and
every chapter uses it.

**Purpose** — Who follows what (`CO-WAT-28`). One row per (person, thing they follow).
Watches are stored per user, exactly as a backend would, so the comment fan-out can ask
"who should hear about this?" without the UI assembling a recipient list
(`src/services/watch-service.ts:8-14`).

**Who creates a record** — `PUT /me/watches` (E-127) from the watch button on the board
toolbar (`src/components/board/board-toolbar.tsx:136`), the record drawer header
(`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:157`) and the document header
(`src/components/document/document-header.tsx:142`); **and** implicitly by E-120, which
auto-watches the comment author. The `user_id` is always the session user — canon P-06
puts the whole collection under `/me` and the user id is never a path or body parameter
(C-09, OQ-19).

**Lifetime** — **Hard delete.** Unwatching (E-128) removes the row; there is nothing to
tombstone. Cascades from `users`, `nodes`, `boards` and `board_rows`. **Trashing a node
keeps the watch** so a restore restores the follow, but E-126 filters trashed and
no-longer-visible targets out of the response (OQ-87).

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | C-01. The natural key is a `UNIQUE` constraint, not the PK. |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | The follower. Session user only. |
| `target_kind` | `entity_kind` | no | — | composite | Constrained to the three watchable kinds. |
| `target_node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | |
| `target_board_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Non-null iff `target_kind = 'row'`. |
| `target_row_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | composite | |
| `target_label` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Display snapshot; re-resolved live on read. |
| `since` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | **"Watching since", not "first ever watched"** — rewritten on every re-watch (`src/services/watch-service.ts:81`, `:114`). |

No `workspace_id`: unlike `comments` and `notifications`, a watch always has a non-null
`target_node_id`, and the node carries the workspace. Adding a redundant copy would create
a second thing to keep in step across a node move.

No JSONB column.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | `users(id)` | `CASCADE` | A watch has no meaning without its follower, and it is private to them — nobody else can read it, so nothing is lost by removing it. |
| `target_node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | The PRD edge case for `CO-WAT-28` is explicit: *"Tài nguyên bị xóa: Tự động gỡ khỏi danh sách Following"*. A `targetKey` naming a purged private resource must not stay readable by the follower. |
| `target_board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same. |
| `target_row_id` | `board_rows(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same; rows are hard-deleted. |

**Unique Constraints**

```sql
UNIQUE (user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)
```

This is the frontend's storage shape made a constraint: `Map<userId, Map<targetKey,
WatchEntry>>` (`src/services/watch-service.ts:17`). `target_row_id` is `NULL` for a
document or board watch, and Postgres treats `NULL`s as distinct in a unique index — so
the constraint must be declared `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, or `target_row_id` must be
defaulted to the all-zero UUID. **Use `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`** (PostgreSQL 15+); a sentinel
UUID is a value that means "no value", which is the bug the null was there to prevent.

E-127 is an **upsert**: `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET since = now(), target_label =
EXCLUDED.target_label`. Watching something twice is idempotent and refreshes `since`.

**Check Constraints**

```sql
CHECK (target_kind IN ('row', 'document', 'board'))                 -- WatchKind
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_row_id   IS NOT NULL))
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_board_id IS NOT NULL))
```

The first is `WatchKind` (`src/types/collab.ts:86`) — *"Only these three can be watched — a
file or folder has no activity stream."* Attempting to watch a `project`, `folder` or
`file` is **rejected, not ignored**: `WATCH_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED`, 400 / `validation`,
message `` `A ${kind} has no activity to follow` `` (`src/services/watch-service.ts:72-76`).
The button hides itself for unsupported targets (`src/hooks/use-watch.ts:38`), so a request
that reaches this check came from something other than the UI.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| The `UNIQUE` constraint's index `(user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)` | E-126 `GET /me/watches` (leading `user_id`), and the E-127 upsert conflict target. |
| `watches_target_idx (target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)` | **The fan-out**: "who watches this target, except the actor?" — run inside the E-120 transaction (`watchService.watchersOf`, `:93-103`). Also backs the four cascades. |

**Relationships**

- **N-1** to `users`.
- **N-1** to `nodes`, `boards`, `board_rows`.
- **N-N** between `users` and watchable targets, with `since` as the edge attribute.
- No relationship to `notifications`: a watch decides *who* gets a `comment` notification,
  but the notification row does not point back at the watch that produced it.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-126 | `GET /me/watches` | session | Returns `WatchEntry[]`, filtered to targets the caller can still see. |
| E-127 | `PUT /me/watches` | visibility on the target | Body is an `EntityRef`. Returns the caller's **full list**, which the store re-indexes wholesale (`src/store/watch-store.ts:67-103`). |
| E-128 | `DELETE /me/watches` | session | Same response contract. |
| E-120 | `POST /comments` | `comment.create` | Auto-watch, then read `watchersOf` — both inside the one transaction. |

`watchersOf` is **internal and must never be exposed as an endpoint.** It answers "who is
watching this?", which is a list of people's interests in a resource — a privacy leak with
no product surface asking for it.

**Auto-watch is a hard requirement, not a nicety.** `docs/COLLABORATION.md:176-177`:
*"Commenting on something starts following it. Without that rule the Following tab stays
empty for everybody who never found the button."*

**Errors** — `WATCH_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED` (400), `NODE_NOT_FOUND` / `ROW_NOT_FOUND` (404),
`PERMISSION_DENIED` (403 — the caller must be able to see what they follow).

**Realtime** — none. A watch is private to one person and there is no second surface in
the same session that needs to converge. The optimistic toggle with rollback
(`src/store/watch-store.ts:67-103`) is the whole consistency story.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-88) — which non-comment events notify watchers?**
> **Evidence** — the PRD for `CO-WAT-28` promises notifications on *"đổi status, có
> comment mới, cập nhật deadline"*. The frontend only ever fans out on a **new comment**;
> the `watch` reason exists **only in seed data** (`src/mock/collab.ts:216-225`), and the
> watch button's own tooltip says only *"You get notified about new comments here"*
> (`src/components/collab/watch-button.tsx:51-53`).
> **Recommendation** — emit a `watch` notification to watchers, excluding the actor, when a
> watched row's **status** column changes, when its **due-date** column changes, and when a
> watched **document is saved** (E-092). Identify "status" and "due" through the same
> column lenses My Work uses (`src/lib/my-work.ts:57-67`, OQ-48) so the two surfaces cannot
> disagree about what a status column is. Debounce per `(watcher, target)` — see OQ-91.
> **Impact if wrong** — either the Following tab only ever shows comments and the PRD
> promise is unmet, or every cell edit on a busy board floods every watcher's inbox.

---

### Table: `notifications`

Canon T-35. **One row per recipient — fan-out on write.**

**Purpose** — One person's inbox item (`CO-NOT-29`). A notification is a **historical
statement**: `title` and `body` are fully rendered strings stored on the row, not
templates, and its target label is frozen at creation (OQ-79). Fan-out happens on write,
one row per recipient, so `list` can only ever return the signed-in user's inbox and the
unread badge is a count of rows rather than a derived guess
(`src/services/notification-service.ts:8-15`).

**Who creates a record** — Never a client. Rows are inserted by the endpoint performing
the action, inside its transaction. Today exactly one endpoint does: **E-120
`POST /comments`**, through the fan-out at `src/services/comment-service.ts:223-250`.
Three more producers are owed and unbuilt (OQ-89): `assigned`, `watch` and `system`.

**Lifetime** — Lives until purged. There is no delete, no dismiss and no archive in the
frontend — read state is the only mutation (`src/types/collab.ts:112`). Cascades from
`users` (the recipient) and `workspaces`; `target_node_id` cascades from `nodes` so an
inbox cannot outlive the thing it names. **RECOMMENDATION (OQ-91):** purge read
notifications after 90 days by a nightly sweep; never purge an unread one.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | C-01. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | **Required**, because a `system` notice has no target at all and would otherwise be unscoped. |
| `recipient_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Whose inbox. The leading column of every read. |
| `reason` | `notification_reason` | no | — | no | `mention`, `assigned`, `comment`, `watch`, `system` (§2.9). The four UI tabs are a projection of this and nothing else. |
| `actor_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Who caused it. Non-nullable, matching `AppNotification.actor` (`src/types/collab.ts:106`). |
| `title` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Fully rendered at write time, e.g. `` `${author.name} mentioned you` ``. Never a template, never an i18n key. |
| `body` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Rendered preview. For a comment: `plainBody`, whitespace collapsed, trimmed, truncated to **140 characters** with a trailing `…` (`src/services/comment-service.ts:25`, `:47-50`). |
| `target_kind` | `entity_kind` | yes | `NULL` | no | All five target columns are `NULL` together for a `system` notice. |
| `target_node_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | |
| `target_board_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | |
| `target_row_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | |
| `target_label` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | **Frozen at creation** (OQ-79) — the one table where the label is not re-resolved on read. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Sort key, newest first. |
| `read_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | `NULL` | no | `isRead` on the wire is `read_at IS NOT NULL`. The frontend contract is unchanged and the "when" comes free. |
| `context` | `JSONB` | yes | `NULL` | no | **RECOMMENDATION (OQ-89/OQ-91).** Structured ids the rendered sentence deliberately omits. Never returned to the client, never rendered. Interface below. |

There is no `is_read BOOLEAN` (canon §1.4) and **no `tab` column**: the tabs are a
projection of `reason`, so a notification can never disagree with the tab it lands in
(`src/lib/notifications.ts:4-6`).

#### `notifications.context` — the JSONB structure, one variant per notification type

**RECOMMENDATION, not an existing requirement.** The frontend has no `payload` field:
`title` and `body` are pre-rendered and that contract must not change
(`src/types/collab.ts:101-113`). This column exists for the same reason
`audit_events.context` does — coalescing (OQ-91) needs to know *which comment* produced a
row, and the unbuilt `assigned` / `watch` / `system` producers (OQ-89) need somewhere to
put ids without polluting the sentence. It is **discriminated on `kind`, matching
`reason` one-for-one, and contains no `any`** (C-05).

```ts
import type { WorkspaceRole } from "./permission";

/** notifications.context. Never returned by any endpoint; investigation and
 *  coalescing only. `kind` always equals the row's `reason`. */
export type NotificationContext =
  | {
      readonly kind: "mention";
      /** The comment whose body named the recipient. */
      readonly commentId: string;
      /** Root of the thread; equal to `commentId` when the comment is a root. */
      readonly rootCommentId: string;
      /** `refKey` of the target, as the frontend stores it. */
      readonly targetKey: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "comment";
      readonly commentId: string;
      readonly rootCommentId: string;
      readonly targetKey: string;
      /** Why this person is here: they follow the target. */
      readonly viaWatchSince: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "assigned";
      readonly boardId: string;
      readonly rowId: string;
      /** The user-typed column the assignee lens resolved to (OQ-48). */
      readonly columnId: string;
      readonly displayId: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "watch";
      readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly boardId: string | null;
      readonly rowId: string | null;
      /** What changed on the watched thing (OQ-88). */
      readonly trigger: "status" | "due" | "document_saved";
      /** Set for `status` and `due`; the column the lens resolved to. */
      readonly columnId: string | null;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "system";
      readonly notice: SystemNotice;
    };

/** The machine-readable half of a `system` notice (OQ-89). */
export type SystemNotice =
  | { readonly code: "storage_quota"; readonly usedBytes: number; readonly totalBytes: number }
  | { readonly code: "role_changed"; readonly roleBefore: WorkspaceRole; readonly roleAfter: WorkspaceRole }
  | { readonly code: "membership_removed"; readonly workspaceName: string }
  | { readonly code: "deadline"; readonly boardId: string; readonly rowId: string; readonly dueDate: string };
```

`SystemNotice.deadline.dueDate` is a **date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` string** and must never be
converted through UTC (C-04, `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24`). "Deadline tomorrow" is a square
on a calendar, not an instant.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | A deleted tenant leaves no inboxes behind. |
| `recipient_id` | `users(id)` | `CASCADE` | An inbox belongs to exactly one person and is readable by nobody else. |
| `actor_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | The actor's name is rendered into `title`, but the row still joins to `users` for the avatar and accent colour. Users are soft-deactivated (T-01), so this never fires in normal operation. |
| `target_node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | An inbox must not outlive the resource it names — the stale label is the leak (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:245-252`). |
| `target_board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same. |
| `target_row_id` | `board_rows(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same. |

**No foreign key to `comments`.** Deleting a comment must not delete the notification that
announced it; the notification is a statement about the past. The link is carried in
`context.commentId`, deliberately without referential integrity.

**Unique Constraints** — **none.** Being notified twice is two facts, not a violation.
Deduplication is a *coalescing* decision (OQ-91), not a constraint: within a short window a
second `comment` notification for the same `(recipient_id, reason, target, actor_id)`
**updates the existing unread row's `created_at` and `body`** instead of inserting.
**`mention` is never coalesced** — being named twice is two distinct asks.

**Check Constraints**

```sql
-- All five target columns are present together, or absent together.
CHECK (num_nonnulls(target_kind, target_node_id, target_label) IN (0, 3))
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_row_id   IS NOT NULL))
CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_board_id IS NOT NULL))
-- Only a system notice may route nowhere (src/types/collab.ts:109-110).
CHECK (reason = 'system' OR target_node_id IS NOT NULL)
CHECK (read_at IS NULL OR read_at >= created_at)
CHECK (context IS NULL OR context->>'kind' = reason::text)
CHECK (length(title) > 0)
```

The last-but-one check is what keeps the JSONB honest: a `context` whose `kind` disagrees
with the row's `reason` is the exact drift a JSONB column invites, and it is one line to
forbid.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `notifications_inbox_idx (recipient_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)` | E-129 with **no** `reason` filter — the **All** tab. Also the keyset cursor (§6.3). |
| `notifications_reason_idx (recipient_id, reason, created_at DESC, id DESC)` | E-129 with `reason` — the **Mentions**, **Assigned** and **Following** tabs. |
| `notifications_unread_idx (recipient_id, reason) WHERE read_at IS NULL` | E-132 `unread-count` (total and per-reason), and E-131 `read-all` collecting the caller's unread ids. Partial, so it stays small as read history grows. |
| `notifications_coalesce_idx (recipient_id, reason, target_node_id, target_row_id, actor_id) WHERE read_at IS NULL` | The coalescing probe on insert (OQ-91). **RECOMMENDATION** — build it only with the coalescing rule. |
| `notifications_target_idx (target_node_id) WHERE target_node_id IS NOT NULL` | Backs the `nodes` cascade, and the server-side visibility filter that drops items for nodes the reader can no longer see. |

**Relationships**

- **N-1** to `users` twice — `recipient_id` (the inbox) and `actor_id` (who caused it).
- **N-1** to `nodes`, `boards`, `board_rows` — the decomposed target, all nullable.
- **N-1** to `workspaces`.
- **1-N from one event**: one comment produces *N* notification rows, one per recipient.
  There is no shared "event" row; fan-out on write is the model, and it is what makes the
  read path a single-table index scan on `(recipient_id, …)`.

#### The four frontend tabs, and exactly which query serves each

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** The tabs are a projection of `reason`
(`src/lib/notifications.ts:7-13`, `NOTIFICATION_TABS` at `:20-25`). The API filters by
`reason` and **never** by tab name — the mapping stays in the frontend (OQ-90), so the
projection cannot drift server-side.

| Tab (`NotificationTab`) | Label | Reasons | Request | Index used | `WHERE` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | All | *(no filter)* | `GET /me/notifications?cursor=&limit=` | `notifications_inbox_idx` | `recipient_id = $me` |
| `mentions` | Mentions | `mention` | `GET /me/notifications?reason=mention&cursor=&limit=` | `notifications_reason_idx` | `recipient_id = $me AND reason = 'mention'` |
| `assigned` | Assigned | `assigned` | `GET /me/notifications?reason=assigned&cursor=&limit=` | `notifications_reason_idx` | `recipient_id = $me AND reason = 'assigned'` |
| `following` | Following | `watch`, `comment` | `GET /me/notifications?reason=watch&reason=comment&cursor=&limit=` | `notifications_reason_idx` | `recipient_id = $me AND reason IN ('watch','comment')` |

**`reason` is a repeatable query parameter, OR-combined** — **RECOMMENDATION**, because
`following` maps to a two-element set (`TAB_REASONS.following = ["watch", "comment"]`,
`src/lib/notifications.ts:12`) and canon's E-129 signature (`?reason=`) does not say how a
set is expressed. Repeating the parameter avoids inventing a comma-splitting rule that
would then need escaping. An unknown `reason` value is `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), not a
silent empty page.

**Ordering is `created_at DESC, id DESC` on every tab** (`newestFirst`,
`src/services/notification-service.ts:24-26`).

**The badges.** `unreadByTab` computes all four counts in one pass over the loaded inbox
(`src/lib/notifications.ts:44-62`), which makes the badge *"unread among the ones we
loaded"* — the exact drift OQ-91 names. E-132 fixes it server-side:

```ts
/** E-132. Server-computed, so the bell badge is not a count of what happened to load. */
interface UnreadCountResponse {
  /** Total unread in this inbox — the bell badge. Equals the `all` tab's badge. */
  readonly unreadCount: number;
  /** Per-reason unread, so the four tab badges are exact without loading the inbox.
   *  The frontend sums `watch + comment` for the Following badge, using the same
   *  TAB_REASONS map it already owns. */
  readonly byReason: Readonly<Record<NotificationReason, number>>;
}
```

A single index-only scan over `notifications_unread_idx` produces every number in that
object. **RECOMMENDATION** for `byReason`; `unreadCount` is required by canon's E-132.

`NotificationPage` (E-129, E-130, E-131) is `{ items, nextCursor, unreadCount }` —
canon §3.21 — so every mutation of read state returns a fresh, authoritative badge.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-129 | `GET /me/notifications?reason=&cursor=&limit=` | session | Per the table above. |
| E-130 | `POST /me/notifications/read` | session | **Ids outside the caller's own inbox are ignored, not applied** (`src/services/notification-service.ts:43-48`) — not a 403, not a 404. Returns `NotificationPage`. |
| E-131 | `POST /me/notifications/read-all` | session | Scoped server-side to the caller. |
| E-132 | `GET /me/notifications/unread-count` | session | |
| E-120 | `POST /comments` | `comment.create` | The only wired producer today. |

**Transaction — the comment fan-out, exactly** (`src/services/comment-service.ts:223-250`).
Three rules to preserve verbatim:

```
mentioned := set(comment.mentioned_user_ids) − { comment.author_id }
for each id in mentioned                                → INSERT (reason='mention')
for each id in watchersOf(target) − { comment.author_id }:
    if id ∈ mentioned: continue                         → hears about it exactly once
    else                                                → INSERT (reason='comment')
```

1. **The author is never notified** — excluded from both loops.
2. **A mentioned watcher gets only the `mention`**, never both.
3. The author's **auto-watch runs before the fan-out**, so it cannot self-notify.

All of it is in the E-120 transaction. **RT-03 `notification.created` is published after
commit and only to the row's `recipient_id`** — the frontend already drops frames for
anyone else (`src/store/notification-store.ts:112`), but the server must not send them at
all (canon §7.1).

**Errors** — `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` (404) only when a single notification is addressed;
E-130 silently ignores foreign ids. `RATE_LIMITED` (429) on the read endpoints.

**Realtime** — RT-03 `notification.created` (recipient only); RT-04 `notification.read`
carrying **only the ids actually scoped to that recipient**, so a client cannot learn that
an id it guessed exists.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-89) — nothing emits `assigned`, `watch` or `system` notifications.**
> **Evidence** — all three reasons exist in the enum (`src/types/collab.ts:97`), own tabs
> (`src/lib/notifications.ts:11-12`) and have seed rows (`src/mock/collab.ts:189-235`), but
> no code path emits one; the board's cell-edit path writes an activity entry
> (`src/services/board-service.ts:531`) and no notification. The single `system` seed is
> attributed to a real colleague (`src/mock/collab.ts:226-235`), which is wrong for a
> machine notice, and `AppNotification.actor` is non-nullable.
> **Recommendation** — (a) `assigned`: when the **assignee-lens** user column
> (`src/lib/my-work.ts:57-67`, OQ-48) gains a user id, emit one row per newly added
> assignee, excluding the actor; emit nothing on removal. (b) `watch`: see OQ-88.
> (c) `system`: reserve a synthetic actor row in `users` (`usr_system`, name "NexDrop", the
> workspace's own avatar) so the non-nullable contract holds without attributing machine
> notices to a colleague. Note that a `system` notice lands in **All only**, because
> `system` is in no other tab's reason list — so a deadline reminder should be emitted as
> `assigned`, not `system`, or it will never be seen where the work is.
> **Impact if wrong** — the Assigned and Following tabs are permanently empty in production
> while the fixtures show them populated, which reads as a regression; or every machine
> notice appears to come from a random teammate.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-91) — retention, coalescing and paging.**
> **Evidence** — `emit` creates one row per recipient per event with no coalescing
> (`src/services/notification-service.ts:88-109`) and the inbox is unpaginated
> (`:28-33`). Ten comments on a watched record produce ten rows for every watcher.
> **Recommendation** — cursor-page at 50 (canon §6.3); coalesce as described above with a
> window of 15 minutes, never for `mention`; purge **read** notifications after 90 days,
> never an unread one. Store `context` so the coalescing probe can tell "another comment on
> the same thread" from "a different thread".
> **Impact if wrong** — a busy thread makes the inbox unusable and the bell badge
> meaningless. Retrofitting coalescing after users have unread history is messy, because
> the rows to merge are already distinct facts on screen.

### Table: `node_favorites`

Canon T-07. The brief calls this `favorites`; the canonical name is `node_favorites`.

**Purpose** — One person starring one node (`CO-FAV-32`). Favouriting is **per user**, not
a flag on the node, so two people cannot fight over one star (OQ-07, position taken in
canon §8.8). The Favorites page adds no second list: it groups what the tree already
knows, *"which is why un-starring here updates the sidebar and the drive grid in the same
frame"* (`src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:16-22`).

**Who creates a record** — `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` (E-028), from the star button
(`src/components/shared/favorite-star.tsx:55-72`), the drive toolbar
(`src/components/drive/drive-toolbar.tsx:81`) and the file table
(`src/components/files/file-table.tsx:147-148`). The user is the session user.

**Lifetime** — **Hard delete.** `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` (E-029) removes the row.
Cascades from `users` and `nodes`. **Trashing a node keeps the row**, so restoring it
restores the star; E-033 filters trashed nodes out of the response, matching
`isVisible` at `src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:35-36`.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | C-01. |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | Whose star. Session user only. |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | The starred node — any of the five `NodeKind` values. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | When it was starred. Not currently rendered; it is the only way to ever offer "recently starred" without a migration. |

No `workspace_id`: the node carries it, and a favourite cannot exist without its node.

No JSONB column.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | `users(id)` | `CASCADE` | Private to one person; nothing is lost by removing it with them. |
| `node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | A star on a purged node is unroutable, and the row would keep no useful information — unlike a comment, it carries no content. |

**Unique Constraints**

```sql
UNIQUE (user_id, node_id)
```

E-028 is an upsert against this constraint (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`), so starring twice
is a no-op and both E-028 and E-029 are idempotent — which is what lets the frontend's
optimistic toggle (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:454-470`) retry safely.

**Check Constraints** — none. Every `NodeKind` is starrable: the Favorites page groups all
five (`GROUP_ORDER`, `src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:24`), so there is no
kind to exclude.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| The `UNIQUE` index `(user_id, node_id)` | E-033 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/favorites` (leading `user_id`), the E-028 conflict target, the E-029 delete, and the `isFavorite` projection when reading a subtree for one viewer (`user_id = $me AND node_id = ANY($ids)`). |
| `node_favorites_node_idx (node_id)` | Backs the `nodes` cascade. Without it, deleting a project with 400 descendants sequential-scans this table 400 times. |

**Relationships**

- **N-N** between `users` and `nodes`, with no edge attributes beyond `created_at`.
- **N-1** to `users`; **N-1** to `nodes`.

`DriveNode.isFavorite` (`src/types/node.ts:58`) is a **DERIVED** boolean on the wire —
`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM node_favorites WHERE user_id = $me AND node_id = n.id)` — computed
per viewer, never stored on `nodes`. Two viewers reading the same node get different
values for the same field, which is exactly the point.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-028 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` | visibility | `204`. Idempotent. |
| E-029 | `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` | visibility | `204`. Idempotent. |
| E-033 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/favorites` | membership | `DriveNode[]`, pruned by visibility and excluding trashed nodes and archived pages. |
| E-020 / E-022 / E-023 | tree and node reads | visibility | Project `isFavorite` for the calling viewer. |

The permission is **visibility, not `node.rename` or any write key**: starring changes
nothing about the node and is invisible to everyone else, so a Viewer may star what a
Viewer may see.

**Errors** — `NODE_NOT_FOUND` (404) — which is also the answer when the caller may not see
the node, per canon §4.2.

**Realtime** — none. A favourite is private to one person; a second tab converges on its
next tree read. Emitting RT-11 `node.changed` for a star would broadcast one person's
private list to every subscriber on that node.

### Not a table: `recent_resources`

**Canon settles this** (§1.2): `recent_entries` is one of the eight explicitly-not-tables.
*"Per-device by nature; stays in `localStorage` under `nexdrop-recent`."* (OQ-96)

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — the evidence.** `src/store/recent-store.ts:9-18`:

> Recent (CO-REC-33). A least-recently-used list of the last {@link RECENT_LIMIT} places
> visited, **kept in this browser only**. It is a navigation convenience, so best-effort
> storage is the right trade: a blocked storage API costs the history, nothing else.

- Storage key `nexdrop-recent`, `RECENT_LIMIT = 10` (`src/config/app.ts:36`).
- Every read is defensive: a non-array parse, or an entry that does not shape-check, is
  **dropped rather than trusted** (`src/store/recent-store.ts:42-65`).
- Every write is wrapped in `try/catch` and failing silently is the designed behaviour
  (`:67-73`).
- `visit(ref)` is called by `useOpenEntity` on every navigation
  (`src/hooks/use-entity-navigation.ts` — *"Every open also records a Recent visit"*).

**Why it is not a table.** A Recent list answers "where was I just now?" on *this device*.
Making it server state means one write per navigation for every user — the highest-volume
write in the product — to produce a list that is wrong the moment the person switches
laptops mid-task, and that carries a denormalised label with the same leak surface as the
inbox (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:245-252`) but none of the inbox's reason to
exist. The frontend already re-resolves it against the visible tree, so no server-side
filter is being skipped.

**If it is ever promoted (RECOMMENDATION, deferred, OQ-96)** it is one table with the
shared target columns plus `visited_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `UNIQUE (user_id, target_kind,
target_node_id, target_row_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, an upsert on visit that rewrites
`visited_at`, an index on `(user_id, visited_at DESC)`, and a trigger or periodic sweep
trimming each user to `RECENT_LIMIT` rows. Nothing about the wire shape (`RecentEntry` —
`{ ref, visitedAt }`, `src/types/collab.ts:184-187`) changes, because the frontend already
speaks it. **Do not build it until product asks for cross-device Recent.**
