### Decision: attachments — one `file_assets` table plus typed join tables

**Canon §1.3.4 settles this and it is reproduced here, not re-litigated.**

**Decision.** `file_assets` (T-27) holds the bytes' metadata exactly **once**. Four typed
reference tables record *where* an asset is used: `file_nodes` (T-28, the tree),
`cell_attachments` (T-29), `comment_attachments` (T-30), `document_asset_refs` (T-31).
There is **no** polymorphic `attachments (owner_kind, owner_id)` table.

**Reasoning (one sentence).** A polymorphic `(owner_kind, owner_id)` pair cannot carry a
foreign key, and every operation that matters here — cascade on row delete, cascade on
comment delete, quota accounting for `StorageQuota.usedBytes`, orphan collection — is
exactly a foreign-key question.

**The trade-off, in full.** The alternative was real: the files fact sheet proposed a
single `asset_references (asset_id, owner_kind, owner_id, owner_slot)` table.

| Axis | `file_assets` + 4 typed join tables (CHOSEN) | One polymorphic `asset_references` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Referential integrity on the owner | An FK per table: `board_rows`, `comments`, `nodes`. The database refuses an orphan. | **None.** `owner_id` is a bare UUID that could name anything or nothing. |
| Cascade on owner delete | Free. Deleting a comment takes its `comment_attachments` rows with it. | A trigger per owner kind, or a sweep job. Every new owner kind is a new trigger somebody forgets. |
| Adding a fifth owner kind | A new table and a migration. **This is the one axis the polymorphic table wins.** | Add a value to the `CHECK`. |
| The "slot" column | Typed per table: `column_id TEXT` on cells, `block_id TEXT` on document refs, absent on comments. Each is exactly what that owner needs. | One nullable `owner_slot TEXT` that means three different things depending on `owner_kind`, and nothing at all for the fourth. |
| Quota accounting (`StorageQuota.usedBytes`) | `SUM(size_bytes)` over `file_assets` for the workspace, once. Identical either way — which is the point of separating the object from its references. | Identical. |
| Orphan collection | `file_assets` with no row in any of the four — a four-way `NOT EXISTS`, each index-backed. | One `NOT EXISTS`, marginally simpler. |
| Query "everything attached to this record" | One index scan on `cell_attachments (row_id)`. | An index scan on `(owner_kind, owner_id)` — same cost, one more equality. |
| What the frontend already believes | Three divergent shapes — `CellAttachment` (`src/types/board.ts:201-212`), `CommentAttachment` (`src/types/collab.ts:30-37`), `FileAsset` (`src/types/file.ts:7-19`) — and one explicit rule: a cell attachment *"does **not** create a file node beside the board"* (`src/types/board.ts:198-200`). The **reference** differs by owner; the **object** does not. | The same three shapes, projected from one table by a `CASE` on `owner_kind`. |

**Binaries live in object storage. Never in PostgreSQL.**

This is not a preference. No table in this schema has a `BYTEA` or `TEXT` column holding
file bytes, base64 or otherwise. `file_assets.storage_key` is an S3-compatible object key
and the bytes are behind it. The reasons, stated once so no chapter re-opens it:

- **Backups and WAL.** A 100 MB upload written to a table is 100 MB of WAL, replicated to
  every standby and rewritten into every base backup. Restore time becomes a function of
  how many screenshots people attached.
- **Streaming and range requests.** A PDF viewer and a video player both need range
  requests. Postgres has no answer to `Range: bytes=…` that is not "read the whole
  `BYTEA` into memory first".
- **Signed URLs.** `url` and `thumbnailUrl` are minted per response as short-lived signed
  URLs (OQ-75) and never accepted on write. The object store issues them; the database
  cannot.
- **The one exception is not a file.** `secrets.value_encrypted BYTEA` (T-23) holds a
  ciphertext of a few dozen bytes, not an uploaded object, and it is deliberately never
  selected on a list read.

**Consequences a writer must honour** (canon §1.3.4):

- Only `assetId` is persisted in cells, blocks and comments. `url` and `thumbnailUrl` are
  **minted per response** and never accepted on write — `src/types/board.ts:206-207`
  describes today's values as *"session URL; null once the session ends"*, which cannot be
  stored.
- `file_assets.size_bytes` is the **single source** for the workspace quota counter
  `workspaces.used_bytes`. One number cannot be computed from three blob stores (OQ-78).

---

### Table: `file_assets`

Canon T-27. Owned by the `files` module; documented here because the collaboration tables
reference it and the brief asks for `storage_key`, `mime`, `size` and `uploaded_by` in one
place.

**Purpose** — The stored object, independent of where it is referenced from
(`src/types/file.ts:6`). One row per uploaded blob. It is the only place a byte count
lives, which is what makes `StorageQuota.usedBytes` a single sum rather than a
reconciliation.

**Who creates a record** — `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` (E-111), after the client
has `PUT` the bytes to the presigned target issued by E-110. Never created by a direct
client write; the row exists only once the object has landed.

**Lifetime** — Lives while any reference to it lives. Deleted by an **orphan sweep**: a
row with no `file_nodes`, `cell_attachments`, `comment_attachments` or
`document_asset_refs` referring to it, and older than a grace window, is deleted along with
its object and `workspaces.used_bytes` is decremented in the same transaction. Hard delete;
there is no tombstone for bytes that are gone.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Also the `assetId` on the wire, and the `id` of `CellAttachment` and `CommentAttachment`. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Quota scope. |
| `name` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Original filename as uploaded. |
| `extension` | `TEXT` | no | `''` | no | Lower-cased, no dot. `''` when the name has no dot (`extensionOf`, `src/lib/node-visuals.ts:211-214`). |
| `mime_type` | `TEXT` | no | `'application/octet-stream'` | no | The **declared** type, sniffed and cross-checked on E-111 (OQ-70). |
| `size_bytes` | `BIGINT` | no | — | no | The single source for the quota counter. |
| `kind` | `file_kind` | no | — | no | `FileKind` (§2.3), derived server-side from `extension` (`src/lib/node-visuals.ts:162-209`), defaulting to `other`. |
| `storage_key` | `TEXT` | no | — | yes | The S3-compatible object key. **The bytes are here, never in this table.** |
| `thumb_key` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | Derivative object key, images only (OQ-71). |
| `checksum` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | SHA-256 of the object, recorded at E-111 for integrity and future dedupe. |
| `owner_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Who uploaded it — **the `uploaded_by` the brief asks for**, named `owner_id` because `FileAsset.owner` is the wire field (`src/types/file.ts:14`). |
| `folder_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | Destination folder for drive uploads; `NULL` for a workspace-level upload and for cell/comment attachments (`src/types/file.ts:17-18`). |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Bumped by E-115 (text content save). |

No JSONB column.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | Deleting a tenant releases its storage; the sweep deletes the objects. |
| `owner_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | The uploader is rendered in the file metadata panel (`src/lib/file-metadata.ts:9-19`, the Owner row) and must keep resolving. |
| `folder_id` | `nodes(id)` | `SET NULL` | Deleting the folder must not destroy an asset a board cell or a comment still references. The asset becomes workspace-level, exactly as `folderId: null` already means. |

**Unique Constraints** — `UNIQUE (storage_key)`. Two rows pointing at one object would let
one orphan sweep delete bytes another row still claims.

**Check Constraints**

```sql
CHECK (size_bytes > 0)                      -- FILE_EMPTY is refused before this row exists
CHECK (length(storage_key) > 0)
CHECK (extension = lower(extension))
```

The **size ceiling is not a check constraint.** Canon's position on OQ-69 is that 100 MB is
the API and storage contract and the client pre-check is served from `GET /config` (E-139)
*"so the two cannot disagree"*. A `CHECK (size_bytes <= 104857600)` would make raising the
limit a migration. E-110 validates size, extension and quota **before** issuing the
presigned target; E-111 re-validates the landed object.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `UNIQUE (storage_key)` | Idempotent E-111 completion, and the sweep's object lookup. |
| `file_assets_quota_idx (workspace_id)` | The `StorageQuota` recomputation (a reconciliation job, not a read path — `workspaces.used_bytes` is maintained transactionally, canon §1.4). |
| `file_assets_folder_idx (folder_id) WHERE folder_id IS NOT NULL` | E-113 `GET /folders/{nodeId}/files`, and the `SET NULL` on folder delete. |

**Relationships**

- **1-1** to `file_nodes` (a drive file).
- **1-N** to `cell_attachments`, `comment_attachments`, `document_asset_refs` — one object
  can be referenced from many places, which is precisely why the reference is not a column
  on the asset.
- **N-1** to `users` (`owner_id`), `workspaces`, `nodes` (`folder_id`).

**APIs that use it** — E-110 (`POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/uploads`), E-111
(`POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` — inserts the row **and** increments
`workspaces.used_bytes` in the same transaction), E-112 (abort), E-113, E-114, E-115,
E-116, and **E-117 `GET /assets/{assetId}/url`**, which is how a cell, a block or a comment
turns a stored `assetId` into a short-lived signed URL (OQ-75). E-117's permission is
*visibility on any owner*: the caller must be able to see at least one of the places the
asset is referenced from, which is a four-way `EXISTS` across the join tables.

**Errors** — `ASSET_NOT_FOUND` (404), `FILE_EMPTY` (400), `FILE_TOO_LARGE` (400),
`FILE_TYPE_REJECTED` (400), `FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` (400), `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` (404),
`UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` (422), `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` (502), `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (507).

---

### Table: `comment_attachments`

Canon T-30. `(comment_id, asset_id)`.

**Purpose** — Which stored objects are attached to which comment. Nothing else: name, MIME
type and size all live on `file_assets`, so a file attached to a comment and the same file
in the drive are one object with one size, counted once against the quota.

**Who creates a record** — `POST /comments` (E-120), in the same transaction as the
comment. The client uploads first (E-110 + E-111 with `createDriveNode: false`, canon
OQ-74) and posts the resulting `assetId`s with the comment body.

**Lifetime** — Deleted by cascade when the comment is hard-deleted, and by nothing else.
**Attachments are immutable after posting**: `commentService.edit` takes only a body
(`src/services/comment-service.ts:159-164`) and the remove button is rendered only in the
composer, never on a posted comment
(`src/components/comments/comment-attachments.tsx:9-11`, `:40`). Soft-deleting a comment
(E-122) does **not** delete these rows; the tombstone renders with `attachments: []` and
the rows are collected when the comment is purged.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | C-01. |
| `comment_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | The owning comment. |
| `asset_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | The stored object. |
| `position` | `INT` | no | `0` | no | Order the attachments were submitted in, so the chips render in the order the author added them. Densely renumbered `0..n-1` on insert. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |

No `uploaded_by`: the uploader is `file_assets.owner_id`, and duplicating it here would let
the two disagree.

No JSONB column.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `comment_id` | `comments(id)` | `CASCADE` | A reference cannot outlive the thing that holds it. This is the cascade a polymorphic table could not have. |
| `asset_id` | `file_assets(id)` | `RESTRICT` | An asset must not be deletable while a comment still shows it. Assets are removed by the orphan sweep, which checks this table first — `RESTRICT` turns a sweep bug into an error instead of a broken thumbnail. |

**Unique Constraints** — `UNIQUE (comment_id, asset_id)`. Attaching the same object twice
to one comment is a duplicate chip, not a feature.

**Check Constraints** — `CHECK (position >= 0)`.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `UNIQUE (comment_id, asset_id)` | Loading a thread's attachments — `WHERE comment_id = ANY($ids)` on E-119 and E-125, one query for the whole page rather than one per comment. |
| `comment_attachments_asset_idx (asset_id)` | The orphan sweep's `NOT EXISTS`, E-117's owner check, and the `RESTRICT` enforcement. |

**Relationships** — **N-N** between `comments` and `file_assets`, with `position` as the
edge attribute. **N-1** to each.

**APIs that use it** — E-120 (create), E-119 / E-125 (read, projected into
`Comment.attachments`), E-117 (mint a signed URL per asset), E-122 (the tombstone hides
them).

**Wire projection.** `CommentAttachment` (`src/types/collab.ts:30-37`) is assembled from
the join plus `file_assets`:

```ts
interface CommentAttachment {
  readonly id: string;          // = file_assets.id — the assetId, never the join-row id
  readonly name: string;        // file_assets.name
  readonly mimeType: string;    // file_assets.mime_type
  readonly sizeBytes: number;   // file_assets.size_bytes
  /** Short-lived signed URL, minted per response. `null` when the caller may
   *  not read the object. Never accepted on write (OQ-75). */
  readonly url: string | null;
}
```

**Security rules that carry over from the drive path and must be enforced here too:**

- The same `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and extension allow-list as every other upload. Today the
  comment path calls neither: `addFiles` calls `onAttach` directly
  (`src/components/comments/comment-composer.tsx:69-80`), bypassing `validateUpload`
  (`src/lib/file-validation.ts:28-78`) — **OQ-73**, flagged `security` in canon.
- `image/svg+xml`, `text/html` and `application/xhtml+xml` are **never served inline**
  (`NON_RENDERABLE_TYPES`, `src/lib/attachments.ts:29`): *"rendering uploaded markup in the
  app's own origin is how an upload becomes stored XSS."* The signed URL for these types
  carries `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
- A comment upload sets `createDriveNode: false` (OQ-74) — a comment attachment is never a
  drive node, so a folder does not fill with `Screenshot 2026-08-27.png`.
- Gate on **`comment.create`**, not `file.upload`: the upload is part of posting a comment.

---

### Table: `cell_attachments`

Canon T-29. `(row_id, column_id, asset_id)` + uploader + timestamp. Owned by `files`;
summarised here because it is the third owner in the attachment decision and the brief asks
for the polymorphism trade-off to be complete.

**Purpose** — A board attachment is owned by the **record**, not by the tree
(`src/types/board.ts:198-200`). This table is the indexed projection of every
`CellValue { kind: "attachment" }` in `board_rows.cells`, written in the same transaction
as the cell.

**Who creates a record** — E-066 `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells`, when the batch
writes an attachment cell. **Lifetime** — cascades from `board_rows`; a row delete takes
its attachment references, and the assets are then collected by the orphan sweep.

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | |
| `row_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | |
| `column_id` | `TEXT` | no | — | composite | The attachment column's id **inside `board_columns`**, stored as text because it is also a JSONB key in `cells`. |
| `asset_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | |
| `uploaded_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Denormalised from the session at write time, because `CellAttachment.uploadedBy` is on the wire (`src/types/board.ts:209`) and the cell JSON carries it. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `CellAttachment.createdAt`. |

**FKs** — `row_id → board_rows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (a record's evidence dies with the
record); `asset_id → file_assets(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (same reason as
`comment_attachments`); `uploaded_by → users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`. There is **no** FK on
`column_id`: canon §1.3.2 accepts that `cells` has no referential integrity on column ids
and requires the same transaction that drops a column to prune the orphans — this table is
pruned there too, by E-054.

**Unique** — `UNIQUE (row_id, column_id, asset_id)`.
**Indexes** — the unique index (serves "attachments of this record"), plus
`cell_attachments_asset_idx (asset_id)` for the orphan sweep and E-117.
**Relationships** — N-N between `board_rows` and `file_assets`, keyed additionally by
column.
**APIs** — E-066 (write), E-047 / E-061 / E-063 (read, projected into the cell), E-117.

---

### Table: `file_nodes`

Canon T-28. `node_id` (PK) → `asset_id` + `version`.

**Purpose** — A drive file is an asset that **also** has a place in the tree. This is the
1:1 side table that joins the two, and it is why `nodes` can stay one table across five
kinds (canon §1.3.1).

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | PK | The drive node. Canon T-28 makes this the primary key — the documented exception to C-01 for 1:1 side tables, shared with `config_documents` and `secret_documents`. |
| `asset_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | The stored object. |
| `version` | `INT` | no | `1` | no | Bumped by E-115 `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/file/content`. Rendered as the Version metadata row. |

**FKs** — `node_id → nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (the side table is part of the node);
`asset_id → file_assets(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (a node must never point at a deleted
object).
**Indexes** — the PK, plus `file_nodes_asset_idx (asset_id)` for the sweep and the
`RESTRICT`.
**Relationships** — **1-1** `nodes` ↔ `file_nodes`; **N-1** to `file_assets` (a saved-as
copy can share an object).
**APIs** — E-111 (when `createDriveNode: true`), E-113, E-114, E-115, E-116.

---

### `document_asset_refs` — specified in the `documents` chapter

Canon T-31. Written out in full further down this section, under
[Table: `document_asset_refs`](#table-document_asset_refs) — the table belongs to the
`files` module but its only writer is the document save path, so it is documented beside
what writes it. `(node_id, block_id, asset_id)`, unique on all three; `node_id → nodes(id)
ON DELETE CASCADE`, `asset_id → file_assets(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`. That `RESTRICT` is what
answers **OQ-72**: an image block's file cannot be deleted while the block references it.

---

### Table: `uploads`

Canon T-32.

**Purpose** — one in-flight upload, from the moment the server issues a presigned target to
the moment the bytes are accounted for. It exists because the browser `PUT`s straight to
object storage and the backend never sees the body: without a row written **before** the
presigned URL is handed out, there is no record that an upload was authorised, no way to
know a half-finished object in the bucket is garbage, and no way to charge the bytes to a
workspace quota after the fact. This table is what makes the direct-to-storage path
auditable rather than merely fast.

It has no frontend counterpart, and that is deliberate. `UploadTask` and `UploadStatus`
(`src/types/file.ts:29-47`) describe the **client's** queue — `queued`, `uploading`,
`success`, `error`, `cancelled`, plus a `progress` float the server can never observe. The
server's `state` is a different, smaller thing and the two must not be conflated.

**Who creates a record** — E-110 `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/uploads`, and nothing else.
It validates before issuing anything: size against `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (25 MB,
`src/lib/file-validation.ts:4`), extension against `ALL_ACCEPTED_EXTENSIONS` (`:14`), and the
workspace's remaining quota against `expected_size_bytes`. A request that fails validation
creates no row and issues no URL.

**How long it lives** — until completed, aborted, or expired. `expires_at` is the presigned
URL's own expiry; a row still `pending` past it is dead by definition. Completed rows are
kept for a short window as the audit trail of who uploaded what, then reaped — the durable
record of the file is `file_assets`, not this.

**How it is deleted** — by the reaper, which sweeps `expires_at < now() AND state = 'pending'`,
marks them `expired` and deletes any orphaned object from storage. E-112 aborts one
explicitly. Never deleted by a user-facing delete of the resulting file.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | The `uploadId` the client echoes back to E-111. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Which quota this is drawn against. |
| `actor_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Who authorised it. Survives into `file_assets.owner_id` on completion. |
| `storage_key` | `TEXT` | no | — | yes | The object key the presigned `PUT` targets. Server-minted, never derived from the client's file name — see Checks. |
| `file_name` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | The original name, kept for the eventual `file_assets.name`. |
| `expected_size_bytes` | `BIGINT` | no | — | no | Claimed by the client, verified against the stored object on complete. |
| `expected_mime_type` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Claimed. Not trusted — see Checks. |
| `destination_kind` | `upload_destination` | no | — | no | `drive`, `cell`, `comment`, `document`. Decides which join table E-111 writes. |
| `destination_node_id` | `UUID` | yes | — | no | Folder, document node, or null for a workspace-root drive upload. |
| `destination_row_id` | `UUID` | yes | — | no | Set for `cell`. |
| `destination_column_id` | `UUID` | yes | — | no | Set for `cell`. |
| `destination_comment_id` | `UUID` | yes | — | no | Set for `comment`. |
| `state` | `upload_state` | no | `'pending'` | no | `pending`, `completed`, `aborted`, `expired`. Four states, none of them the client's five. |
| `asset_id` | `UUID` | yes | — | no | Set by E-111. Null while pending. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `expires_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | — | no | The presigned URL's expiry, mirrored so the sweep is an index scan and not a call to storage. |
| `completed_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | yes | — | no | |

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | |
| `actor_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users deactivate rather than delete; the constraint holds the invariant. |
| `asset_id` | `file_assets(id)` | `SET NULL` | The asset outlives the upload record and may be deleted independently; losing the back-reference must not delete the audit row. |

The four `destination_*` columns carry **no** foreign keys. The destination is validated at
E-110 and again at E-111, and a folder deleted mid-upload should make the completion fail
loudly with a 404 rather than make the row un-writable at the database level.

**Unique Constraints** — `uploads_storage_key_uniq UNIQUE (storage_key)`. Two rows pointing
at one object would let one upload's completion consume the other's bytes.

**Indexes**

| Index | Type | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uploads_pkey` | btree, unique | E-111 and E-112, which address by id |
| `uploads_storage_key_uniq` | btree, unique | the uniqueness above |
| `uploads_sweep_idx (expires_at) WHERE state = 'pending'` | btree, partial | the reaper. Partial, because completed rows are the overwhelming majority and none of them is ever swept |
| `uploads_actor_idx (actor_id, state)` | btree | "what is this person uploading right now", and the per-user concurrency cap |

**Checks**

- `CHECK (expected_size_bytes > 0 AND expected_size_bytes <= 26214400)` — the 25 MB ceiling
  as a database constraint, not only as an application rule, so no future code path can
  issue a URL for more.
- `CHECK (expires_at > created_at)`.
- `CHECK ((state = 'completed') = (asset_id IS NOT NULL))` — a completed upload has an
  asset; a pending one does not. This is the invariant every consumer of the table assumes.
- `CHECK (destination_kind <> 'cell' OR (destination_row_id IS NOT NULL AND destination_column_id IS NOT NULL))`
  and the equivalent for `comment` and `document`.

**MIME and extension are validated, not trusted.** The extension check at E-110 is a
pre-filter only. On E-111 the server sniffs the stored object's leading bytes and compares
them to `expected_mime_type`; a mismatch aborts the upload and deletes the object. An
extension alone never decides what a file is — a `.png` whose magic bytes say otherwise is
rejected, and `storage_key` is server-minted precisely so a crafted file name can never
influence where bytes land.

**Delete Behavior** — hard delete by the reaper. Not soft-deleted; the durable record is
`file_assets` plus the `audit_events` row E-111 writes.

**Relationships** — N-1 to `workspaces` and `users`; 0-1 to `file_assets`. One `uploads` row
becomes at most one `file_assets` row, and then at most one row in exactly one of
`file_nodes`, `cell_attachments`, `comment_attachments` or `document_asset_refs`, chosen by
`destination_kind`.

**APIs that use it** — E-110 creates, E-111 `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` finalises
(verifies the object, creates `file_assets`, writes the destination join row and increments
`workspaces.used_bytes`, all in one transaction), E-112 `DELETE /uploads/{uploadId}` aborts.
The quota increment belongs to E-111 and to nothing else: counting the bytes at E-110 would
charge for uploads that never happened.

---

### Table: `row_activity`

Canon T-14. The brief calls this `activity_logs`; the canonical name is `row_activity`.

**Purpose** — One record's history (`SY-ACT-40`), rendered at write time. **One call is one
entry however many fields it touched** — the PRD edge case requires exactly this:
*"Thay đổi nhiều trường cùng lúc: Gộp chung vào 1 record log duy nhất"*. So *"changed
Status and Due Date"* is one line in the drawer timeline with two changes under it, never
two lines racing for the same second (`src/services/board-service.ts:156-161`).

**Who creates a record** — Never a client. Written by the endpoint performing the write,
inside its transaction: E-062 and E-064 (`created`), E-066 and E-074 (`updated`), E-075
(`archived` / `restored`), E-077 (`moved`), E-085 (`imported`), E-120 (`commented`).
There is **no** `POST /activity` and no chapter may add one.

**Lifetime** — Retained for the life of the record. Cascades from `board_rows`, so
deleting a record deletes its history; **archiving does not** (OQ-52). No soft delete: an
entry the user can neither edit nor remove has nothing to tombstone.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | C-01. |
| `board_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Denormalised from the row, so the E-070 route (`/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/activity`) validates board and row in one predicate. |
| `row_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | The record. |
| `kind` | `activity_kind` | no | — | no | `ActivityKind` (§2.5): `created`, `updated`, `commented`, `attached`, `archived`, `restored`, `imported`, `moved`. |
| `actor_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Session user. |
| `summary` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Human sentence **fragment**, rendered server-side: `changed Status`, `changed 3 fields`, `created TASK-001`, `commented on TASK-004`, `moved TASK-011 from Frontend Sprint`. |
| `changes` | `JSONB` | no | `'[]'` | no | `FieldChange[]` — already rendered to the text the column displays. Interface below. |
| `raw_changes` | `JSONB` | yes | `NULL` | no | Typed `CellValue` before/after per column id. **Never returned by any endpoint** (OQ-51). Interface below. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Sort key, newest first. |

#### `row_activity.changes` — the JSONB structure

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** The payload shape is `FieldChange[]` and nothing else.
`src/lib/activity.ts:6-13` is explicit: *"Nothing here ever reaches for a payload, because
there is no payload to reach for: the user is never shown a serialised audit blob."*

```ts
/** row_activity.changes. Already rendered to the text the column displays. */
interface FieldChange {
  /** The column's name **at the time of the write**, not resolved live. */
  readonly columnName: string;
  /** Rendered `from`. `""` means empty; the UI renders "—". */
  readonly from: string;
  /** Rendered `to`. */
  readonly to: string;
}

type RowActivityChanges = readonly FieldChange[];
```

**`from` and `to` are rendered server-side at write time**, by the equivalent of
`describeEdits` (`src/services/board-service.ts:194-217`) with a `CellContext` that
resolves user ids to names and relation row ids to display ids (`:183-192`). That is the
only moment the column definition, its select options and the directory are all in hand —
a value rendered later against a renamed option would rewrite history.

A field whose rendered `from` equals its rendered `to` is **not recorded** (`:210`), so a
no-op write produces an entry with zero changes rather than a false one. `editSummary`
(`:221-225`): zero changes → the fallback sentence; one → `` `changed ${columnName}` ``;
more → `` `changed ${n} fields` ``.

#### `row_activity.raw_changes` — the JSONB structure

**RECOMMENDATION (OQ-51), position taken in canon §8.8:** *"Store both: rendered `changes`
(returned) and internal `raw_changes` (never returned)."*

```ts
import type { CellValue } from "./board";   // the discriminated union, never `any`

/** row_activity.raw_changes. Internal. The only path to a record-level rollback. */
interface RawFieldChange {
  readonly columnId: string;
  /** Absent-before is `null`; an empty cell is an empty `CellValue` of the
   *  column's kind, which is what `emptyCellFor` writes — the two are different. */
  readonly from: CellValue | null;
  readonly to: CellValue | null;
}

type RowActivityRawChanges = readonly RawFieldChange[];
```

`raw_changes` is `NULL` for entries that carry no field diff (`created`, `commented`,
`imported`, `moved`), and never returned by E-070.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board_id` | `boards(id)` | `CASCADE` | Redundant with the row cascade; declared so the guarantee is a constraint. |
| `row_id` | `board_rows(id)` | `CASCADE` | The history is the record's. A record that no longer exists has no drawer to render its timeline in, and rows are hard-deleted (E-065). |
| `actor_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | *"Thanh changed Status: Doing → Done"* must keep naming Thanh. Users are soft-deactivated (T-01). |

**Unique Constraints** — none. Two writes in the same second are two entries, and that is
the point of `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` being the sort key.

**Check Constraints**

```sql
CHECK (jsonb_typeof(changes) = 'array')
CHECK (raw_changes IS NULL OR jsonb_typeof(raw_changes) = 'array')
CHECK (length(summary) > 0)
```

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `row_activity_row_idx (row_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)` | E-070 `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/activity?cursor=&limit=` — the drawer timeline, keyset-paged. |
| `row_activity_actor_idx (board_id, actor_id, created_at DESC)` | **RECOMMENDATION** — only build it when a "what did this person do on this board" surface exists. It has no query today. |

The second row is listed to be explicit that it is **not** being created: canon's rule is
that every index names the query it serves, and this one names a query that does not exist
yet.

**Relationships**

- **N-1** to `board_rows`, `boards`, `users`.
- **No** relationship to `comments`. A `commented` entry records *that* a comment was
  posted, in the record's own language; it does not link to the comment row. Deleting the
  comment must not rewrite the record's history.
- **No** relationship to `audit_events`. See the next section.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-070 | `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/activity?cursor=&limit=` | visibility | `ActivityPage` = `{ items: ActivityEntry[], nextCursor }` (§6.3 — no `total`). Newest first. |

**The synthesised `created` entry.** `listActivity` returns stored entries **plus** a
`created` entry built from `row.createdAt` / `row.createdBy`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:921-943`). The backend writes a real `created` row at
E-062 instead, so the synthesis disappears; E-070 must still guarantee that the oldest
entry of every record is a `created` one, back-filled for rows that predate the table.

**A correction the backend must NOT reproduce.** `noteActivity`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:911-918`) silently skips the entry when the board is not
loaded in the current tab, and writes nothing at all for a document target. Its own comment
says a real backend writes it server-side regardless (`:906-910`). So: **always** write the
`commented` entry for a row target, inside the E-120 transaction. **Never** write row
activity for a document target — a page's history is version history (E-095), not a row
stream.

**Transaction** — every entry is inserted in the same transaction as the write it
describes. A rollback takes the entry with it, which is the correct behaviour for a
"what happened to this record" log: nothing happened.

**Realtime** — none of its own. The row frame that accompanies the write (RT-06 `row.created`,
RT-07 `row.updated`, RT-08 `row.archived`) is the signal; a client with the drawer open
refetches E-070. Adding an `activity.created` frame would carry rendered cell text across a
permission boundary, which canon §7.2 forbids on principle.

**Errors** — `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` (404), `ROW_NOT_FOUND` (404), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403).

---

### Table: `audit_events`

Canon T-36. The brief calls this `audit_logs`; the canonical name is `audit_events`.

**Purpose** — The workspace security trail (`SY-AUD-41`). Who did what, from where, to
what, and whether it was allowed. It is **evidence**, not a feed: timestamps are absolute,
targets are human labels, details are sentences, and the whole table is append-only by
construction (`src/types/audit.ts:4-10`).

**Who creates a record** — Never a client. **There is no write endpoint for the audit log,
and no chapter may add one** (canon §3.23). Rows are written by the endpoint performing the
action, inside its transaction. The service surface is two calls — `record` and `list` —
*"so no screen can grow an Edit button that quietly works"*
(`src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20`).

**Lifetime** — Append-only and never updated. Purged only by a retention sweep running as
a separate, privileged role (OQ-27). Cascades from `workspaces`.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Opaque, server-minted. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Every read is workspace-scoped and gated on `workspace.audit.view`. |
| `at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | **Absolute, never relative** — *"an audit row is evidence"* (`src/lib/audit.ts:51-54`). Rendered as `26 Aug 2026 · 16:20`. |
| `module` | `audit_module` | no | — | no | The 8 `PermissionModule` values plus `system` (§2.2). |
| `action` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | **Free-form dotted string, constrained by convention to be a `PermissionKey` where one governs the event.** `auditActionLabel` looks it up in the catalogue and otherwise humanises the tail after the first dot: `system.retention.sweep` → *"Retention sweep"* (`src/lib/audit.ts:42-49`). |
| `actor_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | From the session. **Never from the request body** (C-09). |
| `actor_name` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Denormalised, so the row still reads if the user record ever changes or goes. |
| `actor_email` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Same. Also what `search` matches on. |
| `ip` | `INET` | no | — | no | **Stamped by the backend off the socket. The client never sends one** (`src/services/audit-service.ts:276-285`). |
| `severity` | `audit_severity` | no | — | no | `info` / `warn` / `error`. **Independent of `outcome`** — see the policy table. |
| `target` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | The **human label** of the thing acted on. *Never an id, never a payload* (`src/types/audit.ts:35-36`). `NULL` for events with no subject (a session start). |
| `detail` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | **One sentence, written by the service.** *"The UI never renders a raw audit payload"* (`:37-38`). |
| `outcome` | `audit_outcome` | no | `'allowed'` | no | `allowed` / `denied`. |
| `context` | `JSONB` | yes | `NULL` | no | Structured ids the sentence deliberately omits. **Never returned by any endpoint.** Interface below. |

#### `audit_events.context` — the JSONB structure

**RECOMMENDATION (OQ-25).** The frontend never renders it; it exists so an investigation
can reach the ids the human sentence omits. Discriminated on `kind`, no `any`:

```ts
import type { PermissionKey, WorkspaceRole } from "./permission";

/** audit_events.context. Never rendered, never returned. Investigation only. */
export type AuditContext =
  | { readonly kind: "node"; readonly nodeId: string;
      /** Root → node at the time of the action. */
      readonly ancestorIds: readonly string[] }
  | { readonly kind: "access_rule"; readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly subject:
        | { readonly kind: "user"; readonly userId: string }
        | { readonly kind: "role"; readonly role: WorkspaceRole };
      readonly roleBefore: WorkspaceRole | null;
      readonly roleAfter: WorkspaceRole | null }
  | { readonly kind: "membership"; readonly targetUserId: string;
      readonly roleBefore: WorkspaceRole | null;
      readonly roleAfter: WorkspaceRole | null }
  | { readonly kind: "secret"; readonly nodeId: string; readonly secretId: string;
      /** Key name only. The value never enters the audit trail. */
      readonly secretKey: string }
  | { readonly kind: "bulk"; readonly boardId: string;
      readonly requested: number; readonly applied: number; readonly skipped: number }
  | { readonly kind: "denial"; readonly permissionKey: PermissionKey;
      /** Which gate refused. Never returned to the caller. */
      readonly gate: "membership" | "visibility" | "capability" | "trashed" | "frozen" | "locked" }
  | { readonly kind: "comment"; readonly commentId: string; readonly targetNodeId: string;
      readonly wasAuthor: boolean }
  | { readonly kind: "system"; readonly job: string };
```

**The invariant the frontend forces on this column: no secret value, no cell value, no
block content and no file bytes may ever be written into `detail` or `context`.**
`target` is a label; `detail` is a sentence (`src/types/audit.ts:35-38`).

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | The trail is the tenant's; deleting the tenant deletes it. |
| `actor_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | **The trail must never lose its actor.** `actor_name` and `actor_email` are denormalised as a second line of defence, but `RESTRICT` makes an attempt to erase a user who has audit history fail loudly instead of quietly orphaning evidence. |

**No FK to `nodes`, `boards`, `board_rows` or `comments`.** Deliberate, and the opposite of
every other table in this chapter: an audit row must survive the deletion of what it
describes. *"Moved to Trash with 2 items under it"* is exactly the row you need after the
purge. That is why `target` is a denormalised label and the ids live in `context` without
referential integrity.

**Unique Constraints** — none. Two identical actions a second apart are two events.

**Check Constraints**

```sql
CHECK (length(action) > 0 AND action LIKE '%.%')      -- dotted key, always
CHECK (length(actor_name) > 0)
CHECK (context IS NULL OR jsonb_typeof(context) = 'object')
```

There is **no** check tying `severity` to `outcome`. The seed proves they are independent:
`file.upload` appears with `severity: 'error'` and `outcome: 'allowed'`
(`src/services/audit-service.ts:107-115`) — an allowed action that failed technically.

**Append-only, enforced in the database and not only in the service:**

```sql
-- documentation only
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_events FROM app_user;
GRANT  INSERT, SELECT  ON audit_events TO   app_user;
-- plus a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that RAISEs, so a future migration
-- cannot quietly re-grant it. The retention sweep runs as a different role.
```

The page states the promise where somebody would look for the button:
*"Append-only · entries cannot be edited or deleted"*
(`src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:58-62`). A promise the database does not enforce is a
comment.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `audit_events_page_idx (workspace_id, at DESC, id DESC)` | E-136 with no filters, and the keyset cursor. Offset paging cannot survive a live-appending log. |
| `audit_events_module_idx (workspace_id, module, at DESC, id DESC)` | E-136 `?module=` — the module dropdown. |
| `audit_events_actor_idx (workspace_id, actor_id, at DESC, id DESC)` | E-136 `?actorId=`. |
| `audit_events_severity_idx (workspace_id, severity, at DESC, id DESC)` | E-136 `?severity=`, and the `bySeverity` facet counts. |
| `audit_events_search_idx GIN (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(target,'') \|\| ' ' \|\| coalesce(detail,'') \|\| ' ' \|\| action \|\| ' ' \|\| actor_name \|\| ' ' \|\| host(ip)))` | E-136 `?search=`. The frontend's `matchesSearch` spans **actor name, raw action, humanised action label, target, detail and IP** (`src/lib/audit.ts:67-79`), and the tests assert a partial-IP hit — so `ip` must be in the index. |
| `audit_events_retention_idx (workspace_id, at) WHERE severity <> 'error' AND outcome = 'allowed'` | The retention sweep (OQ-27), which must never touch a denial or an error. |

**Filters are AND-combined; `"all"` and absent are equivalent**
(`src/services/audit-service.ts:306-311`).

**Relationships**

- **N-1** to `workspaces` and `users`.
- **Deliberately unrelated to everything else.** The lack of foreign keys to the subjects
  is the design, not an omission.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-136 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit?module=&severity=&actorId=&search=&from=&to=&cursor=&limit=` | `workspace.audit.view` | `AuditPage` = `{ events, total, bySeverity, nextCursor }`. Default `limit` = `AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE = 40` (`src/config/app.ts:56-57`). |
| E-137 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit/export` | `workspace.audit.view` | CSV stream. **The export is itself audited at `warn`** (OQ-27). |

**`total` and `bySeverity` are facets over the WHOLE filtered set, not the page.**
`src/services/audit-service.ts:320-322` counts `matched`, not `matched.slice(0, limit)`,
and `src/types/audit.ts:52-53` says so in a comment: *"Matches before the limit was
applied, so the table can say 'of N'."* Two extra aggregate queries per request, both
served by the filter indexes above.

Denied reads are themselves audited: the seed carries a refused `workspace.audit.view`
(`src/services/audit-service.ts:228-237`) — **attempting to read the audit log is an
audited event.**

**Severity policy, as practised** (`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:225-226`, seed data,
`tests/audit.test.ts:119-130`):

| Situation | Severity | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any denial | `error` (the default when `outcome = 'denied'`) | `denied` |
| Privileged read of plaintext (`secret.reveal`, allowed) | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Any access-rule write (`workspace.permission.manage`) | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Membership or role change (`workspace.member.manage`) | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Bulk or irreversible destruction (`row.delete`, `board.column.delete`, `node.delete`) | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Routine allowed action | `info` | `allowed` |
| Technical failure of an allowed action | `error` | `allowed` |

**Transactionality — two different rules, and getting them wrong loses the evidence:**

- **Allowed actions:** `INSERT` the audit row in the **same transaction** as the mutation,
  so a rollback takes the row with it. An audit row for a write that did not happen is
  worse than none.
- **Refusals:** write on an **autonomous connection, outside the aborted transaction**,
  or the denial record rolls back with the refusal it was recording. This is the whole
  point of `src/services/devtools-service.ts:341-345`: *"Recorded even when refused: a
  denied attempt is worth auditing"*, and `:358-361`: *"A refusal nobody can see is not a
  control."*

**Realtime** — none, and none should be added. An audit frame would push security events to
whoever happens to be connected; the log is read deliberately, through a gated endpoint.

**Errors** — `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403) with the copy *"The audit log is open to workspace
admins"* / *"Your role does not hold 'Read the audit log'."*; `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404)
for a workspace the caller is not a member of.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-27) — audit retention and export.**
> **Evidence** — there is no audit retention period anywhere in the frontend.
> `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS = 30` (`src/config/app.ts:41-42`) is the **trash** window and is
> unrelated; the only retention signal in the audit domain is the seeded
> `system.retention.sweep` event, whose `target` is `"Trash"`
> (`src/services/audit-service.ts:187-196`) — it describes the trash sweep, not an audit
> sweep. Meanwhile the audit page asserts permanence in writing.
> **Recommendation** — retain 12 months on paid plans and 90 days on `free`; **never purge
> a row with `severity = 'error'` or `outcome = 'denied'` before 24 months**; expose E-137
> as a CSV export gated on `workspace.audit.view` and audit the export itself at `warn`.
> Whatever is chosen must be stated in-product, because the page currently promises
> permanence.
> **Impact if wrong** — too short and a breach investigation has no trail; too long and a
> retention sweep that deletes rows contradicts the "cannot be deleted" promise the UI
> makes on screen.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-25) — which actions must emit an audit row?**
> **Evidence** — the fixture trail defines 19 `(module, action)` pairs
> (`src/services/audit-service.ts:44-248`) but only **two** emitters are wired in `src/`:
> access-rule writes (`src/store/permission-store.ts:71-78`, `:99-106`) and secret
> reveal/rotate (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:382-394`). Node deletes, archives,
> member changes, imports, exports and column deletes all appear in the seed and none of
> them call `auditService.record`.
> **Recommendation** — audit **every** action whose permission key is held only from
> `manager` or `admin` (29 of the 39), plus `node.share`, plus **every denial of any key**.
> Do **not** audit ordinary `row.update` / `comment.create` traffic at `info`: `row_activity`
> already covers it, and mixing the two makes the log unreadable at volume.
> **Impact if wrong** — under-auditing loses the trail for exactly the actions the log
> exists for; over-auditing buries 9 error rows in 88,000 info rows and the severity filter
> stops being useful.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-26) — which privileged reads must themselves be audited?**
> **Evidence** — the frontend audits a *refused* `workspace.audit.view` but not a
> successful one, and `src/components/workspace/workspace-restricted-tab.tsx:56-60`
> promises that *"granting yourself access is recorded in the audit log"* — the grant is,
> the **listing** of restricted folders is not.
> **Recommendation** — audit these at `warn`: a successful `workspace.audit.view` (E-136),
> the restricted-node recovery list (E-046), any node's access list (E-040), the audit
> export (E-137), and every `secret.reveal` (E-103, already done).
> **Impact if wrong** — an admin can enumerate every restricted folder in the workspace and
> leave no trace, which undercuts the justification the recovery console is built on.

---

### `row_activity` vs `audit_events` — why these are two tables

They look similar — an actor, a timestamp, a thing acted on, a sentence — and merging them
is the most tempting simplification in this schema. It is wrong, for six independent
reasons. Any one of them would be enough.

**1. They answer different questions for different people.**
`row_activity` answers *"what happened to TASK-042?"* and is read by whoever can see the
record — a Viewer included, through E-070 with plain visibility. `audit_events` answers
*"who did something sensitive in this workspace, and were they allowed to?"* and is read
only by a holder of `workspace.audit.view` (E-136), which lands at **admin**. One table
would mean either exposing security events to every Viewer or hiding record history behind
an admin key.

**2. Their lifetimes are opposite.**
`row_activity` **cascades** from `board_rows`: delete the record and its history goes,
because a timeline with no drawer to render in is dead weight. `audit_events` deliberately
has **no foreign key** to its subject and must survive the purge — *"Moved to Trash with 2
items under it"* is exactly the row an investigation needs after the trash is empty. A
single table cannot both cascade and survive.

**3. Their mutability rules are opposite.**
`audit_events` is append-only enforced at the database grant level: `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE`
plus a raising trigger, with retention purges running as a different role. `row_activity`
is an ordinary table that a row delete cascades through. Applying the audit grants to
record history would make deleting a record impossible; applying the record rules to the
audit trail would void the append-only promise the UI makes in writing.

**4. Their write-on-failure rules are opposite.**
A refused action writes an `audit_events` row on an **autonomous connection outside the
aborted transaction**, because a denial that rolls back is a control nobody can see. A
refused action writes **no** `row_activity` at all — nothing happened to the record.
One table would need both behaviours selected by a column, which is a table pretending to
be two.

**5. Their volume and retention are orders of magnitude apart.**
`row_activity` is one row per record write: the highest-volume write path in the product,
retained for the life of the record. `audit_events` is a few dozen rows a day at most, by
design — OQ-25's recommendation explicitly excludes routine `row.update` traffic *"because
mixing them makes the audit log unreadable at volume"*. Merging them buries the nine error
rows the log exists for under eighty-eight thousand info rows and the severity filter stops
being useful.

**6. Their payloads carry different things and are bound by different rules.**
`row_activity.changes` holds **rendered cell values** — `Doing → Done`, a person's name, a
record's display id — because the drawer renders them. `audit_events.detail` is *"one
sentence, never a payload"* and `context` is bound by an explicit invariant: **no secret
value, no cell value, no block content, no file bytes, ever**
(`src/types/audit.ts:35-38`). Merging the tables would put a column whose purpose is to
carry cell values next to a column whose purpose is to never carry one.

**What belongs in each, as a rule a developer can apply without asking:**

| | `row_activity` (T-14) | `audit_events` (T-36) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scope** | One board record | One workspace |
| **Question** | What happened to this record? | Who did something sensitive, and were they allowed? |
| **Read permission** | Visibility on the board node (E-070) | `workspace.audit.view` (E-136) |
| **Written for** | Every record write: create, cell edit, archive, restore, move, import, comment | Manager/admin-gated actions, `node.share`, every denial (OQ-25) |
| **Written for a refusal?** | No | **Yes**, on an autonomous connection |
| **Actor** | Board writer | Any caller, including anonymous-ish system jobs (`system.retention.sweep`, ip `127.0.0.1`) |
| **Records the IP?** | No | **Yes**, `INET`, stamped off the socket |
| **Records the outcome?** | No — a failed write leaves nothing | **Yes**, `allowed` / `denied` |
| **Severity?** | No | **Yes**, and independent of outcome |
| **Payload** | `changes` = rendered `FieldChange[]`, plus internal `raw_changes` | `detail` = one sentence, plus internal `context` (ids only, never values) |
| **FK to its subject** | `row_id → board_rows ON DELETE CASCADE` | **None, on purpose** |
| **Mutability** | Ordinary table | `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` + raising trigger |
| **Retention** | Life of the record | 12 months / 90 days, denials 24 months (OQ-27) |
| **Cursor sort** | `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` | `(at DESC, id DESC)` |
| **Facets** | None | `total` + `bySeverity` over the whole filtered set |

**The overlap, stated honestly.** Some actions write to both: deleting twelve records in one
bulk call writes twelve `row_activity` rows (one per record — except that the records are
gone, so in practice the cascade removes them) **and** one `audit_events` row with
`action: 'row.delete'`, `severity: 'warn'`, `target: 'Backend Roadmap'`,
`detail: '12 records deleted in one action.'` and `context: { kind: 'bulk', … }`
(`src/services/audit-service.ts:76-84`). That is not duplication: one is the record's
autobiography, the other is the workspace's security ledger, and only the second one
survives.

#### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

These are places where the brief, canon and the frontend did not line up. **In every case
canon was followed** and the note is recorded here rather than resolved in the body.

1. **`comment_mentions` does not exist.** The brief asked for `comment_mentions` "or the
   generic `mentions` table per canon". Canon's 39-table registry (§1.1) contains neither,
   and §1.2 does not list one among the deliberate non-tables either — it is simply absent.
   I followed canon: mentions live in `comments.mentioned_user_ids UUID[]` with a GIN
   index, documented under "Not a table: `comment_mentions`" with the array-vs-join-table
   trade-off written out. If the editor wants a fortieth table, canon §1.1 has to change
   first, and the count in §9 with it.

2. **`notifications` has no JSONB payload in the frontend.** The brief asked for
   "the payload JSONB interface, one variant per notification type". Canon and the
   frontend are explicit that there is none: `title` and `body` are fully rendered strings
   stored on the row, *"no `payload`, no i18n key, no variable bag"*
   (`src/types/collab.ts:101-113`, collab fact sheet §4.1). I did not change the rendering
   contract. I added a **nullable `context JSONB`**, clearly marked **RECOMMENDATION**,
   typed as `NotificationContext` with exactly one variant per `NotificationReason`, on the
   same precedent as `audit_events.context` (which canon T-36 does name). It is never
   returned by any endpoint. It is justified by two open questions canon already reserves —
   OQ-89 (the three unbuilt producers need somewhere to put ids) and OQ-91 (coalescing
   needs to know which comment produced a row). **If the editor prefers a strictly
   canon-literal `notifications`, delete the `context` column, the `NotificationContext`
   interface, the `context->>'kind' = reason` check and the coalescing index; nothing else
   in this chapter depends on them.**

3. **`recent_resources` is not a table.** Canon §1.2 puts `recent_entries` in
   `localStorage` under `nexdrop-recent` (OQ-96). Documented as a non-table with the
   evidence and with the shape it would take if promoted, but not added to the schema.

4. **`is_edited BOOLEAN` → `edited_at TIMESTAMPTZ`.** The collab fact sheet's proposed
   schema has `is_edited boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`; the brief asked for `edited_at`.
   Canon T-33 says only "resolve and soft-delete columns" and canon §1.4 forbids a boolean
   where a timestamp is available ("Never a boolean"). I used `edited_at` and derived
   `isEdited` on read, so the frontend contract (`Comment.isEdited`) is unchanged. Same
   reasoning for `resolved_at` / `deleted_at`, which canon already states.

5. **`comment_attachments` size ceiling.** The collab fact sheet proposed
   `CHECK (size_bytes <= 26214400)` (25 MB, from `src/lib/file-validation.ts:4`). Canon's
   position on OQ-69 is that **100 MB** is the API contract and the client pre-check is
   served from `GET /config` "so the two cannot disagree". I therefore put no ceiling in a
   `CHECK` at all — a limit in a constraint makes raising it a migration — and put the
   enforcement in E-110/E-111 reading the configured value. Also: `comment_attachments`
   carries no `name` / `mime_type` / `size_bytes` of its own (canon T-30 is
   `(comment_id, asset_id)`); those live on `file_assets`.

6. **`watches` has no `workspace_id`.** The collab fact sheet's `comments` carries one and
   its `watches` does not; I kept that asymmetry and gave the reason in the body (a watch
   always has a non-null `target_node_id`, which carries the workspace; a notification may
   not, so it keeps its own). If a future `GET /me/watches?workspaceId=` is added, the
   join is `watches → nodes`.

7. **`UNIQUE … NULLS NOT DISTINCT` is load-bearing** on `watches`. Canon T-34 states the
   unique key as `(user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)`, and
   `target_row_id` is `NULL` for document and board watches. Without `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`
   (PostgreSQL 15+) that constraint enforces nothing for two of the three watchable kinds.
   This is worth a line in the deployment prerequisites: **the schema requires
   PostgreSQL 15 or later.**

8. **`file_nodes.node_id` as a primary key is a stated exception to C-01.** Canon T-28
   ("`node_id` (PK)") and T-20/T-22 do the same for 1:1 side tables, so C-01's "no
   exceptions" and the registry disagree on their face. I followed the registry for the
   side tables and C-01 everywhere else (surrogate `id` plus a `UNIQUE` on the natural
   key). Worth one sentence in §0 so nineteen writers do not each decide it separately.

9. **Attachment tables span two chapters.** `file_assets` (T-27), `file_nodes` (T-28),
   `cell_attachments` (T-29) and `document_asset_refs` (T-31) are `files`-module tables and
   the files chapter will also cover them. They are here because the brief asked for the
   attachment decision and the polymorphism trade-off in full, and because
   `comment_attachments` is unreadable without them. **If the files chapter documents them
   at greater depth, cut `file_nodes` and `document_asset_refs` from this part and keep the
   decision section, `comment_attachments` and `cell_attachments`** — the latter two are
   the ones a collaboration developer reaches for.

This part covers the `documents` module (T-18, T-19), the `devtools` module's content
tables (T-20 … T-25) and the one `files` table that belongs to a document rather than to
the drive (T-31). It closes with the encryption-at-rest architecture for secrets and with
two deliberate non-tables.

Canon bindings this part inherits without re-litigating: C-01 (UUID PKs), C-03/C-04
(instants vs dates), C-05 (no `any`), C-06 (every JSONB column gets a named interface),
C-07 (`readonly` everywhere), C-08 (optional ≠ nullable), C-09 (identity from the session),
C-10 (every write returns the authoritative record), §1.4 (soft delete, audit columns,
`position`, counters).

**Enum types this part uses.** `config_format` (15 members, §2.8), `secret_action`
(`reveal`, `copy`, `rotate`, §2.8), `audit_outcome` (`allowed`, `denied`, §2.2). All are
Postgres `ENUM` types whose values are the frontend literals verbatim (§2.0). `block_type`
(14 members) and `code_language` (8 members) are **not** Postgres enums — they are tags
inside a JSONB document and are enforced by the write-time validator described in
§"Validating `blocks` on write".

**Columns these tables deliberately do not own.** Per canon OQ-30, the node owns `name`,
`isPinned`, `isLocked` and `isArchived`; per §1.3.1 the node also carries the derived
`blockCount` and `excerpt`. Nothing below duplicates them:

| Wire field | Stored where | Written by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WorkspaceDocument.title`, `ConfigDocument.name`, `SecretDocument.name` | `nodes.name` | E-025, and E-092 in the same transaction as the block write |
| `DocumentNode.icon` | `nodes.icon` | E-024 at creation (`page → 📄`, `config → ⚙️`, `secret → 🔐`, `src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:14-18`), E-092 thereafter |
| `WorkspaceDocument.isPinned` | `nodes.is_pinned` | E-093 |
| `WorkspaceDocument.isLocked` / `lockedBy` | `nodes.locked_by`, `nodes.locked_at` — `isLocked` is derived as `locked_by IS NOT NULL` | E-094 |
| `WorkspaceDocument.isArchived` | `nodes.archived_at` | E-030 / E-031 |
| `WorkspaceDocument.owner` | `nodes.owner_id` | E-024 |
| `DocumentNode.blockCount`, `DocumentNode.excerpt` | `nodes.block_count`, `nodes.excerpt` | E-092, in the same transaction (`DocumentSummaryPatch`, `src/services/document-service.ts:149-171`) |
| `ConfigDocument.environmentOptionId`, `SecretEntry.environmentOptionId` → the label and colour behind the id | `environments` (T-26) | E-106 … E-109 |

`environments` (T-26) is referenced by two foreign keys below but is documented with the
rest of the `devtools` reference data, not here.
