### Table: `documents`

**Purpose** — the content of one block-based page (WS-DOC-05): the ordered block array,
its monotonic `version`, and the flattened text the search index and the node excerpt are
derived from. It is the 1:1 content side table for a `nodes` row whose `kind` is `document`
and whose `documentKind` is `page`; config and secret pages are the same node kind with a
different content table (§1.3.1, `src/types/node.ts:41-44`).

**Who creates a record** — E-024 `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` when
`kind: "document"` and `documentKind` is absent or `"page"`, in the same transaction that
inserts the node. E-027 `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate` creates a second row by deep copy.
No other endpoint inserts one.

**Lifetime** — as long as its node. The row is **never** soft-deleted and has no
`deleted_at`: trashing a page is a soft delete on `nodes` (`deleted_at`), so this row
survives untouched and comes back intact on restore. That is an existing requirement —
the frontend's delete path calls `trashNode`, never `documentService.remove`
(`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:114-121`; `documentService.remove` exists at
`src/services/document-service.ts:298` and no component calls it). The row dies only when
the node row is hard-deleted by a permanent purge (E-038, E-039, or the nightly sweep at
`TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`, `src/config/app.ts:42`), through `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `WorkspaceDocument.id`. Kept alongside `node_id` per OQ-30 so board and document sub-resources can hang off their own aggregate id (P-04). |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | yes | The drive node this page is addressed by. `WorkspaceDocument.nodeId`, the routing key every documents endpoint takes. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `WorkspaceDocument.workspaceId`. Denormalised from `nodes.workspace_id` and immutable — a page cannot move between workspaces (E-026 rejects `invalid-target` across tenants). Present so search (E-133) and quota scans do not join `nodes`. |
| `blocks` | `JSONB` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | no | The whole ordered block array, `Block[]`. Structure below. |
| `plain_text` | `TEXT` | no | `''` | no | **RECOMMENDATION.** The server-side equivalent of `documentPlainText(blocks)` (`src/lib/blocks.ts:333-354`), recomputed on every write. Feeds `search_vector` and `nodes.excerpt`. Never returned on the wire. |
| `search_vector` | `TSVECTOR` | no | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', plain_text)) STORED` | no | **RECOMMENDATION** (OQ-93). Canon §1.2 puts a `tsvector` column with a GIN index on `documents` rather than a separate `search_index` table. |
| `version` | `INTEGER` | no | `1` | no | `WorkspaceDocument.version`. Incremented by exactly 1 per non-folded save (`src/services/document-service.ts:211`). The optimistic-concurrency token for `expectedVersion` (OQ-57). |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `WorkspaceDocument.createdAt`. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `WorkspaceDocument.updatedAt`. Server-set on every save; never accepted from the body. |
| `created_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | The author of the first block array. The wire's `owner` comes from `nodes.owner_id`, not from this column. |
| `updated_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Session user of the most recent save (C-09). |

```sql
-- Documentation of intent, not a migration.
CREATE TABLE documents (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  node_id       UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  workspace_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  blocks        JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  plain_text    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  search_vector TSVECTOR NOT NULL
                GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', plain_text)) STORED,
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  updated_by    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  CONSTRAINT documents_version_positive CHECK (version > 0),
  CONSTRAINT documents_blocks_is_array  CHECK (jsonb_typeof(blocks) = 'array'),
  CONSTRAINT documents_never_blockless  CHECK (jsonb_array_length(blocks) >= 1),
  CONSTRAINT documents_block_ceiling    CHECK (jsonb_array_length(blocks) <= 5000)
);
```

#### The `blocks` JSONB structure

`BlockType` has 14 members that collapse into 9 interfaces (§2.8,
`src/types/document.ts:4-110`). This is the exact stored shape — no wrapper object, no
`position` field, no nesting. Order is array order.

```ts
/** src/types/document.ts:4-18. Fourteen tags, nine payload shapes. */
type BlockType =
  | "heading1" | "heading2" | "heading3" | "paragraph" | "quote"
  | "checklist" | "bulletList" | "numberedList"
  | "code" | "image" | "attachment" | "link" | "table" | "embed";

/** src/types/document.ts:20-28. Code BLOCKS only. Not `ConfigFormat` (15 members). */
type CodeLanguage =
  | "plaintext" | "typescript" | "javascript" | "json"
  | "sql" | "bash" | "python" | "go";

interface BlockBase {
  /** Client-minted, opaque, unique WITHIN this document only — never a UUID.
   *  Real values seen in the frontend: `blk_3`, `blk_<nodeId>_1`, `pin_1`. */
  readonly id: string;
}

interface TextBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "heading1" | "heading2" | "heading3" | "paragraph" | "quote";
  readonly text: string;
}

interface ChecklistBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "checklist";
  readonly text: string;
  readonly isChecked: boolean;
}

interface ListBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "bulletList" | "numberedList";
  readonly text: string;
  /** No ordinal is stored. Numbered-list numbers are derived at render time by
   *  counting consecutive `numberedList` blocks
   *  (src/components/document/block-editor.tsx:29-38). */
}

interface CodeBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "code";
  /** `code`, NOT `text`. `blockText()` special-cases it (src/lib/blocks.ts:93-104). */
  readonly code: string;
  readonly language: CodeLanguage;
}

/** One picture inside an image block. A block holds as many as were added. */
interface DocumentImage {
  /** The only persisted reference. `null` only for seeded content that never
   *  had an asset (src/types/document.ts:59-60). */
  readonly assetId: string | null;
  /** MINTED PER RESPONSE as a short-lived signed URL (OQ-75). Never accepted on
   *  write, never stored: the frontend's value is a `blob:` object URL that dies
   *  with the tab (src/services/file-service.ts:247-267). */
  readonly url: string;
  readonly alt: string;
}

interface ImageBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "image";
  /** A gallery, not one image (src/components/document/blocks/image-block.tsx:38-53). */
  readonly images: readonly DocumentImage[];
  /** One caption shared by the whole gallery. */
  readonly caption: string;
}

interface AttachmentBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "attachment";
  readonly assetId: string | null;
  /** name / sizeBytes / mimeType are RESOLVED FROM `file_assets` ON READ when
   *  `assetId` is non-null; the stored copy is a fallback for seeded content. */
  readonly name: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly mimeType: string;
}

interface LinkBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "link";
  readonly url: string;
  /** Produced by the server-side unfurl E-118, never invented by the client
   *  (src/services/link-service.ts:15-37). Stored as returned. */
  readonly title: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly siteName: string;
}

interface TableBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "table";
  readonly hasHeaderRow: boolean;
  /** Rectangular: every row carries the same number of cells. Plain strings —
   *  no column types, no widths, no cell ids (src/lib/blocks.ts:71-75). */
  readonly rows: readonly (readonly string[])[];
}

/** DV-EMB-25: two ids and nothing else. Writes go to the source board, so an
 *  embed is a pointer, never a copy of the board's records
 *  (src/components/document/blocks/embed-block.tsx:31-37). */
interface EmbedBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "embed";
  readonly boardNodeId: string | null;
  readonly viewId: string | null;
}

type Block =
  | TextBlock | ChecklistBlock | ListBlock | CodeBlock
  | ImageBlock | AttachmentBlock | LinkBlock | TableBlock | EmbedBlock;

/** The stored column type. */
type DocumentBlocksJson = readonly Block[];
```

#### Why `blocks JSONB` and not a `document_blocks` table

**DECIDED: JSONB on the document row**, matching canon T-18. The trade-off, in the shape
canon §1.3.2 uses for cells:

| Axis | `blocks JSONB` on the row (CHOSEN) | `document_blocks`, one row per block |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read a page | One row. `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/document` returns the whole document; the editor renders the whole array (`src/components/document/block-editor.tsx`). | N rows plus an ORDER BY on every page load. |
| Write an edit | One `UPDATE`. The save API is whole-document by construction: `DocumentDraft` is `{ title, icon, blocks }` (`src/types/document.ts:137-141`) and `save` replaces `blocks` outright (`src/services/document-service.ts:205-212`). **There is no per-block endpoint anywhere in the frontend**, and P-03 forbids adding one. | Diff the array against the stored rows on every 500 ms debounce, then insert/update/delete/renumber. All of that to serve a client that only ever sends the whole array. |
| Ordering | Array order. No `position` column exists in the frontend and none is needed; every structural operation is an array transform (`insertBlockAt`, `moveBlock`, `mergeWithPrevious`, `src/lib/blocks.ts:117-328`). | A `position` column, densely renumbered on every reorder — and a reorder is one keystroke (Alt+↑). |
| Block ids as keys | Opaque, client-minted, unique **within a document only** (`blk_3`, `pin_1`). Perfectly adequate as JSON object keys. | Poor row keys. Either mint a server UUID per block and translate on every read/write, or accept a non-unique natural key. |
| Version snapshots | A snapshot is the same array, copied (`DocumentVersion.blocks`, `src/types/system.ts:196`). One column copy. | Every snapshot re-materialises N rows into a separate versions table anyway — so the normalised form exists only for the live copy. |
| Finding which asset a block references | Not answerable from the JSONB cheaply. **This is the axis the row-per-block model wins.** It is bought back by `document_asset_refs` (T-31), which is exactly the projection GC and quota need. | Native. |
| Full-text search | `plain_text` + `search_vector`, one generated column. | Aggregate N rows per document per query. |
| Referential integrity on `assetId` | None inside the JSONB. `document_asset_refs` carries the FK. | Native. |
| Row size | A 50-block page is ~10–40 KB and will TOAST. Fine: the only read is whole-document. | n/a |
| Migration if wrong | `jsonb_array_elements` → insert, one pass. | Reverse is `jsonb_agg`, also one pass. |

#### Validating `blocks` on write

The union is not enforceable by a Postgres `CHECK` beyond shape, so the service validates
before the `UPDATE`. Every failure is `BLOCK_TYPE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` (400, `validation`)
except where noted:

1. `blocks` is an array with at least one element — a document is never blockless
   (`src/lib/blocks.ts:139-147`). Violation → `BLOCK_TYPE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`.
2. Every element has a non-empty string `id`, and ids are unique within the array.
3. `type` is one of the 14 `BlockType` members; anything else is rejected, never stored.
4. The payload matches the branch: `code` carries `code` **and** a `language` from the
   8-member `CodeLanguage` union (not `ConfigFormat`); `checklist` carries `isChecked`;
   `table.rows` is rectangular; `image.images` is an array; `embed` carries exactly
   `boardNodeId` and `viewId`.
5. `assetId` values, where non-null, resolve to a `file_assets` row the caller may read.
   An unresolvable id is dropped from `document_asset_refs` but **kept in the block**, so
   the frontend's "no longer available" rendering still fires
   (`src/components/document/blocks/attachment-block.tsx:46-56`).
6. Block count ≤ 5 000 and serialised size ≤ 1 MB → `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` (400). See the
   open question below.
7. `url` on an image block and `url`/`thumbnailUrl` anywhere else are **ignored on write**
   (OQ-75). A `blob:` string is never persisted.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-58)** — the document size ceiling is undefined.
**Evidence** — PRD `WS-DOC-05` targets "< 500 ms for a 50-page document"; the diff engine
degrades to "delete everything / add everything" past 2 000 lines
(`src/lib/diff.ts:11-21`); nothing in the frontend caps block count or payload size.
**Recommendation** — 5 000 blocks and 1 MB serialised, both served from `GET /config`
(E-139) so the client cannot disagree, both refused with `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE`.
**Impact if wrong** — one pasted document multiplies through every version snapshot
(up to the history cap), every excerpt recompute and every diff, and the page-load metric
fails silently on one workspace.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | Content cannot outlive its address. Trash is a soft delete on `nodes` (§1.4), so the cascade never fires on a trash — only on a permanent purge, which is precisely when the content must go too. This is what makes "deleting a document must not delete its content" true without a second flag. |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | Deleting a workspace (E-011) removes its content. The value is immutable, so the FK is a tenancy assertion. |
| `created_by`, `updated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are soft-deactivated (`is_active`), never hard-deleted (T-01), so `RESTRICT` asserts that invariant instead of silently orphaning authorship. |

**Unique Constraints** — `UNIQUE (node_id)`. One page per node; it is what makes
`GET /nodes/{nodeId}/document` a single-row lookup and what canon OQ-30 requires.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `documents_pkey (id)` | Sub-resource routing by document id. |
| `UNIQUE (node_id)` | E-091, E-092, E-095, E-096, E-097 — every documents endpoint enters by node id (P-04). |
| `GIN (search_vector)` | E-133 global search over page bodies. |
| `(workspace_id)` | The search permission funnel, which scopes by workspace **before** scanning (E-133), and the workspace purge. |

No index on `blocks` itself. Asset lookups go through `document_asset_refs` (T-31); that
is what it exists for.

**Check Constraints** — `version > 0`; `jsonb_typeof(blocks) = 'array'`;
`jsonb_array_length(blocks) >= 1` (never blockless); `jsonb_array_length(blocks) <= 5000`.
The 1 MB byte ceiling is enforced in the service, not as a `CHECK`, because a size check
over a TOASTed value on every write is a worse trade than one length check in code.

**Relationships**

| Cardinality | To | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–1 | `nodes` | Enforced by `UNIQUE (node_id)`. The node owns identity, name, icon, pin, lock, archive and trash; this table owns content. |
| 1–N | `document_versions` | Snapshots, newest first. |
| 1–N | `document_asset_refs` | One row per (block, asset) pair referenced by an image or attachment block. |
| N–1 | `workspaces`, `users` ×2 | — |

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-091 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/document` → `WorkspaceDocument` | visibility | read-only | `documentService.get` → `useDocument` (`src/hooks/use-document.ts`) | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| E-092 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document` → `WorkspaceDocument` | `document.update` (Manager+, `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:59`) | one transaction: validate blocks → `UPDATE documents` → `UPDATE nodes` (name, icon, block_count, excerpt, updated_at) → `INSERT document_versions` (or fold) → rewrite `document_asset_refs` | `useAutosave` → `saveScheduler` → `documentService.save` | `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` (409), `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` (409), `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` (400), `BLOCK_TYPE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` (400), `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-093 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document/pin` | `document.update` | writes `nodes.is_pinned` only; returns the projected `WorkspaceDocument` | `useDocumentActions` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-094 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document/lock` | `document.lock` **or** the node's owner | writes `nodes.locked_by`/`locked_at` from the session, never the body (OQ-60) | `useDocumentActions` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-097 | `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/restore` | `document.version.restore` | goes through the E-092 path, so a locked page refuses a restore for exactly the reason it refuses an edit (`src/services/document-service.ts:122-135`) | `useVersionHistory` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` |
| E-027 | `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate` | `node.create` + `document.create` | one transaction: copy node → copy `documents` row with **fresh block ids**, resetting pin, lock, archive and `version: 1` (`src/services/document-service.ts:243-267`) | `useDocumentActions` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-133 | `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/search` | membership | read-only, GIN scan behind the permission funnel | `searchService` | — |

**Save semantics E-092 must reproduce** (all existing requirements):

- A blank title is **coerced, not rejected**: `title.trim().length > 0 ? title : "Untitled"`
  (`src/services/document-service.ts:207`).
- `version` increments by exactly 1 and `updatedAt` is server-set
  (`src/services/document-service.ts:210-211`).
- A locked page refuses with `conflict("This page is locked", "Unlock it before saving
  further changes.")` → 409 `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` (`src/services/document-service.ts:192-194`).
  Locking narrows `edit` and `upload` and leaves reading and commenting alone
  (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:135-141`; `src/components/document/document-page.tsx:137-143`).
- `expectedVersion` is optional: stale → 409 `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`; absent →
  last-write-wins (canon OQ-57).
- The whole draft arrives in one call. The client's save pipeline guarantees the last edit
  reaches the server, flushes on disposal, and treats an abort as `cancelled` rather than an
  error (`src/lib/save-scheduler.ts:56-122`; C-12).

**Realtime** — none. No frame in §7 covers document content; RT-11 `node.changed` carries
only `created | renamed | moved | archived | trashed | restored`, and a save is none of
those. A second tab converges on its next read. See OQ-99.

### Table: `document_versions`

**Purpose** — one full snapshot of a page per version (SY-VER-39): the title and block
array as they stood, the author, and the `+3 −1 lines` summary the history list renders
without opening a diff. Snapshots, never deltas, "so restoring never has to replay a chain"
(`src/services/document-service.ts:63-69`).

**Who creates a record** — E-092 `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document`, inside the same
transaction as the block write. E-097 (restore) creates one too, because a restore is a
save. Nothing else writes here, and there is no endpoint that edits or deletes a version.

**Lifetime** — bounded by the retention rule below and by its document: `ON DELETE CASCADE`
from `documents`, which itself only dies on a permanent purge. Rows are hard-deleted by
the retention sweep; a version is never soft-deleted, because a history with tombstones in
it is not a history anyone can read.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `DocumentVersion.id`, `VersionEntry.id`. |
| `document_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Owning document. |
| `version` | `INTEGER` | no | — | with `document_id` | `DocumentVersion.version`. The value `documents.version` held **after** the save this snapshot records. |
| `title` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | The title at that version — a genuine snapshot, not a projection, because `nodes.name` moves on and `DocumentVersion.title` is what a restore writes back (`src/types/system.ts:195`). |
| `blocks` | `JSONB` | no | — | no | Full `Block[]` snapshot. Same structure as `documents.blocks`; the interface above is the contract for both columns. |
| `summary` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `+3 −1 lines`, or `no line changes`, prefixed `renamed · ` when the title also changed (`src/services/document-service.ts:99-109`; `describeDiff`, `src/lib/diff.ts:87-93`). Computed server-side over `documentLines`, never sent by the client. |
| `is_autosave` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `false` | no | Written by the debounce rather than by a person. Drives the fold rule. |
| `author_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `DocumentVersion.author`. From the session (C-09). |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `DocumentVersion.createdAt`. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Moves when a fold rewrites this row in place; equals `created_at` otherwise. |

#### Snapshot strategy — what triggers one

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** A version is cut on every successful save
(`src/services/document-service.ts:214`). Left alone that is far too often: the page
debounce is `AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500` (`src/lib/autosave.ts:3`), so twenty half-second
pauses would consume the entire retained history.

**Canon position (OQ-59): fold consecutive autosaves by the same author.** The config
service already implements exactly this and the page service does not
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:160-187`). Port it verbatim:

```
foldsIn = isAutosave
       && head exists
       && head.is_autosave = true
       && head.author_id = session user
```

- `foldsIn` → **rewrite the head row in place**: same `id`, same `version`, new `blocks`,
  new `title`, new `summary` (recomputed against the *pre-fold head's* blocks, not against
  the previous document, `src/services/devtools-service.ts:181`), new `updated_at`.
  `documents.version` does **not** advance.
- otherwise → `INSERT` a new row at `documents.version + 1`, and advance
  `documents.version`.

A manual save (⌘S / the Save button) always starts a new version, and so does another
author's edit landing in between. This requires `isAutosave?: boolean` on the E-092 request
body — see Chapter notes.

A **version-1 entry is seeded** the first time a history is read, so the list is never
empty (`src/services/document-service.ts:72-90`). Prefer writing it at creation (E-024)
instead, so a read is never a write.

#### Retention

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT** — `VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT = 20`, oldest dropped
(`src/config/app.ts:62-63`, applied at `src/services/document-service.ts:111`). The limit is
server-owned and served from `GET /config` (E-139).

**Canon position (OQ-59):** "generously capped for pages … never drop the first or the
current version." Concretely, after each insert:

1. Never delete the row with the lowest `version` (the page's origin).
2. Never delete the head.
3. Delete the oldest remaining rows until the count is at or below the cap.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-59)** — the cap number for pages.
**Evidence** — the frontend ships 20 (`src/config/app.ts:63`); config history is uncapped
in the same codebase (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:186`), which is an inconsistency
the two services never reconciled.
**Recommendation** — 200 per document, with folding in place. Twenty was chosen when every
debounce cut a version; once autosaves fold, 200 is roughly a year of deliberate edits for
an active page and costs a few megabytes.
**Impact if wrong** — too low and the useful history is gone by lunchtime and PRD
`SY-VER-39` is met in letter only; too high and a 1 MB page pins 200 MB of snapshots that
nothing prunes.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document_id` | `documents(id)` | `CASCADE` | A snapshot of a document that no longer exists is unreadable and unrestorable. The parent only dies on a permanent purge, so the cascade is the purge finishing its job. |
| `author_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | The author is part of the record. Users are deactivated, not deleted (T-01), so this asserts the invariant. |

**Unique Constraints** — `UNIQUE (document_id, version)`. One row per version number. A
fold does not violate it: the fold rewrites the *same row* at the *same* version
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:163, 176, 185`), it does not insert a second one.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `document_versions_pkey (id)` | E-096, E-097, E-098 — fetch or restore one version. |
| `UNIQUE (document_id, version DESC)` | E-095 `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions` — the cursor page on `(version DESC)` (§6.3), and the "is the head a foldable autosave by me?" lookup on every save. |

**Check Constraints** — `version > 0`; `jsonb_typeof(blocks) = 'array'`;
`jsonb_array_length(blocks) >= 1`.

**Relationships** — N–1 to `documents` (the aggregate root); N–1 to `users`. There is no
relationship to `config_versions` or `secret_rotations`: three subjects, three tables, one
read model (canon T-19/T-21/T-24, resolving OQ-77).

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-095 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions?cursor=&limit=` → `VersionPage` of `VersionEntry` | visibility | read-only | `useVersionHistory`, only while the dialog is open (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:22-31`) | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-096 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}` → `DocumentVersion` | visibility | read-only | `version-detail.tsx` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-097 | `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/restore` → `WorkspaceDocument` | `document.version.restore` | one transaction, through the E-092 save path | `useVersionHistory.restore`, which reloads the list afterwards rather than assuming what is on top (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:71`) | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_LOCKED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-098 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/diff?against=` → `DiffResponse` | visibility | read-only | `version-dialogs.tsx` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |

**Projection to `VersionEntry`** (`src/lib/versions.ts:21-31`): `lines =
documentLines(blocks)` — the structural line form (`# `, `> `, `• `, `[x] `, fenced code,
`[image] …`, `| a | b |`, `[board] …`, `src/lib/blocks.ts:356-393`) — and
`hasSnapshot: true`.

**Restore semantics the backend must preserve** (all existing requirements,
`src/services/document-service.ts:122-135`):

- Restoring **writes forward**; it never rewinds. The new version number is
  `current + 1`, not the restored number.
- Restore inherits every rule `save` has, including the lock refusal.
- **The icon is not restored** — only `title` and `blocks`. The current icon is kept.
- The diff shown to the user is *stored version → what is on screen now*, including the
  client's unsaved draft, so the comparison target is state the server has never seen
  (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:16-18`). Keep the diff client-side; the server serves
  snapshots and E-098 for version-to-version comparison only.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-61)** — does `document.version.restore` gate restore, or is `edit` enough?
**Evidence** — the key exists and is Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:61`) but no
frontend call site uses it; the dialog gates on `capabilities.edit`
(`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:160`), which a Member holds.
**Recommendation** — enforce `document.version.restore` server-side (canon E-097 already
names it) and change the client's gate to read the same key. A restore discards everything
since that version in one click; it is not an ordinary edit.
**Impact if wrong** — either Members lose an ability the UI offers them and every restore
button 403s, or a Member rolls a document back a month without holding the key the matrix
says they need.

**Realtime** — none. See OQ-99.

### Table: `config_documents`

**Purpose** — the content of one config document (DV-CFG-22): raw text, the language it is
written in, and the deployment label it points at. It is the 1:1 content side table for a
`nodes` row whose `documentKind` is `config`. Content is one opaque string — no blocks, no
AST, no per-line rows (`src/types/devtools.ts:39-49`).

**Who creates a record** — E-024 `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` with
`documentKind: "config"`, in the same transaction as the node. The author picks the
language up front, because guessing it from the name gets "Payment Service Config" wrong
(`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:57-66`; `src/services/devtools-service.ts:196-213`).

**Lifetime** — as long as its node, exactly as `documents`: survives a trash, dies with a
purge through `ON DELETE CASCADE`. No `deleted_at`.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | PK | The drive node. **This is the primary key** — canon T-20. `ConfigDocument` carries no id of its own (`src/types/devtools.ts:40`), unlike `WorkspaceDocument`. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Denormalised, immutable. Scopes the environment FK check and the workspace purge without a join. |
| `format` | `config_format` | no | `'env'` | no | `ConfigDocument.format` — **the wire name is `format`, never `language`**; the UI label says "Language" (`src/types/devtools.ts:19-21`). Closed 15-member enum; an unknown value is rejected with `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN`, never stored as free text. Default `env` matches the client's detection fallback (`src/lib/syntax/detect.ts:50-68`). |
| `environment_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | FK into `environments` (T-26). Surfaces as `ConfigDocument.environmentOptionId` on the wire (`src/types/devtools.ts:43-44`). |
| `content` | `TEXT` | no | `''` | no | The raw text, verbatim. |
| `version` | `INTEGER` | no | `1` | no | `ConfigDocument.version`. Advances on every non-folded save. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `ConfigDocument.updatedAt`. |
| `created_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | — |
| `updated_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `ConfigDocument.updatedBy`. From the session. |

`name` is deliberately absent — it comes from `nodes.name` on every read, so a rename
cannot leave the header and the breadcrumb disagreeing about what you are looking at. The
frontend refreshes it explicitly for exactly this reason
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:100-118`). Model it as a join, not a column.

**Content is stored and returned byte-for-byte.** The backend never formats, never
re-indents, never normalises line endings, and never rejects malformed content. Formatting
is a client concern (`src/lib/code-format.ts`), linting is JSON-only and runs on the draft
while typing (`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:69`), and a failed format returns a reason
with **no replacement text** so a caller can never write a half-formatted document over a
good one (`src/lib/code-format.ts:152-186`). If server-side JSON validation is ever wanted
it must be advisory metadata on the response, never a rejection — otherwise a user cannot
save a half-typed file.

**Primary Key** — `node_id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same reasoning as `documents.node_id`: trash is soft, so the cascade is the permanent purge finishing its job. |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | Tenant deletion. |
| `environment_id` | `environments(id)` | `RESTRICT` | E-109 must refuse deleting an environment that is still referenced, with `ENVIRONMENT_IN_USE` (409). `RESTRICT` is that rule expressed in the schema rather than only in a service check. |
| `created_by`, `updated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | Users are deactivated, not deleted. |

**Unique Constraints** — the primary key is the uniqueness: one config document per node.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `config_documents_pkey (node_id)` | E-099, E-100, E-095 — every config endpoint enters by node id. |
| `(environment_id)` | E-109's referenced-check, and "show me every document pointing at Production". |
| `(workspace_id)` | Workspace purge; the environment-usage rollup. |

There is **no** `tsvector` on `content`. Canon §1.2 puts full-text columns on `documents`,
`board_rows`, `comments` and `nodes` only; a config document is reachable in search by its
node name. Indexing credentials-adjacent config text is a decision nobody has taken.

**Check Constraints** — `version > 0`.

**Relationships** — 1–1 to `nodes`; 1–N to `config_versions`; N–1 to `environments`,
`workspaces`, `users` ×2.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-099 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/config` → `ConfigDocument` | visibility | read-only, joined to `nodes` for `name` | `devtoolsService.getConfig` → `useConfigDocument` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| E-100 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/config` → `ConfigDocument` | `document.update` (this endpoint **already enforces** in the frontend, `src/services/devtools-service.ts:148`) | one transaction: `UPDATE config_documents` → fold-or-insert `config_versions` → conditional `audit_events` row | `useConfigDocument` (autosave) and `setFormat` / `setEnvironment` | `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN`, `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-095…E-098 | version history family | visibility / `document.version.restore` | see `config_versions` | `ConfigVersionsDialog` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |

**Request body for E-100** — `SaveConfigRequest`, mirroring `SaveConfigInput`
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:120-135`):

```ts
interface SaveConfigRequest {
  readonly content: string;
  /** Omitted means unchanged. */
  readonly format?: ConfigFormat;
  /** Omitted means unchanged. Wire name keeps the frontend's field name. */
  readonly environmentOptionId?: string;
  /** This save came from the debounce, not from a person. Default false. */
  readonly isAutosave?: boolean;
  readonly expectedVersion?: number;
}
```

Save rules the backend must reproduce:

- The autosave debounce is **1 500 ms**, deliberately longer than a page's 500 ms:
  "code is typed in bursts with real pauses inside them" (`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:12-21`).
- Changing the language or the environment sends the **current content** along, so the
  language and the text land in one version rather than two that disagree
  (`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:109-139`). The endpoint must accept all three fields
  in one call.
- A completed autosave updates the loaded document but leaves the client's draft alone, so
  the response must be the authoritative record (C-10) and nothing more.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-62)** — a Production config change is announced as audited and nothing audits it.
**Evidence** — the confirmation dialog says "This change is recorded against your account"
(`src/components/devtools/environment-picker.tsx:102`) and the option is disabled without
`document.update`; but `saveConfig` writes no `auditService.record` call
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:142-189`) — only secret operations do. PRD `DV-ENV-21`
requires Admin/Manager confirmation for a Production config change.
**Recommendation** — E-100 writes an `audit_events` row in the same transaction whenever
the save either sets `environment_id` to the Production environment or saves a document
already pointing at it: module `document`, action `document.update`, severity `warn`,
`target` the node name, `detail` "Environment changed to Production" or "Production config
saved", outcome `allowed`. No content in the row.
**Impact if wrong** — the product makes a compliance promise in a modal that the log
cannot keep, and a Production config change is untraceable.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-63)** — the Production environment has no stable identity once
environments become rows.
**Evidence** — the frontend's environment ids are derived string constants `env_0`,
`env_1`, `env_2` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:20-37`), and the Production guard is a
literal equality check against `PRODUCTION_OPTION_ID = "env_2"` (line 37), consumed by the
picker (`src/components/devtools/environment-picker.tsx`) and by board templates. Canon
§5.3 shapes `Environment` as `{ id, workspaceId, label, color, position }` — with UUID ids
per C-01 there is nothing left for that equality check to bind to.
**Recommendation** — give `environments` a stable non-display discriminator (`slug TEXT`
with seeded values `development` / `staging` / `production`, unique per workspace) and have
the frontend guard on the slug rather than the id. Seed the three rows per workspace at
creation and refuse to delete a seeded row in v1.
**Impact if wrong** — every stored `environment_id` is fine, but the Production guard —
the confirmation dialog, the "admins only" narrowing, the audit trigger above — silently
stops guarding anything, because no id equals `"env_2"` any more.

**Realtime** — none. See OQ-99.

---

### Table: `config_versions`

**Purpose** — one full text snapshot of a config document per version (SY-VER-39), with the
`is_autosave` flag that drives the fold rule. The one behaviour this table exists to make
possible is "100 % of edits recorded" (DV-CFG-22) without a history of four hundred entries
a keystroke apart (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:125-133`).

**Who creates a record** — E-100 `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/config`, inside the same transaction
as the content write, and E-097 (restore), which is a save. Nothing else.

**Lifetime** — cascades from `config_documents`. **Uncapped** per canon OQ-59: config
history is not pruned. A config file is small text, and the whole point of the feature is
that a change to a boot-time configuration can be found later.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `ConfigVersion.id`. **Stable across a fold** — a fold rewrites this row rather than inserting a new one (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:176`). |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | with `version` | Owning config document. |
| `version` | `INTEGER` | no | — | with `node_id` | `ConfigVersion.version`. |
| `content` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Full snapshot, never a delta. |
| `summary` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `+3 lines` / `−1 lines` / `12 lines` — a line-count delta, computed against the *pre-fold head's* content when folding and against the previous document otherwise (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:181, 215-222`). |
| `is_autosave` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `false` | no | `ConfigVersion.isAutosave`. **Optional on the wire, not nullable** (C-08): the field is omitted when false (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:182`), which is why the column is `NOT NULL DEFAULT false` in the DB and `isAutosave?: boolean` in TypeScript. |
| `author_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `ConfigVersion.author`. From the session. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `ConfigVersion.createdAt`. |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Advances on a fold; equals `created_at` otherwise. |

#### The fold rule, stated once

```
foldsIn = isAutosave
       && head exists
       && head.is_autosave = true
       && head.author_id = session user
```
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:157-163`.)

- `foldsIn` → `UPDATE` the head row: same `id`, same `version`, new `content`, new
  `summary`, new `updated_at`. `config_documents.version` is unchanged.
- otherwise → `INSERT` at `config_documents.version + 1` and advance it.

A manual save always starts a new version, and so does another author's edit landing in
between. The same rule is ported to `document_versions`; the two tables must not drift.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `config_documents(node_id)` | `CASCADE` | A snapshot without its document cannot be read or restored; the parent only dies on a permanent purge. |
| `author_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | The author is part of the record; users are deactivated, not deleted. |

**Unique Constraints** — `UNIQUE (node_id, version)`. This holds **despite** the fold,
because a fold rewrites the existing row at the same version number rather than inserting a
second row at it. See Chapter notes.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `config_versions_pkey (id)` | E-096, E-097, E-098. |
| `UNIQUE (node_id, version DESC)` | E-095's cursor page on `(version DESC)`, and the "is the head a foldable autosave by me?" lookup on every save. |

**Check Constraints** — `version > 0`.

**Relationships** — N–1 to `config_documents`; N–1 to `users`.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-095 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions` → `VersionPage` | visibility | read-only; returns a **copy**, never a live list (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:224-237`) | `ConfigVersionsDialog` → `useVersionHistory` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-096 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}` → `ConfigVersion` | visibility | read-only | `version-detail.tsx` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-097 | `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/restore` → `ConfigDocument` | `document.version.restore` | goes through the E-100 save path, so it cuts a **new** version rather than rewinding (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:239-250`) | `useVersionHistory.restore` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-098 | `.../diff?against=` → `DiffResponse` | visibility | read-only | `version-dialogs.tsx` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |

**Projection to `VersionEntry`** (`src/lib/versions.ts:33-43`): `lines =
content.split("\n")`, `hasSnapshot: true`.

**Realtime** — none. See OQ-99.

---

### Table: `secret_documents`

**Purpose** — the container for a set of named credentials (DV-SEC-23), and nothing else.
It holds no values, no key names and no counts; every one of those lives on `secrets`. Its
job is to give the entry list an owner that a foreign key can cascade from and a permission
check can be scoped to — "there are no per-secret permissions in this model, so the check
is per-document and the answer is all or nothing"
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:419-422`).

**Who creates a record** — E-024 `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` with
`documentKind: "secret"`, in the same transaction as the node.

**Lifetime** — as long as its node: survives a trash, dies with a permanent purge through
`ON DELETE CASCADE`. Purging cascades to `secrets`, `secret_rotations` and
`secret_access_events` — see the note under each on why that is the right answer for the
first and a deliberate compliance decision for the other two.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | PK | The drive node. **Primary key** — canon T-22; `SecretDocument` carries no id of its own (`src/types/devtools.ts:84-88`). |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Denormalised, immutable. Selects the workspace data key for envelope encryption (see below) without a join up the tree. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | Moves on every whole-list replace (E-102). |
| `created_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | — |
| `updated_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Last actor to replace the list. |

`name` is projected from `nodes.name`, exactly as for config documents and for the same
reason (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:288-299`).

**Primary Key** — `node_id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `nodes(id)` | `CASCADE` | Same purge semantics as the other two content tables. |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | A workspace deletion must take its ciphertext with it; leaving encrypted credentials behind after a tenant leaves is a data-retention failure, not a safety net. |
| `created_by`, `updated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | — |

**Unique Constraints** — the primary key. One secret document per node.

**Indexes** — `secret_documents_pkey (node_id)` serves E-101 … E-105 and E-095, all of
which enter by node id. `(workspace_id)` serves the purge and the workspace-wide "how many
secret documents are there" question the admin console asks.

**Check Constraints** — none. Every rule about secrets is a rule about `secrets`.

**Relationships** — 1–1 to `nodes`; 1–N to `secrets`, `secret_rotations`,
`secret_access_events`.

**APIs that use it** — every endpoint in §3.16 resolves this row first and applies the
document-level permission check before touching `secrets`. See the endpoint table under
`secrets`.

**Realtime** — none, and deliberately so: a frame announcing that a credential document
changed is a signal worth nothing to a client that must refetch through a permission check
anyway. See OQ-99, and RT-05's precedent that a frame must never be the thing that leaks
what it announces (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`).

---

### Table: `secrets`

**Purpose** — one named credential: its key, its **encrypted** value and the sidecar
material needed to decrypt it, plus the display fields the masked list renders. This is the
only place plaintext-derived data exists in the system, and it exists only as ciphertext.
Canon T-23 is explicit: "Never selected on a list read."

**Who creates a record** — E-102 `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets`. That is the only writer.
There is no per-secret create, update or delete endpoint: the save is a **whole-list
replacement in the order given**, which is what makes reorder, rename and delete one
operation rather than three endpoints (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:479-487`).

**Lifetime** — until the next whole-list replace removes it, or the document is purged.
Rows are **hard-deleted**, never soft-deleted: a tombstone holding ciphertext is a
credential nobody is looking at any more, which is exactly the thing that should not be
kept. The fact that a key existed and was removed survives in `secret_rotations`, which
holds no value.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `SecretEntry.id`. Stable across a rename — the editor keys rows by it so renaming does not look like delete-plus-add (`src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:26-33`). |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | with `key`, and with `position` | Owning secret document. |
| `key` | `TEXT` | no | — | with `node_id` | `SecretEntry.key`, e.g. `DATABASE_PASSWORD`. A business identifier, never the PK (C-02). |
| `value_encrypted` | `BYTEA` | no | — | no | AES-256-GCM ciphertext of the plaintext value. **Never selected by any list read.** |
| `value_iv` | `BYTEA` | no | — | no | The 96-bit nonce for this ciphertext. Unique per encryption operation; never reused across rows or rotations. |
| `value_auth_tag` | `BYTEA` | no | — | no | The 128-bit GCM authentication tag. A tag mismatch is a 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, never a "wrong value" answer. |
| `value_key_id` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Identifies the data key generation that wrapped this ciphertext. Lets several generations coexist during a rotation. |
| `value_algorithm` | `TEXT` | no | `'AES-256-GCM'` | no | Recorded per row so an algorithm migration can be incremental and auditable rather than a flag day. |
| `environment_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | FK into `environments`. Surfaces as `SecretEntry.environmentOptionId`. Defaults to the workspace's first environment for a newly added entry (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:38, 544`). |
| `note` | `TEXT` | yes | `NULL` | no | `SecretEntry.note` — **optional on the wire, omitted when absent** (`note?: string`, `src/types/devtools.ts:81`; `src/services/devtools-service.ts:547`). |
| `position` | `INTEGER` | no | — | with `node_id` | The stored list order. `SecretDocument.entries` is returned in this order, and E-102 rewrites it from the order in the request. |
| `rotated_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `SecretEntry.rotatedBy` — who last changed this entry. From the session. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | — |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `SecretEntry.updatedAt` — the last rotation. Only advances when the entry actually changed (see below). |

```sql
-- Documentation of intent, not a migration.
CREATE TABLE secrets (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  node_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES secret_documents(node_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  key             TEXT NOT NULL,
  value_encrypted BYTEA NOT NULL,
  value_iv        BYTEA NOT NULL,
  value_auth_tag  BYTEA NOT NULL,
  value_key_id    TEXT  NOT NULL,
  value_algorithm TEXT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'AES-256-GCM',
  environment_id  UUID  NOT NULL REFERENCES environments(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  note            TEXT  NULL,
  position        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  rotated_by      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT secrets_key_shape     CHECK (btrim(key) <> '' AND key !~ '[\s="'']'),
  CONSTRAINT secrets_position_zero CHECK (position >= 0),
  CONSTRAINT secrets_iv_length     CHECK (octet_length(value_iv) = 12),
  CONSTRAINT secrets_tag_length    CHECK (octet_length(value_auth_tag) = 16),
  CONSTRAINT secrets_key_unique    UNIQUE (node_id, key),
  CONSTRAINT secrets_position_unique
    UNIQUE (node_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
);
```

**There is no `masked_value` column.** `SecretEntry.maskedValue` is a constant — twelve
`U+2022` bullets, `MASK = "••••••••••••"` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:35`) — minted
by the server on every read. It must **not** encode the real value's length
(`src/types/devtools.ts:76-77`), and storing it would be storing a fact about the
plaintext.

**The list read must be structurally incapable of returning ciphertext.** E-101 selects
`id, key, environment_id, note, position, rotated_by, updated_at` and nothing else.
**RECOMMENDATION:** express that in the database as well as in code — a view
`secrets_masked` over exactly those columns, with the application's ordinary role granted
`SELECT` on the view and on `secrets` only for the four sidecar columns it needs at reveal
time. A `SELECT *` in a future handler then cannot become an incident.

#### Whole-list replace (E-102) — the algorithm

`SaveSecretsRequest.entries` is `SecretDraftEntry[]` (canon §5.3):

```ts
interface SecretDraftEntry {
  /** The id of an existing secret, or null for one being added. */
  readonly id: string | null;
  readonly key: string;
  /** OMITTED where the value is untouched. Optional, never nullable (C-08). */
  readonly value?: string;
}
```

**The omitted `value` is load-bearing.** It is what lets someone rename a key, reorder the
list or delete a neighbour without a single production credential ever entering the browser
(`src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:16-33`; `src/services/devtools-service.ts:533-536`). The
stored ciphertext is carried forward untouched — it is **not** decrypted and re-encrypted,
because there is no reason to bring plaintext into memory for a rename.

Validation, in this order (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:488-521`):

1. `secret.rotate` on this node, resolved from the session — else `SECRET_ROTATE_DENIED`
   (403), message `Changing these secrets needs the Admin role`.
2. Every key valid: non-empty after trim and free of whitespace, `=`, `"` and `'`
   (`isValidSecretKey`, `src/lib/env-file.ts:122-124`) — else `SECRET_KEY_INVALID` (400),
   `"{key}" is not a usable name for a secret`. The rule is deliberately permissive:
   dotted, hyphenated and lowercase keys are real, and refusing one because it is
   unfashionable would make the editor useless for the config it was needed for.
3. No duplicate trimmed keys — else `SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE` (400), `"{key}" appears twice`.
   `isConventionalSecretKey` (`/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`) is a **client-side warning
   only** and must never become a server rejection (`src/lib/env-file.ts:127-129`).

Then, in one transaction:

- For each draft entry, in request order, assign `position = index`.
- Existing id → keep the row; trim the key; take the new ciphertext if `value` was
  supplied, otherwise carry the stored ciphertext, IV, tag and key id forward unchanged.
- `id: null` → insert, encrypt the supplied value, default `environment_id` to the
  workspace's first environment and `note` to `NULL`.
- `isChanged = !existing || existing.key !== key || value was supplied`. Only when changed
  do `updated_at` and `rotated_by` move (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:538-546`).
- Delete every existing row whose id is absent from the request.
- Write one `secret_rotations` row and one `secret_access_events` row per changed entry
  **and per removed entry** — "a removed secret is a rotation too — the trail has to show
  where it went" (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:554-558`) — plus one `audit_events`
  row each (canon OQ-68).

`environment_id` and `note` are carried over and are **not** writable through this endpoint
today (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:544, 547`).

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-64)** — a secret's environment and note have no write path.
**Evidence** — both fields exist on `SecretEntry` (`src/types/devtools.ts:78, 81`), are
rendered (`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:224-226, 255`) and are seeded
(`src/mock/devtools.ts:51-79`), but `saveSecrets` preserves rather than accepts them and
the editor panel has no control for either.
**Recommendation** — extend `SecretDraftEntry` with optional `environmentOptionId?: string`
and `note?: string`, omission meaning "unchanged", exactly like `value`. Changing either
counts as a change for `updated_at` and for audit, but must **not** be filed as `rotate`:
it is not a write to the stored value. File it as `document.update` in `audit_events` and
leave `secret_rotations` alone.
**Impact if wrong** — a secret created in the UI is stuck on the first environment forever
and its note can never be written; the seeded data implies a feature the app cannot perform.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-12)** — what happens to secrets when a container is duplicated?
**Evidence** — E-027 duplicates a container recursively "content included", and the
frontend's document duplicate copies content wholesale
(`src/services/document-service.ts:243-267`). Nothing in the frontend says what a secret
document does under a duplicate, because the frontend has no duplicate path for one.
**Recommendation** — a duplicate of a secret document copies the **keys, environments,
notes, order and nothing else**; every value is created empty and every copied entry gets a
`secret_rotations` row of kind `added`. A copy is a structure, not a credential handover.
Refuse the duplicate outright if that is unacceptable to product — but never copy
ciphertext into a node with a different access chain.
**Impact if wrong** — duplicating a project silently clones production credentials into a
folder with different permissions, and the audit trail shows a `node.create`, not a
credential distribution.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `secret_documents(node_id)` | `CASCADE` | Ciphertext must not outlive the container that scopes its permission check. A purge of the document is the only thing that reaches here, and it must take the values. |
| `environment_id` | `environments(id)` | `RESTRICT` | E-109 must refuse deleting a referenced environment with `ENVIRONMENT_IN_USE`. Silently repointing a production credential's label is worse than a 409. |
| `rotated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | "Who last rotated this" must not become null; users are deactivated, not deleted. |

**Unique Constraints**

- `UNIQUE (node_id, key)` — the duplicate-key rule enforced in the schema, not only in the
  service. The service still checks first so the error is `SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE` (400) with
  the offending key named, rather than a constraint violation.
- `UNIQUE (node_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` — a whole-list replace
  renumbers every row inside one transaction and would transiently collide against an
  immediate constraint.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `secrets_pkey (id)` | E-103, E-104 — reveal or copy by secret id. |
| `UNIQUE (node_id, position)` | E-101's ordered list read — the order is the stored order (`src/types/devtools.ts:87`). |
| `UNIQUE (node_id, key)` | The duplicate check on E-102. |
| `(environment_id)` | E-109's referenced-check; "which credentials point at Production". |

**Check Constraints** — `key` non-empty after trim and free of whitespace, `=`, `"`, `'`;
`position >= 0`; `octet_length(value_iv) = 12`; `octet_length(value_auth_tag) = 16`.
There is no `CHECK` that can assert the value is encrypted — that is what the code review
rule under "Encryption at rest" is for.

**Relationships** — N–1 to `secret_documents`, `environments`, `users`. 1–N (logically, not
by FK) to `secret_rotations` and `secret_access_events`, which reference `secret_id` without
a foreign key on purpose — see those tables.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-101 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` → `SecretDocument` | visibility | read-only, **masks only**; no code path returns a value (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:288-299`) | `devtoolsService.getSecrets` → `useSecretDocument` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| E-102 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` → `SecretDocument` | `secret.rotate` (Admin only) | one transaction: validate → upsert/delete rows → `secret_rotations` → `secret_access_events` → `audit_events` | `useSecretEditor.save` | `SECRET_ROTATE_DENIED` (403), `SECRET_KEY_INVALID` (400), `SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE` (400), `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| E-103 | `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/{secretId}/reveal` → `RevealSecretResponse` | `secret.reveal` (Admin only) | **writes the two audit rows before returning, allowed or denied alike**, then decrypts and returns the plaintext once | `useSecretDocument.reveal` / `.copy` / `.take` | `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` (404), `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` (403), `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` (429) |
| E-104 | `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/copy` → `CopySecretsResponse` | `secret.reveal` | one permission check, **one audit row per key**, values assembled server-side | `useSecretDocument.copyMany` | `SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY` (400), `SECRET_NOT_FOUND`, `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` |
| E-095 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions` | visibility | read-only, served from `secret_rotations` | `SecretVersionsDialog` | — |

**E-103 request body** — `{ "action": "reveal" | "copy" }`. `copy` has **no permission key
of its own**: it is gated by `secret.reveal` and filed in the workspace log as
`secret.reveal`, because "copying is a read of plaintext… only an actual write to the
stored value is a rotation" (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`). The two are kept
apart in `secret_access_events.action` because they carry different risk: reveal puts a
value on a screen for thirty seconds, copy puts it on a clipboard indefinitely
(`src/types/devtools.ts:90-96`).

**E-104** returns `{ text, keys }` — `KEY=value` lines ready for the clipboard, plus the
key list so the caller can say how many without reading any value
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:405-410`). The `.env` text quotes a value **only** where
leaving it bare would change it — leading/trailing whitespace, a newline, a `#`, or empty —
escaping `\\`, `"`, `\n`, `\r` (`src/lib/env-file.ts:131-153`). `secretIds` requires
`minItems: 1` (canon OQ-66): the frontend's "empty means every secret" default
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:400-401`) is an unsafe wire default, and "Copy all" must
send the full id list explicitly.

**Reveal is the only door plaintext comes through**, and it is rate-limited per user
(`SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED`, 429) with the counter in Redis. Who may open it is Admin
only — `secret.reveal` and `secret.rotate` are in the `ADMIN` addition set
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:66-75`) and neither is in `OWNER_ESCALATIONS`
(`:102-108`), so **owning a secret document does not let you read it**. Canon OQ-23 settles
the PRD's "Admin/Manager" against the frontend's Admin-only in favour of the frontend.
`secret.reveal` is also in `READ_ONLY_KEYS`, so it survives the trashed / frozen / locked
narrowing layers (§2.10).

**Realtime** — none, deliberately. See `secret_documents`.

### Table: `secret_rotations`

**Purpose** — the append-only record that a key changed, by whom and when. It is what
`GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions` serves for a secret document, projected into `VersionEntry`
with `hasSnapshot: false`. **It has no value column and must never acquire one.** The
frontend's history is a projection of the *current* entries
(`src/lib/versions.ts:45-62`), which means a deleted secret vanishes from its own history
and a key rotated three times shows once; this table is what fixes that (canon OQ-67).

**Who creates a record** — E-102 `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets`, one row per changed entry
and one per removed entry, inside the save transaction. Nothing else, ever. There is no
update endpoint and no delete endpoint.

**Lifetime** — append-only for the life of the secret document; cascaded away only by a
permanent purge of the node. No `UPDATE` and no `DELETE` grant on the table.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `VersionEntry.id`. |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | with `version` | Owning secret document. |
| `version` | `BIGINT` | no | — | with `node_id` | `VersionEntry.version`. A per-document counter that only increases, maintained with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on `secret_documents` (§1.4). Removing a key never re-issues its number. |
| `secret_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | The entry this concerns. **Deliberately not a foreign key** — a removal writes a row for a secret being deleted in the same transaction (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:554-558`), and the whole point is that the record outlives the row. |
| `key` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | The key **as it stood at that moment**. A snapshot, not a join, because keys are renamable and "when was `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` last rotated" must stay answerable after it is renamed. |
| `change_kind` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | Internal only, never on the wire: `added`, `renamed`, `rotated`, `removed`. Exists so `summary` can be rendered consistently and so a credential review can filter. See Chapter notes. |
| `summary` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `VersionEntry.summary`, rendered at write time — `rotated DATABASE_PASSWORD`, `removed SANDBOX_API_KEY`. Follows the `row_activity` precedent of storing the rendered string (canon T-14, OQ-51). |
| `rotated_by` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `VersionEntry.author`. From the session (C-09). |
| `rotated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `VersionEntry.createdAt`. |

**There is no `content`, `blocks`, `value`, `before` or `after` column, and no JSONB.**
That is the table's defining property, not an omission. `VersionEntry.hasSnapshot` is
returned as the literal `false` and `lines` as `[]`; the version dialog then hides View,
Compare and Restore entirely (`src/components/versions/version-list.tsx:84`) and shows the
standing notice "Rotation history only. Secret values are never held by this client, so
there is nothing here to compare or restore — reveal a value from the vault instead"
(`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:140-141`).

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `secret_documents(node_id)` | `CASCADE` | The history is a property of the document. A purge takes it; nothing else can. |
| `rotated_by` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | "By whom" is the question this table exists to answer; it must not become null. |
| `secret_id` | *(none)* | — | **No FK on purpose.** A `removed` row is written for a secret that is deleted in the same statement; a foreign key would make the correct write impossible. |

**Unique Constraints** — `UNIQUE (node_id, version)`.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `secret_rotations_pkey (id)` | Fetch one entry. |
| `UNIQUE (node_id, version DESC)` | E-095's cursor page on `(version DESC)` (§6.3). |
| `(node_id, key, rotated_at DESC)` | "When was this key last rotated, and by whom" — the exact question a quarterly credential review asks, and the one the frontend's projection cannot answer after a rename. |

**Check Constraints** — `version > 0`;
`change_kind IN ('added','renamed','rotated','removed')`; `btrim(key) <> ''`.

**Relationships** — N–1 to `secret_documents` and `users`. Logically N–1 to `secrets`,
**intentionally unenforced**.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-095 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions` → `VersionPage` of `VersionEntry`, every entry with `hasSnapshot: false` and `lines: []` | visibility | read-only | `SecretVersionsDialog` → `useVersionHistory` with `restore: null` (`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:155`) | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| E-096 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}` | visibility | — | not called for secrets | **`VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE`** (409) — a secret version has no snapshot and can never be read as one |
| E-097 | `POST .../restore` | — | — | not called for secrets | `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` (409) |
| E-098 | `.../diff` | — | — | not called for secrets | `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` (409) |
| E-102 | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` | `secret.rotate` | writes here in the save transaction | `useSecretEditor.save` | — |

**Realtime** — none.

### Table: `secret_access_events`

**Purpose** — the secret document's own trail: every reveal, copy and rotation, **allowed
and denied alike**, with who, when and from which address, and **no values**. It is what the
right-hand panel renders as `SecretAuditEntry[]`
(`src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx`). It exists beside `audit_events` rather
than instead of it because the panel is a per-document view and the workspace log is a
per-tenant one; canon OQ-68 decides both are written, in one transaction.

**Who creates a record** — E-103 (reveal, and copy-one), E-104 (copy-many, one row per key),
E-102 (rotate, one row per changed or removed entry). Every one of those also writes an
`audit_events` row in the same transaction.

**Lifetime** — append-only. No `UPDATE`, no `DELETE` grant, no soft-delete column. Cascaded
away only by a permanent purge of the node.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | `SecretAuditEntry.id`. |
| `node_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | Owning secret document. |
| `secret_id` | `UUID` | yes | `NULL` | no | `SecretAuditEntry.secretId`. **Not a foreign key**, for the same reason as `secret_rotations.secret_id`. |
| `key` | `TEXT` | no | — | no | `SecretAuditEntry.key` — the key name at that moment, and **the only thing about the value that is ever recorded** (`src/types/audit.ts:36`). |
| `action` | `secret_action` | no | — | no | `reveal`, `copy` or `rotate` (`src/types/devtools.ts:97`). |
| `outcome` | `audit_outcome` | no | — | no | `allowed` or `denied`. **A denied attempt is recorded exactly as carefully as an allowed one** — "a refusal nobody can see is not a control" (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:343, 361`). |
| `actor_id` | `UUID` | no | — | no | `SecretAuditEntry.actor`. From the session, never the body (C-09). |
| `ip` | `INET` | no | — | no | `SecretAuditEntry.ip`. **Server-sourced from the socket, never accepted from a client** (`src/types/devtools.ts:106`; `src/types/audit.ts:32`). |
| `at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | `SecretAuditEntry.at`. |

No `detail` column: the four detail strings are fixed, value-free and derived from
`(action, outcome)` at render time (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:566-571`) —
"Stored value replaced. The value itself is not recorded." / "Value placed on the clipboard
once. Not stored by the client." / "Value returned once and cleared from the client on a
timer." / "Refused: the role does not hold the permission for this action."

**The two-sink mapping, exactly as implemented** (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:363-396`):

| Operation | this table's `action` / `outcome` | `audit_events.action` | `audit_events.severity` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reveal, allowed | `reveal` / `allowed` | `secret.reveal` | `warn` |
| Reveal, refused | `reveal` / `denied` | `secret.reveal` | `error` |
| Copy (single or bulk), allowed | `copy` / `allowed` | `secret.reveal` | `warn` |
| Copy, refused | `copy` / `denied` | `secret.reveal` | `error` |
| Rotate / rename / add / delete | `rotate` / `allowed` | `secret.rotate` | `warn` |

**Ordering matters.** On a refusal the audit rows are written **before** the 403 is
returned, and they are committed even though the request fails — so the audit write is a
separate committed transaction from the (non-existent) business write, not a rollback
casualty. On a bulk copy refusal, one row is written **per chosen key** before the single
403 (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:436-444`).

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-68)** — `SecretAuditEntry` cannot distinguish an allowed access from a
denied one.
**Evidence** — the interface has no `outcome` field (`src/types/devtools.ts:99-108`), and
the mock smuggles the distinction into the address string as
`` `${ip} (denied)` `` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:379`), which the panel then
renders verbatim (`src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx:53`).
**Recommendation** — return `ip` as the bare address and add `outcome: AuditOutcome` to
`SecretAuditEntry`. The field is additive, today's client ignores it, and the panel can
then badge a denial instead of reading it out of a malformed IP.
**Impact if wrong** — either the API keeps emitting a fake IP string forever, or denials
become invisible in the one panel a security reviewer opens.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | `secret_documents(node_id)` | `CASCADE` | The trail is a property of the document. Note the consequence: purging a secret document destroys its access trail. The workspace-level `audit_events` rows survive, and they are the compliance record (OQ-27); this table is the panel's convenience view. |
| `actor_id` | `users(id)` | `RESTRICT` | The actor is the record. |
| `secret_id` | *(none)* | — | No FK on purpose: a rotate row is written for an entry deleted in the same statement. |

**Unique Constraints** — none. Two identical reveals a second apart are two facts.

**Indexes**

| Index | Query it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `secret_access_events_pkey (id)` | — |
| `(node_id, at DESC, id DESC)` | E-105 `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/audit?cursor=&limit=` — the cursor page (§6.3). |
| `(actor_id, at DESC)` | Forensics ("everything this account revealed last Tuesday") and the fallback for the reveal throttle. The live throttle counter is in Redis; this index is what answers the question after the fact. |

**Check Constraints** — `btrim(key) <> ''`.

**Relationships** — N–1 to `secret_documents` and `users`; logically N–1 to `secrets`,
unenforced.

**APIs that use it**

| # | Endpoint | Permission | Transaction | Frontend caller | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-105 | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/audit?cursor=&limit=` → `SecretAccessPage` of `SecretAuditEntry` | `secret.reveal` | read-only | `SecretAuditPanel` via `devtoolsService.listSecretAudit` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| E-102, E-103, E-104 | write here | see each | inside the operation's transaction | — | — |

**Realtime** — none.

### Table: `environments`

Canon T-26. **RECOMMENDATION — OQ-63.**

**Purpose** — the deployment-label list, defined once and pointed at from everywhere.
`ENVIRONMENT_OPTIONS` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:28-35`) is three `SelectOption`s —
Development (cyan), Staging (amber), Production (red) — and the Bug, QA and API board
templates plus every config and secret document reference that one list rather than
re-declaring it (`docs/BOARD.md:434-441`). It is a table rather than a constant because
a workspace that deploys to four environments should not need a release to say so.

**Shape follows `SelectOption` exactly**, because the frontend renders these through the
board's own select chip and has no second control for them
(`src/components/devtools/environment-picker.tsx:17-21`).

**Who creates a record** — seeded with the three built-ins when a workspace is created;
after that, E-107 `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/environments`.

**How long it lives** — for the life of the workspace, unless explicitly deleted.

**How it is deleted** — E-109 `DELETE /environments/{environmentId}`, **refused while
anything still references it**. See Delete Behavior.

**Columns**

| Column | PostgreSQL Type | Nullable | Default | Unique | Description |
| ------ | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `id` | `UUID` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | PK | Projects to `SelectOption.id`. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | — | composite | |
| `label` | `TEXT` | no | — | composite | `Development`. Case-insensitively unique per workspace. |
| `color` | `select_color` | no | `'slate'` | no | The shared `SelectColor` enum — the same one board select options use, so a chip looks the same wherever it is drawn. |
| `position` | `INTEGER` | no | — | no | Display order. Not alphabetical: Development / Staging / Production is a pipeline, and sorting it by name would read as nonsense. |
| `is_production` | `BOOLEAN` | no | `false` | no | Marks the environment that needs manage rights to select. **Load-bearing** — see below. |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now()` | no | |

**`is_production` replaces a hard-coded id, and must.** The frontend currently identifies
Production by literal comparison against `PRODUCTION_OPTION_ID = "env_2"`
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:36`), and gates the move behind manage rights with a
confirmation (`environment-picker.tsx:13`). Once these ids are database UUIDs that string
matches nothing, and the gate silently stops firing — a permission check that fails open.
The flag moves the decision to the server, where it can be enforced rather than compared.
**This is a required frontend change, not an optional one**, and it is the single migration
risk in this table.

**Primary Key** — `id`.

**Foreign Keys**

| Column | References | ON DELETE | Why that behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `workspaces(id)` | `CASCADE` | |

**Unique Constraints** — `environments_label_uniq UNIQUE (workspace_id, lower(label))`. Two
environments called "Staging" and "staging" are one environment typed twice.

**Indexes**

| Index | Type | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `environments_pkey` | btree, unique | |
| `environments_label_uniq` | btree, unique, expression | the uniqueness above |
| `environments_list_idx (workspace_id, position)` | btree | E-106, the only list read. Bounded by construction — canon caps this list as "natural, no pagination" |

**Checks** — `CHECK (btrim(label) <> '')`. At most one production environment per workspace
is enforced by a partial unique index rather than a check:
`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX environments_prod_uniq ON environments (workspace_id) WHERE is_production`.

**Delete Behavior** — hard delete, **refused while referenced**. There is no FK to refuse it
with, because the references live inside JSONB (`board_rows.cells` for a select cell whose
column is the environment list) and in `config_documents.environment_id` and
`secrets.environment_id`. E-109 therefore counts references itself and returns `409` with the
count when it finds any. This is the one place in the schema where referential integrity is
enforced in the service rather than by a constraint, and it is called out here so it is not
mistaken for an oversight: the alternative is either a scan-based FK PostgreSQL cannot
express over JSONB, or a `SET NULL` that would silently un-label every affected record.

**Relationships** — N-1 to `workspaces`. Referenced by `config_documents.environment_id` and
`secrets.environment_id` (both real FKs, `RESTRICT`), and — softly, through JSONB — by any
board select cell whose column was seeded from this list.

**APIs that use it** — E-106 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/environments` (membership;
returns `Environment[]` in `position` order), E-107 create, E-108 `PATCH`, E-109 delete. The
three writes require `workspace.manage` under OQ-63.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-63)** — whether the list is workspace-editable at all, or stays the three
fixed labels the frontend compiles in today. The recommendation is a table, because the
alternative makes a fourth environment a deployment; but if product says three is the answer
forever, this table collapses to seed data and `is_production` is still required.
