### 6.8 System operations

```ts
type BulkActionId  = "status" | "assign" | "move" | "archive" | "restore" | "delete" | "export";
type BulkSkipReason = "archived" | "not_found";                 // snake_case; see the note
type ImportInvalidPolicy = "skip" | "blank";
type ImportStep    = "upload" | "mapping" | "validation" | "result";   // UI only
type MappingTargetKind = "ignore" | "existing" | "create";
type ExportFormat  = "xlsx" | "csv" | "pdf";
type ExportScope   = "board" | "view" | "selection";
type DiffKind      = "same" | "added" | "removed";              // deliberately no "changed"
```

| Enum | Postgres | Stored at / used at | FE sends these exact strings? | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BulkActionId` | **never stored** | the bulk-action bar; maps to E-074…E-077 and E-086 | **Never as a field.** It selects the *endpoint*, it is not a body parameter | Seven actions the selection bar offers (`src/types/system.ts:15`). `status` and `assign` are both E-074 with different `values` |
| `BulkSkipReason` | **JSONB — no type** | `BulkResult.skipped[].reason` in the E-074…E-077 response body | **Receives only.** | Why a selected record was left untouched. **snake_case.** `archived` is the rule the client can prove; per-row permission refusals *"report through this same channel rather than a second one"* (`src/types/system.ts:22-24`), so **`permission_denied` is added as a third member** rather than a parallel array (canon §2.7) |
| `ImportInvalidPolicy` | `import_invalid_policy` | `import_jobs.invalid_policy` | **Not today.** `importRows({ boardId, rows })` sends only pre-built cells (`src/services/board-service.ts:1183-1186`) — the policy is applied client-side. E-085 adds it to the body | What to do with a value the column cannot parse. **Default `skip`** *(OQ-41)* |
| `ImportStep` | **never stored — UI only** | the four-step import dialog | **Never crosses the wire.** Canon §2.7 marks it UI-only | Wizard position. There is no partial-import resume; E-085 is *"one transaction"* |
| `MappingTargetKind` | **JSONB — no type** | `ColumnMapping.target.kind` in the E-084/E-085 body | **Yes, sends.** | A tagged union *"so 'ignored', 'into an existing column' and 'into a column this import creates' cannot overlap and a half-set target cannot exist"* (`src/types/system.ts:76-84`) |
| `ExportFormat` | `export_format` | `export_jobs.format` | **Yes, sends** (E-086 body). The frontend generates the file client-side today *(OQ-42)* | Three writers over one projection (`src/lib/xlsx.ts`, `src/lib/csv.ts`, `src/lib/pdf.ts`) |
| `ExportScope` | `export_scope` | `export_jobs.scope` | **Yes, sends.** | Entire board · the current view · the selection. **`view` includes the active search term**, not only filters and sort (`src/types/system.ts:151-152`) — a backend that reproduces only the filters exports a different set |
| `DiffKind` | **JSONB — no type** | `DiffLine.kind` in the E-098 response | **Receives only.** | *"There is deliberately no `changed`; a modification is `removed` + `added`"* (canon §2.7, `src/types/system.ts:223`). A backend that emits `changed` breaks the renderer, which colours additions green and deletions red and has no third colour |

**Server-side upload state — RECOMMENDATION, not the client's enum.**

```ts
/** uploads.state. The server's view of an in-flight upload. RECOMMENDATION — no FE counterpart. */
type UploadState = "pending" | "completed" | "aborted" | "expired";
```

`upload_state` is a Postgres enum on `uploads.state` (T-32). It is **not** `UploadStatus` (§6.9),
which is the client-side queue's own vocabulary and never reaches the server. `expired` is set by the
reaper on `expires_at`; `aborted` by E-112; `completed` by E-111.

### 6.9 Documents, devtools and files

```ts
type BlockType =
  | "heading1" | "heading2" | "heading3" | "paragraph" | "quote"
  | "checklist" | "bulletList" | "numberedList"
  | "code" | "image" | "attachment" | "link" | "table" | "embed";          // 14 → 9 interfaces
type TextualBlockType =
  | "heading1" | "heading2" | "heading3" | "paragraph" | "quote"
  | "checklist" | "bulletList" | "numberedList";                          // the 8 with a `text` field
type CodeLanguage =
  | "plaintext" | "typescript" | "javascript" | "json" | "sql" | "bash" | "python" | "go";
type ConfigFormat =
  | "json" | "env" | "yaml" | "javascript" | "typescript" | "jsx" | "tsx"
  | "html" | "xml" | "css" | "sql" | "shell" | "dockerfile" | "nginx" | "text";
type SecretAction    = "reveal" | "copy" | "rotate";
type DocumentActionId =
  | "pin" | "unpin" | "lock" | "unlock" | "duplicate" | "move" | "archive" | "restore" | "delete";
type UploadStatus    = "queued" | "uploading" | "success" | "error" | "cancelled";   // client queue
type FilePreviewKind = "image" | "pdf" | "text" | "sheet" | "unsupported";
type SaveStatus      = "idle" | "saving" | "saved" | "error";                        // UI only
```

| Enum | Postgres | Stored at / used at | FE sends these exact strings? | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BlockType` | **JSONB — no type** | `documents.blocks[].type`, `document_versions.blocks[].type` | **Yes, sends.** Every E-092 `DocumentDraft` carries the whole array | 14 values collapsing into **9** interfaces (§5.5.2). `BLOCK_TYPE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`, `400`, when the body does not match its `type` |
| `TextualBlockType` | **never stored separately** | a narrowing of `BlockType`: the 8 blocks that hold a single editable `text` field | **Yes**, as part of `BlockType` | `TextualBlock["type"]` (`src/types/document.ts:113-115`). It is a *derived* union — do not create an eighth-member Postgres type |
| `CodeLanguage` | **JSONB — no type** | `documents.blocks[].language` on `code` blocks **only** | **Yes, sends.** | Eight highlighter grammars. **Not the same list as `ConfigFormat`** and must not be conflated: `CodeLanguage` is for a code *block inside a page*; `ConfigFormat` is for a config *document* |
| `ConfigFormat` | `config_format` | `config_documents.format` | **Yes, sends.** `saveConfig({ nodeId, content, format, environmentOptionId, isAutosave })` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:142-144`) | 15 values. **Closed by design**: *"a document cannot be saved in a language nothing can colour, and every branch that switches on it is checked exhaustively at build time"* (`src/types/devtools.ts:13-17`). An unknown format is `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN`, `400` — **never stored as free text**. The wire field is `format`, never `language`: *"it is what the field has always been called and what the stored documents carry. The UI says 'Language'"* (`:19-21`) |
| `SecretAction` | `secret_action` | `secret_access_events.action` | **Yes, sends.** `revealSecret({ nodeId, secretId, role, action })` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:333-335`); E-103 body is `{ action: "reveal" \| "copy" }` | *"`reveal` and `copy` are both reads of plaintext and are kept apart because they carry different risk: one puts a value on a screen for thirty seconds, the other puts it on a clipboard indefinitely. `rotate` is the write"* (`src/types/devtools.ts:90-95`). **`copy` has no permission key of its own** — gated by `secret.reveal`, audited as a reveal (G-17). E-103 accepts only `reveal` and `copy`; `rotate` reaches the trail through E-102 |
| `DocumentActionId` | **never stored — UI menu** | the document actions menu | **Never crosses the wire.** | Nine menu items. It is not a wire enum, **but it is the exhaustive list of document endpoints owed**: E-093 (pin/unpin), E-094 (lock/unlock), E-027 (duplicate), E-026 (move), E-030/E-031 (archive/restore), E-032 (delete) |
| `UploadStatus` | **never stored** | `UploadTask.status` in `src/store/upload-store.ts` | **Never crosses the wire.** The server sees `uploads.state` instead | Client-side queue state. `cancelled` maps to `AppErrorCode` `cancelled` (C-12), which is *"never a response"* |
| `FilePreviewKind` | **never stored** | the discriminant of `FilePreview` in the E-114 response | **Receives only.** | Five branches. **`unsupported` is a `200` outcome, not an error** — `FilePreview { kind: "unsupported", reason }` (canon §4.3). Strategy is decided by **extension first, MIME second** (`src/lib/preview-strategy.ts:5-9`) |
| `SaveStatus` | **never stored — UI only** | the save indicator | **Never crosses the wire.** | `idle` / `saving` / `saved` / `error`. The autosave debounce's own state |

**`FilePreview.text.language` — RECOMMENDATION.** It is a bare `string` in the frontend
(`src/types/file.ts:25`). **Type it as `ConfigFormat` on the wire**, derived server-side from
`file_assets.extension`, defaulting to `"text"` *(OQ-76)*. That makes the text previewer and the
config editor share one highlighter vocabulary instead of two.

### 6.10 Collaboration, search and insights

```ts
type NotificationReason = "mention" | "assigned" | "comment" | "watch" | "system";
type NotificationTab    = "all" | "mentions" | "assigned" | "following";           // UI only
type SearchResultKind =
  | "document" | "api" | "bug" | "qa" | "row" | "file" | "comment" | "place";
type MyWorkWidgetId   = "assigned" | "mentioned" | "dueToday" | "overdue" | "recentlyUpdated";
type DashboardWidgetId = "task" | "qa" | "deadline";
type TaskBucketId     = "todo" | "doing" | "review" | "done";
type QaBucketId       = "passed" | "failed" | "blocked";
type DeadlineBucketId = "overdue" | "today" | "thisWeek";
type DashboardBucketId = TaskBucketId | QaBucketId | DeadlineBucketId;             // 10 values
type BodySegmentKind  = "text" | "mention" | "record";                             // UI only
```

| Enum | Postgres | Stored at / used at | FE sends these exact strings? | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NotificationReason` | `notification_reason` | `notifications.reason` | **Yes, sends** as `?reason=` on E-129 | Five reasons. **The API filters by `reason`, never by tab name** *(OQ-90)*. Note: nothing in the frontend emits `assigned`, `watch` or `system` today — only `mention` and `comment` are produced, both by the comment fan-out *(OQ-89)* |
| `NotificationTab` | **never stored — UI only** | `src/lib/notifications.ts:7-13` | **Never crosses the wire.** | The four-to-five mapping lives in the frontend: `all → null`, `mentions → [mention]`, `assigned → [assigned]`, `following → [watch, comment]`. *"Inbox tabs are a projection of `reason`, not a second field on the record — one notification can never disagree with the tab it lands in"* (`:3-6`) |
| `SearchResultKind` | **never stored** | `SearchGroup.kind` in the E-133 response | **Receives only.** | Eight buckets. `api`/`bug`/`qa` are **derived from `boards.template_id` at read time** (`src/services/search-service.ts:39-43`); `row` is every other record; `place` is a folder or project. This is the projection §3.1.1 describes — not a schema |
| `MyWorkWidgetId` | **never stored** | `MyWorkWidget.id` in the E-134 response | **Receives only.** | Five widgets, each with `items` (capped at `MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6`) **and** `total` (uncapped) *"so '12 of 40' stays honest"* (`src/types/collab.ts:143-144`) |
| `DashboardWidgetId` | **never stored** | `DashboardWidget.id` in the E-135 response | **Receives only.** | Three readings of the same record set — task progress, QA outcome, deadlines |
| `TaskBucketId` | **never stored** | `DashboardBucket.id` | **Receives only.** | Four buckets, each claiming a **set of lowercased status labels** (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:29-54`) — e.g. `done` claims `done, complete, completed, closed, resolved, fixed, verified, shipped, released`. *"A label no bucket claims is reported as `unmapped` rather than quietly folded into the nearest one — a count you cannot trace is worse than a gap"* (`:11-18`) |
| `QaBucketId` | **never stored** | `DashboardBucket.id` | **Receives only.** | `passed` / `failed` / `blocked`. `isQaBoard` reads the *options* for `passed` or `failed` (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:92-99`) |
| `DeadlineBucketId` | **never stored** | `DashboardBucket.id` | **Receives only.** | `overdue` / `today` / `thisWeek`, over a `DASHBOARD_WEEK_DAYS = 7` horizon. Compared **by calendar day** (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:106-120`) *(OQ-92 — which timezone defines "today" is unresolved)* |
| `DashboardBucketId` | **never stored** | the union of the three above — 10 values | **Receives only.** | A derived union, not a fourth vocabulary. Do not create a Postgres type |
| `BodySegmentKind` | **never stored — UI only** | the parsed form of a comment body | **Never crosses the wire.** | `text` / `mention` / `record`. The **raw** body is what is stored; parsing happens client-side for rendering, and server-side only to extract `mentioned_user_ids` (C-2) |

**`RelationType` — reserved and deliberately not defined.** The brief asked for one; the frontend has
no such enum, and inventing one violates ground rule 3. A relation is a **relation-type column** whose
`RelationConfig` names a target board (`src/types/board.ts:152-160`); a "blocked by" dependency is a
relation column *named* "Blocked by", shipped by the `task` template
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:188`). Containment (`parentRowId`) and relation *"live side by side and
never read each other's data"* (`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:12-16`). **No chapter may introduce a
`RelationType` enum or a typed edge kind without resolving OQ-45.**

### 6.11 Enums that live only inside JSONB

These have **no Postgres type**. They are enforced by the request-schema validator at the API
boundary and by nothing else. Listed with the exact path so a validator author has no guessing to do.

| Enum | JSONB path | Column |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CellValueKind` | `$.<columnId>.kind` | `board_rows.cells` |
| `SelectColor` | `$.options[*].color` | `board_columns.config` (select) |
| `ConditionOperator` | `$.options[*].availability..conditions[*].operator` | `board_columns.config` (select) |
| `ConditionConjunction` | `$.options[*].availability..conjunction` | `board_columns.config` (select) |
| `UnavailableOptionBehavior` | `$.unavailableBehavior` | `board_columns.config` (select) |
| *(the literal `"allow-list"`)* | `$.transitionRules.mode` | `board_columns.config` (select) — a **one-member union**, *"left open for a future deny-list"* (`src/types/board.ts:91-92`). Validate it as a constant, not as an enum |
| `FilterOperator` | `$[*].operator` | `board_views.filters` |
| `SortDirection` | `$[*].direction` | `board_views.sorts` |
| `CellDisplayMode` | `$.<columnId>` | `board_views.column_display` |
| `BlockType` | `$[*].type` | `documents.blocks`, `document_versions.blocks` |
| `CodeLanguage` | `$[*].language` (code blocks only) | `documents.blocks`, `document_versions.blocks` |
| `MappingTargetKind` | `$[*].target.kind` | request bodies only (E-084, E-085) |
| `BulkSkipReason` | `$.skipped[*].reason` | response bodies only |
| `DiffKind` | `$.lines[*].kind` | response bodies only |
| `PermissionKey`, `WorkspaceRole` | `$.permissionKey`, `$.effectiveRole` | `audit_events.context` (internal, never returned) |

**Two mandatory JSONB validator rules that are not "is it a member".**

1. **`board_rows.cells[columnId].kind` must not be forced to equal `board_columns.type`.** B-3. The
   validator checks the tag is a `ColumnType` *member* and stops there.
2. **`"__empty__"` is a reserved option id** and must be rejected as a user-authored
   `options[].id` — `OPTION_ID_RESERVED`, `400` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:27-28`). It is legal as
   a **key** inside `transitionRules.transitions`, where it stands for the empty bucket.

### 6.13 The error vocabulary

Registered in §4, not here, but named so the count reconciles:

- **`AppErrorCode`** — 8 lowercase members (`permission_denied`, `not_found`, `network`,
  `validation`, `upload_failed`, `conflict`, `cancelled`, `unknown`), `src/types/async.ts:2-10`.
  **Never stored.** It is the frontend contract and is **frozen**: `use-embedded-board.ts:140`
  branches on `error.code === "not_found"` and `src/services/errors.ts:31` derives `isRetryable`
  from it. **The frontend receives these and never sends them.**
- **`ErrorReason`** — 104 SCREAMING_SNAKE members, canon §4.3. **RECOMMENDATION**, never stored,
  additive on the wire; the frontend ignores it today.

Neither is a Postgres type. Both are §4's registry.

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

These are places where I followed canon exactly and believe canon should be adjusted, or where two
parts of canon disagree and I had to pick one. None of them changed what I wrote — canon was
followed in every case.

1. **Canon §2.1 says the wire field is `node.kind`; the frontend reads `node.type`.** The rename of
   `DriveNodeType` → `NodeKind` is fine as a *type* name and as a *column* name. But
   `src/types/node.ts:81, 89, 96, 108, 117` declare the JSON field as `type`, and the five guards at
   `:138-142` plus every `switch` in `src/lib/node-visuals.ts` and `src/lib/archive.ts:56-68` read
   `node.type`. Emitting `kind` on `DriveNode` breaks all of them. I documented the enum as
   `NodeKind`, the column as `nodes.kind`, and the wire field as `type` (§6.4). Canon §2.1's phrase
   *"the wire field is `node.kind`"* should say *"the column is `nodes.kind`; the wire field stays
   `type`"*.

2. **T-10 lists `name` on `boards`; §8.8's position on OQ-30 says the node owns `name` and it is
   projected.** The same conflict exists for `documents.title` (T-18), `config_documents.name`
   (T-20) and `secret_documents.name` (T-22). I followed §8.8 — one name, on `nodes`, projected into
   all four shapes — because `summarize()` (`src/services/document-service.ts:160-171`) already
   keeps them in sync from one source and two writable copies would drift. The registry lines for
   T-10, T-18, T-20 and T-22 should drop `name`/`title`.

3. **§8.8's OQ-47 position and C-01 cannot both be read literally.** *"Four built-ins as seed rows
   with `is_builtin = true`; user templates as additional rows with UUID ids"* implies the built-ins
   have non-UUID primary keys, which C-01 forbids ("no exceptions"). I resolved it with
   `board_templates.id UUID PK` + `builtin_id board_template_id NULL UNIQUE`, and had the API project
   the slug for a built-in and the UUID for a user template — which is exactly why canon types the
   wire field `BoardTemplateId | string`. §8.8 should say *"…with a `builtin_id` naming which
   built-in it is"*.

4. **The `documents.md` fact sheet puts `kind` (`page|config|secret`) on `documents`; canon puts the
   per-kind extras on `nodes` (§1.3.1).** I followed canon: `nodes.document_kind`, nullable, absent
   meaning `page` (`src/types/node.ts:44, 144`). Chapters that inherited the fact sheet's placement
   will need correcting, because a `config` node has **no** `documents` row at all — its content is
   in `config_documents`.

5. **The `documents.md` fact sheet uses pre-canon table names** — `drive_nodes`, `secret_entries`,
   `secret_audit_events`. Canon's names are `nodes`, `secrets`, `secret_access_events`. I used
   canon's throughout. Worth a one-line warning at the top of the fact sheet so no chapter copies the
   old names out of it.

6. **Canon §1.3.2 requires four generated columns on `board_rows` "derived from the column the board
   designates for that role", and no such designation exists anywhere.** This is the only place I
   had to propose a new column to make a canon requirement implementable — `boards.assignee_column_id`
   / `due_column_id` / `status_column_id`, written up as the OQ-48 block in §3.3.4 with the existing
   regex kept as a fallback. If the editor prefers not to add them, §1.3.2's generated columns must
   be downgraded to expression indexes over a fixed column *name*, and the trade-off table's
   "Filter / sort on a column" row needs rewriting.

7. **Canon §1.4 lists `deleted_at` on `board_rows`, but no endpoint in §3 sets it** — E-065 and
   E-076 are described as deletes with no trash surface. I wrote it as the OQ-15 block (§3.3.4) and
   documented the column. Either §3.8 should say the delete is soft with a 30-day sweep and no user-
   facing trash, or §1.4 should drop `board_rows` from the soft-delete list.

8. **`environments` (T-26) and `ENVIRONMENT_OPTIONS` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:28-37`) are the
   same three labels in two places.** The Bug, QA and API board templates ship Development / Staging
   / Production as *select options with hard-coded ids* (`env_0`, `env_1`, `env_2`, and
   `PRODUCTION_OPTION_ID = "env_2"` at `:37`), while config documents and secrets reference the
   `environments` table. DV-ENV-21 says the list is defined once. Nothing in canon says how the two
   reconcile at instantiation — whether a board created from the Bug template gets options carrying
   the workspace's `environments.id` values or the literal `env_0`/`env_1`/`env_2` seeds. I did not
   invent a rule; §5.5.3 flags that the two lists must agree. This may deserve its own OQ id.

## 7. API Conventions

Everything in this section binds every endpoint in every chapter. Where canon has already decided a
rule (§6, P-01 … P-10, C-01 … C-15) it is reproduced here with its grounding rather than
re-litigated.

### 7.1 Base URL and versioning

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Base path** | `/api/v1`. Every path in this document is relative to it (P-01). |
| **Versioning** | A breaking change is a **new path prefix** — `/api/v2`. Never an `Accept-Version` header, never a `?version=` parameter (P-01). A version negotiated in a header is invisible in a log, in a CDN cache key and in a browser network panel. |
| **Additive changes do not bump the version** | New optional response fields, new enum members on a UI-only enum, and new realtime frame types ship inside `v1`. The client already tolerates the last of these — "Additive: unknown types are ignored" (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`). |
| **Origin** | One origin for the whole API. The SPA is a static bundle (`next.config.ts:6`) and reaches exactly one host. |
| **The client learns the origin from one constant** | Mirror `src/config/base-path.ts`, whose doc comment states the rule: *"`next.config.ts` and the client both need this… Declaring it twice is how they drift"* (`:1-7`). The API base URL gets the same treatment — one exported constant, injected at build time, never inlined at a call site. |
| **`/health`** | `GET /api/v1/health` → `HealthResponse`, unauthenticated (E-140). It is the only unauthenticated `GET`. |

### 7.2 Resource naming

| # | Rule | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N-1 | Collections are **lowercase, plural, kebab-case nouns**. No underscores, no camelCase in a path segment (P-02). | `/workspaces`, `/nodes`, `/boards`, `/board-templates`, `/access-rules`, `/environments` |
| N-2 | Path parameters are `{camelCase}` and carry a **UUID** (P-02). | `/nodes/{nodeId}`, `/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` |
| N-3 | Nesting is **at most one level below the owning aggregate** (P-03). | `/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` is legal. `/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/cells/{columnId}` is **not** — cell writes are batched through E-066. |
| N-4 | **Content is entered through its node, then addressed by its own id** (P-04). `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` returns a snapshot carrying `board.id`; every board sub-resource then hangs off `/boards/{boardId}`. The same split applies to documents. | Grounded: the frontend derives a board id from a node id today (`src/services/board-service.ts:120-126`), and the API returns **both** so nothing re-derives either (OQ-30). |
| N-5 | A **verb is a path segment only where REST cannot express the operation**, and it is always `POST` (P-05). The complete whitelist: `/reveal`, `/convert`, `/reorder`, `/restore`, `/duplicate`, `/move`, `/resolve`, `/read-all`, `/complete`, `/accept`, `/bulk/*`, `/import`, `/import/plan`, `/export`, `/links/resolve`. | `POST /boards/{boardId}/columns/reorder` |
| N-6 | Session-scoped collections live under **`/me`** (P-06). The user id is **never** a path or body parameter. | `/me`, `/me/watches`, `/me/notifications`, `/me/work`. This is C-09 expressed in the URL grammar: today `userId` is a request parameter on watches, notifications and My Work (OQ-19), and that must not survive. |
| N-7 | Method semantics (P-07): **`PUT`** replaces a whole resource or sets a boolean sub-resource; **`PATCH`** merges a partial; **`POST`** creates or performs an action; **`DELETE`** removes or clears. | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` (set) · `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` (clear) · `PATCH /boards/{boardId}` (partial) |
| N-8 | Plural interface names are forbidden, and so are `I`-prefixes, `Dto`/`Model`/`Entity`/`Data`/`Info` suffixes, and bare `Payload` (canon §5.1). | `BoardRow`, not `IBoardRowDto`. `CreateRowRequest`, `RowPage`. |

### 7.3 The success envelope — there isn't one

**The body *is* the resource, the list, or the page object.** This is not a style preference; the
frontend's stores assign a response directly.

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/boards/9a2e.../rows/3f1c...
{
  "id": "3f1c8b1e-4a3e-4d21-9a2f-7c1d2e5b8a90",
  "boardId": "9a2e0c74-1f88-4a6b-b3d1-2f4e6a8c0d11",
  "displayId": "TASK-042",
  "sequence": 42,
  "cells": { "col_status": { "kind": "select", "optionIds": ["opt_2"] } },
  "parentRowId": null,
  "revision": 7,
  "archivedAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-27T09:31:12.004Z",
  "createdBy": "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"
}
```

Grounding, checked against the source rather than inferred:

- Every service returns the **bare payload** — `Promise<BoardRow>`, `Promise<WorkspaceDocument>`,
  `Promise<readonly SavedView[]>` (`src/services/board-service.ts:1383-1414`). There is no
  `{ data: … }` wrapper anywhere in `src/`.
- The async layer assigns it straight in: `setData(data)` sets the resource state to
  `successState(data)` (`src/hooks/use-async-resource.ts:86-89`), and `reconcileRows` overwrites by
  id (`src/store/board-store.ts:350-352`).
- An envelope would therefore be unwrapped in exactly one place and never used again. Envelopes earn
  their keep when responses carry cross-cutting metadata; here the only such metadata is pagination,
  and the `<Noun>Page` shapes already carry it.

Two consequences that are easy to get wrong:

1. **A list endpoint returns a bare JSON array**, not `{ "items": [...] }` — unless it paginates, in
   which case it returns the `<Noun>Page` object (§7.6).
2. **Every write returns the authoritative record** (C-10). No `204` where the frontend expects an
   object. The exceptions — the endpoints that genuinely return `204` — are `POST /auth/logout`
   (E-002), the favourite set/clear pair (E-028/E-029), member removal (E-015/E-016), invitation
   and environment deletes (E-109), permanent trash delete (E-038), upload abort (E-112) and
   workspace delete (E-011). Nothing else.

### 7.4 The error envelope

**Errors, and only errors, are wrapped:** `{ "error": AppError }`. This shape is not a proposal —
`interface BoardError { readonly error: AppError }` is declared at `src/types/board.ts:508-510` and
is the only error wrapper the frontend has.

```jsonc
// 409 PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/document
{
  "error": {
    "code": "conflict",
    "message": "This page is locked",
    "detail": "Unlock it before saving further changes.",
    "isRetryable": false,
    "reason": "DOCUMENT_LOCKED",
    "requestId": "01JB9Z7QF3K8W2N6R4T5Y0X1M3"
  }
}
```

```ts
/** The four fields the frontend reads. EXISTING REQUIREMENT — src/types/async.ts:12-20. */
interface AppError {
  readonly code: AppErrorCode;      // one of eight; see §7.5
  readonly message: string;         // rendered to the user verbatim
  readonly detail?: string;         // OPTIONAL, not nullable — omit the key when absent
  readonly isRetryable: boolean;    // drives the "Try again" button
  // --- additive, RECOMMENDATION; the frontend ignores both today ---
  readonly reason?: ErrorReason;    // SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, canon §4.3 (104 values)
  readonly requestId?: string;      // §7.10
  readonly fields?: readonly FieldError[];  // only on VALIDATION_FAILED
  readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number;      // only on 429; see §7.9
}

interface FieldError {
  readonly path: string;            // JSON pointer-ish: "cells[0].value.iso"
  readonly reason: ErrorReason;
  readonly message: string;
}
```

Rules that go with it:

| # | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E-1 | `code`, `message`, `detail?`, `isRetryable` **must not change**. `use-embedded-board.ts:140` branches on `error.code === "not_found"`; `errors.ts:31` derives the retry default from the code. | `src/services/errors.ts:31` — `DEFAULT_RETRYABLE = { network, upload_failed, unknown }` |
| E-2 | `detail` is **optional, not nullable**. Omit the key; never send `"detail": null`. | `src/types/async.ts:17` (`detail?: string`), C-08 |
| E-3 | `message` is rendered verbatim: a sentence, sentence-cased, no trailing period unless it is two sentences. | canon §4.4 |
| E-4 | `not_found` messages use the fixed template `` `${what} could not be found` ``. | `src/services/errors.ts:36-37` |
| E-5 | **A refusal must not leak the name of what was denied.** `permission_denied` copy is deliberately name-free; the refusal names the minimum role and nothing else. | `src/services/authz.ts:60-66`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-161` |
| E-6 | The **body is authoritative**, the status is advisory: `toAppError` never sees a status code (`src/services/errors.ts:52-64`). Always send a complete `AppError`, even on a `500`. | `src/services/errors.ts:52-64` |
| E-7 | Set `isRetryable` **explicitly** whenever it differs from the §7.5 default — notably `true` on a `429`. | canon §4.4 rule 5 |
| E-8 | `fields` is for developers and support. The user-facing sentence is still `message`. | canon §6.2 |
| E-9 | **Never return an error body for a partial success.** `BulkResult` and `ImportOutcome` are `200` responses reporting what did and did not apply, with `requested === applied.length + skipped.length`. | `src/services/board-service.ts:958-965` — "a bulk write that silently drops a record is worse than one that refuses" |
| E-10 | In production `detail` never carries a stack, a SQL string or an internal identifier. `INTERNAL_ERROR` sends `message: "Something went wrong"` and puts the original text in `detail` **in non-production only**. | canon §4.3, cross-cutting |

### 7.5 HTTP status usage

`AppErrorCode` is frozen at eight values (`src/types/async.ts:2-10`). Status codes map onto them
one-to-one so `toAppError` keeps working.

| `code` | HTTP | Default `isRetryable` | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validation` | **400** | `false` | Malformed request, or a business rule the caller can fix. |
| `permission_denied` | **403** | `false` | Authenticated but not permitted. |
| `not_found` | **404** | `false` | Does not exist **or the caller may not see it** — the two answer identically. |
| `conflict` | **409** | `false` | A precondition or invariant refuses the write. |
| `upload_failed` | **422** / **507** | `true` | 422 = the object did not land or the size mismatched; 507 = the workspace is out of space. |
| `network` | **502 / 503** | `true` | A dependency (object store, database, unfurl target) is unreachable. |
| `unknown` | **500** | `true` | Unclassified server fault. |
| `cancelled` | *never a response* | `false` | Client-side abort only, produced by `toAppError` from an `AbortError` (`src/services/errors.ts:55-57`). **The server must never emit it.** |

Two statuses have no `AppErrorCode` and must be mapped:

- **`401`** → `code: "permission_denied"`, `reason: AUTH_REQUIRED` / `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` /
  `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` / `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED`. The frontend cannot distinguish 401 from 403,
  which is why the refresh flow in §8 is driven by `reason`, not by the status alone.
- **`429`** → `code: "validation"`, `isRetryable: true` **set explicitly**, plus
  `retryAfterSeconds` in the body and a `Retry-After` header (§7.9).

Also in use:

| Status | When | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **200** | Every successful read, every successful write that returns a record, and **every partial success** (bulk, import). | E-9 above. |
| **201** | Not used. A create returns **200** with the record, because the frontend treats a create response identically to an update response (`replaceRow`, `src/store/board-store.ts`). Introducing 201 would add a branch nobody has. | RECOMMENDATION |
| **204** | The eight endpoints listed in §7.3. | |
| **304** | Not used. There is no `ETag`/`If-None-Match` layer in this API; freshness is handled by realtime frames and explicit refetch. | RECOMMENDATION |
| **413** | Body past the service limit → `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`, `code: "validation"`. | canon §4.3 |
| **507** | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — the upload would exceed `StorageQuota.totalBytes`. | canon §4.3, OQ-05 |

**404-vs-403, stated once because it is a security rule.** A node the caller may not *see* answers
`404 NODE_NOT_FOUND`, identically to a node that does not exist. A node the caller may see but may
not *act on* answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. The frontend already reasons this way — the workspace
guard "answers the same way for a workspace that does not exist as for one they are not in, so the
URL cannot be used to find out which workspaces are real" (`src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:22-25`).

### 7.6 Pagination

**Keyset (cursor) pagination is the default and the only style.** `?cursor=&limit=`; the response is
`{ items, nextCursor: string | null }` plus any facets that resource owes. `nextCursor` is an opaque
base64 encoding of the sort-key tuple — **a client must never construct or parse one**. There is no
`page` parameter and no `offset` parameter anywhere in this API.

Two reasons, both concrete. Every paginated collection here is an append-at-the-head log ordered by
time or by a monotonic sequence, where offset pagination re-shuffles items across page boundaries
between requests. And `BoardSnapshot.nextCursor: string | null` is **already in the frontend
contract** (`src/types/board.ts:430-435`) — it is simply always `null` today.

| Resource | Style | Sort key | Extra facets | Why this, here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Board rows (E-047, E-061) | cursor | `(position, id)` | — | `nextCursor` already exists in `BoardSnapshot`. Filtering and grouping run client-side over the loaded set, so the client fetches pages eagerly until server-side query lands (OQ-36). |
| Row activity (E-070) | cursor | `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` | — | Append-at-head; only the newest page is ever read (OQ-52). |
| Comments (E-119, E-125) | cursor | `(created_at ASC, id ASC)` — **oldest first** | reply count per root | A thread reads forwards. Matches the frontend's `upsertComment` ordering. |
| Notifications (E-129) | cursor | `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` | `unreadCount` | Append-at-head, and the badge **must** be server-computed, not "unread among the ones we loaded" (E-132, OQ-91). |
| Audit (E-136) | cursor | `(at DESC, id DESC)` | **`total`** and **`bySeverity`** | The header renders "of N" and the severity facets over the **whole filtered set, not the page** — `AuditPage.total` is documented as "Matches before the limit was applied" (`src/types/audit.ts:50-54`). Default page size `AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE = 40` (`src/config/app.ts:57`). |
| Versions (E-095) | cursor | `(version DESC)` | — | Newest first; a secret's entries carry `hasSnapshot: false` (OQ-67). |
| Secret access trail (E-105) | cursor | `(at DESC, id DESC)` | — | Same shape as audit, scoped to one secret document. |
| **Search (E-133)** | **neither** | `score DESC, title ASC` within each group | — | Capped at `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5` per group (`src/config/app.ts:30`) so one noisy board cannot crowd out a whole result kind (`src/lib/search-index.ts:69-97`). Deep-paging a ranked search is a different feature (OQ-93). |
| **My Work (E-134)** | **neither** | per widget | **`total` per widget** | Each widget returns `MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6` items **and** the uncapped match count, so "12 of 40" stays honest (`src/config/app.ts:39`; `src/types/collab.ts:144`). |
| Dashboard (E-135) | n/a | — | counts only | A pure aggregate; there is nothing to page. |
| Drive tree (E-020) | **neither** | containers first, then the caller's `SortKey` | — | The whole tree, pruned by visibility. Lazy children beyond a depth is the escape hatch if it grows (OQ-13). |
| Members, columns, views, environments, board list, watches, favourites, trash, subtasks, backlinks | **neither** | natural | — | Bounded by construction. If any grows past a few hundred, promote it to cursor — the change is additive. |

**Every unpaginated list endpoint still accepts `?limit=` and enforces a hard server cap. An
unbounded list is a spec defect.** The caps are served from `GET /config` (§7.14) so the client and
server cannot disagree about them.

### 7.7 Filtering and sorting query syntax

**There is no generic filter DSL, and none may be added.** Grounded, not stylistic: the only
server-side filter surface the whole frontend has is `AuditQuery` — five fields
(`src/types/audit.ts:42-48`) — and board filtering is a client-side engine over the loaded row set
(OQ-36). Inventing an OData-style `$filter` would be building a query language for one caller that
does not use one.

**Filters are flat, typed, named query parameters.**

```
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit
      ?module=secret&severity=warn&actorId=1a2b…&search=stripe
      &from=2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z&to=2026-08-27T23:59:59.999Z
      &cursor=eyJhdCI6…&limit=40
```

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **F-1 — one parameter per dimension** | `module`, `severity`, `actorId`, `search`, `from`, `to`. Never a nested or encoded object. |
| **F-2 — an omitted parameter means "no filter"** | The absence of `severity` is not `severity=info`. |
| **F-3 — `"all"` is an accepted synonym for absent** | **Load-bearing.** `AuditQuery.module` is typed `AuditModule \| "all"` (`src/types/audit.ts:43`) and `useAuditLog` sends **all four keys on every call**, `"all"` included (`src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:23`, `:40-48`). An API that rejects `module=all` breaks the audit page's default state. This applies to `module`, `severity` and `actorId`. |
| **F-4 — repeated parameters mean OR** | `?reason=mention&reason=assigned`. Used by E-129. Never a comma-joined string, except where the frontend already sends one — see F-5. |
| **F-5 — the two comma-joined exceptions** | `GET /boards/{boardId}/relation-index?ids=a,b,c` (E-071) and the id lists on bulk bodies. These are id sets, not filters, and E-071 exists precisely so the client makes **one request per target board, never one per cell** (OQ-44). |
| **F-6 — free text is `search=` on a scoped collection, `q=` on a search endpoint** | `search=` filters an otherwise-complete listing (audit). `q=` *is* the query (E-035 drive quick-find, E-069 row search, E-133 global search). The two are not interchangeable: `q=` with an empty value returns an empty array, never the whole collection (`src/services/search-service.ts:56-57` — `if (needle.length === 0) return []`). |
| **F-7 — booleans are `true`/`false` lowercase** | `?includeArchived=true` (E-061), `?dryRun=true` (E-057). Absent means `false`. |
| **F-8 — dates in a query use the same rules as bodies** | An instant filter is ISO 8601 (`from`, `to`); a date-only filter is `YYYY-MM-DD`. §7.12. |

**Sorting: there is no `sort=` parameter anywhere in this API.** Each collection has exactly one
canonical order, defined by its endpoint and listed in the §7.6 table. Two facts make this the right
call rather than a shortcut:

- The frontend's only sort vocabulary for *server* data is `SortKey = "name" | "updatedAt" | "size" | "type"`
  on the drive listing — and canon marks it **UI-only, never persisted server-side** (canon §2.6),
  alongside `ViewMode`. The drive listing is sorted in the browser over a tree it already holds.
- A board's sort lives in `SavedView.sorts: ViewSort[]` (`src/types/board.ts:311-314`) — a
  *stored, shared view definition*, not a request parameter. Multi-level sort with earlier levels
  winning, and nulls sinking to the end in both directions (`VW-SRT-16`), is a property of the saved
  view, applied by the view engine.

If server-side board query lands (OQ-36), sorting arrives as part of *resolving a saved view
server-side* — `GET /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}/rows` — not as a free-form `sort=` parameter on
the row collection.

### 7.8 Idempotency

| Method | Guarantee | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET`, `HEAD` | Safe and idempotent. | Never mutates, never audits — **with one deliberate exception**: `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/restricted-nodes` (E-046) writes an audit row at `warn`, because it is the admin recovery console (OQ-26). |
| `PUT` | Idempotent by construction. | `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite`, `/archive`, `/document/pin`, `/document/lock`, `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document`, `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` — each sets a state, so replaying it lands the same state. |
| `DELETE` | Idempotent. | Deleting an already-deleted thing answers `204` or the same `404` as the first attempt; it never fails differently on the second call. |
| `PATCH` | Idempotent when the patch is absolute (a value), not when it is relative. **Every `PATCH` in this API sets absolute values**; there is no increment/decrement patch anywhere. | `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` writes `CellValue`s, not deltas (`src/types/board.ts:440-444` `CellEdit`). |
| `POST` | **Not idempotent.** Replaying creates a second row. | The five that need protection are listed below. |

**`Idempotency-Key`, on five endpoints only.** Scoping it narrowly is deliberate — a blanket
idempotency layer over 140 endpoints is exactly the over-engineering ground rule 8 forbids.

| Endpoint | Why it needs a key |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows` (E-062) | The counter only increases; a replayed create burns a `TASK-nnn` that is never reissued (`BD-RID-10`). |
| `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` (E-111) | It increments `workspaces.used_bytes` transactionally. A replay double-counts the quota. **And the client has a real retry path**: `retryUpload` replays the same `File` (`src/store/upload-store.ts:154-166`). |
| `POST /comments` (E-120) | One comment insert fans out to auto-watch, mention notifications, watcher notifications, row activity and a realtime frame. A replay duplicates all five. |
| `POST /boards/{boardId}/import` (E-085) | Up to `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5 000` rows in one transaction (`src/config/app.ts:48`). |
| `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` (E-024) | A replay creates a second node with a second slug (`My folder`, `My folder-2`) that the user did not ask for. |

Mechanics:

```
Idempotency-Key: 018f2b1e-7c3a-7e21-9b44-0c9d1e2f3a4b   // client-generated UUIDv4/v7
```

- The server keys on `(user_id, method, path_template, Idempotency-Key)` in **Redis**, TTL **24 h**.
- First call: the record is claimed before the transaction opens; on commit, the serialised response
  body and status are stored against the key.
- A replay while the first call is still in flight → `409 CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT`.
- A replay after completion → the **stored response, byte for byte**, with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
- A replay of the same key with a **different body hash** → `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`.
- The key is optional. Omitting it is legal and means "no replay protection" — the client is
  responsible for not retrying blindly.

**Two writes that deliberately need no key.** `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` (E-066) is
last-write-wins with a `ConflictNotice` and **always answers `200`, never `409`**
(`src/services/board-service.ts:484-513`), so a replay is harmless — it re-applies the same value and
bumps the revision. Bulk writes carry no concurrency token at all and refusals surface as `BulkSkip`
(OQ-55).

### 7.9 Rate limiting

Four buckets, all in Redis, all returning `429` with `Retry-After`. Nothing here is a general
throttle for its own sake; each bucket exists because a specific endpoint is abusable.

| Bucket | Scope | Limit (**RECOMMENDATION** — no frontend evidence sets a number) | `reason` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Authentication** | per source IP **and** per submitted email address, whichever trips first | 10 attempts / 15 min, with exponential back-off after 5 | `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` |
| **Secret reveal / copy** | per user, per workspace | 20 reveals / 5 min | `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` |
| **Link unfurl** (E-118) | per user | 30 / min | `RATE_LIMITED` |
| **General** | per session | 600 requests / min, burst 60 | `RATE_LIMITED` |

The secret bucket is not optional: E-103 already carries "Rate-limited per user" in canon, and
`DV-SEC-23` requires that **every** reveal — allowed or denied — writes an audit entry with IP and
timestamp. A throttled reveal is a denial and is audited as one before the `429` is returned.

Response shape:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 47
RateLimit-Limit: 20
RateLimit-Remaining: 0
RateLimit-Reset: 47
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
```
```jsonc
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation",
    "message": "Too many attempts",
    "detail": "Try again in a minute.",
    "isRetryable": true,
    "reason": "SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED",
    "retryAfterSeconds": 47,
    "requestId": "01JB9Z7QF3K8W2N6R4T5Y0X1M3"
  }
}
```

`isRetryable: true` is set **explicitly**, because the code is `validation` whose default is `false`
(`src/services/errors.ts:31`). Getting this wrong hides the "Try again" button on the one error where
trying again is exactly right.

### 7.10 Request ids

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Header** | `X-Request-Id`. Accepted from the caller if it is a valid ULID or UUID; otherwise minted server-side. Always **echoed on every response**, success and failure alike. |
| **Format** | ULID (26 chars, Crockford base32) — lexicographically sortable by generation time, which makes a log grep trivially ordered. |
| **In the body** | `error.requestId` on every error (canon §6.2 example). Never in `message`; never in `detail`, which is user-facing copy (E-5, canon §4.4 rule 4). |
| **In the log** | Every log line, every audit row's internal `context`, and every realtime frame published as a result of the request carries it. `AuditContext` (canon §5.3) is the internal, never-returned structured payload beside the human `detail`; the request id belongs there (OQ-25). |
| **`X-Correlation-Id`** | Not used. One id, one hop — the API has no downstream service to correlate with. |

### 7.11 Content types

| Direction | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request bodies | `application/json; charset=utf-8` | The **only** accepted request content type. A body with any other type is `415`, mapped to `code: "validation"`, `reason: VALIDATION_FAILED`. |
| Response bodies | `application/json; charset=utf-8` | With four exceptions, below. |
| **Never** | `multipart/form-data`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` | See below — there is no endpoint that takes a file. |

The four non-JSON exceptions, each grounded:

1. **File bytes never reach the API.** Upload is a presigned `PUT` issued by E-110 and executed by
   the browser **directly against the object store**; E-111 only records that it landed. Download is
   a signed URL (E-116, E-117), not a proxied stream. This is why no endpoint accepts
   `multipart/form-data`.
2. **Import posts parsed JSON, not a spreadsheet.** The browser parses `.xlsx`/`.csv`/`.tsv`
   (`src/lib/xlsx.ts`, `src/lib/csv.ts`) and sends an `ImportSource`
   (`src/types/system.ts:67-74`) — headers plus rows of strings. E-084 and E-085 are ordinary JSON
   endpoints. (This is OQ-42; if it is reversed, this rule gains an exception.)
3. **Audit export streams CSV.** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit/export` (E-137) responds
   `text/csv; charset=utf-8` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. The export is itself audited at
   `warn` (OQ-27).
4. **Whole-board export produces a file in object storage**, not a response body. E-086 with
   `scope: "board"` returns an `ExportJob` and a signed URL (OQ-42); `view` and `selection` scope
   return an `ExportOutcome` as JSON and the browser writes the bytes
   (`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts`).

Other headers: `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br` is honoured on responses; a board snapshot is the one
payload where it matters. `Content-Length` is always set; chunked responses are used only for the
CSV export.

### 7.12 Timestamps and dates — the rule that prevents the classic bug

This is the convention most likely to be broken by a well-meaning ORM default, so it is stated with
its reasoning. The frontend maintains an **entire date-key layer** for it, and the module's own
opening paragraph is the specification:

> A due date is a square on a calendar, not a moment. `27 Aug 2026` is the same square in Hanoi and
> in London, and the classic bug — pick the 27th, save it, reload it as the 26th — happens the
> instant that square is turned into a timestamp in one zone and read back in another.
> So the unit here is a `DayKey`: the string `"2026-08-27"`. It has no zone to get wrong, it sorts
> lexicographically, it compares with `===`.
> — `src/lib/calendar.ts:4-13`

| # | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T-1 | **An instant is `TIMESTAMPTZ` in the database and ISO 8601 with a `Z` on the wire**: `2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z`. Always UTC, always three-digit milliseconds. | C-03; `src/services/backend.ts:64-66` `nowIso()` = `new Date().toISOString()` |
| T-2 | **Never `timestamp without time zone`.** Not for `created_at`, not for `deleted_at`, not for `at` on an audit row. | C-03 |
| T-3 | **A date-only value is `DATE` in the database and `YYYY-MM-DD` on the wire, and it must never be converted through UTC** — not on write, not on read, not on comparison, not in an index. | C-04; `src/lib/calendar.ts:20-21` `type DayKey = string` |
| T-4 | **A date-only value is never widened into an instant.** `board_rows` carries **two** generated columns — `due_date DATE` and `due_at TIMESTAMPTZ` — chosen by `DateConfig.includesTime`. They are not one nullable column with a convention. | canon §1.3.2; OQ-32 |
| T-5 | **The server stores the string it was sent.** A `date` cell is `{ kind: "date", iso: string \| null }` (`src/types/board.ts:222`); the API validates the format and persists it verbatim. It does not normalise, re-zone, or round-trip it through a `Date`. | canon OQ-32 position; `src/lib/calendar.ts:143-148` `withDayKey` keeps the time part of an instant when the day changes |
| T-6 | **Comparison of day keys is string comparison.** `compareDayKeys` is `a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0` — "Day keys are fixed-width ISO, so string order is date order" (`src/lib/calendar.ts:198-201`). A `DATE` column indexes and orders the same way. | `src/lib/calendar.ts:198-201` |
| T-7 | **Locale never touches the wire.** `en-GB` and the Monday-first week are *render* choices with their own constants (`DEFAULT_DATE_LOCALE`, `DEFAULT_WEEK_START`, `src/lib/calendar.ts:45-57`); the API sends `YYYY-MM-DD` and ISO 8601 to every caller in every locale. No `Accept-Language` branch. | `src/lib/calendar.ts:37-57` |
| T-8 | **Validation.** A date-only field that is not `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` **and a real calendar date** is `400 DATE_VALUE_INVALID`. The frontend's own parser rejects `2026-02-31` by round-tripping rather than by a month-length table (`src/lib/calendar.ts:106-108`) — do the same server-side. | canon §4.3 `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` |
| T-9 | **The frozen mock clock does not ship.** `MOCK_NOW = "2026-08-26T09:30:00.000Z"` (`src/config/app.ts:10`) is written into `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `joinedAt` and `deletedAt` by the workspace store today. Every one of those becomes `now()` on the server. | `src/config/app.ts:6-10` |

**What is still open.** "Today" and "overdue" are not date-only questions — they need a timezone to
resolve. My Work's `dueToday`/`overdue` widgets and the dashboard's deadline buckets take a
reference instant `nowIso` today (`src/services/my-work-service.ts:52-55`) and bucket against it.
Which zone defines the boundary — the workspace's, the viewer's, or UTC — is **OQ-92**, and no
chapter may pick one unilaterally. Everything in T-1 … T-9 holds regardless of how OQ-92 resolves.

### 7.13 Cancellation and client disconnect

Every frontend service call takes an `AbortSignal` and every abort maps to `cancelled`, never to a
network error (`src/services/backend.ts:13-32`; C-12). `useAsyncResource` drops a cancellation
silently rather than rendering it as an error (`src/hooks/use-async-resource.ts:58-62`). Three
obligations follow for the server:

1. **A disconnected client is not an error.** Log it at `debug`; do not emit a `500`, do not page
   anyone, do not write an audit row for a request that was abandoned before it committed.
2. **Abort the work.** Cancel the in-flight query and roll the transaction back. A long read
   (search, dashboard, a board snapshot) must observe the disconnect.
3. **Never publish a realtime frame for a write that rolled back.** Frames are published inside the
   committing transaction's boundary, not before it (canon §7.1, RT-01: "inside the same transaction
   as the fan-out").

A write that is cancelled after it commits is an unknown outcome to the client. That is safe here
because C-10 makes every write return the authoritative record and every store reconciles from it —
the client's recovery is a refetch, which it already does.

### 7.14 Server-owned limits

Every ceiling the client enforces is served by the API, so the two cannot disagree. This is E-139,
and it is what closes OQ-69 (the file-size ceiling is 25 MB in the frontend and 100 MB in the PRD).

#### `GET /api/v1/config`

**Purpose** — Return the server's own limits and allow-lists so the client's pre-checks match the
server's refusals exactly. Fetched once at boot and cached for the session.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — None beyond a valid session. The values are not workspace-scoped and leak nothing.
**Path Params** — None.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.
**Response** — `AppConfigResponse`.

```ts
interface AppConfigResponse {
  /** OQ-69: 100 MB is the API and storage contract. The 25 MB in
   *  src/lib/file-validation.ts:4 is superseded by this value. */
  readonly maxUploadBytes: number;              // 104857600
  /** Lowercase, no leading dot. Superset of src/lib/file-validation.ts:6-14. */
  readonly acceptedExtensions: readonly string[];
  /** Human hint the uploader renders. Mirrors ACCEPTED_HINT. */
  readonly acceptedHint: string;
  readonly trashRetentionDays: number;          // 30  — src/config/app.ts:42
  readonly importMaxRows: number;               // 5000 — src/config/app.ts:48
  readonly importIssueLimit: number;            // 50   — src/config/app.ts:51
  readonly versionHistoryLimit: number;         // 20   — src/config/app.ts:63
  readonly searchGroupLimit: number;            // 5    — src/config/app.ts:30
  readonly myWorkWidgetLimit: number;           // 6    — src/config/app.ts:39
  readonly auditPageSize: number;               // 40   — src/config/app.ts:57
  readonly boardRowLimit: number;               // OQ-36
  readonly rowHierarchyMaxDepth: number;        // 5    — canon OQ-33
  readonly commentMaxLength: number;
  readonly documentMaxBlocks: number;           // OQ-58
  /** Null while no socket is deployed, which is what keeps the client on its
   *  in-process bus — mirrors REALTIME_ENDPOINT, src/config/app.ts:65-69. */
  readonly realtimeEndpoint: string | null;
  /** Seconds. How long a signed asset URL stays valid (OQ-75). */
  readonly signedUrlTtlSeconds: number;
}
```

**Database** — No reads, no writes. Served from static service configuration, cached in Redis for
the process lifetime.
**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.
**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — Nothing today: the constants are compiled in at `src/config/app.ts` and
`src/lib/file-validation.ts:4-22`. Those two modules become the consumers — they keep their exported
names so no call site changes, and read their values from this response instead of from a literal.
