## 8. Authentication

### 8.1 What the frontend assumes today

Before anything is designed, here is exactly what is there. Every statement below was read off the
source.

**There is one user, and it is a constant.**

```ts
// src/mock/users.ts:3-9
export const CURRENT_USER: UserSummary = {
  id: "usr_khanh",
  name: "Khanh Luu",
  email: "khanhluu95@gmail.com",
  initials: "KL",
  accentColor: "var(--accent)",
};
```

It is imported by **33 files** — every store except `grid-store` and `dnd-store`, plus fourteen
hooks and six components. The places where it stands in for a value the backend must own:

| Site | What it fabricates |
| --- | --- |
| `src/services/authz.ts:44` | **The caller identity the permission check itself resolves.** `contextFor` reads `CURRENT_USER.id` rather than taking a role or a user as an argument. |
| `src/store/workspace-store.ts:273`, `:346`, `:394` | Workspace-membership checks and the visible-workspace list |
| `src/store/workspace-store.ts:529`, `:767`, `:818` | `owner` on every node the client creates |
| `src/store/workspace-store.ts:622` | `deletedBy` on a trashed node |
| `src/store/board-store.ts:374`, `:485` | `createdBy` on an optimistic row |
| `src/store/notification-store.ts:64`, `:84`, `:102`, `:112` | The inbox owner, the mark-read scope, and the recipient filter on incoming realtime frames |
| `src/store/watch-store.ts:58`, `:82` | The watcher identity |
| `src/store/permission-store.ts:68`, `:74` | `grantedBy` on an access rule, and the audit actor |
| `src/hooks/use-comments.ts:86`, `:158` | The comment author, and the self-filter on mentions |
| `src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:83` | `lockedBy` on a locked page |
| `src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:333` | `ACCESS_ACTOR_ID` — "switching to Restricted grants the actor first" |

**There is no authentication of any kind.**

| Thing that does not exist | Checked |
| --- | --- |
| A login route or screen | The `(workspace)` route group has 13 routes; none is `/login` or `/sign-in`. `src/app/(workspace)/layout.tsx:3` calls them "every authenticated surface" — the comment is aspirational. |
| A token, anywhere | Nothing is persisted in the browser but three keys: `nexdrop-recent`, `nexdrop-comment-draft:<key>` and `nexdrop-theme` (`src/store/recent-store.ts:18`, `src/hooks/use-comment-draft.ts:5`, `src/lib/theme.ts:13`). **No auth token, no user id.** |
| An `Authorization` header | No service constructs one. There is no HTTP client at all — `src/services/*` are in-process functions. |
| A refresh flow, a 401 handler, a session-expiry state | `AsyncState` has four states — `idle`, `loading`, `success`, `error` (`src/types/async.ts:23-27`). None of them is "signed out". |
| A credential, session, token, invitation or identity-provider **type** | `src/types/` has none. `UserSummary` (`src/types/user.ts:4-12`) carries `id`, `name`, `email` and two presentation fields. |
| A working sign-out | The Sign out menu item exists and **has no handler** — `<DropdownMenuItem variant="danger">` with an icon and a label and nothing else (`src/components/layout/header/user-menu.tsx:61-64`). |

**Two things do exist, and they are the seams to build against.**

1. **`WorkspaceMember.joinedAt`** (`src/types/user.ts:24`) implies an invitation flow that is
   otherwise unmodelled, and `workspace.member.manage` is described as "Invite people and change
   what role they hold" (`src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:19`). That is OQ-04, not §8's problem, but it
   is the same `identity`/`workspace` boundary.
2. **The audit log already knows what a sign-in looks like.** The seeded trail contains, verbatim:

```ts
// src/services/audit-service.ts:238-247
{
  minutesAgo: 480,
  module: "system",
  action: "system.session.start",
  actorId: "usr_khanh",
  ip: "10.4.19.22",
  severity: "info",
  target: null,
  detail: "Signed in from a new device.",
}
```

   So the *action name*, module, severity and target-shape for a successful login are already
   settled by the shipped fixture. §8.6 uses them unchanged.

**And one constraint that binds the whole design.** The client never learns an IP address:

> Address the mock backend attributes a call to. A real backend reads it off the socket — the
> client must never send one, which is why this lives here and not in any hook.
> — `src/services/audit-service.ts:280-285`

### 8.2 Therefore: authentication is GREENFIELD

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT** — only two things:

- `SY-RBC-42` requires four roles and states that **"a downgrade takes effect on open screens"**.
  That is a hard constraint on the token design and §8.4 is built around it.
- `DV-SEC-23` and `SY-AUD-41` require an actor and an IP on every audited action, both attributed by
  the server.

Everything else in §8 is **RECOMMENDATION** under **OQ-01**, and the block below is written per
ground rule 3.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-01) — there is no authentication, session or token model anywhere in the
> frontend.**
>
> **Evidence** — `src/types/` contains no credential, session, token, invitation or
> identity-provider type. `CURRENT_USER` is a module constant imported by 33 files
> (`src/mock/users.ts:3-9`). The Sign out control has no handler
> (`src/components/layout/header/user-menu.tsx:61-64`). Nothing is stored in the browser but
> Recent, comment drafts and the theme. There is no login route. `src/services/authz.ts:29-33`
> states outright: *"there is no server here."*
>
> **Recommendation** — email + password with Argon2id, a short-lived JWT access token carried in an
> `Authorization: Bearer` header and held **in memory only**, and a rotating opaque refresh token in
> an httpOnly cookie scoped to the refresh endpoint. Sessions live in `user_sessions` (T-02) as
> refresh-token families with reuse detection. **No role, no workspace and no permission claim goes
> into the access token** (§8.4). Federated identity (OIDC/SAML) is an additive provider on the same
> session model, not a second one.
>
> **Impact if wrong** — contained, and this is the reason to proceed rather than block. Nothing else
> in the schema depends on the choice: `users` (T-01) and `user_sessions` (T-02) are the only tables
> involved, no domain table references a session, and no domain endpoint's request body changes.
> What *would* break is the reverse mistake — putting the role or the workspace into the token,
> which silently violates `SY-RBC-42` (see §8.4, R-4) and cannot be undone without reissuing every
> session. Two things must survive whatever is chosen: `WorkspaceMember.joinedAt`
> (`src/types/user.ts:24`) and `DirectoryUser.isActive` (`src/types/user.ts:18-20`), because removed
> members must stay resolvable so their names still render on old assignments
> (`src/mock/users.ts:36-40`).

### 8.3 RECOMMENDATION — the mechanism, and why, against a static-export SPA

**The decision: `Authorization: Bearer` for the access token, held in memory; an httpOnly cookie for
the refresh token, and for nothing else.**

Not a pure-cookie session, and not tokens-in-`localStorage`. The reasoning is specific to the shape
of this client:

| # | Fact about this frontend | What it rules out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| J-1 | `next.config.ts:6` sets `output: "export"`. **There is no server-render path.** The bundle is static HTML served from a CDN; no request the origin serves can read a session cookie and personalise a page. | A pure-cookie session buys nothing on the render path here, which is its main advantage elsewhere. |
| J-2 | The bundle is currently served from a **different origin** than any API will be — GitHub Pages under `basePath: "/Nekotic-Workspace"` (`src/config/base-path.ts:8`). A session cookie would be cross-site: `SameSite=None; Secure`, at the mercy of third-party-cookie blocking. | A cookie-only design that breaks the day Safari or Chrome tightens third-party cookies. |
| J-3 | **Nothing is persisted in the browser today** except Recent, drafts and theme — stated as an invariant, and reinforced by two modules that refuse to store secret plaintext (`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:48-55`, `src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:92-105`). | Putting a long-lived token in `localStorage`, which would be the first XSS-exfiltratable credential in the app. |
| J-4 | Every service already throws a `ServiceError` carrying a UI-ready `AppError` and every call takes an `AbortSignal` (`src/services/errors.ts:4-12`, `src/services/backend.ts:13-32`). One shared HTTP client can hold the access token in a closure and transparently refresh on `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED`. | A per-service auth implementation. There is exactly one place to put this. |
| J-5 | `AsyncState` has no "signed out" state (`src/types/async.ts:23-27`), and a 401 arrives as `code: "permission_denied"` (§7.5). | Relying on the status code alone to trigger a refresh — the client must branch on `reason`. |

**What that produces:**

- **Access token** — JWT, 15-minute TTL, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, kept in a JavaScript
  variable inside the HTTP client and **never** written to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, a
  cookie, or the URL. It dies with the tab, which matches the invariant in J-3.
- **Refresh token** — opaque, 256 bits of CSPRNG entropy, returned only as a cookie:

  ```
  Set-Cookie: nd_refresh=<opaque>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax;
              Path=/api/v1/auth; Max-Age=2592000
  ```

  `Path=/api/v1/auth` means the cookie is not attached to any of the other 136 endpoints, so the
  95 % of requests that are ordinary API calls carry **no ambient credential at all** and are
  structurally immune to CSRF: a cross-site form cannot set an `Authorization` header.

**Deployment consequence, and it is not optional.** For `SameSite=Lax` to work, the SPA and the API
must share a registrable domain — `app.example.com` + `api.example.com`. **RECOMMENDATION:** move
the static bundle off `github.io` onto the product domain before this ships. If that is impossible,
the fallback is `SameSite=None; Secure` with an explicit CORS allow-list (never `*`) and
`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` — and the refresh flow inherits a dependency on
third-party cookies, which is a known decay risk that must be recorded, not discovered.

**CSRF on the one cookie-bearing endpoint.** `POST /auth/refresh` is the only route the cookie
reaches. Three defences, all cheap: `SameSite=Lax` already blocks cross-site `POST`; the endpoint
requires `Content-Type: application/json` (§7.11), which a cross-site HTML form cannot send without
a preflight; and refresh rotation with reuse detection (§8.4, R-6) turns a successful replay into an
immediate family-wide revocation rather than a silent takeover.

### 8.4 The session model

| # | Rule | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **R-1** | **Access token: JWT, EdDSA (Ed25519), 15-minute TTL.** Claims: `iss`, `aud`, `sub` (the user's UUID), `sid` (the `user_sessions` row id), `jti`, `iat`, `exp`. Nothing else. | Short enough that a revoked session dies quickly without a per-request session lookup; long enough that refresh is not on the hot path. Asymmetric signing so a read replica or a future edge check can verify without the signing key. |
| **R-2** | **Key rotation.** Signing keys are published at a JWKS endpoint with a `kid` header; two keys are live at any time (current + previous) so rotation never invalidates a live token. | Standard, and it makes key compromise recoverable in 15 minutes rather than 30 days. |
| **R-3** | **The token is a bearer of identity only.** | See R-4. |
| **R-4** | **No `role`, no `workspaceId`, no permission set in the token — ever.** The effective role is resolved per request from `workspace_members` joined through the node's ancestor chain. | Two independent reasons. (a) `SY-RBC-42` requires that **"a downgrade takes effect on open screens"**; a role baked into a 15-minute token means a demoted admin keeps admin for up to 15 minutes. (b) The role is not a property of the *session*: it is per workspace (`memberRoleOf`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:29-35`) and then per node through inheritance (`effectiveAccess`, `src/services/authz.ts:42-45`). A single claim cannot express it. |
| **R-5** | **Refresh token: opaque, 32 random bytes, base64url.** Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. TTL 30 days sliding, absolute cap 90 days. | Opaque because it is a database lookup anyway — there is nothing a JWT buys here, and a JWT refresh token cannot be revoked without the same lookup. |
| **R-6** | **Rotation with reuse detection.** Every successful refresh issues a new refresh token and marks the old one used. Presenting an **already-used** token revokes the **entire family** and answers `401 AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED`. | This is what makes a stolen refresh token detectable: the legitimate client's next refresh trips the alarm. `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` is already in the canon error registry (canon §4.3). |
| **R-7** | **One `user_sessions` row per device/family.** `GET /me` reports the session's expiry so the client can schedule a proactive refresh instead of discovering expiry through a failed write. | A failed write is the worst place to discover a dead session — the frontend has optimistic row and comment writes that would roll back for a reason that has nothing to do with the write. |
| **R-8** | **Logout revokes the family.** `revoked_at` is set on every row in the family and the cookie is cleared. Sessions on other devices are untouched. | "Sign out" means this device. Signing every device out is a separate, explicit action (not built; **RECOMMENDATION**, out of §8's four endpoints). |
| **R-9** | **A deactivated user (`users.is_active = false`) is refused at both login and refresh**, and every live access token for that user is rejected by a `sid`→session check that reads `users.is_active`. | T-01: users are soft-deactivated, never hard-deleted, so old assignments still render a name. Deactivation must therefore be a *live* check, not a delete. |
| **R-10** | **`previewAs` is never a session concept.** If a role is ever declared on the wire, the server computes `min(serverResolvedRole, declaredRole)` and ignores a declared role that is higher — ignores, not rejects, so a stale tab degrades rather than breaks. | `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:359-360`: *"Role preview is not a session switch. It narrows what the interface offers; it does not re-authenticate, and a reload clears it."* A server-side "act as" mode is one bug away from a privilege-escalation primitive (OQ-21). |
| **R-11** | **Password hashing: Argon2id**, memory 64 MiB, iterations 3, parallelism 4, 16-byte salt. Re-hash transparently on login when the parameters change. | **RECOMMENDATION**, OQ-01. |
| **R-12** | **Login answers identically for a wrong password, an unknown email and a deactivated account**: `401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, same message, same timing (constant-time compare, and a dummy hash verification when the email is unknown). | Canon's own note on the reason: "Email or password wrong. **Same message for both.**" Extending it to deactivation stops the endpoint being an account-status oracle. |

### 8.5 Tables

Two tables carry authentication. `users` (T-01) is defined in full by the identity chapter; the
columns **§8 requires on it** are called out here so they are not lost. `user_sessions` (T-02) is
owned entirely by this section.

```sql
-- T-01 · users · module: identity
-- Columns §8 depends on. The identity chapter owns the rest (name, initials,
-- avatar_url, accent_color, timestamps).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id             UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email          TEXT        NOT NULL,
  -- Argon2id PHC string. NULL only for a user who has never set a password
  -- (invited-but-not-accepted, or federated-only). Login refuses NULL.
  password_hash  TEXT        NULL,
  -- Soft deactivation. Never a hard delete: DirectoryUser.isActive is false and
  -- the name still renders on old assignments (src/types/user.ts:18-20).
  is_active      BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  last_login_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
  created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Case-insensitive, because email is the login identifier.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_email_lower_key ON users (lower(email));
```

```sql
-- T-02 · user_sessions · module: identity · RECOMMENDATION (OQ-01)
-- One row per refresh token. A family is a chain of rows linked by family_id;
-- rotation appends a row, it does not update the old one in place.
CREATE TABLE user_sessions (
  id                  UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id             UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Constant across every rotation of one device's chain. This is what a reuse
  -- detection revokes, and what `sid` in the access token points at.
  family_id           UUID        NOT NULL,
  -- SHA-256 of the opaque refresh token. The token itself is never stored.
  refresh_token_hash  BYTEA       NOT NULL,
  -- The row this one replaced. NULL on the first token of a family.
  parent_id           UUID        NULL REFERENCES user_sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  -- Set the moment this token is exchanged. A second presentation of a row that
  -- already has this set is a replay (R-6).
  used_at             TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
  revoked_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
  -- Why it was revoked, for the audit trail. Never returned to a caller.
  revoked_reason      session_revoke_reason NULL,
  expires_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  -- Hard ceiling on the family, independent of sliding expiry (R-5).
  family_expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  -- Read off the socket and the request headers. NEVER from a request body
  -- (src/services/audit-service.ts:280-285).
  created_ip          INET        NOT NULL,
  user_agent          TEXT        NULL,
  last_seen_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TYPE session_revoke_reason AS ENUM (
  'logout', 'rotated', 'reuse_detected', 'expired', 'user_deactivated', 'admin_revoked'
);

-- Refresh looks a token up by hash and nothing else. This index carries the
-- whole hot path of the endpoint.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX user_sessions_token_key ON user_sessions (refresh_token_hash);
-- Family revocation on reuse detection: one indexed UPDATE.
CREATE INDEX user_sessions_family_idx ON user_sessions (family_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
-- "Sign out everywhere", and the deactivation sweep.
CREATE INDEX user_sessions_user_live_idx ON user_sessions (user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
-- Nightly reaper.
CREATE INDEX user_sessions_expiry_idx ON user_sessions (expires_at) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
```

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| **Cardinality** | `users` 1 : N `user_sessions`. One row per *token*, not per device: a device that has refreshed 40 times has 40 rows sharing one `family_id`. |
| **Foreign keys** | `user_sessions.user_id → users.id ON DELETE CASCADE`. `user_sessions.parent_id → user_sessions.id ON DELETE SET NULL` (self-referential; a reaped ancestor must not take its children with it). |
| **Unique constraints** | `users (lower(email))`; `user_sessions (refresh_token_hash)`. |
| **Delete behaviour** | Sessions are never deleted by an endpoint — they are **revoked** (`revoked_at` + `revoked_reason`). A nightly sweep hard-deletes rows where `expires_at < now() - 30 days`. Deleting a user cascades, but a user is never deleted: R-9. |
| **Retention** | Revoked and expired rows are kept 30 days so a reuse-detection incident is still investigable, then purged. **RECOMMENDATION** — no frontend or PRD evidence sets this; the audit trail's own retention is OQ-27. |
| **Growth** | ~96 rows per device per month at a 15-minute access token and a refresh on expiry. The sweep is what keeps this table small; without it, it is the fastest-growing table in the schema. |

**The one thing not stored here.** No permission, no role, no workspace. A session says *who*, and
the answer to *what may they do* is recomputed from `workspace_members` and `access_rules` on every
request (R-4).

### 8.6 Endpoints

Four endpoints. All four are **RECOMMENDATION** under OQ-01: none exists in the frontend today and
none has a caller. The "Frontend Used By" field says so explicitly and names what must be built,
because a spec that invents a caller is worse than one that admits there is none.

**Canon path note.** The brief for this chapter named the current-user endpoint `GET /api/v1/auth/me`.
Canon registers it as **E-004, `GET /api/v1/me`**, under P-06 ("session-scoped collections live under
`/me`"). Canon is followed; see Chapter notes.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/auth/login`

**Purpose** — Exchange an email and password for an access token and a refresh-token cookie. This is
the only endpoint that reads `users.password_hash`, and the only way a session comes into existence.

**Authentication** — **Not required.** One of exactly two unauthenticated routes, the other being
`GET /health` (E-140).

**Permission** — None. No `PermissionKey` gates it: permission keys are evaluated against a
workspace membership and a node, and at this point the caller has neither. The gate here is the rate
limiter (§7.9, authentication bucket, keyed on source IP **and** submitted email) and R-12's
uniform refusal.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `LoginRequest`.

```ts
interface LoginRequest {
  /** Compared case-insensitively against users.email. Trimmed before lookup. */
  readonly email: string;
  /** 8–256 characters. Never logged, never echoed, never in an error detail. */
  readonly password: string;
}
```

**Response** — `200` with `LoginResponse`, plus the refresh cookie.

```ts
interface LoginResponse {
  readonly user: UserSummary;
  /** JWT. Held in memory by the client. Never persisted (J-3). */
  readonly accessToken: string;
  readonly tokenType: "Bearer";
  /** Seconds until accessToken expires. 900. */
  readonly expiresIn: number;
  /**
   * Which workspace the shell should open, or null when the caller is a member
   * of none. The store no longer falls back to "whatever is first" — a person
   * who holds nothing gets the first-run screen (src/store/workspace-store.ts:1003-1011,
   * src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:33). So the server must name one.
   */
  readonly defaultWorkspaceId: string | null;
}
```

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Set-Cookie: nd_refresh=8f2b…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/api/v1/auth; Max-Age=2592000
```
```jsonc
{
  "user": {
    "id": "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
    "name": "Khanh Luu",
    "email": "khanhluu95@gmail.com",
    "initials": "KL",
    "accentColor": "var(--accent)"
  },
  "accessToken": "eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSIsImtpZCI6IjIwMjYtMDgifQ…",
  "tokenType": "Bearer",
  "expiresIn": 900,
  "defaultWorkspaceId": "7f3e1c22-9b04-4e58-a1d6-3c5b8e2f0a71"
}
```

`user` is a bare `UserSummary` (`src/types/user.ts:4-12`) — `id`, `name`, `email`, `initials`,
optional `avatarUrl`, optional `accentColor`. It is **not** a `WorkspaceMember`: `role` is per
workspace and arrives with the workspace (`src/types/user.ts:22-25`), never with the session (R-4).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `users` | **READ** — `SELECT id, password_hash, is_active, … WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)`. Uses `users_email_lower_key`. |
| `users` | **WRITE** — `UPDATE … SET last_login_at = now(), updated_at = now()`; **and** `password_hash` when Argon2id parameters have changed and the hash is upgraded in place (R-11). |
| `user_sessions` | **WRITE** — one `INSERT`: fresh `id`, `family_id = id`, `refresh_token_hash`, `parent_id = NULL`, `expires_at = now() + 30d`, `family_expires_at = now() + 90d`, `created_ip`, `user_agent`. |
| `workspace_members` | **READ** — `SELECT workspace_id … WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY joined_at ASC LIMIT 1` to resolve `defaultWorkspaceId`. Returns `null` when the caller is a member of none. |
| `audit_events` | **WRITE** — one row: `module: "system"`, `action: "system.session.start"`, `actor` = the user, `ip` off the socket, `severity: "info"`, `target: null`, `detail: "Signed in from a new device."`, `outcome: "allowed"`. Copied verbatim from the shipped fixture (`src/services/audit-service.ts:238-247`). Written **only** on a family's first token; a refresh does not re-audit. |
| `audit_events` | **WRITE on failure** — a denied row with `outcome: "denied"`, `severity: "error"`, `actor` = the matched user when the email resolved, otherwise a system actor, and `detail` naming the *category* only ("Sign-in refused."). **The submitted email must not be written into `detail`** on an unknown-email failure: that would turn the audit log into a list of email addresses people typed. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The `user_sessions` insert, the `users.last_login_at` update and the
`audit_events` insert commit together. A session that exists with no audit row makes `SY-AUD-41`'s
"every sensitive system action is appended" false at exactly the moment it matters. The rate-limit
counter is incremented in Redis **before** the transaction opens and is not rolled back — a failed
attempt must still cost the attacker a token.

**Realtime** — None. No socket exists yet at this point in the flow; the client opens
`GET /realtime?workspaceId=` (E-138) after it has a token and a workspace.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — missing or malformed `email`/`password`; `fields` names which. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` — wrong password, unknown email, **or a deactivated account**. Identical message and identical timing for all three (R-12). |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` |
| 429 | `validation` | `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` — `isRetryable: true` and `retryAfterSeconds` set explicitly (§7.9). |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` — `Could not reach the workspace service`. |

**Frontend Used By** — **Nothing today. There is no login route and no login component.** What must
be built: a public route outside the `(workspace)` group (which renders `AppShell` and therefore
`WorkspaceGuard`, `src/app/(workspace)/layout.tsx:4`), and a shared HTTP client under
`src/services/` that holds the access token in a closure. The client is the natural home because
every service already throws `ServiceError` and takes an `AbortSignal`
(`src/services/errors.ts:4-12`, `src/services/backend.ts:13-32`), so the token and the refresh
interceptor land in one place rather than seventeen.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`

**Purpose** — Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token and a rotated refresh token. This
is what makes a 15-minute access token usable, and it is where a stolen refresh token is detected.

**Authentication** — **Required, but by the refresh cookie, not by an access token.** A caller with
an expired — or entirely absent — access token must be able to refresh; that is the point. If an
`Authorization` header is also present it is ignored.

**Permission** — None. Possession of an unused, unrevoked, unexpired refresh token in a live family
whose user is still `is_active` is the entire check.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `RefreshSessionRequest`. **Browsers send an empty object.** The optional field
exists for a non-browser client (a native app, an integration test) that cannot hold a cookie; when
the cookie is present the field is ignored.

```ts
interface RefreshSessionRequest {
  /** Omitted by every browser caller — the cookie carries it.
   *  Present only for clients with no cookie jar. */
  readonly refreshToken?: string;
}
```

**Response** — `200` with `RefreshSessionResponse`, plus a rotated cookie.

```ts
interface RefreshSessionResponse {
  readonly accessToken: string;
  readonly tokenType: "Bearer";
  readonly expiresIn: number;   // 900
}
```

No `user` object: the caller already has one, and re-sending it on every refresh would make a
15-minute background call carry a payload nobody reads. Profile changes arrive through `GET /me`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `user_sessions` | **READ** — `SELECT … WHERE refresh_token_hash = $1 FOR UPDATE`, on `user_sessions_token_key`. The row lock is what serialises two concurrent refreshes from the same device so exactly one wins. |
| `users` | **READ** — `is_active` on the row's `user_id`. A deactivated user is refused here as well as at login (R-9). |
| `user_sessions` | **WRITE, happy path** — `UPDATE` the presented row: `used_at = now()`, `revoked_at = now()`, `revoked_reason = 'rotated'`. Then `INSERT` a successor with the same `family_id`, `parent_id` = the presented row, a fresh hash and `expires_at = now() + 30d`, capped at the family's `family_expires_at`. |
| `user_sessions` | **WRITE, reuse detected** — the presented row already has `used_at` set. `UPDATE user_sessions SET revoked_at = now(), revoked_reason = 'reuse_detected' WHERE family_id = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL` — one indexed statement over `user_sessions_family_idx`. |
| `audit_events` | **WRITE, reuse detected only** — `module: "system"`, `action: "system.session.revoke"`, `severity: "error"`, `outcome: "denied"`, `detail: "A session was reused and the whole family was signed out."`, `ip` off the socket. A successful rotation writes **nothing**: at ~96 rotations per device per month it would drown the trail (**RECOMMENDATION**; which actions must emit an audit row is OQ-25). |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Revoke-old and insert-new must be atomic: a crash between them
would leave a device with no valid refresh token and a silent forced sign-out. The reuse-detection
path is a single statement plus the audit insert, also atomic.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` — no cookie and no `refreshToken` field. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` — token unknown, past `expires_at`, past `family_expires_at`, revoked, or the user is deactivated. All four answer identically: a refusal must not describe the state of the credential to whoever is holding it. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` — the presented token was already exchanged. **The family is revoked before the response is written.** |
| 429 | `validation` | `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` |

Every `401` from this endpoint clears the cookie (`Set-Cookie: nd_refresh=; Max-Age=0`), so a client
holding a dead token stops re-presenting it.

**Frontend Used By** — **Nothing today.** What must be built: an interceptor in the shared HTTP
client that fires on `error.reason === "AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED"`, refreshes once, and replays the
original request. Three constraints from the existing code:

- It must branch on `reason`, not on status — a `401` reaches the client as
  `code: "permission_denied"` (§7.5), indistinguishable from a real `403`.
- Concurrent 401s must share **one** in-flight refresh, not one per call. The board page issues
  several parallel reads on mount (`use-board.ts`, `use-directory.ts`, `use-comments.ts`).
- A refresh that fails must produce a signed-out state. `AsyncState` has no such state today
  (`src/types/async.ts:23-27`); it belongs above `AsyncBoundary`, at the root, not inside every
  resource.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/auth/logout`

**Purpose** — End this device's session: revoke the refresh-token family and clear the cookie. It
does not touch sessions on other devices.

**Authentication** — **Required — but satisfied by either credential.** A valid access token *or* a
valid refresh cookie is enough. Requiring the access token would mean a user whose token expired
while the tab was idle could not sign out, which is the moment they most want to.

**Permission** — None. A caller can only ever end their own session; the family is resolved from the
presented credential, never from a body.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `204 No Content`, with the cookie cleared.

```
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Set-Cookie: nd_refresh=; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/api/v1/auth; Max-Age=0
```

This is one of the eight endpoints exempt from C-10 (§7.3): there is no authoritative record to
return, and the frontend expects no object.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `user_sessions` | **READ** — resolve the family: by `refresh_token_hash` when the cookie is present, otherwise by the `sid` claim of the access token. |
| `user_sessions` | **WRITE** — `UPDATE user_sessions SET revoked_at = now(), revoked_reason = 'logout' WHERE family_id = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL`. One statement over `user_sessions_family_idx`. |
| `audit_events` | **WRITE** — `module: "system"`, `action: "system.session.end"`, `severity: "info"`, `outcome: "allowed"`, `target: null`, `detail: "Signed out."` **RECOMMENDATION** — the seeded vocabulary ships `system.session.start` (`src/services/audit-service.ts:238-247`) but no matching end, and OQ-25 owns which actions must emit a row. A trail with sign-ins and no sign-outs is hard to read. |

**Transaction** — **Required**, though it is small: the revocation and the audit row commit
together, so a revoked session is never unexplained in the trail.

**Realtime** — None from this endpoint. The socket the client holds (E-138) is closed by the client;
the server also drops any socket whose `sid` has just been revoked, on its next heartbeat.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` |

**Deliberately absent: there is no `401` here.** Logout is idempotent. A request carrying no
credential, an expired one, or an already-revoked one answers `204` — "you are not signed in" is
precisely the state the caller asked for, and a `401` would leave a client with a dead token unable
to clean up. Calling it twice is `204` twice.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/layout/header/user-menu.tsx:61-64`, the **Sign out**
`DropdownMenuItem`, which today has an icon, a label and **no `onSelect` handler**. It gets one. The
handler must also clear the in-memory access token, close the realtime socket, and drop the caches
that survive a re-render — the pattern already exists in `useAccessSync`, which on access loss calls
`boardService.reset()`, `useBoardStore.clear()`, `useGridStore.reset()` and `useRecentStore.clear()`
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:63-68`). Sign-out is the same teardown with the session added.

---

#### `GET /api/v1/me`

**Purpose** — Resolve the caller from their session. This is the first authenticated call the shell
makes and it is what replaces the `CURRENT_USER` constant. **This is E-004; canon places it under
`/me`, not `/auth/me` (P-06).**

**Authentication** — **Required.** Access token in the `Authorization` header.

**Permission** — None beyond a valid session. It returns only the caller's own identity, so there is
nothing to gate — and nothing here is workspace-scoped, so no membership check applies either.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `200` with `CurrentUserResponse`.

```ts
interface CurrentUserResponse {
  /** Exactly src/types/user.ts:4-12. Replaces CURRENT_USER in all 33 importers. */
  readonly user: UserSummary;
  /**
   * Where to open. Null when the caller is a member of no workspace, which is
   * the first-run screen (src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:33) and
   * not an error. The store deliberately no longer falls back to the first
   * workspace in the list (src/store/workspace-store.ts:1003-1011).
   */
  readonly defaultWorkspaceId: string | null;
  /**
   * ISO 8601. When the access token presented on THIS call expires, so the
   * client can schedule a proactive refresh instead of discovering expiry
   * through a failed optimistic write (R-7).
   */
  readonly sessionExpiresAt: string;
}
```

```jsonc
{
  "user": {
    "id": "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
    "name": "Khanh Luu",
    "email": "khanhluu95@gmail.com",
    "initials": "KL",
    "accentColor": "var(--accent)"
  },
  "defaultWorkspaceId": "7f3e1c22-9b04-4e58-a1d6-3c5b8e2f0a71",
  "sessionExpiresAt": "2026-08-27T09:45:00.000Z"
}
```

**What this response deliberately does not carry, and why:**

| Not here | Where it lives | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The workspace list | `GET /workspaces` (E-007) — `Workspace[]`, only those the caller is a member of | `Workspace` carries `members` and `storage` (`src/types/workspace.ts:12-26`); embedding the array here would make a call the shell repeats on every mount carry every member of every workspace. |
| The caller's **role** | `Workspace.members[]` as a `WorkspaceMember` (`src/types/user.ts:22-25`) | Role is per workspace and then narrowed per node by inheritance (R-4). There is no such thing as "the user's role". |
| Capabilities / permission keys | `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/capabilities` (E-044), `GET /permissions/catalog` (E-045) | Resolved per node. A global set would be meaningless and would invite a client to cache it. |
| A refreshed token | `POST /auth/refresh` | `/me` is a read. It never rotates a credential. |

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `user_sessions` | **READ** — by the `sid` claim: confirm `revoked_at IS NULL` and `expires_at > now()`. **This lookup is what makes revocation take effect inside the 15-minute token window**, and it is why the token's signature alone is not the whole check. Cacheable in Redis for ≤ 60 s keyed on `sid`, with the cache entry deleted synchronously on revoke. |
| `users` | **READ** — `id, name, email, initials, avatar_url, accent_color, is_active`. `is_active = false` refuses (R-9). |
| `workspace_members` | **READ** — `SELECT workspace_id … WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY joined_at ASC LIMIT 1`. |
| `user_sessions` | **WRITE (optional)** — `last_seen_at = now()`, throttled to at most once a minute per session so a busy tab does not turn every read into a write. |

**Transaction** — **Not required.** All reads; the `last_seen_at` touch is a single fire-and-forget
statement whose failure must not fail the request.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` — no `Authorization` header, malformed header, bad signature, unknown `kid`. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` — token past `exp`, or its session revoked, or the user deactivated. **This is the reason the client's refresh interceptor branches on.** |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` |

**Frontend Used By** — **Nothing today; `CURRENT_USER` is imported directly by 33 files.** The
migration is mechanical and has one right shape: a single session store (or a React context mounted
above `AppShell`) that holds the `CurrentUserResponse`, exports a `useCurrentUser()` hook, and is
populated before `AppShell` renders — because `WorkspaceGuard` decides membership before anything
inside a workspace mounts (`src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx:49-52`,
`src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:10-16`). Every `import { CURRENT_USER } from "@/mock/users"`
becomes a read from that store. The 33 sites are listed in §8.1.

**Out of §8's scope, same family:** `PATCH /me` (E-005, `UpdateProfileRequest` → `UserSummary`) and
`GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/directory` (E-006, `DirectoryUser[]` — **including deactivated
members, flagged `isActive: false`**, `src/mock/users.ts:36-58`) belong to the `identity` chapter.
They are named here only so nobody builds them twice.

### 8.7 What every other endpoint takes from the session

The single most important consequence of §8, and the reason OQ-16 – OQ-21 are marked critical. Once
a session exists, these five values are **resolved, never accepted**:

| Value | Resolved from | Must be deleted from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userId` / actor | `sub` claim | `WatchService.list/set` (`userId` is a parameter today), `NotificationService.list/markRead/markAllRead`, `MyWorkInput.userId` (`src/services/my-work-service.ts:47-48`), `SearchInput.user` (`src/services/search-service.ts:45-48`) — OQ-19, OQ-20 |
| Effective role | `workspace_members` joined through the node's ancestor chain, per request | `SearchInput.role`, `RevealInput.role` — where a role *is* declared it may only narrow, `min()` never `max()` (R-10, OQ-21) |
| Node visibility | `access_rules` + the ancestor chain, server-side | `ListFilesInput.canView` — the caller currently passes its own visibility predicate (`src/services/file-service.ts:96`, `:105`, `:113` — OQ-18) |
| IP address | The socket / trusted proxy header | Everything. *"A real backend reads it off the socket — the client must never send one"* (`src/services/audit-service.ts:280-285`) |
| The clock | `now()` on the server | `MOCK_NOW` is written into `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `joinedAt` and `deletedAt` by the workspace store today (`src/config/app.ts:10`) |

`owner`, `createdBy`, `deletedBy`, `grantedBy`, `lockedBy`, `recipientId` and `actor` all follow the
same rule: the server stamps them from `sub`. A request body that carries one is ignored, not
rejected — a stale client should degrade, not break.

### 8.8 Open questions this section raises or inherits

| id | Question | Position taken here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OQ-01** | There is no authentication, session or token model anywhere in the frontend. | §8.2 block above. Session-cookie-backed refresh + in-memory JWT access token; identity from the session, never the body. |
| OQ-02 | Is there a tenant above the workspace, and who owns a workspace? | Out of §8. Canon: single tenant, `workspaces.slug` globally unique. `defaultWorkspaceId` therefore needs no tenant scope. |
| OQ-03 | Is there a fifth role, "Super Admin"? | Out of §8, and **it must stay out**: R-4 keeps every role out of the token, so adding a fifth role later is a matrix change and not a session change. |
| OQ-04 | The invitation flow implied by `WorkspaceMember.joinedAt` is unmodelled. | Out of §8; `workspace` module, E-013/E-018/E-019. Note that `POST /invitations/{token}/accept` (E-019) requires an *authenticated* caller, so an invited person signs up or signs in **first** and accepts second. |
| OQ-19 | `userId` is a request parameter on watches, notifications and My Work. | §8.7. Resolved from `sub`; the parameters are deleted. |
| OQ-21 | How does role preview (`previewAs`) reach a real API? | R-10. It does not become a session concept. `min(serverResolvedRole, declaredRole)`, never `max`, and a higher declared role is ignored rather than rejected. |
| OQ-25 | Which actions must emit an audit row? | §8.6 takes a position for three: login **always** (grounded in the shipped fixture), logout and reuse-detection as **RECOMMENDATION**; a successful token rotation emits **nothing**. |
| OQ-65 | How are secret values encrypted, and what is the reveal contract? | Out of §8, but it depends on it: envelope encryption uses a per-workspace data key, and the *reveal* is gated by `secret.reveal` resolved per request — never by a claim in the access token (R-4). |
| OQ-92 | Which timezone defines "today" and "overdue"? | Out of §8. Noted here because a `timezone` column on `users` is the most likely answer and would be a §8-adjacent schema change (§7.12). |

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **`/auth/me` vs `/me`.** The chapter brief asked for `GET /api/v1/auth/me`. Canon registers the
   current-user read as **E-004, `GET /api/v1/me`**, and P-06 makes `/me` the prefix for every
   session-scoped resource (`/me/watches`, `/me/notifications`, `/me/work`). I followed canon and
   documented `GET /api/v1/me`, flagging the divergence inline in §8.6. If the editor prefers
   `/auth/me`, three things change together: E-004's path, P-06's wording, and the `/me/*` family in
   canon §3.20–3.22 — otherwise the API has session data under two different prefixes.

2. **Two response DTOs got fields canon does not specify.** Canon §5.5 names `LoginResponse`,
   `RefreshSessionResponse` and `CurrentUserResponse` but does not define their shapes, so §8.6
   defines them. Three field choices are worth an editor's eye:
   `LoginResponse.defaultWorkspaceId` and `CurrentUserResponse.defaultWorkspaceId` (needed because
   `selectActiveWorkspace` no longer falls back to the first workspace,
   `src/store/workspace-store.ts:1003-1011`); `CurrentUserResponse.sessionExpiresAt` (so the client
   refreshes proactively rather than through a failed write); and the deliberate **absence** of a
   workspace array on both, which assumes E-007 is called at boot.

3. **`session_revoke_reason` is a new Postgres enum** created in §8.5 for `user_sessions.revoked_reason`.
   It is not in canon §2's registry of 68 enums because it never crosses the wire — it is internal,
   like `AuditContext`. If the editor wants canon's enum count to stay exhaustive, it should be
   added there marked *internal, never on the wire*.

4. **`AppConfigResponse` (§7.14) is fuller than canon E-139's summary.** Canon lists eight fields;
   §7.14 adds `acceptedHint`, `importIssueLimit`, `rowHierarchyMaxDepth`, `commentMaxLength`,
   `documentMaxBlocks`, `realtimeEndpoint` and `signedUrlTtlSeconds`, each mirroring a constant the
   frontend already compiles in. If another chapter also defines `AppConfigResponse`, this list
   should be merged rather than duplicated. Note also that every endpoint block in this file uses a
   `####` heading so it nests under its numbered `###` subsection; if the other eighteen files used
   a bare `###`, normalise on assembly.

5. **§7 asserts three things canon states but does not number.** `201` is never used (a create
   returns `200` with the record, because the stores treat create and update responses
   identically); `304`/`ETag` is not used anywhere; and `multipart/form-data` is never accepted,
   because uploads are presigned and import posts a browser-parsed `ImportSource`. All three are
   marked **RECOMMENDATION** in §7.5 and §7.11. If any chapter needs an exception — server-side
   spreadsheet parsing under OQ-42 is the likely one — it must be raised, not assumed.

6. **The `"all"` sentinel on audit filters (§7.7, F-3) is easy to miss and will break the audit page
   if it is.** `useAuditLog` sends `module=all&severity=all&actorId=all` on its very first render
   (`src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:23`, `:40-48`). Any chapter documenting E-136 must accept the
   literal string `"all"` as a synonym for "filter absent".

7. **§2.2 and canon §1.1 need to be read together.** §2.2 lists sidebar collapse, drive view mode,
   drive sort, collapsed groups and column widths as frontend-only *today*, while canon reserves
   `board_view_preferences` (T-16, OQ-46) and `user_ui_preferences` (T-37, OQ-98) for their values.
   §2.2.1 states the distinction explicitly — the grid's cursor is never persisted, a widened column
   is — but if the schema chapter creates T-16 and T-37 without that framing, the two sections will
   look contradictory.

---

## 9. Workspace APIs

Module `workspace` (canon C-14). Endpoints E-007 … E-019 of the registry (canon §3.2). Tables
`workspaces` (T-03), `workspace_members` (T-04), `workspace_invitations` (T-05), joined to `users`
(T-01).

### 9.0 What a workspace is, and the rule every endpoint below inherits

A workspace is the tenant boundary. Every other row in the schema is scoped to exactly one, and
membership of it is **the outermost gate** — the question that comes before any question about a
folder, a board or a role (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`).

Three properties bind all eleven endpoints and are not restated in each one:

1. **"Not a member" is not "viewer".** `memberRoleOf` returns `WorkspaceRole | null` and never a
   default (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:30-36`) — *"A default here is a way in."* A caller with no
   `workspace_members` row holds no role at all; they do not fall through to the bottom of the ladder.
2. **A workspace you are not in and one that does not exist answer identically.** `workspaceAccess`
   returns the same shape for both (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:60-76`), *"so the URL cannot be used
   to learn which workspaces exist."* On the wire that is one reason code for both cases:
   `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` → **404 / `not_found`** (canon §4.3). No endpoint below ever answers `403`
   for a workspace the caller is not in.
3. **The workspace never loses its last admin.** One rule read from three directions —
   demote (E-014), remove (E-015), leave (E-016) — all refuse with `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN`
   (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-162`). *"A workspace with no administrator cannot be repaired
   from inside it."*

**Role ladder.** `viewer` < `member` < `manager` < `admin`; declaration order is the rank
(`src/types/permission.ts:8-20`). The six workspace keys are all Admin-only
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:66-75`): `workspace.manage`, `workspace.settings.view`,
`workspace.member.manage`, `workspace.permission.manage`, `workspace.audit.view`,
`workspace.delete`.

**Identity.** The caller's user id, role and IP come from the session and the socket, never from a
request body (canon C-09, `src/services/authz.ts:24-27`). No endpoint below takes a `userId` in a
body, and `DELETE .../members/me` exists precisely so "leave" never needs one.

---

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces`

**Purpose** — List the workspaces the signed-in user is a member of. This is what the switcher
renders, and it is the only list any surface reads.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Session only. No permission key. The read **starts at membership and joins
outward**: it is not "all workspaces, filtered". `visibleWorkspaces`
(`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:38-50`) states why — filtering a full list in one place *"would leave
every other consumer — a URL, a keyboard shortcut, a stale link — reading the full one."*

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | 100 | Hard server cap 200. Bounded by construction (canon §6.3); no cursor. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly Workspace[]`, ordered `name ASC, id ASC` so the switcher is stable between
requests.

```ts
/** src/types/workspace.ts:12-26 — unchanged. */
interface Workspace {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly description?: string;        // OPTIONAL: omit the key when NULL (canon C-08)
  readonly slug: string;
  readonly plan: WorkspacePlan;         // "free" | "team" | "enterprise"
  readonly badge: string;               // 1–2 chars
  readonly color: string;               // CSS colour
  readonly members: readonly WorkspaceMember[];
  readonly storage: StorageQuota;       // { usedBytes, totalBytes }
}
```

`members` and `storage` are **composed, not stored**: `members` from `workspace_members ⋈ users`,
`storage` from `workspaces.used_bytes` and the plan quota. They are embedded because that is the
frontend's shape (`src/types/workspace.ts:24-25`), and the switcher reads
`workspace.members.length` directly (`src/components/layout/sidebar/workspace-switcher.tsx:108`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | `SELECT workspace_id, role FROM workspace_members WHERE user_id = :session_user` — index `workspace_members_user_idx (user_id)`. This is the driving scan. |
| `workspaces` | READ | `WHERE id = ANY(:ids)` on the PK. Never a full-table scan. |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Second pass on `(workspace_id)` for each returned workspace, to build the embedded `members` array. |
| `users` | READ | `WHERE id = ANY(:member_ids)` for `UserSummary` fields. Deactivated users are still joined — `users.is_active` is not a filter here, because a removed member has no `workspace_members` row at all. |

**Transaction** — Not required. A single read-only snapshot (`REPEATABLE READ` is sufficient if the
member arrays must be consistent with the workspace rows; a default `READ COMMITTED` is acceptable).

**Realtime** — None. The list changes only as a consequence of a membership write, which emits
`permission.changed` (RT-05) and prompts the client to re-read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` — no valid session. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

An empty array is `200`, not `404`. The frontend renders a first-run screen for it
(`src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:33` → `NoWorkspaces`).

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-workspace-access.ts:41-45` (`useMyWorkspaces`), consumed by
`src/components/layout/sidebar/workspace-switcher.tsx:56` and
`src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:30`.

### `POST /api/v1/workspaces`

**Purpose** — Create a workspace and make the caller its first admin, in one write.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Session only. There is no key above this: a person with no workspace must be able to
make one (`src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:38-55` is the screen that offers it).

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. Mirrors NewWorkspaceInput, src/lib/workspace-access.ts:189-194. */
interface CreateWorkspaceRequest {
  readonly name: string;          // trimmed, 1–60 chars (WORKSPACE_NAME_MAX)
  readonly description?: string;  // trimmed, ≤ 280 chars (WORKSPACE_DESCRIPTION_MAX)
  readonly badge?: string;        // 1–2 chars; derived from the name when absent
  readonly color?: string;        // CSS colour; cycles the palette when absent
}
```

Validation is the frontend's, enforced server-side:

- `name` — `validateWorkspaceName` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:200-207`): trimmed length 1…60.
  Empty → *"Give the workspace a name."*; over 60 → *"Keep the name under 60 characters."*
- `description` — trimmed; **stored only when non-empty** (`:233`), so an empty string becomes `NULL`
  and the response omits the key.
- `badge` — when supplied, `trim().slice(0, 2).toUpperCase()` (`:236`); otherwise `badgeFor(name)`
  (`:167-177`: first two letters of a single word, or the initials of the first two words, upper-cased,
  falling back to `"W"`).
- `color` — when absent, `TILE_COLORS[slugsTaken.length % 6]` (`:180-187, :237`). The palette cycles;
  the backend picks from the same six tokens.
- `slug` — **never accepted from the caller.** Minted server-side as
  `uniqueSlug(slugify(name), takenSlugs)` (`:234`) and globally unique (canon OQ-02 position: single
  tenant, no tenant table).
- `plan` — **never accepted.** A new workspace is always `free` with 15 GiB (`:235, :239`).

**Response** — `Workspace`, `201 Created`, with `members` already carrying exactly one entry: the
creator at `admin`.

```jsonc
// 201 POST /api/v1/workspaces
{
  "id": "9f1c2d7a-…",
  "name": "NexDrop Development",
  "description": "Development workspace for NexDrop products.",
  "slug": "nexdrop-development",
  "plan": "free",
  "badge": "ND",
  "color": "var(--accent)",
  "members": [
    {
      "id": "usr_khanh-…", "name": "Khanh Luu", "email": "khanh@nexdrop.vn",
      "initials": "KL", "role": "admin", "joinedAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "storage": { "usedBytes": 0, "totalBytes": 16106127360 }
}
```

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaces` | READ | `SELECT slug FROM workspaces WHERE slug LIKE :base || '%'` to seed `uniqueSlug`. Uses `workspaces_slug_uniq`. |
| `workspaces` | INSERT | `id`, `name`, `description`, `slug`, `plan='free'`, `badge`, `color`, `used_bytes=0`, `storage_limit_bytes=NULL`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by=:session_user`. |
| `workspace_members` | INSERT | `workspace_id=<the row just inserted>`, `user_id=:session_user`, `role='admin'`, `joined_at=now()`, `invited_by=NULL`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.manage`, severity `info`, target = the workspace name, outcome `allowed`. |

**Nothing else is seeded.** No tree, no trash bin, no default folder, no sample board. The frontend is
explicit (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:304-307`): *"A new workspace has no tree and no bin. Seeding
it with either would put somebody else's fixtures inside something a person just made."*

**Transaction** — **Required.** This is the one endpoint in this section whose atomicity is a
correctness property rather than a tidiness preference.

```
BEGIN;
  slug   := uniqueSlug(slugify(:name), SELECT slug FROM workspaces FOR SHARE);
  ws     := INSERT INTO workspaces (...) RETURNING id;
  INSERT INTO workspace_members (workspace_id, user_id, role, joined_at)
       VALUES (ws.id, :session_user, 'admin', now());
  INSERT INTO audit_events (...);
COMMIT;
```

The workspace row and the creator's admin membership **must land or fail together.**
`makeWorkspace` returns the workspace with `members: [{ ...creator, role: "admin", joinedAt }]`
already inside it (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:210-241`) and the comment above it is the
specification:

> The creator's membership is part of *making* the workspace rather than a step after it: a workspace
> whose creator has to be added afterwards has a moment where nobody can administer it, **and a
> failure in between leaves one that nobody can ever administer.**

There is no repair path for that state from inside the product: the members who exist (none) cannot
invite anyone, cannot promote anyone, and cannot delete the workspace, because all three need
`workspace.member.manage` or `workspace.delete` — Admin keys. A workspace whose creator is not a
member must therefore be **unrepresentable**, not merely unlikely. Two mechanisms enforce it and both
are required:

1. The two inserts are in one transaction, as above.
2. A deferred database assertion — `workspaces` is checked at `COMMIT` for the existence of at least
   one `workspace_members` row with `role = 'admin'`. Expressed as a `CONSTRAINT TRIGGER … DEFERRABLE
   INITIALLY DEFERRED` on `workspaces` and on `workspace_members`, it also becomes the enforcement
   for the last-admin rule (E-014/E-015/E-016) rather than a second, separate mechanism. It is not a
   `CHECK`: the invariant is a cross-table count, which `CHECK` cannot express.

On slug collision under concurrency: `workspaces_slug_uniq` raises, the API retries the mint **once**
with the next suffix, and returns `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` if it collides again.

**Realtime** — None. The creator is the only member, and they are the caller; there is nobody to
notify. (Contrast E-019, which does emit RT-05.)

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — name empty, name > 60, description > 280, badge > 2 chars. `error.fields` names the offending path. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` — the mint lost twice. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/create-workspace-dialog.tsx:68`, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:290` (`createWorkspace`).

---

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`

**Purpose** — One workspace, with its members and storage quota embedded.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Membership of `{workspaceId}`. No key. A non-member gets `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, not
`PERMISSION_DENIED` (§9.0 rule 2).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `Workspace`. Identical shape to one element of E-007.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | **Gate first**: `SELECT role FROM workspace_members WHERE workspace_id = :id AND user_id = :session_user` — one probe on `workspace_members_pair_uniq`, ideally index-only via `INCLUDE (role)`. No row → 404 and stop. |
| `workspaces` | READ | PK lookup. |
| `workspace_members ⋈ users` | READ | The embedded `members` array, `(workspace_id)` index. |

`storage.totalBytes` is `COALESCE(workspaces.storage_limit_bytes, quota_for(workspaces.plan))` — the
plan quotas are static service config, deliberately not a `plans` table (canon §1.2, OQ-06).

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown **or** not a member. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/workspace-store.ts:1010` (`selectActiveWorkspace`), read by
`src/components/workspace/workspace-general-tab.tsx:24`,
`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:60`,
`src/components/layout/sidebar/storage-meter.tsx:17` and `src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:71`.

### `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`

**Purpose** — Change the workspace's name, description and switcher tile.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.manage` on the workspace, **plus** membership. Admin-only
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:67`). The frontend renders the fields read-only rather than hiding
them for anybody without the key (`src/components/workspace/workspace-general-tab.tsx:79, 119-127`)
— *"knowing what the workspace is called is not a privilege — only changing it is"* — which is why
`workspace.settings.view` gates the tab and `workspace.manage` gates this call.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. Every field optional — a partial merge (canon P-07). */
interface UpdateWorkspaceRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly description?: string;   // "" clears it to NULL
  readonly badge?: string;
  readonly color?: string;
  readonly plan?: WorkspacePlan;   // RECOMMENDATION — see below
}
```

Merge semantics reproduce `updateWorkspace` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:316-332`) exactly:

| Field | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Applied **only when the trimmed value is non-empty**. `{"name":"   "}` is a no-op, not a validation error. | `:323` — `patch.name?.trim() ? …` |
| `description` | Applied whenever the key is **present**, trimmed. An empty string sets the column to `NULL`. This is the one field where "absent" and "empty" differ. | `:324-326` — `patch.description !== undefined` |
| `badge` | Applied only when non-empty after trim; then `slice(0,2).toUpperCase()`. | `:327` |
| `color` | Applied when truthy. | `:328` |
| `plan` | **RECOMMENDATION.** The frontend never sends it (`NewWorkspaceInput` has no `plan` field, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:189-194`). Accept it only from `workspace.manage`, and expect a billing system to own it in practice. | — |

`slug` is **not** patchable. It is minted at creation and addresses the workspace; re-minting it
would break every stored link, which is the same reasoning that keeps `nodes.slug` fixed on rename
(canon OQ-09 position).

**Response** — `Workspace` — the authoritative record, per canon C-10. Not `204`: the frontend
replaces its optimistic state with the response.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + role, for `workspace.manage`. |
| `workspaces` | UPDATE | Only the columns present in the merged patch, plus `updated_at = now()`. |
| `workspaces`, `workspace_members`, `users` | READ | Re-compose the response. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.manage`, severity `info`, target = the new name, `detail` naming which fields changed. |

**Transaction** — Required, but only to keep the `UPDATE` and its audit row together. No lock is
needed: there is no cross-row invariant here.

**Realtime** — None. **RECOMMENDATION:** none is needed either — a renamed workspace is cosmetic, and
the switcher re-reads on the next navigation. Do not reuse `permission.changed` for it; that frame
means access changed and receivers act on it by dropping loaded data
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — name > 60, description > 280, badge > 2. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — member, but not Admin. `message` = `You do not have permission to manage this workspace`, `detail` = `Needs the Admin role or above` (`src/services/authz.ts:67-74`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:173-176`). |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/workspace-general-tab.tsx:58`, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:316`.

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`

**Purpose** — Destroy a workspace and everything scoped to it.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.delete` on the workspace, plus membership. Admin-only
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:72`). It is the only key that gates the "Danger zone" tab
(`src/components/workspace/workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:34`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Confirmation is a frontend gate, not a wire field.** The danger zone requires the admin to type the
workspace's exact name before the button enables (`src/components/workspace/workspace-danger-zone.tsx:29`
— `typed.trim() === workspace.name`), and the comment says why: *"it is the one confirmation that
cannot be given by muscle memory, and this is the only action in the product that takes a whole tenant
with it."* The API takes **no** `confirmName` field. A server that compares a string the client just
sent verifies nothing about whether a human typed it; the real control is that `workspace.delete` is
Admin-only and the deletion is audited at `error` severity. (This is the position part 4 takes for the
same question — see its `workspaces` table, OQ-02.)

**Response** — `204 No Content`. This is the documented exception to canon C-10: there is no
authoritative record left to return.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.delete`. |
| `file_assets` | READ | Sum `size_bytes` for every asset owned by this workspace, for the audit row's `detail` — recorded **before** the delete, because afterwards there is nothing to count. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.delete`, severity `error`, target = the workspace name, `detail` = counts of nodes, members and bytes destroyed. Written **before** the delete statement. |
| `workspaces` | DELETE | One statement. `ON DELETE CASCADE` takes `workspace_members`, `workspace_invitations`, `nodes` (and through them `boards`, `documents`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents`, `file_nodes`, `access_rules`, `node_favorites`, `trash_entries`), `environments`, `board_templates` (user-authored), `comments`, `watches`, `notifications`. |
| object storage | DELETE | Every `file_assets.storage_key` for the workspace, **after** the database commit, by a background reaper reading a tombstone list. Never inside the transaction — an S3 failure must not roll back a committed delete, and an orphaned object costs money while an orphaned row costs correctness. |

**`audit_events` is the one table that must survive.** It is workspace-scoped and would cascade,
which destroys the record of the destruction. **RECOMMENDATION:** `audit_events.workspace_id` is
`ON DELETE SET NULL` with the workspace's name and id kept in the row's `target` and `context`, so the
trail of a deleted tenant remains readable by an operator. This is a schema decision that belongs to
the `audit_events` table; it is named here because E-011 is the endpoint that depends on it.

**Transaction** — Required. Audit row, byte accounting and the cascade are one transaction. The
object-store sweep is explicitly outside it.

**Realtime** — **RECOMMENDATION:** publish `permission.changed` (RT-05) with
`{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds: <every former member> }` immediately before commit, so open
tabs drop the tree they are holding rather than rendering a workspace that no longer exists
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:19-91`). The frame carries ids only. This is the same frame a
membership change emits; a client that receives it for a workspace it can no longer read falls back
to E-007, finds it gone, and switches (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:346-352`).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not Admin. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` — the database refused; nothing was deleted. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/workspace-danger-zone.tsx:35`, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:338`.

---

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members`

**Purpose** — The people in a workspace, each with the role they hold and when they joined.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Membership. **No key.** Every member may see who else is in the workspace: the
members table renders for everybody and only its *controls* are gated on
`workspace.member.manage` (`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:72, 155-171, 175`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | 200 | Hard cap 500. Unpaginated by construction (canon §6.3); promote to cursor if a workspace ever exceeds it. |

Search is **not** a query parameter. The frontend filters the loaded array on name and email
(`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:74-83`), and the list is bounded, so a server
filter would be a second implementation of the same predicate.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly WorkspaceMember[]`, ordered `roleRank DESC, name ASC` so admins lead.

```ts
/** src/types/user.ts:22-25. Extends UserSummary; carries NO workspaceId — it is
 *  always read in the context of one workspace. */
interface WorkspaceMember extends UserSummary {
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly joinedAt: string;   // ISO 8601
}
```

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | `WHERE workspace_id = :id`, index `workspace_members_pair_uniq` leading column. |
| `users` | READ | `WHERE id = ANY(:member_ids)` → `id`, `name`, `email`, `initials`, `avatar_url`, `accent_color`. |

`isActive` is **not** on `WorkspaceMember` — it belongs to `DirectoryUser` (E-006), and the invite
dialog is careful not to carry it across when building a membership
(`src/components/workspace/invite-member-dialog.tsx:76-85`). Everyone in this response is by
definition current.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None on read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:60` (through
`Workspace.members`), `src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:85-102` (the access dialog's candidate list),
`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:131-134` (one `ResolvedAccess` row per member).

### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members`

**Purpose** — Invite somebody to the workspace at a given role.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.member.manage`, plus membership. Admin-only
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:69`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. */
interface InviteMemberRequest {
  readonly email: string;        // case-insensitive; the invitee need not have an account
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;  // default "member" in the UI
}
```

`userId` is deliberately **not** a field. The frontend picks a `DirectoryUser` and then rebuilds a
`UserSummary` from it (`src/components/workspace/invite-member-dialog.tsx:76-85`), but an address is
the only identifier that works for somebody who has never signed in — which is exactly the case the
frontend refuses to handle and says so on screen (`:167-173`): *"Sending an invitation to an address
is not part of this build — the backend has no invitation flow yet, so adding them silently would be
a lie."*

**Response** — `WorkspaceInvitation`, `201 Created`. **Not** `WorkspaceMember`: nobody has joined yet.

```ts
/** canon §5.3 — RECOMMENDATION, no frontend counterpart (OQ-04). */
interface WorkspaceInvitation {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly email: string;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly invitedBy: string;          // user id, from the session
  readonly expiresAt: string;          // ISO 8601
  readonly acceptedAt: string | null;  // null while pending
}
```

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT vs RECOMMENDATION — state this plainly.** The frontend's dialog performs
`addMember(workspace.id, user, role)` (`:87`) and the person is a full member on the next frame
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:362-367` → `withMember`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:244-259`). There
is no pending state anywhere in `src/`. The invitation table and this response shape are the canon
position on **OQ-04**; the immediate-add behaviour the frontend ships is a mock convenience, not a
requirement. A backend that implements invitations must expect the current client to break on this
one endpoint until it is updated — this is the single largest wire divergence in §9.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.member.manage`. |
| `users` | READ | `WHERE lower(email) = lower(:email)` — to detect an existing account. Not required for the write. |
| `workspace_members` | READ | If the address resolves to a user, `WHERE (workspace_id, user_id)` — already a member → `MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS`. |
| `workspace_invitations` | INSERT | `workspace_id`, `email` (`CITEXT`), `role`, `token_hash = sha256(token)`, `invited_by = :session_user`, `expires_at = now() + 14 days`. The raw token is emailed and never stored. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.member.manage`, severity `warn`, target = the address, `detail` = `Invited as {Role}.` |

The partial unique index `workspace_invitations_pending_uniq (workspace_id, email) WHERE accepted_at
IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL` is what makes a duplicate invite a `409` rather than a second row.

**Transaction** — Required: invitation row + audit row together. Sending the email is **outside** the
transaction and after commit; a delivery failure must not lose the invitation, and the admin can
re-issue.

**Realtime** — None. Nobody's access changed yet. RT-05 fires on acceptance (E-019), not here.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed address, or `role` not one of the four. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not Admin. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` — *"Already a member or already invited"* (canon §4.3). |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED` — invitation spam throttle, `retryAfterSeconds`, `isRetryable: true`. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/invite-member-dialog.tsx:87`, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:362` (`addMember`).

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations`

**Purpose** — Pending invitations, so an admin can see who has been asked and has not yet joined.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.member.manage`, plus membership. **RECOMMENDATION** (canon OQ-04); no
frontend surface reads it today.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeConsumed` | boolean | no | `false` | When true, also returns accepted and revoked rows, for the audit view of who invited whom. |
| `limit` | integer | no | 100 | Hard cap 200. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly WorkspaceInvitation[]`, newest first (`created_at DESC, id DESC`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.member.manage`. |
| `workspace_invitations` | READ | `WHERE workspace_id = :id AND accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()` unless `includeConsumed`. Served by `workspace_invitations_pending_uniq`. |
| `users` | READ | Resolve `invited_by` for display. |

`token_hash` is **never** selected into a response.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — **None today.** The surface that would consume it is
`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx`, which currently renders only current members
(`:142-189`). Building the invitation flow means adding a "Pending" section there.
