### `POST /api/v1/invitations/{token}/accept`

**Purpose** — Turn an invitation into a membership.

**Authentication** — Required. The caller must be signed in; the invitation names an address, and the
session names a person.

**Permission** — Authenticated only. The invitation itself is the authorisation.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | opaque string | The raw invitation token. Never a UUID from the table — the table stores only `sha256(token)`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. Empty today; reserved so the shape can grow. */
interface AcceptInvitationRequest {}
```

**Response** — `Workspace` — the workspace just joined, with `members` already including the caller,
so the client can switch straight into it without a second read.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_invitations` | READ | `WHERE token_hash = sha256(:token) FOR UPDATE`. Assert `accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()`. |
| `users` | READ / INSERT | Resolve the session user. **RECOMMENDATION:** require `lower(session.email) = lower(invitation.email)`, or accept any signed-in user and record the mismatch — see the open question below. |
| `workspace_members` | INSERT | `ON CONFLICT (workspace_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET role = EXCLUDED.role` — re-accepting an invitation for somebody already in is a role change, matching `withMember` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:244-259`). |
| `workspace_invitations` | UPDATE | `accepted_at = now()`, `accepted_by = :session_user`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.member.manage`, severity `warn`, target = the person's name, `detail` = `Joined as {Role}.` |

**Transaction** — **Required, and all five statements are one unit.** A consumed invitation with no
membership behind it is unrecoverable from the UI: the token is spent, the person is not in, and the
admin has no way to see that from
`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx`.

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05) with `{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds: [newMember] }`.
`nodeId` is `null` because the change is workspace membership rather than one node
(`src/types/realtime.ts:26-31`). The new member's visible tree just went from nothing to something,
and the frame is what tells their other open tabs to re-read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `INVITATION_INVALID` — unknown, consumed, revoked **or** expired. All four answer identically so a token cannot be probed for its state. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` — cannot occur here; listed only to record that acceptance never reduces the admin count. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — **None today.** There is no `/invitations/[token]` route in `src/app/`.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-04)** — must the accepting session's email match the invited address?
**Evidence** — the frontend models no invitation at all, so nothing settles it. The dialog's own
refusal text (`src/components/workspace/invite-member-dialog.tsx:167-173`) says the backend has no
invitation flow, and `WorkspaceMember.joinedAt` (`src/types/user.ts:24`) is the only trace that a
moment of joining exists.
**Recommendation** — require the match. An invitation link forwarded to a colleague should not admit
the colleague; the admin chose an address. Where the addresses differ, return `INVITATION_INVALID`
(the same 404 as every other failure, so a forwarded link leaks nothing about who was invited).
**Impact if wrong** — a forwarded or leaked link becomes a workspace-wide access grant to whoever
opens it first, and the audit row names the wrong person as the invitee.

---

### `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}`

**Purpose** — Change one member's role.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.member.manage`, plus membership. Admin-only.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |
| `userId` | UUID | The member whose role is changing. Never the caller's own id implicitly — self-demotion is allowed and goes through this same endpoint, subject to the last-admin rule. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. */
interface UpdateMemberRoleRequest {
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;   // "viewer" | "member" | "manager" | "admin"
}
```

**Response** — `WorkspaceMember` — the updated row, per canon C-10.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.member.manage` for the caller. |
| `workspace_members` | READ | `SELECT user_id FROM workspace_members WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND role = 'admin' FOR UPDATE` — locks the **admin set**, not one row. |
| `workspace_members` | UPDATE | `SET role = :role, updated_at = now(), updated_by = :session_user WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND user_id = :userId`. |
| `users` | READ | Compose the response. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.member.manage`, severity `warn`, target = the member's name, `detail` = `{Name} is now {Role}.` |

**The last-admin guard.** `canChangeRole` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:149-162`):

```
IF :role <> 'admin' AND isLastAdmin(workspace, :userId):
    REJECT WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN
    message: "{workspace.name} would have no admin left. Promote somebody else first."
```

`isLastAdmin` is *"the admin set has exactly one member and it is this person"*
(`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:85-88`).

**Transaction** — **Required, and the lock is not optional.** Without `FOR UPDATE` over the admin set,
two concurrent demotions of the two remaining admins each see one other admin, each pass their own
check, and the workspace commits with zero admins — the unrepairable state E-008's transaction exists
to prevent. Reads of the admin set and the write are one transaction; the deferred constraint trigger
described under E-008 is the backstop.

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05) with
`{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds: [:userId] }`. A demoted user's open board must stop accepting
edits without a reload (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`). The frame carries **ids only** — *"a frame
announcing a revocation must not be the thing that leaks what was revoked"*
(`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`). The same write must bust any server-side authorisation cache keyed
`(workspaceId, userId)`; revocation that takes effect on the next cache expiry is not revocation.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `role` is not one of the four members of `WorkspaceRole`. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not Admin. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (caller not a member) or `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` (target not a member). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:94` (`changeRole`, which
consults `canChangeRole` first at `:88`), through `src/store/workspace-store.ts:369`
(`setMemberRole`).

### `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}`

**Purpose** — Remove somebody else from the workspace.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.member.manage`, plus membership. Admin-only.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |
| `userId` | UUID | **Must not be the caller.** Removing yourself is a different action with a different name and its own endpoint. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `204 No Content`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.member.manage`. |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Admin set `FOR UPDATE`, as in E-014. |
| `workspace_members` | DELETE | `WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND user_id = :userId`. A **hard delete** — there is no soft-deleted membership, because that is exactly the "holds no role but is not absent" state §9.0 rule 1 exists to make impossible. |
| `access_rules` | *(no write)* | User-scoped rules naming the removed person are **left in place** — see the open question. |
| `users` | *(no write)* | The person is untouched. `users.is_active` is a directory-level flag, not a membership one; a removed member still resolves by name on every record they touched (`src/types/user.ts:14-17`). |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.member.manage`, severity `warn`, target = the member's name, `detail` = `Removed from the workspace.` |

**Two guards, both from `canRemoveMember` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:122-146`):**

```
IF :userId == caller.id:
    REJECT — "Use Leave workspace to take yourself out — removing is for other people."
IF isLastAdmin(workspace, :userId):
    REJECT WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN
    message: "{workspace.name} would have no admin left. Make somebody else an admin first."
```

The self-target refusal is not pedantry: E-016 does something this endpoint does not (it switches the
caller out of the workspace they are standing in, below), and folding the two would make it possible
to remove yourself by accident from a control labelled for removing other people. The frontend keeps
them as separate buttons with separate wording for the same reason
(`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:47-58`).

**Transaction** — Required, with the admin-set lock, exactly as E-014.

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05), `{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds: [:userId] }`,
published before the response returns. The removed person's open tabs must drop the loaded tree, the
open board's records and the row cache — *"Those are copies, and a copy does not re-derive itself"*
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:19-91`).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `userId` is the caller. `message` = `Use Leave workspace to take yourself out`, `detail` = `Removing is for other people.` |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not Admin. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` or `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:227` (inside the
`ConfirmDialog`, gated by `confirmRemove` at `:98-106`), through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:388` (`removeMember`).

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-04, membership half)** — what happens to `access_rules` rows naming a person who
has been removed?
**Evidence** — `withoutMember` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:261-263`) drops the membership and
touches no rules. `roleOf` returns `null` for a non-member (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:66-73`),
so a **role-scoped** rule stops matching them immediately; a **user-scoped** rule still matches by id
and `hasGrantOn` would still admit them — but `VisibilityInput.isMember` is `false`, so
`nodeVisibility` refuses at `visibility.ts:161` before the grant is ever consulted. Net effect today:
harmless, and the orphaned rows persist.
**Recommendation** — keep the rows (they are audit evidence and make a re-invite predictable), but
(a) filter non-members out of `resolveAccess` rows so the access dialog does not list ghosts
(`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:131-146` currently derives its subject list from `members`, so
this already holds — assert it), and (b) make membership authoritative in the resolver so a rule can
never be the thing that lets somebody back in.
**Impact if wrong** — deleting the rows loses the record of who was granted what and when; keeping
them *without* membership being authoritative silently restores folder access on re-invite to a
folder nobody re-shared.

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/me`

**Purpose** — Leave a workspace.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Membership. No key: leaving is the member's own action, not an administrative one.
A Viewer may leave; an Admin may leave unless they are the last one.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

The literal segment `me` is the whole point (canon P-06): the user id is never a path or body
parameter, so there is no version of this call that can take somebody *else* out.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `204 No Content`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. Absent → `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (`canLeaveWorkspace` refuses a non-member with *"You are not a member of this workspace."*, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:107-109`). |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Admin set `FOR UPDATE`. |
| `workspace_members` | DELETE | `WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND user_id = :session_user`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.member.manage`, severity `warn`, actor = the leaver, target = their own name, `detail` = `Left the workspace.` |

**The last-admin guard**, `canLeaveWorkspace` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:106-119`):

```
IF NOT isWorkspaceMember(workspace, caller):  REJECT (404)
IF isLastAdmin(workspace, caller):            REJECT WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN
    message: "You are the only admin of {name}. Make somebody else an admin first,
              or delete the workspace."
```

Note the refusal names the remedy, and the remedy is two endpoints: E-014 (promote somebody) or
E-011 (delete the workspace). That sentence is rendered verbatim in the members tab
(`src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:203`).

**What the client does next, and what the server owes it.** `removeMember`
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:388-408`) does two things in one state write when the person leaving
is the caller *and* the workspace is the one they are standing in: it drops the membership **and**
switches them to another workspace they hold — *"so there is no frame in which the app is showing a
tree they no longer hold."* The API cannot switch anything; it returns `204` and the client re-reads
E-007. The server-side obligation is narrower and firm: **publish RT-05 before the response
returns**, so a second tab of the same user converges instead of rendering a stale tree.

**Transaction** — Required, with the admin-set lock.

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05), `{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds: [caller] }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown, or the caller is not a member. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/workspace/workspace-members-tab.tsx:242` (the leave
`ConfirmDialog`, gated by `leaveVerdict` at `:85`), through `src/store/workspace-store.ts:410`
(`leaveWorkspace`, which delegates to `removeMember`).

### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/ownership` — **RECOMMENDATION, not in canon §3.2**

**Purpose** — Hand the workspace's ownership attribute to another admin.

**This endpoint is not in the canon endpoint registry.** Canon numbers 140 endpoints, E-001 … E-140,
and there is no transfer-ownership entry among E-007 … E-019. It is documented here because the
chapter brief asks for it, and it is marked so no reader mistakes it for settled. See "Notes for the
editor".

**What "workspace ownership" even is, first.** The frontend has **no owner concept for a workspace**.
`Workspace` (`src/types/workspace.ts:12-26`) has no `ownerId`, no `createdBy` and no `owner`. The
only thing resembling ownership is the `admin` role plus the last-admin rule, and canon OQ-03 takes
the position that *"the workspace creator is an ownership attribute, not a fifth role."* Part 4's
`workspaces` table gives that attribute a home: `created_by UUID NOT NULL`, present *"so 'who made
this tenant' is answerable"* — and nothing reads it for authorisation.

So transferring workspace ownership means exactly one thing: moving `workspaces.created_by`. It grants
nothing and revokes nothing. **Do not build a version of this that grants anything**, because the
moment `created_by` confers a capability it becomes the fifth role canon OQ-03 rejected.

*(Node ownership — `nodes.owner_id` — is a genuinely load-bearing axis and a different question. It
escalates five keys on your own things (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:102-108`) and always admits you
to a restricted node (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:87-93`). Transferring it is discussed in
§11 under the folder access endpoints.)*

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.delete` on the workspace, plus membership. Deliberately the strongest key
rather than `workspace.member.manage`: it is the key that already means "you may end this tenant", and
ownership is the same class of decision.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** RECOMMENDATION. Named per canon §5.1 (<Verb><Noun>Request). */
interface TransferWorkspaceOwnershipRequest {
  readonly userId: string;   // must be a current member holding role 'admin'
}
```

**Response** — `Workspace` — the authoritative record (canon C-10), whose `members` array is
unchanged. The transfer is visible only in the audit trail and in whatever surface later chooses to
render `created_by`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.delete` for the caller. |
| `workspace_members` | READ | `WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND user_id = :userId` — the target must be a member, and must already hold `role = 'admin'`. Ownership never promotes: promoting is E-014, and doing both in one call hides a role change inside an action named something else. |
| `workspaces` | UPDATE | `SET created_by = :userId, updated_at = now()`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.manage`, severity `warn`, target = the workspace name, `detail` = `Ownership transferred to {Name}.` |

**Transaction** — Required: the `UPDATE` and the audit row together. No lock: `created_by` is not part
of any cross-row invariant, which is precisely because it grants nothing.

**Realtime** — None. Nobody's access changed. Emitting `permission.changed` here would make receivers
drop loaded data for no reason (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `userId` is the current owner (a no-op), or the target is a member but not an admin. `detail` = `Make them an admin first.` |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not Admin. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, or `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` for a target who is not in the workspace. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — **None.** No component reads or writes workspace ownership; the closest
surface is `src/components/workspace/workspace-danger-zone.tsx`, which would be where a transfer
control belongs if one is built.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-02)** — is there a workspace owner at all, and does it confer anything?
**What is unclear** — whether "transfer ownership" means moving an inert `created_by` attribute (as
specified above), or promoting a distinguished principal that outranks `admin`.
**Evidence** — the frontend has four roles and no fifth (`src/types/permission.ts:8-15`,
`WORKSPACE_ROLES`), no `owner` field on `Workspace`, and a last-admin rule that treats every admin as
interchangeable (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:80-88` — `adminsOf` returns a set, and `isLastAdmin` is
a cardinality test, not an identity test). The PRD does mention a "Super Admin" who creates the
workspace (`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:12`, `WS-ARC-02`), which canon records as
**OQ-03** and resolves as *"four roles."*
**Recommendation** — as specified: `created_by` moves, nothing else. If a distinguished owner is
genuinely wanted, it must be a fifth `WorkspaceRole` member and a fifth column of the role matrix
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:77-82`), not a special case bolted onto `admin` — and that is a
change to canon §2.2, not to this chapter.
**Impact if wrong** — if ownership is meant to confer authority, this endpoint is a no-op wearing an
important name, and every "only the owner may…" rule written later will find nothing to hang on. If
it is meant to be inert and is built to confer authority, the four-role matrix silently becomes five
and every permission decision has an undocumented branch.


---

## 10. Project APIs

Module `drive`. **A project is not a table.** It is a row in `nodes` (T-06) whose `kind` is
`project` (canon §2.3, `NodeKind`), and every endpoint in this section is a node endpoint —
E-022, E-024, E-025, E-030, E-031, E-032, E-037 — behaving in the way the `project` discriminant
selects. There is no `/projects` path in canon §3.3 and no chapter may add one.

### 10.0 What the `project` kind actually is

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** PRD `WS-ARC-02` fixes the hierarchy: `Workspace → Project → Folder →
Content`, unlimited projects per workspace, and a project lifecycle of `Active / Archived /
Restored / Moved to Trash` (`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:12`).

In the frontend a project is `ProjectNode` (`src/types/node.ts:80-86`): `DriveNodeBase` plus four
fields.

```ts
interface ProjectNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "project";               // → wire field `kind` (canon §2.1, the one rename)
  readonly description?: string;
  readonly status: ProjectStatus;         // "active" | "paused" | "archived"
  readonly color: string;                 // REQUIRED — unlike FolderNode.color?
  readonly children: readonly DriveNode[];
}
```

Three properties separate it from a folder, and they are the whole difference:

| Property | Project | Folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | **required** (`src/types/node.ts:84`) | optional (`:91`) |
| `description` | optional, present | not on the type |
| `status` | `ProjectStatus`, required | not on the type |
| container | yes (`isContainer`, `:146-147`) | yes |
| sorts first | yes — `TYPE_WEIGHT.project = 0` (`src/lib/tree.ts:247-253`) | `1` |
| archive label | `"project"` (`src/lib/archive.ts:58-59`) | `"folder"` |

Everything else — parenting, slugs, favourites, access modes, archive, trash, move, duplicate — is
the shared `DriveNodeBase` behaviour, and the code path is literally shared: `resolvePath`,
`collectAllowed`, `moveNode`, `cloneNode` and `effectiveAccess` all take `DriveNode` without
narrowing (`src/lib/tree.ts:15-320`, `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`).

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-11, project half)** — the frontend has no way to create a project.
**What is unclear** — whether `POST /workspaces/{id}/nodes` with `kind: "project"` is a real
endpoint the product needs, or whether projects are seed-only structure.
**Evidence** — no component creates one. The sidebar's "Projects" section header carries a `+`
button whose handler is `createFolder(null, "Untitled project folder")` — a **folder** at the root,
labelled `aria-label="New top-level folder"`
(`src/components/layout/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:102-109`). The create menu offers Page, Folder,
Board, Config document, Secret document, Upload — and no Project
(`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:52-143`). The store has `createFolder`,
`createDocument` and `createBoard` and **no** `createProject`
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:181-206`). Every `ProjectNode` in the running app comes from
`src/mock/factory.ts:149-158`, hydrated from four `project(...)` specs in `src/mock/tree.ts:142,
233, 266, 342`. `ProjectStatus` is declared, seeded, and read by **no component** — `grep
ProjectStatus src/` returns the type, the factory and one import.
**Recommendation** — ship the `project` arm of E-024 as specified below. The PRD is explicit that a
user *"có quyền tạo các Project độc lập"* (`WS-ARC-02`), and the tree is already a five-kind
discriminated union that costs nothing extra to write. Do not make the backend's `project` kind
depend on a frontend surface that does not exist yet; do make the frontend's `+` button create a
project rather than a folder called "Untitled project folder", which is the tell that the concept is
half-built.
**Impact if wrong** — if projects are genuinely seed-only, this endpoint is dead surface and
`nodes.color`/`nodes.project_status` are columns nothing writes. If they are not, the product ships
a hierarchy the PRD names in its second feature and no user can construct.

### 10.1 The lifecycle, and every legal transition

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Four states, and the frontend resolves them through two independent
mechanisms — `deleted_at` (trash) and `archived_at` (archive) — which canon collapses into the
derived, read-only `NodeState` (canon §2.4). Precedence is top to bottom and is not negotiable:

```ts
type NodeState =
  | "trashed"    // deleted_at IS NOT NULL — accepts nothing but node.delete
  | "frozen"     // an ANCESTOR is archived — every write refused, and this node
                 //   cannot be thawed on its own
  | "archived"   // this node's own archived_at — read-only, but Restore is offered
  | "active";
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> active : E-024 create (kind = project)
    active --> archived : E-030 PUT /nodes/{id}/archive
    archived --> active : E-031 DELETE /nodes/{id}/archive
    active --> trashed : E-032 DELETE /nodes/{id}
    archived --> trashed : E-032 DELETE /nodes/{id}
    trashed --> active : E-037 POST /trash/{entryId}/restore
    trashed --> [*] : E-038 DELETE /trash/{entryId}  (permanent)
    trashed --> [*] : nightly sweep at 30 days
    active --> frozen : an ANCESTOR is archived (no call on this node)
    frozen --> active : E-031 on the ARCHIVED ANCESTOR
```

Read the diagram with four rules:

1. **`frozen` has no endpoint of its own.** A node becomes frozen because something above it was
   archived, and it leaves that state only when the ancestor is restored. `E-031` on a frozen node is
   refused with `NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED` (409 / `conflict`) — *"a page inside an archived project
   cannot be thawed on its own — the project has to be restored first"*
   (`src/lib/archive.ts:30-36`). This is why `archiveSourceOf` walks **root-first** and returns the
   *outermost* archived ancestor (`src/lib/archive.ts:19-28`), and why the Archive listing shows only
   topmost archived nodes (`src/components/collections/archive-page.tsx:28-34`): restoring a child
   would do nothing.
2. **`archived` is read-only, not hidden.** *"Archived means frozen, not hidden away: the content
   stays readable and addressable, and every write path is closed until it is restored"*
   (`src/lib/archive.ts:4-11`). An archived project stays out of the working drive listing
   (`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:47-49`) and out of the sidebar tree
   (`src/components/tree/folder-tree.tsx:53`), and stays searchable and reachable by URL.
3. **`trashed` accepts exactly one key.** `can()` short-circuits: `if (node?.isTrashed) return key
   === "node.delete"` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-81`). Not rename, not move, not archive,
   not restore-from-archive. The restore that *does* work is E-037, which addresses the **trash
   entry**, not the node.
4. **`archived → trashed` is legal, `trashed → archived` is not.** Deleting an archived project is an
   ordinary delete; archiving a trashed one is refused by rule 3.

**Archiving does not cascade to a `project_status` of `archived`.** `ProjectStatus` and `archived_at`
are two spellings of overlapping facts, and part 4's `nodes` table resolves it (OQ-56): `archived_at`
is the single source of truth for the freeze, `project_status` stays a product status (`active` /
`paused`), and the API **rejects `projectStatus: "archived"` on write** with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.
`setNodeArchived` writes `isArchived` and never touches `status`
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:592-611`), which is the frontend behaviour this preserves.

---

### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` — creating a project

**Purpose** — Create a node. One endpoint for all creatable kinds, discriminated by `kind` in the
body (canon E-024). This section documents the `project` arm; §11 documents the `folder` arm and
§12 the `document`/`page` arm.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` on the **parent** — the workspace root when `parentId` is `null` —
plus membership. Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:39`). The `project` arm needs no second key;
`board.create` and `document.create` are the extra keys the board and document arms require
(canon §3.3).

The check is on the parent, not on the new node, because the new node does not exist yet and its
effective role is whatever it will inherit. `effectiveAccess` on the parent
(`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`) is the role the check runs against, and visibility of
the parent is gate 2.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | The tenant the node is created in. Never taken from the body. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4 CreateNodeRequest — a discriminated union on `kind` (canon C-05). */
type CreateNodeRequest =
  | CreateProjectNodeRequest
  | CreateFolderNodeRequest
  | CreateDocumentNodeRequest
  | CreateBoardNodeRequest;

interface CreateNodeRequestBase {
  /** Container to create inside. `null` is the workspace root and is always legal. */
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  readonly name: string;
}

interface CreateProjectNodeRequest extends CreateNodeRequestBase {
  readonly kind: "project";
  readonly color: string;                    // REQUIRED — ProjectNode.color is not optional
  readonly description?: string;
  readonly projectStatus?: ProjectStatus;    // "active" | "paused"; defaults to "active"
}
```

There is **no `file` arm.** A file node is created by the upload flow (E-110 / E-111), which inserts
`file_assets`, `file_nodes` and the `nodes` row together; the frontend's equivalent is
`addUploadedAsset` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:716-743`), a separate action from every other
create.

`slug`, `id`, `ownerId`, `createdAt`, `isFavorite`, `isShared`, `isArchived` and `accessMode` are
**never accepted.** All are server-owned.

Validation:

| Field | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Trimmed; **empty falls back to a default**, it is not rejected. For a project, `"Untitled project"`. | The three existing create paths all coerce: `"Untitled folder"` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:326`), `"Untitled"` (`:759`), `"Untitled board"` (`:810`). |
| `parentId` | `NULL`, or a live node in the same workspace with `kind IN ('project','folder')`. | `isContainer` (`src/types/node.ts:146-147`); the refusal message the frontend shows for the document arm is *"Pages can only live inside folders"* (`:752`). |
| `color` | Required, non-empty. A CSS colour token; the frontend uses `var(--…)` custom properties (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:180-187`), so do not validate it as a hex triple. | `src/types/node.ts:84` |
| `description` | ≤ 280 characters. Trimmed; stored `NULL` when empty. | Consistent with `WORKSPACE_DESCRIPTION_MAX`; `ProjectNode.description?` is optional (canon C-08). |
| `projectStatus` | `active` \| `paused`. **`archived` is rejected** — see §10.1. | `src/types/node.ts:46` + part 4's OQ-56 position. |

**Nesting a project inside a project is legal.** `isContainer` admits both kinds and nothing
anywhere restricts a project to the root. The PRD's `Workspace → Project → Folder → Content` is the
*intended* shape, not an enforced one, and enforcing it would be a new rule the frontend does not
have (ground rule 3). **RECOMMENDATION:** allow it, and let the UI stop offering it.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `project` variant), `201 Created`.

```jsonc
// 201 POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes
{
  "id": "b21f…", "kind": "project",
  "name": "NexDrop Express", "slug": "nexdrop-express",
  "parentId": null, "workspaceId": "9f1c…",
  "owner": { "id": "usr_…", "name": "Khanh Luu", "email": "khanh@nexdrop.vn", "initials": "KL" },
  "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z",
  "isFavorite": false, "isTrashed": false, "isShared": false,
  "state": "active",
  "color": "var(--accent)", "status": "active",
  "description": "Delivery platform",
  "children": []
}
```

`isArchived` and `accessMode` are **omitted**, not `null` (canon C-08): absent means `false` and
`"inherit"` respectively (`src/types/node.ts:66, 77`; `accessModeOf`,
`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:47-50`). `children` is `[]` and is **derived** from `parent_id`,
never stored (canon §1.3.1).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1: membership + role. |
| `nodes` | READ | The parent, `WHERE id = :parentId AND workspace_id = :ws AND deleted_at IS NULL FOR UPDATE`. Assert `kind IN ('project','folder')`. Skipped when `parentId IS NULL`. |
| `nodes` | READ | The parent's ancestor chain, for gate 2 (visibility) and the frozen check — `archived_at IS NOT NULL` anywhere above → `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Rows on the ancestor chain, to resolve the caller's effective role on the parent. |
| `nodes` | READ | Live sibling slugs: `SELECT slug FROM nodes WHERE parent_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM :parentId AND workspace_id = :ws AND deleted_at IS NULL`. Seeds `uniqueSlug`. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | `workspace_id`, `parent_id`, `kind='project'`, `name`, `slug`, `owner_id=:session_user`, `access_mode='inherit'`, `color`, `description`, `project_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by=:session_user`. Every other kind-specific column stays `NULL` — the `nodes_extras_confined` check enforces it. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.create`, severity `info`, target = the project name, `detail` = `Created in {parent path}.` |

**No side table.** Unlike `board`, `document`, `config`, `secret` and `file`, a project has no 1:1
content row: `color`, `description` and `project_status` are columns on `nodes` itself. That is why
this arm is the simplest of the four.

**Transaction** — **Required**, and it takes the same per-workspace advisory lock as every other
write that changes the shape of the tree (create, move, trash, restore), so slug minting and the
container check cannot race a concurrent move.

```
BEGIN;
  pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(:workspaceId));
  <gate 1, gate 2, container check, frozen check>
  slug := uniqueSlug(slugify(:name), liveSiblingSlugs(:parentId));
  INSERT INTO nodes (...);
  INSERT INTO audit_events (...);
COMMIT;
```

Atomic together: the node row and its audit row. (For the `board` and `document` arms the side-table
row joins them — a board node with no `boards` row is a 404 on a URL the sidebar is already showing.)

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11) with
`{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "created" }`. Ids only; the receiver refetches
(canon §7.2). Scoped to subscribers who can see the parent — a project created inside a restricted
folder must not announce itself to people who cannot see that folder (**OQ-100**).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `color` missing, `description` > 280, `projectStatus` = `"archived"`, `kind` not a `NodeKind` member. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.create` on the parent. `detail` = `Needs the Manager role or above`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` — the parent chain contains an archived node. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` — the parent is in the trash. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`; `NODE_NOT_FOUND` for a parent that does not exist **or that the caller may not see**. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — the parent is a document, board or file. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` — the mint lost twice under concurrency. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — **None for the `project` arm** (see OQ-11 above). The nearest callers are
`src/components/layout/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:102` and
`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:63`, which both create a **folder**, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:516` (`createFolder`).

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — reading a project

**Purpose** — One node with the caller's capabilities on it.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **Visibility** on the node — the resource-access axis, not the capability axis. The
two are never merged: *"a Viewer who is granted a restricted folder sees it and edits nothing, a
Manager who is not granted it does not see it, whatever their role"*
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:15-33`). A node the caller may not see answers
`NODE_NOT_FOUND` (404), never 403.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeChildren` | boolean | no | `false` | When true, `children` carries the node's **direct** children, pruned by visibility. When false it is `[]`. Use E-023 for a listing; this flag exists so a project page can render in one round trip. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — the `project` variant of `DriveNode`, plus the caller's `CapabilitySet`.

```ts
/** canon E-022 returns DriveNode + CapabilitySet. */
interface NodeResponse {
  readonly node: DriveNode;
  readonly capabilities: CapabilitySet;   // { view, edit, upload, delete, share, manage }
  readonly state: NodeState;              // derived; also mirrored onto the node
}
```

`CapabilitySet` is a **projection of the catalogue, never declared beside it** — `capabilitiesFor`
derives all six from `can` so *"`capabilities.edit` and `can("row.update")` can never disagree"*
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:116-132`). For a project, `edit` resolves through
`editKeyFor(node)` to `node.rename` (`:108-114`, the default branch), `delete` to `node.delete`,
`share` to `node.share`, `manage` to `node.archive`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + workspace role floor. |
| `nodes` | READ | PK lookup, then the **ancestor chain root-ward** by recursive CTE on `parent_id`, depth-bounded (part 4's `nodes` documentation SQL). |
| `access_rules` | READ | `WHERE node_id = ANY(:chain)`, index `access_rules_workspace_idx (workspace_id, node_id)`. Feeds both `admits()` (gate 2) and `effectiveAccess` (gate 3). |
| `node_favorites` | READ | `WHERE user_id = :session_user AND node_id = :nodeId` → `isFavorite`. **Per user** (canon OQ-07), even though the frontend types it as a plain boolean on the node. |
| `nodes` | READ | `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM access_rules WHERE node_id = :nodeId)` → `isShared`, which is derived and never stored (canon §1.3.1). |
| `users` | READ | `owner_id` → `UserSummary`. |
| `nodes` | READ | Direct children when `includeChildren=true`, index `nodes_parent_idx`, then pruned. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown, trashed-and-purged, in another workspace, **or not visible to the caller**. The refusal names nothing: `DENIED_REASON` is deliberately name-free (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-167`). |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:42` (through `resolvePath` over the loaded
tree), `src/components/drive/node-detail.tsx`, and `src/hooks/use-permissions.ts:130`
(`useCapabilities`) for the capability half.

---

### `PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — updating a project

**Purpose** — Rename a node, and change the presentation fields its kind carries.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.rename` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+ **or the node's
owner**: `node.rename` is in `OWNER_ESCALATIONS` (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:102-108`), which
applies from `member` upward (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:72-74` — `roleRank(role) >=
roleRank("member")`). A Viewer who owns a project still cannot rename it.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4 RenameNodeRequest. `name` is EXISTING; the rest is RECOMMENDATION —
 *  ProjectNode carries these fields and no other endpoint can write them. */
interface RenameNodeRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly description?: string | null;    // project only; null clears
  readonly color?: string;                 // project | folder only
  readonly projectStatus?: ProjectStatus;  // project only; "archived" rejected
}
```

Rules:

- `name` — trimmed; **an empty name is a no-op, not an error** (`renameNode` returns the state
  untouched, `src/store/workspace-store.ts:483-486`). The database also refuses it
  (`nodes_name_not_blank`), so the API returns the current record rather than writing.
- **The slug is not re-minted.** Canon OQ-09 position: minted once at creation, re-uniquified only on
  move. This is the one place the frontend contradicts itself and canon picks a side: `renameNode`
  from the drive tree *does* re-slug (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:494-497`) while
  `applyDocumentSummary` deliberately does not — *"The slug is the routing key and is minted once, at
  creation: renaming a page the user is standing on must not break its URL"*
  (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:883-885`). Canon takes the second, so a rename never breaks a
  stored link.
- Fields that do not belong to the node's kind are rejected with `VALIDATION_FAILED`, not ignored —
  `color` on a document, `projectStatus` on a folder. Silently dropping them makes a client that
  sends the wrong shape look like it worked.
- `parentId` is **not** patchable here. Moving is E-026 and has its own transaction, its own
  rejections and its own realtime frame.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `project` variant), the authoritative record.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | The node + its ancestor chain: gate 2 (visibility), gate 3 (`node.rename`, with owner escalation from `owner_id`), and the narrowing layers — `deleted_at IS NOT NULL` → refuse; any ancestor `archived_at IS NOT NULL` → refuse. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules, for `effectiveAccess`. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `name`, `description`, `color`, `project_status` as supplied; always `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by = :session_user`. **`slug` is not in the statement.** |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.rename`, severity `info`, target = the **new** name, `detail` = `Renamed from "{old}".` |

`nodes.search_vector` is `GENERATED … STORED` over `name` and `excerpt`, so the rename reindexes
itself with no extra statement.

**Transaction** — Required (update + audit). **No advisory lock**: a rename does not change the shape
of the tree, and because the slug is not re-minted it cannot collide with a sibling.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "renamed" }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — a field that does not belong to this kind, `description` > 280, `projectStatus` = `"archived"`. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.rename` and not the owner. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` — a trashed node accepts only `node.delete`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/shared/rename-dialog.tsx:63` and
`src/components/shared/node-title-input.tsx:60`, both through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:482` (`renameNode`); reachable from
`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:101` (`requestRename`) and the tree row.
