### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/archive` — archiving a project

**Purpose** — Freeze a project and everything under it (SY-ARC-37): still readable, still
addressable, accepting no writes.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.archive` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+ **or the
owner** (`node.archive` is in `OWNER_ESCALATIONS`, `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:105`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None. `PUT` on a boolean sub-resource is idempotent (canon P-07): archiving an
already-archived project is `200` with the unchanged record, not an error. The frontend short-circuits
the same way (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:594-595` — `if (!node || isArchivedNode(node) ===
isArchived) return state`).

*(Canon §5.4 also names a `SetNodeArchivedRequest`; it is the body of the single-endpoint form
`{ isArchived: boolean }`. This specification uses the `PUT` / `DELETE` pair canon §3.3 lists as
E-030 / E-031, so the body is empty in both directions.)*

**Response** — `DriveNode`, with `isArchived: true` and `state: "archived"`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + ancestor chain, `FOR UPDATE` on the node. Gate 2, gate 3, `deleted_at IS NULL`. |
| `nodes` | READ | **The ancestor check that matters**: if any ancestor already has `archived_at IS NOT NULL`, the node is already frozen and `node.archive` is closed for it — `can()` returns false for every write key when `isFrozen` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:83`). Refuse with `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `SET archived_at = now(), archived_by = :session_user, updated_at = now()` **on this row only**. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.archive`, severity `info`, target = the project name. |

**Archiving writes one row.** It does **not** stamp descendants. The freeze is *resolved* by walking
the ancestor chain on read (`archiveSourceOf` / `inheritedArchiveOf`, `src/lib/archive.ts:19-45`) —
*"a board inside an archived project is read-only even though its own flag is unset — so nothing
branches on `node.isArchived` directly"* (`:9-11`). Archiving a project with ten thousand descendants
is one `UPDATE`, exactly as restricting a folder is one `INSERT` (§11).

The consequence a backend developer must hold: **every capability check on every descendant must walk
the chain.** There is no denormalised `is_frozen` column, and adding one would need a subtree rewrite
on every archive and every move.

**Transaction** — Required (update + audit). No advisory lock: archiving does not re-parent anything.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "archived" }`. Every client
holding a descendant re-resolves its own capabilities; because the freeze is derived from the chain,
nothing else needs to be pushed.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.archive` and not the owner. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` — already frozen from above; archive the ancestor's ancestor or restore it first. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:150`, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:592` (`setNodeArchived`). Feedback copy: *"Archived project “{name}” —
it is read-only until restored"* (`:604-605`, via `archiveLabelFor`, `src/lib/archive.ts:56-68`).

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/archive` — restoring a project from the archive

**Purpose** — Thaw a project.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.archive` on the node, plus membership and visibility. **This is the one write
key a node in the `archived` state still holds**, and that is deliberate: `can()` reads
`isFrozen` from the **ancestors only** and never from the node's own flag, *"because a surface must
keep offering Restore on the thing you are standing on"*
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:57-62`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None. Idempotent: restoring an unarchived project is `200`.

**Response** — `DriveNode`, with `isArchived` omitted and `state: "active"` — unless an ancestor is
still archived, in which case the call is refused rather than returning `frozen`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + ancestor chain `FOR UPDATE`. |
| `nodes` | READ | **`inheritedArchiveOf`**: the chain excluding the node itself (`src/lib/archive.ts:37-45`). Any ancestor with `archived_at IS NOT NULL` → refuse `NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED` (409 / `conflict`). |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `SET archived_at = NULL, archived_by = NULL, updated_at = now()`. The `nodes_archive_pair` check keeps the two columns as one fact. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.archive`, severity `info`, `detail` = `Restored from the archive.` |

**Why the ancestor refusal is a hard rule, not a nicety.** Clearing this node's own flag while an
ancestor is archived produces a node that *looks* active in the drive listing and refuses every write
anyway, because the capability resolver reads the chain. The user would restore something, watch it
reappear, and find it read-only with no explanation. The frontend prevents the situation from the
other end: the Archive page lists only **topmost** archived nodes
(`src/components/collections/archive-page.tsx:28-34, 114-128`), so the Restore button is never
rendered for a node whose restore would do nothing.

**Transaction** — Required (update + audit).

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "restored" }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` — a trashed node is restored by E-037, not here. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED` — an archived ancestor holds this node frozen. `message` = `That project is inside an archived item`, `detail` = `Restore the item above it first.` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/collections/archive-page.tsx:101` and
`src/components/shared/archived-banner.tsx:57` (which restores `archiveSourceOf(node)` — the
outermost archived ancestor, not the node the user is looking at), both through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:592`.

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — moving a project to the trash

**Purpose** — Soft-delete a project and detach its whole subtree (SY-TRH-38).

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.delete` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+ **or the owner**
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:104`). It is also the **only** key a trashed node still holds
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-81`), which is what lets E-037 and E-038 work.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**The PRD's re-type-the-name rule.** `WS-ARC-02` states: *"Xóa Project đang có thành viên làm việc:
Bắt buộc nhập lại tên Project để xác nhận"* — deleting a project with members working in it requires
the caller to re-type the project's name.

**This is a frontend confirmation, not a backend requirement.** Three reasons, stated so nobody
re-opens it:

1. A `confirmName` field on the wire verifies nothing. The server would compare a string the client
   just sent against a string the client already had; a script sends both. The only real control is
   the permission key, and `node.delete` is Manager-or-owner.
2. The product already has exactly this pattern, and it lives entirely in the client:
   `src/components/workspace/workspace-danger-zone.tsx:29` gates the Delete button on
   `typed.trim() === workspace.name` and the API takes nothing (see E-011).
3. Part 4 takes the same position for the same PRD sentence in its `workspaces` table (OQ-02):
   *"treat the PRD rule as a client-side gate for projects (E-032 on a node of kind `project`) and add
   nothing to the wire for it."*

**GAP — the frontend does not implement it today.** `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:161`
calls `trashNode(node.id)` straight from the menu item with no confirmation of any kind, for every
node kind including `project`. The confirmation dialog that WS-ARC-02 requires does not exist. What
the backend owes instead is the trail: the audit row below is written at `warn` for a project, so a
deletion is always answerable after the fact even when nobody was asked to type anything.

**Response** — `TrashEntry`, `200`.

```ts
/** src/types/system.ts:171-180 — unchanged. */
interface TrashEntry {
  readonly id: string;                              // == the deleted node's id
  readonly node: DriveNode;                         // the whole subtree, marked isTrashed
  readonly deletedAt: string;                       // ISO 8601
  readonly deletedBy: UserSummary;
  readonly originalAncestorIds: readonly string[];  // root first
  readonly originalPath: string;                    // "Development / Backend"
  readonly purgeAt: string;                         // ISO 8601 — RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-14)
}
```

`purgeAt` is `deletedAt + TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` (30, `src/config/app.ts:41-42`). It is returned
because *"the backend owns the sweep, so the UI reports 'due' rather than inventing it"*
(`src/lib/trash.ts:127-130`); `daysRemaining` currently recomputes it client-side from the constant
(`:131-138`), which is a duplicated rule the server should end.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + ancestor chain `FOR UPDATE`. Gate 2, gate 3 (`node.delete`, owner escalation), `deleted_at IS NULL`. A frozen node **can** be trashed: `can()` refuses writes when `isFrozen`, and `node.delete` is a write — so **an archived ancestor does block the delete** (`evaluate.ts:83`, before the lock check). Refuse `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| `nodes` | READ | `originalAncestorIds` — the chain **excluding the node itself**, root first (`src/lib/trash.ts:37`), and `originalPath` = the ancestors' names joined `" / "`, or `"Workspace root"` (`pathLabel`, `src/lib/tree.ts:74-78`). **Resolved now, while the ancestors still exist** (`src/lib/trash.ts:49-51`) — after a purge there is nothing left to resolve it from. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | The whole subtree in one statement, driven by a downward recursive CTE on `parent_id`: `SET deleted_at = now(), deleted_by = :session_user`. `parent_id` is **not** changed — the row keeps its place so a restore can put it back. |
| `trash_entries` | INSERT | `node_id`, `workspace_id`, `deleted_by`, `deleted_at`, `original_parent_id`, `original_ancestor_ids UUID[]`, `original_path TEXT`, `purge_at`. One row for the **root** of the deleted subtree; descendants get `deleted_at` and no entry, which is what makes the trash listing show one item rather than a subtree's worth. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.delete`, severity `warn` for `kind = 'project'` (`info` for a leaf), target = the project name, `detail` = `Moved to Trash from {originalPath}; {n} items.` |

**Slug uniqueness releases immediately.** The partial unique indexes carry `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`
(part 4, `nodes`), so a trashed project stops reserving its slug the moment it is deleted. That is
what makes E-037 have to re-uniquify on restore.

**Content is not touched.** No `documents`, `boards`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents` or
`file_nodes` row is written or deleted. *"Deleting a document must not delete its content. Trash
detaches the node subtree; content stays keyed by `nodeId` and comes back intact on restore."* The
frontend never calls `documentService.remove` at all (`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:114-121`).

**Transaction** — **Required**, with the per-workspace advisory lock. Subtree `UPDATE`, trash entry
and audit row are one unit. A trash entry without the `deleted_at` stamps would list an item that is
still in the tree; the stamps without the entry would hide a subtree nobody can restore.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "trashed" }`. One frame for
the subtree root, not one per descendant: the receiver refetches the tree.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.delete` and not the owner. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — including a node already in the trash (it is no longer in the tree). |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:161` (single) and
`src/components/drive/drive-toolbar.tsx:108` (multi-select, one write for the whole selection),
through `src/store/workspace-store.ts:612` / `:614` (`trashNode` / `trashNodes`). Also
`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:118` for a page.

---

### `POST /api/v1/trash/{entryId}/restore` — restoring a project from the trash

**Purpose** — Put a deleted project back, and say where it landed when its original home is gone.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.delete` on the trashed node, plus membership. Canon E-037 names this key
deliberately: `node.delete` is the only key a trashed node holds
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-81`), so gating restore on `node.create` or `node.archive`
would make it uncallable.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entryId` | UUID | The trash entry's id, which equals the deleted node's id (`src/lib/trash.ts:44`). |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None. The destination is **not** a parameter: it is computed from the recorded
ancestor chain, so a restore cannot be used to relocate something into a folder the caller could not
otherwise write to.

**Response** — `RestoreOutcome`, `200`.

```ts
/** src/types/system.ts:182-188 — unchanged. */
interface RestoreOutcome {
  readonly node: DriveNode;              // the restored subtree root, isTrashed: false
  readonly parentId: string | null;      // where it actually landed
  readonly isRelocated: boolean;         // true when that is NOT the original parent
  readonly location: string;             // the parent's name, or "Workspace"
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/trash/{entryId}/restore
{
  "node": { "id": "b21f…", "kind": "project", "name": "NexDrop Express", "parentId": null, "…": "…" },
  "parentId": null,
  "isRelocated": true,
  "location": "Workspace"
}
```

**The destination algorithm** — `restoreTargetFor` (`src/lib/trash.ts:96-114`), reproduced exactly:

```
FUNCTION restoreTargetFor(entry):
  original := entry.node.parentId

  # originalAncestorIds is root-first, so reversing walks from the DEEPEST
  # recorded ancestor upward: the closest surviving home wins.
  FOR candidate IN reverse(entry.originalAncestorIds):
      n := node(candidate)
      IF n IS NULL:            CONTINUE      # purged
      IF NOT isContainer(n):   CONTINUE      # no longer able to hold children
      IF n.deleted_at:         CONTINUE      # itself in the trash
      RETURN { parentId: candidate, isRelocated: candidate <> original }

  # Nothing on the chain survives — the workspace root always does.
  RETURN { parentId: null, isRelocated: original IS NOT NULL }
```

This is precisely PRD `SY-TRH-38`'s edge case: *"Khôi phục 1 Document nhưng Folder cha của nó đã bị
xóa vĩnh viễn: Khôi phục Doc ra ngoài Root của Project."* `isRelocated` is **not an error** — canon
§4.3 records `TRASH_RESTORE_RELOCATED` explicitly as a `200` outcome reported in the body, so no
chapter mistakes it for a failure. The frontend renders it as a different sentence, not a different
result: *"Restored “{name}” to {location} — its original folder no longer exists"*
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:670-676`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `trash_entries` | READ | `WHERE id = :entryId FOR UPDATE`. |
| `nodes` | READ | The trashed subtree root: `WHERE id = :entryId AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL`. Gate 3 (`node.delete`). |
| `nodes` | READ | `WHERE id = ANY(entry.original_ancestor_ids)` — resolve survivors for the algorithm above. Also gate 2 on the chosen destination: the caller must be able to **see** where it is going. |
| `nodes` | READ | Live sibling slugs at the destination. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | The subtree: `SET deleted_at = NULL, deleted_by = NULL`. Plus, on the root row only, `parent_id = :destination`, `slug = :newSlug`, `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by = :session_user`. |
| `trash_entries` | DELETE | The entry is consumed. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.delete`, severity `info`, `detail` = `Restored to {location}.` (or `… — its original folder no longer exists.`) |

**The slug must be re-uniquified.** Because the sibling-uniqueness indexes exclude trashed rows, the
slug was released at deletion and something else may have taken it — or the node is landing in a
different parent entirely after a relocation. `newSlug := uniqueSlug(node.slug,
liveSiblingSlugs(destination))`, exactly as E-026 does on move. Without it the restore violates
`nodes_slug_child_uniq` and fails on a write the user has no way to understand.

**Transaction** — **Required**, with the per-workspace advisory lock (it re-parents a subtree, so it
is one of the four shape-changing writes). Subtree un-stamp, re-parent, slug mint, entry delete and
audit row are one unit.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "restored" }`. When the restore
relocated the node into a different access chain, **also** publish `permission.changed` (RT-05) with
the ids of members whose visibility changed — the same computation E-026 performs
(`moveVisibilityImpact`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:313-333`), because a relocation is a move.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.delete` on the trashed node. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `TRASH_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND` — unknown, already restored, or purged. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` — the mint lost twice at the destination. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/collections/trash-page.tsx:91`, through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:653` (`restoreNode`).

**Permanent deletion** — `DELETE /trash/{entryId}` (E-038) and `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/trash`
(E-039, `EmptyTrashResponse`) end the lifecycle. They are `system`-module endpoints and are
specified with the trash chapter, not here; §10.1's diagram names them so the state machine is
complete. Both hard-delete through the `nodes` cascade, decrement `workspaces.used_bytes` under
`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` for every reachable `file_assets` row, and write their audit row **before**
the delete — because afterwards there is nothing left to describe.
`src/components/collections/trash-page.tsx:108` and `:120` are their callers.


---

## 11. Folder APIs

Module `drive` for the tree operations, `governance` for access. **A folder is not a table either.**
It is a `nodes` row whose `kind` is `folder` — the second of the two container kinds
(`isContainer`, `src/types/node.ts:146-147`).

```ts
interface FolderNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "folder";                  // → wire field `kind`
  readonly children: readonly DriveNode[];  // DERIVED from parent_id, never stored
  readonly color?: string;                  // OPTIONAL, unlike ProjectNode.color
}
```

Four of this section's endpoints — archive, un-archive, trash and restore-from-trash — are
**kind-agnostic** and are specified in full in §10. They are repeated here in the required shape with
only their folder-specific deltas spelled out, so a reader working on folders does not have to
reconstruct them.

PRD `WS-FLD-03` fixes the operation set — *create, rename, drag-move, duplicate, archive, soft-delete,
share* — the containment set (sub-folders, documents, boards, files, config documents, secret
documents), a depth floor of **at least 10 levels with unbounded node count**, and the cycle rule.

---

### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` — creating a folder

**Purpose** — Create a folder inside a project, another folder, or at the workspace root.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` on the parent (the workspace root when `parentId` is `null`), plus
membership and visibility of the parent. Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:39`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
interface CreateFolderNodeRequest extends CreateNodeRequestBase {
  readonly kind: "folder";
  readonly color?: string;   // optional, unlike a project's
}
```

- `name` — trimmed; **empty falls back to `"Untitled folder"`**, never rejected
  (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:326`).
- `parentId` — `NULL` (root), or a live `project` / `folder` in this workspace. A folder under a
  document, board or file is `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER`.
- `slug` — server-minted, `uniqueSlug(slugify(name), liveSiblingSlugs)`
  (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:521`).
- `accessMode` — **not accepted.** A new folder always starts `inherit`; restricting it is E-041, a
  separate, audited write.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `folder` variant), `201 Created`, with `children: []`,
`isFavorite: false`, `isTrashed: false`, `isShared: false`, and `isArchived` / `accessMode` omitted.

The frontend's create-then-rename flow matters for the response: after creating, the store sets
`renameRequestId` to the new node so the caret lands in the name
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:342-347`) — *"creating one and having to hunt for 'Rename' afterwards
is two steps where one will do."* The API's part of that contract is simply returning the node with
its id; the focus handoff is the client's.

**Database** — identical to §10's project arm, with `kind = 'folder'`, `color` nullable, and
`description` / `project_status` left `NULL` (enforced by `nodes_extras_confined`).

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Parent `FOR UPDATE` + ancestor chain (gate 2, frozen check, container check). |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules → the caller's effective role on the parent. |
| `nodes` | READ | Live sibling slugs for the mint. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | `kind='folder'`, `access_mode='inherit'`, `owner_id = :session_user`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.create`, severity `info`. |

**Transaction** — Required, under the per-workspace advisory lock.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "created" }`.

**Possible Errors** — as §10's project arm, minus the `color`-required and `projectStatus` rows:

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `description`, `projectStatus` or `icon` sent on a folder. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER`, `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:63`,
`src/components/drive/drive-toolbar.tsx:194`, `src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx:160`,
`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:143`, and
`src/components/layout/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:102` (which creates a root-level folder labelled
*"Untitled project folder"* — see §10's OQ-11). All through `src/store/workspace-store.ts:516`.

---

### `PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — renaming a folder

**Purpose** — Change a folder's name, and its optional colour.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.rename` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+ **or the
owner** (owner escalation, `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:103`).

**Path Params** — `nodeId` (UUID).

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `RenameNodeRequest` (§10). For `kind = 'folder'` the accepted fields are `name?`
and `color?`; `description` and `projectStatus` are rejected with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `folder` variant).

**Database** — as §10: gate reads over `nodes` + `access_rules`, one `UPDATE nodes` touching
`name` / `color` / `updated_at` / `updated_by`, one `audit_events` insert
(module `node`, action `node.rename`, severity `info`). **`slug` is not in the `UPDATE`.**

**Transaction** — Required (update + audit). No advisory lock.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "renamed"`.

**Possible Errors** — as §10's `PATCH /nodes/{nodeId}`.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/shared/rename-dialog.tsx:63`,
`src/components/shared/node-title-input.tsx:60`, reached from
`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:101` and the sidebar tree row.

**A divergence a backend developer must know about.** The frontend's `renameNode` **does** re-mint
the slug (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:494-499`) — it computes `uniqueSlug(slugify(trimmed),
siblingSlugs)` and writes it. Canon (OQ-09 position) says the slug is minted once and re-uniquified
only on move, and this specification follows canon. The frontend's own document path already behaves
canon's way and says why: *"renaming a page the user is standing on must not break its URL"*
(`:883-885`). Follow canon; the client's re-navigation after a rename becomes unnecessary rather than
wrong.

---

### `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/move`

**Purpose** — Re-parent a folder (and, unchanged, everything under it) into a different container.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.move` on the node being moved, plus membership, **plus visibility of both the
node and the destination**. Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:41`); `node.move` is **not** in
`OWNER_ESCALATIONS`, so an owning Member cannot move their own folder.

Requiring visibility of the destination is not decoration: without it, a caller could relocate a
subtree into a restricted folder they cannot see, learn from the response whether the target exists,
and hand the subtree to a group they are not part of.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The node being moved. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. */
interface MoveNodeRequest {
  /** Destination container. `null` is the workspace root. */
  readonly targetParentId: string | null;
}
```

**Response** — `MoveNodeResponse`, `200`.

```ts
/** canon §5.5 names it; this is its shape, built from MoveResult
 *  (src/lib/tree.ts:160-164) and MoveImpact (src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:304-309). */
interface MoveNodeResponse {
  readonly node: DriveNode;                  // authoritative, with the NEW parentId and slug
  readonly previousParentId: string | null;
  /** True when the slug had to change to fit the new sibling set (OQ-10). */
  readonly didSlugChange: boolean;
  readonly impact: MoveImpact;
}

interface MoveImpact {
  /** Members who could see it before and cannot now. Ids only. */
  readonly losing: readonly string[];
  /** Members who could not see it before and can now. Ids only. */
  readonly gaining: readonly string[];
}
```

`impact` exists because *"Moving something is a permission change wearing the costume of a drag: a
board dropped into a restricted folder becomes invisible to everybody the folder is not shared with,
and nothing about the board itself changed. The only honest thing to do is say so before it
happens"* (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:293-302`). The store renders the count as feedback:
*"Moved “{name}” to {target} — 3 people can no longer see it"*
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:571-589`). **Ids only, never names** — the same rule as the RT-05
frame.

`didSlugChange` is returned because the client re-navigates after a move
(`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:126-129` — the move *"changed the node's path, so its old URL is
now stale"*), and a changed slug is the difference between re-navigating and 404-ing.

#### Cycle prevention — the validation, as pseudocode

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** PRD `WS-FLD-03`: *"Kéo Folder cha vào chính Folder con của nó: Chặn thao
tác và báo lỗi cấu trúc vòng lặp."* The frontend implements it in `moveNode`
(`src/lib/tree.ts:170-197`) and the rejection vocabulary is a closed, **kebab-case** enum
(canon §2.3):

```ts
type MoveRejection = "same-parent" | "into-self" | "into-descendant" | "invalid-target";
```

| `MoveRejection` | Error reason | HTTP / code | Frontend sentence (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:977-988`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `same-parent` | `NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT` | 409 / `conflict` | "Item is already in that folder" — a **no-op the caller should treat as success**; the store returns state untouched and shows nothing (`:555`). |
| `into-self` | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF` | 409 / `conflict` | "A folder cannot be moved into itself" |
| `into-descendant` | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT` | 409 / `conflict` | "A folder cannot be moved into one of its own subfolders" |
| `invalid-target` | `NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET` | 409 / `conflict` | "That destination cannot hold items" |

```
FUNCTION move(actor, nodeId, targetParentId) -> MoveNodeResponse:

  BEGIN TRANSACTION
  # One workspace-wide advisory lock, held for the transaction. Two moves that
  # each pass in isolation can still produce a cycle: A→B and B→A concurrently
  # are both legal alone and illegal together, and no constraint can catch it
  # afterwards. Moves are human-paced; the lock costs nothing real.
  pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(workspace_id))

  node := SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE id = nodeId FOR UPDATE
  IF node IS NULL:                          REJECT NODE_NOT_FOUND

  # --- gates, before any structural reasoning --------------------------------
  REQUIRE membership(actor, node.workspace_id)      ELSE WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND
  REQUIRE visible(actor, nodeId)                    ELSE NODE_NOT_FOUND
  REQUIRE visible(actor, targetParentId)            ELSE NODE_NOT_FOUND
  REQUIRE capability(actor, nodeId, "node.move")    ELSE PERMISSION_DENIED
  REQUIRE node.deleted_at IS NULL                   ELSE NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY
  REQUIRE no ancestor of nodeId has archived_at     ELSE NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR

  # --- the two trivial rejections, in the frontend's order -------------------
  IF targetParentId = nodeId:                       REJECT NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF
  IF node.parent_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM targetParentId:
                                                    REJECT NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT

  # --- the destination -------------------------------------------------------
  IF targetParentId IS NOT NULL:
      target := SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE id = targetParentId FOR UPDATE
      IF target IS NULL
         OR target.deleted_at IS NOT NULL
         OR target.workspace_id <> node.workspace_id
         OR target.kind NOT IN ('project','folder'):
                                                    REJECT NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET
      IF EXISTS ancestor of targetParentId with archived_at:
                                                    REJECT NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR

      # ----- THE CYCLE CHECK ------------------------------------------------
      # Walk ROOT-WARD from the destination. If the node being moved appears
      # anywhere on that chain, the destination is inside the node: the move
      # would detach the subtree into itself. The rows survive, every walk from
      # the root stops finding them, and the branch is silently orphaned.
      #
      # Direction matters. The frontend walks DOWN from the node
      # (isDescendantOf, src/lib/tree.ts:147-156) because it holds the whole
      # tree in memory. The backend walks UP: the answer is identical and the
      # cost is bounded by depth (<= 10 in practice, 64 as a runaway stop)
      # instead of by subtree size, which WS-FLD-03 declares unbounded.
      ancestors := ancestorChainOf(targetParentId)      # [target, parent, …, root]
      IF nodeId IN ancestors:                     REJECT NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT

      # ----- depth guard, a runaway stop and not a product limit ------------
      IF depthOf(targetParentId) + 1 + heightOf(nodeId) > MAX_TREE_DEPTH:  # 64
                                                  REJECT NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET

  # --- slug, re-uniquified against the NEW siblings (canon OQ-10) ------------
  # The slug is minted once and never re-minted on rename, but a move can land
  # it beside a sibling that already holds it, and the partial unique index
  # nodes_slug_child_uniq would refuse the write with an error the user cannot
  # act on.
  newSlug := uniqueSlug(node.slug, liveSiblingSlugsOf(targetParentId))

  # --- visibility impact, computed BEFORE the write --------------------------
  impact := visibilityImpact(node, targetParentId)      # see below

  UPDATE nodes
     SET parent_id  = targetParentId,
         slug       = newSlug,
         updated_at = now(),
         updated_by = actor.id
   WHERE id = nodeId

  INSERT INTO audit_events (module: 'node', action: 'node.move',
                            severity: 'info', target: node.name,
                            detail: 'Moved from {oldPath} to {newPath}.')
  COMMIT

  publish RT-11 node.changed      { workspaceId, nodeId, change: "moved" }
  IF impact.losing OR impact.gaining:
      publish RT-05 permission.changed { workspaceId, nodeId,
                                         userIds: impact.losing ∪ impact.gaining }

  RETURN { node, previousParentId, didSlugChange: newSlug <> node.slug, impact }
```

The ancestor chain as documentation SQL:

```sql
-- documentation only. Root-ward from :target_id, cycle-safe, depth-bounded.
WITH RECURSIVE chain(id, parent_id, depth) AS (
    SELECT n.id, n.parent_id, 0 FROM nodes n WHERE n.id = :target_id
  UNION ALL
    SELECT n.id, n.parent_id, chain.depth + 1
      FROM nodes n JOIN chain ON n.id = chain.parent_id
     WHERE chain.depth < 64        -- runaway stop; if the data already holds a
)                                  -- cycle, fail fast instead of spinning
SELECT id FROM chain;
```

`MAX_TREE_DEPTH = 64` is a **RECOMMENDATION** and six times the PRD's floor of 10. It is not a product
limit and must never be described to a user as one.

#### What a move does to descendants' effective access

This is the question the endpoint exists to answer carefully, so it is stated in full.

**No row below the moved node is written. Not one.** `UPDATE nodes … WHERE id = nodeId` touches
exactly the moved row. No `access_rules` row is created, copied, deleted or re-pointed; no
descendant's `access_mode` changes; no descendant's `archived_at` changes. The frontend's model is
identical — `moveNode` returns `{ ...removed, parentId: targetParentId }` and re-inserts the same
subtree object (`src/lib/tree.ts:192-196`).

**And yet every descendant's effective access can change, because access is resolved and never
stored.** `visibility.ts:29-33`: *"Nothing is copied down the tree. Access is resolved by walking from
the root to the node, so restricting a folder with ten thousand descendants writes one field, and a
child's own mode is the only thing that can change what it inherited."* The walk is one boolean
carried root-ward-to-node (`admits`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:121-135`):

```
admits(n, inherited):
  switch n.access_mode:
    case 'workspace':  return isMember                        # opens up, from here down
    case 'restricted': return isMember AND hasGrantOn(n)      # discards what flowed in
    default:           return inherited                       # 'inherit' passes it through
```

A move replaces the **chain prefix** of every descendant. For a descendant `D` whose chain was
`[W … P_old, F … D]`, after moving `F` under `P_new` it is `[W … P_new, F … D]`. Everything from `F`
downward is recomputed on the next read, from the new prefix.

The consequences, each with its rule:

| Situation | Effect on the subtree | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `F.access_mode = 'inherit'` (the majority) | The whole subtree adopts whatever flows out of `P_new`. Members who could see `P_old` but not `P_new` lose the entire subtree; members granted `P_new` gain it. | `admits` default branch |
| `F.access_mode = 'restricted'` | The flow into `F` is discarded at `F`, so *within* the subtree nothing changes — the same grants admit the same people. **But `F` itself is still gated by the path above it**, so a person not admitted by `P_new` cannot reach `F` at all, and therefore cannot reach anything under it. | `nodeVisibility` returns at the first refusing node (`visibility.ts:167-173`) |
| `F.access_mode = 'workspace'` | Same: `workspace` widens **from `F` downward** and **cannot punch back up** through a restriction above it. Moving a `workspace` folder under a restricted one hides it from everyone not granted the restricted parent. | `visibility.ts:109-120` — *"a tree cannot render a child whose parent is missing, and showing one anyway would leak the name of the folder it sits in"* |
| A descendant declares its own `workspace` mode | Unchanged by the move in itself, and still unreachable if the new prefix refuses `F`. | same |
| `F` has an owner | The owner is always admitted **on `F`** (`hasGrantOn`, `visibility.ts:87-93`), but that admission does not survive a refusing ancestor. An owner **can** lose sight of their own folder when it is moved under a restriction they are not in. | `nodeVisibility` walks the whole chain |
| `P_new` (or an ancestor of it) is archived | The subtree becomes `frozen`: every write refused, reads intact, and no descendant can be thawed on its own. Nothing is written; `inheritedArchiveOf` resolves it. | `src/lib/archive.ts:30-45` |
| Favourites, Recent and notification entries pointing into the subtree | Dropped **entirely, name and all**, for anyone who lost visibility — `keepVisibleRefs` filters against the visible tree so *"the resource is gone, and its name is still on screen"* cannot happen. | `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:242-268` |
| A refused node in any flat read | Takes its whole subtree with it: search, favourites and relation pickers all read the pruned tree, not the raw one. | `visibleTree` (`:197-240`), `collectAllowed` (`src/lib/tree.ts:297-320`) |

**Computing `impact` — and one place the frontend under-reports.** `moveVisibilityImpact`
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:313-333`) iterates the workspace's members and compares
`canSeeNode(node.id)` **now** with `canSeeNode(targetParentId)` **now**, using the destination's
current visibility as a proxy for the node's future visibility. That proxy is exact for an inheriting
node. But the function opens with

```ts
if (accessModeOf(node) !== "inherit") return NO_IMPACT;   // visibility.ts:318
```

which is **not** exact: as the table above shows, a `workspace` or `restricted` folder moved under a
restriction still becomes invisible to everyone not admitted by the new parent, through path gating.
The resolver (`nodeVisibility`) is the authority and gets this right; the notice under-reports.

**RECOMMENDATION** — the backend must compute `impact` from the resolver, not from the shortcut:
for each workspace member, evaluate `canSeeNode` against the pre-move chain and against the
hypothetical post-move chain, and diff. It is one chain walk per member over a chain bounded by
depth, inside a transaction that already holds a workspace lock. Do not port the early return.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1; also the member list for the impact computation. |
| `nodes` | READ | The node `FOR UPDATE`; the destination `FOR UPDATE`; both ancestor chains by recursive CTE (`nodes_pkey`, then `parent_id`). |
| `access_rules` | READ | Rules on both chains, `access_rules_workspace_idx (workspace_id, node_id)`. |
| `nodes` | READ | Live sibling slugs at the destination (`nodes_parent_idx`). |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | **One row.** `parent_id`, `slug`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.move`, severity `info`, target = the folder name, `detail` naming the old and new paths. |

Cardinality note: the composite foreign key `(parent_id, workspace_id) → nodes(id, workspace_id)`
makes a cross-workspace move structurally impossible, which is why the pseudocode's
`target.workspace_id <> node.workspace_id` check is a fast refusal rather than the only defence.

**Transaction** — **Required**, with the per-workspace advisory lock held for its duration. A cycle is
a property of a *set* of rows and PostgreSQL has no constraint that can express one — no `CHECK`, no
`EXCLUDE`, no race-free trigger. The alternatives are `SERIALIZABLE` for the whole endpoint or this
lock; the lock is cheaper and does not make unrelated writes retryable. Take the same lock in create
(E-024), trash (E-032) and restore (E-037) so the invariant holds across all four shape-changing
writes, not only against other moves.

**Realtime** — two frames, both ids-only:

- `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "moved" }` — sidebars converge.
- `permission.changed` (RT-05), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, userIds: losing ∪ gaining }` — canon §7.1
  lists a move explicitly as an RT-05 trigger *"which relocates a node under a different access
  chain."* Receivers re-resolve their own access and drop what they may no longer hold
  (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`). Emit it only when the impact is non-empty.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.move` (Manager+; ownership does not escalate it). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — the node or the destination is unknown **or invisible**. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT` — treat as success. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET` — missing, not a container, another workspace, or past the depth guard. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` — the re-mint lost twice. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-node-dnd.ts:138` (drive grid drag-and-drop),
`src/components/tree/arborist-tree.tsx:27` (sidebar tree drop, one call per dragged id),
`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:126` (the page's "Move to…" dialog,
`src/components/document/move-page-dialog.tsx:44`). All through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:549` (`moveNode`).

### `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate`

**Purpose** — Copy a folder and everything inside it, beside the original.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` on the **parent** of the source (the copy lands as a sibling), plus
membership and visibility of the source. Manager+ (canon E-027).

**RECOMMENDATION — additionally require, for every descendant being copied, the read visibility the
caller already has.** Because the copy is server-side and recursive, a caller who can see a folder but
not one restricted sub-folder inside it must not receive a copy that contains it. Duplicate the
**visible** subtree — the same pruning `visibleTree` performs (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:197-240`)
— and report what was skipped. The frontend cannot express this: `cloneNode` runs over the tree the
store already pruned (`src/lib/tree.ts:203-217`), so it never sees the invisible parts in the first
place.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The folder to copy. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. Both fields optional; the defaults reproduce the frontend. */
interface DuplicateNodeRequest {
  /** Where the copy goes. Defaults to the source's own parent — beside it. */
  readonly targetParentId?: string | null;
  /** Defaults to `${source.name} (copy)`. */
  readonly name?: string;
}
```

**Response** — `DriveNode` — the new subtree root, `201 Created`.

**What the copy is** — `cloneNode` (`src/lib/tree.ts:203-217`) plus the store's two additions
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:853-859`):

| Property | Value on the copy | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | fresh UUID, **for every descendant** | `cloneNode` mints per node via `idFactory` |
| `parentId` | the target (default: the source's parent) | `:209` |
| `name` | `"{source.name} (copy)"` | `:854` |
| `slug` | `uniqueSlug(slugify(copyName), liveSiblingSlugs(target))` — *"Slug uniqueness is deliberately the caller's job because it needs the sibling list"* (`src/lib/tree.ts:200-202`) | `:858` |
| `isFavorite` | **`false`**, always | `src/lib/tree.ts:209` |
| `isShared` | **`false`**, always | `:209` |
| `owner` | **the caller**, not the source's owner | RECOMMENDATION — ownership escalates five keys on your own things (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:102-108`), and inheriting somebody else's ownership hands those keys to the wrong person. The frontend's `cloneNode` copies `owner` because it has no session concept. |
| `accessMode` | **`'inherit'`**, not copied | RECOMMENDATION — see below |
| `access_rules` | **none copied** | RECOMMENDATION — `isShared: false` is the frontend already saying so |
| `archived_at` | `NULL` | The copy is new and active. |
| `deleted_at` | `NULL` | Trashed descendants are not copied at all. |
| content | **copied** — every descendant document, board, config and file reference | canon OQ-12 position |

`accessMode` and the rules are not copied because `cloneNode` sets `isShared: false`, and `isShared`
is derived from *"any `access_rules` row exists on the node"* (canon §1.3.1). A copy that carried the
grants would be `isShared: true` on the first read, contradicting the record the frontend produces.
Duplicating a restricted folder therefore yields an **inheriting** folder — which is more open, so
the endpoint must say so in its response and the client must warn. **This is the single most
dangerous default in the section.**

**Content duplication, per descendant kind** (canon OQ-12):

| Kind | What is copied |
| --- | --- |
| `folder`, `project` | the row only; children recursively |
| `document` (`page`) | the `documents` row with **fresh block ids**, `version: 1`, `is_pinned: false`, lock cleared, and **no version history** — `documentService.duplicate` (`src/services/document-service.ts:243-267`) |
| `board` | the `boards` row, its `board_columns`, its `board_views`, and its `board_rows` with fresh ids and a `next_sequence` restarted — specified in the boards chapter |
| `config` | the `config_documents` row; no version history |
| `secret` | **keys only, values empty.** Never duplicate ciphertext. The copy is audited at `warn`. |
| `file` | a new `file_nodes` row pointing at the **same** `file_assets` row — the bytes are not re-uploaded, and `workspaces.used_bytes` is **not** incremented, because `file_assets.size_bytes` is counted once per asset (canon §1.3.4) |

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Source + ancestor chain (gates); then the **whole subtree** by downward recursive CTE on `parent_id WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain + subtree, to prune invisible descendants. |
| `nodes` | READ | Live sibling slugs at the destination. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | One row per copied node, parents before children, `owner_id = :session_user`, `access_mode = 'inherit'`, `created_by = :session_user`. |
| `documents`, `document_versions` | INSERT / — | One `documents` row per copied page with fresh block ids; **no** `document_versions` rows (a copy has no history). A version-1 row is written at creation per part 6's recommendation. |
| `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_views`, `board_rows` | INSERT | Per copied board. |
| `config_documents`, `secret_documents`, `secrets` | INSERT | Per copied config / secret; `secrets.value_encrypted` is **not** copied. |
| `file_nodes` | INSERT | Per copied file, `asset_id` **reused**. |
| `file_assets`, `workspaces.used_bytes` | *(no write)* | Assets are shared; the quota counter does not move. |
| `node_favorites` | *(no write)* | `isFavorite: false` on the copy. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.create`, severity `info` (`warn` when a secret document was copied), `detail` = `Duplicated “{name}” — {n} items.` |

**Transaction** — **Required**, and it is a large one: the whole subtree lands or none of it does. The
frontend's two-call sequence (`duplicateNode` then `documentService.duplicate`,
`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:90-99`) can leave an orphan node when the second call fails and
has **no compensating delete** — which is precisely why this must be one server-side transaction.

**RECOMMENDATION — a size ceiling.** A recursive duplicate of a large project is unbounded work in
one transaction. Cap it (subtree node count, and total `file_assets.size_bytes` against the remaining
quota) and refuse past the cap with `VALIDATION_FAILED` rather than starting. Serve the cap from
`GET /config` (E-139).

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId: <the copy's root>, change: "created" }`.
One frame; the receiver refetches the tree rather than reconstructing a subtree from frames.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — past the duplicate size cap. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — source or destination. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — the destination cannot hold children. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` |
| 507 | `upload_failed` | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — only if a chosen implementation copies bytes; the specified one does not, so this should never fire. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:93` (`duplicateNode`) through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:840`. There is **no folder-duplicate control in the UI today** — the
drive item menu offers Open, Favourite, Rename, Share link, Manage access, Roles, Download, Archive
and Trash (`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:86-166`) and no Duplicate. PRD `WS-FLD-03` lists
duplicate among the required folder operations, so the endpoint is owed and the control is missing.

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/archive` — archiving a folder

**Purpose** — Freeze a folder and, by inheritance, everything under it.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.archive`, Manager+ or owner. Identical to §10.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None. Idempotent, as in §10.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (`folder` variant), `isArchived: true`, `state: "archived"`.

**Database** — identical to §10: gate reads, then `UPDATE nodes SET archived_at = now(), archived_by
= :session_user, updated_at = now() WHERE id = :nodeId` — **one row**, never the subtree — plus one
`audit_events` insert (module `node`, action `node.archive`, severity `info`). The freeze on
descendants is derived by walking the chain (`src/lib/archive.ts:19-45`); there is no `is_frozen`
column and adding one would mean a subtree rewrite on every archive **and every move**.

**Transaction** — Required (update + audit). No advisory lock.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "archived"`.

**Possible Errors** — as §10: `AUTH_REQUIRED` (401), `PERMISSION_DENIED` /
`NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` (403), `NODE_NOT_FOUND` (404),
`INTERNAL_ERROR` (500).

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:150` through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:592`. Feedback: *"Archived folder “{name}” — it is read-only until
restored"* (`archiveLabelFor` returns `"folder"`, `src/lib/archive.ts:60-61`).

**Un-archiving** is `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/archive` (E-031), specified in full in §10. For a
folder the behaviour is identical, including the `NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED` refusal when an ancestor is
still archived. Callers: `src/components/collections/archive-page.tsx:101`,
`src/components/shared/archived-banner.tsx:57`.

### `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — moving a folder to the trash

**Purpose** — Soft-delete a folder and detach its whole subtree.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.delete`, Manager+ or owner. Identical to §10.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `TrashEntry` (§10), whose `node` carries the **whole subtree** marked `isTrashed`
(`markTrashed`, `src/lib/trash.ts:21-26`) and whose `originalPath` is the ancestors' names joined
`" / "`, resolved at deletion.

**Database** — identical to §10: chain reads for the gates and for `originalAncestorIds` /
`originalPath`; one subtree `UPDATE nodes SET deleted_at, deleted_by` driven by a downward recursive
CTE; one `trash_entries` INSERT for the **subtree root only**; one `audit_events` INSERT (module
`node`, action `node.delete`, severity `info` for a folder, `warn` for a project). `parent_id` is not
changed. No content table is touched.

The folder-specific note: because one entry covers the subtree, deleting a folder that already
contains individually-trashed items leaves those items' own entries in the bin. That is deliberate —
*"a folder can be purged for good while a page deleted out of it earlier survives, which is the one
case where restoring has to find the item a new home — and say so"* (`src/lib/trash.ts:6-13`). It is
also exactly what makes E-037's relocation branch reachable.

**Transaction** — Required, with the per-workspace advisory lock.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "trashed"`. One frame for the subtree root.

**Possible Errors** — as §10.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:161`,
`src/components/drive/drive-toolbar.tsx:108` (multi-select — *"One state write for a multi-select
delete, not one per item"*, `src/store/workspace-store.ts:187-188`).
