### `POST /api/v1/trash/{entryId}/restore` — restoring a folder

**Purpose** — Put a deleted folder subtree back, relocating it when its original home is gone.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.delete` on the trashed node. Identical to §10.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entryId` | UUID | Equal to the deleted node's id. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None. The destination is computed, never supplied.

**Response** — `RestoreOutcome` (§10) — `{ node, parentId, isRelocated, location }`.

**Database** — identical to §10, including the deepest-surviving-ancestor walk
(`restoreTargetFor`, `src/lib/trash.ts:96-114`) and the **mandatory slug re-mint** against the
destination's live siblings.

One folder-specific consequence worth stating: `untrash` clears `isTrashed` down the whole subtree and
re-points each child's `parentId` at its restored parent (`src/lib/trash.ts:117-125`). Server-side
that is a single subtree `UPDATE … SET deleted_at = NULL, deleted_by = NULL`; the `parent_id` values
below the root were never changed by the delete, so nothing else needs re-pointing.

**Transaction** — Required, with the per-workspace advisory lock.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "restored"`; plus `permission.changed` (RT-05) when
the restore relocated the subtree under a different access chain.

**Possible Errors** — as §10: `TRASH_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND` (404), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403),
`NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` (409).

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/collections/trash-page.tsx:91` through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:653`.

---

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/children`

**Purpose** — The direct children of one container.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility of `{nodeId}`. The children are additionally pruned by their own
visibility, subtree-wide.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | Must be a `project` or `folder`. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeArchived` | boolean | no | `false` | The drive listing excludes archived children (`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:47-49`); the Archive view needs them. |
| `includeTrashed` | boolean | no | `false` | Trashed nodes are detached and normally absent. `true` is for an admin diagnostic, never a product surface. |
| `limit` | integer | no | 500 | Hard cap 1000. Unpaginated (canon §6.3). |

Sort is **not** a query parameter: `sortNodes` runs client-side over the loaded array
(`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:54`, `src/lib/tree.ts:255-276`) and `ViewMode` / `SortKey` are
drive-listing-only, `ViewMode` explicitly never persisted server-side (canon §2.6).

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly DriveNode[]`, ordered deterministically as
`(container_first, lower(name), id)` — matching the client's default
`{ key: "name", direction: "asc" }` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:234`) and its `TYPE_WEIGHT`
grouping (`project` 0, `folder` 1, `document` 2, `board` 3, `file` 4 — `src/lib/tree.ts:247-253`).
`id` is the tiebreaker so two same-named siblings never swap between requests. Each element's
`children` is `[]`; use this endpoint again, or E-020, to go deeper.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | `{nodeId}` + ancestor chain — gate 2 on the container itself. |
| `nodes` | READ | `WHERE parent_id = :nodeId AND deleted_at IS NULL` (+ `archived_at IS NULL` unless `includeArchived`), index `nodes_parent_idx (parent_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Rows on the chain **and on each child**, to run `admits` per child. |
| `node_favorites` | READ | `WHERE user_id = :session_user AND node_id = ANY(:children)` → each child's `isFavorite`. |
| `users` | READ | Owners. |
| `boards`, `documents`, `file_nodes`, `file_assets` | READ | The kind-specific projected fields — `templateId`, `blockCount`/`excerpt`, `sizeBytes`/`extension`/`mimeType`/`version`. |

**Pruning is subtree-wide, and that is the point.** A child the caller may not see is **absent**, not
greyed out — and because a refused node takes its whole subtree with it, the invisible child's own
descendants can never leak into a later call either (`collectAllowed`, `src/lib/tree.ts:297-320`).

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None on read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown or invisible. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — `{nodeId}` is a document, board or file. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:42-49` (`location.children`, filtered and
sorted into `visibleChildren`), rendered by `src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx` and
`src/components/drive/drive-grid.tsx`. The sidebar's recursive tree reads the same data from the
store (`src/components/tree/folder-tree.tsx:48-104`).

---

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/tree`

**Purpose** — The whole drive tree of a workspace, nested, as the caller is allowed to know it.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Membership. Per-node visibility is applied inside the response, not as a gate on the
call.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `depth` | integer | no | unlimited | **RECOMMENDATION** (canon OQ-13). Children beyond `depth` are omitted and their container carries `hasMoreChildren: true`, to be fetched with E-023. The frontend tolerates a partial tree already: `resolvePath` returns `isNotFound` with the crumbs it did resolve (`src/lib/tree.ts:40-60`). |
| `includeArchived` | boolean | no | `true` | Archived nodes stay **in** the tree — they are filtered at the listing layer, not here (`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:47-49`), and the Archive view needs them (`src/components/collections/archive-page.tsx:28-34`). |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly DriveNode[]` — the root-level nodes, each container carrying its
`children` array recursively. Trashed nodes are **never** included: they are detached and live in the
trash listing (E-036).

**The pruning contract** — `visibleTree` (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:197-240`), and this is
the single most load-bearing read in the product:

- Pruned **once, from the root down, carrying the decision** — one pass over the tree rather than a
  chain walk per node.
- A refused node **takes its whole subtree with it**. *"That is what stops a board inside a restricted
  folder from surfacing in search, favourites or a relation picker just because the board itself
  carries no restriction of its own."*
- A non-member gets `[]` (`:201`) — not an error, not a partial tree.
- Everything downstream reads *this* tree: *"no surface asks 'may I show this', because what it was
  handed is already the answer"* (`:192-196`). Search (E-035, E-133), favourites (E-033), My Work
  (E-134), the dashboard (E-135) and the relation picker (E-071) all resolve against the pruned set,
  which is why this endpoint's correctness is not a listing concern.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + the caller's workspace role, which is the floor for `effectiveAccess`. |
| `nodes` | READ | **One flat scan**: `WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND deleted_at IS NULL`, index `nodes_workspace_kind_idx (workspace_id, kind) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. Nested in memory by `parent_id`. No recursive CTE — the whole workspace is being read anyway, and a CTE would be strictly more work. |
| `access_rules` | READ | **All rules for the workspace**, `WHERE workspace_id = :ws`, index `access_rules_workspace_idx`. Loaded into a `Record<nodeId, AccessRule[]>` — exactly the shape the resolver walks (`src/store/permission-store.ts:21-31`). |
| `node_favorites` | READ | `WHERE user_id = :session_user AND workspace_id = :ws`, one set membership test per node. |
| `users` | READ | Every distinct `owner_id`, resolved once and shared. |
| `boards`, `documents`, `file_nodes ⋈ file_assets` | READ | The projected per-kind fields, one batch join each. **Never a board's rows** — E-048 makes that rule explicit and it applies here too. |

The whole read is `O(nodes + rules)` with no per-node query. That is the reason for the flat scan:
one round trip, one prune pass, one response.

**Transaction** — Not required. Use one read-only snapshot so the tree cannot be internally
inconsistent (a child present whose parent was concurrently trashed).

**Realtime** — None on read. Convergence comes from `node.changed` (RT-11) and `permission.changed`
(RT-05).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown or not a member. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/workspace-store.ts:1041` (`selectTree`) and
`src/hooks/use-workspace-access.ts:88` (`useVisibleTree`), which together feed
`src/components/tree/folder-tree.tsx`, `src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx`,
`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:33`, `src/lib/breadcrumbs.ts` and every smart-view page under
`src/components/collections/`.

---

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/access`

**Purpose** — Who can see this folder, what each of them can do once inside, and **where each answer
came from**. This one endpoint serves both "get access" and "list who has access": the mode and the
list are one read because the dialog asks one question in two halves — *is this shut*, and if so,
*who is in* (`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:117-127`).

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.access.manage` on the node, **or** `workspace.permission.manage`, plus
membership. That disjunction is the frontend's:
`canManage = can("node.access.manage") || can("workspace.permission.manage")`
(`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:80`). `node.access.manage` is Manager+ — *"Restricting a folder is
structural, not administrative: a project lead shuts their own folder without waiting on a workspace
admin"* (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:44-47`) — and `workspace.permission.manage` is Admin.

**RECOMMENDATION — the read and the write need different keys.** The dialog renders for anybody who
can open the menu entry and shows *"You can see who has access, but not change it"* when they cannot
manage (`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:301-305`), so the **read** should require
only visibility, and the response should carry a `canManage` flag. Canon E-040 lists
`node.access.manage`; this specification follows canon for the gate and adds the flag, so a future
loosening is additive.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | Any node. **Not folders only** — the mode has always been on the base node type and the resolver has always walked every kind; *"the restriction was only ever in the menu"* (`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:52-60`). Restricting a single `.env` file is the case people reach for first. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `NodeAccessResponse`, `200`.

```ts
/** canon E-040. */
interface NodeAccessResponse {
  readonly accessMode: NodeAccessMode;              // "inherit" | "workspace" | "restricted"
  /** The nearest ancestor that actually decides something, for the
   *  "Right now that is Backend" line on the Inherit card. Null when the
   *  chain is unbroken `inherit` all the way up — the UI then says
   *  "the whole workspace". */
  readonly inheritedFrom: AccessOrigin | null;      // { nodeId, name }
  /** One row per workspace member, plus one per role-scoped rule anywhere on
   *  the chain. Sorted by roleRank DESCENDING. */
  readonly entries: readonly ResolvedAccess[];
  /** Whether THIS caller may write the endpoints below. RECOMMENDATION. */
  readonly canManage: boolean;
}

/** src/types/permission.ts:160-171 — unchanged. */
interface ResolvedAccess {
  readonly subject: AccessSubject;                  // { kind:"user", userId } | { kind:"role", role }
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;                     // what they effectively hold HERE
  readonly source: AccessSource;                    // workspace | inherited | explicit | override
  readonly origin: AccessOrigin | null;             // node the rule is written on; null = workspace default
  readonly inheritedRole: WorkspaceRole | null;     // what they would have had with no rule here
  readonly inheritedFrom: AccessOrigin | null;      // ancestor the inherited value came from
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive: the id DELETE .../access-rules/{ruleId} needs.
   *  Null when `source` is "workspace" or "inherited" — there is no rule here
   *  to revoke. */
  readonly ruleId: string | null;
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/access
{
  "accessMode": "restricted",
  "inheritedFrom": { "nodeId": "a11e…", "name": "Development" },
  "canManage": true,
  "entries": [
    {
      "subject": { "kind": "user", "userId": "usr_duc" },
      "role": "member", "source": "override",
      "origin": { "nodeId": "b22f…", "name": "Backend" },
      "inheritedRole": "manager",
      "inheritedFrom": { "nodeId": "a11e…", "name": "Development" },
      "ruleId": "d4c1…"
    },
    {
      "subject": { "kind": "role", "role": "viewer" },
      "role": "member", "source": "explicit",
      "origin": { "nodeId": "b22f…", "name": "Backend" },
      "inheritedRole": null, "inheritedFrom": null,
      "ruleId": "e5b2…"
    }
  ]
}
```

**The four `AccessSource` values, and exactly what each means**
(`src/types/permission.ts:146-153`, computed at `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:108-119`):

| `source` | Meaning | How it is decided |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace` | No rule anywhere on the chain; they hold their workspace role. | `chain` has no match at all |
| `inherited` | A rule on an **ancestor** reaches them; nothing is written here. | `own` is null, `inherited` is not |
| `explicit` | A rule **is** written here, and it agrees with what would have flowed down. | `own.role === wouldHave` |
| `override` | A rule is written here and **replaces** what would have flowed down. | `own.role !== wouldHave` |

Badge labels: `"Workspace role"`, `"Inherited"`, `"Explicit"`, `"Override"`
(`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:170-175`).

**Row composition** — `resolveAccess` (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:127-167`):

1. One row for **every workspace member**, whether or not any rule names them.
2. Plus one row for **every role-scoped rule anywhere on the chain** whose subject is not already
   listed — *"a grant that covers a group is never invisible just because it names no one"*
   (`:136-146`).
3. Sorted `roleRank(b.role) - roleRank(a.role)` — admins first (`:166`).

**Matching, within one node** — `matchIn` (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:55-79`): a rule naming
the **person** outranks a rule naming their **role** at the same depth, and the **deepest** node on
the chain wins overall. That is canon's OQ-22 position — *"Deepest node wins; at one node a
user-scoped rule beats a role-scoped rule; the workspace role is the floor"* — and it is deliberately
**not** the PRD's `SY-INH-43` edge case, which says *"Áp dụng mức quyền cao hơn (Union of
permissions)."* Follow canon; the code is the deepest-wins version and a union would silently widen
every override that narrows.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1, the caller's role, **and** the full member list — every member becomes a row. |
| `nodes` | READ | The node + its ancestor chain, root-first, by recursive CTE. `accessMode` and `inheritedFrom` both come from this walk: `inheritedFrom` is the deepest ancestor (excluding self) whose `access_mode <> 'inherit'` (`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:104-116`); when there is none, the client renders *"the whole workspace"*. |
| `access_rules` | READ | `WHERE node_id = ANY(:chain)` → `{ id, node_id, subject_kind, subject_user_id, subject_role, role, granted_at, granted_by }`. Index `access_rules_workspace_idx (workspace_id, node_id)`. |
| `users` | READ | Names for the subjects. |

Cardinality: at most one rule per `(node_id, subject)` — enforced by the two partial unique indexes
`access_rules_node_user_uniq` and `access_rules_node_role_uniq`, because `matchIn` takes the **first**
match within a node and a duplicate would make resolution order-dependent.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None on read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — neither `node.access.manage` nor `workspace.permission.manage`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown or invisible. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:82-116` (`granted`, `candidates`,
`inheritedFrom`) and `src/hooks/use-permissions.ts:148-157` (`useAccessList` → `resolveAccess`),
rendered by `src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:223-291` and
`src/components/permissions/access-list.tsx:22-27`.

**One deliberate omission.** The response never carries `NodeVisibility.deniedAt` — the node that
refused. It exists for the server's own bookkeeping and is *"never rendered to the person who was
refused, who is not entitled to learn that a folder called Finance exists"*
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:137-145`).

---

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/access-mode`

**Purpose** — Set how a folder decides who may see it: `inherit`, `workspace` or `restricted`.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.access.manage` (Manager+) **or** `workspace.permission.manage` (Admin), plus
membership and visibility.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | Any node kind. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. */
interface SetNodeAccessModeRequest {
  readonly accessMode: NodeAccessMode;   // "inherit" | "workspace" | "restricted"
}
```

**What each mode does** (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:35-45, 121-135`, and the three cards the
dialog renders):

| Mode | Behaviour | Card copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inherit` | Passes through whatever flows in from the nearest deciding ancestor. **The default; almost every node.** | *"Whoever can see the folder this sits in."* + *"Right now that is {ancestor}."* |
| `workspace` | Every workspace member, **from this node downward**. Cannot punch back up through a restriction above. | *"Everyone in the workspace, whatever the parent says."* |
| `restricted` | Discards what flowed in. Only the subjects granted here — plus the node's owner — are admitted. Stops inheritance at this node. | *"Only the people listed below."* |

**Response** — `DriveNode` — the authoritative record, with `accessMode` set (and **omitted** from the
JSON when it is `inherit`, per canon C-08 and `accessModeOf`).

**The lock-out rule — this endpoint's one non-obvious obligation.**

```
IF accessMode = 'restricted' AND NOT hasGrantOn(node, actor):
    INSERT the actor's own access_rules row FIRST, at their current effective role
UPDATE nodes SET access_mode = 'restricted'
```

Both statements are in **one transaction, in that order**. `useNodeAccess.setMode`
(`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:118-143`) does exactly this and says why:

> Grant before restricting, not after: the order is what makes it impossible to lock yourself out
> with one dropdown.

The role granted is the actor's own workspace role, falling back to `"manager"`
(`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:132`). `wouldLockOut` (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:342-348`) is
the predicate; it is checked **before** the write because *"a folder you cannot see is a folder you
cannot re-open."* A mode flip that commits without the grant produces a folder only its owner and the
admin recovery console can reopen.

`hasGrantOn` already admits the node's **owner** unconditionally
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:87-93`) — *"Somebody has to be able to get back into a folder they
shut, and 'whoever made it' is a rule a person can hold in their head"* — so an owner restricting
their own folder needs no extra row, and the guard correctly does nothing.

**Widening is the change worth confirming.** `restricted → workspace` shows a confirmation dialog
first (`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:165-173, 316-327`) — *"Widening access is
the change worth stopping to confirm: it is the one that shows a folder to people who could not see it
a moment ago."* That is a client gate; the API takes no confirmation field, for the same reason E-011
and E-032 do not.

**Existing grants survive a mode change.** Switching to `workspace` does not delete the
`access_rules` rows — the dialog says so: *"The people listed here keep the roles they were given"*
(`:320`). They stop gating **visibility** (because `admits` returns `isMember` for `workspace`) while
continuing to decide **capability** through `effectiveAccess`. The two axes stay separate, which is
the whole design.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1, the caller's role, and the role the self-grant will use. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + ancestor chain `FOR UPDATE` on the node — gate 2, gate 3, `deleted_at IS NULL`, no archived ancestor. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Rows on this node — is the actor already granted? |
| `access_rules` | INSERT | **Conditionally**, the actor's own rule, before the update. `ON CONFLICT (node_id, subject_user_id) WHERE subject_kind='user' DO UPDATE SET role = EXCLUDED.role`. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `SET access_mode = :mode, updated_at = now(), updated_by = :session_user`. **One row.** Descendants are never stamped: `tests/folder-access.test.ts:423-442` builds a 201-deep tree, restricts the root, and asserts exactly one rule key exists. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.permission.manage`, severity **`warn`**, target = the node name, `detail` = e.g. `Access set to Restricted.` The frontend already audits both rule writes at `warn` (`src/store/permission-store.ts:71-78, 99-106`); the mode change belongs in the same trail. |

`is_shared` on the wire is derived — `EXISTS(access_rules WHERE node_id = …)` — so the conditional
self-grant flips it as a side effect, correctly.

**Transaction** — **Required.** Self-grant, mode update and audit row are one unit. This is the second
transaction in the specification whose ordering is a correctness property rather than tidiness.

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, userIds }` where `userIds` is
every member whose visibility of this node changed — computed the same way as E-026's `impact`, by
evaluating `canSeeNode` before and after. Ids only: *"a frame announcing a revocation must not be the
thing that leaks what was revoked"* (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`). The same write must bust any
server-side authorisation cache keyed `(workspaceId, userId)`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `accessMode` is not one of the three. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:136` (`setNodeAccessMode`) through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:412`, driven by
`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:200-215` (the three `RadioCard`s).

---

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules`

**Purpose** — Grant a user (or a whole role) a role on this folder, or change the one they already
have. Upsert by `(node, subject)`.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.access.manage` **or** `workspace.permission.manage`, plus membership and
visibility.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. */
interface SetAccessRuleRequest {
  readonly subject: AccessSubject;   // { kind: "user", userId } | { kind: "role", role }
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
}
```

`PUT` rather than `POST` because it is idempotent: *"upsert by `(node, subject)`; **replaces any
existing rule for the same subject**"* (canon E-042). The frontend's write path is the same function
for "add somebody" and "change their role" — `access.grant(userId, role)` is called from the add box
(`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:181`) and from the per-row role select (`:249`).

**The subject must be a workspace member.** Folder access is downstream of membership and never a way
around it — the add box's empty state says so: *"Nobody matching “{query}” is a member of this
workspace. Invite them in Workspace settings first"*
(`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:100-115`), with the comment *"silently pulling
them in here would make a folder dialog a membership control."* A `user` subject that is not a member
is `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` (404).

**The default role when adding somebody** is the role they already hold in the workspace
(`:178-182` — *"Somebody is added at the role they already hold in the workspace; the select on their
row is where it gets narrowed afterwards"*). The client sends it explicitly; the API has no default.

**Response** — `AccessRule`, `200` (or `201` when the row is new).

```ts
/** src/types/permission.ts:136-144 — unchanged. */
interface AccessRule {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly subject: AccessSubject;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly grantedAt: string;   // ISO 8601, server clock
  readonly grantedBy: string;   // user id, FROM THE SESSION (canon C-09)
}
```

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + the caller's role. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain — gate 2, gate 3, `deleted_at IS NULL`, no archived ancestor. |
| `workspace_members` | READ | The **subject**, for a `user` subject: must be a member of this workspace. |
| `access_rules` | UPSERT | `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (node_id, subject_user_id) WHERE subject_kind='user' DO UPDATE SET role = EXCLUDED.role, granted_at = now(), granted_by = :session_user` (and the mirror index for `role` subjects). One row per `(node, subject)`; the `subject_is_exclusive` check keeps `subject_user_id` and `subject_role` mutually exclusive. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.permission.manage`, severity **`warn`**, target = the node name, `detail` = `{subjectLabel} set to {Role} on this item.` — verbatim from `src/store/permission-store.ts:71-78`, where `subjectLabel` is the person's name or *"everyone with the {Role} role"* (`:42-45`). |

**Transaction** — Required (upsert + audit). No advisory lock: this does not change the tree's shape,
and the unique indexes make the upsert race-safe on their own.

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, userIds }`. For a `user`
subject, `userIds` is that one id. For a `role` subject it is **every member currently holding that
role** — the grant reaches them by role, and each of them must re-resolve.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed `subject`, unknown `role`, or a `user` subject naming the node's owner with a role that would be ignored anyway (accept it; the owner is admitted regardless). |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`; `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` — the subject is not in this workspace. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:145-151` (`grant`) through
`src/store/permission-store.ts:56` (`setAccessRule`), driven by
`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:181, 249` and
`src/components/permissions/access-list.tsx:25` (`onGrant`), and by the admin recovery surface
`src/components/workspace/workspace-restricted-tab.tsx:39`.

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules/{ruleId}`

**Purpose** — Revoke one grant, so the subject inherits again.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.access.manage` **or** `workspace.permission.manage`, plus membership and
visibility.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |
| `ruleId` | UUID | The `access_rules` row. Comes from `AccessRule.id` (E-042's response) or from `ResolvedAccess.ruleId` (E-040's response, the additive field). |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `204 No Content`. This is the second documented exception to canon C-10: the resource
is gone, and the client re-reads E-040 to see the node's new resolved state — which it must anyway,
because removing one rule can change several rows' `source` from `override` to `inherited`.

**What revoking means.** *"Remove the rule written here, so the node inherits again"*
(`src/store/permission-store.ts:37`). It does not deny anybody: it deletes the local decision and
lets the ancestor's decision flow through. On a `restricted` node that is effectively a removal,
because nothing flows through a restriction; on an `inherit` or `workspace` node the subject keeps
whatever they had from above.

**A no-op writes nothing, including no audit row.** `clearAccessRule` returns the state unchanged
when nothing matched (`src/store/permission-store.ts:97`) and therefore records nothing —
`tests/audit.test.ts:275-284` asserts it. The API's equivalent: a `ruleId` that does not exist on
this node is `404`, and no audit row is written.

**Revoking the last grant is allowed, and announced.** `useNodeAccess.revoke`
(`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:153-169`) pushes feedback when `granted.length === 1`: *"{name} now has
nobody but its owner. An admin can reopen it from Workspace settings."* The API does **not** refuse
it — the owner is always admitted (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:87-93`) and the admin recovery
console (E-046) can always reach it — so no folder can be locked beyond recovery.

**Owners cannot be revoked from their own node.** The dialog hides the control for the owner row
(`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:257`) and, more importantly, the owner's admission
does not come from a rule at all: `hasGrantOn` returns true on the first line, before any rule is
consulted. Deleting an owner's explicit rule (if one exists) is legal and changes nothing about their
visibility; it may change their **capability**, which comes from `effectiveAccess`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + the caller's role. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain — gate 2, gate 3, `deleted_at IS NULL`, no archived ancestor. |
| `access_rules` | READ | `WHERE id = :ruleId AND node_id = :nodeId FOR UPDATE`. The `node_id` predicate is not redundant: without it a rule id from another node would delete somebody else's grant. |
| `access_rules` | DELETE | The row. **Hard delete** — a grant is either written here or not; a soft-deleted grant is a third state the resolver has no branch for. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `workspace`, action `workspace.permission.manage`, severity **`warn`**, target = the node name, `detail` = `{subjectLabel} now inherits access instead of holding it here.` — verbatim from `src/store/permission-store.ts:99-106`. |

**Transaction** — Required (delete + audit).

**Realtime** — `permission.changed` (RT-05), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, userIds }` — the revoked user, or
every member holding the revoked role. This is the frame that matters most: without it a revoked user
keeps a loaded board on screen until they reload, and the load already happened
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:19-91` — *"stop showing it"* is free because the tree is derived,
*"drop what was already loaded"* is not, because *"those are copies, and a copy does not re-derive
itself"*).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, or no such rule on this node. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:153-169` (`revoke`) through
`src/store/permission-store.ts:92` (`clearAccessRule`), driven by
`src/components/permissions/node-access-dialog.tsx:262` and
`src/components/permissions/access-list.tsx:26` (`onReset`).

**A wire mismatch a backend developer will hit immediately.** The frontend revokes **by subject** —
`clearAccessRule(workspaceId, node, { kind: "user", userId })` — and never handles a rule id. Canon
E-043 addresses the rule by id. Follow canon; the `ruleId` field recommended on `ResolvedAccess`
(E-040) is what closes the gap, and it is additive. See Chapter notes.

**Node ownership transfer.** There is no endpoint for it and canon reserves none.
`nodes.owner_id` is genuinely load-bearing — it escalates `node.rename`, `node.delete`,
`node.archive`, `file.delete` and `document.lock` from `member` upward
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:102-108`) and it unconditionally admits the owner to a restricted node
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:87-93`) — so a transfer moves real authority, unlike the
workspace-ownership attribute in §9. Nothing in the frontend changes `owner`: the only writer is
creation, and `cloneNode` copies it (`src/lib/tree.ts:209`). If a transfer endpoint is ever added it
belongs beside these four, gated on `workspace.permission.manage`, restricted to targets who are
workspace members, audited at `warn`, and emitting RT-05 for both the old and the new owner — because
the old owner may lose sight of a restricted node the moment they stop owning it.


---

## 12. Page APIs

Module `documents`. A **page** is a `nodes` row with `kind = 'document'` and `document_kind = 'page'`
(absent means `page` — `documentKindOf`, `src/types/node.ts:144`), plus its 1:1 content row in
`documents` (T-18). Config and secret documents are the same node kind with a different content
table and are specified in the devtools chapter; everything in this section is the `page` kind.

Canon P-04 governs the addressing: **content is entered through its node.** `GET
/nodes/{nodeId}/document` returns the document including `document.id`; the node id is the routing
key every endpoint here takes, and it is what the frontend already holds
(`WorkspaceDocument.nodeId`, *"Drive node this document is addressed by"*,
`src/types/document.ts:119-120`).

### 12.0 The content model, stated once

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `WorkspaceDocument.blocks: readonly Block[]` — **a flat, ordered array. No
nesting, no `position` field, no per-block endpoint anywhere in the frontend.**

- Order **is** array order. Every structural operation is an array transform:
  `insertBlockAt`, `insertBlockAfter`, `removeBlock`, `duplicateBlock`, `moveBlock`,
  `moveBlockToInsertionIndex`, `moveBlockBy` (`src/lib/blocks.ts:117-200`).
- Numbered-list ordinals are **derived at render time** by counting consecutive `numberedList`
  blocks and resetting on anything else
  (`src/components/document/block-editor.tsx:29-38`). No ordinal is stored.
- **A page is never blockless.** Removing the last block yields a fresh empty paragraph
  (`src/lib/blocks.ts:139-147`), and a new page starts with exactly one
  (`emptyDocumentBlocks`, `src/lib/blocks.ts:78-80`).
- **Block ids are client-minted and unique only within a document** — `blk_<n>` from `useBlockIds`,
  `blk_<nodeId>_<n36>` at creation (`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:75`), `blk_<seq>` on duplicate
  (`src/services/document-service.ts:251`), and hand-written ids like `pin_1` in the seed data
  (`src/mock/document-content.ts:9`). They are **not** UUIDs and are **not** globally unique.

`Block` is a 9-interface discriminated union over 14 `BlockType` values
(`src/types/document.ts:4-110`); its JSONB structure and the validation rules for each arm are
specified with the `documents` table in part 6, and this section does not restate them.

Three derived values the server owns, because both sides otherwise compute them and drift:

| Value | Definition | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `documentLines(blocks)` | The structural line projection — `# `, `## `, `> `, `• `, `[x] `, fenced code, `[image] …`, `[file] …`, `[link] …`, `\| a \| b \|`, `[board] …` (`src/lib/blocks.ts:371-393`). | version summaries, diffs, search |
| `documentExcerpt(blocks, 120)` | Plain text collapsed to single spaces, trimmed, truncated with `…` (`src/lib/blocks.ts:395-398`). | `nodes.excerpt`, drive listing subtitle |
| `blocks.length` | — | `nodes.block_count` |

---

### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` — creating a page

**Purpose** — Create a page: the drive node and its first block array, in one call.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` **and** `document.create` on the parent, plus membership and
visibility of the parent. Both are Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:39, 58`); canon E-024
requires the second key *"by kind"*.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
interface CreateDocumentNodeRequest extends CreateNodeRequestBase {
  readonly kind: "document";
  /** Absent means "page" — the original document kind (src/types/node.ts:97-98). */
  readonly documentKind?: DocumentKind;   // "page" | "config" | "secret"
  /** Emoji. Defaults by kind: page 📄, config ⚙️, secret 🔐. */
  readonly icon?: string;
  /** Config documents only; ignored by every other kind. */
  readonly format?: ConfigFormat;
}
```

`blocks` is **not** a field. A new page's content is fixed: exactly one empty paragraph
(`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:69-76` seeds `emptyDocumentBlocks`). Accepting a block array here
would be a second write path into `documents.blocks` with none of E-092's validation, folding or
version accounting.

Defaults, reproduced from `createDocument` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:745-790`) and
`useCreateDocument` (`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:14-18, 40-88`):

| Field | Default | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `"Untitled"` when the trimmed value is empty | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:759` |
| `icon` | `"📄"` for `page` | `src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:15` |
| `documentKind` | `"page"`; **omitted from the stored row and from the wire when it is `page`** | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:774` — `...(documentKind === "page" ? {} : { documentKind })` |
| `blocks` | one empty `paragraph` block | `src/lib/blocks.ts:78-80` |
| `blockCount` | `1` | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:776` |
| `excerpt` | `""` | `:777` |
| `isPinned`, `isLocked`, `isArchived` | `false` | `:778-780` |
| `version` | `1` | `src/services/document-service.ts:294` |

**Containment is enforced, with the frontend's own sentence.** A page under a document, board or file
is refused: *"Pages can only live inside folders"* (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:749-755`) →
`NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` (409 / `conflict`).

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `document` variant), `201 Created`.

**RECOMMENDATION** — return `{ node, document }` so the client can navigate straight into an editor
without a second round trip. The frontend performs two calls today (`createNode` then
`documentService.create`, `src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:50, 69`) precisely because the mock has
no combined endpoint; the response shape is additive and the `node`-only form stays valid.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Parent `FOR UPDATE` + chain: gate 2, gate 3 (both keys), container check, frozen check. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules → effective role on the parent. |
| `nodes` | READ | Live sibling slugs for the mint. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | `kind='document'`, `document_kind` (`NULL` for a page), `icon`, `name`, `slug`, `owner_id = :session_user`, `is_pinned = false`, `locked_at = NULL`, `block_count = 1`, `excerpt = ''`, `access_mode = 'inherit'`. |
| `documents` | INSERT | `node_id` (**`UNIQUE NOT NULL`**), `workspace_id`, `blocks = [one paragraph]`, `plain_text = ''`, `version = 1`, `created_by`/`updated_by = :session_user`. |
| `document_versions` | INSERT | The version-1 snapshot, `is_autosave = false`, `summary` = `"1 lines"`. Part 6 recommends writing it here rather than lazily on first read, *"so a read is never a write"* — the frontend seeds it on read today (`src/services/document-service.ts:72-90`). |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.create`, severity `info`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The `nodes` row, the `documents` row and the version-1 snapshot land
together. A document node with no `documents` row is a `404` on a URL the sidebar is already
showing — the client navigates to the new page immediately
(`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:80`). The per-workspace advisory lock applies, as for every
create.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "created" }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `documentKind` not one of the three; `format` sent for a non-config kind; `color` sent on a document. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN` — `documentKind: "config"` with a `format` outside the 15 `ConfigFormat` values. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — missing `node.create` or `document.create`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_NOT_FOUND` (parent). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — *"Pages can only live inside folders"*. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:50` and `:69`, called from
`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:57` (the "Page" item),
`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx` and the drive toolbar. Through
`src/store/workspace-store.ts:745` and `src/services/document-service.ts:270`.

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/document`

**Purpose** — Read a page: its title, icon, block array, lock state and version.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility of `{nodeId}`. Reading is unaffected by the lock and by archiving —
*"Archived means frozen, not hidden away: the content stays readable and addressable"*
(`src/lib/archive.ts:7-9`), and locking narrows only `edit` and `upload`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:134-141`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | Must be `kind = 'document'` with `document_kind` `page` or `NULL`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `WorkspaceDocument`, `200`.

```ts
/** src/types/document.ts:117-134 — unchanged. */
interface WorkspaceDocument {
  readonly id: string;              // documents.id
  readonly nodeId: string;          // the routing key
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly title: string;           // PROJECTED from nodes.name
  readonly icon: string;            // PROJECTED from nodes.icon (emoji)
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
  readonly isPinned: boolean;       // PROJECTED from nodes.is_pinned
  readonly isLocked: boolean;       // nodes.locked_at IS NOT NULL
  readonly lockedBy: UserSummary | null;   // nodes.locked_by; null when unlocked
  readonly isArchived: boolean;     // nodes.archived_at IS NOT NULL — REQUIRED here,
                                    //   unlike the optional isArchived? on DriveNodeBase
  readonly owner: UserSummary;      // nodes.owner_id
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly version: number;         // documents.version
}
```

Six fields are **projections of the node, not duplicated columns** (canon OQ-30 position): `title`
from `nodes.name`, `icon`, `isPinned`, `isLocked`/`lockedBy`, `isArchived`, `owner`. One source of
truth, and the join is on a unique index.

`isArchived` is **required** on `WorkspaceDocument` and on `DocumentNode`
(`src/types/node.ts:103`), unlike the optional `isArchived?` on `DriveNodeBase` (`:66`). Emit it
always for documents; omit it when false everywhere else.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | `{nodeId}` + ancestor chain — gate 2, and `kind`/`document_kind` assertion. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules for gate 2 and for the `CapabilitySet` the page surface needs. |
| `documents` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :nodeId` — `documents_node_id_key` unique index, one probe. |
| `users` | READ | `owner_id` and `locked_by`. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None on read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` — `That document could not be found`. Also the answer for a node the caller may not see. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` — the node exists and is a board, a folder or a config document. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document.ts:53-57` (`documentService.get` inside
`useAsyncResource`), rendered by `src/components/document/document-page.tsx:37`.

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/document`

**Purpose** — Save a page. This is the auto-save endpoint and the only write path into
`documents.blocks`.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `document.update` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:59`). `document.update` is in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:36-49`), which is exactly the set a lock closes — so a locked page
refuses this call at the permission layer *and* at the service layer, below.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4 — SaveDocumentRequest wraps DocumentDraft plus two optional fields. */
interface SaveDocumentRequest {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly icon: string;
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
  /** Optimistic concurrency (canon OQ-57). Absent = last-write-wins. */
  readonly expectedVersion?: number;
  /** True when the debounce produced this write rather than a person
   *  (⌘S, the Save button). Drives the version fold (canon OQ-59). */
  readonly isAutosave?: boolean;
}

/** src/types/document.ts:137-141 — the frontend's own body, unchanged. */
interface DocumentDraft {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly icon: string;
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
}
```

#### Auto-save: what "500 ms after typing stops" means for this endpoint

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500` (`src/lib/autosave.ts:3`), matching PRD
`WS-DOC-05`: *"Tự động lưu (Auto-save) sau mỗi 500ms khi ngừng gõ."* Config documents deliberately
use a slower one, `CONFIG_AUTOSAVE_MS = 1500` (`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:21`).

**The method is `PUT` with the whole draft, not `PATCH` with the changed blocks.** That is a
consequence of the client, not a preference, and there are five independent reasons — any one of
which would be sufficient:

1. **The client never computes a delta.** `useDocument.edit` builds `{ ...draft, ...patch }` — the
   complete draft — and hands that to the scheduler (`src/hooks/use-document.ts:92-101`). There is no
   diff, no dirty-block set and no baseline anywhere in the write path. A delta protocol would mean
   inventing all three.
2. **The scheduler coalesces, so intermediate states never reach the wire.** `schedule(draft)`
   overwrites `pending` and restarts the timer (`src/lib/save-scheduler.ts:90-102`); an edit landing
   while a request is in flight replaces `pending` and is re-sent whole once the request settles
   (`:56-87`). A delta stream requires every intermediate to arrive, in order. A coalescing client
   cannot produce one, and the guarantee the scheduler *does* make — *"the last thing the user typed
   always reaches the service"* (`:31-37`) — is a whole-state guarantee.
3. **A failed save keeps the draft pending and re-sends the same body** (`:78`, so `retry` has
   something to send). Re-sending a delta computed against a baseline the server may have moved past
   is unsound; re-sending the whole document is idempotent.
4. **Blocks have no positions and no server-stable identity.** Order is array order, and ids are
   client-minted and unique only within a document (§12.0). A patch expressing a reorder or a
   deletion would have to carry the resulting order — which is the whole array. The only "delta" that
   is expressible is the array itself.
5. **A version snapshot holds the full array anyway** (`DocumentVersion.blocks`,
   `src/types/system.ts:196`), so the server needs the complete document on every version-cutting
   save regardless of how the request was framed.

The endpoint is therefore a **full replace of the three draft fields**, and it is idempotent apart
from version accounting — which the fold rule below makes idempotent in practice too.

Three further behaviours the scheduler imposes on the server:

- **Navigating away still saves.** `dispose({ flushPending: true })` fires the pending draft
  fire-and-forget (`src/lib/save-scheduler.ts:114-122`), so the request outlives the component. The
  endpoint must not depend on the connection staying open past the write.
- **Cancellation is not a failure.** An aborted request is swallowed rather than reported
  (`:73-79`; `isCancellation`, mapping to `AppErrorCode` `cancelled`, `src/services/errors.ts:55-57`).
  Canon C-12 makes this a wire rule: an abort is `cancelled`, never a network error, and it is never
  an HTTP status because it never reaches one.
- **Saving is disabled lazily.** `isEnabled()` is re-read before every attempt, so a page locked
  mid-debounce stops saving before the server refuses it (`:61-62`). That is a courtesy; the server
  still refuses, because a stale tab in another window has no such courtesy.

**Write volume, and why it is not alarming.** A 500 ms debounce caps one editor at roughly two writes
per second while typing continuously, and in practice far fewer. **RECOMMENDATION:** rate-limit per
`(nodeId, userId)` at ~5 writes/second with `RATE_LIMITED` (429, `retryAfterSeconds`,
`isRetryable: true`), which no honest client can hit. The expensive half — cutting a version — is
folded away by the rule below, so a burst of autosaves is one `UPDATE documents` each and one
`UPDATE document_versions` on the head row, not 20 inserts.

#### Server-side rules on the body

| Rule | Behaviour | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blank title | **Coerced, not rejected**: `draft.title.trim().length > 0 ? draft.title : "Untitled"`. Note it stores the *untrimmed* original when non-blank. | `src/services/document-service.ts:207` |
| `version` | Incremented by exactly 1 on a non-folded save, server-side. Never accepted from the body. | `:211` |
| `updatedAt` | Server clock. Never accepted from the body. | `:210` |
| Locked page | **Refused before content is touched**: `conflict("This page is locked", "Unlock it before saving further changes.")` → `DOCUMENT_LOCKED`, 409. | `:192-194` |
| Block validation | Reject an unknown `type`, a `code` block with no `language`, a ragged `table.rows`, an `image` block whose `images[].assetId` names an asset the caller cannot reach. | part 6, `documents.blocks` |
| Size ceiling | ≤ 5000 blocks and ≤ 1 MB serialised → `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` (400). | part 6 `documents_block_ceiling`; canon OQ-58 |
| Never blockless | An empty array is rejected; the client cannot produce one (`src/lib/blocks.ts:139-147`). | `documents_never_blockless` |
| `assetId` references | `url` and `thumbnailUrl` inside image blocks are **ignored on write** — only `assetId` is persisted, and URLs are minted per response as short-lived signed URLs (canon OQ-75). | `src/types/document.ts:58-63` |

#### Concurrency

Canon §6.4: **optional `expectedVersion`; `409` `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` when stale,
last-write-wins when absent.**

```
IF request.expectedVersion IS PRESENT AND request.expectedVersion <> documents.version:
    REJECT DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT (409 / conflict)
    body: { error: {...}, current: <the authoritative WorkspaceDocument> }
```

Returning the current document in the error body is what lets a client say *"someone else edited this
page"* and show what it now holds. `DocumentDraft` carries no version today
(`src/types/document.ts:137-141`) and `save` compares none
(`src/services/document-service.ts:184-216`), so the field must be **tolerated when absent** or every
current client breaks on its first keystroke.

The silent-clobber risk is real and worth naming: the client keeps a local overlay draft that wins
over server data for non-content actions (`src/hooks/use-document.ts:103-119`), so a lost paragraph
never even flickers on screen.

#### Versioning — the fold rule

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT with a canon correction (OQ-59).** The mock cuts a version on **every**
successful save (`src/services/document-service.ts:214`), which at a 500 ms debounce means twenty
half-second pauses consume the entire 20-entry history (`VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`,
`src/config/app.ts:63`). The config service already solved this and the document service never
adopted it (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:160-187`). Canon's position: **fold consecutive
autosaves by the same author.**

```
foldsIn := request.isAutosave = true
        AND a head version exists
        AND head.is_autosave = true
        AND head.author_id = session.user

IF foldsIn:
    UPDATE document_versions          -- SAME row, SAME version number
       SET blocks = :blocks, title = :title,
           summary = describeDiff(pre-fold head.blocks -> :blocks),
           updated_at = now()
     WHERE id = head.id
    -- documents.version does NOT advance
ELSE:
    documents.version := documents.version + 1
    INSERT INTO document_versions (version = documents.version, is_autosave = :isAutosave, ...)
```

A manual save (⌘S, `src/components/document/document-page.tsx:59`) always starts a new version, and
so does another author's edit landing in between. The `summary` is recomputed against the **pre-fold
head's** blocks, not against the previous document — matching `devtools-service.ts:181` — so a folded
entry describes the whole span it now covers.

Retention: never drop the lowest version, never drop the head, then trim to the cap. Part 6
recommends 200 per page once folding is in place.

**Response** — `WorkspaceDocument`, `200`, the authoritative record (canon C-10). The client assigns
it directly: `resource.setData(saved)` (`src/hooks/use-document.ts:80`).

**RECOMMENDATION** — also return the updated `DriveNode`, so the client stops deriving the tree
summary itself:

```ts
interface SaveDocumentResponse {
  readonly document: WorkspaceDocument;
  readonly node: DriveNode;          // RECOMMENDATION, additive
}
```

The frontend computes `summarize(saved)` and applies it to the tree
(`src/hooks/use-document.ts:81`, `src/services/document-service.ts:160-171`); computing it
server-side inside the same transaction is one fewer rule living in two places.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + role. |
| `nodes` | READ | `{nodeId}` + ancestor chain `FOR UPDATE` on the node — gate 2, gate 3 (`document.update`), `deleted_at IS NULL` → else `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, no archived ancestor → else `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `locked_at IS NULL` → else `DOCUMENT_LOCKED`. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules → effective role. |
| `documents` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :nodeId FOR UPDATE` — the concurrency check and the version read. |
| `documents` | UPDATE | `blocks`, `plain_text = documentPlainText(blocks)`, `version` (unless folded), `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by = :session_user`. `search_vector` is `GENERATED … STORED` over `plain_text`, so it reindexes with no extra statement. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | The summary projection: `name = :coercedTitle`, `icon`, `block_count = length(blocks)`, `excerpt = documentExcerpt(blocks, 120)`, `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by`. **`slug` is NOT in the statement** — *"The slug is the routing key and is minted once, at creation: renaming a page the user is standing on must not break its URL"* (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:883-885`). |
| `document_versions` | INSERT or UPDATE | Per the fold rule. Unique `(document_id, version)`; a fold rewrites the same row at the same number and does not violate it. |
| `document_versions` | DELETE | Retention trim, if the cap is exceeded. |
| `document_asset_refs` | DELETE + INSERT | The `(node_id, block_id, asset_id)` projection of image and attachment blocks, rewritten to match the new array — it is what makes orphan collection and quota one query (canon T-31). |
| `audit_events` | — | **No row.** A page edit is ordinary activity, not an audit event; the audit log covers governance, secrets and structural actions (`src/services/audit-service.ts` seed set). Version history is the record of an edit. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** `documents`, the `nodes` summary, the version row and
`document_asset_refs` are one unit. A `documents` row whose `nodes.block_count` disagrees renders a
drive listing that contradicts the page; a version row without the content write is a history entry
for something that never happened.

**Realtime** — **None.** Canon §7 ships no document frame: RT-01…RT-05 cover comments,
notifications and permissions, and the recommended RT-06…RT-11 cover rows, board schema and the drive
tree. A page save emits nothing, so a second viewer sees stale content until they refetch. That is a
known gap (canon OQ-99), not an omission here — real-time co-editing of blocks is a different feature
with a different data model, and canon RT-12 (`presence.changed`) is explicitly *"Do not build this
until a surface asks for it."*

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed body. |
| 400 | `validation` | `BLOCK_TYPE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` — a block body that does not match its `type`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` — past the block-count or byte ceiling. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `document.update`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` — `This page is locked` / `Unlock it before saving further changes.` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` — `expectedVersion` is stale. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED` — carries `retryAfterSeconds`, `isRetryable: true`. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` — retryable; the client keeps the draft and offers Retry (`src/lib/autosave.ts:46-53`). |

Note `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` and `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` are `403`, not `409`: they are permission
narrowings (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-84`), and canon §4.3 files them under
`permission_denied`.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document.ts:77-84` (`persist`), driven by
`src/hooks/use-autosave.ts:32-77` and `src/lib/save-scheduler.ts:38-129`. Reachable from every edit
in `src/components/document/block-editor.tsx`, the title and icon in
`src/components/document/document-header.tsx`, and `⌘S`
(`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:59`). The status the user sees —
`Saving… / Saved · HH:MM / Unsaved changes / <error> + Retry` — is
`src/components/document/save-indicator.tsx:44-76`, and `beforeunload` is armed whenever
`hasPendingChanges || status === "saving" || status === "error"` (`src/lib/autosave.ts:66-68`,
`src/hooks/use-unsaved-warning.ts`).

### `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — deleting a page

**Purpose** — Move a page to the trash. The "D" of the block-document CRUD.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.delete` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+ **or the owner**.
Note the key is `node.delete`, not a `document.*` key: deleting a page is a drive operation, and the
frontend's page menu gates it on `capabilities.delete`, which projects `node.delete`
(`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:101`; `capabilitiesFor`,
`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:128`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `TrashEntry` (§10).

**Database** — as §10 and §11, with one page-specific rule stated as an **EXISTING REQUIREMENT**:

**No `documents`, `document_versions` or `document_asset_refs` row is touched.** Trash detaches the
node; content stays keyed by `node_id` and comes back intact on restore. The frontend proves it by
omission: the delete path calls `trashNode(node.id)` and navigates to the parent
(`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:114-121`); `documentService.remove` exists
(`src/services/document-service.ts:298-301`) and **no component calls it**. Part 6 makes the same
point from the schema side: `documents` has no `deleted_at` and is never soft-deleted.

The content dies only when the node is hard-deleted — E-038, E-039 or the 30-day sweep — through
`ON DELETE CASCADE`.

**Transaction** — Required, with the per-workspace advisory lock: subtree `deleted_at` stamp (a page
has no subtree, so one row), `trash_entries` insert, audit row.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "trashed"`.

**Possible Errors** — as §10: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` (403),
`NODE_NOT_FOUND` (404).

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:118`, from
`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:102`; also
`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:161`. Restore is E-037 (§10).

---

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/document/lock`

**Purpose** — Lock a page against edits, or unlock it.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `document.lock` on the node **or** the document's owner — `canToggleLock`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:143-153`):

```ts
export function canToggleLock(resolve, document, user): boolean {
  return resolve("document.lock") || document.owner.id === user.id;
}
```

`document.lock` is Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:60`) **and** is in `OWNER_ESCALATIONS`
(`:107`), so the owner path is doubly expressed; the escalation applies only from `member` upward
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:72-74`), meaning a Viewer who owns the page still cannot lock it.

**`document.lock` is NOT in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`** (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:36-49`), which is
what makes unlocking possible: a lock closes the content keys, and if it closed its own key the page
would be permanently frozen.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. One endpoint, both directions — PUT on a boolean sub-resource. */
interface SetDocumentLockedRequest {
  readonly isLocked: boolean;
}
```

**`lockedBy` is never in the body.** It is taken from the session (canon C-09, canon E-094 — *"`lockedBy`
is taken from the session, never the body"*). The frontend passes `CURRENT_USER`
(`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:83`) because a mock has no session; a real client passes nothing.

**Response** — `WorkspaceDocument`, `200`, with `isLocked` and `lockedBy` updated. Idempotent:
locking a locked page returns the record unchanged.

**What a lock is, and is not.**

- It is a **flag, not a lease**: no expiry, no heartbeat, no "locked for editing by me". Anyone with
  the key can unlock anyone's lock.
- It **narrows capabilities**: `edit` and `upload` become false
  (`documentCapabilities`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:134-141`). Reading is unaffected.
- It is **a write barrier, not a UI state**: the service refuses the save as well
  (`src/services/document-service.ts:192-194`), *"so a stale editor can never write over a page
  somebody froze."* The backend must refuse the same way.
- **Commenting is not editing.** The comment panel stays enabled on a locked page, gated on the
  *pre-lock* capability (`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:137-143`). A lock must not close
  `comment.create`.
- Unlocking clears `lockedBy` (`src/services/document-service.ts:232`); the pair is one fact and the
  `nodes_lock_pair` check enforces it.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + role. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain — gate 2, `deleted_at IS NULL`, no archived ancestor, and `owner_id` for the `canToggleLock` disjunction. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules → effective role. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `locked_at = now(), locked_by = :session_user` on lock; `locked_at = NULL, locked_by = NULL` on unlock. Plus `updated_at`, `updated_by`. |
| `documents` | UPDATE | `updated_at = now()` only. **`version` does not advance** — a lock is not an edit and must not appear in the history (`src/services/document-service.ts:223-235` bumps `updatedAt` and no version). |
| `document_versions` | *(no write)* | — |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | **RECOMMENDATION**: module `document`, action `document.lock`, severity `info`, target = the page title. The frontend records nothing, and canon OQ-25 leaves the emitter set open; a lock is a governance-adjacent act on shared content and is cheap to record. |

**Transaction** — Required (both updates + audit together).

**Realtime** — **None today** (canon OQ-99). The consequence is real: a second editor keeps typing
into a page that has just been locked and discovers it on their next debounce, as a `409` surfaced as
*"This page is locked"* with their draft still pending and retryable. **RECOMMENDATION:** when a
document frame is added, lock/unlock is its first justified use, because it changes what other people
may do rather than only what they see.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `isLocked` missing or not a boolean; `lockedBy` present in the body (reject it rather than ignoring it, so a client sending a claim learns it is not a fact). |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — neither `document.lock` nor the owner. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:77-88` (`toggleLock`), from
`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:66` and the banner's Unlock button
(`src/components/document/locked-banner.tsx:31-52`, which names the locker). Gated by
`actions.canToggleLock` (`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:135`).

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/document/pin`

**Purpose** — Pin a page to the sidebar, or unpin it.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `document.update` on the node, plus membership and visibility (canon E-093,
OQ-08). Manager+.

The frontend gates the menu item on **nothing at all** —
`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:59-62` has no `disabled` prop, unlike every
neighbouring item. That is a gap, not a rule: `documentService.setPinned` checks no permission either
(`src/services/document-service.ts:218-221`), which is the class of omission canon OQ-16 names
(*"40+ write operations carry no permission check in the mock"*) and canon's position closes
(*"Every write is gated server-side with the catalogue key the matrix defines"*).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. */
interface SetDocumentPinnedRequest {
  readonly isPinned: boolean;
}
```

**Response** — `WorkspaceDocument`, `200`. Idempotent.

**Pinning is global, not per-user — and that is a decision, not an accident.** The flag lives on the
shared record (`src/types/document.ts:126`, `nodes.is_pinned`), so one person's pinned page appears
in **everyone's** sidebar. The sidebar filter is
`isDocument(node) && node.isPinned && !node.isTrashed && !node.isArchived`
(`src/components/layout/sidebar/pinned-pages.tsx:26`). Only documents can be pinned; no other node
kind has the field.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-08)** — should pinning be per user?
**What is unclear** — the flag is global, yet the menu labels are *"Pin to sidebar"* / *"Unpin from
sidebar"* (`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:61`), and a sidebar is a personal
surface.
**Evidence** — `WorkspaceDocument.isPinned: boolean` and `DocumentNode.isPinned: boolean` are plain
booleans on the shared record. Favourites, the neighbouring concept, have the same tension
(`src/types/node.ts:58`) and canon **resolves that one the other way**: OQ-07's position is per user,
in `node_favorites` (T-07). Pinning gets no such table — canon OQ-08's position is *"Per user…
pinning follows the same shape once confirmed"*, which is a position deferred.
**Recommendation** — keep it global for v1 to match the frontend exactly, and document the migration:
a `node_pins (user_id, node_id)` join table, `is_pinned` becoming a per-request projection exactly as
`isFavorite` already is. Do not build the table now — nothing in the frontend reads a per-user list,
and building it would put `isPinned` and `isFavorite` on two different mechanisms for no benefit.
**Impact if wrong** — on a 40-person workspace the Pinned section fills with other people's pages and
becomes unusable, and the fix is a data migration rather than a schema addition.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + role. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain — gate 2, gate 3 (`document.update`), `deleted_at IS NULL`, no archived ancestor. **A locked page may still be pinned**: `document.update` is in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`, so a lock *does* close it — pinning a locked page is refused with `DOCUMENT_LOCKED`. That follows the frontend's capability model exactly, even though the menu item is not disabled. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `is_pinned = :isPinned`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`. |
| `documents` | UPDATE | `updated_at = now()` only. **`version` does not advance** (`src/services/document-service.ts:218-221`). |
| `audit_events` | *(no row)* | Pinning is a listing preference, not a governance act. |

**Transaction** — Required (both updates together), so the node and its content row cannot report
different `updatedAt` values.

**Realtime** — **RECOMMENDATION:** `node.changed` (RT-11) with `change: "renamed"` is the wrong verb
and there is no `"pinned"` member of the change enum (canon §7.2). Emit nothing today; when the enum
grows, a pin is a sidebar-convergence event and belongs there. Until then a second tab shows a stale
Pinned section until it refetches — a cosmetic staleness, unlike a permission one.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `isPinned` missing or not a boolean. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:68-75` (`togglePin`), from
`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:59`; the result is folded back with
`applyDocument`, which **protects an unsaved local draft** — *"Those actions never touch content, so
a local draft that has not been saved yet wins — otherwise toggling Pin would silently revert what
was typed"* (`src/hooks/use-document.ts:103-119`). The API's part of that contract is simply not
returning stale `blocks`: it returns what is stored, and the client decides.

### `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate` — duplicating a page

**Purpose** — Copy a page beside itself, content included.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` on the parent (the copy is a sibling) **and** `document.create`, plus
membership and visibility of the source. Manager+.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The page to copy. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `DuplicateNodeRequest` (§11): optional `targetParentId` and `name`.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `document` variant), `201 Created`.
**RECOMMENDATION**: `{ node, document }`, as for create, so the client can navigate straight in — it
does exactly that today (`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:97`).

**What the copy is** — the node rules from §11, plus the content reset from
`documentService.duplicate` (`src/services/document-service.ts:243-267`):

| Property | Value on the copy |
| --- | --- |
| `blocks` | copied, with **fresh block ids** for every block (`:251`) |
| `title` | the new node's name — `"{source.name} (copy)"` by default |
| `icon` | copied |
| `version` | **`1`** — the copy has no history |
| `document_versions` | **none copied**; a version-1 snapshot is written for the copy |
| `isPinned` | `false` (`:259`) |
| `isLocked` / `lockedBy` | `false` / `null` (`:260-261`) |
| `isArchived` | `false` (`:262`) |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | now (`:263-264`) |
| `owner` | **the caller** (RECOMMENDATION, §11) |
| `isFavorite`, `isShared`, `accessMode` | `false`, `false`, `inherit` |
| `document_asset_refs` | rewritten for the new node id, pointing at the **same** `file_assets` rows — no bytes are copied and `workspaces.used_bytes` does not move |

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Source + chain (gates); destination parent + live sibling slugs. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | The new document node. |
| `documents` | READ | The source's `blocks`. |
| `documents` | INSERT | The copy, fresh block ids, `version = 1`. |
| `document_versions` | INSERT | Version 1 for the copy. |
| `document_asset_refs` | INSERT | `(new_node_id, new_block_id, asset_id)` per image/attachment block. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | module `node`, action `node.create`, severity `info`. |

**Transaction** — **Required, and this is the specific failure the frontend cannot recover from.**
The client makes two calls — `duplicateNode(node.id)` then
`documentService.duplicate(sourceNodeId, clone.id, clone.name)`
(`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:90-99`) — and **has no compensating delete**, so a failure between
them leaves an orphan node with no content: a `404` on a URL the tree is already rendering. One
server-side transaction removes the state entirely.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "created"`.

**Possible Errors** — as §11's duplicate, plus `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` (404) when the source node has no
`documents` row.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:90-99`, from
`src/components/document/document-actions-menu.tsx:79`.
