### `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/versions`

**Purpose** — The page's version history, projected into the shape the shared history dialog reads.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility of `{nodeId}`. Reading history is reading.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | Page, config document or secret document — one endpoint family serves all three, and the node's kind selects the store (canon §3.14). |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | opaque base64 | no | — | Keyset cursor over `(version DESC)`. Never constructed or parsed by a client (canon §6.3). |
| `limit` | integer | no | 20 | Hard cap 100. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `VersionPage`, `200`.

```ts
interface VersionPage {
  readonly items: readonly VersionEntry[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/** src/types/system.ts:208-221 — unchanged. */
interface VersionEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;               // "+3 −1 lines" | "no line changes" | "renamed · …"
  readonly lines: readonly string[];      // documentLines(version.blocks)
  /** False when the version records THAT something changed without holding the
   *  value — a rotated secret. Never diffable, never restorable. */
  readonly hasSnapshot: boolean;
}
```

For a page: `lines = documentLines(version.blocks)` and `hasSnapshot: true`
(`documentVersionEntry`, `src/lib/versions.ts:21-31`). For a config: `content.split("\n")`,
`hasSnapshot: true`. For a secret: `lines: []`, `hasSnapshot: false` (`:50-62`) — and the UI hides
View, Compare and Restore entirely for those (`src/components/versions/version-list.tsx:84`).

**The projection is the server's job.** Returning `VersionEntry` already projected is what keeps the
three subjects identical on the client; returning `DocumentVersion` would put `documentLines` in the
browser for pages and `split("\n")` for configs, which is exactly the drift `src/lib/versions.ts`
exists to prevent.

**Return a copy, not a live list.** The config service snapshots the array on read for this reason
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:224-237`); server-side it is simply a `SELECT`, and the note
exists so nobody hands back a mutable cache.

**Ordering** — `version DESC` (newest first). The frontend's history is newest-first by construction
(`history.unshift(...)`, `src/services/document-service.ts:101`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain — gate 2, and the kind that selects the store. |
| `documents` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :nodeId` → `documents.id`. |
| `document_versions` | READ | `WHERE document_id = :id ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT :limit+1`, index `UNIQUE (document_id, version DESC)`. |
| `users` | READ | `author_id` → `UserSummary`. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:46-52` (`load`), through
`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:58` and `src/services/document-service.ts:114`. Loaded **only while
the dialog is open** (`enabled`, `src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:22-31`): *"A version list read at
mount is stale by the time somebody opens it — the page has been edited since."*

---

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}`

**Purpose** — One stored snapshot in full.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility of `{nodeId}`.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |
| `versionId` | UUID | Must belong to this node's document. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `DocumentVersion` for a page (`ConfigVersion` for a config document), `200`.

```ts
/** src/types/system.ts:192-201 — unchanged. */
interface DocumentVersion {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly title: string;                 // the title AT that version — a real snapshot
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];      // full snapshot, never a delta
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;               // "+3 −1 lines"
}
```

**Snapshots, never deltas** — *"so restoring never has to replay a chain"*
(`src/services/document-service.ts:63-69`). `summary` is server-computed:
`describeDiff(summarizeDiff(diffLines(documentLines(before), documentLines(after))))`, prefixed
`renamed · ` when the title also changed (`:99-109`; label forms `+3 −1 lines` / `no line changes`,
`src/lib/diff.ts:87-93`). It is never sent by a client.

**A secret version is refused here.** Canon E-096: *"`404`-equivalent refusal for a secret version"* —
`VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` (409) if the caller reached a rotation row by id, because a rotation records
*that* a key changed and holds no value (canon T-24, `src/lib/versions.ts:45-62`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain — gate 2. |
| `documents` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :nodeId`. |
| `document_versions` | READ | `WHERE id = :versionId AND document_id = :documentId` — **both predicates.** Without the second, a version id from another document would be readable through any node the caller can see. |
| `users` | READ | `author_id`. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` — `That version could not be found`. Also the answer for a version belonging to a different document. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` — a secret rotation has no snapshot and can never be read, diffed or restored. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/versions/version-detail.tsx:39` and
`src/components/versions/version-list.tsx`, which read the `lines` already carried by
`VersionEntry` from E-095. A page that needs the raw `blocks` — a future "open this version
read-only" surface — calls this endpoint directly.

**Compare stays on the client.** `diffLines` is an LCS line diff degrading past 2000 lines
(`src/lib/diff.ts:14-77`), and the comparison is always **stored version → what is on screen now**,
not version → version (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:16-18`,
`src/components/versions/version-detail.tsx:39`) — for a config that "now" includes the **unsaved
draft** (`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:115`), which is state the server has never seen.
`GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/diff?against=` (E-098) exists for version-to-version
comparison and is not what this surface uses.

### `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/restore`

**Purpose** — Bring a stored snapshot back as the current content.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `document.version.restore` on the node, plus membership and visibility. Manager+
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:61`). The key is also in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:42`), so a lock and an archived ancestor both close it — which is
the correct behaviour and the same one `save` has.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | — |
| `versionId` | UUID | Must belong to this node's document. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** canon §5.4. Empty; the version is addressed by path. */
interface RestoreVersionRequest {}
```

**Response** — `WorkspaceDocument` (or `ConfigDocument` for a config node), `200` — the document as it
now stands, at `version = previous + 1`.

**Restoring writes forward; it never rewinds.** `restoreVersion`
(`src/services/document-service.ts:126-135`) is literally implemented as a save:

```
restoreVersion(nodeId, versionId):
  version := the snapshot                       -> 404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND if absent
  RETURN save(nodeId, { title:  version.title,
                        icon:   <the CURRENT icon>,   -- not the version's
                        blocks: version.blocks })
```

Five consequences the backend must preserve, each an EXISTING REQUIREMENT:

1. **Restore inherits every rule `save` has.** A locked page refuses a restore for exactly the reason
   it refuses an edit (`:122-125`) → `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` (409). So do a trashed node and an archived
   ancestor.
2. **The icon is not restored.** Only `title` and `blocks`. The current icon is kept
   (`:134`).
3. **The new version number is `current + 1`**, not the restored number. The restore itself cuts a
   version, and *"the record of what happened stays complete, which is the whole point of keeping
   it"* (`:63-69`).
4. **A restore is never folded.** It is not an autosave: `isAutosave` is false, so it always inserts.
5. **The client reloads the list afterwards** rather than assuming what is on top
   (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:71`), because the restore added an entry.

Additionally: content restore **replaces the local draft outright**, unlike pin and lock which protect
it — *"the content is what changed, so the draft is replaced rather than protected. Anything unsaved
would otherwise sit on top of the version that was just brought back"*
(`src/hooks/use-document.ts:121-133`). The API's obligation is to return the authoritative document;
`applyRestoredDocument` does the rest.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + role. |
| `nodes` | READ | Node + chain `FOR UPDATE` — gate 2, gate 3 (`document.version.restore`), `deleted_at IS NULL`, no archived ancestor, `locked_at IS NULL`. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Chain rules. |
| `documents` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :nodeId FOR UPDATE` — the current version and blocks. |
| `document_versions` | READ | `WHERE id = :versionId AND document_id = :documentId` — both predicates. |
| `documents` | UPDATE | `blocks = version.blocks`, `plain_text`, `version = version + 1`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`. `icon` is **not** written. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | Summary projection: `name = version.title`, `block_count`, `excerpt`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`. **`slug` unchanged**, **`icon` unchanged**. |
| `document_versions` | INSERT | The new head, `is_autosave = false`, `summary` computed from the pre-restore blocks to the restored blocks, prefixed `renamed · ` when the title moved. |
| `document_versions` | DELETE | Retention trim, never touching the lowest version or the head. |
| `document_asset_refs` | DELETE + INSERT | Rewritten to match the restored block array. **This is the step most likely to be forgotten**: restoring an old version brings back image blocks whose assets may have been orphaned since, and the refs table is what keeps quota and garbage collection honest. An asset that was hard-deleted in the interim must be surfaced as a broken reference, not resurrected (canon OQ-72). |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | **RECOMMENDATION**: module `document`, action `document.version.restore`, severity `info`, target = the page title, `detail` = `Restored version {n}.` A restore discards everything since that version in one click; it is worth a row where an ordinary edit is not. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Content update, node summary, new version row, retention trim and the
asset-ref rewrite are one unit.

**Realtime** — None today (canon OQ-99), same gap as E-092.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `document.version.restore`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` — a secret rotation. |
| 400 | `validation` | `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` — cannot occur for a snapshot this server wrote; listed because a restored version from before a ceiling change could exceed it, and the honest answer is to refuse rather than to write an over-size row. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:54-59` (`restore`), through
`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:63-80` and `src/services/document-service.ts:126`. The result is
folded in with `applyRestoredDocument` (`src/hooks/use-document.ts:126-133`).

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-61)** — does `document.version.restore` gate restore, or is `edit` enough?
**What is unclear** — which key the endpoint checks.
**Evidence** — the key exists in the catalogue and the matrix at Manager+
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:61`, `src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts`) and **no frontend call site
uses it**. The dialog gates on `capabilities.edit`
(`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:160`), which a Member holds through node capabilities,
and `documentService.restoreVersion` checks nothing at all.
**Recommendation** — enforce `document.version.restore` server-side, as canon E-097 already names,
and change the client's gate to read the same key. Restoring is destructive in a way an ordinary edit
is not: it discards everything since that version in one action, and the diff the user saw was
against their *unsaved* screen state, not against the stored head.
**Impact if wrong** — either Members lose an ability the UI visibly offers them and every Restore
button returns `403`, or a Member rolls a shared page back a month without holding the key the matrix
says they need — and the only trace is a version entry that looks like an ordinary edit.

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

Ordered by how much they matter to a reader of the assembled document.

1. **§9 contains one endpoint that is not in canon's registry.**
   `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/ownership` ("transfer ownership") is marked **RECOMMENDATION, not
   in canon §3.2** in its own heading and again in its first line. Canon numbers 140 endpoints,
   E-001 … E-140, and E-007 … E-019 contain no transfer. The chapter brief asked for it explicitly,
   so it is specified rather than omitted, and it is specified as inert on purpose (it moves
   `workspaces.created_by` and grants nothing) so that adopting it cannot smuggle in the fifth role
   canon OQ-03 rejected. **If canon is extended, it wants an E-number between E-014 and E-015.** If it
   is not, delete the block and keep the OQ-02 discussion attached to §9.0.

2. **E-043 revokes by `ruleId`; the frontend revokes by subject, and E-040 does not return a rule id.**
   Canon E-042/E-043 address a grant as `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules` then
   `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules/{ruleId}`, but the read that populates the dialog (E-040)
   returns `ResolvedAccess[]`, and `ResolvedAccess` (`src/types/permission.ts:160-171`) has **no
   `id`**. As written, a client cannot obtain the `ruleId` it needs to revoke. §11 follows canon and
   closes the gap by adding `ruleId: string | null` to `ResolvedAccess` on the wire — additive,
   `null` when `source` is `workspace` or `inherited` because there is no rule here to revoke. The
   frontend's own action is subject-keyed (`clearAccessRule(workspaceId, node, subject)`,
   `src/store/permission-store.ts:92`). **Either canon §5.2 gains the `ruleId` field, or E-043 should
   accept a subject in the body instead of an id in the path.** One of the two must happen or the
   revoke flow does not close.

3. **The frontend re-mints the slug on rename; canon says it does not.** §10 and §11 follow canon
   (OQ-09: minted once, re-uniquified only on move) and flag the divergence at
   `src/store/workspace-store.ts:494-499` in place, because a backend developer will otherwise read
   the store and implement the other behaviour. The frontend already contradicts itself here — the
   document summary path deliberately does not re-slug (`:883-885`) — so canon is picking the
   consistent side, not overruling a settled rule.

4. **`moveVisibilityImpact` under-reports, and §11 says so.** `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:318`
   returns `NO_IMPACT` for any node whose own `accessMode` is not `inherit`, on the reasoning that
   *"a node with a mode of its own carries that mode with it, so nothing shifts."* That is untrue for
   path gating: a `workspace` or `restricted` folder moved under a restriction still disappears for
   everyone not admitted by the new parent, because `nodeVisibility` refuses at the first refusing
   node on the chain (`:167-173`). §11 specifies that the backend compute `impact` from the resolver
   rather than porting the early return. This is a **frontend defect**, not a canon question, and it
   is worth a ticket against the UI notice as well.

5. **Two `204` responses exist, against canon C-10.** `DELETE /workspaces/{id}` (E-011),
   `DELETE .../members/{userId}` (E-015), `DELETE .../members/me` (E-016) and
   `DELETE /nodes/{id}/access-rules/{ruleId}` (E-043) return `204`. Canon C-10 says *"No endpoint
   returns `204` where the frontend expects an object."* These are the cases where there is no
   authoritative record left to return, and canon §3.2 itself lists `204` for E-011, E-015 and E-016,
   so the rule and the registry already agree. Flagged only so a reviewer checking C-10 mechanically
   does not file it as a defect.

6. **§10's "delete a project requires re-typing the name" answer is: frontend confirmation.** Stated
   under E-032, with the reasoning and with the note that the frontend **does not implement it at
   all** today (`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:161` trashes straight from the menu). This
   matches the position part 4 takes for the same PRD sentence in its `workspaces` table. If a later
   reviewer wants it server-verified, the change is a `confirmName` field on E-032 for
   `kind = 'project'` — and it should be argued against part 4's OQ-02 block, not decided here.

7. **§12's auto-save answer is: `PUT` with the whole draft.** Five independent reasons are given
   under E-092. The one that settles it on its own is that the client's scheduler **coalesces** —
   intermediate drafts never reach the wire (`src/lib/save-scheduler.ts:56-102`) — so no delta
   protocol is expressible against it. Two fields are added to the body beyond `DocumentDraft`:
   `expectedVersion?` (canon OQ-57) and `isAutosave?` (canon OQ-59, and part 6 requires it for the
   fold rule). Both must be **tolerated when absent** or the current client breaks on its first
   keystroke.

8. **Endpoints documented in more than one section.** E-024 appears three times (project arm §10,
   folder arm §11, page arm §12) because it is one endpoint with a discriminated body and each arm
   has different required fields, permissions and side tables. E-030/E-031/E-032/E-037 are specified
   in full in §10 and repeated in §11 in the required shape with folder-specific deltas only, each
   cross-referenced. E-027 appears in §11 (recursive, the general case) and §12 (the page's content
   reset). If the editor prefers single-location endpoints, the natural home for the kind-agnostic
   four is §10 and §11 should keep only its cross-references.

9. **`GET /workspaces/{id}/storage` (E-017) is not documented here.** It is a workspace-module
   endpoint but reads `workspaces.used_bytes` and the plan quota, both of which belong to the files
   and quota chapter. §9's E-009 documents how `storage` is composed into `Workspace`; the standalone
   endpoint is owed by whoever writes the quota section.

10. **PRD `SY-INH-43` says "union of permissions"; §11 implements "deepest wins".** Canon OQ-22's
    position is deepest-wins with a user-scoped rule beating a role-scoped rule at the same node, and
    the code is unambiguous (`matchIn`, `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:55-79`). §11 states the
    conflict in place rather than silently following one. It is the single most consequential
    PRD-vs-code disagreement in these four sections.

## 13. Board APIs

### 13.0 What a board is, and what it is not

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** One board owns **one schema** and **one record set**. Table, Kanban,
Calendar and Gantt are projection functions over the same rows; there is no per-view record store
(`docs/BOARD.md:11-13`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:15-20`).

```
nodes (kind='board')  ──1:1──  boards ──1:N── board_columns      the schema
                                      ──1:N── board_views        presentation (§ Views)
                                      ──1:N── board_rows         the records
                                                     ├─self FK── board_rows.parent_row_id  (§16)
                                                     └─1:N────── board_row_relations       (§17)
```

Grounded: `src/types/board.ts:412-427` (`Board`), `src/lib/board-view.ts:194` (`queryRowIds`),
`src/store/board-store.ts:53-59` ("The board is the single source of truth… There is deliberately no
per-view copy of the data").

**Board id and node id are two identifiers, both kept** (canon §8.8, OQ-30). The mock derives one
from the other — `boardIdFor(nodeId) => "brd_" + nodeId`, `nodeIdFromBoardId` strips the prefix
(`src/services/board-service.ts:120-126`) — and every permission call converts board id back to node
id (`:564`, `:600`, `:653`, `:672`, `:687`, `:728`, `:1189`). The API does **not** reproduce that
trick: `boards.node_id` is a real `UNIQUE NOT NULL` foreign key and both ids ship on every `Board`,
exactly as `src/types/board.ts:413-417` already declares them.

#### 13.0.1 Why schema and rows are separate calls — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

The frontend already ships the seam: `BoardSnapshot.nextCursor` exists and is `null` today
(`src/types/board.ts:434-435`; `src/services/board-service.ts:239-240` — "The whole record set
arrives in one page today; see the API report"), and `docs/BOARD.md:271-276` marks record pagination
**blocking**: "At 5.000 rows that is already a multi-megabyte payload and it does not scale."

The concrete numbers, from the code:

| Payload | Size driver | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema (`columns` + `views`) | 5–15 columns, 1–6 views. A select column with 6 options, an availability `ConditionGroup` and a transition table is the largest single object, and is still under 4 KB. | `src/lib/board-templates.ts:126-406` |
| One record | 12 cells ≈ 1–3 KB of `CellValue` JSON, more when an attachment cell holds files | `src/types/board.ts:219-230`, canon §1.3.2 |
| 5 000 records | 5–15 MB in one response | `docs/BOARD.md:271-276` |

Three consequences make the split structural, not an optimisation:

1. **The schema is re-read wholesale, the rows are not.** Canon C-11: a schema response is a
   complete array, never a delta — the store overwrites `board.columns` and `board.views` outright
   (`src/store/board-store.ts:687-699`, `:827-835`). A realtime `board.schema.changed` frame (RT-10)
   carries `{ boardId }` and nothing else, so the client must be able to refetch the schema **without
   refetching 5 000 rows**. `GET /boards/{boardId}` (E-049) is that call.
2. **Rows page, the schema cannot.** Cursor pagination on `(position, id)` (canon §6.3) needs a
   stable column list to render the first page against; a client that pages rows asks for the schema
   once and the rows N times.
3. **Column writes rewrite rows.** Deleting, duplicating or converting a column rewrites `cells` on
   every record and bumps every `revision` (`src/services/board-service.ts:700-707`, `:621-629`,
   `:742-752`). Those endpoints return the **schema** plus only the rows they touched — never the
   whole board — which is only expressible if the two are separately addressable.

`GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` (E-047) stays as the **first-paint** call because that is what the store
does today (one request, then render); it returns the schema plus the *first page* of rows and a real
`nextCursor`. `GET /boards/{boardId}` (E-049) returns schema and views with **no** `rows` key at all.

---

### 13.1 Tables owned by this chapter

#### `boards` — T-10

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TABLE boards (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  node_id           uuid NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  workspace_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name              text NOT NULL,
  template_id       text,                     -- BoardTemplateId | user template uuid | NULL (OQ-47)
  row_id_prefix     text NOT NULL CHECK (row_id_prefix ~ '^[A-Z]{1,6}$'),
  primary_column_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES board_columns(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED,
  next_sequence     bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- Column roles for the four indexed projections on board_rows (OQ-48).
  status_column_id   uuid REFERENCES board_columns(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  assignee_column_id uuid REFERENCES board_columns(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  due_column_id      uuid REFERENCES board_columns(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  updated_by        uuid REFERENCES users(id)
);
CREATE INDEX boards_workspace_idx ON boards (workspace_id);
```

| Column | Meaning | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | The drive node the board is addressed by. `UNIQUE` — a node is at most one board. | `src/types/board.ts:416-417`; canon §8.8 OQ-30 |
| `name` | **Projected from `nodes.name`, not a second copy** (canon §8.8 OQ-30). The API resolves it on read and the column exists only as a denormalised read cache maintained in the same transaction as a node rename. | `src/store/workspace-store.ts:811` writes the name on the node |
| `row_id_prefix` | `TASK`, `BUG`, `QA`, `API`. Seeded from the template. `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` matches `normalizePrefix` exactly. | `src/lib/row-id.ts:9,18-20`; `src/mock/board.ts:71-73` |
| `primary_column_id` | The one column that titles a record. Deferrable because the board and its first column are inserted in the same statement pair. | `src/types/board.ts:422`; `src/lib/board-schema.ts:132-134` |
| `next_sequence` | The atomic row-id counter. **Monotonic; a deleted number is never re-issued.** Allocated with `UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING next_sequence` inside the row's transaction — never `MAX(sequence)+1`. | `src/services/board-service.ts:66-68`, `:304`; `docs/BOARD.md:277-280`; PRD `BD-RID-10` |
| `status_column_id` / `assignee_column_id` / `due_column_id` | Which column plays each role. The frontend guesses by name today (`/status\|result\|state/i`, `/assign\|owner\|tester\|responsible/i`, `/due\|deadline/i` — `src/lib/my-work.ts:22-67`); the backend stores the answer so a rename cannot silently move it. **RECOMMENDATION**, OQ-48. Seeded from the heuristic at board creation. | `src/lib/my-work.ts:22-67`; canon §1.3.2 |
| `template_id` | Reference only. Nothing may branch on it except `SearchResultKind` bucketing and the API duplicate detector. | `src/types/board.ts:414-415`; `src/lib/api-catalog.ts:28-40`; canon §1.3.5 |

**Cardinality.** `nodes` 1:1 `boards`; `workspaces` 1:N `boards`; `boards` 1:N `board_columns`
(5–15 typical), 1:N `board_views` (1–6), 1:N `board_rows` (target 5 000, `docs/BOARD.md:271`).

**Delete behaviour.** `nodes` are **soft**-deleted (`deleted_at`, canon §1.4); the `ON DELETE
CASCADE` on `node_id` only fires when the trash sweep purges the node for good (OQ-14). Trashing a
board therefore leaves `boards`, `board_columns` and `board_rows` intact and restorable —
which is what `POST /trash/{entryId}/restore` (E-037) needs.

#### `board_columns` — T-11

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TABLE board_columns (
  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  board_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name       text NOT NULL,
  type       column_type NOT NULL,             -- ENUM: text,longText,select,date,user,attachment,relation
  position   int  NOT NULL CHECK (position >= 0),
  width      int  NOT NULL DEFAULT 180 CHECK (width BETWEEN 88 AND 720),
  hidden     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  is_primary boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  config     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,   -- ColumnConfigByType[type]; §14.1
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (board_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX board_columns_one_primary
  ON board_columns (board_id) WHERE is_primary;
-- matches normalizeColumnName(): trim, lower-case, strip non-alphanumerics
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX board_columns_unique_name
  ON board_columns (board_id, lower(regexp_replace(name, '[^a-zA-Z0-9]', '', 'g')));
CREATE INDEX board_columns_board_position_idx ON board_columns (board_id, position);
```

`column_type` is a Postgres `ENUM` whose values are the frontend literals verbatim, `longText`
included (canon §2.0). `position` is `0..n-1`, densely renumbered across the whole schema on every
insert, move and delete — `reposition` (`src/lib/board-schema.ts:202-206`) — which is why the
`UNIQUE (board_id, position)` must be `DEFERRABLE`.

**Cardinality.** `boards` 1:N `board_columns`; exactly one row per board has `is_primary = true`.
**Delete behaviour.** `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `boards`. The primary column itself cannot be deleted
(§14.7); `boards.primary_column_id` has no `ON DELETE` action, so the FK refuses.

#### `board_rows` — T-12

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TABLE board_rows (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  board_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sequence      bigint NOT NULL,
  custom_id     text   NOT NULL,                    -- 'TASK-001'; business id, never the PK (C-02)
  parent_row_id uuid   REFERENCES board_rows(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  position      numeric NOT NULL,                   -- fractional index (OQ-34)
  cells         jsonb  NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb, -- Record<columnId, CellValue>
  revision      bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  archived_at   timestamptz,
  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  -- Indexed projections out of `cells`, maintained with every write (OQ-48, canon §1.3.2)
  due_date          date,
  due_at            timestamptz,
  status_option_id  text,
  assignee_ids      uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  search_tsv        tsvector,
  UNIQUE (board_id, sequence),
  UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)
);
CREATE INDEX board_rows_order_idx     ON board_rows (board_id, position, id);
CREATE INDEX board_rows_parent_idx    ON board_rows (parent_row_id);
CREATE INDEX board_rows_cells_gin     ON board_rows USING gin (cells jsonb_path_ops);
CREATE INDEX board_rows_due_idx       ON board_rows (board_id, due_date) WHERE archived_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX board_rows_status_idx    ON board_rows (board_id, status_option_id) WHERE archived_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX board_rows_assignee_gin  ON board_rows USING gin (assignee_ids);
CREATE INDEX board_rows_search_gin    ON board_rows USING gin (search_tsv);
CREATE INDEX board_rows_active_idx    ON board_rows (board_id) WHERE archived_at IS NULL;
```

| Column | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `sequence` | From `boards.next_sequence`. `UNIQUE (board_id, sequence)`. |
| `custom_id` | `formatRowId(prefix, sequence)` = `` `${prefix}-${String(sequence).padStart(3,"0")}` ``; numbers past the padding simply grow (`TASK-1024`). Written by the service in the same transaction that allocates `sequence`. `UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)`. Unique **per board only** — two boards may both hold `TASK-001`. On the wire it is `displayId`. | 
| `position` | `NUMERIC` fractional index. Defaulted on insert to `max(position)+1024` for an append, or the midpoint between the anchor and its successor for an insert. `board_rows_order_idx` is the keyset for E-061. |
| `cells` | `Record<columnId, CellValue>`. The `CellValue` union is canon §2.5; §15.4 restates it. Dense by construction — the frontend writes an explicit empty `CellValue` per column, never `null` (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:24-36`, `src/services/board-service.ts:537-539`). |
| `revision` | The optimistic-concurrency token, `+1` per write, **once per row per call however many cells that call touched** (`src/services/board-service.ts:514-519`). |
| `archived_at` | `NULL` = active. `isRowArchived` is `typeof archivedAt === "string" && length > 0` (`src/lib/archive.ts:52-53`). Archived records are frozen, not deleted. |
| `search_tsv` | `to_tsvector` over the text projection of every cell (`cellText`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:87-124`) plus `custom_id`. Feeds E-069 and E-133. Canon §1.2 — no separate `search_index` table. |

`due_date` / `due_at` are **two columns, never one** (canon C-04, OQ-32): a `date` column whose
`DateConfig.includesTime` is false projects into `due_date` and a date-only value never passes
through UTC; one with `includesTime: true` projects into `due_at`.

**Cardinality.** `boards` 1:N `board_rows` (5 000 target). `board_rows` 1:N `board_rows` through
`parent_row_id` (§16, depth cap 5 per OQ-33).
**Delete behaviour.** `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `boards`. `parent_row_id … ON DELETE SET NULL` is the
database half of "children are lifted to the top level, never cascade-deleted"
(`src/services/board-service.ts:460-470`).

---

### 13.2 `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` — create a board (blank or from a template)

**Purpose** — Create a board. One endpoint creates every node kind; `kind: "board"` selects this
branch, and `templateId` selects the schema it starts from. There is no separate
`POST /boards` (canon P-04: content is entered through its node).

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` **and** `board.create` on the parent node (workspace root when
`parentId` is `null`), plus workspace membership. Both keys are Manager-and-above
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:38-48`). The parent must be a container: a board under a document or
a file is refused, matching `src/store/workspace-store.ts:800-806` — "Boards can only live inside
folders".

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | `uuid` | Tenant. Must be a workspace the caller is a member of, or `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CreateNodeRequest`, board branch. The drive chapter owns the shared fields; the
board-specific ones are `templateId`, `boardKind` and `rowIdPrefix`.

```ts
/** E-024, board branch. `kind` discriminates; the other four branches live in the drive chapter. */
interface CreateBoardNodeRequest {
  readonly kind: "board";
  /** Container the board is created in. `null` = workspace root. */
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  /** Trimmed. Empty falls back to the template name, then to "Untitled board". */
  readonly name?: string;
  /**
   * Built-in id (`task` | `bug` | `qa` | `apiDocs`) or a user template's uuid (OQ-47).
   * Omitted or null = a blank board: one primary text column named "Name", one table view.
   */
  readonly templateId?: BoardTemplateId | string | null;
  /** Presentation hint stored on the node. Defaults to "table". Never validated against BoardViewType (OQ-31). */
  readonly boardKind?: BoardKind;
  /** Overrides the template's prefix. `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` after normalisation. */
  readonly rowIdPrefix?: string;
}
```

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `BoardNode` variant), `201`. The caller then opens the board with
E-047; creation deliberately does not return a `BoardSnapshot`, because the frontend navigates by
node id and loads the board on the next route
(`src/hooks/use-create-board.ts:28-29` — `createNode(...)` then `openNode(hrefForNode(...))`).

```jsonc
// 201
{
  "id": "0f3a…", "type": "board", "name": "Task board", "slug": "task-board",
  "parentId": "9c21…", "workspaceId": "4a77…",
  "owner": { "id": "usr_…", "name": "Mai Linh", "email": "…", "isActive": true },
  "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z", "updatedAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z",
  "isFavorite": false, "isTrashed": false, "isShared": false, "isArchived": false,
  "boardKind": "table", "templateId": "task", "itemCount": 0, "openCount": 0,
  "state": "active"
}
```

`itemCount` and `openCount` are **DERIVED** projections onto the node, not stored twice
(`src/types/node.ts:112-113`; canon §1.3.1): `itemCount` = `count(*) FROM board_rows WHERE board_id
= $1 AND archived_at IS NULL`, `openCount` = the same restricted to rows whose `status_option_id`
is not in `SelectConfig.completedOptionIds`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `INSERT` — one row, `kind='board'`, `slug` minted once from the name and uniquified against the surviving (non-trashed) siblings (canon §8.8 OQ-09). |
| `boards` | `INSERT` — one row. `next_sequence = 0`, `row_id_prefix` from the request or the template (`prefixForBoard`, `src/mock/board.ts:71-73`), `template_id` recorded for reference. |
| `board_templates` | `SELECT` — the template row, when `templateId` is given. Read-only; a template is inert data (canon §1.3.5). |
| `board_columns` | `INSERT` — one row per template column, **deep-copied**: config, every `SelectOption`, every option's `availability` `ConditionGroup` recursively, `completedOptionIds`, and each target array inside `transitionRules.transitions`. New `id` per column and per option. (`instantiateColumns`, `src/lib/board-templates.ts:422-479`.) A blank board gets one `text` column named "Name", `is_primary = true`, `width = 280`. |
| `boards` | `UPDATE` — `primary_column_id` set once the columns exist. |
| `board_views` | `INSERT` — one row per `TemplateView`, with the missing fields defaulted: `filterConjunction:"and"`, `columnOrder:[]`, `columnWidths:{}`, `rowHeight:"medium"`, `hideEmptyGroups:false`, `null` anchors (`src/mock/board.ts:80-96`). The view whose `type` matches the node's `boardKind` is hoisted to `position 0` (`src/mock/board.ts:98-102`, via `VIEW_TYPE_BY_BOARD_KIND` which maps the tree's legacy `timeline` onto `gantt` — `src/services/board-service.ts:76-81`). A blank board gets one `table` view named "All records". |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `module: "board"`, `action: "board.create"`, `outcome: "allowed"`. |

**No rows are created.** A board from a template starts empty; the mock's `rowCount: node.itemCount`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:96`) is fixture generation, not product behaviour —
`createBoard` sets `itemCount: 0` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:827`).

**Transaction** — **Required.** Node, board, every column, `primary_column_id` and every view land
together or none do. A board with columns but no primary column is unreadable: `cellOf`,
`relationIndex` and every title projection dereference `board.primaryColumnId`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:1306`, `:1312`).

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11) with `change: "created"` to the workspace channel. No board
frame: nobody has the board open yet.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `kind` missing, `name` past the length cap, unknown `boardKind`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID` — `rowIdPrefix` is not `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` after normalisation. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — caller lacks `node.create` or `board.create` on the parent. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` — the parent sits under an archived ancestor. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown workspace, or one the caller is not a member of. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown `parentId`, or one the caller may not see. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` → served as `not_found` with message `That template could not be found`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — the parent is a document, board or file. Message: `Boards can only live inside folders`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` — the slug is taken among the target's surviving siblings. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:70-95` (the Board → template
submenu) and `src/components/dashboard/onboarding-panel.tsx:19-22`, both through
`src/hooks/use-create-board.ts:23-35` → `src/store/workspace-store.ts:794-838`.

> **RECOMMENDATION — blank boards.** The frontend offers **only** the four templates
> (`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:77`); `BOARD_TEMPLATES` is the whole menu. Omitting
> `templateId` is an API affordance, not a shipped surface. It exists because
> `templateForBoard(name, templateId)` falls back to `task` when nothing is declared
> (`src/mock/board.ts:57-69`), and a fallback that silently gives a user a Status column with five
> options they did not ask for is worse than an explicit blank board.

### 13.3 `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/board` — open a board (schema + views + first page)

**Purpose** — Everything one board needs before its first paint: the schema, the saved views, the
first page of records, and the directory the `user` cells render from.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on the node (`effectiveAccess` through the inheritance chain,
`src/services/authz.ts:36-53`). No action key: reading a board is not an action
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:11-16` — viewer holds zero action keys, and still reads).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | `uuid` | The drive node. Must be `kind='board'` or `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH`. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `int 1..500` | `200` | Records in the first page. |
| `includeArchived` | `boolean` | `false` | Archived records are excluded from every view until the board is asked for them (`src/lib/board-view.ts:187,212`; `src/components/board/board-toolbar.tsx:45`). |
| `viewId` | `uuid` | — | Optional. When present the server applies that view's filters, sorts and grouping order server-side (§15.1). Absent = board order. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `BoardSnapshot` (canon §5.5).

```ts
interface BoardSnapshot {
  readonly board: Board;
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly people: readonly DirectoryUser[];
  /** Null when the whole record set arrived in one page. */
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

interface Board {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly templateId?: BoardTemplateId | string;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly rowIdPrefix: string;
  readonly primaryColumnId: string;
  readonly columns: readonly BoardColumn[];   // ordered by position, ASC
  readonly views: readonly SavedView[];       // ordered by position, ASC
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
}
```

`people` is the **whole workspace directory including deactivated members**, flagged
`isActive: false` — a user removed from the workspace must keep rendering their name with an
`(Inactive)` tag (canon E-006; `src/mock/users.ts:41-58`; PRD `BD-CEL-09`;
`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-composer.tsx:85`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `SELECT` by id; assert `kind='board'`, `deleted_at IS NULL`. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `nodes` (ancestor walk) | `SELECT` — resolve visibility. |
| `boards` | `SELECT` by `node_id`. |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 ORDER BY position`. |
| `board_views` | `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 ORDER BY position`. |
| `board_view_preferences` | `SELECT` for the caller, merged onto the views (OQ-46; § Views owns the merge). |
| `board_rows` | `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 [AND archived_at IS NULL] ORDER BY position, id LIMIT $limit+1`. |
| `workspace_members` ⨝ `users` | `SELECT` — the directory. |

**Transaction** — Not required. A single read-only snapshot (`REPEATABLE READ` is sufficient if the
schema and the first row page must agree; a client that sees a newer schema than its rows already
copes — `cellOf` reads a mismatched cell as empty, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:43-46`).

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — visible node, no read access. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown node **or** one the caller may not see; the two answer identically (canon §4.2). |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — the node exists but no `boards` row hangs off it. Message: `That board could not be found`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` — the node is not a board. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-board.ts:25-28` → `src/store/board-store.ts:269-291`
(`load`) → `src/services/board-service.ts:229-242`. Also
`src/hooks/use-embedded-board.ts:57-65` for the `DV-EMB-25` embedded-view block, which reads a board
it does not own and writes back through the same cell endpoint.

---

### 13.4 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}` — the schema and views alone

**Purpose** — Refetch a board's schema and saved views **without its records**. This is the call a
client makes after an `RT-10 board.schema.changed` frame, and the call a second surface makes when it
needs the column list to render something it already holds rows for.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on `boards.node_id`. No action key.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | `uuid` | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `Board`, exactly the interface above, with **no `rows` key**. Returning `Board` bare
rather than wrapping it in a `GetBoardResponse` follows canon §5.1: a response that is a domain
object is returned as that domain object.

**Database** — `boards` `SELECT` by id → `nodes` `SELECT` for visibility and `name` →
`board_columns` `SELECT … ORDER BY position` → `board_views` `SELECT … ORDER BY position` →
`board_view_preferences` `SELECT` for the caller.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION.** No component calls it today: the frontend reads the board
out of `BoardSnapshot` and re-reads the whole snapshot on `reload`
(`src/store/board-store.ts:293-296`). It is owed because C-11 ("a schema response is a complete
array, never a delta") plus RT-10 (`{ boardId }`, ids only) together require a schema-only refetch;
without it, every column rename by a colleague costs a 5 000-row download.

---

### 13.5 `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}` — update a board

**Purpose** — Change board-level settings: the record-id prefix and the three column roles. The
board's **name is not editable here** — the node owns it (canon §8.8 OQ-30), so a rename is
`PATCH /nodes/{nodeId}` (E-025).

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.manage` on `boards.node_id` (Manager and above,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:45`), plus workspace membership.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | `uuid` | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-050. Every field optional; an omitted field is untouched (canon P-07: PATCH is a merge). */
interface UpdateBoardRequest {
  /** Normalised with normalizePrefix(): strip non-letters, upper-case, cap at 6. */
  readonly rowIdPrefix?: string;
  /** Column roles for the four indexed projections (OQ-48). `null` clears the role. */
  readonly statusColumnId?: string | null;
  readonly assigneeColumnId?: string | null;
  readonly dueColumnId?: string | null;
}
```

**Response** — `Board`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `boards` | `UPDATE` — the named fields, `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by`. |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT` — validate that each role id belongs to this board and is of the right type (`statusColumnId` must be `select`, `assigneeColumnId` `user`, `dueColumnId` `date`). |
| `board_rows` | `UPDATE` — **only** when a role column changes: the four indexed projections are recomputed for every row of the board. Not when only `rowIdPrefix` changes. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.update`. |

**Transaction** — **Required** when a role column changes: the role and the projections it drives
must not disagree, or My Work and the dashboard read a stale lens.

**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10), `{ boardId }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID` — not `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` after normalisation. |
| 400 | `validation` | `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` — a role id points at a column of the wrong type. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.manage`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` / `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_ID_PREFIX_LOCKED` → served as `conflict` — see the open question below. |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION.** `board.rowIdPrefix` is *rendered*
(`src/components/board/board-toolbar.tsx:67` — the `TASK-000` badge) and never written;
`normalizePrefix` is exported and called by nothing in `src/components/**` or `src/store/**`
(`src/lib/row-id.ts:18-20`). The role columns are guessed by name today
(`src/lib/my-work.ts:22-67`) and have no editor at all.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-43)** — may `rowIdPrefix` change after records exist?
> **Evidence** — `custom_id` is stored per row, not derived on read
> (`src/types/board.ts:240-243`; `src/services/board-service.ts:308-310`), so changing the prefix
> would leave `TASK-001 … TASK-041` beside `BUG-042`. `extractRowReferences`
> (`src/lib/row-id.ts:37-43`) turns `TASK-041` in a comment body into a link, and those links would
> silently stop resolving.
> **Recommendation** — refuse the change once `next_sequence > 0`, with
> `conflict` / `ROW_ID_PREFIX_LOCKED`. If a rename is wanted later, make it an explicit background
> job that rewrites every `custom_id`, writes one `row_activity` entry per record and one
> `audit_events` row for the run.
> **Impact if wrong** — mixed prefixes on one board, dead `TASK-041` references in comments, and a
> `UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)` collision the moment the old prefix is re-selected.

---

### 13.6 `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` — delete a board

**Purpose** — Move a board to the Trash. Deleting a board is deleting its **node**; there is no
`DELETE /boards/{boardId}`.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `node.delete` on the node (Manager and above, or the node's **owner** from `member`
upward via `OWNER_ESCALATIONS` — `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:98-105`,
`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:71-74`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | `uuid` | The board's node. |

**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `TrashEntry` (owned by the system chapter), carrying `purgeAt` (OQ-14).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `UPDATE` — `deleted_at = now()`, `deleted_by`. Soft, never a hard delete (canon §1.4). |
| `trash_entries` | `INSERT` — actor, timestamp, `original_ancestor_ids`, the human path resolved **at deletion time**. |
| `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_rows`, `board_views`, `row_activity` | **Untouched.** Nothing is deleted; the board is simply unreachable until it is restored or the sweep purges the node. |
| `board_row_relations` | **Untouched** — including rows on *other* boards that point into this one. A relation whose target board is trashed resolves to nothing on the next `relation-index` read and renders `[Deleted Item]`, exactly as a deleted row does (§17.4). |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `node.delete`, severity `warn`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Node flag, trash entry and audit row are one write.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11) with `change: "trashed"`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `node.delete`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` — an archived ancestor refuses every write. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:156-163` ("Move to Trash",
`disabled={!can("node.delete")}`) → `src/store/workspace-store.ts` `trashNode`.

> Note the asymmetry, and keep it: **a board node gets a 30-day trash; a board *record* does not.**
> `bulkDelete` is permanent — "records have no trash of their own"
> (`src/services/board-service.ts:1049`), and the confirm copy says so:
> "Records are removed outright — the Trash holds files, pages and boards, not rows"
> (`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:326`). Canon reserves **OQ-15** for whether that is
> intended; this chapter implements what the frontend does.

---

### 13.7 `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate` — duplicate a board

**Purpose** — Copy a board: its node, its schema, its views and — per canon's position on OQ-12 —
its records.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `node.create` on the **destination parent** (the source's parent), plus visibility
on the source. A caller who may not read the source may not copy it.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | `uuid` | The board node to copy. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-027. Shared with the drive chapter; the board branch reads `includeRecords`. */
interface DuplicateNodeRequest {
  /** Destination container. Omitted = the source's own parent. */
  readonly parentId?: string | null;
  /** Defaults to `${source.name} (copy)` (src/store/workspace-store.ts:855). */
  readonly name?: string;
  /** Copy the records too. Default true — see the open question below. */
  readonly includeRecords?: boolean;
}
```

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `BoardNode` variant), `201`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `INSERT` — new id, `parent_id` = destination, name `"… (copy)"`, **`is_favorite = false`, `is_shared = false`** (`cloneNode`, `src/lib/tree.ts:203-217`), slug re-uniquified against the destination's siblings. |
| `boards` | `INSERT` — new id, same `row_id_prefix` and `template_id`, `next_sequence` copied from the source when records come along (so the copy's ids continue rather than restart), `0` when they do not. |
| `board_columns` | `INSERT` — one per source column, **new ids**, config deep-copied including every option id. |
| `board_views` | `INSERT` — one per source view, new ids, with every `columnId` reference remapped old→new (`filters[].columnId`, `sorts[].columnId`, `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnOrder`, `columnWidths` keys, `columnDisplay` keys, `groupByColumnId`, `dateColumnId`, `endDateColumnId`). |
| `board_rows` | `INSERT` — one per source row when `includeRecords`, new ids, `cells` remapped old→new column id, `parent_row_id` remapped old→new row id, `position` copied, `revision = 1`, `created_by` = the **caller**, `created_at = now()`. |
| `board_row_relations` | `INSERT` — for relation cells whose target is **inside the copied board**, remapped to the new row ids. A relation pointing **outside** the board keeps the original target (the copy links to the same external record). |
| `row_activity` | **Not copied.** History belongs to the record it happened to. One `created` entry per new row is written instead. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `node.create` with a `context` naming the source. |

**Column id remapping is the whole difficulty here.** `cells` is keyed by column id and views name
columns by id, so a copy that reuses the old ids would have two boards sharing one column identity —
and a subsequent `DELETE` on either would orphan the other's cells. Build the old→new map once and
apply it to `cells`, every view field and every `SelectOption` id inside `config` before any insert.

**Transaction** — **Required**, one transaction over the whole subtree. A half-copied board — views
pointing at columns that were not inserted — is unreadable.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "created"`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `node.create` on the destination. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — source or destination. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — destination is not a container. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — the copy would exceed the row ceiling (OQ-36). |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION.** `duplicateNode` exists in the store
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:840-870`) but its only caller today is the document header
(`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:49,93`); `src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx` has no
Duplicate item. The endpoint is owed because the store action is generic over `DriveNode` and the
board is the one kind whose duplication has non-trivial semantics.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-12)** — does duplicating a board copy its records?
> **Evidence** — `cloneNode` (`src/lib/tree.ts:203-217`) copies the **tree node only**: it recurses
> into `children` and touches no content store. `duplicateNode`
> (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:840-870`) never calls the board service, so in the frontend a
> duplicated board would seed itself fresh from its template on first open
> (`seedFromNode`, `src/services/board-service.ts:83-108`) — i.e. schema and *fixture* rows, which is
> not a copy of anything.
> **Recommendation** — `includeRecords` defaults to `true`. A board is its records; a "duplicate"
> that produced an empty board would be a template instantiation wearing the wrong verb, and the
> product already has a verb for that. Offer `includeRecords: false` for the "same schema, fresh
> start" case rather than making it the default.
> **Impact if wrong** — a user who duplicates a 5 000-row board to try a schema change gets an empty
> board and has to import their own data back; or, in the other direction, a routine "duplicate for a
> new sprint" silently copies 5 000 stale records.

---

### 13.8 `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/boards` — list boards

**Purpose** — Every board in the workspace the caller may see, named cheaply. This is the list a
relation column picks a target from and the list "Move records to…" offers.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Workspace membership. Each board is then filtered by **visibility on its node** —
the caller never passes a `canView` flag (canon OQ-18: taking that from the caller is a
critical defect).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | `uuid` | Tenant. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `int 1..500` | `200` | Hard server cap. An unbounded list is a spec defect (canon §6.3). |
| `excludeBoardId` | `uuid` | — | Optional. Drops one board from the result — what the move dialog does client-side today (`src/components/board/bulk/bulk-move-dialog.tsx:61`). |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly BoardDescriptor[]`.

```ts
/** canon §5.3. What listing a board costs: four ids and a name. */
interface BoardDescriptor {
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  /** Active records. Projected from board_rows, not stored on the board. */
  readonly itemCount: number;
  readonly templateId?: BoardTemplateId | string;
}
```

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `SELECT … WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND kind = 'board' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, pruned to what the caller may see. **Trashed boards are excluded** (`boardNodes()`, `src/services/board-service.ts:1228-1232`). |
| `boards` | `SELECT` joined on `node_id`. |
| `board_rows` | `SELECT board_id, count(*) … WHERE archived_at IS NULL GROUP BY board_id` — one grouped aggregate for the whole page, never one query per board. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `SELECT` — visibility resolution. |

**This endpoint must never read or seed a board's rows beyond that count.** The frontend is explicit:
"Derived from the tree, so listing them never seeds — a 5.000-record board is not built just to name
it" (`src/services/board-service.ts:1234-1237`), and the move dialog repeats it
(`src/components/board/bulk/bulk-move-dialog.tsx:26-29`). Canon E-048 states it as a rule.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `limit` out of range. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown workspace or not a member. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-board-list.ts:9-18` → `src/services/board-service.ts:1238-1246`,
consumed by `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:90,231` (the relation column's "Linked board"
submenu) and `src/components/board/bulk/bulk-move-dialog.tsx:40-43`.

## 14. Column APIs

### 14.0 The two kinds of "hidden", and why they are different endpoints

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** A column has a schema-level `hidden` flag **and** a per-view
`hiddenColumnIds` list, and they are not the same thing:

| Gesture | Writes | Visible to | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Column menu → "Hide column" | `SavedView.hiddenColumnIds` | that view only | `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}` (E-080) |
| Column settings → schema `hidden` | `board_columns.hidden` | every view | `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}` (E-053) |

`src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:321-327` calls `setColumnHidden`, which patches the
**view** (`src/store/board-store.ts:1076-1091`), not the column. `resolveColumns` merges the two:
a column is hidden in a view when `view.hiddenColumnIds` contains it **or** the schema flag is set,
and **never when it is primary** (`src/lib/board-view.ts:24-41`). `docs/BOARD.md:106-118` states the
split as a rule: "Hiding a column in the table therefore cannot blank the Kanban card."

This chapter owns the schema flag. The view list belongs to the Views chapter.

### 14.1 `board_columns.config` — the complete JSONB contract

Canon C-06: no chapter writes `config JSONB` and stops. `config` is exactly
`ColumnConfigByType[type]`, validated at the boundary against the branch named by `type`
(`src/types/board.ts:99-170`):

```ts
type ColumnType = "text" | "longText" | "select" | "date" | "user" | "attachment" | "relation";

interface TextConfig { readonly placeholder?: string; }            // declared, unused (OQ-54)

interface StepNumbering {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  readonly prefix: string;      // "B", "T", "Step " — may be empty
  readonly start: number;       // the number the first step takes
  readonly separator: string;   // ":" or "."
}
interface LongTextConfig {
  readonly rows: number;                        // preferred editor height; default 4
  readonly stepNumbering?: StepNumbering;
}

interface SelectOption {
  readonly id: string;                          // IMMUTABLE once minted — §14.9
  readonly label: string;                       // display only
  readonly color: SelectColor;                  // gray|blue|green|amber|red|violet|cyan|pink
  readonly isDisabled?: boolean;                // never selectable, whatever a record holds
  readonly availability?: ConditionGroup | null;// null/absent = always offered
}
interface TransitionRules {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  readonly mode: "allow-list";                  // the only value today
  /** fromKey -> allowed toKeys. Keys are option ids, plus "__empty__". */
  readonly transitions: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
}
interface SelectConfig {
  readonly options: readonly SelectOption[];
  readonly isMulti: boolean;
  readonly unavailableBehavior?: "disabled" | "hidden";  // default "disabled"
  readonly completedOptionIds?: readonly string[];       // which options mean "finished"
  readonly transitionRules?: TransitionRules;
}

interface DateConfig       { readonly includesTime: boolean; }
interface UserConfig       { readonly isMulti: boolean; }
interface AttachmentConfig { readonly maxFiles: number; }
interface RelationConfig {
  readonly boardId: string | null;         // target board; null = this board
  readonly displayColumnId: string | null; // column whose value labels each chip
  readonly isMulti: boolean;
}

interface ColumnConfigByType {
  readonly text: TextConfig;           readonly longText: LongTextConfig;
  readonly select: SelectConfig;       readonly date: DateConfig;
  readonly user: UserConfig;           readonly attachment: AttachmentConfig;
  readonly relation: RelationConfig;
}
```

`Condition` / `ConditionGroup`, nested inside `SelectOption.availability`
(`src/types/board.ts:45-64`):

```ts
type ConditionOperator =
  | "is" | "isNot" | "contains" | "notContains"
  | "isAnyOf" | "isNoneOf" | "before" | "after" | "on"
  | "isEmpty" | "isNotEmpty";

interface Condition {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  /** Option id / user id / YYYY-MM-DD / free text — read the way the column reads it. */
  readonly operator: ConditionOperator;
  readonly value: string;
  readonly values?: readonly string[];   // the list for isAnyOf / isNoneOf
}
interface ConditionGroup {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly conjunction: "and" | "or";
  readonly conditions: readonly Condition[];
  readonly groups: readonly ConditionGroup[];   // A and (B or C)
}
```

**Defaults for a new column** (`DEFAULT_CONFIG`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:36-44`):
`text` → `{}`; `longText` → `{ rows: 4 }`; `select` → `{ options: [], isMulti: false }`;
`date` → `{ includesTime: false }`; `user` → `{ isMulti: false }`;
`attachment` → `{ maxFiles: 10 }`; `relation` → `{ boardId: null, displayColumnId: null, isMulti: true }`.
A `longText` column with no `stepNumbering` reads as
`{ enabled: false, prefix: "", start: 1, separator: ":" }` (`src/lib/step-numbering.ts:29-34`).

**Validation rules at the boundary:**
1. `config` is validated against the branch named by the column's **current** `type`; unknown keys
   are rejected (`COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH`). The frontend never sends a config for another type.
2. `width` is clamped to `[88, 720]`, not rejected (`clampColumnWidth`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:70-72`).
3. `"__empty__"` is a **reserved** option id and must be refused as a user-authored one
   (`OPTION_ID_RESERVED`, `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:28`).
4. A `ConditionGroup` past the nesting or size cap is refused with `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP`
   (OQ-38).

---

### 14.2 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns` — list columns

**Purpose** — The board's schema, ordered. Serves the surfaces that need a column list without the
records.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on `boards.node_id`.

**Path Params** — `boardId` `uuid`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly BoardColumn[]`, ordered by `position` ascending. A **complete array**,
never a delta (C-11).

```ts
interface ColumnBase {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly position: number;   // 0-based, dense
  readonly width: number;      // 88..720
  readonly hidden: boolean;    // schema-level; never true on the primary column
  readonly isPrimary: boolean;
}
type BoardColumnOf<T extends ColumnType> = ColumnBase & {
  readonly type: T;
  readonly config: ColumnConfigByType[T];
};
type BoardColumn = { [T in ColumnType]: BoardColumnOf<T> }[ColumnType];
```

**Database** — `boards` `SELECT` (visibility) → `board_columns` `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 ORDER BY position`.
**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION.** No component calls it; the schema arrives inside
`BoardSnapshot`. It is owed for the same reason as E-049: a client refetching after RT-10 must be
able to ask for the columns alone.

---

### 14.3 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns` — create a column

**Purpose** — Add a column, optionally at a position rather than at the end. **One endpoint** serves
Insert-left, Insert-right and Add-at-end; there is no `insert-left` route.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.create` on `boards.node_id`, plus workspace membership. The service
already checks exactly this key today (`src/services/board-service.ts:564`).

**Path Params** — `boardId` `uuid`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-052. */
interface CreateColumnRequest {
  readonly type: ColumnType;
  /** Requested name. De-duplicated server-side — see below. */
  readonly name: string;
  /**
   * Anchor. The new column takes the slot immediately after this one.
   *   omitted            -> append at the end
   *   null               -> insert at the very front (position 0)
   *   "<columnId>"       -> insert directly after that column
   * Insert-left of column C is `insertAfterColumnId` = the id of C's predecessor,
   * or null when C is first.
   */
  readonly insertAfterColumnId?: string | null;
  /** Optional initial config; validated against `type`. Omitted = defaultConfigFor(type). */
  readonly config?: ColumnConfigByType[ColumnType];
}
```

> **RECOMMENDATION — `insertAfterColumnId` rather than an index.** The frontend passes an
> **index**: `createColumn(boardId, type, name, atIndex?)`
> (`src/services/board-service.ts:555-583`), and the column menu computes it as `index` for
> Insert-left and `index + 1` for Insert-right
> (`src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:306-313`). An index is a claim about a list the
> caller does not own: two managers inserting at the same moment, or an insert racing a reorder,
> place a column somewhere neither asked for. An anchor id is unambiguous under both.
> Canon reserves **OQ-39** for exactly this gap ("`ColumnPatch` has no `type` and no `position`").
> The **index → anchor** mapping is mechanical and belongs in the client: `atIndex` → the id of the
> column currently at `atIndex - 1`, or `null` at 0.

**Name de-duplication — EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** The server makes the name unique against the board's
*current* schema before inserting: `Notes`, then `Notes 2`, `Notes 3`, up to 999
(`uniqueColumnName`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:170-180`). Collision is tested on the **normalised**
name — trimmed, lower-cased, non-alphanumerics stripped (`normalizeColumnName`, `:148-153`) — so
`Due date`, `due-date` and `DueDate` are one name. An empty or whitespace name becomes
`New column`. **This is a silent de-duplication, not a `409`**: `COLUMN_NAME_CONFLICT` is reserved
for a caller that demanded an exact name (canon §4.3). The reason is in the code: "Two columns
called the same thing is how a board becomes ambiguous — to the person reading it, and to the
importer, which pairs source columns to board columns by name"
(`src/services/board-service.ts:550-553`).

**Response** — `BoardColumn`, `201` — the column as stored, with the name the server actually chose
and its final `position`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the board's columns (to renumber safely) → `INSERT` the new column → `UPDATE` `position = position + 1` for every column at or after the insert point. Dense `0..n` throughout (`reposition`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:202-206`). |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`. |
| `board_rows` | **Not written.** A new column adds no key to any `cells` document; `cellOf` reads a missing key as the column's empty value (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:43-46`). This is why adding a column to a 5 000-row board is O(columns), not O(rows). |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.create`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The insert and the renumbering are one write, or the deferred
`UNIQUE (board_id, position)` fires.

**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10), `{ boardId }`. Ids only; the receiver refetches the
schema (C-11).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `type` not a `ColumnType`, `name` past the length cap. |
| 400 | `validation` | `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` — `config` does not match `type`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` — an initial select option claims `"__empty__"`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` — an option's `availability` is past the cap (OQ-38). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.create`. Copy: `You do not have permission to add a column` / `Needs the Manager role or above` (`src/services/authz.ts:67-74`). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`, or `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` when `insertAfterColumnId` names nothing on this board. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:109-112` (Insert left / Insert
right), `src/components/board/table/grid-header.tsx:61,75` (the `+` header button) and
`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts` (the importer creates the columns its mapping needs before writing a
single record), all through `src/store/board-store.ts:675-702`.

---

### 14.4 `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}` — rename and reconfigure

**Purpose** — Change a column's name, its schema-level width and hidden flag, and its typed config —
including a select column's whole option list, its conditional rules and its transition table.
**It never changes `type` and never changes `position`.**

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.update` on `boards.node_id`. Checked in the service today
(`src/services/board-service.ts:653`), with the reasoning stated in the code: "a member who may write
a Status cell is not thereby entitled to rewrite the workflow that governs every card on the board"
(`:636-645`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | `uuid` | |
| `columnId` | `uuid` | Must belong to `boardId`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `ColumnPatch` (the frontend's own name, `src/types/board.ts:446-451`), sent as
`UpdateColumnRequest`.

```ts
/** E-053. Every field optional; an omitted field is untouched. */
interface UpdateColumnRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  /** Clamped to [88,720], never rejected. */
  readonly width?: number;
  /** Silently ignored on the primary column. */
  readonly hidden?: boolean;
  /** Shallow-merged over the stored config, validated against the column's CURRENT type. */
  readonly config?: Partial<ColumnConfigByType[ColumnType]>;
}
```

Three behaviours are load-bearing and must be reproduced exactly (`patchColumn`,
`src/lib/board-schema.ts:86-104`):

1. **`hidden` on the primary column is ignored, not refused.** `...(patch.hidden === undefined ||
   column.isPrimary ? {} : { hidden: patch.hidden })` — the primary column titles the row and can
   never be hidden. Canon E-053 states it as a rule.
2. **`config` is a shallow merge**, one level deep: `{ ...column.config, ...patch.config }`. Sending
   `{ config: { stepNumbering: {...} } }` leaves `rows` alone; sending
   `{ config: { options: [...] } }` **replaces the whole options array**, which is exactly how the
   options dialog commits (`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx` →
   `onSave(config)` → `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:350`).
3. **`width` is clamped, not validated.** A caller sending `9999` gets `720` back, not a `400`.

**Renaming and the name conflict.** Unlike creation, a rename **refuses** a colliding name rather
than de-duplicating: `findColumnByName(board.columns, trimmed, columnId)` and a refusal reading
`This board already has a column called "{name}"`
(`src/store/board-store.ts:739-759`). The backend must do the same —
`409` / `COLUMN_NAME_CONFLICT` — because a rename is a caller demanding an exact name. An empty or
whitespace-only name is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

**Response** — `BoardColumn` — the authoritative column (C-10).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the target → `UPDATE name/width/hidden/config`, `updated_at = now()`. |
| `board_rows` | **Not written.** Renaming a column, adding an option or rewriting a transition table touches no record. This is the entire reason option ids are immutable (§14.9). |
| `board_row_relations` | **Not written** by a config change — including a change to `RelationConfig.boardId`. Existing cells keep pointing where they pointed; the chips simply stop resolving against the new target board and render as unknown until they are re-picked (`relationResolved`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:14-22`). |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.update`. |

**Transaction** — **Required** when `config.options` shrinks: the option removal, the pruning of
`completedOptionIds` and the pruning of `transitionRules.transitions` (both keys and target lists)
are one write. The frontend already does all three together
(`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:180-190`; `pruneTransitionRules`,
`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:256-268`) — "Removing an option must take its rules with it, or the
table keeps referring to a status that no longer exists."

**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — empty name. |
| 400 | `validation` | `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` — `config` names a key from another branch. |
| 400 | `validation` | `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` — an option in the replacement list claims `"__empty__"`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` (OQ-38). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.update`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` — message `That column could not be found`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `COLUMN_NAME_CONFLICT` — the name is taken by another column on this board. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/grid-header.tsx:181,225` (double-click rename) →
`src/store/board-store.ts:739-759`; `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:89,135,236,350,356`
(step numbering, linked board, the options-and-rules dialog);
`src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:74` — all through
`src/store/board-store.ts:761-790` (`updateColumnConfig`).
