### 14.5 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/convert` — change a column's type

**Purpose** — Change a column's type and rewrite every record's value into the new type. Values the
target type cannot parse are **kept as text and flagged**, never dropped.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.update` on `boards.node_id` (`src/services/board-service.ts:728`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `columnId`.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dryRun` | `boolean` | `false` | `true` computes and returns a `ConversionPreview` and **writes nothing**. |

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-057. */
interface ConvertColumnRequest {
  readonly type: ColumnType;
  /** Optional config for the new type. Omitted = defaultConfigFor(type) — the FE always omits it. */
  readonly config?: ColumnConfigByType[ColumnType];
}
```

#### The conversion contract — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

This is `BD-TBL-08`'s named edge case ("changing Text→Date keeps the unparseable text and warns
rather than dropping it") and it is implemented as a property of the model, not a special case:

1. **Every conversion goes through the cell's plain-text projection.** `convertCell(value, source,
   target, context)` renders the old value with `cellText` and re-parses it with `parseTextIntoCell`
   (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:85-100`).
2. **Three short-circuits, in order** (`:91-97`):
   - same type in and out → the value is returned untouched, `ok: true`;
   - `isCellEmpty(value)` → `emptyCellFor(target.type)`, `ok: true`;
   - `attachment → attachment` → returned untouched. Files survive a round trip.
3. **A value that will not parse is preserved as `text` on the new value**, and the cell renders that
   string with a warning badge (`hasUnparsedText`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:67-74`;
   `src/components/board/cells/select-cell.tsx:73`, `date-cell.tsx:29`, `relation-cell.tsx:96`):

| Target | Parses when | Preserved shape when it does not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` / `longText` | always | — (never fails) |
| `select` | every comma-split label matches an option, case-insensitively | `{kind:"select", optionIds:[…matched…], text: trimmed}` |
| `date` | ISO, then `DD/MM/YYYY` (**day-first**), then `YYYY/MM/DD`, then `Date.parse` | `{kind:"date", iso:null, text: trimmed}` |
| `user` | every name or email matches a directory entry | `{kind:"user", userIds:[…], text: trimmed}` |
| `attachment` | **never** — "files cannot be recreated from their names" | `{kind:"attachment", attachments:[], text: trimmed}` |
| `relation` | every token resolves to a row id or a display label | `{kind:"relation", rowIds:[…], text: trimmed}` |

   (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:25-82`.)
4. **`text` is opaque payload.** Do not strip it, normalise it or try to re-parse it server-side. It
   is cleared only when the cell is written with a value that parses.
5. **The config is reset to `defaultConfigFor(type)`.** `retypeColumn`
   (`src/lib/board-schema.ts:209-220`) does not attempt to carry a select's options into a date
   column. A conversion away from `select` and back does **not** restore the old options.
6. **Date parsing is day-first before the engine.** `03/04/2026` is 3 April, and `buildIso` rejects
   rolled-over dates such as 31 February (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:176-207`). A server-side
   importer or paste path must match this exactly or the same file lands differently in two places.

**Response**

```ts
/** E-057, dryRun=false. */
interface ConvertColumnResponse {
  readonly column: BoardColumn;
  /** ONLY the rows whose value changed, authoritative, revision already bumped. */
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  /** How many values were kept as text with a warning. */
  readonly preserved: number;
  /** Null when every changed row fitted in this response — see the scale note. */
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/** E-057, dryRun=true. Same shape the client computes locally today. */
interface ConversionPreview {
  readonly total: number;      // converted + preserved (empty cells are not counted)
  readonly converted: number;
  readonly preserved: number;
  readonly samples: readonly string[];  // at most 5 source strings that will be preserved
}
```

`ConversionPreview` is the frontend's own interface (`src/types/board.ts:453-460`) and
`previewConversion` already produces exactly this, capped at 5 samples
(`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:103-128`). Serving it from `?dryRun=true` lets the dialog stop
recomputing the answer over a record set it may only partly hold.

**Conversion is deliberately NOT optimistic.** The server rewrites the rows and returns them; the
store replaces the column and reconciles the rows from the response
(`docs/BOARD.md:255-256`; `src/store/board-store.ts:792-815`).

> **RECOMMENDATION — conversion at scale.** `docs/BOARD.md:301-305` flags returning every rewritten
> row as unworkable at 5 000. Contract: return at most `limit` (default 500) changed rows plus a
> `nextCursor`; a client that receives a non-null cursor may either page the rest or refetch. The
> `preserved` count is always the **whole-board** figure, because the warning it drives is about the
> conversion, not about the page.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` → `UPDATE type = $new, config = defaultConfigFor($new)`. |
| `board_rows` | `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1` (streamed) → `UPDATE cells = jsonb_set(cells, '{<columnId>}', $converted), revision = revision + 1, updated_at = now()` for **every row that holds a value in this column** (`src/services/board-service.ts:742-752`). Rows with no key for the column are skipped. The four indexed projections are recomputed when the converted column is a role column. |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`. |
| `row_activity` | **Not written.** The mock writes no activity for a conversion, and one entry per row on a 5 000-row board would drown every record's history. **RECOMMENDATION:** one `audit_events` row for the operation instead. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.update`, `context` carrying `{ from, to, converted, preserved }`. |

**Transaction** — **Required, and all-or-nothing.** A column that is `date` while half its cells are
still `select` is not a state any reader can make sense of — although note that a reader would *cope*
(`cellOf` reads a mismatched cell as empty, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:43-46`), which is the safety net,
not the design. `?dryRun=true` opens no write transaction at all.

**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10) **and** `row.updated` (RT-07) per changed row, or one
batched frame carrying `rowIds`. Ids only.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `type` is not a `ColumnType`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` — `config` does not match the requested `type`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.update`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `COLUMN_CONVERT_UNSUPPORTED` — no conversion path. **Reserved, not currently reachable**: every pair is expressible through the text projection, and the "unconvertible" cases (anything → `attachment`) preserve rather than fail. Keep the code for a future type that genuinely has no text form. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/convert-column-dialog.tsx:36,52` (the preview
dialog) and `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:82,132` (the "Steps" preset, which converts
to `longText` and then switches numbering on in a second call), both through
`src/store/board-store.ts:792-815`.

### 14.6 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/reorder` — reorder columns

**Purpose** — Move a column in the board's schema order. Positions are renumbered densely across the
whole schema.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.update` on `boards.node_id` (`src/services/board-service.ts:672`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-056. Either form is accepted; `columnIds` is authoritative when both are sent. */
interface ReorderColumnsRequest {
  /** The board's complete column order, every id exactly once. */
  readonly columnIds?: readonly string[];
  /** Single-column move — what the FE's `moveColumn(columnId, toIndex)` sends. */
  readonly columnId?: string;
  readonly toIndex?: number;
}
```

The frontend moves one column at a time (`moveColumn`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:183-200`;
`reorderColumn`, `src/services/board-service.ts:664-678`), clamping `toIndex` into
`[0, length - 1]` and returning the array unchanged when nothing moved. `columnIds` is the
**RECOMMENDATION**: it is idempotent and cannot be misapplied against a schema that changed
underneath the caller.

**Response** — `readonly BoardColumn[]` — the whole renumbered schema, `position` dense `0..n-1`.
A complete array (C-11).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE ORDER BY position` → `UPDATE position` for every column whose position changed. Renumber to `0..n-1`; the deferrable `UNIQUE (board_id, position)` permits the intermediate states inside the statement. |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`. |
| `board_rows`, `board_views` | **Not written.** `cells` is keyed by column id and a view's `columnOrder` is its own list; neither is affected by schema position. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.update`. |

**Note the interaction with per-view order.** A view with a non-empty `columnOrder` renders in *its*
order and ignores the schema order entirely; ids missing from `columnOrder` fall back to
`position + 1000` (`resolveColumns`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:40`). Dragging a header in the grid
writes the **view**, not the schema (`moveColumnTo`, `src/store/board-store.ts:1093-1117`). This
endpoint therefore changes the fallback order and the order a view with no `columnOrder` shows.

**Transaction** — **Required.** All positions or none.
**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `columnIds` is not a permutation of the board's columns, or `toIndex` is out of range. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.update`. Copy: `You do not have permission to reorder columns`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/services/board-service.ts:664-678` (`reorderColumn`). No component calls
it today: the header drag writes the view instead
(`src/components/board/table/grid-header.tsx:60,70`). It is owed because the schema order is what a
board with no per-view order shows, and what a new view inherits.

### 14.7 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/duplicate` — duplicate a column

**Purpose** — Copy a column, its configuration **and its values**, immediately to the right of the
original.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.create` on `boards.node_id` (`src/services/board-service.ts:600`) —
duplicating is adding, not updating.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `columnId`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response**

```ts
/** E-055. */
interface DuplicateColumnResponse {
  readonly column: BoardColumn;
  /** Every row that gained a value, authoritative, revision already bumped. */
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;   // same scale escape hatch as convert
}
```

**Contract — EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (`src/services/board-service.ts:593-633`):

- **The values come too.** "A duplicate that carried the shape but not the contents would be a
  differently-named empty column, which is what Insert right already gives you" (`:585-591`).
- **The copy is never primary.** `isPrimary: false` is forced — "a board has exactly one column that
  titles a row" (`:610-611`).
- **The copy lands at `source.position + 1`**, renumbering everything after it.
- **The name is de-duplicated** with `uniqueColumnName`, so `Notes` becomes `Notes 2`.
- **Select option ids are copied verbatim.** The two columns then share option ids. That is
  deliberate and harmless: option ids are only ever looked up *within their column*
  (`optionById(column.config.options, id)`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:76-81`), and copying the cells
  without copying the ids would blank every value.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `INSERT` the copy at `position + 1`; `UPDATE position = position + 1` for everything at or after it. |
| `board_rows` | `UPDATE cells = jsonb_set(cells, '{<newColumnId>}', cells->'<sourceColumnId>'), revision = revision + 1` for every row that **holds a key** for the source column (`:622-629` — rows without one are skipped, not given an empty value). |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`. |
| `board_row_relations` | `INSERT` — when the source is a **relation** column, the projection rows are duplicated for the new column id, so backlinks through the copy are indexed too (§17.3). |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.create`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Column, renumbering and every rewritten row.
**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10) plus `row.updated` (RT-07) for the changed rows.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.create`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — reserved; a duplicate adds no rows, so unreachable today. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:88,114-117,314-317`
("Duplicate column", which then opens the new header for renaming) →
`src/store/board-store.ts:704-729`.

### 14.8 `DELETE /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}` — delete a column

**Purpose** — Remove a column from the schema, from every record's `cells`, and from every view that
referenced it.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.delete` on `boards.node_id` (`src/services/board-service.ts:687`).
This is the one column operation with its own key — deleting a column destroys data on every record.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `columnId`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly BoardColumn[]` — the whole remaining schema, renumbered. A complete array
(C-11), which is what the store assigns (`src/store/board-store.ts:817-836`).

#### The protected-column error — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

**Exactly one column is protected: the primary.** `isProtectedColumn(column)` is
`column.isPrimary`, and nothing else (`src/lib/board-schema.ts:132-134`). The comment is emphatic
and must be honoured: "A column is not made permanent by where it came from: one an import created
is a column like any other, and there is no `system`, `locked` or `isImported` flag anywhere in the
schema for it to be caught by."

The refusal is `409` / `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED` with the message, verbatim, from
`src/services/board-service.ts:693-695`:

```jsonc
// 409 DELETE /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}
{
  "error": {
    "code": "conflict",
    "message": "“Title” titles every record and cannot be deleted",
    "isRetryable": false,
    "reason": "COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED",
    "requestId": "01JB9…"
  }
}
```

The curly quotes are the frontend's (`“${target.name}”`) and are rendered to the user verbatim
(canon §4.4 rule 1). `removeColumn` returns the list unchanged rather than throwing
(`src/lib/board-schema.ts:136-144`); the **service** is where the refusal lives, and the UI disables
the menu item on top of it (`src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:328-338`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`; refuse if `is_primary`. `DELETE` the row; `UPDATE position` to renumber `0..n-1`. |
| `board_rows` | `UPDATE cells = cells - '<columnId>', revision = revision + 1, updated_at = now()` for every row that holds the key (`src/services/board-service.ts:700-705`). Rows without it are untouched. |
| `board_views` | `UPDATE` — **prune every reference in the same transaction**: `filters` and `sorts` entries naming the column, `hidden_column_ids`, `column_order`, `column_widths` keys, `column_display` keys, and `group_by_column_id` / `date_column_id` / `end_date_column_id` set to `NULL`. This is `pruneView` (`src/lib/board-view.ts`), applied by the store at `src/store/board-store.ts:832`; canon E-054 makes it a rule. The three anchor FKs carry `ON DELETE SET NULL` so the database enforces half of it; the JSONB half is the service's. |
| `board_row_relations` | `DELETE … WHERE source_column_id = $1` — the projection rows for a deleted relation column go with it. |
| `board_columns` (other) | `UPDATE config` — any **other** select column whose `availability` conditions reference the deleted column. **Not required**: `evaluateCondition` returns `true` for a condition pointing at a deleted column — it is ignored, not failed closed (`src/lib/conditions.ts:189-198`), and that behaviour is load-bearing ("a deleted column must not silently lock every option"). Leave the stale condition in place. |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`; `status_column_id` / `assignee_column_id` / `due_column_id` set to `NULL` by their own `ON DELETE SET NULL`. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.delete`, severity `warn`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Column, every row's `cells`, every view's references and the
relation projection land together. A view holding a filter on a column that no longer exists renders
nothing and offers no way back.

**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10) plus `row.updated` (RT-07) for the rewritten rows.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.delete`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED` — see above. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:86,142-145,362-376` (the confirm
dialog counts the records that hold a value first, with `countFilledCells`) and
`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts` (the importer removes columns the mapping dropped), through
`src/store/board-store.ts:817-836`.

---

### 14.9 Select options — the rule everything else depends on

**Option ids are immutable, and rules reference ids, not labels.**

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT**, stated in the code and relied on by four separate structures:

| Structure | References an option by | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A cell value | `optionIds: string[]` | `src/types/board.ts:222` |
| `SelectConfig.completedOptionIds` | ids; `isRowCompleted` builds a `Set` of ids | `src/types/board.ts:136`; `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:149-160` |
| `TransitionRules.transitions` | ids on **both** sides, plus `"__empty__"` | `src/types/board.ts:93`; `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:28` |
| `SelectOption.availability` conditions | ids in `Condition.value` / `Condition.values` | `src/types/board.ts:45-51` |

"Nothing here reads a label, so renaming 'Done' to 'Shipped' changes nothing"
(`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:130-137`); "the table the user wrote, keyed by immutable option id, so
renaming a status never breaks the workflow" (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:6-11`).

**Backend rules that follow:**
1. **Renaming an option never re-mints its id.** A `PATCH` that changes `label` changes only `label`.
2. **Deleting an option cascades inside the config**: out of `completedOptionIds`, out of
   `transitions` (both keys and every target list), and out of any `availability` condition naming
   it. The frontend already does all three locally
   (`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:180-190`; `pruneTransitionRules`,
   `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:256-268`).
3. **Deleting an option does NOT prune cells.** Records keep the orphaned id and the UI renders it as
   an unknown option rather than an empty cell. Canon E-060 states it: "cells keep the orphaned id;
   the frontend renders it as unknown, not deleted." `cellText` falls back to `value.text ?? ""` when
   no label resolves (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:93-99`).
4. **`"__empty__"` is reserved.** A user-authored id equal to it is refused with
   `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` (`400`).
5. **There is one label lookup, and it is on the read side only**: filters and conditions accept an
   id *or* the rendered label so a hand-written rule agrees with a UI-written one
   (`src/lib/board-view.ts:63-84`; `matchesIdentity`, `src/lib/conditions.ts:141-155`), and
   `parseTextIntoCell` matches an incoming *label* case-insensitively on import and paste
   (`findOptionId`, `src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:140-147`). Neither writes an id.

---

### 14.10 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/options` — add an option

**Purpose** — Add one option to a select column. This is the create-on-type path: a user types a
value that does not exist yet in a select cell and the option is minted for the whole board.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.update` on `boards.node_id`.

> **EXISTING REQUIREMENT vs. the mock.** `createSelectOption` checks **no** permission today
> (`src/services/board-service.ts:758-786`) — canon OQ-16 records that the gaps in the mock's
> permission column are gaps in the mock, not intended policy, and `src/services/authz.ts:16-33` is
> explicit that the real API re-checks every key. Minting a board-wide status from a cell editor is a
> schema write; it takes the schema key.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `columnId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-058. */
interface CreateSelectOptionRequest {
  /** Trimmed server-side before matching and before storing. */
  readonly label: string;
  /**
   * Picked client-side by cycling the palette; the server stores what it is given,
   * validated against SelectColor. Omitted = nextOptionColor(existing options).
   */
  readonly color?: SelectColor;
}
```

The client picks the colour by cycling `blue, green, amber, red, violet, cyan, pink, gray` at
`options.length % 8` (`src/store/board-store.ts:845-847`; `SELECT_COLORS`,
`src/lib/board-schema.ts:25-34`; `nextOptionColor`, `:225-227`). Canon §1.3.3 fixes the policy: the
backend stores what it is given.

**Response** — `SelectOption`. **`200` with the existing option** when the label already exists;
`201` when a new one is minted.

#### Dedupe by label — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

`docs/BOARD.md:298-300`, listed among the contracts the backend still owes:

> **Select option creation must dedupe by label.** Two users typing "Blocked" at the same moment must
> end up with one option. Contract: `POST` returns the existing option when the label already exists
> (**200, not 409**).

Matching is on the **trimmed, case-folded** label — `findOptionByLabel` compares
`label.trim().toLowerCase()` against `option.label.toLowerCase()`
(`src/lib/board-schema.ts:231-237`). Note it is *not* the aggressive `normalizeColumnName`
normalisation used for column names: `In progress` and `In-progress` are two distinct options,
because a status label is content the user chose, not an identifier.

Canon OQ-53 asks for this to be confirmed; canon §1.3.3 has already taken the position. Implement it
with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` semantics inside a row-locked read of the column, so the race
the requirement names actually cannot happen: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the column, re-check the label,
then append.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the column; assert `type = 'select'`. If a case-folded label match exists, **return it and write nothing.** Otherwise `UPDATE config = jsonb_set(config, '{options}', config->'options' \|\| $newOption)`. The new id is minted server-side. |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at` (only on a real insert). |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.update` (only on a real insert). |
| `board_rows` | **Never.** Adding an option does not touch a record — and adding a status never freezes the board, because a key the transition table does not mention is ungoverned (`isGoverned`, `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:63-65`). |

**Option id format.** The frontend mints `opt_<columnId>_<base36 counter>`
(`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:79`) precisely because "option ids key the
completed set, the transition table and the conditions written against them, and two columns sharing
one is a collision waiting for whichever of those looks an id up without its column" (`:70-78`).
Server-minted ids are `nextId("opt")` (`src/services/board-service.ts:773`). **RECOMMENDATION:** the
server mints `opt_<uuid-v4-without-dashes>`; ids are opaque to every reader, and template seeds keep
their stable synthetic ids (`status_0`…`status_4`, `env_0`…`env_2`, `method_0`… —
`src/lib/board-templates.ts:20-22`) so a seeded rule keeps pointing at the right option.

**Transaction** — **Required** (the `FOR UPDATE` read, the label re-check and the append).
**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10), on a real insert only.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — empty label after trimming, or `color` not a `SelectColor`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` — reserved for a request that supplies its own id. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `board.column.update`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `SELECT_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` — the column is missing **or is not of type `select`**. The mock conflates the two (`src/services/board-service.ts:770` — `notFound("That select column")`) and so does the API. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx:75,201` and
`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:61,221` (`onCreateOption`), through
`src/store/board-store.ts:838-875`.

---

### 14.11 `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/options/{optionId}` — update an option

**Purpose** — Change one option's label, colour, disabled flag or availability rule. **Never its id.**

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.update` on `boards.node_id`.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `columnId`, `optionId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-059. `id` is not a field: an option's id is immutable. */
interface UpdateSelectOptionRequest {
  readonly label?: string;
  readonly color?: SelectColor;
  /** Switched off in column settings — never selectable, whatever a record holds. */
  readonly isDisabled?: boolean;
  /** null clears the rule; omitted leaves it untouched (C-08). */
  readonly availability?: ConditionGroup | null;
}
```

`availability` is a whole-tree replace, not a merge — it is a recursive structure and there is no
sensible partial form.

**Response** — `SelectOption`.

**Database** — `board_columns` `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` → `UPDATE config` with the option replaced in
place, **at its existing index** (order is meaningful: select cells sort by option order,
`cellSortKey`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:148-153`, and Kanban builds its columns from the schema order,
`docs/BOARD.md`). `boards` `UPDATE updated_at`. `audit_events` `INSERT`.
**No `board_rows` write** — a rename changes what every cell *displays* and nothing about what any
cell *stores*.

**Transaction** — Required (read-modify-write of one JSONB document).
**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — empty label, bad colour. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` — `availability` past the cap (OQ-38). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `SELECT_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` / `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `OPTION_LABEL_CONFLICT` → served as `conflict` when the new label case-folds onto another option on the same column. **RECOMMENDATION**: creation dedupes silently, but a *rename* onto an existing label is a caller demanding an exact name, and two options labelled "Done" make the board unreadable. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:152-157` (`patchOption`)
— but note the dialog commits the **whole config in one write** through `updateColumnConfig`
(`src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:350`), "so a half-written rule never lands"
(`:342-343`). This single-option endpoint is therefore a **RECOMMENDATION**: it exists so the
create-on-type path and a future inline colour picker do not have to send the whole option array.

---

### 14.12 Reordering options — **no dedicated endpoint**

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Reordering options is a `config` rewrite through
`PATCH /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}` (E-053) carrying the complete `options` array in the new
order. That is exactly what the dialog does: `move(index, delta)` splices the local draft
(`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:159-168`) and the whole draft is committed
once on save.

There is deliberately **no** `POST /columns/{columnId}/options/reorder` in canon §3.7, and this
chapter does not add one. The reasons are worth recording, because the symmetric operation on
*columns* does get its own endpoint (E-056):

- Options live inside one JSONB document with three structures that reference them by id
  (`completedOptionIds`, `transitions`, `availability`). A reorder that arrived separately from a
  concurrent option delete would have to be merged against a document that had already changed.
- The option list is small and always read whole. Sending it whole is neither expensive nor lossy.
- Column `position` is a real indexed column with a uniqueness constraint; option order is an array
  index. They are not the same problem.

**Server-side rule:** on an E-053 write that replaces `options`, the server verifies the new array is
a **permutation-or-subset** of the stored ids plus any newly minted ones — an id that appears twice
is `VALIDATION_FAILED`, and an id that disappears is treated as a delete and triggers the
`completedOptionIds` / `transitions` / `availability` pruning described in §14.4.

---

### 14.13 `DELETE /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/options/{optionId}` — delete an option

**Purpose** — Remove one option from a select column and every rule that referenced it. Records keep
the orphaned id.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `board.column.update` on `boards.node_id`.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `columnId`, `optionId`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly SelectOption[]` — the column's remaining options, in order. A complete array
(C-11), matching canon E-060.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` → one `UPDATE config` that does **all four** things at once: removes the option from `options`; removes it from `completedOptionIds`; removes it as a key **and** as a target from `transitions` (`pruneTransitionRules`, `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:256-268`); removes any `Condition` naming it from every remaining option's `availability` tree. |
| `board_rows` | **Never.** "The frontend keeps an unknown option id rather than dropping it, so the backend must not prune cells silently" (canon §1.3.3). A record that held the deleted status still shows *something* rather than silently becoming empty, and the record's history stays honest. |
| `boards` | `UPDATE updated_at`. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — `board.column.update`, `context` naming the removed option and how many records still reference it (a `SELECT count(*) … WHERE cells->'<columnId>'->'optionIds' ? '<optionId>'`, which the GIN index on `cells` serves). |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The option and its three rule references are one write; a transition
table pointing at an option that no longer exists strands every card in that bucket.

**Realtime** — `board.schema.changed` (RT-10).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `SELECT_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` / `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:180-190`
(`removeOption`), committed as part of the whole-config write. As with the option `PATCH`, the
single-option endpoint is a **RECOMMENDATION** that spares a caller the whole array.

---

## 15. Row APIs

### 15.0 The record, and the cell update contract

#### 15.0.1 `BoardRow` on the wire

```ts
interface BoardRow {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  /** `TASK-001` — assigned by the backend, never derived on the client. */
  readonly displayId: string;
  /** Numeric part of the display id; monotonic per board, never reused. */
  readonly sequence: number;
  readonly cells: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
  readonly createdAt: string;                 // ISO 8601
  readonly updatedAt: string;                 // ISO 8601
  readonly createdBy: string;                 // user id
  /** Bumped by the server on every write — the optimistic-concurrency token. */
  readonly revision: number;
  /** When the record was archived (SY-ARC-37). Null/absent = active. */
  readonly archivedAt?: string | null;
  /** Parent record in the task hierarchy, or null/absent at the top level (§16). */
  readonly parentRowId?: string | null;
  /** CLIENT-ONLY. True while the row exists optimistically. The API never sends it. */
  readonly isPending?: boolean;
}
```

`src/types/board.ts:236-266`. Two fields deserve emphasis:

- **`isPending` never crosses the wire.** It marks a `tmp_…` row the client invented while a create
  is in flight (`src/store/board-store.ts:360-377`). A server response carrying it would make a real
  row render as a placeholder.
- **`BoardRow` has `createdBy` and no `updatedBy`** (canon OQ-35). This chapter follows the
  frontend: `board_rows` stores `created_by` only, and "who changed this" is answered by
  `row_activity`, which is where the drawer already reads it from
  (`src/components/board/drawer/activity-timeline.tsx`).

#### 15.0.2 `CellValue` — the value union

```ts
type CellValue =
  | { readonly kind: "text";       readonly value: string }
  | { readonly kind: "longText";   readonly value: string }
  | { readonly kind: "select";     readonly optionIds: readonly string[]; readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "date";       readonly iso: string | null;           readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "user";       readonly userIds: readonly string[];   readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "attachment"; readonly attachments: readonly CellAttachment[]; readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "relation";   readonly rowIds: readonly string[];    readonly text?: string };

interface CellAttachment {
  readonly id: string;              // file_assets.id — the ONLY thing persisted
  readonly name: string;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  /** Minted per response as a short-lived signed URL. NEVER accepted on write (OQ-75). */
  readonly url: string | null;
  readonly thumbnailUrl: string | null;
  readonly uploadedBy?: string;
  readonly createdAt?: string;
}
```

`src/types/board.ts:201-230`. Five rules bind every write path:

1. **The `kind` lives on the value, not on the column, and a mismatch is legal.** After a conversion
   a `date` column can hold `{kind:"date", iso:null, text:"sometime next sprint"}`; a reader that
   sees a `kind` disagreeing with its column's `type` reads the cell as **empty**, never as an error
   (`cellOf`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:43-46`). **The API must not normalise a mismatch away**
   (canon §2.5).
2. **`text` is opaque payload.** It holds the original string the target type could not parse. Do
   not strip, normalise or re-parse it server-side; it is cleared only when the cell is rewritten
   with a value that parses (§14.5).
3. **Validation is on the tag, not on the column.** `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` (`400`) fires when
   `kind` is not a `ColumnType` member. It does **not** fire when `kind !== column.type`.
4. **Dates.** For a column with `DateConfig.includesTime === false` the `iso` must be a `YYYY-MM-DD`
   day key or a midnight-UTC instant, and it **must never be converted through a local timezone**
   (canon C-04; `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24` — "A due date is a square on a calendar, not a moment";
   `isoOfDayKey`, used by the subtask composer at
   `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-composer.tsx:105`). A malformed value is
   `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` (`400`). Canon §8.8 OQ-32: store the string as sent, project into
   `due_date` or `due_at` by `includesTime`.
5. **Attachments.** Only `assetId` (`CellAttachment.id`) is persisted. `url` and `thumbnailUrl` are
   minted per response and **rejected on write** (canon §1.3.4, OQ-75). The uploader also writes a
   `cell_attachments` row (T-29) in the same transaction — that table, not the JSONB, is what
   quota accounting and cascade-on-row-delete read.

#### 15.0.3 Which columns changed, and what one write costs

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** The unit of a cell write is `CellEdit`, and the unit of the *response* is
the whole row:

```ts
interface CellEdit {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly value: CellValue;
}
```

- The caller names **exactly the cells it changed** — never the whole `cells` document. A `PATCH`
  that carried the whole document would overwrite a concurrent edit to a column this caller never
  touched, and the conflict policy below could not tell the two apart.
- The server merges each edit into the row's `cells` (`{ ...current.cells, [columnId]: value }`,
  `src/services/board-service.ts:514-518`) and returns the **authoritative row** (C-10).
- **`revision` is bumped once per row per call, however many cells that call touched**
  (`:514-519`). Ten edits on one row is `revision + 1`, not `+10`. The activity log follows the same
  rule: "a write that changes Status and Due Date together is a single line in the timeline with two
  changes under it, never two lines racing for the same second"
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:157-163`; PRD `SY-ACT-40`).
- Edits are applied **in request order**, and a second edit to the same row in the same call reads
  the already-touched row (`touched.get(edit.rowId) ?? record.rows.get(edit.rowId)`, `:501`).
- An edit naming a row that does not exist is **silently skipped**, not an error (`:502` —
  `if (!current) continue;`). The response's `rows` array is the answer to what happened.

#### 15.0.4 Optimistic concurrency — last-write-wins **plus a notice**, never a `409`

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT**, and the single most easily got-wrong rule in this chapter.
`docs/BOARD.md:237-242`, PRD `BD-COR-07`, canon E-066 and canon §6.4 all say the same thing:

> The client sends the `revision` each edit was based on. If the server has moved on it **applies the
> write anyway** and returns a `ConflictNotice`, which the board renders as a dismissible banner.

`E-066` **always returns `200`.** `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` is explicitly *never* used for cell writes
(canon §4.3, cross-cutting table).

Detection reproduces three properties exactly (`src/services/board-service.ts:504-512`):

| Property | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Absent base | `baseRevisions[rowId] === undefined` → **never** conflicts. A caller that does not claim a base is not making a stale claim. |
| Comparison | `base < current.revision` conflicts. `base === current.revision` and `base > current.revision` do **not**. |
| At most one notice per row per call | Raised by the **first** edit that touches the row (`&& !touched.has(edit.rowId)`), so a five-cell edit on a stale row produces one banner, not five. |

```ts
interface ConflictNotice {
  readonly id: string;        // server-minted; the client dismisses by it
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly columnId: string;  // the FIRST edit that touched the row
  readonly message: string;   // rendered verbatim
}
```

The message is fixed: `` `${displayId} changed elsewhere — your edit was kept` ``
(`src/services/board-service.ts:510`). The trailing clause is the contract in one phrase: the edit
was kept.

**Bulk writes carry no concurrency token at all** (canon §6.4, OQ-55) — `bulkUpdate`,
`bulkArchive`, `bulkDelete` and `bulkMove` are unconditional, and refusals surface as `BulkSkip`
rather than as conflicts, because the client has no conflict UI for them
(`src/store/board-store.ts:565-657`).

---

### 15.1 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows` — list records

**Purpose** — A page of a board's records, optionally narrowed by a saved view, ad-hoc filters, a
sort and a search term.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on `boards.node_id`. No action key — reading records is not an action.

**Path Params** — `boardId` `uuid`.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `string` | — | Opaque base64 of the sort-key tuple. **A client must never construct or parse one** (canon §6.3). |
| `limit` | `int 1..500` | `200` | Page size. Hard server cap. |
| `includeArchived` | `boolean` | `false` | Archived records stay out of every view until asked for (`src/lib/board-view.ts:187,212`; the toolbar's "Show archived" toggle, `src/components/board/board-toolbar.tsx:45`). |
| `viewId` | `uuid` | — | Apply this saved view's `filters`, `filterConjunction` and `sorts` server-side. |
| `filter` | repeated | — | Ad-hoc filter, `columnId:operator:value`. Combined with `viewId`'s filters under `conjunction`. |
| `conjunction` | `and` \| `or` | `and` | How the filters combine (`FilterConjunction`). |
| `sort` | repeated | — | `columnId:asc` / `columnId:desc`. Multi-level, **earlier entries win and later ones break ties** (`src/types/board.ts:341`). Overrides the view's sorts when present. |
| `search` | `string` | — | Free text across every visible column. |
| `parentRowId` | `uuid` \| `null` | — | Restrict to one parent's direct children (§16.1 is the named alias for this). |

#### Pagination: keyset on `(position, id)` — and why

**Keyset (cursor), not offset.** Canon §6.3 fixes it board-wide, and for rows specifically:

- `BoardSnapshot.nextCursor` **already exists in the frontend contract**
  (`src/types/board.ts:434-435`) and is `null` today — the seam is shipped, only the server side is
  missing.
- The sort key is `(position, id)`. `position` is the `NUMERIC` fractional index (OQ-34), `id` breaks
  ties, and `board_rows_order_idx (board_id, position, id)` serves it directly.
- Offset pagination re-shuffles records across page boundaries: a create files itself
  *after a named anchor* (`afterRowId`) or *after its parent's last descendant*
  (`lastDescendantOf`, `src/services/board-service.ts:342-352`) — i.e. **in the middle of the
  order**, not at the end. Every concurrent insert would shift a page-2 reader's window.
- No `page` or `offset` parameter exists anywhere in this API.

When a `sort` is applied the cursor encodes `(sortKey…, position, id)`; the trailing pair keeps the
key total even when the sorted columns tie.

#### Server-side query — RECOMMENDATION, with the semantics fixed by the frontend

Filter, sort and search run **in the browser** today, over the full record set
(`queryRowIds`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:194-236`). `docs/BOARD.md:306-310` calls that "fine at 5.000
rows and wrong at 100.000", and canon OQ-36 rates it **critical**. Because every view funnels through
one pure function, a server-side query can be swapped in without touching a view — but it must
reproduce that function's semantics **exactly**, or the same board reads differently before and after
the swap:

| Rule | Behaviour | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filter order | filters → search → sort, in that order | `src/lib/board-view.ts:206-235` |
| Unknown column | a filter or sort naming a column that no longer exists is **dropped**, not failed | `:204`, `:230` |
| `isEmpty` / `isNotEmpty` | tested with `isCellEmpty`, which is per-kind and *not* just "no key" | `src/lib/cell-values.ts:48-64` |
| Identity columns (`select`, `user`, `relation`) | match the stored **id** first, then the whole rendered **label**, case-insensitively; `contains` / `notContains` additionally allow a substring of the label | `src/lib/board-view.ts:63-84` |
| Dates | compared as **calendar days**, never instants; an unparsable bound returns `true` (permissive); a null `iso` returns `false` | `:112-126` |
| Everything else | `cellText(...).toLowerCase()` compared with the trimmed, lower-cased needle | `:87-101` |
| Sort: empties | **always sink**, whichever direction the sort runs | `src/lib/board-view.ts:158-160`; `cellSortKey`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:137-142` |
| Sort: select | sorts by **option order within the column**, not by label — the meaningful order for statuses; an unknown option id sorts last (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) | `src/lib/cell-values.ts:148-153` |
| Sort: date | by parsed instant | `:144-146` |
| Sort: everything else | `cellText` lower-cased, `localeCompare` | `:155`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:170-173` |
| Search | substring of the text projection of any **visible** column | `rowMatchesSearch`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:238+` |

`search` is served by `board_rows.search_tsv` for the coarse pass and re-checked against the same
`cellText` projection for the exact substring semantics; the two must agree on which columns are
visible in the requested view.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response**

```ts
/** E-061. */
interface RowPage {
  readonly items: readonly BoardRow[];
  /** Null on the last page. Opaque. */
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

No `total`. Canon §6.3 records why: the board's counts that matter (`itemCount`, `openCount`) are
projections onto the node, and a count over a filtered 100 000-row board is a second query nobody
renders.

**Database** — `boards` `SELECT` (visibility) → `board_views` `SELECT` when `viewId` is given →
`board_columns` `SELECT` (needed to interpret filters and sorts) →
`board_rows` `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 [AND archived_at IS NULL] [AND (position,id) > cursor]
ORDER BY … LIMIT $limit + 1`. The `+1` decides `nextCursor` without a second query.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed `cursor`, `limit` out of range, unparseable `filter`/`sort`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` — a date filter bound that is neither `YYYY-MM-DD` nor ISO 8601. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` / `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION for the paging half.** The store loads rows through
`BoardSnapshot` (`src/store/board-store.ts:274`) and holds the whole set; `nextCursor` is read but
never followed because it is always `null` (`src/services/board-service.ts:239-240`). Canon's
position on OQ-36 is that the client fetches pages **eagerly** until the server-side query lands, so
this endpoint is the second and subsequent pages of E-047.

---

### 15.2 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` — one record

**Purpose** — One record, authoritative. What a deep link into a drawer resolves, and what a client
re-reads after a realtime frame it cannot apply from ids alone.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on `boards.node_id`.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`. `rowId` must belong to `boardId` or `ROW_NOT_FOUND`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `BoardRow`. The example in canon §6.2 is this endpoint's response.

**Database** — `boards` `SELECT` (visibility) → `board_rows` `SELECT … WHERE id = $1 AND board_id = $2`.
**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` — message `That record could not be found` (`src/services/board-service.ts:153`). |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION.** The drawer reads `rowsById[drawerRowId]` from the store
(`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:55`) and never fetches a single record. It is owed for
the RT-07 path: `row.updated` carries `{ boardId, rowId, revision }` and nothing else (canon §7.2),
so the receiver must be able to fetch one row.

---

### 15.3 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows` — create a record

**Purpose** — Create one record. The **backend owns the id sequence**; the client never invents a
`TASK-00n`.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.create` on `boards.node_id` (Member and above,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:23-25`), plus workspace membership.

**Path Params** — `boardId` `uuid`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-062. */
interface CreateRowRequest {
  /** Insert directly after this record. Omitted/null = append at the end. */
  readonly afterRowId?: string | null;
  /** Initial values, keyed by column id. Omitted = an empty CellValue per column. */
  readonly cells?: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
  /** Parent record, for a subtask (§16.2). Overrides `afterRowId` for placement. */
  readonly parentRowId?: string | null;
}
```

`src/services/board-service.ts:277-288`. When `cells` is omitted the server writes
`emptyCellFor(column.type)` for **every** column (`:312`, `:537-539`) — records are dense by
construction, which is why the JSONB choice loses nothing on sparsity (canon §1.3.2).

#### Atomic custom-id generation — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

PRD `BD-RID-10`: "100 % unique under concurrent creation via an atomic counter"; "deleting
`TASK-005` must never re-issue `005`". `docs/BOARD.md:277-280` names it **blocking**:

> `displayId` must come from a real database sequence, not `MAX(sequence) + 1`. Two simultaneous
> creates must never produce `TASK-005` twice, and a deleted number must never be reissued.

The exact procedure, inside the create transaction:

```sql
-- documentation only
UPDATE boards
   SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1,
       updated_at    = now()
 WHERE id = $boardId
RETURNING next_sequence, row_id_prefix;
-- then, in the same transaction:
INSERT INTO board_rows (board_id, sequence, custom_id, position, cells, created_by, ...)
VALUES ($boardId, $seq, $prefix || '-' || lpad($seq::text, 3, '0'), $position, $cells, $actor, ...);
```

The `UPDATE … RETURNING` takes a row lock on the `boards` row, which serialises concurrent creates on
one board and makes the counter genuinely atomic. It is **not** a Postgres `SEQUENCE`: a sequence is
not transactional (a rolled-back create would burn a number, producing a gap) and it cannot be
per-board without one sequence object per board.

Formatting matches `formatRowId` exactly: `` `${prefix}-${String(sequence).padStart(3,"0")}` `` —
`TASK-007`, and numbers past the padding simply grow to `TASK-1024`
(`src/lib/row-id.ts:13-15`).

**The counter only ever increases.** `deleteRow` and `bulkDelete` never decrement it
(`src/services/board-service.ts:449-470`, `:1050-1070`), so `005` is gone for good.

#### Placement

```
parentRowId given  ->  directly after that parent's LAST DESCENDANT in board order
afterRowId given   ->  directly after that record
neither            ->  at the end
```

`src/services/board-service.ts:320-324`. The subtask rule ("the board's own order already reads as
the tree even before a view nests it") is why `position` must be a fractional index and not an
integer: a child is inserted *between* two existing rows.

`position` is computed as: append → `max(position) + 1024`; insert after `A` with successor `B` →
`(A.position + B.position) / 2`; insert after the last row → `A.position + 1024`. When the gap
between two neighbours shrinks below the representable step, the board's positions are renumbered in
the same transaction (a rare `UPDATE` over the board).

**Response** — `BoardRow`, `201`. `revision: 1`, `displayId` and `sequence` server-assigned.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `boards` | `UPDATE next_sequence = next_sequence + 1 … RETURNING` — the row lock. |
| `board_rows` | `SELECT` the anchor (and, for a subtask, the parent's subtree, to find its last descendant) → `INSERT` one row. The four indexed projections are computed from `cells` on insert. |
| `board_row_relations` | `INSERT` — one row per target id in every relation cell of `cells` (§17.3). |
| `cell_attachments` | `INSERT` — one row per attachment id in every attachment cell. |
| `row_activity` | `INSERT` — `kind: "created"`, summary `created TASK-042`, or `created TASK-042 under TASK-041` when a parent is named. **Plus a second entry on the parent**: `added subtask TASK-042`, `kind: "updated"` (`src/services/board-service.ts:327-336`). |
| `nodes` | `UPDATE itemCount` / `openCount` projections (or leave them derived; §13.2). |
| `audit_events` | Not written. Record creation is board traffic, not governance traffic (canon OQ-25). |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Counter, row, relation projection, attachment links and both
activity entries are one write. A record that exists without having consumed its sequence number, or
a sequence consumed without a record, both break `UNIQUE (board_id, sequence)` on the next create.

**Realtime** — `row.created` (RT-06), `{ boardId, rowId, revision }`. Ids only; the receiver fetches.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `cells` names a column that is not on this board. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` — a `CellValue.kind` that is not a `ColumnType`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.create`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND` — message `That parent record could not be found` (`src/services/board-service.ts:302`). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` — the parent is already at the depth cap (§16, OQ-33). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` / `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` — an initial `select` value the column's rules refuse. The subtask composer already filters its status list by availability with `ignoreTransitions: true` (`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-composer.tsx:60-73`), so a create is gated by `isDisabled` and `availability` but **not** by transitions — there is no "from" state to transition out of. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (OQ-36). |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/board-toolbar.tsx:47,171` ("Add record"),
`src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx` (the trailing add row),
`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx` (add-in-column), and
`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:55` / `src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:35,64`
for the subtask branch — all through `src/store/board-store.ts:356-398` (`addRow`) and `:464-515`
(`createSubtask`).

### 15.4 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/duplicate` — duplicate a record

**Purpose** — Copy one record's values into a new record placed directly after it.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.create` on `boards.node_id` — duplicating is creating
(`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:55` gates on `row.create`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `BoardRow`, `201`.

**Contract — EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (`src/services/board-service.ts:433-447`): a copy is a
**sibling**. It keeps the source's `parentRowId`, not the source itself — duplicating a subtask
produces another subtask of the same parent, never a child of the record you copied. It takes
`afterRowId = rowId`, a fresh `id`, a fresh `displayId` from the counter, and `revision: 1`.
`archivedAt` is **not** copied: a duplicate of an archived record is active.

**Database** — identical to §15.3, with `cells` read from the source row inside the same transaction.
`row_activity` gets a `created` entry on the copy; the source is untouched.

**Transaction** — **Required**, same reasons as §15.3.
**Realtime** — `row.created` (RT-06).

**Possible Errors** — as §15.3, plus:

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | `not_found` | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` — the source. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:32,55-58` and
`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:59,281-288` → `src/store/board-store.ts:400-431`.

### 15.5 `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` — write cells (single and batch)

**Purpose** — The one endpoint every cell write goes through, from one keystroke in the table to a
300-cell paste. **Always `200`.**

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.update` on `boards.node_id` (Member and above), plus workspace membership.

**Path Params** — `boardId` `uuid`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-066. A single-cell edit is an array of length 1 — there is no second endpoint. */
interface UpdateCellsRequest {
  readonly edits: readonly CellEdit[];
  /**
   * The revision each edit was based on, per row. A row absent from this map
   * never conflicts. See §15.0.4.
   */
  readonly baseRevisions?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
}
```

**Batch size.** `docs/BOARD.md:281-285`: "One paste can produce hundreds of edits…
needs a documented max batch size." **RECOMMENDATION:** 1 000 `CellEdit`s per call, refused with
`REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` (`413`) beyond it. A 200-column × 5-row paste is 1 000 edits; the clipboard path
already bounds itself to the grid (`pasteRange`, `src/lib/grid-clipboard.ts:50-82`).

**Response**

```ts
/** E-066. ALWAYS 200. Never 409. */
interface UpdateCellsResponse {
  /** Authoritative rows, revision already bumped. Only the rows that changed. */
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly conflicts: readonly ConflictNotice[];
}
```

```jsonc
// 200
{
  "rows": [
    {
      "id": "3f1c…", "boardId": "9a2e…", "displayId": "TASK-042", "sequence": 42,
      "cells": {
        "col_title":  { "kind": "text",   "value": "Fix the export encoding" },
        "col_status": { "kind": "select", "optionIds": ["status_2"] },
        "col_due":    { "kind": "date",   "iso": "2026-09-04" }
      },
      "createdAt": "2026-08-20T11:02:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-08-27T09:31:12.004Z",
      "createdBy": "usr_7f…", "revision": 8, "archivedAt": null, "parentRowId": null
    }
  ],
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "id": "cfl_01JB…",
      "rowId": "3f1c…",
      "columnId": "col_status",
      "message": "TASK-042 changed elsewhere — your edit was kept"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 15.5.1 CRITICAL — a status change is validated wherever it arrives from

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT, and the reason this endpoint is singular.** The Table, the Drawer, the
Kanban drag, the Gantt bar, the Calendar drop, the subtask checkbox and a clipboard paste **all** hit
this endpoint. `src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:6-13` states the rule:

> Transition rules and conditional options are *record* rules: they hold wherever the value is
> written from — a Kanban drag, a cell editor, the drawer, a paste. Enforcing them in one place is
> what stops the Kanban rule being bypassable by opening the same record's Status cell in the table.

Today `guardCellEdits` is **client-side only**: `boardService.updateCells` never calls it
(`src/services/board-service.ts:488-535`). Canon OQ-16 records that this is a gap in the mock, and
`src/services/authz.ts:16-33` is unambiguous: "Hiding a button is a courtesy. This is the refusal."
**The backend MUST re-run the gate.** Without it the workflow is advisory and one `curl` bypasses it.

`docs/BOARD.md` and `src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:15-18` also insist the two checks stay separate and
are never collapsed into one boolean: **permission** answers "may this person edit Status at all";
a **transition rule** answers "may Status go from here to there". A refusal from each says something
different, and the copy differs accordingly.

#### 15.5.2 The ordered flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["1. Authenticate<br/>session -> actor id, IP, clock (C-09)"] --> B
  B["2. Workspace membership<br/>not a member is not viewer"] --> C
  C["3. Resource access<br/>board -> node -> ancestor chain -> access_rules"] --> D
  D["4. Permission<br/>can('row.update', ctx); narrowing: trashed / frozen / locked"] --> E
  E["5. Load current rows FOR UPDATE<br/>+ the board's columns"] --> F
  F["6. Per-edit record rules<br/>isDisabled -> availability -> transition"] --> G
  G["7. Write<br/>merge cells, revision + 1 per row, projections"] --> H
  H["8. Activity log<br/>one row_activity entry per row, rendered changes"] --> I
  I["9. Realtime<br/>row.updated, ids only"] --> J
  J["10. Response<br/>200 { rows, conflicts }"]
  F -->|refused| K["409 TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED<br/>or OPTION_UNAVAILABLE<br/>nothing is written"]
  D -->|refused| L["403 PERMISSION_DENIED<br/>name-free copy"]
```

**1. Authenticate.** The actor id, role, IP and clock come from the session and the socket, never
from the body (C-09; `src/services/audit-service.ts:280-285`). A `createdBy` or `actorId` in the body
is ignored.

**2. Workspace membership.** Resolved before anything else. "Not a member" answers as
`WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (`404`), not as `permission_denied` — a non-member must not learn the workspace
exists (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`).

**3. Resource access.** `boardId` → `boards.node_id` → the node's ancestor chain →
`access_rules` + `workspace_members` → the caller's **effective role on that node**
(`effectiveAccess`, `src/services/authz.ts:36-53`). Deepest node wins; at one node a user-scoped rule
beats a role-scoped rule; the workspace role is the floor (canon §8.8, OQ-22). A node the caller may
not see answers `404` / `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — identical to "does not exist" (canon §4.2).

**4. Permission.** `can("row.update", { role, user, node, isFrozen, isLocked })`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:69-87`). Three layers only ever **narrow**:
- `node.isTrashed` → only `node.delete` passes (`:81`);
- `isFrozen` (an **archived ancestor**; the node's own flag is deliberately not read) → every write
  refused (`:83`; `src/lib/archive.ts:30-45`);
- `isLocked` → `row.update` is in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`, so a lock refuses it (`:84`, `:36-49`).

Then the **row-level** freeze: an archived record is read-only until it is restored
(`src/lib/archive.ts:5-11`; `src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:93-95` —
`isEditable = canEdit && !isArchived`). An edit naming an archived row is refused with
`409` / `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY`.

**5. Load current values.** `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the addressed rows, ordered by `id` to avoid
deadlocks between two concurrent batches, plus the board's columns. This is where `revision` is read
for the conflict comparison (§15.0.4) and where the **current** option is read for the transition
check.

**6. Record rules.** For each edit, in this order (`guardCellEdits`,
`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:43-90`; `resolveOptionAvailability`,
`src/lib/select-availability.ts:69-115`):

  a. **Not a select write?** The edit passes untouched. Only edits where the column is `select`
     **and** `value.kind === "select"` are gated (`:54-57`).

  b. **No rules on the column?** Pass. The short-circuit is
     `transitionRules?.enabled === false` **and** no option is `isDisabled` or condition-gated
     (`:59-68`) — a rule-free board pays one map lookup per edit.

  c. **Clearing is always legal.** `optionIds: []` is never gated; only *arriving* somewhere is
     (`:77-78`).

  d. **Gate 1 — `option.isDisabled`.** Refusal reason `disabled`, explanation
     `Turned off in column settings`.

  e. **Gate 2 — `availability`.** The option's `ConditionGroup` is evaluated against **the record as
     it will be after this batch's earlier edits**, using `evaluateConditionGroup`
     (`src/lib/conditions.ts:258-273`). Semantics that must be reproduced exactly:
     an **empty group is satisfied** ("no conditions means no gate"); a condition pointing at a
     **deleted column returns `true`** — ignored, not failed closed (`:189-198`); dates compare
     calendar days; identity cells match the stored id first, then the rendered label. Explanation:
     `` `Requires ${describeConditionGroup(...)}` `` — e.g.
     `Requires Blocked by is empty` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:118-124` ships exactly this rule on
     the Task template's "Done").

  f. **Gate 3 — transition rules.** `evaluateTransition(column, fromKey, toKey)`
     (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:102-133`). `fromKey` is the record's **first current option id**,
     or `"__empty__"` (`currentKey`, `src/lib/select-availability.ts:55-62`). It returns *allowed*
     when **any** of: rules are off; `from === to`; **either end is ungoverned**
     (`Object.hasOwn(transitions, key)` is false — this is what makes adding a status safe); or
     `transitions[from]` includes `to`. Otherwise the refusal message names both ends and the way
     out: `` `Status cannot go straight from Debug to Done. Debug can move to Review, Blocked.` ``

  g. A refused edit **is not written**. In a single-cell call the whole call is
     `409` / `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` (or `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` for gates 1 and 2) with the
     explanation as `message`. In a batch, the refused edits are reported and the rest still apply —
     which is what the client already does for bulk (`src/store/board-store.ts:569-587`): "Refusing
     the whole batch because one record cannot make the move would be worse than telling the user
     which ones could not." **RECOMMENDATION:** the batch form returns `200` with the refusals in
     `conflicts` alongside the stale-write notices, each carrying the rule's own sentence; the
     frontend renders `ConflictNotice.message` verbatim and needs no new shape
     (`src/components/board/conflict-notices.tsx`).

**7. Write.** Per row, once: `cells = cells || $merged`, `revision = revision + 1`,
`updated_at = now()`, plus the four indexed projections recomputed. Then the relation and attachment
projections for the columns this call touched.

**8. Activity log.** One `row_activity` entry per row, whatever the number of cells
(`src/services/board-service.ts:524-532`), with `changes` **already rendered to text**:

```ts
interface FieldChange {
  readonly columnName: string;
  readonly from: string;      // cellText of the old value
  readonly to: string;        // cellText of the new value
}
```
Cells whose text projection did not change are dropped from `changes` entirely
(`describeEdits`, `:209-216`). The summary is `changed Status` for one field,
`changed 3 fields` for more, and `updated TASK-042` when nothing rendered differently
(`editSummary`, `:221-225`). Canon §8.8 OQ-51: store **both** the rendered `changes` (returned) and
an internal `raw_changes` (never returned).

**9. Realtime.** One `row.updated` (RT-07) per changed row, or one batched frame carrying `rowIds`.
Ids and `revision` only — no cell content ever crosses a permission boundary in a frame (canon §7.2,
following the RT-05 precedent).

**10. Response.** `200` with the authoritative rows and the notices. The store replaces its
optimistic state from `rows` and appends `conflicts` (`src/store/board-store.ts:350-353`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `SELECT` — steps 2–4. |
| `board_columns` | `SELECT` — needed for the rule gate, the text projection and the value validation. |
| `board_rows` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` (step 5) → `UPDATE cells, revision, updated_at, due_date, due_at, status_option_id, assignee_ids, search_tsv` (step 7). |
| `board_row_relations` | `DELETE … WHERE source_row_id = $r AND source_column_id = $c` then `INSERT` the new target list, for each relation cell written (§17.3). |
| `cell_attachments` | `INSERT` / `DELETE` to match the new attachment list, for each attachment cell written. |
| `row_activity` | `INSERT` — one row per changed record. |
| `notifications`, `watches` | Out of scope here; the collaboration chapter owns whether a cell write notifies watchers (canon OQ-88). |

**Transaction** — **Required, one transaction for the whole batch.** Rows, relation projection,
attachment links and activity entries land together. The rule gate runs **inside** the transaction,
after `FOR UPDATE`, because it reads the current option — running it before the lock would let two
concurrent drags both pass a rule only one of them may.

**Realtime** — `row.updated` (RT-07) per changed row.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `edits` empty, or a `columnId` not on this board. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` — the `CellValue` tag is not a `ColumnType` member. |
| 400 | `validation` | `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` — not `YYYY-MM-DD` for a date-only column, not ISO 8601 for a timestamp column (OQ-32). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.update`. Copy is name-free (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-163`). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_LOCKED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` — an archived record is read-only until restored. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` — gate 3. Single-edit calls only; batches report it. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` — gates 1 and 2. Same rule. |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` — past the batch cap. |
| — | — | **`CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` is never returned by this endpoint.** |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/board-store.ts:315-354` (`editCells`) is the only caller, and
everything funnels through it: `src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx:74` (grid cells),
`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:58,111-114` (drawer fields),
`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:67-95` (drag),
`src/components/board/views/calendar-board.tsx` (day drop),
`src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx` (bar drag),
`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:57,67-81` (the completion checkbox),
`src/hooks/use-grid-clipboard.ts` (paste, cut and Delete) and
`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts`. Plus `src/hooks/use-embedded-board.ts:120-124`, which writes
straight back to the source board from inside a document.

### 15.6 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/update` — write the same values across a selection

**Purpose** — Write one set of values to many records in **one request, never a loop**
(PRD `SY-BLK-34`: 100 records in under 1.5 s).

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.update` on `boards.node_id`.

**Path Params** — `boardId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-074. */
interface BulkUpdateRowsRequest {
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];
  /** One value per column, written to every record the action may touch. */
  readonly values: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
}
```

**Response**

```ts
interface BulkSkip {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;   // the rowId itself when the record was not found
  readonly reason: BulkSkipReason;
}
type BulkSkipReason = "archived" | "not_found" | "permission_denied";

interface BulkResult {
  readonly requested: number;
  /** Authoritative records for the ids that changed. */
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly applied: readonly string[];
  readonly skipped: readonly BulkSkip[];
}
```

`src/types/system.ts:15-50`. **The invariant is `requested === applied.length + skipped.length`** —
"a bulk write that silently drops a record is worse than one that refuses"
(`src/services/board-service.ts:958-965`). Canon §6.2 forbids returning an error body for a partial
success: this is a `200`.

`permission_denied` is added to `BulkSkipReason` per canon §2.7 — `src/types/system.ts:29-32` says
permission skips "report through this same channel", so they are a reason, not a parallel array.

**Partitioning — EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (`partitionBulkTargets`, `src/lib/bulk.ts:30-55`):
a missing id → `{reason:"not_found", displayId: rowId}`; an **archived** row → `{reason:"archived"}`
unless the call is one of the two that may target archived rows. `bulkUpdate` **skips** archived
rows.

**The record rules apply to a hundred records exactly as to one.** `src/store/board-store.ts:558-564`:
"a bulk status change is still a status change, so the selection is split into the records the rules
permit and the ones they do not before anything is written." The server runs step 6 of §15.5.2 per
row; refused rows land in `skipped` with `reason: "permission_denied"` and the rule's sentence.

**Database** — as §15.5 step 7–8, over the partitioned target set. One `row_activity` entry per
record, with the rendered `FieldChange`s (`src/services/board-service.ts:991-992`).

**Transaction** — **Required, one transaction per call** (`docs/BOARD.md:330-334`;
board.md R-10). Documented maximum: **500 rows** per bulk call, `413` beyond it.

**Realtime** — `row.updated` (RT-07), one batched frame carrying `rowIds`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `rowIds` empty, `values` names an unknown column. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` / `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.update`. A **whole-call** refusal; per-row refusals are skips. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-bulk-actions.ts:67` (the status and assignee actions, which
resolve their target columns by **role** — `lensesFor(board)`, `src/lib/my-work.ts:22-67` — because a
selection may span templates) → `src/store/board-store.ts:565-598`, rendered by
`src/components/board/bulk/bulk-action-bar.tsx`.

### 15.7 `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/position` — move a record

**Purpose** — Reposition one record in the board's canonical order.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.move` on `boards.node_id` (Member and above,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:25`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-073. Exactly one of the two anchors is given. */
interface SetRowPositionRequest {
  /** Place directly after this record. null = the very front of the board. */
  readonly afterRowId?: string | null;
  /** Place directly before this record. */
  readonly beforeRowId?: string;
}
```

Anchors, not an index — for the same reason as §14.3: an index is a claim about a list the caller
does not own, and rows are inserted mid-order routinely.

**Response** — `BoardRow` — with its new `position` reflected in the board's order and `revision`
bumped.

**Database** — `board_rows` `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the moved row and its two new neighbours →
`UPDATE position = midpoint, revision = revision + 1, updated_at = now()`. A renumbering pass over
the board when the gap is exhausted. `row_activity` `INSERT` with `kind: "moved"`.

**Transaction** — **Required** (the midpoint read and the write).
**Realtime** — `row.updated` (RT-07).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — both anchors given, or neither. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.move`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` — the row or an anchor. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` |

**Frontend Used By** — **RECOMMENDATION.** Nothing calls it. `rowOrder` is "the array the server
sent" (`docs/BOARD.md:355-358`) and the grid offers no row drag.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-34)** — how are records ordered with no sort applied, and is manual reordering
> required?
> **Evidence** — `rowOrder` is documented as "canonical server order"
> (`src/store/board-store.ts:69`, `docs/BOARD.md:26`), and an order already carries meaning: a create
> files itself after `afterRowId` (`src/services/board-service.ts:322-324`) and a subtask after its
> parent's **last descendant** (`lastDescendantOf`, `:342-352`). `docs/BOARD.md:302-305` asks for "an
> explicit order key (fractional index / LexoRank) and `PATCH /rows/:id/position`". No component
> offers a row drag.
> **Recommendation** — canon has taken the position: `board_rows.position NUMERIC` fractional index,
> defaulted on insert, with this endpoint reserved. It costs one column now and is a full-table
> rewrite later.
> **Impact if wrong** — without an order key two concurrent inserts race for the same slot and the
> board's order differs per client, which then makes `SY-BLK-34`'s shift-click range selection select
> **different records for different people** (`extendRowSelection`,
> `src/store/grid-store.ts:204-222`).

---

### 15.8 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/archive` — archive and restore

**Purpose** — Freeze or unfreeze records. **This is the archive endpoint and the restore endpoint**;
`isArchived` selects the direction, and there is no single-record variant.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.archive` on `boards.node_id` (Manager and above,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:56`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-075. */
interface BulkArchiveRowsRequest {
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];
  /** true = archive, false = restore. */
  readonly isArchived: boolean;
}
```

**Response** — `BulkResult`.

**Contract — EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (`src/services/board-service.ts:1002-1047`):

- **This is the one call that may target archived records.** `partitionBulkTargets(…,
  { allowArchived: true })` (`:1015-1017`) — restoring is the write a frozen record must still
  accept.
- Sets `archived_at = now()` or `NULL`, and bumps `revision` either way.
- **A no-op re-archive is honoured but not logged twice**: the `row_activity` entry is written only
  when `wasArchived !== isArchived` (`:1036-1043`).
- Archived means **frozen, not hidden**: content stays readable, still commentable
  (`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:265` — "Commenting is not editing: a frozen record
  still takes one"), and every write path is closed
  (`src/lib/archive.ts:5-11`; PRD `SY-ARC-37`).

**A single-record archive goes through this endpoint too.** Both single-row surfaces call
`bulkArchive([row.id], !isArchived)` — the drawer footer
(`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:62,290-297`) and the row actions menu
(`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:34,89-90`). No `PUT /rows/{rowId}/archive` exists
and none is needed.

**Database** — `board_rows` `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` → `UPDATE archived_at, revision, updated_at`.
`row_activity` `INSERT` with `kind: "archived"` / `"restored"`, summary `archived this record` /
`restored this record`. `nodes` `UPDATE` the `itemCount` / `openCount` projections (archived records
are excluded from both).

**Transaction** — **Required**, one per call. Cap 500 rows.
**Realtime** — `row.archived` (RT-08), `{ boardId, rowId, revision, isArchived }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `rowIds` empty. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.archive`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` — an archived **board** refuses even this. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-bulk-actions.ts` (the bulk bar's Archive / Restore),
