`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:292-300`,
`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:89-90` — all through
`src/store/board-store.ts:600-613`.

---

### 15.9 `DELETE /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` — delete one record

**Purpose** — Remove one record permanently. **Records have no trash of their own.**

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.delete` on `boards.node_id` (Manager and above,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:57`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`.
**Query Params** — None.
**Request Body** — None.

**Response**

```ts
/** E-065. */
interface DeleteRowResponse {
  readonly deletedRowId: string;
  /**
   * The deleted record's children, lifted to the top level and returned so the
   * client reconciles rather than guesses. Empty when it had none.
   */
  readonly detachedRows: readonly BoardRow[];
}
```

**Children are lifted, never cascade-deleted — EXISTING REQUIREMENT.**
`detachOrphans` sets `parentRowId: null` and bumps `revision` on every child of a removed row
(`src/services/board-service.ts:460-470`): "Deleting a container must not silently delete work nobody
asked about — the subtasks stay, addressable, as records of their own." The client mirror is
`detachChildren` (`src/lib/board-records.ts:158-180`). The database half is
`parent_row_id … ON DELETE SET NULL`; the service still returns the affected rows because their
`revision` changed and the client's copy is now stale.

Permanent is said at the call site, in the confirm copy: "Records are removed outright — the Trash
holds files, pages and boards, not rows. This cannot be undone."
(`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:326`). Canon reserves **OQ-15** for whether the
asymmetry with node deletion is intended.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_rows` | `DELETE … WHERE id = $1 AND board_id = $2`. Children's `parent_row_id` set to `NULL` by the FK; the service additionally bumps their `revision` and `updated_at`. |
| `row_activity` | `DELETE … WHERE row_id = $1` — the record's history goes with it (`src/services/board-service.ts:1066` does this for the bulk path). |
| `board_row_relations` | `DELETE` — both `source_row_id = $1` (its outbound links) and `target_row_id = $1` (the inbound projection) by `ON DELETE CASCADE`. |
| `board_rows` (other) | **`cells` is NOT rewritten.** Rows on this or another board that pointed at the deleted record **keep the dangling id** in their relation cell, so `[Deleted Item]` keeps rendering and history stays honest (canon §8.8 OQ-44; `src/lib/cell-values.ts:22,117-122`). |
| `cell_attachments` | `DELETE … WHERE row_id = $1` — cascade. The `file_assets` rows survive until orphan collection; `workspaces.used_bytes` is decremented in the same transaction for assets that lost their last reference. |
| `comments` | Comments whose target is this row: out of scope here (the collaboration chapter owns it; canon OQ-87 covers watch pruning). |
| `nodes` | `UPDATE` the `itemCount` / `openCount` projections. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** Row, activity, relation projection, attachment links, child
detachment and the quota decrement are one write.

**Realtime** — `row.deleted` (RT-09), `{ boardId, rowIds: [rowId] }`, **plus** `row.updated` (RT-07)
for each detached child, whose `revision` moved.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.delete`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` / `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |

Note there is **no** `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` here: "archiving freezes edits, not removal — a frozen
record can still be binned" (`src/services/board-service.ts:1058`).

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:33` and
`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:60,299-306` → `src/store/board-store.ts:433-453`.

---

### 15.10 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/delete` — delete many records

**Purpose** — Remove a selection permanently, in one request.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.delete` on `boards.node_id`.

**Path Params** — `boardId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-076. The shared shape for the bulk calls that need only ids. */
interface BulkDeleteRowsRequest {
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];
}
```

**Response** — `BulkResult` with **`rows: []`** and the deleted ids in `applied`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:1069`) — there are no authoritative records to return, and the client
uses `applied` to drop them (`removeRows`, `src/store/board-store.ts:625`).

**Contract** — may target **archived** rows (`allowArchived: true`, `:1059-1061`). Children of every
deleted parent are lifted to the top level, exactly as §15.9.

**Database** — as §15.9, over the target set; one `DELETE` per table rather than per row.
**Transaction** — **Required**, one per call. Cap 500 rows.
**Realtime** — `row.deleted` (RT-09), one frame carrying every id, plus `row.updated` for detached
children.

**Possible Errors** — as §15.9, plus `VALIDATION_FAILED` for an empty `rowIds` and
`REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` past the cap.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-bulk-actions.ts` → `src/store/board-store.ts:615-628`,
behind the same confirm copy as the single delete.

---

### 15.11 `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/move` — move records to another board

**Purpose** — Move a selection onto a different board, converting every cell into the destination's
schema.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.delete` on the **source** board's node **and** `row.create` on the
**target** board's node (canon E-077, OQ-17). Records leave one board and are created on the other;
gating only one of them is the critical defect canon OQ-17 records — the mock gates **neither**
(`src/services/board-service.ts:1088-1104`).

**Path Params** — `boardId` (the source).
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-077. */
interface BulkMoveRowsRequest {
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];
  /** Drive node of the destination board — a node id, not a board id. */
  readonly targetNodeId: string;
}
```

The frontend picks a **node** id, not a board id
(`src/components/board/bulk/bulk-move-dialog.tsx:77` — `setTargetId(board.nodeId)`), because that is
what the permission chain is keyed by.

**Response**

```ts
interface BulkMoveResult extends BulkResult {
  readonly targetBoardId: string;
  readonly targetNodeId: string;
  /** Source columns the target has no counterpart for, by name. */
  readonly droppedColumns: readonly string[];
}
```

**The two halves land in two different places** (`src/store/board-store.ts:630-657`):
`applied` carries the **source** ids the client must forget; `rows` carries the records' **new**
identities on the destination.

**Contract — EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (`src/services/board-service.ts:1080-1168`):

- A move to the **same board** is refused: `409` / `BULK_TARGET_BOARD_SAME`, message
  `Those records are already on that board` (`:1097-1099`).
- `targetNodeId` that is not a board is `409` / `BULK_TARGET_NOT_A_BOARD` — the mock does not check
  this (canon OQ-17).
- **Columns are paired by normalised name**: lower-cased with every non-alphanumeric stripped
  (`normalizeName`, `:1077-1078`). `Due date` on the source pairs with `due-date` on the target.
- **Every cell travels through `convertCell`** into the destination column's type, so the
  preserve-as-`text` rule of §14.5 applies unchanged (`:1130`).
- **Source columns with no counterpart are named in `droppedColumns`**, never dropped silently
  (`:1114-1116`). The dialog says so up front: "Columns are matched by name. Anything the destination
  has no column for is reported before it is dropped."
  (`src/components/board/bulk/bulk-move-dialog.tsx:52-55`).
- **The destination assigns its own record ids** from its own counter; the source `displayId` is not
  carried (`:1133-1137`). `createdAt` and `createdBy` are carried over; `updatedAt` is now and
  `revision` restarts at `1` (`:1140-1143`).
- The source rows **and their activity** are deleted (`:1151-1156`).
- Archived rows are **skipped** (the default partition).

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-40)** — how do select values migrate across boards?
> **Evidence** — `convertCell` on a `select → select` pair takes the same-type short-circuit and
> returns the value **untouched** (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:91`), so the moved record keeps the
> **source board's option ids**, which mean nothing on the destination: `cellText` finds no label and
> falls back to `value.text ?? ""` (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:93-99`), rendering an empty Status.
> **Recommendation** — when both columns are `select`, re-map by **label** (trimmed, case-folded)
> against the destination's options, and preserve the source label as `text` when no option matches —
> the same shape `parseTextIntoCell` already produces for an unmatched label
> (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:40-48`). Report the count in `droppedColumns`' sibling field rather
> than silently blanking a status.
> **Impact if wrong** — a 100-record move onto a board with the same status names silently blanks
> every Status cell, and the bulk result reports full success.

**Database** — one transaction spanning **both** boards:

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `boards` (target) | `UPDATE next_sequence = next_sequence + $n … RETURNING` — one allocation for the batch. |
| `board_rows` (target) | `INSERT` one per moved record, converted `cells`, new `custom_id`, `position` appended, `revision = 1`. |
| `board_rows` (source) | `DELETE` the moved records; children left behind are detached (`parent_row_id` → `NULL`). **`parentRowId` is not carried across** — the mock's `moved` row omits it entirely (`:1134-1144`), so a moved subtask arrives at the top level of the destination. |
| `row_activity` (source) | `DELETE` for the moved ids. |
| `row_activity` (target) | `INSERT` — `kind: "moved"`, summary `moved TASK-042 from Frontend Sprint` (`:1148`). |
| `board_row_relations` | `DELETE` the source projections; `INSERT` new ones for relation cells whose target still resolves. A relation pointing at a record left behind on the source board keeps its dangling id in the cell. |
| `cell_attachments` | `UPDATE row_id` to the new record — the asset does not move, only its reference. |
| `nodes` (both) | `UPDATE` the `itemCount` / `openCount` projections. |
| `audit_events` | `INSERT` — one row for the operation, naming both boards. |

**Transaction** — **Required, one transaction over both boards.** Half a move is records existing
twice or not at all.

**Realtime** — `row.deleted` (RT-09) on the **source** board's channel and `row.created` (RT-06) on
the **target's**.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `rowIds` empty. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.delete` on the source **or** `row.create` on the target. The refusal does not say which (canon §4.4 rule 3). |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — source; `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — target, or one the caller may not see. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BULK_TARGET_BOARD_SAME` — `Those records are already on that board`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BULK_TARGET_NOT_A_BOARD` — `targetNodeId` does not address a board. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — the destination would exceed the ceiling (OQ-36). |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/bulk/bulk-move-dialog.tsx` →
`src/hooks/use-bulk-actions.ts` → `src/store/board-store.ts:635-657`.

---

### 15.12 `row_activity` — T-14, the table these endpoints write

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TABLE row_activity (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  row_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES board_rows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  board_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  kind        activity_kind NOT NULL,     -- created|updated|commented|attached|archived|restored|imported|moved
  actor_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  summary     text NOT NULL,              -- 'changed Status', 'created TASK-001'
  changes     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,   -- FieldChange[] — RETURNED
  raw_changes jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,   -- before/after CellValue — NEVER returned (OQ-51)
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX row_activity_row_idx ON row_activity (row_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);
```

```ts
/** row_activity.changes — already rendered to the text the column displays. */
interface FieldChange {
  readonly columnName: string;
  readonly from: string;
  readonly to: string;
}
/** row_activity.raw_changes — internal. RECOMMENDATION, canon §8.8 OQ-51. */
interface RawFieldChange {
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly from: CellValue | null;
  readonly to: CellValue | null;
}
```

**One entry per write, however many fields it touched** (PRD `SY-ACT-40`;
`src/services/board-service.ts:157-163`). The timeline "reads these — it never sees, and never
renders, a raw payload" (`src/types/board.ts:479-482`), which is why `changes` is stored rendered:
a column renamed after the fact must not rewrite what the history says happened.

**Cardinality.** `board_rows` 1:N `row_activity`, unbounded — canon **OQ-52** covers retention and
paging. **Delete behaviour.** `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both FKs; the service also deletes explicitly on
bulk delete and bulk move (`:1066`, `:1156`) so the source board's history does not follow a moved
record.

`ActivityKind` = `created | updated | commented | attached | archived | restored | imported | moved`
(`src/types/board.ts:469-477`). `commented` and `attached` are written by the collaboration and files
chapters through the same table (`noteActivity`, `src/services/board-service.ts:911-918`), which is
why `row_activity` carries `board_id` as well as `row_id`: a writer outside this module has the
`EntityRef` (`{ kind:"row", boardId, rowId }`) and not the board lookup.

Read through `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/activity` (E-070), cursor-paginated on
`(created_at DESC, id DESC)`, consumed by `src/hooks/use-row-activity.ts:19-32` and rendered by
`src/components/board/drawer/activity-timeline.tsx`.

---

## 16. Subtask APIs

### 16.0 A subtask is an ordinary board row with a `parent_row_id`

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** There is no subtask table, no subtask type and no nested array.

> "A subtask is a full board record — its own display id, status, assignee, attachments, comments and
> history — so the parent stores a pointer, never a nested copy."
> — `src/types/board.ts:257-263`

> "Everything here works on `parentRowId` alone — no nested arrays, no second copy of a record… TASK-001 containing TASK-002 is containment."
> — `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:6-18`

Storage is one nullable self-referential FK on `board_rows` (§13.1):

```sql
parent_row_id uuid REFERENCES board_rows(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
CREATE INDEX board_rows_parent_idx ON board_rows (parent_row_id);
```

**Cardinality.** `board_rows` 1:N `board_rows`. A parent has 0..N direct children; a child has 0..1
parent. Same board only (§16.4). **Delete behaviour.** `ON DELETE SET NULL` — children are lifted to
the top level, never cascade-deleted (§15.9).

#### 16.0.1 EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN: serialising subtasks into the parent row

No endpoint in this specification may accept or return a nested `subtasks: BoardRow[]` array on a
`BoardRow`, and `board_rows.cells` may never hold a child's data. This is not a style preference;
five shipped behaviours depend on the pointer model:

| Behaviour | Why nesting breaks it | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A subtask has its own drawer, comments, attachments and activity | A nested object is not addressable — `openDrawer(row.id)` opens *its* drawer, with its own comment thread and its own `row_activity` | `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:32-38`, `:146` |
| A subtask has its own `TASK-00n` from the same counter | A nested value has no `sequence`, so it cannot participate in `UNIQUE (board_id, sequence)` | `src/services/board-service.ts:304-310` |
| Ticking a subtask in the drawer updates the table row, and vice versa, with no synchronisation code | Both read the same normalised record; a nested copy is a second source of truth that must be kept in step | `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:34-38` |
| A view can show subtasks `nested`, `flat` or `hidden` — **per view** | `flat` means "every record is a top-level row", which is only expressible if a subtask *is* a row | `src/types/board.ts:373-378`; `layoutHierarchy`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:244-284` |
| Deleting a parent keeps its children | A nested array would delete them with the parent, which the code refuses to do | `src/services/board-service.ts:460-470` |

A parent's `revision` is **not** bumped when a child changes. The only writes a parent takes because
of its children are the `added subtask X` activity entry at creation
(`src/services/board-service.ts:334-336`) and nothing else — progress is computed on read
(`subtaskProgress`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:182-199`), never stored.

#### 16.0.2 Completion and progress — configuration, not inference

Read-only, computed by the client from data it already holds; documented here because a server-side
`openCount` (§13.2) uses the same rule:

- The completion column is **the first `select` column that declares any `completedOptionIds`**
  (`completionColumnOf`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:139-147`). Nothing reads a label, so renaming
  "Done" to "Shipped" changes nothing.
- `isRowCompleted` = any of the row's `optionIds` is in that set (`:149-160`).
- Progress counts **direct children only** and returns `{total, completed, ratio, percent,
  isMeasurable}`; `isMeasurable` is false when no column declares completed options, and the bar is
  hidden (`:162-199`).
- **Completing every subtask deliberately does not complete the parent** — "that would be an
  automation rule, and no such rule has been configured; the progress bar reports, it does not act"
  (`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:40-42`). **No endpoint may write the parent as a
  side effect of a child's status change.**

Canon **OQ-49** covers the competing definition of "done" (`completedOptionIds` vs the hard-coded
English label table); canon's position is to prefer `completedOptionIds` where configured.

---

### 16.1 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/subtasks` — a parent's children

**Purpose** — One record's **direct** children, in board order.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on `boards.node_id`. A subtask carries no access of its own: the whole
board is one permission surface (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:108-113` resolves a board node's
edit key to `row.update`; there is no row-level permission — canon `docs/BOARD.md:344` lists
field- and row-level permissions as a future module).

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeArchived` | `boolean` | `false` | Same rule as every other record read. |
| `depth` | `int 1..5` | `1` | `1` = direct children (what the frontend shows). Greater values return the subtree, depth-first in board order. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `readonly BoardRow[]`, ordered by `position` ascending. Ordinary rows; nothing is
nested. Depth is expressed by `parentRowId`, which the client indexes itself
(`buildHierarchy`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:49-69`).

**Database** — `boards` `SELECT` (visibility) → `board_rows` `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 AND
parent_row_id = $2 [AND archived_at IS NULL] ORDER BY position, id`, served by
`board_rows_parent_idx`. For `depth > 1`, one recursive CTE bounded by the depth cap.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `depth` out of range. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` / `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/services/board-service.ts:414-431` (`listSubtasks`), described there as
"the seam the real `GET /boards/:id/rows/:rowId/subtasks` replaces". The drawer's subtask panel does
**not** call it — it derives children from the record set it already holds
(`src/hooks/use-subtasks.ts:42-72`), which is exactly why "editing a subtask anywhere updates every
one of them on the next frame". The endpoint exists for the surfaces that do not hold the board:
row-level deep links, notifications, and any client paging a 5 000-row board.

---

### 16.2 Creating a subtask — `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows` with `parentRowId`

**Purpose** — Create a record under a parent. **There is no separate endpoint**: a subtask is
created by the ordinary row-create call with `parentRowId` set (§15.3), so nothing downstream has to
special-case it (`src/services/board-service.ts:283-287`).

Everything in §15.3 applies unchanged — the atomic counter, the dense empty cells, the permission
key (`row.create`). Four behaviours are specific to the parent branch:

| Behaviour | Rule | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent must exist | `404` / `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND`, message `That parent record could not be found` | `src/services/board-service.ts:302` |
| Placement | The child is filed **directly after its parent's last descendant** in board order, so "the board's own order already reads as the tree even before a view nests it". `parentRowId` overrides `afterRowId`. | `:320-324`, `lastDescendantOf` `:342-352` |
| Two activity entries | `created TASK-042 under TASK-041` on the **child** (`kind: "created"`) and `added subtask TASK-042` on the **parent** (`kind: "updated"`) — one write, two records' histories | `:327-336` |
| Depth | Refused with `409` / `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` when the parent already sits at the cap (§16.4) | canon §4.3, OQ-33 |

The composer pre-fills title, status, assignee and a deadline by finding the **first** column of each
type (`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-composer.tsx:56-58`) and offers only statuses the
availability rules permit, with `ignoreTransitions: true` because no record exists yet to transition
*from* (`:60-73`). The server must gate an initial `select` value on `isDisabled` and `availability`
for the same reason, and must **not** run the transition gate on a create.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:55,197-201` (the composer) and
`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:35,59-71` ("Add subtask", which then opens the new
record's own drawer), through `src/store/board-store.ts:464-515` (`createSubtask`).

---

### 16.3 `PUT /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/parent` — reparent or promote

**Purpose** — Move a record under a new parent, or lift it back to the top level. `PUT` because it
replaces one value idempotently (canon P-07).

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — `row.move` on `boards.node_id` (Member and above,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:25`; the UI gates the promote item on exactly this key —
`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:75`).

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`.
**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
/** E-067. */
interface SetRowParentRequest {
  /** null promotes the record to the top level. */
  readonly parentRowId: string | null;
}
```

`parentRowId` is **nullable, not optional** (C-08): `null` is the promote operation, and a missing
key is a malformed request.

**Response** — `BoardRow` — the authoritative record, `revision` bumped
(`src/services/board-service.ts:394-399`).

#### The four refusals

| Condition | Reason | HTTP | Message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parentRowId === rowId` | `ROW_PARENT_SELF` | 409 | `A record cannot be its own parent` (`src/services/board-service.ts:384`) |
| The proposed parent is already a **descendant** of this record | `ROW_PARENT_CYCLE` | 409 | `` `${parent.displayId} is already under ${row.displayId}` `` (`:389-391`) |
| The proposed parent is on a **different board** | `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD` | 409 | Parent and child must share a board (OQ-33) |
| The move would push the subtree past the depth cap | `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` | 409 | (OQ-33) |

**The cycle guard is the last line, not the first.** The client checks too
(`wouldCreateCycle`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:118-127`, called before the optimistic write at
`src/store/board-store.ts:529-532`), and the service comment says why the server must repeat it:
"The cycle guard lives here as well as in the client: a hierarchy that loops would hang every reader,
and the backend is the last place that can refuse" (`src/services/board-service.ts:367-372`).

Server-side detection is a recursive CTE, evaluated inside the write transaction after
`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on both rows:

```sql
-- documentation only: is $newParent already inside $row's subtree?
WITH RECURSIVE up AS (
  SELECT id, parent_row_id, 1 AS depth FROM board_rows WHERE id = $newParent
  UNION ALL
  SELECT r.id, r.parent_row_id, up.depth + 1
    FROM board_rows r JOIN up ON r.id = up.parent_row_id
   WHERE up.depth < 64                       -- hard stop; corrupt data must not spin
)
SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM up WHERE id = $row) AS would_cycle,
       max(depth)                            AS ancestor_depth
  FROM up;
```

The `depth < 64` bound mirrors the client's `seen`-guards, which exist for the same reason: "cycle-safe
… so a cyclic write can never hang a render" (`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:80-110`). The same query
yields `ancestor_depth`, which the depth check reads.

**A no-op is success, not an error.** `(row.parentRowId ?? null) === parentRowId` returns early with
`true` in the store (`src/store/board-store.ts:527`); the API returns `200` and the unchanged row
without bumping `revision`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `board_rows` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the row and the proposed parent; the recursive CTE above; then `UPDATE parent_row_id, revision = revision + 1, updated_at = now()`. |
| `board_rows` | `UPDATE position` — **RECOMMENDATION**: re-file the record after its new parent's last descendant, matching the create rule (§16.2). Without it a nested view shows a child that sits far from its parent in board order. The mock does not do this (`setRowParent` only writes the pointer), which is visible today as a subtask that keeps its old row position. |
| `row_activity` | `INSERT` — `kind: "moved"`, summary `moved under TASK-041` or `moved to the top level` (`src/services/board-service.ts:403-409`). |
| `board_row_relations` | Untouched. **Containment is not a relation** and never writes one (`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:14-18`). |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The cycle check must read the same snapshot the write commits
against, or two concurrent reparents can each pass the check and together close a loop.

**Realtime** — `row.updated` (RT-07), `{ boardId, rowId, revision }`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `parentRowId` key missing. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — needs `row.move`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `ROW_NOT_FOUND` / `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_PARENT_SELF` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_PARENT_CYCLE` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` — an archived record accepts only archive/restore. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:56,183-190` (the Unlink button,
titled "Move to the top level — the record itself is kept") and
`src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:36,73-81` ("Move to the top level"), through
`src/store/board-store.ts:523-554`.

---

### 16.4 Depth, cross-board parents and the archive cascade

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-33)** — what bounds the subtask hierarchy?
>
> **What is unclear.** The frontend bounds **nothing** except cycles. Depth, cross-board parents and
> what archiving or deleting a parent does to its subtree are all unstated, and two of them are
> stated as *deliberate* non-limits.
>
> **Evidence.**
> - **Depth is explicitly unbounded.** `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:6-12`: "no nested arrays, no
>   second copy of a record, and **no depth limit**. `TASK-002` can own `TASK-006` the day someone
>   needs it, and every helper below already walks that far."
>   `src/types/board.ts:259-262`: "Nothing here caps the depth: a subtask may itself be a parent, and
>   the hierarchy helpers walk as far as the data goes." `SubtaskEntry.childCount` is documented as
>   "the hierarchy is not depth-capped" (`src/hooks/use-subtasks.ts:18-19`), and `layoutHierarchy`
>   recurses until the data stops (`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:265-275`).
> - **Cross-board parents are impossible by construction, and nowhere refused.**
>   `setRowParent(boardId, rowId, parentRowId)` looks the parent up in the *same* `BoardRecord`
>   (`src/services/board-service.ts:386-388`), so a cross-board id reads as `notFound`. No rule says
>   it should not be allowed — it simply never comes up.
> - **Archiving a parent does not cascade.** `bulkArchive` writes `archived_at` on exactly the ids it
>   was given (`src/services/board-service.ts:1022-1031`); children are untouched and stay visible.
> - **Deleting a parent does not cascade** — children are lifted (`detachOrphans`, `:460-470`). This
>   one **is** settled; it is stated as a rule and mirrored on the client.
> - An orphan whose parent is missing is treated as a **root** rather than disappearing
>   (`buildHierarchy`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:49-69`), and in a nested view a child whose parent
>   was filtered out is **promoted to the top level** rather than vanishing (`:239-242`, `:277-283`).
>
> **Recommendation** — canon has already taken the position (§8.8, OQ-33) and this chapter implements
> it: **same board; depth cap 5; cycles rejected by a recursive CTE; archiving a parent does not
> cascade; deleting a parent lifts its children.** The depth cap is the only one of the four that
> contradicts a frontend comment, and it is worth the contradiction: an unbounded hierarchy makes the
> "last descendant" insert rule (§16.2) an unbounded walk on every create, makes a nested layout an
> unbounded recursion on every render, and makes `GET …/subtasks?depth=` unanswerable. Five levels is
> more than any of the four shipped templates suggests and is enforced at the two write points
> (`POST /rows` with `parentRowId`, `PUT /rows/{rowId}/parent`) rather than on read, so existing data
> can never become unreadable.
>
> **Impact if wrong** — too low a cap refuses a legitimate breakdown and there is no migration back
> from data that was never allowed to exist; too high (or none) and one malformed import can produce
> a 10 000-deep chain that times out every board read. Allowing cross-board parents would be worse
> than either: `lastDescendantOf`, `layoutHierarchy` and `subtaskProgress` all operate over one
> board's record map and would silently drop the half of the tree they cannot see, while
> `parent_row_id`'s `ON DELETE SET NULL` would let a delete on board A silently restructure board B.

**How the cap is enforced.** On both write paths, inside the transaction, the recursive CTE of §16.3
returns `ancestor_depth` for the proposed parent and a second CTE returns the moved record's own
subtree height. `ancestor_depth + subtree_height > 5` → `409` / `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP`. Enforcing on
the **sum** is what stops a legal-looking single move from burying a deep subtree.

**Cross-board is enforced by the query, not by a check**: every subtask read and write is scoped
`WHERE board_id = $boardId`, so a `parentRowId` from another board resolves to nothing and answers
`PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND`. `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD` is returned only when the id *does* resolve on
another board and the caller can see it — the more useful message.

---

## 17. Relation and Blocked-By APIs

### 17.0 A relation is a cell, not an edge

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT, and the single most important thing in this section.**

- A relation **column** declares its target board: `RelationConfig { boardId, displayColumnId,
  isMulti }` (`src/types/board.ts:152-160`).
- A relation **cell** stores target **row ids**, in order:
  `{ kind: "relation", rowIds: string[], text?: string }` (`src/types/board.ts:230`).
- "Blocked by" is **a relation column named "Blocked by"**, shipped by the `task` template
  (`col_blocks`, `src/lib/board-templates.ts:188`). `bug` and `apiDocs` ship `col_task`
  "Related task"; `qa` ships `col_bug` "Related bug".
- **Containment is not relation.** "TASK-003 blocked by TASK-002 is a dependency, TASK-001 containing
  TASK-002 is containment. The two live side by side and never read each other's data"
  (`src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:14-18`, restated for the Gantt at `src/lib/board-gantt.ts:29-32`).

Consequently **there is no "create relation" endpoint and no "delete relation" endpoint.**
Creating a link is a cell write (E-066) that adds a row id to `rowIds`; deleting one is a cell write
that removes it. Everything in §15.5 — the permission chain, the conflict policy, the activity
entry — applies unchanged.

**Canon forbids inventing a typed edge.** §2.9: "`RelationType` — reserved and deliberately not
defined… No chapter may introduce a `RelationType` enum or a typed edge kind without resolving
OQ-45." This chapter does not.

### 17.1 `board_row_relations` — T-13, the projection

The JSONB cell stays **authoritative** — the frontend reads `rowIds` in order and an ordered list is
not a set. `board_row_relations` is a projection written in the same transaction, so a backlink is an
indexed query instead of a scan over every board.

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TABLE board_row_relations (
  id               uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  source_row_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES board_rows(id)    ON DELETE CASCADE,
  source_column_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES board_columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  source_board_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id)        ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target_row_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES board_rows(id)    ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target_board_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id)        ON DELETE CASCADE,
  position         int  NOT NULL,                 -- index within the cell's rowIds array
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (source_row_id, source_column_id, target_row_id)
);
CREATE INDEX board_row_relations_target_idx ON board_row_relations (target_row_id);
CREATE INDEX board_row_relations_source_idx ON board_row_relations (source_row_id);
CREATE INDEX board_row_relations_target_board_idx ON board_row_relations (target_board_id);
```

| Column | Why it is there |
| --- | --- |
| `source_column_id` | A backlink names the column it came through — `via Blocked by` (`src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:57-59`). Without it a record linked from two columns of one board reads as one backlink. |
| `source_board_id` / `target_board_id` | Denormalised so E-072 filters by the caller's access on the source board's node without a join back through `board_rows`. |
| `position` | The cell's array index. Rebuilt on every write; it exists so the projection can be read back in the cell's own order for diagnostics. |
| `UNIQUE (source, column, target)` | A cell holding the same id twice is a client bug; the projection de-duplicates it rather than doubling a backlink. |

**Cardinality.** One `board_rows` row has 0..N outbound relations per relation column and 0..N
inbound. **Delete behaviour.** `ON DELETE CASCADE` on all four FKs. Deleting a row removes both its
outbound and its inbound projection rows — **but never rewrites another row's `cells`** (§17.4).

**Maintenance.** On every write that touches a relation cell (E-062, E-064, E-066, E-074, E-077,
E-085, and the row-rewriting halves of E-054, E-055, E-057), the same transaction runs
`DELETE … WHERE source_row_id = $r AND source_column_id = $c` followed by an `INSERT` of the new
list. Never a partial diff: the cell is the truth and the projection is rebuilt from it.

**A target id that does not resolve is still projected** when the target row exists on a board the
writer could see; an id that resolves to nothing is **not** inserted (the FK would fail) but
**stays in the cell**. That asymmetry is deliberate and is §17.4.

### 17.2 Creating and deleting a relation — `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/cells`

**Purpose** — Link or unlink records. Documented here as the relation-shaped use of E-066; the full
contract is §15.5.

**Request Body** — an ordinary `UpdateCellsRequest` whose `value` is a relation cell:

```jsonc
// PATCH /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/rows/cells
{
  "edits": [
    {
      "rowId": "3f1c…",
      "columnId": "col_blocks",
      "value": { "kind": "relation", "rowIds": ["7b02…", "c910…"] }
    }
  ],
  "baseRevisions": { "3f1c…": 7 }
}
```

**The whole list is sent, always.** There is no add-one or remove-one form: the editor commits the
selected set (`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:138-141` — a single-value column commits
`[rowId]` outright; a multi column commits the toggled array). Unlinking is the same call with the id
absent.

**Validation specific to relation cells:**

| Rule | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `isMulti === false` | More than one id is `VALIDATION_FAILED`. |
| A target id that does not exist | **Accepted and stored.** The cell keeps it; the projection row is not written; the chip renders `[Deleted Item]`. See §17.4. |
| A target on a board the caller may not see | **Accepted and stored.** Access is resolved at *read* time (§17.5), not at write time — refusing the write would tell the caller the record exists. |
| `RelationConfig.boardId` is `null` | The target board is **this** board (`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:104-106`). |
| Self-reference | Accepted at the storage layer. The Gantt already skips `blockerId === row.rowId` when drawing (`src/lib/board-gantt.ts:377`). See §17.6. |

**Database, Transaction, Realtime, Errors** — §15.5, plus the `board_row_relations` rebuild described
in §17.1, inside the same transaction.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:112-160`
(`RelationCellEditor`) via the grid's and drawer's cell commit paths, and
`src/components/board/drawer/drawer-field.tsx`.

---

### 17.3 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/relation-index` — resolve chips

**Purpose** — Every linkable record of one board, reduced to what a chip needs. **One request per
target board, never one per cell.**

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on the **target** board's node — i.e. on `boards.node_id` for the
`boardId` in the path. This is the read that decides whether a chip may reveal a record's display id
and title (canon OQ-44).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | `uuid` | The **target** board a relation column points at. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | repeated `uuid` | — | Sparse resolution: only these records. Omitted = every record of the board, capped by `limit`. |
| `limit` | `int 1..2000` | `1000` | Hard cap on the whole-board form. |
| `cursor` | `string` | — | Keyset on `(position, id)`, for a board past the cap. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response**

```ts
/** canon §5.3. */
interface RelationTarget {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  /** The primary column's text value. Empty string when the record is untitled. */
  readonly title: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly boardName: string;
}
```

`src/services/board-service.ts:1290-1324`. The chip label is
`` `${displayId} · ${title}` `` when a title exists, else `displayId`
(`src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts:58-62`).

#### `relationResolved` — the rule this endpoint exists to serve

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Until **every** referenced board has answered, an id missing from the map
is **unknown**, never `[Deleted Item]`:

```ts
// src/lib/cell-values.ts:14-22, 117-122
readonly relationResolved?: boolean;   // "an id that is missing from the map is unknown, not deleted"
```
`src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts:17-18,74-76` returns `PENDING` (`isResolved: false`) until all
requests settle, and `RelationCellView` only paints the danger style when `isResolved`
(`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:64,36`).

The backend consequence: **a filtered-out record and a deleted record must be indistinguishable to
this endpoint's caller.** When the caller may not see the target board at all, answer `404` /
`BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — the client then never reaches `isResolved: true` for that board and renders the
ids raw rather than as deletions. When the caller may see the board, return the surviving subset;
canon's position on OQ-44 is that "the FE already treats an unresolved id as *unknown*, not deleted,
so a filtered-out row degrades gracefully."

**Database** — `boards` `SELECT` + node visibility → `board_columns` `SELECT primary_column_id`'s row
→ `board_rows` `SELECT id, custom_id, cells->'<primaryColumnId>' … WHERE board_id = $1 [AND id =
ANY($ids)] [AND archived_at IS NULL] ORDER BY position, id LIMIT $limit`. Only the primary cell is
projected; the rest of `cells` is not read.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `limit` out of range, more than 500 `ids`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — reserved; visibility failures answer `404`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown board **or** one the caller may not see. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts:31-72`, which collects the distinct
`config.boardId` values across the board's relation columns and issues one request each
(`:35-40, 51`). Consumed by `src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:47-100` and by every
`cellText` projection that renders a relation (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:117-122`).

---

### 17.4 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/backlinks` — the other direction

**Purpose** — Which records point **at** this one, through any relation column, on any board.

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on the **target** record's board node, plus per-result filtering by
visibility on each **source** board's node. A backlink from a board the caller may not open is
dropped from the list, not returned with a redacted name.

**Path Params** — `boardId`, `rowId`.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `int 1..200` | `50` | Hard cap. |
| `cursor` | `string` | — | Keyset on `(source_board_id, source_row_id)`. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response**

```ts
/** canon §5.3. */
interface Backlink {
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly boardNodeId: string;   // so the panel can build an href
  readonly boardName: string;
  readonly columnName: string;    // "via Blocked by"
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly title: string;
}
```

**Backlinks are derived, never stored — EXISTING REQUIREMENT.**

> "Nothing is stored for a backlink: it is derived by asking which rows point here, so the two
> directions can never disagree."
> — `src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:14-18`; PRD `DV-REL-24`

`board_row_relations` is not a contradiction of that rule: it is a projection of the cells, rebuilt
from them on every write, with no independent write path. **No endpoint may write it directly, and
no endpoint may write a mirrored value into the target record's cells** (canon §8.8, OQ-44: "no
mirrored value").

The mock scans every loaded board (`listBacklinks`, `src/services/board-service.ts:1342-1376`) and
says so: "A real backend answers this from a link table" (`:1339-1341`). Canon E-072 makes it a rule:
"an indexed query over `board_row_relations`, never a scan."

**Database**

```sql
-- documentation only
SELECT r.source_board_id, r.source_row_id, r.source_column_id
  FROM board_row_relations r
 WHERE r.target_row_id = $rowId
 ORDER BY r.source_board_id, r.source_row_id
 LIMIT $limit + 1;
```
served by `board_row_relations_target_idx`, then joined to `board_rows` (for `custom_id` and the
primary cell), `board_columns` (for `name`) and `boards` ⨝ `nodes` (for `name`, `node_id` and the
visibility filter). Rows whose source board fails the visibility check are dropped **before**
`limit` is applied, so a page is never short for a reason the caller cannot see.

**"Nothing links here" and "the lookup failed" are different facts, and only one of them is about the
record** (`src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:27-29`): an empty list is `200` with
`items: []`, never an error, and an error is never rendered as emptiness.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None. A backlink appears when the *source* record is written, which already emits
`row.updated` on the source board's channel; the target's drawer refetches on open.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — bad cursor or limit. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` / `ROW_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:19-30`, mounted in the record
drawer's Details tab beneath the subtask panel, deliberately kept apart from it: "Relations are
dependencies, not containment — kept apart from Subtasks on purpose"
(`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:253-254`).

#### Deleted targets — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

When a target record is deleted (§15.9):

1. `board_row_relations` rows naming it are removed by `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
2. **The dangling id stays in the source cell.** No `cells` document is rewritten. Canon §8.8,
   OQ-44: "leave the dangling id in the JSONB cell so `[Deleted Item]` keeps rendering and the
   history stays honest."
3. On the next read the id resolves to nothing in the relation index; once `relationResolved` is
   true the chip renders `[Deleted Item]` in the danger style with an unlink affordance
   (`DELETED_LABEL`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:22`;
   `src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:64,75-77`). PRD `DV-REL-24` requires exactly this.
4. Cleaning up dangling ids is an explicit maintenance action, never a silent rewrite.

---

### 17.5 `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/search` — pick a target

**Purpose** — Find records on a board by display id or primary text. This is the relation picker's
lookup; it is scoped to one board and is **not** the workspace-wide search (E-133).

**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — Visibility on `boards.node_id` — the **target** board's node, which is the same
gate as §17.3.

**Path Params** — `boardId` `uuid`.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | `string` | `""` | Empty returns the first `limit` records in board order — how the picker opens (`src/services/board-service.ts:267`). |
| `limit` | `int 1..100` | `20` | The frontend's default is 20 (`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:127`). |

**Request Body** — None.
**Response** — `readonly BoardRow[]`, in board order, capped at `limit`.

**Matching — EXISTING REQUIREMENT** (`src/services/board-service.ts:244-272`,
`matchesRowId`, `src/lib/row-id.ts:46-62`). A record matches when **either**:

1. `matchesRowId(displayId, q)`:
   - a case-insensitive **substring** of the upper-cased display id (`ASK-04` finds `TASK-042`); or
   - a `prefix + digits` split on whitespace or hyphens where the prefix matches exactly and the
     numbers compare **numerically** — so `TASK 7`, `task-7` and `Task 007` all find `TASK-007`.
2. The **primary column's** text value contains `q`, lower-cased.

Only the primary column is searched. `cellText` over every column is what E-133 does; this endpoint
is the cheap one.

**Database** — `board_rows` `SELECT … WHERE board_id = $1 AND (upper(custom_id) LIKE '%'||upper($q)||'%'
OR lower(cells->'<primaryColumnId>'->>'value') LIKE '%'||lower($q)||'%') ORDER BY position, id LIMIT
$limit`. The `prefix + digits` form is resolved by parsing `q` server-side into
`(prefix, sequence)` and adding `OR (sequence = $n AND row_id_prefix = $prefix)`, which the
`UNIQUE (board_id, sequence)` index answers directly rather than by scanning.

**Transaction** — Not required.
**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `limit` out of range. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:126-131`
(`RelationCellEditor`'s debounced lookup) → `src/services/board-service.ts:244-272`.

---

### 17.6 Cross-board relations

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** A relation column names its target board and `null` means "this board"
(`RelationConfig.boardId`, `src/types/board.ts:157`;
`src/components/board/cells/relation-cell.tsx:104-106`). The target board is chosen from
`GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/boards` (§13.8) in the column menu
(`src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:224-247`).

Four backend consequences:

1. **`board_row_relations` spans boards.** `source_board_id` and `target_board_id` are separate
   columns and are routinely different. Backlinks are therefore a cross-board query, which is why
   `board_row_relations_target_idx` exists.
2. **Resolution is one request per target board, not one per cell.**
   `src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts:32-51` collects the distinct `config.boardId` values across the
   whole schema. An endpoint shaped per-cell would be N+1 on a 5 000-row board (canon OQ-44 (d)).
3. **Permission is resolved on the target board's node, at read time** (§17.3). A chip must not
   reveal the display id or title of a record on a board the viewer cannot open — canon OQ-44 (c)
   calls this "exactly the kind of leak nobody audits", and the `relationResolved` flag is what makes
   a filtered-out record degrade into "unknown" rather than into "deleted".
4. **Changing a column's `RelationConfig.boardId` does not rewrite any cell** (§14.4). Existing ids
   keep pointing where they pointed; they simply stop resolving against the new target board.

**A cross-board move (`E-077`) does not carry relations.** A moved record's relation cells keep their
ids, which now point at records on the board it left; the projection is rebuilt against whatever
still resolves (§15.11). This follows from the move contract, not from a relation rule.

---

### 17.7 Cycle detection for BLOCKED_BY

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-45)** — should a relation cycle be rejected, and by what rule?
>
> **What is unclear.** `SavedView.showDependencies` draws "blocked by" connectors on the Gantt
> (`src/types/board.ts:369-370`), but **no dependency type exists** and nothing anywhere refuses a
> cycle. A relation column is a generic link; the fact that one of them is *called* "Blocked by" is a
> template's column name (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:188`), not a schema fact. There is nothing in
> the data that says which relation columns are dependencies.
>
> **Evidence.**
> - `buildGanttLinks` skips only **self**-blocking — `if (blockerId === row.rowId) continue;` — and
>   de-duplicates by `` `${blockerId}->${row.rowId}` ``. It has no cycle guard
>   (`src/lib/board-gantt.ts:356-395`). A → B → A draws two connectors and terminates, because the
>   builder iterates rows once rather than walking the graph.
> - A dependency conflict is **reported, never corrected**: "A conflict is *reported*, never
>   corrected. 'Blocked by' states an intent about order; it is not permission for the chart to move
>   someone's dates" (`src/lib/board-gantt.ts:350-354`). `GanttLink.isConflict` is
>   `dayIndex(row.start) < dayIndex(blocker.end)` and drives an amber connector, nothing more.
> - Containment **is** cycle-guarded, in two places and with an explicit reason
>   (`wouldCreateCycle`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:118-127`; `setRowParent`,
>   `src/services/board-service.ts:384-392`) — so the codebase clearly distinguishes "a loop would
>   hang every reader" (containment) from "a loop is a plan somebody wrote" (relation).
> - Canon §2.9 forbids introducing a `RelationType` enum or a typed edge kind to resolve this.
>
> **Recommendation — reject cycles, on one narrowly defined edge, and only there.**
>
> 1. **Do not add a `RelationType`.** Instead add one boolean to `RelationConfig`:
>    `isDependency?: boolean` — "links in this column express an ordering constraint". It defaults to
>    `false`, so every relation column that exists today is unaffected, and the `task` template's
>    `col_blocks` ships with it `true`. This is the smallest thing that can distinguish a dependency
>    from a link without inventing an edge vocabulary, and it lives where the frontend already puts
>    per-column behaviour.
> 2. **Reject a cycle only among columns with `isDependency: true`.** A "Related task" link that
>    happens to loop is not a contradiction and must keep working.
> 3. **Detection.** On a cell write to a dependency column, inside the same transaction as §15.5 step
>    6, run a recursive CTE over `board_row_relations` restricted to dependency columns:
>
> ```sql
> -- documentation only: would linking $source -> $target close a loop?
> WITH RECURSIVE reach AS (
>   SELECT r.target_row_id AS row_id, 1 AS depth
>     FROM board_row_relations r
>     JOIN board_columns c ON c.id = r.source_column_id
>    WHERE r.source_row_id = $target
>      AND (c.config -> 'isDependency')::boolean IS TRUE
>   UNION                                   -- UNION, not UNION ALL: the set prunes revisits
>   SELECT r.target_row_id, reach.depth + 1
>     FROM board_row_relations r
>     JOIN reach ON r.source_row_id = reach.row_id
>     JOIN board_columns c ON c.id = r.source_column_id
>    WHERE (c.config -> 'isDependency')::boolean IS TRUE
>      AND reach.depth < 256                -- hard stop, as the client's `seen` guards do
> )
> SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reach WHERE row_id = $source) AS would_cycle;
> ```
>
>    Plain `UNION` (not `UNION ALL`) makes the CTE terminate on already-cyclic legacy data by
>    discarding rows it has already produced; the `depth < 256` bound is the belt to that braces.
>    The walk is **cross-board** — dependencies may span boards (§17.6) — and is served by
>    `board_row_relations_source_idx`.
> 4. **The refusal** is `409` / `RELATION_CYCLE` with a message shaped like the containment one so
>    the two read alike: `` `${target.displayId} already depends on ${source.displayId}` ``. In a
>    batch it is reported per edit, exactly as a transition refusal is (§15.5.2 step 6g).
> 5. **Self-reference is refused on the same edge** (`source === target`) rather than skipped
>    silently, because the Gantt's `continue` is a rendering accommodation for data that should never
>    have been written.
> 6. **Existing data is never invalidated.** Detection runs on write only; a board that already holds
>    a cycle keeps rendering, and the Gantt keeps drawing both connectors.
>
> **Impact if wrong.**
> - **If we reject and should not have**: a team using "Blocked by" to mean "related to" hits a
>   refusal they cannot reason about. Mitigated by `isDependency` defaulting to `false` — only the
>   `task` template's column opts in, and a manager can switch it off through `board.column.update`.
> - **If we allow and should have rejected**: every consumer that walks the dependency graph has to
>   carry its own cycle guard forever. The Gantt's current builder does not walk the graph, so it
>   survives — but the first feature that does (critical path, "what unblocks this", auto-scheduling,
>   a dependency-ordered export) hangs on real customer data, and the fix is then a data migration
>   over cycles that were legal when they were written.
> - **If we add a `RelationType` enum instead**: canon §2.9 is violated, every relation cell grows a
>   discriminant the frontend does not send, and the "Blocked by" column stops being an ordinary
>   relation column that a user may rename, retype or delete — which is the property `DV-TMP-19`
>   exists to protect.

**Until OQ-45 is resolved**, the shipped behaviour is: **cycles are stored, and reported nowhere.**
No endpoint in this specification rejects one today, and `board_row_relations` carries no constraint
that would prevent one. A backend implementing this chapter before the question is answered should
add the `isDependency` flag and the CTE behind a configuration switch that is **off**, so turning it
on is a decision rather than a migration.

---

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **Path parameter syntax.** The brief's endpoint template shows `### METHOD /api/v1/path/:param`,
   while canon P-02 says "Path parameters are `{camelCase}` UUIDs". I followed canon and used
   `{boardId}` / `{rowId}` / `{columnId}` throughout, on the assumption that nineteen files agreeing
   on one syntax matters more than the template's illustrative colon. If the editor prefers `:param`,
   it is a mechanical substitution over the headings in §§13–17.

2. **Canon §1.3.2 calls the four `board_rows` projections "generated columns, maintained by
   Postgres".** A Postgres `GENERATED ALWAYS AS … STORED` expression may only reference columns of
   the same row, and these projections must read `boards.status_column_id` /
   `assignee_column_id` / `due_column_id` to know *which* key of `cells` to project. I have
   documented them as ordinary columns maintained by the same statement that writes `cells` (a
   `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger is the mechanical equivalent). The contract canon states — four
   indexed projections, always in step with `cells`, `due_date` and `due_at` never collapsed into one
   — is unchanged. Canon may want to soften the word "generated".

3. **Canon has no endpoint for reordering select options** (§3.7 lists E-058 create, E-059 update,
   E-060 delete). I did not add one: the frontend reorders options inside the column-config dialog
   and commits the whole `config` through E-053, so a reorder endpoint would be a second write path
   into one JSONB document. §14.9 documents the omission explicitly so a reader who came looking for
   it finds the reason rather than a gap. If canon wants the symmetry with E-056, the endpoint should
   be added to §3.7 rather than invented here.

4. **`CreateColumnRequest.insertAfterColumnId` deviates from the frontend**, which passes an index
   (`atIndex`). The brief named the field; I have documented the index→anchor mapping and marked the
   deviation as a RECOMMENDATION citing OQ-39. If the editor would rather keep the frontend's index,
   §14.3 is the only place to change.

5. **`BulkSkipReason` gains `permission_denied`** per canon §2.7's instruction to add it "rather than
   a parallel array". Since §15.5 also reports *rule* refusals (transition and availability) in bulk
   calls, those reuse `permission_denied` as the skip reason. That is slightly imprecise — a
   transition refusal is not a permission refusal, and the code is emphatic that the two are
   different things (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:15-18`). A future `rule_refused` member would be
   cleaner; adding one is a canon change, so I did not.

6. **§15.5 returns rule refusals in `conflicts` for batch calls and as a `409` for single-edit
   calls.** That asymmetry is not stated in canon; it follows from E-066 being "always 200" while a
   one-cell Kanban drag needs a hard refusal the client can show as a toast. The frontend already
   refuses the drag locally before any request leaves (`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:79-86`),
   so the `409` path is only reachable by a stale tab or a direct API call — which is exactly when it
   should be a hard refusal.

7. **Single-record archive has no endpoint of its own, by design.** Both single-row surfaces call
   `bulkArchive([rowId], …)` (`src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:292-300`,
   `src/components/board/table/row-actions-menu.tsx:89-90`). If another chapter documents a
   `PUT /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}/archive`, it is a duplicate and should be removed.

8. **Error reasons this chapter needs that canon §4.3 does not yet register.** All four are marked
   RECOMMENDATION where they appear; each should be added to the registry (or the endpoint changed to
   use an existing reason) before another chapter reaches for a different name:

   | Reason | HTTP | `code` | Raised by |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | §13.2 — `templateId` names nothing. Message `That template could not be found`. |
   | `ROW_ID_PREFIX_LOCKED` | 409 | `conflict` | §13.5 — the prefix cannot change once records exist (OQ-43). |
   | `OPTION_LABEL_CONFLICT` | 409 | `conflict` | §14.11 — a rename onto an existing option's label. Creation still dedupes silently (E-058). |
   | `RELATION_CYCLE` | 409 | `conflict` | §17.7 — only if OQ-45 is resolved in favour of rejecting cycles. |

9. **`RelationConfig.isDependency` (§17.7) is a new config field, not a new enum.** It is the
   smallest thing that lets a cycle check distinguish "Blocked by" from "Related task" without
   violating canon §2.9's ban on a `RelationType`. It is a RECOMMENDATION attached to OQ-45 and is
   not implemented until that question is answered. Nothing else in this chapter reads it.

---

## 18. Kanban Transition Rules

### What a transition rule is, and what it is not

A transition rule answers one question: **may this record's status go from where it is to where it
is being put?** It is authored by a user, stored as data on the select column, and keyed by
immutable option id — "nothing in this file, or anywhere else, knows that *Debug* may not reach
*Done*: it only knows how to read the table the user wrote"
(`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:4-25`).

Three separate gates stand between a Kanban drop and a written cell. They are deliberately not
merged, because each one refuses for a different reason and each one says something different:

| # | Gate | Question | Where it is answered | Refusal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Permission** | May this person edit Status at all? | `row.update` on the board's node (`src/services/authz.ts:67-74`) | `403` `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| 2 | **Option availability** | Is this option offered for *this* record? | `option.isDisabled`, then `option.availability` (`src/lib/select-availability.ts:82-102`) | `409` `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` |
| 3 | **Transition** | May Status move *from here to there*? | `TransitionRules` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:102-133`) | `409` `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` |

Gate 1 is about the person; gates 2 and 3 are about the record. The source says so in three
separate places and the backend must keep them separate too — "Permission answers 'may this person
edit Status at all'; a transition rule answers 'may Status go from here to there'. Both are checked,
separately, before a drop is written" (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:22-24`;
`src/lib/select-availability.ts:24-29`; `src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:11-18`).

**Grounding.** Transition rules are an **EXISTING REQUIREMENT** of the frontend, not of the PRD.
The PRD's Kanban requirement (`VW-KAN-12`) asks only for the permission bounce — "Kéo thẻ vào cột mà
user không có quyền chuyển: Thẻ tự động bật ngược lại vị trí cũ kèm thông báo"
(`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:72`). The rule engine, its data shape, its evaluation
order and its refusal copy are all settled by the shipped frontend, and this chapter transcribes
them rather than proposing them.

---

### 18.1 Data model recap

**Storage: `board_columns.config.transitionRules`, a member of the `SelectConfig` JSONB document
(T-11). There is no `transition_rules` table and no chapter may add one.** The decision and its
reasoning belong to canon §1.3.3 and the schema chapter §4.14; what follows is the recap this
chapter's endpoints depend on.

```ts
/** src/types/board.ts:89-94. Stored at board_columns.config.transitionRules. */
interface TransitionRules {
  /** Off by default. With `false` every move is permitted. */
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  /** Only declared transitions pass. The single value today; the field exists
   *  so a future deny-list is an added member, not a schema change. */
  readonly mode: "allow-list";
  /** fromKey -> the keys it may move to. Keys and targets are BOTH
   *  `board_columns.config.options[].id` values, plus the sentinel "__empty__". */
  readonly transitions: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
}
```

| Property | Value | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owning table | `board_columns` (T-11), column `config jsonb` | canon §1.1 |
| Cardinality | **0..1 per select column.** Never present on a non-select column. | `SelectConfig.transitionRules?` (`src/types/board.ts:137`) |
| Absent reads as | `{ enabled: false, mode: "allow-list", transitions: {} }` | `NO_TRANSITION_RULES`, `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:35-39` |
| Key domain | every `options[].id` of the **same column**, plus `"__empty__"` | `transitionKeys`, `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:46-48` |
| Target domain | identical to the key domain | same |
| Reserved id | `"__empty__"` (`EMPTY_OPTION_KEY`) may never be a user-authored option id | `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:28`; `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` (canon §4.3) |
| Referential integrity | **none available.** The referenced ids live in a sibling key of the same JSONB document, so no FK can protect them. Boundary validation on write and `pruneTransitionRules` on option delete are the whole defence. | canon §1.3.3 |
| Index | **none.** The table is never queried; it is read with its column, always. | `transitionRulesOf`, `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:41-43` |
| Size bound | at most `N+1` keys × `N` targets for `N` options, inside the 64 KB `config` ceiling (§4.12, OQ-38) | — |

**The `__empty__` sentinel stands on both sides.** A record with no status is a legitimate source
("a record with no status has to start somewhere",
`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:181-185`) and a legitimate target (clearing the cell). Kanban's own
ungrouped column key is a *different* constant, `UNGROUPED_KEY = "__ungrouped__"`
(`src/lib/board-grouping.ts:14`), translated at the boundary by `transitionKeyOf`
(`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:31-33`). **`"__ungrouped__"` must never appear in stored data.** A
write carrying it is a client bug; reject it with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

**What a stored table looks like.** The `bug` template ships this one, seeded and disabled
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:249-260`):

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "mode": "allow-list",
  "transitions": {
    "status_0": ["status_1", "status_5"],
    "status_1": ["status_2", "status_5"],
    "status_2": ["status_3", "status_1"],
    "status_3": ["status_4", "status_2"],
    "status_4": ["status_2"],
    "status_5": ["status_1"],
    "__empty__": ["status_0"]
  }
}
```

Two built-ins ship a table — `task` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:163-170`) and `bug`
(`:249-260`) — both with `enabled: false`, because "a board should behave exactly as it always has
until someone opts into the rules" (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:159-161`). `qa` and `apiDocs` ship
none. The backend seeds these as ordinary `board_templates` rows and deep-copies them at
instantiation (§4.20); **no code path anywhere depends on the pairs declared there**
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:104-109`).

---

### 18.2 The evaluation contract the backend must reproduce exactly

`evaluateTransition(column, fromKey, toKey)` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:102-133`).

**The move is ALLOWED when any one of these holds**, tested in this order:

1. `rules.enabled === false`. Off by default; a board behaves like a plain Kanban until someone opts
   in (`:108`).
2. `transitionKeyOf(fromKey) === transitionKeyOf(toKey)` — a move that changes nothing (`:112`).
3. `!isGoverned(from) || !isGoverned(to)`, where `isGoverned(k)` is `Object.hasOwn(transitions, k)`
   (`:63-65`, `:115`). **A key the table does not mention is ungoverned and unrestricted, on either
   side of the move.** This is load-bearing: "an allow-list that silently strands every new status
   would be a trap, and 'configure it or the board stops working' is not a reasonable default"
   (`:55-61`). Adding an option therefore never freezes it and never freezes the board around it.
4. `transitions[from]` contains `to` (`:118`).

**Otherwise the move is REFUSED**, and the refusal sentence names both ends *and* where the record
can go instead (`:120-132`). Two exact templates, reproduced verbatim on the wire:

```
{column.name} cannot go straight from {fromLabel} to {toLabel}. {fromLabel} can move to {a}, {b}.
{column.name} cannot go straight from {fromLabel} to {toLabel}. {fromLabel} has no permitted moves.
```

The second form is used when `transitions[from]` is empty. Labels come from
`transitionLabel(key, options)`: the option's `label`, or the literal **`No value`** for
`"__empty__"`, or the raw key when the option is gone (`:50-53`). Targets are joined with `", "` in
the order the table stores them.

**Three details that are easy to get wrong.**

- **The source key is the record's *first* option id**, or `"__empty__"` when the cell is empty —
  even on a multi-select column (`currentKey`, `src/lib/select-availability.ts:57-62`).
- **Clearing a status is always legal.** Only *arriving* somewhere is gated; an edit whose
  `optionIds` is `[]` has no target to test (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:77-80`).
- **A multi-value write is refused if *any* target option is unavailable.** The guard maps every
  `optionId` in the incoming value through the availability table and takes the first failure
  (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:78-85`).

**`allowedTargets(column, fromKey)`** (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:141-155`) is the set Kanban
precomputes when a drag starts, so hovering a column is a set lookup rather than a rule evaluation
and never a request. It is `[from, ...transitions[from], ...ungovernedKeys]`, or every key when the
rules are off or the source is ungoverned. **The backend does not need to expose it** — it is
derivable from the stored table, which the client already has.

**Diagnostics the editor renders, also pure functions over the stored table:**

| Helper | Meaning | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ungovernedKeys(rules, options)` | keys the table says nothing about — what the editor offers to set up | `:68-73` |
| `strandedKeys(rules, options)` | governed keys whose target list is empty — cards there cannot leave | `:76-83` |

Neither is an endpoint. Both are computed client-side from the column the read already returned.

**Truth table for the `bug` table above, with `enabled: true`:**

| from | to | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status_0` (New) | `status_1` (Triaged) | allowed | rule 4 |
| `status_0` | `status_4` (Verified) | **refused** | governed both ends, not listed |
| `status_0` | `status_0` | allowed | rule 2 |
| `__empty__` | `status_0` | allowed | rule 4 |
| `__empty__` | `status_3` (Fixed) | **refused** | `__empty__` is governed and lists only `status_0` |
| `status_0` | `status_9` (an option added after the table was written) | allowed | rule 3 — target ungoverned |
| `status_9` | `status_4` | allowed | rule 3 — source ungoverned |
| anything | anything | allowed | rule 1 when `enabled: false` |

---

### 18.3 Why there is no `/transition-rules` sub-resource

The rules have no endpoints of their own. They are read with their column and written with their
column, for three reasons that are all settled elsewhere:

1. **Canon P-03** caps nesting at one level below the owning aggregate;
   `/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/transition-rules` is two.
2. **Canon §1.3.3** keeps the whole select configuration atomic: the transition table, the
   `completedOptionIds` list and each option's `availability` tree all reference option ids by
   value, so a write that touches options and rules together must be one write or the references
   can disagree. The frontend already commits them as one draft — the Options & rules dialog builds
   a single `SelectConfigDraft` and saves it once
   (`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:113-124`, `:425-437`).
3. **The frontend has no such call.** `updateColumnConfig(columnId, { config })` is the only write
   path (`src/store/board-store.ts:761-790`), reached from
   `src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:164-173` and
   `src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:344-351`.

So: **read through E-051, write through E-053.** Both are documented in full below, scoped to what
this chapter owns.

---

### `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns`

**Purpose** — Return the board's column schema, including each select column's `config`, which is
where the transition table lives. This is the only read a client needs to evaluate, render or
explain a transition rule.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **Visibility** on the board's node: workspace membership on `boards.node_id`'s
workspace, plus the resolved access chain granting `view` on that node (canon E-051, §3.7).
**No `board.column.update` is required to read the rules.** Below that permission the editor renders
read-only rather than hidden — "the rule that refuses your drag is worth being able to look up, and
a board whose workflow is invisible to the people working it is one where every refusal reads as a
bug" (`src/components/board/config/transition-rules-editor.tsx:30-37`, `:70-73`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `BoardColumn[]`, in ascending `position` order.

```ts
type ColumnType = "text" | "longText" | "select" | "date" | "user" | "attachment" | "relation";

interface SelectOption {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly color: SelectColor;
  readonly isDisabled?: boolean;
  readonly availability?: ConditionGroup | null;
}

interface SelectConfig {
  readonly options: readonly SelectOption[];
  readonly isMulti: boolean;
  readonly unavailableBehavior?: "disabled" | "hidden";
  readonly completedOptionIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly transitionRules?: TransitionRules;
}

type BoardColumnOf<T extends ColumnType> = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly position: number;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly hidden: boolean;
  readonly isPrimary: boolean;
  readonly type: T;
  readonly config: ColumnConfigByType[T];
};

type BoardColumn = { [T in ColumnType]: BoardColumnOf<T> }[ColumnType];
```

```jsonc
// 200 — the select column of a bug board, rules on
[
  {
    "id": "3b0d…",
    "name": "Status",
    "position": 1,
    "width": 150,
    "hidden": false,
    "isPrimary": false,
    "type": "select",
    "config": {
      "isMulti": false,
      "unavailableBehavior": "disabled",
      "completedOptionIds": ["status_4", "status_5"],
      "options": [
        { "id": "status_0", "label": "New",        "color": "gray"   },
        { "id": "status_1", "label": "Triaged",    "color": "violet" },
        { "id": "status_2", "label": "In progress","color": "blue"   },
        { "id": "status_3", "label": "Fixed",      "color": "cyan"   },
        { "id": "status_4", "label": "Verified",   "color": "green"  },
        { "id": "status_5", "label": "Won't fix",  "color": "pink"   }
      ],
      "transitionRules": {
        "enabled": true,
        "mode": "allow-list",
        "transitions": {
          "status_0": ["status_1", "status_5"],
          "status_1": ["status_2", "status_5"],
          "status_2": ["status_3", "status_1"],
          "status_3": ["status_4", "status_2"],
          "status_4": ["status_2"],
          "status_5": ["status_1"],
          "__empty__": ["status_0"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
]
```

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards` | read | `id = :boardId` → `node_id`, `workspace_id`. |
| `nodes` | read | the board's node, for the visibility check and its state (trashed / archived ancestors). |
| `workspace_members` | read | membership floor for the caller. |
| `access_rules` | read | the ancestor chain, resolved deepest-first (canon OQ-22). |
| `board_columns` | read | `WHERE board_id = :boardId ORDER BY position`. Index `(board_id, position)`. `config` is returned whole. |

No writes.

**Transaction** — Not required. A single consistent read; a repeatable-read snapshot is enough so
the option list and the transition table returned in one response cannot disagree.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` — no session. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown board, **or one the caller may not see** (canon §4.2: the two answer identically). |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — the caller is not a member of the board's workspace. |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `boardService.getBoard` (`src/services/board-service.ts:229-242`) delivers the
same columns inside `BoardSnapshot.board.columns`; the dedicated list is the seam E-051 replaces.
Readers of the rules: `transitionRulesOf` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:41-43`),
`KanbanBoard` (`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:78-109`),
`TransitionRulesEditor` (`src/components/board/config/transition-rules-editor.tsx:60-73`),
`ViewConfigBar`'s workflow button (`src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:86-98`),
`guardCellEdits` (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:59-68`).

---

### `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}`

**Purpose** — Reshape a column. For this chapter: enable, replace, disable or clear its transition
table. It is the same call the Options & rules dialog makes when it commits its draft, which is why
options, conditions, the completed set and the transition table all land in one write.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **`board.column.update`** on the board's node, plus workspace membership. Manager
and above hold it (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:37-63`); member and viewer do not. The service
already re-checks it —
`requirePermission(nodeId, "board.column.update", "change this column")`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:652`) — with the rationale spelled out at `:637-644`: "a member who
may write a Status cell is not thereby entitled to rewrite the workflow that governs every card on
the board." The frontend gate at `src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:75` "is not
security" (canon P-09).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |
| `columnId` | UUID | `board_columns.id`, must belong to `boardId`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `UpdateColumnRequest`. Only the `config` branch matters here; the other members
are documented in §4.12.

```ts
/** The transition-rule half of a select column's config patch.
 *  `null` on `transitionRules` REMOVES the key; omitting it leaves it alone. */
interface SelectConfigPatch {
  readonly options?: readonly SelectOption[];
  readonly isMulti?: boolean;
  readonly unavailableBehavior?: "disabled" | "hidden";
  readonly completedOptionIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly transitionRules?: TransitionRules | null;
```
