```ts
}

interface UpdateColumnRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly width?: number;
  readonly hidden?: boolean;
  readonly config?: SelectConfigPatch | TextConfigPatch | LongTextConfigPatch
                 | DateConfigPatch | UserConfigPatch | AttachmentConfigPatch | RelationConfigPatch;
}
```

**Merge semantics — one level deep, no deeper.** `config` is shallow-merged over the stored object
(`patchColumn`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:85-104`; §4.12). So a `transitionRules` object in the body
**replaces the stored one wholesale**; there is no per-edge patch and no deep merge of
`transitions`. The frontend relies on this: the editor's `toggleTransition`, `setTransitions` and
`clearTransitionsFor` all return a **new whole table** and the dialog saves it as one draft
(`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:224-253`;
`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:425-437`).

**The three write intents, and the exact body for each:**

| Intent | Body | Result | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Turn rules on** (first time) | `{"config":{"transitionRules":{"enabled":true,"mode":"allow-list","transitions":{…}}}}` | stored as sent | the editor seeds `linearTransitions(options,{allowBackward:true})` client-side and sends the result (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:217-219`; `transition-rules-editor.tsx:81-92`) |
| **Replace the table** | same shape, different `transitions` | stored as sent | `toggleTransition` / `setTransitions` / the four presets |
| **Turn rules off, keep the table** | `{"config":{"transitionRules":{"enabled":false,"mode":"allow-list","transitions":{…}}}}` | `enabled` flips; the table survives so re-enabling restores it | "Re-enabling keeps whatever table was already written" (`transition-rules-editor.tsx:83-90`) |
| **Remove the rules entirely** — RECOMMENDATION | `{"config":{"transitionRules":null}}` | the key is deleted from `config`; reads fall back to `NO_TRANSITION_RULES` | the frontend never sends this; it is the only way to express "delete" through a shallow merge, since JSON cannot carry `undefined` |

**The backend never computes a preset.** `allowAllTransitions`, `clearAllTransitions`,
`linearTransitions` and `seedTransitionRules` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:160-219`) are client-side
authoring helpers; the API stores the table it is given. The one exception is board creation from a
template, which deep-copies the template's stored table (§4.20;
`src/lib/board-templates.ts:427-450`).

**Validation on write — boundary validation, not a database constraint.** The referenced ids live
in a sibling key of the same JSONB document, so nothing in Postgres can enforce them:

| Rule | Failure |
| --- | --- |
| `transitionRules` is only accepted on a `select` column | `400` `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` |
| `mode` must be exactly `"allow-list"` | `400` `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` |
| `enabled` must be a boolean; `transitions` must be an object of string arrays | `400` `VALIDATION_FAILED` |
| every **key** is an existing `options[].id` of this column, or `"__empty__"` | `400` `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` (unknown id) |
| every **target** is an existing `options[].id` of this column, or `"__empty__"` | `400` `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` |
| `"__ungrouped__"` appears nowhere | `400` `VALIDATION_FAILED` — a client bug; `transitionKeyOf` should have translated it (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:31-33`) |
| a user-authored option id equal to `"__empty__"` in the same `options` patch | `400` `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:28`) |
| duplicate targets within one list | accepted and de-duplicated on write — `toggleTransition` cannot produce one, and rejecting is harsher than the UI implies |
| serialised `config` past 64 KB | `400` `VALIDATION_FAILED` (§4.12, OQ-38) |

**Validation order matters when options and rules arrive together.** Validate the incoming
`options` array first, then the transition table against **the post-merge option set** — otherwise a
single draft that renames and re-links statuses at once would be rejected against the stale list.
This mirrors the dialog, which prunes the table against its own draft options immediately before
sending (`src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx:433-435`).

**Response** — `BoardColumn` — the authoritative column, config included (canon C-10; the store
replaces its optimistic copy with it, `src/store/board-store.ts:784-789`).

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards` | read | `id = :boardId` → `node_id`. |
| `nodes` | read | permission chain + state (`NodeState`: a trashed or frozen node refuses this write). |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | permission resolution. |
| `board_columns` | **write** | `UPDATE … SET config = :config, updated_at = now(), updated_by = :actor WHERE id = :columnId AND board_id = :boardId`. Row-level lock for the read-modify-write of the shallow merge: `SELECT config … FOR UPDATE`. |
| `boards` | **write** | `updated_at = now()` — the service touches the board on every schema write (`src/services/board-service.ts:656`). |
| `audit_events` | **write** | one row, module `board`, action `board.column.update`, `context` naming the column and whether `transitionRules.enabled` changed (T-36, OQ-25). |

**No row is rewritten.** Changing the workflow never touches `board_rows`. A record already sitting
in a status the new table forbids **stays there** — the rules gate *arriving*, not *being*. This
follows from `evaluateTransition` never being consulted on read, and from `pruneTransitionRules`
being the only cleanup the frontend performs (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:256-269`).

**Transaction** — **Required.** The `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` of the existing `config`, the merged
write, the `boards.updated_at` touch and the audit row are one transaction. Two managers editing the
same column's rules must serialise; the shallow merge is a read-modify-write and last-write-wins on
the whole `config` document is only safe under the row lock.

**Realtime** — **RT-10 `board.schema.changed`** with payload `{ boardId }`. Ids only; the client
refetches the whole schema, matching canon C-11. This is what makes a second tab's Kanban stop
offering a move the rules no longer permit.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` — `transitionRules` sent to a non-select column, or `mode` not `"allow-list"`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` — an option was authored with the id `"__empty__"`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed table, `"__ungrouped__"` present, or `config` past its ceiling. |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` — when the same draft also carries `options[].availability` (§4.15). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — below manager. `message`: `You do not have permission to change this column`; `detail`: `Needs the Manager role or above`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` — `That column could not be found`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` — a key or target names an option this column does not have. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` — reserved; only if a future `expectedConfigVersion` is added. Not used today. |

**Frontend Used By** — `boardService.updateColumn` (`src/services/board-service.ts:645-662`) behind
`useBoardStore.updateColumnConfig` (`src/store/board-store.ts:761-790`), called from
`src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:170-172` (the board's **Transition rules** button,
shown whenever a Kanban view groups by a select column, `:70-71`) and from
`src/components/board/table/column-menu.tsx:350` (the column header's **Options & rules**). The
dialog itself is `src/components/board/config/select-column-dialog.tsx`, whose transition section is
`src/components/board/config/transition-rules-editor.tsx`.

---

### 18.4 Rules that keep the stored table honest

These are consequences of §18.1's "no FK can protect the option ids". Each belongs to another
endpoint, and each is listed here so the transition table is never the thing that was forgotten.

| Event | Endpoint | Obligation | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An option is **deleted** | E-060 `DELETE …/options/{optionId}`, or E-053 with a shorter `options` array | Drop the option's **key** and remove it from **every** target list, in the same transaction. This is `pruneTransitionRules` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:256-269`), which the dialog already runs locally (`select-column-dialog.tsx:180-190`). Also strip it from `completedOptionIds`. | `select-column-dialog.tsx:184-189` |
| An option is **renamed** | E-059 | Nothing. The table is keyed by id, so "renaming a status never breaks the workflow" (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:10-11`). **The id must never be re-minted on rename.** | §4.13 |
| An option is **created** | E-058 | Nothing. The new key is ungoverned, therefore unrestricted (rule 3). | `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:16-20` |
| The column is **converted** away from `select` | E-057 | The whole `config` branch is replaced by `defaultConfigFor(newType)`; the rules are gone. This is why the endpoint offers `?dryRun=true`. | `retypeColumn`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:209-220` |
| The column is **duplicated** | E-055 | The copy carries the same `config`, transition table included, and is never primary. | `src/services/board-service.ts:606-613` |
| The column is **deleted** | E-054 | Refused on the primary column; otherwise the rules go with it. No other column can reference them. | `src/services/board-service.ts:680-707` |

**A stored table may legitimately name an option that no longer exists** if a write slipped past a
prune. The reader must survive it: `transitionLabel` falls back to the raw key (`:52`) and
`isGoverned` still reports `true`, so the pair is simply unmatched. **Never repair on read** — a
read that rewrites data is a read that can lose a concurrent write.

---

### 18.5 The validation contract

#### Where it is enforced

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — one gate, every write path.** `guardCellEdits`
(`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:43-91`) exists precisely so the Kanban rule cannot be bypassed by
opening the same record's Status cell somewhere else: "Transition rules and conditional options are
*record* rules: they hold wherever the value is written from — a Kanban drag, a cell editor, the
drawer, a paste. Enforcing them in one place is what stops the Kanban rule being bypassable by
opening the same record's Status cell in the table" (`:7-13`).

Every one of these frontend surfaces funnels into `useBoardStore.editCells`, which runs the guard
before it writes anything:

| Surface | Call site |
| --- | --- |
| Kanban drop | `src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:93`, `:276` |
| Table cell editor | `src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx:195` |
| Record drawer field | `src/components/board/drawer/row-drawer.tsx:113` |
| Subtask completion tick | `src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:80` |
| Calendar drag | `src/components/board/views/calendar-board.tsx:72` |
| Gantt bar drag | `src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx:178` |
| Clipboard paste / cut / clear | `src/hooks/use-grid-clipboard.ts:40`, `:57`, `:76` |
| Attachment field | `src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:58` |
| Bulk edit | `src/store/board-store.ts:565-585` (a second, independent call to the same guard) |

**RECOMMENDATION — the backend must re-run the identical gate.** Today `guardCellEdits` is
client-side only: `board-service.updateCells` does not call it
(`src/services/board-service.ts:488-534`), and neither does `bulkUpdate` (`:966-1000`). Without a
server-side gate the workflow is advisory and any direct API call, or any tab holding a stale
schema, bypasses it. The endpoints that must enforce it:

| Endpoint | Enforce? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E-066 `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` | **Yes** | The one call behind every surface in the table above. |
| E-074 `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/update` | **Yes** | "The same record rules apply to a hundred records as to one" (`src/store/board-store.ts:557-564`). |
| E-077 `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows/bulk/move` | **Yes**, on the destination board | A cross-board move re-reads values into the destination's columns; the destination's rules govern them. |
| E-057 `POST …/columns/{columnId}/convert` | **No** | A conversion rewrites every cell mechanically; a rule that refused the rewrite would strand the board mid-conversion, and the target type's config is fresh anyway. |
| E-062 / E-064 / E-085 (record creation, duplication, import) | **See the open question below** | — |

#### OPEN QUESTION (OQ-102) — do record rules gate record *creation*?

**What is unclear.** Whether a transition rule may refuse an edit that has no "from" — creating a
record with a status already set (E-062), duplicating a record (E-064), or importing a file whose
Status column is populated (E-085).

**Evidence.** The frontend never gates any of them: `guardCellEdits` is called only from
`editCells` and `bulkUpdate` (`src/store/board-store.ts:324`, `:569`), not from `addRow`
(`:356-397`), `duplicateRow` (`:400-…`) or the import commit. On the service side, `createRow`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:294-313`) and `importRows` (`:1183-1216`) write `cells` straight
through. Meanwhile **both** shipped templates govern the empty bucket with a single target —
`"__empty__": ["status_0"]` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:169`, `:259`) — so gating creation on a
board with rules enabled would refuse every import that carries any status other than the first, and
would refuse duplicating a *Verified* bug.

**Recommendation.** **Gate transitions, not creations.** Run the record-rule gate on E-066, E-074
and E-077's destination writes; do **not** run it on E-062, E-064 or E-085. A transition presumes a
prior state, and a record being born has none. Keep the *availability* half of the gate
(`option.isDisabled`) on creation paths, because "switched off in column settings — never
selectable, whatever a record holds" (`src/types/board.ts:72-73`) is a statement about the option,
not about a move; refuse those with `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`. Note that this narrows the board fact
sheet's R-03, which listed E-085 as a gated path.

**Impact if wrong.** Gating creation makes import unusable on any board with rules on, and makes
"Duplicate record" fail on exactly the records people duplicate most. Not gating it leaves one hole:
a member with `row.create` can reach a forbidden status by creating a new record rather than moving
an existing one — which is a *new* record in that status, not a record that skipped the workflow, and
is visible in `row_activity` as a `created` entry.

#### The gate, in order

For each incoming `CellEdit` on a **select** column whose incoming `value.kind === "select"`
(anything else passes straight through, `src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:54-57`):

1. **Short-circuit.** If `transitionRules.enabled` is false **and** no option is `isDisabled` **and**
   no option carries a non-empty `availability` group, the edit is allowed with no further work
   (`:59-68`). A rule-free board pays one map lookup per edit.
2. **Clearing.** If `value.optionIds` is empty, allow (`:77-80`).
3. For each `optionId` in `value.optionIds`, resolve availability in this order and take the **first**
   failure (`resolveOptionAvailability`, `src/lib/select-availability.ts:82-117`):
   1. `option.isDisabled` → refuse, `explanation` = `Turned off in column settings`.
   2. `option.availability` does not hold for this record → refuse,
      `explanation` = `` `Requires ${describeConditionGroup(...)}` `` (§4.15).
   3. `evaluateTransition(column, currentKey(row), option.id)` refuses → refuse, `explanation` =
      the verdict's own sentence (§18.2).
4. If any option failed, the edit is rejected and carries that `explanation` as its message
   (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:82-85`).

**The source row must be read under the same lock as the write.** `currentKey` reads the record's
*stored* first option id, so the "from" the server evaluates is the committed state, not the state
the client believed. A batch that moves the same row twice evaluates the second edit against the
first edit's result — the frontend's guard reads `rowsById` once and does not, so the backend is
**stricter here by construction**; this is correct and must not be softened.

#### What the error looks like

**E-066 refuses the whole batch.** `UpdateCellsResponse` carries exactly `rows` and `conflicts`
(canon §5.5) and has no channel for a per-edit rejection, and E-066 is one transaction. So a batch
containing any rule-refused edit applies **nothing** and returns:

```jsonc
// 409 PATCH /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/rows/cells
{
  "error": {
    "code": "conflict",
    "message": "Status cannot go straight from New to Verified. New can move to Triaged, Won't fix.",
    "detail": "TASK-042",
    "isRetryable": false,
    "reason": "TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED",
    "requestId": "01JB9…"
  }
}
```

`message` is `evaluateTransition`'s sentence **verbatim** — the UI shows it unchanged, which is the
whole point of the API returning it rather than a code the client has to re-render (canon §4.4 rule
1). `detail` carries the offending record's `displayId` so the toast can name it; it is omitted, not
`null`, when a single-record surface made the call. `reason` is `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` instead when
gate 3.1 or 3.2 fired, and the `message` is that gate's `explanation`.

**Canon's "E-066 is always 200, never 409" is about *concurrency*, not about record rules.** The
sentence in canon §3.8 and §6.4 governs stale-revision collisions: those are applied last-write-wins
and reported as `ConflictNotice[]`. A transition refusal is not a collision — it is a business rule
saying the write must not happen at all — and canon §4.3 registers it as `409 / conflict`. See
Chapter notes.

**E-074 skips the refused records and applies the rest.** `BulkResult` has the channel that
`UpdateCellsResponse` lacks, and the frontend's own bulk path already splits the selection rather
than refusing it: "Refusing the whole batch because one record cannot make the move would be worse
than telling the user which ones could not" (`src/store/board-store.ts:557-564`).

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/rows/bulk/update
{
  "requested": 100,
  "rows": [ /* 97 authoritative records */ ],
  "applied": ["…", "…"],
  "skipped": [
    { "rowId": "…", "displayId": "BUG-014", "reason": "rule_blocked" },
    { "rowId": "…", "displayId": "BUG-031", "reason": "rule_blocked" },
    { "rowId": "…", "displayId": "BUG-077", "reason": "archived" }
  ]
}
```

`requested === applied.length + skipped.length` holds, as it must for every bulk response
(canon §3.9).

**RECOMMENDATION — one new `BulkSkipReason` member: `rule_blocked`.** `BulkSkipReason` is
`archived | not_found` today (`src/types/system.ts:24`), and canon §2.7 already sanctions extending
it with `permission_denied` "rather than a parallel array". The type's own comment anticipates
exactly this: "Per-row ACLs live on the backend; when they land they report through this same channel
rather than a second one" (`src/types/system.ts:18-23`). Add the label
`rule_blocked: "blocked by a rule"` beside the two in `BULK_SKIP_LABELS`
(`src/lib/bulk.ts:14-17`), so `describeBulkResult` renders
`Updated 97 records · 3 skipped (blocked by a rule, archived)` with no other change.

#### What the frontend does with it

**In the ordinary case, nothing — because the request is never made.** The client evaluates the same
rules from the schema it already holds and refuses locally, so no round trip happens and the card
never visits the column it was refused from. Two layers do this:

1. **Kanban refuses the drop.** `drop()` checks permission, then `evaluateTransition`, and returns
   before the optimistic write; it nudges the card (`setRefusedId`) and pushes the verdict's
   sentence as an error toast (`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:67-95`). Dragging is
   deliberately never blocked — "a drag that dies under the cursor with no explanation is worse than
   one that is refused out loud" (`:30-35`). Columns the card cannot reach are dimmed from a set
   precomputed at drag start (`allowedTargets`, `:100-108`, `:120-122`).
2. **The store refuses the edit.** `editCells` runs `guardCellEdits` first: "an edit a transition
   rule or a conditional option refuses never becomes an optimistic write, so nothing has to be
   rolled back and no request leaves the client" (`src/store/board-store.ts:317-332`). Each rejection
   becomes one error toast.

**When the server refuses anyway** — a tab whose schema predates a rule change, or a non-browser
client — the store's `write` wrapper catches it, runs the rollback and shows `error.message`:
`revertCellEdits` puts the cell back exactly as `captureCells` recorded it
(`src/store/board-store.ts:190-203`, `:334-348`). The card returns to its column and the toast is the
server's sentence. This is the same rollback the table uses, and it is the PRD's stated Kanban
behaviour — "Thẻ tự động bật ngược lại vị trí cũ kèm thông báo" (`VW-KAN-12`).

For a bulk call the store reports both halves rather than rolling back:
`` `${blocked.size} records could not make that change — ${firstMessage}` ``
(`src/store/board-store.ts:580-585`), then `describeBulkResult` renders the server's `skipped` list
(`src/lib/bulk.ts:57-60`).

#### Sequence — a status change being rejected

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Member
    participant K as kanban-board.tsx
    participant S as board-store.editCells
    participant G as guardCellEdits
    participant API as E-066 PATCH rows/cells
    participant PG as PostgreSQL

    U->>K: drop BUG-014 on the "Verified" column
    K->>K: evaluateTransition(Status, "status_0", "status_4")

    alt refused by the rules already loaded (the normal case)
        K-->>U: toast "Status cannot go straight from New to Verified.<br/>New can move to Triaged, Won't fix."
        Note over K,API: no request is made; the card never leaves "New"
    else allowed on the client
        K->>S: editCells([{ rowId, columnId: Status, value }])
        S->>G: same gate over the batch
        G-->>S: allowed
        S->>S: optimistic write + captureCells(reverts)
        S->>API: { edits, baseRevisions }
        API->>PG: BEGIN · SELECT board_rows.cells FOR UPDATE<br/>SELECT board_columns.config
        PG-->>API: committed first option id + stored transitionRules
        API->>API: gate 1 permission · gate 2 availability · gate 3 transition

        alt the tab held a stale schema, so the server refuses
            API->>PG: ROLLBACK
            API-->>S: 409 { error: { code: "conflict",<br/>reason: "TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED", message } }
            S->>S: revertCellEdits(reverts)
            S-->>U: toast error.message · card returns to "New"
        else server allows
            API->>PG: UPDATE board_rows SET cells, revision + 1<br/>INSERT row_activity · COMMIT
            API-->>S: 200 UpdateCellsResponse { rows, conflicts }
            S->>S: reconcileRows(result.rows)
            API-->>U: RT-07 row.updated { boardId, rowId, revision } to other tabs
        end
    end
```

---

### 18.6 Audit and realtime, stated once

| Event | Audit row | Realtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rules enabled, replaced, disabled or cleared (E-053) | `audit_events`: module `board`, action `board.column.update`, severity `info`, `detail` naming the column; `context` records `transitionRulesEnabled` before/after (T-36, OQ-25) | RT-10 `board.schema.changed { boardId }` |
| A cell write refused by a rule | **No audit row.** A refused business-rule write is not a governance event; `audit_events` records `denied` outcomes for *permission*, not for record rules (`src/types/audit.ts:20`; canon §4.3 `AuditOutcome`) | none |
| A cell write allowed | `row_activity` entry, kind `updated`, one entry per write however many fields it touched (T-14) | RT-07 `row.updated` |

---

## 19. Saved Views

### A saved view stores configuration only, and never records

This is the load-bearing sentence of the whole module, and the frontend states it three times:

> "Presentation only. Records and schema live on the board, so switching views never copies data — a
> view just describes how to read it." — `src/types/board.ts:330-333`

> "A view never owns records — it describes how to read the board's." — `src/lib/board-view.ts:15-21`

> "A saved view is configuration only. Creating one never touches a record."
> — `src/services/board-service.ts:817`

It is enforced by test, not by convention. Three tests assert that `rowsById` keeps its **object
identity** across a view write:

| Test | Asserts | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filters, conjunction and sorts round-trip | `rowsById` is the same object after three view writes | `tests/board-view-config.test.ts:68-90` |
| duplicating copies the configuration, not the records | the copy carries the filters and grouping; `rowsById` unchanged | `:145-165` |
| records are never touched by a reorder | `rowsById` unchanged after `moveViewTo` | `:305-312` |

**Consequences a backend developer must honour:**

- `board_views` (T-15) has **no** foreign key to `board_rows` and no column that could hold one.
- No view endpoint reads, writes, counts or paginates rows. `GET /boards/{boardId}/views` (E-078)
  never touches `board_rows`.
- Switching views is **client-side only**. There is no "activate view" endpoint; the active view id
  lives in the store (`activeViewId`, `src/store/board-store.ts:307`) and is not persisted anywhere
  server-side.
- Deleting a view deletes configuration. The confirm dialog says so: "Everyone on this board loses
  this view, with its filters, sorting and grouping. The records themselves are not affected."
  (`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:374-379`).
- A view is **shared per board**, not per reader. "A saved view is shared, and so is where it sits"
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:851-857`). Per-viewer overrides live in the companion table
  `board_view_preferences` (T-16, E-083, canon OQ-46), never on `board_views`.

PRD anchor: `VW-SAV-18` — "Lưu trữ các góc nhìn, bộ lọc và cách sắp xếp yêu thích thành các Tab truy
cập nhanh", with the edge case "Cột bị xóa trong cấu hình Saved View: Tự động loại bỏ điều kiện lọc
của cột đó và giữ nguyên View"
(`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:96`), which §19's `pruneView` obligation satisfies.

---

### The `SavedViewConfig` contract

`SavedViewConfig` names the whole presentation payload; `SavedView` is that payload plus identity.
Every member maps to one `board_views` column (§4.19); the six documented as JSONB are stored as
documents, the rest as scalars.

```ts
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- vocabulary */

type BoardViewType     = "table" | "kanban" | "calendar" | "gantt";
type FilterConjunction = "and" | "or";
type SortDirection     = "asc" | "desc";
type CellDisplayMode   = "compact" | "wrap" | "full";
type RowHeight         = "short" | "medium" | "tall";
type SubtaskDisplay    = "nested" | "flat" | "hidden";
type GanttZoom         = "week" | "month" | "quarter";   // "day" accepted, coerced to "week"

type FilterOperator =
  | "isNotEmpty" | "isEmpty" | "contains" | "notContains"
  | "is" | "isNot" | "before" | "after" | "onOrBefore" | "onOrAfter";

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------- parts */

/** board_views.filters — a FLAT list. There is no nesting; see §19.1. */
interface ViewFilter {
  readonly id: string;                 // client-minted, stable within the view
  readonly columnId: string;           // board_columns.id on THIS board
  readonly operator: FilterOperator;
  /** Read the way the column reads it: an option id OR its label for select, a
   *  user id OR the person's name for user, `YYYY-MM-DD` for date, free text
   *  otherwise. Always present; the empty string is a value, not an absence. */
  readonly value: string;
}

/** board_views.sorts — multi-level; earlier entries win, later ones break ties. */
interface ViewSort {
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly direction: SortDirection;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ payload */

interface SavedViewConfig {
  readonly filters: readonly ViewFilter[];                             // jsonb
  readonly filterConjunction: FilterConjunction;
  readonly sorts: readonly ViewSort[];                                 // jsonb
  readonly hiddenColumnIds: readonly string[];                         // jsonb
  /** Per-view column order. Ids missing from it fall back to schema position,
   *  appended after every explicitly ordered column. */
  readonly columnOrder: readonly string[];                             // jsonb
  readonly columnWidths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;             // jsonb
  /** A column missing from the map is `compact`. */
  readonly columnDisplay?: Readonly<Record<string, CellDisplayMode>>;  // jsonb
  readonly rowHeight: RowHeight;
  readonly groupByColumnId: string | null;
  readonly hideEmptyGroups: boolean;
  readonly dateColumnId: string | null;
  readonly endDateColumnId: string | null;
  readonly subtaskDisplay?: SubtaskDisplay;                            // default "nested"
  readonly ganttZoom?: GanttZoom;                                      // default "week"
  readonly showDependencies?: boolean;                                 // default true
}

/** The wire shape. `id` and `boardId` are forcibly preserved against any patch. */
interface SavedView extends SavedViewConfig {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
}
```

Source: `src/types/board.ts:334-371`. **Optional versus nullable is not collapsible** (canon C-08):
`columnDisplay?`, `subtaskDisplay?`, `ganttZoom?` and `showDependencies?` may be *absent* and each
absence has a defined default; `groupByColumnId`, `dateColumnId` and `endDateColumnId` are *always
present* and may be `null`. The API must emit them that way — omit the optional keys rather than
sending `null`, and always send the three nullable ones.

**Defaults for a fresh view**, written by the server and not sent by the client
(`src/services/board-service.ts:827-843`):

```json
{
  "filters": [], "filterConjunction": "and", "sorts": [],
  "hiddenColumnIds": [], "columnOrder": [], "columnWidths": {},
  "rowHeight": "medium", "groupByColumnId": null, "hideEmptyGroups": false,
  "dateColumnId": null, "endDateColumnId": null
}
```

`columnDisplay`, `subtaskDisplay`, `ganttZoom` and `showDependencies` are **absent** from a fresh
view, not defaulted into it. They acquire values only when a control writes one.

**`ganttZoom` and the legacy `"day"` — mandatory.** A stored view may still hold `"day"`, a per-day
scale that was removed (`src/types/board.ts:272-281`). The API **accepts `"day"` on read and on
write and coerces it to `"week"`**; it never rejects it (canon §2.6). Storage is `text` with a check
that admits all four values, never an enum that refuses `'day'`.

---

### Which config keys each view type actually reads

Only these combinations are consumed. Everything else is stored and ignored — a view that switches
type keeps the keys the new type does not read, which is what makes switching back lossless.

| Key | table | kanban | calendar | gantt | Reader |
| --- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | --- |
| `filters`, `filterConjunction` | yes | yes | yes | yes | `queryRowIds`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:194-236` |
| `sorts` | yes | yes | yes | yes | same |
| `hiddenColumnIds` | yes | yes | yes | yes | `resolveColumns`, `:24-41` — also narrows what free-text search scans (`use-board-view.ts:106`) |
| `columnOrder` | yes | yes | yes | yes | `resolveColumns`, `:28`, `:40` |
| `columnWidths` | yes | — | — | — | the table grid only; clamped to `[88,720]` on read (`:38`). The Gantt's task-panel width is **local component state**, not this key (`src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx:73`) |
| `columnDisplay` | yes | — | — | — | `src/components/board/table/table-grid.tsx:132`; only `text` and `longText` are flexible (`isFlexibleColumn`, `src/lib/cell-display.ts:60-69`) |
| `rowHeight` | yes | — | — | — | the control is rendered only for `type === "table"` (`view-config-bar.tsx:119-134`) |
| `groupByColumnId` | optional | **required** | — | — | `use-board-view.ts:147`, `:152`; Kanban *is* grouping |
| `hideEmptyGroups` | yes | forced `false` | — | — | `use-board-view.ts:158` — Kanban always shows empty buckets |
| `dateColumnId` | — | — | **required** | start anchor | `use-board-view.ts:148` |
| `endDateColumnId` | — | — | — | end anchor | `use-board-view.ts:149` |
| `subtaskDisplay` | yes | yes | yes | yes | applied **before** grouping (`use-board-view.ts:120-133`) |
| `ganttZoom` | — | — | — | yes | `src/components/board/gantt/gantt-board.tsx:82-83`; normalised on read |
| `showDependencies` | — | — | — | yes | same |

**`VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` fires on a *bad* anchor, never on a *missing* one.** The frontend
creates and retypes views into the "required column is null" state as a matter of course:
`createView(name, type)` sends only a name and a type (`view-tabs.tsx:138`) and the service defaults
`groupByColumnId` to `null` (`board-service.ts:838`); `setViewType(type)` patches the type alone
(`src/store/board-store.ts:919-921`, reached from `view-tabs.tsx:312-337`). Kanban renders a helpful
empty state for it — "Pick a column to group by · Kanban needs a Select or User column to build its
columns from" (`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:111-122`). So:

- A missing `groupByColumnId` on a Kanban view, or a missing `dateColumnId` on a calendar view, is
  **accepted** and returned as `null`.
- A `groupByColumnId` / `dateColumnId` / `endDateColumnId` that does not name a column of this board
  is `404` `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND`.
- A `dateColumnId` or `endDateColumnId` naming a column whose `type` is not `date` is `400`
  `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN`.
- A `groupByColumnId` naming a column whose `type` is not one of `select`, `user`, `date`, `text`
  is `400` `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` — **RECOMMENDATION**, grounded in the picker's own candidate
  set (`GROUPABLE`, `src/components/board/config/group-menu.tsx:16`). Tolerate such a value on
  **read** if one was ever stored; `groupKeyOf` has a working fallback for every column type
  (`src/lib/board-grouping.ts:45-46`).

See Chapter notes — the schema chapter reads this error more strictly.

---

### `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/views`

**Purpose** — List the board's saved views, in tab-strip order. This is what the tab strip renders
and what every filter, sort and grouping control reads its current state from.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **Visibility** on the board's node plus workspace membership. Reading a board
through a view "takes nothing" — the filter, sort and group controls below the tabs are ungated
reading affordances (`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:61-66`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None. The list is bounded by construction (canon §6.3); it still honours a
server-side hard cap, and a board past it is a spec defect rather than a paging problem.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SavedView[]`, ordered by `position` ascending.

```jsonc
// 200
[
  {
    "id": "7c11…", "boardId": "9a2e…", "name": "Triage", "type": "kanban",
    "filters": [
      { "id": "f1", "columnId": "3b0d…", "operator": "isNot", "value": "status_5" }
    ],
    "filterConjunction": "and",
    "sorts": [{ "columnId": "8ee1…", "direction": "desc" }],
    "hiddenColumnIds": [], "columnOrder": [], "columnWidths": {},
    "rowHeight": "medium",
    "groupByColumnId": "3b0d…", "hideEmptyGroups": false,
    "dateColumnId": null, "endDateColumnId": null,
    "subtaskDisplay": "nested"
  }
]
```

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards` | read | `id = :boardId` → `node_id`. |
| `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | visibility resolution. |
| `board_views` | read | `WHERE board_id = :boardId ORDER BY position`. Index `(board_id, position)`. |

**No read of `board_rows`, ever.**

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown, or not visible to the caller. |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`. |

**Frontend Used By** — delivered inside `BoardSnapshot.board.views` by
`boardService.getBoard` (`src/services/board-service.ts:229-242`); consumed by
`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:96-118` (the strip),
`selectActiveView` (`src/store/board-store.ts:1126-1129`) and
`useBoardView` (`src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:57`).

---

### `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/views`

**Purpose** — Create a saved view, optionally by copying an existing one. **`from` is how
"duplicate" works** — there is no separate duplicate endpoint, because a duplicate is a create whose
configuration came from somewhere.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **`board.view.manage`** on the board's node, plus workspace membership. Manager and
above (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:52`). "Creating, renaming and deleting a saved view changes
what the whole team sees, so it takes `board.view.manage`"
(`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:61-66`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CreateViewRequest`.

```ts
interface CreateViewRequest {
  readonly name: string;                 // 1..120 chars after trim; not unique
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
  /** Copy every SavedViewConfig key from this view. Must belong to the same
   *  board. Absent = a fresh view with the documented defaults. */
  readonly fromViewId?: string;
  /** Explicit overrides applied ON TOP of the copy or the defaults. */
  readonly config?: Partial<SavedViewConfig>;
}
```

**`fromViewId`, not `from`.** The in-memory service takes the whole source object
(`CreateViewInput.from`, `src/services/board-service.ts:810-816`) because it has it in hand; over
HTTP the client must send an id and let the server read the source, or a caller could inject a
configuration the board never held. Everything else about the contract is unchanged.

**Precedence** — defaults, then `fromViewId`'s config, then `config`, then the forced values:
`id` is minted, `boardId` is the path's, `name` and `type` are the body's, `position` is
`max(position) + 1`. Copying never carries the source's `id`, `boardId` or `position`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:845`).

**Duplicate naming is the client's.** The store sends `` `${source.name} copy` ``
(`src/store/board-store.ts:961-975`); the server stores the name it is given and does **not**
de-duplicate. View names are deliberately not unique.

**Response** — `SavedView` — the created view, complete.

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | permission and node state. |
| `board_views` | read | `fromViewId` when present — must satisfy `board_id = :boardId`. |
| `board_views` | read | `SELECT max(position) FROM board_views WHERE board_id = :boardId FOR UPDATE` — the strip is densely ordered, so the tail must be taken under a lock. |
| `board_columns` | read | validating `groupByColumnId` / `dateColumnId` / `endDateColumnId` and pruning any copied ids the schema no longer has. |
| `board_views` | **write** | one `INSERT`. |
| `boards` | **write** | `updated_at = now()` (`src/services/board-service.ts:846`). |
| `audit_events` | **write** | module `board`, action `board.view.manage` (OQ-25). |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The position allocation, the insert, the board touch and the audit
row are atomic. Two managers adding a tab at once must not collide on
`UNIQUE (board_id, position)`.

**Realtime** — **RT-10 `board.schema.changed { boardId }`**. Ids only; the receiver refetches the
schema, matching canon C-11 ("a schema response is a complete array, never a delta").

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — empty `name`, unknown `type`, malformed `config`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` — an anchor of the wrong column type. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — `You do not have permission to create a view` / `Needs the Manager role or above`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` — `fromViewId` unknown or on another board. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` — an anchor names a column this board does not have. |

**Frontend Used By** — `boardService.createView` (`src/services/board-service.ts:818-848`) behind
`useBoardStore.createView` (`src/store/board-store.ts:943-959`) and
`useBoardStore.duplicateView` (`:961-984`); the controls are the strip's **+** menu
(`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:119-147`) and the tab menu's **Duplicate view**
(`:306-309`). Both set the new view active on success.

---

### `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}`

**Purpose** — Partially update a saved view: rename it, change its type, or write any
`SavedViewConfig` key. This is the single endpoint behind every filter, sort, group, date-anchor,
row-height, subtask, Gantt and column-presentation control on the board.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **`board.view.manage`** on the board's node, plus workspace membership.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |
| `viewId` | UUID | `board_views.id`; must satisfy `board_id = :boardId`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `UpdateViewRequest`.

```ts
interface UpdateViewRequest extends Partial<SavedViewConfig> {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly type?: BoardViewType;
}
```

**Patch semantics — replace per key, never merge inside a key.** `columnWidths` and `columnDisplay`
are maps, and the client always sends the **whole** map after spreading its own copy
(`src/store/board-store.ts:1048-1074`). The server stores what it is given. Sending
`{"columnWidths": {"3b0d…": 240}}` therefore **discards every other width**, which is exactly what
the client intends and exactly what it sends.

**`id` and `boardId` are forcibly preserved against the patch**, even if present in the body:
`{ ...view, ...patch, id: view.id, boardId: view.boardId }`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:800-802`). **`position` is not patchable here** — the tab strip is
reordered by E-082 alone.

**Changing the type is an ordinary patch.** `{"type": "kanban"}` and nothing else. The view keeps
every key the new type does not read, so switching table → kanban → table is lossless
(`src/store/board-store.ts:919-921`; the menu at
`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:312-337` also sets the view active first, "so the type
change lands on this view, whichever tab was active when the menu opened").

**Response** — `SavedView` — the authoritative view. Every caller replaces its optimistic copy with
it (canon C-10; `patchActiveView`'s rollback closes over the fields it touched,
`src/store/board-store.ts:245-259`).

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | permission and node state. |
| `board_views` | read | `SELECT … WHERE id = :viewId AND board_id = :boardId FOR UPDATE`. |
| `board_columns` | read | validating anchors and every `columnId` inside `filters`, `sorts`, `columnOrder`, `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnWidths`, `columnDisplay`. |
| `board_views` | **write** | one `UPDATE` of the named columns plus `updated_at`. |
| `boards` | **write** | `updated_at = now()` (`src/services/board-service.ts:803`). |
| `audit_events` | **write** | one row per patch, action `board.view.manage`. **RECOMMENDATION:** coalesce the high-frequency presentation writes (a column resize commits one call per drag) — see the note under E-083. |

**Transaction** — **Required**, and short. The read-modify-write of a single row plus the board
touch and the audit row. No cross-row work: a view patch never reaches `board_rows` and never
reaches another view.

**Realtime** — **RT-10 `board.schema.changed { boardId }`**.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — unknown key, wrong JSON type, empty `name`, a `columnWidths` value outside `[88,720]` after rounding (clamp rather than refuse, matching `clampColumnWidth`, `src/lib/board-schema.ts:70-72`), a duplicate `columnId` in `sorts`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` — an anchor of the wrong column type. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — `Needs the Manager role or above`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` — `That view could not be found` (`src/services/board-service.ts:806`). |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`, `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `boardService.updateView` (`src/services/board-service.ts:790-808`) behind
`patchActiveView` (`src/store/board-store.ts:245-259`), which every one of these actions calls:
`setSorts`, `setFilters`, `setFilterConjunction`, `setGroupBy`, `setHideEmptyGroups`,
`setDateColumn`, `setEndDateColumn`, `setViewType`, `setRowHeight`, `setSubtaskDisplay`,
`setGanttZoom`, `setShowDependencies` (`:879-941`), plus `renameView` (`:985-999`),
`commitColumnWidth` (`:1048-1060`), `setColumnDisplay` (`:1062-1074`), `setColumnHidden`
(`:1076-1091`) and `moveColumnTo` (`:1093-1119`). UI: `FilterMenu`, `SortMenu`, `GroupMenu`,
`DateMenu` (`src/components/board/config/`), the row-height and subtask pickers
(`view-config-bar.tsx:102-134`) and the tab menu (`view-tabs.tsx:300-337`).

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}`

**Purpose** — Remove a saved view from the board. The records are untouched.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **`board.view.manage`** on the board's node, plus workspace membership.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |
| `viewId` | UUID | `board_views.id`; must satisfy `board_id = :boardId`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SavedView[]` — **the remaining views, in order**, not `204`. The store assigns the
response straight into `board.views` and re-points `activeViewId` at `views[0]` when it deleted the
active tab (`src/store/board-store.ts:1024-1039`). Canon C-10 makes this the rule, not a preference.

**A board always keeps at least one view.** Deleting the last one is refused with `409`
`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`, message `A board needs at least one view`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:887-892`). The check reads the **current committed count** inside
the transaction, not a count the client sent.

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | permission and node state. |
| `board_views` | read | `SELECT count(*) … WHERE board_id = :boardId FOR UPDATE` — the last-view guard. |
| `board_views` | **write** | `DELETE WHERE id = :viewId`, then a dense renumber of the survivors to `0..n-1`. |
| `board_view_preferences` | **write** | `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `board_views` (T-16) — per-viewer overrides die with the view they override. |
| `boards` | **write** | `updated_at = now()`. |
| `audit_events` | **write** | action `board.view.manage`, `detail` naming the deleted view. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The count check, the delete, the renumber and the cascade are one
unit. Without it two concurrent deletes each see two views and leave the board with none.

**Realtime** — **RT-10 `board.schema.changed { boardId }`**.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `VIEW_LAST_REMAINING` — `A board needs at least one view`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `boardService.deleteView` (`src/services/board-service.ts:878-897`) behind
`useBoardStore.deleteView` (`src/store/board-store.ts:1024-1039`), from the tab menu's **Delete
view** behind a `ConfirmDialog` (`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:361-383`).

---

### `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/views/reorder`

**Purpose** — Move a saved view along the tab strip. The frontend drags view tabs, and the same
move is reachable from the tab menu's **Move left** / **Move right** for anyone without a pointer.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **`board.view.manage`** on the board's node, plus workspace membership. This is the
one presentation write that is explicitly *not* a free reader preference: "The order is the board's,
not the reader's: a saved view is shared, and so is where it sits. Which is why this takes
`board.view.manage` — the same key that guards creating and deleting one"
(`src/services/board-service.ts:851-857`). The service checks it before anything else
(`:865`), and a test asserts the refusal (`tests/board-view-config.test.ts:361-364`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `ReorderViewsRequest`.

```ts
interface ReorderViewsRequest {
  readonly viewId: string;
  /** Destination index in the strip, 0-based. CLAMPED, not validated:
   *  a drop past the last tab means "last", which is what the gesture
   *  looked like (src/lib/board-view.ts:258-262, :271). */
  readonly toIndex: number;
}
```

`toIndex` is `Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(toIndex), 0), views.length - 1)`
(`src/lib/board-view.ts:271`). A non-integer, a negative or an out-of-range index is **never an
error**.

**Response** — `SavedView[]` — the whole strip in its new order. A move that changes nothing returns
the strip unchanged and writes nothing (`src/services/board-service.ts:871-872`;
`reorderViews` returns the identical array, `src/lib/board-view.ts:269`, `:272`). That identity check
is what lets the client skip the round trip for a drop that landed back where it started
(`src/store/board-store.ts:1005-1007`).

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | permission and node state. |
| `board_views` | read | `SELECT id, position … WHERE board_id = :boardId ORDER BY position FOR UPDATE`. |
| `board_views` | **write** | dense renumber of the whole strip to `0..n-1` in one statement, under the deferred `UNIQUE (board_id, position)`. |
| `boards` | **write** | `updated_at = now()`. |
| `audit_events` | **write** | action `board.view.manage`. |

**Transaction** — **Required**, over the whole strip. `UNIQUE (board_id, position)` is
`DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` (§4.19) precisely so the renumber can be a single statement that
passes through intermediate collisions.

**Realtime** — **RT-10 `board.schema.changed { boardId }`**.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — `You do not have permission to reorder views` / `Needs the Manager role or above` (`src/services/board-service.ts:865`). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` — an unknown `viewId`. **`reorderViews` treats it as a no-op client-side** (`src/lib/board-view.ts:269`); the API is stricter because a request naming a view that is not there is a real mismatch worth reporting. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `boardService.reorderView` (`src/services/board-service.ts:859-876`) behind
`useBoardStore.moveViewTo` (`src/store/board-store.ts:998-1022`), from the tab drag
(`src/components/board/config/view-tabs.tsx:75-83`, `:205-233`) and the tab menu's **Move left** /
**Move right** (`:339-354`). The rollback is instructive and the backend should not fight it: it
undoes the move **by moving the view back**, not by restoring a snapshot of the array, because "a
rename that landed while this was in flight lives in that array too, and undoing the move should not
undo somebody else's edit with it" (`src/store/board-store.ts:1014-1021`).

---

### `PUT /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}/preferences`

**Purpose** — Store one viewer's private overrides on a shared view: their column widths and their
collapsed groups. **RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-46, E-083).** It exists so a Viewer can resize a column
without holding `board.view.manage` and without changing the board for everyone else.
**Authentication** — Required.
**Permission** — **Visibility** on the board's node plus workspace membership. No
`board.view.manage`: the row is the caller's own and can affect nobody else.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |
| `viewId` | UUID | `board_views.id`; must satisfy `board_id = :boardId`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `UpdateViewPreferencesRequest` — a whole-document replace, per canon P-07.

```ts
interface ViewPreferences {
  readonly viewId: string;
  /** Per-viewer overrides of the shared view's widths. Same clamp, [88,720]. */
  readonly columnWidths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  /** Group keys this viewer has folded, including "__ungrouped__". */
  readonly collapsedGroupKeys: readonly string[];
  /** Parent record ids whose subtasks this viewer has folded. */
  readonly collapsedParentRowIds: readonly string[];
}

type UpdateViewPreferencesRequest = Omit<ViewPreferences, "viewId">;
```

**Response** — `ViewPreferences` — the stored document.

**Resolution order the client already implements.** `resolveColumns` merges schema and view in one
function (`src/lib/board-view.ts:24-41`); preferences slot in as the last, narrowest layer:
effective width = `preferences.columnWidths[id] ?? view.columnWidths[id] ?? column.width`, clamped.
Because the merge point is a single function, adding the layer is contained
(`docs/BOARD.md:312-315`).

**What stays shared, and why.** Canon's position on OQ-46: `board_views` keeps `filters`, `sorts`,
`groupByColumnId`, `hideEmptyGroups`, the date anchors, `type` and `name` — **"filters and sorts stay
shared: they are what a named view *is*"**. "This Sprint" has to mean the same thing to everyone on
the board, or it is not a view a team can agree on.

**What this endpoint changes about today's behaviour.** Column widths and collapse state are the two
that move:

| State | Today | With E-083 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columnWidths` | written to the shared view (`src/store/board-store.ts:1048-1060`) — one person's resize reaches everyone | per viewer, shared value as the default |
| collapsed groups / parents | **in-memory only**, per view id, lost on reload (`src/store/grid-store.ts:49-56`, `:169-192`; the store is not persisted) | per viewer, durable |
| `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnOrder`, `rowHeight`, `columnDisplay` | shared | **stay shared** — canon OQ-46 moves only widths and collapse state |

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | read | visibility. |
| `board_views` | read | existence and ownership by `boardId`. |
| `board_view_preferences` | **write** | `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (view_id, user_id) DO UPDATE` — one row per `(view, user)`, T-16. `user_id` comes from the session and **never** from the body (canon C-09). |

**Transaction** — Not required beyond the single upsert's own atomicity. Nothing else is written; no
board touch, because the shared view did not change.

**Realtime** — **None.** The row is visible to one person; a frame would tell other viewers about a
change they cannot see (canon RT-05's precedent: a frame must never be the thing that leaks).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — a width outside `[88,720]` after rounding is clamped, not refused; a non-numeric width is refused. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` — a trashed node accepts nothing but `node.delete`. **`NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` does not apply**: a per-viewer reading preference on an archived board is a read affordance, not a write to the board. |

**Frontend Used By** — **nothing today.** The store writes widths to the shared view
(`useBoardStore.commitColumnWidth`, `src/store/board-store.ts:1048-1060`) and keeps collapse state in
`useGridStore` (`setCollapsedGroups` / `setCollapsedParents`, `src/store/grid-store.ts:177-192`,
read through `selectCollapsedGroups` / `selectCollapsedParents`, `:268-279`). Those two call sites
are the migration surface; `resolveColumns` is where the merge lands.

**RECOMMENDATION on write volume.** A column drag commits one `PUT` on mouse-up
(`commitColumnWidth`, not the per-frame `resizeColumn`, `src/store/board-store.ts:1041-1046`), so the
rate is already bounded. Collapse toggles are not: coalesce them behind the client's existing debounce
before this endpoint ships, and do **not** write an audit row for a preference — it is not a
governance event.

---

### 19.1 Filter Engine

**PRD anchor `VW-FLT-15`** — "Người dùng thiết lập điều kiện lọc (VD: `Status != Done AND Priority =
High AND Assignee = Thanh`). Hệ thống áp dụng bộ lọc tức thì trên Table, Kanban, Calendar và
Timeline", p95 < 200 ms over 5 000 rows, and an empty result is a state rather than an error
(`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:84`).

#### The DTO — flat, not nested

**There is no `FilterGroup` and no `FilterCondition` in this system.** A view's filter set is a
**flat array plus one conjunction**:

```ts
interface ViewFilter {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly operator: FilterOperator;
  readonly value: string;
}

type FilterConjunction = "and" | "or";

// on SavedView:
//   readonly filters: readonly ViewFilter[];
//   readonly filterConjunction: FilterConjunction;
```

`src/types/board.ts:296-309`. The nested shape does exist in this codebase — `ConditionGroup` /
`Condition`, with arbitrary nesting and its own operator set (`src/types/board.ts:38-64`) — but it
governs **conditional select-option availability** (§4.15, §18.5), not view filters, and the two
vocabularies are different (see below). Canon §5.2 fixes both names; a chapter must not rename or
re-scope them.

**Why the flat shape is right here and must not be "upgraded".** One conjunction over a flat list is
what the filter bar renders — a row of removable pills plus an all-of/any-of toggle
(`src/components/board/config/filter-menu.tsx:36-59`, and the pill strip at
`src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:136-162`). Nesting would need an expression editor
the product does not have, and it would change the meaning of every saved view already stored.

**`ConditionOperator` is not a superset of `FilterOperator`,** despite the comment at
`src/types/board.ts:20-24` claiming it is (canon §2.5, OQ-37). They overlap:

| | `FilterOperator` (views) | `ConditionOperator` (option availability) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shared | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `notContains`, `before`, `after`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` | same |
| only here | `onOrBefore`, `onOrAfter` | `isAnyOf`, `isNoneOf`, `on` |

**Ship two enums.** A backend that folds them into one will accept `isAnyOf` on a view filter, which
`matchesFilter` cannot evaluate (it falls through to `default: return true`,
`src/lib/board-view.ts:99-100`) — a filter that silently matches everything.

#### The exact operator set per column type

Transcribed from `OPERATORS_BY_TYPE` (`src/lib/board-filters.ts:24-59`). **The order is the offered
order**, and the first entry is what `makeFilter` selects when a filter is added (`:80-83`).

| Column type | Operators, in offer order |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `notContains`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `longText` | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `notContains`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `select` | `is`, `isNot`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `user` | `is`, `isNot`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `date` | `is`, `before`, `after`, `onOrBefore`, `onOrAfter`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `attachment` | `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| `relation` | `contains`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |

"Operators are per cell type: 'contains' is meaningless on a date and 'before' is meaningless on a
select, so neither is offered there" (`src/lib/board-filters.ts:4-9`).

**Server-side validation.** A `ViewFilter` whose `operator` is not in its column's row is `400`
`VALIDATION_FAILED` on E-079 / E-080. The client cannot produce one: changing a filter's column runs
`reconcileOperator`, which keeps the operator if the new type supports it and otherwise takes that
type's first (`src/lib/board-filters.ts:86-89`).

**The value input the UI renders**, for completeness — `valueKindFor`
(`src/lib/board-filters.ts:64-77`): presence operators → `none`; `select` → `option` picker; `user` →
`user` picker; `date` → date picker; everything else → free text.

#### Matching semantics, per branch

`matchesFilter(row, filter, column, context)` (`src/lib/board-view.ts:49-102`). The cell is read
through `cellOf`, which returns the column's **empty value** when the stored cell's `kind` no longer
matches the column's `type` — a schema change that raced an edit is treated as empty, never rendered
by the wrong reader (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:38-46`).

**1 — Presence operators, first and unconditional.**
`isEmpty` → `isCellEmpty(value)`; `isNotEmpty` → its negation. `filter.value` is **ignored entirely**
(`:57-58`). Emptiness per kind (`isCellEmpty`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:48-64`):

| Kind | Empty when |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `longText` | `value.trim().length === 0` |
| `select` | `optionIds.length === 0` **and** no `text` escape hatch |
| `date` | `iso === null` **and** no `text` |
| `user` | `userIds.length === 0` **and** no `text` |
| `attachment` | `attachments.length === 0` |
| `relation` | `rowIds.length === 0` **and** no `text` |

The `text` clause matters: a select cell holding unparsed text from a column conversion is **not
empty** (`src/types/board.ts:214-218`).

**2 — Date cells** (`matchesDate`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:112-139`). **Calendar days, never
instants** (canon C-04):

- `iso === null` → **`false`**, for every operator. A record with no date never matches a date
  comparison.
- `Date.parse(filter.value)` is `NaN` → **`true`**, permissive. An unparsable or empty bound does not
  hide rows.
- otherwise compare `dayNumber(iso.slice(0,10))` against `dayNumber(bound)`, where
  `dayNumber(iso) = Math.floor(Date.parse(iso.slice(0,10)) / 86_400_000)`:
  `is` → `=`; `before` → `<`; `after` → `>`; `onOrBefore` → `<=`; `onOrAfter` → `>=`.
- any other operator → `true`.

**The `.slice(0,10)` is the whole date-key layer in one call.** A `date` column with
`includesTime: true` still filters by its calendar day; the instant is never widened or narrowed
through a timezone (`src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24`).

**3 — Identity cells** (`select`, `user`, `relation`) (`src/lib/board-view.ts:64-85`). The needle is
`filter.value.trim().toLowerCase()`; the haystack is the cell's **ids** and its **rendered label**:

```
hit = ids.any(id => id.toLowerCase() === needle)
   || label === needle
   || (operator is contains|notContains && label.includes(needle))
```

`is`/`contains` return `hit`; `isNot`/`notContains` return `!hit`; anything else returns `true`.
`label` is `cellText(value, column, context)` lower-cased — option labels joined with `", "`, people's
names joined with `", "`, relation targets' display ids or `[Deleted Item]`
(`src/lib/cell-values.ts:83-121`).

**Matching an id *or* a label is deliberate**: "a filter written by the UI (an id) and one written by
hand (a name) agree" (`src/lib/board-view.ts:62-63`). The backend must accept both. It also means
`Status is status_4` and `Status is Verified` are the same filter, and both survive a rename of the
option in only one direction — the id form survives, the label form starts matching a different
status. That is the FE's behaviour and this spec does not change it.

**4 — Everything else** (`text`, `longText`, `attachment`) (`:87-101`). Compare
`cellText(...).toLowerCase()` against the trimmed lower-cased needle: `contains` → `includes`;
`notContains` → `!includes`; `is` → `===`; `isNot` → `!==`; anything else → `true`.

#### How an empty value behaves — the exact rule

`makeFilter` creates every new filter with `value: ""` (`src/lib/board-filters.ts:80-83`), so this is
not an edge case: **it is the state of every filter the moment it is added.** The empty string is a
**value**, not an absence, and it is compared as one. There is no "ignore filters with no value"
guard anywhere in `matchesFilter`.

| Branch | Operator | Behaviour with `value: ""` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any | `isEmpty` / `isNotEmpty` | value ignored; the filter is fully meaningful |
| `date` | any | rows **with** a date match; rows with `iso === null` do **not** — `Date.parse("")` is `NaN`, so the bound is permissive, but the null guard fires first |
| identity, text | `contains` | matches **every** row — `"anything".includes("")` is always true |
| identity, text | `notContains` | matches **no** row |
| identity, text | `is` | matches rows whose rendered label is exactly `""`, i.e. effectively the empty ones |
| identity, text | `isNot` | the complement of the above |

**Consequence the UI shows and the backend must reproduce.** For a `text` column the offered order
puts `is` first, so adding a Title filter immediately narrows the board to records with an empty
Title. The pill renders `Name is` with no value (`describeFilter`,
`src/lib/board-filters.ts:91-97`), which is the honest rendering of exactly that. **Do not "fix" this
server-side.** A backend that skips valueless filters would return a different row set from the one
the client shows, and the disagreement would be invisible until someone counted.

#### Conjunction

One conjunction governs the whole flat list (`src/lib/board-view.ts:219-221`):

- `filterConjunction === "or"` → `filters.some(test)`;
- anything else (including a missing value) → `filters.every(test)`;
- **zero filters → everything passes**, checked before either branch (`filters.length === 0`).

**Filters naming a column the schema no longer has are dropped before evaluation, not failed**
(`src/lib/board-view.ts:204`). This is the same tolerance `pruneView` makes permanent
(`:288-334`) and the same rule `VW-SAV-18` states: "Cột bị xóa trong cấu hình Saved View: Tự động
loại bỏ điều kiện lọc của cột đó và giữ nguyên View."

**Free-text search is not a filter.** `search` is a separate needle matched against `row.displayId`
**and** the text of every *visible* column (`rowMatchesSearch`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:238-249`; the
columns passed in are `columnsShown`, `src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:106`). It is not stored on the
view and never persists. The order of operations in `queryRowIds` is fixed:

```
archived exclusion  ->  filters (+conjunction)  ->  free-text search  ->  sort
```

(`src/lib/board-view.ts:194-236`.) Any server-side implementation must apply the same order, because
search scans only the columns the view leaves visible and a filter on a hidden column still applies.

---

#### Passing a filter to the row list — the transport

##### EXISTING REQUIREMENT: today, you do not

`GET /boards/{boardId}/rows` (E-061) takes `?cursor=&limit=&includeArchived=` and **no filter
parameter** (canon §3.8). The frontend loads the whole record set and filters it in the browser:
`getBoard` returns every row with `nextCursor: null`
(`src/services/board-service.ts:229-242`, and the comment at `:239` — "The whole record set arrives
in one page today"), and `queryRowIds` runs over `rowOrder` on every keystroke
(`src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:100-112`). Canon's position on OQ-36 is the same: "Real `nextCursor`
on `(position, id)`; the client fetches pages eagerly until server-side query lands."

**So the filter transport is a RECOMMENDATION for a capability that does not exist yet.** Nothing
calls it today, and it must not be built before the threshold below is crossed.

##### RECOMMENDATION: a JSON body on a POST query endpoint

**Decision: `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/query` with the filter set in the request body.**
This is a **new endpoint** — canon's registry ends at E-140 and does not carry it; adding it requires
appending to canon §3.8. See Chapter notes.

**The two candidates.**

| | `GET …/rows?filter=<encoded>` | `POST …/rows/query` with a JSON body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Payload size | capped by the URL limit | capped by the body limit (`REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`, 413) |
| Encoding | the filter set must be base64url'd or percent-encoded; `+`, `&`, `#` and non-ASCII labels all need care, and a double-encoding bug is silent | JSON, exactly the shape the view already stores |
| Cacheability | cacheable in principle | not cacheable |
| Bookmarkable | yes | no |
| REST purity | a read is a GET | a read behind a POST |

**Why POST wins here.**

1. **URL length is a real ceiling, and this payload has no bound.** A `ViewFilter` carries a UUID
   `columnId` (36 bytes), an operator and a free-text value; a `ViewSort` carries another UUID. A
   ten-filter view with three sort levels, a search term and a cursor is roughly 700–1 200 bytes
   before encoding and 950–1 600 after base64url — already past IE-era limits and uncomfortably close
   to the 2 048-byte figure many corporate proxies and WAFs still enforce. And the payload grows
   without a bound the product controls: a user may type a paragraph into a `contains` value, and if
   the availability vocabulary (`isAnyOf` with a `values` list, §4.15) is ever admitted into view
   filters the set operators alone can carry dozens of ids. A transport whose failure mode is a
   truncated or refused request at an unpredictable size is not a transport.
2. **The cache benefit is not available anyway.** The response is permission-filtered per caller
   (subtree-wide pruning, canon E-020) and invalidated by every cell write on the board, so no shared
   cache may hold it and a private cache would be stale within seconds.
3. **The body is already the shape.** The request is `SavedViewConfig`'s `filters`,
   `filterConjunction` and `sorts` verbatim — the same JSON the view stores and the same JSON E-080
   accepts. No second encoding, no second parser, no drift.
4. **Canon already permits the verb.** P-05: a verb is a path segment when REST cannot express the
   operation, and `/query` joins `/search`, `/reorder`, `/convert` and `/bulk/*` on that list. P-03 is
   satisfied — `/boards/{boardId}/rows/query` is one level below the aggregate.

**Bookmarkability is not lost**, because the thing worth bookmarking is the *view*, which already has
a URL and an id. An ad-hoc filter set is transient by design — the pill strip's "Clear all" is one
click (`src/components/board/config/view-config-bar.tsx:157-160`).

**E-061 stays.** The unfiltered `GET` remains the cheap path for "give me this board's rows"; the
POST is the query form, and the two return the same `RowPage`.

```ts
interface RowQueryRequest {
  /** Same DTO the saved view stores. An empty array matches everything. */
  readonly filters?: readonly ViewFilter[];
  readonly filterConjunction?: FilterConjunction;   // default "and"
  /** Multi-level; earlier entries win. See §19.2. */
  readonly sorts?: readonly ViewSort[];
  /** Free-text needle. Scanned across displayId and the columns named in
   *  `visibleColumnIds`, matching rowMatchesSearch exactly. */
  readonly search?: string;
  /** The view's visible columns, so search scans what the reader can see.
   *  Absent = every column. */
  readonly visibleColumnIds?: readonly string[];
  /** SY-ARC-37: archived records stay out unless asked for. Default false. */
  readonly includeArchived?: boolean;
  /** Opaque; base64 of the sort-key tuple. Never constructed by a client. */
  readonly cursor?: string | null;
  readonly limit?: number;                           // server-capped
}

interface RowPage {
  readonly items: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

**Alternatively, and preferably where it fits: `viewId`.** A client rendering a saved view should
send `{ "viewId": "7c11…", "search": "…", "cursor": null }` and let the server read the stored
configuration, so the filter set travels once (at save time) instead of on every page. The inline
`filters`/`sorts` form is for the unsaved, in-flight state the pill strip produces. Both forms return
the same `RowPage`; sending both is `400` `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

**Permission** — visibility on the board's node, exactly as E-061. A query endpoint must not become a
way to learn about rows a `GET` would not return.
**Errors** — `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`, `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` (a filter or sort names a column this board does
not have — **or drop it silently, matching `queryRowIds`; pick one and state it in the endpoint
doc**; this spec recommends **dropping silently for `filters`/`sorts` supplied inline** so a stale
tab behaves like the client does, and `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` when `viewId` is used, since the stored view
should have been pruned), `VALIDATION_FAILED` (operator not offered for the column type),
`REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` (413).

#### When the backend must filter, and the migration path

**The threshold.** Two numbers in the source agree, and they are the same number:

- `docs/BOARD.md:317` — client-side query "is fine at 5.000 rows and wrong at 100.000".
- `VW-FLT-15` — p95 < 200 ms over **5 000 rows**; `docs/BOARD.md:145` — "the target is 5.000 records
  with no jank".
- `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5_000` (`src/config/app.ts:48`) already caps a single import at the same figure.

**RECOMMENDATION — `BOARD_CLIENT_QUERY_MAX_ROWS = 5000`, served from `GET /config` (E-139) so the two
sides cannot disagree** (canon E-139 already ships the client's limits this way). The rule:

| Board's live (non-archived) row count | Who filters |
| --- | --- |
| ≤ 5 000 | **The client.** E-047 returns the whole set with `nextCursor: null`; `queryRowIds` runs in the browser, which is what makes filter, sort, group and search feel instant and lets an offline tab keep working. |
| > 5 000 | **The server.** E-047 returns the first page with a real `nextCursor`; the client sends its filter set to the query endpoint and renders what comes back. |

The switch must be **observable to the client** rather than inferred: `BoardSnapshot` already carries
`nextCursor`, and a non-null value is the signal that the client no longer holds the whole set and
must stop filtering locally (`src/types/board.ts:434-435`). No new field is needed.

**Migration path, in the order it must happen.**

1. **Make `nextCursor` real** (canon OQ-36). E-047 and E-061 page on `(position, id)`. The client
   already fetches pages eagerly, so nothing else changes yet and `queryRowIds` still runs over the
   full set once the pages have landed.
2. **Move archived exclusion server-side.** `includeArchived` already exists on E-061; make it the
   authoritative filter rather than a client-side `continue` (`src/lib/board-view.ts:212`). This is
   the only filter the server owns today and it is the cheapest one to prove correct.
3. **Ship `POST …/rows/query`** implementing §19.1 and §19.2 **exactly** — including "empties always
   sink", select-by-option-order sorting, id-or-label matching, and the empty-value rules above.
   Verify it against the frontend's own comparator on a seeded board before switching anything over.
4. **Flip one board.** `use-board-view.ts` funnels every view through one call
   (`queryRowIds`, `src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:100-112`), so the swap is a single call site —
   "the client already funnels every view through one function, so the swap is contained"
   (`docs/BOARD.md:316-320`).
5. **Move grouping last**, and only if §19.3's precondition is met.

**What must not change during the migration.** The saved view's stored shape. `SavedViewConfig` is
the query language; making the server understand it is an implementation change, not a contract
change, and every view already stored must keep meaning what it meant.

#### Reaching inside `cells` — how the operators land in PostgreSQL

Documentation of the mapping, so step 3 above is unambiguous. `board_rows.cells` is
`Record<columnId, CellValue>` (canon §1.3.2); `:col` is the column's id used as a JSONB key.

| Column type | Projection used for comparison | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text`, `longText` | `cells -> :col ->> 'value'` | lower-cased both sides; `contains` is a substring test |
| `select` | `cells -> :col -> 'optionIds'` (a JSON array) plus the rendered label | id match is array containment; label match needs the option list from `board_columns.config` |
| `user` | `cells -> :col -> 'userIds'` plus the directory name | same shape |
| `relation` | `cells -> :col -> 'rowIds'` plus the target's `display_id` | same shape |
| `date` | the **generated columns** `due_date DATE` / `due_at TIMESTAMPTZ` where the board designates the role, else `left(cells -> :col ->> 'iso', 10)` | compare day keys, never instants (canon §1.3.2, C-04) |
| `attachment` | `jsonb_array_length(cells -> :col -> 'attachments')` | only presence operators exist |

**Indexes.** GIN `jsonb_path_ops` on `cells` serves containment for the identity kinds; the three
generated projections canon §1.3.2 requires (`due_date`, `due_at`, `status_option_id`,
`assignee_ids`) serve the hot filters the product actually runs — My Work, the deadline dashboard and
"my open bugs". **Do not index the whole document for substring search**; free-text search is the
`tsvector` column on `board_rows` (canon §1.2), not a `LIKE` over JSONB.

**The label half of an identity match cannot be indexed** and must not be pretended otherwise: it
requires the column's option list or the directory. Resolve labels to ids **before** the query where
possible — the UI already sends an option id from its picker (`valueKindFor` → `option`,
`src/lib/board-filters.ts:68-70`) — and treat the label path as the compatibility branch it is.

---

### 19.2 Sorting

**PRD anchor `VW-SRT-16`** — multi-level sort, "Cấp 1 sắp xếp theo `Priority DESC`, Cấp 2 sắp xếp
theo `Due Date ASC`", p95 < 100 ms, and the edge case that decides everything below: "Ô có giá trị
Null/Rỗng: Luôn tự động đưa về cuối danh sách"
(`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:85`).

#### The DTO

```ts
interface ViewSort {
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly direction: "asc" | "desc";
}

// on SavedView:  readonly sorts: readonly ViewSort[];
```

`src/types/board.ts:311-314`. **Multi-level: earlier entries win, later ones break ties**
(`:341`). There is no `id` on a sort level — the array position *is* the level, and the level's own
identity is its `columnId`.

**One level per column.** The sort menu offers each column to at most one level: a level keeps its
own column and offers the ones no other level has claimed, because "taking one twice would make the
second copy dead weight, since the first already settled that key"
