### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/uploads`

**Purpose** — Reserve an upload: validate everything that can be validated before the bytes
move, then hand back a presigned `PUT` target and the `uploadId` that step 3 completes.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `file.upload` on the destination, **plus** workspace membership. The
destination is the folder named by `folderId`; `null` means the workspace root and the check
is then `capabilitiesFor({ role, user, node: null }).upload`, exactly as `canUploadTo` does
(`src/store/upload-store.ts:182-190`). The `upload` capability is narrowed to false by lock
and by archive (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:139-140`, `src/lib/archive.ts:48-50`) — you
cannot add files to a frozen folder.

**Additionally, per `purpose`:**

| `purpose` | Extra check |
| --- | --- |
| `drive` | none beyond `file.upload` on `folderId` |
| `documentBlock` | `document.update` on the page node named by `ownerNodeId` |
| `boardCell` | `row.update` on the board node named by `ownerNodeId` |
| `comment` | `comment.create` on the target node named by `ownerNodeId` |

The `comment` case is the one worth spelling out. Canon binds E-110 to `file.upload`; the
collaboration fact sheet argues for `comment.create` because the upload is part of posting a
comment (OQ-73). **Both are required, never either** — the two narrow, they do not widen,
and Member holds both, so nothing observable changes today while a future role that may
comment but not upload is representable.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | Quota scope and tenant boundary. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CreateUploadRequest`.

```ts
/** Canon §5.4, `files`. */
interface CreateUploadRequest {
  /** Original file name, as picked. The server derives `extension` from it and
   *  never trusts a client-supplied extension field — there is no such field. */
  readonly fileName: string;
  /** Declared byte count. Re-verified against the landed object at E-111. */
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  /** `File.type`, which is "" for many files and is ATTACKER-CONTROLLED.
   *  Recorded as declared, sniffed and cross-checked at E-111 (canon OQ-70). */
  readonly mimeType: string;
  /** Destination folder for a drive upload; null is the workspace root
   *  (src/types/file.ts:17-18). */
  readonly folderId: string | null;
  /** Where the asset will be referenced from. Decides the extra permission
   *  check above and the default for `createDriveNode`. */
  readonly purpose: UploadPurpose;
  /** The node the reference will hang off: the page for a document block, the
   *  board for a cell, the comment's target for a comment. Absent for `drive`. */
  readonly ownerNodeId?: string;
  /** Canon OQ-74. Default TRUE for `drive` and `documentBlock`,
   *  FALSE for `boardCell` and `comment`. */
  readonly createDriveNode?: boolean;
}

/** RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-74). No frontend counterpart; the mock has one path. */
type UploadPurpose = "drive" | "documentBlock" | "boardCell" | "comment";
```

**Response** — `CreateUploadResponse`, `201`.

```ts
interface CreateUploadResponse {
  readonly uploadId: string;
  /** Presigned target. Single-use, bound to one key, one content type, one
   *  size ceiling. Never a URL the client composes. */
  readonly uploadUrl: string;
  readonly method: "PUT";
  /** Headers the client MUST send with the PUT, verbatim. */
  readonly headers: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  /** ISO 8601. The PUT must start before this. */
  readonly expiresAt: string;
  /** Server-owned ceiling, echoed so the client can fail fast on a re-pick. */
  readonly maxBytes: number;
}
```

```jsonc
{
  "uploadId": "0192f5aa-…",
  "uploadUrl": "https://objects.example.net/ws-9a2e/up/0192f5aa…?X-Amz-Signature=…",
  "method": "PUT",
  "headers": { "Content-Type": "image/png" },
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-27T09:45:00.000Z",
  "maxBytes": 104857600
}
```

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | read | Membership + role. |
| `nodes` | read | `folderId` must exist, be a container, be visible, and not be trashed/archived/locked; `ownerNodeId` likewise for the non-`drive` purposes. |
| `workspaces` | read | `used_bytes` and the plan's `totalBytes`, for the quota pre-check. |
| `uploads` | **insert** | One row, `state = 'pending'`. |

`uploads` (canon T-32) is the only table this endpoint writes. Its column set, reproduced
here because every endpoint in this section reads or writes it:

| Column | Type | Nullable | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `UUID` PK | no | `gen_random_uuid()`; the `uploadId` on the wire. |
| `workspace_id` | `UUID` | no | FK → `workspaces(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`. |
| `created_by` | `UUID` | no | FK → `users(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Session user; **only this user may complete or abort it.** |
| `storage_key` | `TEXT` | no | `UNIQUE`. Minted by the server; the client never sees it, only the signed URL that wraps it. |
| `declared_name` | `TEXT` | no | `fileName` as sent. |
| `declared_size_bytes` | `BIGINT` | no | `> 0`. |
| `declared_mime_type` | `TEXT` | no | `File.type`, or `application/octet-stream`. |
| `extension` | `TEXT` | no | Derived server-side from `declared_name` by `extensionOf` (`src/lib/node-visuals.ts:211-214`) — lower-cased, no dot, `''` when the name has no dot. |
| `folder_id` | `UUID` | yes | FK → `nodes(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`. |
| `purpose` | `upload_purpose` | no | Postgres enum, four members. |
| `owner_node_id` | `UUID` | yes | FK → `nodes(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`. |
| `create_drive_node` | `BOOLEAN` | no | Resolved default written at insert, so E-111 does not re-derive it. |
| `state` | `upload_state` | no | `pending` \| `completed` \| `aborted` \| `expired`. Default `pending`. |
| `asset_id` | `UUID` | yes | FK → `file_assets(id)` `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Set by E-111. |
| `expires_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no | `now() + interval '30 minutes'`. |
| `created_at` / `completed_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | no / yes | |

Constraints: `CHECK ((state = 'completed') = (asset_id IS NOT NULL))`,
`CHECK (declared_size_bytes > 0)`,
`CHECK ((purpose = 'drive') = (owner_node_id IS NULL))`.
Indexes: `UNIQUE (storage_key)`; `uploads_sweep_idx (state, expires_at) WHERE state =
'pending'` for the reaper; `uploads_owner_idx (created_by, created_at DESC)`.

**Transaction** — Not required. One insert, and the presign is a pure computation. The quota
read here is **advisory**; the authoritative check is E-111's `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`.

**Realtime** — None. A reservation is not an event.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `FILE_EMPTY` — `sizeBytes` is 0. Message `“{name}” is empty` / detail *"Files must contain at least one byte."* (`src/lib/file-validation.ts:29-36`). |
| 400 | `validation` | `FILE_TOO_LARGE` — past the server ceiling. Message `“{name}” exceeds the {N} MB limit` (`:38-45`). |
| 400 | `validation` | `FILE_TYPE_REJECTED` — extension not on the allow-list. Detail is the `ACCEPTED_HINT` string (`:22`, `:47-55`). |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `purpose` unknown; `ownerNodeId` present on `drive` or absent on the other three. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `upload` capability on the destination. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_LOCKED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `FOLDER_NOT_FOUND` — `“{name}” could not be found`; also the answer when the folder is invisible. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown `ownerNodeId`. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` — the object store would not issue a presigned target. |
| **507** | `upload_failed` | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — `used_bytes + sizeBytes > totalBytes` (canon OQ-05). |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/upload-store.ts:68-78` (`fileService.upload`), reached
from every call site listed in §21.1. The `folderId` for a document block is the page's own
parent folder (`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:133` →
`src/components/document/block-editor.tsx:17`); for a board cell it is the board's parent
(`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:81`).

### `POST /api/v1/uploads/:uploadId/complete`

**Purpose** — Turn a landed object into a `file_assets` row, optionally a drive node, and
charge it against the workspace quota. This is the only endpoint that creates a
`file_assets` row.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `file.upload`, re-checked against the destination recorded on the `uploads`
row, **and the caller must be `uploads.created_by`**. A reservation is not transferable: the
`uploadId` is a capability and completing somebody else's would attribute their bytes to
your quota and your name.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uploadId` | UUID | Must be `state = 'pending'` and not past `expires_at`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CompleteUploadRequest`.

```ts
interface CompleteUploadRequest {
  /** Bytes the client believes it sent. Compared with the object store's HEAD;
   *  a mismatch is UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE, not a silent correction. */
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  /** Optional SHA-256 of the object, hex. Recorded on file_assets.checksum. */
  readonly checksum?: string;
}
```

**Response** — `201`.

```ts
/** The asset always; the node only when the upload asked for one. */
interface CompleteUploadResponse {
  readonly asset: FileAsset;
  /** Present iff `uploads.create_drive_node`. Exactly the FileNode the mock
   *  builds today at src/store/workspace-store.ts:716-743. */
  readonly node: FileNode | null;
}
```

```jsonc
{
  "asset": {
    "id": "0192f5b0-…",
    "name": "payment-error.png",
    "extension": "png",
    "mimeType": "image/png",
    "sizeBytes": 248113,
    "kind": "image",
    "owner": { "id": "usr_lan", "name": "Lan Nguyen", "initials": "LN" },
    "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:31:04.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-08-27T09:31:04.000Z",
    "folderId": null
  },
  "node": null
}
```

**Database** — all inside one transaction:

| # | Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `uploads` | read `FOR UPDATE` | The row, its state, `expires_at`, `created_by`, `purpose`, `create_drive_node`, `folder_id`, `storage_key`. Locking it makes completion idempotent under a double-submit. |
| 2 | — | object store | `HEAD storage_key` → real `Content-Length`; read the first bytes for the sniff. |
| 3 | `workspaces` | read `FOR UPDATE` | `used_bytes` and the plan ceiling. C-§1.4: the counter is maintained transactionally, never recomputed by aggregate. |
| 4 | `file_assets` | **insert** | `name`, `extension`, `mime_type`, `size_bytes` (the **HEAD** value, not the declared one), `kind` (derived from extension), `storage_key`, `checksum`, `owner_id`, `folder_id`, `workspace_id`. |
| 5 | `nodes` + `file_nodes` | **insert** | Only when `create_drive_node`. `slug` de-duplicated against the destination's siblings (`uniqueSlug`, mirroring `src/store/workspace-store.ts:719-722`), `owner` = uploader, `is_favorite/is_trashed/is_shared = false`, `file_nodes.version = 1`. |
| 6 | `workspaces` | **update** | `used_bytes = used_bytes + file_assets.size_bytes`. |
| 7 | `uploads` | **update** | `state = 'completed'`, `asset_id`, `completed_at = now()`. |

The **reference row is not written here.** `cell_attachments`, `comment_attachments` and
`document_asset_refs` are written by the endpoint that stores the reference — E-066 for a
cell, E-120 for a comment, E-092 for a document block — in *their* transactions, because
that is the only way the reference and the value it projects cannot drift. Between E-111 and
that write the asset is an orphan; the sweep's grace window (below) is what keeps it alive.

**Transaction** — **Required.** The asset row, the node, the quota increment and the state
transition are one unit. A quota increment without an asset row leaks capacity nobody can
reclaim; an asset row without the increment lets the workspace exceed its plan one upload at
a time. Isolation: `READ COMMITTED` with the two `FOR UPDATE` locks. The workspace row lock
serialises concurrent uploads into the same workspace, which is exactly what a counter
needs.

**Realtime** — **RT-11 `node.changed`** `{ workspaceId, nodeId, change: "created" }` when a
drive node was created, so a second tab's sidebar converges without polling. No frame when
`createDriveNode` is false — a cell or comment attachment announces itself through
RT-07/RT-01 when the referencing write lands.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `FILE_TYPE_REJECTED` — the sniffed type is on the deny-list, whatever the name says. |
| 400 | `validation` | `FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` — sniffed content contradicts the declared extension (canon OQ-70). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — the caller is not `created_by`, or lost `upload` on the destination between the two calls. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown, already completed, aborted, or expired. One reason for all four: an expired reservation and a stolen one must be indistinguishable. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `FOLDER_NOT_FOUND` — the destination was deleted while the bytes were moving. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` — only if slug de-duplication is exhausted; normally impossible. |
| **422** | `upload_failed` | `UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` — the `HEAD` shows no object, or a size that disagrees with `sizeBytes`. `isRetryable: true`. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. |
| 507 | `upload_failed` | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — the authoritative check. A workspace that filled up while the bytes were in flight is refused here; the object is deleted and the row goes to `aborted`. |

**Frontend Used By** — the tail of `src/store/upload-store.ts:68-78`; the returned asset is
handed to `useWorkspaceStore.addUploadedAsset` (`:76`) and then, per surface, to
`attachmentFromAsset` (`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:87-90`), to a `DocumentImage`
(`src/components/document/blocks/image-block.tsx:44-47`) or to an `AttachmentBlock`
(`src/components/document/blocks/attachment-block.tsx:30`).

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/uploads/:uploadId`

**Purpose** — Abort a reservation: the user cancelled, or the transfer failed and will not
be retried.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `file.upload`, and the caller must be `uploads.created_by`.

**Path Params** — `uploadId` (UUID).

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `204`, no body. The one endpoint in this section that returns nothing:
there is no authoritative record to return, because the point is that no record was created
(C-10 is about writes that produce a resource).

**Database** — `uploads`: **update** `state = 'aborted'`. The object at `storage_key` is
deleted best-effort; if the delete fails the nightly sweep collects it. `workspaces.used_bytes`
is **not** touched, because E-111 never ran.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not the reservation's owner. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown or already terminal. |

Aborting an already-aborted upload returns `204`, not `404`: the state requested is the
state achieved, and the client's `cancelUpload` fires the abort locally first
(`src/store/upload-store.ts:149-152`), so a retry is normal.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/upload-store.ts:149-152` (`cancelUpload`) and `:163-167`
(`removeTask`, which also aborts). Surfaced by the cancel control on
`src/components/files/upload-task-row.tsx` inside `upload-queue-panel.tsx` and
`upload-dialog.tsx`.

---

### 21.3 Listing attachments

There is **no** `GET /attachments` and there must not be one. An attachment is reached
through the thing that owns it, which is what makes the permission check the owner's check
rather than a second, parallel one that can disagree.

| Owner | How the attachments arrive | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Board record cell | inside `BoardRow.cells[columnId]` as `CellValue { kind: "attachment", attachments }` | E-047, E-061, E-063 |
| Comment | inside `Comment.attachments` | E-119, E-125 |
| Document block | inside `WorkspaceDocument.blocks[]` as `ImageBlock.images[]` / `AttachmentBlock` | E-091 |
| Drive folder | as `FileNode[]` | **E-113**, below |

In every case the response embeds the metadata (`name`, `mimeType`, `sizeBytes`) joined from
`file_assets`, plus a freshly minted `url`. The join tables are read by the owning
endpoint's query, never by a second round trip per attachment.

---

### `GET /api/v1/folders/:nodeId/files`

**Purpose** — The files directly inside one folder, for the Files screen.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on `nodeId`, **resolved server-side**. The mock takes a
`canView` boolean from the caller (`src/services/file-service.ts:92-98`), which canon OQ-18
marks `critical`: the API must never accept an access decision as an input.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The folder or project. A literal `root` addresses the workspace root, matching `folderId: null` in the client. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | int | no | `500` | Hard server cap 1000 (§6.3: no list is unbounded). |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `FileNode[]`, `200`. Trashed files are excluded, matching
`src/services/file-service.ts:124`. `previewUrl` and `thumbnailUrl` are short-lived signed
URLs minted per response; `sizeBytes`, `mimeType`, `extension` and `kind` come from
`file_assets`; `version` from `file_nodes`.

**Database** — `nodes` (visibility walk, then `WHERE parent_id = $1 AND kind = 'file' AND
deleted_at IS NULL`), `file_nodes`, `file_assets`, `users` (owner), `node_favorites`
(`isFavorite` for **this** viewer), `access_rules` (`isShared` = a rule exists).

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — message `You do not have access to “{name}”`, detail *"Ask the owner to share it with you."* (`src/services/file-service.ts:113-118`). Note this is the one place the frontend does name the folder, because the caller reached it by navigating to it. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `FOLDER_NOT_FOUND` — `That folder could not be found`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` — `nodeId` is not a container. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-file-catalog.ts:43-46` → `fileService.listFiles`,
rendered by `src/components/files/files-view.tsx` and `src/components/files/file-table.tsx`.

### `GET /api/v1/assets/:assetId/url`

**Purpose** — Turn a stored `assetId` into a short-lived signed URL. This is how a board
cell, a document block and a comment attachment all get their bytes, and it is the reason
nothing persists a URL.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **Visibility on any owner.** The caller must be able to see at least one of
the places the asset is referenced from — a four-way `EXISTS` across `file_nodes`,
`cell_attachments`, `comment_attachments` and `document_asset_refs`, each resolved to a node
and each node run through the visibility walk. An asset with no surviving reference is
`ASSET_NOT_FOUND` even to its uploader: the reference is the grant.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | UUID | `file_assets.id` — the same value as `CellAttachment.id` and `CommentAttachment.id`. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"original" \| "thumbnail"` | no | `"original"` | `thumbnail` returns a URL for `thumb_key`; **falls back to the original** when `thumb_key` is null, because the client's contract is "a URL or null", and a null thumbnail already means "use the original" (`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:89`). |
| `disposition` | `"inline" \| "attachment"` | no | `"inline"` | Forced to `attachment` for the non-renderable set, whatever is asked. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SignedUrlResponse`, `200`.

```ts
interface SignedUrlResponse {
  readonly url: string;
  /** ISO 8601. The client treats the URL as ephemeral, which it already does. */
  readonly expiresAt: string;
  /** Echoed so a caller can tell a real thumbnail from the original fallback. */
  readonly variant: "original" | "thumbnail";
}
```

**Database** — `file_assets` (read: `storage_key`, `thumb_key`, `mime_type`, `name`);
`file_nodes` / `cell_attachments` / `comment_attachments` / `document_asset_refs` (read:
the ownership `EXISTS`); `nodes`, `boards`, `board_rows`, `comments` (read: resolve each
reference to a node id for the visibility walk).

**Transaction** — Not required. Read-only.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | `not_found` | `ASSET_NOT_FOUND` — unknown asset, or one with no reference the caller may see. Never `403`: distinguishing them tells the caller an asset exists. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED` — this endpoint is called once per attachment chip and must be throttled per user, not per asset. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/services/file-service.ts:247-251` (`getAssetUrl`), called from
`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:87-90` (cell attachments, minting both `url` and
`thumbnailUrl`) and `src/components/document/blocks/image-block.tsx:44-46`. Consumed by
`src/components/board/attachments/attachment-viewer.tsx:46-58` and
`src/components/comments/comment-attachments.tsx:23-29`.

**Caching.** Signed URLs are minted per response with a **15-minute** lifetime and the
response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. A board page with forty attachment
chips therefore mints forty URLs; batch them by returning `url` and `thumbnailUrl` already
populated inside `BoardSnapshot` and `CommentPage` rather than making the client call this
endpoint forty times. E-117 exists for the cases the batch cannot cover — a lightbox opened
long after the page loaded, and a URL that has since expired.

---

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/file/download`

**Purpose** — A URL suitable for an `<a download>`.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on `nodeId`. `canDownload` is gated on `capabilities.view` in
the frontend (`src/components/files/file-preview-dialog.tsx:55`) — reading a file is
downloading it, so there is no separate download key.

**Path Params** — `nodeId` (UUID), must address a `file` node.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SignedUrlResponse`. The signed `GET` carries
`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<original name>"` **server-side**, so the browser
honours the original name even though the client also sets `anchor.download`
(`src/hooks/use-file-preview.ts:63-72`) — a signed URL alone does not carry a filename.

**Database** — `nodes` (visibility, kind), `file_nodes`, `file_assets` (`storage_key`,
`name`, `mime_type`).

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` / `ASSET_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` — the node is not a file. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-file-preview.ts:37-43` (`download`) and `:49-54`
(`useFileDownload`), from the viewer header (`src/components/files/preview/viewer-header.tsx`),
the file table, the drive item menu (`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:135-140`) and
the document attachment block (`src/components/document/blocks/attachment-block.tsx:45-63`).

---

### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/file/preview`

**Purpose** — Everything the preview surface needs, resolved server-side into a
discriminated union, so the client never decides how to render bytes it has not seen.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on `nodeId`.

**Path Params** — `nodeId` (UUID), must address a `file` node.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `FilePreview` (`src/types/file.ts:21-27`), `200` in every case including
`unsupported`.

```ts
type FilePreview =
  | { readonly kind: "image"; readonly url: string; readonly alt: string }
  | { readonly kind: "pdf"; readonly url: string }
  | { readonly kind: "text"; readonly content: string; readonly language: ConfigFormat }
  | { readonly kind: "sheet"; readonly rows: readonly (readonly string[])[]; readonly sheetName: string }
  | { readonly kind: "unsupported"; readonly reason: string };
```

- `image` and `pdf` carry a **signed URL**, not bytes. For `image` that URL is the
  **original**, never the thumbnail — see §21.5.
- `text` carries the **content itself**, not a URL (`src/services/file-service.ts:147-150`).
  `language` is typed as `ConfigFormat` on the wire and derived from the extension,
  defaulting to `"text"` (canon OQ-76; the frontend field is a bare `string` today).
- `sheet` carries the parsed grid and a `sheetName` — the filename minus its extension,
  truncated to 31 characters (Excel's limit), falling back to `"Sheet1"`
  (`src/services/file-service.ts:301-303`).
- `unsupported` is **not an error**: canon §4.3 records `PREVIEW_UNSUPPORTED` explicitly as a
  `200` outcome. Its `reason` is the human sentence
  `"{EXT} files cannot be previewed in the browser. Download the file to open it."`
  (`:337-340`), which is the PRD's "download button with a warning".

**The strategy is decided by extension first, MIME second** (`previewStrategyFor`,
`src/lib/preview-strategy.ts:89-105`), and the comment at `:92-93` is the rule:
*"A recognised extension is authoritative — MIME types are often generic and sometimes plain
wrong."* Order: 7 image extensions → `pdf` → 3 sheet extensions → 31 text extensions →
24 known-binary extensions → then the MIME fallbacks (`kind === "image"`,
`application/pdf`, `text/*`) → else `none`.

**Database** — `nodes`, `file_nodes`, `file_assets`; the object store for `text` and `sheet`
(the bytes are read and parsed server-side).

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` / `ASSET_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH`. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-file-preview.ts:26-35`, rendered by
`src/components/files/preview/preview-surface.tsx` and its five per-kind children.

---

### 21.4 Deleting an attachment

**There is no `DELETE /assets/{assetId}`, and no chapter may add one.** An asset is
removed by removing the **reference**; the object is collected afterwards.

| What the user did | Endpoint | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Removed a file from a board attachment cell | E-066 `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` | The cell value is rewritten without it; the `cell_attachments` row is deleted in the same transaction. `src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:98-104` (`remove`) writes exactly this. |
| Removed an image from a document block | E-092 `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document` | `blocks` is rewritten; `document_asset_refs` is rewritten in the same transaction. |
| Deleted a comment | E-122 (soft) → purge (hard) | The tombstone renders `attachments: []`; `comment_attachments` rows survive the soft delete and cascade on purge. |
| Trashed a drive file | E-032 `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}` | Soft delete on `nodes`. The asset and `file_nodes` row survive — a restore must restore the bytes. |
| Purged a drive file | E-038 / E-039 / the nightly trash sweep | `nodes` row is hard-deleted; `file_nodes` cascades. |

**The orphan sweep.** A `file_assets` row with no row in `file_nodes`, `cell_attachments`,
`comment_attachments` or `document_asset_refs`, **and** older than a **24-hour grace
window**, is deleted along with its object, and `workspaces.used_bytes` is decremented in the
same transaction. The grace window exists because E-111 creates the asset before the
referencing write lands; without it, a slow comment post would race the sweep.

Every reference table uses `asset_id → file_assets(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`. That is
deliberate: `RESTRICT` turns a sweep bug into a loud error instead of a silently broken
thumbnail on a colleague's record. Canon OQ-72 — what happens to a document image block when
its drive file is deleted — is answered by the same constraint: the block's
`document_asset_refs` row keeps the asset alive, so trashing the *node* never destroys the
*object* the page still shows.

---

### 21.5 Validation, trust, and the image viewer

#### Size

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT (frontend).** `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 25 * 1024 * 1024`
(`src/lib/file-validation.ts:4`), with the message `“{name}” exceeds the 25 MB limit` and
the hint *"PDF, PNG, JPG, XLSX, CSV, TXT and source code · up to 25 MB"* (`:22`, `:38-45`).
The PRD `WS-FIL-06` says 100 MB.

**Canon's position (OQ-69) is binding: 100 MB is the API and storage contract, and the
client's pre-check number is served from `GET /config` (E-139) so the two cannot disagree.**
The hint string and the message are rendered from that value, not from a constant. Empty
files are refused at 0 bytes (`FILE_EMPTY`) — `file_assets` carries
`CHECK (size_bytes > 0)`, and the ceiling is deliberately **not** a check constraint so
raising it is a config change, not a migration.

Enforced **three times**: in the client for a fast toast, at E-110 against the declared size
and the quota, and at E-111 against the object store's `HEAD`. Only the third is
authoritative.

#### MIME type, and why the extension is not trusted either

**Both inputs are attacker-controlled and the frontend says so.**

- `mimeType` is `file.type || "application/octet-stream"` (`src/services/file-service.ts:82`,
  `src/lib/upload-queue.ts:16`) — a browser-supplied string with no verification anywhere.
- The extension is part of a filename the user typed.
- `src/lib/file-validation.ts` validates the **extension only**; the MIME type is **not
  validated at all**.
- `src/lib/attachments.ts:33-38` states the rule the backend inherits: *"A declared MIME
  type is not trustworthy on its own, and neither is a file extension — the client may set
  either. Both have to agree before the byte stream is put in an `<img>`."*

**The server-side rule, in order:**

1. **Derive** `extension` from the filename with `extensionOf` semantics — lower-cased, no
   dot, `""` when there is no dot (`src/lib/node-visuals.ts:211-214`). Never accept an
   `extension` field.
2. **Check the extension against the allow-list** at E-110. The list is server config served
   by `GET /config`, seeded from `ACCEPTED_EXTENSIONS` (19 entries:
   `pdf txt md · png jpg jpeg · xlsx csv · ts tsx js jsx json sql py go sh yml yaml`,
   `src/lib/file-validation.ts:7-14`). Canon OQ-70 records that this list blocks formats the
   previewer handles (`gif webp svg tsv xml html css env markdown`) and recommends adding at
   least those while keeping `exe dmg bin iso` out.
3. **Sniff the landed object at E-111** — read the leading bytes and compare the detected
   type with what the extension implies. Disagreement is `FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` (400):
   the upload is aborted, the object deleted, the quota untouched.
4. **Store `mime_type` as the sniffed type**, not the declared one, when the sniff is
   confident; otherwise store the declared value and mark `kind` from the extension. `kind`
   is always derived server-side (`kindFromFileName`, `src/lib/node-visuals.ts:206-209`),
   never accepted.
5. **Serve with the stored type, never with a client-supplied one.** The signed `GET`
   carries `Content-Type` from `file_assets.mime_type` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

#### Never rendered inline — the stored-XSS rule

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `NON_RENDERABLE_TYPES = { "image/svg+xml", "text/html",
"application/xhtml+xml" }` with the reason written down at `src/lib/attachments.ts:24-29`:
*"SVG is markup, and rendering uploaded markup in the app's own origin is how an upload
becomes stored XSS."*

Backend obligations:

- Serve every user-uploaded object from a **separate origin** from the application, so even
  a bypass cannot reach the app's cookies or `localStorage`.
- Force `Content-Disposition: attachment` for anything in that set, whatever `disposition`
  E-117 was asked for.
- Send `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` on object responses.
- `isImageAttachment` requires the declared MIME **and** the extension to agree
  (`src/lib/attachments.ts:39-43`); the server reproduces that check before it ever labels an
  asset `kind: "image"`.

#### The image viewer needs the original, at its own resolution

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT, and it constrains the API.** The viewer is a pan/zoom canvas, not a
box:

- `ImageCanvas` documents its `url` prop as *"Full-resolution asset. Thumbnails belong in
  cells and lists, not here."* (`src/components/shared/image-canvas.tsx:11-13`).
- The canvas sizes itself from `image.naturalWidth` / `naturalHeight` on load
  (`:77-81`) and offers **Fit** and **100%** controls with `=` / `-` / `0` hotkeys
  (`:49-51`). *"100%"* is a promise about pixels: if the URL served a 1600 px derivative of a
  3200 px screenshot, 100% would show the image at half size and every measurement taken off
  it would be wrong.
- `AttachmentViewer` says it again: *"The full-resolution asset is what the viewer loads;
  thumbnails stay in the cell and the drawer list."*
  (`src/components/board/attachments/attachment-viewer.tsx:29-30`), and passes
  `url: current.url` with `thumbnailUrl` handed separately as the blurred placeholder
  (`:48-53` → `ImageLightbox` → `ImageCanvas.placeholderUrl`).

Therefore:

1. **E-117 `variant=original` returns the untouched uploaded object.** No server-side
   resize, no re-encode, no EXIF-driven rotation baked in, no format substitution.
2. **`thumbnailUrl` is a separate field and a separate object** (`file_assets.thumb_key`),
   never a resized rendering of the same URL. `CellAttachment` carries both
   (`src/types/board.ts:206-208`) and the cell renders the thumbnail while the viewer renders
   the original.
3. **`thumbnailUrl` may be `null` and the client already handles it** — it falls back to the
   original (`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:89`). So thumbnail generation is
   asynchronous and non-blocking: E-111 returns before it exists.
4. The recommended derivative (canon OQ-71): longest edge **400 px**, WebP or JPEG, EXIF
   stripped, images only, `thumb_key` written when it lands. A grid of twenty chips must not
   download twenty full-size photographs.

---

### 21.6 Open questions

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-73) — comment attachments bypass validation, permission and the node model.**
> **Evidence** — `commentService.attach` mints a session object URL and nothing more
> (`src/services/comment-service.ts:209-219`). It does not call `validateUpload`, does not
> touch the upload store, does not check `file.upload`, and does not create a node;
> `addFiles` calls `onAttach` directly (`src/components/comments/comment-composer.tsx:69-80`).
> `docs/COLLABORATION.md:330` records that the attachments do not survive a reload.
> **Recommendation** — route them through E-110/E-111 with `purpose: "comment"` and
> `createDriveNode: false`, applying the same size ceiling, the same allow-list and the same
> sniff, and requiring **both** `file.upload` and `comment.create`. Store them in
> `comment_attachments` referencing `file_assets`, and mint `CommentAttachment.url` per
> response.
> **Impact if wrong** — an unvalidated upload path exists on the busiest surface in the
> product: a 4 GB executable reaches object storage through a comment box, uncounted against
> any quota.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-74) — should a document-block or board-cell upload appear in Drive?**
> **Evidence** — it does today, unavoidably: `startUploads` always calls
> `addUploadedAsset` (`src/store/upload-store.ts:76`), and every block passes the page's own
> parent folder (`src/components/document/document-page.tsx:133`). Nobody chose it per
> surface; it falls out of the shared funnel. The board type comment says the opposite —
> a cell attachment *"does not create a file node beside the board"* (`src/types/board.ts:198-200`).
> **Recommendation** — canon's position: `createDriveNode` on `CreateUploadRequest`, default
> `true` for `drive` and `documentBlock` (a page's images live beside the page and inherit
> its folder permissions) and `false` for `boardCell` and `comment`. Confirm with product
> before changing what ships.
> **Impact if wrong** — either every project folder fills with `Screenshot 2026-08-27.png`,
> or a page's images become orphans nobody can find, share or permission.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-75) — stored attachment URLs are session object URLs.**
> **Evidence** — `CellAttachment.url` is documented as *"Session URL for the real bytes;
> null once the session that made it ends"* (`src/types/board.ts:206-207`); the same for
> `CommentAttachment.url` (`src/types/collab.ts:35-36`) and `DocumentImage.url`.
> `getAssetUrl` returns null once the blob is gone (`src/services/file-service.ts:247-251`).
> **Recommendation** — persist **only** `assetId` in cells, blocks and comments. Mint `url`
> and `thumbnailUrl` per response as short-lived signed URLs (E-117) and never accept either
> on write; strip them from any request body that carries them.
> **Impact if wrong** — every attachment renders broken the moment the uploading tab closes,
> and the database fills with `blob:` strings that mean nothing to anyone else.

## 22. Config Documents

Module `devtools` (canon C-14). Endpoints **E-099** and **E-100** (canon §3.15), plus the config
projection of the shared version family **E-095 … E-098** (canon §3.14). Tables `config_documents`
(T-20) and `config_versions` (T-21), joined to `nodes` (T-06), `environments` (T-26) and `users`
(T-01). Requirement codes: `DV-CFG-22` (the editor), `DV-ENV-21` (the environment label),
`SY-VER-39` (version history).

### 22.0 What a config document is, and the six rules every endpoint below inherits

A config document is a **drive node whose `kind` is `document` and whose `documentKind` is
`config`**, with one row of content beside it. It is not a separate kind of node and it is not a
file: it shares routing, permissions, favourites, pin/lock/archive and the trash lifecycle with
every other document — *"Documents come in three shapes. They share routing, permissions and the
pin/lock/archive lifecycle; only their editor differs."* (`src/types/node.ts:40-44`). The
frontend picks the editor at render time from `documentKindOf(node)`
(`src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx:118-123`), and the backend picks the content table the same
way.

Six rules bind E-099, E-100 and the four version endpoints, and are not restated in each:

1. **The wire field is `format`, never `language`.** *"`format` rather than `language` on the wire:
   it is what the field has always been called and what the stored documents carry. The UI says
   'Language'."* (`src/types/devtools.ts:19-21`). Canon §2.1 records this as the one place a
   proposed name (`DocumentLanguage`) loses to the frontend's (`ConfigFormat`). No endpoint, column,
   query parameter or error message in this chapter uses the word `language`.

2. **`name` is not stored on the config row.** It is read from `nodes.name` on every read, so a
   rename cannot leave the page header and the breadcrumb disagreeing about what you are looking at
   — the frontend refreshes it explicitly for exactly that reason
   (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:100-118`). Model it as a join, never a column. There is no
   config-rename endpoint: renaming is `PATCH /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` (E-025).

3. **`content` is opaque.** The backend stores the bytes it was sent, verbatim. It does not format,
   re-indent, normalise line endings, strip a BOM, sort `.env` keys, or reject malformed content.
   See §22.2 — this is a decision, not an omission.

4. **Content and metadata land in one write.** Changing the format or the environment sends the
   current content along, *"so the language and the text land in one version rather than in two that
   disagree"* (`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:109-113`, and the two callers at `:114-139`).
   E-100 therefore accepts `content`, `format` and `environmentOptionId` in a single request and
   must never require three.

5. **Every write returns the authoritative record** (canon C-10). `useConfigDocument` assigns the
   response with `setData(saved)` and does **not** touch the local draft
   (`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:73-82`), because *"replacing the draft with the server's copy
   is correct only if nothing was typed while the request was in flight, and on a code surface
   something usually was; doing it anyway is how an editor eats a sentence"* (`:45-54`). The
   response is the record and nothing more — no echo of the draft, no diff, no formatted body.

6. **The three narrowing layers apply.** A config document under a **trashed** node accepts nothing
   but `node.delete`; one under an **archived ancestor** is frozen and refuses every write; a
   **locked** document refuses `document.update` because that key is in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`
   (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:36-49, 79-85`). These are resolved before the permission key is
   even consulted and produce `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` and `NODE_LOCKED`
   respectively (canon §4.3).

---

### 22.1 `ConfigFormat` — the language enum

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Fifteen members, a closed union, stored on the document
(`src/types/devtools.ts:22-37`):

```ts
/** src/types/devtools.ts:22-37 — canon §2.8. Config documents only. */
type ConfigFormat =
  | "json" | "env" | "yaml"
  | "javascript" | "typescript" | "jsx" | "tsx"
  | "html" | "xml" | "css"
  | "sql" | "shell" | "dockerfile" | "nginx"
  | "text";
```

The union is *"deliberately short and deliberately not extensible from data … so a document cannot
be saved in a language nothing can colour, and every branch that switches on it is checked
exhaustively at build time"* (`src/types/devtools.ts:13-17`).

| Member | Display label | Formatter (client-side) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `json` | JSON | `JSON.parse` + `JSON.stringify` | The only format that is linted. |
| `env` | ENV | bespoke, whitespace around the first `=` only | The detection fallback and the storage default. |
| `yaml` | YAML | Prettier `yaml` | |
| `javascript` | JavaScript | Prettier `babel` | |
| `typescript` | TypeScript | Prettier `typescript` | |
| `jsx` | JSX | Prettier `babel` | |
| `tsx` | TSX | Prettier `typescript` | |
| `html` | HTML | Prettier `html` | |
| `xml` | XML | **none** | Button shown and disabled. |
| `css` | CSS | Prettier `css` | |
| `sql` | SQL | **none** | |
| `shell` | Shell | **none** | |
| `dockerfile` | Dockerfile | **none** | |
| `nginx` | Nginx | **none** | |
| `text` | Plain Text | **none** | |

Labels and picker order: `CONFIG_FORMAT_LABELS` (`src/lib/syntax/grammars.ts:167-185`); the picker
iterates `CONFIG_FORMATS`, which is `Object.keys` of that map, so **the declaration order above is
the order the dropdown shows** (`src/lib/syntax/grammars.ts:185`;
`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:107-121`). Parser assignment:
`src/lib/code-format.ts:51-64`.

**Storage.** A Postgres `ENUM` named `config_format` whose values are the frontend literals verbatim
(canon §2.0):

```sql
-- Documentation of intent, not a migration.
CREATE TYPE config_format AS ENUM (
  'json','env','yaml','javascript','typescript','jsx','tsx',
  'html','xml','css','sql','shell','dockerfile','nginx','text'
);
```

Do **not** normalise `javascript` to `js` or introduce a `long_text`-style rewrite: the wire value
and the stored value must be identical so no mapping layer can drift.

**The enum is closed on write.** A `format` outside those fifteen is `400 / validation`, reason
`CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN` (canon §4.3). It is never stored as free text and never coerced to `text`.
The frontend has a matching type guard, `isConfigFormat`, for anything arriving from storage or a
paste (`src/lib/syntax/grammars.ts:187-190`).

**`ConfigFormat` is not `CodeLanguage`.** A fenced code *block* inside a page uses a different,
eight-member enum — `plaintext`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `sql`, `bash`, `python`, `go`
(`src/types/document.ts:20-28`, canon §2.8). Two independent enums, two independent columns. They
must not be merged, and a `ConfigFormat` value must never be written into a code block's `language`
field or vice versa.

**Detection at creation is a client-side guess, and only a starting point.** `formatFromName`
resolves by exact name first (`dockerfile`, `containerfile`, `.env`, `nginx`, `makefile`), then by
the last dotted segment against a 24-entry extension map, then a `.env*` prefix, then falls back to
**`env`** (`src/lib/syntax/detect.ts:14-68`). *"Nothing infers a language from the content: a JSON
object and a JavaScript object literal are the same bytes, and choosing between them by sniffing
would silently switch a document's language out from under whoever wrote it."*
(`src/lib/syntax/detect.ts:8-11`). **The backend must not sniff content either.** The author picks
the format in the create menu precisely because the guess gets "Payment Service Config" wrong
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:196-203`), so `format` arrives on the create request and the
server stores what it is given.

---

### 22.2 Formatting and linting are client concerns — the backend offers neither

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT, stated as plainly as the brief asks: there is no formatter endpoint, and
none may be added.**

Reformatting happens entirely in the browser, in `src/lib/code-format.ts`, with Prettier loaded **on
demand** — *"nothing here is in the page's bundle until somebody presses Format, and only the one
parser that language needs is fetched"* (`src/lib/code-format.ts:8-14`). Plugins are dynamically
imported and cached per parser (`:98-137`). JSON and ENV deliberately bypass Prettier: JSON because
`JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` are already exact and already loaded, ENV because Prettier has no
parser for it and *"format" here means only the whitespace around the first `=`* — **order is never
touched**, because `.env` files are read top to bottom by tools that let a later line win, so
sorting one alphabetically can change what a service boots with (`src/lib/code-format.ts:16-26`,
implementation at `:66-89`).

Six consequences the backend must honour:

| # | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| F-1 | **No `POST /config/format` endpoint, no `?format=true` parameter, no server-side pretty-printer.** The Format button calls `formatSource` locally and then `controller.setDraft(result.text)` — a local state write, not a request (`src/components/devtools/config-document-page.tsx:52-61`). |
| F-2 | **The stored bytes are the submitted bytes.** No trailing-newline insertion, no CRLF→LF rewrite, no whitespace trimming, no re-encoding. A `PUT` followed by a `GET` must return a byte-identical `content`. |
| F-3 | **Malformed content is never rejected.** Linting is JSON-only, runs on the *draft* while typing, and is a client-side call to `lintJson` (`src/lib/json-lint.ts:20-30`, wired at `src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:69`). It disables the Format button, not the Save button (`src/components/devtools/config-document-page.tsx:116, 142-146`). A server that refused invalid JSON would make it impossible to save a half-typed file. |
| F-4 | If server-side validation is ever wanted, it is **advisory metadata on the response**, never a rejection. That is a new optional field, not a new status code. **RECOMMENDATION**, not required today. |
| F-5 | **A failed format produces no replacement text.** `FormatResult` is a discriminated union — `{ ok: true, text }` or `{ ok: false, message }` (`src/lib/code-format.ts:34-36`) — so a caller can never write a half-formatted document over a good one. Any future server-side equivalent must keep that property. |
| F-6 | **Syntax highlighting is client-side too**, a pure tokenizer over grammars-as-data (`src/lib/syntax/grammars.ts`, `src/lib/syntax/tokenize.ts`). The API sends text and a format; it never sends tokens, spans or HTML. |

**What the backend does own:** persisting `content` and `format`, cutting versions, resolving the
environment reference, enforcing `document.update`, and auditing a Production save (OQ-62).

---

### 22.3 Content persistence, versioning and the fold rule

**Content** is one `TEXT` column holding the raw text (`src/types/devtools.ts:44`). No blocks, no
AST, no per-line rows — a config document is a string, and the frontend's editor is a controlled
`<textarea>`-class surface over that string (`src/components/devtools/code-editor.tsx`).

**Versioning.** Every save writes to `config_versions` in the same transaction as the content write.
`ConfigVersion` holds a **full snapshot, never a delta** (`src/types/devtools.ts:51-64`) so a
restore never has to replay a chain.

**The fold rule, stated once** (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:156-187`):

```
foldsIn = isAutosave === true
       && a head version exists
       && head.is_autosave = true
       && head.author_id = the session user
```

- `foldsIn` → **`UPDATE` the head row**: same `id`, same `version`, new `content`, new `summary`,
  new `updated_at`. `config_documents.version` is unchanged and the response carries the same
  number.
- otherwise → **`INSERT`** at `config_documents.version + 1`, and advance the document's `version`.

*"It is the difference between 'I have finished this edit' and 'you stopped typing for a moment',
and history should only record the first. Consecutive autosaves by the same author fold into one
version rather than cutting a new one every second and a half — a history of four hundred entries,
each a keystroke apart, is not a history anybody can restore from."*
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:125-133`.)

A **manual** save always starts a new version, and so does **another author's** edit landing in
between. The client's autosave debounce is `CONFIG_AUTOSAVE_MS = 1_500`, deliberately longer than a
page's, and the comment is explicit that this figure *"is about traffic rather than about history"*
(`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:12-21`) — the fold is what protects history, so the backend must
not treat the debounce as a substitute for it.

**`summary`** is computed server-side at write time and stored, never derived on read. It is a
line-count delta: `+N lines`, `−N lines`, or `N lines` when the count is unchanged
(`describeChange`, `src/services/devtools-service.ts:215-222`). When folding, the delta is computed
against the **pre-fold head's** content, not against the current document
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:181`) — otherwise a fold would report `0 lines` for an edit that
added ten.

**Retention.** Config history is **uncapped** (canon OQ-59). `VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT = 20`
(`src/config/app.ts:62-63`) is applied to pages only (`src/services/document-service.ts:111`) and
deliberately not to configs (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:186`). A config file is small text
and `DV-CFG-22` asks for *"100% of edits recorded, none missed"*.

**Reads return a copy.** `listConfigVersions` snapshots the array — *"Handing out the record's own
list meant a caller holding yesterday's history watched it grow as new versions landed — the
'before' in a comparison quietly became the 'after'."* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:224-237`).
On a real backend this is a `SELECT` and is a copy by construction; the rule to carry over is that
a version list is a point-in-time read and is never a live handle.

---

### 22.4 Endpoints

#### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/nodes`

**Purpose** — Create a config document. This is **E-024, the one node-creation endpoint** (canon
§3.3); this entry documents only its config slice — the fields it takes for
`documentKind: "config"` and the rows it writes in `config_documents` and `config_versions`. The
drive chapter owns the endpoint in full.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` **and** `document.create` on the target parent node, plus workspace
membership. Both are Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:48, 58`). There is no config-specific
key: a config document is a document.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | The tenant. Membership is checked before anything else (canon §4.3 `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`). |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CreateNodeRequest` (canon §5.4), config slice:

```ts
interface CreateNodeRequest {
  readonly kind: NodeKind;              // "document"
  readonly parentId: string | null;     // must address a project or folder
  readonly name: string;                // "Untitled JSON config" by default
  readonly documentKind?: DocumentKind; // "config"
  readonly icon?: string;               // "⚙️" — src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:14-18
  /** Config only. The author's choice, not a guess. Defaults to "env". */
  readonly format?: ConfigFormat;
  /** Config only. Defaults to the workspace's first environment. */
  readonly environmentOptionId?: string;
}
```

`format` is on the create request because the client sends it there: the create menu offers a
Language submenu and passes the chosen format straight through
(`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:107-121` →
`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:60-66`). In the mock this is a second call,
`devtoolsService.createConfig({ nodeId, format })` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:204-213`);
**the API folds it into E-024 so a node cannot exist for a moment with the wrong format** and so a
half-completed creation cannot leave a document with no content row at all.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `DocumentNode` variant), `200`. Content is not returned; the client
navigates to the node and then calls E-099.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Parent lookup; must be a `project` or `folder` else `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` (409) — *"Pages can only live inside folders"* (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:749-755`). |
| `nodes` | READ | Sibling slugs for `uniqueSlug(slugify(name), taken)` (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:757, 764`). Excludes trashed rows so a restore never collides. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | One row: `kind = 'document'`, `document_kind = 'config'`, `icon`, `owner_id` = session user. |
| `environments` | READ | Resolve `environmentOptionId`, or take the workspace's first environment by `position` when absent. `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND` (404) if the id is unknown. |
| `config_documents` | INSERT | `node_id`, `workspace_id`, `format`, `environment_id`, `content = ''`, `version = 1`, `created_by`/`updated_by` = session user. |
| `config_versions` | INSERT | Version 1, `content = ''`, `summary = '1 lines'`, `is_autosave = false`, `author_id` = session user. Seeded so history is never empty — the frontend seeds a v1 entry on first read for the same reason (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:84-94`). |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | `module: "node"`, `action: "node.create"`, severity `info`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The `nodes` row, the `config_documents` row and the v1
`config_versions` row commit together or not at all. A node whose content row is missing renders as
a broken document with no recovery path.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11) with `change: "created"` — ids only.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN` — `format` is not one of the fifteen. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — empty `name` after trim, or `documentKind` outside `page \| config \| secret`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `node.create` / `document.create`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` — the parent is under an archived node. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_NOT_FOUND` (unknown parent), `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` — the parent is a document, board or file. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` — only if the caller supplied a slug; the server mints one otherwise. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:40-88` (`useCreateDocument`), invoked from
`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:99-124`.

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/config`

**Purpose** — Return one config document: its text, its format, its environment label and its
version. This is the read the editor opens with.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **Visibility** on the node, resolved server-side through the access chain
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility`, entered via `effectiveAccess`), plus workspace membership. No
action key: reading a config document is reading a document. A node the caller may not see answers
`404 NODE_NOT_FOUND`, identically to one that does not exist.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The drive node. Must be `kind = 'document'` with `document_kind = 'config'`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `ConfigDocument`.

```ts
/** src/types/devtools.ts:39-49 — unchanged. */
interface ConfigDocument {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  /** Projected from nodes.name on every read. Never a stored column. */
  readonly name: string;
  readonly format: ConfigFormat;
  /** Option id from the shared environment list (DV-ENV-21). */
  readonly environmentOptionId: string;
  readonly content: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly updatedAt: string;          // ISO 8601 (C-03)
  readonly updatedBy: UserSummary;
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/nodes/7c1e…/config
{
  "nodeId": "7c1e2a90-…",
  "name": "Payment Service Config",
  "format": "json",
  "environmentOptionId": "b2d0…",          // the Production environment row
  "content": "{\n  \"port\": 6868,\n  \"apiUrl\": \"https://api.nexdrop.vn\"\n}\n",
  "version": 7,
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-27T09:31:12.004Z",
  "updatedBy": { "id": "usr_khanh-…", "name": "Khanh Luu", "email": "khanh@nexdrop.vn", "initials": "KL" }
}
```

`ConfigDocument` carries **no `id` of its own** — `node_id` is the primary key (canon T-20,
`src/types/devtools.ts:40`). This is the deliberate asymmetry with `WorkspaceDocument` and `Board`,
which do carry an id (canon OQ-30).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | By PK. Supplies `name`, and the ancestor walk for visibility and freeze resolution. Refuses when `document_kind <> 'config'`. |
| `access_rules` | READ | Ancestor-chain resolution for visibility (deepest node wins; a user rule beats a role rule at the same node — canon OQ-22). |
| `workspace_members` | READ | The role floor. |
| `config_documents` | READ | By PK `node_id`. |
| `users` | READ | `updated_by` → `UserSummary`. |
| `environments` | READ | Not required for the response (the id is returned raw), but joined when the caller also needs the label; the picker gets labels from E-106. |

**Transaction** — Not required. A single read-only snapshot.

**Realtime** — None. See canon OQ-99 — no realtime frame exists for config content today, and
adding one is out of scope for this chapter.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown node, **or one the caller may not see**. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` — the node exists and is visible but has no `config_documents` row (a data fault; log it at `error`). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` — the node is a page, a secret document, a board or a file. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:59-64` (the `useAsyncResource` loader),
rendered by `src/components/devtools/config-document-page.tsx:37, 65`.

---

#### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/config`

**Purpose** — Save a config document: its text, and optionally its format and its environment. Cuts
a version, or folds into the open one.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **`document.update` on this node**, plus workspace membership. Manager+
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:59`). This is one of the few frontend endpoints that *already*
enforces — `requirePermission(nodeId, "document.update", "edit this config document")`
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:148`) — so the server is reproducing an existing check, not
inventing one. The refusal message is `You do not have permission to edit this config document`
with `detail` = `Needs the Manager role or above` (`src/services/authz.ts:67-74`;
`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:173-176`).

Narrowing, in this order, before the key is consulted: trashed → `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`; frozen by
an archived ancestor → `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`; locked → `NODE_LOCKED`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-85`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The config document's node. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `SaveConfigRequest` (canon §5.4), mirroring `SaveConfigInput`
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:120-135`):

```ts
interface SaveConfigRequest {
  /** The full text. Always sent, even when only the format changed. */
  readonly content: string;
  /** OPTIONAL: omitted means unchanged (C-08). Never null. */
  readonly format?: ConfigFormat;
  /** OPTIONAL: omitted means unchanged. Wire name keeps the frontend's field name. */
  readonly environmentOptionId?: string;
  /** This save came from the debounce, not from a person. Default false. */
  readonly isAutosave?: boolean;
  /** OPTIONAL optimistic-concurrency token (canon OQ-57). Omitted = last-write-wins. */
  readonly expectedVersion?: number;
}
```

Validation:

- `content` — required, a string. Any bytes, including empty. Capped by the service body limit
  (`413 REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`), not by a config-specific rule.
- `format` — when present, one of the fifteen, else `400 CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN`.
- `environmentOptionId` — when present, an existing `environments` row **in this workspace**, else
  `404 ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND`.
- `expectedVersion` — when present and `<> config_documents.version`, `409
  DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`. When absent, last-write-wins (canon §6.4).

**Response** — `ConfigDocument`, `200`, the authoritative record. Same shape as E-099. `version` is
the **post-save** number: `previous.version` on a fold, `previous.version + 1` otherwise.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check, ancestor archive resolution, `name` for the response and for the audit `target`. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | Effective role for `document.update`. |
| `config_documents` | READ `… FOR UPDATE` | Row lock on `node_id`. Two concurrent autosaves must not both read version 6 and both write 7. |
| `config_versions` | READ | The head row — `WHERE node_id = :n ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1` on `UNIQUE (node_id, version DESC)` — to evaluate `foldsIn` (`is_autosave` and `author_id`). |
| `environments` | READ | Only when `environmentOptionId` is present. Also identifies whether the target is the workspace's Production environment (OQ-63). |
| `config_documents` | UPDATE | `content`, `format`, `environment_id`, `version`, `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by = :session_user`. |
| `config_versions` | UPDATE **or** INSERT | Fold → `UPDATE` the head row (same `id`, same `version`). Otherwise → `INSERT` at the new version. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `updated_at = now()`, so the tree, Recent and drive sorting reflect the edit. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | **Conditional** — only for a Production-environment save. See OQ-62 below. Module `document`, action `document.update`, severity `warn`, `target` = the node name, `detail` = `Environment changed to Production` or `Production config saved`. **No content in the row, ever.** |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The content update, the version fold-or-insert, the `nodes` touch
and the conditional audit row are one atomic unit. Two properties depend on it: `config_documents.version`
and the head `config_versions.version` can never disagree, and *"100% of edits recorded, none
missed"* (`DV-CFG-22`) cannot hold if a content write can commit without its version row.

**Realtime** — None (canon OQ-99). A second tab converges on its next read; the drive tree converges
through `node.changed` (RT-11) only when the node's own row changes in a way the tree renders,
which a content save does not.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN` — `format` is not a `ConfigFormat` member. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `content` missing or not a string; `isAutosave` not a boolean. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `document.update`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_LOCKED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` — `expectedVersion` is stale (canon OQ-57). |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — three call sites, all in `src/hooks/use-config-document.ts`:
`:73-82` (`persist`, the 1 500 ms autosave, sends `isAutosave: true`), `:114-125` (`setFormat`,
sends the current content plus the new format), `:127-139` (`setEnvironment`, sends the current
content plus the new environment). Surfaced by
`src/components/devtools/config-document-page.tsx:89-95, 139-146` and the `mod+s` hotkey at `:42`.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-62)** — a Production config change is announced as audited, and nothing audits it.
**Evidence** — the confirmation dialog says *"Production configuration is read by live services.
This change is recorded against your account."* (`src/components/devtools/environment-picker.tsx:100-103`)
and the Production option is disabled without `document.update`, labelled "admins only" (`:79, 90-92`).
But `saveConfig` writes no `auditService.record` call anywhere
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:142-189`); only the secret operations do (`:382-395`). PRD
`DV-ENV-21` requires confirmation for a Production config change.
**Recommendation** — E-100 writes one `audit_events` row **in the same transaction** whenever the
save either moves `environment_id` to the workspace's Production environment or saves a document
already pointing at it: module `document`, action `document.update`, severity `warn`, `target` = the
node name, `detail` = `Environment changed to Production` / `Production config saved`, outcome
`allowed`. No content, no diff, no excerpt in the row.
**Impact if wrong** — the product makes a compliance promise in a modal that the log cannot keep,
and a change to a configuration live services boot from is untraceable.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-63)** — the Production environment has no stable identity once environments
become rows.
**Evidence** — the frontend's environment ids are derived string constants `env_0`, `env_1`, `env_2`
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:28-37`), and the Production guard is a literal equality check against
`PRODUCTION_OPTION_ID = "env_2"` (`:37`), consumed by the picker
(`src/components/devtools/environment-picker.tsx:51, 78`). Canon §5.3 shapes `Environment` as
`{ id, workspaceId, label, color, position }` with UUID ids (C-01) — nothing is left for that
equality check to bind to.
**Recommendation** — give `environments` a stable non-display discriminator (`slug TEXT`, unique per
workspace, seeded `development` / `staging` / `production`) and have both the frontend guard and the
OQ-62 audit trigger read the slug rather than the id. Refuse to delete a seeded row in v1.
**Impact if wrong** — every stored `environment_id` still resolves, but the Production guard, the
"admins only" narrowing and the audit trigger silently stop guarding anything, because no id equals
`"env_2"` any more.

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/versions`

**Purpose** — The version list for a config document. This is **E-095**, the shared version family
(canon §3.14); the node's kind selects the store, and this entry documents the config store's
behaviour. Pages and secrets enter the same path.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on the node, plus workspace membership. Reading history is reading the
document.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The config document's node. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | — | Opaque base64 of the sort-key tuple. Never constructed or parsed by a client (canon §6.3). |
| `limit` | integer | no | 50 | Hard server cap 200. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `VersionPage` of `VersionEntry`, newest first, sorted `(version DESC)`.

```ts
interface VersionPage {
  readonly items: readonly VersionEntry[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/** src/types/system.ts:208-221 — unchanged. */
interface VersionEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;              // "+3 lines" | "−1 lines" | "12 lines"
  readonly lines: readonly string[];     // content.split("\n")
  readonly hasSnapshot: boolean;         // ALWAYS true for a config version
}
```

The projection is `configVersionEntry` (`src/lib/versions.ts:33-43`): `lines =
version.content.split("\n")`, `hasSnapshot: true`. **The server performs the split**, so all three
subjects arrive in the same shape and the three clients stay identical — the frontend does this
today only because the mock hands it a `ConfigVersion`.

**`lines` carries the full snapshot of every version in the page.** That is required, not
incidental: the compare view diffs `entry.lines` against the content on screen entirely client-side
(`src/components/versions/version-detail.tsx:34-39`), and for a config that "on screen" includes the
**unsaved draft** (`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:115`) — content the server has never
seen. A page of 50 versions of a 200-line file is roughly 500 KB of JSON; the `limit` cap is what
bounds it.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | Visibility resolution. |
| `config_versions` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :n ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT :limit + 1`, on `UNIQUE (node_id, version DESC)`. The extra row decides `nextCursor`. |
| `users` | READ | `author_id` → `UserSummary`, batched with one `WHERE id = ANY(...)`. |

**Transaction** — Not required. Read-only, and a point-in-time read by construction.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:100-106` (`ConfigVersionsDialog`'s
`load`), driven by `src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:58-61`, opened from
`src/components/devtools/config-document-page.tsx:126-134, 180-187`. The dialog loads **only while
open** (`enabled: isOpen`) — *"A version list read at mount is stale by the time somebody opens it"*
(`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:23-30`).

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/versions/:versionId`

**Purpose** — One config version in full. This is **E-096**; for a config node it returns a
`ConfigVersion`.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on the node, plus workspace membership.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The config document's node. |
| `versionId` | UUID | `config_versions.id`. Must belong to this node — a version id from another document answers `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, never that document's content. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `ConfigVersion`.

```ts
/** src/types/devtools.ts:51-64 — unchanged. */
interface ConfigVersion {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly content: string;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;
  /** OPTIONAL: present only when true (C-08). Omitted, never false, never null. */
  readonly isAutosave?: boolean;
}
```

`isAutosave` is omitted rather than sent as `false` because the frontend spreads it conditionally —
`...(isAutosave ? { isAutosave: true } : {})` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:182`) — and the
fold predicate reads `head.isAutosave === true` (`:161`). The column is `NOT NULL DEFAULT false`;
the serialiser drops it when false.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check. |
| `config_versions` | READ | By PK `id`, **with `AND node_id = :nodeId`** in the same predicate. |
| `users` | READ | `author_id` → `UserSummary`. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — **None today.** The client already holds `lines` from E-095 and renders the
selected version from them (`src/components/versions/version-detail.tsx:34-39`). This endpoint
exists so a future client can page the list cheaply — serving `VersionEntry` without `lines` and
fetching one snapshot on demand — without a new route. Ship it; do not wait for a caller.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/versions/:versionId/restore`

**Purpose** — Restore a config document to an earlier version by **writing that content forward as a
new version**. This is **E-097**.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **`document.version.restore`** on this node, plus workspace membership. Manager+
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:61`). Canon §3.14 names this key; canon OQ-61 records that the
frontend dialog gates on `capabilities.edit` instead
(`src/components/devtools/config-document-page.tsx:184` passes `canRestore={canEdit}`) and the mock
service checks nothing. **Enforce the key server-side.** Restoring is destructive in a way an
ordinary edit is not: it discards everything since that version in one click.

Restore additionally **inherits every rule the save has** — the trashed, frozen and locked layers
all apply, because a restore *is* a save (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:239-250`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The config document's node. |
| `versionId` | UUID | The version to restore. Must belong to this node. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `RestoreVersionRequest` (canon §5.4). Empty object today; reserved so a reason
string can be added without a route change.

```ts
interface RestoreVersionRequest {
  /** RECOMMENDATION, unused by the frontend: a note recorded on the new version's summary. */
  readonly note?: string;
}
```

**Response** — `ConfigDocument`, `200` — the document **after** the restore, with
`version = previous.version + 1`. Not the restored version's number. The client reloads the list
afterwards rather than assuming what is now on top (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:70-72`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind, archive and lock state. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | `document.version.restore` resolution. |
| `config_versions` | READ | The source snapshot, `WHERE id = :versionId AND node_id = :nodeId`. |
| `config_documents` | READ `… FOR UPDATE` | Row lock. |
| `config_documents` | UPDATE | `content` = the snapshot's content, `version + 1`, `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by` = session user. **`format` and `environment_id` are not restored** — see below. |
| `config_versions` | INSERT | A new row at the new version, `is_autosave = false`, `summary` = the delta from the pre-restore content. A restore **never folds**: `isAutosave` is not sent (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:249`). |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `updated_at = now()`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | Conditional, exactly as E-100: a restore of a Production-labelled document is a Production config save (OQ-62). |

**A restore replaces content only.** The frontend's restore call passes `{ nodeId, content }` and
nothing else (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:249`), so `format` and `environmentOptionId` fall
through the `?? previous` defaults in `saveConfig` (`:168-169`) and keep their **current** values.
This matches the page editor, where *"the icon is not restored — only title and blocks"*
(`src/services/document-service.ts:134`). A restore must not silently move a document back to
Staging.

**Transaction** — **Required.** Snapshot read, content update, version insert, node touch and the
conditional audit row are one unit.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `document.version.restore`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `NODE_LOCKED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` — only reachable when `nodeId` addresses a **secret** document; see §23. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:108-113`
(`ConfigVersionsDialog`'s `restore`) → `src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:63-80` → the result is
handed back through `onRestored` to `controller.applyDocument`
(`src/hooks/use-config-document.ts:101-107`), which **clears the local draft** — a content restore
replaces what is on screen outright.

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/versions/:versionId/diff`

**Purpose** — The line diff between one stored version and another. This is **E-098**.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on the node, plus workspace membership.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The config document's node. |
| `versionId` | UUID | The left-hand side. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `against` | UUID | yes | The right-hand side. Another version of the **same** node; a foreign id is `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND`. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `DiffResponse`.

```ts
interface DiffResponse {
  readonly lines: readonly DiffLine[];
  readonly summary: DiffSummary;
}

/** src/types/system.ts:225-238 — unchanged. */
type DiffKind = "same" | "added" | "removed";      // no "changed", deliberately
interface DiffLine { readonly kind: DiffKind; readonly text: string; }
```
