```ts
interface DiffSummary { readonly added: number; readonly removed: number; }
```

There is deliberately **no `changed` kind**: a modification is a `removed` followed by an `added`
(canon §2.7). The algorithm is an LCS line diff, degrading to "delete everything / add everything"
past 2 000 lines on either side (`src/lib/diff.ts:14-77`); a server implementation must reproduce
that degradation so the two sides cannot disagree about a large file.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check. |
| `config_versions` | READ | Two rows, both constrained by `node_id = :nodeId`. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `against` missing or not a UUID. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` (either side) |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH`, `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` (a secret version has no snapshot to diff) |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — **None today, and by design.** The frontend compares *stored version → what
is on screen now*, never version → version (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:16-18`;
`src/components/versions/version-detail.tsx:34-39`), and for a config that "now" includes the
unsaved draft the server has never seen (`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:115`). Keep
the client diff. This endpoint serves version-to-version comparison, which no surface offers yet.

---

#### Deleting a config document — no endpoint of its own

There is **no `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/config`**, and none may be added. A config document is deleted
by deleting its node — `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}` (E-032), permission `node.delete`, which
soft-deletes the node and detaches the subtree, returning a `TrashEntry`. `config_documents` and
`config_versions` carry no `deleted_at`: they survive the trash and are removed by the permanent
purge through `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `node_id`. Restoring from trash therefore restores the content
and the whole history with it, which is the behaviour the 30-day window exists to provide (canon
OQ-14).

The same applies to rename (E-025), move (E-026), duplicate (E-027), favourite (E-028/E-029) and
archive (E-030/E-031): a config document is a node, and the drive chapter owns those six.

---

### 22.5 Config documents — open questions carried

| OQ | What it decides for this chapter | Position taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OQ-57 | Whether config saves are concurrency-checked | Optional `expectedVersion`; `409 DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` when stale, last-write-wins when absent. |
| OQ-59 | Version folding and the retention cap | Fold consecutive autosaves by the same author. **Uncapped** for config. Never drop the first or the current version. |
| OQ-61 | Whether `document.version.restore` gates restore | Enforce the key (Manager+); the client should read the same key rather than `capabilities.edit`. |
| OQ-62 | Whether a Production config change is audited | Yes — one `audit_events` row inside E-100's transaction. Detailed above. |
| OQ-63 | How the Production environment is identified once environments are rows | A stable `slug` on `environments`, not the literal id `"env_2"`. Detailed above. |
| OQ-77 | Three version shapes, one table or three | Three tables (`document_versions`, `config_versions`, `secret_rotations`), one **read model** (`VersionEntry`) and one endpoint family. The shapes differ in what they can hold; the projection is where they meet. |

---

## 23. Secret Documents

Module `devtools` (canon C-14). Endpoints **E-101 … E-105** (canon §3.16), plus the secret
projection of **E-095** and the deliberate refusals on **E-096 … E-098**. Tables `secret_documents`
(T-22), `secrets` (T-23), `secret_rotations` (T-24), `secret_access_events` (T-25), joined to
`nodes` (T-06), `environments` (T-26), `users` (T-01) and `audit_events` (T-36). Requirement codes:
`DV-SEC-23` (the vault), `SY-AUD-41` (the workspace audit log), `SY-VER-39` (rotation history),
`SY-RBC-42` (the role matrix).

**This section is written to be read by a security reviewer.** §23.1 states the rules that are not
negotiable; §23.2 states the permission model; §23.3 the response headers; §23.4 the audit contract;
§23.5 the reveal path as a diagram; §23.6 the endpoints; §23.7 a checklist a reviewer can run
against an implementation.

---

### 23.1 The five non-negotiable rules

These are not recommendations and no endpoint below may weaken one. Each is grounded in the
frontend, which was built to hold this shape — *"The secret half is deliberately shaped like a
service that holds encrypted material: `getSecrets` can only ever return masks, and plaintext leaves
the module through one permission-checked call that also writes an audit entry. Nothing here — and
nothing that calls it — persists a revealed value."* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:26-33`).

**S-1 · The list endpoint never returns a plaintext value.**
`GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` (E-101) returns masks and metadata only. `SecretEntry` has no
`value` field, and the omission is documented as intentional: *"There is no `value` here on purpose:
plaintext only ever arrives from an explicit, permission-checked reveal, and it is never written
back into this shape."* (`src/types/devtools.ts:68-73`). The service comment is stronger still:
*"Masks only. There is no code path that returns a value from this call."*
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:288`). Implementation obligation: E-101's query selects
`id, key, environment_id, note, position, rotated_by, updated_at` and **never** `value_encrypted`,
`value_iv`, `value_auth_tag` or `value_key_id`. Express it in the database too — a `secrets_masked`
view over exactly those columns, with the application role granted `SELECT` on the ciphertext
columns only through the reveal path — so a future `SELECT *` cannot become an incident.

**S-2 · The mask is a constant.**
`maskedValue` is twelve `U+2022` bullets, `MASK = "••••••••••••"`
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:35`), *"Fixed-width mask; never derived from the real value's
length."* (`src/types/devtools.ts:76-77`). It is **minted by the server on every read** and there is
no `masked_value` column: storing it would be storing a fact about the plaintext. A mask whose
length tracks the value is an oracle — it distinguishes a 12-character password from a 64-character
API key, which is exactly the information an attacker wants first.

**S-3 · Only the reveal endpoints return plaintext, and each writes its audit rows in the same
transaction.**
Two endpoints decrypt: E-103 (one secret) and E-104 (several, as a clipboard blob). Both are gated
on `secret.reveal`. Both write a `secret_access_events` row **and** an `audit_events` row before the
response is produced — *"It checks the role, records an audit entry with a timestamp and the
caller's address, and returns the value once."* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:329-332`) — and
both do so **on refusal as well**: *"Recorded even when refused: a denied attempt is worth
auditing."* (`:343`), *"A denied attempt is recorded exactly as carefully as an allowed one — a
refusal nobody can see is not a control."* (`:360-362`). There is no third decrypting path, no
`?includeValues=true`, and no bulk endpoint that returns a per-secret plaintext map.

**S-4 · Values are encrypted at rest, and nothing plaintext is ever logged, cached, or put in an
error message.**
Envelope encryption: one AES-256-GCM data key per workspace, wrapped by a KMS master key that never
leaves the key service (canon OQ-65; the architecture is set out under "Encryption at rest for
secret values" in §4). Enumerated:
- Not in `secrets` (ciphertext, IV, tag, key id only), not in `secret_rotations`, not in
  `secret_access_events`, not in `audit_events`, not in `config_versions`, not in a temp table, not
  in a queue, not in object storage, not in Redis.
- Not in request logs, access logs, error bodies, stack traces or APM spans. `RevealSecretResponse`
  and `CopySecretsResponse` are the only carriers, and neither is logged, echoed or retained.
- Not in an error message. `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` is `That secret could not be found`;
  `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` is `Revealing {key} needs the Admin role` — the **key name**, never the
  value. `SECRET_KEY_INVALID` and `SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE` interpolate the key, never the value
  (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:505, 516`).
- A GCM tag mismatch is `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, never `404` and never a plausible-looking wrong
  value. A tag failure means the row or the key is wrong; that is a fault, not an answer.
- Redis holds the reveal throttle counter and nothing else about secrets.

**S-5 · Versions of a secret are encrypted — because there are none.**
A secret document's history is **rotation events with no snapshot**. `secret_rotations` (T-24) has
no `value`, `before`, `after`, `content` or JSONB column and **must never acquire one**; adding one
is a schema change that has to be refused in review. `VersionEntry.hasSnapshot` is the literal
`false` and `lines` is `[]` (`src/lib/versions.ts:50-62`), which makes View, Compare and Restore
disappear from the dialog (`src/components/versions/version-list.tsx:84`) and puts a standing notice
in its place: *"Rotation history only. Secret values are never held by this client, so there is
nothing here to compare or restore — reveal a value from the vault instead."*
(`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:140-141`). `restore: null` is passed explicitly
(`:155`). Where a secret *value* is stored — the `secrets` row and any re-encryption of it during a
data-key rotation — it is ciphertext under the rules of S-4, so the statement "versions of a secret
are also encrypted" holds vacuously in the only direction it can: **there is no unencrypted
historical copy anywhere, because there is no historical copy at all.**

---

### 23.2 Who may do what

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `secret.reveal` and `secret.rotate` are **Admin-only** in the role matrix
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:66-75`, cumulative accumulation at `:84-96`). Neither key is in
`OWNER_ESCALATIONS` (`:102-108`), so **owning a secret document does not let you read it** — the one
place in the whole matrix where ownership buys nothing.

| Key | Roles holding it | Governs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret.reveal` | `admin` only | E-103 (reveal one, copy one), E-104 (copy several), E-105 (read the trail). **`copy` has no key of its own** — it is gated by `secret.reveal` and audited as a reveal (canon §2.8; `src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`). |
| `secret.rotate` | `admin` only | E-102 (the whole-list replace: add, rename, replace, reorder, delete). |
| `node.create` + `document.create` | `manager`, `admin` | Creating the secret document node itself (E-024). |
| visibility | any member with access to the node | E-101 — the masked list. |

**`secret.reveal` is in `READ_ONLY_KEYS`** (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:29-33`), so it survives
all three narrowing layers: a trashed, frozen or locked secret document can still be **read**, but
`secret.rotate` is a write and is refused by every one of them.

**The two-question check the frontend already models.** `mayUnlock` asks twice and both must say yes
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:301-320`):

```ts
function mayUnlock(nodeId, role, key: "secret.reveal" | "secret.rotate") {
  return roleHas(role, key)        // the role the CLIENT is running as — the preview
      && callerCan(nodeId, key);   // the real signed-in user's effective role on this node
}
```

The comment is the specification: the client-supplied `role` *"can only ever narrow"*, and the
authoritative answer is `callerCan`, resolved from the store, *"because a role arriving in a call is
a claim, and an endpoint that trusts one is asking the caller how much access they would like."*

**On the wire this becomes:** the server resolves the caller's effective role from the session and
the node's access chain — never from a body field (canon C-09). The role-preview mode reaches the
API as an optional `previewAs` narrowing filter that may only reduce the answer; a `previewAs` that
outranks the caller's real role is `400 PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES` (canon §4.3, OQ-21). **`RevealInput.role`
and `SaveSecretsInput.role` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:325, 476`) do not appear in any
request body in this specification.**

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-23)** — the PRD says Admin *or Manager* may reveal; the frontend says Admin only.
**Evidence** — PRD `DV-SEC-23` (`PRD_FSD_All_in_One_Workspace_45_Detailed.md:126`) grants Reveal and
Copy to Admin/Manager. The matrix puts both keys under `ADMIN`
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:73-74`), and **every** user-facing string in the app says Admin:
`Revealing ${entry.key} needs the Admin role` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:346`),
`Copying these values needs the Admin role` (`:441`), `Changing these secrets needs the Admin role`
(`:497`), `Copying values needs the Admin role` (`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:145, 161`),
`Changing secrets needs the Admin role` (`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:111`),
and *"Only owners and admins can reveal or copy these values."* (`:157`).
**Recommendation** — follow the frontend: **Admin only**, expressed as `secret.reveal` /
`secret.rotate` so that moving the line later is one row in the matrix and no endpoint change.
Canon §8.8 has already taken this position. Confirm with the product owner before the first release.
**Impact if wrong** — either Managers cannot do their job and six user-facing strings are lies, or
Managers can read production credentials the UI told them they could not.

---

### 23.3 Response headers — every endpoint in this section

**Every response from E-101 … E-105, success and failure alike, carries:**

```
Cache-Control: no-store
Pragma: no-cache
```

| Header | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Cache-Control` | `no-store` | The only directive that forbids writing the response to **any** store, including disk. `no-cache` alone permits storage and merely requires revalidation, which is not the property wanted here. |
| `Pragma` | `no-cache` | HTTP/1.0 belt-and-braces for intermediaries that predate `Cache-Control`. Redundant on a modern stack, required by the brief, and harmless. |
| `Expires` | `0` | **RECOMMENDATION.** Same reasoning as `Pragma`. |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | **RECOMMENDATION.** Stops a browser re-interpreting a JSON body as something renderable. |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `no-referrer` | **RECOMMENDATION.** No secret id or node id leaves in a `Referer`. |
| `X-Request-Id` | ULID | Echoed on every response (§7.10). It is the join key between an error, a log line and an `audit_events` row. |

`no-store` is applied to the **masked** endpoints too, not only the revealing ones. E-101 returns
key names, environment labels and rotation timestamps; that is an inventory of a workspace's
credentials, and it does not belong in a shared proxy cache or a disk cache either. There are no
`ETag`s and no conditional requests anywhere in this API (§7.5), so nothing is lost by refusing to
cache.

**Nothing in this section is ever served from a CDN, and no response body from it is written to
Redis.** The reveal throttle counter is the only secret-related value in Redis, and it is a count.

---

### 23.4 The audit contract — two sinks, one transaction

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Every secret operation writes to **two** places, and canon OQ-68 settles
that both are real rows in one transaction rather than one being a projection of the other:

1. **`secret_access_events`** (T-25) — the document's own trail, rendered by the right-hand panel as
   `SecretAuditEntry[]` (`src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx`). Per-document,
   per-secret, with the key name and the caller's address.
2. **`audit_events`** (T-36) — the workspace log (`SY-AUD-41`), read by the admin audit screen
   through E-136. Per-tenant, filterable by module, severity and actor.

They exist side by side because they answer different questions: *"who has touched this vault"* and
*"what has happened in this workspace"*. The frontend writes both from one function
(`pushAudit`, `src/services/devtools-service.ts:363-396`) — *"One write, two readers: the document's
own trail and the workspace audit log (SY-AUD-41)."*

**The mapping, exactly as implemented** (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:382-395`):

| Operation | `secret_access_events.action` | `.outcome` | `audit_events.action` | `.severity` | `.outcome` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reveal, allowed | `reveal` | `allowed` | `secret.reveal` | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Reveal, refused | `reveal` | `denied` | `secret.reveal` | `error` | `denied` |
| Copy one, allowed | `copy` | `allowed` | `secret.reveal` | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Copy one, refused | `copy` | `denied` | `secret.reveal` | `error` | `denied` |
| Copy several, allowed | `copy` (one row **per key**) | `allowed` | `secret.reveal` (one row per key) | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Copy several, refused | `copy` (one row **per chosen key**) | `denied` | `secret.reveal` (per key) | `error` | `denied` |
| Rotate / rename / add / delete | `rotate` (one row per changed or removed entry) | `allowed` | `secret.rotate` | `warn` | `allowed` |
| Rotate, refused | *(none — the check precedes the per-entry loop)* | — | `secret.rotate` | `error` | `denied` |

Copy files under `secret.reveal` in the workspace log because *"Copying is a read of plaintext, so
it files under reveal. Only an actual write to the stored value is a rotation."*
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`). The two are still kept apart in
`secret_access_events.action` because they carry different risk: *"one puts a value on a screen for
thirty seconds, the other puts it on a clipboard indefinitely"* (`src/types/devtools.ts:90-96`).

**`audit_events.detail` is a fixed, value-free sentence chosen by `(action, outcome)`**
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:566-571`):

| Case | `detail` |
| --- | --- |
| `rotate`, allowed | `Stored value replaced. The value itself is not recorded.` |
| `copy`, allowed | `Value placed on the clipboard once. Not stored by the client.` |
| `reveal`, allowed | `Value returned once and cleared from the client on a timer.` |
| any, denied | `Refused: the role does not hold the permission for this action.` |

**`target` is the key name and nothing else** — *"Human label of the thing acted on — never an id,
never a payload."* (`src/types/audit.ts:35-36`). **There is no `detail` column on
`secret_access_events`**: the panel derives the sentence from `(action, outcome)` at render time.

**`ip` is server-sourced from the socket, never accepted from a client.** Both type comments say so
(`src/types/devtools.ts:106`, `src/types/audit.ts:32`), and the mock's placeholder exists precisely
to stand in for it (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:369-370`). A client-supplied address in an
audit row makes the whole log worthless.

**Ordering, which is the part most easily got wrong.** On a refusal the audit rows are written
**before** the `403` is returned and are **committed even though the request fails**. That means the
audit write is its own committed transaction, not a rollback casualty of the business transaction
that never happened. On a bulk copy refusal, one row per chosen key is written before the single
`403` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:436-444`). On success the audit rows commit **with** the
operation, so a reveal that returns a value it did not record is impossible.

**The workspace log is append-only by construction.** The service exposes `record` and `list` and
nothing else, *"so no screen can grow an Edit button that quietly works"*
(`src/types/audit.ts:4-10`; `src/services/audit-service.ts:14-19`). There is no write endpoint for
`audit_events` and no chapter may add one (canon §3.23). `secret_access_events` and
`secret_rotations` follow the same rule: no `UPDATE` grant, no `DELETE` grant, no soft-delete
column.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-68)** — `SecretAuditEntry` cannot distinguish an allowed access from a denied one.
**Evidence** — the interface has no `outcome` field (`src/types/devtools.ts:99-108`), and the mock
smuggles the distinction into the address string as `` `${ip} (denied)` ``
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:379`), which the panel then renders verbatim
(`src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx:53`).
**Recommendation** — return `ip` as the bare address and add `outcome: AuditOutcome` to
`SecretAuditEntry`. The field is additive, today's client ignores unknown fields, and the panel can
then badge a denial instead of reading it out of a malformed IP string.
**Impact if wrong** — either the API emits a fake IP forever, or denials become invisible in the one
panel a security reviewer opens first.

---

### 23.5 The reveal path

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client · use-secret-document.ts
    participant API as API edge
    participant AZ as Authz · session · membership · access chain
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant R as Redis · reveal throttle
    participant KMS as Key service

    C->>API: POST /api/v1/nodes/nodeId/secrets/secretId/reveal<br/>body · action = reveal

    API->>AZ: resolve session cookie
    alt no valid session
        AZ-->>API: none
        API-->>C: 401 AUTH_REQUIRED<br/>Cache-Control: no-store · Pragma: no-cache
    end

    API->>AZ: workspace membership for this node's workspace
    alt not a member
        AZ-->>API: no role at all
        API-->>C: 404 NODE_NOT_FOUND<br/>same answer as "does not exist"
    end

    API->>DB: nodes + access_rules ancestor walk → node access
    alt node not visible
        DB-->>API: pruned
        API-->>C: 404 NODE_NOT_FOUND
    end

    API->>AZ: does the effective role hold secret.reveal on this node?
    Note over AZ: Admin only · owner escalation does NOT apply<br/>previewAs may narrow, never widen

    API->>R: increment the reveal counter · 20 per 5 min · per user per workspace

    alt denied — by permission or by throttle
        API->>DB: BEGIN · INSERT secret_access_events outcome=denied<br/>INSERT audit_events secret.reveal severity=error outcome=denied · COMMIT
        API-->>C: 403 SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED · or 429 SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED<br/>Cache-Control: no-store · Pragma: no-cache<br/>no value, no ciphertext, no length hint
    else allowed
        API->>DB: SELECT value_encrypted · value_iv · value_auth_tag · value_key_id<br/>FROM secrets WHERE id = secretId AND node_id = nodeId
        API->>KMS: unwrap the workspace data key · cached, short TTL, memory only
        KMS-->>API: DEK
        Note over API: AES-256-GCM decrypt<br/>AAD = workspace_id ‖ node_id ‖ secret id ‖ key<br/>tag mismatch → 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, never a value
        API->>DB: BEGIN · INSERT secret_access_events outcome=allowed<br/>INSERT audit_events secret.reveal severity=warn outcome=allowed · COMMIT
        API-->>C: 200 RevealSecretResponse · value returned once<br/>Cache-Control: no-store · Pragma: no-cache
        Note over C: component state only · auto-hides after 30 s<br/>never localStorage, sessionStorage, a cache, a URL or a log
    end
```

Two properties of the diagram are load-bearing:

- **The audit write precedes the response on both branches.** The denial branch commits its rows and
  *then* answers `403`; the success branch commits its rows in the same transaction boundary as the
  read and *then* answers `200`. There is no path from "decrypted" to "returned" that skips the
  write.
- **404 before 403.** Membership and node visibility answer `404 NODE_NOT_FOUND` — identical to a
  node that does not exist — so the URL cannot be used to discover that a secret document exists. The
  `403` is reserved for a caller who *can* see the vault but may not open it, which is exactly the
  case the UI already renders (`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:153-161`).

---

### 23.6 Endpoints

#### `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/nodes`

**Purpose** — Create a secret document. This is **E-024**, the one node-creation endpoint; this
entry documents only its secret slice — the fields it takes for `documentKind: "secret"` and the
row it writes in `secret_documents`.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `node.create` **and** `document.create` on the target parent, plus workspace
membership. Manager+ (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:48, 58`).

**A reviewer should notice what this means, because it is deliberate and it is not obvious:** a
Manager can create an empty secret document but can neither fill it (`secret.rotate` is Admin) nor
read it (`secret.reveal` is Admin). The frontend confirms this is the intent — the create menu item
is gated only by the create flow (`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:126-133`), and
`useCreateDocument` calls **no** devtools service at all for `kind === "secret"`
(`src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:60-66`), so the vault is created empty by construction. It is not
a privilege escalation: creating a container grants no access to anything, and the Edit button is
disabled with the tooltip *"Changing secrets needs the Admin role"*
(`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:107-112`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | The tenant. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CreateNodeRequest`, secret slice:

```ts
interface CreateNodeRequest {
  readonly kind: NodeKind;              // "document"
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  readonly name: string;                // "Untitled secrets" by default
  readonly documentKind?: DocumentKind; // "secret"
  readonly icon?: string;               // "🔐" — src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:14-18
}
```

There is **no `entries` field.** A vault is never created with credentials in it: entries arrive
only through E-102, which is Admin-gated and audited per key. Accepting values on a create request
would give `node.create` a path to writing secrets.

**Response** — `DriveNode` (the `DocumentNode` variant), `200`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Parent must be a container; sibling slugs for uniquification. |
| `nodes` | INSERT | `kind = 'document'`, `document_kind = 'secret'`, `icon = '🔐'`. |
| `secret_documents` | INSERT | `node_id`, `workspace_id`, `created_by`/`updated_by` = session user. **No entries.** |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | `module: "node"`, `action: "node.create"`, severity `info`. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** The `nodes` row and the `secret_documents` row commit together.

**Realtime** — `node.changed` (RT-11), `change: "created"`, ids only.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — empty `name`, unknown `documentKind`. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-create-document.ts:40-88`, invoked from
`src/components/shared/create-menu-items.tsx:126-133`.

**Response Headers** — the standard §23.3 set. Even though this response carries no secret material,
it carries the existence of a vault.

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/secrets`

**Purpose** — Return the secret document's metadata **and its entry list, masked**. One endpoint
serves both: `SecretDocument` is `{ nodeId, name, entries }`, so "get the metadata" and "list the
entries" are the same read (`src/types/devtools.ts:84-88`).

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **Visibility** on the node, plus workspace membership. **No `secret.reveal`
required** — a Viewer with access to the folder sees the key names and the masks, which is the
screen the UI renders with the banner *"Only owners and admins can reveal or copy these values.
Asking anyway is refused by the server and still recorded."*
(`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:153-161`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The secret document's node. Must be `document_kind = 'secret'`. |

**Query Params** — None. The list is bounded by construction (a vault holds tens of keys, not
thousands) and is returned whole, in stored order.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SecretDocument`.

```ts
/** src/types/devtools.ts:84-88 — unchanged. */
interface SecretDocument {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  /** Projected from nodes.name on every read. Never a stored column. */
  readonly name: string;
  /** THE ORDER IS THE STORED ORDER — secrets.position ASC. */
  readonly entries: readonly SecretEntry[];
}

/** src/types/devtools.ts:73-82 — unchanged. NO `value` FIELD, DELIBERATELY. */
interface SecretEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly key: string;                  // e.g. DATABASE_PASSWORD
  /** Constant: twelve U+2022 bullets. Never derived from the real length. */
  readonly maskedValue: string;
  readonly environmentOptionId: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;            // last rotation, ISO 8601
  readonly rotatedBy: UserSummary;
  /** OPTIONAL: omitted when absent, never null (C-08). */
  readonly note?: string;
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/nodes/9b3f…/secrets
// Cache-Control: no-store
// Pragma: no-cache
{
  "nodeId": "9b3f7c21-…",
  "name": "Payment Secrets",
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "4a1c…",
      "key": "DATABASE_PASSWORD",
      "maskedValue": "••••••••••••",
      "environmentOptionId": "b2d0…",
      "updatedAt": "2026-08-21T14:02:55.100Z",
      "rotatedBy": { "id": "usr_khanh-…", "name": "Khanh Luu", "email": "khanh@nexdrop.vn", "initials": "KL" },
      "note": "Rotate with the quarterly credential review."
    },
    {
      "id": "77e2…",
      "key": "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY",
      "maskedValue": "••••••••••••",
      "environmentOptionId": "b2d0…",
      "updatedAt": "2026-08-19T08:11:03.000Z",
      "rotatedBy": { "id": "usr_mai-…", "name": "Mai Tran", "email": "mai@nexdrop.vn", "initials": "MT" }
    }
  ]
}
```

Every `maskedValue` in that response is the identical twelve-bullet constant. Two secrets of wildly
different lengths are indistinguishable, which is the point (S-2).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check, `name` for the response. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | Visibility resolution. |
| `secret_documents` | READ | By PK `node_id`. |
| `secrets` | READ | **`SELECT id, key, environment_id, note, position, rotated_by, updated_at … ORDER BY position ASC`** on `UNIQUE (node_id, position)`. **The four ciphertext columns are not in the projection.** Serve it through the `secrets_masked` view (S-1). |
| `users` | READ | `rotated_by` → `UserSummary`, batched. |
| `environments` | READ | Not needed for the response; the id is returned raw and the picker resolves labels from E-106. |

**No audit row.** Reading the masked list is not a privileged read: it returns no plaintext and no
length information. Canon OQ-26 audits privileged *reads* — E-046, the admin recovery console, and
E-137, the audit export — and this is not one. Auditing every vault page-view would bury the reveals
that matter in noise.

**Transaction** — Not required. A single read-only snapshot.

**Realtime** — None, and deliberately so: a frame announcing that a credential document changed is
worth nothing to a client that must refetch through a permission check anyway, and RT-05's precedent
is that *"a frame announcing a revocation must not be the thing that leaks what was revoked"*
(`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`).

**Response Headers** — `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache` (§23.3).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown node **or one the caller may not see**. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` — visible node with no `secret_documents` row. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` — the node is a page, a config document, a board or a file. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:60-64` (the `useAsyncResource` loader),
rendered by `src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:30-83` via
`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:43, 178`.

---

#### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/secrets`

**Purpose** — Write the document's secrets. **This is the add endpoint, the update endpoint, the
delete endpoint and the reorder endpoint, all at once**: the request carries the whole list in the
order it should be stored, and the server makes the stored list match it.

**Why one endpoint and not four.** *"The whole list is replaced in the order given, which is what
makes reordering, renaming and deleting one operation rather than three endpoints."*
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:479-487`). The consequence is worth stating for a reviewer: there
is exactly **one** write path into `secrets`, it is Admin-gated, and it audits per key. Four
narrower endpoints would be four places to get the permission check right.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **`secret.rotate` on this node**, plus workspace membership. Admin only
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:74`). Not owner-escalatable. `secret.rotate` is a **write**, so the
trashed, frozen and locked narrowing layers all refuse it
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-85`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The secret document's node. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `SaveSecretsRequest` (canon §5.4):

```ts
interface SaveSecretsRequest {
  /** THE WHOLE LIST, in the order it should be stored. */
  readonly entries: readonly SecretDraftEntry[];
}

/** canon §5.3, mirroring src/services/devtools-service.ts:458-471. */
interface SecretDraftEntry {
  /** The id of an existing secret, or null for one being added. */
  readonly id: string | null;
  readonly key: string;
  /**
   * OPTIONAL, and this is the load-bearing part: an OMITTED value means
   * "leave the stored value untouched". Never null — `null` is not a way
   * to clear a secret, and there is no clear operation.
   */
  readonly value?: string;
}
```

**The omitted `value` is the security property of this endpoint.** *"That is what lets the editor
rename a key, reorder the list or delete a neighbour without ever holding the plaintext of the rows
it is not changing — the stored value stays where it is and is never round-tripped through the
client."* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:462-470`; the client side is
`src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:16-33, 69-76`, where an untouched row carries `value: null` and the
DTO builder simply omits the key). The server carries the **ciphertext, IV, tag and key id forward
unchanged**; it does **not** decrypt and re-encrypt, because there is no reason to bring plaintext
into memory for a rename.

**The four operations, expressed in this one body.** Given a stored list of
`[{A}, {B}, {C}]`:

| Operation | Request `entries` | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Add** an entry | `[{id:"A"}, {id:"B"}, {id:"C"}, {id:null, key:"NEW_KEY", value:"…"}]` (keys elided) | One `INSERT`, `position = 3`. `secret_rotations.change_kind = 'added'`. |
| **Update** a value | `[{id:"A", key:"A_KEY", value:"new"}, {id:"B"…}, {id:"C"…}]` | `A` re-encrypted with a **fresh IV**; `updated_at`/`rotated_by` move. `change_kind = 'rotated'`. |
| **Rename** a key | `[{id:"A", key:"RENAMED"}, …]` — no `value` | `A.key` updated, ciphertext untouched; `updated_at`/`rotated_by` still move, because a rename **is** a change (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:538`). `change_kind = 'renamed'`. |
| **Delete** an entry | `[{id:"A"…}, {id:"C"…}]` — `B` simply absent | `B` hard-deleted. A `secret_rotations` and a `secret_access_events` row are still written for it — *"A removed secret is a rotation too — the trail has to show where it went."* (`:554-558`). `change_kind = 'removed'`. |
| **Reorder** | the same three ids in a different order | `position` renumbered `0..n-1`. `isChanged` is false for all three, so **no** `updated_at` move and **no** audit rows: reordering is not a rotation. |

Note the last row carefully: `isChanged = !existing || existing.key !== key || value was supplied`
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:538`). Position is not in that predicate. A pure reorder is a
metadata write, not a credential event, and must not fill the trail with false rotations.

**Validation, in this exact order** (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:488-521`):

1. **`secret.rotate`** on this node, resolved from the session → else `403 SECRET_ROTATE_DENIED`,
   message `Changing these secrets needs the Admin role`, detail
   `Ask a workspace admin to rotate them for you.` This check comes **first**, before any key
   validation, so a caller without the permission learns nothing about which keys are acceptable.
2. **Every key valid**: non-empty after trim, and free of whitespace, `=`, `"` and `'`
   (`isValidSecretKey`, `src/lib/env-file.ts:122-124`) → else `400 SECRET_KEY_INVALID`,
   `"{key}" is not a usable name for a secret`, detail
   `A name cannot be empty or contain spaces, quotes or an equals sign.` The rule is **deliberately
   permissive** — *"Plenty of real deployments use keys this side of the `UPPER_SNAKE` convention —
   dotted namespaces, hyphens, lowercase — and refusing to store one because it is unfashionable
   would make the editor useless for the config it was needed for."* (`src/lib/env-file.ts:113-121`).
3. **No duplicate trimmed keys** → else `400 SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE`, `"{key}" appears twice`, detail
   `Every secret in a document needs its own name.`

`isConventionalSecretKey` — `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/` (`src/lib/env-file.ts:127-129`) — is a
**client-side warning only** and **must never become a server rejection**. The editor renders it as
amber text (`src/components/devtools/secret-editor-panel.tsx:118-123`).

**`environmentOptionId` and `note` are not writable here today.** They are carried over from the
existing entry, and a newly added entry defaults to the workspace's first environment
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:38, 544, 547`). See OQ-64.

**Response** — `SecretDocument`, `200` — the whole masked list in its new order, exactly the E-101
shape. **It contains no values**, even for the entries the caller just supplied values for. The
client applies it through `controller.apply`, which *"forgets every revealed value, because it has
to: a save can rename, replace or remove any of them, and a plaintext still on screen under a key
that no longer holds it is worse than no plaintext at all"* (`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:37-45,
170-178`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind, trashed/frozen/locked state, `name` for the response and the audit `target`. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | `secret.rotate` resolution. |
| `secret_documents` | READ `… FOR UPDATE` | Row lock. Serialises two concurrent whole-list replaces and guards the `secret_rotations.version` counter (canon §1.4). |
| `secrets` | READ | The current list, `WHERE node_id = :n`, **including** ciphertext sidecars for the rows being carried forward. |
| `environments` | READ | Only for newly added entries, to resolve the default. |
| `secrets` | INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE | Upsert the supplied list; renumber `position` `0..n-1`; hard-delete every existing row whose id is absent from the request. `UNIQUE (node_id, position)` is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` because the renumber transiently collides. |
| `secret_rotations` | INSERT | One row per **changed** entry and one per **removed** entry. `version` from the per-document counter, `key` snapshotted as it stood, `change_kind`, `summary` rendered at write time, `rotated_by` from the session. **No value column.** |
| `secret_access_events` | INSERT | One row per changed and removed entry: `action = 'rotate'`, `outcome = 'allowed'`, `key`, `actor_id`, `ip` from the socket. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | `module: "secret"`, `action: "secret.rotate"`, severity `warn`, `target` = the key name, `detail` = `Stored value replaced. The value itself is not recorded.`, outcome `allowed`. One per changed/removed entry. |
| `secret_documents` | UPDATE | `updated_at = now()`, `updated_by` = session user. |
| `nodes` | UPDATE | `updated_at = now()`. |

**On refusal** (step 1 above) the transaction that would have written the list never opens; instead a
**separate committed transaction** writes one `audit_events` row — `secret.rotate`, severity
`error`, outcome `denied`, detail `Refused: the role does not hold the permission for this action.`
The mock writes no per-entry `secret_access_events` rows on a rotate refusal, because the check
precedes the per-entry loop (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:495-500`); reproduce that.

**Transaction** — **Required, and it is the widest transaction in this chapter.** Atomic together:
every `secrets` insert, update and delete; every `secret_rotations` row; every
`secret_access_events` row; every `audit_events` row; the `secret_documents` and `nodes` touches.
Two failure modes this prevents: a partially-applied list (some keys rotated, some not, with no way
for the client to tell which), and a rotation that lands without its trail. The client's contract
depends on the first — *"A failed save keeps the draft: a network error does not cost someone the
credential they just pasted in."* (`src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:94-106, 236-243`) — which is only
safe if a failed save changed nothing.

**Realtime** — None. See E-101.

**Response Headers** — `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `SECRET_KEY_INVALID` — a key is empty after trim or contains whitespace, `=`, `"` or `'`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE` — two entries carry the same trimmed key. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `entries` missing or not an array; an entry's `value` is `null` rather than omitted; an `id` that is neither `null` nor a UUID. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `SECRET_ROTATE_DENIED` — **audited before the refusal is returned.** |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `NODE_LOCKED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` — an `id` in the request does not belong to this document. **A foreign id is never silently treated as a new entry.** |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` — includes any encryption failure. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-secret-editor.ts:222-244` (`save`), whose body is built by
`toDraft` at `:69-76`; surfaced by `src/components/devtools/secret-editor-panel.tsx:35-144` and the
Save button at `src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:92-99`. The `.env` paste path feeds
the same draft: parsing is entirely client-side and pure — *"takes a string and returns a structure.
Nothing here logs, caches, or persists"* (`src/lib/env-file.ts:10-12`) — and the pasted text lives in
one component's state and dies with it (`src/components/devtools/secret-env-paste.tsx:28-29`).
**No `.env` text is ever posted to the API**; it is parsed to entries first.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-64)** — a secret's environment and note have no write path.
**Evidence** — both fields exist on `SecretEntry` (`src/types/devtools.ts:78, 81`), are rendered
(`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:224-226, 255`) and are seeded
(`src/mock/devtools.ts:51-79`), but `saveSecrets` preserves rather than accepts them
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:544, 547`) and the editor panel has no control for either
(`src/components/devtools/secret-editor-panel.tsx:51-127`).
**Recommendation** — extend `SecretDraftEntry` with optional `environmentOptionId?: string` and
`note?: string`, omission meaning "unchanged", exactly like `value`. Changing either moves
`updated_at` and writes an `audit_events` row, but **must not** be filed as `rotate` and must not
write a `secret_rotations` row: it is not a write to the stored value. File it as `document.update`.
**Impact if wrong** — a secret created in the UI is stuck on the first environment forever and its
note can never be written; the seeded data implies a feature the app cannot perform.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/secrets/:secretId/reveal`

**Purpose** — Return one secret's plaintext, once. This is **the only single-value door**, and it
serves both the eye icon (reveal to screen) and the copy icon (reveal to clipboard) — the two are
distinguished by `action`, not by endpoint.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **`secret.reveal` on this node**, plus workspace membership. Admin only
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:73`). Not owner-escalatable. `secret.reveal` is in `READ_ONLY_KEYS`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:29-33`), so it survives the trashed, frozen and locked layers — a
credential in an archived project can still be read, which is deliberate: archiving a project must
not lock an on-call engineer out of a production key.

**`action: "copy"` has no permission key of its own.** It is gated by the same `secret.reveal` and
filed in the workspace log as `secret.reveal`, because *"Copying is a read of plaintext, so it files
under reveal. Only an actual write to the stored value is a rotation."*
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The secret document's node. |
| `secretId` | UUID | `secrets.id`. **Must belong to this node** — the query predicate is `WHERE id = :secretId AND node_id = :nodeId`, so a secret id from another vault answers `404 SECRET_NOT_FOUND`, never that vault's value. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `RevealSecretRequest` (canon §5.4):

```ts
interface RevealSecretRequest {
  /**
   * Which read this is. Not a permission distinction — both need
   * `secret.reveal` — but a RISK distinction, and it is recorded:
   * reveal puts a value on a screen for thirty seconds, copy puts it
   * on a clipboard indefinitely (src/types/devtools.ts:90-96).
   */
  readonly action: "reveal" | "copy";
}
```

`"rotate"` is a member of `SecretAction` but is **not accepted here**: rotation is E-102. A body
carrying `action: "rotate"` is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`. **No `role` field**, and no other field —
the caller's identity and role come from the session (C-09).

**Response** — `RevealSecretResponse`, `200`.

```ts
interface RevealSecretResponse {
  /** The plaintext. Returned once. Never stored by the client, never logged by the server. */
  readonly value: string;
  /** Echoed so the client can label the field it just filled without a second lookup. */
  readonly key: string;
  /** Server clock, for the client's 30-second auto-hide timer. */
  readonly revealedAt: string;
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/nodes/9b3f…/secrets/77e2…/reveal   { "action": "reveal" }
// Cache-Control: no-store
// Pragma: no-cache
{
  "value": "sk_live_51NdX2mKq7RfP0aZ4tYb8Uv",
  "key": "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY",
  "revealedAt": "2026-08-27T09:31:12.004Z"
}
```

**Rate limiting.** Per user, per workspace: **20 reveals / 5 minutes** (§7.9, `RECOMMENDATION` — no
frontend evidence sets a number), counter in Redis. A throttled reveal is a **denial** and is
audited as one before the `429` is returned. Both E-103 and E-104 draw on the same bucket, and E-104
draws `keys.length` from it — otherwise "Copy all" would be an unlimited reveal wearing a different
name.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check, ancestor walk. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | `secret.reveal` resolution. |
| `secret_documents` | READ | By PK; supplies `workspace_id` for the data key. |
| `secrets` | READ | `SELECT key, value_encrypted, value_iv, value_auth_tag, value_key_id WHERE id = :secretId AND node_id = :nodeId`. This is the **only** query in the system that selects the ciphertext columns, alongside E-104's. |
| `secret_access_events` | INSERT | `action` = the request's action, `outcome` = `allowed` \| `denied`, `key`, `secret_id`, `actor_id`, `ip` from the socket, `at = now()`. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | `module: "secret"`, `action: "secret.reveal"`, severity `warn` (allowed) or `error` (denied), `target` = the key name, `detail` per §23.4, outcome to match. |

**Transaction** — **Required**, and the ordering matters more than the atomicity:

- **Allowed:** the `secret_access_events` and `audit_events` inserts commit **before the response
  body is written**. If the audit write fails, the request fails with `500` and **no value is
  returned**. A reveal the log does not know about must be impossible.
- **Denied:** the two audit rows are written in their **own committed transaction**, and only then is
  the `403` (or `429`) returned. They are not rolled back by the failure of the request they
  describe — *"a refusal nobody can see is not a control"* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:360-362`).
- The audit rows for a denial are written **even when the secret id does not exist**? **No** — the
  order is: resolve the node → resolve the secret (`404 SECRET_NOT_FOUND` with no audit row, because
  there is no key to name) → check the permission (`403` **with** audit rows, naming the key). This
  is the frontend's order exactly (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:338-349`) and it is the right
  one: auditing a reveal attempt against a non-existent id would let an attacker write arbitrary key
  names into the security log.

**Realtime** — None. A frame announcing that somebody revealed a credential would broadcast to every
open tab in the workspace the fact that a specific key was read, which is information the workspace
log already holds behind `workspace.audit.view`.

**Response Headers** — `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`. Non-negotiable on this
endpoint above all others: the response body is a live credential.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `action` missing, or not `reveal` \| `copy`. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` — `Revealing {key} needs the Admin role`, detail `Ask a workspace admin to share it with you.` **Two audit rows are written first.** |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown node or one the caller may not see. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` — `That secret could not be found`. Also the answer for a `secretId` belonging to a different document. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 429 | `validation` | `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` — `isRetryable: true` and `retryAfterSeconds` set explicitly; `Retry-After` header. **Audited as a denial first.** |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` — includes a GCM tag mismatch, a missing data key, and a failed audit write. |

**Frontend Used By** — three call sites in `src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts`:
`:97-120` (`reveal`, `action: "reveal"` — puts the value in component state and starts the 30-second
timer), `:134-156` (`copy`, `action: "copy"` — writes to the clipboard and **does not** put the value
in `revealed`, so the screen stays masked), `:122-132` (`take`, `action: "reveal"` — hands one value
to the editor's field without revealing it on the read view or starting a timer). Rendered by
`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:233-252` and
`src/components/devtools/secret-editor-panel.tsx:38-46, 89-100`.

**Client-side lifetime the backend must not undermine** (`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts`): a
revealed value lives in component state only — never `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, a cache, a URL
or a log (`:48-55`) — auto-hides after `AUTO_HIDE_MS = 30_000` (`:11-12`), and every timer is cleared
and every value dropped on unmount (`:87-95`). The server supports this by returning the plaintext
**once**, with `no-store`, and by offering no endpoint that would let a client populate a whole page
with values.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/secrets/copy`

**Purpose** — Reveal **several** secrets at once, as a single `.env`-formatted clipboard blob. This
is both "Copy selected" and "Copy all" — one endpoint, one permission check, one audit row per key.

**Why not a loop of E-103 calls.** *"The values assembled here rather than fetched one at a time by
the client — a loop of single reveals would write the same audit trail but leave every value sitting
in the page in between."* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:412-418`). And why the response is a
blob rather than a map: *"The values go from the service straight to the clipboard; none of them
enters `revealed`, so the screen stays masked throughout. That separation is the point of having a
bulk copy at all — the alternative, revealing everything and letting the user select the text, puts a
whole credential file on a screen in an office."* (`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:158-169`).
**There is no endpoint that returns a per-secret plaintext map, and none may be added.**

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **`secret.reveal` on this node**, plus workspace membership. Admin only. *"There are
no per-secret permissions in this model, so the check is per-document and the answer is all or
nothing. If per-secret scopes are ever added, this is the one function that has to learn to return a
subset."* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:419-422`).

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The secret document's node. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `CopySecretsRequest` (canon §5.4):

```ts
interface CopySecretsRequest {
  /**
   * Which secrets. minItems: 1 — an empty array is REFUSED, never
   * interpreted as "every secret" (canon OQ-66).
   */
  readonly secretIds: readonly string[];
}
```

**`minItems: 1` is a security decision, not a validation preference.** The frontend's service treats
an empty list as "every secret in the document — Copy all" (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:400-401,
431-434`), and "Copy all" is wired as `controller.copyMany([])`
(`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:63`). Canon OQ-66 rejects that as *"an unsafe wire
default"*: a bug that drops the id list — a serialisation failure, a filter that matched nothing, a
stale selection — would silently escalate a two-key copy into a whole-vault export, and the audit
trail would faithfully record it as intended. **"Copy all" must send the full id list explicitly**,
which the client already has (`document.entries.map(entry => entry.id)`, the shape used by "Select
every secret" at `src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:60`). An empty array is
`400 SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY`.

**Response** — `CopySecretsResponse`, `200`.

```ts
interface CopySecretsResponse {
  /** `KEY=value` lines, ready for the clipboard. */
  readonly text: string;
  /** Keys included, so the caller can say how many without reading values. */
  readonly keys: readonly string[];
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/nodes/9b3f…/secrets/copy   { "secretIds": ["4a1c…", "77e2…"] }
// Cache-Control: no-store
// Pragma: no-cache
{
  "text": "DATABASE_PASSWORD=pg-3f9c-Ab21-Qz77-payments\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_51NdX2mKq7RfP0aZ4tYb8Uv\n",
  "keys": ["DATABASE_PASSWORD", "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"]
}
```

`keys` exists *"so the caller can say how many without reading values"*
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:405-410`) — the client renders
`Copied ${keys.length} secret(s) — the values were not stored`
(`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:187-190`) without ever parsing `text`.

**`.env` serialisation, server-side.** `toEnvText` (`src/lib/env-file.ts:149-153`) emits
`KEY=value` lines in the order given, one trailing newline. A value is quoted **only** where leaving
it bare would change it — leading or trailing whitespace, a newline, a `#`, or empty — escaping
`\\`, `"`, `\n` and `\r` (`:131-147`). *"Quoting everything makes a copied file noisier to read for
no gain."* Reproduce this exactly: a round trip through `parseEnv`
(`src/lib/env-file.ts:73-111`) must return the same values, and the rule that *"a value is everything
after the **first** `=`"* (`:14-17`) is what makes that true for connection strings, base64 and JWTs.

**Ordering.** The response follows the **stored** order (`secrets.position ASC`) filtered to the
requested ids, not the order of `secretIds`. The frontend filters `document.entries` and so is
already in stored order (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:431-434`).

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | `secret.reveal` resolution. |
| `secret_documents` | READ | By PK; `workspace_id` for the data key. |
| `secrets` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :n AND id = ANY(:secretIds) ORDER BY position ASC`, selecting the ciphertext sidecars. If the result is empty → `404 SECRET_NOT_FOUND`, `Those secrets could not be found` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:436`). |
| `secret_access_events` | INSERT | **One row per key**, `action = 'copy'`, outcome to match. |
| `audit_events` | INSERT | **One row per key**, `action = 'secret.reveal'`, severity `warn` or `error`, `target` = the key name. |

**Transaction** — **Required.** All decryptions and all audit rows are one unit; the response is
written only after the audit rows commit. On refusal, one `secret_access_events` row and one
`audit_events` row are written **per chosen key** in their own committed transaction, and only then
is the `403` returned (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:438-444`) — the trail must show which keys
somebody tried to take, not merely that they tried.

**Realtime** — None.

**Response Headers** — `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY` — `secretIds` must carry at least one id (canon OQ-66). |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `secretIds` missing, not an array, or containing a non-UUID. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` — `Copying these values needs the Admin role`, detail `Ask a workspace admin to share them with you.` **One audit row per chosen key is written first.** |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` — none of the ids match this document. **RECOMMENDATION:** a *partial* match returns the matched subset with `200`; the client already prunes ids that no longer exist (`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:36-40`). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 429 | `validation` | `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` — draws `keys.length` from the reveal bucket. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:180-198` (`copyMany`), called from
`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:62-63` — "Copy selected" passes the live selection, "Copy
all" passes `[]` today and must be changed to pass every id (OQ-66).

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/secrets/audit`

**Purpose** — The document's own access trail: every reveal, copy and rotation, **allowed and denied
alike**, with who, when and from which address, and **no values**.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **`secret.reveal` on this node**, plus workspace membership. Admin only. The trail
names which keys exist and who has been reading them; that is not information a Viewer with folder
access should hold. (The frontend renders the panel behind a button available to anyone
(`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:132-141`) and the mock's `listSecretAudit` checks
nothing (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:573-579`); canon §3.16 sets the key, and the client should
gate the button on `can("secret.reveal")` to match.)

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | The secret document's node. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | — | Opaque base64 of `(at, id)`. Never constructed or parsed by a client. |
| `limit` | integer | no | 50 | Hard server cap 200. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SecretAccessPage` of `SecretAuditEntry`, newest first, `(at DESC, id DESC)`.

```ts
interface SecretAccessPage {
  readonly items: readonly SecretAuditEntry[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/** src/types/devtools.ts:99-108 — unchanged. */
interface SecretAuditEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly action: SecretAction;     // "reveal" | "copy" | "rotate"
  readonly secretId: string;
  readonly key: string;
  readonly actor: UserSummary;
  readonly at: string;
  /** Recorded by the server — the client never sources this. */
  readonly ip: string;
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive — see OQ-68. */
  readonly outcome?: AuditOutcome;   // "allowed" | "denied"
}
```

**There is no value field and no `detail` field.** *"Every reveal, copy and rotation, allowed or
refused, with who and when — and no values. A trail that recorded what was revealed would be a
second copy of the secrets, in a log, readable by everyone who can read logs."*
(`src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx:11-17`.)

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | READ | Visibility, kind check. |
| `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | `secret.reveal` resolution. |
| `secret_access_events` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :n ORDER BY at DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit + 1`, on `(node_id, at DESC, id DESC)`. |
| `users` | READ | `actor_id` → `UserSummary`, batched. |

**Transaction** — Not required. Read-only.

**Realtime** — None. The panel reloads on open (`keepPreviousData: true`,
`src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx:24-26`).

**Response Headers** — `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `secret.reveal`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 409 | `conflict` | `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/devtools/secret-audit-panel.tsx:19-26`, toggled from
`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:132-141, 184`.

---

#### `GET /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/versions` — the secret projection

**Purpose** — A secret document's history: **which key rotated, by whom, when.** No snapshots, no
values, no diffs, no restore. This is **E-095** entered on a secret node; canon §3.14 makes the
node's kind select the store, and for a secret the store is `secret_rotations` (T-24).

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on the node, plus workspace membership. The rotation history names keys
and actors but no values; it is the same disclosure level as E-101's masked list, so it takes the
same gate.

**Path Params** — `nodeId` (UUID), the secret document's node.

**Query Params** — `cursor`, `limit` — as E-095 for config. Sort key `(version DESC)`.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `VersionPage` of `VersionEntry`, **every entry with `hasSnapshot: false` and
`lines: []`**.

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/nodes/9b3f…/versions
// Cache-Control: no-store
// Pragma: no-cache
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "0f2a…",
      "version": 14,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-21T14:02:55.100Z",
      "author": { "id": "usr_khanh-…", "name": "Khanh Luu", "email": "khanh@nexdrop.vn", "initials": "KL" },
      "summary": "rotated DATABASE_PASSWORD",
      "lines": [],
      "hasSnapshot": false
    },
    {
      "id": "c81b…",
      "version": 13,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-19T08:11:03.000Z",
      "author": { "id": "usr_mai-…", "name": "Mai Tran", "email": "mai@nexdrop.vn", "initials": "MT" },
      "summary": "removed SANDBOX_API_KEY",
      "lines": [],
      "hasSnapshot": false
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null
}
```

`hasSnapshot: false` is what makes the shared dialog safe for this subject: View, Compare and Restore
disappear (`src/components/versions/version-list.tsx:84`), `restore` is `null`
(`src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:155`), and `useVersionHistory.restore` returns early
for any entry without a snapshot even if a caller tried (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:65`).

**Why this must be served from a table and not projected from live rows.** The frontend derives the
history from the *current* entries' `updatedAt`/`rotatedBy` (`src/lib/versions.ts:50-62`), which
means a **deleted secret vanishes from its own history** and a key rotated three times shows once.
`secret_rotations` fixes that (canon OQ-67): it snapshots `key` as it stood, keeps `secret_id`
without a foreign key so a removal row can outlive its row, and is indexed on
`(node_id, key, rotated_at DESC)` — *the* index for "when was this key last rotated, and by whom",
which is the exact question a quarterly credential review asks.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | READ | Visibility. |
| `secret_rotations` | READ | `WHERE node_id = :n ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT :limit + 1`. **No value column exists to select.** |
| `users` | READ | `rotated_by` → `UserSummary`. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Response Headers** — `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx:148-174`
(`SecretVersionsDialog`), opened from `src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:119-128,
145-151`. Today it computes entries locally from `secretRotationEntries(document)`
(`src/lib/versions.ts:50-62`); pointing its `load` at this endpoint is a one-line change and the
dialog needs nothing else — *"The FE needs no change: it already renders whatever entries it is
given."*

#### E-096, E-097 and E-098 on a secret node — refused, not served

**E-096, E-097 and E-098 answer `409 / conflict`, reason `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE`, on any secret
node.** *"A secret version has no snapshot and can never be diffed or restored"* (canon §4.3). The
refusal is a `409` rather than a `404` because the version genuinely exists — the entry is listed by
E-095 — it simply has nothing to serve. Message: `That version cannot be restored`, detail
`A secret's history records that a key changed, not what it changed to.`

No frontend caller reaches these paths for a secret: `restore: null` is passed explicitly, and the
list hides the buttons. The refusal exists for a hand-written request, and it is the one a reviewer
should try first.

---

### 23.7 What a reviewer must be able to check

A checklist that maps one-to-one onto testable assertions. Every line is grounded above.

| # | Assertion | How to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R-1 | `GET /nodes/{id}/secrets` never returns a value or a length hint. | Inspect the SQL projection; assert every `maskedValue` in a response with mixed-length secrets is byte-identical and 12 `U+2022`. |
| R-2 | No endpoint other than E-103 and E-104 selects `value_encrypted`. | `grep` the repository for the column name; two call sites. |
| R-3 | A denied reveal writes both audit rows **and** returns 403. | Call E-103 as a Manager; assert one `secret_access_events` row with `outcome='denied'` and one `audit_events` row with `severity='error'`, both committed. |
| R-4 | A reveal whose audit write fails returns 500 and no value. | Fault-inject the audit insert. |
| R-5 | A throttled reveal is audited as a denial before the 429. | Exceed the bucket; assert the rows exist. |
| R-6 | A secret id from another document answers 404, not the value. | Call E-103 with a foreign `secretId`. |
| R-7 | `secretIds: []` is refused. | Assert `400 SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY`, not a whole-vault export. |
| R-8 | A rename does not decrypt. | Send E-102 with a changed key and no `value`; assert the DEK unwrap counter does not move and the ciphertext bytes are unchanged. |
| R-9 | A pure reorder writes no rotation rows. | Send E-102 with the same ids reordered; assert `secret_rotations` and `secret_access_events` are unchanged and `updated_at` has not moved. |
| R-10 | A deleted secret still leaves a trail. | Delete an entry via E-102; assert a `secret_rotations` row with `change_kind='removed'` and the snapshotted key. |
| R-11 | `secret_rotations` and `secret_access_events` have no value column and no UPDATE/DELETE grant. | Inspect the schema and the role grants. |
| R-12 | Every response in §23 carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. | Assert on every status code, including 403, 404 and 429. |
| R-13 | No plaintext appears in any log. | Reveal a secret with a known sentinel value; grep application logs, access logs, the audit tables and any APM export for it. |
| R-14 | Owning a secret document grants nothing. | As the node's owner at `member`, call E-101 (200, masked), E-103 (403), E-102 (403). |
| R-15 | A GCM tag mismatch is 500, not a value and not a 404. | Corrupt a `value_auth_tag` in a test fixture. |
| R-16 | E-096 / E-097 / E-098 refuse on a secret node. | Assert `409 VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE`. |
| R-17 | The IP in an audit row comes from the socket. | Send `X-Forwarded-For` and a body claiming an address; assert neither reaches the row except through the trusted proxy chain. |

---

### 23.8 Secret documents — open questions carried

| OQ | What it decides | Position taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OQ-12 | What a container duplicate does to a secret document | Copy keys, environments, notes and order; **every value empty**; one `secret_rotations` row of kind `added` per copied entry. Never copy ciphertext into a node with a different access chain. Refusing the duplicate outright is the acceptable alternative. |
| OQ-23 | Admin only, or Admin and Manager | **Admin only**, per the frontend and canon §8.8. Detailed in §23.2. |
| OQ-64 | Whether `environmentOptionId` and `note` are writable | Not today. Extend `SecretDraftEntry` with two optional fields, omission meaning unchanged; file the change as `document.update`, not `rotate`. |
| OQ-65 | How values are encrypted and what the reveal contract is | Envelope encryption, one AES-256-GCM data key per workspace wrapped by a KMS master key; ciphertext, IV, tag and key id in the row; AAD binds the ciphertext to `workspace_id ‖ node_id ‖ secrets.id ‖ key`. Reveal returns plaintext once, always audits, always rate-limited. |
| OQ-66 | `secretIds: []` | `minItems: 1`. "Copy all" sends every id explicitly. |
| OQ-67 | How rotation history is persisted with no snapshot | `secret_rotations` (T-24), append-only, no value column, projected to `VersionEntry` with `hasSnapshot: false`. |
| OQ-68 | Whether `SecretAuditEntry` is its own table or a projection | Both tables are written, in one transaction. Add `outcome` to the wire type; stop encoding a denial in the IP string. |

---

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **The brief asked for six secret endpoints that canon has as one.** The task specified "add an
   entry, update an entry, delete an entry" as separate APIs. Canon §3.16 has only E-101 … E-105,
   and canon T-23 plus `src/services/devtools-service.ts:479-487` make the whole-list replace
   (E-102) the single write path — *"which is what makes reordering, renaming and deleting one
   operation rather than three endpoints."* I followed canon and documented how each of the four
   operations is expressed inside E-102's body (the recipe table under that endpoint). If the editor
   wants three narrower endpoints, that is a canon change, not a chapter change — and it would need
   a story for how a rename and a reorder in the same edit stay atomic, which the current shape gets
   for free.

2. **The brief's list shape `{ id, key, maskedValue, hasValue }` is not the frontend's.**
   `SecretEntry` is `{ id, key, maskedValue, environmentOptionId, updatedAt, rotatedBy, note? }`
   (`src/types/devtools.ts:73-82`), and all seven fields are rendered
   (`src/components/devtools/secret-list.tsx:212-255`). I followed the frontend and canon §5.2.
   **`hasValue` is worth adding as an additive field, though**, and the reason is concrete: E-102
   falls back to the empty string when a new entry arrives with no value
   (`const value = draft.value ?? … ?? ""`, `src/services/devtools-service.ts:535`), so an entry
   whose stored value is `""` is representable — and today it renders as twelve bullets that lie
   about holding something. `hasValue: boolean` costs nothing, leaks nothing (it is one bit, not a
   length), and lets the list badge an empty credential. Not adopted here because no OQ id covers
   it; raise it as a new OQ if you want it.

3. **The brief asked for "reveal several".** There is no such endpoint and there should not be: the
   only multi-secret read is E-104, which returns a `.env` blob for the clipboard rather than a
   per-secret map, precisely so that revealing several never puts several values on the screen
   (`src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:158-169`). I documented E-104 under both "reveal several" and
   "copy all" and said why the two are one call.

4. **E-095 for a config document ships the full text of every version in the page.**
   `VersionEntry.lines` is required, not optional (`src/types/system.ts:216`), and the client diffs
   locally against an unsaved draft the server has never seen. That is correct behaviour and I have
   specified it, but it means the version list is the heaviest read in the devtools module. E-096
   exists as the lazy path if that ever bites; adopting it would mean making `lines` optional, which
   is a frontend type change and therefore a canon question (closest: OQ-59).

5. **`GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/audit` is gated on `secret.reveal` here**, per canon §3.16, but the
   frontend's Audit log button is available to everyone
   (`src/components/devtools/secret-document-page.tsx:132-141`) and the mock service checks nothing.
   The client needs a one-line change to hide the button behind `can("secret.reveal")`, or a Viewer
   will see a panel that always errors.

6. **Canon §3.15 lists E-100 as `PUT`, and the mock's `saveConfig` is a partial update** (`format`
   and `environmentOptionId` are both optional, meaning "unchanged"). That is `PATCH` semantics under
   canon P-07. It is a `PUT` because `content` — the resource's substance — is always sent in full,
   so replaying the request lands the same state, which is the property P-07 actually cares about.
   Flagging it so nobody "fixes" it to `PATCH` and breaks the idempotency note in §7.8.

---

## 24. Import / Export

Module `system` (canon C-14). Two features, `SY-IMP-35` and `SY-EXP-36`, that share one property:
**the file is the browser's problem, not the server's.** Nothing in this chapter parses a
spreadsheet on the backend, and no endpoint here accepts `multipart/form-data`.

Endpoints: **E-084**, **E-085**, **E-086** (canon §3.11), plus one addition, **E-141**, that canon's
own `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` error already implies. Tables: **T-38 `import_jobs`**, **T-39
`export_jobs`**. Permission keys: `board.import`, `board.export` (canon §2.10). Realtime: RT-06 and
RT-10 on a committed import; nothing on an export.

---

### 24.1 What the frontend actually does — read this before designing anything

The single most consequential fact about this chapter, established by reading the wizard rather than
assuming a shape: **the frontend parses the spreadsheet entirely client-side and posts normalised
records.** There is no upload, no staging object, no server-side parse, and no session to resume.

`useImportWizard` reads the picked `File` in the browser and never sends the bytes anywhere:

```ts
// src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:156-159
const parsed =
  extension === "xlsx"
    ? await parseXlsx(new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()))
    : { rows: parseDelimited(await file.text(), delimiterFor(extension)), sheetName: null };
```

`parseXlsx` is a hand-rolled single-sheet XLSX reader over the unzipped package parts
(`src/lib/xlsx.ts:1-12`, `:67-84`). `parseDelimited` is an RFC 4180 CSV/TSV reader
(`src/lib/csv.ts:3-6`, `:7-51`). Both produce a `Grid` — `readonly (readonly string[])[]`
(`src/lib/grid.ts:3`) — padded rectangular by `normalizeGrid` (`src/lib/grid.ts:12-21`). The `Grid`
lives in React state (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:82`); `ImportSource` and `ImportPlan` are both
`useMemo` derivations over it (`:100-116`); `reset()` throws all of it away (`:118-129`).

The module header states the design intent outright:

> Everything before "confirm" is a computation over the parsed file: the board is not touched until
> the user has seen exactly which rows would fail and chosen what should happen to them.
> — `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:38-42`

**The four wizard steps** are `upload | mapping | validation | result` (`ImportStep`,
`src/types/system.ts:145`). Canon §2.7 marks `ImportStep` **UI-only — it never crosses the wire**.
There is no partial-import resume, because there is nothing on the server to resume from.

| Stage | Where it runs today | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extension gate (`xlsx` / `csv` / `tsv`) | browser | `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:74`, `:136-145` |
| Size / type gate (`validateUpload`) | browser | `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:147-151`; `src/lib/file-validation.ts:28-58` |
| Parse to `Grid` | browser | `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:156-159` |
| Number the source rows, split the header | browser | `readImportSource`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:55-78` |
| Guess the mapping | browser | `autoMapColumns`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:145-184` |
| Parse every mapped cell, collect issues | browser | `planImport`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:357-423` |
| Choose the invalid-value policy | browser | `src/components/board/import/import-validation-step.tsx:60-74` |
| **Write** | server | `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:224-290` |

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Do not specify a server-side spreadsheet parser, an upload-then-parse
pipeline, an `import_sessions` table, or a `multipart` variant of any endpoint in this chapter. Part
6 of this document already recorded the same decision for `import_sessions`; this chapter is the
other half of it.

**Where this chapter deliberately extends what the frontend does.** The frontend's final call today
is `boardService.importRows({ boardId, rows })` where `rows` is
`readonly Readonly<Record<columnId, CellValue>>[]` (`src/services/board-service.ts:1171-1176`) — a
bare array of cell maps with **the source row number stripped off**. That is a fidelity loss the
frontend itself warns against three files earlier (§24.3), and it is why row-level errors cannot be
reported back today. E-085 therefore carries the `ImportSource` — the numbered rows of strings —
and lets the server re-derive the cells. Reasons, in order of weight:

1. **Row-level errors need the row number.** The frontend wants them (`ImportIssue.rowNumber` is
