   rendered verbatim at `src/components/board/import/import-validation-step.tsx:89`), and a response
   cannot name a row it was never told about.
2. **The server must not trust a client-supplied `CellValue`.** A hostile client can post a
   `select` cell naming an option that does not exist, a `user` cell naming somebody outside the
   workspace, or a `relation` cell naming a row on a board it may not read. Parsing text against the
   board's own schema server-side closes all three by construction.
3. **The lookups live server-side anyway.** `parseTextIntoCell` needs the column's `SelectConfig`
   options, the workspace directory and the relation target index
   (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:25-82`) — all three are server data the client is holding a copy of.

The wire payload is still **already-parsed JSON, not a spreadsheet**: headers plus rows of strings.

---

### 24.2 The parse layer the backend inherits but does not run

The backend never executes this code. It is documented because two of its rules are correctness
rules the backend must not undo, and because a future "re-import server-side" feature would have to
reproduce them exactly.

**XLSX — a sheet is addressed, not sequential.** Excel writes no `<row>` element for a row nobody
touched and no `<c>` for an empty cell, so document order is not position:

> a sheet whose rows 4 and 5 are blank jumps straight from `r="3"` to `r="6"`. Reading the elements
> in document order therefore pulls every later row up by the number of blank ones above it, which
> is how a value that belongs to source row 8 ends up against row 5.
> — `src/lib/xlsx.ts:98-104`

`readSheet` reads the `r="N"` attribute and fills the gaps with empty rows
(`src/lib/xlsx.ts:109-128`); `readRow` does the same one level down with `r="C2"` cell references
(`:131-146`). Row indices are capped at `MAX_SHEET_ROWS = 100_000` so a hostile `r` cannot allocate
the sheet's whole 1 048 576-row address space (`:25-30`, `:120`). Both inline strings
(`t="inlineStr"`) and the shared-string table (`t="s"`) are resolved, and rich text split across
several `<t>` runs is concatenated (`:148-164`).

**A multi-sheet workbook imports its first worksheet only.** `parseXlsx` takes
`xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml`, or the first entry under `xl/worksheets/` if that name is absent
(`src/lib/xlsx.ts:71-75`). Documented as a known limitation at `docs/SYSTEM.md:338-340`. The
`ImportSource.sheetName` field exists so the user is told which sheet they got
(`src/components/board/import/import-mapping-step.tsx:142`).

**CSV / TSV** is RFC 4180: quoted fields, `""` escapes, embedded separators and newlines
(`src/lib/csv.ts:7-51`). The delimiter is a tab for `.tsv` and a comma for everything else
(`:70-72`).

**`normalizeGrid` pads every row to the widest one** so the grid is rectangular
(`src/lib/grid.ts:12-21`). The backend receives a rectangular grid as a consequence, but must
**still tolerate a short row** and read a missing index as `""` — that is exactly what the planner
does (`row.cells[mapping.sourceIndex] ?? ""`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:390`).

---

### 24.3 The row-alignment invariant — the bug this chapter exists to prevent

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** This is the one rule in the chapter that is stated as an invariant in the
frontend's own source, in three separate files, because it was a real defect that shipped and was
fixed. A backend that re-derives rows by any other shape will reintroduce it.

> **A row is a row.** Cells are carried per source row, with the file's own row number attached, and
> nothing is ever filtered out of a column and zipped back together by position. **That is the shape
> of the bug where a blank cell high in the file pulls every value below it up a row.**
> — `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:30-35`

The failure mode, concretely. A file has a Tester column where rows 2 and 3 are blank. A pipeline
that reads one column at a time and drops the blanks produces a five-element list of testers for an
eight-row file, then zips it back against the eight rows by index. Every tester from row 4 onwards is
now attached to a row three earlier than its own. Nothing throws, nothing is logged, and the import
reports success. The QA lead discovers it a week later when the wrong person is chased for a failed
regression case.

Three mechanisms hold it straight, and all three matter:

**1 · The number travels with the cells, never in a parallel array.**

```ts
// src/types/system.ts:62-65
export interface ImportSourceRow {
  /** 1-based row in the sheet, counting the header — what Excel shows. */
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;
  readonly cells: readonly string[];
}
```

> The number travels with the cells rather than beside them. Every findings list, preview and error
> message downstream quotes it, and a row number kept in a parallel array is one filter away from
> describing a different row than the one it is printed next to.
> — `src/types/system.ts:55-59`

**2 · Numbering happens before the header is removed and before the row cap is applied.**

```ts
// src/lib/import-mapping.ts:70-77
const numbered: ImportSourceRow[] = normalized.map((cells, index) => ({
  sourceRowNumber: index + 1,
  cells,
}));

const body = hasHeaderRow ? numbered.slice(1) : numbered;

return { fileName, sheetName, headers, rows: body.slice(0, IMPORT_MAX_ROWS) };
```

So `sourceRowNumber` always means "the row Excel would show you", whatever the wizard does with the
rows afterwards (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:49-53`). With a header row, the first data row is
`sourceRowNumber: 2`. **This is why `hasHeaderRow` is not a wire field** — the numbering already
encodes it.

**3 · Emptiness is a property of the row in the file, not of the mapped columns.**

```ts
// src/lib/import-mapping.ts:376-380
// Whole-row emptiness, decided before anything is mapped.
if (row.cells.every((cell) => cell.trim().length === 0)) {
  blankCount += 1;
  continue;
}
```

> deciding it per mapped column made a row that carried data the user chose not to import disappear,
> taking its row number with it.
> — `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:352-355`

And within a row, an empty cell is written, not skipped:

```ts
// src/lib/import-mapping.ts:392-395
// An empty source cell stays empty. It is never filled from a
// neighbouring row, and it never causes the row to be dropped.
cells[column.id] = result.value;
```

#### 24.3.1 The rules this puts on the backend

These are normative. Every one of them is the negative of a way the bug comes back.

| # | Rule | What breaks if it is ignored |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IA-1 | **Never re-sort `request.source.rows`.** The supplied order is the file's order and is the order records are created in. No `ORDER BY`, no set-returning function whose order is unspecified, no parallel insert. | `TASK-042 … TASK-141` stops matching the file, and the result step's promise "They were imported in the file's row order" (`src/components/board/import/import-result-step.tsx:51-58`) becomes false. |
| IA-2 | **Never renumber.** `sourceRowNumber` is supplied and is carried, unchanged, into every `ImportIssue`, every `ImportSkippedRow` and every `ImportedRow`. The server does not compute it from an array index. | Error messages name a row the user cannot find in their sheet. |
| IA-3 | **Never filter a column and re-zip.** Do not build `array_agg(cell) FILTER (WHERE cell <> '')` per column. Iterate rows; index cells within the row. | The original defect, verbatim. |
| IA-4 | **A blank cell produces an empty `CellValue` of the column's type, never a skipped key and never `NULL`.** `parseTextIntoCell` returns `emptyCellFor(column.type)` with `ok: true` for whitespace-only text (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:30-31`). | Rows become sparse; `cellOf` falls back per read; and a `cells` map with holes cannot be told apart from one where a column was never mapped. |
| IA-5 | **A row is dropped only when *every* cell in it is whitespace.** Not "every mapped cell", not "the primary column is empty". | A row whose only populated column the user chose to ignore vanishes silently, taking its number with it. |
| IA-6 | **Row identity within one commit is `sourceRowNumber`, and it is unique per request.** Reject a request with a duplicate `sourceRowNumber` as `VALIDATION_FAILED`. | Two issues reported against "row 7" with no way to tell which. |
| IA-7 | **A short `cells` array is read as trailing blanks**, not as an error and not as a shift. | A CSV whose last field is empty on some lines shifts those lines. |

`IA-1` has a concrete consequence for the write: the per-board record counter must be advanced **in
the request's row order**, so record *i* in the file gets sequence `base + i`. The frontend's mock
does exactly this with a sequential loop (`src/services/board-service.ts:1195-1214`). A backend that
reserves a block of sequence numbers and then assigns them from an unordered insert satisfies "no
gaps" and still breaks the contract.

---

### 24.4 Column mapping

```ts
// src/types/system.ts:85-93 — verbatim
export type MappingTarget =
  | { readonly kind: "ignore" }
  | { readonly kind: "existing"; readonly columnId: string }
  | { readonly kind: "create"; readonly name: string; readonly type: ColumnType };

export interface ColumnMapping {
  readonly sourceIndex: number;
  readonly target: MappingTarget;
}
```

`MappingTargetKind` = `ignore | existing | create` (canon §2.7). A tagged union rather than a bag of
optional fields, "so 'ignored', 'into an existing column' and 'into a column this import creates'
cannot overlap and a half-set target cannot exist" (`src/types/system.ts:76-83`). Each source column
owns exactly one target; there is no shared draft.

**Auto-mapping** (`autoMapColumns`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:145-184`) — a client-side convenience
the backend does not reproduce, documented because it explains the shapes that arrive:

1. Names are normalised by lower-casing and stripping every non-alphanumeric character
   (`normalizeName`, `:87-89`).
2. Exact normalised match first, then a containment match in either direction; **each board column
   is claimed at most once** (`:151-157`).
3. Anything left over becomes a `create` target named after the file's own header — "which is what
   makes an extra column in the sheet arrive as a column on the board rather than being silently
   dropped" (`:138-144`).
4. The type guess is deliberately shallow (`guessColumnType`, `:129-136`): a header matching
   `/(^|[^a-z])(date|due|deadline|start|end|created|updated)([^a-z]|$)/i` → `date`; one matching
   `/(step|description|note|notes|detail|details|summary|expected|actual|result)/i` → `longText`;
   otherwise `text`. "Text takes anything, so being wrong costs a dropdown rather than a failed
   import" (`:122-127`). The dialog's own "Create new column" default is `text`
   (`src/components/board/import/import-mapping-step.tsx:122`).

**Changing one mapping releases nothing.** Pointing a source column at a board column another source
column already writes leaves the first one in place and reports a conflict — "a change the user did
not ask for is worse than an error they can see" (`setMappingTarget`,
`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:186-204`).

**The four blocking conflicts** (`mappingConflicts`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:255-316`), each
reported against the `sourceIndex` that has to change:

| # | Condition | Message rendered to the user |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MC-1 | Two source columns target one board column | `“{column}” is already taken by “{first header}”` |
| MC-2 | A `create` target with an empty name | `A new column needs a name` |
| MC-3 | A `create` name that a board column already has (normalised) | `The board already has a column called “{name}” — map onto it instead` |
| MC-4 | Two `create` targets with the same normalised name | `“{first header}” is already creating a column called “{name}”` |

`plan.conflicts.length > 0` blocks the wizard's Confirm button entirely
(`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:225`; `ValidateButton`,
`src/components/board/import/import-dialog.tsx:194-218`).

**Provisional column ids.** A column the import would create is addressed as `` `new_${sourceIndex}` ``
during planning (`provisionalColumnId`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:113-119`), and `planColumns`
appends a stand-in `BoardColumn` for each so values can be parsed against the right type (`:331-345`).
`resolveProvisionalIds` swaps them for the real ids after the columns are created, and **a
provisional id with no real column behind it has its cell dropped, never invented** (`:477-502`).

**On the wire, provisional ids do not exist.** E-084 and E-085 both take `ColumnMapping[]`, so the
server allocates real ids inside its own transaction and never sees a `new_*` key. This is one of the
two things the two-call client sequence collapses into one server call (the other is ordering, §24.9).

---

### 24.5 Validation and the invalid-value policy

`planImport` parses every mapped cell with `parseTextIntoCell` and records, per row, which columns
could not read their value (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:357-423`). **Nothing is thrown and nothing is
written** — "an unparsable date is a finding, not a failure" (`:348-350`).

```ts
// src/types/system.ts:101-113 — verbatim
export interface ImportIssue {
  /** Row number in the file, header included — what the sheet itself shows. */
  readonly rowNumber: number;
  readonly sourceHeader: string;
  readonly columnName: string;
  readonly value: string;
  readonly message: string;
}

export interface ImportDraftRow {
  /** The file's own row number, never the board's. */
  readonly rowNumber: number;
  readonly cells: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
  /** Columns whose source value the type could not parse. */
  readonly invalidColumnIds: readonly string[];
}
```

**Per-type failure messages** (`messageFor`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:425-440`) — reproduce these
strings verbatim; they are user-facing copy:

| Column type | `ImportIssue.message` |
| --- | --- |
| `date` | `Not a date the column can read — try DD/MM/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `select` | `` `No option named this on “${column.name}”` `` |
| `user` | `No workspace member with that name or email` |
| `relation` | `No record on the linked board with that id or title` |
| `attachment` | `Files cannot be created from a spreadsheet cell` |
| `text` / `longText` (never reached) | `` `Could not be read as ${column.type}` `` |

**What "could not read" means per type** (`parseTextIntoCell`, `src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:25-82`):

- `text` / `longText` — always succeed. The raw string is stored, untrimmed.
- `select` — labels are matched case-insensitively against `config.options[].label`
  (`findOptionId`, `:140-147`); a multi-select splits the cell on commas (`splitList`, `:132-138`).
  Any unmatched label makes the whole cell `ok: false`, and the value stored is
  `{ kind: "select", optionIds: <the ones that matched>, text: <the raw cell> }`.
- `date` — `parseDate` accepts ISO (with optional `T`/space time), **day-first `DD/MM/YYYY`**,
  `YYYY/MM/DD`, and anything `Date.parse` understands; day-first is tested before the engine "so
  `03/04/2026` reads as 3 April, matching the locale this workspace is written for"
  (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:170-195`). `31/02/2026` is rejected rather than rolled over (`:198-204`).
- `user` — matched against the directory by exact lower-cased `name` **or** `email`
  (`findUserId`, `:149-158`).
- `relation` — matched against the target board by exact row id **or** lower-cased display label
  (`findRelationId`, `:160-168`).
- `attachment` — **always `ok: false`**. "Files cannot be recreated from their names; keep the text
  as evidence" (`:67-69`).

**Three things an import must never do, and the frontend proves each one:**

| Rule | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| **Never create a select option from an imported value.** An unmatched label is a finding; the option list is not grown. | `parseTextIntoCell` case `select` returns `ok: false` and preserves the raw text; it has no write path (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:40-48`). Option creation is E-058 and needs `board.column.update`. |
| **Never invent a user.** An unmatched name is a finding. | `findUserId` returns `null` (`:149-158`). |
| **Never create a record on a relation target board.** | `findRelationId` returns `null` (`:160-168`); the unmatched ids are simply absent from `rowIds`. |

This is why a `create` mapping of type `select` is a trap the UI steers away from: a newly created
select column has `defaultConfigFor("select")` — an empty option list — so **every** value in that
source column would be flagged. `guessColumnType` never guesses `select`, `user`, `relation` or
`attachment` (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:129-136`).

**The invalid-value policy.**

```ts
// src/types/system.ts:134
export type ImportInvalidPolicy = "skip" | "blank";
```

- `skip` — **the default** (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:87`), and canon's position on OQ-41.
  Flagged rows are left out entirely.
- `blank` — the row is imported with the offending cells replaced by `emptyCellFor(column.type)`.

Both from `rowsToCreate` (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:449-468`), and they are the two answers the PRD
gives (`SY-IMP-35`: "a badly formatted date leaves the cell blank or is reported per row for the user
to fix"). Neither is chosen silently — the validation step makes it a radio group
(`src/components/board/import/import-validation-step.tsx:60-74`).

**A flagged row is flagged as a whole, not per cell.** `invalidCount` counts *rows* that have at
least one invalid column (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:411`), and `skip` drops the whole row even if
eleven of its twelve cells parsed. That is the behaviour the count on the Import button promises
(`import-dialog.tsx:172-177`).

**Limits.**

| Constant | Value | Where | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` | `5_000` | `src/config/app.ts:48` | **Server**, as `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (400). The client's `.slice(0, IMPORT_MAX_ROWS)` and its `isTruncated` banner are a courtesy, not the control (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:77`, `:81-83`; `import-mapping-step.tsx:148-153`). |
| `IMPORT_PREVIEW_ROWS` | `8` | `src/config/app.ts:45` | Client only — the mapping-step preview table. |
| `IMPORT_ISSUE_LIMIT` | `50` | `src/config/app.ts:51` | Client display cap (`import-validation-step.tsx:26`). See §24.9 for the separate server cap on the returned `issues` array. |

All three are already in canon's `GET /config` payload family (E-139) and must be served from there
so the two sides cannot disagree.

---

### 24.6 Does an import need a session or a staging table? — **DECIDED: no**

**Decision.** There is **no `import_sessions` table, no `import_drafts` table, no staged file object
and no `planId`.** E-084 is a pure function of its request body and persists nothing. E-085 is a
single self-contained transaction that does not require E-084 to have been called.

**Reasoning, from the frontend.**

1. **There is nothing to stage.** The bytes never leave the browser
   (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:156-159`). A session table exists to hold the parsed file between
   two calls; here the client is already holding it, in a `useMemo` chain over React state
   (`:100-116`).
2. **The wizard has no resume, by construction.** `reset()` clears grid, file name, sheet name,
   mappings, policy, removal flag, outcome and error (`:118-129`), and it is called both by "Choose
   another file" and by closing the dialog (`import-dialog.tsx:55-58`, `:141-145`). A closed wizard
   is a wizard that starts again.
3. **Canon says the plan is not persisted.** E-084 returns "`ImportPlan` — computed before anything
   is written; not persisted" (canon §3.11).
4. **A session table would be the only thing in the schema with no reader.** Nothing in
   `src/types/system.ts` addresses an import by id before the commit; `ImportOutcome` has no session
   field.

**The cost of this decision, stated honestly.** The `ImportSource` is sent twice when the client
calls E-084 and then E-085. For a 5 000-row × 12-column sheet of short strings that is roughly
1.5–4 MB of JSON per call. **RECOMMENDATION:** accept it. The alternative — a Redis-cached plan under
a `planId`, with a TTL, an eviction story and a "your plan expired, start again" error the wizard has
no state for — buys nothing the user can see, and E-085 has to re-derive and re-validate the plan
anyway (§24.8, the re-plan rule), so the cached copy could never be authoritative. Set the JSON body
limit for these two routes to **16 MB** (against a 1 MB default elsewhere) and let
`REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` (413) be the guard.

**What does get a row is `import_jobs` (T-38)** — written *after* the fact, inside the commit
transaction, so a strange import is diagnosable a week later. It is a record, not a session: nothing
reads it to continue an operation.

---

### 24.7 Table: `import_jobs` (T-38)

Module `system`. **RECOMMENDATION** — the frontend has no counterpart; canon reserves the table and
OQ-41 covers it.

```sql
-- Documentation only.
CREATE TABLE import_jobs (
  id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  board_id            UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  actor_id            UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  file_name           TEXT NOT NULL,
  sheet_name          TEXT,                       -- NULL for csv/tsv

  requested_count     INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- source.rows.length
  created_count       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  skipped_count       INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- policy-skipped rows only
  blank_count         INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- whole-blank source rows

  invalid_policy      import_invalid_policy NOT NULL DEFAULT 'skip',

  issues              JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,   -- ImportIssue[], capped
  issue_count         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,           -- uncapped
  skipped_row_numbers INTEGER[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',      -- source row numbers, in file order

  created_column_ids  UUID[]  NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  removed_columns     JSONB   NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb, -- string[] of column names

  created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT import_jobs_counts_add_up
    CHECK (requested_count = created_count + skipped_count + blank_count)
);

CREATE INDEX import_jobs_board_idx ON import_jobs (board_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX import_jobs_actor_idx ON import_jobs (actor_id, created_at DESC);
```

**Columns, and why each is there.**

| Column | Type | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID PK | Canon C-01. Returned as `ImportOutcome.jobId`. |
| `board_id` | UUID FK → `boards.id`, CASCADE | The import is a board event. Deleting the board takes its import history. |
| `actor_id` | UUID FK → `users.id`, RESTRICT | From the session, never the body (canon C-09). RESTRICT because `users` is soft-deactivated and never hard-deleted (canon T-01). |
| `file_name` | TEXT | The seeded audit detail quotes it: "48 records imported from **sprint-backlog.xlsx**, 3 rows left out" (`src/services/audit-service.ts:93`). |
| `sheet_name` | TEXT NULL | A multi-sheet workbook imports its first sheet; the job must say which one that was. `ImportSource.sheetName` is `string \| null` (`src/types/system.ts:71`). |
| `requested_count` | INTEGER | `source.rows.length`. |
| `created_count` | INTEGER | `ImportOutcome.created`. |
| `skipped_count` | INTEGER | `ImportOutcome.skipped` — **policy-skipped only**, matching the frontend's arithmetic `plan.drafts.length - rows.length` (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:279`). |
| `blank_count` | INTEGER | `ImportPlan.blankCount` (`src/types/system.ts:128`). Without it the CHECK cannot be written and "where did the other 40 rows go" has no answer. |
| `invalid_policy` | ENUM `import_invalid_policy` | `skip` \| `blank`, canon §2.7, values verbatim. |
| `issues` | JSONB | `ImportIssue[]`, capped (§24.9). |
| `issue_count` | INTEGER | The uncapped count, so a truncated `issues` array is never mistaken for the whole story. |
| `skipped_row_numbers` | INTEGER[] | Which rows of the file did not land, by the file's own numbering. This is the column somebody opens the table for. |
| `created_column_ids` | UUID[] | Which columns this import added — the first question when a board suddenly has four new columns. |
| `removed_columns` | JSONB | `string[]` of names, matching `ImportOutcome.removedColumns` (`src/types/system.ts:142`). Names, not ids, because the columns no longer exist. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | Canon C-03. |

**JSONB structure — `import_jobs.issues`** (canon C-06):

```ts
/** One entry per (row, column) whose source value the column could not read. */
interface ImportIssue {
  readonly rowNumber: number;      // the FILE's row number, header counted
  readonly sourceHeader: string;   // the spreadsheet column's header text
  readonly columnName: string;     // the board column's final name
  readonly value: string;          // the raw cell text, verbatim
  readonly message: string;        // user-facing, from the table in §24.5
}
```

**JSONB structure — `import_jobs.removed_columns`:** `readonly string[]` — board column names, in
the order they were removed, which is board column `position` order.

**Cardinality.** One `boards` row → 0..N `import_jobs`. One `users` row → 0..N. No row references an
`import_jobs` row; it is a leaf.

**Unique constraints.** None. Two identical imports are two facts, not a conflict. Replay protection
for E-085 is the Redis `Idempotency-Key` ledger, not a database constraint.

**Indexes.** `(board_id, created_at DESC)` — "what has been imported into this board" is the only
listing query. `(actor_id, created_at DESC)` — the governance question "what did this person load".

**Delete behaviour.** `board_id` CASCADE (the board's history goes with the board); `actor_id`
RESTRICT. **`created_column_ids` carries no FK** — deliberately: it must survive a later
`DELETE FROM board_columns`, and a job row whose columns were dropped afterwards is exactly the
diagnostic somebody needs. Same reasoning as canon's rule for a relation cell keeping a dangling id.

**Retention.** **RECOMMENDATION** — keep indefinitely. A row is ~1 KB and a workspace produces a
handful a week. If a sweep is ever wanted, key it on `created_at` and drop `issues` before dropping
the row.

---

### 24.8 Error semantics — all-or-nothing vs partial success

The frontend wants **row-level errors**. Canon E-085 mandates **one transaction**. Both are
satisfiable, because they are answers to two different questions, and the contract below says which
question each row's outcome belongs to.

#### 24.8.1 The two candidate designs, analysed

**Design A — partial success, the `BulkResult` shape.** Insert what can be inserted; report the rest
as skips. This is what canon §6.2 mandates for the four bulk endpoints: `requested === applied.length
+ skipped.length`, and "a bulk write that silently drops a record is worse than one that refuses"
(`src/services/board-service.ts:958-965`).

**Design B — all-or-nothing.** Everything lands or nothing does.

**Why import is not a bulk write.** A bulk endpoint (E-074 … E-077) acts on records that **already
exist**. A skipped record leaves the board byte-for-byte as it was, so a partial result is a complete
and honest description of the world. An import is different in four ways:

| | Bulk (E-074 – E-077) | Import (E-085) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Touches rows that already exist | yes | **no — it creates them** |
| May change the board's *schema* | no | **yes — it may create and remove columns** |
| Burns a monotonic counter that never reissues | no | **yes — `boards.next_sequence`** (`src/types/board.ts:240`; canon E-062) |
| Has an undo the user can reach | the selection is still there to retry | **no** — the wizard's only exit is Done (`import-dialog.tsx:156-157`) |

A half-applied import therefore leaves a board with new columns it did not have, some of the records,
a spent block of `TASK-nnn` identifiers, and no way back. The frontend already says so, in the one
place it can partially fail today — when a column cannot be created mid-confirm:

```ts
// src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:246-251
appError("conflict", `Could not create the “${draft.name.trim()}” column`, {
  detail: "Nothing was imported. Map that column onto an existing one and try again.",
  isRetryable: false,
})
```

**DECIDED: Design B for execution, with per-row reporting for validation.**

#### 24.8.2 The contract

**Two classes of row outcome, and they are not the same thing.**

| Class | Decided | Effect on the transaction | Reported as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Validation outcome** — a cell the column cannot read, or a whole-blank row | Before any insert, by `ImportInvalidPolicy` | **None.** The transaction still commits. | `ImportIssue[]` (per cell) + `ImportSkippedRow[]` (per row) + the three counts |
| **Execution failure** — permission, row ceiling, unresolved mapping, column-name collision, storage fault | At commit | **Full rollback. Zero rows, zero columns, `next_sequence` unchanged.** | An `ErrorResponse` with the `reason` from the endpoint's error table |

**The re-plan rule.** E-085 does not trust and does not require a plan computed by the client. It
re-derives the whole plan from `source` + `mappings` against the board's schema **inside the
transaction**, after any new columns are created. A value that was valid when the wizard planned it
and is invalid at commit — an option deleted, a relation target trashed, a member deactivated between
the two calls — is treated exactly as a plan-time failure: the policy decides, and it appears in
`issues`. **The commit never fails for a data reason.** It fails only for a structural one.

That is what makes all-or-nothing acceptable: by the time E-085 can fail, the user has already seen
every row-level problem in the validation step, and none of them can fail the call.

**What comes back for a row that did not land:**

```ts
/** RECOMMENDATION — snake_case to match BulkSkipReason (canon §2.7). */
type ImportSkipReason =
  | "invalid_value"   // at least one cell the column could not read, under policy "skip"
  | "blank_row";      // every cell in the source row was whitespace

interface ImportSkippedRow {
  /** The FILE's row number. Never an array index. (IA-2) */
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;
  readonly reason: ImportSkipReason;
  /** Board column names that failed. Empty for "blank_row". */
  readonly columnNames: readonly string[];
}
```

Every `invalid_value` entry is joined to its `ImportIssue`s by `sourceRowNumber`, and every issue
carries the raw `value` and the user-facing `message`. That is the row-level error the frontend
wants, and it arrives on a `200`.

**What comes back for a row that *did* land:**

```ts
interface ImportedRow {
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;   // the file's row
  readonly rowId: string;             // the board's UUID
  readonly displayId: string;         // TASK-042 — assigned by the server, never the client
}
```

`importedRows` is in the request's row order (IA-1). **No parallel arrays** — the identity travels
with the record, for the same reason `ImportSourceRow` carries its own number
(`src/types/system.ts:55-59`).

**The four arithmetic invariants**, all checkable by the client and all asserted server-side before
the response is written:

```
created            === importedRows.length === rowIds.length
skipped            === skippedRows.filter(r => r.reason === "invalid_value").length
blankCount         === skippedRows.filter(r => r.reason === "blank_row").length
source.rows.length === created + skipped + blankCount
```

The second one is the frontend's existing meaning of `skipped`
(`plan.drafts.length - rows.length`, `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:279`) — blank rows never became
drafts and are therefore not in it. `blankCount` is the third number that makes the total add up.

#### 24.8.3 What partial success would have cost, for the record

Had Design A been chosen, `ImportOutcome` would need to describe a board in an intermediate state:
which columns were created before the failure, which records landed, what `next_sequence` now is, and
which of the created columns are now empty. There is no frontend surface that renders any of that —
`ImportResultStep` renders four sentences and a column list
(`src/components/board/import/import-result-step.tsx:14-60`). Specifying a state nothing can display
is how a spec grows a feature nobody asked for.

---

### 24.9 Import endpoints

#### `POST /api/v1/boards/:boardId/import/plan`

**Purpose** — Compute what an import *would* write, without writing anything. Returns the per-row
findings, the counts and the blocking mapping conflicts, so the user fixes the mapping while it is
still fixable. Canon E-084.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `board.import` on the board's node, plus workspace membership. The board's node is
resolved from `boards.node_id`; visibility on that node is checked first, so an unreadable board
answers `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` (404) rather than `403` (canon §4.2). `board.import` is a
`CONTENT_WRITE_KEY` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:45`), so a trashed node, an archived ancestor
or a lock refuses it (`evaluate.ts:79-86`) — planning is gated exactly as the write it previews,
because offering a plan for a write that cannot happen is a worse answer than refusing.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`, not `nodes.id` (canon P-04). |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeDrafts` | `boolean` | `false` | When `false`, `ImportPlan.drafts` is returned as `[]`. **Every count is still computed over the full set** — `validCount + invalidCount` is the true draft count. The frontend computes its own drafts locally (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:357-423`) and needs only the issues, the counts and the conflicts; returning 5 000 parsed `CellValue` maps it will discard is 3–5 MB of nothing. Set it to `true` only for a client that has stopped planning locally. |

**Request Body**

```ts
interface PlanImportRequest {
  /**
   * The parsed sheet. The browser produced this; the server never sees the file.
   * `rows` is in the file's order and carries the file's own row numbers (IA-1, IA-2).
   */
  readonly source: ImportSource;
  readonly mappings: readonly ColumnMapping[];
}

interface ImportSource {
  readonly fileName: string;              // 1..255
  readonly sheetName: string | null;      // null for csv/tsv
  readonly headers: readonly string[];    // one per source column; synthesised "Column A" when absent
  readonly rows: readonly ImportSourceRow[];
}

interface ImportSourceRow {
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;       // >= 1, unique within the request (IA-6)
  readonly cells: readonly string[];      // shorter than `headers` means trailing blanks (IA-7)
}

type MappingTarget =
  | { readonly kind: "ignore" }
  | { readonly kind: "existing"; readonly columnId: string }
  | { readonly kind: "create"; readonly name: string; readonly type: ColumnType };

interface ColumnMapping {
  readonly sourceIndex: number;           // 0-based index into `source.headers`
  readonly target: MappingTarget;
}
```

Validation at the boundary: `source.rows.length <= IMPORT_MAX_ROWS`; every `sourceIndex` in range and
appearing at most once; every `sourceRowNumber >= 1` and unique; every `existing.columnId` a live
column of this board; every `create.type` a `ColumnType` member (canon §2.5). `hasHeaderRow` is
**not** a field — the numbering already encodes it (§24.3).

**Response** — `200` `ImportPlan`, the frontend's interface verbatim
(`src/types/system.ts:119-130`):

```ts
interface ImportPlan {
  readonly drafts: readonly ImportDraftRow[];   // [] unless ?includeDrafts=true
  readonly issues: readonly ImportIssue[];      // capped; see issueCount
  readonly mappedColumnCount: number;           // targets of kind "existing"
  readonly newColumnCount: number;              // targets of kind "create"
  readonly validCount: number;                  // drafts with no invalid column
  readonly invalidCount: number;                // drafts with at least one
  readonly blankCount: number;                  // whole-blank source rows
  readonly conflicts: readonly MappingConflict[]; // empty when the mapping is runnable
}

interface MappingConflict {
  readonly sourceIndex: number;
  readonly message: string;   // the four messages in the MC table, §24.4
}
```

**RECOMMENDATION — one additive field.** `issues` is capped server-side at
`IMPORT_ISSUE_CAP = 500` (ten times the client's display limit of 50) because a 5 000-row file with
a wholly mis-typed column produces 60 000 findings. The response therefore also carries
`readonly issueCount: number`, the uncapped total. The frontend's "…and N more findings across the
file" line currently computes `plan.issues.length - shown.length`
(`src/components/board/import/import-validation-step.tsx:106-110`); it becomes
`issueCount - shown.length`. One line. `IMPORT_ISSUE_CAP` is served from `GET /config` (E-139).

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/import/plan?includeDrafts=false
{
  "drafts": [],
  "issues": [
    {
      "rowNumber": 7,
      "sourceHeader": "Executed",
      "columnName": "Executed on",
      "value": "sprint 4",
      "message": "Not a date the column can read — try DD/MM/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD"
    },
    {
      "rowNumber": 7,
      "sourceHeader": "Owner",
      "columnName": "Tester",
      "value": "h.nguyen",
      "message": "No workspace member with that name or email"
    }
  ],
  "issueCount": 2,
  "mappedColumnCount": 6,
  "newColumnCount": 1,
  "validCount": 47,
  "invalidCount": 1,
  "blankCount": 3,
  "conflicts": []
}
```

**Database** — reads only, no writes.

| Table | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `boards` | `id`, `node_id`, `workspace_id`, `row_id_prefix`, `primary_column_id` — one row. |
| `nodes` | The board's node and its ancestor chain, for visibility, archive-freeze and lock. |
| `board_columns` | Every column of the board: `id`, `name`, `type`, `position`, `is_primary`, `config`. `config.options` is what a `select` value is matched against. |
| `workspace_members` + `users` | The directory, for `user` cells (`findUserId`). Includes deactivated members, flagged (canon E-006). |
| `board_rows` | **Only** on the target board of a `relation` column, and only `id` + the primary cell, for `findRelationId`. One query per distinct target board, never one per cell (canon E-071). |
| `access_rules` | Via the resolver, for visibility on each relation target board — a value must not resolve to a record the caller cannot read. |

No writes. No `import_jobs` row: a plan that is never committed leaves no trace, which is the point
of §24.6.

**Transaction** — Not required. A single `REPEATABLE READ` snapshot so the schema cannot change
between the column read and the cell parse.

**Realtime** — None. Nothing changed.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — `source.rows.length > IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` (5 000). |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — duplicate `sourceRowNumber` (IA-6), duplicate or out-of-range `sourceIndex`, `create.type` not a `ColumnType`, `sourceRowNumber < 1`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `IMPORT_FILE_UNPARSEABLE` — reserved. It cannot be raised here (the server never parses a file); it exists for a future server-parse path and must not be repurposed. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `board.import`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_LOCKED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown board, or one the caller may not see. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` — an `existing.columnId` that is not a live column of this board. |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` — body past the 16 MB route limit. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED` — the general per-session bucket. |

Note what is **not** here: nothing about an unreadable cell. A cell the column cannot read is an
`ImportIssue` on a `200`, never an error. That is the whole point of the endpoint.

**Frontend Used By** — the `plan` memo in `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:105-116`, which today calls
`planImport` locally (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:357-423`). Rendered by
`src/components/board/import/import-validation-step.tsx` and read for the conflict badges by
`src/components/board/import/import-mapping-step.tsx:110-113` and the gate in
`src/components/board/import/import-dialog.tsx:194-218`.

---

#### `POST /api/v1/boards/:boardId/import`

**Purpose** — Commit an import: create the columns the mapping asks for, insert the records in the
file's order, and optionally remove the board columns the file had no data for. Canon E-085 — **one
transaction; all of it lands or none of it does.**

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `board.import` on the board's node, plus workspace membership. **Two conditional
keys**, and this expands canon's Perm column rather than contradicting it:

| Condition | Additional key | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any `mappings[].target.kind === "create"` | `board.column.create` | The wizard's confirm calls `boardStore.addColumn` (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:243`) → `boardService.createColumn`, which is canon E-052, `board.column.create`. |
| `removeUnmappedColumns === true` | `board.column.delete` | The same confirm calls `boardStore.deleteColumn` (`:233`) → canon E-054, `board.column.delete`. |

This composition is not cosmetic. `board.import` and `board.column.create` are both Manager keys
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:50`, `:52`, `:55`), so today no role can hold one without the
others and the frontend never notices. A backend that checks only `board.import` grants column creation to any
future role that gains import and not schema rights. Check all three, and check them **before** the
transaction opens so the refusal names the missing key.

`board.import` is a `CONTENT_WRITE_KEY` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:45`): a trashed node, an
archived ancestor, an archived board or a lock refuses it. `docs/SYSTEM.md:179-180` states the
resulting behaviour: on an archived board "Import is disabled. **Export stays enabled** — archiving
stops writes, not reads."

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Headers** — `Idempotency-Key` (recommended, per §7.8): up to 5 000 rows and a spent block of
`TASK-nnn` identifiers make a blind retry expensive. Keyed on
`(user_id, POST, /boards/{boardId}/import, key)` in Redis, 24 h TTL.

**Request Body**

```ts
interface CommitImportRequest {
  /** Identical shape to PlanImportRequest.source. The file's rows, in the file's order. */
  readonly source: ImportSource;
  readonly mappings: readonly ColumnMapping[];
  /** What to do with a row holding a value a column cannot read. Default "skip" (OQ-41). */
  readonly policy?: ImportInvalidPolicy;
  /**
   * Remove the board columns this import writes nothing into.
   * Default false, and deliberately: "Dropping a column takes its value off every record
   * already on the board. That is a reasonable thing to want when a file defines the real
   * schema, and never a reasonable thing to do because nobody said otherwise."
   * — src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:88-94
   */
  readonly removeUnmappedColumns?: boolean;
}
```

**No `planId`, and no client-supplied `CellValue`.** Both are deliberate (§24.6, §24.1).

**Response** — `200`.

```ts
interface ImportOutcome {
  /** RECOMMENDATION — the import_jobs row, so a run is addressable afterwards. */
  readonly jobId: string;

  // ---- the frontend's existing fields (src/types/system.ts:136-143) ----
  readonly created: number;
  readonly skipped: number;                          // policy-skipped rows only
  readonly issues: readonly ImportIssue[];           // capped at IMPORT_ISSUE_CAP
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];                // === importedRows.map(r => r.rowId)
  readonly removedColumns?: readonly string[];       // omitted, not null, when nothing was removed

  // ---- RECOMMENDATION, additive ----
  readonly issueCount: number;                       // uncapped
  readonly blankCount: number;                       // whole-blank source rows
  readonly importedRows: readonly ImportedRow[];     // in the file's order
  readonly skippedRows: readonly ImportSkippedRow[];
  readonly createdColumns: readonly BoardColumn[];   // authoritative, with real ids and positions
}

interface ImportedRow {
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
}

interface ImportSkippedRow {
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;
  readonly reason: ImportSkipReason;                 // "invalid_value" | "blank_row"
  readonly columnNames: readonly string[];
}
```

`rowIds` is retained unchanged because the frontend reads it
(`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:281`); it is exactly `importedRows.map(r => r.rowId)`, same order.
`createdColumns` is returned so the store does not have to refetch the schema to render the new
columns — it is the same reason canon C-10 exists.

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/import
{
  "jobId": "01JB9K7M2Q8V4X6Z0A1B2C3D4E",
  "created": 47,
  "skipped": 1,
  "blankCount": 3,
  "issueCount": 2,
  "issues": [
    {
      "rowNumber": 7,
      "sourceHeader": "Executed",
      "columnName": "Executed on",
      "value": "sprint 4",
      "message": "Not a date the column can read — try DD/MM/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD"
    },
    {
      "rowNumber": 7,
      "sourceHeader": "Owner",
      "columnName": "Tester",
      "value": "h.nguyen",
      "message": "No workspace member with that name or email"
    }
  ],
  "rowIds": ["3f1c…", "3f1d…"],
  "importedRows": [
    { "sourceRowNumber": 2, "rowId": "3f1c…", "displayId": "QA-118" },
    { "sourceRowNumber": 3, "rowId": "3f1d…", "displayId": "QA-119" }
  ],
  "skippedRows": [
    { "sourceRowNumber": 7,  "reason": "invalid_value", "columnNames": ["Executed on", "Tester"] },
    { "sourceRowNumber": 51, "reason": "blank_row",     "columnNames": [] }
  ],
  "createdColumns": [
    {
      "id": "c81f…", "name": "Browser", "type": "text", "position": 10,
      "width": 200, "hidden": false, "isPrimary": false, "config": {}
    }
  ],
  "removedColumns": ["Story points"]
}
```

**Database** — every read and write, in the order the transaction performs them.

*Reads, before anything is written:*

| Table | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | The board's node and ancestors — visibility, `deleted_at`, ancestor archive, lock. |
| `boards` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the board row. This is the lock that serialises `next_sequence` and makes "no gaps" true (canon §1.4). |
| `board_columns` | Every column: `id`, `name`, `type`, `position`, `is_primary`, `config`. Needed for conflict re-check, for parsing, and for the dense-cell fill. |
| `board_rows` | `MAX(position)` on this board, for the append point. Plus `id` + primary cell on each distinct **relation target** board. |
| `workspace_members` + `users` | The directory, for `user` cells. |
| `access_rules` | Visibility on each relation target board's node. |

*Writes, in this exact order:*

| # | Table | Write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `board_columns` | One `INSERT` per `create` mapping, **in ascending `sourceIndex` order** — "so a new column lands where the file puts it rather than in whatever order the promises settle" (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:238-239`). `position` = current max + 1, +2, …; `is_primary = false`; `config = defaultConfigFor(type)`; `width = DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH`. Real UUIDs are minted here and replace the provisional `new_<i>` keys the client's plan used. |
| 2 | `boards` | `UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence + $N` under the `FOR UPDATE` lock, reserving a contiguous block of N sequence numbers. |
| 3 | `board_rows` | N `INSERT`s, **in the request's row order** (IA-1). Per row: `id` = `gen_random_uuid()`; `sequence` = `base + i`; `custom_id` = `formatRowId(board.row_id_prefix, sequence)` (`src/lib/row-id.ts:13-15`); `position` = an increasing fractional index after the current max (canon OQ-34); `cells` = **the type's empty value for every column, overwritten by the mapped ones** (`{ ...emptyCells(columns), ...cells }`, `src/services/board-service.ts:1203`); `revision = 1`; `created_by` = the session user; `parent_row_id = NULL`; `archived_at = NULL`. |
| 4 | `board_row_relations` | For every relation cell whose ids resolved: one row per `(source_row_id, source_column_id, target_row_id)`. Rebuilt, never diffed (part 8, §17.1). |
| 5 | `row_activity` | One row per imported record: `kind = 'imported'`, `summary = 'imported {custom_id}'`, actor = the session user. Verbatim from `src/services/board-service.ts:1212`. `ActivityKind` includes `imported` (canon §2.5). |
| 6 | `board_columns` | *Only when `removeUnmappedColumns`*: `DELETE` each unmapped, non-primary column. |
| 7 | `board_rows` | *Only when columns were removed*: `UPDATE board_rows SET cells = cells - $columnId` for **every** row on the board, new and pre-existing. This is what "taking their value off every record already on the board" means (`import-mapping-step.tsx:260-262`). |
| 8 | `board_views` | *Only when columns were removed*: prune every reference — filters, sorts, `group_by_column_id`, `date_column_id`, `end_date_column_id`, `column_widths`, `column_display` — in the same transaction, exactly as canon E-054 requires. |
| 9 | `import_jobs` | One row (§24.7). |
| 10 | `audit_events` | One row: `module = 'board'`, `action = 'board.import'`, `severity = 'info'`, `outcome = 'allowed'`, `target` = the board's name, `detail` = `` `${created} records imported from ${fileName}, ${skipped} rows left out.` `` — the seeded format, verbatim (`src/services/audit-service.ts:85-94`). Actor, IP and clock from the session (canon C-09). |

**Two ordering rules that are not interchangeable, even inside one transaction:**

- **Columns are created before rows** because a record cannot carry a value for a column that does
  not exist yet (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:42-47`), and because step 3's dense-cell fill must
  be computed against the **post-creation** schema, or the new columns arrive empty on the very rows
  that brought them.
- **Columns are removed after rows** because the dense-cell fill must be computed against the
  **pre-removal** schema, and because — outside a transaction, which is where the frontend lives —
  "a failed import must never be the thing that emptied the board's schema"
  (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:273-274`). Inside one transaction the rollback covers it, but the
  order still matters for step 7: removing first would mean rewriting `cells` on rows that do not
  exist yet.

**Transaction** — **Required. One transaction, `READ COMMITTED`, covering steps 1–10.** Canon E-085:
"column creation, column removal and row inserts all land or none do", and canon's position on
OQ-41: "One transaction covering column creation, column removal and row inserts." The `SELECT …
FOR UPDATE` on `boards` is taken first and held for the whole transaction; it serialises concurrent
imports and concurrent `POST /rows` on the same board, which is what makes the record identifiers
contiguous.

Rollback surface: the created columns, every inserted record, every relation projection row, every
activity row, the column removals, the `cells` rewrite on pre-existing rows, the view pruning, the
`import_jobs` row, the `audit_events` row, and `boards.next_sequence`. **All of it.** A refused
import leaves `next_sequence` untouched, so no `TASK-nnn` is burned.

**Realtime** — two frames, emitted after commit:

| Frame | Payload | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RT-10 `board.schema.changed` | `{ boardId }` | **Only when columns were created or removed.** Ids only; the client refetches the whole schema, matching canon C-11. |
| RT-06 `row.created` | `{ boardId, rowIds, revision }` | **One batched frame carrying every created `rowId`**, not 5 000 frames. Canon §7.2 explicitly allows "one batched frame carrying `rowIds`". Ids only — no cell content ever crosses a realtime frame (canon §7.2). |

Order matters: RT-10 first, so a receiving tab has the new columns before it fetches rows that fill
them.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED` — the server's own re-check of `mappingConflicts` against the **current** schema is non-empty. The `MappingConflict[]` is returned in `error.fields`, one entry per conflict, `path` = `mappings[<sourceIndex>].target`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — `source.rows.length > IMPORT_MAX_ROWS`. **Refused, never truncated.** Silently importing 5 000 of 6 000 rows is the same class of defect as §24.3. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — duplicate `sourceRowNumber`, duplicate/out-of-range `sourceIndex`, `policy` not `skip`/`blank`, `create.name` empty after trimming. |
| 400 | `validation` | `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` — a `create.type` outside `ColumnType`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` — **never raised by this endpoint.** An unparseable date is an `ImportIssue`, governed by the policy. Listed so nobody adds it. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — missing `board.import`, or missing `board.column.create` with a `create` mapping, or missing `board.column.delete` with `removeUnmappedColumns`. The `detail` names the role, never the column (canon §4.4 rule 3). |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_LOCKED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` — an `existing.columnId` deleted between plan and commit. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `COLUMN_NAME_CONFLICT` — a `create` name taken by a column added between plan and commit. **Refused, not silently de-duplicated to `Notes 2`**: the user's mapping said "a new column", and the right answer is the frontend's own message, "map onto it instead" (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:296-299`). |
| 409 | `conflict` | `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED` — `removeUnmappedColumns` reached the primary column. Cannot happen from this client (`unmappedBoardColumns` excludes `isProtectedColumn`, `src/lib/import-mapping.ts:233`) and must still be refused. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — `existing rows + created rows` exceeds the board ceiling (OQ-36). Checked **before** any insert. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` — an `Idempotency-Key` replay while the first call is still in flight. |
| 413 | `validation` | `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` — full rollback; nothing landed. |

**Transition rules are deliberately NOT enforced here.** Part 9 settled it under OQ-102: run the
record-rule gate on E-066, E-074 and E-077's destination writes, and **not** on E-062, E-064 or
E-085 — "a transition presumes a prior state, and a record being born has none". Both shipped
templates govern the empty bucket with a single target, so gating creation would refuse every import
carrying any status but the first. The *availability* half still applies: an option switched off in
column settings is refused with `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`. This chapter follows part 9.

**Frontend Used By** — `confirm` in `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:224-290`, which today performs
the three calls this endpoint collapses: `boardStore.addColumn` (`:243`), `boardStore.importRows`
(`:271`) → `src/store/board-store.ts:659-671` → `src/services/board-service.ts:1183-1216`, and
`boardStore.deleteColumn` (`:233`). The result is rendered by
`src/components/board/import/import-result-step.tsx`.

**One note the result step depends on.** Records are appended at the end of the board's order, in the
file's order (`appendRows`, `src/lib/board-records.ts:197-209`), and the result step says so when the
active view sorts: "They were imported in the file's row order. This view is sorted, so it is showing
them in the sort's order instead" (`import-result-step.tsx:54-58`). IA-1 is what makes that sentence
true.

### 24.10 A QA/QC import, end to end

The concrete case: a QA lead has a `regression-suite.xlsx` with 52 rows (a header, 47 good cases, one
case whose *Executed* column says `sprint 4` and whose *Owner* is an ex-contractor, and three blank
rows at the bottom left over from a filter). The board came from the `qa` template — `Test case`,
`Result`, `Suite`, `Environment`, `Tester`, `Planned on`, `Executed on`, `Expected result`,
`Evidence`, `Related bug` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:282-327`), prefix `QA`. The sheet has one
column the board lacks, `Browser`, and the board has one column the sheet lacks, `Story points`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor QA as QA lead
    participant W as Import wizard in the browser
    participant API as Backend service
    participant PG as PostgreSQL
    participant RT as Redis pub/sub

    Note over QA,W: Step 1 — upload. Nothing leaves the browser.
    QA->>W: drop regression-suite.xlsx
    W->>W: extension is xlsx csv or tsv · validateUpload size and type
    W->>W: parseXlsx → Grid, gaps filled from the r attribute, never document order
    W->>W: readImportSource → 52 rows numbered, header split off, 51 data rows
    W->>W: autoMapColumns → 9 existing, 1 create named Browser of type text

    Note over QA,W: Step 2 — mapping. Still nothing written.
    QA->>W: leave the guess · tick remove Story points
    W->>API: POST /boards/:boardId/import/plan with source and mappings
    API->>PG: board + columns + directory + relation targets, read only
    PG-->>API: schema, options, people
    API->>API: parse every mapped cell · number every finding by its file row
    API-->>W: 200 ImportPlan · valid 47 · invalid 1 · blank 3 · 2 issues · no conflicts

    Note over QA,W: Step 3 — validation. The user decides, before the write.
    W-->>QA: row 7 · Executed on · sprint 4 · not a date<br/>row 7 · Tester · h.nguyen · no such member
    QA->>W: policy = "skip"
    QA->>W: Import 47 rows

    Note over API,PG: Step 4 — one transaction. All of it, or none of it.
    W->>API: POST /boards/:boardId/import with source, mappings, policy skip, removeUnmappedColumns true
    API->>API: re-check permissions: board.import + board.column.create + board.column.delete
    API->>PG: BEGIN
    API->>PG: SELECT boards FOR UPDATE
    API->>API: re-run mappingConflicts against the CURRENT schema → empty
    API->>PG: INSERT board_columns Browser at position 10
    API->>API: re-plan every cell against the post-creation schema
    API->>PG: UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 47
    API->>PG: INSERT 47 board_rows, in the file's row order, QA-118 … QA-164
    API->>PG: INSERT board_row_relations for resolved Related bug cells
    API->>PG: INSERT 47 row_activity of kind imported
    API->>PG: DELETE board_columns Story points
    API->>PG: UPDATE board_rows SET cells = cells minus col_points on every row of the board
    API->>PG: UPDATE board_views to prune every reference to col_points
    API->>PG: INSERT import_jobs · requested 51 · created 47 · skipped 1 · blank 3
    API->>PG: INSERT audit_events board.import with the seeded detail sentence
    API->>PG: COMMIT
    PG-->>API: ok

    API->>RT: RT-10 board.schema.changed carrying boardId
    API->>RT: RT-06 row.created carrying boardId and 47 rowIds
    API-->>W: 200 ImportOutcome · created 47 · skipped 1 · blankCount 3<br/>skippedRows row 7 invalid_value and rows 50-52 blank_row<br/>createdColumns Browser · removedColumns Story points
    W-->>QA: Imported 47 records · 1 row left out · Removed 1 column
```

Read the diagram for two things. First, **every step before the last box is a read**: the board is
untouched while the user is still able to change their mind. Second, **the numbers on the way out are
the numbers on the way in** — row 7 is row 7 of the sheet in the plan, in the outcome and in the
audit trail, because `sourceRowNumber` never left the row it belongs to.
