### 24.11 Export — scopes, formats, and what never reaches a file

```ts
// src/types/system.ts:149-160 — verbatim
export type ExportFormat = "xlsx" | "csv" | "pdf";
export type ExportScope  = "board" | "view" | "selection";

export interface ExportOutcome {
  readonly fileName: string;
  readonly rowCount: number;
  readonly columnCount: number;
  /** Columns withheld because the viewer may not read them. */
  readonly omittedColumns: readonly string[];
}
```

Permission: **`board.export`**, a **Member** key — "Taking data out of the product is a step past
reading it, so it starts here rather than at Viewer" (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:32-34`). It is
one of three `READ_ONLY_KEYS` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:28-33`), so it survives every
narrowing layer: an archived board, an archived ancestor and a lock all still permit export
(`evaluate.ts:77`, `:94-101`; `docs/SYSTEM.md:179-180`). A **trashed** node is the one exception —
`can` refuses everything but `node.delete` on a trashed node (`evaluate.ts:79-81`), and a
`READ_ONLY_KEY` returns before that check, so export of a trashed board is permitted by the client
resolver; the server must still refuse it with `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, because a record in the bin
is not a record you export.

#### 24.11.1 The three scopes

| Scope | Label | Rows | Includes archived? | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board` | "Entire board" | `rowOrder` — every record on the board | **Yes.** It does not pass through `queryRowIds`. | `src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:61`; `docs/SYSTEM.md:346-348` |
| `view` | "Current view" | `model.rowIds` — the active view's filters, sort, grouping, `subtaskDisplay` **and the active search term** | No, unless the view is showing archived | `src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:61`; `queryRowIds`, `src/lib/board-view.ts:194-234` |
| `selection` | "Selected records" | the ticked `selectedIds` | whatever was ticked | `src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:61` |

**`view` includes the search term** — canon §2.7 states it and `queryRowIds` proves it (`search`
is a first-class parameter at `src/lib/board-view.ts:200`, applied at `:225`). A backend that
reproduces only the saved view's filters and sorts exports a **different set of records** from the
one on the user's screen. The search term must therefore be in the request body.

A scope with zero records stays visible and unpickable in the dialog, "so the reason the export is
empty is on screen" (`src/components/board/export/export-dialog.tsx:120-123`).

#### 24.11.2 One projection, three writers

`buildExportGrid` (`src/lib/board-export.ts:86-106`) builds one rectangular `Grid` that all three
formats consume, "so XLSX, CSV and PDF cannot disagree about what a record says" (`:7-14`):

- **Header row** = `["ID", ...columns.map(c => c.name)]`.
- **One body row per record** = `[row.displayId, ...cellText(value, column, context)]`, an empty
  string for an absent cell.

**Leading every record with its display id is deliberate — "so an export round-trips"**
(`src/lib/board-export.ts:81`). `includeRecordId` defaults to `true` (`:82`, `:91`). Keep it: an
exported `QA-118` re-imported into a `Related bug` relation column resolves, because
`findRelationId` matches on the row id *or* the display label (`src/lib/cell-conversion.ts:160-167`).

| Format | Writer | Details the backend must reproduce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xlsx` | `buildXlsx(grid, boardName)` | Single sheet, cells as inline strings, no shared-string table (`src/lib/xlsx.ts:4-12`, `:53-65`). The sheet name is sanitised by `safeSheetName`: `: \ / ? * [ ]` replaced with a space, trimmed to 31 characters, fallback `Sheet1` — "Excel refuses to open a workbook whose sheet name it considers invalid, so a board called 'Q3: Launch' has to be cleaned" (`:32-39`). |
| `csv` | `toDelimited(grid)` | RFC 4180 quoting (`src/lib/csv.ts:55-67`), prefixed with a **UTF-8 byte-order mark** — "what makes Excel read the file as UTF-8 rather than Latin-1" (`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:130-131`). |
| `pdf` | `buildPdf({ title, lines: pdfLinesFrom(grid) })` | One line per record: cells whitespace-collapsed, joined with `"  ·  "`, clipped to `EXPORT_PDF_LINE_WIDTH = 92` characters with an ellipsis (`src/lib/board-export.ts:126-136`). The writer paginates and substitutes glyphs its single-byte Helvetica cannot draw (`src/lib/pdf.ts:1-9`, `:28-34`). The dialog is explicit that PDF is "A paginated list, for reading rather than re-importing" (`export-dialog.tsx:38`) — it is **not** required to round-trip. |

**MIME types** (`src/lib/board-export.ts:28-32`) —
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `text/csv;charset=utf-8`,
`application/pdf`.

**File name** (`exportFileName`, `src/lib/board-export.ts:109-119`):
`` `${slugify(boardName) || "board"}${scope === "board" ? "" : "-" + slugify(scopeLabel)}-${YYYY-MM-DD}.${ext}` `` —
e.g. `regression-suite-current-view-2026-08-27.csv`. The date is `nowIso.slice(0, 10)`, a **date key,
never converted through UTC** (canon C-04).

#### 24.11.3 Permission-sensitive fields are excluded — EXISTING REQUIREMENT

`SY-EXP-36`: "a column the caller may not read is removed from the exported file." The frontend
implements it by removing the column from the projection **before any writer sees it**:

```ts
// src/lib/board-export.ts:64-75
export function selectExportColumns(
  columns: readonly BoardColumn[],
  { canViewSensitive }: ColumnFilterOptions,
): ColumnSelection {
  if (canViewSensitive) return { columns, omitted: [] };

  const kept = columns.filter((column) => !isSensitiveColumn(column));
  return { columns: kept, omitted: columns.filter(isSensitiveColumn).map((c) => c.name) };
}
```

- **The test** is the column's **name** against
  `/secret|token|password|credential|api[\s_-]?key|private[\s_-]?key/i`
  (`src/lib/board-export.ts:48-51`).
- **The gate** is `can("secret.reveal")` (`src/components/board/board-page.tsx:82`) — "Columns that
  look like credentials only leave the workspace with someone who is allowed to read a secret in the
  first place" (`:80-81`).
- **The report** is `ExportOutcome.omittedColumns`, rendered as a warning line naming every withheld
  column (`src/components/board/export/export-dialog.tsx:129-138`).
- The code is explicit that this is a stand-in: "Column-level ACLs are a backend concern; until they
  exist this name test is the honest stand-in, and it is deliberately conservative — a column called
  'API key' leaves the file rather than leaking into a spreadsheet somebody mails on"
  (`src/lib/board-export.ts:42-47`).

**Also excluded, by construction rather than by rule.** State these, because a backend writer
reproducing "export the board" from scratch will otherwise include them:

| Not in the file | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Attachment bytes and URLs | An `attachment` cell renders as a comma-joined list of file **names** (`cellText`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts:114-115`). No signed URL, ever — canon's OQ-75 position is that URLs are minted per response and never persisted; putting one in a spreadsheet that gets mailed on is exactly the leak that rule exists to prevent. |
| `revision`, `createdBy`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `archivedAt`, `parentRowId` | Not in `buildExportGrid`'s projection (`src/lib/board-export.ts:97-103`). The parent/child relationship is therefore invisible in an export. |
| Comments and activity | Different aggregates; not reachable from the grid. |
| A relation target's cells | A `relation` cell renders as the target's resolved label only (`src/lib/cell-values.ts:117-123`). |

**Not excluded, deliberately: hidden columns.** `model.columns` is documented as "Every column in
view order, hidden ones included" (`src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:21-23`) and it is what reaches
`selectExportColumns` (`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:53-56`). Hiding a column is a presentation
choice, not a permission. **The server must not "helpfully" filter hidden columns** — that would
silently change what an export contains.

**The honest security note, and it belongs in this document.** As long as the client holds the whole
board — which it does today, because `BoardSnapshot` ships every row and `nextCursor` is always
`null` (canon OQ-36) — the export column gate is **advisory, not a boundary**. A client that ignores
`omittedColumns` can build the same file from cells it already has. The real boundary is the *read*:
if a viewer may not read a column, that column must not be in the snapshot. Until column-level ACLs
exist (OQ-29), E-086's `omittedColumns` is an honest report of the server's decision and a correct
input to the audit trail, and it is not a control.

**RECOMMENDATION.** Move the pattern and the gating key into `GET /config` (E-139) — as
`sensitiveColumnPattern: string` and `sensitiveColumnPermission: PermissionKey` — so the two sides
cannot disagree, exactly as canon does for the upload ceiling under OQ-69 ("the client pre-check is
served from `GET /config` so the two cannot disagree"). The server remains the authority: it
recomputes the selection and returns the authoritative `omittedColumns`, whoever wrote the bytes.
Do **not** add an `is_sensitive` column to `board_columns` — canon T-11 fixes that table's column
list and part 4 fixes its `config` contract; a real solution is column-level ACLs under OQ-29, not a
boolean smuggled in ahead of the decision.

---

### 24.12 Sync vs async — the threshold, and the recommendation

**Today the server is not involved at all.** `useBoardExport.run` makes **no service call**: it
builds the grid, writes the bytes and triggers a browser download
(`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:79-113`, `writeFile` at `:118-137`). Two consequences follow, and
both are reasons E-086 must exist even for the small cases:

1. **The `board.export` audit row can never be written.** The seed advertises one — `module: "board"`,
   `action: "board.export"`, detail "31 records exported to XLSX. 1 sensitive column omitted."
   (`src/services/audit-service.ts:197-206`) — and nothing can produce it while the export never
   reaches a server. `SY-EXP-36` and `SY-AUD-41` together make an unaudited data egress a compliance
   defect.
2. **The permission decision is made by the client.** See §24.11.3.

**DECIDED, following canon E-086.** The **response shape is chosen by scope**, not by row count:

| Scope | Response | Who writes the bytes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `view`, `selection` | `200` `ExportOutcome` | The **client**, from rows it already holds. The server's job is the authoritative `omittedColumns`, the `rowCount`/`columnCount` it agrees to, the canonical `fileName`, and the audit row. |
| `board` | `ExportJob` | The **server**, into S3-compatible object storage, delivered as a short-lived signed URL. |

**The sync/async threshold sits inside the `board` scope**, and it decides the job's *state in the
first response*, not the response's shape:

> **RECOMMENDATION — `EXPORT_SYNC_ROW_LIMIT = 5 000`.** When the resolved row count for a `board`
> scope export is at or below it, generate inline and answer `200` with
> `state: "ready"` and a `downloadUrl`. Above it, enqueue and answer `202` with `state: "pending"`;
> the client polls E-141.

Why 5 000 and not a guess:

- `SY-EXP-36`'s own performance target is **5 000 rows to Excel in under 2 s** (PRD, feature 36).
  A number the product already committed to is the number to hold a synchronous request open for.
- It is the same ceiling as `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` (`src/config/app.ts:48`), so a board a user can fill
  in one import is a board they can export in one request.
- `docs/SYSTEM.md:331-334` draws the line at exactly this scale: "Excel and CSV are streamed from one
  projection and are fine at board scale, but a 500.000-record export belongs on the server."
- It is a config value, not a constant in code: serve it from `GET /config` as
  `exportSyncRowLimit` so it can be lowered without a client release.

Two refinements, both cheap:

- **PDF is capped lower.** A PDF draws one line per record with ~34 lines per page
  (`src/lib/pdf.ts:22-26`), so 5 000 records is a ~150-page document nobody reads. **RECOMMENDATION:**
  async for `format: "pdf"` above **1 000** rows, and keep generating it — refusing a large PDF is a
  worse answer than making the user wait for one.
- **Never truncate.** An export that silently stops at 5 000 rows and calls itself "the board" is the
  export equivalent of §24.3. Cross the threshold, do not shrink the answer.

**Job delivery, retention and cleanup.**

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Where do the bytes go? | S3-compatible object storage, key `exports/{workspaceId}/{jobId}/{fileName}`. **Not** `file_assets` — an export is not a workspace file, it has no drive node, and it must not count against `StorageQuota.usedBytes` (canon §1.3.4 reserves `file_assets.size_bytes` for the quota). |
| How is it fetched? | A signed URL on `ExportJob.downloadUrl`, minted per response, never stored on the row. Same rule as canon's OQ-75 position for attachments. |
| How long does it live? | **RECOMMENDATION** — `expires_at = created_at + 24 h`. A nightly sweep deletes the object and the row. The signed URL's own TTL is shorter: **15 minutes**, re-mintable by calling E-141 again. |
| What if it fails? | `state = 'failed'`, `error` carries an `AppError` with `isRetryable: true`; the client re-POSTs E-086. |

---

### 24.13 Table: `export_jobs` (T-39)

Module `system`. **RECOMMENDATION** — the frontend has no counterpart; canon reserves the table and
OQ-42 covers it.

**Scope of the table: server-generated exports only.** A `view` or `selection` export writes **no
row here** — the bytes were never on the server, so a row would record a file that does not exist.
That export's permanent record is its `audit_events` row, which is the thing a compliance question
actually asks about.

```sql
-- Documentation only.
CREATE TABLE export_jobs (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  board_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  actor_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)  ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  scope           export_scope  NOT NULL,          -- always 'board' today; see the CHECK
  format          export_format NOT NULL,          -- 'xlsx' | 'csv' | 'pdf'
  view_id         UUID REFERENCES board_views(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  state           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
                  CHECK (state IN ('pending','running','ready','failed')),

  file_name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  row_count       INTEGER,                         -- NULL until counted
  column_count    INTEGER,
  omitted_columns JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,   -- string[] of column names

  storage_key     TEXT,                            -- NULL until state = 'ready'
  error_reason    TEXT,                            -- ErrorReason, set only when state = 'failed'

  expires_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT export_jobs_server_generated CHECK (scope = 'board'),
  CONSTRAINT export_jobs_ready_has_key
    CHECK ((state = 'ready') = (storage_key IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT export_jobs_failed_has_reason
    CHECK ((state = 'failed') = (error_reason IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE INDEX export_jobs_board_idx  ON export_jobs (board_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX export_jobs_queue_idx  ON export_jobs (state, created_at)
  WHERE state IN ('pending','running');
CREATE INDEX export_jobs_reaper_idx ON export_jobs (expires_at)
  WHERE state = 'ready';
```

**Columns, and why each is there.**

| Column | Type | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID PK | Canon C-01. Addressed by E-141. |
| `board_id` | UUID FK → `boards.id`, CASCADE | The export belongs to a board. |
| `actor_id` | UUID FK → `users.id`, RESTRICT | Session-derived (canon C-09). Only the actor may poll or download (§24.14). |
| `scope` | ENUM `export_scope` | Canon §2.7, values `board`/`view`/`selection` verbatim. The CHECK pins it to `board` because only that scope produces a server-side file; the column is typed for the full enum so lifting the restriction later is a CHECK drop, not a migration. |
| `format` | ENUM `export_format` | `xlsx` \| `csv` \| `pdf`, canon §2.7. |
| `view_id` | UUID FK → `board_views.id`, SET NULL | Unused while `scope = 'board'`; kept so a future `view`-scope job can name the view it froze. SET NULL because a deleted view must not delete the record that an export happened. |
| `state` | TEXT + CHECK | Four values. **Not a Postgres ENUM** — part 2 already fixed this: "`export_jobs.state` is a job-runner state with no frontend counterpart and no exhaustive switch." A job-runner state changes more often than a domain enum. |
| `file_name` | TEXT | Computed by the server with `exportFileName`'s rule, so the download's name matches what the dialog promised. |
| `row_count` / `column_count` | INTEGER NULL | Mirror `ExportOutcome`. NULL until the worker has resolved the scope. |
| `omitted_columns` | JSONB | The withheld column **names**, as `ExportOutcome.omittedColumns`. Names, because that is what the warning line renders. |
| `storage_key` | TEXT NULL | The object key. Never the URL — URLs are minted per response with a 15-minute TTL. |
| `error_reason` | TEXT NULL | An `ErrorReason` (canon §4.3), so a failure is classifiable without parsing a message. |
| `expires_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ NULL | When the object and this row are swept. |
| `completed_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ NULL | For the "how long do exports take" question the first incident asks. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | Canon C-03. |

**JSONB structure — `export_jobs.omitted_columns`** (canon C-06): `readonly string[]`, board column
names in `position` order, exactly the array `ExportOutcome.omittedColumns` carries.

**Cardinality.** One `boards` row → 0..N `export_jobs`. One `users` row → 0..N. One `board_views`
row → 0..N (all NULL today). Leaf table; nothing references it.

**Unique constraints.** None. Two identical exports are two events. E-086 replay protection, if
wanted, is an `Idempotency-Key`; it is **not** on part 1's list of five, and it should not be — a
duplicate export costs one object, and the audit trail wants both rows anyway.

**Indexes.** `(board_id, created_at DESC)` for the per-board history; a partial
`(state, created_at)` for the worker's claim query, partial so the index holds only live work; a
partial `(expires_at)` for the reaper.

**Delete behaviour.** `board_id` CASCADE — deleting a board removes its export history, and the
sweep must also delete the orphaned objects (a `DELETE` trigger enqueuing the storage key, or the
nightly reaper reconciling storage against the table). `actor_id` RESTRICT. `view_id` SET NULL.

**Retention.** Rows are removed with their object at `expires_at` (24 h). The permanent record of
"an export happened" lives in `audit_events`, which has its own 12-month retention question
(OQ-27) — that separation is deliberate: the file is transient, the fact is not.

---

### 24.14 Export endpoints

#### `POST /api/v1/boards/:boardId/export`

**Purpose** — Resolve an export's scope and column selection server-side, record that it happened,
and either hand back the authoritative `ExportOutcome` for the client to write the file
(`view`/`selection`) or start a server-side generation (`board`). Canon E-086.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `board.export` on the board's node, plus workspace membership. A **Member** key
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:32-34`). Because it is a `READ_ONLY_KEY`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:28-33`) it passes the archive, freeze and lock narrowings — an
archived board still exports. **The server must additionally refuse a trashed node** with
`NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`: the client resolver returns early for read-only keys and never reaches the
trashed check (`evaluate.ts:77-81`), and a record in the bin is not a record you take out of the
product.

`secret.reveal` on the same node is read separately — not as a gate on the call, but as the input to
the column selection (§24.11.3). Absence narrows the file; it never refuses the request.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body**

```ts
interface CreateExportRequest {
  readonly scope: ExportScope;            // "board" | "view" | "selection"
  readonly format: ExportFormat;          // "xlsx" | "csv" | "pdf"

  /** Required when scope === "view". The saved view whose filters, sorts and grouping apply. */
  readonly viewId?: string;

  /**
   * The active search term. Part of what "the current view" MEANS — queryRowIds applies it
   * alongside the filters (src/lib/board-view.ts:200, :225). Omitted or "" means no search.
   * Ignored for the other two scopes.
   */
  readonly search?: string;

  /** Required when scope === "selection". minItems: 1. */
  readonly rowIds?: readonly string[];

  /**
   * Lead every record with its display id. Default true — "so an export round-trips"
   * (src/lib/board-export.ts:81).
   */
  readonly includeRecordId?: boolean;

  /**
   * Default true for scope "board" (rowOrder carries archived records), and for scope "view"
   * it defaults to the view's own archived toggle. src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:58-68.
   */
  readonly includeArchived?: boolean;
}
```

**Response** — a discriminated union on `scope`, because the two branches are genuinely different
answers and collapsing them would need `null`s in both.

```ts
type CreateExportResponse =
  | { readonly kind: "outcome"; readonly outcome: ExportOutcome }   // scope view | selection
  | { readonly kind: "job";     readonly job: ExportJob };          // scope board

/** Verbatim from src/types/system.ts:154-160. */
interface ExportOutcome {
  readonly fileName: string;
  readonly rowCount: number;
  readonly columnCount: number;
  readonly omittedColumns: readonly string[];
}

type ExportJobState = "pending" | "running" | "ready" | "failed";

interface ExportJob {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly scope: ExportScope;
  readonly format: ExportFormat;
  readonly state: ExportJobState;
  readonly fileName: string;
  readonly rowCount: number | null;              // null until resolved
  readonly columnCount: number | null;
  readonly omittedColumns: readonly string[];
  /** Signed, 15-minute TTL, minted per response. null unless state === "ready". */
  readonly downloadUrl: string | null;
  readonly expiresAt: string | null;             // ISO 8601
  readonly error: AppError | null;               // set only when state === "failed"
  readonly createdAt: string;
}
```

Status: `200` for `kind: "outcome"`; `200` for `kind: "job"` with `state: "ready"` (generated
inline, under the threshold); `202` for `kind: "job"` with `state: "pending"`.

```jsonc
// 200 POST /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/export   { "scope": "view", "format": "csv", "viewId": "v_1", "search": "smoke" }
{
  "kind": "outcome",
  "outcome": {
    "fileName": "regression-suite-current-view-2026-08-27.csv",
    "rowCount": 31,
    "columnCount": 9,
    "omittedColumns": ["API key"]
  }
}
```

```jsonc
// 202 POST /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/export   { "scope": "board", "format": "xlsx" }
{
  "kind": "job",
  "job": {
    "id": "01JB9M…", "boardId": "9a2e…", "scope": "board", "format": "xlsx",
    "state": "pending",
    "fileName": "regression-suite-2026-08-27.xlsx",
    "rowCount": null, "columnCount": null, "omittedColumns": [],
    "downloadUrl": null, "expiresAt": null, "error": null,
    "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

**Database**

*Reads:*

| Table | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | The board's node and ancestors — visibility, `deleted_at`. |
| `boards` | `id`, `node_id`, `name` (the file name and the sheet name come from it), `row_id_prefix`. |
| `board_columns` | Every column, hidden ones included, in `position` order. The selection is computed here. |
| `board_views` | The named view, when `scope = "view"`: filters, `filter_conjunction`, sorts, grouping, `subtask_display`. |
| `board_rows` | The resolved set. `scope: "board"` → every row including archived; `scope: "view"` → filters + search + sort applied; `scope: "selection"` → `WHERE id = ANY($rowIds) AND board_id = $boardId` (an id from another board is dropped, not an error — the frontend filters unknown ids the same way, `src/components/board/board-page.tsx:72-75`). |
| `workspace_members` + `users` | To render `user` cells as names. |
| `board_row_relations` / `board_rows` | To render `relation` cells as target labels, one query per target board. |
| `access_rules` | Visibility on the board's node and on relation target boards. |

*Writes:*

| Table | Write |
| --- | --- |
| `export_jobs` | One row — **only for `scope: "board"`** (§24.13). |
| `audit_events` | One row, **every scope**: `module = 'board'`, `action = 'board.export'`, `severity = 'info'`, `outcome = 'allowed'`, `target` = the board's name, `detail` = `` `${rowCount} records exported to ${FORMAT}. ${n} sensitive column omitted.` `` — the seeded format verbatim (`src/services/audit-service.ts:197-206`), with the second sentence omitted when `n === 0`. |

**Transaction** — **Required, but small.** The `export_jobs` insert and the `audit_events` insert are
one transaction. The row read is not inside it: an export is a snapshot of a moving board and does
not need repeatable-read isolation across a 5 000-row scan. **Nothing about generating the file is
in a transaction** — the worker writes to object storage and then flips `state` in its own short
transaction.

**Realtime** — **None.** An export changes nothing anybody else is looking at, and canon defines no
frame for it. A client waiting on a job polls E-141; adding a frame for one client's own job would be
a socket message with an audience of one.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `EXPORT_SCOPE_INVALID` — `scope: "selection"` with `rowIds` absent or empty, or `scope: "view"` with no `viewId`. Canon §4.3 names exactly these two cases. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `format` or `scope` outside its enum; `rowIds` longer than the board's row count. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `board.export`. |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` — the board is in the bin. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` — unknown board, or one the caller may not see. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` — `viewId` is not a view of this board. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED` — see the note below. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` — object storage refused the inline generation. `isRetryable: true`. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR`. |

**Rate limiting — RECOMMENDATION.** A whole-board export is the cheapest way to exfiltrate a
workspace and the most expensive read the API offers. Add a fifth bucket to part 1's four: **10
exports / 5 minutes, per user per workspace**, returning `RATE_LIMITED` with `retryAfterSeconds` and
`isRetryable: true`. Unlike the secret bucket, a throttled export is **not** audited as a denial —
nothing was read.

**Frontend Used By** — `run` in `src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:79-113`, called from
`src/components/board/export/export-dialog.tsx:153-155`. The dialog is opened from
`src/components/board/board-toolbar.tsx:148-157` (scope `board`) and from
`src/components/board/bulk/bulk-action-bar.tsx:190-199` (scope `selection`), and the two are kept
apart by remounting on the scope key (`src/components/board/board-page.tsx:186-193`).

---

#### `GET /api/v1/boards/:boardId/export/:jobId`

**RECOMMENDATION — E-141.** Canon's registry stops at 140 endpoints and has no read for an export
job, yet canon §4.3 already defines `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` (409 / `conflict`, "The async export is
still running"), which nothing in the registry can raise. This endpoint is the missing half of that
error. Flagged for the editor at the end of this chapter.

**Purpose** — Poll an asynchronous whole-board export, and mint a fresh signed download URL once it
is ready.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `board.export` on the board's node, **and** `export_jobs.actor_id = session.user.id`.
An export job is personal: the file may contain columns the requester could read and a colleague
could not, so a second user with `board.export` must start their own. A job belonging to somebody
else answers `404` `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_FOUND`, never `403` — canon §4.2's rule that "the resource does
not exist" and "the caller may not see it" answer identically.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boardId` | UUID | `boards.id`. Must match `export_jobs.board_id`. |
| `jobId` | UUID | `export_jobs.id`. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `redirect` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true` and the job is ready, answer `302` to the signed URL instead of a JSON body — so the job id can be a plain link. When `true` and the job is not ready, answer `409` `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY`. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `200` `ExportJob` (the interface in E-086). `downloadUrl` is minted on every call with
a fresh 15-minute TTL and is `null` unless `state === "ready"`.

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/boards/9a2e…/export/01JB9M…
{
  "id": "01JB9M…", "boardId": "9a2e…", "scope": "board", "format": "xlsx",
  "state": "ready",
  "fileName": "regression-suite-2026-08-27.xlsx",
  "rowCount": 41230, "columnCount": 9,
  "omittedColumns": ["API key"],
  "downloadUrl": "https://objects.example.net/exports/…?X-Amz-Expires=900&…",
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-28T09:30:00.000Z",
  "error": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z"
}
```

**Database**

| Table | Read/Write |
| --- | --- |
| `export_jobs` | **Read** one row by `(id, board_id)`, plus `actor_id` for the ownership check. |
| `nodes` | **Read** the board's node, for visibility. |

No writes. The signed URL is minted from `storage_key`; it is never stored.

**Transaction** — Not required. A single-row read.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — no `board.export` on the board. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_FOUND` — unknown job, a job on another board, a job belonging to another user, or one already swept at `expires_at`. **RECOMMENDATION**: this reason is not in canon §4.3 and needs adding. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` — `?redirect=true` on a job that is `pending` or `running`. Canon §4.3 already defines it. |
| 502 | `network` | `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` — the object store could not issue a signed URL. |

**Frontend Used By** — nothing today. `useBoardExport` writes the bytes itself
(`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:118-137`) and has no polling state. The change is contained: `run`
gains a branch on `kind === "job"` and a poll loop, and the dialog's existing `isExporting` spinner
covers the wait.

---

### 24.15 Open questions

#### OPEN QUESTION (OQ-42) — are import parsing and export generation client-side by design, or by absence of a server?

**What is unclear** — whether the browser should keep owning the spreadsheet, or whether a real
backend is expected to take it.

**Evidence** — the whole import pipeline is browser code: XLSX unzip and parse (`src/lib/xlsx.ts`),
CSV/TSV parse (`src/lib/csv.ts`), mapping (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:145-184`), validation
(`:357-423`). The only thing crossing the wire is a batch of cells
(`src/services/board-service.ts:1171-1176`). Export makes **no service call at all**
(`src/hooks/use-board-export.ts:79-113`) and writes XLSX, CSV and PDF in the browser
(`src/lib/xlsx.ts`, `src/lib/csv.ts`, `src/lib/pdf.ts`). `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5 000`
(`src/config/app.ts:48`) is a ceiling a browser holds comfortably, and `SY-EXP-36`'s own target is
5 000 rows to Excel in under 2 s — a browser figure.

**Recommendation** — **keep it, with the server as the authority.** The browser parses the file
(that is where the file is, and it is what gives the user errors while the mapping is still
editable); the server parses the *cells* against the board's schema and owns the write. Export stays
client-generated for `view` and `selection`, becomes server-generated for `board`, and E-086 is
called in every case so the audit row lands and the column decision is the server's. This is canon's
position on E-084/E-085/E-086 and part 1's §7.11, and this chapter follows it.

**Impact if wrong** — if the server must parse the file, E-084 and E-085 gain a
`multipart/form-data` variant, part 1's "JSON only" rule gains an exception, `import_jobs` gains a
staged-object reference, and the row-alignment rules in §24.3 stop being inherited and become code
somebody has to write correctly a second time. The endpoint shapes survive; the content-type contract
does not.

#### OPEN QUESTION (OQ-41) — default invalid-value policy, transactionality, and the row ceiling

**What is unclear** — the frontend defaults the policy and truncates the file client-side; neither is
stated as a rule the server enforces.

**Evidence** — `useState<ImportInvalidPolicy>("skip")` (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:87`) is a
component default, not a contract. `readImportSource` does `.slice(0, IMPORT_MAX_ROWS)`
(`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:77`) and the banner says "Only the first 5,000 rows of this file will be
imported" (`import-mapping-step.tsx:148-153`). The mock service has no transaction at all — it
mutates a `Map` in a loop (`src/services/board-service.ts:1195-1214`).

**Recommendation** — canon has already taken the position and this chapter implements it: **default
`skip`; one transaction covering column creation, column removal and row inserts.** Add: the row
ceiling is **enforced with a 400, never by truncation** (§24.9), because truncating is the same class
of silent data loss as §24.3.

**Impact if wrong** — a `blank` default would import flagged rows nobody agreed to import. Truncation
instead of refusal would put 5 000 of 6 000 records on a board and report success.

#### OPEN QUESTION (OQ-29) — `ExportOutcome.omittedColumns` implies column-level permissions that exist nowhere

**What is unclear** — `SY-EXP-36` requires that "a column the caller may not read is removed from the
exported file", but there is no column-scoped permission key and no column-scoped ACL anywhere.

**Evidence** — the 39-key catalogue has no column-level key (`src/types/permission.ts:31-78`), and
the frontend stands in a **name regex** for the missing rule:
`/secret|token|password|credential|api[\s_-]?key|private[\s_-]?key/i` gated on `secret.reveal`
(`src/lib/board-export.ts:48-51`; `src/components/board/board-page.tsx:80-82`). The code says so:
"Column-level ACLs are a backend concern; until they exist this name test is the honest stand-in"
(`:42-45`). `docs/SYSTEM.md:335-337` repeats it.

**Recommendation** — for this release, **reproduce the heuristic server-side, exactly**, gated on
`secret.reveal`, and serve the pattern and the key from `GET /config` so the two sides cannot
disagree. Do **not** add `board_columns.is_sensitive` and do **not** invent a `board.column.read`
key ahead of the decision — either would freeze a workaround into the schema. And record, in this
document, that the gate is advisory while the client holds the whole board (§24.11.3): the real fix
is that a column a viewer may not read is absent from `BoardSnapshot`, which is a change to E-047,
not to E-086.

**Impact if wrong** — a column named "Client token" leaves the workspace in a spreadsheet, or a
column innocently named "Password policy" is withheld from an export that needed it. The first is a
breach; the second is a support ticket.

#### OPEN QUESTION (OQ-88) — does a committed import notify watchers?

**What is unclear** — an import creates 47 records on a board people are watching. Nothing says
whether that is 47 notifications, one, or none.

**Evidence** — `WatchKind` includes `board` (`src/types/collab.ts:86`), so a board is watchable, but
the only fan-out in the frontend is the comment path (`src/services/comment-service.ts:222-266`).
`notificationService.emit` is never called from any board write. Canon's RT-06 covers the realtime
frame — which is not a notification.

**Recommendation** — **one notification per watcher per import**, `reason: "system"`, title
`` `${created} records imported into ${boardName}` ``, linking to the board. Never one per record: 47
inbox rows for one action is how a notification centre becomes something people mute. Emit it in the
same transaction as the commit, as canon requires for the comment fan-out.

**Impact if wrong** — either a silent bulk change on a watched board, or an inbox flooded 5 000
deep by one import.

#### Two frontend defects found while writing this chapter

Neither changes a backend contract; both are recorded so nobody specifies around a bug.

**FE-1 · `.tsv` is offered and then rejected.** `useImportWizard` accepts the extension
(`SPREADSHEET_EXTENSIONS = { xlsx, csv, tsv }`, `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:74`), the upload step
advertises it (`ACCEPT = ".xlsx,.csv,.tsv"`, `import-upload-step.tsx:18`; the hint says "XLSX, CSV or
TSV", `:70-72`), and `delimiterFor` handles it (`src/lib/csv.ts:70-72`). But the very next gate,
`validateUpload`, tests against `ALL_ACCEPTED_EXTENSIONS`, which contains `xlsx` and `csv` and **not**
`tsv` (`src/lib/file-validation.ts:7-14`). Every `.tsv` file is refused with "is not an accepted file
type". **Backend position:** the API accepts a parsed `ImportSource` and does not care what the file
was called, so nothing here changes; but `GET /config`'s accepted-extension list must include `tsv`
if the wizard is to keep advertising it.

**FE-2 · `importRows` drops `sourceRowNumber`.** `rowsToCreate` returns
`readonly Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>[]` (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:449-453`) — the row
number that `ImportDraftRow` carefully carried (`src/types/system.ts:107-113`) is discarded at the
last step before the write. It is why `ImportOutcome` can report a count of skipped rows but not
*which* rows, and why the store cannot map a created record back to a line in the sheet.
**Backend position:** E-085 takes the `ImportSource` and returns `importedRows` and `skippedRows`,
both keyed by `sourceRowNumber` (§24.8.2), which closes it.

---

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

Canon was followed everywhere below; each entry is a **canon edit**, not a chapter edit, and is
recorded here rather than resolved in place.

1. **One endpoint added: E-141 `GET /boards/{boardId}/export/{jobId}`.** Canon §3.11 gives E-086 an
   `ExportJob` response for `board` scope but no way to read the job afterwards, while canon §4.3
   already defines `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` (409) — an error no registered endpoint can raise. §24.14
   specifies the missing read. Canon's endpoint count becomes **141**. If the editor prefers not to
   grow the registry, the alternative is re-POSTing E-086 with the same `Idempotency-Key`, which
   returns the stored response and therefore can never show a state change — it does not work.

2. **One error reason added: `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_FOUND`** (404 / `not_found`, module `system`), for
   E-141. Canon §4.3's import/export block has `EXPORT_SCOPE_INVALID` and `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` but
   no not-found for a job.

3. **One enum added: `ImportSkipReason`** = `invalid_value` \| `blank_row`, snake_case to match
   `BulkSkipReason` (canon §2.7). It carries the per-row reason in `ImportOutcome.skippedRows`, which
   is what "the frontend wants row-level errors" resolves to. Canon's enum count becomes 69 (61 on
   the wire). **One enum documented, not added: `ExportJobState`** = `pending` \| `running` \|
   `ready` \| `failed` — part 2 already fixed these four values and stored them as TEXT with a CHECK
   rather than a Postgres ENUM; this chapter follows that and does not register it as a domain enum.

4. **E-085's Perm column is composed, not replaced.** Canon lists `board.import`. §24.9 additionally
   requires `board.column.create` when the mapping contains a `create` target and
   `board.column.delete` when `removeUnmappedColumns` is true, because the frontend's confirm makes
   exactly those three calls (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:233`, `:243`, `:271`). Both extra keys
   are Manager keys alongside `board.import`, so no role today can hold one without the others and
   nothing observable changes — but a future role that gains import and not schema rights would
   otherwise get column creation for free. Suggest amending canon §3.11's Perm cell to
   `board.import` (+ `board.column.create` / `board.column.delete` conditionally).

5. **Three additive fields on `ImportOutcome`, and one on `ImportPlan`.** `ImportOutcome` gains
   `jobId`, `issueCount`, `blankCount`, `importedRows`, `skippedRows`, `createdColumns`; `ImportPlan`
   gains `issueCount`. Every existing field keeps its name, type and meaning, so no frontend read
   breaks. The one frontend line that changes is
   `src/components/board/import/import-validation-step.tsx:106-110`, which currently derives "…and N
   more findings" from `plan.issues.length` and must derive it from `issueCount` once the array is
   capped.

6. **Three columns on `import_jobs` and five on `export_jobs` beyond part 2's ERD.** `import_jobs`
   gains `sheet_name`, `blank_count`, `issue_count`, `skipped_row_numbers` and `created_column_ids`;
   `export_jobs` gains `file_name`, `row_count`, `column_count`, `omitted_columns`, `error_reason`
   and `completed_at`. Each is justified at its table (§24.7, §24.13); `blank_count` in particular is
   what makes the counts add up, and without it the `CHECK` constraint cannot be written. Part 2's
   ERD should be reconciled to match, or these treated as its detail.

7. **`export_jobs` holds server-generated exports only**, pinned by
   `CHECK (scope = 'board')`. Canon T-39 describes it as "Async whole-board export", which this
   follows; the consequence worth stating in canon is that a `view` or `selection` export's only
   permanent record is its `audit_events` row.

8. **Three constants proposed for `GET /config` (E-139)**, whose canon payload list is
   "max upload bytes, accepted extensions, trash retention days, import max rows, version history
   limit, search group limit, my-work widget limit, audit page size": add `importIssueCap` (500),
   `exportSyncRowLimit` (5 000) and the pair `sensitiveColumnPattern` /
   `sensitiveColumnPermission`. The last two exist so the export column gate cannot drift between
   client and server, which is the same reasoning canon already applied to the upload ceiling under
   OQ-69.

9. **A fifth rate-limit bucket proposed:** whole-workspace export, 10 per 5 minutes per user per
   workspace (§24.14). Part 1 defines four buckets and states each exists because a specific endpoint
   is abusable; E-086 with `scope: "board"` is the cheapest bulk-egress path in the API.

10. **A per-route body limit proposed:** 16 MB for E-084 and E-085, against a 1 MB default. Part 1
    names `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` but sets no number, and a 5 000-row × 12-column `ImportSource` is
    1.5–4 MB of JSON. §24.6 explains why sending it twice is preferable to caching a plan.

11. **Two sub-questions filed under existing OQ ids rather than new ones**, per canon §8's rule
    against inventing ids: the "is sending `ImportSource` twice acceptable" question sits under
    OQ-42 (§24.6), and "does the row ceiling truncate or refuse" sits under OQ-41 (§24.15). If the
    editor would rather they were separately traceable, they need their own ids appended to canon.

12. **Part 9's OQ-102 is followed over the board fact sheet's R-03.** R-03 listed E-085 as a path
    that must enforce select transition rules; part 9 narrowed that to "gate transitions, not
    creations" and excluded E-085. §24.9 follows part 9. Flagging it so the two do not both stand.

## 25. Notifications

Module: `collab`. Tables touched: `notifications` (T-35), `users` (T-01), `nodes` (T-06),
`boards` (T-10), `board_rows` (T-12), `watches` (T-34, read by the producer).
Endpoints: **E-129, E-130, E-131, E-132**. Realtime: **RT-03**, **RT-04**.

**One row per recipient — fan-out on write.** There is no shared "event" row and no
subscription join at read time. That is what makes every read a single-table index scan on
a leading `recipient_id`, and it is what lets `list` only ever return the signed-in user's
inbox (`src/services/notification-service.ts:8-15`).

---

### 25.1 The wire model

```ts
/** src/types/collab.ts:97 */
type NotificationReason = "mention" | "assigned" | "comment" | "watch" | "system";

/** src/types/collab.ts:101-113 */
interface AppNotification {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly reason: NotificationReason;
  /** Inbox this belongs to. Every read is already scoped to the caller; the
   *  field is on the wire because the realtime ingest checks it
   *  (src/store/notification-store.ts:112). */
  readonly recipientId: string;
  readonly actor: UserSummary;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly body: string;
  /** Null for workspace-level system notices that route nowhere. */
  readonly target: EntityRef | null;
  readonly createdAt: string;   // ISO 8601
  /** Derived: notifications.read_at IS NOT NULL. */
  readonly isRead: boolean;
}

/** E-129, E-130, E-131. Canon §3.21. */
interface NotificationPage {
  readonly items: readonly AppNotification[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
  /** Total unread in this inbox, AFTER the write this response reports.
   *  Every read-state mutation therefore returns a fresh, authoritative badge. */
  readonly unreadCount: number;
}
```

**`title` and `body` are fully rendered strings stored on the row** — not templates, not
i18n keys, no variable bag. There is no `payload` field anywhere in the frontend's type.
A notification is a **historical statement**: it says what was true when it was written, and
canon OQ-79 makes `notifications` the one table whose `target_label` is **frozen at creation**
rather than re-resolved on read.

**`isRead` is the only mutable field.** There is no `readAt` on the wire, no archive, no
dismiss and no delete (`src/types/collab.ts:112`). The database stores `read_at TIMESTAMPTZ`
and derives the boolean, so the frontend contract is unchanged and the "when" comes free
(canon §1.4 — never a boolean where a timestamp answers both questions).

---

### 25.2 The four tabs, and exactly how each query is served

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Tabs are a **projection of `reason`**, never a stored field. The
map is `TAB_REASONS` (`src/lib/notifications.ts:7-13`), and the module comment states the
invariant: *"Inbox tabs are a projection of `reason`, not a second field on the record — one
notification can never disagree with the tab it lands in"* (`:3-6`).

**The API filters by `reason` and never by tab name** (canon OQ-90). The mapping stays in the
frontend, where `NOTIFICATION_TABS` (`:20-25`) already owns it, so there is exactly one copy
of it and no way for the two sides to drift.

| Tab (`NotificationTab`) | Label | Reasons | Request | Index used | Predicate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | All | *(none — no filter)* | `GET /me/notifications?cursor=&limit=` | `notifications_inbox_idx (recipient_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)` | `recipient_id = $me` |
| `mentions` | Mentions | `mention` | `?reason=mention` | `notifications_reason_idx (recipient_id, reason, created_at DESC, id DESC)` | `recipient_id = $me AND reason = 'mention'` |
| `assigned` | Assigned | `assigned` | `?reason=assigned` | `notifications_reason_idx` | `recipient_id = $me AND reason = 'assigned'` |
| `following` | Following | `watch`, `comment` | `?reason=watch&reason=comment` | `notifications_reason_idx` | `recipient_id = $me AND reason IN ('watch','comment')` |

**Why those two indexes and not one.**

- The **All** tab has no `reason` predicate, so an index led by `(recipient_id, reason, …)`
  cannot serve its ordering: Postgres would have to sort, because the index orders by
  `reason` before `created_at`. `notifications_inbox_idx` puts `created_at DESC, id DESC`
  directly after `recipient_id`, so All is an index scan that stops after `limit + 1` rows —
  no sort node, and the keyset cursor is a direct seek into the same order.
- The three filtered tabs each have an equality on `reason`, which makes
  `notifications_reason_idx` an index scan over one contiguous range per reason value,
  already in `created_at DESC` order. `following` scans two such ranges and merges them; the
  planner does this as a `BitmapOr` or two index scans with a merge append, and both stop
  early because the ordering is preserved within each range.
- Both indexes carry `id DESC` as the tie-breaker so the keyset cursor is **total**. Without
  it, two notifications written in the same transaction (the fan-out writes several) share a
  `created_at` and a cursor built on `created_at` alone would skip or repeat one of them.

**`reason` is a repeatable query parameter, OR-combined.** **RECOMMENDATION**: canon's E-129
signature is `?reason=` and does not say how a set is expressed; `following` needs two
values. Repeating the parameter avoids inventing a comma-splitting rule that would then need
escaping for a value set that is a closed enum anyway. An unknown value is
`VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), never a silently empty page.

**Ordering is `created_at DESC, id DESC` on every tab** — `newestFirst`
(`src/services/notification-service.ts:24-26`).

---

### `GET /api/v1/me/notifications`

**Purpose** — The signed-in user's inbox, newest first, optionally filtered by reason, with
the authoritative unread count attached.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Session only. **There is no `userId` parameter** (P-06, C-09): the recipient
is the session user. The mock takes `userId` as an argument
(`src/services/notification-service.ts:28`), which canon OQ-19 marks `critical` — an inbox
addressed by a parameter is every inbox.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | `NotificationReason`, repeatable | no | *(none = All)* | OR-combined. Unknown value → `VALIDATION_FAILED`. |
| `cursor` | opaque base64 | no | — | Keyset on `(created_at DESC, id DESC)`. Never constructed or parsed by a client. |
| `limit` | int | no | `50` | Server cap 100. |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | no | — | **RECOMMENDATION.** Scope the inbox to one workspace. The frontend has one active workspace at a time (`selectActiveWorkspace`) and `notifications.workspace_id` is `NOT NULL`, so an unscoped inbox mixes tenants in the bell. Omitted = every workspace the caller is still a member of. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `NotificationPage`, `200`.

```jsonc
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "0192f6a0-…",
      "reason": "mention",
      "recipientId": "usr_mai",
      "actor": { "id": "usr_lan", "name": "Lan Nguyen", "initials": "LN", "accentColor": "violet" },
      "title": "Lan Nguyen mentioned you",
      "body": "Reproduced on staging. Can you confirm the signature check is the one failing?",
      "target": {
        "kind": "row", "nodeId": "nd_bug_tracker", "boardId": "brd_bug_tracker",
        "rowId": "row_7", "label": "BUG-007"
      },
      "createdAt": "2026-08-27T09:30:00.000Z",
      "isRead": false
    },
    {
      "id": "0192f5f1-…",
      "reason": "system",
      "recipientId": "usr_mai",
      "actor": { "id": "usr_system", "name": "NexDrop", "initials": "ND" },
      "title": "Storage is at 52% of the team plan",
      "body": "Archive the 2026 incident bundles to free the largest share.",
      "target": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-26T05:30:00.000Z",
      "isRead": true
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": "eyJhdCI6IjIwMjYtMDgtMjZUMDU6MzA6MDBaIiwiaWQiOiIwMTkyZjVmMS0ifQ==",
  "unreadCount": 4
}
```

**Server-side visibility filtering is mandatory, not optional.** An inbox outlives the
access that filled it, and a notification carries the **name** of what it is about. The
frontend already re-resolves every item against the tree the reader can see **now** and
drops the ones whose node is gone or no longer visible — `keepVisibleRefs`
(`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:58-64`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:242-268`), with
the reason written out at `:49-57`: *"one that arrived while somebody held a folder keeps
naming that folder after they lose it… which also stops the click-through from being a way
back in."* The backend applies the same rule in the query and never relies on the client
dropping them. **Items with `target === null` are always kept** — a workspace announcement
has no node to check.

The filter is a join, not a post-pass: `LEFT JOIN nodes … WHERE n.id IS NULL OR
<visible(n.id, $me)>`, so the `limit` still returns a full page. This is the same
correctness argument as §27.3.

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` | read | `WHERE recipient_id = $me [AND reason = ANY($reasons)] [AND workspace_id = $ws]` ordered `created_at DESC, id DESC`, `LIMIT $limit + 1`. Index per the table in §25.2. |
| `nodes` | read | Visibility resolution for every non-null `target_node_id` — an ancestor-chain walk, batched for the page's node ids. |
| `users` | read | `actor_id` → `UserSummary`. |
| `notifications` | read | `unreadCount`: `count(*) WHERE recipient_id = $me AND read_at IS NULL`, over the partial index `notifications_unread_idx`. |

`target_label` is **not** re-resolved (OQ-79). `board_rows` and `boards` are not joined on
this path at all — the label the notification shows is the one it was written with.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None (read).

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — unknown `reason`, `limit` above the cap, malformed `cursor`. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — `workspaceId` names a workspace the caller is not a member of. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/notification-store.ts:60-71` (`refresh`, via
`notificationService.list(CURRENT_USER.id)`), reached by `load()` (load-once, `:55-58`) from
`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:45-47`. Rendered by
`src/components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx` inside both
`notification-bell.tsx:70-75` and `notifications-page.tsx:55`.

---

### `POST /api/v1/me/notifications/read`

**Purpose** — Mark specific notifications read. Opening a notification is reading it: the
feed marks read **and** routes in the same handler
(`src/components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:31-38`), so this endpoint fires on
every click.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Session only.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — `MarkNotificationsReadRequest`.

```ts
/** Canon §5.4, `collab`. */
interface MarkNotificationsReadRequest {
  readonly ids: readonly string[];
}
```

**Response** — `NotificationPage`, `200`. The **caller's list plus the fresh
`unreadCount`** — the store assigns the response directly
(`src/store/notification-store.ts:84`), which is why this is not a `204`.

**Ids outside the caller's own inbox are ignored, not applied — and not an error.**
`src/services/notification-service.ts:43-48` intersects the requested ids with the set the
caller actually owns, then marks only that. Not `403`, not `404`, and not a partial-failure
report: a `404` on a foreign id would confirm that the id exists, turning the endpoint into
an existence oracle over every inbox in the system. Canon's `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` is
reserved for a route that addresses a **single** notification, and this is not one.

`ids: []` is a valid request and a no-op that still returns the current page — the client's
`markRead` guards against it locally (`src/store/notification-store.ts:78`) but the server
must not depend on that.

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` | **update** | `UPDATE notifications SET read_at = now() WHERE recipient_id = $me AND id = ANY($ids) AND read_at IS NULL RETURNING id`. The `recipient_id` predicate **is** the scoping, done in the statement rather than in a check-then-write. `read_at IS NULL` keeps the first read time. |
| `notifications` | read | The page and the recomputed `unreadCount`. |

**Transaction** — Not required. One `UPDATE` and one read; the read is allowed to see a
notification that arrived in between, which is the desired behaviour.

**Realtime** — **RT-04 `notification.read`** `{ notificationIds }`, carrying **only the ids
actually scoped to that recipient** — the `RETURNING` set, not the requested set. Delivered
to that recipient's own sockets only. A client must not be able to learn that an id it
guessed exists by seeing it echoed back.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `ids` is not an array of strings, or is longer than 500. |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/notification-store.ts:76-88` (`markRead`), optimistic with
rollback: it applies `markReadLocally` first *"so the badge drops on click, not on the round
trip"* (`:80-81`) and restores the previous array on failure (`:85-87`). Triggered from
`src/components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:32`.

---

### `POST /api/v1/me/notifications/read-all`

**Purpose** — Empty the badge.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Session only.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | no | — | **RECOMMENDATION**, matching E-129. Scopes the clear to one workspace so "Mark all read" in one tenant does not silently clear another. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `NotificationPage`, `200`, with `unreadCount: 0` (for the given scope).

**It clears every unread notification in the inbox, not the active tab's.** The control sits
in the popover header and the page header, outside the tab strip, and is disabled on
`controller.unread === 0` — the **total**, not the tab count
(`src/components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx:49-58`,
`src/components/notifications/notifications-page.tsx:29-38`).

**Database** — `notifications`: **update**
`SET read_at = now() WHERE recipient_id = $me AND read_at IS NULL [AND workspace_id = $ws]
RETURNING id`, driven by the partial index `notifications_unread_idx`, which stays small
however long the read history grows. Then one read for the page.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — **RT-04 `notification.read`** with the `RETURNING` ids — the ones actually
marked, matching `src/services/notification-service.ts:63-68`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/notification-store.ts:90-106` (`markAllRead`), also
optimistic with rollback.

---

### `GET /api/v1/me/notifications/unread-count`

**Purpose** — The bell badge, computed by the server over the whole inbox.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Session only.

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | no | — | **RECOMMENDATION**, matching E-129. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `UnreadCountResponse`, `200`.

```ts
interface UnreadCountResponse {
  /** Total unread — the bell badge, and the All tab's badge. */
  readonly unreadCount: number;
  /** Per-reason unread, so the four tab badges are exact without loading the
   *  inbox. RECOMMENDATION; `unreadCount` is what canon E-132 requires.
   *  The frontend sums watch + comment for Following, using the TAB_REASONS
   *  map it already owns (src/lib/notifications.ts:12). */
  readonly byReason: Readonly<Record<NotificationReason, number>>;
}
```

```jsonc
{
  "unreadCount": 4,
  "byReason": { "mention": 2, "assigned": 1, "comment": 1, "watch": 0, "system": 0 }
}
```

**Why this endpoint exists.** The frontend derives every badge from the loaded array:
`countUnread` (`src/lib/notifications.ts:39-41`), the memoised
`all.filter(item => !item.isRead).length` (`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:66`), and
`unreadByTab`, which computes all four counts in one pass over the inbox
(`src/lib/notifications.ts:44-62`). That is deliberate and correct **while the inbox is
unpaginated** — the badge cannot drift from the list because it is the list. The moment
E-129 pages, the badge silently becomes *"unread among the ones we loaded"*, which is canon
OQ-91's exact complaint. E-132 restores the invariant from the other side: the count is
authoritative and the list is a window onto it.

**Database** — `notifications`: one index-only scan over
`notifications_unread_idx (recipient_id, reason) WHERE read_at IS NULL`, producing
`count(*)` and the `GROUP BY reason` in the same pass. The index is partial, so its size is
a function of *unread* rows, not of all history — a user with 40 000 read notifications and
3 unread pays for 3.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None. The count moves through RT-03 (an insert) and RT-04 (a read), and the
client recomputes; this endpoint is the resync, not the stream.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — **None today** — the badge is derived
(`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:66`, rendered at
`src/components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx:35-39`). It becomes the badge's source
the moment E-129 is paged. **RECOMMENDATION**, canon OQ-91.

---

### 25.3 Who writes a notification

**Never a client.** There is no `POST /me/notifications` and no chapter may add one. Rows
are inserted by the endpoint performing the action, inside its transaction — the same rule
as `audit_events` (canon §3.23), for the same reason: a writable inbox is a spam primitive.

| `reason` | Icon | Producer today | Producer owed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mention` | `AtSign` | **E-120** — `fanOut` (`src/services/comment-service.ts:226-235`) | — |
| `comment` | `MessageSquare` | **E-120** — `fanOut` (`:238-249`) | — |
| `assigned` | `UserPlus` | **none** — seed data only (`src/mock/collab.ts:189-206`) | E-066 / E-074 (OQ-89) |
| `watch` | `Eye` | **none** — seed data only (`:216-225`) | E-066, E-092 (OQ-88) |
| `system` | `Bell` | **none** — seed data only (`:226-235`) | quota, membership, deadlines (OQ-89) |

Icon mapping: `src/components/notifications/notification-item.tsx:10-16`. The comment
fan-out itself is specified in full in §20.5 and is not repeated here.

---

### 25.4 Open questions

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-89) — nothing emits `assigned`, `watch` or `system` notifications.**
> **Evidence** — all three reasons exist (`src/types/collab.ts:97`), own tabs
> (`src/lib/notifications.ts:11-12`) and have seed rows (`src/mock/collab.ts:189-235`), but
> no code path emits one: the cell-edit path writes an activity entry
> (`src/services/board-service.ts:531`) and no notification. The single `system` seed is
> attributed to a real colleague (`:226-235`), which is wrong for a machine notice, and
> `AppNotification.actor` is non-nullable (`src/types/collab.ts:106`).
> **Recommendation** — (a) `assigned`: when the **assignee-lens** user column
> (`src/lib/my-work.ts:57-67`, OQ-48) gains a user id, emit one row per newly added
> assignee, excluding the actor; emit nothing on removal. (b) `watch`: see OQ-88.
> (c) `system`: reserve a synthetic actor row in `users` (`usr_system`, name "NexDrop") so
> the non-nullable contract holds. Note that `system` appears in **All only**, because it is
> in no other tab's reason list — so the PRD's "Deadline tomorrow: TASK-81" must be emitted
> as `assigned`, or it lands where nobody is looking.
> **Impact if wrong** — the Assigned and Following tabs are permanently empty in production
> while the fixtures show them populated, which reads as a regression.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-88) — which non-comment events notify watchers?**
> **Evidence** — the PRD for `CO-WAT-28` promises notifications on status change, new
> comment and deadline update. The frontend fans out **only** on a new comment
> (`src/services/comment-service.ts:238-249` is the sole producer), and the watch button's
> own tooltip says only *"You get notified about new comments here"*
> (`src/components/collab/watch-button.tsx:51-53`).
> **Recommendation** — emit a `watch` notification to watchers, excluding the actor, when a
> watched row's **status-lens** column changes, when its **due-lens** column changes, and
> when a watched **document is saved**. Use the same lenses My Work uses
> (`src/lib/my-work.ts:59-68`) so "status" and "due" mean one thing across surfaces.
> Debounce per `(watcher, target)` under the OQ-91 coalescing window.
> **Impact if wrong** — either the Following tab only ever shows comments and the PRD
> promise is unmet, or every cell edit on a busy board floods every watcher's inbox.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-91) — retention, coalescing and paging.**
> **Evidence** — `emit` creates one row per recipient per event with no coalescing
> (`src/services/notification-service.ts:88-109`), and the inbox is unpaginated and returns
> everything (`:28-33`). Ten comments on a watched record are ten rows for every watcher.
> **Recommendation** — cursor-page at 50 (canon §6.3); within a **15-minute** window, a
> second `comment` notification for the same `(recipient_id, reason, target, actor_id)`
> updates the existing **unread** row's `created_at` and `body` instead of inserting, over
> `notifications_coalesce_idx`; **never coalesce `mention`** — being named twice is two
> distinct asks; purge **read** notifications after 90 days by a nightly sweep and never
> purge an unread one.
> **Impact if wrong** — a busy thread makes the inbox unusable and the bell badge
> meaningless. Retrofitting coalescing after users have unread history is messy, because the
> rows to merge are already distinct facts on somebody's screen.
