## 26. Favorites / Recent

Module: `drive`. Tables touched: `node_favorites` (T-07), `nodes` (T-06).
Endpoints: **E-028, E-029, E-033**. Not a table: `recent_entries` (canon §1.2).

Two features that look alike and are not. A favourite is a **durable, per-user, per-node
fact** that belongs in the database. A recent visit is a **per-device navigation
convenience** that canon keeps in `localStorage`. §26.4 says exactly what changes if that
decision is ever reversed.

---

### 26.1 Favourites are per user, and generic over the node

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `isFavorite: boolean` sits on `DriveNodeBase`
(`src/types/node.ts:58`), so **all five `NodeKind` values are starrable** — project, folder,
document, board and file. The Favorites page groups exactly those five
(`GROUP_ORDER`, `src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:24-32`).

**Canon settles the per-user question (OQ-07, position in §8.8): per user, in
`node_favorites (user_id, node_id)`, never a flag on the node.** The frontend stores it on
the node only because the whole tree is a single-user in-memory mock
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:454-470`); a shared boolean would mean two colleagues fighting
over one star.

So `DriveNode.isFavorite` is a **DERIVED, per-viewer** field on the wire:

```sql
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM node_favorites f WHERE f.user_id = $me AND f.node_id = n.id)
```

Two viewers reading the same node get different values for the same field. That is the
point, and it is why the column does not exist on `nodes`.

**The generic resource is `nodes`.** There is no `favorites (resource_kind, resource_id)`
table, because a board record, a comment and a version are not favouritable — only things
with a place in the tree are, and everything with a place in the tree is a `nodes` row
(canon §1.3.1). A polymorphic favourite would trade a real foreign key for a generality
nothing asks for.

**The Favorites view adds no second list.** *"Starring already lives on the drive node, so
this view adds no second list — it groups what the tree already knows, which is why
un-starring here updates the sidebar and the drive grid in the same frame"*
(`src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:16-22`).

---

### `PUT /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/favorite`

**Purpose** — Star a node for the signed-in user.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **Visibility on `nodeId`. No action key.** Starring changes nothing about
the node and is invisible to everyone else, so a Viewer may star what a Viewer may see.
Requiring `node.rename` or any write key would make "keep a link to this" a privilege.

Starring is **not** blocked by archive, freeze or lock. Those layers narrow *writes to the
node*; a favourite is a write to the reader's own row. It **is** blocked on a trashed node,
which accepts nothing but `node.delete` (`NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`) — and E-033 filters
trashed nodes out anyway.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | UUID | Any `NodeKind`. |

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None. `PUT` on a boolean sub-resource, per P-07: the path *is* the
assertion.

**Response** — `204`, no body. Canon E-028 specifies it, and it is the deliberate exception
to C-10: there is no authoritative record to return, because the resource is the presence or
absence of a row. The client already knows what it asked for and the tree read that follows
carries `isFavorite`.

**Database** — `nodes` (read: existence, visibility walk, `deleted_at IS NULL`);
`node_favorites` (**insert**): `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (user_id, node_id) DO NOTHING`.

**Idempotent.** The unique constraint `(user_id, node_id)` is the conflict target, so
starring twice is a no-op — which is what lets the frontend's optimistic toggle retry
safely.

**Transaction** — Not required. One statement.

**Realtime** — **None.** A favourite is private to one person. Emitting RT-11
`node.changed` would broadcast one person's private list to every subscriber on that node; a
second tab of the *same* user converges on its next tree read.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown node, **or one the caller may not see** (canon §4.2: the two answer identically). |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/store/workspace-store.ts:454-470` (`toggleFavorite`), reached
from `src/components/shared/favorite-star.tsx:66` (`FavoriteButton`), the drive item menu
(`src/components/drive/drive-item-menu.tsx:93`), the drive toolbar's multi-select
(`src/components/drive/drive-toolbar.tsx:100` — `selectedIds.forEach(toggleFavorite)`, i.e.
**N independent calls, not a bulk endpoint**), the node detail panel
(`src/components/drive/node-detail.tsx:81`), the file manager
(`src/components/files/file-manager.tsx:111`) and the file viewer header
(`src/components/files/preview/viewer-header.tsx:118`).

> The toolbar's `selectedIds.forEach(toggleFavorite)` is a **toggle** per node, so a mixed
> selection ends up mixed. Because the API splits the toggle into `PUT` and `DELETE`, the
> client resolves each node's current state before choosing the verb — which is strictly
> better than today: a re-issued toggle over a partly-starred selection currently inverts
> each node independently, and two clicks are not a no-op. Splitting the verb makes both
> operations idempotent.

---

### `DELETE /api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/favorite`

**Purpose** — Un-star a node for the signed-in user.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Visibility on `nodeId`, exactly as E-028.

**Path Params** — `nodeId` (UUID).

**Query Params** — None.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `204`.

**Database** — `node_favorites` (**delete**): `DELETE WHERE user_id = $me AND node_id = $1`.
**Hard delete** — there is nothing to keep. Deleting a favourite that is not there returns
`204`, not `404`: the state requested is the state achieved.

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | `not_found` | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown or invisible node. Note the asymmetry: a **missing favourite** is not an error, but a **missing node** is, because the route addresses the node. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — the same `toggleFavorite` call sites as E-028; the unstar branch is
reached from the Favorites page, where every row is starred by definition
(`src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:99-101`).

---

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/favorites`

**Purpose** — Everything the signed-in user has starred in one workspace, for the Favorites
smart view.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — Workspace membership. Each returned node is additionally filtered by the
caller's visibility of it.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | Membership gate; "not a member" is not "viewer" (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`). |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | int | no | `500` | Hard cap 1000. §6.3 lists favourites as bounded-by-construction, but an unbounded list is a spec defect. |

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `DriveNode[]`, `200`. Flat, not nested — the page groups by `type` itself
(`src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:42-52`), and a nested tree would have to
carry unstarred ancestors just to hold the shape.

**Three exclusions, matching `isVisible` at
`src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:35-36`:**

1. **trashed nodes** — `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`;
2. **archived pages** — `isDocument(node) && node.isArchived`; archived pages have their own
   smart view (E-034) and appearing in both reads as a duplicate;
3. **nodes the caller can no longer see** — the visibility walk, which is also what stops a
   star surviving as the name of a folder somebody was shut out of.

**The favourite row is kept when the node is trashed.** Restoring the node restores the
star. Filtering happens on read, not by deleting the row — a delete would make Trash
restore a node the user has to re-star, which is data loss dressed as tidiness.

Ordering is left to the client: the page sorts within each group by
`a.name.localeCompare(b.name)` (`:49`). The API returns rows ordered
`(kind, name)` so a client that does not sort still renders sensibly.

**Database**

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node_favorites` | read | `WHERE user_id = $me`, leading column of the `UNIQUE (user_id, node_id)` index. |
| `nodes` | read | Join on `node_id`, `WHERE workspace_id = $ws AND deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT (kind = 'document' AND archived_at IS NOT NULL)`, then the visibility walk. |
| `users` | read | `owner_id` → `UserSummary`. |
| `access_rules` | read | `isShared` = a rule exists on the node. |
| per-kind side tables | read | `boards` / `documents` / `file_nodes` for the kind-specific fields of each `DriveNode` variant. |

**Transaction** — Not required.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown, or one the caller is not a member of. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`. |

**Frontend Used By** — `src/components/collections/favorites-page.tsx:42-52`, which today
derives the list from the already-loaded tree via `collectNodes(tree, isVisible)`. The
sidebar's Favorites smart view links to it (`src/config/app.ts:85-89`,
`src/components/layout/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:46`).

---

### 26.2 Recents: how they are recorded today

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — this is `localStorage`, and canon keeps it there.**
`recent_entries` is one of the eight explicitly-not-tables (canon §1.2), citing
`src/store/recent-store.ts:9-18`:

> Recent (CO-REC-33). A least-recently-used list of the last {@link RECENT_LIMIT} places
> visited, **kept in this browser only**. It is a navigation convenience, so best-effort
> storage is the right trade: a blocked storage API costs the history, nothing else.

| Fact | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Storage key `nexdrop-recent` | `src/store/recent-store.ts:18` |
| `RECENT_LIMIT = 10` | `src/config/app.ts:36` |
| Entry shape `{ ref: EntityRef, visitedAt: ISO }` | `src/types/collab.ts:184-187` |
| LRU: touching moves to the front, the tail past the limit is dropped | `touchEntry`, `src/lib/lru.ts:7-19` |
| Keyed by `refKey(entry.ref)` | `src/store/recent-store.ts:35` |
| Every read is shape-validated entry-by-entry and anything malformed is **dropped rather than trusted** | `:42-65` (`isRecentEntry`) |
| Every write is `try/catch`; failing silently is designed behaviour | `:67-73` |
| `isHydrated` starts `false` so SSR and client markup agree | `:23`, `src/hooks/use-recent.ts:23` |
| Entries are re-resolved against the visible tree on render and **dropped outright** when invisible | `src/components/collections/recent-page.tsx:37-40` (`keepVisibleRefs`) |
| Cleared wholesale when access is lost | `src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:68` |

**Recording is implicit, on read — and it already is.** There is no explicit "record a
visit" call anywhere in the frontend's UI layer. `useOpenEntity` calls `visit(ref)` on every
successful navigation (`src/hooks/use-entity-navigation.ts:34`), before it routes, and
`useTrackRecent(ref)` records a visit from an effect keyed on `refKey(ref)` and the label —
*"Keyed on the target, so re-rendering a page does not push a new entry — only actually
arriving somewhere else does"* (`src/hooks/use-recent.ts:28-46`).

**What changes when there is a backend: nothing.** Canon's position (OQ-96): Recent stays in
`localStorage`. The client keeps writing `nexdrop-recent`, the API gains no endpoint, and no
table is created. Two consequences a backend developer must know so they do not go looking:

- **The Recent list is not in any response.** `GET /workspaces/{id}/tree` does not carry
  `visitedAt`, and the empty-query state of the search palette reads Recent from the store,
  not from the API (`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:117-133`).
- **The server-side filter that Recent needs is already free.** The client re-resolves every
  entry against the tree the API returned, so a person who lost a folder stops seeing its
  name without the server ever knowing they had it in a list.

**Why not a table.** A Recent list answers *"where was I just now?"* on **this device**.
Making it server state means **one write per navigation for every user** — which would be
the highest-volume write in the product, higher than cell edits — to produce a list that is
wrong the moment somebody switches laptops mid-task, and that carries a denormalised label
with the same leak surface as the inbox but none of the inbox's reason to exist.

---

### 26.3 If Recent is promoted: keep top N **at query time**

**RECOMMENDATION, deferred, canon OQ-96.** Do not build this until product asks for
cross-device Recent. When they do, this is the shape — and the wire type does not change,
because the frontend already speaks `RecentEntry`.

```sql
-- Documentation of intent, not a migration. Only if OQ-96 is resolved "yes".
CREATE TABLE recent_visits (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)      ON DELETE CASCADE,
  workspace_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target_kind     entity_kind NOT NULL,
  target_node_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id)      ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target_board_id UUID NULL     REFERENCES boards(id)     ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target_row_id   UUID NULL     REFERENCES board_rows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  visited_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT recent_row_board CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_board_id IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT recent_row_id    CHECK ((target_kind = 'row') = (target_row_id   IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT recent_identity  UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT
    (user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)
);

CREATE INDEX recent_visits_read_idx ON recent_visits (user_id, workspace_id, visited_at DESC);
```

`UNIQUE … NULLS NOT DISTINCT` is load-bearing: without it, `target_row_id IS NULL` on a
document visit would never conflict with itself and every visit would insert a new row.

**No `target_label` column.** Recent is the one place a stale label buys nothing: the read
already joins `nodes` for visibility, so it can take the live name in the same query.

**The write is an upsert, and only an upsert:**

```sql
INSERT INTO recent_visits (user_id, workspace_id, target_kind, target_node_id,
                           target_board_id, target_row_id)
VALUES (…)
ON CONFLICT (user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id)
DO UPDATE SET visited_at = now();
```

**The read caps at query time. It does not delete on write.**

```sql
SELECT … FROM recent_visits r
  JOIN nodes n ON n.id = r.target_node_id
 WHERE r.user_id = $me AND r.workspace_id = $ws
   AND n.deleted_at IS NULL AND <visible(n.id, $me)>
 ORDER BY r.visited_at DESC
 LIMIT $n;                                  -- RECENT_LIMIT = 10 today
```

**Why limiting at query time beats deleting on every write** — five reasons, in the order
they matter:

1. **The write is the hot path, and pruning doubles it.** A visit is one upsert. Trimming on
   write turns it into an upsert **plus** a `DELETE … WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id … ORDER BY
   visited_at DESC LIMIT 10)` — a sort and a second write, per navigation, per user. The read
   happens when somebody opens the Recent page or ⌘K; the write happens on every click in
   the product. Paying the cost on the rare side is the whole argument.
2. **Pruning on write serialises concurrent visits.** Two tabs navigating at once both run
   the delete over the same user's rows and take conflicting row locks; one waits. The
   upsert alone touches exactly one row.
3. **The visibility filter makes a fixed-size table wrong anyway.** The read drops entries
   whose node the caller can no longer see. If the table held exactly 10 rows and 4 of them
   are now invisible, the page shows 6 and there is nothing to fall back to. Keeping more
   rows than the display limit is what makes "the last 10 things you can actually open"
   answerable.
4. **`LIMIT` on `(user_id, workspace_id, visited_at DESC)` stops after N rows.** It is an
   index scan with an early exit; the table's size does not enter the plan. There is no
   query the cap makes faster.
5. **The display limit is a product decision that will change.** `RECENT_LIMIT` is a
   frontend constant today (`src/config/app.ts:36`) and belongs in `GET /config` (E-139).
   Raising it from 10 to 25 must be a config change, not a backfill of rows that were
   deleted.

**Bound the table with a sweep, not with the write path.** A nightly job deletes rows past
rank **100** per `(user_id, workspace_id)` and rows older than 90 days, with
`ON DELETE CASCADE` from `users`, `nodes`, `boards` and `board_rows` handling the rest.
100 is ten times the display limit — enough headroom that the visibility filter never
empties a page, small enough that the table stays a rounding error.

---

### 26.4 Open questions

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-96) — should Recent become cross-device server state?**
> **Evidence** — the store is explicit that it is *"kept in this browser only"*
> (`src/store/recent-store.ts:9-18`), and canon §1.2 lists `recent_entries` among the tables
> that deliberately do not exist. Nothing in the frontend reads a Recent list from a service.
> **Recommendation** — keep it in `localStorage`. Build §26.3 only when product asks for
> cross-device Recent; the wire type (`RecentEntry`) does not change either way, so the
> decision is reversible at any time and costs one table and two endpoints.
> **Impact if wrong** — building it now adds the product's highest-volume write for a
> convenience that already works; not building it means Recent does not follow a person from
> their laptop to their desktop.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-08) — is `isPinned` per user or global, like `isFavorite`?**
> **Evidence** — `DocumentNode.isPinned` sits on the node
> (`src/types/node.ts:101`) exactly as `isFavorite` does, and the sidebar's pinned-pages
> section reads it from the tree (`src/components/layout/sidebar/pinned-pages.tsx`). But
> pinning is written through `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document/pin` (E-093) gated on
> `document.update` — a **write key**, unlike a favourite's visibility-only gate — which
> reads as a shared, workspace-wide pin rather than a private one.
> **Recommendation** — canon's §8.8 position is *"per user; pinning follows the same shape
> once confirmed"*. Confirm with product: if pinning is private, E-093 must drop to a
> visibility gate and gain a `node_pins` table shaped like `node_favorites`; if it is
> shared, `nodes.is_pinned` stays and `document.update` is correct. **They cannot both be
> right**, and the current pairing — a per-node column written with a shared write key while
> its twin is per-user — is the inconsistency.
> **Impact if wrong** — either one person's pin rearranges everybody's sidebar, or a
> workspace-wide "these are the pages that matter" convention becomes unexpressible.

---

---

## 27. Search

Module: `search`. Endpoint: **E-133** — one endpoint over every resource type the frontend
searches. Reads `nodes` (T-06), `boards` (T-10), `board_rows` (T-12), `documents` (T-18),
`comments` (T-33), `access_rules` (T-08), `workspace_members` (T-04), `users` (T-01).
**Writes nothing.**

E-035 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/search?q=` is a **different endpoint** — the
drive's cheap name-only quick-find, returning `SearchHit[]` (canon OQ-94, position: two
endpoints). It belongs to the `drive` chapter and is not documented here. Anything a user
types into ⌘K goes to E-133.

---

### 27.1 What is searchable, and what a hit looks like

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Eight result kinds, from four underlying sources
(`src/types/collab.ts:153-161`, `src/services/search-service.ts`):

| Kind | Group label | Source | Fields matched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | Documents | `nodes` where `kind = 'document'` | `name`; then `excerpt` at 0.4 weight, **only when the name scored zero** |
| `api` | API endpoints | `board_rows` whose board's `template_id` is `apiDocs` | `custom_id` (row-id match) and the row's title |
| `bug` | Bugs | rows whose board's `template_id` is `bug` | as above |
| `qa` | QA cases | rows whose board's `template_id` is `qa` | as above |
| `row` | Records | **every other** board row | as above |
| `file` | Files | `nodes` where `kind = 'file'` | `name`; then `excerpt ?? ""` at 0.4 |
| `comment` | Comments | `comments` | `body_plain` at 0.4, with a snippet |
| `place` | Places | every other visible node — projects, folders, boards | `name` only; the body is `""` |

`api` / `bug` / `qa` are **derived from `boards.template_id` at read time**
(`TEMPLATE_KINDS`, `src/services/search-service.ts:39-43`) — a projection, never a schema
(canon §1.3.5). A board reshaped after it was created from a template keeps reporting the
template it came from here, which is the one place `templateId` is load-bearing.

**Group order is fixed and is not a ranking**: `document → api → bug → qa → row → file →
comment → place` (`SEARCH_GROUP_ORDER`, `src/lib/search-index.ts:11-20`). Labels at `:22-31`.
**Empty groups are omitted entirely** (`:84-85`).

```ts
/** src/types/collab.ts:163-180 */
interface SearchResult {
  /** Node id, row id, or comment id. Unique only within its kind — the palette
   *  keys on `${kind}:${id}` (src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:112). */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly kind: SearchResultKind;
  readonly title: string;
  /** Where it lives — the board name or the folder path. */
  readonly subtitle: string;
  /** Matching excerpt, for comments and long text. Null when the hit was on the title. */
  readonly snippet: string | null;
  readonly ref: EntityRef;
  /** Higher sorts first inside its group. */
  readonly score: number;
}

interface SearchGroup {
  readonly kind: SearchResultKind;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly results: readonly SearchResult[];
  /** RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-93). Matches BEFORE the per-group cap, so the
   *  palette can say "5 of 41" instead of implying there were five. */
  readonly total: number;
}
```

**Subtitle construction** — reproduce exactly:

| Kind | `subtitle` |
| --- | --- |
| node kinds (`document`, `file`, `place`) | `` `${Kind} · ${pathLabel}` `` — kind capitalised, then the ancestor chain joined by `" / "`, or `"Workspace root"` (`src/services/search-service.ts:156`, `src/lib/tree.ts:74-78`) |
| row kinds (`api`, `bug`, `qa`, `row`) | `` `${row.displayId} · ${boardNodeName}` `` (`:103`) |
| `comment` | `"Record comment"` when the target is a row, `"Page comment"` otherwise (`:127`) |

For a comment the **title** is `` `${author.name} on ${target.label}` `` (`:126`), and
`target.label` is resolved live — the comment's frozen `target_label` is not used here.

**Snippet** — `snippetAround(text, needle, radius = 48)`: 48 characters either side of the
match, `…` where truncated, falling back to the first 96 characters when the needle is
absent (`src/lib/search-index.ts:55-63`).

---

### 27.2 Ranking — explainable, not fuzzy, and reproduced verbatim

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `src/lib/search-index.ts:3-9` states the constraint:
*"Scoring is deliberately explainable rather than fuzzy… The result order is therefore
reproducible in a test."*

`scoreMatch(haystack, needle)` (`:39-52`), both sides trimmed and lower-cased:

| Condition | Score |
| --- | --- |
| exact equality | **100** |
| `startsWith` | **70** |
| substring whose preceding character is one of `\s / _ - . :` (a word start) | **50** |
| any other substring | **30** |
| no match | **0** — the caller drops it |

Modifiers:

- a **row-id match floors at 90** (`ROW_ID_SCORE`, `src/services/search-service.ts:35`), and
  the row's final score is `max(idScore, scoreMatch(title, needle))` (`:93-96`);
- **body and excerpt hits are multiplied by 0.4** (`BODY_WEIGHT`, `:37`), so a name match
  always beats a body match. For nodes the body is scored **only when the name scored zero**
  (`:147`) — a document whose title matches never also reports a body snippet;
- within a group: `score DESC`, ties by `title.localeCompare` (`src/lib/search-index.ts:91`),
  then the per-group cap.

**Reproduce these bands explicitly in SQL. Do not use `ts_rank`.** `ts_rank` is
length-normalised, corpus-dependent and not reproducible in a test — it would change the
order of two documents because a third one was edited. The bands are a `CASE` expression over
`position()` and `starts_with()` on the same normalised text the `tsvector` was built from:

```sql
-- Documentation of intent. `hay` is the lower-cased trimmed candidate text,
-- `q` the lower-cased trimmed query.
CASE
  WHEN hay = q                                             THEN 100
  WHEN hay LIKE q || '%'                                   THEN  70
  WHEN substr(hay, position(q in hay) - 1, 1) ~ '[\s/_.:-]' THEN  50
  WHEN position(q in hay) > 0                              THEN  30
  ELSE 0
END
```

The `tsvector` index decides **which rows are candidates**; this expression decides **what
order they come back in**. Splitting the two is what keeps the ranking testable while the
scan stays index-backed.

---

### 27.3 The permission rule — and why it must be in the query

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** Permission is resolved **once, at the node, with inheritance**, and
every result kind inherits it (`src/services/search-service.ts:26-32`, `:61-72`):

```ts
const visible = collectAllowed(
  tree,
  (node) => !node.isTrashed && capabilitiesFor({ role, user, node }).view,
);
const visibleNodeIds = new Set(visible.map((n) => n.id));
```

`collectAllowed` (`src/lib/tree.ts:304-320`) prunes a refused node **together with its whole
subtree** — it does not descend past a refusal. The doc comment says why:
*"a file inside a folder the viewer cannot open must not surface in search results just
because the file itself carries no restriction of its own."* Consequences the backend
inherits:

- board rows are scanned only for boards whose node id is in the visible set (`:81-84`);
- comments are kept only when `visibleNodeIds.has(comment.target.nodeId)` (`:117`);
- the tree the service reads is **already** the visibility-pruned one
  (`visibleTree`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:197-240`).

**The funnel runs before scanning, never after** (canon E-133: *"The permission funnel runs
before scanning, not after"*). In SQL that means the visible node-id set is computed first
and appears as a **predicate inside every scan**, not as a filter applied to a result set:

```sql
WITH visible AS (
  -- recursive walk of `nodes` applying accessMode + access_rules + workspace role,
  -- pruning a refused node together with its subtree; materialised per request
  SELECT id FROM …
)
SELECT … FROM board_rows r
  JOIN boards b ON b.id = r.board_id
 WHERE b.node_id IN (SELECT id FROM visible)     -- the funnel, in the query
   AND r.archived_at IS NULL
   AND (r.search_tsv @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', $q) OR r.custom_id ILIKE $prefix)
```

**Why post-filtering breaks pagination — and it is not only a leak.**

1. **The page size becomes non-deterministic.** Fetch 5 rows, drop 3 as invisible, return 2.
   The client sees a group of 2 with a "more" affordance that is wrong in both directions:
   there may be 40 more, or none. There is no over-fetch factor that fixes this, because the
   ratio of visible to invisible rows is a property of the *user*, not of the query — for a
   Viewer with one shared folder in a workspace of 400 restricted ones, a page of 5 needs a
   scan of thousands.
2. **The cursor stops being a position.** A keyset cursor encodes the sort key of the last
   row **returned**. If rows were dropped after the ordering, the last returned row is not
   the last row *examined*, so the next page re-examines everything between them — an
   O(n²) walk that also re-drops the same invisible rows on every page. Encoding the last
   *examined* row instead means the cursor names a row the caller may not see, which is a
   disclosure in a value the client stores and replays.
3. **Every count is a lie.** `total` per group, "Nothing matches", the group heading
   `${label} (${n})` (`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:109`) — all of them are
   computed over the pre-filter set. A user learns that 41 things match a competitor's name
   and is shown 3, which is precisely the fact the restriction exists to withhold.
4. **The cap becomes a denial of service against the reader.** `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5` is
   applied after ordering. Post-filtering means the 5 slots may be filled by rows that are
   then dropped, so a user with narrow access sees empty groups for kinds that do have
   matches they *may* see, further down the list.
5. **It is a leak even when nothing is rendered.** Timing and result counts are observable.
   A scan that touches restricted rows and discards them is slower in a measurable,
   query-dependent way.

The correct construction, therefore: **one `visible` CTE per request, referenced by every
branch of the union, with the per-group cap applied after ordering *within already-filtered
rows*.** `LIMIT 5` then means "the 5 best of what this person may see", which is the only
statement that survives paging.

**Nothing about visibility comes from the request.** The mock takes `role` and `user` as
input (`src/services/search-service.ts:45-50`), which canon OQ-20 marks `critical`. Both come
from the session (C-09). `previewAs` may only ever **narrow** (canon OQ-21), never widen; a
`previewAs` above the caller's real role is `PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES` (400).

### 27.4 Row-id lookup (QA-128) — a distinct fast path

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT (PRD `BD-RID-10`).** *"Use the ID for global search, to attach a link
or to refer to it in a comment (e.g. `QA-128 Failed do BUG-042`)."* This is a different query
from a text search and must not be buried inside one.

**The format.** `formatRowId(prefix, sequence)` = `` `${prefix}-${String(sequence).padStart(3,"0")}` ``
(`src/lib/row-id.ts:8`, `:13-15`). Prefixes are **uppercase letters only, at most 6**
(`normalizePrefix`, `:18-20`). The sequence comes from an **atomic counter owned by the
backend**, uniqueness is total, and **a deleted row's number is never reused**
(`src/lib/row-id.ts:1-6`, canon E-062). `custom_id` is a separate column; the PK is a UUID
(C-02).

**The matcher — reproduce both rules exactly** (`matchesRowId`, `src/lib/row-id.ts:46-62`):

1. Upper-case both sides. **If `displayId` contains the query, it matches.** This is what
   makes partial ids work: `API-0` finds `API-003`, and `128` finds `QA-128`.
2. Otherwise split the query on `[\s-]+`. If that yields **exactly two** parts
   `[prefix, digits]` with `digits` all numeric, compare `prefix` against the id's prefix and
   compare the **integer values** of the digit groups. So `task 7` and `task-7` both find
   `TASK-007`, while `TASK-8` does not.

Rule 2 is an integer comparison, not a string one — which is why it cannot be expressed as a
`LIKE` and needs its own branch.

**Detection.** A query is a **row-id candidate** when it matches
`^\s*[A-Za-z]{1,6}[\s-]*\d{1,6}\s*$` (rule 2's shape) or when, upper-cased, it is a
substring of some `custom_id` (rule 1). The second is not detectable from the query alone, so
the fast path is always attempted and simply returns nothing when it does not apply.

**The plan.**

```sql
-- Fast path. Runs against board_rows.custom_id only, over visible boards.
SELECT r.id, r.custom_id, r.board_id
  FROM board_rows r
  JOIN boards b ON b.id = r.board_id
 WHERE b.node_id IN (SELECT id FROM visible)
   AND r.archived_at IS NULL
   AND (
        r.custom_id ILIKE '%' || $qUpper || '%'                       -- rule 1
     OR (r.row_id_prefix = $prefix AND r.sequence = $digits::bigint)  -- rule 2
   )
 LIMIT 25;
```

- Rule 1 is a **leading-wildcard `ILIKE`**, which no btree can serve. It is served by a
  **`GIN (custom_id gin_trgm_ops)`** index from `pg_trgm` — the single reason the extension is
  needed at all.
- Rule 2 is an equality on `(row_id_prefix, sequence)` and is served by the plain btree
  `board_rows_custom_id_idx (board_id, custom_id)` plus the board's `row_id_prefix`; `sequence`
  is already a column (canon T-12), so no parsing happens in the query.
- A hit scores `max(90, scoreMatch(custom_id, q))` and lands in its template-derived group
  (`api` / `bug` / `qa` / `row`), so `QA-128` surfaces under **QA cases**, above every text
  match in that group.

**This fast path also backs E-069** `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/search?q=&limit=` — the
board-scoped relation and subtask pickers — with one extra predicate (`r.board_id = $1`) and
a primary-column substring fallback. Same index, same two rules, one implementation.

**Cross-board ambiguity is real and unresolved.** The prefix is configured **per board**
(`normalizePrefix`; `prefixForBoard`, `src/services/board-service.ts:1417`) with nothing
enforcing uniqueness across boards, so two boards may both use `QA` and `QA-128` may name two
records. Today that is harmless — search shows both, in their own groups, with the board name
in the subtitle. It stops being harmless the moment a `QA-128` token in a comment body is
expected to resolve to a link. See OQ-95.

---

### `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/search`

**Purpose** — One ranked, grouped, permission-filtered search across documents, board
records, files, comments and places. Serves ⌘K and nothing else needs a second search
endpoint.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — **Workspace membership** for the endpoint; **per-node visibility** for every
result, applied inside the query (§27.3). No action key: search returns what you may see, and
seeing is not an action.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | Tenant scope. Every branch of the union is filtered on it before anything else. Not a member → `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404). |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | string | yes | — | Trimmed. **An empty or whitespace-only `q` returns `[]`, not an error** (`src/services/search-service.ts:56-57`) — the palette shows Recent and quick actions instead (`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:117-172`). Max 200 characters. |
| `limitPerGroup` | int | no | `5` | `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT` (`src/config/app.ts:30`). Hard cap 50. |
| `kind` | `SearchResultKind`, repeatable | no | *(all eight)* | **RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-93).** The type filter. Restricts which groups are computed **and scanned**, so `?kind=comment` does not touch `nodes` or `board_rows` at all. Unknown value → `VALIDATION_FAILED`. |
| `offset` | int | no | `0` | **RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-93).** The "see all" drill-down, and **valid only with exactly one `kind`** — an offset across eight independently-capped groups has no meaning. `VALIDATION_FAILED` when `offset > 0` and `kind` is absent or repeated. Hard cap 500; deep ranked paging is a different feature. |

**Pagination, stated plainly.** Canon §6.3 puts search under **"neither"** — no cursor and no
offset in the baseline. The baseline response is capped at `limitPerGroup` per group *"so one
noisy board cannot crowd out a kind"*. `offset` above is the additive drill-down canon OQ-93
reserves, and it is offset-based rather than keyset **because ranked results are ordered by a
computed score, not by a stored key** — there is no column a cursor could encode, and the
ordering is stable only for the duration of one query. That is the one place in this API where
offset is correct, and it is capped precisely because it is O(offset).

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `SearchGroup[]`, `200`. A bare array (§6.2: no envelope), in the fixed group
order, empty groups omitted.

```jsonc
[
  {
    "kind": "qa",
    "label": "QA cases",
    "total": 3,
    "results": [
      {
        "id": "0192f7b1-…",
        "kind": "qa",
        "title": "Refund flow rejects an expired card",
        "subtitle": "QA-128 · Payment QA",
        "snippet": null,
        "ref": {
          "kind": "row", "nodeId": "nd_payment_qa", "boardId": "brd_payment_qa",
          "rowId": "0192f7b1-…", "label": "QA-128"
        },
        "score": 100
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "kind": "comment",
    "label": "Comments",
    "total": 12,
    "results": [
      {
        "id": "0192f4c1-…",
        "kind": "comment",
        "title": "Lan Nguyen on BUG-007",
        "subtitle": "Record comment",
        "snippet": "…confirm the signature check is the one failing? QA-128 covers it…",
        "ref": { "kind": "row", "nodeId": "nd_bug_tracker", "boardId": "brd_bug_tracker", "rowId": "row_7", "label": "BUG-007" },
        "score": 12
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

Note the comment's `score` of `12`: `scoreMatch` returned `30` for a plain substring and
`BODY_WEIGHT = 0.4` applied. The number is on the wire because the frontend's type declares it
(`src/types/collab.ts:173`); nothing renders it, but it makes the order auditable.

**Database** — one query per kind, unioned, all sharing the `visible` CTE:

| Table | Access | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | read | Membership and the caller's role — the floor for the visibility walk. |
| `nodes` | read | The recursive `visible` CTE (accessMode + inherited grants + subtree pruning), then the `document` / `file` / `place` branches: `name` scored always, `excerpt` scored only when `name` scored zero. |
| `access_rules` | read | Feeds the `visible` CTE. |
| `boards` | read | `template_id` → the `api` / `bug` / `qa` / `row` bucket; `node_id` → the visibility join; `name` → the row subtitle. |
| `board_rows` | read | `search_tsv` over the primary-column text, `custom_id` for the fast path. `archived_at IS NULL`. |
| `documents` | read | `search_tsv` over `plain_text`, **when full-body indexing is enabled** (OQ-93); otherwise this branch reads only `nodes.excerpt`. |
| `comments` | read | `search_tsv` over `body_plain`, `deleted_at IS NULL`, `target_node_id IN (SELECT id FROM visible)`. |
| `users` | read | Comment author names for the comment title. |

**Writes: none.** Search is a pure read. It writes no audit row either — canon OQ-26 asks
which privileged *reads* must be audited, and search is not on the list; only
`GET /workspaces/{id}/restricted-nodes` (E-046) and the audit export (E-137) are.

**Transaction** — **Not required.** A single read-committed snapshot. Running the union
inside one statement (or one implicit transaction) matters only so that all eight branches
see the same `visible` set — a permission revoked mid-query must not leave one group filtered
and another not.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — `q` longer than 200; unknown `kind`; `limitPerGroup` above the cap; `offset > 0` without exactly one `kind`. |
| 400 | `validation` | `PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES` — `previewAs` outranks the caller's real role (OQ-21). |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown workspace, **or one the caller is not a member of**. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED` — the frontend debounces at 180 ms (`SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`, `src/config/app.ts:33`, applied at `src/hooks/use-global-search.ts:33`), but a debounce is a courtesy, not a limit. |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`. |

**A failed search must be an error, not an empty result.** The palette renders a distinct
failure state and says so: *"A failed search is not an empty one. Without this branch the
dialog answers 'nothing matches' when the request never came back — the quietest kind of
wrong answer a search box can give"*
(`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:51-56`, rendered at `:84-91`). Never return
`[]` on a partial backend failure; if one branch of the union fails, the request fails.

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-global-search.ts:35-44` (`searchService.search`,
`enabled` only when the trimmed query is non-empty, `keepPreviousData: true`), rendered by
`src/components/search/global-search-dialog.tsx:106-115`, opened by ⌘K
(`src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx:30`) and the header search button
(`src/components/layout/header/global-search.tsx:17`).

---

### 27.5 The PostgreSQL approach: `tsvector` + GIN, plus `pg_trgm` for ids

**RECOMMENDATION**, and canon §1.2 already takes the shape: *"a separate `search_index`
table"* is one of the things that deliberately does not exist — **`tsvector` columns on
`documents`, `board_rows`, `comments` and `nodes`, with GIN indexes.**

**Why generated columns on the source tables rather than one index table.** A single
`search_index (entity_kind, entity_id, tsv)` needs a trigger or an application write on every
insert and update of four tables, and it holds a copy of text that can silently fall behind.
A `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (…) STORED` column cannot fall behind: Postgres recomputes it in the
same statement that changed the text, and there is no code path that can forget to. The cost
is that the four branches must be unioned at read time — which they must be anyway, because
each one joins to different tables for its subtitle and its `EntityRef`.

**What is indexed, exactly:**

| Table | Column | Definition | Index |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `documents` | `plain_text TEXT` | server-side `documentPlainText(blocks)` (`src/lib/blocks.ts:333-354`), recomputed on every save (E-092), never returned on the wire | — |
| `documents` | `search_tsv` | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', plain_text)) STORED` | `GIN (search_tsv)` |
| `comments` | `body_plain TEXT` | `plainBody(body)` — mention tokens flattened to `@Name` (`src/lib/mentions.ts:133-135`) | — |
| `comments` | `search_tsv` | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', body_plain)) STORED` | `GIN (search_tsv)` |
| `board_rows` | `primary_text TEXT` | generated projection of the primary column's cell text, alongside the `due_date` / `status_option_id` / `assignee_ids` projections canon §1.3.2 already requires | — |
| `board_rows` | `search_tsv` | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', primary_text)) STORED` | `GIN (search_tsv)` |
| `board_rows` | `custom_id TEXT` | `TASK-001` (C-02) | `GIN (custom_id gin_trgm_ops)` **and** btree `(board_id, custom_id)` |
| `nodes` | `name TEXT` | | `GIN (name gin_trgm_ops)` — the drive quick-find (E-035) and the `place` branch both do substring matching on names |
| `nodes` | `excerpt TEXT` | derived summary, 120 characters (`src/services/document-service.ts:165`) | covered by the `nodes` name index; not separately indexed |

**Text-search configuration.** `'simple'` for comments, row text and names — no stemming, no
stop-word removal. Product identifiers, code fragments and names are what people search for
here, and an English stemmer turns `parsing` into `pars` and drops `a`, `the`, `on` and `to`
from a body that may be nothing but those. `'english'` is used **only** on `documents.plain_text`,
where the text really is prose and stemming earns its keep. Two configurations, each with a
stated reason, is better than one that is wrong half the time.

**`pg_trgm` is needed for exactly two things** and should not be reached for beyond them:

1. `custom_id` partial matching — rule 1 of §27.4 is a leading-wildcard `ILIKE`;
2. `nodes.name` substring matching — `scoreMatch` awards 30 for *any* substring
   (`src/lib/search-index.ts:47-51`), so `ayment` must find `Payment Sprint`, which a
   `tsvector` on a lexeme boundary will not do.

Both are `GIN … gin_trgm_ops`. `pg_trgm`'s similarity operators (`%`, `<->`) are **not** used
— that is fuzzy matching, and the scoring contract is explicitly not fuzzy.

**The full-text index is a candidate filter, not the ranking.** The `@@` operator narrows the
scan; the `CASE` of §27.2 orders what survives. Where the two disagree — a query that is a
substring but not a lexeme prefix — the trigram index is the one that finds the row, and the
`CASE` still scores it 30. Neither index is authoritative on its own, which is why both exist.

**Cost control.** GIN indexes are written lazily via `fastupdate` and read cheaply, which is
the right trade for four tables that are written far more often than they are searched. The
`documents.search_tsv` column is the only large one; a page past a few hundred kilobytes of
text should have its `plain_text` truncated for indexing purposes at a documented ceiling
(the same ceiling as `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE`, canon OQ-58) rather than growing the index without
bound.

---

### 27.6 Open questions

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-93) — is search paginated, and are document bodies indexed at all?**
> **Evidence** — the frontend caps at 5 per group with no "show more"
> (`src/config/app.ts:30`, `src/lib/search-index.ts:91-92`) and matches documents on `name`
> and `excerpt` only, never on full block content (`src/services/search-service.ts:146`).
> The `excerpt` is a 120-character summary (`src/services/document-service.ts:165`).
> **Recommendation** — index the full block text server-side into `documents.plain_text` and
> keep returning the top `limitPerGroup` per group **plus a per-group `total`**, with the
> `?kind=&offset=` drill-down above for "see all".
> **Impact if wrong** — search silently misses most document content, and the capped groups
> hide the fact: a user searching for a phrase from the middle of a page gets "Nothing
> matches" for text that is definitely there, which reads as the product being broken rather
> than as a limitation.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-94) — one search endpoint or two?**
> **Evidence** — the frontend has two surfaces with two shapes: `SearchHit`
> (`{ node, path, href }`, the drive quick-find, `src/lib/tree.ts:279-295`) and `SearchResult`
> (the ranked, grouped, cross-kind palette result).
> **Recommendation** — canon's position: **two endpoints.** E-035 stays a cheap
> name-only prefix match over `nodes` for the drive's own filter box, and E-133 is the
> full-text search. Collapsing them would make every keystroke in a folder filter run the
> eight-branch union.
> **Impact if wrong** — either the drive filter becomes slow enough to feel, or the palette
> stops finding comments and records.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-95) — do `QA-128` references in comment bodies resolve, and are board prefixes unique?**
> **Evidence** — `parseBody` emits a `{ kind: "record", displayId }` segment
> (`src/lib/mentions.ts:122`) and `CommentBody` renders it as a **styled chip with no link and
> no click handler** (`src/components/comments/comment-body.tsx:23-32`), while the composer's
> placeholder invites the syntax: *"Leave a comment… @ to mention, or reference records like
> QA-128"* (`src/components/comments/comment-panel.tsx:119`). `extractRowReferences`
> (`src/lib/row-id.ts:37-43`) is exported and unit-tested but called nowhere in `src/`. The
> prefix is per board (`prefixForBoard`, `src/services/board-service.ts:1417`) with nothing
> enforcing cross-board uniqueness.
> **Recommendation** — resolve references **server-side at read time, never at write time**:
> E-119 and E-125 return `references: { raw: string; ref: EntityRef | null }[]` alongside the
> body, resolved against the boards the **reading** user may see. Resolving at write time
> would bake in the author's access and turn the chip into a disclosure of a record the reader
> cannot open; `null` keeps today's plain-chip rendering as the correct fallback.
> Additionally enforce **workspace-unique `boards.row_id_prefix`** at board creation and on
> E-050 (canon OQ-43).
> **Impact if wrong** — resolving at write time leaks record titles across permission
> boundaries; leaving prefixes non-unique makes every cross-board reference ambiguous and the
> feature unshippable.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-92) — which timezone defines a date, for the search-adjacent surfaces?**
> **Evidence** — not a search question directly, but E-133's row branch shares
> `board_rows`' generated projections with My Work and the dashboard, and every date
> comparison there goes through `dayKey`, which slices the UTC ISO string
> (`src/lib/board-dates.ts:6-10`).
> **Recommendation** — canon's position: UTC day-keys everywhere, `due_date` stored as `DATE`
> so no conversion is possible (C-04). Search itself does no date arithmetic; this is recorded
> so no chapter adds a `?dueBefore=` filter with different semantics.
> **Impact if wrong** — a date filter on search would disagree with My Work and the dashboard
> for every user outside UTC.

---

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **§21 documents E-113, E-114 and E-116 in full.** They are `files`-module endpoints and
   may also appear in the files chapter. They are here because the brief for this section
   asks for "list" and "get a download/preview URL" as part of the attachment story, and an
   attachment chapter that stops at the upload is not usable on its own. If the files chapter
   documents them too, keep one copy and leave a cross-reference here — the two must not
   diverge on the extension-over-MIME rule or on the original-resolution rule.

2. **The `uploads` table (T-32) column set is reproduced in §21.** No existing part appears
   to own it, and every endpoint in that section reads or writes it, so the depth bar could
   not be met by reference alone. If a files chapter defines it, delete the inline table here
   and keep only the FK and index notes.

3. **`UploadPurpose` is a new enum this section names** (`drive` | `documentBlock` |
   `boardCell` | `comment`). It has no frontend counterpart — the mock has one upload path —
   and it exists to carry canon OQ-74's `createDriveNode` default and the per-surface
   permission check. Canon §2 counts 68 enums; if this one is adopted, it is the 69th and
   should be registered in §2.8 beside `UploadStatus`.

4. **Four additive fields on `Comment`** — `isResolved`, `resolvedAt`, `resolvedBy`,
   `isDeleted` — follow canon's OQ-80 position (`is_resolved`/`resolved_by`/`resolved_at` on
   the root, `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` for a tombstone) but are not in
   `src/types/collab.ts:39-58` today. They are marked RECOMMENDATION at their definition. The
   frontend ignores unknown fields, so shipping them is safe ahead of the UI.

5. **`SearchGroup.total` is additive** and is not in `src/types/collab.ts:176-180`. It is
   required for canon OQ-93's "see all" drill-down to be honest, and it mirrors what
   `MyWorkWidget.total` already does for the same reason ("12 of 40" stays honest,
   `src/types/collab.ts:143-144`).

6. **`?workspaceId=` on E-129, E-131 and E-132 is additive** and not in canon's §3.21
   signatures. `notifications.workspace_id` is `NOT NULL` and the frontend has exactly one
   active workspace at a time, so an unscoped bell mixes tenants. If the editor prefers to
   stay strictly on canon's signature, the parameter can be dropped and the scope taken from
   the session's active workspace instead — but it must be scoped somewhere.

7. **E-119 and E-125 gain `?includeDeleted=`.** Canon's signatures do not have it. It exists
   because canon OQ-80's tombstone rule needs a way to express "omit deleted comments with no
   replies" versus "show tombstones", and the default (`true`) reproduces the shape
   `buildThreads` expects. Drop it if the editor would rather hard-code the default.

8. **Canon E-028/E-029 return `204`, which is the one documented exception to C-10.** It is
   called out at the endpoint so no reviewer files it as a violation.

9. **The `reason` query parameter on E-129 is repeatable.** Canon writes `?reason=` without
   saying how the two-value `following` tab is expressed. If the editor prefers a
   comma-separated list, change it in one place — but repeated parameters avoid an escaping
   rule for a closed enum.

10. **§21 asserts that both `file.upload` and `comment.create` gate a comment attachment.**
    Canon E-110 says `file.upload`; the collaboration fact sheet argues `comment.create`
    (OQ-73). Requiring both narrows and never widens, and Member holds both, so nothing
    observable changes today. If canon is amended to pick one, this section follows it.

---

## 28. RBAC / Permissions

This is the chapter a security reviewer reads first, so it states its own thesis before anything
else: **the frontend enforces nothing.** Three separate files say so in their own words —
`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:22-26` (*"None of this is security. It decides what the UI offers;
the backend decides what actually happens, and must re-check every one of these keys"*),
`src/hooks/use-permissions.ts:31-34` (*"Hiding a button is a courtesy to the user; the backend still
has to refuse the call"*), and the permission dialog's own footer, rendered next to the control,
which tells the user: *"Preview only narrows what you see. The server re-checks every one of these
on its own."* (`src/components/permissions/permission-dialog.tsx:182-185`).

Everything below is therefore a transcription of a model the frontend already built and a
specification of the enforcement it deliberately does not have.

Requirement codes covered: `SY-RBC-42` (role-based access control), `SY-INH-43` (permission
inheritance), `SY-FAC` (folder/resource access), `SY-WSA` (workspace membership).

---

### 28.1 The model, in one sentence per axis

There are **two independent questions** and the system never merges them.

| Axis | Question | Frontend module | Answer is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ACCESS** | *May I see this resource at all?* | `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts` | a boolean, decided by walking the ancestor chain and reading each node's `accessMode` |
| **CAPABILITY** | *Given that I can see it, what may I do to it?* | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts` | a boolean per `PermissionKey`, decided by the role matrix + ownership, then narrowed by lifecycle state |

`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:15-33` is the design statement, and it is worth quoting in full
because it is the property the whole chapter exists to preserve:

> This is a different question from the one `evaluate.ts` answers. That one decides what somebody
> may **do** once they are looking at something; this one decides whether they get to look. Keeping
> them apart is the whole point:
>
>   - a Viewer who is granted a restricted folder **sees it** and edits nothing,
>   - a Manager who is not granted it **does not see it**, whatever their role.
>
> Merging the two would make "high enough role" a way into a folder somebody deliberately shut,
> which is exactly the property a restricted folder exists to have.

**Say this unmistakably, because it is the rule most likely to be implemented wrong:**

> **A manager who is not granted a RESTRICTED folder does not see it. Not greyed out, not
> read-only, not "visible but locked" — absent.** It is missing from the drive tree, missing from
> search results, missing from the relation picker, missing from favourites, missing from Recent,
> and a direct URL to it or to anything inside it answers exactly as a URL to a node that never
> existed. Their role is irrelevant. An **Admin** is in the same position: the one and only surface
> that looks past this is the recovery console in §28.12.3, which shows names and paths and no
> content.

`tests/folder-access.test.ts:176-195` asserts each of those five surfaces; `:395-408` asserts that
a Recent entry pointing at a now-hidden node is dropped **name and all**, because the denormalised
label is the leak.

The mirror-image property is asserted just as hard. `tests/permissions.test.ts:66-78` and
`tests/rbac.test.ts:137-147` both show `can()` returning **`true`** on a restricted node for a role
that could never reach it:

```ts
// tests/rbac.test.ts:137-147 — this is not a bug.
expect(can("board.export", { role: "admin", user: CURRENT_USER, node: restricted })).toBe(true);
expect(can("row.update",   { role: "member", user: memberAt(3), node: restricted })).toBe(true);
```

The capability evaluator is only ever called with a node the access walk already admitted. **A
backend that runs the capability check alone leaks every restricted folder to anybody who can guess
a node id.** Both gates, every request, in the order given in §28.8.

---

### 28.2 The four roles

#### 28.2.1 EXISTING REQUIREMENT — the ladder

```ts
// src/types/permission.ts:8-20
export type WorkspaceRole = "viewer" | "member" | "manager" | "admin";

export const WORKSPACE_ROLES: readonly WorkspaceRole[] = [
  "viewer", "member", "manager", "admin",
] as const;

/** Rank, used to compare two grants — never to derive what a role may do. */
export function roleRank(role: WorkspaceRole): number {
  return WORKSPACE_ROLES.indexOf(role);   // viewer=0, member=1, manager=2, admin=3
}
```

**Order is rank.** `roleRank` is `indexOf`, so declaring the Postgres enum in the same order makes
rank reproducible in SQL:

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TYPE workspace_role AS ENUM ('viewer', 'member', 'manager', 'admin');
-- rank(role)  ==  array_position(enum_range(NULL::workspace_role), role) - 1
-- role >= 'member'::workspace_role  is a valid rank comparison
```

`roleRank` is used for **comparison only** — clamping a role preview (`src/hooks/use-permissions.ts:54-57`),
sorting the access list (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:166`) and the owner-escalation floor
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:73-74`). It is **never** used to decide whether a role holds a
key; that is always a set lookup (`roleHas`, `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:125-127`).

**Four roles, not five.** The PRD names a "Super Admin" in two places — `WS-ARC-02` (*"Super Admin
khởi tạo Workspace"*) and `SY-AUD-41`'s edge case (*"Chỉ có role Super Admin mới có quyền truy cập
và xuất file Audit Log"*) — but its own `SY-RBC-42` matrix declares exactly four, and the frontend
has four. **Canon OQ-03 has decided: four roles; the workspace creator is an ownership attribute,
not a fifth role.** Do not add one. Read the PRD's "Super Admin" as "Admin", which is what holds
`workspace.audit.view` and `workspace.delete`.

There are **no custom roles** and no role editor: `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:315-317` — *"Four roles, as
specified."* This is why `workspace_role` is an enum and not a table (canon §1.2).

#### 28.2.2 EXISTING REQUIREMENT — the sets accumulate; they are not declared independently

`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:84-96` builds each role as *the role below it plus what it adds*,
carrying a single `Set` forward through `WORKSPACE_ROLES` in ladder order:

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:84-96
function accumulate(): Readonly<Record<WorkspaceRole, PermissionSet>> {
  const result: Partial<Record<WorkspaceRole, PermissionSet>> = {};
  const carried = new Set<PermissionKey>();

  for (const role of WORKSPACE_ROLES) {
    for (const key of ADDITIONS[role]) carried.add(key);
    result[role] = new Set(carried);
  }

  return result as Record<WorkspaceRole, PermissionSet>;
}
```

The invariant this produces, and which the backend must preserve: **every permission held by a
lower role is held by every higher role.** `tests/rbac.test.ts:68-77` asserts it for all 39 keys ×
all 4 roles:

```ts
for (const key of ROLE_PERMISSIONS[lower]) {
  expect(roleHas(higher, key), `${higher} must hold ${key} because ${lower} does`).toBe(true);
}
```

**RECOMMENDATION for the backend.** Store the **additions** (four literal arrays) and accumulate at
boot, exactly as the frontend does — or, if the accumulated sets are stored, assert containment on
every deploy. Four independently-maintained permission lists will drift the first time a key is
added, and the drift is silent: a Member holding something a Manager does not.

#### 28.2.3 The four addition sets, transcribed verbatim

**VIEWER — 0 keys.**

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:11-16
/**
 * Viewer holds no action keys at all. "Read only" is exactly that: being able
 * to see a node is decided by access resolution, not by an action — so the
 * viewer column of the matrix is empty by construction rather than by omission.
 */
const VIEWER: readonly PermissionKey[] = [];
```

`tests/rbac.test.ts:79-81` asserts `ROLE_PERMISSIONS.viewer.size === 0`. A Viewer who can see a node
can read it and **cannot export it** — export starts at Member.

**MEMBER — adds 10, total 10.**

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:22-35
const MEMBER: readonly PermissionKey[] = [
  "row.create", "row.update", "row.move",
  "comment.create", "comment.resolve", "comment.delete",
  "file.upload", "file.update",
  "node.share",
  // Taking data out of the product is a step past reading it, so it starts
  // here rather than at Viewer.
  "board.export",
];
```

**MANAGER — adds 21, total 31.**

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:38-63
const MANAGER: readonly PermissionKey[] = [
  "node.create", "node.rename", "node.move", "node.delete", "node.archive",
  // Restricting a folder is structural, not administrative: a project lead
  // shuts their own folder without waiting on a workspace admin. It only ever
  // applies to a folder they can already see, so it hands out nothing.
  "node.access.manage",
  "board.create", "board.manage",
  "board.column.create", "board.column.update", "board.column.delete",
  "board.view.manage", "board.template.manage", "board.import",
  "row.archive", "row.delete",
  "document.create", "document.update", "document.lock", "document.version.restore",
  "file.delete",
];
```

**ADMIN — adds 8, total 39 (the whole catalogue).**

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:66-75
const ADMIN: readonly PermissionKey[] = [
  "workspace.manage", "workspace.settings.view", "workspace.member.manage",
  "workspace.permission.manage", "workspace.audit.view", "workspace.delete",
  "secret.reveal", "secret.rotate",
];
```

`tests/rbac.test.ts:106-117` asserts `minimumRoleFor` is `"admin"` for `workspace.manage`,
`workspace.member.manage`, `workspace.permission.manage`, `workspace.audit.view`, `secret.reveal`
and `secret.rotate`.

Two rows in that table are deliberate product decisions, not accidents, and a reviewer will ask
about both:

- **`board.export` is a Member key, not a Viewer key.** *"A viewer can read a board in the product;
  taking the data out is a step past reading. Reasonable products disagree, and it is one line in
  the matrix"* (`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:350-354`; `src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:32-34`).
- **`node.access.manage` is a Manager key, not an Admin key.** *"Restricting a folder is structural,
  not administrative: a project lead shuts their own folder without waiting on a workspace admin. It
  only ever applies to a folder they can already see, so it hands out nothing"*
  (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:44-47`). Note the safety property in that last clause: because gate
  2 runs first, a Manager can only restrict a folder they can already reach, so the key can never be
  used to acquire access.

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:110-122
ROLE_LABELS = { viewer: "Viewer", member: "Member", manager: "Manager", admin: "Admin" };

ROLE_SUMMARIES = {
  viewer:  "Reads everything they are given access to. Changes nothing.",
  member:  "Works inside boards: cells, records, comments, uploads.",
  manager: "Everything a member does, plus the structure it lives in.",
  admin:   "The workspace itself — people, access, audit and secrets.",
};
```

These strings are rendered verbatim in the role picker, the matrix header tooltips and every
`Needs the {Role} role or above` refusal. Do not paraphrase them server-side.

### 28.3 The permission catalogue — 39 keys and what each one guards

#### 28.3.1 The module is derived from the key, never declared beside it

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:65-68
/** First segment of the key — `board.column.create` lives under `board`. */
export function moduleOf(key: PermissionKey): PermissionModule {
  return key.slice(0, key.indexOf(".")) as PermissionModule;
}
```

*"A key can therefore never be filed under a module it does not belong to"*
(`src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:8-14`). `tests/rbac.test.ts:48-53` asserts
`definition.key.startsWith(definition.module + ".")` for all 39. **The backend must derive it the
same way and must not store a module column beside a key.**

| Module | Display label | Keys |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `workspace` | Workspace | 6 |
| `node` | Drive | 7 |
| `board` | Boards | 9 |
| `row` | Records | 5 |
| `document` | Documents | 4 |
| `file` | Files | 3 |
| `comment` | Comments | 3 |
| `secret` | Secrets | 2 |
| | | **39** |

Labels from `src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:79-88`. Module order from `PERMISSION_MODULES`
(`:90-99`) — it is the order the matrix renders in, so serve the catalogue in it.

#### 28.3.2 The contract

```ts
// src/types/permission.ts:101-107 — EXISTING, do not re-scope (canon §5.2)
export interface PermissionDefinition {
  readonly key: PermissionKey;
  readonly module: PermissionModule;
  /** Imperative label for the matrix row: "Create columns". */
  readonly label: string;
  readonly summary: string;
}

export type PermissionSet = ReadonlySet<PermissionKey>;
/** Answers one question about one subject. Handed to components as `can`. */
export type PermissionResolver = (key: PermissionKey) => boolean;
```

#### 28.3.3 The catalogue, key by key

`Label` and `Summary` are transcribed verbatim from `src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:16-63` — they
are user-visible copy. `Class` is the classification from §28.3.4. "Guards" names the real
enforcement point where one exists.

**Module `workspace` — "Workspace" (6 keys, all Admin)**

| Key | Label | Summary | Class | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.manage` | Manage workspace | Rename the workspace, change its plan and settings | write | E-010 `PATCH /workspaces/{id}`. Gates the editable General tab (`src/components/workspace/workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:31`, `workspace-general-tab.tsx`). |
| `workspace.settings.view` | Open workspace settings | See the workspace settings screen at all | write¹ | Gates the General tab's existence (`workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:31`). |
| `workspace.member.manage` | Manage members | Invite people and change what role they hold | write | E-013/E-014/E-015. Gates the Members tab and the Invite button (`workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:32`, `workspace-members-tab.tsx:73`). |
| `workspace.permission.manage` | Manage access | Write and remove access rules on any node | write | E-042/E-043 (as the admin-wide alternative to `node.access.manage`), E-046. Gates the Access tab (`workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:33`), the access-list editor (`permission-dialog.tsx:97`) and the recovery console (`workspace-restricted-tab.tsx`). |
| `workspace.audit.view` | Read the audit log | Open the workspace audit trail | **read-only** | E-136, E-137. `src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:37`; the denied panel at `src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:31-41`. |
| `workspace.delete` | Delete the workspace | Destroy the workspace and everything in it | write | E-011. Gates the Danger zone tab (`workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:34`). |

¹ `workspace.settings.view` is a *read* by name but is **not** in `READ_ONLY_KEYS`, so it is
classified `write` by `isWrite` (`evaluate.ts:67`) and is narrowed by trash/freeze/lock like any
other write. That is the literal behaviour of the shipped code; it is harmless because the key is
only ever evaluated at workspace scope where `node` is `null` and no narrowing layer applies.

**Module `node` — "Drive" (7 keys)**

| `node.access.manage` | Manage folder access | Restrict a folder, and choose who may see it | write | E-040 – E-043. `useNodeAccess` accepts **either** this **or** `workspace.permission.manage` (`src/hooks/use-node-access.ts:80`). |

| Key | Label | Summary | Class | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row.create` | Add records | Create a record on a board | **content write** | E-062, E-064, and the target half of E-077. |
| `row.update` | Edit cells | Change the value in a record's cell | **content write** | E-066, E-074. Also the `edit` capability for a **board** node (`evaluate.ts:112`). |
| `row.move` | Move records | Drag a record between Kanban columns and dates | **content write** | E-067, E-073. |
| `row.archive` | Archive records | Freeze records out of every view | write | E-075. |
| `row.delete` | Delete records | Remove records from a board | **content write** | E-065, E-076, and the **source** half of E-077 — *"Bulk 'Move to board' is gated on `row.delete`, because it removes records from the source board. It is the destructive half that decides"* (`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:350-351`). |

**Module `document` — "Documents" (4 keys)**

| Key | Label | Summary | Class | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document.create` | Create pages | Add a page, config or secret document | write | E-024 with `kind: "document"`. |
| `document.update` | Edit pages | Write in a page and change its blocks | **content write** | E-092, E-093, E-100. Enforced at `src/services/devtools-service.ts:148` for config documents. |
| `document.lock` | Lock pages | Take a page out of edit mode for everyone | write · **owner-escalated** | E-094. **Deliberately not a content write**, so the person who locked a page can unlock it (`evaluate.ts:84`; `tests/permissions.test.ts:117-125`). |
| `document.version.restore` | Restore versions | Write an earlier version back over a page | **content write** | E-097. |

**Module `file` — "Files" (3 keys)**

| Key | Label | Summary | Class | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file.upload` | Upload files | Add files to a folder or a record | **content write** | E-110, E-111. Projected as `capabilities.upload`. |
| `file.update` | Edit files | Change the contents of a text or sheet file | **content write** | E-115. The `edit` capability for a **file** node (`evaluate.ts:111`). |
| `file.delete` | Delete files | Send a file to Trash | write · **owner-escalated** | E-032 on a file node. |

**Module `comment` — "Comments" (3 keys, all Member)**

| Key | Label | Summary | Class | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `comment.create` | Comment | Post comments and replies, and mention people | write | E-120. |
| `comment.resolve` | Resolve threads | Close a comment thread | write | E-123, E-124. |
| `comment.delete` | Delete comments | Remove a comment from a thread | write | E-122. **Scoped by ownership server-side** — canon OQ-24: own comment at `member`, anyone else's at `manager`. |

**Module `secret` — "Secrets" (2 keys, both Admin)**

| Key | Label | Summary | Class | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secret.reveal` | Reveal secrets | Read a secret value in plaintext, once, audited | **read-only** | E-103, E-104, E-105. `copy` has **no key of its own** — it is gated by `secret.reveal` and audited as a reveal (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`). Classified read-only so a **frozen** node still allows it. Enforced by the two-part check at `devtools-service.ts:302-317`. |
| `secret.rotate` | Rotate secrets | Replace a secret value with a new one | write | E-102. Enforced at `devtools-service.ts:493`. |

**Documentation drift, decided.** `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:52` claims *"36 keys"* and its listing omits
`workspace.settings.view`, `workspace.delete` and `node.access.manage`. `src/types/permission.ts:31-78`
contains all 39 and `tests/rbac.test.ts:37-46` asserts the catalogue length against it.
**Build against the 39 in the code.** The doc is stale.

#### 28.3.4 The two classification sets — the only thing that decides how a key is narrowed

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:28-49
/** Keys that read rather than write. A frozen or locked node still allows them. */
const READ_ONLY_KEYS: ReadonlySet<PermissionKey> = new Set([
  "board.export",
  "workspace.audit.view",
  "secret.reveal",
]);

/** Writes that put *content* into a node, which is what a lock stops. */
const CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS: ReadonlySet<PermissionKey> = new Set([
  "row.create", "row.update", "row.move", "row.delete",
  "document.update", "document.version.restore",
  "file.update", "file.upload",
  "board.import",
  "board.column.create", "board.column.update", "board.column.delete",
]);

const isWrite = (key: PermissionKey): boolean => !READ_ONLY_KEYS.has(key);
```

Three keys are read-only; twelve are content writes; the other twenty-four are ordinary writes.

- **Everything not in `READ_ONLY_KEYS` is a write** and is refused by a trashed node, an archived
  ancestor, or (if it is also a content write) a lock.
- **Everything not in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS` is unaffected by a lock** — including `document.lock`
  itself, which is what lets the locker unlock.
- The three read-only keys pass through **all** narrowing layers. `board.export` on an archived
  board is the case this exists for: *"reads stay open — export above all"*
  (`docs/SYSTEM.md:178-180`, `tests/permissions.test.ts:108-115`).

**RECOMMENDATION.** Ship these two sets as service constants next to the catalogue, and expose the
classification on E-045's payload only if canon's `PermissionDefinition` is ever widened (§28.12.2
and the editor note). Do not re-derive them from key names — `secret.reveal` reads and
`secret.rotate` writes, and no naming convention separates them.

### 28.4 The CAPABILITY algorithm, verbatim

```ts
// src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:51-87
export interface PermissionContext {
  /** Effective role on this node, already resolved through inheritance. */
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly user: UserSummary;
  /** Node being acted on; omit for workspace-level checks. */
  readonly node?: DriveNode | null;
  /**
   * An archived *ancestor* holds this node frozen. The node's own archive flag
   * is deliberately not read here: a surface must keep offering Restore on the
   * thing you are standing on.
   */
  readonly isFrozen?: boolean;
  /** Document lock — stops content writes, never the unlock itself. */
  readonly isLocked?: boolean;
}

export function can(key: PermissionKey, context: PermissionContext): boolean {
  const { role, user, node, isFrozen = false, isLocked = false } = context;

  const owns = Boolean(node) && node?.owner.id === user.id;
  const isEscalated =
    owns && OWNER_ESCALATIONS.has(key) && roleRank(role) >= roleRank("member");

  if (!roleHas(role, key) && !isEscalated) return false;     // (1) matrix + ownership
  if (!isWrite(key)) return true;                            // (2) reads stop here

  // (3) A trashed node accepts nothing but the calls that get it out of the
  //     bin again, or end it for good.
  if (node?.isTrashed) return key === "node.delete";

  if (isFrozen) return false;                                // (4) archived ancestor
  if (isLocked && CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS.has(key)) return false;  // (5) document lock

  return true;
}
```

Five steps, and **steps 2–5 can only subtract**. `tests/rbac.test.ts:149-159` runs all 39 keys × all
4 roles and asserts that no narrowing layer ever returns `true` where the open answer was `false`:

```ts
expect(can(key, { ...base, role, isFrozen: true })  && !open, key).toBe(false);
expect(can(key, { ...base, role, isLocked: true }) && !open, key).toBe(false);
```

**The backend must preserve monotonicity.** A layer that can hand a permission back is a bug that
will be found by a fuzzer before it is found by a reviewer.

Three details worth stating on their own:

1. **`isFrozen` counts ancestors only.** The node's own `isArchived` is deliberately not read here,
   so a board archived in its own right keeps `node.archive` and can therefore be restored
   (`evaluate.ts:57-61`; `tests/rbac.test.ts:170-182`). The server resolves it as
   `inheritedArchiveOf(nodeId) !== null` — the archived ancestor **strictly above** the node
   (`src/lib/archive.ts:36-43`, `src/services/authz.ts:51`).
2. **A trashed node accepts exactly one key.** `if (node?.isTrashed) return key === "node.delete"`.
   `tests/rbac.test.ts:161-168` and `tests/permissions.test.ts:80-88` assert that even an **Admin**
   on a trashed node gets `node.delete` and nothing else — no rename, no upload, no share. Note the
   overload: `node.delete` is the key for moving to trash **and** for restoring **and** for purging;
   there is no `node.restore` and no `node.purge` in the catalogue.
3. **A lock refuses only content writes.** `tests/permissions.test.ts:117-125`:
   `document.update` false, `document.lock` true, `node.share` true.
