## 29. Audit Logs

`SY-AUD-41`. The workspace security trail: who did what, from where, to what, and whether it was
allowed. It is **evidence**, not a feed — timestamps are absolute, targets are human labels, details
are sentences, and the table cannot be edited or deleted.

---

### 29.1 Append-only by construction, not by discipline

`src/types/audit.ts:4-10` and `src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20` say the same thing twice:

> The record is append-only by construction: the service exposes `record` and `list`, and nothing
> else. There is no update path and no delete path, so no surface can offer one.

```ts
// src/services/audit-service.ts:335
export const auditService = { record, list, reset };   // reset is the test seam only
```

`tests/audit.test.ts:88-92` asserts the **shape of the object itself** —
`expect(Object.keys(auditService).sort()).toEqual(["list", "record", "reset"])` — because *"a
missing capability is the only kind of guarantee a UI cannot undo"*. `:94-107` asserts that a
returned page is a copy, so mutating it changes nothing in the store. The page states the promise
where somebody would look for the button: *"Append-only · entries cannot be edited or deleted"*
(`src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:58-62`), and the table has six columns and no seventh —
*"there is no actions column, because a record of what happened that someone can tidy up is not a
record"* (`src/components/audit/audit-table.tsx:22-27`).

**Three consequences that are all normative:**

1. **There is no write endpoint for the audit log, and no chapter may add one** (canon §3.23). Rows
   are written by the endpoint performing the action, inside its transaction. `POST /audit`,
   `PATCH /audit/{id}` and `DELETE /audit/{id}` do not exist.
2. **Enforce it in the database, not the service layer.** A promise the database does not enforce is
   a comment:

```sql
-- documentation only
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_events FROM app_user;
GRANT  INSERT, SELECT  ON audit_events TO   app_user;

-- Plus a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that RAISEs, so a future migration
-- cannot quietly re-grant it:
CREATE FUNCTION audit_events_immutable() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'audit_events is append-only (SY-AUD-41)';
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

CREATE TRIGGER audit_events_no_update_delete
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON audit_events
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_events_immutable();
```

3. **The retention sweep runs as a different, privileged role** that the application user cannot
   assume, and is itself audited (§29.10).

---

### 29.2 The record shape

```ts
// src/types/audit.ts:12-40 — EXISTING, returned verbatim on the wire
export type AuditSeverity = "info" | "warn" | "error";

/** Everything the RBAC catalogue governs, plus `system` for events no user initiated. */
export type AuditModule = PermissionModule | "system";
//  = "workspace" | "node" | "board" | "row" | "document" | "file" | "comment" | "secret" | "system"

export type AuditOutcome = "allowed" | "denied";

export interface AuditEvent {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly at: string;                 // ISO 8601, absolute
  readonly module: AuditModule;
  /**
   * What happened, as a catalogue key where one exists (`secret.reveal`) so a
   * row can be traced back to the permission that governs it.
   */
  readonly action: string;
  readonly actor: UserSummary;
  /** Address the call came from. Recorded by the backend, never derived here. */
  readonly ip: string;
  readonly severity: AuditSeverity;
  /** Human label of the thing acted on — never an id, never a payload. */
  readonly target: string | null;
  /** One sentence. The UI never renders a raw audit payload (SY-ACT-40). */
  readonly detail: string | null;
  readonly outcome: AuditOutcome;
}
```

Field by field, with the rule attached to each:

| Field | Wire type | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` (UUID) | Opaque, server-minted. Never guessable, never sequential. | `audit-service.ts:290` |
| `at` | ISO 8601 | **Absolute, never relative** — *"an audit row is evidence"*. Rendered `26 Aug 2026 · 16:20`. | `src/lib/audit.ts:51-54`; `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:217` |
| `module` | `AuditModule` | One of the 8 permission modules, or `system`. For a catalogue action it **must equal `moduleOf(action)`** — the two vocabularies are the same vocabulary. | `src/types/audit.ts:14-18`; `src/lib/audit.ts:13-28` |
| `action` | `string` | **A free-form dotted string, constrained by convention to be a `PermissionKey` wherever one governs the event.** Anything else is humanised by taking the tail after the first dot: `system.retention.sweep` → *"Retention sweep"*. | `src/lib/audit.ts:38-49`; `tests/audit.test.ts:186-190` |
| `actor` | `UserSummary` | `{ id, name, email, initials, avatarUrl?, accentColor? }`. **From the session, never the body.** | `src/types/audit.ts:31`; canon C-09 |
| `ip` | `string` | **Stamped off the socket. The client never sends one** — which is why it is set in the service and in no hook. | `audit-service.ts:276-285`; `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:223-224` |
| `severity` | `AuditSeverity` | `info` / `warn` / `error`. **Independent of `outcome`** — §29.7. Defaults to `error` when `outcome === "denied"`, `info` otherwise. | `audit-service.ts:296`; `tests/audit.test.ts:119-130` |
| `target` | `string \| null` | The **human label** of the thing acted on. *Never an id, never a payload.* `null` for an event with no subject (a session start). | `src/types/audit.ts:35-36` |
| `detail` | `string \| null` | **One sentence, written server-side.** Never serialised JSON. | `src/types/audit.ts:37-38`; `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:228-229` |
| `outcome` | `AuditOutcome` | `allowed` / `denied`. Defaults to `allowed`. | `audit-service.ts:299` |

The append itself, which the backend reproduces including its two defaults:

```ts
// src/services/audit-service.ts:287-304
/** Append one event. Nothing in this module can change or remove it again. */
function record(input: AuditInput): AuditEvent {
  const event: AuditEvent = {
    id: nextId("aud"),
    at: nowIso(),
    module: input.module,
    action: input.action,
    actor: input.actor,
    ip: input.ip ?? LOCAL_IP,
    severity: input.severity ?? (input.outcome === "denied" ? "error" : "info"),
    target: input.target ?? null,
    detail: input.detail ?? null,
    outcome: input.outcome ?? "allowed",
  };

  events = [event, ...events];        // newest first; the log only grows at the head
  return event;
}
```

`tests/audit.test.ts:111-117` asserts newest-first ordering; `:119-130` asserts the severity
defaulting.

**The `target` is a label and stays a label.** The reason is a security property, not a stylistic
one: the audit page is read by an admin who may not have access to the resource the row describes,
and a resolvable id would be a lookup key. A name is a fact about what happened; an id is a handle
onto something that still exists. The ids live in `context` (§29.4), which no endpoint returns.

---

### 29.3 The table

Owned by §4 (part-05); the columns and indexes that matter to this chapter, restated:

```sql
-- documentation only
CREATE TYPE audit_severity AS ENUM ('info', 'warn', 'error');
CREATE TYPE audit_outcome  AS ENUM ('allowed', 'denied');
CREATE TYPE audit_module   AS ENUM (
  'workspace', 'node', 'board', 'row', 'document', 'file', 'comment', 'secret', 'system'
);

CREATE TABLE audit_events (
  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  workspace_id UUID           NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  at           TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  module       audit_module   NOT NULL,
  action       TEXT           NOT NULL,     -- dotted key; a PermissionKey where one governs
  actor_id     UUID           NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  actor_name   TEXT           NOT NULL,     -- denormalised: the row must still read
  actor_email  TEXT           NOT NULL,
  ip           INET           NOT NULL,
  severity     audit_severity NOT NULL,
  target       TEXT,                        -- human label only
  detail       TEXT,                        -- one sentence, server-written
  outcome      audit_outcome  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'allowed',
  context      JSONB,                       -- §29.4. NEVER returned by any endpoint.

  CHECK (length(action) > 0 AND action LIKE '%.%'),
  CHECK (length(actor_name) > 0),
  CHECK (context IS NULL OR jsonb_typeof(context) = 'object')
);

CREATE INDEX audit_events_page_idx     ON audit_events (workspace_id, at DESC, id DESC);
CREATE INDEX audit_events_module_idx   ON audit_events (workspace_id, module,   at DESC, id DESC);
CREATE INDEX audit_events_actor_idx    ON audit_events (workspace_id, actor_id, at DESC, id DESC);
CREATE INDEX audit_events_severity_idx ON audit_events (workspace_id, severity, at DESC, id DESC);
CREATE INDEX audit_events_search_idx   ON audit_events USING GIN (
  to_tsvector('simple',
    coalesce(target,'') || ' ' || coalesce(detail,'') || ' ' ||
    action || ' ' || actor_name || ' ' || host(ip)));
CREATE INDEX audit_events_retention_idx ON audit_events (workspace_id, at)
       WHERE severity <> 'error' AND outcome = 'allowed';
```

The five facts a reviewer will check:

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| FKs | `workspace_id → workspaces` **CASCADE** (the trail is the tenant's). `actor_id → users` **RESTRICT** — the trail must never lose its actor; `actor_name`/`actor_email` are the second line of defence. |
| FKs to the **subjects** | **None**, deliberately — and it is the opposite of every other table in the schema. An audit row must survive the deletion of what it describes: *"Moved to Trash with 2 items under it"* is exactly the row you need after the purge. That is why `target` is a denormalised label and the ids live in `context` with no referential integrity. |
| Unique constraints | **None.** Two identical actions a second apart are two events. |
| Delete behaviour | Nothing deletes a row except the retention sweep, running as a privileged role the app cannot assume. |
| `severity` vs `outcome` | **No check ties them.** The seed proves independence: `file.upload` at `severity: 'error'`, `outcome: 'allowed'` — an allowed action that failed technically (`audit-service.ts:107-115`). |

`host(ip)` is in the search index because `matchesSearch` spans the IP column
(`src/lib/audit.ts:67-79`) and `tests/audit.test.ts:152-158` asserts a **partial** IP hit
(`"10.4.31"`). A `to_tsvector` over `host(ip)` will not serve a partial-octet prefix; see §29.11 for
how the search is actually executed.

---

### 29.4 `audit_events.context` — the JSONB structure

**RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-25).** The frontend never renders it; it exists so an investigation can
reach the ids the human sentence deliberately omits. Discriminated on `kind`, no `any` (canon C-05,
C-06):

```ts
import type { PermissionKey, WorkspaceRole } from "./permission";

/** audit_events.context. Never rendered, never returned by any endpoint. */
export type AuditContext =
  | { readonly kind: "node";
      readonly nodeId: string;
      /** Root → node at the time of the action. Survives the tree changing. */
      readonly ancestorIds: readonly string[] }
  | { readonly kind: "access_rule";
      readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly subject:
        | { readonly kind: "user"; readonly userId: string }
        | { readonly kind: "role"; readonly role: WorkspaceRole };
      readonly roleBefore: WorkspaceRole | null;
      readonly roleAfter:  WorkspaceRole | null }
  | { readonly kind: "access_mode";
      readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly modeBefore: NodeAccessMode;
      readonly modeAfter:  NodeAccessMode;
      /** Ids only — who lost and gained sight of it. Never names. */
      readonly losing:  readonly string[];
      readonly gaining: readonly string[] }
  | { readonly kind: "membership";
      readonly targetUserId: string;
      readonly roleBefore: WorkspaceRole | null;
      readonly roleAfter:  WorkspaceRole | null }
  | { readonly kind: "secret";
      readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly secretId: string;
      /** Key name only. The value never enters the audit trail. */
      readonly secretKey: string }
  | { readonly kind: "bulk";
      readonly boardId: string;
      readonly requested: number;
      readonly applied: number;
      readonly skipped: number }
  | { readonly kind: "export";
      readonly boardId: string | null;
      readonly scope: "board" | "view" | "selection";
      readonly format: "xlsx" | "csv" | "pdf";
      readonly rowCount: number;
      readonly omittedColumnIds: readonly string[] }
  | { readonly kind: "version";
      readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly versionId: string;
      readonly versionNumber: number }
  | { readonly kind: "comment";
      readonly commentId: string;
      readonly targetNodeId: string;
      readonly wasAuthor: boolean }
  | { readonly kind: "denial";
      readonly permissionKey: PermissionKey;
      /** Which gate refused. NEVER returned to the caller. */
      readonly gate: "membership" | "visibility" | "capability" | "trashed" | "frozen" | "locked";
      /** The role the client declared, when it declared one (§28.11). */
      readonly declaredRole: WorkspaceRole | null;
      readonly resolvedRole: WorkspaceRole | null }
  | { readonly kind: "system"; readonly job: string };
```

**The invariant the frontend forces on this column, and the single most important line in this
section:**

> **No secret value, no cell value, no block content, no file bytes and no plaintext of any kind may
> ever be written into `detail` or `context`.**

`src/types/audit.ts:35-38` — `target` is a label, `detail` is a sentence. `auditDetail`
(`src/services/devtools-service.ts:567-571`) is the model: *"What the trail says happened. Never the
value — that is the whole point."*

```ts
// src/services/devtools-service.ts:567-571
function auditDetail(action: SecretAction): string {
  if (action === "rotate") return "Stored value replaced. The value itself is not recorded.";
  if (action === "copy")   return "Value placed on the clipboard once. Not stored by the client.";
  return "Value returned once and cleared from the client on a timer.";
}
```

**`context` is never returned.** Not by E-136, not by E-137, not by any read. It is reached by a
direct database query during an investigation, by someone whose access to the database is itself
controlled. Adding it to a response would turn the audit page into an id-enumeration surface for
resources the reader may not be able to see.

---

### 29.5 Every audited action

#### 29.5.1 The two categories of evidence in the frontend

**Wired emitters — the only two that actually call `record`:**

| Emitter | `module` | `action` | `severity` | `outcome` | `target` | `detail` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `setAccessRule` (`src/store/permission-store.ts:71-78`) | `workspace` | `workspace.permission.manage` | `warn` | `allowed` | node name | *"{subject} set to {Role} on this item."* |
| `clearAccessRule` (`src/store/permission-store.ts:99-106`) | `workspace` | `workspace.permission.manage` | `warn` | `allowed` | node name | *"{subject} now inherits access instead of holding it here."* |
| `pushAudit` on reveal / copy (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:382-395`) | `secret` | `secret.reveal` | `warn` / `error` | `allowed` / `denied` | secret **key** | reveal detail, or *"Refused: the role does not hold the permission for this action."* |
| `pushAudit` on rotate (same function, `action === "rotate"`) | `secret` | `secret.rotate` | `warn` / `error` | `allowed` / `denied` | secret **key** | *"Stored value replaced. The value itself is not recorded."* |

`subjectLabel` (`permission-store.ts:42-45`) renders a role subject as *"everyone with the {Role}
role"* and a user subject as their directory name. **A clear that matched nothing writes no row** —
`clearAccessRule` returns the state unchanged (`:97`) and `tests/audit.test.ts:275-284` asserts the
total does not move. Reproduce that: a no-op is not an event.

`devtools-service.ts:384-386` files a **copy** under `secret.reveal`, *"because copying is a read of
plaintext; only a write to the stored value is a rotation."*

**Seeded vocabulary — the 19 `(module, action)` pairs the UI is built to render**
(`src/services/audit-service.ts:44-248`). This is the set the backend must be able to produce:

| # | `module` | `action` | Severities seen | Outcomes seen | Example `detail` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `secret` | `secret.reveal` | `warn`, `error` | allowed, denied | *"Revealed once and cleared after 30 seconds."* / *"Refused: the Viewer role does not hold Reveal secrets."* |
| 2 | `secret` | `secret.rotate` | `warn` | allowed | *"Rotated. The previous value is no longer readable."* |
| 3 | `workspace` | `workspace.permission.manage` | `warn` | allowed | *"Duc Pham set to Member on this folder, overriding Manager."* |
| 4 | `workspace` | `workspace.member.manage` | `warn` | allowed | *"Role changed from Member to Viewer."* (target = **the person**) |
| 5 | `workspace` | `workspace.audit.view` | `error` | denied | *"Refused: the Viewer role does not hold Read the audit log."* |
| 6 | `node` | `node.archive` | `info` | allowed | *"Archived out of the active workspace."* |
| 7 | `node` | `node.delete` | `warn` | allowed | *"Moved to Trash with 2 items under it."* |
| 8 | `node` | `node.share` | `info` | allowed | *"Link created for the workspace, view only."* |
| 9 | `board` | `board.import` | `info` | allowed | *"48 records imported from sprint-backlog.xlsx, 3 rows left out."* |
| 10 | `board` | `board.export` | `info` | allowed | *"31 records exported to XLSX. 1 sensitive column omitted."* |
| 11 | `board` | `board.column.delete` | `warn` | allowed | *"Column "Story points" removed with its values."* |
| 12 | `row` | `row.delete` | `warn` | allowed | *"12 records deleted in one action."* |
| 13 | `row` | `row.update` | `info` | allowed | *"Status moved to In review."* (target = `TASK-118`) |
| 14 | `document` | `document.lock` | `info` | allowed | *"Locked for editing while the release is cut."* |
| 15 | `document` | `document.update` | `error` | denied | *"Refused: the page is locked."* |
| 16 | `file` | `file.upload` | `error` | **allowed** | *"Upload failed after 3 attempts: the connection dropped."* |
| 17 | `comment` | `comment.delete` | `info` | allowed | *"Removed a reply on a resolved thread."* |
| 18 | `system` | `system.retention.sweep` | `info` | allowed | *"4 items past the 30-day window were purged."* (target `"Trash"`, ip `127.0.0.1`) |
| 19 | `system` | `system.session.start` | `info` | allowed | *"Signed in from a new device."* (target `null`) |

Two observations a backend developer needs:

1. **`system` actions are not permission keys.** `auditActionLabel` falls back to humanising the
   tail after the first dot (`src/lib/audit.ts:42-49`), so `action` is a free-form dotted string
   constrained by convention. `tests/audit.test.ts:186-190` asserts
   `auditActionLabel("system.retention.sweep") === "Retention sweep"`.
2. **Row 16 is not a typo.** `severity: "error"` with `outcome: "allowed"` — an allowed action that
   failed technically. Severity is an independent operational signal, not a function of outcome.

#### 29.5.2 The audit action registry — what the backend emits

**RECOMMENDATION (canon OQ-25).** Only two emitters exist in the frontend, so the policy below is a
decision, not a transcription. The rule, stated once:

> **Audit every action whose permission key is held only from `manager` or `admin` — all 29 of them
> — plus `node.share` and `board.export`, plus every `system.*` event, plus every denial of any key.
> Do not audit routine `row.update` / `comment.create` / `file.upload` successes: `row_activity`
> already covers that traffic, and mixing the two makes the log unreadable at volume.**

**Tier A — always audited, allowed and denied alike (31 catalogue actions).**

| `action` | `module` | Severity when allowed | Endpoint(s) | `context.kind` | `target` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.manage` | `workspace` | `warn` | E-010 | `system` | workspace name |
| `workspace.settings.view` | `workspace` | `info` | (tab open — client-side only) | `system` | workspace name |
| `workspace.member.manage` | `workspace` | **`warn`** | E-013, E-014, E-015, E-016 | `membership` | **the person's name** |
| `workspace.permission.manage` | `workspace` | **`warn`** | E-042, E-043, E-046 | `access_rule` / `system` | node name |
| `workspace.audit.view` | `workspace` | `warn` | E-136, E-137 | `system` | `"Audit log"` |
| `workspace.delete` | `workspace` | **`warn`** | E-011 | `system` | workspace name |
| `node.create` | `node` | `info` | E-024, E-027 | `node` | node name |
| `node.rename` | `node` | `info` | E-025 | `node` | the **new** name |
| `node.move` | `node` | **`warn`** | E-026 | `node` | node name |
| `node.delete` | `node` | **`warn`** | E-032, E-037, E-038, E-039 | `node` | node name |
| `node.share` | `node` | `info` | (share flow) | `node` | node name |
| `node.archive` | `node` | `info` | E-030, E-031 | `node` | node name |
| `node.access.manage` | `node` | **`warn`** | E-041 | `access_mode` | node name |
| `board.create` | `board` | `info` | E-024 (`kind: board`) | `node` | board name |
| `board.manage` | `board` | `info` | E-050 | `node` | board name |
| `board.column.create` | `board` | `info` | E-052, E-055 | `node` | board name |
| `board.column.update` | `board` | `info` | E-053, E-056, E-058 – E-060 | `node` | board name |
| `board.column.update` (convert) | `board` | **`warn`** | E-057 (not `dryRun`) | `node` | board name |
| `board.column.delete` | `board` | **`warn`** | E-054 | `node` | board name |
| `board.view.manage` | `board` | `info` | E-079 – E-082 | `node` | board name |
| `board.template.manage` | `board` | `info` | E-089, E-090 | `node` | template name |
| `board.import` | `board` | `info` | E-085 | `bulk` | board name |
| `board.export` | `board` | `info` (scope `view`/`selection`) · **`warn`** (scope `board`) | E-086, E-137 | `export` | board name |
| `row.archive` | `row` | `info` | E-075 | `bulk` | board name |
| `row.delete` | `row` | **`warn`** | E-065, E-076, E-077 | `bulk` | board name |
| `document.create` | `document` | `info` | E-024 (`kind: document`) | `node` | page name |
| `document.update` | `document` | `info` | E-092, E-100 — **only when not an autosave fold** | `node` | page name |
| `document.lock` | `document` | `info` | E-094 | `node` | page name |
| `document.version.restore` | `document` | **`warn`** | E-097 | `version` | page name |
| `file.delete` | `file` | **`warn`** | E-032 on a file node | `node` | file name |
| `secret.reveal` | `secret` | **`warn`** | E-103, E-104 | `secret` | **the key name** |
| `secret.rotate` | `secret` | **`warn`** | E-102 | `secret` | **the key name** |

**Tier B — audited only on failure or refusal (the 8 remaining Member keys).** A successful
`row.update` goes to `row_activity` (T-14) and not here. A `row.update` that is **denied** is a Tier
A-grade event and is written at `error` / `denied`; a `file.upload` that is **allowed but failed
technically** is written at `error` / `allowed`, which is exactly seed row 16.

| `action` | `module` | On success | On technical failure | On refusal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row.create`, `row.update`, `row.move` | `row` | `row_activity` only | `error` / `allowed` | `error` / `denied` |
| `comment.create`, `comment.resolve`, `comment.delete` | `comment` | `row_activity` only | `error` / `allowed` | `error` / `denied` |
| `file.upload`, `file.update` | `file` | `row_activity` only | `error` / `allowed` | `error` / `denied` |

**Divergence from the seed, flagged.** Seed rows 13 (`row.update`, `info`, allowed) and 17
(`comment.delete`, `info`, allowed) are Tier B successes and would **not** be written under this
policy. They exist in the fixture to prove the table can render every module, and the audit page's
module filter offers all nine. Nothing breaks if a deployment chooses to write them — the schema,
the filters and the UI all accommodate it — but at real volume the 9 `error` rows disappear into
88,000 `info` rows and the severity filter stops being useful. **This is canon OQ-25; the position
taken here is the one canon's §8.8 endorses.**

**Tier C — `system.*` events, no permission key, no interactive actor.**

| `action` | `module` | Severity | Fires when | `target` | `context` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system.session.start` | `system` | `info` | A successful login (E-001) | `null` | `{ kind: "system", job: "login" }` |
| `system.session.end` | `system` | `info` | Explicit logout (E-002) | `null` | `{ kind: "system", job: "logout" }` |
| `system.session.reuse` | `system` | `error` | Refresh-token replay detected; the family is revoked | `null` | `{ kind: "system", job: "refresh_reuse" }` |
| `system.retention.sweep` | `system` | `info` | The nightly trash purge (canon OQ-14) | `"Trash"` | `{ kind: "system", job: "trash_retention" }` |
| `system.audit.sweep` | `system` | `warn` | The audit retention purge (§29.10) | `"Audit log"` | `{ kind: "system", job: "audit_retention" }` |
| `system.upload.reap` | `system` | `info` | Expired `uploads` rows reaped | `null` | `{ kind: "system", job: "upload_reap" }` |

`actor_id` for a `system.*` row is the account the job runs as; `ip` is the loopback address
(`127.0.0.1`, as the seed shows at `audit-service.ts:187-196`). Login/logout positions are inherited
from §8 (part-01), which already took them.

#### 29.5.3 The security actions that MUST be audited

Non-negotiable. Each row names the endpoint, and each is `PRD` where `SY-AUD-41` or `DV-SEC-23`
names it and `FE` where the frontend already emits it.

| # | Action | Endpoint(s) | `module` | `action` | Severity | `target` | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Reveal a secret** | E-103 (`action: "reveal"`) | `secret` | `secret.reveal` | `warn` allowed · `error` denied | the key name | **PRD** `DV-SEC-23` (*"Mọi thao tác Reveal/Copy tự động ghi nhận vào Workspace Audit Log"*, *"100% hành vi Reveal/Copy phải sinh Audit Log kèm IP và Timestamp"*); **FE** `devtools-service.ts:382-395` |
| 2 | **Copy a secret** | E-103 (`action: "copy"`), E-104 | `secret` | `secret.reveal` — **one row per key copied** | `warn` allowed · `error` denied | the key name | **PRD** `DV-SEC-23`; **FE** `devtools-service.ts:384-386`, `:446-452` |
| 3 | **Change a member's role** | E-014 | `workspace` | `workspace.member.manage` | `warn` | **the person's name** | **PRD** `SY-AUD-41` (*"Thay đổi Role thành viên"*); **FE** seed `audit-service.ts:137-145` |
| 4 | **Change a permission (an access rule)** | E-042, E-043 | `workspace` | `workspace.permission.manage` | `warn` | the node name | **FE** `permission-store.ts:71-78`, `:99-106`; `tests/audit.test.ts:261-274` |
| 5 | **Change a node's access mode** | E-041 | `node` | `node.access.manage` | `warn` | the node name | **RECO** — `setNodeAccessMode` (`workspace-store.ts:412-418`) emits nothing today, and a restriction that leaves no trace is the one change most worth tracing |
| 6 | **Delete a board** | E-032 on a board node; E-038 / E-039 to purge | `node` | `node.delete` | `warn` | the board name | **PRD** `SY-AUD-41` (*"Xóa Board"*); **FE** seed `audit-service.ts:126-135` |
| 7 | **Restore a config version** | E-097 on a `config` document | `document` | `document.version.restore` | `warn` | the document name | **PRD** `SY-AUD-41` (*"Khôi phục Config"*), `DV-ENV-21` (*"Thay đổi cấu hình Prod: Bắt buộc yêu cầu xác nhận role Admin/Manager"*); canon OQ-62 records that this is *"announced as audited and is not"* |
| 8 | **Remove a workspace member** | E-015, and E-016 for a self-removal | `workspace` | `workspace.member.manage` | `warn` | **the person's name** | **PRD** `SY-AUD-41`; the same key as #3, distinguished by `context.roleAfter === null` |
| 9 | **Export** | E-086 (board data), E-137 (the audit log itself) | `board` / `workspace` | `board.export` / `workspace.audit.view` | `info` for a view/selection export · **`warn`** for a whole-board export and **always** for the audit export | the board name / `"Audit log"` | **PRD** `SY-AUD-41` (*"Chỉ có role Super Admin mới có quyền truy cập và xuất file Audit Log"*), `SY-EXP-36`; **FE** seed `audit-service.ts:197-206` |

Four more that belong on the same list even though the brief does not name them, because each is a
one-click irreversible or privileged operation with no other trace:

| # | Action | Endpoint | `module` | `action` | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | **Empty the trash** | E-039 | `node` | `node.delete` | `warn`, `context.kind = "bulk"` with the count |
| 11 | **Delete the workspace** | E-011 | `workspace` | `workspace.delete` | `warn` |
| 12 | **List every restricted node** | E-046 | `workspace` | `workspace.permission.manage` | `warn` — §28.12.3, canon OQ-26 |
| 13 | **Read the audit log** | E-136 | `workspace` | `workspace.audit.view` | `warn` — canon OQ-26; the refusal is already audited by the seed, the success is not |

**Which privileged *reads* are audited, decided (canon OQ-26).** Reads are normally silent. These
five are not, and each is a `warn`:

- `secret.reveal` and the multi-key copy (E-103, E-104) — already done by the frontend;
- the restricted-node recovery list (E-046) — §28.12.3;
- a **successful** `workspace.audit.view` (E-136) — the refusal is already in the seed;
- the audit export (E-137);
- a node's access list (E-040) — **RECOMMENDATION**, and the weakest of the five: it is read
  every time the access dialog opens, which is often. If the volume is unacceptable, drop this one
  and keep the other four; do not drop E-046.

Everything else — reading a board, a page, a file, a comment thread — is not audited. That traffic
belongs to `row_activity` and to ordinary request logs.

---

### 29.6 Severity policy

Severity is an **independent operational signal**, not a function of outcome. `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:225-226`
states the default: *"A refusal defaults to Error, a privileged read to Warn."*

| Situation | Severity | Outcome | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Any denial, at any gate | **`error`** (the default when `outcome = 'denied'`) | `denied` | `audit-service.ts:296`; `tests/audit.test.ts:119-130` |
| Privileged read of plaintext (`secret.reveal`, allowed) | **`warn`** | `allowed` | `devtools-service.ts:389`; `tests/audit.test.ts:244-259` |
| Any access-rule or access-mode write | **`warn`** | `allowed` | `permission-store.ts:75`, `:103` |
| Membership or role change | **`warn`** | `allowed` | seed `audit-service.ts:137-145` |
| Bulk or irreversible destruction (`row.delete`, `board.column.delete`, `node.delete`, `workspace.delete`, empty trash) | **`warn`** | `allowed` | seed `:76-84`, `:146-155`, `:126-135` |
| A privileged **read** on the list in §29.5.3 | **`warn`** | `allowed` | canon OQ-26 |
| Routine allowed action in Tier A | `info` | `allowed` | default |
| **Technical failure of an allowed action** | **`error`** | **`allowed`** | seed `:106-115` — the row that proves the two axes are independent |

**Do not add a check constraint tying `severity` to `outcome`.** The `error`/`allowed` combination
is load-bearing: it is how an operator finds the uploads that were permitted and still did not land.

The severity is also what the audit page's facet counts and colour ramp read
(`src/components/audit/audit-table.tsx:11-20`: `info` neutral, `warn` amber, `error` red), so it is
user-visible and must be chosen deliberately per emitter rather than defaulted.

---

### 29.7 Refusals are recorded exactly as carefully as successes

```ts
// src/services/devtools-service.ts:341-348
if (!mayReveal(nodeId, role)) {
  // Recorded even when refused: a denied attempt is worth auditing.
  pushAudit(record, entry, action, false);
  throw permissionDenied(
    `Revealing ${entry.key} needs the Admin role`,
    "Ask a workspace admin to share it with you.",
  );
}
```

`devtools-service.ts:358-361`: *"A denied attempt is recorded exactly as carefully as an allowed one
— a refusal nobody can see is not a control."* `tests/audit.test.ts:223-242` asserts the denied row
carries `outcome: "denied"`, `severity: "error"` and the correct `target`.

**Every DENY branch of the §28.8 pipeline appends a row**, including the ones that answer 404:

| Gate that refused | `module` | `action` | `severity` | `outcome` | `context.gate` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · authentication | `system` | `system.session.denied` | `error` | `denied` | — (no workspace, so no row is written; log it to the request log instead) |
| 2 · workspace membership | `workspace` | the key the call needed | `error` | `denied` | `"membership"` |
| 3 · resource access | the key's module | the key the call needed | `error` | `denied` | `"visibility"` |
| 4b · capability | the key's module | the key | `error` | `denied` | `"capability"` |
| 4c · trashed | the key's module | the key | `error` | `denied` | `"trashed"` |
| 4c · frozen | the key's module | the key | `error` | `denied` | `"frozen"` |
| 4c · locked | the key's module | the key | `error` | `denied` | `"locked"` |

Two rules that apply to every one of them:

1. **The `detail` names the missing role, never the resource.** *"Refused: the Viewer role does not
   hold Reveal secrets."* — the seed's own phrasing (`audit-service.ts:63`, `:235`). The `target`
   may be a resource label because the reader of the audit log is an admin; the **response** to the
   refused caller names nothing (§28.8.3). These are two different audiences and two different
   strings.
2. **A gate-2 or gate-3 refusal is written even though the caller was told 404.** The row is the
   only record that somebody probed a resource they could not see, which is precisely the signal an
   investigation is looking for. `context.gate` distinguishes them; it is never returned.

**Gate 1 has no workspace**, so there is no `workspace_id` to write and no row. Failed
authentication belongs to the request log and to whatever rate-limiting counter backs
`AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`; `system.session.start` covers the success. This is the one deliberate hole in
"every denial is audited", and it is bounded: an unauthenticated caller has named no resource.

---

### 29.8 What must never enter the log

A checklist, because every item on it has been got wrong in some product:

| Never in `target` or `detail` | Instead |
| --- | --- |
| A secret's **value** | the key name in `target`; `context.secretKey` |
| A cell value, a block's text, a comment body, a file's bytes | a count or a column name in `detail` |
| A raw id | the human label in `target`; the id in `context` |
| Serialised JSON of a request or a response | one sentence, written by the service |
| A node name in a **refusal returned to the caller** | the audit row may carry it; the API response may not (§28.8.3) |
| A password, a token, a refresh-token family id, a signed URL | nothing; `context.kind = "system"` with a job name |
| Another tenant's data | `workspace_id` scopes every read; there is no cross-workspace audit query |

`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:228-229` and `src/types/audit.ts:35-38` are the grounding: *"the detail line is
a sentence the service wrote — never a payload rendered as JSON"*, *"the UI never renders a raw
audit payload (SY-ACT-40)"*.

---

### 29.9 Transactionality

**Two different rules, and getting them the wrong way round loses the evidence.**

| Case | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Allowed action** | `INSERT` the audit row in the **same transaction** as the mutation. | A rollback must take the row with it. An audit row for a write that did not happen is worse than no row: it is a false record. |
| **Refusal** | Write on an **autonomous connection**, outside the transaction that is about to abort. | Otherwise the denial record rolls back with the refusal it was recording — and *"a refusal nobody can see is not a control"* (`devtools-service.ts:358-361`). |

`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:329-330` names it as a backend obligation: *"Server-stamped audit entries with a
real client address, written inside the same transaction as the action — including refusals."*

**Implementation shape.** A request-scoped audit buffer with two sinks:

```
begin request
  audit.deferred := []          # flushed with the transaction
  audit.immediate := []         # flushed on an autonomous connection, always

  ... pipeline ...
  on DENY:  audit.immediate.push(row)   ; abort ; flush(immediate) ; respond
  on ALLOW: audit.deferred.push(row)    ; commit (rows land with the write) ; respond
end
```

Ordering within a transaction does not matter — the row and the mutation are visible together or not
at all. **Do not** write the audit row before the permission check "so it is not forgotten": a row
describing an action that was then refused, with `outcome: "allowed"`, is worse than a missing row.

**One action, one row — with two deliberate exceptions.** `SY-ACT-40` sets the principle for the
activity stream (*"Thay đổi nhiều trường cùng lúc: Gộp chung vào 1 record log duy nhất"*) and the
audit log follows it: a bulk delete of twelve records is **one** row with
`detail: "12 records deleted in one action."` and `context.kind = "bulk"`, not twelve rows. The two
exceptions:

- **`secret.reveal` on a multi-key copy (E-104) writes one row per key.** `copySecrets` loops
  `pushAudit(record, entry, "copy", true)` per entry (`devtools-service.ts:446-452`) — *"a loop of
  single reveals would write the same audit trail but leave every value sitting in the page in
  between"*. Each key that left the server is its own event.
- **`secret.rotate` on a whole-list save writes one row per key touched**, including one for each
  key that was **removed** — *"A removed secret is a rotation too — the trail has to show where it
  went"* (`devtools-service.ts:553-557`).

---

### 29.10 Retention

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — 12 months.** `SY-AUD-41`'s metrics say it in one line: *"Bảng Audit Log là
Append-only (Tuyệt đối không cho phép sửa/xóa log). Thời gian lưu trữ 12 tháng."* Append-only, and
retained for twelve months.

Note carefully what the frontend does **not** say. `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`
(`src/config/app.ts:41-42`) is the **trash** window and is unrelated; the only retention signal in
the audit domain is the seeded `system.retention.sweep` event, whose `target` is `"Trash"`
(`audit-service.ts:187-196`) — it describes the trash sweep, not an audit sweep. So the PRD is the
only source, and it is enough.

**The policy, decided:**

| Rule | Value | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline retention | **12 months** from `at` | **PRD** `SY-AUD-41` |
| Rows with `severity = 'error'` **or** `outcome = 'denied'` | **24 months**, never purged earlier | **RECOMMENDATION** (canon OQ-27). These are the rows a breach investigation needs and they are a small minority — the seed's ratio is 3 in 20. |
| Free plan | 12 months, same as everyone. **RECOMMENDATION:** do not shorten it by plan. The audit page promises permanence in writing and a plan-dependent trail is a support burden that buys very little storage. | canon OQ-27 |
| Sweep cadence | Nightly, off `audit_events_retention_idx (workspace_id, at) WHERE severity <> 'error' AND outcome = 'allowed'` | — |
| Who runs it | A **separate database role** with `DELETE` on `audit_events`, which the application user cannot assume (§29.1) | `docs/GOVERNANCE.md:331` |
| The sweep is itself audited | `system` / `system.audit.sweep`, `severity: "warn"`, `target: "Audit log"`, `detail: "{N} entries past the 12-month window were removed."`, `context: { kind: "system", job: "audit_retention" }` | mirrors the shape of `system.retention.sweep` |

**The in-product contradiction, and how to resolve it.** The audit page currently renders *"the trail
itself is never trimmed"* in its empty state (`src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:96-100`) and
*"Append-only · entries cannot be edited or deleted"* in its header. Both are true of the API
surface and neither is true of a 12-month sweep. **Whichever window is chosen must be stated in the
product**, next to those two sentences: *"Append-only · entries cannot be edited or deleted ·
retained for 12 months"*. A promise of permanence that a cron job breaks is worse than a shorter
promise that holds.

*Impact if wrong:* too short and a breach investigation has no trail; too long and the severity
filter drowns while the storage bill grows in a table nothing ever deletes from.

---

### 29.11 The read API

#### 29.11.1 `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit`

**Purpose** — Read the workspace security trail, newest first, narrowed by module, severity, actor,
free text and a date range. It is the only way to read `audit_events`, and there is no companion
write endpoint by construction.

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.audit.view` (Admin only), plus workspace membership.
`src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:36-37` gates the whole hook on it; the page renders a permission-denied
panel otherwise (`src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:31-41`) with the exact copy:
*"The audit log is open to workspace admins"* / *"Your role does not hold "Read the audit log". Ask
an admin if you need it."*

`workspace.audit.view` is one of the three `READ_ONLY_KEYS` (§28.3.4), so it survives a frozen or
locked context — but that is academic here: the key is evaluated at workspace scope with `node: null`
and no narrowing layer applies.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | Every read is workspace-scoped. There is no cross-workspace audit query and no global audit endpoint. |

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `module` | `AuditModule \| "all"` | no | `"all"` | One of the 9 values. `"all"` and absent are **equivalent** (`audit-service.ts:307`). |
| `severity` | `AuditSeverity \| "all"` | no | `"all"` | `info` / `warn` / `error`. |
| `actorId` | UUID \| `"all"` | no | `"all"` | `event.actor.id`. The picker lists workspace members (`src/components/audit/audit-filters.tsx:64-73`). |
| `search` | string | no | `""` | Case-insensitive substring. Spans **actor name, raw action, humanised action label, target, detail and IP** — see below. An empty or whitespace-only value matches everything (`src/lib/audit.ts:68-69`; `tests/audit.test.ts:196-199`). |
| `from` | ISO 8601 | no | — | Inclusive lower bound on `at`. **RECOMMENDATION** (canon OQ-28) — the frontend has no date filter today; canon E-136 registers the parameter. |
| `to` | ISO 8601 | no | — | Exclusive upper bound on `at`. Same. |
| `cursor` | opaque base64 | no | — | Keyset cursor over `(at DESC, id DESC)`. Opaque; a client must never construct or parse one (canon §6.3). |
| `limit` | integer | no | **40** | `AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE` (`src/config/app.ts:56-57`). Hard server cap **200**. |

**Filters are AND-combined** (`audit-service.ts:306-311`). An unknown `module` or `severity` value is
a `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), not a silent `"all"`.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `AuditPage`, `200`.

```ts
/** src/types/audit.ts:50-55, plus the cursor canon §6.3 requires. */
interface AuditPage {
  readonly events: readonly AuditEvent[];
  /** Matches BEFORE the limit was applied, so the table can say "of N". */
  readonly total: number;
  readonly bySeverity: Readonly<Record<AuditSeverity, number>>;
  /** Null when this page is the last. Additive to the existing interface. */
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

```jsonc
// 200 GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit?module=secret&severity=error&limit=40
{
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "9f31c0e2-…",
      "at": "2026-08-26T09:24:00.000Z",
      "module": "secret",
      "action": "secret.reveal",
      "actor": {
        "id": "usr_hai", "name": "Hai Vo", "email": "hai@nexdrop.io", "initials": "HV"
      },
      "ip": "10.4.31.87",
      "severity": "error",
      "target": "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY",
      "detail": "Refused: the Viewer role does not hold Reveal secrets.",
      "outcome": "denied"
    }
  ],
  "total": 128,
  "bySeverity": { "info": 88, "warn": 31, "error": 9 },
  "nextCursor": "eyJhdCI6IjIwMjYtMDgtMjZUMDk6MjQ6MDAuMDAwWiIsImlkIjoiOWYzMWMwZTIifQ"
}
```

**`total` and `bySeverity` are facets over the WHOLE filtered set, not the page.**
`audit-service.ts:318-322` counts `matched`, not `matched.slice(0, limit)`, and
`src/types/audit.ts:52-53` says so in a comment: *"Matches before the limit was applied, so the
table can say 'of N'."* `tests/audit.test.ts:144-150` asserts
`bySeverity.info + bySeverity.warn + bySeverity.error === total` while `events.length === 2`. The
header renders both (`src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:98-115`), including
*"Showing the {n} most recent"* when `events.length < total`.

Two extra aggregate queries per request, both served by the filter indexes:

```sql
-- documentation only — three queries, one predicate
-- 1. the page
SELECT * FROM audit_events
 WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND :predicate
   AND (at, id) < (:cursor_at, :cursor_id)      -- keyset, omitted on the first page
 ORDER BY at DESC, id DESC
 LIMIT :limit + 1;                              -- the extra row decides nextCursor

-- 2. total
SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND :predicate;

-- 3. bySeverity
SELECT severity, count(*) FROM audit_events
 WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND :predicate GROUP BY severity;
```

**Ordering is newest-first, always** (`audit-service.ts:302` — *"the log only ever grows at the
head"*), and there is **no sort parameter**. Offset paging cannot survive a live-appending log:
`page=2` re-shuffles the moment a row is written, so canon §6.3 puts this resource in the cursor
class.

**Executing `search`.** `matchesSearch` is a case-insensitive `includes` over six fields
(`src/lib/audit.ts:66-79`), two of which are not columns:

```ts
return [
  event.actor.name,
  event.action,
  auditActionLabel(event.action),   // ← the catalogue LABEL, e.g. "Create columns"
  event.target ?? "",
  event.detail ?? "",
  event.ip,
].some((field) => field.toLowerCase().includes(needle));
```

- `auditActionLabel` must be resolved server-side from the catalogue, so searching *"Reveal
  secrets"* finds rows whose `action` is `secret.reveal`. Materialise it: keep a lookup of
  `PermissionKey → label` in the service and expand the needle into
  `action = ANY(:keys_whose_label_matches)` before the text predicate.
- `ip` is `INET` and `tests/audit.test.ts:152-158` asserts a **partial-octet** match (`"10.4.31"`).
  `to_tsvector` will not serve that, so the predicate is
  `host(ip) LIKE :needle || '%'` OR the tsquery over the other fields. Add
  `CREATE INDEX audit_events_ip_prefix_idx ON audit_events (workspace_id, (host(ip)) text_pattern_ops)`
  so the prefix form is indexed.
- The GIN `to_tsvector` index serves the word-boundary case for `target`, `detail`, `action` and
  `actor_name`. For a true substring (`"STRIPE_SEC"`), fall back to `pg_trgm`:
  `CREATE INDEX audit_events_trgm_idx ON audit_events USING GIN (target gin_trgm_ops, detail gin_trgm_ops)`.
  **RECOMMENDATION:** ship the trigram index; the frontend's contract is substring, not full-text,
  and a full-text-only implementation silently fails to find `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` from `SECRET_KEY`.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + the `workspace.audit.view` check (`role = 'admin'`). One row via `workspace_members_pkey`. |
| `audit_events` | READ ×3 | The page (`audit_events_page_idx` or one of the three filter indexes), `count(*)`, and the severity `GROUP BY`. `context` is **excluded from the projection** — never selected, never returned. |
| `users` | READ | Not required. `actor_name` and `actor_email` are denormalised on the row; join only to enrich `avatarUrl` / `initials` / `accentColor` for the `UserSummary`, and tolerate a missing user. |
| `audit_events` | **WRITE** | One row: this read is itself audited at `warn` (§29.5.3 #13, canon OQ-26). |

**Transaction** — **Required**, for the same reason as E-046: the read and its own audit row must be
atomic. The three read queries additionally want one snapshot so `total`, `bySeverity` and `events`
agree; `REPEATABLE READ` is sufficient.

**Realtime** — **None, and none should be added.** An audit frame would push security events to
whoever happens to be connected; the log is read deliberately, through a gated endpoint. No frame in
canon §7 targets `audit_events`.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — the role does not hold `workspace.audit.view`. `message`: `The audit log is open to workspace admins`; `detail`: `Your role does not hold “Read the audit log”. Ask an admin if you need it.` **Audited at `error` / `denied`** — the seed carries exactly this row (`audit-service.ts:228-237`). |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` — unknown workspace, or one the caller is not in. |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — unknown `module` / `severity`, malformed `cursor`, `limit` out of range, `from` after `to`. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `network` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` — *"Could not reach the workspace service"*. The page renders a retry (`AsyncBoundary`), and `tests/audit.test.ts:170-173` asserts a failing backend **rejects** rather than returning half a trail. |

**An empty result is a `200` with an empty page, never an error.**
`tests/audit.test.ts:161-168`: `{ events: [], total: 0, bySeverity: { info: 0, warn: 0, error: 0 } }`.
The page then renders *"Nothing has been recorded yet"* or *"No entries match those filters"*
(`audit-page.tsx:88-100`).

**Frontend Used By** — `src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:50-55` (`auditService.list(query, signal)`),
rendered by `src/components/audit/audit-page.tsx:29` with filters from
`src/components/audit/audit-filters.tsx:20-88` and rows from
`src/components/audit/audit-table.tsx:29-116`. The route is
`src/app/(workspace)/audit/page.tsx`.

**Cancellation** — the hook passes an `AbortSignal` (`use-audit-log.ts:51`); an aborted request maps
to `cancelled` client-side and is never a server response (canon C-12).

#### 29.11.2 `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit/export`

**Purpose** — Stream the filtered trail as CSV, for an investigation, a compliance request or an
external archive. `SY-AUD-41`'s edge case requires it: *"Chỉ có role Super Admin mới có quyền truy
cập và **xuất file** Audit Log."*

**Authentication** — Required.

**Permission** — `workspace.audit.view` (Admin), plus workspace membership. Same key as E-136; there
is no separate export key in the catalogue and none should be added — the PRD couples access and
export in the same sentence.

**Path Params**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | — |

**Query Params** — **Identical to E-136** (`module`, `severity`, `actorId`, `search`, `from`, `to`),
minus `cursor` and `limit`: an export is the whole filtered set, streamed. A missing `from`/`to`
exports the full retained window, which may be twelve months of rows.

**Request Body** — None.

**Response** — `200`, `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`,
`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="audit-{workspaceSlug}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv"`, streamed with
`Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Not a JSON body, and therefore the one endpoint in this chapter that
does not return a domain object.

Columns, in the order the table renders them (`src/components/audit/audit-table.tsx:36-44`) plus the
two fields the table folds into the Action cell:

```csv
at,module,action,action_label,actor_name,actor_email,ip,severity,target,detail,outcome
2026-08-26T09:24:00.000Z,secret,secret.reveal,Reveal secrets,Hai Vo,hai@nexdrop.io,10.4.31.87,error,STRIPE_SECRET_KEY,Refused: the Viewer role does not hold Reveal secrets.,denied
```

- `at` is **ISO 8601, not the rendered form** — a CSV is machine input.
- `action_label` is `auditActionLabel(action)`, included so a reader without the catalogue can read
  the file.
- **`context` is not a column.** It is never exported, for the same reason it is never returned.
- **`id` is not a column.** It is an internal handle; the row's identity for an investigator is
  `(at, actor, action, target)`.
- Escaping: RFC 4180. `detail` routinely contains commas and typographic quotes
  (*"Column "Story points" removed with its values."*), so every field is quoted and inner quotes
  doubled. **Prefix any field beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` with a single quote** — a CSV
  opened in a spreadsheet is a formula-injection surface, and `detail` is server-written but
  `target` is a user-chosen node name.

**Database**

| Table | Operation | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members` | READ | Gate 1 + `workspace.audit.view`. |
| `audit_events` | READ | A **server-side cursor** over the same predicate as E-136, ordered `at DESC, id DESC`, streamed in batches. No `count(*)`, no facets. |
| `audit_events` | **WRITE** | One row, **before the stream opens** — see below. |

**Transaction** — The audit row is committed **before** the first byte of the stream is written, on
its own transaction. This is the inverse of the §29.9 rule and the exception is deliberate: a stream
that fails halfway has still disclosed rows, so the record of the attempt must not roll back with
it. The read itself then runs on a `REPEATABLE READ` snapshot so the file is internally consistent.

**Audit** — module `workspace`, action `workspace.audit.view`, severity **`warn`**,
`outcome: "allowed"`, `target: "Audit log"`,
`detail: "Exported the audit log as CSV."` (plus the filter summary when one was applied, e.g.
*"Exported the audit log as CSV, filtered to Secrets."*),
`context: { kind: "system", job: "audit_export" }`. A refusal is audited at `error` / `denied`.
Canon E-137 states it: *"the export is itself audited at `warn`"*.

**Rate limiting** — **RECOMMENDATION:** one export per workspace per minute, `429` with
`RATE_LIMITED`, `retryAfterSeconds` and `isRetryable: true` (canon §4.2). A twelve-month export is
the most expensive read in the system and the most useful one to abuse.

**Realtime** — None.

**Possible Errors**

| HTTP | Code | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `permission_denied` | `AUTH_REQUIRED` |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` — not `workspace.audit.view`. Audited at `error` / `denied`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` |
| 400 | `validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed filter, `from` after `to`. |
| 429 | `validation` | `RATE_LIMITED`, `isRetryable: true`, `retryAfterSeconds` set. |
| 500 | `unknown` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` — **before** the first byte. Once the stream has started there is no way to signal an error in-band; truncate and rely on the audit row plus server logs. |

**Frontend Used By** — **None today.** No component calls it; the audit page offers filtering and
nothing else (*"Filtering is the only thing anyone can do to it"*,
`src/components/audit/audit-filters.tsx:17`). This endpoint exists because `SY-AUD-41` requires it
and canon registers it as E-137 (RECO, OQ-27). When the button lands it belongs in the audit page
header beside the append-only badge, gated on the same `canView` the hook already exposes
(`src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:32`).

---

### 29.12 The relationship to `row_activity`

Named here so no one merges them. `row_activity` (T-14) and `audit_events` (T-36) look similar — an
actor, a timestamp, a thing acted on, a sentence — and §4 (part-05) sets out six reasons they are
two tables. The two that matter to a security reviewer:

1. **Different readers, different gates.** `row_activity` is read by anyone who can see the record,
   through the row drawer's Activity tab (`SY-ACT-40`). `audit_events` is read only by an Admin
   holding `workspace.audit.view`. Merging them would mean either leaking security events to every
   member or hiding the record's own history from the people working on it.
2. **Different lifetimes and different delete behaviour.** `row_activity` cascades away with its
   row. `audit_events` has **no foreign key to what it describes**, precisely so it survives the
   purge — *"Moved to Trash with 2 items under it"* is exactly the row you need after the subtree is
   gone.

The practical rule for an implementer choosing where a write goes: **if the permission key that
governs it is held from `manager` or `admin`, it is an audit event; if it is a Member key and it
succeeded, it is row activity.** §29.5.2's tiers are that rule made explicit.

### 29.13 Open questions carried by this section

| id | Question | Position taken here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OQ-25 | Which actions must emit an audit row? | §29.5.2. Tier A (31 catalogue actions) always; Tier B (8 Member keys) on failure or refusal only; Tier C `system.*`; every denial of any key. |
| OQ-26 | Which privileged **reads** must themselves be audited? | §29.5.3. Five, all at `warn`: `secret.reveal`/copy, E-046, a successful E-136, E-137, and (weakest) E-040. |
| OQ-27 | Audit retention and export | §29.10. **12 months** — and this is an EXISTING REQUIREMENT from `SY-AUD-41`, not a recommendation. `error`/`denied` rows kept 24 months. E-137 exists, is gated on `workspace.audit.view`, and is audited at `warn`. The in-product copy must state the window. |
| OQ-28 | Audit list has a limit but no cursor and no date range | §29.11.1. Keyset cursor on `(at DESC, id DESC)`; `from`/`to` added as canon E-136 registers them; `total` and `bySeverity` stay facets over the whole filtered set. |
| OQ-68 | Is `SecretAuditEntry` a separate table, or a projection of `AuditEvent`? | Canon's position (OQ-68): **write both**, in one transaction — a `secret_access_events` row (T-25, the per-document trail the secret panel renders) and an `audit_events` row (the workspace trail). `devtools-service.ts:382-395` does exactly that in one function. |
| OQ-62 | Changing a Production config is announced as audited and is not | §29.5.3 #7. `document.version.restore` and `document.update` on a config document both emit, at `warn` and `info` respectively. |
| OQ-03 | "Super Admin" in `SY-AUD-41` | Read as Admin. `workspace.audit.view` and E-137 are Admin-gated; no fifth role. |

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **E-046's response shape diverges from canon.** Canon §3.5 says
   `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/restricted-nodes` returns `DriveNode[]`. §28.12.3 returns a narrow
   `RestrictedNodeEntry[]` instead, because a `DriveNode` carries `excerpt`, `blockCount`,
   `itemCount`, `openCount`, `previewUrl`, `thumbnailUrl` and `children` — content about a node the
   caller is explicitly **not** allowed to see, which contradicts the endpoint's own contract
   (*"it exposes names and paths and no content"*, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:270-278`). I
   believe canon is wrong here and have said so rather than following it silently; if canon is
   right, the response must at minimum be a `DriveNode` with those seven fields stripped, which is
   a `DriveNode` in name only. This is the one place in this file where I did not follow canon
   literally. **Please decide.**

2. **`PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES` is registered with no emitter.** Canon §4.3 lists it (400,
   `validation`) while canon §8.8's OQ-21 position says a higher declared role is *"ignored, not
   rejected"*. Both cannot be the default. §28.11.2 follows the OQ-21 position and marks the error
   reason as reserved for an opt-in strict mode. If the editor prefers the error to be live, three
   things change: the header becomes rejected rather than clamped, a stale tab breaks rather than
   degrades, and the error-reason count in canon §9 stays right either way.

3. **E-045 serves the catalogue but not the matrix.** `PermissionDefinition`
   (`src/types/permission.ts:101-107`) has no `heldBy`, and canon §5.2 forbids re-scoping an
   existing domain interface, so the four role sets stay as service config on both sides.
   `spec/audit/governance.md:420-450` proposed a richer `{ roles, permissions }` body with `heldBy`
   and a `classification` field. If the editor wants the matrix served, the additive shape that
   breaks nothing is a **sibling** endpoint — `GET /permissions/roles` →
   `{ role, label, summary, rank, keys }[]` — rather than widening `PermissionDefinition`. I have
   specified the deploy-time containment assertions as the alternative.

4. **A governance consequence of soft delete has no canon id.** §28.5.6 shows that deleting a
   restricted node detaches it from the tree, which makes `findPathToId` return `[]`, which makes
   `nodeVisibility` return **visible** and `effectiveAccess` return the plain workspace role — so
   "restrict, then delete" declassifies a subtree to every member. The fix (resolve gate 2/3 against
   `trash_entries.original_ancestor_ids`) is available because the chain is already captured at
   deletion. I cited **OQ-14** and **OQ-15** because ground rule 3 forbids inventing an id, but this
   is really its own question and deserves one — suggest appending it to canon §8.2 or §8.3.

5. **Two seed rows are excluded by the audit policy I specified.** Seed rows 13 (`row.update`,
   `info`, allowed) and 17 (`comment.delete`, `info`, allowed) in `src/services/audit-service.ts`
   are Tier B successes and would not be written under §29.5.2. They stay renderable — nothing in
   the schema, the filters or the table changes — but a reader comparing the fixture to the policy
   will notice. This is canon OQ-25's own recommendation, followed.

6. **Audit retention is an EXISTING REQUIREMENT, not an open question.** Canon OQ-27 and
   `spec/audit/governance.md:2044-2064` both state that *"there is no audit retention period
   anywhere in the frontend"*. That is true of the frontend and false of the PRD:
   `SY-AUD-41` says *"Thời gian lưu trữ 12 tháng"* in its Metrics. §29.10 treats 12 months as
   settled and keeps only the `error`/`denied` extension as a recommendation. Suggest updating
   OQ-27's entry in canon §8.3 to "retention settled at 12 months by `SY-AUD-41`; export and the
   denial-row extension remain open".

7. **`workspace.settings.view` is classified as a write.** It is not in `READ_ONLY_KEYS`
   (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:29-33`), so `isWrite` returns true for it and it is narrowed by
   trash/freeze/lock like any mutation. That is the shipped behaviour and it is harmless because the
   key is only ever evaluated with `node: null`. Flagging it in case a reviewer reads the name and
   expects it in the read-only set; adding it there would be a behaviour change, not a fix, and I
   did not make one.

8. **Scope boundary.** I documented E-044, E-045, E-046, E-136 and E-137 in full endpoint shape.
   E-040 – E-043 are specified in §11 (part-07) and I referenced rather than duplicated them; the
   `access_rules` and `audit_events` DDL is owned by §4 (part-03 and part-05) and appears here only
   in compressed recap form, with the same column names, index names and delete behaviour. If any
   of those three recaps has drifted from its owning chapter, the owning chapter wins.

## 30. Realtime Events

Module: `realtime` (canon C-14). Endpoint: **E-138** — `GET /api/v1/realtime?workspaceId=`,
WebSocket upgrade. Infrastructure: Redis pub/sub for cross-instance fan-out; no queue, no
broker, no job runner (canon scope statement).

**Tables owned: none.** Realtime is the only module in this specification with no table of its
own. It *reads* `workspace_members` (T-04), `nodes` (T-06), `access_rules` (T-08),
`users.is_active` (T-01) and `user_sessions` (T-02) to decide who may receive what, and it
writes nothing to PostgreSQL. Its own state lives in Redis and in per-connection process
memory, and every key it uses is registered in §30.4.6. **Losing Redis entirely must cost a
reconnect, never a record** (part-01 §2, infrastructure table).

Frames: **RT-01 … RT-12** (canon §7). Payload interface names: canon §5.6.
Open questions this section answers under an explicit position: **OQ-99**, **OQ-100**, **OQ-101**.

---

### 30.1 What the frontend already is

Nothing in this section is a greenfield design. The frontend ships a complete realtime
architecture with the socket removed, and the shape of what the backend must build is fixed by
it. Read this first; everything after it is a consequence.

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT — the seam is declared, in the type file, as a promise to the backend:**

> Realtime is expressed as a transport interface, not as a socket client. The backend does not
> expose a realtime endpoint yet, so the only transport wired today is the in-process one. When
> a socket does land, it implements this interface and `createTransport` returns it — nothing
> above this line changes.
> — `src/types/realtime.ts:3-10`

Four files and three subscribers:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `src/types/realtime.ts` | The contract: `RealtimePayload`, `RealtimeEvent`, `RealtimeTransport`, `RealtimeStatus`. 56 lines, no `any`, every field `readonly`. |
| `src/lib/realtime/transport.ts` | The interface's only implementation today — an in-process bus (`createLocalTransport`, `:21-53`) and the factory that would choose a socket (`createTransport`, `:62-68`). |
| `src/lib/realtime/client.ts` | The shared client: dedupe by event id, then fan-out to subscribers. Created and **connected at import time** (`:130-132`). |
| `src/config/app.ts:65-69` | `REALTIME_ENDPOINT: string \| null = null` — "Null while the backend exposes no socket, which is what keeps `lib/realtime/transport` on the in-process bus." |

| Subscriber | Site | What it does with a frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useComments` | `src/hooks/use-comments.ts:55-65` | Ignores anything that is not `comment.created` / `comment.updated`, then ignores any frame whose `targetKey` is not this thread's, then `upsertComment(current, payload.comment)`. |
| `useNotificationStore.ingest` | `src/store/notification-store.ts:108-126`, subscribed once at `:130` | `notification.created` → re-checks `recipientId === CURRENT_USER.id` (`:112`) and upserts; `notification.read` → marks the named ids read. A frame arriving before the first load flips `status: "idle" → "ready"` so the inbox populates from the socket alone (`:115-116`). |
| `useAccessSync` | `src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:74-83` | Ignores anything that is not `permission.changed`; ignores it unless `userIds.includes(CURRENT_USER.id)`; then re-resolves the viewer's own access and, if the open node is no longer visible, resets `boardService`, the board store, the grid store and the recent store (`:41-69`). |

**The two guarantees the client already has, and which the backend must not undermine**
(`docs/COLLABORATION.md:62-76`; `src/lib/realtime/client.ts:13-17`):

1. **Delivery** — every frame carries an `id`; the client remembers the last
   `SEEN_LIMIT = 512` ids in insertion order and drops a repeat, counting it in
   `duplicatesDropped` (`src/lib/realtime/client.ts:21`, `:52-67`).
2. **Application** — every writer goes through an id-keyed upsert (`upsertComment`,
   `upsertNotification`). Applying the same *record* twice replaces it rather than appending.

The unread badge is **derived** from the inbox (`countUnread`), never incremented
(`src/store/notification-store.ts:140-141`), which removes the third way a count can drift.

**Consequence for the backend, stated once and relied on everywhere below: delivery is
at-least-once. Exactly-once is not required and must not be engineered for.** Canon §7 says
so; the client's dedupe window says so; the id-keyed upserts say so twice.

**The one behaviour that has no analogue in the local bus.** `RealtimeStatus` declares four
states — `idle`, `connecting`, `open`, `closed` (`src/types/realtime.ts:12`) — and the local
transport only ever produces three: it starts `idle`, `connect()` sets `open`, `close()` sets
`closed` (`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:23`, `:33`, `:36`). `connecting` exists in the type
and is unreachable in the implementation. That is not an oversight; it is the shape of a
socket transport showing through a type written for one.

---

### 30.2 The transport: WebSocket, not SSE

**DECIDED (canon E-138): one WebSocket per workspace, Redis pub/sub for fan-out across
instances.** This section justifies that against the interface the frontend actually declares,
because the interface is narrow enough that both options are technically expressible and the
reasons to prefer one are specific rather than general.

#### 30.2.1 The interface the transport must satisfy

```ts
/** src/types/realtime.ts:47-56 — reproduced verbatim. Note that `connect`,
 *  `close`, `publish` and `subscribe` are the two deliberate exceptions to
 *  canon C-07 ("every field is readonly"). */
export interface RealtimeTransport {
  /** Shown in diagnostics so it is obvious which transport is live. */
  readonly name: string;
  readonly status: RealtimeStatus;
  connect: () => void;
  close: () => void;
  /** Send a frame. The local transport echoes it back to its own subscribers. */
  publish: (event: RealtimeEvent) => void;
  subscribe: (handler: RealtimeHandler) => () => void;
}
```

There is **no `join`, no `leave`, no `subscribeTo(room)`, no cursor, no `since`, no resume
token** on this interface. That single fact settles §30.4: the client cannot name a room, so
the server must decide the audience. It is not a simplification the backend chose; it is the
contract.

#### 30.2.2 The comparison, member by member

| `RealtimeTransport` member / requirement | WebSocket | SSE (`EventSource`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connect()` | `new WebSocket(url)` | `new EventSource(url)` |
| `close()` | `ws.close(1000)` | `es.close()` |
| `subscribe(handler)` | `onmessage` → parse → deliver | `onmessage` → parse → deliver |
| `status: RealtimeStatus` (4 states) | `CONNECTING`→`connecting`, `OPEN`→`open`, `CLOSING`/`CLOSED`→`closed`, pre-`connect()`→`idle`. All four used. | `readyState` 0/1/2 maps the same way. All four used. |
| `publish(event)` | Local echo only; nothing goes upstream (§30.2.4). | Local echo only; SSE is one-way by construction. |
| **Authentication on connect** | **A control frame sent after the upgrade.** No credential in the URL, no credential in a log. | **Impossible without one.** `EventSource` cannot set headers; the refresh cookie is scoped `Path=/api/v1/auth` (part-01 §8.3) and is therefore not attached to `/api/v1/realtime`; the access token is held in a JavaScript variable, never in a cookie (part-01 §8.3, J-3). SSE leaves only `?access_token=` — a 15-minute bearer credential in every access log, proxy log and `Referer`. |
| **Connections per origin** | One socket, no meaningful cap. | HTTP/1.1 allows **6 per origin**, shared with ordinary API calls. Three tabs open plus a board loading is a real starvation risk. HTTP/2 fixes it and binds the deployment to h2 end-to-end through every proxy and load balancer. |
| **Control channel** (heartbeat, resume handshake, drain notice) | Native — ping/pong plus application control frames. | None. Every control interaction becomes a side-channel HTTP call. |
| **Reconnect** | Hand-written backoff (§30.3.6). | **Built in**, plus `Last-Event-ID` replay for free. |
| Message framing | Binary or text, no per-message HTTP overhead. | Text only, `data:`-prefixed lines. Fine here — every frame is small JSON. |
| Proxy tolerance | Needs `Upgrade` to survive the path; a misconfigured proxy fails loudly at connect. | Needs response buffering disabled; a misconfigured proxy fails *silently* by buffering, which presents as "realtime is slow" rather than "realtime is broken". |

#### 30.2.3 The decision, and what it costs

**WebSocket.** The deciding argument is authentication, and it is not stylistic. The session
model this specification already fixed (part-01 §8.3–8.4) puts the access token in an
`Authorization: Bearer` header held in memory, and deliberately scopes the refresh cookie to
`Path=/api/v1/auth` so that *"the 95 % of requests that are ordinary API calls carry no ambient
credential at all"*. An `EventSource` can present neither. Choosing SSE would mean either
putting a bearer token in a query string — reversing a decision made for CSRF and log-hygiene
reasons — or minting a second cookie scoped to `/api/v1/realtime`, which re-introduces the
ambient credential the design removed. WebSocket lets the credential travel in the first
application frame, over an already-established TLS connection, where nothing logs it.

Everything else is secondary but consistent: one connection instead of one of six, a real
control channel, and a failure mode that is loud.

**What SSE would have given free and we must therefore build:**

| Free with SSE | Built here |
| --- | --- |
| Automatic reconnect with backoff | §30.3.6 — client-side, in the one factory branch. |
| `Last-Event-ID` resume | §30.5.5 — an explicit `lastEventId` in the `auth` control frame, served from a capped Redis Stream. |

Neither is large, and both end up better specified for having been written down: the replay
window is bounded to half the client's dedupe window (§30.5.4), which `Last-Event-ID` would
not have been.

**The frontend cost of the decision is one factory branch.** `createTransport`
(`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:62-68`) already reserves it: *"A socket transport plugs in here
once the endpoint exists. Until then the branch is unreachable by construction rather than by
accident."* Setting `REALTIME_ENDPOINT` (`src/config/app.ts:69`) to the socket URL and
returning `createSocketTransport()` is the whole change. No store, no hook and no component
moves.

#### 30.2.4 `publish` is a local echo. It never travels upstream.

**This is a security rule, not an implementation detail.**

The client's `emit` builds a frame and hands it to `transport.publish` rather than calling
handlers directly, *"so a local write and a remote one travel the identical code path"*
(`src/lib/realtime/client.ts:114-117`). In the local bus, `publish` loops over subscribers
(`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:41-44`). If a socket transport forwarded that frame to the
server instead, a browser would be able to author a `notification.created` frame addressed to
somebody else's inbox, or a `comment.created` frame carrying a body nobody wrote.

Two rules, both required, because either alone can be defeated:

| # | Rule | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RT-P1 | The socket transport's `publish` delivers to this tab's subscribers and **sends nothing upstream**. | Frontend, in the one factory branch. |
| RT-P2 | **The server accepts exactly two inbound frame types — `auth` and `resume-ack` — plus protocol-level pong. Any other inbound frame closes the connection with `4400`.** A `RealtimePayload` arriving from a client is never parsed, never routed, and never logged with its body. | Backend. Non-negotiable. |

RT-P2 stands whether or not RT-P1 is implemented correctly, which is the point of writing both
down. The server has no reason to ever trust a client-authored domain frame: every frame the
system produces is produced by a committed transaction (§30.5.1).

#### 30.2.5 Wire format

Text frames, UTF-8 JSON, one JSON value per frame. Two families, distinguished by shape:

- an **event frame** is exactly a `RealtimeEvent` — `{ id, at, origin, payload }`, four keys, no
  more. The socket transport delivers these to `subscribe` handlers unmodified.
- a **control frame** carries a top-level `"control"` key and never a `payload` key. The socket
  transport consumes these and never delivers them to a subscriber. A client that does not
  understand a control frame ignores it, which is the same additive rule the payload union
  already has (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`).

```ts
/* ---------------------------------------------- client → server (only these) */

/** First frame after the upgrade. Nothing else is accepted before it. */
interface RealtimeAuthFrame {
  readonly control: "auth";
  /** The 15-minute access JWT (part-01 §8.4 R-1). Never in the URL. */
  readonly accessToken: string;
  /** Resume point from a previous connection's `ready`/`event` frames.
   *  Absent on a first connection. See §30.5.5. */
  readonly lastEventId?: string;
}

/** Sent once after a resumed connection has applied its replay. Advisory:
 *  it lets the server close the replay cursor early and is safe to omit. */
interface RealtimeResumeAckFrame {
  readonly control: "resume-ack";
  readonly lastEventId: string;
}

type RealtimeInboundFrame = RealtimeAuthFrame | RealtimeResumeAckFrame;

/* ---------------------------------------------- server → client (control) */

/** Sent once, after a successful `auth`. The connection is live from here. */
interface RealtimeReadyFrame {
  readonly control: "ready";
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  /** Opaque resume token for the next connection's `auth.lastEventId`.
   *  A Redis Stream entry id; the client stores it and never parses it. */
  readonly resumeToken: string;
  /** True when `auth.lastEventId` was inside the replay window and the
   *  backlog that follows is complete. False means frames were missed and
   *  §30.5.6 applies. Absent on a first connection. */
  readonly resumed?: boolean;
  /** Server clock at ready, ISO 8601 (C-03). Diagnostics only. */
  readonly at: string;
}

/** The server is shutting this connection down on purpose. Sent immediately
 *  before a close frame so the client can distinguish a drain from a fault. */
interface RealtimeClosingFrame {
  readonly control: "closing";
  /** Matches the close code that follows. §30.3.5. */
  readonly code: 1000 | 1001 | 1013 | 4400 | 4401 | 4403 | 4409;
  /** Name-free, per canon §4.4 rule 3. Never identifies a resource. */
  readonly reason: string;
  /** Seconds the client should wait before reconnecting. Present on 1013. */
  readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number;
}

type RealtimeControlFrame = RealtimeReadyFrame | RealtimeClosingFrame;
```

**Compression.** `permessage-deflate` is enabled with `server_no_context_takeover`. Frames are
small and highly repetitive JSON; context takeover across frames is disabled because these
frames carry attacker-influenceable content (a comment body) alongside stable structure, which
is the shape a CRIME-style compression-ratio attack needs. This costs a few percent of
compression ratio and removes the class.

**Size cap.** An outbound frame larger than **64 KiB** is a defect: it means a payload rule was
broken (§30.6). The publisher rejects it at publish time with an internal error rather than
truncating. Inbound frames are capped at **8 KiB** (an access token plus a resume token is well
under 1 KiB); anything larger closes the connection with `4400`.

---

### 30.3 Connection lifecycle

#### 30.3.1 `GET /api/v1/realtime` — E-138

**Purpose** — Upgrade an HTTP connection to a WebSocket carrying one workspace's realtime
frames to one browser tab.

**Authentication** — Required, but **not at the handshake**. See §30.3.2.

**Permission** — Membership of `workspaceId`, resolved server-side after authentication. Canon
P-09: every endpoint re-checks its gate; the frontend's checks "are not security"
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:24-25`).

**Path Params** — None.

**Query Params**

| Name | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | UUID | **yes** | One socket per workspace. Malformed or missing → the handshake is refused **before** the upgrade with `400` and the standard error envelope (canon §6.2). |

**Request Body** — None (it is a `GET` upgrade).

**Response** — `101 Switching Protocols`, then the frame protocol in §30.2.5.
