| E-015 | `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/members/{userId}` | **RT-05** `{nodeId:null}` → that user · then **close their sockets `4403`** | user |
| E-016 | `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/members/me` | Same as E-015, for the caller | user |
| E-019 | `POST /invitations/{token}/accept` | **RT-05** `{nodeId:null}` → the accepting user | user |
| **`drive`** | | | |
| E-024 | `POST /workspaces/{id}/nodes` | **RT-11** `created` | node: `[parentId]` |
| E-025 | `PATCH /nodes/{id}` (rename) | **RT-11** `renamed` | node: `[nodeId]` |
| E-026 | `POST /nodes/{id}/move` | **RT-11** `moved` · **RT-05** `{nodeId}` → `losing ∪ gaining` | node: `[oldParentId,newParentId]` · user × N |
| E-027 | `POST /nodes/{id}/duplicate` | **RT-11** `created` *(one frame for the copied root; descendants are inside it and the receiver re-reads the tree)* | node: `[parentId]` |

| E-032 | `DELETE /nodes/{id}` (soft) | **RT-11** `trashed` | node: `[parentId]` |
| **`system` (trash)** | | | |

| E-038 | `DELETE /trash/{entryId}` | — *(already out of every tree)* | |
| E-039 | `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/trash` | — | |
| **`governance`** | | | |

| **`boards`** | | | |

#### 30.8.2 Writes that emit nothing because there is nothing to converge

Grouped so the "—" rows above are not read as omissions.

| Cluster | Endpoints | Why no frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Per-user state** | E-028, E-029 (favourites), E-083 (view preferences), E-127, E-128 (watches) | The write belongs to one person. Their other tabs go briefly stale; nobody else is affected. A frame would need a `user` audience and would exist to synchronise a checkbox. |
| **In-flight state** | E-110, E-112, E-084, E-086 | Belongs to one request or one client. An import plan is not persisted; an export job is polled. |
| **Read-mostly reference data** | E-087–E-090 (templates), E-106–E-109 (environments) | Small lists re-read whenever the surface that uses them opens. |
| **Session state** | E-001, E-002, E-003 | Handled by close codes, not frames (§30.3.5). |
| **Secrets** | E-102, E-103, E-104 | Prohibited, not merely absent (§30.6.3). |
| **Already invisible** | E-038, E-039 | The node left every tree at E-032. |

#### 30.8.3 The real gap: documents, config documents and file content have no frame

**EXISTING, and it is a gap, not a decision.** Canon §7.2's recommended frames cover boards and
the drive tree. They do not cover document bodies, config document content or file text — so
**E-092, E-094, E-097, E-100 and E-115 emit nothing**, and two people editing one page discover
each other only when one of them saves.

**Why this specification does not invent a `document.changed` frame.** Canon fixes the frame
list at twelve and its position on OQ-99 is *"Ship RT-06 … RT-11, ids only, no cell content."*
Adding a thirteenth type here would put a frame in the wire vocabulary that no other chapter
knows about. It is recorded instead, with the mitigations that already exist:

| Surface | What protects it without a frame |
| --- | --- |
| Pages (E-092) | Optional `expectedVersion`; a stale save is refused `409 DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` rather than silently overwriting (canon §6.4, OQ-57). A lost race costs a re-read, not data. |
| Config documents (E-100) | The same, plus the autosave fold. |
| Locked pages (E-094) | A save into a locked page is refused `409 DOCUMENT_LOCKED` (canon E-092). A second editor keeps typing until they save — the frame would have told them sooner; the refusal tells them eventually. Canon **OQ-60** already flags the lock model. |
| File text (E-115) | `SaveTextResult` bumps `file_nodes.version`; last-write-wins. |
| The tree's derived summaries (`blockCount`, `excerpt`) | Re-read with the tree on any navigation. |

**RECOMMENDATION for a future release, so the shape is agreed before somebody needs it:** a
`document.changed` frame with payload `{ workspaceId, nodeId, version }` — ids and a version
stamp, exactly RT-07's shape one level up — anchored `{ kind: "node", nodeIds: [nodeId] }`.
It would fire on E-092, E-097, E-100 and E-115. It must **not** carry blocks, an excerpt, or
content of any kind (P-1). Raising it requires amending canon §7.2, not this section.

### 30.9 The publish path, end to end

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Browser A (writer)
    participant API as Backend instance 1
    participant PG as PostgreSQL
    participant R as Redis
    participant I2 as Backend instance 2
    participant B as Browser B (reader)

    C->>API: POST /api/v1/comments  (E-120)
    API->>PG: BEGIN
    API->>PG: INSERT comments, watches, notifications, row_activity
    Note over API: envelopes appended to the request outbox<br/>RT-01 (node audience) + RT-03 x N (user audience)
    API->>PG: COMMIT
    API-->>C: 200 Comment
    API->>R: one Lua script per envelope, in order - XADD rt:log then PUBLISH rt:ws
    R-->>I2: envelope (RT-01)
    Note over I2: for each local connection in this workspace:<br/>1. dirty? rebuild visible-node set<br/>2. audience check (miss is not a denial, V-1)<br/>3. narrow payload if RT-05<br/>4. enqueue
    I2-->>B: RealtimeEvent - id, at, origin remote, payload
    Note over B: client.admit(id) -> first sight<br/>useComments.upsertComment(comment)
```

**Steps 4 and 6 are the two that must not be reordered.** The outbox is filled inside the
transaction and flushed after it; the Redis write is one Lua script per envelope so the stream
entry and the published message carry the same `streamId` and can never disagree (§30.4.6).

---

### 30.10 Errors, limits and observability

#### 30.10.1 Errors

Realtime produces two kinds of failure and they use two different mechanisms.

| Stage | Mechanism | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the upgrade | HTTP status + the standard error envelope (canon §6.2) | `{ "error": { "code": "validation", "message": "…", "isRetryable": false, "reason": "VALIDATION_FAILED", "requestId": "01JB9…" } }` — used only for a malformed or missing `workspaceId` (`400`). |
| After the upgrade | WebSocket close code, preceded by a `closing` control frame | §30.3.5. |

```jsonc
// 400 GET /api/v1/realtime  (no workspaceId)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation",
    "message": "That request is missing a workspace",
    "isRetryable": false,
    "reason": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
    "requestId": "01JB9…",
    "fields": [
      { "path": "workspaceId", "reason": "VALIDATION_FAILED", "message": "Required" }
    ]
  }
}
```

**A publish failure is never an error to the caller.** If Redis is unreachable when the outbox
flushes, the write has already committed and the HTTP response has already been decided. The
flush logs at `error`, increments `realtime_publish_failures_total`, and returns. Turning a
successful write into a failed response because a notification could not be broadcast would be
the wrong trade in every case (`DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` is for a dependency the *response*
needs).

**No realtime failure is audited.** `audit_events` records what a person did, not what the
transport managed; canon §3.23 forbids a write endpoint for the audit log and this module has
no endpoint that performs an auditable action. A connection close is a log line and a metric.

#### 30.10.2 Limits, collected

| Limit | Value | Section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auth deadline after upgrade | 5 s | 30.3.2 A-2 |
| Heartbeat ping / pong deadline | 30 s / 10 s | 30.3.4 |
| Re-authorization tick | 60 s | 30.3.4 H-3 |
| Visible-node set TTL | 60 s | 30.4.4 V-3 |
| Negative visibility cache TTL | 60 s | 30.4.4 V-2 |
| Connections per user per workspace / overall | 5 / 12 | 30.3.7 |
| Handshakes per user per minute | 30 | 30.3.7 |
| Outbound queue depth per connection | 256 frames | 30.3.7 |
| Outbound frame size | 64 KiB | 30.2.5 |
| Inbound frame size | 8 KiB | 30.2.5 |
| Replay buffer | `MAXLEN ~ 2048`, `MINID` = now − 120 s | 30.5.5 R-3 |
| Replay delivered per reconnect | 256 frames | 30.5.5 R-3 / D-3 |
| `notification.read` ids per frame | 500 | 30.7 RT-04 |
| Row ids per `row.created` / `row.deleted` frame | 1 000 | 30.7 RT-06 |

**None of these is served from `GET /config` (E-139).** Canon fixes that response's fields, and
none of them is a realtime limit — correctly, because every one of these numbers is consumed by
the server or by the transport's own reconnect loop, and no client surface needs to agree with
the server about any of them. Adding a realtime block to `AppConfigResponse` would create a
second place for the numbers to live.

#### 30.10.3 Metrics

| Metric | Type | Labels | Why it is the one that matters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `realtime_connections_active` | gauge | `workspace_id` bucketed | Capacity. |
| `realtime_connection_closes_total` | counter | `code` | `4401` climbing means token or session handling is wrong; `1013` climbing means a slow-client or fan-out problem; `4409` climbing means a reconnect loop. |
| `realtime_publish_latency_seconds` | histogram | `type` | The PRD targets **< 500 ms** for comment delivery (`CO-CMT-26`) and notification push (`CO-NOT-29`). Measured commit → enqueue on the receiving connection. |
| `realtime_publish_failures_total` | counter | `type` | §30.10.1. Every increment is a frame nobody received. |
| `realtime_audience_evaluations_total` | counter | `result` = `hit` / `miss_resolved` / `denied` | A rising `miss_resolved` means the visible-node set is being invalidated too aggressively (§30.4.5) and every frame is paying for a chain walk. |
| `realtime_replay_frames_total` | counter | `outcome` = `resumed` / `window_exceeded` | `window_exceeded` is the direct measure of §30.5.6 — how often a client silently missed frames. If it is not near zero, the buffer bounds (R-3) are wrong for this deployment. |
| `realtime_queue_depth` | histogram | — | Feeds the 256 cap. |

**One log line per connection, at close**, carrying `connectionId`, `userId`, `workspaceId`,
duration, frames delivered, frames dropped by audience, close code — and **no frame bodies**.
A comment body in a log is the same leak as a comment body in a frame with the wrong audience.

---

### 30.11 Open questions

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-99) — realtime covers comments, notifications and permissions, but not
> boards.**
>
> **What is unclear** — Whether board and document activity should reach other viewers live at
> all, and if so with what payload.
>
> **Evidence** — `RealtimePayload` has exactly five members: two comment frames, two
> notification frames and `permission.changed` (`src/types/realtime.ts:15-32`). There is no
> `row.created`, no `row.updated`, no column frame and no presence frame — yet
> `BoardRow.revision` is *"the optimistic-concurrency token"* (`src/types/board.ts:248-249`) and
> `ConflictNotice` (`src/types/board.ts:462-467`) exists specifically to report a lost race.
> The type file says plainly that *"the backend does not expose a realtime endpoint yet"*
> (`:6-7`).
>
> **Recommendation** — Canon's position, adopted unchanged: ship RT-06 … RT-11, **ids only, no
> cell content** (canon §8.8). Frames are additive and unknown types are ignored
> (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`), so they land without a client release, and each can ship
> independently. RT-12 presence is specified and not built (§30.7 RT-12). Documents remain
> uncovered (§30.8.3).
>
> **Impact if wrong** — Asymmetric, which is why shipping is safe. Without row frames, two
> people on one board discover a collision when a write reports a `ConflictNotice` — degraded,
> not broken, and canon §6.4 already makes that path lossless (last-write-wins plus a notice,
> never a `409`). Putting cell content *into* a frame, by contrast, would leak values across a
> permission boundary and is not recoverable by a later fix, because the frames would already
> have been delivered.

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-100) — frame scoping and authorization: who receives which frame, and how
> is that proved?**
>
> **What is unclear** — The frontend has no scoping model to copy. The local transport
> broadcasts to every subscriber in the tab and has no concept of a recipient
> (`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:41-44`).
>
> **Evidence** — Three different disciplines coexist in the five existing frames, and they are
> not consistent with each other. `comment.created` carries the **whole `Comment`, body and
> author included** (`src/types/realtime.ts:16`) and is filtered by the *receiver* on
> `targetKey` (`src/hooks/use-comments.ts:59-60`). `notification.created` is filtered by
> recipient on **both** send and receive (`src/services/notification-service.ts:104-106`,
> `src/store/notification-store.ts:112`). `permission.changed` carries no content at all and is
> filtered by the receiver on `userIds` (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:81`). None of the three
> receiver-side checks is a security boundary; all three run after the bytes arrived.
>
> **Recommendation** — §30.4, in full: the client can name no room; the server computes the
> audience for every frame from `workspace_members` and `access_rules`; a `node` audience is
> evaluated per connection against a server-resolved visible-node set with V-1 … V-4; a `user`
> audience is one inbox; RT-05's `userIds` is narrowed per recipient; every replayed frame is
> re-authorized at delivery against the connection's *current* state (R-2). The receiver-side
> checks stay exactly where they are — as conveniences on top of a boundary, not as the
> boundary.
>
> **Impact if wrong** — This is the **security** severity in canon's registry and it deserves
> it. A `comment.created` broadcast to the workspace room leaks the text of comments on
> restricted boards to every connected session, silently, with no audit trail and no error. A
> `notification.created` sent to more than its recipient leaks a rendered sentence naming a
> resource the receiver may not open. Both are unrecoverable after the fact.

**OQ-101** is answered in §30.5.5 with its own four-part block.

---

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

Every item below is a place where this section followed canon and would have written something
different on its own, or where it read canon in a way another chapter should confirm.

1. **Frame names.** The brief for this section asked for `board.row.created` /
   `board.row.updated` / `board.row.deleted`, `board.column.*`, `board.view.*` and
   `node.moved` / `node.renamed` / `node.trashed`. Canon §7.2 registers **`row.created`,
   `row.updated`, `row.archived`, `row.deleted`, `board.schema.changed`** and a single
   **`node.changed`** carrying a `change` discriminator with exactly those members. Canon's
   names are used throughout. Canon is also right on the merits for the two collapses:
   `board.column.*` and `board.view.*` would both mean "re-read the schema", and C-11 forbids a
   delta, so two frame types would carry identical information and identical client behaviour.

2. **`row.created` payload.** Canon §7.2 gives `{ boardId, rowId, revision }` and then sanctions
   *"one frame per row, or one batched frame carrying `rowIds`"* in the same cell. §30.7 ships
   **one** shape — `{ boardId, nodeId, rowIds }` — because the batched form subsumes the single
   form, and drops `revision` because canon E-062 fixes a created row's revision at `1`. If the
   editor prefers canon's literal singular shape, the change is mechanical, but the batching
   requirement in §30.7 RT-06 must survive it: an import of 5 000 rows publishing 5 000 frames
   overruns both the outbound queue cap and the client's 512-id dedupe window in one write.

3. **`nodeId` added to every board frame.** Canon's sketches carry `boardId` alone. §30.7 adds
   `nodeId` because the audience anchor is a node, the refetch route is
   `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` (E-047) and the frontend's board store is keyed by node id
   (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:44`). Without it every receiver must maintain its own
   board→node map to act on the frame.

4. **`row.updated` / `row.archived` carry `rows: RowRevisionStamp[]`,** not a single
   `{rowId, revision}`, for the same batching reason (E-066 is a batch endpoint by definition,
   E-074 and E-075 are bulk).

5. **RT-10 is read as "re-read the board snapshot", not "re-read the schema array".** Canon's
   wording is *"The client refetches the whole schema"*. Three of the writes that fire RT-10 —
   E-054, E-057, E-060 — also change cells, and E-047 returns board and rows together, so one
   refetch satisfies both. Flagged because a reader of canon alone would implement the narrower
   thing.

6. **E-050 added to RT-10's firing list**, which canon gives as E-052–E-060 and E-079–E-082.
   `rowIdPrefix` is a field of `Board` and `Board` is what the client re-reads. A board
   **rename** is RT-11 `renamed`, because canon OQ-30 puts `name` on the node.

7. **OQ-101 is answered with bounded replay, against the audit fact sheet's recommendation of
   refetch.** Canon deliberately left the question open. The reason for the other choice is in
   §30.5.5: there is no reconnect hook anywhere in the frontend to hang a refetch on, and adding
   one means changing the file `src/types/realtime.ts:6-9` promises will not change. If the
   editor prefers refetch, delete `rt:log` and §30.5.5 R-1 … R-5; §30.5.6's table of stale
   surfaces then becomes the whole answer, and the synthetic RT-05 becomes more important, not
   less.

8. **RT-05's `userIds` is narrowed to one id per recipient at delivery.** Canon's payload is
   `{ workspaceId, nodeId | null, userIds }` and does not say whether the list is the full
   affected set. Narrowing is wire-compatible (`use-access-sync.ts:81` only tests membership)
   and closes a small leak. If another chapter relies on a recipient seeing the full list — no
   chapter does today — this must be revisited.

9. **A `document.changed` frame is proposed and not shipped** (§30.8.3). Adding it means
   amending canon §7.2 and canon §5.6, which this section may not do. It is the largest
   remaining gap in the module.

10. **Two Redis facilities are used: pub/sub and one capped Stream.** Canon's scope line says
    "Redis (pub/sub + short-lived cache)". The Stream is a bounded circular buffer read with
    `XRANGE` — no consumer groups, no acknowledgements, no pending-entries list — and is
    argued in §30.4.6 to be a short-lived cache rather than a queue. If the editor reads the
    scope line more strictly, see note 7: dropping replay removes this key and nothing else.

11. **The `auth` control frame and the `ready` / `closing` control frames are new wire
    vocabulary.** They are not `RealtimePayload` members and never reach a `subscribe` handler,
    so they do not touch the frontend's union or its "unknown types are ignored" rule
    (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`). They are recorded here because they are the only part of the
    protocol that is not in canon at all.

12. **Canon's endpoint count is unchanged at 140.** This section adds no endpoint. In
    particular it does **not** add a `POST /realtime/ticket`: authentication happens in the
    first application frame instead, which is why §30.2.3's argument against SSE is the
    deciding one rather than a preference.

---

## 31. Error Codes

Module ownership: every module in canon C-14 produces errors, so this chapter is owned by none of
them and binds all of them. It is the normative catalogue behind canon §4 and §7.4 of this
document. Where §7.4 states the envelope rules, this chapter states the **values**: every
`ErrorReason` the service may emit, the HTTP status and `AppErrorCode` each maps to, the exact
copy the frontend renders, the structured `details` each carries, and what the frontend does when
it arrives.

### 31.0 The one thing that is frozen, and the one thing that is not

There are two vocabularies and they are not interchangeable.

**`AppErrorCode` is frozen at eight values.** `src/types/async.ts:2-10`. It is not decoration: the
client branches on it in three places that ship today —

| Site | What it does with `code` |
| --- | --- |
| `src/hooks/use-embedded-board.ts:138-141` | `error.code === "not_found"` → renders the embed as **missing**, not as a failure. Any other code renders an error panel. |
| `src/components/shared/async-boundary.tsx:32-36` | `state.error.code === "permission_denied"` → `PermissionDeniedState` (no retry control); anything else → `ErrorState` (retry control, if retryable). |
| `src/components/board/board-page.tsx:133-138` | The same split, hand-written for the board because the board owns its own loading shell. |

and a fourth derives the retry default from it:

```ts
// src/services/errors.ts:28-31
return { code, message, detail, isRetryable: isRetryable ?? DEFAULT_RETRYABLE.has(code) };
const DEFAULT_RETRYABLE = new Set<AppErrorCode>(["network", "upload_failed", "unknown"]);
```

Adding a ninth code, renaming one, or changing which code an existing failure carries is a
**breaking change to a shipped client**. It does not happen inside `v1`.

**`ErrorReason` is additive and is where all the precision lives.** Eight codes cannot specify a
backend: "conflict" covers a locked page, a slug collision, a cycle in the subtask tree and a
board that already holds the records being moved. So every error carries a second field —
`reason`, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, one value per distinguishable failure. Canon §4.3 registers 104 of
them. The frontend ignores `reason` today; the backend, the logs, support and every future client
branch on it.

**The mapping is a function, not a table lookup in both directions.** One `reason` → exactly one
`code` and exactly one HTTP status. Many reasons share a code. A writer specifying a failure names
the **reason**; the code and the status follow from §31.4 and are never chosen independently.

---

### 31.1 The error envelope

Success has no envelope — the body is the resource (§7.3). **Errors, and only errors, are
wrapped**, in the one wrapper the frontend actually declares:

```ts
// src/types/board.ts:507-509 — EXISTING REQUIREMENT
export interface BoardError {
  readonly error: AppError;
}
```

The wire shape, complete:

```ts
/**
 * The API error envelope. `ErrorResponse` is the canon name for what the frontend
 * calls `BoardError`; the JSON is identical.
 */
interface ErrorResponse {
  readonly error: ApiError;
}

/**
 * The four fields at the top are EXISTING REQUIREMENT — src/types/async.ts:12-20.
 * They must not change name, type, optionality or meaning inside /api/v1.
 * Everything below the divider is RECOMMENDATION and additive; the frontend
 * ignores all of it today and must keep compiling if it appears.
 */
interface ApiError {
  readonly code: AppErrorCode;                 // one of eight — §31.2
  readonly message: string;                    // rendered to the user VERBATIM
  readonly detail?: string;                    // OPTIONAL, never nullable — omit the key
  readonly isRetryable: boolean;               // drives the "Try again" control
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ additive
  readonly reason?: ErrorReason;               // §31.4 — 104 values
  readonly requestId?: string;                 // ULID, echoed from X-Request-Id (§7.10)
  readonly fields?: readonly FieldError[];     // VALIDATION_FAILED only — §31.5.1
  readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number;         // 429 only — §7.9
  readonly details?: ErrorDetails;             // structured payload per reason — §31.5
}

/** One failed field. For developers and support; the user still reads `message`. */
interface FieldError {
  /** Pointer into the request body: `cells[0].value.iso`, `entries[3].key`. */
  readonly path: string;
  readonly reason: ErrorReason;
  /** Sentence for a form control that can render an inline error. */
  readonly message: string;
}
```

`ApiError` is a superset of the frontend's `AppError`. A response body assigned to `AppError`
compiles unchanged; the five additive keys are excess properties the structural type ignores.

Worked example — a locked page refusing a save (E-092):

```jsonc
// 409 PUT /api/v1/nodes/01J8.../document
{
  "error": {
    "code": "conflict",
    "message": "This page is locked",
    "detail": "Unlock it before saving further changes.",
    "isRetryable": false,
    "reason": "DOCUMENT_LOCKED",
    "requestId": "01JB9Z7QF3K8W2N6R4T5Y0X1M3",
    "details": {
      "reason": "DOCUMENT_LOCKED",
      "nodeId": "01J8C4V7QZ9K2M5N8P1R3T6W0X",
      "lockedBy": {
        "id": "01J7A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9J0K1L2",
        "name": "Khanh Luu",
        "email": "khanhluu95@gmail.com",
        "initials": "KL"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `message` and `detail` are verbatim from `src/services/document-service.ts:193`. Nothing in
`details` is rendered; the panel renders `message` as its title and `detail` as its body
(`src/components/shared/state-panels.tsx:118-128`).

**Nine rules bind the envelope.** Six restate §7.4 because a writer reading only this chapter must
still get them right; three are new here.

| # | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V-1 | `detail` is **optional, not nullable**. Omit the key. `"detail": null` violates C-08 and would render the string `null` in nothing — but it is still wrong, because `detail?: string` says absent, not empty. | `src/types/async.ts:17` |
| V-2 | The **body is authoritative, the status is advisory**. `toAppError` never sees a status code — it normalises a thrown object and nothing else (`src/services/errors.ts:52-64`). Send a complete `ApiError` on every failure including `500`, `502` and `503`. A status with an empty or non-JSON body reaches the client as `{ code: "unknown", message: "Something went wrong" }` and the user learns nothing. | `src/services/errors.ts:52-64` |
| V-3 | `isRetryable` is set **explicitly** whenever it differs from the §31.2 default. The two that matter: `429` (code `validation`, default `false`, must be `true`) and a `conflict` that genuinely is worth retrying (there is none today — every `conflict` in §31.4 is `false`). | canon §4.4 rule 5 |
| V-4 | **A refusal must not name what was denied.** `permission_denied` copy is deliberately name-free — *"A refusal that reads 'Finance is restricted' hands the name of a private folder to the one person who was told they may not have it"* (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-161`). This governs `message`, `detail` **and** `details`. §31.9.2 lists what may appear in a refusal. | `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-165` |
| V-5 | `not_found` messages use the fixed template `` `${what} could not be found` `` and nothing else. The `what` values are enumerated in §31.4 and come straight from the service call sites. | `src/services/errors.ts:36-37` |
| V-6 | **Never return an error body for a partial success.** `BulkResult`, `BulkMoveResult` and `ImportOutcome` are `200`s that report what did and did not apply. `requested === applied.length + skipped.length` is the invariant. §31.6. | `src/services/board-service.ts:958-965` |
| V-7 | `details` is **machine-readable only**. Nothing in it is ever rendered. If a fact needs to reach the user it goes in `message` or `detail` as a sentence. This is why `details` may safely carry ids while `message` may not. | new here; follows from V-4 and `state-panels.tsx:118-128` |
| V-8 | `details.reason` **repeats** `error.reason`. The duplication is deliberate: it makes `ErrorDetails` a self-contained discriminated union that a client can narrow without reading its parent, satisfying C-05. A response where the two disagree is a server bug. | new here |
| V-9 | `requestId` is echoed on **every** response, success and failure. In an error it also appears in the body so a user can paste it into a support ticket from a screenshot. It never appears inside `message` or `detail`. | §7.10 |

---

### 31.2 `AppErrorCode` → HTTP → default retryability → what the frontend does

| `code` | HTTP | Default `isRetryable` | Meaning | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validation` | **400** (also 413, 415, 429) | `false` | The request is malformed, or breaks a business rule the caller can fix by changing the request. | **Read:** `ErrorState` panel, title = `message`, body = `detail`, **no** Try again (not retryable). **Write:** optimistic state reverted, toast with `message`. **Wizard/form:** rendered inline in the panel (`use-import-wizard.ts:136-150`). |
| `permission_denied` | **403** (and **401**, mapped) | `false` | Authenticated but not permitted — or not authenticated at all. | **Dedicated screen**: `PermissionDeniedState`, shield icon, no Try again control, default body *"Ask a workspace admin to grant you access."* (`async-boundary.tsx:32-33`, `board-page.tsx:134`, `state-panels.tsx:130-138`). **Write:** toast only. On `reason: AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` the HTTP client refreshes once and replays instead (§8, and §31.3 B-8). |
| `not_found` | **404** | `false` | The resource does not exist **or the caller may not see it**. The two answer identically (§31.9.1). | **Embedded board:** status becomes `missing` — an empty-state, not an error (`use-embedded-board.ts:138-141`). **Everywhere else:** `ErrorState` with no Try again. **Write:** revert + toast; the store drops the local copy of the id. |
| `conflict` | **409** | `false` | A precondition or invariant refuses the write. The caller can usually fix it by reloading and retrying deliberately — never automatically. | Revert + toast. Never auto-retried: a `conflict` re-sent unchanged fails identically, and re-sending a *stale* write is the failure mode `expectedVersion` exists to stop. |
| `upload_failed` | **422** (object did not land) / **507** (out of space) | `true` | The bytes did not land. | The upload task row goes to `status: "error"` and shows a **Retry** control because `task.error?.isRetryable` (`src/components/files/upload-task-row.tsx:66-72`). The retry payload is kept (`src/store/upload-store.ts:88`). |
| `network` | **502 / 503** | `true` | A dependency — object store, database, unfurl target — is unreachable. | `ErrorState` **with** Try again, wired to the resource's `reload()` (`state-panels.tsx:126`, `use-async-resource.ts:84`). |
| `unknown` | **500** | `true` | Unclassified server fault. `message` is `Something went wrong`; the original text goes in `detail` **in non-production only**. | `ErrorState` with Try again. |
| `cancelled` | *never a response* | `false` | Client-side abort only. Produced by `toAppError` from a `DOMException` named `AbortError` (`src/services/errors.ts:55-57`). | **Swallowed everywhere.** Four separate stores drop it before it can reach a panel or a toast (§31.3 B-6). **The server must never emit this code.** C-12. |

Two statuses have no `AppErrorCode` of their own and must be mapped rather than invented:

- **`401`** → `code: "permission_denied"`, with `reason` one of `AUTH_REQUIRED`,
  `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED`, `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED`. The client cannot tell
  401 from 403 by code alone, which is precisely why the refresh interceptor branches on `reason`
  (§8.3, J-5).
- **`429`** → `code: "validation"`, `isRetryable: true` **set explicitly** (V-3), plus
  `retryAfterSeconds` in the body and a `Retry-After` header (§7.9).

**Two statuses that are deliberately never used.** `201` — a create returns `200` with the record,
because the frontend treats a create response exactly like an update response and introducing a
second success status adds a branch nobody has. `304` — there is no `ETag`/`If-None-Match` layer;
freshness comes from realtime frames and explicit refetch.

---

### 31.3 The frontend behaviour vocabulary

The **Frontend behaviour** column in §31.4 uses these ten labels. Each is a real code path, cited.
A backend developer choosing between two candidate reasons should pick the one whose behaviour is
what the user should actually get.

| # | Label | What happens | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **B-1** | **Permission screen** | The whole surface is replaced by `PermissionDeniedState`: shield icon, title = `message`, body = `detail` or the fallback *"Ask a workspace admin to grant you access."* There is **no retry control**, regardless of `isRetryable`. | `src/components/shared/async-boundary.tsx:32-33`; `src/components/board/board-page.tsx:133-135`; `src/components/shared/state-panels.tsx:130-138` |
| **B-2** | **Error panel, retryable** | `ErrorState`: warning icon, title = `message`, body = `detail` or *"The request did not complete. Nothing was changed."*, plus a **Try again** button wired to `reload()`. Shown only when `isRetryable && onRetry`. | `src/components/shared/state-panels.tsx:119-128`; `src/hooks/use-async-resource.ts:84` |
| **B-3** | **Error panel, terminal** | The same panel with **no** button, because `isRetryable` is false. The user's only move is to change something and act again. | `state-panels.tsx:126` (the conditional) |
| **B-4** | **Revert + toast** | A write path. The store rolls the optimistic state back and pushes `error.message` as a danger toast. The counter is settled in `finally` so the pending-write badge cannot stick. | `src/store/board-store.ts:188-202`; `src/hooks/use-embedded-board.ts:126-129`; `src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:113-117, 126-129, 149-153, 191-193` |
| **B-5** | **Missing, not failed** | `not_found` on an embedded board becomes `status: "missing"` — the embed renders its own empty state rather than an error. A deleted board inside a page is not an error on the page. | `src/hooks/use-embedded-board.ts:134-141` |
| **B-6** | **Silent** | The error is dropped before it reaches any surface. Four stores do this for `cancelled`, and `useAsyncResource` additionally drops anything that arrives after `signal.aborted`. | `use-async-resource.ts:58-62`; `board-store.ts:198`; `notification-store.ts:68`; `upload-store.ts:80-86` |
| **B-7** | **Upload row + retry** | The task in the upload tray shows `status: "error"` with the `AppError` attached, and a Retry control appears when `isRetryable`. The file and destination are cached so the retry needs no new picker. | `src/components/files/upload-task-row.tsx:66-72`; `src/store/upload-store.ts:79-89` |
| **B-8** | **Refresh session, replay once** | The shared HTTP client sees `reason === "AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED"`, calls `POST /auth/refresh`, and replays the original request exactly once. Only on failure does the error reach a surface as B-1. **RECOMMENDATION** (OQ-01), specified in §8.7. | §8.3 J-4/J-5; §8.7 |
| **B-9** | **Inline in the wizard** | The import wizard holds an `AppError` in local state and renders it in the dialog beside the controls that produced it — not as a toast, because the user is mid-flow and the fix is one field away. | `src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:136-150, 244-254` |
| **B-10** | **Re-resolve access, drop what is gone** | Not an error path at all: an `RT-05 permission.changed` frame arrives, the client re-resolves its own access and discards anything it may no longer hold. This is what turns a would-be `403` on the *next* request into no request at all. | `src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`; `src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`; canon §7.1 RT-05 |

**The write-path default is B-4.** Every service call the stores make is wrapped in a try/catch that
calls `toAppError` and pushes `message` as a toast; the read-path default is B-2 or B-3 depending on
`isRetryable`. When §31.4 names a behaviour, it names the *distinctive* one — the row for
`DOCUMENT_LOCKED` says B-4 because a locked page refuses a save, and the save is a write.

---

### 31.4 The `ErrorReason` catalogue

104 reasons, grouped by the module that owns the endpoints producing them (canon C-14). Two further
rows — `TRASH_RESTORE_RELOCATED` and `PREVIEW_UNSUPPORTED` — appear at the end of §31.6 because
they are `200` outcomes recorded here only so no chapter mistakes them for failures.

Columns: **Reason** · **HTTP** · **`code`** · **Meaning, and the message the API sends** ·
**Frontend behaviour**. Where a message is quoted with `` ` `` it is **verbatim from the frontend**
and must not be reworded; `${…}` marks interpolation. Where a message is unquoted the frontend has
no copy for it and the text is a **RECOMMENDATION** following the rules in §31.7.

#### 31.4.1 Authentication and session — `identity`

Endpoints E-001 … E-006. Every reason here is **RECOMMENDATION** under **OQ-01** — the frontend has
no authentication of any kind (§8.1). They are catalogued because §8 needs them and because
`AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` is the one reason the HTTP client is required to branch on.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | `permission_denied` | No valid session on a protected route. `Sign in to continue` · detail `Your session is not active on this device.` | B-1. The client has no signed-out state (`src/types/async.ts:23-27`), so this renders as a permission screen until §8's route guard lands. |
| `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | `permission_denied` | Email or password wrong. **The same message, and the same response timing, for a wrong password, an unknown email and a deactivated account** (§8, R-12): `Those credentials did not work` · detail `Check the email address and password and try again.` | B-3 on the login form (E-001 has no session to screen). |
| `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` | 401 | `permission_denied` | The access token is past `exp`, its session was revoked, or the user was deactivated. `Your session has expired` · detail `Sign in again to continue.` | **B-8** — this is the one reason the client must not surface directly. Refresh once, replay, and only then fall through to B-1. |
| `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` | 401 | `permission_denied` | A refresh token was presented twice. The whole family is revoked in the same transaction (§8, R-6). `Your session has expired` · detail `Sign in again to continue.` — **deliberately identical to `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED`**, so a replay attacker learns nothing from the copy. | B-1. The client must **not** retry the refresh; `reason` is what distinguishes the two. |
| `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | `validation` | Too many attempts, per IP **and** per submitted email (§7.9). `Too many attempts` · detail `` `Try again in ${n} seconds.` ``. `isRetryable: true` **explicit**, `retryAfterSeconds` set. | B-3 with a countdown; the form disables submit until the window passes. |
| `INVITATION_INVALID` | 404 | `not_found` | The token is unknown, already consumed, or expired (E-019). `That invitation could not be found` · detail `Ask for a new invitation link.` | B-3. **RECOMMENDATION** under OQ-04. |

#### 31.4.2 Workspaces and membership — `workspace`

Endpoints E-007 … E-019.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | An unknown workspace **or one the caller is not a member of**. The two answer identically — *"a workspace that does not exist and one the person is not in return the same shape on purpose: the surface shows the same screen either way, so the URL cannot be used to learn which workspaces exist"* (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:60-64`). `That workspace could not be found` | B-3, via `WorkspaceGuard`, which already renders one screen for both cases (`src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:22-25`). |
| `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` | 409 | `conflict` | The slug is not unique across the tenant (`src/types/workspace.ts:17-18` — "unique across the tenant"). `That workspace address is already taken` · detail `` `Try “${suggestion}”.` `` | B-4. `details` carries the free suggestion `uniqueSlug` would have produced. |
| `WORKSPACE_NAME_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | Empty, or past 60 characters. Messages verbatim from the frontend validator: `Give the workspace a name.` / `` `Keep the name under ${WORKSPACE_NAME_MAX} characters.` `` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:196-207`). | B-3 inline on the create dialog, which already renders exactly these strings before the button is enabled. |
| `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` | 409 | `conflict` | The change would leave the workspace with no admin. The frontend has three guards that read `isLastAdmin` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157`); the API must be the fourth and the authoritative one. `The workspace needs at least one admin` · detail `Make somebody else an admin first.` | B-4. Applies to E-014 (demotion), E-015 (removal) and E-016 (leaving). |
| `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | No such membership on this workspace. `That member could not be found` | B-4. |
| `MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` | 409 | `conflict` | Already a member, or already holding a live invitation. `That person is already in this workspace` · detail `Change their role instead.` | B-4. |
| `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | **507** | `upload_failed` | The upload would push `usedBytes` past `totalBytes` (`src/types/workspace.ts:5-10`). `` `“${fileName}” would exceed the workspace storage limit` `` · detail `` `${used} of ${total} used.` `` | **B-7** — it arrives on an upload, so it lands on the task row. `isRetryable` is `true` by the code's default, which is correct: freeing space and retrying is exactly the fix. **OQ-05.** |

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-05) — nothing maintains `usedBytes`, and no rule says what happens at 100 %.**
>
> **Evidence** — `StorageQuota` is two numbers on the workspace (`src/types/workspace.ts:5-10`),
> seeded at `{ usedBytes: 0, totalBytes: 15 GiB }` by `makeWorkspace`
> (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:239`) and never incremented anywhere. `validateUpload`
> (`src/lib/file-validation.ts:28-58`) checks emptiness, size and extension — **never the quota**.
> No surface renders a quota refusal.
>
> **Recommendation** — as canon §8.8 takes it: `workspaces.used_bytes` maintained transactionally
> with every `file_assets` insert and delete, checked at **E-110** (issue the presigned target)
> rather than at E-111, so the bytes are never uploaded at all. `507` + `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` +
> `details.usedBytes/totalBytes/requestedBytes`.
>
> **Impact if wrong** — checking at E-111 instead means a 90 MB upload completes over a slow link
> and is then refused, which is the worst possible place to learn. Not checking at all means the
> product has a storage plan it does not enforce.

#### 31.4.3 Permissions, access and audit — `governance`

Endpoints E-040 … E-046, E-136, E-137, plus the three narrowing layers that apply to **every** write
in the system.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | 403 | `permission_denied` | The generic refusal, and by volume the most common error in the system — it guards all 140 endpoints (P-09). Message `` `You do not have permission to ${action}` ``, detail `requirementFor(key)` → `` `Needs the ${Role} role or above` `` — both verbatim from `src/services/authz.ts:67-74`. `${action}` is the endpoint's own phrase (`add a column`, `change this column's type`, `import into this board`); §31.7.3 lists them. | B-1 on a read, B-4 on a write. **`details` carries `requiredKey` and `requiredRole` and nothing else** — never the node, never who does hold it (V-4). |
| `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` | 403 | `permission_denied` | A trashed node accepts **nothing but `node.delete`**. Resolved before the permission key is consulted (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:69-88`). `That item is in Trash` · detail `Restore it before making changes.` | B-4. The client should already have hidden the control; the API is the refusal. |
| `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` | 403 | `permission_denied` | An archived **ancestor** refuses every write. The node's own archive flag is deliberately **not** read for this — *"you can always restore the thing you are standing on, but a page inside an archived project cannot be thawed on its own"* (`src/lib/archive.ts:30-36`). `` `“${ancestorName}” is archived` `` · detail `Restore it to make changes below it.` | B-4. **This is the one `permission_denied` that may name a node**: the frontend already renders the ancestor's name on screen — *"Inside the archived project “Acme Rebuild” — this board is read-only until that project is restored"* (`src/components/shared/archived-banner.tsx:36-42`, fed by `archiveSourceOf`) — so the name is not a secret, and the caller can already see the node. |
| `NODE_LOCKED` | 403 | `permission_denied` | A document lock refuses the content-write key set. The lock never blocks the unlock itself (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:63-64`). See also `DOCUMENT_LOCKED`, which is the same situation reported by the document endpoint as a `conflict` — §31.9.4 explains why both exist. | B-4. |
| `PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES` | 400 | `validation` | A `previewAs` parameter naming a role that outranks the caller's real role. Preview may only **narrow**. `A preview cannot grant more access than you hold` | B-3. **OQ-21.** |
| `ACCESS_RULE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | E-043 on an id that is not a rule on that node. `That access rule could not be found` | B-4. |
| `ACCESS_SUBJECT_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | The subject is neither `{ kind: "user", userId }` nor `{ kind: "role", role }` (`src/types/permission.ts:132-134`), or names a user who is not a member of the workspace. `That person is not in this workspace` | B-3, inline in the access dialog. |

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-16) — 40+ write operations carry no permission check in the mock.**
>
> **Evidence** — `requirePermission` is called at exactly nine sites, all in `board-service.ts` and
> `devtools-service.ts` (`src/services/authz.ts:67-74` and its callers). `createRow`,
> `updateCells`, every bulk operation, every view write, every comment write, every watch write and
> every document write reach the store with no check at all. The module says so itself: *"there is
> no server here… a faithful model of the check a real API must make, not a substitute for it"*
> (`src/services/authz.ts:29-33`).
>
> **Recommendation** — every endpoint re-checks the `PermissionKey` its row in canon §3 names,
> server-side, before any other validation, and emits `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The **Perm** column of
> canon §3 is normative, not advisory.
>
> **Impact if wrong** — the entire RBAC matrix (`SY-RBC-42`) becomes decoration. A downgraded user
> in a stale tab keeps every capability the tab was rendered with, which is precisely the scenario
> `SY-RBC-42`'s "a downgrade takes effect on open screens" exists to prevent.

#### 31.4.4 Drive tree — `drive`

Endpoints E-020 … E-035.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | An unknown node, **or one the caller may not see**. §31.9.1. `That item could not be found` | B-3 on a read; B-4 on a write, and the store drops its local copy. |
| `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT` | 409 | `conflict` | The slug is taken among the target's siblings. *"two siblings sharing one is not a cosmetic clash: `resolvePath` walks the chain and takes the first match, so the loser becomes unreachable and every link to it silently opens the other"* (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:472-480`). `` `“${name}” already exists here` `` · detail `` `Saved as “${suggestion}”.` `` where the API de-duplicated, omitted where it refused. | B-4. In practice the API **de-duplicates rather than refusing** on create and move (`uniqueSlug`), so this reason fires only where the caller demanded an exact slug. |
| `NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT` | 409 | `conflict` | `same-parent` — the node is already there. `That item is already there` | B-6-adjacent: the frontend's drag layer never issues this call (`src/lib/tree.ts:170-197` rejects it client-side), so the API refusal exists only for a non-UI caller. Treat as success in a client. |
| `NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF` | 409 | `conflict` | `into-self`. `An item cannot be moved into itself` | B-4. |
| `NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT` | 409 | `conflict` | `into-descendant` — the cycle rule. `` `“${name}” cannot be moved into something inside it` `` | B-4. |
| `NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET` | 409 | `conflict` | `invalid-target` — the destination is missing, trashed, or not a container. `That is not a place items can go` | B-4. |
| `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` | 409 | `conflict` | A document, board or file was addressed as a parent on create. `Pages can only live inside folders` | B-4. Distinct from `NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET`: that one is a move, this one is a create (E-024). |
| `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` | 409 | `conflict` | The node exists but is not the kind this route addresses — `GET /nodes/{id}/board` on a document node. Grounded: `if (!node || !isBoard(node)) throw notFound("That board")` (`src/services/board-service.ts:85`) collapses both cases into `not_found`; **the API separates them**, because a caller holding the id already knows the node exists. `That item is not a board` | B-3. See the note below. |
| `NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED` | 409 | `conflict` | E-031 restore on a node whose **ancestor** is archived. `` `“${ancestorName}” is archived` `` · detail `Restore it first.` | B-4. |
| `NODE_NAME_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | Empty after trimming, or past the name ceiling. The frontend refuses an empty rename silently (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:483-485`); the API must say why. `Give it a name` | B-3. |
| `TRASH_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | E-037/E-038 on an unknown entry id. `That item could not be found` | B-4. |

**A note on `NODE_KIND_MISMATCH` versus `NODE_NOT_FOUND`.** The frontend collapses "no such node"
and "wrong kind of node" into one `notFound("That board")`. The API must not, and the reason is
security-neutral: reaching `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` requires the caller to already hold `nodeId`
and to have passed the visibility check, so they already know the node exists and what it is called.
Answering `404` there would send a client into B-5 (render as missing) for a node that is sitting in
its own sidebar. **Where visibility fails, the answer is `NODE_NOT_FOUND` and nothing else.**

#### 31.4.5 Trash and system-wide operations — `system`

Endpoints E-036 … E-039, E-139, E-140.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TRASH_ALREADY_PURGED` | 404 | `not_found` | The entry was swept by the retention job between the list read and the restore. `That item could not be found` · detail `` `Items are removed permanently after ${TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS} days.` `` | B-4; the row disappears from the list on the next read. **RECOMMENDATION**, OQ-14. |
| `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | `validation` | The body is past the service limit. Not the same as `FILE_TOO_LARGE`: this is the JSON body, and the two ceilings are different numbers. `That request was too large` | B-4. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | `validation` | The general or link-unfurl throttle (§7.9). `Too many requests` · detail `` `Try again in ${n} seconds.` ``. `isRetryable: true` **explicit**. | B-2 — the retry control is correct here and the only place a `validation` error gets one. |
| `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` | 409 | `conflict` | A generic optimistic-concurrency refusal. **Never used for cell writes** — those are last-write-wins with a `ConflictNotice` and always answer `200` (E-066, §31.6). `This was changed by somebody else` · detail `Reload to see the current version.` | B-4. |
| `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | `network` | Postgres, Redis or the object store is unreachable. Message verbatim from the frontend's own constructor: `Could not reach the workspace service` (`src/services/errors.ts:39-40`). | **B-2** — the Try again button, and the only common error where an automatic client retry with backoff is also appropriate. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | `unknown` | Anything unclassified. `Something went wrong` — verbatim from `toAppError` (`src/services/errors.ts:60`). The original text goes in `detail` **in non-production only**; in production `detail` is omitted entirely and the text lives only in the log line keyed by `requestId`. | B-2. |

#### 31.4.6 Boards and records — `boards`

Endpoints E-047 … E-050, E-061 … E-073.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That board could not be found` — verbatim, `src/services/board-service.ts:85`. | B-5 in an embedded board (`use-embedded-board.ts:140`); B-3 on the board page. |
| `ROW_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That record could not be found` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:153` (`rowOrThrow`). | B-4; the drawer closes and the row is dropped from the local map. |
| `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That parent record could not be found` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:302` and `:388`. | B-4. |
| `ROW_PARENT_SELF` | 409 | `conflict` | `A record cannot be its own parent` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:384`. | B-4. |
| `ROW_PARENT_CYCLE` | 409 | `conflict` | `` `${parent.displayId} is already under ${row.displayId}` `` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:390`. Both display ids are already on the caller's screen, so naming them is safe. | B-4. |
| `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD` | 409 | `conflict` | Parent and child must share a board. `That record is on another board` · detail `Subtasks live on the same board as their parent.` **OQ-33.** | B-4. |
| `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` | 409 | `conflict` | Past the hierarchy depth cap. `` `Subtasks can only go ${MAX_SUBTASK_DEPTH} levels deep` `` **OQ-33** — canon §8.8 takes depth 5. | B-4. |
| `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` | 409 | `conflict` | An archived record is read-only until restored (`src/types/board.ts:250-254`). `That record is archived` · detail `Restore it before making changes.` | B-4. **In bulk this is not an error** — it is a `BulkSkip` with `reason: "archived"` inside a `200` (§31.6). |
| `ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | Not `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` after normalisation (`src/lib/row-id.ts:9,17-20`). `A record prefix is one to six capital letters` | B-3, inline in board settings. **OQ-43** governs whether it may change at all once rows exist. |
| `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | The `CellValue` tag is not a `ColumnType` member. **Note carefully what this does *not* cover:** a `kind` that disagrees with its column's `type` is **legal** and must be stored as sent — *"A converted column can therefore keep the text it could not parse instead of dropping the user's data"* (`src/types/board.ts:214-218`). Only an unknown tag is an error. `That value is not one this column understands` | B-4. |
| `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | Not `YYYY-MM-DD` on a date-only column, or not ISO 8601 on a timestamp column. C-04, **OQ-32**. `That is not a date` | B-4. |

#### 31.4.7 Columns, options and transition rules — `boards`

Endpoints E-051 … E-060, and the select gate that fires on E-066 and E-074.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That column could not be found` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:604, 660, 691, 732, 736`. | B-4. |
| `SELECT_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | Missing **or not of type `select`** — the frontend collapses both: `if (!column \|\| column.type !== "select") throw notFound("That select column")` (`board-service.ts:770`). `That select column could not be found`. Kept as one reason because, unlike the node case, the caller is addressing a column *by role* rather than by identity. | B-4. |
| `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED` | 409 | `conflict` | `` `“${target.name}” titles every record and cannot be deleted` `` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:694`. Also the refusal for converting or unsetting the primary column. | B-4. |
| `COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` | 400 | `validation` | The `config` does not match the branch named by `type` — a `SelectConfig` on a `date` column. The seven branches are `ColumnConfigByType` (`src/types/board.ts:162-170`). `That column setting does not match its type` · `fields` names the offending path. | B-4. |
| `COLUMN_NAME_CONFLICT` | 409 | `conflict` | Only where the caller demanded an exact name. Creation otherwise **de-duplicates silently** to `Notes`, `Notes 2`, … — *"Two columns called the same thing is how a board becomes ambiguous — to the person reading it, and to the importer, which pairs source columns to board columns by name"* (`board-service.ts:550-554`). `` `“${name}” is already a column here` `` | B-4. |
| `COLUMN_CONVERT_UNSUPPORTED` | 409 | `conflict` | No conversion path between the two types. **Rare by design**: the conversion engine preserves anything it cannot parse as `CellValue.text` rather than refusing (`board-service.ts:720-757`), so this fires only where the target type has no text escape hatch at all. `` `A ${from} column cannot become a ${to} column` `` | B-4. |
| `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | E-059/E-060 on an unknown option id. `That option could not be found` | B-4. |
| `OPTION_ID_RESERVED` | 400 | `validation` | `"__empty__"` is the reserved key standing for the empty bucket on both sides of a transition (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:27-28`). A user-authored option may not claim it. `That option id is reserved` | B-4. |
| `OPTION_LABEL_EMPTY` | 400 | `validation` | An option label that is empty after trimming. `Give the option a name` | B-3. |
| `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` | 409 | `conflict` | The select column's transition rules refuse this move. The message is verbatim from `evaluateTransition` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:118-132`) and **names the way out, not just the wrong turn** — *"a rejection worth reading tells you the way out"* (`:98-100`): `` `${column} cannot go straight from ${from} to ${to}. ${from} can move to ${a}, ${b}.` ``, or `` `… ${from} has no permitted moves.` `` when the source is a dead end. **Clearing a status is always legal; only arriving somewhere is gated** (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:77-80`). Two rules make this fire less than it looks: the whole gate is off unless `transitionRules.enabled`, and **a status the table does not mention is not governed** (`:114-115`), so adding an option never freezes the board around it. | B-4. The Kanban drag is reverted and the card returns to its column. |
| `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` | 409 | `conflict` | The option's `availability` conditions do not hold for this record, or it is `isDisabled`. Messages verbatim: `Turned off in column settings` (`select-availability.ts:88`) or `` `Requires ${describeConditionGroup(...)}` `` (`:99`). | B-4. |
| `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` | 400 | `validation` | Past the nesting or size cap on a `ConditionGroup`. `That rule is too complex` · detail `` `Rules can nest ${maxDepth} levels deep and hold ${maxConditions} conditions.` `` **OQ-38.** | B-3, inline in the rule builder. |

**One rule binds this whole group and is easy to get wrong.** Transition rules and option
availability are **record rules, not permission**: *"Permission answers 'may this person edit Status
at all'; a transition rule answers 'may Status go from here to there'. Both are checked, separately,
before a drop is written"* (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:22-24`; the same statement again at
`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:15-17`). They therefore produce `conflict`, never `permission_denied`,
and they are evaluated **after** `row.update` has already passed. Emitting `permission_denied` for a
refused transition would send the user to a permission screen (B-1) for a rule that has nothing to
do with their role.

**And one rule about creating an option, which is a `200` and not an error.** *"Creating an option
must dedupe by trimmed, case-insensitive label and return the existing option with `200`, never
`409`"* (canon §1.3.3, OQ-53). E-058 has no `OPTION_LABEL_DUPLICATE` reason and must not grow one.

#### 31.4.8 Saved views — `views`

Endpoints E-078 … E-083.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `VIEW_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That view could not be found` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:806`. | B-4; the board falls back to its first view. |
| `VIEW_LAST_REMAINING` | 409 | `conflict` | `A board needs at least one view` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:889-891`. | B-4. |
| `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN` | 400 | `validation` | A kanban view with no `groupByColumnId`, or a calendar/gantt view with no `dateColumnId`. `` `A ${type} view needs a ${field} column` `` · `details` names which. | B-3, inline in the view editor. |
| `VIEW_COLUMN_UNKNOWN` | 400 | `validation` | A `columnId` in `filters`, `sorts`, `columnOrder`, `columnWidths`, `columnDisplay`, `hiddenColumnIds`, `groupByColumnId`, `dateColumnId` or `endDateColumnId` that is not on the board. **The API prunes rather than refusing on a column delete** (E-054 "prunes every view of references in the same transaction"); this reason is for a client that *sends* an unknown id. `That column is not on this board` | B-4. |
| `VIEW_NAME_EMPTY` | 400 | `validation` | Empty after trimming. `Give the view a name` | B-3. |

**`GanttZoom` never produces an error.** A saved view may still hold `"day"`, a scale that was
removed. **The API accepts `"day"` on write and on read and coerces it to `"week"`** — it never
rejects it (`src/types/board.ts:272-281`, `normalizeGanttZoom`). There is no
`VIEW_ZOOM_INVALID` reason and no chapter may add one without a data migration first.

#### 31.4.9 Bulk operations — `system` + `boards`

Endpoints E-074 … E-077. **Read §31.6 before this table**: almost everything that goes wrong in a
bulk call is *not* an error.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BULK_TARGET_BOARD_SAME` | 409 | `conflict` | `Those records are already on that board` — verbatim, `board-service.ts:1098`. | B-4. |
| `BULK_TARGET_NOT_A_BOARD` | 409 | `conflict` | `targetNodeId` does not address a board. `That is not a board` · detail `Pick a board to move the records into.` **OQ-17** — the frontend verifies neither the target's kind nor either board's permissions. | B-4. |
| `BULK_SELECTION_EMPTY` | 400 | `validation` | `rowIds` is empty. The frontend never sends it, but an empty bulk write that answers `200` with `requested: 0` is indistinguishable from a silent no-op. `Select at least one record` | B-3. |
| `BULK_SELECTION_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | `validation` | Past the per-call selection ceiling. `` `Bulk actions handle up to ${limit} records at a time` `` **RECOMMENDATION** — the frontend caps nothing. | B-3. |

Everything else a bulk call meets is a `BulkSkip` inside a `200`: a row that is archived
(`reason: "archived"`), a row that no longer exists (`reason: "not_found"`), and — once server-side
ACLs land — a row the caller may not touch. The frontend's own comment settles the last one:
*"Per-row ACLs live on the backend; when they land they report through this same channel rather
than a second one"* (`src/types/system.ts:20-23`). Canon §2.7 therefore adds `permission_denied` to
`BulkSkipReason` rather than creating a parallel array.

#### 31.4.10 Import and export — `system`

Endpoints E-084 … E-086.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED` | 400 | `validation` | `ImportPlan.conflicts` is non-empty — the mapping is not runnable. `Finish the column mapping first` · `details.conflicts` carries the `MappingConflict[]` the wizard already knows how to render. | **B-9** — inline in the wizard, next to the mapping table. |
| `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 400 | `validation` | Past `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5 000` (`src/config/app.ts:48` — *"so a mis-picked file cannot flood a board"*). `` `That file has ${n} rows; the limit is ${IMPORT_MAX_ROWS}` `` | B-9. |
| `IMPORT_FILE_UNPARSEABLE` | 400 | `validation` | Not a readable `.xlsx` / `.csv` / `.tsv`. Message verbatim from the wizard's own client-side check: `` `“${file.name}” is not a spreadsheet` `` · detail `Import accepts .xlsx, .csv and .tsv files.` (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:138-142`). | B-9. |
| `IMPORT_COLUMN_CREATE_FAILED` | 409 | `conflict` | A column the plan said it would create could not be created — the wizard already models this outcome and its copy is unambiguous about the transaction: `` `Could not create the “${name}” column` `` · detail `Nothing was imported. Map that column onto an existing one and try again.` (`use-import-wizard.ts:246-252`). | B-9. **The detail is a promise the API must keep**: E-085 is one transaction (canon §3.11), so "nothing was imported" is literally true. |
| `EXPORT_SCOPE_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | `selection` with no ids, or `view` with no view. `Choose what to export` | B-3. |
| `EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` | 409 | `conflict` | The async whole-board export is still running. `That export is still being prepared` · detail `Try again in a moment.` **OQ-42.** | B-2 — retryable in substance; set `isRetryable: true` explicitly (V-3). |

**Row-level import errors are not errors.** They travel inside the `200` `ImportOutcome` as
`ImportIssue[]` — `{ rowNumber, sourceHeader, columnName, value, message }`
(`src/types/system.ts:101-108`) — with `rowNumber` being *"Row number in the file, header included —
what the sheet itself shows"*. The first `IMPORT_ISSUE_LIMIT = 50` are listed and the rest collapse
to a count (`src/config/app.ts:51`). A row whose value the column cannot parse is **skipped or
blanked** according to `ImportInvalidPolicy` (`src/types/system.ts:133-134`), never fatal. §31.5.4
gives the shape.

#### 31.4.11 Documents, versions and diffs — `documents`, `system`

Endpoints E-091 … E-098.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` | 409 | `conflict` | `This page is locked` · detail `Unlock it before saving further changes.` — verbatim, `document-service.ts:193`. | B-4. The editor keeps the user's text — it does **not** discard the draft on a failed save. |
| `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` | 409 | `conflict` | The `expectedVersion` on the save is stale. `This page was changed by somebody else` · detail `Reload to see their version before saving.` · `details` carries `currentVersion`, `expectedVersion`, `updatedAt` and `updatedBy`. **OQ-57.** | B-4, and the draft is kept. |
| `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | `validation` | Past the block-count or byte ceiling. `` `That page is too long to save` `` · detail `` `Pages hold up to ${maxBlocks} blocks.` `` **OQ-58.** | B-4. |
| `BLOCK_TYPE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` | 400 | `validation` | A block body that does not match its `type` — a `code` block with `images`, a `table` block with ragged rows (`src/types/document.ts:87-92`: *"Rectangular grid — every row carries the same number of cells"*). `That page could not be saved` · `fields` names the block. | B-4. |
| `VERSION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That version could not be found` — verbatim, `document-service.ts:132` and `devtools-service.ts:247`. | B-4. |
| `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` | 409 | `conflict` | A secret version has no snapshot and can never be diffed or restored — *"Such an entry can be read but never diffed or restored, because the client never holds the plaintext to restore"* (`src/types/system.ts:215-220`). `That version cannot be restored` · detail `A rotated secret records that it changed, not what it changed to.` | B-4. The history list already renders these rows without a Restore control, from `hasSnapshot: false`. |
| `DIFF_TARGET_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | `?against=` names a version on a different node, or a version with `hasSnapshot: false`. `Those versions cannot be compared` | B-3. |

Endpoints E-099 … E-109.

| Reason | HTTP | `code` | Meaning / message | Frontend behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN` | 400 | `validation` | Not one of the 15 `ConfigFormat` values. The enum is *"deliberately short and deliberately not extensible from data… so a document cannot be saved in a language nothing can colour"* (`src/types/devtools.ts:12-16`). `That is not a format this workspace can store` | B-4. |
| `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | An `environmentOptionId` that is not in the workspace's environment list (DV-ENV-21). `That environment could not be found` | B-4. |
| `ENVIRONMENT_IN_USE` | 409 | `conflict` | E-109 delete while a config document or secret still points at it. `` `“${label}” is still in use` `` · detail `` `${n} items point at it.` `` | B-4. **OQ-63.** |
| `ENVIRONMENT_LABEL_DUPLICATE` | 409 | `conflict` | Two environments with the same trimmed, case-folded label in one workspace. `` `“${label}” already exists` `` | B-4. **OQ-63.** |
| `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `not_found` | `That secret could not be found` / `Those secrets could not be found` — verbatim, `devtools-service.ts:340`, `:352` and `:436`. Note `:352`: the entry exists but no plaintext does, and it answers **the same way**, because distinguishing them would confirm a key's existence to somebody who cannot read it. | B-4. |
| `SECRET_KEY_INVALID` | 400 | `validation` | `` `“${key}” is not a usable name for a secret` `` · detail `A name cannot be empty or contain spaces, quotes or an equals sign.` — both verbatim, `devtools-service.ts:504-510`. | B-4. |
| `SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE` | 400 | `validation` | `` `“${key}” appears twice` `` · detail `Every secret in a document needs its own name.` — verbatim, `devtools-service.ts:515-521`. | B-4. |
| `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` | 403 | `permission_denied` | `` `Revealing ${entry.key} needs the Admin role` `` · detail `Ask a workspace admin to share it with you.` — verbatim, `devtools-service.ts:345-348`. For the multi-key path: `Copying these values needs the Admin role` · `Ask a workspace admin to share them with you.` (`:440-443`). **Two audit rows are written before the refusal returns** — §31.9.3. | B-4. This is the one `permission_denied` the frontend surfaces as a toast rather than a screen, because the reveal happens inside an open document. |
| `SECRET_ROTATE_DENIED` | 403 | `permission_denied` | `Changing these secrets needs the Admin role` · detail `Ask a workspace admin to rotate them for you.` — verbatim, `devtools-service.ts:496-499`. | B-4. |
| `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | `validation` | The per-user reveal throttle (§7.9: 20 / 5 min). `Too many reveals` · detail `` `Try again in ${n} seconds.` ``. `isRetryable: true` **explicit**. **A throttled reveal is a denial and is audited as one** before the `429` returns. | B-4. |
| `SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY` | 400 | `validation` | `secretIds` must carry at least one id. **This reason exists to close a hole**: the frontend treats `secretIds: []` as *"every secret in the document — 'Copy all'"* (`devtools-service.ts:400-401`), which makes an empty array the most dangerous possible wire default. `Choose at least one secret` **OQ-66.** | B-4. |

**`copy` has no permission key of its own.** It is gated by `secret.reveal` and audited as a reveal
(`src/types/devtools.ts:90-97`; `src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`). There is no
`SECRET_COPY_DENIED`; the reason is `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` with the multi-key copy.
