### 31.5 The `details` object

`details` is the **machine-readable** half of an error. It is a discriminated union on `reason`, it
is never rendered, and it is omitted — not `null` — for every reason not listed below. Sixty-odd
reasons carry no structured data at all: `message` and `detail` say everything the caller needs.

```ts
/**
 * Structured payload beside the human sentence. Discriminated on `reason`,
 * which repeats `error.reason` so the union narrows on its own (V-8).
 * Every variant is exhaustive: there is no index signature and no `unknown`.
 */
type ErrorDetails =
  // ---- governance
  | PermissionDeniedDetails
  | NodeFrozenDetails
  | NodeLockedDetails
  // ---- drive
  | SlugConflictDetails
  | MoveRejectedDetails
  // ---- workspace / storage
  | QuotaExceededDetails
  | LastAdminDetails
  // ---- boards
  | RowParentCycleDetails
  | RowParentDepthDetails
  | RowLimitDetails
  | ColumnConvertDetails
  | ColumnNameConflictDetails
  | TransitionDetails
  | OptionUnavailableDetails
  | ConditionTreeDetails
  | ViewRequiresColumnDetails
  // ---- bulk / io
  | BulkTargetKindDetails
  | ImportMappingDetails
  | ImportLimitDetails
  | ExportJobDetails
  // ---- documents / devtools
  | VersionConflictDetails
  | DocumentTooLargeDetails
  | SecretKeyDetails
  | EnvironmentInUseDetails
  // ---- files
  | FileSizeDetails
  | FileTypeDetails
  | UploadIncompleteDetails
  | LinkBlockedDetails
  // ---- cross-cutting
  | RequestTooLargeDetails
  | ConcurrencyDetails;
```

#### 31.5.1 Validation failures — the one that is *not* in `details`

Canon §6.2 puts field-level validation in a **top-level** `fields` array, not in `details`:

```ts
// error.fields?: readonly FieldError[]   — VALIDATION_FAILED and any `validation` code
interface FieldError {
  readonly path: string;      // "cells[0].value.iso", "entries[3].key", "views[1].ganttZoom"
  readonly reason: ErrorReason;
  readonly message: string;
}
```

`VALIDATION_FAILED` is the generic reason for a schema failure with no more specific reason of its
own; where a specific reason exists (`SECRET_KEY_INVALID`, `DATE_VALUE_INVALID`,
`ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID`) the API sends **that** reason and may still populate `fields` to point at
the offending path. `fields` is for developers and support; the user-facing sentence is always
`message` (canon §6.2, §7.4 E-8).

Example — a batched cell write with two bad values (E-066):

```jsonc
// 400 PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/cells
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation",
    "message": "Some of those values could not be saved",
    "detail": "Two cells were rejected. Nothing was written.",
    "isRetryable": false,
    "reason": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
    "requestId": "01JB9Z7QF3K8W2N6R4T5Y0X1M3",
    "fields": [
      { "path": "edits[0].value.iso",  "reason": "DATE_VALUE_INVALID",
        "message": "Dates on this column are written as YYYY-MM-DD." },
      { "path": "edits[3].value.kind", "reason": "CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID",
        "message": "“duration” is not a value kind this board understands." }
    ]
  }
}
```

Note what this example is **not**: it is not a concurrency failure. A stale cell write is applied
last-write-wins and reported as a `ConflictNotice` inside a `200` — E-066 never answers `409`
(§31.6).

#### 31.5.2 Governance and drive

```ts
/**
 * PERMISSION_DENIED. Deliberately minimal: the required key and the minimum
 * role, both of which the caller can already read from GET /permissions/catalog
 * (E-045). NEVER the node, the resource name, the rule that denied it, or who
 * does hold it — V-4.
 */
interface PermissionDeniedDetails {
  readonly reason: "PERMISSION_DENIED" | "COMMENT_DELETE_DENIED"
                 | "SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED" | "SECRET_ROTATE_DENIED";
  readonly requiredKey: PermissionKey;
  /** Minimum role holding `requiredKey`; null when no role does. */
  readonly requiredRole: WorkspaceRole | null;
}

/**
 * NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR / NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED. Names the ancestor because
 * the caller can see it — ArchivedBanner already renders exactly this from
 * archiveSourceOf and rendered by ArchivedBanner
 * (src/lib/archive.ts:19-27; src/components/shared/archived-banner.tsx:36-42).
 */
interface NodeFrozenDetails {
  readonly reason: "NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR" | "NODE_ARCHIVE_INHERITED";
  readonly frozenByNodeId: string;
  readonly frozenByName: string;
}

/** NODE_LOCKED / DOCUMENT_LOCKED. `lockedBy` is already on WorkspaceDocument. */
interface NodeLockedDetails {
  readonly reason: "NODE_LOCKED" | "DOCUMENT_LOCKED";
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly lockedBy: UserSummary | null;
}

/** NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT / WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN. `suggestion` is what uniqueSlug would mint. */
interface SlugConflictDetails {
  readonly reason: "NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT" | "WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN";
  readonly slug: string;
  readonly suggestion: string;
  /** Null for a workspace slug, which is tenant-scoped rather than sibling-scoped. */
  readonly parentId: string | null;
}

/**
 * The four NODE_MOVE_* reasons. `rejection` is the frontend's own MoveRejection
 * enum (src/lib/tree.ts:170-197, kebab-case), so a client can reuse the copy it
 * already has for the client-side check.
 */
interface MoveRejectedDetails {
  readonly reason: "NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT" | "NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF"
                 | "NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT" | "NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET";
  readonly rejection: MoveRejection;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly targetParentId: string | null;
}
```

#### 31.5.3 Storage, membership and concurrency

```ts
/** QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The three numbers the "N of M used" line needs. */
interface QuotaExceededDetails {
  readonly reason: "QUOTA_EXCEEDED";
  readonly usedBytes: number;
  readonly totalBytes: number;
  /** Size of the object that would not fit. */
  readonly requestedBytes: number;
}

/** WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN. A count, never the admins' identities. */
interface LastAdminDetails {
  readonly reason: "WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN";
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly adminCount: number;   // always 1 when this fires
}

/**
 * DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT. Everything the "changed by somebody else" banner
 * needs without a second request.
 */
interface VersionConflictDetails {
  readonly reason: "DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT";
  readonly currentVersion: number;
  readonly expectedVersion: number;
  readonly updatedAt: string;          // ISO 8601, C-03
  readonly updatedBy: UserSummary;
}

/** CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT — the generic form, for resources with no richer shape. */
interface ConcurrencyDetails {
  readonly reason: "CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT";
  readonly currentVersion: number;
  readonly expectedVersion: number;
}

/** REQUEST_TOO_LARGE. Both numbers in bytes. */
interface RequestTooLargeDetails {
  readonly reason: "REQUEST_TOO_LARGE";
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly maxBytes: number;
}
```

#### 31.5.4 Boards

```ts
/** ROW_PARENT_CYCLE. The path is root-first and every id in it is already on screen. */
interface RowParentCycleDetails {
  readonly reason: "ROW_PARENT_CYCLE";
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly parentRowId: string;
  /** The existing ancestry that the requested parent already sits inside. */
  readonly pathRowIds: readonly string[];
}

interface RowParentDepthDetails {
  readonly reason: "ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP";
  readonly depth: number;
  readonly maxDepth: number;      // canon §8.8 OQ-33: 5
}

interface RowLimitDetails {
  readonly reason: "BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED";
  readonly rowCount: number;
  readonly limit: number;
}

interface ColumnConvertDetails {
  readonly reason: "COLUMN_CONVERT_UNSUPPORTED";
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly fromType: ColumnType;
  readonly toType: ColumnType;
}

interface ColumnNameConflictDetails {
  readonly reason: "COLUMN_NAME_CONFLICT";
  readonly name: string;
  /** What uniqueColumnName would have produced: "Notes 2". */
  readonly suggestion: string;
}

/**
 * TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED. `fromOptionId` and `toOptionId` may be the reserved
 * "__empty__" key, which stands for the empty bucket on both sides
 * (src/lib/transition-rules.ts:27-28).
 */
interface TransitionDetails {
  readonly reason: "TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED";
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly fromOptionId: string;
  readonly toOptionId: string;
  /** Option ids the record may move to from here. Empty means nowhere. */
  readonly allowedOptionIds: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * OPTION_UNAVAILABLE. `unavailableReason` is the frontend's UnavailableReason
 * (src/lib/select-availability.ts:32) — NOT an ErrorReason. The field is renamed
 * on the wire so the two vocabularies cannot be confused.
 */
interface OptionUnavailableDetails {
  readonly reason: "OPTION_UNAVAILABLE";
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly optionId: string;
  readonly unavailableReason: "disabled" | "condition";
}

interface ConditionTreeDetails {
  readonly reason: "CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP";
  readonly depth: number;
  readonly maxDepth: number;
  readonly conditionCount: number;
  readonly maxConditions: number;
}

interface ViewRequiresColumnDetails {
  readonly reason: "VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN";
  readonly viewType: BoardViewType;
  readonly missingField: "groupByColumnId" | "dateColumnId";
}

interface BulkTargetKindDetails {
  readonly reason: "BULK_TARGET_NOT_A_BOARD";
  readonly targetNodeId: string;
  readonly actualKind: NodeKind;
}
```

#### 31.5.5 Import, export and files

```ts
/**
 * IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED. Carries ImportPlan.conflicts verbatim, so the
 * wizard renders the API's refusal with the component it already has
 * (src/types/system.ts:95-99).
 */
interface ImportMappingDetails {
  readonly reason: "IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED";
  readonly conflicts: readonly MappingConflict[];
}

interface ImportLimitDetails {
  readonly reason: "IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED";
  readonly rowCount: number;
  readonly limit: number;          // IMPORT_MAX_ROWS, served by GET /config
}

interface ExportJobDetails {
  readonly reason: "EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY";
  readonly jobId: string;
  readonly state: "queued" | "running";
  readonly retryAfterSeconds: number;
}

interface FileSizeDetails {
  readonly reason: "FILE_TOO_LARGE" | "DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE";
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly maxBytes: number;
}

interface DocumentTooLargeDetails {
  readonly reason: "DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE";
  readonly blockCount: number;
  readonly maxBlocks: number;
}

interface FileTypeDetails {
  readonly reason: "FILE_TYPE_REJECTED" | "FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH";
  readonly extension: string;
  /** Declared MIME on FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH; null when only the extension was checked. */
  readonly declaredMimeType: string | null;
  readonly acceptedExtensions: readonly string[];
}

interface UploadIncompleteDetails {
  readonly reason: "UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE";
  readonly uploadId: string;
  readonly expectedBytes: number;
  /** Bytes the object store actually holds; null when the object is absent. */
  readonly actualBytes: number | null;
}

/**
 * LINK_TARGET_BLOCKED. `host` is echoed from the caller's own URL, so it leaks
 * nothing. The API never says WHY it was blocked — see §31.4.13.
 */
interface LinkBlockedDetails {
  readonly reason: "LINK_TARGET_BLOCKED";
  readonly host: string;
}
```

#### 31.5.6 Devtools

```ts
interface SecretKeyDetails {
  readonly reason: "SECRET_KEY_INVALID" | "SECRET_KEY_DUPLICATE";
  readonly key: string;
  /** Indices in the submitted `entries` array holding the offending key. */
  readonly positions: readonly number[];
}

interface EnvironmentInUseDetails {
  readonly reason: "ENVIRONMENT_IN_USE";
  readonly environmentId: string;
  readonly configDocumentCount: number;
  readonly secretCount: number;
}
```

**A secret error never carries a value.** `SecretKeyDetails` carries the *key*, which is not a
secret (it is rendered in the list). No `ErrorDetails` variant anywhere in this catalogue carries
plaintext, ciphertext, an IV or a key id. `secret_rotations` exists precisely so that "what changed"
can be recorded without "what it changed to" (T-24, OQ-67), and an error envelope must hold to the
same line.

---

### 31.6 What is not an error

Four things go wrong in this product without producing an error body. Getting any of them wrong
turns a working feature into a broken one.

**1. Partial success is a `200`.** `BulkResult`, `BulkMoveResult` and `ImportOutcome` report what
did and did not apply. *"a bulk write that silently drops a record is worse than one that refuses"*
(`src/services/board-service.ts:958-965`), and the invariant is
`requested === applied.length + skipped.length` (`src/types/system.ts:32-36`). The frontend renders
this as one toast whose tone is derived from the result, not from an exception
(`src/store/board-store.ts:185-186` — `report(result, verb)`).

**2. A stale cell write is a `200` with a notice.** E-066 is last-write-wins: the stale write is
**applied**, the revision bumped, and the collision reported per `(rowId, columnId)` as a
`ConflictNotice`. Three properties must be reproduced exactly
(`src/services/board-service.ts:504-512`): a missing `baseRevisions[rowId]` never conflicts;
`base < current.revision` conflicts while equal or greater does not; and **at most one notice per
row per call**, raised by the first edit that touches it. There is no `409` on this endpoint and no
`ErrorReason` for it.

**3. `TRASH_RESTORE_RELOCATED` is a `200` field.** When the original parent is gone, the restore
walks `originalAncestorIds` for the deepest surviving container and reports where it landed:
`RestoreOutcome { node, parentId, isRelocated, location }` (`src/types/system.ts:182-188`). It is
registered in canon §4.3 only so that no chapter mistakes it for a failure.

**4. `PREVIEW_UNSUPPORTED` is a `200` body.** E-114 answers
`FilePreview { kind: "unsupported", reason }` (`src/types/file.ts:27`) rather than refusing. A file
the previewer cannot render is a normal state of the file browser, not an error condition.

And one more, easy to miss: **an empty search is `[]`, not a `400`**
(`src/services/search-service.ts:56-57`).

---

### 31.7 Writing the copy

#### 31.7.1 The five rules

Grounded in `src/services/errors.ts:33-49`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-165` and
`src/components/shared/state-panels.tsx:118-138`.

1. **`message` is rendered verbatim.** It is a sentence, sentence-cased, with **no trailing period**
   unless it is two sentences. It is the panel title and the toast text. Every quoted string in
   §31.4 obeys this.
2. **`not_found` uses one template**: `` `${what} could not be found` ``, where `${what}` is a
   capitalised noun phrase beginning with "That" or "Those" — `That board`, `That record`,
   `That parent record`, `That column`, `That select column`, `That view`, `That document`,
   `That version`, `That folder`, `That comment`, `That secret`, `Those secrets`. The complete list
   is `src/services/errors.ts:36-37` plus its twelve call sites.
3. **A refusal names nothing it was protecting.** `permission_denied` copy is deliberately name-free:
   *"A refusal that reads 'Finance is restricted' hands the name of a private folder to the one
   person who was told they may not have it"* (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-158`). The one
   sanctioned exception is `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, where the caller can already see the ancestor.
4. **`detail` is the second line: what to do about it.** `Needs the Manager role or above`,
   `Ask the owner to share it with you.`, `Unlock it before saving further changes.` It is
   **optional** and omitted, never `null`. Unlike `message`, `detail` **does** take a trailing
   period, because the frontend's own strings do.
5. **`isRetryable` drives a button, so it is a product decision, not a technical one.** Set it
   explicitly whenever it differs from the §31.2 default. The user reads it as "is trying again
   worth my time".

#### 31.7.2 What a message never contains

| Never | Because |
| --- | --- |
| A stack trace, a SQL fragment, a table or column name | `message` is rendered to the user verbatim. In production `INTERNAL_ERROR` sends `Something went wrong` and omits `detail` entirely; the original text lives in the log line keyed by `requestId`. |
| A UUID, a node id, a request id | `message` is prose. Ids belong in `details` (V-7) and `requestId` has its own field (V-9). A **display id** (`TASK-042`) is different and is allowed — the frontend already puts them in messages (`board-service.ts:390`). |
| The name of a resource the caller may not see | V-4. |
| An email address or a person's name, in a refusal | V-4. `ROW_PARENT_CYCLE` naming two display ids is fine; "Ask Priya" is not. |
| A secret key's **value**, in any form | §31.5.6. |
| An internal service name, host or port | It tells an attacker about the topology and tells a user nothing. |

#### 31.7.3 The `${action}` phrases in `PERMISSION_DENIED`

`authz.ts:73` builds the message as `` `You do not have permission to ${action}` ``. The nine
phrases the frontend already ships must be reused verbatim so a user who sees the refusal twice
sees the same sentence twice:

| Endpoint | `${action}` | Site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E-052 | `add a column` | `board-service.ts:566` |
| E-055 | `duplicate a column` | `board-service.ts:602` |
| E-053 | `change this column` | `board-service.ts:655` |
| E-056 | `reorder columns` | `board-service.ts:674` |
| E-054 | `delete this column` | `board-service.ts:689` |
| E-057 | `change this column's type` | `board-service.ts:730` |
| E-085 | `import into this board` | `board-service.ts:1191` |
| E-100 | `edit this config document` | `devtools-service.ts:148` |
| E-102 | *(role-specific copy)* `Changing these secrets needs the Admin role` | `devtools-service.ts:496-499` |

Every other endpoint needs a phrase minted to the same pattern: a lower-case verb phrase that
completes "You do not have permission to …". `delete this record`, `move these records`,
`resolve this thread`, `restore this version`, `share this folder`.

### 31.9 Four rules that are security rules, not style

#### 31.9.1 `404` and `403` are chosen by *visibility*, never by convenience

A resource the caller **may not see** answers `404` with the ordinary not-found copy, identically to
one that does not exist. A resource the caller **may see but may not act on** answers `403`. The
frontend already reasons this way at the workspace boundary: *"a workspace that does not exist and
one the person is not in return the same shape on purpose: the surface shows the same screen either
way, so the URL cannot be used to learn which workspaces exist"* (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:60-64`;
the same statement in the guard at `src/components/workspace/workspace-guard.tsx:22-25`).

The rule extends down the tree, because access is inherited: a node inside a `restricted` folder the
caller has no rule on is invisible, and every endpoint addressing it answers `NODE_NOT_FOUND`. This
includes `PATCH`, `DELETE` and every sub-resource — an endpoint that answers `403` where a sibling
answers `404` is an enumeration oracle.

#### 31.9.2 What a `permission_denied` may contain

| Field | Allowed | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `` `You do not have permission to ${action}` `` — the action, never the object | `authz.ts:73` |
| `detail` | `` `Needs the ${Role} role or above` `` — the minimum role, never the holder | `requirementFor`, `evaluate.ts:168-176` |
| `details.requiredKey` | The `PermissionKey`. It is public: `GET /permissions/catalog` (E-045) serves all 39. | canon §2.10 |
| `details.requiredRole` | The minimum role. Also public, from the same catalogue. | — |
| **Never** | The node name, the folder name, the rule that denied it, who granted it, who holds it, whether the resource exists at all | `evaluate.ts:155-158` |

#### 31.9.3 A denied secret read is audited **before** it is refused

`DV-SEC-23`. The frontend's mock already does this and says why: *"Recorded even when refused: a
denied attempt is worth auditing"* (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:342-349`) and
*"A denied attempt is recorded exactly as carefully as an allowed one"* (`:358-360`). The order is
not negotiable — the audit write and the refusal are one transaction, and the audit row commits
whether or not the caller gets a value:

1. Resolve the secret. If it does not exist → `SECRET_NOT_FOUND`, **no audit row** (there is nothing
   to attribute).
2. Check the permission. On refusal: write a `secret_access_events` row **and** an `audit_events`
   row with `outcome: "denied"`, `severity: "warn"` (canon OQ-68 — both, one transaction), commit,
   **then** return `403 SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED`.
3. On the rate limit: the same two rows with `outcome: "denied"`, then `429`.
4. On success: the same two rows with `outcome: "allowed"`, then the plaintext, once.

The same discipline applies to E-046 (the restricted-node recovery console) and E-137 (audit
export), both of which are **privileged reads audited at `warn`** (OQ-26, OQ-27).

#### 31.9.4 Why `NODE_LOCKED` and `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` both exist

They describe the same state through two doors and carry two different codes on purpose.

- **`NODE_LOCKED` (403, `permission_denied`)** is produced by the **permission evaluator**, which
  treats a lock as one of three narrowing layers alongside trashed and frozen
  (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:63-88`). It fires on any endpoint whose key is in
  `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS` — a board write on a locked board node, a file write on a locked file.
- **`DOCUMENT_LOCKED` (409, `conflict`)** is produced by the **document endpoint itself**, verbatim
  from `document-service.ts:193`, because that is what the frontend already shows and the copy is
  specific and actionable: `This page is locked` / `Unlock it before saving further changes.`

A save to a locked page (E-092) sends `DOCUMENT_LOCKED`. Anything else blocked by a lock sends
`NODE_LOCKED`. Collapsing them would either lose the shipped copy or send the editor to a permission
screen (B-1) for something the user can fix in one click.

### 31.10 Open questions carried by this chapter

Every one is already registered in canon §8; this chapter adds no new ids. Listed here because the
error catalogue is where their absence shows up first.

| OQ | What is unsettled | What §31 does anyway |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OQ-01** | No authentication exists, so §31.4.1 is entirely a proposal. | Catalogues six reasons and makes `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` the one the client branches on (B-8). |
| **OQ-05** | Nothing maintains `usedBytes`. | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` at 507, checked at E-110 rather than E-111. |
| **OQ-16 – OQ-21** | 40+ writes carry no permission check; `canView`, `userId` and `role` are request parameters. | Every endpoint in §31.8 lists `PERMISSION_DENIED`. |
| **OQ-32** | Whether a date cell holds a day key or an instant. | `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` refuses both wrong shapes; canon's two-generated-column position decides which is which. |
| **OQ-33** | Nothing bounds the subtask hierarchy. | Three reasons — `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD`, `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP`, `ROW_PARENT_CYCLE` — reserved even though only the third is enforced today. |
| **OQ-36** | Row pagination does not exist. | `CURSOR_INVALID` reserved. |
| **OQ-38** | No cap on condition-tree depth. | `CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP` reserved with both numbers in `details`. |
| **OQ-41** | Import transactionality and the row ceiling. | `IMPORT_COLUMN_CREATE_FAILED` carries the frontend's own promise that nothing was written. |
| **OQ-57** | `DocumentDraft` carries no version. | `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT` fires only when `expectedVersion` is sent; absent means last-write-wins. |
| **OQ-58** | No document size ceiling. | `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` reserved. |
| **OQ-66** | `secretIds: []` means "every secret". | `SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY` closes it. |
| **OQ-69 / OQ-70** | 25 MB vs 100 MB; the allow-list blocks previewable formats and nothing sniffs MIME. | `FILE_TOO_LARGE` and `FILE_TYPE_REJECTED` take their numbers from `GET /config`; `FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` is new and has no frontend counterpart. |
| **OQ-80** | `comment.resolve` has no state and no endpoint. | Two reasons reserved for E-123/E-124. |
| **OQ-91** | Notification retention, dedupe and paging. | `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` restricted to the single-notification case. |
| **OQ-100** | Realtime frame scoping and authorisation. | Two close-frame reasons; the socket never sends an HTTP error body after upgrade. |

## 32. TypeScript Contract Interfaces

This is the wire contract in one place: every interface the API emits or accepts, in dependency
order, with no `any` anywhere. It is the authority a backend developer generates serialisers from
and a frontend developer type-checks against.

**Where these types come from.** 84 of them already exist in `src/types/` and are reproduced here
**verbatim, name for name and field for field**. Eleven are added by canon §5.3 because the API
needs a shape the frontend has no counterpart for. Nothing else is invented. Where a domain
interface differs from its database row — casing, a computed field, a masked value, a field that
exists on the wire and not in the table — the difference is stated in a comment on the field itself,
and §32.5 collects them into one table.

### 32.0 The rules this chapter obeys

| # | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T-1 | **Every field is `readonly`.** Universally true across `src/types/`, with two deliberate exceptions that are both UI-only and neither of which crosses the wire: `RealtimeTransport`'s four methods and the inner objects of `BreadcrumbItem.siblings`. | C-07; `src/types/` |
| T-2 | **Optional and nullable are different and must not be collapsed.** `x?: T` = may be absent, and absence has a defined default. `x: T \| null` = always present, may be empty. `BoardRow.archivedAt?: string \| null` is deliberately both: absent means never archived, `null` means restored. | C-08; `src/types/board.ts:76-79` vs `:223` vs `:254` |
| T-3 | **No `any`, ever.** Every dynamic value is a discriminated union with a literal tag: `CellValue.kind`, `Block.type`, `AccessSubject.kind`, `FilePreview.kind`, `MappingTarget.kind`, `RealtimePayload.type`, `ErrorDetails.reason`. `Record<string, T>` is used only where the key is genuinely an id (`cells`, `columnWidths`, `transitions`). | C-05; ground rule 6 |
| T-4 | **The wire is `camelCase`; the database is `snake_case`.** The conversion happens once, at the HTTP boundary. No interface here carries a `snake_case` field and no table carries a `camelCase` column. | canon §1 |
| T-5 | **Enum members are the exact frontend string literal, casing included.** `longText`, `apiDocs`, `dueToday`, `bulletList`, `permission_denied`, `not_found`, `into-self`, `my-work`… the four casing styles coexist and are not normalised. | C-13; canon §2.0 |
| T-6 | **Instants are ISO 8601 strings; date-only values are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings.** Both are typed `string` because that is what the frontend declares; the distinction is carried in the field comment and enforced by the endpoint. A date-only value never passes through UTC. | C-03, C-04; `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24` |
| T-7 | **Ids are `string` on the wire.** They are UUIDs (C-01), but nothing in the contract narrows them to a branded type, because the frontend does not and mints `tmp_` ids client-side for optimistic rows (`src/types/board.ts:237`). | C-01; `src/types/board.ts:236-238` |
| T-8 | **A domain object is returned bare.** A response DTO exists only where the response is not a domain object. `POST /workspaces` returns `Workspace`, not `CreateWorkspaceResponse`. | canon §5.1 |
| T-9 | **Forbidden names**: `I`-prefixes, `Dto`/`Model`/`Entity`/`Data`/`Info` suffixes, bare `Payload` on a domain type, and any plural interface name. | canon §5.1 |

#### 32.0.1 Alias resolution — the brief's names → the canonical names

The specification brief proposed names for several of these types before the frontend was read.
**The frontend's name wins in every case** (canon §5.2). This table exists so a reader following a
reference from the brief lands on the right interface rather than concluding it is missing.

| Proposed name | Canonical name | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `User` | **`UserSummary`** / **`DirectoryUser`** | Two shapes, not one. `DirectoryUser` adds `isActive` and is what any list of people returns. `src/types/user.ts:4-20` |
| `Node` | **`DriveNode`** | The union. Its members are `ProjectNode`, `FolderNode`, `DocumentNode`, `BoardNode`, `FileNode`. `src/types/node.ts:130` |
| `Project` / `Folder` | **`ProjectNode`** / **`FolderNode`** | Variants of `DriveNode`, not standalone entities. |
| `Page` / `Document` | **`WorkspaceDocument`** | `src/types/document.ts:117`. The tree-side projection is `DocumentNode`. |
| `DocumentBlock` | **`Block`** | 14 `BlockType` values collapsing into 9 interfaces. `src/types/document.ts:101-110` |
| `NodeAccess` | **`AccessRule`** (stored) + **`ResolvedAccess`** (computed) + **`NodeAccessResponse`** (the endpoint) | Three different things the brief's one name conflated. §32.1.3 |
| `BoardColumnConfig` | **`ColumnConfigByType`** | A mapped type over seven per-type interfaces, not one shape. `src/types/board.ts:162-170` |
| `BoardColumnOption` | **`SelectOption`** | `src/types/board.ts:68-79` |
| `TransitionRuleConfig` | **`TransitionRules`** | Lives inside `SelectConfig`, not beside it. `src/types/board.ts:89-94` |
| `SavedViewConfig` | *(no such type)* | `SavedView` is **flat**. There is no nested config object; the 17 presentation fields sit directly on it. §32.1.7 |
| `FilterGroup` | *(no such type for views)* | View filters are a **flat array plus one conjunction** (`filters`, `filterConjunction`). Nesting exists only in `ConditionGroup`, which governs select-option availability — a different feature with a different operator enum. §32.1.4 and the warning box there. |
| `FilterCondition` | **`ViewFilter`** | `src/types/board.ts:301-306` |
| `SortRule` | **`ViewSort`** | `src/types/board.ts:311-314` |
| `GroupRule` | *(no such type)* | Grouping is two fields on `SavedView`: `groupByColumnId` and `hideEmptyGroups`. |
| `Attachment` | **`CellAttachment`** / **`CommentAttachment`** / **`FileAsset`** / **`DocumentImage`** | Four divergent shapes over one `file_assets` row. Canon §1.3.4 keeps them apart deliberately. §32.5.2 |
| `RowRelation` | *(no such type)* | A relation is a **relation-type column** whose cell holds `rowIds`. The read models are `RelationTarget` and `Backlink`. **No `RelationType` enum and no typed edge may be introduced** (canon §2.9, OQ-45). |
| `Mention` | *(no such type)* | A mention is an encoding inside `Comment.body` — `@[Name](usr_id)` — plus the parsed `mentionedUserIds`. The parsed segment type `BodySegment` is UI-only and never crosses the wire. §32.1.12 |
| `Notification` | **`AppNotification`** | `src/types/collab.ts:101-113`. Named `App…` because `Notification` is a DOM global. |
| `NotificationPayload` | *(no such type)* | A notification carries **pre-rendered `title` and `body`**, not a per-reason payload. §32.1.12 and the OQ-89 block there. |
| `Favorite` | *(not a wire type)* | Per-user, stored in `node_favorites` (T-07), projected onto `DriveNode.isFavorite`. §32.5.1 |
| `RecentResource` | **`RecentEntry`** | Stays in `localStorage` under `nexdrop-recent`; **not a table and not an endpoint** (OQ-96). `src/types/collab.ts:184-187` |
| `ActivityLog` | **`ActivityEntry`** (+ `ActivityPage`) | `src/types/board.ts:496-505` |
| `AuditLog` | **`AuditEvent`** (+ `AuditPage`) | `src/types/audit.ts:22-55` |
| `SecretEntryMasked` | **`SecretEntry`** | There is only the masked shape. *"There is no `value` here on purpose"* (`src/types/devtools.ts:68-73`). |
| `ConfigDocument`, `SecretDocument`, `Condition`, `ConditionGroup`, `SavedView`, `Comment`, `Watch`→`WatchEntry`, `DocumentVersion`, `BoardRow`, `CellValue`, `Board`, `BoardColumn`, `Workspace`, `WorkspaceMember` | **unchanged** | The brief's name is already the frontend's name. |

---

### 32.1 Domain interfaces

Fifteen layers. Nothing in a layer references anything below it, so the file compiles top to bottom.

#### 32.1.0 Layer 0 — the enum vocabulary

Reproduced as type aliases so this chapter compiles standalone. **§6 is the authority**; if a member
here disagrees with §6, §6 wins. Every literal is the exact frontend string (T-5).

```ts
/* identity, tenancy, governance ------------------------------------------ */
type WorkspaceRole   = "viewer" | "member" | "manager" | "admin";   // order IS the rank
type WorkspacePlan   = "free" | "team" | "enterprise";
type NodeAccessMode  = "inherit" | "workspace" | "restricted";
type AccessSource    = "workspace" | "inherited" | "explicit" | "override";
type Capability      = "view" | "edit" | "upload" | "delete" | "share" | "manage";
type PermissionModule =
  | "workspace" | "node" | "board" | "row" | "document" | "file" | "comment" | "secret";
type PermissionKey   = /* the 39 keys — canon §2.10, src/types/permission.ts:31-78 */ string & {};
type AuditSeverity   = "info" | "warn" | "error";
type AuditModule     = PermissionModule | "system";
type AuditOutcome    = "allowed" | "denied";

/* drive ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
type NodeKind        = "project" | "folder" | "document" | "board" | "file";
type DocumentKind    = "page" | "config" | "secret";      // absent means "page"
type BoardKind       = "kanban" | "table" | "timeline" | "doc";
type ProjectStatus   = "active" | "paused" | "archived";
type FileKind =
  | "image" | "document" | "spreadsheet" | "pdf" | "video" | "audio" | "archive" | "code" | "other";
type MoveRejection   = "same-parent" | "into-self" | "into-descendant" | "invalid-target";
type EntityKind      = NodeKind | "row";                  // NodeKind PLUS row
type WatchKind       = "row" | "document" | "board";      // a strict subset of EntityKind
type BreadcrumbKind  = NodeKind | "workspace";
type NodeState       = "trashed" | "frozen" | "archived" | "active";   // derived, §32.1.2

/* board schema and cells ------------------------------------------------- */
type ColumnType      = "text" | "longText" | "select" | "date" | "user" | "attachment" | "relation";
type SelectColor     = "gray" | "blue" | "green" | "amber" | "red" | "violet" | "cyan" | "pink";
type ConditionOperator =
  | "is" | "isNot" | "contains" | "notContains" | "isAnyOf" | "isNoneOf"
  | "before" | "after" | "on" | "isEmpty" | "isNotEmpty";
type ConditionConjunction   = "and" | "or";
type UnavailableOptionBehavior = "disabled" | "hidden";
type BoardTemplateId = "task" | "bug" | "qa" | "apiDocs";
type ActivityKind =
  | "created" | "updated" | "commented" | "attached" | "archived" | "restored" | "imported" | "moved";

/* views ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
type BoardViewType   = "table" | "kanban" | "calendar" | "gantt";
type FilterOperator =
  | "isNotEmpty" | "isEmpty" | "contains" | "notContains" | "is" | "isNot"
  | "before" | "after" | "onOrBefore" | "onOrAfter";
type FilterConjunction = "and" | "or";
type SortDirection   = "asc" | "desc";
type CellDisplayMode = "compact" | "wrap" | "full";       // a column missing from the map is compact
type RowHeight       = "short" | "medium" | "tall";
type SubtaskDisplay  = "nested" | "flat" | "hidden";
type GanttZoom       = "week" | "month" | "quarter";      // "day" is ACCEPTED on the wire and coerced

/* documents, devtools, files --------------------------------------------- */
type BlockType =
  | "heading1" | "heading2" | "heading3" | "paragraph" | "quote" | "checklist"
  | "bulletList" | "numberedList" | "code" | "image" | "attachment" | "link" | "table" | "embed";
type CodeLanguage =
  | "plaintext" | "typescript" | "javascript" | "json" | "sql" | "bash" | "python" | "go";
type ConfigFormat =
  | "json" | "env" | "yaml" | "javascript" | "typescript" | "jsx" | "tsx" | "html"
  | "xml" | "css" | "sql" | "shell" | "dockerfile" | "nginx" | "text";
type SecretAction    = "reveal" | "copy" | "rotate";
type UploadState     = "pending" | "completed" | "aborted" | "expired";  // server-side; T-32

/* system ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
type BulkSkipReason  = "archived" | "not_found" | "permission_denied";
type ImportInvalidPolicy = "skip" | "blank";
type ExportFormat    = "xlsx" | "csv" | "pdf";
type ExportScope     = "board" | "view" | "selection";
type DiffKind        = "same" | "added" | "removed";      // no "changed": a modification is removed+added

/* collaboration, search, insights ---------------------------------------- */
type NotificationReason = "mention" | "assigned" | "comment" | "watch" | "system";
type SearchResultKind =
  | "document" | "api" | "bug" | "qa" | "row" | "file" | "comment" | "place";
type MyWorkWidgetId  = "assigned" | "mentioned" | "dueToday" | "overdue" | "recentlyUpdated";
type DashboardWidgetId = "task" | "qa" | "deadline";
type TaskBucketId    = "todo" | "doing" | "review" | "done";
type QaBucketId      = "passed" | "failed" | "blocked";
type DeadlineBucketId = "overdue" | "today" | "thisWeek";
type DashboardBucketId = TaskBucketId | QaBucketId | DeadlineBucketId;

/* errors ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
type AppErrorCode =
  | "permission_denied" | "not_found" | "network" | "validation"
  | "upload_failed" | "conflict" | "cancelled" | "unknown";
```

**Eight enums are UI-only and never appear in any interface below**: `ViewMode`, `SortKey`,
`ImportStep`, `DocumentActionId`, `SaveStatus`, `NotificationTab`, `BodySegmentKind`, `SmartViewId`.
`UploadStatus` (`queued`/`uploading`/`success`/`error`/`cancelled`) is a **client queue state** and
is likewise absent; the server's own upload state is `UploadState` above.

`PermissionKey` is written above as `string & {}` only so this block compiles without inlining 39
literals; the real declaration is the union at `src/types/permission.ts:31-78` and canon §2.10, and
the API validates against exactly those 39 values.

#### 32.1.1 Layer 1 — identity and tenancy

```ts
/**
 * Minimal identity, embedded in nodes, activity, comments, versions and audit rows.
 * DB: `users`. `initials` is DERIVED server-side from `name`; it is not a column
 * (the frontend renders it as an avatar fallback, src/types/user.ts:8-9).
 */
interface UserSummary {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly email: string;
  /** Two letters, rendered when `avatarUrl` is absent. DERIVED from `name`. */
  readonly initials: string;
  readonly avatarUrl?: string;
  readonly accentColor?: string;
}

/**
 * A person as the directory knows them. `isActive` is `users.is_active`.
 * A removed member stays resolvable so their name still renders on old
 * assignments — flagged inactive, never dropped (src/types/user.ts:14-20).
 * E-006 MUST include deactivated members.
 */
interface DirectoryUser extends UserSummary {
  readonly isActive: boolean;
}

/**
 * A membership row, flattened onto the person. DB: `workspace_members` joined
 * to `users`. `role` and `joinedAt` are the join row's columns; everything
 * else is the user's.
 */
interface WorkspaceMember extends UserSummary {
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly joinedAt: string;   // ISO 8601
}

/**
 * DB: `workspaces.used_bytes` and the plan's allowance. `totalBytes` is NOT a
 * column — it comes from static plan config (canon §1.2, OQ-06). `usedBytes` IS
 * a column, maintained transactionally with every asset insert and delete (OQ-05).
 */
interface StorageQuota {
  readonly usedBytes: number;
  readonly totalBytes: number;
}

/**
 * DB: `workspaces`. Two fields are joins, not columns:
 *   - `members` — the whole `workspace_members` join, embedded because the
 *     frontend resolves the caller's own role from it (memberRoleOf,
 *     src/lib/workspace-access.ts:29-35). See the note below on `role`.
 *   - `storage` — one column plus one config lookup.
 * `description` is OPTIONAL, not nullable (src/types/workspace.ts:15-16): the
 * frontend omits the key when it is empty (workspace-access.ts:233).
 */
interface Workspace {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly description?: string;
  /** URL-safe, unique across the tenant. Minted at creation, never re-minted. */
  readonly slug: string;
  readonly plan: WorkspacePlan;
  /** 1–2 characters for the switcher tile. */
  readonly badge: string;
  /** A CSS colour token, e.g. "var(--kind-video)". Stored as sent. */
  readonly color: string;
  readonly members: readonly WorkspaceMember[];
  readonly storage: StorageQuota;
}
```

> **There is no `role` field on `Workspace`, and adding one would be a mistake.**
> The brief asked for a computed `role`. The frontend does not have one: it derives the caller's
> role with `memberRoleOf(workspace, userId)` over the embedded `members` array
> (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:29-35`), and the module exists specifically to stop the fallback
> that a nullable convenience field invites — *"The rule this file exists to stop is the quiet one:
> falling back to the lowest role for somebody who holds no role. 'Not a member' is not 'viewer'"*
> (`:11-14`). A `role: WorkspaceRole` field would have to be nullable to be honest, and a nullable
> role is exactly the shape that gets defaulted to `"viewer"` at the first call site that forgets.
> `members` is already on the wire; the caller's row is in it. **RECOMMENDATION: keep it derived.**

#### 32.1.2 Layer 2 — the drive tree

```ts
/**
 * The shared column set of every node. Not exported by the frontend (it is a
 * bare `interface DriveNodeBase` at src/types/node.ts:48), reproduced here
 * because five interfaces extend it.
 *
 * DB: `nodes` (T-06), one table for all five kinds (canon §1.3.1).
 * THREE fields are DERIVED and are not columns:
 *   - `isTrashed`  = `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`
 *   - `isShared`   = an `access_rules` row exists on this node
 *   - `isFavorite` = a `node_favorites` row exists for (this node, the CALLER).
 *     Per user, not a flag on the node (OQ-07) — so two people reading the same
 *     node see different values in this field, which is correct.
 */
interface DriveNodeBase {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  /** URL-safe segment, unique among siblings EXCLUDING trashed rows. The routing key. */
  readonly slug: string;
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly owner: UserSummary;          // join on nodes.owner_id
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly isFavorite: boolean;         // DERIVED, per caller
  readonly isTrashed: boolean;          // DERIVED from deleted_at
  readonly isShared: boolean;           // DERIVED from access_rules
  /**
   * This node's OWN archive flag. Archiving is inherited, and a consumer must
   * resolve it through the ancestor chain rather than reading this alone
   * (src/types/node.ts:61-66). Use `state` for the resolved answer.
   */
  readonly isArchived?: boolean;
  /** Absent means `inherit`. Resource visibility, not capability. */
  readonly accessMode?: NodeAccessMode;
  /**
   * RECOMMENDATION (OQ-11), additive. The resolved lifecycle state, precedence
   * top-down: trashed > frozen (an ANCESTOR is archived) > archived (this node's
   * own flag) > active. Never a stored column. `isArchived` and `isTrashed` stay
   * on the wire because the frontend reads them.
   */
  readonly state?: NodeState;
}

/**
 * `children` is DERIVED from `parent_id` and is never stored (src/types/node.ts:150-151).
 * A leaf has no `children` field at all — not an empty array.
 */
interface ProjectNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "project";
  readonly description?: string;
  readonly status: ProjectStatus;
  readonly color: string;
  readonly children: readonly DriveNode[];
}

interface FolderNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "folder";
  readonly children: readonly DriveNode[];
  readonly color?: string;
}

/**
 * The tree-side projection of a page, config document or secret document.
 * `blockCount` and `excerpt` are DERIVED projections kept in sync by the
 * documents module (DocumentSummaryPatch, src/services/document-service.ts:149-158);
 * `isPinned`, `isLocked` and `isArchived` are the NODE's columns and the
 * document row must not duplicate them (canon OQ-30, OQ-56).
 */
interface DocumentNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "document";
  /** Absent means a block page — the original document kind. */
  readonly documentKind?: DocumentKind;
  readonly icon: string;
  readonly blockCount: number;          // DERIVED
  readonly isPinned: boolean;
  readonly isLocked: boolean;
  readonly isArchived: boolean;         // NON-optional here, unlike the base
  readonly excerpt: string;             // DERIVED, first ~120 chars of text
}

/**
 * `itemCount` and `openCount` are DERIVED counts over `board_rows`.
 * `templateId` is a bare `string`, "for reference only" (src/types/node.ts:110-111)
 * — it is NOT `BoardTemplateId`, because a user template carries a UUID.
 */
interface BoardNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "board";
  readonly boardKind: BoardKind;        // presentation hint; NOT validated against BoardViewType (OQ-31)
  readonly templateId?: string;
  readonly itemCount: number;           // DERIVED
  readonly openCount: number;           // DERIVED
}

/**
 * DB: `nodes` joined to `file_nodes` (T-28) joined to `file_assets` (T-27).
 * `previewUrl` and `thumbnailUrl` are MINTED PER RESPONSE as short-lived signed
 * URLs and are NEVER accepted on write (OQ-75). `sizeBytes`, `mimeType` and
 * `extension` are the asset's, not the node's.
 */
interface FileNode extends DriveNodeBase {
  readonly type: "file";
  readonly kind: FileKind;
  readonly extension: string;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly previewUrl?: string;         // signed, short-lived, response-only
  readonly thumbnailUrl?: string;       // signed, short-lived, response-only
  readonly excerpt?: string;            // DERIVED, text-like files only
  readonly version: number;             // file_nodes.version
}

type DriveNode    = ProjectNode | FolderNode | DocumentNode | BoardNode | FileNode;
type ContainerNode = ProjectNode | FolderNode;    // can hold children, and are drop targets
type LeafNode      = DocumentNode | BoardNode | FileNode;

/** E-021. `isNotFound` is true when the URL names a segment that does not exist. */
interface DriveLocation {
  readonly node: DriveNode | null;                 // null at the workspace root
  readonly ancestors: readonly DriveNode[];        // root down to, EXCLUDING, `node`
  readonly children: readonly DriveNode[];
  readonly isNotFound: boolean;
}

/** E-035, the cheap drive quick-find. Distinct from `SearchResult` (OQ-94). */
interface SearchHit {
  readonly node: DriveNode;
  /** `Development / Backend` — the ancestor path, resolved for display. */
  readonly path: string;
  readonly href: string;
}

/**
 * Computed for a header, never stored. The one place C-07 is relaxed: the inner
 * sibling objects are not `readonly` in the frontend (src/types/breadcrumb.ts:14).
 * The API emits them readonly anyway; the frontend's looser type still accepts it.
 */
interface BreadcrumbItem {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly href: string;
  readonly kind: BreadcrumbKind;
  readonly isCurrent: boolean;
  readonly siblings: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly label: string; readonly href: string }[];
}

type BreadcrumbTrail = readonly BreadcrumbItem[];

/**
 * DB: `trash_entries` (T-09). `node` is the DETACHED subtree root — it is not in
 * the tree any more, which is why the entry carries its own ancestry.
 * `originalPath` is resolved AT DELETION so it survives the purge of its
 * ancestors (src/types/system.ts:176-179).
 */
interface TrashEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly node: DriveNode;
  readonly deletedAt: string;
  readonly deletedBy: UserSummary;
  /** Ancestors at the moment of deletion, root first. Walked in order on restore. */
  readonly originalAncestorIds: readonly string[];
  readonly originalPath: string;
  /**
   * RECOMMENDATION (OQ-14), additive: `deletedAt + TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`.
   * The frontend already tells the user "purged after 30 days"
   * (src/config/app.ts:41-42, SMART_VIEWS trash description).
   */
  readonly purgeAt?: string;
}

/** E-037. `isRelocated` is TRUE when the original parent is gone. Not an error. */
interface RestoreOutcome {
  readonly node: DriveNode;
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  readonly isRelocated: boolean;
  /** Human path of where it actually landed. */
  readonly location: string;
}
```

#### 32.1.3 Layer 3 — governance

```ts
/** Who a rule is about. Roles cover everyone holding them; users are exact. */
type AccessSubject =
  | { readonly kind: "user"; readonly userId: string }
  | { readonly kind: "role"; readonly role: WorkspaceRole };

/**
 * DB: `access_rules` (T-08). One grant, written on one node, for one subject.
 * The subject is stored decomposed — `subject_kind` plus one of
 * `subject_user_id` / `subject_role` — and recomposed into the union on read,
 * because a polymorphic pair cannot carry a foreign key (the same reasoning as
 * canon §1.3.4). `grantedBy` is a user id, NOT a UserSummary — the frontend
 * types it `string` (src/types/permission.ts:143).
 */
interface AccessRule {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly subject: AccessSubject;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly grantedAt: string;
  readonly grantedBy: string;
}

/** Node a rule is written on, for "Inherited from Backend". Never a whole node. */
interface AccessOrigin {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly name: string;
}

/**
 * One row of the access list. FULLY DERIVED — nothing here is stored.
 * `source` distinguishes: `inherited` (nothing written here), `explicit`
 * (written here and agrees with what would flow down), `override` (written here
 * and REPLACES it), `workspace` (the membership floor).
 */
interface ResolvedAccess {
  readonly subject: AccessSubject;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly source: AccessSource;
  readonly origin: AccessOrigin | null;
  /** What the subject would have had with no rule here. Null when nothing. */
  readonly inheritedRole: WorkspaceRole | null;
  readonly inheritedFrom: AccessOrigin | null;
}

/**
 * What ONE subject holds on ONE node, and where it came from. Declared outside
 * src/types/ (src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:81-85) but it is a wire shape:
 * it is what E-044 resolves before projecting to a CapabilitySet.
 */
interface EffectiveAccess {
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly source: AccessSource;
  readonly origin: AccessOrigin | null;
}

/**
 * Coarse flags, a PROJECTION of the 39-key catalogue via capabilitiesFor
 * (src/types/permission.ts:111-118). Returned by E-022 and E-044 so a surface
 * does not have to hold the whole catalogue to grey out a button.
 */
type CapabilitySet = Readonly<Record<Capability, boolean>>;

/**
 * Static config served by E-045 so both sides agree on the copy. NOT a table
 * (canon §1.2). `module` is DERIVED from the key's first segment and is never
 * declared beside it (src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:8-14).
 */
interface PermissionDefinition {
  readonly key: PermissionKey;
  readonly module: PermissionModule;   // DERIVED from `key`
  /** Imperative: "Create columns". */
  readonly label: string;
  readonly summary: string;
}

/**
 * DB: `audit_events` (T-36). Append-only by construction — the service exposes
 * `record` and `list` and nothing else, "so no screen can grow an Edit button
 * that quietly works" (src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20). There is NO write
 * endpoint and no chapter may add one.
 *
 * `target` and `detail` are HUMAN strings and are nullable, never ids and never
 * a payload: "The UI never renders a raw audit payload (SY-ACT-40)"
 * (src/types/audit.ts:35-38). The structured payload lives in the internal
 * `context` column and is NEVER returned — see `AuditContext`.
 *
 * `ip` is stamped by the server off the socket. C-09: "the client must never
 * send one" (src/services/audit-service.ts:280-285).
 */
interface AuditEvent {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly at: string;
  readonly module: AuditModule;
  /** A catalogue key where one exists (`secret.reveal`), so a row traces to its permission. */
  readonly action: string;
  readonly actor: UserSummary;
  readonly ip: string;
  readonly severity: AuditSeverity;
  readonly target: string | null;
  readonly detail: string | null;
  readonly outcome: AuditOutcome;
}

/**
 * RECOMMENDATION (canon §5.3, OQ-25). The internal structured payload beside the
 * human `detail`. Stored in `audit_events.context JSONB`. NEVER serialised into
 * any response, including E-136 and the E-137 CSV export.
 */
interface AuditContext {
  readonly requestId: string;                    // the ULID from X-Request-Id (§7.10)
  readonly nodeId?: string;
  readonly boardId?: string;
  readonly rowId?: string;
  readonly secretId?: string;
  readonly targetUserId?: string;
  /** The permission key checked, when the row records an authorisation decision. */
  readonly permissionKey?: PermissionKey;
  readonly errorReason?: ErrorReason;
  readonly userAgent?: string;
}
```

#### 32.1.4 Layer 4 — board schema

```ts
/**
 * One test against one column of the record being evaluated.
 * `value` is read the way the column reads it: an option id for select, a user
 * id for user, `YYYY-MM-DD` for date, free text otherwise. `values` carries the
 * list for the set operators; single-value operators ignore it
 * (src/types/board.ts:38-51).
 */
interface Condition {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly operator: ConditionOperator;
  readonly value: string;
  readonly values?: readonly string[];
}

/** Conditions plus nested groups. Nesting is what makes `A and (B or C)` expressible. */
interface ConditionGroup {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly conjunction: ConditionConjunction;
  readonly conditions: readonly Condition[];
  readonly groups: readonly ConditionGroup[];       // recursive; depth capped by OQ-38
}

/**
 * A select option. Lives INSIDE board_columns.config — there is no
 * `select_options` table (canon §1.3.3), because three sibling structures in the
 * same config reference option ids by value.
 *
 * `id` is minted by the client today (src/store/board-store.ts:844) and the
 * backend stores what it is given; `"__empty__"` is RESERVED and must be refused
 * (src/lib/transition-rules.ts:27-28).
 */
interface SelectOption {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly color: SelectColor;
  /** Switched off in column settings — never selectable, whatever a record holds. */
  readonly isDisabled?: boolean;
  /** Null or absent means "always offered". */
  readonly availability?: ConditionGroup | null;
}

/**
 * What a Kanban drag, or a status edit, is allowed to do. Data, keyed by option
 * id, authored by the user: "nothing in the codebase knows that 'debug' may not
 * reach 'done'" (src/types/board.ts:82-88).
 *
 * `transitions` maps a SOURCE option id to the option ids it may move to.
 * `"__empty__"` stands for the empty bucket ON BOTH SIDES.
 * `mode` is a one-member union today, "left open for a future deny-list" (:91-92).
 */
interface TransitionRules {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  readonly mode: "allow-list";
  readonly transitions: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
}

/** Turning a long-text column into numbered steps: `B1:`, `T2.` — three fields, not a template language. */
interface StepNumbering {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  readonly prefix: string;       // may be empty
  readonly start: number;
  readonly separator: string;
}

/* ---- the seven JSONB payloads. One per ColumnType; C-06 requires all seven. --- */

interface TextConfig       { readonly placeholder?: string; }          // declared, unused today (OQ-54)
interface LongTextConfig   { readonly rows: number; readonly stepNumbering?: StepNumbering; }
interface SelectConfig {
  readonly options: readonly SelectOption[];
  readonly isMulti: boolean;
  readonly unavailableBehavior?: UnavailableOptionBehavior;
  /** Options meaning "finished". Subtask progress counts against these. */
  readonly completedOptionIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly transitionRules?: TransitionRules;
}
interface DateConfig       { readonly includesTime: boolean; }         // picks due_date vs due_at (OQ-32)
interface UserConfig       { readonly isMulti: boolean; }
interface AttachmentConfig { readonly maxFiles: number; }
interface RelationConfig {
  readonly boardId: string | null;
  readonly displayColumnId: string | null;
  readonly isMulti: boolean;
}

/** The mapped type that makes a column's config depend on its type. */
interface ColumnConfigByType {
  readonly text: TextConfig;
  readonly longText: LongTextConfig;
  readonly select: SelectConfig;
  readonly date: DateConfig;
  readonly user: UserConfig;
  readonly attachment: AttachmentConfig;
  readonly relation: RelationConfig;
}

/**
 * DB: `board_columns` (T-11). `config` is the JSONB column, and the pairing of
 * `type` with `config` is what COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH enforces (§31.4.7).
 */
interface ColumnBase {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly position: number;       // INT, densely renumbered 0..n-1 on reorder
  readonly width: number;          // clamped [88, 720] by E-053
  readonly hidden: boolean;        // silently ignored on the primary column
  /** The one column that titles a row. It can never be hidden or deleted. */
  readonly isPrimary: boolean;
}

type BoardColumnOf<T extends ColumnType> = ColumnBase & {
  readonly type: T;
  readonly config: ColumnConfigByType[T];
};

type BoardColumn = { [T in ColumnType]: BoardColumnOf<T> }[ColumnType];
```

> **`ConditionOperator` is not a superset of `FilterOperator`, despite the comment saying it is.**
> `src/types/board.ts:20-23` claims *"Deliberately a superset of `FilterOperator`"*. It is not:
> `FilterOperator` uniquely has `onOrBefore` and `onOrAfter`; `ConditionOperator` uniquely has
> `isAnyOf`, `isNoneOf` and `on`. **Ship two enums, exactly as the code has them** (canon §2.5,
> OQ-37). They govern two different features — view filtering and select-option availability — and
> a backend that merges them will accept `onOrBefore` in an availability rule that no evaluator can
> read.
>
> **And view filters do not nest.** `SavedView.filters` is a flat `ViewFilter[]` with a single
> `filterConjunction` (`src/types/board.ts:339-340`). `ConditionGroup` — the recursive one — is used
> **only** by `SelectOption.availability`. There is no `FilterGroup`, and adding one would give the
> filter bar an expressive power the frontend cannot render.

#### 32.1.5 Layer 5 — cell values

```ts
/**
 * A file attached to a RECORD. The board holds a reference, never the bytes.
 * Attachments belong to the record, not to the Drive tree — "uploading one into
 * a task does not create a file node beside the board" (src/types/board.ts:198-200).
 *
 * DB: `cell_attachments` (T-29) joined to `file_assets` (T-27). Only `assetId`
 * is persisted in the cell; `url` and `thumbnailUrl` are MINTED PER RESPONSE as
 * short-lived signed URLs and are NEVER accepted on write (OQ-75). The
 * frontend's own comment says why they cannot be stored: "Session URL for the
 * real bytes; null once the session that made it ends" (:206-207).
 *
 * `id` here IS the asset id. `uploadedBy` and `createdAt` are OPTIONAL on the
 * frontend type and the API always sends them.
 */
interface CellAttachment {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly url: string | null;            // signed, short-lived, response-only
  readonly thumbnailUrl: string | null;   // signed, short-lived, response-only
  readonly uploadedBy?: string;           // directory id
  readonly createdAt?: string;
}

/**
 * THE discriminated union of the system. Tagged with its own `kind` rather than
 * inferred from the column, so a converted column can keep the text it could
 * not parse instead of dropping the user's data (src/types/board.ts:214-218).
 *
 * A cell's `kind` MAY legitimately disagree with its column's `type`. The API
 * must not normalise that away (canon §2.5). Only an unknown tag is an error.
 *
 * The optional `text` on five of the seven branches is the escape hatch that
 * carries an unparseable value through a conversion. It is OPTIONAL, not
 * nullable: absent means there was nothing to preserve.
 *
 * DB: `board_rows.cells JSONB`, `Record<columnId, CellValue>` (canon §1.3.2).
 * There is no `cell_values` table.
 */
type CellValue =
  | { readonly kind: "text";       readonly value: string }
  | { readonly kind: "longText";   readonly value: string }
  | { readonly kind: "select";     readonly optionIds: readonly string[]; readonly text?: string }
  /** `iso` is `YYYY-MM-DD` when the column's DateConfig.includesTime is false,
   *  and full ISO 8601 when it is true. Stored as the string it was sent as; a
   *  date-only value NEVER passes through UTC (C-04, OQ-32). */
  | { readonly kind: "date";       readonly iso: string | null;           readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "user";       readonly userIds: readonly string[];   readonly text?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "attachment"; readonly attachments: readonly CellAttachment[]; readonly text?: string }
  /** `rowIds` may hold ids of DELETED rows. The frontend renders those as
   *  `[Deleted Item]`; the backend must NOT prune them (OQ-44). */
  | { readonly kind: "relation";   readonly rowIds: readonly string[];    readonly text?: string };

type CellValueOf<T extends ColumnType> = Extract<CellValue, { kind: T }>;
```

**A cell is never `null`.** The frontend writes an explicit **empty `CellValue` of the column's
kind** rather than deleting the key (`emptyCellFor`, `src/lib/cell-values.ts`), which is why
`board_rows.cells` is dense by construction and the sparsity argument for an EAV table is theoretical
(canon §1.3.2). The API does the same: clearing a cell writes `{ kind: "text", value: "" }`,
`{ kind: "select", optionIds: [] }`, `{ kind: "date", iso: null }` — never `undefined`, never a
missing key.

#### 32.1.6 Layer 6 — records

```ts
/**
 * DB: `board_rows` (T-12). One record.
 *
 * `displayId` is `custom_id` — "assigned by the BACKEND, never derived on the
 * client" (src/types/board.ts:240) — and `sequence` is its numeric part, from
 * `boards.next_sequence`, which ONLY INCREASES: deleting TASK-005 never
 * re-issues 005.
 *
 * `revision` is the optimistic-concurrency token, bumped once per WRITE however
 * many cells it touched (src/services/board-service.ts:500-520).
 *
 * `isPending` is a CLIENT-ONLY flag for an optimistic row and must never appear
 * in a response (src/types/board.ts:264-265). `id` may be a `tmp_` value on the
 * client for the same reason; the API only ever emits a UUID.
 *
 * `archivedAt` is optional AND nullable, deliberately: absent means never
 * archived, `null` means archived and then restored.
 */
interface BoardRow {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;                       // `custom_id`, e.g. TASK-042
  readonly sequence: number;                        // monotonic per board, never reused
  readonly cells: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly createdBy: string;                       // a user id, NOT a UserSummary (OQ-35)
  readonly revision: number;
  readonly archivedAt?: string | null;
  readonly parentRowId?: string | null;
  readonly isPending?: boolean;                     // CLIENT ONLY — never emitted
}

/** One cell write. The unit of E-066's batch. */
interface CellEdit {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly value: CellValue;
}

/**
 * A partial column update. Note what it does NOT carry: no `type` and no
 * `position` (OQ-39). Conversion is E-057, reordering is E-056 — both separate
 * endpoints, because both rewrite every row.
 *
 * `config` is `Partial<...>` on the frontend, which loses the type/config
 * pairing. The API narrows it back: the patch's config branch must match the
 * column's CURRENT type, or COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH.
 */
interface ColumnPatch {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly width?: number;
  readonly hidden?: boolean;
  readonly config?: Partial<ColumnConfigByType[ColumnType]>;
}

/** What a conversion WOULD do, shown before the user commits. E-057 `?dryRun=true`. */
interface ConversionPreview {
  readonly total: number;
  readonly converted: number;
  /** Values kept as `CellValue.text` with a warning because they could not be parsed. */
  readonly preserved: number;
  readonly samples: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * A stale write that was APPLIED anyway. E-066 is last-write-wins and always
 * answers 200 (§31.6). At most ONE notice per row per call.
 */
interface ConflictNotice {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly message: string;
}

/** One field that changed, ALREADY RENDERED to the text the column displays. */
interface FieldChange {
  readonly columnName: string;
  readonly from: string;
  readonly to: string;
}

/**
 * DB: `row_activity` (T-14). One entry per WRITE however many fields it touched:
 * "changed Status and Due Date" is one line with two changes under it rather
 * than two competing lines at the same second (src/types/board.ts:489-495).
 *
 * `changes` is the RENDERED form and is what the timeline reads — "it never
 * sees, and never renders, a raw payload" (:480-482). The internal
 * `raw_changes` column holding before/after CellValues is stored and NEVER
 * returned (OQ-51).
 */
interface ActivityEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly kind: ActivityKind;
  readonly actor: DirectoryUser;
  /** Human sentence fragment: `changed Status`, `created TASK-001`. */
  readonly summary: string;
  readonly changes: readonly FieldChange[];
  readonly createdAt: string;
}
```

#### 32.1.7 Layer 7 — saved views

```ts
/**
 * One filter condition. `value` is interpreted by the column's type: an option
 * id or label for select, a user id or name for user, `YYYY-MM-DD` for date,
 * free text otherwise (src/types/board.ts:296-300).
 */
interface ViewFilter {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly operator: FilterOperator;
  readonly value: string;
}

/** Multi-level: earlier entries win, later ones break ties. */
interface ViewSort {
  readonly columnId: string;
  readonly direction: SortDirection;
}

/**
 * DB: `board_views` (T-15). SHARED per board and governed by `board.view.manage`
 * — "the order is the board's, not the reader's" (E-082). Filters and sorts stay
 * shared: they are what a named view IS (OQ-46).
 *
 * Presentation only. "Records and schema live on the board, so switching views
 * never copies data" (src/types/board.ts:330-333).
 *
 * FLAT by design: there is no nested config object and no filter group.
 * Seventeen fields, five of them optional with defined defaults (T-2):
 *   columnDisplay absent  -> every column is `compact`
 *   subtaskDisplay absent -> `nested`
 *   ganttZoom absent      -> `week` (DEFAULT_GANTT_ZOOM, src/lib/board-timeline.ts:42);
 *                            a stored "day" is COERCED to "week", never rejected (:65-67)
 *   showDependencies absent -> false
 */
interface SavedView {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
  readonly filters: readonly ViewFilter[];
  readonly filterConjunction: FilterConjunction;
  readonly sorts: readonly ViewSort[];
  readonly hiddenColumnIds: readonly string[];
  /** Per-view column order; ids missing from it fall back to schema position. */
  readonly columnOrder: readonly string[];
  readonly columnWidths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  readonly columnDisplay?: Readonly<Record<string, CellDisplayMode>>;
  readonly rowHeight: RowHeight;
  readonly groupByColumnId: string | null;
  readonly hideEmptyGroups: boolean;
  readonly dateColumnId: string | null;
  readonly endDateColumnId: string | null;
  readonly subtaskDisplay?: SubtaskDisplay;
  readonly ganttZoom?: GanttZoom;
  readonly showDependencies?: boolean;
}

/**
 * RECOMMENDATION (canon §5.3, OQ-46). DB: `board_view_preferences` (T-16),
 * keyed `(view_id, user_id)`. What one VIEWER overrides on a SHARED view.
 * Deliberately narrow: widths and collapse state, never filters or sorts.
 */
interface ViewPreferences {
  readonly viewId: string;
  readonly columnWidths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  /** Group keys the viewer has collapsed. `__ungrouped__` is a legal key. */
  readonly collapsedGroupKeys: readonly string[];
  /** Row ids whose subtask children this viewer has collapsed. */
  readonly collapsedRowIds: readonly string[];
}
```

#### 32.1.8 Layer 8 — the board aggregate, templates and relations

```ts
/**
 * DB: `boards` (T-10). `node_id` is UNIQUE NOT NULL — the board keeps BOTH ids
 * and nothing re-derives either (OQ-30, P-04).
 *
 * `name` is PROJECTED from `nodes.name`, not duplicated: renaming is E-025 on
 * the node, and there is no board-rename endpoint.
 *
 * `columns` and `views` are embedded because C-11 makes a schema response a
 * COMPLETE ARRAY, never a delta — the store re-reads it wholesale
 * (src/store/board-store.ts:698).
 *
 * `templateId` is typed `BoardTemplateId` on the frontend but a user template
 * carries a UUID in the same field, so the wire type widens (OQ-47).
 */
interface Board {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly templateId?: BoardTemplateId | string;   // "for reference only"
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly name: string;                            // PROJECTED from nodes.name
  /** `TASK`, `BUG`, `QA`. `^[A-Z]{1,6}$`. */
  readonly rowIdPrefix: string;
  readonly primaryColumnId: string;
  readonly columns: readonly BoardColumn[];
  readonly views: readonly SavedView[];
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
}

/**
 * RECOMMENDATION (canon §5.3). E-048. What a board list returns WITHOUT seeding
 * or reading a single row — "Cheap — no seeding" (src/services/board-service.ts:1227).
 * The frontend's own `BoardDescriptor` (:1221-1225) carries three fields; the
 * API adds two counts it can serve from an index.
 */
interface BoardDescriptor {
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly itemCount: number;
  readonly templateId?: BoardTemplateId | string;
}

/** A view as a TEMPLATE declares it — ids are minted when it is instantiated. */
interface TemplateView {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
  readonly groupByColumnId?: string;
  readonly dateColumnId?: string;
  readonly endDateColumnId?: string;
  readonly hiddenColumnIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly sorts?: readonly ViewSort[];
  readonly filters?: readonly ViewFilter[];
}

/**
 * DB: `board_templates` (T-17), with `columns` and `views` as JSONB — a template
 * is inert data, deep-copied at instantiation, never queried per column.
 *
 * The four built-ins ship as seed rows with `is_builtin = true`. There is NO
 * tasks table, NO bugs table, NO qa_cases table and NO api_endpoints table, and
 * no chapter may introduce one (canon §1.3.5).
 *
 * `id` widens to `string` for user-authored templates (OQ-47).
 */
interface BoardTemplate {
  readonly id: BoardTemplateId | string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly rowIdPrefix: string;
  readonly primaryColumnId: string;
  readonly columns: readonly BoardColumn[];
  readonly views: readonly TemplateView[];
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive: false for a workspace-authored template. */
  readonly isBuiltin?: boolean;
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive: null for a built-in. */
  readonly workspaceId?: string | null;
}

/**
 * E-071. Every linkable row of ONE board, so relation chips resolve in ONE
 * request per target board rather than one per cell (OQ-44).
 * Filtered by read access on the target board's node.
 */
interface RelationTarget {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly title: string;              // the primary column's rendered text
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly boardName: string;
}

/**
 * E-072. Rows pointing AT this row through any relation column.
 * DB: an indexed query over `board_row_relations` (T-13), never a scan —
 * "the two directions can never disagree"
 * (src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:14-19). There is no
 * `backlinks` table and no mirrored value.
 */
interface Backlink {
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly boardNodeId: string;
  readonly boardName: string;
  readonly columnName: string;
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly title: string;
}
```

#### 32.1.9 Layer 9 — documents, blocks and versions

```ts
/** Every block carries an id. Nine interfaces cover fourteen BlockType values. */
interface BlockBase { readonly id: string; }

/** Five BlockTypes, one interface: a single editable line of prose. */
interface TextBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "heading1" | "heading2" | "heading3" | "paragraph" | "quote";
  readonly text: string;
}

interface ChecklistBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "checklist";
  readonly text: string;
  readonly isChecked: boolean;
}

interface ListBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "bulletList" | "numberedList";
  readonly text: string;
}

interface CodeBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "code";
  readonly code: string;
  readonly language: CodeLanguage;      // NOT ConfigFormat — code blocks only
}

/**
 * One picture inside an image block. `assetId` is what is PERSISTED;
 * `url` is minted per response as a signed URL (OQ-75). The frontend types
 * `assetId` as nullable only because the mock dataset seeds images without one
 * (src/types/document.ts:58-60) — the API always sends an asset id.
 */
interface DocumentImage {
  readonly assetId: string | null;
  readonly url: string;                 // signed, short-lived, response-only
  readonly alt: string;
}

interface ImageBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "image";
  readonly images: readonly DocumentImage[];   // a block holds as many as you add
  readonly caption: string;
}

interface AttachmentBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "attachment";
  readonly assetId: string | null;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly mimeType: string;
}

/** Unfurled by E-118, server-side and SSRF-guarded. The four fields are stored. */
interface LinkBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "link";
  readonly url: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly siteName: string;
}

interface TableBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "table";
  readonly hasHeaderRow: boolean;
  /** RECTANGULAR — every row carries the same number of cells. Validated on write. */
  readonly rows: readonly (readonly string[])[];
}

/** DV-EMB-25: two ids, never a copy of the board's records. */
interface EmbedBlock extends BlockBase {
  readonly type: "embed";
  readonly boardNodeId: string | null;
  readonly viewId: string | null;
}

type Block =
  | TextBlock | ChecklistBlock | ListBlock | CodeBlock
  | ImageBlock | AttachmentBlock | LinkBlock | TableBlock | EmbedBlock;

/** Blocks that hold a single editable `text` field. */
type TextualBlock = TextBlock | ChecklistBlock | ListBlock;
type TextualBlockType = TextualBlock["type"];

/**
 * DB: `documents` (T-18), `node_id` UNIQUE NOT NULL. `blocks` is the JSONB column.
 *
 * FIVE fields are PROJECTED from `nodes`, not stored twice (OQ-30, OQ-56):
 * `title` (= nodes.name), `icon`, `isPinned`, `isLocked`, `isArchived`.
 * The node owns them; the document row must not carry a second copy.
 *
 * `lockedBy` is resolved from the SESSION at lock time, never from the request
 * body (C-09, OQ-60).
 */
interface WorkspaceDocument {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly title: string;               // PROJECTED from nodes.name
  readonly icon: string;                // emoji
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
  readonly isPinned: boolean;           // PROJECTED
  readonly isLocked: boolean;           // PROJECTED
  readonly lockedBy: UserSummary | null;
  readonly isArchived: boolean;         // PROJECTED
  readonly owner: UserSummary;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly version: number;             // bumped per saved version, not per keystroke
}

/** What E-092 accepts. Never the whole document — no ids, no flags, no owner. */
interface DocumentDraft {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly icon: string;
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
}

/**
 * DB: `document_versions` (T-19). A FULL block snapshot per version.
 * `summary` is `+3 −1 lines`, computed at write time.
 */
interface DocumentVersion {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;
}

/**
 * The SHARED history read model, "whatever produced it" — a page, a config
 * document, or a rotated secret (src/types/system.ts:203-207). E-095 returns
 * these for all three; the node's kind selects the store.
 *
 * `hasSnapshot: false` is the secret case: the entry records THAT something
 * changed without holding the value, and can be read but never diffed or
 * restored (:215-220). `lines` is empty for such an entry.
 */
interface VersionEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;
  readonly lines: readonly string[];
  readonly hasSnapshot: boolean;
}

interface DiffLine { readonly kind: DiffKind; readonly text: string; }
interface DiffSummary { readonly added: number; readonly removed: number; }
```

#### 32.1.10 Layer 10 — devtools

```ts
/**
 * RECOMMENDATION (canon §5.3, OQ-63). DB: `environments` (T-26), workspace-scoped,
 * seeded Development / Staging / Production. DV-ENV-21 requires ONE shared list
 * that the bug board, the QA board, the API board, config documents and secrets
 * all point at rather than re-declaring (src/lib/board-templates.ts:24-34).
 *
 * Shaped like SelectOption on purpose: the config editor and the secret panel
 * render it with the same control the select columns use.
 */
interface Environment {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly color: SelectColor;
  readonly position: number;
}

/**
 * DB: `config_documents` (T-20), `node_id` as the PK — a config document has NO
 * id of its own (OQ-30; the frontend type carries only `nodeId`).
 *
 * The wire field is `format`, NEVER `language`: "It is what the field has always
 * been called and what the stored documents carry. The UI says 'Language'"
 * (src/types/devtools.ts:19-21).
 *
 * `name` is PROJECTED from nodes.name. `environmentOptionId` references
 * `environments.id`.
 */
interface ConfigDocument {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly name: string;                // PROJECTED from nodes.name
  readonly format: ConfigFormat;
  readonly environmentOptionId: string;
  readonly content: string;             // opaque; stored verbatim, never reformatted
  readonly version: number;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly updatedBy: UserSummary;
}

/**
 * DB: `config_versions` (T-21). A full content snapshot per version.
```
