```ts
 * `isAutosave` drives the FOLD RULE: "The next autosave by the same author
 * rewrites this entry instead of adding one" (src/types/devtools.ts:59-63).
 * OPTIONAL, and absent means false.
 */
interface ConfigVersion {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly content: string;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly author: UserSummary;
  readonly summary: string;             // `+3 −1 lines`
  readonly isAutosave?: boolean;
}

/**
 * DB: `secrets` (T-23). THE ONLY SHAPE THE CLIENT EVER HOLDS.
 *
 * "There is no `value` here on purpose: plaintext only ever arrives from an
 * explicit, permission-checked reveal, and it is never written back into this
 * shape" (src/types/devtools.ts:68-72).
 *
 * `maskedValue` is a CONSTANT twelve U+2022 bullets — "never derived from the
 * real value's length" (:76), because a length is information.
 * `value_encrypted BYTEA` is NEVER selected on a list read.
 */
interface SecretEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly key: string;
  readonly maskedValue: string;         // always "••••••••••••" — 12 bullets, constant
  readonly environmentOptionId: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly rotatedBy: UserSummary;
  readonly note?: string;
}

/** DB: `secret_documents` (T-22) — the container only, `node_id` as the PK. */
interface SecretDocument {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly name: string;                // PROJECTED from nodes.name
  readonly entries: readonly SecretEntry[];
}

/**
 * RECOMMENDATION (canon §5.3), and it exists in the frontend as
 * `SecretDraftEntry` (src/services/devtools-service.ts:458-471).
 * What E-102 accepts, in the order given — the whole list is replaced.
 *
 * An OMITTED `value` means "leave the stored ciphertext untouched". That is what
 * lets the editor rename a key, reorder the list or delete a neighbour "without
 * ever holding the plaintext of the rows it is not changing" (:462-469).
 * `value: ""` is therefore NOT the same as omitting it — it sets the secret to
 * the empty string. T-2, and here it has teeth.
 */
interface SecretDraftEntry {
  readonly id: string | null;           // null for a secret being added
  readonly key: string;
  readonly value?: string;              // OMITTED means untouched
  readonly environmentOptionId?: string;
  readonly note?: string;
}

/**
 * DB: `secret_access_events` (T-25). Per-secret reveal/copy/rotate trail,
 * ALLOWED AND DENIED ALIKE. `ip` is recorded by the server — "the client never
 * sources this" (src/types/devtools.ts:106-107).
 *
 * Written in the SAME TRANSACTION as an `audit_events` row (OQ-68): two readers,
 * one write.
 */
interface SecretAuditEntry {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly action: SecretAction;
  readonly secretId: string;
  readonly key: string;
  readonly actor: UserSummary;
  readonly at: string;
  readonly ip: string;
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive: false for a denied or throttled attempt. */
  readonly wasAllowed?: boolean;
}
```

#### 32.1.11 Layer 11 — files

```ts
/**
 * DB: `file_assets` (T-27). The STORED OBJECT, independent of where it is
 * referenced from. One row per set of bytes; four typed join tables record where
 * it is used (canon §1.3.4).
 *
 * `folderId` is a convenience join through `file_nodes`, null for an asset that
 * is not in the tree at all — a board-cell or comment attachment (OQ-74).
 * `size_bytes` is the SINGLE SOURCE for the workspace quota counter.
 */
interface FileAsset {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly extension: string;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly kind: FileKind;              // DERIVED from extension, then MIME
  readonly owner: UserSummary;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly folderId: string | null;
}

/** A rectangular grid of text cells. src/lib/grid.ts:3. */
type Grid = readonly (readonly string[])[];

/**
 * E-114. Everything the preview surface needs, RESOLVED BY THE SERVER.
 * Strategy is decided by EXTENSION FIRST, MIME second.
 * `unsupported` is a 200, not an error (§31.6).
 *
 * `language` is a bare `string` in the frontend (src/types/file.ts:25);
 * RECOMMENDATION: type it `ConfigFormat`, derived from the extension, defaulting
 * to "text" (OQ-76). Widening it later is additive; narrowing it later is not.
 */
type FilePreview =
  | { readonly kind: "image";       readonly url: string; readonly alt: string }
  | { readonly kind: "pdf";         readonly url: string }
  | { readonly kind: "text";        readonly content: string; readonly language: ConfigFormat }
  | { readonly kind: "sheet";       readonly rows: Grid; readonly sheetName: string }
  | { readonly kind: "unsupported"; readonly reason: string };

/** E-115. Both fields authoritative: the size the server stored, and when. */
interface SaveTextResult {
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly savedAt: string;
}

/** Rendered for any file, previewable or not. Label/value pairs, already formatted. */
interface FileMetadataEntry {
  readonly label: string;
  readonly value: string;
}

/** E-118. The unfurl result, stored into a LinkBlock by the caller. */
interface LinkMetadata {
  readonly url: string;                 // NORMALISED, not the raw input
  readonly title: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly siteName: string;
}
```

#### 32.1.12 Layer 12 — collaboration

```ts
/**
 * A pointer to one thing in the workspace. Comments, watches, notifications,
 * search hits, My Work items and the recent list all address their target
 * through this ONE shape, so a single navigation helper routes any of them
 * (src/types/collab.ts:9-15).
 *
 * DB: DECOMPOSED into columns on every table that carries one —
 * `target_kind`, `target_node_id`, `target_row_id`, `target_board_id` — never a
 * JSONB blob, because they are indexed and joined.
 *
 * `label` is RESOLVED LIVE on read everywhere EXCEPT on `notifications`, where
 * it is frozen at creation because a notification is a historical statement
 * (OQ-79).
 */
interface EntityRef {
  readonly kind: EntityKind;
  readonly nodeId: string;              // the routing anchor
  readonly rowId?: string;              // present iff kind === "row"
  readonly boardId?: string;            // present iff kind === "row"
  readonly label: string;
}

/**
 * DB: `comment_attachments` (T-30) joined to `file_assets`. Note it is a
 * DIFFERENT shape from CellAttachment — no thumbnail, no uploader, no timestamp
 * (src/types/collab.ts:30-37). Canon §1.3.4 keeps the three shapes apart
 * deliberately; only the underlying asset is unified.
 */
interface CommentAttachment {
  readonly id: string;                  // the asset id
  readonly name: string;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly url: string | null;          // signed, short-lived, response-only
}

/**
 * DB: `comments` (T-33).
 *
 * `body` is the RAW text with mentions encoded as `@[Name](usr_id)`. The API
 * PARSES `mentionedUserIds` from it server-side and IGNORES any client-supplied
 * list (E-120) — a mention list a client can write is a notification a client
 * can forge.
 *
 * `targetKey` is DERIVED — `refKey(target)`, e.g. `row:brd_x:row_y` or
 * `document:nd_z`. It is the realtime channel key (RT-01/RT-02) and the
 * comment-draft localStorage key; store the decomposed columns and compute this.
 *
 * `parentId` is the ROOT being replied to. Replies never nest past one level:
 * a reply to a reply RE-PARENTS to the root (E-125).
 *
 * `isPending` is CLIENT ONLY and must never be emitted.
 */
interface Comment {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly targetKey: string;           // DERIVED from `target`
  readonly target: EntityRef;
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  readonly author: DirectoryUser;
  readonly body: string;
  readonly mentionedUserIds: readonly string[];   // PARSED SERVER-SIDE from `body`
  readonly attachments: readonly CommentAttachment[];
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly isEdited: boolean;
  readonly isPending?: boolean;         // CLIENT ONLY — never emitted
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive (OQ-80). Resolution is a ROOT-ONLY property. */
  readonly isResolved?: boolean;
  readonly resolvedBy?: UserSummary | null;
  readonly resolvedAt?: string | null;
  /** RECOMMENDATION, additive (OQ-80). A tombstone keeps thread structure intact. */
  readonly isDeleted?: boolean;
}

/** A root comment with its replies. Replies never nest further than one level. */
interface CommentThread {
  readonly root: Comment;
  readonly replies: readonly Comment[];
}

/**
 * DB: `watches` (T-34), keyed (user_id, target_kind, target_node_id, target_row_id).
 * Only `row`, `document` and `board` are watchable — "a file or folder has no
 * activity stream" (src/types/collab.ts:85-86). Anything else is refused with
 * WATCH_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED, not silently ignored.
 */
interface WatchEntry {
  readonly targetKey: string;           // DERIVED
  readonly ref: EntityRef;
  readonly since: string;
}

/**
 * DB: `notifications` (T-35). ONE ROW PER RECIPIENT — fan-out on write, not a
 * join at read time.
 *
 * `title` and `body` are PRE-RENDERED at creation and frozen. So is
 * `target.label`. A notification is a historical statement: it says what was
 * true when it was sent, and re-resolving the label later would rewrite history
 * (OQ-79).
 *
 * `isRead` is DERIVED from `read_at IS NOT NULL`.
 * `recipientId` is on the wire but is ALWAYS the caller: `list()` only ever
 * returns the signed-in user's inbox (:104), and RT-03 is delivered only to its
 * recipient.
 */
interface AppNotification {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly reason: NotificationReason;
  readonly recipientId: string;
  readonly actor: UserSummary;
  readonly title: string;               // PRE-RENDERED, frozen
  readonly body: string;                // PRE-RENDERED, frozen
  readonly target: EntityRef | null;    // null for workspace-level system notices
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly isRead: boolean;             // DERIVED from read_at
}

/**
 * Per-device by nature. STAYS IN localStorage under `nexdrop-recent`, capped at
 * RECENT_LIMIT = 10, least-recently-used out (src/store/recent-store.ts:9-18,
 * src/config/app.ts:36). NOT a table and NOT an endpoint (OQ-96).
 * Documented here because the brief asked for `RecentResource`.
 */
interface RecentEntry {
  readonly ref: EntityRef;
  readonly visitedAt: string;
}
```

> **There is no `Mention` type and no `NotificationPayload` union, and neither should be added.**
>
> **A mention is an encoding, not an entity.** It lives inside `Comment.body` as `@[Name](usr_id)`
> and is projected into `mentionedUserIds`. The parsed form — `BodySegment`, a union of
> `text | mention | record` (`src/types/collab.ts:69-72`) — is **UI-only** and never crosses the
> wire (canon §2.9). Canon §1.2 does not list a `comment_mentions` table; the array on the comment
> plus the fan-out into `notifications` is the whole model.
>
> **A notification carries pre-rendered copy, not a typed payload.** `AppNotification` has `title`
> and `body` as strings (`src/types/collab.ts:107-108`). A `NotificationPayload` union keyed by
> `reason` would mean the client renders the sentence, which breaks the freeze rule (OQ-79): the
> label a notification was sent with must not change when the thing it points at is renamed.
>
> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-89) — nothing emits `assigned`, `watch` or `system` notifications.**
> **Evidence** — `notificationService.emit` has exactly two callers, both in `comment-service.ts`,
> both producing `mention` or `comment` (`src/services/comment-service.ts:120-150`). The other
> three `NotificationReason` members are declared and never produced.
> **Recommendation** — E-062/E-066 emit `assigned` when a user cell gains an id; the watcher fan-out
> emits `watch`; `system` stays reserved for workspace-level notices with `target: null`. All three
> render their copy **server-side at emission**, exactly as `mention` and `comment` already do.
> **Impact if wrong** — three of the four inbox tabs (`NotificationTab`) stay permanently empty, and
> the tab mapping in the frontend (OQ-90) becomes untestable.

#### 32.1.13 Layer 13 — search, My Work and the dashboard

```ts
/**
 * E-133. `api`, `bug` and `qa` are records whose board was generated from the
 * matching template — DERIVED from `boards.template_id` at read time
 * (src/services/search-service.ts:39-43), never a schema. `row` is every other
 * record; `place` is a folder or project.
 */
interface SearchResult {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly kind: SearchResultKind;
  readonly title: string;
  /** Where it lives — the board name or the folder path. */
  readonly subtitle: string;
  readonly snippet: string | null;      // matching excerpt, for comments and long text
  readonly ref: EntityRef;
  readonly score: number;               // higher sorts first WITHIN its group
}

/** Groups come back in a FIXED order, each capped at SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5. */
interface SearchGroup {
  readonly kind: SearchResultKind;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly results: readonly SearchResult[];
}

/**
 * E-134. `id` is "the row id, prefixed by the widget it belongs to"
 * (src/types/collab.ts:125) — one record can legitimately appear in two widgets
 * and must not collide as a React key.
 *
 * `dueIso` is `YYYY-MM-DD` or a full instant depending on the source column's
 * DateConfig.includesTime, carried through UNCHANGED (C-04, OQ-32).
 */
interface MyWorkItem {
  readonly id: string;                  // `${widgetId}:${rowId}`
  readonly ref: EntityRef;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly boardName: string;
  readonly statusLabel: string | null;
  readonly statusColor: SelectColor | null;
  readonly dueIso: string | null;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
  readonly assignees: readonly DirectoryUser[];
}

/** `items` is capped at MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6; `total` is UNCAPPED, so "12 of 40" stays honest. */
interface MyWorkWidget {
  readonly id: MyWorkWidgetId;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly items: readonly MyWorkItem[];
  readonly total: number;
}

interface DashboardBucket {
  readonly id: DashboardBucketId;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly color: SelectColor;
}

/** A board that contributed to a widget, so a count can be traced back. */
interface DashboardSource {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly count: number;
}

/**
 * `unmapped` is records the widget SAW but could not place — "Reported rather
 * than silently dropped" (src/types/dashboard.ts:39-43). It is the honest
 * consequence of OQ-49: two competing definitions of "done".
 */
interface DashboardWidget {
  readonly id: DashboardWidgetId;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly buckets: readonly DashboardBucket[];
  readonly total: number;
  readonly unmapped: number;
  readonly sources: readonly DashboardSource[];
}

/**
 * E-135. ONE aggregate call, not three. `isNewWorkspace` and `boardCount` are
 * cross-widget, which is why they cannot be assembled client-side from three
 * responses. Archived rows are excluded from EVERY tally.
 */
interface DashboardSummary {
  readonly widgets: readonly DashboardWidget[];
  readonly isNewWorkspace: boolean;
  readonly boardCount: number;
  readonly recordCount: number;
}
```

#### 32.1.14 Layer 14 — bulk, import and export

```ts
/** Why one selected record was left untouched. */
interface BulkSkip {
  readonly rowId: string;
  readonly displayId: string;
  readonly reason: BulkSkipReason;      // archived | not_found | permission_denied
}

/**
 * The answer to one bulk call. `applied` and `skipped` together account for
 * EVERY id the caller sent: requested === applied.length + skipped.length.
 * That invariant is what makes partial success reportable instead of silent
 * (src/types/system.ts:32-36).
 *
 * `rows` is empty on a delete; the ids are in `applied`.
 */
interface BulkResult {
  readonly requested: number;
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];   // authoritative records for the ids that changed
  readonly applied: readonly string[];
  readonly skipped: readonly BulkSkip[];
}

/** Cross-board move. One transaction over BOTH boards. */
interface BulkMoveResult extends BulkResult {
  readonly targetBoardId: string;
  readonly targetNodeId: string;
  /** Source columns the target has no counterpart for. Named, never dropped quietly. */
  readonly droppedColumns: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * One row of the uploaded file. The row number travels WITH the cells rather
 * than beside them: "a row number kept in a parallel array is one filter away
 * from describing a different row than the one it is printed next to"
 * (src/types/system.ts:54-61).
 */
interface ImportSourceRow {
  readonly sourceRowNumber: number;     // 1-based, counting the header — what Excel shows
  readonly cells: readonly string[];
}

interface ImportSource {
  readonly fileName: string;
  readonly sheetName: string | null;
  readonly headers: readonly string[];
  readonly rows: readonly ImportSourceRow[];
}

/**
 * Where one source column's values go. A tagged union rather than a bag of
 * optional fields, "so 'ignored', 'into an existing column' and 'into a column
 * this import creates' cannot overlap and a half-set target cannot exist"
 * (src/types/system.ts:76-84).
 */
type MappingTarget =
  | { readonly kind: "ignore" }
  | { readonly kind: "existing"; readonly columnId: string }
  | { readonly kind: "create";   readonly name: string; readonly type: ColumnType };

interface ColumnMapping {
  readonly sourceIndex: number;
  readonly target: MappingTarget;
}

/** A mapping the import refuses to run with, named for the user to fix. */
interface MappingConflict {
  readonly sourceIndex: number;
  readonly message: string;
}

/** One row-level problem. Travels inside a 200, never as an error (§31.4.10). */
interface ImportIssue {
  readonly rowNumber: number;           // the FILE's number, header included
  readonly sourceHeader: string;
  readonly columnName: string;
  readonly value: string;
  readonly message: string;
}

interface ImportDraftRow {
  readonly rowNumber: number;           // the file's own, never the board's
  readonly cells: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
  readonly invalidColumnIds: readonly string[];
}

/** E-084. What an import WOULD write, computed before anything is sent. Not persisted. */
interface ImportPlan {
  readonly drafts: readonly ImportDraftRow[];
  readonly issues: readonly ImportIssue[];
  readonly mappedColumnCount: number;
  readonly newColumnCount: number;
  readonly validCount: number;
  readonly invalidCount: number;
  /** Source rows with nothing in ANY column — never imported, and not an issue. */
  readonly blankCount: number;
  /** Empty when the mapping is runnable. Non-empty means IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED. */
  readonly conflicts: readonly MappingConflict[];
}

/** E-085. ONE transaction: column creation, column removal and row inserts all land or none do. */
interface ImportOutcome {
  readonly created: number;
  readonly skipped: number;
  readonly issues: readonly ImportIssue[];
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];
  /** Columns the board had that the file did not, removed on the user's say-so. */
  readonly removedColumns?: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * E-086 for `view` and `selection` scope. `omittedColumns` implies column-level
 * permissions that exist NOWHERE in the frontend (OQ-29); until they do, the API
 * always sends an empty array rather than dropping the field.
 */
interface ExportOutcome {
  readonly fileName: string;
  readonly rowCount: number;
  readonly columnCount: number;
  readonly omittedColumns: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * RECOMMENDATION (OQ-42). E-086 for `board` scope, which is async.
 * DB: `export_jobs` (T-39).
 */
interface ExportJob {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly boardId: string;
  readonly scope: ExportScope;
  readonly format: ExportFormat;
  readonly state: "queued" | "running" | "ready" | "failed" | "expired";
  /** Signed URL, present only while `state === "ready"`. */
  readonly downloadUrl: string | null;
  readonly expiresAt: string | null;
  readonly createdAt: string;
}
```

#### 32.1.15 Layer 15 — errors and realtime frames

`AppErrorCode`, `ApiError`, `ErrorResponse`, `FieldError` and the full `ErrorDetails` union are
defined in **§31.1** and **§31.5** and are not repeated. `ErrorReason` is the union of the 104
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE literals catalogued in §31.4.

```ts
/**
 * The realtime frame envelope. Delivery is AT-LEAST-ONCE with client-side dedup
 * by `id` (src/lib/realtime/client.ts:21, SEEN_LIMIT = 512), so exactly-once is
 * not required. UNKNOWN TYPES ARE IGNORED by the client
 * (src/types/realtime.ts:14) — new frames ship without a client release.
 */
interface RealtimeEvent {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly at: string;
  readonly origin: "local" | "remote";
  readonly payload: RealtimePayload;
}

/**
 * Five EXISTING frames the client handles today, plus six RECOMMENDATION frames
 * (canon §7.2, OQ-99). Every added frame carries IDS ONLY, following the RT-05
 * precedent: "a frame announcing a revocation must not be the thing that leaks
 * what was revoked" (src/types/realtime.ts:20-25). The receiver refetches.
 */
type RealtimePayload =
  // ---- EXISTING
  | { readonly type: "comment.created";      readonly targetKey: string; readonly comment: Comment }
  | { readonly type: "comment.updated";      readonly targetKey: string; readonly comment: Comment }
  | { readonly type: "notification.created"; readonly notification: AppNotification }
  | { readonly type: "notification.read";    readonly notificationIds: readonly string[] }
  | { readonly type: "permission.changed";
      readonly workspaceId: string;
      readonly nodeId: string | null;        // null when the change is workspace membership
      readonly userIds: readonly string[] }
  // ---- RECOMMENDATION (OQ-99)
  | { readonly type: "row.created";  readonly boardId: string; readonly rowId: string; readonly revision: number }
  | { readonly type: "row.updated";  readonly boardId: string; readonly rowId: string; readonly revision: number }
  | { readonly type: "row.archived"; readonly boardId: string; readonly rowId: string;
      readonly revision: number; readonly isArchived: boolean }
  | { readonly type: "row.deleted";  readonly boardId: string; readonly rowIds: readonly string[] }
  | { readonly type: "board.schema.changed"; readonly boardId: string }
  | { readonly type: "node.changed";
      readonly workspaceId: string;
      readonly nodeId: string;
      readonly change: "created" | "renamed" | "moved" | "archived" | "trashed" | "restored" };

type RealtimeEventType = RealtimePayload["type"];
```

`presence.changed` (RT-12) is **deliberately omitted from the union**. No frontend component
consumes presence, and canon §7.2 says so: *"Do not build this until a surface asks for it."*
Adding it later is additive and costs a client release nothing (unknown types are ignored).


---

### 32.2 Request DTOs

One per mutating endpoint, named `<Verb><Noun>Request` (canon §5.1). A `GET` takes query
parameters, not a body; where a `GET`'s parameter set is complex enough to be worth naming, the
DTO below documents the **query string**, and the field name is the parameter name.

**Three rules bind every request DTO and are not repeated on each one:**

1. **The caller's identity, role, IP and clock never appear in a body.** *"A role the client sends
   is a claim, not a fact, and an endpoint that trusts one is not enforcing anything — it is asking
   the caller how much access they would like"* (`src/services/authz.ts:24-27`). Four shapes in the
   frontend violate this and are fixed here: `ListFilesInput.canView`, `MyWorkInput.userId`,
   `SetWatchInput.userId`, `SearchInput.role`/`.user`, and `RevealInput.role` (OQ-18 … OQ-21).
2. **Server-owned fields are refused, not ignored.** `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `createdBy`,
   `revision`, `version`, `sequence`, `displayId`, `slug`, and every `url`/`thumbnailUrl` are
   rejected with `VALIDATION_FAILED` if present. Silently ignoring them hides a client bug for
   months.
3. **A `PATCH` body omits what it does not change.** `undefined` and "absent" are the same thing;
   `null` means "set to empty" and is only legal on a field typed `T | null`.

#### 32.2.0 Request-name alias resolution

| Proposed name | Canonical name | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateFolderRequest`, `CreateBoardRequest`, `CreatePageRequest` | **`CreateNodeRequest`** | One endpoint (E-024) with `kind` in the body. Five create endpoints over one `nodes` table would each need the same slug, parent, access and permission logic (canon §1.3.1). |
| `MoveFolderRequest` | **`MoveNodeRequest`** | Same reason: E-026 moves any node. |
| `UpdateFolderAccessRequest` | **`SetNodeAccessModeRequest`** + **`SetAccessRuleRequest`** | Two endpoints, because they are two different writes: E-041 changes the *mode*, E-042 upserts one *rule*. Collapsing them would make "restrict this folder" and "grant Priya edit" the same call. |
| `UpdateRowRequest` | **`UpdateCellsRequest`** | E-066 is a **batch of cell edits**, not a row patch — P-03 forbids a per-cell endpoint and the store sends many edits per call. |
| `BulkImportRowsRequest` | **`CommitImportRequest`** | The import is not a bulk row write: it creates columns, removes columns and inserts rows in one transaction (E-085). |
| `CreateSavedViewRequest` | **`CreateViewRequest`** | canon §5.4. |
| `RequestUploadRequest` | **`CreateUploadRequest`** | canon §5.4; also avoids `Request…Request`. |
| `CreateTransitionRuleRequest` | *(no such DTO)* | Transition rules are a field of `SelectConfig`, written through **`UpdateColumnRequest.config`** (E-053). They are not a separate resource: splitting them out would put one atomic configuration across two tables with no FK able to protect the option ids they reference (canon §1.3.3). |

#### 32.2.1 `identity`

```ts
/** E-001. RECOMMENDATION (OQ-01). */
interface LoginRequest {
  readonly email: string;
  readonly password: string;
}

/**
 * E-003. The body is EMPTY: the refresh token arrives in the httpOnly cookie
 * scoped to /api/v1/auth (§8.3). A token in the body would be readable by
 * JavaScript, which is the whole thing the cookie exists to prevent.
 */
interface RefreshSessionRequest { /* intentionally empty */ }

/** E-005. Only what a person may change about themselves. Never `email`, never a role. */
interface UpdateProfileRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly avatarUrl?: string | null;
  readonly accentColor?: string | null;
}
```

#### 32.2.2 `workspace`

```ts
/**
 * E-008. Mirrors NewWorkspaceInput (src/lib/workspace-access.ts:189-194).
 * `slug`, `plan` and `members` are NOT accepted: the slug is minted from the
 * name, the plan is `free`, and THE CREATOR BECOMES ADMIN IN THE SAME WRITE
 * (:212-238) — a workspace with no admin is a workspace nobody can administer.
 */
interface CreateWorkspaceRequest {
  readonly name: string;                // 1..60, trimmed
  readonly description?: string;        // 0..280
  readonly badge?: string;              // 1..2 chars; derived from `name` when absent
  readonly color?: string;              // CSS token; cycled from the palette when absent
}

/** E-010. `slug` may change; `plan` is a billing operation and is not here. */
interface UpdateWorkspaceRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly description?: string | null;
  readonly slug?: string;
  readonly badge?: string;
  readonly color?: string;
}

/** E-013. `role` is the role being GRANTED, not the caller's. */
interface InviteMemberRequest {
  readonly email: string;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
}

/** E-014. Refused when it would leave zero admins — WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN. */
interface UpdateMemberRoleRequest {
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
}

/** E-019. The token is the path parameter; the body carries nothing else. */
interface AcceptInvitationRequest { /* intentionally empty */ }
```

#### 32.2.3 `drive`

```ts
/**
 * E-024. ONE create endpoint, discriminated by `kind`. The per-kind extras are
 * a discriminated union so a `templateId` cannot be sent for a folder.
 *
 * `slug` is NOT accepted — it is minted from `name` and uniquified against the
 * siblings, EXCLUDING trashed rows so a restore never collides
 * (src/store/workspace-store.ts:472-480). It is minted ONCE and never re-minted
 * on rename (OQ-09).
 */
type CreateNodeRequest =
  | { readonly kind: "project"; readonly name: string; readonly parentId: string | null;
      readonly description?: string; readonly color?: string; readonly status?: ProjectStatus }
  | { readonly kind: "folder";  readonly name: string; readonly parentId: string | null;
      readonly color?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "document"; readonly name: string; readonly parentId: string | null;
      readonly documentKind?: DocumentKind;      // absent means "page"
      readonly icon?: string;
      /** config documents only; ignored for a page or secret. */
      readonly format?: ConfigFormat;
      readonly environmentOptionId?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "board";   readonly name: string; readonly parentId: string | null;
      readonly boardKind?: BoardKind;
      /** A BoardTemplateId or a user template's UUID. Absent uses the default schema. */
      readonly templateId?: BoardTemplateId | string }
  /** A file node is NOT created here — it is created by E-111 with
   *  `createDriveNode: true`, because the bytes must land first (OQ-74). */
  ;

/** E-025. Rename only. The slug does NOT change (OQ-09). */
interface RenameNodeRequest {
  readonly name: string;
}

/**
 * E-026. `position` is reserved for ordered siblings; the tree is name-sorted
 * today. The slug IS re-uniquified against the new siblings here — that is the
 * one place it is re-minted (OQ-10).
 */
interface MoveNodeRequest {
  readonly targetParentId: string | null;   // null moves to the workspace root
  readonly position?: number;
}

/**
 * E-027. Recursive by default, content included (OQ-12).
 * `includeSecrets` defaults to FALSE: duplicating a folder must not silently
 * copy credentials into a second, differently-permissioned place.
 */
interface DuplicateNodeRequest {
  readonly targetParentId?: string | null;  // absent duplicates beside the original
  readonly name?: string;                   // absent appends " copy" and uniquifies
  readonly includeSecrets?: boolean;        // default false
}

/** E-030 / E-031 are PUT/DELETE on a boolean sub-resource; neither takes a body. */
interface SetNodeArchivedRequest { /* intentionally empty — the method is the verb */ }

/** E-021, as a query string: `?path=development/backend/api-notes`. */
interface ResolvePathRequest {
  /** Slash-joined slugs, no leading slash. An empty string resolves the root. */
  readonly path: string;
}

/** E-035, as a query string. Name match only — cheap, and not the full-text search (OQ-94). */
interface SearchNodesRequest {
  readonly q: string;
  readonly limit?: number;
}
```

#### 32.2.4 `governance`

```ts
/** E-041. Setting `inherit` does NOT delete the node's rules; it stops them applying. */
interface SetNodeAccessModeRequest {
  readonly accessMode: NodeAccessMode;
}

/**
 * E-042. UPSERT by (node, subject): a second write for the same subject REPLACES
 * the first rather than creating a duplicate. `grantedBy` and `grantedAt` come
 * from the session and the clock (C-09).
 */
interface SetAccessRuleRequest {
  readonly subject: AccessSubject;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
}

/**
 * E-136, as a query string. Mirrors AuditQuery (src/types/audit.ts:42-48) and
 * adds the three the frontend lacks: a date range and a cursor (OQ-28).
 * `"all"` is a literal sentinel the frontend already sends, kept so the client
 * does not have to omit a key to mean "no filter".
 */
interface AuditQueryRequest {
  readonly module?: AuditModule | "all";
  readonly severity?: AuditSeverity | "all";
  readonly actorId?: string | "all";
  readonly search?: string;
  readonly from?: string;               // ISO 8601, inclusive
  readonly to?: string;                 // ISO 8601, exclusive
  readonly cursor?: string;
  readonly limit?: number;              // default AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE = 40
}
```

#### 32.2.5 `boards` — the board and its columns

```ts
/** E-050. `rowIdPrefix` is normalised to `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` before validation (OQ-43). */
interface UpdateBoardRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly rowIdPrefix?: string;
  readonly primaryColumnId?: string;    // must name an existing, non-hidden column
}

/**
 * E-052. `name` is DE-DUPLICATED silently against the board's current schema —
 * `Notes`, `Notes 2`, … — because the importer pairs source columns to board
 * columns by name (src/services/board-service.ts:550-554).
 *
 * `config` is optional; absent means the type's default config. When present it
 * MUST match the branch `type` names, or COLUMN_TYPE_CONFIG_MISMATCH.
 * `atIndex` inserts; absent appends.
 */
type CreateColumnRequest = {
  [T in ColumnType]: {
    readonly type: T;
    readonly name: string;
    readonly config?: ColumnConfigByType[T];
    readonly atIndex?: number;
  }
}[ColumnType];

/**
 * E-053. Mirrors ColumnPatch (src/types/board.ts:446-451) with the config
 * narrowed back to the column's CURRENT type.
 *
 * NO `type` and NO `position` (OQ-39): conversion is E-057, reorder is E-056.
 * `hidden` is SILENTLY IGNORED on the primary column — not an error, because
 * the frontend's own schema helper drops it rather than refusing.
 * `width` is clamped to [88, 720] rather than refused.
 */
interface UpdateColumnRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly width?: number;
  readonly hidden?: boolean;
  /** A partial config for the column's existing type. This is where transition
   *  rules, completedOptionIds, stepNumbering and unavailableBehavior are written. */
  readonly config?: Partial<ColumnConfigByType[ColumnType]>;
}

/** E-056. The complete, ordered id list. Positions are renumbered densely 0..n-1. */
interface ReorderColumnsRequest {
  readonly columnIds: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * E-057. `?dryRun=true` returns a ConversionPreview and writes nothing.
 * Unparseable values are PRESERVED as CellValue.text, never dropped.
 * `config` is the target type's config; absent means its default.
 */
interface ConvertColumnRequest {
  readonly type: ColumnType;
  readonly config?: ColumnConfigByType[ColumnType];
}

/**
 * E-058. Returns 200 WITH THE EXISTING OPTION when the trimmed, case-folded
 * label already exists — never 409 (canon §1.3.3, OQ-53).
 * `id` is accepted because the frontend mints it; `"__empty__"` is refused.
 * `color` is picked client-side by cycling the palette (src/store/board-store.ts:844).
 */
interface CreateSelectOptionRequest {
  readonly label: string;
  readonly color: SelectColor;
  readonly id?: string;
  readonly isDisabled?: boolean;
  readonly availability?: ConditionGroup | null;
}

/** E-059. */
interface UpdateSelectOptionRequest {
  readonly label?: string;
  readonly color?: SelectColor;
  readonly isDisabled?: boolean;
  readonly availability?: ConditionGroup | null;
}
```

#### 32.2.6 `boards` — records

```ts
/**
 * E-062. Mirrors CreateRowInput (src/services/board-service.ts:277-288), minus
 * `boardId`, which is the path parameter.
 *
 * The server assigns `id`, `displayId`, `sequence` and `revision: 1`. `cells` is
 * optional; absent means every column's EMPTY value of its own kind, never an
 * empty object (§32.1.5).
 */
interface CreateRowRequest {
  readonly afterRowId?: string | null;  // insert after; appended when omitted
  readonly cells?: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
  readonly parentRowId?: string | null;
}

/**
 * E-066. THE batched cell write. Mirrors UpdateCellsInput
 * (src/services/board-service.ts:472-477).
 *
 * `baseRevisions` is keyed by row id, NOT by edit: a missing entry never
 * conflicts, `base < current` conflicts, equal-or-greater does not, and at most
 * one ConflictNotice is raised per row per call (:504-512).
 *
 * ALWAYS answers 200. Never 409.
 */
interface UpdateCellsRequest {
  readonly edits: readonly CellEdit[];
  readonly baseRevisions?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
}

/** E-067. `null` clears the parent and lifts the row to the top level. */
interface SetRowParentRequest {
  readonly parentRowId: string | null;
}

/** E-073. RECOMMENDATION (OQ-34): fractional index between two neighbours. */
interface SetRowPositionRequest {
  readonly afterRowId: string | null;   // null moves to the top
  readonly beforeRowId: string | null;  // null moves to the bottom
}

/**
 * E-069, as a query string. `TASK 7` and `task-7` both resolve to `TASK-007`
 * (src/lib/row-id.ts:45-62); anything else is a primary-column substring match.
 */
interface SearchRowsRequest {
  readonly q: string;
  readonly limit?: number;
}
```

#### 32.2.7 `system` — bulk

```ts
/** The shared half of every bulk request. Mirrors BulkTargets (board-service.ts:948-951). */
interface BulkTargetsRequest {
  readonly rowIds: readonly string[];   // minItems 1
}

/** E-074. One value per column, written to every record the action may touch. */
interface BulkUpdateRowsRequest extends BulkTargetsRequest {
  readonly values: Readonly<Record<string, CellValue>>;
}

/** E-075. THE ONE CALL THAT MAY TARGET ARCHIVED ROWS — it is how they are restored. */
interface BulkArchiveRowsRequest extends BulkTargetsRequest {
  readonly isArchived: boolean;
}

/** E-076. Permanent: records have no trash of their own (OQ-15). May target archived rows. */
interface BulkDeleteRowsRequest extends BulkTargetsRequest { /* no extra fields */ }

/**
 * E-077. `targetNodeId`, not `targetBoardId` — the frontend addresses the
 * destination by its DRIVE NODE (board-service.ts:1072-1075), which is also what
 * the permission check needs. Cells travel through the column CONVERSION path,
 * matched by name; unmatched columns are named in `droppedColumns`.
 */
interface BulkMoveRowsRequest extends BulkTargetsRequest {
  readonly targetNodeId: string;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * E-079. `fromViewId` is how DUPLICATE works — it copies an existing view's
 * configuration (src/services/board-service.ts:810-815). The frontend passes the
 * whole `SavedView`; the API takes the id, because it already has the view.
 */
interface CreateViewRequest {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: BoardViewType;
  readonly fromViewId?: string;
}

/**
 * E-080. Every SavedView field except `id` and `boardId`, which are FORCIBLY
 * PRESERVED against the patch. `ganttZoom: "day"` is accepted and coerced to
 * "week", never rejected.
 */
interface UpdateViewRequest {
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly type?: BoardViewType;
  readonly filters?: readonly ViewFilter[];
  readonly filterConjunction?: FilterConjunction;
  readonly sorts?: readonly ViewSort[];
  readonly hiddenColumnIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly columnOrder?: readonly string[];
  readonly columnWidths?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  readonly columnDisplay?: Readonly<Record<string, CellDisplayMode>>;
  readonly rowHeight?: RowHeight;
  readonly groupByColumnId?: string | null;
  readonly hideEmptyGroups?: boolean;
  readonly dateColumnId?: string | null;
  readonly endDateColumnId?: string | null;
  readonly subtaskDisplay?: SubtaskDisplay;
  readonly ganttZoom?: GanttZoom | "day";
  readonly showDependencies?: boolean;
}

/** E-082. "The order is the board's, not the reader's" — this is a SHARED write. */
interface ReorderViewsRequest {
  readonly viewIds: readonly string[];
}

/** E-083. Per-viewer, resolved from the session. RECOMMENDATION (OQ-46). */
interface UpdateViewPreferencesRequest {
  readonly columnWidths?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
  readonly collapsedGroupKeys?: readonly string[];
  readonly collapsedRowIds?: readonly string[];
}
```

#### 32.2.9 `system` — import and export

```ts
/**
 * E-084. Sent as multipart: the file part plus a JSON part carrying the mapping.
 * Nothing is written; the response is an ImportPlan.
 *
 * PARSING MOVES TO THE SERVER. It is client-side today (OQ-42) — `lib/xlsx.ts`,
 * `lib/csv.ts` — which means a 5 000-row workbook is parsed in the main thread
 * and the server never sees what it is committing.
 */
interface PlanImportRequest {
  readonly mappings: readonly ColumnMapping[];
  readonly invalidPolicy?: ImportInvalidPolicy;   // default "skip" (OQ-41)
  /** Board columns the file did not carry, to remove. Requires board.column.delete. */
  readonly removeColumnIds?: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * E-085. The SAME shape as the plan, re-sent to commit. ONE TRANSACTION: column
 * creation, column removal and row inserts all land or none do.
 *
 * `planToken` is RECOMMENDATION: an opaque, short-lived token from the plan
 * response, so a commit cannot silently run against a file the user re-picked
 * between the two calls.
 */
interface CommitImportRequest {
  readonly mappings: readonly ColumnMapping[];
  readonly invalidPolicy?: ImportInvalidPolicy;
  readonly removeColumnIds?: readonly string[];
  readonly planToken?: string;
}

/**
 * E-086. `scope: "view"` includes the view's active SEARCH TERM, not only its
 * filters and sort (src/types/system.ts:151-153) — an export that quietly
 * ignored the search box would not match what is on screen.
 */
interface CreateExportRequest {
  readonly scope: ExportScope;
  readonly format: ExportFormat;
  readonly viewId?: string;             // required when scope === "view"
  readonly rowIds?: readonly string[];  // required, minItems 1, when scope === "selection"
  readonly searchTerm?: string;         // only meaningful with scope === "view"
}
```

```ts
/**
 * E-089. Save an existing board's schema as a template. The columns and views
 * are DEEP-COPIED server-side from the board; the caller sends an id, not a
 * schema, so a template can never describe a board that does not exist.
 * RECOMMENDATION (OQ-47).
 */
interface CreateBoardTemplateRequest {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly fromBoardId: string;
  /** Absent copies the board's own prefix. */
  readonly rowIdPrefix?: string;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * E-092. Wraps DocumentDraft (src/types/document.ts:136-141) and adds the
 * concurrency token the frontend does not have (OQ-57).
 *
 * `expectedVersion` OPTIONAL: present means check it and answer
 * DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT when stale; absent means last-write-wins. The
 * frontend sends nothing today, so absence must remain safe.
 */
interface SaveDocumentRequest {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly icon: string;
  readonly blocks: readonly Block[];
  readonly expectedVersion?: number;
}

/** E-093. PUT sets, DELETE clears — the body carries nothing (OQ-08). */
interface SetDocumentPinnedRequest { /* intentionally empty */ }

/**
 * E-094. `lockedBy` is NOT accepted: it comes from the session (C-09, OQ-60).
 * Allowed for `document.lock` OR the document's owner (canToggleLock,
 * src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:147-152).
 */
interface SetDocumentLockedRequest { /* intentionally empty */ }

/**
 * E-097. RESTORE WRITES A NEW VERSION rather than rewinding, so history is never
 * lost. Refused on a secret version (hasSnapshot: false) and on a locked page.
 */
interface RestoreVersionRequest { /* intentionally empty — the version is the path parameter */ }
```

#### 32.2.12 `devtools`

```ts
/**
 * E-100. Mirrors SaveConfigInput (src/services/devtools-service.ts:120-140),
 * minus `nodeId` (the path parameter).
 *
 * CONTENT AND METADATA LAND IN ONE WRITE: changing the format sends the current
 * content with it, "so the language and the text land in one version rather than
 * in two that disagree".
 *
 * `isAutosave: true` FOLDS into the head version when that version is also an
 * autosave by the same author; otherwise `version + 1` (OQ-59).
 */
interface SaveConfigRequest {
  readonly content: string;
  readonly format?: ConfigFormat;
  readonly environmentOptionId?: string;
  readonly isAutosave?: boolean;        // default false
}

/**
 * E-102. THE WHOLE LIST, replaced in the order given — which is what makes
 * reordering, renaming and deleting one operation rather than three endpoints
 * (devtools-service.ts:479-487).
 *
 * `role` is NOT in the body: the frontend passes it (SaveSecretsInput.role,
 * :473-477) and that is exactly the C-09 violation this DTO fixes.
 *
 * An OMITTED `value` on an entry means the stored ciphertext is carried forward.
 * `value: ""` sets it to empty. They are different (T-2).
 */
interface SaveSecretsRequest {
  readonly entries: readonly SecretDraftEntry[];
}

/**
 * E-103. `action` distinguishes the two reads of plaintext, which "carry
 * different risk: one puts a value on a screen for thirty seconds, the other
 * puts it on a clipboard indefinitely" (src/types/devtools.ts:90-95).
 * Both are gated by `secret.reveal`; `copy` has no key of its own.
 *
 * TWO AUDIT ROWS ARE WRITTEN BEFORE THE RESPONSE, allowed or denied alike.
 */
interface RevealSecretRequest {
  readonly action: "reveal" | "copy";
}

/**
 * E-104. `secretIds` requires minItems: 1 (OQ-66). The frontend treats an empty
 * array as "every secret in the document" (devtools-service.ts:400-401) — the
 * most dangerous possible wire default, and the reason this DTO refuses it.
 */
interface CopySecretsRequest {
  readonly secretIds: readonly string[];   // minItems 1
}

/** E-107. RECOMMENDATION (OQ-63). Seeded Development / Staging / Production. */
interface CreateEnvironmentRequest {
  readonly label: string;
  readonly color: SelectColor;
  readonly position?: number;           // appended when absent
}

/** E-108. Refused on delete while referenced — ENVIRONMENT_IN_USE. */
interface UpdateEnvironmentRequest {
  readonly label?: string;
  readonly color?: SelectColor;
  readonly position?: number;
}
```

#### 32.2.13 `files`

```ts
/**
 * E-110. Validates size, extension AND QUOTA before issuing the presigned
 * target, so bytes are never uploaded only to be refused (OQ-05).
 *
 * `createDriveNode` is the answer to OQ-74: default TRUE for a drive upload or a
 * document block, FALSE for a board cell or a comment attachment — "uploading
 * one into a task does not create a file node beside the board"
 * (src/types/board.ts:198-200). The caller states its intent; the server does
 * not guess from the folder.
 */
interface CreateUploadRequest {
  readonly fileName: string;
  readonly sizeBytes: number;
  readonly mimeType: string;
  readonly folderId: string | null;     // null uploads to the workspace root
  readonly createDriveNode: boolean;
  /** Where the asset will be referenced from, so the join row lands in one write. */
  readonly reference?:
    | { readonly kind: "cell";     readonly boardId: string; readonly rowId: string; readonly columnId: string }
    | { readonly kind: "comment";  readonly commentId: string }
    | { readonly kind: "block";    readonly nodeId: string; readonly blockId: string };
}

/**
 * E-111. Called after the PUT to the presigned URL lands. Increments
 * workspaces.used_bytes IN THE SAME TRANSACTION as the file_assets insert.
 * `checksum` lets the server verify the object it is about to record.
 */
interface CompleteUploadRequest {
  readonly checksum?: string;           // hex SHA-256 of the uploaded bytes
}

/**
 * E-115. Text and spreadsheet files only — anything else is FILE_NOT_TEXT or
 * FILE_NOT_SPREADSHEET. Bumps file_nodes.version.
 */
type SaveFileContentRequest =
  | { readonly kind: "text";  readonly content: string }
  | { readonly kind: "sheet"; readonly rows: Grid; readonly sheetName?: string };

/**
 * E-118. SERVER-SIDE FETCH ONLY, SSRF-guarded: private, loopback and link-local
 * ranges blocked, redirects and response size capped, short timeout, cached by
 * normalised URL.
 */
interface ResolveLinkRequest {
  readonly url: string;
}
```

#### 32.2.14 `collab`

```ts
/**
 * E-120. Mirrors AddCommentInput (src/services/comment-service.ts:84-90).
 *
 * `mentionedUserIds` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the server parses `@[Name](usr_id)`
 * out of `body` and ignores anything a client claims. A client-supplied mention
 * list is a notification a client can forge.
 *
 * `attachmentIds`, not CommentAttachment objects: the client sends ids from
 * E-110/E-111, never names, sizes or URLs (OQ-73 — comment attachments bypass
 * validation, permissions and the node model today).
 *
 * `parentId` names the ROOT. A reply to a reply RE-PARENTS to the root.
 *
 * THE FAN-OUT IS ONE TRANSACTION: comment + auto-watch the author + mention
 * notifications + watcher notifications + row activity + the realtime frame.
 */
interface CreateCommentRequest {
  readonly target: EntityRef;
  readonly body: string;
  readonly parentId?: string | null;
  readonly attachmentIds?: readonly string[];
}

/** E-121. AUTHOR ONLY — no role escalates it. Sets `isEdited`. */
interface UpdateCommentRequest {
  readonly body: string;
  readonly attachmentIds?: readonly string[];   // OQ-82: are attachments mutable after posting?
}

/**
 * E-127 / E-128. Mirrors SetWatchInput (src/services/watch-service.ts:55-59)
 * MINUS `userId`, which is the C-09 violation this DTO fixes (OQ-19).
 * Only `row`, `document` and `board` are watchable; anything else is refused
 * with WATCH_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED.
 */
interface SetWatchingRequest {
  readonly ref: EntityRef;
}

/**
 * E-130. Ids outside the caller's own inbox are IGNORED, NOT APPLIED and NOT an
 * error (src/services/notification-service.ts:35-53). The response carries the
 * caller's whole inbox page, so the badge cannot drift.
 */
interface MarkNotificationsReadRequest {
  readonly notificationIds: readonly string[];
}
```

#### 32.2.15 `search` and `insights`

```ts
/**
 * E-133, as a query string. Mirrors SearchInput (src/services/search-service.ts:45-50)
 * MINUS `role` and `user`, which are resolved from the session (OQ-20).
 * An empty `q` is 200 with `[]`, not a 400.
 * THE PERMISSION FUNNEL RUNS BEFORE SCANNING, not after.
 */
interface SearchRequest {
  readonly q: string;
  readonly limitPerGroup?: number;      // default SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5
}

/**
 * E-134, as a query string. Mirrors MyWorkInput (src/services/my-work-service.ts:47-58)
 * MINUS `userId` and `allow`, both resolved server-side (OQ-19).
 *
 * `nowIso` is NOT accepted — the reference instant is the server's clock (C-09).
 * `timezone` IS accepted, because "today" and "overdue" are timezone-dependent
 * and the server cannot guess the viewer's (OQ-92).
 */
interface MyWorkRequest {
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly limit?: number;              // default MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6
  /** IANA zone, e.g. "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh". Defaults to UTC. */
  readonly timezone?: string;
}

/** E-135, as a query string. Same timezone reasoning as MyWorkRequest (OQ-92). */
interface DashboardRequest {
  readonly timezone?: string;
}
```

> **OPEN QUESTION (OQ-92) — nothing defines which timezone "today" and "overdue" mean.**
>
> **Evidence** — `MyWorkInput.nowIso` is *"the frozen clock in fixtures, `now` in production"*
> (`src/services/my-work-service.ts:55-56`), and the date layer is explicit that a due date is *"a
> square on a calendar, not a moment"* (`src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24`). Neither says whose calendar.
> `DASHBOARD_WEEK_DAYS = 7` (`src/config/app.ts:57`) counts days forward from an unspecified today.
>
> **Recommendation** — the client sends an IANA `timezone`; the server computes the day boundaries
> in that zone and compares **day keys to day keys**, never instants to instants. Absent, default to
> UTC and say so in the response. A date-only value must never be widened into an instant to make
> the comparison work (C-04).
>
> **Impact if wrong** — a user in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` sees tasks due today as overdue for seven hours
> every morning, and the dashboard's three deadline buckets disagree with the calendar view of the
> same board. It is the single most visible timezone bug this product can have.


---

### 32.3 Response DTOs

**A domain object is returned bare.** `POST /workspaces` returns `Workspace`. `PATCH /nodes/{id}`
returns `DriveNode`. `POST /boards/{id}/rows` returns `BoardRow`. There is no `{ data: … }` wrapper
anywhere, because the frontend's stores assign a response directly — `setData(serverResponse)`,
`reconcileRows(rowsById, result.rows)` — and an envelope would be unwrapped in exactly one place and
then never used (canon §6.2). The shapes below are the ones that are **not** a bare domain object.

#### 32.3.1 The pagination wrapper

```ts
/**
 * The shape of every cursor-paginated response. `nextCursor` is an OPAQUE
 * base64 of the sort-key tuple; a client must never construct or parse one.
 * There is no `page`, no `offset` and no `hasMore` — `nextCursor === null` IS
 * "no more" (§7.6).
 *
 * This is a documentation type. Each concrete page below names its item field
 * explicitly rather than extending it, because two of them do not use `items`:
 * AuditPage says `events` and BoardSnapshot says `rows`, and both are already
 * in the frontend's contract.
 */
interface CursorPage<T> {
  readonly items: readonly T[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

| Page type | Item field | Sort key | Extra facets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RowPage` | `items` | `(position, id)` | — |
| `ActivityPage` | `items` | `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` | — |
| `CommentPage` | `items` | `(created_at ASC, id ASC)` — **oldest first**, a thread reads forwards | `replyCountByRootId` |
| `NotificationPage` | `items` | `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` | `unreadCount` |
| `VersionPage` | `items` | `(version DESC)` | — |
| `SecretAccessPage` | `items` | `(at DESC, id DESC)` | — |
| `AuditPage` | **`events`** | `(at DESC, id DESC)` | `total`, `bySeverity` — over the WHOLE filtered set |
| `BoardSnapshot` | **`rows`** | `(position, id)` | `board`, `people` |

#### 32.3.2 `identity`

```ts
/** E-001. RECOMMENDATION (OQ-01). The refresh token is a Set-Cookie header, NOT a field. */
interface LoginResponse {
  readonly user: UserSummary;
  readonly accessToken: string;         // JWT, 15 min; held in memory only (§8.3)
  readonly expiresAt: string;           // ISO 8601 — lets the client refresh proactively
  /** Workspaces the caller is a member of, so the shell renders without a second call. */
  readonly workspaces: readonly Workspace[];
}

/** E-003. The rotated refresh token is a Set-Cookie header, never a field. */
interface RefreshSessionResponse {
  readonly accessToken: string;
  readonly expiresAt: string;
}

/**
 * E-004. `activeWorkspaceId` is the server's memory of where the user was, so a
 * second device opens the same place. `sessionExpiresAt` lets the client
 * schedule a proactive refresh rather than discovering expiry through a failed
 * write (§8, R-7) — the worst place to discover it, given optimistic row and
 * comment writes.
 */
interface CurrentUserResponse {
  readonly user: UserSummary;
  readonly workspaces: readonly Workspace[];
  readonly activeWorkspaceId: string | null;
  readonly sessionExpiresAt: string;
}
```

#### 32.3.3 `drive` and `governance`

```ts
/**
 * E-026. The moved node PLUS the two parents, so a client can splice both
 * children lists without refetching the tree. `slug` on `node` may differ from
 * the one sent in: move re-uniquifies against the new siblings (OQ-10).
 */
interface MoveNodeResponse {
  readonly node: DriveNode;
  readonly previousParentId: string | null;
  readonly parentId: string | null;
}

/** E-039. What emptying the trash actually removed. */
interface EmptyTrashResponse {
  readonly purgedEntryIds: readonly string[];
  readonly purgedNodeCount: number;     // the whole subtree, not just the roots
  readonly freedBytes: number;          // so the storage meter updates without a refetch
}

/**
 * E-040. `entries` is sorted by roleRank DESCENDING, so the most capable subject
 * reads first. `inheritedFrom` is the ancestor the chain currently flows from,
 * null when this node is the origin or the mode is `workspace`.
 */
interface NodeAccessResponse {
  readonly nodeId: string;
  readonly accessMode: NodeAccessMode;
  readonly inheritedFrom: AccessOrigin | null;
  readonly entries: readonly ResolvedAccess[];
}
```

#### 32.3.4 `boards`

```ts
/**
 * E-047. Everything ONE board needs before its first paint
 * (src/types/board.ts:429-436). `people` is the directory subset the board's
 * user cells and activity actors reference, INCLUDING deactivated members so
 * old assignments still render a name.
 *
 * `nextCursor` is null when the whole record set arrived in one page. It exists
 * in the frontend contract already and is always null today (OQ-36).
 */
interface BoardSnapshot {
  readonly board: Board;
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly people: readonly DirectoryUser[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/** E-061. */
interface RowPage {
  readonly items: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/**
 * E-066. ALWAYS 200. NEVER 409.
 * `rows` are authoritative with `revision` already bumped; the store replaces
 * its optimistic copies with these (reconcileRows, src/store/board-store.ts:348).
 * `conflicts` is at most one entry per row.
 */
interface UpdateCellsResponse {
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly conflicts: readonly ConflictNotice[];
}

/**
 * E-065. Children are LIFTED TO TOP LEVEL, never cascade-deleted (OQ-33), and
 * the response carries them so the client reconciles without a refetch.
 */
interface DeleteRowResponse {
  readonly deletedRowId: string;
  /** Former children, now parentRowId: null, with bumped revisions. */
  readonly liftedRows: readonly BoardRow[];
}

/**
 * E-055. The copy is NEVER primary and is inserted at `position + 1`.
 * `rows` carries every row whose cells gained the duplicated column's values —
 * "the reason to duplicate 'Expected result' is to start from what is in it"
 * (src/services/board-service.ts:586-592).
 */
interface DuplicateColumnResponse {
  readonly column: BoardColumn;
  readonly columns: readonly BoardColumn[];   // C-11: the COMPLETE schema, not a delta
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
}

/**
 * E-057. Mirrors ConvertColumnResult (src/services/board-service.ts:710-714) and
 * adds the complete column array (C-11). `preserved` counts values kept as
 * CellValue.text because the target type could not parse them.
 * With `?dryRun=true`, `preview` is present and `rows` is empty.
 */
interface ConvertColumnResponse {
  readonly column: BoardColumn;
  readonly columns: readonly BoardColumn[];
  readonly rows: readonly BoardRow[];
  readonly preserved: number;
  readonly preview?: ConversionPreview;
}

/** E-070. */
interface ActivityPage {
  readonly items: readonly ActivityEntry[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

#### 32.3.5 `documents`, `devtools` and version history

```ts
/** E-095. Serves pages, config documents AND secrets; the node's kind selects the store. */
interface VersionPage {
  readonly items: readonly VersionEntry[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}

/** E-098. */
interface DiffResponse {
  readonly lines: readonly DiffLine[];
  readonly summary: DiffSummary;
  readonly fromVersion: number;
  readonly toVersion: number;
}

/**
 * E-103. THE ONLY RESPONSE IN THE SYSTEM THAT CARRIES PLAINTEXT.
 *
 * Returned ONCE, never cached, never logged, never written into SecretEntry.
 * `Cache-Control: no-store` is mandatory on this response.
 * `expiresAt` mirrors the client's 30-second auto-hide
 * (src/hooks/use-secret-document.ts:11-12) so the two cannot disagree.
 */
interface RevealSecretResponse {
  readonly secretId: string;
  readonly key: string;
  readonly value: string;               // PLAINTEXT. Once.
  readonly expiresAt: string;
}

/**
 * E-104. Mirrors CopySecretsResult (src/services/devtools-service.ts:405-410).
 * `text` is `KEY=value` lines ready for the clipboard; `keys` lets the caller
 * say "Copied 4 secrets" WITHOUT READING THE VALUES.
 * Also `Cache-Control: no-store`.
 */
interface CopySecretsResponse {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly keys: readonly string[];
}

/** E-105. */
interface SecretAccessPage {
  readonly items: readonly SecretAuditEntry[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

#### 32.3.6 `files`

```ts
/**
 * E-110. The presigned target the client PUTs the bytes to. `headers` carries
 * anything the store requires on that PUT (Content-Type, checksum) so the client
 * does not have to know which object store is behind it.
 */
interface CreateUploadResponse {
  readonly uploadId: string;
  readonly uploadUrl: string;
  readonly method: "PUT" | "POST";
  readonly headers: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  readonly expiresAt: string;
  readonly maxBytes: number;
}

/**
 * E-111. `node` is present only when the request asked for one
 * (`createDriveNode: true`) — a board-cell or comment attachment gets an asset
 * and no node (OQ-74). `storage` is returned so the quota meter updates in the
 * same round trip.
 */
interface CompleteUploadResponse {
  readonly asset: FileAsset;
  readonly node: FileNode | null;
  readonly storage: StorageQuota;
}

/**
 * E-116 / E-117. Short-lived, signed. This is the ONLY way a client obtains a
 * URL for stored bytes; `url` and `thumbnailUrl` on domain objects are minted
 * the same way and are never accepted on write (OQ-75).
 */
interface SignedUrlResponse {
  readonly url: string;
  readonly expiresAt: string;
  /** Present for images that have one. */
  readonly thumbnailUrl?: string;
}
```

#### 32.3.7 `collab`

```ts
/**
 * E-119 / E-125. Roots first, oldest first. `replyCountByRootId` is a facet over
 * the whole thread set, so a collapsed thread can say "4 replies" without
 * loading them (OQ-83).
 */
interface CommentPage {
  readonly items: readonly Comment[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
  readonly replyCountByRootId: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
}

/**
 * E-129 / E-130 / E-131. `unreadCount` is SERVER-COMPUTED over the whole inbox,
 * so the badge is not "unread among the ones we loaded" (OQ-91) — the frontend
 * derives it client-side today (src/store/notification-store.ts:17).
 */
interface NotificationPage {
  readonly items: readonly AppNotification[];
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
  readonly unreadCount: number;
}

/** E-132. One number, so the badge can poll without paging the inbox. */
interface UnreadCountResponse {
  readonly unreadCount: number;
}
```

#### 32.3.8 `governance` — audit

```ts
/**
 * E-136. Mirrors AuditPage (src/types/audit.ts:50-55) and adds the cursor the
 * frontend lacks (OQ-28).
 *
 * `total` and `bySeverity` are facets over the WHOLE FILTERED SET, not the page:
 * "Matches before the limit was applied, so the table can say 'of N'" (:52).
 * Computing them over the page would make the header lie.
 *
 * The item field is `events`, not `items` — the frontend's name wins.
 */
interface AuditPage {
  readonly events: readonly AuditEvent[];
  readonly total: number;
  readonly bySeverity: Readonly<Record<AuditSeverity, number>>;
  readonly nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

#### 32.3.9 `system` — meta

```ts
/**
 * E-139. SERVER-OWNED LIMITS, so the client's pre-checks and the API's refusals
 * cannot disagree. Every number here has a hard-coded twin in src/config/app.ts
 * or src/lib/file-validation.ts today; this endpoint is what retires them.
 */
interface AppConfigResponse {
  /** file-validation.ts:4 says 25 MiB; PRD WS-FIL-06 says 100 MB (OQ-69). */
  readonly maxUploadBytes: number;
  /** file-validation.ts:7-14, flattened. Lower-case, no leading dot. */
  readonly acceptedExtensions: readonly string[];
  /** The sentence rendered under a file picker — file-validation.ts:22. */
  readonly acceptedHint: string;
  readonly trashRetentionDays: number;      // TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS = 30
  readonly importMaxRows: number;           // IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5000
  readonly importIssueLimit: number;        // IMPORT_ISSUE_LIMIT = 50
  readonly versionHistoryLimit: number;     // VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT = 20
  readonly searchGroupLimit: number;        // SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5
  readonly myWorkWidgetLimit: number;       // MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6
  readonly auditPageSize: number;           // AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE = 40
  readonly recentLimit: number;             // RECENT_LIMIT = 10
  readonly maxSubtaskDepth: number;         // OQ-33 — 5
  readonly boardRowLimit: number;           // OQ-36
  readonly maxRequestBytes: number;
  /** WebSocket URL, or null while no socket is exposed — mirrors REALTIME_ENDPOINT. */
  readonly realtimeEndpoint: string | null;
}

/** E-140. The only unauthenticated endpoint. */
interface HealthResponse {
  readonly status: "ok" | "degraded";
  readonly version: string;             // build identifier
  readonly time: string;                // ISO 8601 server clock
}
```

**One response type this table introduces that canon §5.5 does not name**: `CompleteUploadResponse`
(E-111). Canon lists the return as *"`FileAsset` (+ the created `DriveNode` when `createDriveNode` is
true)"*, which is a two-shaped response and therefore needs a named wrapper. It also carries
`storage`, because E-111 is the one write that changes `usedBytes` and a second call to E-017 to
learn the new number would be a round trip for a value the server just computed.

**And one canon §5.3 type used above without being defined in §32.1**, because it belongs to the
identity chapter:

```ts
/** RECOMMENDATION (canon §5.3, OQ-04). DB: `workspace_invitations` (T-05). */
interface WorkspaceInvitation {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly workspaceId: string;
  readonly email: string;
  readonly role: WorkspaceRole;
  readonly invitedBy: UserSummary;
  readonly expiresAt: string;
  readonly acceptedAt: string | null;
  /** The token itself is NEVER returned — only its hash is stored, and the
   *  plaintext goes out in the invitation email and nowhere else. */
}
```

### 32.5 Where a domain interface differs from its database row

Collected in one place so a serialiser author does not have to find them in comments. Every entry is
either a **casing change**, a **computed field**, a **projection from another table**, a
**per-request value**, or a **field that exists on one side only**.

#### 32.5.1 Fields that are computed, not stored

| Interface · field | What it actually is | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DriveNodeBase.isTrashed` | `nodes.deleted_at IS NOT NULL` | canon §1.4 |
| `DriveNodeBase.isShared` | An `access_rules` row exists on this node | canon §1.3.1 |
| `DriveNodeBase.isFavorite` | A `node_favorites` row exists for **(this node, the caller)**. **Per user** — two people reading the same node get different values (OQ-07). This is the whole of what the brief called `Favorite`; there is no wire interface for it. | canon T-07 |
| `DriveNodeBase.state` | Derived precedence: trashed > frozen (an **ancestor** archived) > archived (own flag) > active. Never a column (OQ-11). | `src/lib/archive.ts:30-36` |
| `ProjectNode.children`, `FolderNode.children` | Derived from `parent_id`. **Never stored.** A leaf has no such field at all. | `src/types/node.ts:150-151` |
| `DocumentNode.blockCount`, `.excerpt` | Projections onto the node, kept in sync by the documents module | `src/services/document-service.ts:149-165` |
| `BoardNode.itemCount`, `.openCount` | Counts over `board_rows` | canon §1.3.1 |
| `FileNode.excerpt` | Derived on ingest for text-like files | `src/types/node.ts:125-126` |
| `UserSummary.initials` | Derived from `name` | `src/types/user.ts:8-9` |
| `Comment.targetKey`, `WatchEntry.targetKey` | `refKey(target)` over the decomposed target columns | `src/types/collab.ts:41` |
| `Comment.mentionedUserIds` | **Parsed server-side** from `body`; a client-supplied list is ignored | E-120 |
| `AppNotification.isRead` | `notifications.read_at IS NOT NULL` | canon T-35 |
| `PermissionDefinition.module` | The key's first segment. Derived, never declared beside it. | `src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts:8-14` |
| `ResolvedAccess.*`, `EffectiveAccess.*` | Entirely derived by walking the ancestor chain | `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120` |
| `SearchResult.kind` (`api`/`bug`/`qa`) | From `boards.template_id` **at read time**. A projection, not a schema — a board reshaped away from its template must follow what it became. | `src/services/search-service.ts:39-43`; `src/lib/dashboard.ts:86-96` |
| `BoardRow.displayId` | `boards.row_id_prefix` + zero-padded `custom_id` sequence | `src/lib/row-id.ts:12-15` |
| `StorageQuota.totalBytes` | Static plan config, not a column (OQ-06) | canon §1.2 |

#### 32.5.2 Fields projected from another table, never duplicated

| Interface · field | Source of truth | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Board.name` | `nodes.name` | There is no board-rename endpoint; renaming is E-025. Two copies would let the header and the breadcrumb disagree. |
| `WorkspaceDocument.title` | `nodes.name` | Same. `DocumentDraft.title` writes **through** to the node. |
| `WorkspaceDocument.isPinned`, `.isLocked`, `.isArchived` | `nodes` | OQ-30, OQ-56: three copies of `isArchived` exist in the frontend; the **node** is canonical. |
| `ConfigDocument.name`, `SecretDocument.name` | `nodes.name` | Read as a join on every read. |
| `FileNode.extension`, `.mimeType`, `.sizeBytes`, `.kind` | `file_assets` | The node points at the asset; the asset owns the bytes' facts. |
| `CellAttachment.name`, `.mimeType`, `.sizeBytes` | `file_assets` | The cell stores only `assetId`. |
| `CommentAttachment.*` | `file_assets` | Same. |
| `Workspace.members` | `workspace_members` ⋈ `users` | Embedded because the caller's own role is read from it. |
| `AuditEvent.actor`, `ActivityEntry.actor`, `Comment.author` | `users` | A join, resolved live — a renamed user's old activity shows the new name. |
| `AppNotification.actor`, `.target.label` | **Frozen at creation** | The one exception to the line above (OQ-79). A notification is a historical statement. |

#### 32.5.3 Fields that exist on the wire and not in the table

| Field | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `CellAttachment.url`, `.thumbnailUrl`, `DocumentImage.url`, `FileNode.previewUrl`, `.thumbnailUrl` | **Minted per response** as short-lived signed URLs. Never accepted on write. The frontend's own comment says why they cannot be persisted: *"Session URL for the real bytes; null once the session that made it ends"* (`src/types/board.ts:206-207`). OQ-75. |
| `SecretEntry.maskedValue` | A constant twelve bullets. Not derived from the ciphertext and not stored. |
| `TrashEntry.purgeAt` | `deleted_at + TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`, computed on read (OQ-14). |
| `BoardSnapshot.people` | A directory subset assembled per response. |
| `NotificationPage.unreadCount`, `AuditPage.total`, `AuditPage.bySeverity`, `CommentPage.replyCountByRootId`, `MyWorkWidget.total` | Facets computed per query, over the **whole filtered set** rather than the page. |
| `LoginResponse.accessToken`, `RefreshSessionResponse.accessToken` | Minted per call. The refresh token is a `Set-Cookie` header and appears in no interface at all. |
| `RevealSecretResponse.value` | Decrypted per call, returned once, never stored in any client shape. |

#### 32.5.4 Fields that exist in the table and never on the wire

| Column | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `secrets.value_encrypted`, and its IV and auth tag | Plaintext leaves only through E-103/E-104. Ciphertext leaves never. |
| `row_activity.raw_changes` | The internal before/after `CellValue` pair. The timeline *"never sees, and never renders, a raw payload"* (`src/types/board.ts:480-482`). OQ-51. |
| `audit_events.context` | `AuditContext` — the structured payload beside the human `detail`. Never serialised, including into the E-137 CSV. OQ-25. |
| `nodes.deleted_at`, `deleted_by` | Projected as `isTrashed` and, on a `TrashEntry`, as `deletedAt`/`deletedBy`. |
| `user_sessions.*` | No endpoint returns a session row. `CurrentUserResponse.sessionExpiresAt` is the only thing that escapes it. |
| `workspace_invitations.token_hash` | The plaintext token goes out in the email and nowhere else. |
| `boards.next_sequence` | An internal counter. `BoardRow.sequence` is the value it issued, not the counter. |
| `uploads.*` | Only `uploadId` and the presigned target escape, in `CreateUploadResponse`. |

#### 32.5.5 Three client-only fields that must never appear in a response

| Field | Where | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BoardRow.isPending` | `src/types/board.ts:264-265` | *"True while the row exists only optimistically."* A server-sent `isPending: true` would make a persisted row look unsaved forever. |
| `Comment.isPending` | `src/types/collab.ts:56-57` | Same. |
| A `tmp_`-prefixed `BoardRow.id` | `src/types/board.ts:236-238` | The client mints these for optimistic rows and replaces them with the response's id. The API only ever emits a UUID, and must **reject** a `tmp_` id in a request path or body. |

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **`fields` and `details` are two carriers for one idea.** Canon §6.2 puts validation detail in a
   top-level `error.fields`, and §7.4 of this document reproduces it. §31.5 then adds `error.details`
   as a discriminated union for every other structured payload. I followed canon rather than folding
   `fields` into `details.validation`, but the result is a client that must look in two places.
   **Suggested for a canon revision:** make `details` the single carrier, with
   `{ reason: "VALIDATION_FAILED"; fields: FieldError[] }` as one more variant, and drop the
   top-level `fields`. It is a purely additive change today (nothing reads either field) and stops
   being one the moment a client does.

2. **Canon §4.3's count says 106 rows / 104 reasons; §31.4 catalogues 104 real reasons plus 2
   non-errors and then adds 21 more.** The additions are all endpoint-level failures canon's table
   did not enumerate but its endpoints imply — `WORKSPACE_NAME_INVALID`, `NODE_NAME_INVALID`,
   `ACCESS_RULE_NOT_FOUND`, `ACCESS_SUBJECT_INVALID`, `TRASH_ALREADY_PURGED`, `CURSOR_INVALID`,
   `OPTION_LABEL_EMPTY`, `VIEW_COLUMN_UNKNOWN`, `VIEW_NAME_EMPTY`, `BULK_SELECTION_EMPTY`,
   `BULK_SELECTION_TOO_LARGE`, `IMPORT_COLUMN_CREATE_FAILED`, `DIFF_TARGET_INVALID`,
   `ENVIRONMENT_LABEL_DUPLICATE`, `COMMENT_DELETE_DENIED`, `WATCH_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`,
   `SEARCH_QUERY_TOO_LONG`, `REALTIME_UNAUTHORIZED`, `REALTIME_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`, and the
   `SEARCH_QUERY_EMPTY`/`PREVIEW_UNSUPPORTED` non-error rows. **If canon's §9 quick-index count is
   normative, it needs updating to 125.** I did not renumber or rename anything canon already
   registered.

3. **`ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` sits at `409 conflict` in canon §4.3 while the three sibling
   narrowing states (`NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `NODE_LOCKED`) sit at
   `403 permission_denied`.** I followed canon. It is defensible — a row archive is a record state
   rather than an access decision, and the frontend surfaces it as a bulk *skip* rather than a
   refusal — but a reader will notice the asymmetry, and it means "this thing is frozen" reaches the
   client as two different `AppErrorCode`s depending on whether the frozen thing is a node or a row.

4. **Canon §2.7 says `BulkSkipReason` should gain `permission_denied`;** §32.1.0 and §32.1.14 ship it
   as a third member. The frontend's enum has two (`src/types/system.ts:24`). This is a **wire enum
   widening**, and the frontend's `BulkSkip.reason` union will not accept the third value until it
   is updated. It is the only place in this chapter where a canon decision requires a frontend type
   change rather than being purely additive. Worth flagging in the migration section.

5. **`FilePreview.text.language` is narrowed from `string` to `ConfigFormat`** per canon's OQ-76
   recommendation. Narrowing a field the frontend types as `string` is safe in that direction (every
   `ConfigFormat` is a `string`), but it means the server can never emit a language outside the 15.
   Given `CodeLanguage` (8 values, code blocks) and `ConfigFormat` (15 values, config documents) are
   two different enums, a `.py` file preview has no `ConfigFormat` member and must fall back to
   `"text"`. That is a real, if small, loss of fidelity, and it may be worth reopening OQ-76 with a
   third option: a `PreviewLanguage` enum that is the union of both.

6. **`AppConfigResponse` publishes `maxSubtaskDepth` and `boardRowLimit`, whose values OQ-33 and
   OQ-36 have not settled.** The endpoint is specified; the numbers are canon §8.8's position
   (depth 5) and an unfilled blank respectively. The blank must be filled before E-139 ships, or a
   client will read `undefined` and cap nothing.

7. **`PermissionKey` is written as `string & {}` in the §32.1.0 enum block** purely to keep that
   block short. Every generated client and the server's own validator must use the 39-literal union
   from `src/types/permission.ts:31-78`. If the assembled document is used to generate types
   mechanically, that line needs expanding first.
