## 33. API ↔ Database Mapping

This chapter is the checklist a developer runs an implementation against: for each of the 140
endpoints in canon §3, which of the 39 tables in canon §1.1 it reads, which it writes, whether the
write must be one transaction, and which realtime frame it publishes. It invents nothing — every
row is either an endpoint canon already declares, a table canon already names, or a frame canon
already registers (§7).

### 33.0 How to read these tables

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **API** | The canon endpoint id, method and path, relative to `/api/v1` (canon P-01). |
| **Tables Read** | Tables the handler must `SELECT` from, including the ones read only to authorise the call. Authorisation reads are listed because forgetting them is the most common way an endpoint ends up unguarded (OQ-16). |
| **Tables Written** | Tables the handler `INSERT`s, `UPDATE`s or `DELETE`s. `audit_events` appears only where §33.26 says the action is auditable — it is not decoration. |
| **Transaction** | `—` = single statement, no explicit transaction needed. `single` = one row, one statement, but wrapped because it also writes an audit row. `TX` = two or more tables, or two or more rows, that must land together; the cell names what breaks without it. |
| **Realtime Event** | The frame id from canon §7. `—` = the endpoint publishes nothing. |

Four conventions apply to every row and are not repeated in the cells:

1. **Every read of a `nodes` row is also a read of `access_rules` and `workspace_members`.** Canon
   P-09 makes the server-side permission re-check normative, and `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts`
   resolves a capability by walking the ancestor chain (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`)
   with the workspace role as the floor (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:84-96`). Where those two
   tables are the *only* thing an endpoint reads them for, they are written as
   `nodes, access_rules, workspace_members` in the Tables Read cell; where an endpoint reads `nodes`
   for content as well, they still appear.
2. **The caller's identity never comes from the body** (canon C-09). No endpoint reads `users` to
   find out who is calling; the session supplies that. `users` appears in Tables Read only where a
   *name or avatar of somebody else* is projected into the response.
3. **Every write returns the authoritative record** (canon C-10), so every `W` endpoint also reads
   back what it wrote. That read-back is not listed separately.
4. **A trashed, frozen or locked target is refused before any write.** That check reads `nodes`
   (own `deleted_at`, own archive flag, and the ancestor chain for `frozen`) — canon §2.4,
   `src/lib/archive.ts:30-36`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-88`.

---

### 33.1 Identity and session — `identity`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-001** `POST /auth/login` | `users` (by email, `is_active`), `workspace_members` (to pick the landing workspace) | `user_sessions` (new refresh family), `audit_events` | **TX** — the session row and the `allowed`/`denied` audit row must agree; a login that is recorded but hands out no token, or hands out a token it never recorded, is unauditable | — |
| **E-002** `POST /auth/logout` | `user_sessions` | `user_sessions` (revoke the family), `audit_events` | **single** | — |
| **E-003** `POST /auth/refresh` | `user_sessions` (family lookup), `users` | `user_sessions` (rotate; on replay **revoke the whole family**), `audit_events` (only on `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED`) | **TX** — rotation is delete-old + insert-new; a crash between them logs the user out silently instead of detecting a replay | — |
| **E-004** `GET /me` | `users`, `workspace_members`, `workspaces`, `user_ui_preferences` | — | — | — |
| **E-005** `PATCH /me` | `users` | `users` | **—** | — |
| **E-006** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/directory` | `workspace_members`, `users` | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- E-001/E-003 are **RECO** (canon E-001, E-003, OQ-01): the frontend has no auth layer at all —
  `CURRENT_USER` is a module constant (`src/mock/users.ts`) imported by 14 files, so nothing in
  `src/` constrains the token model. Canon §8.8 takes the position (cookie session + rotating
  refresh family in `user_sessions`); this chapter maps that position and does not extend it.
- E-006 **must include deactivated members** flagged `isActive: false` (canon E-006). The query is
  `workspace_members JOIN users` with **no** `WHERE users.is_active` filter — canon T-01 keeps a
  user row forever precisely so an old `{ kind: "user" }` cell still renders a name.
- `user_ui_preferences` (T-37) is read on E-004 so the shell can restore sidebar collapse and drive
  view mode without a second round trip. It is a **RECOMMENDATION** (OQ-98); today those live in
  the Zustand store and die on reload (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:140`, `:118-119`).

---

### 33.2 Workspaces and membership — `workspace`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-007** `GET /workspaces` | `workspaces`, `workspace_members` | — | — | — |
| **E-008** `POST /workspaces` | `workspaces` (slug uniqueness) | `workspaces`, `workspace_members` (**creator → `admin`**), `audit_events` | **TX** — a workspace that exists with no admin cannot be administered by anyone; `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:212-238` creates the membership in the same act | — |
| **E-009** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}` | `workspaces`, `workspace_members`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-010** `PATCH /workspaces/{workspaceId}` | `workspaces` (slug uniqueness when `slug` is in the patch) | `workspaces`, `audit_events` | **single** | — |
| **E-011** `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}` | `workspaces`, `workspace_members` | `workspaces` **+ every workspace-scoped table by FK cascade** (`workspace_members`, `workspace_invitations`, `nodes`→ all five side tables, `access_rules`, `trash_entries`, `board_*`, `document_*`, `config_*`, `secret_*`, `environments`, `file_assets`, `file_nodes`, `cell_attachments`, `comment_attachments`, `document_asset_refs`, `uploads`, `comments`, `watches`, `notifications`, `import_jobs`, `export_jobs`, `node_favorites`, `board_view_preferences`), `audit_events` | **TX** — and the audit row must be written to a trail that outlives the workspace, so `audit_events.workspace_id` is **`ON DELETE SET NULL`, not cascade** | — |
| **E-012** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members` | `workspace_members`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-013** `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members` | `workspace_members`, `users` (does the email already hold an account), `workspace_invitations` (already invited) | `workspace_invitations`, `audit_events` | **TX** | **RT-05** `permission.changed` |
| **E-014** `PATCH /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}` | `workspace_members` **`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` over the admin set** | `workspace_members`, `audit_events` | **TX** — `isLastAdmin` is a read-then-write race; two concurrent demotions each see one other admin and both succeed (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157`) | **RT-05** |
| **E-015** `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}` | `workspace_members` (same last-admin lock) | `workspace_members`, `audit_events` | **TX** | **RT-05** |
| **E-016** `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/me` | `workspace_members` (same lock) | `workspace_members`, `audit_events` | **TX** | **RT-05** |
| **E-017** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/storage` | `workspaces` (`used_bytes`, plan) | — | — | — |
| **E-018** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations` | `workspace_invitations`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-019** `POST /invitations/{token}/accept` | `workspace_invitations` (by token hash, unexpired, unconsumed), `users` | `workspace_members`, `workspace_invitations` (`accepted_at`), `audit_events` | **TX** — consuming the token and creating the membership are the same act, or a replayed link mints a second membership | **RT-05** |

**Notes.**

- **E-017 never aggregates.** `StorageQuota.usedBytes` is read from the `workspaces.used_bytes`
  counter, maintained transactionally by E-111 and by every asset delete (canon §1.4, OQ-05).
  `SUM(file_assets.size_bytes)` on a sidebar render is the failure mode this counter exists to
  prevent — the meter is on every screen (`src/components/layout/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:164`).
- **E-014/E-015/E-016 share one guard.** All three read `isLastAdmin` and all three must hold the
  same row lock. `leaveWorkspace` delegates to `removeMember` in the frontend
  (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:410`), so the backend should share one internal routine too.
- **E-016 has a client-side consequence the backend must enable:** removing yourself from the
  workspace you are standing in switches you out in the same write
  (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:388-408`). The response must therefore be enough for the client to
  pick a new active workspace — return `204` and let the client re-read E-007, which is what canon
  specifies.
- **RT-05 on E-013 (invite).** Canon §7.1 lists E-013 among the frames' triggers. An invitation
  grants nothing until E-019, so the frame's `userIds` is empty unless the invited email already
  maps to a `users` row. See the note in Chapter notes.

### 33.3 Drive tree — `drive`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-020** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/tree` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `node_favorites`, and the five side tables for the derived summaries (`boards`, `documents`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents`, `file_nodes`) | — | — | — |
| **E-021** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/resolve?path=` | `nodes` (walk by `slug` per level), `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `node_favorites` | — | — | — |
| **E-022** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `node_favorites`, the one side table for its `kind` | — | — | — |
| **E-023** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/children` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `node_favorites` | — | — | — |
| **E-024** `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes` | `nodes` (parent is a container; sibling slugs excluding trashed), `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `board_templates` (when `kind = "board"`) | `nodes`, **plus by kind**: `boards` + `board_columns` + `board_views` (deep-copied from the template), `documents`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents`, `file_nodes`; `audit_events` | **TX** — a `nodes` row whose side table never landed is a node the router can address and no surface can render | **RT-11** `node.changed` (`created`) |
| **E-025** `PATCH /nodes/{nodeId}` | `nodes` | `nodes` (`name` only — **the slug is not re-minted**, OQ-09), `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-11** (`renamed`) |
| **E-026** `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/move` | `nodes` (recursive CTE for the descendant check; target sibling slugs), `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `nodes` (`parent_id`, `slug` **re-uniquified against the new siblings**, OQ-10), `audit_events` | **TX** — the cycle check and the reparent must share a lock, or two concurrent moves make a detached ring | **RT-11** (`moved`) **and RT-05** — a move relocates the subtree under a different access chain (canon §7.1) |
| **E-027** `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/duplicate` | `nodes` (whole subtree), all five side tables, `board_columns`, `board_rows`, `board_views`, `document_asset_refs`, `cell_attachments` | `nodes` (N), `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_rows`, `board_views`, `documents`, `config_documents`, `secret_documents`, `file_nodes`, `cell_attachments`, `document_asset_refs`, `audit_events` | **TX** — a half-copied subtree has no correct partial state; see OQ-12 for secrets | **RT-11** (`created`) |
| **E-028** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `node_favorites` (upsert) | **—** | — |
| **E-029** `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/favorite` | `nodes` | `node_favorites` | **—** | — |
| **E-030** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/archive` | `nodes` (ancestor chain) | `nodes` (`is_archived`, `archived_at`, `archived_by`), `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-11** (`archived`) |
| **E-031** `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/archive` | `nodes` (ancestor chain — **refused when an ancestor is archived**) | `nodes`, `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-11** (`restored`) |
| **E-032** `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}` | `nodes` (whole subtree, ancestor chain for the human path) | `nodes` (`deleted_at`, `deleted_by` over the **whole subtree**), `trash_entries` (**one** row, for the subtree root), `audit_events` | **TX** — the subtree stamp and the single restore record are one fact; a `trash_entries` row pointing at a subtree that is still live is a restore that duplicates the tree | **RT-11** (`trashed`) |
| **E-033** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/favorites` | `node_favorites`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | — | — | — |
| **E-034** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/archive` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | — | — | — |
| **E-035** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/search?q=` | `nodes` (name match), `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **E-020 prunes subtree-wide.** `collectAllowed` (`src/lib/tree.ts:297-320`) drops a node *and
  everything under it* when the caller may not see it — a child is never surfaced through a hidden
  parent. Implement as one recursive CTE that carries the resolved capability down, not as a
  post-filter over a flat list.
- **The four derived projections on `nodes` are read, never computed here.** `blockCount`,
  `excerpt`, `itemCount` and `openCount` are columns kept in sync by the owning module
  (canon §1.3.1; `src/services/document-service.ts:149-158` `DocumentSummaryPatch`). E-020 must not
  count `board_rows` — that is exactly what canon E-048 forbids for the board list, and the tree is
  the hotter path.
- **`is_shared` is derived**, not stored: `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM access_rules WHERE node_id = …)`.
- **Slug uniqueness excludes trashed rows** so a restore never collides
  (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:472-480`). The constraint is therefore a **partial unique index**:
  `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, plus a second partial index scoped by
  `workspace_id` for `parent_id IS NULL` roots.
- **E-026 must also answer "who loses sight of this".** The frontend already renders that count
  before the move (`moveVisibilityImpact`, `src/store/workspace-store.ts:568`), which means the
  backend needs a "subjects who can see node X" query, not just a boolean check.
- **E-035 and E-133 are two different searches** (OQ-94): E-035 is a name-only quick-find over
  `nodes`; E-133 is the full-text one in §33.22.

### 33.4 Trash — `system`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-036** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/trash` | `trash_entries`, `nodes`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-037** `POST /trash/{entryId}/restore` | `trash_entries`, `nodes` (walk `original_ancestor_ids` for the deepest **surviving** container) | `nodes` (`deleted_at = NULL` over the subtree; `parent_id` rewritten when relocated), `trash_entries` (delete), `audit_events` | **TX** — restoring the subtree and consuming the entry are one act | **RT-11** (`restored`) |
| **E-038** `DELETE /trash/{entryId}` | `trash_entries`, `nodes` (subtree), `file_assets` (bytes to reclaim) | `nodes` (hard delete → FK cascade over `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_rows`, `board_row_relations`, `row_activity`, `board_views`, `board_view_preferences`, `documents`, `document_versions`, `config_documents`, `config_versions`, `secret_documents`, `secrets`, `secret_rotations`, `secret_access_events`, `file_nodes`, `cell_attachments`, `document_asset_refs`, `comments`, `comment_attachments`, `watches`, `node_favorites`, `access_rules`), `file_assets` (orphans), `workspaces` (`used_bytes` decrement), `trash_entries`, `audit_events` | **TX** — the quota counter and the byte deletion cannot drift; object-store deletion is queued **after** commit, never inside it | **RT-11** |
| **E-039** `DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}/trash` | same as E-038, over every entry | same as E-038, over every entry | **TX** | **RT-11** (one frame; the client refetches) |

**Notes.**

- `purgeAt` on `TrashEntry` is `deleted_at + TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` (30 —
  `src/config/app.ts:41`, and `src/hooks/use-trash.ts` renders the countdown). Canon OQ-14 makes
  retention a 30-day nightly sweep, and the sweep is E-038's logic on a schedule, not a second
  code path.
- **`isRelocated` is not an error.** When the original parent is gone, the entry restores to the
  deepest surviving ancestor and says so in `RestoreOutcome` (canon `TRASH_RESTORE_RELOCATED`, a
  `200` outcome; `restoreTargetFor`, `src/store/workspace-store.ts:653-679`).
- **Object bytes are deleted after commit.** An S3 delete inside a transaction cannot be rolled
  back; the correct order is commit the metadata, then reclaim. A crash in between leaves an
  orphan object, which the reaper collects — the opposite order loses a file that the database
  still says exists.

### 33.5 Access and permissions — `governance`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-040** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/access` | `access_rules` (this node **and every ancestor**), `nodes`, `workspace_members`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-041** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/access-mode` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `nodes` (`access_mode`), `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-05** |
| **E-042** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules` | `access_rules` (existing rule for the same subject), `nodes`, `workspace_members` (the subject must be a member) | `access_rules` (**upsert by `(node_id, subject_kind, subject_user_id, subject_role)`**), `audit_events` | **TX** — the replace-by-subject and the audit row are one act; two rules for one subject on one node is an unresolvable state | **RT-05** |
| **E-043** `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules/{ruleId}` | `access_rules`, `nodes` | `access_rules`, `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-05** |
| **E-044** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/capabilities` | `nodes` (ancestor chain for `frozen`), `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | — | — | — |
| **E-045** `GET /permissions/catalog` | **none** — static service config | — | — | — |
| **E-046** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/restricted-nodes` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `audit_events` (**`severity: "warn"` — the read itself is audited**, OQ-26) | **single** | — |

**Notes.**

- **E-042's uniqueness is by subject, not by rule id.** `setAccessRule` replaces any existing rule
  for the same subject on the same node (`sameSubject` filter,
  `src/store/permission-store.ts:56-91`). Express it as
  `UNIQUE (node_id, subject_kind, COALESCE(subject_user_id, '00000000-…'), COALESCE(subject_role, ''))`
  or as two partial unique indexes, one per `subject_kind`.
- **E-043 clearing the last rule makes the node inherit again** (canon E-043;
  `clearAccessRule` deletes the node's key entirely, `src/store/permission-store.ts:92-113`). That
  is a consequence of `access_mode` staying `restricted` with zero rules being meaningless — the
  handler must either flip `access_mode` back to `inherit` or the resolver must treat
  `restricted` + zero rules as inherit. **RECOMMENDATION:** flip the column, so the stored state
  and the rendered state cannot disagree.
- **E-045 has no table on purpose.** Canon §1.2: the 39-key catalogue is static config
  (`src/lib/permissions/catalog.ts`), served so both sides agree rather than stored so both sides
  can drift.
- **E-046 is the recovery console.** It deliberately looks past resource access and returns name +
  path and nothing inside
  (`src/components/workspace/workspace-restricted-tab.tsx:15-31`) — which is exactly why the read
  is audited at `warn`.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-16)** — *Which endpoints actually enforce a permission key?*
**Evidence** — the mock enforces on a handful of board operations only:
`requirePermission(...)` appears at `src/services/board-service.ts:564`, `:601`, `:652`, `:668`,
and in `src/services/devtools-service.ts` for secrets; the entire drive tree, membership, trash and
access-rule surface is a client-side Zustand store with no check at all
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts` imports no service). The frontend's own gate is explicitly
disclaimed: *"this is not security"* (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:24-25`).
**Recommendation** — take the **Perm** column of canon §3 as normative and re-check it server-side
on every endpoint in this chapter, resolving the subject from the session (canon C-09). Treat a
missing check as a defect, not an omission.
**Impact if wrong** — a viewer can rename, move, archive, trash or re-share any node in the
workspace, because nothing but the button's `disabled` attribute stops them.

### 33.6 Boards — `boards`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-047** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/board` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_views`, `board_view_preferences`, `board_rows`, `cell_attachments`, `file_assets` (to mint signed URLs), `users` (the `people` directory) | — | — | — |
| **E-048** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/boards` | `nodes` (`item_count` projection), `boards` | — | — | — |
| **E-049** `GET /boards/{boardId}` | `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_views`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | — | — | — |
| **E-050** `PATCH /boards/{boardId}` | `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | `boards` (`name`, `row_id_prefix`), `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-10** `board.schema.changed` |

**Notes.**

- **E-047 is one snapshot, four views.** Table, Kanban, Calendar and Gantt all project the same
  `rowsById` + `rowOrder` through `useBoardView` (`src/hooks/use-board-view.ts:100`); switching
  views never refetches (`src/hooks/use-board.ts:15`). There must be **no per-view row endpoint**.
- `people` is the whole directory including inactive members — the same shape E-006 returns, embedded
  so the first paint of a board needs one request.
- **E-048 must not touch `board_rows`.** `listBoards` is documented as derived from the tree and
  forbidden from seeding a board (`src/services/board-service.ts:1234-1246`); `itemCount` comes from
  the `nodes` projection column.
- **E-050 and `rowIdPrefix`.** Changing the prefix after rows exist is OQ-43. Canon takes no
  position beyond validating `^[A-Z]{1,6}$` (`ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID`,
  `src/lib/row-id.ts:18-20`). **RECOMMENDATION:** accept the change, do **not** rewrite existing
  `board_rows.custom_id` — a `TASK-004` that silently becomes `BUG-004` breaks every comment that
  referenced it by name (OQ-95) and every export already downloaded.

### 33.7 Columns — `boards`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-051** `GET /boards/{boardId}/columns` | `board_columns`, `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | — | — | — |
| **E-052** `POST /boards/{boardId}/columns` | `board_columns` (existing names for de-duplication, positions) | `board_columns`, `boards` (`updated_at`), `audit_events` | **TX** — `reposition` rewrites every column's `position` densely `0..n-1` when `atIndex` is given (`src/lib/board-schema.ts:144-167`) | **RT-10** |
| **E-053** `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}` | `board_columns` | `board_columns` (`name`, `width` clamped `[88,720]`, `hidden`, `config`), `boards` (`updated_at`) | **single** | **RT-10** |
| **E-054** `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}` | `board_columns` (primary guard), `board_rows`, `board_views` | `board_columns`, `board_rows` (**drop the key from `cells` on every row, `revision + 1`**), `board_views` (**prune `hiddenColumnIds`, `columnOrder`, `columnWidths`, `columnDisplay`, `filters`, `sorts`, `groupByColumnId`, `dateColumnId`, `endDateColumnId`**), `board_row_relations` (when the column was a relation), `cell_attachments` (when it was an attachment column), `audit_events` | **TX** — canon E-054 requires the view prune in the same transaction; a view pointing at a deleted column renders an empty grid | **RT-10** |
| **E-055** `POST /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/duplicate` | `board_columns`, `board_rows` | `board_columns` (copy at `position + 1`, never primary), `board_rows` (**copy the cell value on every row that has one, `revision + 1`**), `boards`, `audit_events` | **TX** — `src/services/board-service.ts:620-632` copies values row by row | **RT-10** |
| **E-056** `POST /boards/{boardId}/columns/reorder` | `board_columns` | `board_columns` (positions renumbered densely `0..n-1`), `boards` | **TX** | **RT-10** |
| **E-057** `POST /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/convert` | `board_columns`, `board_rows` | `board_columns` (`type`, new `config`), `board_rows` (**rewrite the cell on every row**), `board_row_relations` (drop when converting *away from* `relation`), `audit_events` | **TX** — `?dryRun=true` reads and returns `ConversionPreview` and writes **nothing** | **RT-10** (not fired on `dryRun`) |
| **E-058** `POST /boards/{boardId}/columns/{columnId}/options` | `board_columns` (`config.options` for the label de-duplication) | `board_columns` (`config`), `boards` | **single** | **RT-10** |
| **E-059** `PATCH …/options/{optionId}` | `board_columns` | `board_columns` (`config`) | **single** | **RT-10** |
| **E-060** `DELETE …/options/{optionId}` | `board_columns`, `board_rows` (orphan scan) | `board_columns` (`config`) — **`board_rows` is NOT written; cells keep the orphaned id** | **single** | **RT-10** |

**Notes.**

- **E-052 does not backfill cells.** `createColumn` writes only the schema
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:555-583`); the row's empty value for the new column is produced by
  `emptyCellFor` at render time (`src/lib/cell-values.ts`). A cell key that is absent is an empty
  value of the column's kind — canon §1.3.2 records that rows are dense by construction *for
  columns that existed when the row was written*, which is why the read path must still tolerate a
  missing key.
- **E-053 accepts no `type` and no `position`** (canon E-053, OQ-39): `ColumnPatch` is
  `{ name?, width?, config? }` (`src/types/board.ts:446`). Type change is E-057; position change is
  E-056. `hidden` on the primary column is **silently ignored**, not refused
  (`src/lib/board-schema.ts:60`, `:93-95`).
- **E-058 dedupes and returns `200`.** Trimmed, case-folded label match returns the existing
  option — never `409` (canon E-058, OQ-53, `docs/BOARD.md:300`). The colour is chosen client-side
  by cycling the palette and sent in the request (`src/store/board-store.ts:844`); the server
  validates it against `SelectColor` and stores what it is given.
- **E-060 deliberately leaves orphans.** The frontend renders an unknown option id as unknown rather
  than as deleted, so silently pruning `cells` would destroy data the user can still see. Canon
  E-060 is explicit.
- **`"__empty__"` is reserved** as an option id (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:28`) — E-058/E-059
  reject it with `OPTION_ID_RESERVED`.
- **Every column write bumps `boards.updated_at`.** The mock does it on all six paths
  (`board-service.ts:579`, `:618`, `:657`, `:673`, `:700`); the board's `updatedAt` is what the tree
  renders as "last touched".

### 33.8 Rows — `boards`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-061** `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows` | `board_rows`, `cell_attachments`, `file_assets`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | — | — | — |
| **E-062** `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows` | `boards` (**`next_sequence` `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`**), `board_columns` (to build the empty cell set), `board_rows` (the parent, and its last descendant for placement) | `boards` (`next_sequence + 1`), `board_rows`, `row_activity` (**1 row, or 2 when it is a subtask**), `board_row_relations` (when `cells` carry a relation) | **TX** — counter increment + insert + order placement + activity are one fact; `src/services/board-service.ts:290-335` | **RT-06** `row.created` |
| **E-063** `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` | `board_rows`, `cell_attachments`, `file_assets` | — | — | — |
| **E-064** `POST …/rows/{rowId}/duplicate` | same as E-062 plus the source row | same as E-062 (cells copied) | **TX** | **RT-06** |
| **E-065** `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/rows/{rowId}` | `board_rows` (the row and its children) | `board_rows` (delete the row; **children `parent_row_id → NULL`**), `row_activity` (purge the row's entries), `board_row_relations` (both directions), `cell_attachments` | **TX** — `detachOrphans` re-parents children in the same act (`src/services/board-service.ts:460-470`), and the response must carry those lifted children so `reconcileRows` sees them | **RT-09** `row.deleted` |
| **E-066** `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` | `board_rows` (**`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` per touched row**), `board_columns` (transition rules, option availability, `CellValue.kind` validation) | `board_rows` (`cells`, `revision + 1`, `updated_at`), `row_activity` (**one entry per row, however many fields it touched**), `board_row_relations` (rewrite the projection for relation cells), `cell_attachments` | **TX** — the revision compare and the write must be atomic per row, or two clients both read revision 7 and both write revision 8 | **RT-07** `row.updated` |
| **E-067** `PUT …/rows/{rowId}/parent` | `board_rows` (**recursive CTE cycle check inside the lock**) | `board_rows` (`parent_row_id`, `position` re-anchored after the parent's last descendant), `row_activity` | **TX** | **RT-07** |
| **E-068** `GET …/rows/{rowId}/subtasks` | `board_rows` | — | — | — |
| **E-069** `GET /boards/{boardId}/rows/search` | `board_rows` (`custom_id` exact, then primary-column substring) | — | — | — |
| **E-070** `GET …/rows/{rowId}/activity` | `row_activity`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-071** `GET /boards/{boardId}/relation-index?ids=` | `boards`, `board_rows` (target board), `nodes`, `access_rules` (**read access on the target board's node**) | — | — | — |
| **E-072** `GET …/rows/{rowId}/backlinks` | `board_row_relations`, `board_rows`, `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | — | — | — |
| **E-073** `PATCH …/rows/{rowId}/position` | `board_rows` (neighbours, for the fractional index) | `board_rows` (`position`) | **single** | **RT-07** |

**Notes.**

- **E-062's counter is per board and only ever increases.** `boards.next_sequence BIGINT` under
  `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`; deleting `TASK-005` never re-issues `005`
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:290-293`). `custom_id` is
  `` `${prefix}-${String(n).padStart(3,"0")}` `` (`src/lib/row-id.ts:13-15`) with
  `UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)`. A shared Postgres `SEQUENCE` is wrong — it is table-wide, and
  every board needs its own run of numbers.
- **E-065 lifts children, never cascades.** `ON DELETE SET NULL` on `board_rows.parent_row_id`
  expresses it in the schema; the response's `DeleteRowResponse` carries the lifted rows because
  `reconcileRows` is a pure overwrite by id and leaves rows the response does not mention alone
  (`src/lib/board-records.ts:109`).
- **E-066 is always `200`.** Last-write-wins plus `ConflictNotice[]` — never `409`
  (canon §6.4). Three properties reproduce exactly
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:504-512`): a missing `baseRevisions[rowId]` never conflicts;
  `base < current.revision` conflicts while equal-or-greater does not; **at most one notice per row
  per call**. N edits on one row produce **one** `revision + 1` and **one** `row_activity` entry.
- **Relation cells write two places.** The `cells` JSONB is the truth; `board_row_relations` is the
  indexed projection written in the same transaction, so `E-072` is a lookup rather than a scan
  (canon T-13; `src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:14-19` — "the two directions can
  never disagree"). Dangling target ids stay in the cell so `[Deleted Item]` keeps rendering
  (canon OQ-44 position).
- **E-071 is one request per target board, never one per cell** (canon E-071, OQ-44;
  `src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts`). The `?ids=` list is a batch.
- **E-073 is RECO** (OQ-34). Canon's position: `board_rows.position NUMERIC` fractional index,
  defaulted on insert. The frontend has no drag-to-reorder for rows today — the order is the
  server-declared `rowOrder` array (`src/store/board-store.ts:68`).
- **Archived rows.** `board_rows.archived_at` freezes edits but not removal
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:1058`); E-066 and E-074 refuse an archived row with
  `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY`, E-075 and E-076 may target it.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-51)** — *What does `row_activity` store for a cell change?*
**Evidence** — the frontend renders `ActivityEntry.changes` as already-rendered `FieldChange` text
(`src/types/board.ts:469-490`) and never reads a raw before/after value; the drawer's timeline
shows a sentence, not a diff (`src/components/board/drawer/activity-timeline.tsx`).
**Recommendation** — canon's position: store both. `row_activity.changes JSONB` holds the rendered
`FieldChange[]` that is returned, and `row_activity.raw_changes JSONB` holds the before/after
`CellValue` pair and is **never returned by E-070**. The second column is what makes an
"undo this change" feature or a support investigation possible later without a migration.
**Impact if wrong** — storing only rendered text makes the activity log unusable for anything but
display, and re-deriving it later is impossible because the old values are gone.

### 33.9 Bulk — `system` + `boards`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-074** `POST …/rows/bulk/update` | `board_rows` (`FOR UPDATE`, archived rows are skipped), `board_columns` (transition + availability rules) | `board_rows` (N rows, each `revision + 1`), `row_activity` (N entries), `board_row_relations`, `audit_events` | **TX** — `requested === applied.length + skipped.length` must hold for the whole call | **RT-07** (batched) |
| **E-075** `POST …/rows/bulk/archive` | `board_rows` (**may target archived rows**) | `board_rows` (`archived_at`), `row_activity` (conditional), `audit_events` | **TX** | **RT-08** `row.archived` |
| **E-076** `POST …/rows/bulk/delete` | `board_rows` (**may target archived rows**) | `board_rows` (delete; children lifted), `row_activity` (purge), `board_row_relations`, `cell_attachments`, `audit_events` | **TX** | **RT-09** |
| **E-077** `POST …/rows/bulk/move` | `board_rows` (source), `board_columns` (**both boards**, paired by normalised name), `boards` (target `next_sequence` `FOR UPDATE`), `nodes`, `access_rules` (**both boards**) | `boards` (target counter), `board_rows` (**insert on the target, delete on the source**), `row_activity` (moved), `board_row_relations`, `cell_attachments` (re-pointed), `audit_events` | **TX** — **one transaction spanning two boards**; a move that inserted on the target and failed to delete on the source duplicates every record | **RT-06** on the target + **RT-09** on the source |

**Notes.**

- **Partial success is a `200`, never an error body** (canon §6.2;
  `src/services/board-service.ts:958-965` — "a bulk write that silently drops a record is worse than
  one that refuses"). `BulkSkip.reason` is `BulkSkipReason` — `archived`, `not_found`, and canon
  §2.7 adds `permission_denied` to the same enum rather than a parallel array.
- **`bulkDelete` returns `rows: []`** and only `applied`; the store removes those ids
  (`src/store/board-store.ts:626`).
- **Column pairing on E-077 is by normalised name** — lowercase, strip non-alphanumerics
  (`src/services/board-service.ts:1080`). Source columns with no counterpart are named in
  `droppedColumns` and their values are discarded, which is the honest half of OQ-40. Select values
  migrating across two different option sets is the unresolved half.
- **Bulk writes carry no concurrency token** (canon §6.4; `baseRevisions` is not sent —
  `src/store/board-store.ts:565-635`). They are unconditional; refusals surface as `BulkSkip`,
  not as `409` (OQ-55).

### 33.10 Views — `views`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-078** `GET /boards/{boardId}/views` | `board_views`, `board_view_preferences`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | — | — | — |
| **E-079** `POST /boards/{boardId}/views` | `board_views` (the `from` source, and the max position) | `board_views`, `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-10** |
| **E-080** `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}` | `board_views` | `board_views` (**`id` and `board_id` forcibly preserved against the patch** — `src/services/board-service.ts:801`) | **single** | **RT-10** |
| **E-081** `DELETE /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}` | `board_views` (**count check inside the lock**) | `board_views`, `board_view_preferences` (cascade), `audit_events` | **TX** — refused when it would leave zero views (`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`, `src/services/board-service.ts:886-892`); two concurrent deletes on a two-view board would otherwise both succeed | **RT-10** |
| **E-082** `POST /boards/{boardId}/views/reorder` | `board_views` | `board_views` (`position` renumbered densely) | **TX** | **RT-10** |
| **E-083** `PUT /boards/{boardId}/views/{viewId}/preferences` | `board_views`, `board_view_preferences` | `board_view_preferences` (upsert on `(view_id, user_id)`) | **—** | — (per-viewer; no frame) |

**Notes.**

- **A saved view is shared, not per-viewer.** Reorder takes `board.view.manage` because "the order
  is the board's, not the reader's" (`src/services/board-service.ts:850-857`). Filters, sorts,
  grouping and the date anchors stay on `board_views` — they are what a named view *is*
  (canon OQ-46 position).
- **`board_view_preferences` (T-16, RECO, OQ-46)** carries only the two things that are genuinely
  per-reader: column widths and collapse state. Today `columnWidths` is on the shared `SavedView`
  and *is* written to the server (`src/store/board-store.ts:1048`), while collapsed groups are
  client-only in the grid store (`collapsedByView`, `src/store/grid-store.ts`) — the split is
  currently in the wrong place, and E-083 is where it moves.
- **`ganttZoom: "day"` must be accepted** on write and on read and coerced to `"week"`
  (canon §2.6, `normalizeGanttZoom`, `src/types/board.ts:272-281`). A Postgres enum that refuses
  `'day'` breaks every already-saved view.
- **Kanban requires `groupByColumnId`; calendar requires `dateColumnId`** —
  `VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN`, validated on E-079 and E-080.

### 33.11 Import and export — `system`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-084** `POST /boards/{boardId}/import/plan` | `board_columns`, `boards` | **none** — the plan is computed and returned, never persisted | — | — |
| **E-085** `POST /boards/{boardId}/import` | `board_columns`, `boards` (`next_sequence` `FOR UPDATE`) | `board_columns` (**creations first**), `board_rows` (N inserts, contiguous display ids), `row_activity` (`imported`), `boards` (counter advanced N times), `board_columns` (**removals last**), `import_jobs`, `audit_events` | **TX** — canon E-085: column creation, column removal and row inserts all land or none do. The frontend already sequences it that way client-side so "a failed import can never be the thing that emptied the schema" (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:238-283`) | **RT-06** (batched `rowIds`) + **RT-10** when columns changed |
| **E-086** `POST /boards/{boardId}/export` | `board_columns`, `board_rows`, `board_views`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `users`, `file_assets` | `export_jobs` (**`board` scope only**), `audit_events` | **TX** for the job row; the generation itself runs outside the request | — |

**Notes.**

- **`import_jobs` (T-38, RECO, OQ-41)** exists so a partial or surprising import is diagnosable:
  board, actor, counts, `ImportIssue[]`, and the `ImportInvalidPolicy` used. Default policy is
  `skip` (canon §2.7). `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5000` per import (`src/config/app.ts:48`), enforced
  server-side as `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
- **Row ids from an import have no gaps** — the counter advances N times inside the same
  transaction (`src/services/board-service.ts:1196`).
- **E-086 splits by scope.** `view` and `selection` return `ExportOutcome` synchronously (they are
  bounded by what the client already has loaded); `board` scope writes an `export_jobs` row and
  returns a signed URL when ready (`EXPORT_JOB_NOT_READY` while running). `ExportScope.view`
  includes the active **search term**, not only filters and sort (canon §2.7,
  `src/types/system.ts:151-153`).
- **`ExportOutcome.omittedColumns` implies column-level permissions that exist nowhere** (OQ-29).
  The frontend drops columns the viewer may not read *before* any writer sees them
  (`selectExportColumns`, `src/hooks/use-board-export.ts`), but the only permission granularity in
  the catalogue is per node. **RECOMMENDATION:** populate `omittedColumns` as an empty array until
  column-level access exists, rather than inventing a rule.

### 33.12 Board templates — `templates`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-087** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/board-templates` | `board_templates` (`is_builtin = true` **OR** `workspace_id = :id`) | — | — | — |
| **E-088** `GET /board-templates/{templateId}` | `board_templates` | — | — | — |
| **E-089** `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/board-templates` | `boards`, `board_columns`, `board_views` (the source board) | `board_templates`, `audit_events` | **TX** | — |
| **E-090** `DELETE /board-templates/{templateId}` | `board_templates` (**refused on `is_builtin`**) | `board_templates`, `audit_events` | **single** | — |

**Notes.**

- `columns` and `views` are JSONB on `board_templates` (canon T-17): a template is inert data,
  deep-copied at instantiation by E-024, never queried per column
  (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:12-18`).
- **There is no `tasks`, `bugs`, `qa_cases` or `api_endpoints` table** (canon §1.3.5). The four
  built-ins are seed rows. `BoardNode.templateId` is "for reference only"
  (`src/types/node.ts:111`), and the dashboard classifies a board by *what it became* — a status
  column offering `passed`/`failed` — not by template id (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:86-96`).
- E-089/E-090 are **RECO** (OQ-47): the frontend ships four constants and has no save-as-template
  UI, but `board.template.manage` is one of the 39 keys, which is the only evidence that
  user-authored templates are intended.

### 33.13 Documents (pages) — `documents`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-091** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/document` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `documents`, `document_asset_refs`, `file_assets` (signed URLs for image/attachment blocks), `users` (`lockedBy`) | — | — | — |
| **E-092** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document` | `documents` (**`version` compare when `expectedVersion` is sent**), `nodes` (lock, archive, trash state) | `documents` (`title`, `icon`, `blocks`, `version + 1`), `document_versions` (**snapshot insert**), `document_asset_refs` (rewrite the projection of image/attachment blocks), `nodes` (`name`, `block_count`, `excerpt` projections) | **TX** — document update + version insert + the node summary patch are one fact (`src/services/document-service.ts:101-111`, `:149-158`) | **RT-11** (`renamed`) when the title changed |
| **E-093** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document/pin` | `documents`, `nodes` | `documents` (`is_pinned`) **or** `nodes` — see the note | **single** | — |
| **E-094** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/document/lock` | `documents`, `nodes`, `access_rules` | `documents` (`is_locked`, `locked_by`, `locked_at`), `audit_events` | **single** | — |

**Notes.**

- **`lockedBy` is taken from the session, never the body** (canon E-094, C-09). Today it is
  client-supplied: `documentService.setLocked(nodeId, isLocked, CURRENT_USER)`
  (`src/hooks/use-document-actions.ts:79-84`) — OQ-60.
- **E-092 refuses a locked page with `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` (`409` / `conflict`)**, and refuses a stale
  `expectedVersion` with `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`. When `expectedVersion` is absent the write is
  last-write-wins (canon §6.4, OQ-57) — the frontend sends no version today
  (`DocumentDraft` is `{ title, icon, blocks }`, `src/hooks/use-document.ts:77`).
- **Pin storage.** Canon OQ-08 takes the position that pinning is per user, matching favourites
  (T-07). But `WorkspaceDocument.isPinned` is a document field the frontend toggles globally
  (`src/services/document-service.ts` `setPinned`), and the sidebar renders one shared
  "Pinned pages" list (`src/components/layout/sidebar/pinned-pages.tsx`).
  **RECOMMENDATION:** keep `documents.is_pinned BOOLEAN` — the workspace-wide semantic the UI
  actually implements — and revisit only if OQ-08 resolves the other way. Do not ship both.
- **`document_asset_refs` (T-31) is rewritten on every save**, not appended: it is a projection of
  the block tree, so garbage collection and quota are one query (canon §1.3.4). An image block
  removed from the body must remove its ref, or the asset is never collectable.
- **Archive, move, duplicate and delete of a page are drive operations**, not document ones:
  E-030/E-031, E-026, E-027, E-032. `documentService.setArchived` / `duplicate` / `remove` exist in
  the mock (`src/services/document-service.ts:309-322`) only because the mock has no node service;
  the real split is `nodes` owns lifecycle, `documents` owns content (canon OQ-30 position, OQ-56).

### 33.14 Version history — `system`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-095** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions` | `nodes` (kind selects the store), then **one of** `document_versions` \| `config_versions` \| `secret_rotations`; `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-096** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}` | `document_versions` \| `config_versions` — **a secret version is refused** (`VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE`) | — | — | — |
| **E-097** `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/restore` | `document_versions` \| `config_versions`, `documents` \| `config_documents`, `nodes` (lock state) | `documents` \| `config_documents` (`version + 1`), `document_versions` \| `config_versions` (**a new snapshot**), `document_asset_refs`, `nodes` (summary projections), `audit_events` | **TX** — restore is a save, not a rewind (`src/hooks/use-version-history.ts:44-50`) | — |
| **E-098** `GET …/versions/{versionId}/diff?against=` | `document_versions` \| `config_versions` | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **One endpoint family, three stores.** `VersionEntry` is the shared read model "whatever produced
  it" (`src/types/system.ts:208-221`); the node's `kind` and `document_kind` select the table
  (canon §3.14, OQ-77).
- **A secret's entries carry `hasSnapshot: false` and no `lines`** — `secret_rotations` records
  *that* a key rotated, by whom, when, and has **no value column, ever** (canon T-24, OQ-67). E-096,
  E-097 and E-098 all refuse it.
- **`DiffKind` has no `changed`** — a modification is `removed` + `added`
  (`src/types/system.ts:227`), which is why `document_versions` and `config_versions` store a full
  snapshot rather than a patch.
- **Version trimming is a scheduled job, not part of the write path.** `VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT = 20`
  (`src/config/app.ts:64`) is what the mock enforces inline
  (`src/services/document-service.ts:101-111`); canon OQ-59's position is to fold consecutive
  autosaves by the same author, keep config and secrets uncapped, cap pages generously, and never
  drop the first or the current version.

### 33.15 Config documents — `devtools`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-099** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/config` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `config_documents`, `environments`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-100** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/config` | `config_documents`, `config_versions` (**the head version, to decide the fold**), `nodes` | `config_documents` (`content`, `format`, `environment_id`, `version`), `config_versions` (**insert a new row, or `UPDATE` the head row in place when the fold applies**), `nodes` (`excerpt` projection), `audit_events` | **TX** — the document update and the version insert-or-fold are one act | — |

**Notes.**

- **The fold is the whole point.** `isAutosave: true` collapses into the head version **when that
  version is also an autosave by the same author**; a manual save, or anyone else's edit landing in
  between, starts a new version (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:159-186`). Without it a 1.5 s
  debounce (`CONFIG_AUTOSAVE_MS`, `src/hooks/use-config-document.ts`) produces a history nobody can
  restore from. `config_versions.is_autosave BOOLEAN` is the column that drives it.
- **The wire field is `format`, never `language`** (canon §2.1;
  `src/types/devtools.ts:19-21` — "It is what the field has always been called and what the stored
  documents carry. The UI says 'Language'."). `ConfigFormat` is closed: an unknown format is
  rejected with `CONFIG_FORMAT_UNKNOWN`, never stored as free text.
- **Changing a Production config is announced as audited and is not** (OQ-62). The frontend renders
  a warning for `PRODUCTION_OPTION_ID` (`src/lib/board-templates.ts:37`) but writes no audit row.
  §33.26 lists `config.save` as auditable at `warn` when `environment_id` is the production
  environment.

### 33.16 Secret documents — `devtools`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-101** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `secret_documents`, `secrets` (**`key`, `environment_id`, `note`, `position`, `rotated_by` — never `value_encrypted`**), `environments`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-102** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` | `secrets` (existing rows, to carry ciphertext forward for omitted values), `secret_documents` | `secrets` (**whole list replaced in the order given**), `secret_rotations` (one per changed key), `secret_access_events` (`rotate`), `audit_events` (**one row per changed and per removed key**) | **TX** — `src/services/devtools-service.ts:479-560`; a partially-applied secret list is a deployment that half-works | — |
| **E-103** `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/{secretId}/reveal` | `secrets` (`value_encrypted`), `secret_documents`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members` | `secret_access_events`, `audit_events` | **TX** — **two rows written before the response, allowed or denied alike** (canon E-103, OQ-68) | — |
| **E-104** `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/copy` | `secrets` (N), `secret_documents` | `secret_access_events` (N), `audit_events` (N) | **TX** | — |
| **E-105** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/audit` | `secret_access_events`, `users` | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **A denied reveal is audited before it is refused.** `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` is a `403` whose audit
  row is already committed (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:382-396`, `:424`). This is the one place
  where a failure path writes more than a success path in some systems does — it must not be
  optimised away.
- **`maskedValue` is a constant 12 `U+2022` bullets**, never derived from the real length
  (canon E-101) — a mask that leaks length is a mask that leaks entropy.
- **An omitted `value` in `SecretDraftEntry` means "leave the stored value untouched"**
  (`{ id: string | null; key: string; value?: string }`,
  `src/services/devtools-service.ts:458-470`). This is load-bearing: it is what lets the editor
  rename a key, reorder the list or delete a neighbour without ever holding the plaintext of rows it
  is not changing. Optional-vs-nullable here is canon C-08 in its sharpest form — `value: null`
  would mean "set it to empty".
- **Encryption** (canon OQ-65 position): envelope encryption, per-workspace data key wrapped by a
  KMS master key, AES-256-GCM; ciphertext + IV + tag in `secrets.value_encrypted BYTEA`.
- **`copy` has no permission key of its own** — it is gated by `secret.reveal` and audited as a
  reveal (`src/types/devtools.ts:97`; `src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`).
- **`secretIds` requires `minItems: 1`** on E-104 (`SECRET_SELECTION_EMPTY`). Today an empty array
  means "every secret" (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:398-419`), which is an unsafe wire default
  — OQ-66.

`SelectOption`-shaped (`{ id, label, color: SelectColor, position }`), seeded with those three, so
the bug template's column config can keep referencing them by id.

### 33.18 Files and uploads — `files`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-110** `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/uploads` | `workspaces` (`used_bytes` vs plan quota), `nodes` (destination folder), `access_rules` | `uploads` (`pending`, presigned target, expected size/mime, destination, `createDriveNode`) | **single** | — |
| **E-111** `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` | `uploads`, object store (**HEAD the object: it landed, and its size matches**), `nodes` (destination) | `file_assets`, `file_nodes` **+ `nodes`** (only when `createDriveNode` is true), `uploads` (`completed`), `workspaces` (**`used_bytes + size` under `FOR UPDATE`**), `audit_events` | **TX** — canon E-111: the asset row and the quota counter increment in the same transaction. An asset without its bytes counted is a quota that drifts down forever | **RT-11** (`created`) when a drive node was made |
| **E-112** `DELETE /uploads/{uploadId}` | `uploads` | `uploads` (`aborted`) | **single** | — |
| **E-113** `GET /folders/{nodeId}/files` | `nodes`, `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `file_nodes`, `file_assets` | — | — | — |
| **E-114** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/file/preview` | `file_nodes`, `file_assets`, object store | — | — | — |
| **E-115** `PUT /nodes/{nodeId}/file/content` | `file_nodes`, `file_assets` | object store, `file_assets` (`size_bytes`, `updated_at`), `file_nodes` (`version + 1`), `workspaces` (**`used_bytes` delta**), `nodes` (`excerpt`) | **TX** — the size delta and the counter must agree | — |
| **E-116** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/file/download` | `file_nodes`, `file_assets` | — | — | — |
| **E-117** `GET /assets/{assetId}/url` | `file_assets`, **and one of** `cell_attachments` \| `comment_attachments` \| `document_asset_refs` \| `file_nodes` (**to prove the caller may see at least one owner**), `nodes`, `access_rules` | — | — | — |
| **E-118** `POST /links/resolve` | — (external fetch, Redis cache by normalised URL) | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **The upload is three calls, not one.** The mock's single `fileService.upload` returning a
  `FileAsset` (`src/services/file-service.ts:56-90`) collapses presign → PUT → complete because it
  keeps bytes in a `Map`. The real shape is E-110/E-112/E-111, and the client's
  `onProgress(fraction)` contract does not change — it moves from a simulated step loop
  (`file-service.ts:55-72`) to `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`.
- **`owner` must stop being a request field.** `UploadInput.owner: UserSummary` is supplied by the
  client today (`src/services/file-service.ts:43-49`; `src/store/upload-store.ts` passes
  `CURRENT_USER`). Canon C-09: the owner is the session.
- **`canView` must stop being a request field.** `ListFilesInput.canView: boolean`
  (`src/services/file-service.ts:92-98`) is the caller telling the server what it is allowed to
  see — OQ-18. E-113 resolves it server-side.
- **`createDriveNode` is the answer to OQ-74**: default `true` for drive uploads and document
  blocks, `false` for board cells and comments — a cell attachment "does **not** create a file node
  beside the board" (`src/types/board.ts:198-200`).
- **`url` and `thumbnailUrl` are never accepted on write and never stored.** Only `assetId` is
  persisted; the URLs are minted per response as short-lived signed URLs
  (canon §1.3.4, OQ-75; `src/types/board.ts:206-207` — "session URL; null once the session ends").
  That is why E-047, E-091, E-101 and E-119 all read `file_assets`.
- **E-118 is SSRF-guarded** (canon E-118): private, loopback and link-local ranges blocked
  (`LINK_TARGET_BLOCKED`), redirects and response size capped, short timeout, cached by normalised
  URL. It touches no table.
- **`uploads` (T-32) has no frontend counterpart** — `UploadStatus`
  (`queued`/`uploading`/`success`/`error`/`cancelled`, `src/types/file.ts:29`) is the client queue.
  The server's `uploads.state` is `pending` / `completed` / `aborted` / `expired`
  (canon §2.8, RECOMMENDATION).

### 33.19 Comments — `collab`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-119** `GET /comments?targetKind=&targetNodeId=&targetBoardId=&targetRowId=` | `comments`, `comment_attachments`, `file_assets`, `users`, `nodes`, `access_rules` (**visibility on the target**) | — | — | — |
| **E-120** `POST /comments` | `nodes`, `access_rules` (target visibility), `users` (mention resolution), `watches` (**watchers of the target, minus the author**), `board_rows` (when the target is a row) | `comments`, `comment_attachments`, `watches` (**auto-watch the author**), `notifications` (**one row per recipient**: `mention` for mentioned users, `comment` for the remaining watchers), `row_activity` (when the target is a row) | **TX** — canon E-120: comment + auto-watch + mention notifications + watcher notifications + row activity + the realtime frame are one act (`src/services/comment-service.ts:139-145`) | **RT-01** `comment.created` **+ RT-03** `notification.created` per recipient |
| **E-121** `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` | `comments` (**author check**) | `comments` (`body`, `is_edited`, `updated_at`), `notifications` (only if newly-mentioned users are notified — OQ-84) | **single**, or **TX** if it notifies | **RT-02** `comment.updated` |
| **E-122** `DELETE /comments/{commentId}` | `comments`, `workspace_members` (own at `member`, anyone else's at `manager`) | `comments` (`deleted_at`, `deleted_by` — **tombstone, so replies do not orphan**), `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-02** |
| **E-123** `POST /comments/{commentId}/resolve` | `comments` (**root only**) | `comments` (`is_resolved`, `resolved_by`, `resolved_at`), `audit_events` | **single** | **RT-02** |
| **E-124** `DELETE /comments/{commentId}/resolve` | `comments` | `comments` | **single** | **RT-02** |
| **E-125** `GET /comments/{commentId}/replies` | `comments`, `comment_attachments`, `file_assets`, `users` | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **`mentionedUserIds` is parsed server-side and a client-supplied list is ignored** (canon E-120).
  The body format is `@[Name](usr_id)`; `extractMentionIds` runs client-side for the optimistic
  render (`src/lib/mentions.ts`, used at `src/services/comment-service.ts:130`) and again on the
  server, where it is authoritative.
- **The thread is exactly two levels.** A reply to a reply re-parents to the root — `rootIdFor`
  (`src/services/comment-service.ts:148-156`). Resolve on insert; store `parent_id` as the root id.
- **Ordering is oldest-first**, `(created_at ASC, id ASC)` — `upsertComment`
  (`src/lib/comments.ts:11-39`). A thread reads forwards; that is the opposite of notifications and
  activity, and the index must match.
- **`targetKey` is derived, not authoritative.** `refKey(ref)` is
  `row:${boardId ?? nodeId}:${rowId}` for rows and `${kind}:${nodeId}` otherwise
  (`src/lib/entity-ref.ts:20`). Store the structured columns (`target_kind`, `target_node_id`,
  `target_board_id`, `target_row_id`) as the truth and `target_key` as a generated column with an
  index, because it is what the realtime frame and the watch row both carry.
- **E-122/E-123/E-124 are MISSING from the frontend entirely** — no resolve or delete affordance
  exists in `src/components/comments/`, and `commentService` exposes only
  `list, countFor, listMentioning, scan, add, edit, attach`
  (`src/services/comment-service.ts:257-266`). The keys `comment.resolve` and `comment.delete`
  exist in the catalogue with nothing behind them (OQ-80). Canon's position — `is_resolved` on the
  root only, `deleted_at` tombstone — is what these three endpoints implement.

### 33.20 Watches — `collab`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-126** `GET /me/watches` | `watches`, `nodes`, `board_rows` (label resolution) | — | — | — |
| **E-127** `PUT /me/watches` | `nodes`, `access_rules` (visibility on the target) | `watches` (upsert) | **—** | — |
| **E-128** `DELETE /me/watches` | — | `watches` | **—** | — |

**Notes.**

- **Only `row`, `document`, `board` are watchable**; anything else is refused with
  `WATCH_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED` (`validation`), not ignored
  (`src/services/watch-service.ts:70-76`; `WatchKind` is a strict subset of `EntityKind`,
  `src/types/collab.ts:86`).
- **The user id is never a parameter** (canon P-06, OQ-19). Today it is:
  `watchService.list(userId)`, `setWatching({ ref, userId, isWatching })`
  (`src/services/watch-service.ts:55-59`).
- **`autoWatch` is not an endpoint** — it runs inside E-120's transaction
  (`src/services/watch-service.ts:113-121`). The client refreshes its watch list after posting
  precisely because the rule lives on the server (`src/hooks/use-comments.ts:106`).
- **Pruning on delete, trash or access loss is unresolved** (OQ-87). `watches.target_node_id`
  should be `ON DELETE CASCADE` so a hard-purged node cannot leave a dangling watch; whether losing
  *access* prunes the row is a product decision this chapter does not take.

### 33.21 Notifications — `collab`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-129** `GET /me/notifications?reason=` | `notifications` (**`recipient_id = session user`**), `users` (actor) | — | — | — |
| **E-130** `POST /me/notifications/read` | `notifications` | `notifications` (`read_at`; **ids outside the caller's own inbox are ignored, not applied**) | **single** — scope to the caller in the same `UPDATE … WHERE recipient_id = :me` | **RT-04** `notification.read` |
| **E-131** `POST /me/notifications/read-all` | `notifications` | `notifications` (`read_at` over the caller's unread set) | **single** | **RT-04** |
| **E-132** `GET /me/notifications/unread-count` | `notifications` (`COUNT(*) WHERE recipient_id = :me AND read_at IS NULL`) | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **One row per recipient — fan-out on write** (canon T-35). There is no join table and no
  "read receipts" table; `notifications` *is* the inbox.
- **The label is frozen at creation** (canon §1.4, OQ-79). `AppNotification` carries a denormalised
  `EntityRef.label` so an item renders without a second lookup
  (`src/types/collab.ts:16`); a notification is a historical statement, so unlike everywhere else the
  label is **not** resolved live.
- **Filtering is by `reason`, never by tab name** (canon E-129, OQ-90). The four `NotificationTab`
  values are a frontend mapping over the five `NotificationReason` values
  (`src/lib/notifications.ts` `filterByTab`).
- **The badge is server-computed** (E-132, OQ-91). Today it is derived from the loaded page
  (`countUnread`, `src/store/notification-store.ts:141`), which makes it "unread among the ones we
  fetched".
- **Nothing emits `assigned`, `watch` or `system` today** (OQ-89) — only `mention` and `comment`, both
  from E-120 (`src/services/comment-service.ts` `fanOut`). §33.26 lists where the other three would
  originate; this chapter does not invent the triggers.
- **E-130 must ignore foreign ids silently**, not `404` — `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` applies only when
  a single notification is addressed (canon §4.3).

### 33.22 Search and insights — `search`, `insights`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-133** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/search?q=` | `nodes` (+ `tsvector`), `documents` (+ `tsvector`), `board_rows` (+ `tsvector`), `comments` (+ `tsvector`), `boards` (`template_id`, to bucket `api`/`bug`/`qa`), `access_rules`, `workspace_members`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-134** `GET /me/work?workspaceId=` | `board_rows` (generated columns `assignee_ids`, `due_date`, `due_at`, `status_option_id`), `board_columns`, `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `comments` (the `mentioned` widget), `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-135** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/dashboard` | `board_rows` (generated columns), `board_columns` (`completedOptionIds`, option labels), `boards`, `nodes`, `access_rules`, `users` | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **The permission funnel runs before scanning, not after** (canon E-133). The frontend encodes the
  same intent by passing an `allow` predicate *into* the service
  (`src/hooks/use-my-work.ts:14-20`, `src/hooks/use-dashboard.ts:14-20`) so a board the user cannot
  open is never read — "so it cannot be counted and then filtered out of a number they already
  saw". Server-side that becomes a join against the resolved-visibility CTE, not a post-filter.
- **`role` and `user` must stop being request parameters.** `SearchInput` is
  `{ query, role, user, limitPerGroup }` (`src/services/search-service.ts:45`) and
  `useGlobalSearch` sends `role` from the store and `CURRENT_USER` from the mock
  (`src/hooks/use-global-search.ts:36-38`) — OQ-20. A role in a body is a claim, not a fact
  (canon C-09).
- **Search is capped, not paged**: `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5` per group, fixed group order,
  `score DESC, title ASC` (`src/lib/search-index.ts:69-97`; `src/config/app.ts:30`). Deep paging a
  ranked search is a different feature (OQ-93).
- **My Work returns capped `items` *and* uncapped `total` per widget** so "12 of 40" stays honest
  (`MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6`, `src/config/app.ts:38`; `src/types/collab.ts:144`). Sort is
  `due_date ASC NULLS LAST, updated_at DESC` (`src/services/my-work-service.ts:145-157`).
- **Archived rows are excluded from every dashboard tally** (canon E-135), and `isNewWorkspace` and
  `boardCount` are cross-widget — one aggregate call, not three
  (`src/services/dashboard-service.ts:44-92`).
- **No `search_index` table** (canon §1.2): `tsvector` columns with GIN indexes on `documents`,
  `board_rows`, `comments` and `nodes`.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-92)** — *Which timezone defines "today" and "overdue"?*
**Evidence** — `MY_WORK_WIDGETS` compares with `isSameCalendarDay` / `isBeforeDay` against a
`nowIso` the client supplies (`src/lib/my-work.ts:57-67`, `src/services/my-work-service.ts:47-52`);
`src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24` insists a due date is "a square on a calendar, not a moment"; nothing
anywhere stores a user or workspace timezone.
**Recommendation** — add `users.timezone TEXT` (IANA name, defaulted from the browser at first
login) and compute "today" per recipient. E-134 and E-135 read it from the session; `due_date DATE`
is compared against `(now() AT TIME ZONE users.timezone)::date`, never against UTC midnight.
**Impact if wrong** — a task due 27 Aug shows as overdue at 17:00 on the 26th for a user in
UTC+7 and is still "today" at 06:00 on the 28th for a user in UTC−7. Both are the exact bug
`src/lib/calendar.ts` was written to prevent, resurfacing on the server side.

### 33.23 Audit — `governance`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-136** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit` | `audit_events`, `users` | — | — | — |
| **E-137** `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/audit/export` | `audit_events`, `users` | `audit_events` (**the export is itself audited at `warn`**) | **single** | — |

**Notes.**

- **There is no write endpoint and no chapter may add one** (canon §3.23). The service exposes
  `record` and `list` and nothing else, "so no screen can grow an Edit button that quietly works"
  (`src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20`, `:335`). Grant the application role `INSERT` and `SELECT`
  on `audit_events` and **not** `UPDATE` or `DELETE`.
- **`total` and `bySeverity` are facets over the whole filtered set, not the page**
  (`src/services/audit-service.ts:311-325`; `src/types/audit.ts:50-55`). The header renders "of N".
  Two queries: the page, and `COUNT(*) … GROUP BY severity` over the same predicate.
- **`ip` is stamped by the server, never sent.** The mock says so at the constant:
  *"A real backend reads it off the socket — the client must never send one, which is why this lives
  here and not in any hook"* (`src/services/audit-service.ts:280-285`).
- **`severity` defaults from `outcome`**: `denied → error`, otherwise `info`
  (`src/services/audit-service.ts:295`).
- **`audit_events.context JSONB` is internal and never returned** (canon §5.3 `AuditContext`,
  OQ-25). `detail` is the human line the table renders; `context` is what an investigation needs.
- **Retention is unresolved** (OQ-27). The frontend has no retention affordance. **RECOMMENDATION:**
  no automatic deletion; partition `audit_events` by month so an operator can detach cold
  partitions deliberately.

### 33.24 Realtime and meta — `realtime`, `system`

| API | Tables Read | Tables Written | Transaction | Realtime Event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E-138** `GET /realtime?workspaceId=` | `workspace_members` (**at handshake**), `nodes`, `access_rules` (**per frame, to decide who may receive it**) | — | — | all of RT-01 … RT-11 |
| **E-139** `GET /config` | — (static service config) | — | — | — |
| **E-140** `GET /health` | — (a liveness probe; a readiness probe may `SELECT 1`) | — | — | — |

**Notes.**

- **One socket per workspace**, Redis pub/sub for fan-out across instances (canon §7). Delivery is
  at-least-once with client-side dedup by `RealtimeEvent.id`
  (`src/lib/realtime/client.ts:21`, `SEEN_LIMIT = 512`), so exactly-once is not required.
- **Unknown frame types are ignored by the client** (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`), so RT-06 … RT-12
  can ship before any client release consumes them.
- **`REALTIME_ENDPOINT` is `null` today** (`src/config/app.ts:69`), which keeps
  `createTransport` on an in-process, same-tab bus (`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:56`). Adding a
  socket is a new `RealtimeTransport` implementation plus one line — nothing above it changes.
- **E-139 exists so the client cannot disagree with the server about a limit.** It serves the values
  that are duplicated as constants today: max upload bytes, accepted extensions,
  `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`, `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS`, `VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`, `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT`,
  `MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT`, `AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE` — all currently in `src/config/app.ts:30-64`.

**OPEN QUESTION (OQ-100)** — *How does the server prove a subscriber may receive a frame?*
**Evidence** — the socket is scoped to a workspace (canon E-138), but access is per node and
resolved by walking an ancestor chain (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120`). RT-03 is
already recipient-scoped by construction (`notifications.recipient_id`), and RT-05 deliberately
carries no content so it is safe to broadcast to the ids it names
(`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`). RT-01, RT-06 … RT-11 carry a `nodeId` or `boardId` and nothing
in the frontend decides who may see them.
**Recommendation** — maintain a per-connection set of node ids the subscriber currently holds
`view` on, refreshed on RT-05 and on reconnect; publish content frames to a Redis channel per
node id and let the connection's subscription set be the filter. Frames carry ids only
(canon §7.2), so the worst case of a stale set is a refetch that then returns `404`/`403` — never
a leak of the payload.
**Impact if wrong** — a user who lost access to a board keeps receiving row ids from it, which is
a slow enumeration oracle even without cell content.

### 33.26 Which endpoints write `audit_events`

`audit_events` is the one table almost every module writes, so it gets its own list. The mock
seeds a trail advertising 19 distinct action types and then has exactly **three** places that
write one: `src/store/permission-store.ts:71` (grant), `:99` (revoke) and
`src/services/devtools-service.ts:382` (a secret reveal or copy). Two of those three are in a
*client-side store*, which is the shape of the problem — OQ-25. The rule below is this chapter's reading of
canon's Perm column, not an invention: **every endpoint whose permission key is a `manage`,
`delete`, `archive`, `rotate` or `reveal` key writes an audit row, plus the two privileged reads
canon names.**

| Module | Endpoints that write an audit row | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | E-001 (`allowed`/`denied`), E-002, E-003 (only on `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED`) | `info` / `error` |
| `workspace` | E-008, E-010, E-011, E-013, E-014, E-015, E-016, E-019 | `info`; E-011 `warn` |
| `node` | E-024, E-025, E-026, E-027, E-030, E-031, E-032, E-037, E-038, E-039 | `info`; E-038/E-039 `warn` |
| `governance` | E-041, E-042, E-043, **E-046 (a read)**, **E-137 (a read)** | `info`; E-046/E-137 `warn` |
| `board` | E-050, E-052, E-054, E-055, E-057, E-085, E-086, E-089, E-090 | `info` |
| `row` | E-074, E-075, E-076, E-077 | `info`; a bulk delete of >10 rows `warn` |
| `document` | E-094 (lock/unlock), E-097 (version restore) | `info` |
| `devtools` | E-100 **when `environment_id` is the production environment** (OQ-62), E-107, E-108, E-109 | `warn` for production config |
| `secret` | E-102, **E-103 (allowed *and* denied)**, **E-104 (allowed *and* denied)** | `warn`; `denied` → `error` |
| `file` | E-111, E-115 | `info` |
| `comment` | E-122, E-123 | `info` |

**Every one of these rows is written inside the mutating transaction, never fire-and-forget.** An
audit trail that can disagree with the state it describes is worse than none — canon §3.23, and
the mock's own note that `record` is synchronous by design.

---

### 33.27 Transaction inventory — the twenty-one multi-table writes

The endpoints where getting the transaction boundary wrong produces a corrupt state rather than a
retryable failure. This is the list to review in code review.

| Endpoint | What must land together | The corrupt state if it does not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E-008 | `workspaces` + `workspace_members(admin)` | A workspace nobody can administer. |
| E-014/E-015/E-016 | last-admin check + `workspace_members` write | Two concurrent demotions each see one other admin; the workspace loses its last admin. |
| E-019 | `workspace_invitations.accepted_at` + `workspace_members` | A replayed invite link mints a second membership. |
| E-024 | `nodes` + the side table for its kind | A node the router can address and no surface can render. |
| E-026 | descendant check + `nodes.parent_id` | Two concurrent moves create a detached ring the tree walk never terminates on. |
| E-027 | the whole subtree copy | A half-copied project with dangling parent ids. |
| E-032 | subtree `deleted_at` + `trash_entries` | A restore that duplicates the subtree, or a subtree nothing can restore. |
| E-037 | subtree un-delete + entry consumption | A restore that can be replayed. |
| E-038/E-039 | cascade + `workspaces.used_bytes` | The quota drifts and eventually blocks all uploads. |
| E-042 | rule upsert + audit | Two rules for one subject on one node — an unresolvable grant. |
| E-054/E-055/E-057 | schema change + a cell rewrite on every row + view prune | Views pointing at a dead column; cells keyed by a column that no longer exists. |
| E-062/E-064 | `next_sequence` + row + order + activity | A skipped or duplicated `TASK-nnn`. |
| E-065 | row delete + children lifted + activity purge | Orphaned subtasks that render under a parent that no longer exists. |
| E-066 | per-row `FOR UPDATE` + cells + revision + activity | Two clients both read revision 7 and both write revision 8; one edit vanishes with no conflict notice. |
| E-077 | insert on target + delete on source, **across two boards** | Every moved record exists twice. |
| E-085 | column create + rows + column remove | A failed import that emptied the schema. |
| E-092/E-097/E-100 | content + version snapshot (+ the config fold) | A version history with a gap, or a head version that does not match the document. |
| E-102 | `secrets` list replace + rotations + audit | A deployment reading half the new secrets and half the old. |
| E-103/E-104 | audit rows **before** the plaintext leaves | A reveal with no trail — the single worst failure in this system. |
| E-111 | `file_assets` + `file_nodes` + `nodes` + `workspaces.used_bytes` | Bytes stored and never counted, or counted and never stored. |
| E-120 | comment + auto-watch + N notifications + activity + frame | A comment nobody is told about, or notifications for a comment that was rolled back. |

---

## 34. Frontend ↔ API Mapping

Every frontend surface that needs the backend, walked from the real source: every route under
`src/app/`, every hook under `src/hooks/` that calls a service, and every store action that writes.

### Status definitions

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **EXISTS** | A mock service in `src/services/` already implements this operation, the frontend calls it through a service boundary, and the request and response shapes are settled. The backend implements the named endpoint against that contract. |
| **MOCKED** | The frontend fakes it. Either a Zustand store mutates in-memory state with no service call, or a module constant stands in for server data. The contract must be invented — the shape is a proposal, not a settled fact. |
| **MISSING** | The frontend needs it and nothing implements it, in the mock or otherwise. Usually a permission key with no endpoint behind it, or a rule the UI assumes the server will apply. |
| **UNKNOWN** | The frontend cannot tell us. Two readings of the same evidence are equally supported; an OQ id carries it. |

The honest headline: **the mock service layer covers boards, documents, config, secrets, files,
comments, notifications, watches, search, My Work, dashboard and audit — and covers the drive tree,
workspaces, membership, access rules and trash not at all.** `src/store/workspace-store.ts` (1 111
lines) and `src/store/permission-store.ts` (127 lines) import no service; they are seeded from
`src/mock/tree.ts` and `src/mock/access.ts` at module load. Those two stores are where every
MOCKED row in this section comes from.

---
