### Status tally

Counted over the fourteen tables above. A handful of rows carry two statuses — the node half is
MOCKED while the content half EXISTS (create a page, duplicate a page, archive a page) — so the
marks total slightly more than the rows.

| Status | Marks | Where they cluster |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **EXISTS** | 112 | Boards (schema, rows, cells, views, bulk), documents, config, secrets, files, comments, watches, notifications, search, My Work, dashboard, audit read. |
| **MOCKED** | 63 | The entire drive tree, workspaces, membership, access rules, trash, favourites, archive; import parsing; export generation; version diffing; the realtime transport; environments; the current user. |
| **MISSING** | 23 | Auth and session; per-viewer view preferences; row cursor pagination; the unread count; comment resolve and delete; `assigned`/`watch`/`system` notifications; audit export; environment management; secret note and environment writes; UI preferences; move visibility impact; server-side enforcement of transition rules and conditional option availability; a dry-run column conversion. |
| **UNKNOWN** | 3 | Gantt dependency semantics (OQ-45); board column roles (OQ-48); the definition of "done" (OQ-49). |

**The most valuable rows in this section are the MOCKED ones for the drive tree and governance.**
Fifteen `workspace-store` actions and two `permission-store` actions carry business rules — slug
uniqueness among siblings, the four move rejection kinds, restore relocation, last-admin
protection, "pages can only live inside containers", subtree-wide visibility pruning — that exist
**only** as client code today. They are real requirements (the frontend behaves that way and the UI
depends on it) and they have no wire contract at all. Canon §3.3, §3.4 and §3.5 are that contract;
§33 above is what those endpoints touch.

### 34.1 Feature Coverage Matrix

Every module, without exception. Columns:

- **DB** — the tables from canon §1.1 that hold it. `—` means "no table by design", with the reason.
- **API** — the canon endpoint ids. `—` means no endpoint.
- **Realtime** — the canon §7 frame ids that announce a change to it.
- **Permission** — the `PermissionKey` (canon §2.10) that gates the writes. `membership` = any
  member; `visibility` = resolved `view` on the node; `session` = any authenticated caller.
- **Notes** — the one thing a developer gets wrong if they skim.

| Feature | DB | API | Realtime | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Workspace** | `workspaces` (T-03) | E-007 – E-011, E-017 | RT-05 (membership only) | `workspace.manage`, `workspace.delete`, `workspace.settings.view` | `used_bytes` is a transactional counter, never `SUM(file_assets)`. Slug is globally unique (OQ-02). Entirely **MOCKED** in the FE. |
| **Membership** | `workspace_members` (T-04), `workspace_invitations` (T-05) | E-012 – E-016, E-018, E-019 | RT-05 | `workspace.member.manage`; E-016 needs only membership | The last-admin guard is a read-then-write race — `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` over the admin set. "Not a member" answers `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, not `403`. |
| **Project** | `nodes` (T-06) `kind='project'` | E-020 – E-032 | RT-11 | `node.create`, `node.rename`, `node.move`, `node.archive`, `node.delete` | Not a separate table. `ProjectStatus` (`active`/`paused`/`archived`) is a nullable column on `nodes`. |
| **Folder** | `nodes` (T-06) `kind='folder'` | E-020 – E-032 | RT-11 | same as Project | `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` must hold **across kinds** — the reason for one `nodes` table (canon §1.3.1). |
| **Folder Access** | `access_rules` (T-08), `nodes.access_mode` | E-040 – E-044, E-046 | RT-05 | `node.access.manage`; E-046 `workspace.permission.manage` | Deepest node wins; at one node a user rule beats a role rule; the workspace role is the floor (OQ-22). Clearing the last rule makes the node inherit again. E-046 is audited at `warn`. |
| **Page / Document** | `nodes` (T-06) `kind='document'`, `documents` (T-18) | E-091 – E-094 (+ E-024, E-026, E-027, E-030 – E-032) | RT-11 (title/lifecycle) | `document.create`, `document.update`, `document.lock` \| owner | `blocks JSONB` is 14 `BlockType`s collapsing into 9 interfaces. `node_id` is `UNIQUE NOT NULL`; the node owns `name`, `isArchived`, and they are projected, not duplicated (OQ-30, OQ-56). |
| **Document Versions** | `document_versions` (T-19) | E-095 – E-098 | — | `document.version.restore`; read is `visibility` | Full snapshot per version, never a patch — `DiffKind` has no `changed`. Restore writes a **new** version. Trim by a scheduled job, not in the write path. |
| **Config Document** | `nodes` `kind='document'` + `document_kind='config'`, `config_documents` (T-20), `config_versions` (T-21) | E-099, E-100 (+ E-095 – E-098) | — | `document.update` | The wire field is `format`, never `language`. The autosave **fold** (`is_autosave` + same author) is what makes the history restorable. Production saves audit at `warn` (OQ-62). |
| **Secret Document** | `secret_documents` (T-22), `secrets` (T-23), `secret_rotations` (T-24), `secret_access_events` (T-25) | E-101 – E-105 (+ E-095) | — | `secret.reveal`, `secret.rotate` | `value_encrypted` is never in a list read. `maskedValue` is a constant 12 bullets. Reveal audits **before** returning, allowed or denied. `copy` has no key of its own. |
| **Board** | `nodes` `kind='board'`, `boards` (T-10) | E-047 – E-050 (+ E-024) | RT-10, RT-11 | `board.create`, `board.manage` | `next_sequence BIGINT` under `FOR UPDATE`, per board, monotonic. E-048 must never read `board_rows`. |
| **Columns** | `board_columns` (T-11) | E-051 – E-057 | RT-10 | `board.column.create` / `.update` / `.delete` | `position` is dense `0..n-1`, renumbered on every structural change. Exactly one primary column: never hidden, never deleted, never duplicated as primary. E-053 accepts no `type` and no `position`. |
| **Select Options** | `board_columns.config` JSONB (`SelectConfig.options`) | E-058 – E-060 | RT-10 | `board.column.update` | **No `select_options` table** (canon §1.3.3) — three sibling structures reference option ids by value. `"__empty__"` is reserved. Create dedupes by trimmed, case-folded label and returns `200`. Delete leaves orphaned ids in cells on purpose. |
| **Conditional Select** | `board_columns.config` (`options[].availability`, `unavailableBehavior`) | E-053 | RT-10 | `board.column.update` | The condition tree is `Condition` \| `ConditionGroup` with `ConditionOperator` — **not** `FilterOperator` (OQ-37). The server must re-evaluate it on E-066; `guardCellEdits` is a client courtesy (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:43`). Nesting depth is capped (`CONDITION_TREE_TOO_DEEP`, OQ-38). |
| **Transition Rules** | `board_columns.config.transitionRules` | E-053 | RT-10 | `board.column.update` | Keyed by option id with the reserved key `"__empty__"` (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:28`). Enforced server-side on E-066 with `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED`. Currently **MISSING** server-side. |
| **Rows** | `board_rows` (T-12) | E-061 – E-069, E-073 | RT-06, RT-07, RT-08, RT-09 | `row.create`, `row.update`, `row.move`, `row.archive`, `row.delete` | `position NUMERIC` fractional index (OQ-34). `archived_at` freezes edits but not removal. Rows have **no trash** — deletion is permanent by product decision (OQ-15). |
| **Custom Row ID** | `board_rows.custom_id`, `board_rows.sequence`, `boards.row_id_prefix`, `boards.next_sequence` | E-062, E-064, E-077, E-085 (assign); E-050 (prefix) | — | `row.create` | `` `${prefix}-${String(n).padStart(3,"0")}` ``, prefix `^[A-Z]{1,6}$`, `UNIQUE (board_id, custom_id)`. The counter only increases — deleting `TASK-005` never re-issues `005`. **Never the primary key** (canon C-02). |
| **Cells** | `board_rows.cells` JSONB + generated columns `due_date`, `due_at`, `status_option_id`, `assignee_ids` | E-066 (+ E-054, E-055, E-057 rewrites) | RT-07 | `row.update` | **No `cell_values` table** (canon §1.3.2). A cell's `kind` may legitimately disagree with its column's `type` after a conversion — do not normalise it. An empty value is an explicit empty `CellValue`, never `null`. Always `200` + `ConflictNotice[]`, never `409`. |
| **Subtasks** | `board_rows.parent_row_id` | E-062 (with `parentRowId`), E-067, E-068 | RT-06, RT-07 | `row.move` | Same board only, depth cap 5, cycles rejected by recursive CTE, archiving a parent does **not** cascade, deleting a parent **lifts** children (`ON DELETE SET NULL`) (OQ-33). There is no subtask collection anywhere — progress is derived. |
| **Relations / Blocked By** | `board_rows.cells` (`{ kind: "relation", rowIds }`) + `board_row_relations` (T-13) projection | E-071, E-072 (+ E-066 writes) | RT-07 | `row.update` | **No `RelationType` enum and no edge table** (canon §2.9). "Blocked by" is a relation column shipped by the `task` template. Backlinks are an indexed query, never a scan. Dangling ids stay in the cell so `[Deleted Item]` renders (OQ-44, OQ-45). |
| **Table view** | `board_views` (T-15) `type='table'` | E-078 – E-082 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | Column order, width, visibility and display mode live on the **view**, not the schema. `CellDisplayMode` absent means `compact`. |
| **Kanban** | `board_views` `type='kanban'` | E-078 – E-082 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | Needs `groupByColumnId` (`VIEW_TYPE_REQUIRES_COLUMN`). Grouping runs client-side over the loaded rows — no per-view row endpoint. |
| **Calendar** | `board_views` `type='calendar'` | E-078 – E-082 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | Needs `dateColumnId`. A due date is `YYYY-MM-DD` and **must never pass through UTC** (canon C-04, `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-24`). |
| **Gantt** | `board_views` `type='gantt'` (`ganttZoom`, `endDateColumnId`, `showDependencies`) | E-078 – E-082 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | **`ganttZoom: "day"` must be accepted and coerced to `"week"`** — saved views still hold it. An inverted date range is reported, never swapped (OQ-50). |
| **Saved Views** | `board_views` (T-15), `board_view_preferences` (T-16) | E-078 – E-083 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage`; E-083 `visibility` | A view is **shared**; the order is the board's, not the reader's. E-080 preserves `id` and `boardId` against the patch. Deleting the last view is refused. Per-viewer widths/collapse move to T-16 (OQ-46). |
| **Filters** | `board_views.filters`, `filter_conjunction` | E-080 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | `FilterOperator` has `onOrBefore`/`onOrAfter`; `ConditionOperator` does not. **Two enums** (OQ-37). Filtering executes client-side over the loaded set (`queryRowIds`) until server-side query lands (OQ-36). |
| **Sorts** | `board_views.sorts` | E-080 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | Multi-level; earlier entries win. `SortDirection` is `asc`/`desc`. |
| **Groups** | `board_views.group_by_column_id`, `hide_empty_groups` | E-080 | RT-10 | `board.view.manage` | Collapsed group state is per viewer and belongs in T-16, not here. |
| **Import** | `import_jobs` (T-38); writes `board_columns`, `board_rows` | E-084, E-085 | RT-06, RT-10 | `board.import` | **One transaction**: column creation, row inserts, column removal. Default `ImportInvalidPolicy` is `skip`. `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5000`. Display ids are contiguous — no gaps. Parsing is client-side today (**MOCKED**). |
| **Export** | `export_jobs` (T-39) for `board` scope only | E-086 | — | `board.export` — a **`READ_ONLY_KEY`** that passes trashed/frozen/locked narrowing | `ExportScope.view` includes the active **search term**. `omittedColumns` implies column-level permissions that do not exist (OQ-29). Entirely client-side today (**MOCKED**). |
| **Attachments** | `file_assets` (T-27) + `cell_attachments` (T-29), `comment_attachments` (T-30), `document_asset_refs` (T-31) | E-117 (+ E-066, E-092, E-120 as writers) | RT-07 | `file.upload`, `file.delete`; read is `visibility` on any owner | **Typed join tables, not polymorphic** (canon §1.3.4) — every operation that matters is a foreign-key question. Only `assetId` is persisted; `url`/`thumbnailUrl` are minted per response and never accepted on write (OQ-75). A cell attachment does **not** create a file node. |
| **Uploads** | `uploads` (T-32), `file_assets` (T-27), `file_nodes` (T-28), `workspaces.used_bytes` | E-110 – E-112 | RT-11 (when a node is made) | `file.upload` | Presign → PUT → complete. Quota checked at presign **and** enforced at complete. `owner` from the session, never the body. `createDriveNode` decides whether a `nodes` row appears (OQ-74). |
| **Comments** | `comments` (T-33), `comment_attachments` (T-30) | E-119 – E-125 | RT-01, RT-02 | `comment.create`, `comment.resolve`, `comment.delete` | Exactly two levels — a reply to a reply re-parents to the root. Oldest-first, `(created_at ASC, id ASC)`. Soft delete is a tombstone so replies do not orphan. Resolve is a **root-only** property. E-122 – E-124 are **MISSING** from the FE. |
| **Mentions** | `comments.body` (`@[Name](usr_id)`), `comments.mentioned_user_ids`; drives `notifications` | E-120 (parse), E-006 (picker) | RT-03 | `comment.create` | Parsed **server-side**; a client-supplied list is ignored. Mentioning somebody without access is unhandled (OQ-85). Does editing notify the newly mentioned? Unresolved (OQ-84). |
| **Watches** | `watches` (T-34) | E-126 – E-128 | — | `visibility` on the target for E-127; `session` otherwise | Only `row`, `document`, `board` — anything else is `WATCH_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED`. Auto-watch on first comment happens inside E-120's transaction, not as a second call. `userId` must leave the request (OQ-19). |
| **Notifications** | `notifications` (T-35) | E-129 – E-132 | RT-03, RT-04 | `session` — always the caller's own inbox | **One row per recipient**, fan-out on write. The label is **frozen at creation** — the one place a denormalised label is not resolved live (OQ-79). Filter by `reason`, never by tab. RT-03 goes only to its `recipientId`. `assigned`/`watch`/`system` have no emitter (OQ-89). |
| **My Work** | *(no table)* — computed over `board_rows` generated columns + `comments` | E-134 | — | `session` | Five widgets, each with capped `items` **and** uncapped `total`. `MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT = 6`. Sort `due_date ASC NULLS LAST, updated_at DESC`. The visibility filter runs **before** aggregation. Column roles are name heuristics (OQ-48); "today" needs a timezone (OQ-92). |
| **Search** | *(no `search_index` table)* — `tsvector` + GIN on `nodes`, `documents`, `board_rows`, `comments` | E-035 (drive quick-find), E-133 (global) | — | `membership` + per-node `visibility` | Two endpoints on purpose (OQ-94). The permission funnel runs **before** scanning. `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5` per group, fixed group order, `score DESC, title ASC`. `api`/`bug`/`qa` buckets derive from `boards.template_id`. `role` and `user` must leave the request (OQ-20). |
| **Favourites** | `node_favorites` (T-07) | E-028, E-029, E-033 | — | `visibility` | **Per user, not a flag on the node** (OQ-07). The FE renders `node.isFavorite`, which the API must project per caller. |
| **Recent** | *(no table — `localStorage` `nexdrop-recent`)* | — | — | — | Per-device by nature; canon OQ-96 keeps it client-side. `RECENT_LIMIT = 10`, LRU, shape-validated on read. `useAccessSync` clears it on revocation. |
| **Dashboard** | *(no table)* — computed over `board_rows`, `board_columns`, `boards`, `nodes` | E-135 | — | `membership` | **One aggregate call, not three.** Archived rows excluded from every tally. A board is QA by *what it became*, not by template id. Two competing definitions of "done" (OQ-49). |
| **Activity Log** | `row_activity` (T-14) | E-070 (+ every row write as producer) | RT-07 | `visibility` to read | One entry per write however many fields it touched. Newest-first. Rendered `changes` returned; internal `raw_changes` never returned (OQ-51). The synthetic `created` entry must be either always synthesised or always persisted — not sometimes each. |
| **Audit Log** | `audit_events` (T-36) | E-136, E-137 — **no write endpoint, ever** | — | `workspace.audit.view` — a **`READ_ONLY_KEY`** | Append-only by grant: `INSERT` + `SELECT` only. `ip` off the socket. `severity` defaults from `outcome`. `total` and `bySeverity` are facets over the **whole filtered set**. `context JSONB` is internal. Rows are written inside the mutating transaction (§33.26). |
| **Trash** | `trash_entries` (T-09), `nodes.deleted_at` | E-036 – E-039 | RT-11 | `node.delete` | Delete **detaches the whole subtree** and writes **one** entry for the subtree root, with the human path resolved at deletion. Restore relocates to the deepest surviving ancestor and reports `isRelocated` — a `200`, not an error. 30-day retention, nightly sweep, `purgeAt` returned. |
| **Archive** | `nodes.is_archived`, `archived_at`, `archived_by` | E-030, E-031, E-034 | RT-11 | `node.archive` | An **ancestor's** archive flag freezes a node; its own flag makes it read-only with Restore offered — the precedence in `NodeState` (canon §2.4). A node under an archived ancestor cannot be thawed on its own. E-034 returns only the outermost archived node per subtree. |
| **RBAC** | `workspace_members.role`, `access_rules`; the 39-key catalogue is **static config, not a table** | E-044, E-045, E-040 – E-043; enforced on **all 140** | RT-05 | `workspace.permission.manage`, `node.access.manage` | Roles are cumulative: viewer 0 keys, member +10, manager +21, admin +8. Owner escalation applies from `member` up. Three narrowing layers (trashed, frozen, locked) only ever take away; `READ_ONLY_KEYS = { board.export, workspace.audit.view, secret.reveal }` pass through all three. `previewAs` may only narrow (OQ-21). |
| **Realtime** | *(no table)* — Redis pub/sub | E-138 | RT-01 … RT-12 | `membership` at handshake; per-frame `visibility` | At-least-once with client dedup by frame id. Unknown frame types are ignored, so new frames ship without a client release. RT-05 carries **no content on purpose**. RT-06 … RT-11 carry **ids only**. Scoping and replay are open (OQ-100, OQ-101). |
| **Auth** | `users` (T-01), `user_sessions` (T-02) | E-001 – E-005 | — | `session` | **Nothing in the frontend constrains this** (OQ-01) — `CURRENT_USER` is a module constant. Canon's position: cookie session, short-lived access token, rotating refresh family, replay revokes the family. Identity, role, IP and clock come from the session and the socket, never from a body (canon C-09). |

#### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

Five places where following canon exactly produced a result worth a second look. In every case
this chapter followed canon.

1. **RT-05 on E-013 (invite).** Canon §7.1 lists E-013 among `permission.changed`'s triggers, and
   §33.2 follows it. But an invitation grants no access until E-019 is accepted, and the frame's
   payload is `{ workspaceId, nodeId | null, userIds }` — for an invited email with no `users` row
   there is no id to put in `userIds`. Either the frame is a no-op for that case, or E-013 should
   be dropped from RT-05's trigger list and E-019 kept. **Suggestion:** drop E-013; keep E-014,
   E-015, E-016, E-019.

2. **`user_ui_preferences` (T-37) has no endpoint.** It is the only table in canon §1.1 with no
   writer anywhere in canon §3 (§33.25). Either add `PUT /me/preferences/{scope}` as E-141 (and
   `GET /me` already returns the read side), or remove T-37 and let OQ-98 stay unresolved. The
   frontend state that would fill it is real — sidebar collapse (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:140`)
   and drive view mode + sort (`:118-119`) — so this chapter recommends the endpoint.

3. **Document pinning: canon §8.8 (OQ-07/OQ-08) says "per user", the frontend says "per document".**
   `documentService.setPinned(nodeId, isPinned)` toggles a field on `WorkspaceDocument`
   (`src/services/document-service.ts:309-322`), the sidebar shows one shared list
   (`src/components/layout/sidebar/pinned-pages.tsx`), and canon E-093 returns a
   `WorkspaceDocument` rather than a `204` — which is the shape of a document-level flag, not a
   per-user one. §33.13 keeps `documents.is_pinned` and flags the divergence rather than shipping a
   `node_pins` table nothing asks for. Favourites (T-07) genuinely are per user; pinning, as
   implemented, is not.

4. **`GET /nodes/{nodeId}/versions/{versionId}/diff` (E-098) has no frontend consumer.** The diff is
   computed in the browser from two snapshots (`src/lib/diff.ts`,
   `src/components/versions/version-dialogs.tsx`), and both snapshots are already available from
   E-096. E-098 is therefore either a bandwidth optimisation for large pages or a redundant
   endpoint. It is mapped in §33.14 because canon declares it; a reviewer may wish to mark it
   deferred.

5. **`GET /boards/{boardId}/relation-index` (E-071) sits under `/boards/{boardId}` but reads the
   *target* board.** `boardService.relationIndex` is called once per target board with a batch of
   ids (`src/hooks/use-relation-index.ts`), so `{boardId}` in the path is the board being *read
   into*, while the rows returned belong to another board entirely — and canon E-071 says the
   result is "filtered by read access on the target board's node". The path reads as though the
   permission check is on `{boardId}`. It is not, and §33.8 lists both `nodes` and `access_rules`
   for the target. Consider `GET /boards/{targetBoardId}/rows/resolve?ids=` in a later revision.

## 35. Index Strategy

This section is the consolidated index registry. Every index that the 39 tables of canon §1.1 need
is listed once, with the query it exists for. Where a schema chapter (§4.x) already declared an
index, this section reproduces it under the same name so the two cannot drift; where a table has no
schema chapter yet, this section is the declaration.

### 35.1 The five rules that generated this list

| # | Rule | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| X-01 | **Every index names one query, and that query names an endpoint.** An index with no reader is a write cost with no benefit. | `row_activity_actor_idx` is listed and deliberately **not created** — there is no "what did this person do on this board" surface (§4.x, part 5). |
| X-02 | **The first column of a composite is the tenancy or ownership scope**, because every query in this API is already scoped by one: `workspace_id`, `board_id`, `node_id`, `recipient_id`, `user_id`. A leading `created_at` would be a full-table scan wearing an index's clothes. | `notifications (recipient_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)`, never `(created_at DESC)`. |
| X-03 | **Every cursor-paginated list gets an index whose column list is exactly its sort key, tiebreaker included** (canon §6.3). A cursor is a keyset seek; without the tiebreaker in the index the seek degrades to a sort. | `audit_events (workspace_id, at DESC, id DESC)`; `comments (target_node_id, target_kind, target_row_id, created_at ASC, id ASC)`. |
| X-04 | **Soft delete goes in the index predicate, not in the column list.** `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` keeps the index the size of the live set. §35.4. | `nodes_parent_idx (parent_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. |
| X-05 | **JSONB gets a GIN index only where a query actually reaches inside it.** Everywhere else the JSONB is read whole, with the row, by primary key. §35.5. | `board_rows` gets `GIN (cells jsonb_path_ops)`; `board_columns.config`, `documents.blocks`, `board_templates.columns` and `notifications.context` get none. |

Naming convention: `<table>_<purpose>_idx` for a plain index, `<table>_<purpose>_uniq` for a unique
one, `<table>_pkey` for the primary key. The convention is not decoration — the audit chapter's
`EXPLAIN` budgets and the operational runbook both address indexes by name.

### 35.2 The registry

#### 35.2.1 `identity`

| Table | Index | Type | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `users` | `users_pkey (id)` | btree, PK | Every join from `nodes.owner_id`, `workspace_members.user_id`, `access_rules.subject_user_id`, `comments.author_id`, `notifications.actor_id`, `audit_events.actor_id`. |
| `users` | `users_email_uniq UNIQUE (lower(email))` | btree, unique, expression | E-001 `POST /auth/login` — one probe by address. E-013 invite-by-address, which must not create a second account for `Mai@x.com` when `mai@x.com` exists. |
| `user_sessions` | `user_sessions_token_uniq UNIQUE (refresh_token_hash)` | btree, unique | E-003 `POST /auth/refresh` — resolve the presented token in one probe, then `FOR UPDATE` on the row it found (§36.11). |
| `user_sessions` | `user_sessions_family_idx (family_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | The replay response: `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` revokes every live row in the family in one statement. Partial, because a revoked family is never revoked again. |
| `user_sessions` | `user_sessions_user_idx (user_id, revoked_at)` | btree | E-002 logout-everywhere; deactivating a user (`users.is_active = false`) must close their sessions. |
| `user_sessions` | `user_sessions_expiry_idx (expires_at)` | btree | The nightly sweep of expired rows. |
| `user_ui_preferences` | `user_ui_preferences_uniq UNIQUE (user_id, scope)` | btree, unique | The whole table. Read is `WHERE user_id = $me`, write is an upsert on the pair. **RECOMMENDATION**, OQ-98 — build it only when OQ-98 is answered. |

#### 35.2.2 `workspace`

| Table | Index | Type | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaces` | `workspaces_pkey (id)` | btree, PK | Every workspace-scoped read; the `FOR UPDATE` that guards `used_bytes` (E-111, §36.11). |
| `workspaces` | `workspaces_slug_uniq UNIQUE (slug)` | btree, unique | Resolving a workspace from a URL segment; the `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` check on E-008 and E-010. Globally unique — canon's OQ-02 position is one tenant level. |
| `workspace_members` | `workspace_members_pair_uniq UNIQUE (workspace_id, user_id) INCLUDE (role)` | btree, unique, covering | **The hottest index in the schema.** Gate 1 on every single request: "is this caller a member of this workspace, and with what role" (`isWorkspaceMember`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`). `INCLUDE (role)` makes it an index-only scan, which is what keeps SY-RBC-42's p99 budget reachable. |
| `workspace_members` | `workspace_members_user_idx (user_id)` | btree | E-007 `GET /workspaces` — the workspaces this person is in. The read starts here and joins outward to `workspaces`; it never scans `workspaces` and filters (`visibleWorkspaces`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:45-50`). |
| `workspace_members` | `workspace_members_admin_idx (workspace_id) WHERE role = 'admin'` | btree, partial | The last-admin guard on E-014, E-015 and E-016 (`isLastAdmin`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157`). Partial because the question is only ever asked about admins, and it is asked under `FOR UPDATE` over the whole matched set (§37.6). |
| `workspace_invitations` | `workspace_invitations_token_uniq UNIQUE (token_hash)` | btree, unique | E-019 `POST /invitations/{token}/accept` — one probe, then `FOR UPDATE`. |
| `workspace_invitations` | `workspace_invitations_pending_uniq UNIQUE (workspace_id, lower(email)) WHERE accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL` | btree, partial unique | E-018's listing, and the `MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` check on E-013. Partial so that re-inviting somebody whose earlier invite was accepted or revoked is legal. |
| `workspace_invitations` | `workspace_invitations_expiry_idx (expires_at) WHERE accepted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | The reaper. |

#### 35.2.3 `drive`

| Table | Index | Type | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `nodes_pkey (id)` | btree, PK | E-022 `GET /nodes/{nodeId}`, and every step of every ancestor-chain walk (`findPathToId`, `src/lib/tree.ts`). |
| `nodes` | `nodes_id_workspace_uniq UNIQUE (id, workspace_id)` | btree, unique | Carries no business meaning. It is the target of the composite `(parent_id, workspace_id)` FK that makes a cross-tenant child impossible. |
| `nodes` | `nodes_slug_child_uniq UNIQUE (parent_id, slug) WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial unique | Slug uniqueness per sibling set. `resolvePath` takes the **first** match, so a duplicate makes the loser permanently unreachable (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:472-480`). Serves E-021 `nodes/resolve?path=`, and is the constraint E-024/E-026/E-037 retry against. |
| `nodes` | `nodes_slug_root_uniq UNIQUE (workspace_id, slug) WHERE parent_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial unique | The same rule at the root, where `parent_id IS NULL` would otherwise make every row distinct. |
| `nodes` | `nodes_parent_idx (parent_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | E-023 `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/children`; the downward recursive CTE behind archive impact, move impact, subtree delete and subtree restore. |
| `nodes` | `nodes_workspace_kind_idx (workspace_id, kind) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | E-020 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/tree` — one flat scan of the workspace, nested in memory, no CTE. Also E-048 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/boards`, filtering `kind = 'board'`, which **must never seed or read a board's rows** (`src/services/board-service.ts:1234-1246`). |
| `nodes` | `nodes_owner_idx (workspace_id, owner_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | The owner-escalation path (`OWNER_ESCALATIONS`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:71-74`) when it has to answer "which of these nodes do I own" for a page of nodes at once. |
| `nodes` | `nodes_archived_idx (workspace_id, archived_at DESC) WHERE archived_at IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | E-034 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/archive`, which returns **only the outermost archived node per subtree** — the index finds the candidates, the ancestor walk filters them (`src/lib/archive.ts:19-45`). |
| `nodes` | `nodes_trash_idx (workspace_id, deleted_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL` | btree, partial | E-036 trash listing, newest-deleted first (`sortTrash`, `src/lib/trash.ts:140-143`), and the nightly retention sweep on `deleted_at < now() - interval '30 days'` (OQ-14). |
| `nodes` | `nodes_restricted_idx (workspace_id) WHERE access_mode = 'restricted' AND deleted_at IS NULL` | btree, partial | E-046 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/restricted-nodes` — the admin recovery console (`restrictedNodesOf`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:279-291`). Tiny in every real workspace. **This read is itself audited at `warn`** (OQ-26, §38.4). |
| `nodes` | `nodes_search_idx GIN (search_vector)` | GIN, tsvector | E-133 global search — the `document`, `file` and `place` buckets are produced from node `name` and `excerpt` (`src/services/search-service.ts:137-161`). §35.6. |
| `nodes` | `nodes_name_trgm_idx GIN (lower(name) gin_trgm_ops) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | GIN, `pg_trgm` | E-035 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/search?q=` — drive quick-find. Its semantics are **substring**, not full-text: `searchNodes` does `name.toLowerCase().includes(needle)` (`src/lib/tree.ts:278-295`), which a `tsvector` cannot answer and a trigram index can. |
| `node_favorites` | `node_favorites_uniq UNIQUE (user_id, node_id)` | btree, unique | E-033 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/favorites` (leading `user_id`); the E-028 `PUT` conflict target; the E-029 `DELETE`; and the `isFavorite` projection when a subtree is read for one viewer (`user_id = $me AND node_id = ANY($ids)`). Favourites are **per user**, never a flag on the node (OQ-07). |
| `node_favorites` | `node_favorites_node_idx (node_id)` | btree | Backs the `nodes` cascade. Without it, purging a project with 400 descendants sequential-scans this table 400 times. |
| `trash_entries` | `trash_entries_node_uniq UNIQUE (node_id)` | btree, unique | One entry per deleted subtree **root**; descendants get `nodes.deleted_at` and no entry, which is what makes the trash listing show one item rather than a subtree's worth. |
| `trash_entries` | `trash_entries_page_idx (workspace_id, deleted_at DESC, id DESC)` | btree | E-036 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/trash`, newest-deleted first. |
| `trash_entries` | `trash_entries_purge_idx (purge_at)` | btree | The nightly retention sweep (OQ-14: 30 days, `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`, `src/config/app.ts:44`). |

#### 35.2.4 `governance`

| Table | Index | Type | Query it serves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `access_rules` | `access_rules_pkey (id)` | btree, PK | E-043 `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}/access-rules/{ruleId}`. |
| `access_rules` | `access_rules_node_user_uniq UNIQUE (node_id, subject_user_id) WHERE subject_kind = 'user'` | btree, partial unique | **A correctness constraint, not hygiene.** `matchIn` takes the first matching rule within a node (`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:63-76`), so a duplicate would make resolution order-dependent. Also the `ON CONFLICT` target that makes E-042 an upsert. |
| `access_rules` | `access_rules_node_role_uniq UNIQUE (node_id, subject_role) WHERE subject_kind = 'role'` | btree, partial unique | The same rule for the role-scoped branch. |
| `access_rules` | `access_rules_chain_idx (node_id) INCLUDE (subject_kind, subject_user_id, subject_role, role)` | btree, covering | **The hot governance query.** Given the ancestor chain of a node, fetch every rule written on any node in it: `WHERE node_id = ANY(:chain)`. `INCLUDE` makes it index-only, which matters because this runs on every permission resolution that is not answered from the Redis cache (§37.6). |
| `access_rules` | `access_rules_workspace_node_idx (workspace_id, node_id)` | btree | The bulk load when one request resolves many nodes at once — a tree read (E-020) or the search funnel (E-133). Mirrors the frontend's own index shape, `Record<workspaceId, Record<nodeId, AccessRule[]>>` (`src/store/permission-store.ts:21-31`). |
| `access_rules` | `access_rules_subject_idx (subject_user_id) WHERE subject_kind = 'user'` | btree, partial | "Which nodes is this person explicitly granted" — needed to compute the `userIds` payload of **RT-05 `permission.changed`** when a node's access mode changes (E-041). |
| `audit_events` | `audit_events_page_idx (workspace_id, at DESC, id DESC)` | btree | E-136 with no filters, and the keyset cursor. Offset paging cannot survive a log that appends at the head between two requests. |
| `audit_events` | `audit_events_module_idx (workspace_id, module, at DESC, id DESC)` | btree | E-136 `?module=` — the module dropdown. |
| `audit_events` | `audit_events_actor_idx (workspace_id, actor_id, at DESC, id DESC)` | btree | E-136 `?actorId=`. |
| `audit_events` | `audit_events_severity_idx (workspace_id, severity, at DESC, id DESC)` | btree | E-136 `?severity=`, and the `bySeverity` facet counts over the whole filtered set. |
| `audit_events` | `audit_events_search_idx GIN (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(target,'') \|\| ' ' \|\| coalesce(detail,'') \|\| ' ' \|\| action \|\| ' ' \|\| actor_name \|\| ' ' \|\| host(ip)))` | GIN, expression | E-136 `?search=`. `matchesSearch` spans **actor name, raw action, humanised action label, target, detail and IP** (`src/lib/audit.ts:67-79`), and the tests assert a partial-IP hit — so `ip` must be inside the index expression or the search silently stops matching addresses. |

### 35.3 The brief's shorthand, mapped to the canonical names

The brief for this section named several indexes in a shorthand that predates canon. Each maps to
exactly one row above; the canonical name is the one to build.

| Named in the brief | Canonical | Why the difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_members(user_id, workspace_id)` | `workspace_members_user_idx (user_id)` **plus** `workspace_members_pair_uniq (workspace_id, user_id) INCLUDE (role)` | Two queries, two column orders. Gate 1 asks `(workspace_id, user_id)`; E-007 asks `(user_id)`. One composite cannot serve both leading columns. |
| `nodes(workspace_id, parent_id)` | `nodes_parent_idx (parent_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` | `parent_id` is already unique to one workspace (the composite FK guarantees it), so `workspace_id` in front adds a column and no selectivity. The workspace-leading index that *is* needed is `nodes_workspace_kind_idx`, for the whole-tree read. |
| `nodes(parent_id, state)` | the four partial indexes `nodes_parent_idx`, `nodes_archived_idx`, `nodes_trash_idx`, `nodes_restricted_idx` | `NodeState` is **derived and never a stored column** (canon §2.4). It cannot be indexed. Each of its four values is a predicate over `deleted_at`, `archived_at` or the ancestor chain, so each gets a partial index instead. |
| `board_rows(board_id, position)` | `board_rows_page_idx (board_id, position, id) WHERE …` | `id` is the cursor's tiebreaker (X-03); without it the keyset seek is not total and the page boundary can skip or repeat a row. |
| `board_rows(board_id, parent_row_id)` | `board_rows_parent_idx (parent_row_id) WHERE parent_row_id IS NOT NULL` | Same reasoning as `nodes.parent_id`: the composite FK already confines a parent to one board, and the partial predicate removes every top-level row from the index. |
| `board_rows(board_id, custom_id)` unique | `board_rows_custom_id_uniq` | Exactly as asked. |
| `board_columns(board_id, position)` | `board_columns_order_idx` + the deferrable unique | As asked, plus §37.9's uniqueness. |
| "cell storage lookups" | `board_rows_cells_gin` + the four projection indexes | §35.5. |
| `notifications(user_id, read_at, created_at)` | `notifications_inbox_idx` + `notifications_unread_idx` | The column is `recipient_id`, not `user_id`. And the single composite is worse than the pair: a `read_at` in the middle of the sort key makes the index useless for the All tab (which does not filter on it) and larger than necessary for the badge (which only ever wants `read_at IS NULL`). A predicate beats a column here. |
| `comments(target…, created_at)` | `comments_thread_idx` | As asked, with the target decomposed into the three columns canon stores. |
| `audit_logs(workspace_id, created_at)` | `audit_events_page_idx (workspace_id, at DESC, id DESC)` | The table is `audit_events` (canon T-36) and the column is `at` (`src/types/audit.ts:23`). |
| `row_relations` both directions | `board_row_relations_source_idx` + `board_row_relations_target_idx` | The table is `board_row_relations` (canon T-13). |
| `favorites(user_id)` | `node_favorites_uniq (user_id, node_id)` | The unique constraint already leads with `user_id`; a second index would be redundant. |
| `attachments(owner…)` | `cell_attachments_uniq`, `comment_attachments_uniq`, `document_asset_refs_uniq`, `file_nodes_pkey` | There is no polymorphic owner. Canon §1.3.4 splits the reference into four typed tables precisely so each "owner" lookup is a real foreign key with a real index. |
| "search vectors" | `nodes_search_idx`, `board_rows_search_idx`, `documents_search_idx`, `comments_search_idx` | §35.6. |

### 35.4 Partial indexes and soft delete

Three tables soft-delete: `nodes`, `comments`, `board_rows` (canon §1.4). Two more carry a
lifecycle column that behaves the same way: `board_rows.archived_at` and `user_sessions.revoked_at`.

**The rule.** Where a query never wants the dead rows, `WHERE <col> IS NULL` goes in the index
predicate, not in the column list. Three reasons, in order of how much they matter here:

1. **Size.** A workspace that has been used for two years has a trash that has been swept and a
   `nodes` table whose live set is most of it — so far, so unimpressive. `board_rows` is the
   opposite: a busy board deletes and re-imports constantly, and the archived set grows without
   bound because archiving is explicitly *not* deletion (`src/lib/archive.ts` — "freeze, do not
   hide"). `board_rows_page_idx` excluding both means the default board read walks an index that is
   the size of the visible board, not the size of its history.
2. **Plan stability.** With the predicate in the index, the planner can prove that the index alone
   answers `deleted_at IS NULL` and never has to visit the heap to re-check it.
3. **Correctness of unique constraints.** `nodes_slug_child_uniq` *must* be partial. A trashed node
   is detached from the tree (`src/lib/trash.ts:6-13`), so it is not a sibling of anything; if it
   kept its slug reserved, restoring it into a parent that has since gained a node with the same
   name would have nowhere legal to land. The predicate is what makes E-037's re-uniquification
   possible at all.

**The two deliberate exceptions.**

- `board_rows_sequence_uniq (board_id, sequence)` and `board_rows_custom_id_uniq (board_id,
  custom_id)` **include** soft-deleted rows. A number that has been issued is spent, deleted or not
  (`src/types/board.ts:242-243` — "monotonic per board, never reused"). Making these partial would
  hand `TASK-005` to a second record after the first was deleted, which is the exact behaviour E-062
  forbids.
- `audit_events` has no soft delete and no partial index for one. The log is append-only by
  construction (`src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20`); the only deletion is the retention sweep,
  which has its own partial index whose predicate is a safety rail (§35.2.4).

**What a partial index costs.** A query that does not repeat the predicate cannot use the index. So
every read path that relies on one of these must carry `deleted_at IS NULL` (and, on the board's
default read, `archived_at IS NULL`) in its `WHERE` clause verbatim — not in an application filter,
not in a view that the planner has to inline. That is a code-review rule, and it is the reason
`board_rows` has *two* page indexes: `includeArchived=true` is a genuinely different predicate and
needs a genuinely different index.

### 35.5 When a JSONB column needs a GIN index — and when it does not

Canon §1.3.2 puts cell values in `board_rows.cells JSONB`, and canon §1.3.3 puts select options in
`board_columns.config JSONB`. Those two decisions have opposite indexing consequences, and the
difference is the rule.

**The test: does any query filter *by* a value inside the document, without already knowing the
row?** If yes, GIN. If the document is only ever read whole, alongside the row that owns it, then
the primary key is the index and GIN is pure write cost.

| JSONB column | GIN? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `board_rows.cells` | **Yes** — `GIN (cells jsonb_path_ops)` | Server-side filtering (`ViewFilter`), bulk selection and any future cross-board query must reach inside it without knowing which row. `jsonb_path_ops` rather than the default `jsonb_ops`: it is roughly a third the size and supports `@>`, which is the only operator these queries need. It does **not** support key-existence (`?`), which nothing here asks for. |
| `board_columns.config` | No | Options are never read without their column (canon §1.3.3), and a board has tens of columns, not millions. `board_columns_order_idx` already fetches the whole ordered set for a board in one seek. |
| `documents.blocks` | No | A page is read whole by node id. Full-text search goes through `documents.search_vector`, and asset references go through `document_asset_refs` (T-31) — *that table exists so that this index does not have to*. |
| `board_templates.columns` / `.views` | No | A template is inert data, deep-copied at instantiation, **never queried per column** (canon T-17). |
| `notifications.context` | No | It is read with its row and never filtered on. The `CHECK (context->>'kind' = reason::text)` keeps it honest without an index. |
| `user_ui_preferences.value` | No | Read by `(user_id, scope)`, written wholesale. |
| `row_activity.changes` / `.raw_changes` | No | Rendered for one row's timeline, never searched (OQ-51). |
| `import_jobs.issues`, `export_jobs`' scope payload | No | Diagnostic payloads read with their job row. |

**The four generated projection columns are not an alternative to the GIN index — they are the hot
path, and the GIN index is the cold one.** `due_date`, `due_at`, `status_option_id` and
`assignee_ids` (canon §1.3.2) each carry a btree or array GIN index of their own because My Work
(E-134) and the dashboard (E-135) run them across every board in the workspace. A GIN scan over
`cells` would answer the same question and would be an order of magnitude slower, because the
projection index is `(board_id, due_date)` — two columns, one range seek — while the GIN index has
to intersect posting lists and then re-check every candidate against the JSONB.

**Maintenance cost, stated plainly.** GIN's `fastupdate` defers index maintenance into a pending
list, which makes writes cheap and occasional autovacuum passes expensive and bursty. On
`board_rows`, where E-066 rewrites `cells` on every keystroke-batch, set `fastupdate = on` (the
default) and `gin_pending_list_limit` to a small value (~1–2 MB) so the flush happens often and
briefly rather than rarely and visibly.

### 35.6 Full-text: four `tsvector` columns, no `search_index` table

Canon §1.2 is explicit that there is **no separate search-index table**. The four vectors:

| Column | Source text | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes.search_vector` | `name`, `excerpt` | E-133's `document`, `file` and `place` groups (`src/services/search-service.ts:137-161`). |
| `board_rows.search_vector` | the textual cells — `text` and `longText` values, plus `custom_id` | E-133's `row` / `api` / `bug` / `qa` groups, and E-069's primary-column substring search. |
| `documents.search_vector` | the flattened text of `blocks` | E-133 over page bodies (OQ-93). |
| `comments.search_tsv` | `body_plain` — mention tokens already flattened to `@Name` (`plainBody`, `src/lib/mentions.ts:133-135`) | E-133's `comment` group. |

Three rules that make these usable:

1. **Configuration is `'simple'`, not `'english'`.** The content is multilingual (the fixture
   workspace is Vietnamese and English), and the frontend's own matcher is a case-folded substring
   test (`src/lib/search-index.ts`). Stemming an identifier like `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` or `TASK-042`
   loses more than it gains.
2. **Generated and stored, never trigger-maintained.** `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (…) STORED` where the
   source is columns of the same row (`comments`, `nodes`); an explicit `UPDATE` in the same
   statement as the content write where the source is JSONB that needs flattening (`board_rows`,
   `documents`). A trigger would put the flattening logic somewhere the service cannot test.
3. **Ranking is not the index's job.** `scoreMatch` gives an exact `custom_id` match the top score,
   a partial row-id match `ROW_ID_SCORE = 90`, and weights body and excerpt hits at
   `BODY_WEIGHT = 0.4` (`src/services/search-service.ts:34-37`). That ranking is computed in the
   service over the candidate set the GIN index returned; `ts_rank` is not used, because it cannot
   express the row-id rule.

`E-035` is deliberately **not** served by any of these. Drive quick-find is substring matching over
node names (`src/lib/tree.ts:278-295`), which is `pg_trgm`'s job, not `tsvector`'s — hence
`nodes_name_trgm_idx`. Canon OQ-94's position is two endpoints, and this is the schema-level reason
they cannot share one index.

### 35.7 What this costs on write

Three tables carry enough indexes to be worth a budget.

| Table | Indexes | Write amplification | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board_rows` | 12 | Every E-066 batch touches the page index (if `position` changed — it does not), the GIN on `cells`, the GIN on `search_vector`, and up to four projection btrees. In practice a cell edit dirties **2–3** indexes, because `due_date` / `status_option_id` / `assignee_ids` only change when the corresponding column was the one edited. | Set the four projections in the **same `UPDATE`** as `cells` (canon §1.3.2) so there is one row version, not five. Never `UPDATE` a projection to its own value — write it conditionally. |
| `nodes` | 11 | A rename dirties `nodes_search_idx` and `nodes_name_trgm_idx`; a move dirties `nodes_parent_idx` and both slug uniques. Both are human-paced. | None needed. The tree is a low-write, high-read structure. |
| `audit_events` | 6 | Every audited action pays six index inserts, inside the caller's transaction (§36.1). At the recommended coverage — every manager/admin-only key plus every denial (OQ-25) — this is a few writes per second per workspace, not per request. | Do **not** audit ordinary `row.update` / `comment.create` traffic at `info`; the activity stream already covers it. Over-auditing is the failure mode here, and it is an index cost before it is a readability cost. |

---

## 36. Transaction Requirements

### 36.0 The four rules that decide what goes inside

| # | Rule | Grounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T-01 | **The audit row is written inside the transaction that performs the action.** There is no write endpoint for the audit log and no chapter may add one; rows are written by the endpoint that performs the action, in its transaction (canon §3.23). If the action rolls back, so does the claim that it happened. | `src/services/audit-service.ts:14-20` |
| T-02 | **Realtime publishes happen after commit, never inside.** A frame published inside a transaction that then rolls back tells every other tab about a write that did not happen, and the client's dedup by `RealtimeEvent.id` cannot undo it. The transaction returns, the response is serialised, and *then* the frames are published. | `src/lib/realtime/client.ts:21`; canon §7 |
| T-03 | **Object-storage writes happen outside the transaction, and the transaction is the thing that decides whether they count.** S3 has no rollback. The order is always: object first, database second. An object with no row is garbage the reaper collects; a row with no object is a broken link the product cannot repair. | canon E-110/E-111; `src/lib/upload-queue.ts` |
| T-04 | **A transaction holds no network call, no signed-URL mint, no MIME sniff, no email.** Everything slow is either before `BEGIN` or after `COMMIT`. The longest thing legitimately inside a transaction in this system is E-085's bulk insert. | — |

**Default isolation is `READ COMMITTED`.** It is named explicitly below only where the flow would be
wrong without something stronger, or where a lock is doing the work that a stronger isolation level
would otherwise have to do. This system prefers an explicit row lock to `SERIALIZABLE`, because a
serialisation failure is a retry the client has to be taught about, and a `FOR UPDATE` is a wait the
client never sees.

### 36.1 Create workspace + creator membership — E-008

`POST /api/v1/workspaces`. **EXISTING REQUIREMENT**: "the creator becomes admin in the same write"
(`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:212-238`).

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `workspaces` | `INSERT … RETURNING id` | `slug` from the name, uniquified. `used_bytes = 0`, `plan` from the request or `'free'`. |
| 2 | `workspace_members` | `INSERT (workspace_id, user_id, role, joined_at)` | `user_id` from the **session** (C-09), `role = 'admin'`. |
| 3 | `environments` | `INSERT ×3` | Development / Staging / Production, seeded (DV-ENV-21, OQ-63). Positions 0, 1, 2. |
| 4 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'workspace'`, `action: 'workspace.manage'`, `severity: 'info'`, `outcome: 'allowed'`. |

**Inside**: all four. A workspace with no admin is unreachable — nobody can invite anybody into it,
and `isLastAdmin` would refuse every subsequent change (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157`). This
is the clearest case in the system where two rows are one fact.

**Outside**: nothing. There is no realtime frame — the creator is the only member, and they get the
`Workspace` in the response.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED`. The only contention is `workspaces_slug_uniq`; on `23505` retry once
with a suffixed slug, then return `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` (409).

**Errors**: `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`.
**Frontend caller**: `useWorkspaceStore` workspace creation; the response replaces optimistic state
wholesale (C-10).

### 36.2 Create board from template + columns + options — E-024 with `kind: "board"`

`POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes`. `instantiateTemplate` deep-copies inert template data
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:12-18`); the board it produces is an ordinary board.

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | — | `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(:workspaceId))` | The per-workspace tree lock. §37.4 explains why every node-creating write takes it. |
| 1 | `nodes` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the parent | Gate 2 (visibility), gate 3 (`node.create` + `board.create`), `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER` if the parent is not a project or folder, `deleted_at IS NULL`. |
| 2 | `board_templates` | `SELECT` | Built-in by `builtin_id`, or the workspace's own by `id`. Read-only. |
| 3 | `nodes` | `INSERT` | `kind = 'board'`, slug uniquified against live siblings, `owner_id` from the session. |
| 4 | `boards` | `INSERT` | `node_id`, `row_id_prefix` from the template, `next_sequence = 0`, `template_id`. |
| 5 | `board_columns` | `INSERT × n` | One per template column, `position` dense `0..n-1`. **`config` — select options included — is copied verbatim from the template's JSONB.** There is no `select_options` table (canon §1.3.3), so "create the options" is part of this insert, not a fifth step. |
| 6 | `boards` | `UPDATE primary_column_id` | Now that the primary column has an id. |
| 7 | `board_views` | `INSERT × m` | One per `TemplateView`, `position` dense. A board with zero views is illegal (`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`). |
| 8 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'board'`, `action: 'board.create'`. |

**Inside**: 1–8. A board with no primary column cannot render a record title; a board with no views
cannot be opened. Half a template is not a board.

**Outside**: RT-11 `node.changed` (`created`). No RT-10 — nobody has the board open yet.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED` under the advisory lock. The lock serialises slug allocation and the
container check against a concurrent move of the parent (§37.4).

**Errors**: `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER`, `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT`, `ROW_ID_PREFIX_INVALID`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`,
`NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`.
**Frontend caller**: the create-node dialog in the drive; `useWorkspaceStore`.

### 36.3 Create row + custom id allocation — E-062

`POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows`. The whole of §37.1 hangs off step 2.

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `boards` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, or fold into step 2 | Existence, `row_id_prefix`, and gate 2/3 (`row.create`) through the board's node. |
| 2 | `boards` | `UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING next_sequence` | **The allocation.** One statement, takes the row lock the transaction needs anyway. `MAX(sequence) + 1` is forbidden — §37.1. |
| 3 | `board_rows` | `SELECT … FOR SHARE` on `parent_row_id` | Only when a parent was given. `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND`; the depth check; `lastDescendantOf` to compute `position` (`src/services/board-service.ts:342-356`). |
| 4 | `board_rows` | `INSERT` | `custom_id = format(prefix, sequence)`, `revision = 1`, `cells` = `emptyCellFor(column.type)` per column (never `null` — `src/lib/cell-values.ts`), the four projections computed from those cells, `created_by` from the session. |
| 5 | `board_row_relations` | `INSERT × k` | Only if the supplied `cells` carry relation values. §36.5. |
| 6 | `row_activity` | `INSERT ×1 or ×2` | `created {displayId}`, plus `added subtask {displayId}` on the **parent** when there is one (`src/services/board-service.ts:329-337`). |

**Inside**: 1–6. The `custom_id` and the row are one fact; an activity entry for a row that does not
exist is a lie.

**Outside**: RT-06 `row.created` `{ boardId, rowId, revision }` — ids only, no cell content
(canon §7.2).

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED`. Step 2's row lock is the serialisation point and is held to commit.

**Errors**: `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`, `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND`, `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP`,
`BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (OQ-36), `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
**Frontend caller**: `useBoardStore.addRow` (`src/store/board-store.ts:357-397`) — the optimistic row
carries `` `${prefix}-…` ``, `sequence: 0`, `revision: 0`, `isPending: true` and is replaced in place
by `replaceRow` when the response lands.

### 36.4 Status update + activity log — E-066

`PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/cells`. **Always `200`. Never `409` for staleness.**

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `boards` + `nodes` | `SELECT` | Gate 2/3 (`row.update`), `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`. |
| 2 | `board_columns` | `SELECT` whole schema | Needed to validate every `CellValue.kind`, to evaluate transition rules and conditional availability, and to know which columns are the projection roles. |
| 3 | `board_rows` | `SELECT … WHERE id = ANY($rowIds) FOR UPDATE` | **Ordered by `id`** so two concurrent batches touching the same rows cannot deadlock. Reads `revision` for the conflict comparison and `archived_at` for `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY`. |
| 4 | — | rule evaluation | Transition rules and option availability, reproduced from `guardCellEdits` (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:43-90`). A refusal aborts the **whole batch** — §37.8. |
| 5 | `board_rows` | `UPDATE … SET cells, revision = revision + 1, updated_at, due_date, due_at, status_option_id, assignee_ids` | **One `UPDATE` per row, however many cells that row's edits touched** — one revision per write, not per cell (`src/services/board-service.ts:514-519`). The four projections are set in the same statement so they can never lag. |
| 6 | `board_row_relations` | `DELETE` by `(source_row_id, source_column_id)` then `INSERT` | Only for edited relation cells. §36.5. |
| 7 | `row_activity` | `INSERT × rows` | One entry per row, not per cell: `editSummary(changes, 'updated {displayId}')` with the rendered `changes` and the internal `raw_changes` (OQ-51). |

**Inside**: 1–7.
**Outside**: RT-07 `row.updated` per row, ids and `revision` only.
**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED` with `FOR UPDATE` in a deterministic id order. The conflict test
(`base < current.revision`) reads the value it just locked, so it cannot see a torn revision.

**The `ConflictNotice` is not an error and does not affect the transaction.** It is computed during
step 3–5 and returned in the `200` body. `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` exists in the registry and is
explicitly never used here (canon §4.3).

**Errors**: `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY`, `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID`, `DATE_VALUE_INVALID`,
`TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED`, `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE`, `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND`.
**Frontend caller**: `useBoardStore.editCells` (`src/store/board-store.ts:315-354`) — optimistic
apply, `revertCellEdits` on failure, `reconcileRows` on success.

### 36.5 The relation projection, stated once

`board_row_relations` (T-13) is a **projection of relation cells**, written in the same transaction
as the cell (canon T-13). Wherever `cells` changes and a relation column is among the changed keys:

```sql
-- documentation only
DELETE FROM board_row_relations
 WHERE source_row_id = :row AND source_column_id = :column;
INSERT INTO board_row_relations (source_row_id, source_column_id, target_row_id,
                                 target_board_id, position)
SELECT :row, :column, t.id, t.board_id, ord
  FROM unnest(:targetRowIds) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(id, ord)
  JOIN board_rows t ON t.id = u.id;
```

Three consequences a writer must honour: a target row that no longer exists simply produces no edge,
while **the dangling id stays in the cell** so `[Deleted Item]` keeps rendering (canon OQ-44); the
delete-then-insert is why `board_row_relations_source_idx` leads with `(source_row_id,
source_column_id)`; and the two directions can never disagree, because there is only one write
(`src/components/board/drawer/backlinks-panel.tsx:14-19`).

### 36.6 Comment + mentions + notifications — E-120

`POST /api/v1/comments`. Canon: "the fan-out is one transaction".

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `nodes` (+ `boards`, `board_rows`) | `SELECT` | Gate 2 on the **target**, gate 3 (`comment.create`), and resolution of `target_label`. |
| 2 | `comments` | `SELECT` the parent | Only when `parentId` is given. `rootIdFor`: unknown parent → `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND`; a parent that is itself a reply **silently re-parents to that reply's root** and is not an error (`src/services/comment-service.ts:149-156`). |
| 3 | `comments` | `INSERT` | `mentioned_user_ids` parsed **server-side** from `@[Name](usr_id)` (`src/lib/mentions.ts:13`); a client-supplied list is ignored (canon E-120). `body_plain` written in the same statement. |
| 4 | `comment_attachments` | `INSERT × k` | By `asset_id` only. `url` is never accepted on write (OQ-75). |
| 5 | `watches` | `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` | **The author auto-watches the target** (`watchService.autoWatch`, `src/services/comment-service.ts:140`). |
| 6 | `watches` | `SELECT` watchers of the target, excluding the author | `watchService.watchersOf` (`src/services/watch-service.ts:97-103`). |
| 7 | `notifications` | `INSERT × mentioned` | `reason: 'mention'`, title `` `${author.name} mentioned you` ``, body = 140-char preview of `body_plain`. **Fan-out on write: one row per recipient** (canon T-35). The label is **frozen** here, not resolved on read (OQ-79). |
| 8 | `notifications` | `INSERT × (watchers − mentioned)` | `reason: 'comment'`. A person who was mentioned hears about it once, as a mention (`src/services/comment-service.ts:237-240`). |
| 9 | `row_activity` | `INSERT` | Only when the target is a row: `commented on {label}`, kind `commented` (`boardService.noteActivity`). |
| 10 | `audit_events` | — | **Not written.** Ordinary comment traffic is `info` noise the activity stream already covers (OQ-25 position). |

**Inside**: 1–9. A mention that produced no notification is the bug the fan-out exists to prevent.

**Outside**: RT-01 `comment.created` `{ targetKey, comment }` to everyone with that `targetKey` open,
and RT-03 `notification.created` **delivered only to its `recipientId`** — the frontend drops frames
for anyone else (`src/store/notification-store.ts:112`), and the server must not send them at all.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED`. The one read-then-write is the watcher list; a watcher who
subscribes a millisecond later misses this one comment, which is correct — `WatchEntry.since` is a
timestamp, and they were not watching when it was posted.

**Errors**: `COMMENT_EMPTY`, `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_NOT_FOUND`.
**Frontend caller**: `commentService.add` behind the comment composer; the optimistic comment carries
`isPending: true` and is replaced by `upsertComment` (`src/lib/comments.ts:23-39`).

### 36.7 Import — E-085

`POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/import`. Canon: "**one transaction**: column creation, column removal
and row inserts all land or none do".

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `import_jobs` | `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (board_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id` | **RECOMMENDATION** (§37.7, OQ-41). Zero rows returned means this is a replay: read the stored `outcome` and return it with `200`, doing nothing else. |
| 1 | `boards` | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` | The board's schema lock, and the counter's lock. Gate 2/3 (`board.import`). |
| 2 | `board_columns` | `INSERT × created` | Every `MappingTarget` of kind `create`. Names de-duplicated by `uniqueColumnName` (`src/lib/board-schema.ts:170-180`). Positions appended densely. |
| 3 | `board_columns` | `DELETE × unmapped` | Only the columns the plan named. **Never the primary column** (`COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED`). Each delete also prunes `board_views` references (the three `SET NULL` FKs do this) and orphan keys in `board_rows.cells`. |
| 4 | `boards` | `UPDATE next_sequence = next_sequence + :n RETURNING next_sequence` | One statement for the whole file, so the import lands as `TASK-042 … TASK-141` **with no gaps** (`src/services/board-service.ts:1196-1204`). |
| 5 | `board_rows` | `INSERT × n` | Bulk insert with the allocated sequence block. `cells` = `emptyCells(columns)` merged with the mapped values; the four projections computed per row. |
| 6 | `board_row_relations` | `INSERT` | If any created column is a relation. |
| 7 | `row_activity` | `INSERT × n` | `imported {displayId}` (`src/services/board-service.ts:1212`). |
| 8 | `import_jobs` | `UPDATE` | Counts, `issues`, `invalid_policy`, `completed_at`, and the serialised `ImportOutcome`. |
| 9 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'board'`, `action: 'board.import'`, `severity: 'info'`, detail in the shape the seed uses: *"48 records imported from sprint-backlog.xlsx, 3 rows left out."* (`src/services/audit-service.ts:86-95`). |

**Order matters**: create before delete before insert. Creating first means a mapped-to-a-new-column
value has a column to land in; deleting before inserting means the removed columns' keys are never
written into `cells` at all, so step 3 does not have to be repeated over the new rows.

**Inside**: 0–9.

**Outside**: RT-10 `board.schema.changed` (the schema moved, so every open client refetches it
wholesale — C-11), then RT-06 `row.created` as **one batched frame carrying `rowIds`**, not `n`
frames (canon §7.2). Parsing the `.xlsx`/`.csv` and computing the `ImportPlan` (E-084) happen before
`BEGIN` and are not persisted.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED` under the board's `FOR UPDATE`. That lock is what makes E-085 and a
concurrent E-052/E-054/E-056 mutually exclusive (§37.9).

**Errors**: `IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED`, `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5000`,
`src/config/app.ts:48`), `IMPORT_FILE_UNPARSEABLE`, `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED`,
`BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
**Frontend caller**: `useBoardStore.importRows` (`src/store/board-store.ts:659-668`).

### 36.8 Secret reveal + audit — E-103

`POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/{secretId}/reveal`. Canon: "**Writes two audit rows before
returning, allowed or denied alike.**"

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Redis | throttle check | Outside the transaction. Over the limit → `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` (429), **and the attempt is still audited** (steps 4–5 run in their own transaction). |
| 2 | `secret_documents` + `nodes` | `SELECT` | Gate 2, gate 3 (`secret.reveal` — Admin only, OQ-23). |
| 3 | `secrets` | `SELECT id, key, environment_id, value_encrypted` | The **only** query in the system that selects `value_encrypted`. Never `SELECT *` on this table. |
| 4 | `secret_access_events` | `INSERT` | `action` (`reveal` \| `copy`), `secret_id`, `key`, `actor_id`, `at`, `ip` from the socket. This is the `SecretAuditEntry` the panel renders. |
| 5 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'secret'`, `action: 'secret.reveal'` (a **copy files under reveal** — `src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`), `severity: 'warn'` allowed / `'error'` denied, `outcome`, `target = key`, `detail` = *"Revealed once and cleared after 30 seconds."* or *"Refused: the role does not hold the permission for this action."* **`detail` never contains the value.** |

**Inside**: 2–5, and 4–5 on the denied path too. **The audit rows commit before the plaintext is
returned** — a reveal whose audit row was lost is an unlogged disclosure, which is the one failure
this endpoint exists to prevent.

**Outside**: decryption. The envelope unwrap (KMS `Decrypt` of the workspace DEK, then AES-256-GCM of
the ciphertext) is a network call and must not be inside `BEGIN` (T-04). Order: commit the audit
rows, then decrypt, then respond. If decryption fails after the audit committed, the log records an
attempt that returned an error — which is the honest record.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED`. No lock; a reveal takes nothing.

**Errors**: `SECRET_NOT_FOUND`, `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED`, `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED`.
**Frontend caller**: the secret panel's reveal button; `devtoolsService.revealSecret`.
**No realtime frame.** A frame announcing a reveal would put the key name on every socket in the
workspace.

### 36.9 Delete board (node) + trash state + audit — E-032

`DELETE /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}`. Soft delete; **detaches the whole subtree**.

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | — | `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(:workspaceId))` | It re-shapes the tree. |
| 1 | `nodes` | `SELECT` node + ancestor chain `FOR UPDATE` | Gate 2, gate 3 (`node.delete` or owner escalation). **`deleted_at IS NULL`.** An archived *ancestor* still blocks: `can()` refuses writes when `isFrozen`, and `node.delete` is a write → `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:83`). |
| 2 | `nodes` | recursive CTE → `UPDATE … SET deleted_at = now(), deleted_by = :me` over the whole subtree | One statement. Descendants get `deleted_at`; **only the root gets a trash entry**, which is what makes the trash listing show one item rather than a subtree's worth. |
| 3 | `trash_entries` | `INSERT` | `node_id`, `original_parent_id`, `original_ancestor_ids UUID[]`, `original_path TEXT` — **the human path resolved now, while the ancestors still exist** (`src/lib/trash.ts:49-51`) — and `purge_at = now() + 30 days`. |
| 4 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'node'`, `action: 'node.delete'`, `severity: 'warn'`. |

**Inside**: 0–4. The trash entry's frozen path is only correct if it is computed in the same
transaction that detaches the subtree; one statement later, an ancestor may itself be gone.

**Outside**: RT-11 `node.changed` (`trashed`). **No RT-05** — deleting does not change anybody's
access rules; the node simply stops being in the tree, and every client's derived tree repaints
(`use-access-sync.ts:24-31`).

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED` under the advisory lock.

**Nothing is removed from object storage, and no `used_bytes` is reclaimed.** A trashed node is
restorable for 30 days. Byte reclamation happens on **purge** (E-038 / E-039 / the sweep), which is a
different transaction: it computes reclaimed bytes and writes its audit row **before** issuing
`DELETE FROM nodes`, then deletes the objects after commit.

**Errors**: `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
**Frontend caller**: `useWorkspaceStore` delete action; the trash surface reads `TrashEntry[]`.

### 36.10 Role change + audit + `permission.changed` — E-014

`PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}`.

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `workspace_members` | `SELECT user_id FROM workspace_members WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND role = 'admin' FOR UPDATE` | **Locks the admin *set*, not one row.** Without it, two concurrent demotions of the last two admins each see one other admin and both succeed. §37.6. |
| 2 | — | last-admin guard | `isLastAdmin` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157`) → `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN` (409). |
| 3 | `workspace_members` | `UPDATE role` | |
| 4 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'workspace'`, `action: 'workspace.member.manage'`, `severity: 'warn'`, `target` = the member's name, `detail` in the seed's shape: *"Duc Pham set to Member on this folder, overriding Manager."* |
| 5 | Redis | `INCR access-epoch:{workspaceId}` | §37.6. Inside the transaction's logical unit but not rollback-safe — bump it **after commit**, and accept that a rolled-back role change may over-invalidate a cache, which is harmless. |

**Inside**: 1–4.
**Outside**: the epoch bump, then **RT-05 `permission.changed` `{ workspaceId, nodeId: null, userIds: [thatUser] }`**. `nodeId` is `null` because the change is workspace membership rather than one
node (canon RT-05). The frame **carries no resource content on purpose** — "a frame announcing a
revocation must not be the thing that leaks what was revoked" (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`).
Receivers re-resolve their own access and drop what they may no longer hold.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED`, and the `FOR UPDATE` over the matched set is not optional.

**Errors**: `WORKSPACE_LAST_ADMIN`, `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
**Frontend caller**: the members table in workspace settings; `useAccessSync` is what acts on RT-05
in every other tab (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:38-60`).

### 36.11 Move node + descendant access recomputation — E-026

`POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/move`. **There is no materialised access table, so there is nothing to
recompute in the database.** Effective access is resolved by walking the ancestor chain on read
(`chainFor`, `src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:41-43`), so relocating a node *is* the
recomputation. What the transaction owes is the slug, the audit row and the impact set.

| Order | Table | Statement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | — | `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(:workspaceId))` | **Mandatory.** A cycle is a property of a set of rows and cannot be expressed as a constraint; two concurrent moves that each pass their own check can still produce one (§37.4). |
| 1 | `nodes` | `SELECT` node `FOR UPDATE` + ancestor chain | Gate 2/3 (`node.move`), `deleted_at IS NULL`, frozen check. |
| 2 | `nodes` | `SELECT` target `FOR UPDATE` | `NODE_MOVE_INVALID_TARGET` when missing or not a container; `NODE_MOVE_SAME_PARENT`; `NODE_MOVE_INTO_SELF`. |
| 3 | `nodes` | recursive CTE downward from the node | `NODE_MOVE_INTO_DESCENDANT` when the target is inside the subtree (`isDescendantOf`, `src/lib/tree.ts:186-188`). |
| 4 | — | `moveVisibilityImpact` | Computed from `access_rules` + `workspace_members`, **before** the update: who can see it now and would not afterwards, and vice versa (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:313-333`). Only meaningful when `access_mode = 'inherit'`; a node with a mode of its own carries it with it. |
| 5 | `nodes` | `UPDATE parent_id, slug, updated_at, updated_by` | **The slug is re-uniquified against the new siblings** and never re-minted from the name (OQ-09/OQ-10 position). |
| 6 | `audit_events` | `INSERT` | `module: 'node'`, `action: 'node.move'`, `severity: 'warn'` when `losing` is non-empty, `'info'` otherwise. |

**Inside**: 0–6. Step 4 must be inside, because it reads the pre-move chain; computing it after
commit would answer for the world the move created.

**Outside**: RT-11 `node.changed` (`moved`), then **RT-05 `permission.changed` `{ workspaceId, nodeId, userIds: [...losing, ...gaining] }`**. RT-05 on a move is not optional — canon lists a move
among the events that fire it, because *"moving something is a permission change wearing the costume
of a drag"* (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:294-299`). Also outside: `INCR access-epoch:{workspaceId}`.

**Isolation**: `READ COMMITTED` under the advisory lock. The lock is doing the work `SERIALIZABLE`
would otherwise do, without teaching the client to retry.

**Errors**: the four `NODE_MOVE_*` reasons, `NODE_SLUG_CONFLICT`, `NODE_NOT_CONTAINER`,
`PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR`.
**Frontend caller**: the drive's drag-and-drop and the Move dialog; `moveNode` (`src/lib/tree.ts:170-197`) is the client-side pre-check whose four rejections the API reproduces.

### 36.12 Isolation levels, summarised

| Level | Where | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `READ COMMITTED` (default) | Every write in this specification. | Postgres's default; combined with explicit `FOR UPDATE` it is sufficient for every flow above, and it never produces a serialisation failure the client has to be taught to retry. |
| `READ COMMITTED` + `FOR UPDATE` on one row | E-062/E-064/E-077/E-085 (`boards.next_sequence`), E-111 (`workspaces.used_bytes`), E-003 (`user_sessions` by token hash), E-102 (`secret_documents.version`), E-037 (`trash_entries`), E-111 (`uploads`). | A counter or a state machine that must advance exactly once. |
| `READ COMMITTED` + `FOR UPDATE` on a **matched set** | E-014/E-015/E-016 (the admin set). | The invariant is over a set, not a row. §37.6. |
| `READ COMMITTED` + `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(workspace_id))` | E-024, E-026, E-032, E-037. | Tree-shape invariants — cycles and sibling-slug uniqueness — that no constraint can express. Moves are rare and human-paced; the lock costs nothing measurable. |
| `READ COMMITTED` + `FOR UPDATE` on `boards` | Every board **schema** write: E-052, E-054, E-055, E-056, E-057, E-058, E-059, E-060, E-085, and view writes E-079…E-082. | One serialisation point per board for everything that changes the shape of the board, so a column delete and a column reorder cannot interleave. **RECOMMENDATION**, §37.9. |
| `REPEATABLE READ`, read-only | E-047 `BoardSnapshot`, E-135 `DashboardSummary`, E-136 `AuditPage`, E-129 `NotificationPage`, E-134 `MyWorkWidget[]`. | These responses carry a page **and** an aggregate computed over more than the page — `AuditPage.total` and `bySeverity` are facets over the whole filtered set, `NotificationPage.unreadCount` is server-computed, `MyWorkWidget` carries `items` (capped) **and** `total` (uncapped), and `BoardSnapshot` ships `board`, `rows` and `people` together. Under `READ COMMITTED` each statement gets a fresh snapshot, so "12 of 40" can be computed against two different worlds. One snapshot makes the page and its facets agree. |
| `SERIALIZABLE` | **Nowhere.** | Every invariant in this system is expressible as a row lock, a set lock, an advisory lock or a unique constraint. `SERIALIZABLE` would add retry handling to every write path to buy nothing the locks above do not already give. |

### 36.13 Realtime publishing is at-least-once, and that is deliberate

Frames are published **after commit**, from the request thread, to Redis pub/sub. If the process dies
between `COMMIT` and `PUBLISH`, the frame is lost and the other tabs are stale until their next read.

**RECOMMENDATION.** Accept it. Delivery is already at-least-once with client-side dedup by
`RealtimeEvent.id` (`src/lib/realtime/client.ts:21`, `SEEN_LIMIT = 512`), unknown frame types are
ignored (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`), and every recommended frame carries **ids only**, so the client
refetches anyway. A transactional outbox table would make delivery exactly-once-ish at the cost of a
40th table, a poller, and an ordering guarantee the client does not need.

**The one frame this reasoning does not cover is RT-05 `permission.changed`**, because a lost RT-05
leaves a revoked user holding a loaded board until they reload
(`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts`). Mitigate it without an outbox: the Redis access epoch (§37.6) is
bumped on the same path, and every subsequent request re-resolves access against the new epoch — so a
lost frame delays the drop until the tab's next request rather than until its next reload. See
**OQ-101** (reconnect and replay) for the general case.

---

## 37. Concurrency / Race Conditions

Nine races, each with the failure mode it produces, the mitigation, and the contract the frontend
sees. A summary table closes the section.

### 37.1 Custom row id generation under concurrent creates

**EXISTING REQUIREMENT.** `docs/BOARD.md:266-269` names it a blocking backend requirement: *"Two
simultaneous creates must never produce `TASK-005` twice."* The frontend never invents an id — the
optimistic row carries `` `${prefix}-…` `` with `sequence: 0` and `isPending: true`
(`src/store/board-store.ts:364-375`) — and the type comment is unambiguous: *"assigned by the
BACKEND, never derived on the client"* (`src/types/board.ts:240`).

**Failure mode.** Two `POST /boards/{boardId}/rows` arrive at two application instances at the same
millisecond. Both compute the next number from the current row set. Both get `5`. One of three things
then happens, all bad: two records both called `TASK-005` (no unique constraint), or a `23505` that
surfaces to the user as `unknown` / 500 on an ordinary create (with the constraint), or — worse and
silent — a retry loop that re-reads `MAX` and collides again under sustained load.

**The mechanism, precisely.** One `bigint` counter column, `boards.next_sequence`, allocated with a
single statement inside the row-insert transaction:

```sql
-- documentation only
UPDATE boards
   SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1
 WHERE id = $1
```
