| **5** | `files` | 1, 2, 3 | `/files`, `FilesView` → `FileManager` → `FileTable` + `FileMetadataTable`, `FileDropzone`, `UploadDialog`, `UploadDropTarget`, `UploadQueuePanel` + `UploadTaskRow`, `FilePreviewDialog` and all six `preview/*` surfaces, `DrivePreviewDialog`. `AttachmentCell`, `AttachmentPanel`, `AttachmentGallery`, `AttachmentViewer`. `ImageBlock`, `AttachmentBlock`, `LinkBlock`. `StorageMeter` becomes truthful. | **P1** |
| **6** | `collab`, `realtime` (RT-01 … RT-04), `files` (T-30) | 1, 2, 3, 5 | `CommentPanel`, `CommentComposer`, `MentionTextarea`, `CommentItem`, `CommentBody`, `CommentAttachments`, the drawer's Comments tab (`DrawerTabs`), `WatchButton`, `NotificationBell`, `/notifications` with `NotificationFeed` + `NotificationTabs` + `NotificationItem`. The `mentioned` My Work widget stops being empty. | **P1** |
| **7** | `devtools`, `system` (version history — config/secret half) | 0 (T-26), 1 | `ConfigDocumentPage`, `CodeEditor`, `LanguagePicker`, `EnvironmentPicker`, `SecretDocumentPage`, `SecretList`, `SecretEditorPanel`, `SecretAuditPanel`, `SecretEnvPaste`, `VersionHistoryDialog` for config documents and secret rotations. | **P1** |
| **8** | `system` (trash console, bulk, import, export) | 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 | `/trash` with `TrashPage`, `BulkActionBar`, `BulkMoveDialog`, `ImportDialog` + `ImportUploadStep` / `ImportMappingStep` / `ImportValidationStep` / `ImportResultStep`, `ExportDialog`. | **P1** |
| **9** | `search`, `relations`, `templates` (user-authored) | 1, 2, 6 | `GlobalSearchDialog` and the header's `GlobalSearch` (⌘K). `RelationCell` chips resolve, `BacklinksPanel` fills, `GanttDependencies` draws its connectors. "Save board as template". | `search` **P1**, `relations` **P2**, user templates **P2** |

Phases 5, 6 and 7 have no ordering constraint between them beyond `collab`'s dependency on `files`
for `comment_attachments`. Two teams can run 5 → 6 and 7 in parallel from the end of Phase 3.
Phases 8 and 9 depend on almost everything and are genuinely last.

---

### Phase 0 — session and tenancy

**Tables:** T-01 `users`, T-02 `user_sessions`, T-03 `workspaces`, T-04 `workspace_members`,
T-05 `workspace_invitations`, T-26 `environments`, T-37 `user_ui_preferences`.

**Endpoints:** E-001 – E-006 (`identity`), E-007 – E-019 (`workspace`), E-139 `GET /config`,
E-140 `GET /health`.

**What the frontend can start using at the end of it.** The shell boots. `WorkspaceGuard` settles
membership before anything inside a workspace mounts (`src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx:49-52`),
so this is the first phase that produces a screen at all. The workspace switcher lists only
workspaces the caller is in (`visibleWorkspaces`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:45-50`); the members
tab reads E-012 and writes E-013 – E-016 with the last-admin guard live
(`isLastAdmin`, `src/lib/workspace-access.ts:84-157`); E-139 replaces `src/config/app.ts`'s
client-side constants so the browser's pre-checks and the server's limits cannot disagree
(`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS`, `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`, `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT`,
`MY_WORK_WIDGET_LIMIT`, `AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE`, `VERSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`).

**Still degraded.** `StorageMeter` renders `0 B of 15 GB` — `workspaces.used_bytes` is a real column
maintained transactionally (canon §1.4) but nothing increments it until Phase 5. Every navigation
below `/` is a dead end.

**Why T-26 is here and not in Phase 7.** `POST /workspaces` seeds Development / Staging / Production
inside its transaction (part 17 §36.1 step 3). Creating the table in Phase 7 would mean backfilling
every workspace made before it, which is a migration bought for nothing — the table has three rows
per workspace and one foreign key.

---

### Phase 1 — the tree and the gate

**Tables:** T-06 `nodes`, T-07 `node_favorites`, T-08 `access_rules`, T-36 `audit_events`,
T-09 `trash_entries`.

**Endpoints:** E-020 – E-035 (`drive`), E-040 – E-046 (`governance`), E-136 and E-137 (audit),
E-138 (the socket, carrying **RT-05 only**), E-135 as a **stub** returning a zeroed
`DashboardSummary` with `isNewWorkspace: true`.

**Why `trash_entries` is created here but its console is not.** E-032 `DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}`
returns a `TrashEntry` and writes the row — the frozen `original_path`, resolved while the ancestors
still exist, is only correct if it is written in the same transaction that detaches the subtree
(part 17 §36.9; `src/lib/trash.ts:49-51`). So the table must exist the moment delete does. The
console that reads it back (E-036 – E-039) is Phase 8. Between the two, nothing is lost — it is
merely unrecoverable through the UI.

**Why a one-frame realtime hub ships here.** RT-05 `permission.changed` is the one frame that is a
correctness requirement rather than a convergence convenience: without it a revoked user keeps a
loaded board on screen until they reload (canon §7.1; `src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:74-83`). It
needs only `workspace_members` and `access_rules`, both delivered in this phase, and it carries ids
and nothing else — "a frame announcing a revocation must not be the thing that leaks what was
revoked" (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`). Shipping the hub here also means Phases 2 – 9 add frames
without touching the transport.

**Why E-135 ships as a stub.** `src/app/(workspace)/page.tsx` redirects `/` to `/dashboard`. Until
Phase 4 the real aggregate cannot be computed, and without *some* answer the first screen a user
sees is an error panel. A zeroed `DashboardSummary` with `isNewWorkspace: true` renders
`OnboardingPanel`, which is the correct screen for a workspace with no boards
(`src/components/dashboard/onboarding-panel.tsx`), and it is replaced in Phase 4 with no client
change.

**What the frontend can start using.** The whole drive: E-020's pruned tree feeds `AppSidebar`,
`TreePanel`, `BreadcrumbNav`, the drive grid and list, favourites and archive. Access management is
complete — mode (E-041), rules (E-042/E-043), the resolved list (E-040) and the admin recovery
console (E-046). The audit log renders with real facets over the whole filtered set (E-136).

**Still degraded.** Every leaf node in the tree — board, page, config, secret, file — resolves to a
node the surface cannot open. The drive lists them; opening one is Phases 2, 3, 5 and 7.

---

### Phase 2 — the board engine

**Tables:** T-17 `board_templates`, T-10 `boards`, T-11 `board_columns`, T-12 `board_rows`,
T-14 `row_activity`, T-15 `board_views`, T-16 `board_view_preferences`.

**Endpoints:** E-047 – E-050 (board), E-051 – E-060 (columns), E-061 – E-070 and E-073 (rows),
E-078 – E-083 (views), E-087 and E-088 (template reads). Frames RT-06 – RT-10.

**Not in this phase, deliberately:** E-071 and E-072 (`relations`, Phase 9), E-074 – E-077 (bulk,
Phase 8), E-084 – E-086 (import/export, Phase 8), E-089/E-090 (user-authored templates, Phase 9).

**What the frontend can start using.** Everything a board is. `BoardSnapshot` (E-047) is the one
call `use-board.ts` makes on open; every view type renders off the same loaded set because filtering,
sorting and grouping are client-side over `rowsById` (canon OQ-36 position). The record drawer, the
activity timeline, subtasks, the whole column-schema surface including transition rules and
conditional availability, and saved views with the "a board needs at least one view" guard
(`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`, E-081).

**Still degraded, and how honestly.** Two cell types render but cannot complete:

- **Attachment cells** show the metadata stored in the cell value with `url: null`. The frontend
  already treats a null URL as "bytes this session cannot reach" (`isReachable`,
  `src/lib/attachments.ts:79-82`), so the degradation is designed, not accidental. Phase 5 fixes it.
- **Relation cells** render the stored row id rather than a resolved chip, and a dangling id renders
  `[Deleted Item]` with an unlink action — which is exactly the behaviour canon fixes in place
  (OQ-44/OQ-45 position: "dangling ids stay in the cell so `[Deleted Item]` keeps rendering").
  Phase 9 fixes it.

**Why `templates` is inside this phase and not before it.** Board creation goes through E-024 with
`kind: "board"`, which reads `board_templates` and deep-copies its columns and views into the new
board (part 17 §36.2 step 2; `src/lib/board-templates.ts:12-18`). The four built-ins are seed rows;
there is no `tasks`, `bugs`, `qa_cases` or `api_endpoints` table and no chapter may add one
(canon §1.3.5).

---

### Phase 3 — pages

**Tables:** T-18 `documents`, T-19 `document_versions`.

**Endpoints:** E-091 – E-094 (`documents`), and E-095 – E-098 (version history) **restricted to
nodes of kind `document` with `documentKind: "page"`**. The same four endpoints gain their config
and secret branches in Phase 7 — one endpoint family, the node's kind selects the store
(canon §3.14).

**What the frontend can start using.** `DocumentPage` and the whole block editor; autosave through
`use-autosave.ts` against E-092 with `expectedVersion`; the lock, allowed for `document.lock` **or
the document's owner**, with `lockedBy` taken from the session and never the body (E-094, OQ-60);
pinning (E-093), which also lights up `PinnedPages` in the sidebar; and version history — list,
detail, diff and restore — for pages.

**Still degraded.** `ImageBlock`, `AttachmentBlock` and `LinkBlock` render their placeholder states
until Phase 5 (E-117 signed URLs, E-118 link unfurl). Document text is not searchable until Phase 9.

**Why this phase is P0 rather than P1.** Document nodes are in the seeded tree from the first frame,
and boards, pages, config and secret documents all render *inside* `/drive/<path>`
(`src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx:11-14`). Shipping Phase 1 without Phase 3 means the sidebar
shows pages that 404 when clicked.

---

### Phase 4 — the landing screen

**Tables:** none. Both endpoints are projections computed on read; canon §1.2 lists
`my_work_items` and `dashboard_widgets` among the tables that deliberately do not exist.

**Endpoints:** E-135 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/dashboard` (replacing the Phase 1 stub),
E-134 `GET /me/work`.

**What the frontend can start using.** `/dashboard` becomes real: Task, QA and Deadline widgets with
their ten buckets, `isNewWorkspace` and `boardCount` as cross-widget facts, and click-through to the
source board. `/my-work` renders five widgets, each with capped `items` **and** an uncapped `total`
so "12 of 40" stays honest (`src/types/collab.ts:144`).

**Still degraded.** The `mentioned` widget returns `{ items: [], total: 0 }` until Phase 6 — it is
the one bucket computed from comments (`src/services/my-work-service.ts` mentions branch), and the
widget's own empty state already reads correctly. The dashboard's QA widget classifies a board by
**what it became** — its status column offering a `passed` or `failed` option — and explicitly not
by template id (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:86-96`), so it works from Phase 2 data alone.

**Why a P1 module lands fourth.** O-3. `/` redirects to `/dashboard`, and every subsequent phase is
easier to demonstrate when the front door opens.

---

### Phase 5 — bytes

**Tables:** T-27 `file_assets`, T-32 `uploads`, T-28 `file_nodes`, T-29 `cell_attachments`,
T-31 `document_asset_refs`. **Not** T-30 `comment_attachments` — its FK target does not exist yet.

**Endpoints:** E-110 – E-118.

**What the frontend can start using.** `/files` and the whole file manager; the three-step presigned
upload behind the same `fileService.upload` signature the store already calls, so no store, reducer
or component changes (part 10 §21.2); previews for image, PDF, text and sheet; text and spreadsheet
save (E-115); downloads and signed asset URLs (E-116, E-117); board attachment cells and the drawer
attachment panel; document image and attachment blocks; link unfurl (E-118). `StorageMeter` becomes
truthful because `workspaces.used_bytes` is now incremented inside E-111's transaction.

**The rule this phase must not break.** Only `assetId` is persisted in cells, blocks and comments;
`url` and `thumbnailUrl` are minted per response as short-lived signed URLs and are never accepted on
write (canon §1.3.4, OQ-75; `src/types/board.ts:206-207`). And the reference row —
`cell_attachments`, `document_asset_refs` — is written by the endpoint that stores the reference
(E-066, E-092) in *its* transaction, not by E-111, so the reference and the cell value it projects
cannot drift (part 10 §21.2).

---

### Phase 6 — collaboration

**Tables:** T-33 `comments`, T-34 `watches`, T-35 `notifications`, T-30 `comment_attachments`.

**Endpoints:** E-119 – E-125 (comments), E-126 – E-128 (watches), E-129 – E-132 (notifications).
Frames RT-01 – RT-04.

**What the frontend can start using.** The comment panel on every target kind — `EntityKind` is
`NodeKind` plus `row` (`src/types/collab.ts:7`), so one thread model serves a record and a page; the
mention composer; watch/unwatch; the notification bell with a **server-computed** unread count
(E-132, OQ-91) rather than "unread among the ones we loaded"; and `/notifications` with its four
tabs, which are a client-side projection of `reason` and never a wire value (canon §2.9, OQ-90).

**The transaction this phase exists to get right.** E-120 is one transaction: the comment, the
author's auto-watch, the mention notifications, the watcher notifications, the row activity entry
and the attachment references (part 17 §36.6). `mentionedUserIds` is parsed **server-side** from
`@[Name](usr_id)` and a client-supplied list is ignored (canon E-120; `src/lib/mentions.ts`).

**What this phase also finishes.** The `mentioned` My Work widget (Phase 4) and
`comment_attachments`, the last of the five file reference tables.

---

### Phase 7 — dev tools

**Tables:** T-20 `config_documents`, T-21 `config_versions`, T-22 `secret_documents`,
T-23 `secrets`, T-24 `secret_rotations`, T-25 `secret_access_events`. (T-26 `environments` already
exists from Phase 0.)

**Endpoints:** E-099 – E-105, E-106 – E-109, and the config and secret branches of E-095 – E-098.

**What the frontend can start using.** The config document page with its fifteen `ConfigFormat`
values and the autosave fold — `isAutosave: true` folds into the head version when that version is
also an autosave by the same author (E-100, OQ-59 position). The secret document page: masks only on
read, whole-list replace on write with an omitted `value` meaning "leave the stored value untouched"
(E-102), audited reveal and copy (E-103, E-104), the per-document access trail (E-105), and the
environment picker (E-106).

**Ship it complete or not at all.** Part 1 §2.3 states this and it is the reason the module is one
phase rather than two: a half-built secret store with an unaudited reveal is worse than no secret
store. Concretely, E-103 must write `secret_access_events` **and** `audit_events` and commit them
*before* the plaintext is returned, on the allowed and the denied path alike (part 17 §36.8;
`src/services/devtools-service.ts:342-349` — "a refusal nobody can see is not a control").

---

### Phase 8 — bulk, trash, import and export

**Tables:** T-38 `import_jobs`, T-39 `export_jobs`.

**Endpoints:** E-036 – E-039 (trash console), E-074 – E-077 (bulk), E-084 – E-086 (import/export).

**What the frontend can start using.** `/trash` with restore that walks `original_ancestor_ids` for
the deepest surviving container and reports `isRelocated` (E-037); the bulk action bar over a grid
selection, including the cross-board move that runs one transaction over **both** boards and names
unmatched columns in `droppedColumns` (E-077); the import wizard end to end; and the export dialog
for all three scopes and three formats.

**Why it is this late.** E-077 needs two boards (Phase 2). Export scope `view` needs saved views
(Phase 2) and reads the active **search term**, not only filters and sort (canon §2.7). Version
history's config and secret branches need Phase 7. And the trash console's restore has to be able to
put a page, a board, a file and a secret document back, which means every content module must exist
first or restore will succeed into a node nothing can open.

---

### Phase 9 — finding and linking

**Tables:** T-13 `board_row_relations`. Search adds **no table** — `tsvector` columns with GIN
indexes on `documents`, `board_rows`, `comments` and `nodes` (canon §1.2, part 17 §35.6).

**Endpoints:** E-133 (search), E-071 and E-072 (relations), E-089 and E-090 (user-authored
templates).

**What the frontend can start using.** ⌘K opens a populated dialog with eight result kinds in fixed
group order, capped per group so one noisy board cannot crowd out a kind, and **the permission
funnel runs before scanning, not after** (canon E-133). Relation chips resolve through one request
per target board rather than one per cell (E-071), and `BacklinksPanel` becomes an indexed query over
`board_row_relations` rather than a scan (E-072). `GanttDependencies` draws its "blocked by"
connectors — which are a relation column named "Blocked by" shipped by the `task` template
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:192`), not an edge type; no chapter may introduce a `RelationType`
without resolving OQ-45 (canon §2.9).

**Why `relations` is P2 and still gets built.** The degradation is already designed — a relation cell
renders its stored id and a deleted target renders `[Deleted Item]` — so nothing is broken without
it. But `board_row_relations` is written in the same transaction as the cell it projects
(canon T-13, part 17 §36.5), which means the **projection writer** has to exist from Phase 2 even
though the **readers** (E-071, E-072) land here. Ship the write side with the board engine and the
read side here; a projection that starts empty and is backfilled is a migration nobody needs.

---

### The P0 / P1 / P2 register

Bands are part 1 §2.3's and are not re-decided here. `P0` = the shell does not boot, or boots into a
refusal, without it. `P1` = the shell boots and P0 surfaces work, but a numbered PRD feature is dead.
`P2` = the feature degrades into behaviour the frontend already handles, or it is a
`RECOMMENDATION` whose OQ is still open.

| Module | Band | Phase | The sentence that decides the band | What the user sees without it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | **P0** | 0 | 33 files import a hardcoded user (`src/mock/users.ts:3`); no request can name an actor. | Nothing. There is no caller. |
| `workspace` | **P0** | 0 | "Not a member" is not "viewer" (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:4-14`), and `WorkspaceGuard` settles membership before anything mounts. | The refusal screen, for everyone. |
| `drive` | **P0** | 1 | Every route resolves a slug chain against the tree; boards, pages, config and secret documents all render **inside** `/drive/<path>`. | An empty sidebar and a dead URL space. |
| `governance` | **P0** | 1 | Not "no permissions" — **no safe read at all**. E-020 is pruned by visibility before it returns (`visibility.ts:197-240`). | Either everything, to everyone, or nothing. |
| `boards` | **P0** | 2 | `BD-COR-07`. Table view is the default surface of every board node. | Board nodes that cannot be opened. |
| `views` | **P0** | 2 | A board must have at least one view; E-081 refuses the delete that would leave zero (`VIEW_LAST_REMAINING`). | A board that loads and cannot render. |
| `templates` (built-ins) | **P0** | 2 | Board creation takes a `templateId`; the four seeds are what E-024 deep-copies. | No way to create a board with columns. |
| `documents` | **P0** | 3 | Document nodes exist in the seeded tree from the first frame. | A sidebar full of pages that 404. |
| `insights` | **P1** | 4 | `/` redirects to `/dashboard`, so this is the landing screen (`SY-DSH-44`, `CO-MYW-30`). | An error panel as the first screen. |
| `files` | **P1** | 5 | `WS-FIL-06` and the whole `/files` route. File **nodes** still list from `drive`. | The tree is intact; the bytes are not. |
| `collab` | **P1** | 6 | `CO-CMT-26`, `CO-MEN-27`, `CO-WAT-28`, `CO-NOT-29`. | The bell reads zero; the drawer's Comments tab is empty. |
| `realtime` | **P1**, one **P0** frame | 1 and 6 | RT-05 is not optional: a revoked user keeps a loaded board on screen (`use-access-sync.ts:74-83`). The other eleven frames are convergence, not correctness. | Stale tabs — and, without RT-05, a data-exposure window. |
| `devtools` | **P1** | 7 | `DV-CFG-22`, `DV-SEC-23`, `DV-ENV-21`. Ship it complete or not at all. | Config and secret nodes that cannot be opened. |
| `system` | **P1** | 1, 3, 7, 8 | `SY-BLK-34` … `SY-VER-39`. Node soft-delete itself is `drive` (E-032), so nothing is lost, only unrecoverable through the UI. | `/trash` empty; multi-select loses its action bar; no import, no export, no history. |
| `search` | **P1** | 9 | `CO-SCH-31`. The cheap drive quick-find (E-035) is a `drive` endpoint and survives (OQ-94). | ⌘K opens an empty dialog. |
| `relations` | **P2** | 2 (write) / 9 (read) | `DV-REL-24`. A relation cell renders its stored id; a deleted target renders `[Deleted Item]` with an unlink action. | Unresolved chips and an empty backlinks panel. |
| `templates` (user-authored) | **P2** | 9 | `RECOMMENDATION` under OQ-47 — the frontend has no surface that saves a board as a template. | Nothing; the control does not exist yet. |
| `board_view_preferences` (E-083) | **P2** | 2 | `RECOMMENDATION` under OQ-46 — per-viewer column widths and collapse state. | Widths reset between sessions, which is today's behaviour. |

---

### The smallest shippable slice

Part 1 §2.3 names it and this ordering preserves it, so it is repeated here as an acceptance test
rather than an aspiration:

> **sign in → list workspaces → read the pruned tree → open one board with one view → edit one cell
> → see it after a refresh.**

That slice is the end of **Phase 2** and touches exactly eleven endpoints: E-001, E-004, E-007,
E-009, E-020, E-022, E-044, E-047, E-062, E-066, E-139. If those eleven work against a real database
with a real session and a real permission check, every remaining phase is additive and — except for
`realtime`, which needs one constant changed (`REALTIME_ENDPOINT`, `src/config/app.ts:65-69`) — no
frontend release is required for any of them.

---

### One question this ordering raises

**OPEN QUESTION (new — proposed OQ-105; see Chapter notes)** — when a URL path resolves to
a node the caller may not see, does the API tell them *something* is there?

**Evidence.** The frontend renders a distinct refusal screen for this case. `useDriveLocation`
computes `isDenied` by resolving the path against the pruned tree **and** the full tree, and treating
"missing from one, present in the other" as a refusal
(`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:56`); `DriveView` then renders `PermissionDeniedState` with
"You don't have access to this item" *before* it considers `isNotFound`
(`src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx:87-98`). The frontend has reasoned about the leak explicitly
and accepted it: "knowing that *something* is there is unavoidable once a URL resolves, knowing what
it is called is not" (`use-drive-location.ts:21-27`), and the refusal deliberately names nothing
(`DENIED_REASON`, `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-167`). But canon §4.2 says `not_found` means
"the resource does not exist, **or the caller may not see it** — the two answer identically", and
canon E-021's `DriveLocation` carries `isNotFound` and no `isDenied`. A real API serves only the
pruned tree, so `isDenied` computes to `false` for everyone and the screen becomes unreachable.

**Recommendation.** Follow canon: E-021 returns `isNotFound: true` with the crumbs resolved so far
and no `isDenied` field, and E-022 returns `404 NODE_NOT_FOUND`. Treat `isDenied` as dead frontend
code to be removed rather than as a contract to satisfy. If product wants the refusal screen back,
add it as an explicit, audited field on E-021 only — never on E-022 — and accept that it confirms the
existence of a node at a guessed path.

**Impact if wrong.** If the refusal screen must survive and E-021 does not carry the flag, a user who
follows a shared link into a folder they were not granted sees "Not found" and reasonably concludes
the link is broken — support cost, not a security defect. If the flag is added carelessly to E-022,
node ids become an existence oracle for the whole workspace, which is a security defect.

---

### 39.1 Example Flows

Seven flows, each drawn against the same five participants — **Frontend**, **API**, **DB**,
**Storage**, **Realtime** — with participants a flow does not touch named in the text rather than
drawn as an idle lane. Every diagram makes the authorization stages explicit, using one vocabulary
defined once here and never re-explained.

#### The five gates, stated once

Reproduced from the governance chapter's server-side algorithm, which is itself transcribed from
`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:67-76`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:156-174`,
`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:91-120` and `src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:69-87`.

| Gate | Question | Source of truth | Refusal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1 · Membership** | Is the caller in this workspace at all? | `workspace_members`. A missing row is **not** `viewer` — "a default here is a way in" (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:30-36`). | `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` 404 — identical to a workspace that does not exist. |
| **2 · Visibility** | May the caller *see* this node? | Walk `nodes` root → node. `inherit` passes the decision through, `workspace` opens to every member, `restricted` discards what flowed in and asks `hasGrantOn` (owner, then a user-scoped rule, then a role-scoped rule). | `NODE_NOT_FOUND` 404, or the node is simply absent from a listing. |
| **3 · Effective role** | Which role does the caller hold *here*? | Walk the same chain over `access_rules`; the **last** match wins, and a rule naming the person beats one naming their role at the same depth. It is not a `max()` — a rule can lower the role. The workspace role is the floor. | — (produces a role, never a refusal) |
| **4 · Capability** | Does that role hold this `PermissionKey`? | `ROLE_PERMISSIONS[R]`, plus owner escalation for the five keys in `OWNER_ESCALATIONS` from `member` upward. | `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, `detail` = `Needs the {Role} role or above`. |
| **5 · Lifecycle** | Is the node in a state that accepts this write? | `nodes.deleted_at`, an archived **ancestor**, `nodes.is_locked`. The three layers only ever take away; `READ_ONLY_KEYS` pass through all of them. | `NODE_TRASHED_READ_ONLY` / `NODE_FROZEN_BY_ANCESTOR` / `NODE_LOCKED`, all 403. |

Gates 1 and 2 answer with `not_found`, never `permission_denied`, because "the resource does not
exist, or the caller may not see it — the two answer identically" (canon §4.2). Gates 4 and 5 answer
with `permission_denied` and the copy is deliberately name-free
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:155-167`).

**Audit and gates.** A gate-4 or gate-5 refusal on a write is audited with `outcome: 'denied'`. A
gate-2 exclusion from a *listing* is not — it is a listing that legitimately contains nothing, not a
refusal, and `visibleTree` returns a pruned tree with no error at all
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:197-240`). Privileged **reads** that are audited at `warn` are
enumerated by canon OQ-26: E-040, E-046, E-136, E-137 — and E-103, which is audited on both paths.

---

#### 39.1.1 Create a workspace — the two-insert transaction

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · CreateWorkspaceDialog
    participant API as API · workspace
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    FE->>FE: validateWorkspaceName · trimmed, 1 to 60 chars
    FE->>API: POST /api/v1/workspaces { name, description, badge, color }

    Note over API: Gate 1 does not apply. There is no workspace to be a member of yet.
    API->>API: session required, else AUTH_REQUIRED 401
    API->>API: name trimmed and length checked, description max 280
    API->>API: slug = uniqueSlug(slugify(name), taken)

    rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
    Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION · READ COMMITTED
    API->>DB: BEGIN
    API->>DB: INSERT workspaces · plan free · used_bytes 0 · total 15 GiB
    API->>DB: INSERT workspace_members · user_id from the SESSION · role admin
    API->>DB: INSERT environments x3 · Development, Staging, Production
    API->>DB: INSERT audit_events · workspace.manage · info · allowed
    API->>DB: COMMIT
    end

    DB-->>API: ok
    API-->>FE: 201 Workspace · members = [creator as admin] · storage 0 of 15 GiB
    FE->>FE: switch active workspace · empty tree · empty bin

    alt slug collision, unique violation 23505
        DB-->>API: 23505 on workspaces_slug_uniq
        API->>API: retry once with a suffixed slug
        API-->>FE: 409 WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN if it collides again
    end
```

**Participants not shown:** Storage (no object), Realtime (the creator is the only member and holds
the response).

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoint.** `POST /api/v1/workspaces` — canon **E-008**. Request DTO `CreateWorkspaceRequest`
   `{ name: string; description?: string; badge?: string; color?: string }`, mirroring
   `NewWorkspaceInput` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:189-194`). Response is the bare `Workspace`
   (canon §5.1: a `POST` returning a `Workspace` returns `Workspace`, not
   `CreateWorkspaceResponse`).
2. **Permission checked.** Session only. Gate 1 cannot apply — the workspace does not exist yet, and
   canon's Perm column for E-008 is `session`. Gates 2 – 5 have no node.
3. **Validation, before `BEGIN`.** `name.trim()` must be non-empty and at most `WORKSPACE_NAME_MAX`
   = 60 (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:196-207`); `description` is trimmed and **stored only when
   non-empty** (`:233`) — the frontend omits the key rather than storing `""`, and C-08 forbids
   collapsing optional into nullable. `badge` defaults to `badgeFor(name)`, two upper-case letters
   (`:167-177`); `color` defaults to the tile palette cycled by the number of existing slugs
   (`:180-187`). Refusals here are `VALIDATION_FAILED` 400 with a `fields` array.
4. **Tables touched.** `workspaces` (T-03) — insert; `workspace_members` (T-04) — insert;
   `environments` (T-26) — three inserts; `audit_events` (T-36) — insert. `users` (T-01) is read
   only to project the creator into the response's `members[0]`.
5. **Columns.** `workspaces`: `id`, `name`, `slug`, `description`, `plan = 'free'`, `badge`,
   `color`, `used_bytes = 0`, `total_bytes = 15 * 1024^3`, `created_at`, `created_by`.
   `workspace_members`: `(workspace_id, user_id)` composite unique, `role = 'admin'`, `joined_at`.
   **`user_id` comes from the session and never from the body** (C-09) — a `creatorId` in a request
   body is a claim, not a fact.
6. **The transaction boundary.** All four statements, one transaction, `READ COMMITTED` (part 17
   §36.1). This is the clearest case in the system where two rows are one fact: the frontend's own
   comment says a workspace whose creator has to be added afterwards "has a moment where nobody can
   administer it, and a failure in between leaves one that nobody can ever administer"
   (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:211-218`). It is unrepairable from inside: with no admin, `isLastAdmin`
   refuses every subsequent change and nobody left can invite or promote anyone
   (`:84-157`, `:98-119`).
7. **Which frontend calls it.** `useWorkspaceStore.createWorkspace`
   (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:290-314`), from `CreateWorkspaceDialog`. Note what the store does
   next and the API must match: `treeByWorkspace[id] = []` and `trashByWorkspace[id] = []` —
   "a new workspace has no tree and no bin. Seeding it with either would put somebody else's
   fixtures inside something a person just made" (`:303-305`). **The API must not seed a sample
   project.**
8. **Realtime event.** None. There is exactly one member and they are holding the response.
9. **Errors.** `VALIDATION_FAILED` 400, `WORKSPACE_SLUG_TAKEN` 409, `AUTH_REQUIRED` 401. The slug is
   globally unique (canon OQ-02 position: single tenant), so the collision is real and is resolved
   by one retry with a suffix before the 409 is returned.

---

#### 39.1.2 Open a RESTRICTED folder — the allowed path and the denied path

The scenario is the seeded one: *Development* contains *Backend*, which is `restricted`. Duc holds a
user-scoped rule on *Backend*; Hai does not (`src/mock/access.ts:24-53`).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · DriveView + useDriveLocation
    participant API as API · drive and governance
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    FE->>API: GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/resolve?path=development/backend
    API->>DB: SELECT role FROM workspace_members WHERE workspace_id AND user_id
    DB-->>API: role, or NULL

    Note over API,DB: GATE 1 · membership. NULL is not viewer.
    alt not a member
        API-->>FE: 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND
    else member, role R0
        API->>DB: SELECT nodes WHERE workspace_id AND deleted_at IS NULL
        API->>DB: SELECT access_rules WHERE workspace_id
        DB-->>API: the flat node set and every rule, keyed by node

        Note over API: GATE 2 · walk root to node, carrying the decision.<br/>inherit passes through · workspace opens to all members ·<br/>restricted discards what flowed in and asks hasGrantOn

        alt ALLOWED · Duc is granted on Backend
            Note over API: hasGrantOn(Backend, Duc) is true · owner, then user rule, then role rule
            API->>DB: SELECT node_favorites, owners, per-kind projections for the survivors
            API-->>FE: 200 DriveLocation · node Backend · ancestors [Development] · children · isNotFound false
            FE->>API: GET /nodes/{nodeId}/capabilities
            Note over API: GATE 3 · effective role on Backend · last rule on the chain wins<br/>GATE 4 · project the 39 keys into the six CapabilitySet flags<br/>GATE 5 · narrow for trashed, frozen, locked
            API-->>FE: 200 CapabilitySet
            FE->>FE: render the folder, its children and its enabled controls
        else DENIED · Hai has no grant on Backend
            Note over API: Backend is refused, and takes its WHOLE SUBTREE with it.<br/>No audit row · this is a listing that contains nothing, not a refusal
            API-->>FE: 200 DriveLocation · node Development · isNotFound true · children of Development
            FE->>FE: NotFoundState for the segment "backend"
        end
    end

    Note over FE,API: The direct lookup answers the same way
    FE->>API: GET /nodes/{backendNodeId}
    API-->>FE: 404 NODE_NOT_FOUND · never 403, never the folder's name
```

**Participants not shown:** Storage, Realtime — this is a pure read.

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoints.** `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/resolve?path=a/b/c` — canon **E-021**,
   returning `DriveLocation` `{ node, ancestors, children, isNotFound }`. Then
   `GET /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/capabilities` — **E-044** — returning `CapabilitySet`. The whole-tree
   read the sidebar uses is **E-020**; the direct lookup is **E-022**; the children listing is
   **E-023**.
2. **Permission checked.** E-021 and E-020: *membership* (gate 1). E-022, E-023, E-044:
   *visibility* (gates 1 – 2). None of them checks a `PermissionKey` — seeing a node is decided by
   access resolution, not by an action, which is why the viewer column of the role matrix is empty
   by construction (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:11-16`).
3. **The two axes are never merged.** "A Viewer who is granted a restricted folder **sees it** and
   edits nothing; a Manager who is not granted it **does not see it**, whatever their role"
   (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:15-33`). Gate 2 does not consult the role matrix and gate 4
   does not consult the access mode. Merging them would make "high enough role" a way into a folder
   somebody deliberately shut.
4. **Tables touched.** `workspace_members` (T-04) — read, gate 1 and the floor role.
   `nodes` (T-06) — one flat read, `WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND deleted_at IS NULL`, nested in
   memory by `parent_id`; no recursive CTE, because the whole workspace is being read anyway.
   `access_rules` (T-08) — read, all rules for the workspace, loaded into `Record<nodeId, rules[]>`,
   exactly the shape the resolver walks (`src/store/permission-store.ts:21-31`).
   `node_favorites` (T-07), `users` (T-01) and the per-kind side tables (`boards`, `documents`,
   `file_nodes ⋈ file_assets`) — read, for the survivors only. **Never a board's rows.**
5. **The pruning rule the denied path depends on.** A refused node takes its whole subtree with it —
   "that is what stops a board inside a restricted folder from surfacing in search, favourites or a
   relation picker just because the board itself carries no restriction of its own"
   (`visibility.ts:184-196`). This is why the denial is a *listing* property and does not need to be
   re-checked by search (E-133), favourites (E-033), My Work (E-134), the dashboard (E-135) or the
   relation picker (E-071): they all resolve against the pruned set.
6. **The owner is always admitted.** `hasGrantOn` returns true for the node's owner before it looks
   at any rule (`visibility.ts:87-93`): "somebody has to be able to get back into a folder they
   shut, and 'whoever made it' is a rule a person can hold in their head — which an emergency
   override buried in an admin console is not."
7. **Transaction boundary.** None required. Use **one read-only snapshot** for E-020 and E-021 so
   the tree cannot be internally inconsistent — a child present whose parent was concurrently
   trashed.
8. **Which frontend calls it.** `useDriveLocation` (`src/hooks/use-drive-location.ts:32-58`) for the
   path resolve; `useCapabilities` for E-044; `selectTree` / `visibleTreeFor`
   (`src/store/workspace-store.ts:1063-1085`) for the sidebar. `DriveView` branches on the result
   (`src/components/drive/drive-view.tsx:87-115`).
9. **Realtime event.** None on read. Convergence comes from RT-11 `node.changed` and RT-05
   `permission.changed`; the latter is what makes a *revocation* take effect on an already-open tab
   (`src/hooks/use-access-sync.ts:74-83`).
10. **Errors.** `WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` 404 (gate 1), `NODE_NOT_FOUND` 404 (gate 2 on E-022/E-023/
    E-044). E-021's denied path is **not an error**: it is a `200` whose `isNotFound` is `true` and
    whose `node` is the deepest ancestor the caller *may* see. See the open question at the end of
    §39 for the one behaviour this changes on the client.
11. **The admin recovery path is the single deliberate bypass.** E-046
    `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/restricted-nodes` looks past gate 2 for a caller holding
    `workspace.permission.manage`, exposes names and paths and no content, and **the read itself is
    audited at `warn`** (`visibility.ts:270-291`; canon OQ-26).

---

#### 39.1.3 Update a status where a transition rule rejects it

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · KanbanBoard + board-store.editCells
    participant API as API · boards
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant RT as Realtime

    FE->>FE: evaluateTransition(Status, from, to) against the loaded schema

    alt refused by rules the tab already holds · the normal case
        FE-->>FE: toast "Status cannot go straight from New to Verified. New can move to Triaged."
        Note over FE,API: no request leaves the client · the card never moves
    else allowed locally, but this tab's schema is stale
        FE->>FE: guardCellEdits splits the batch · optimistic write · captureCells reverts
        FE->>API: PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells { edits, baseRevisions }

        API->>DB: SELECT boards JOIN nodes · ancestor chain · access_rules
        Note over API,DB: GATES 1-4 · membership, visibility, effective role, row.update<br/>GATE 5 · trashed, frozen by an archived ancestor, locked
        API->>DB: SELECT board_columns · the whole schema, for kind and rule validation
        API->>DB: SELECT board_rows WHERE id = ANY($ids) FOR UPDATE ORDER BY id
        DB-->>API: committed cells and revisions

        Note over API: RECORD RULES · not permission, evaluated separately<br/>1 option isDisabled · 2 option availability conditions · 3 transitionRules
        API->>API: evaluateTransition against the COMMITTED first option id

        alt a rule refuses any edit in the batch
            API->>DB: ROLLBACK
            API-->>FE: 409 conflict · TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED · message verbatim from the rule
            FE->>FE: revertCellEdits · the card returns to New
            FE-->>FE: toast error.message
            Note over API,RT: no row_activity, no revision bump, no frame, no audit row
        else every edit passes
            API->>DB: UPDATE board_rows SET cells, revision + 1, updated_at, and the 4 projections
            API->>DB: INSERT row_activity · one entry per row, however many cells it touched
            API->>DB: COMMIT
            API-->>FE: 200 UpdateCellsResponse { rows, conflicts }
            FE->>FE: reconcileRows(result.rows)
            API->>RT: RT-07 row.updated { boardId, rowId, revision } · ids only
        end
    end
```

**Participants not shown:** Storage.

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoint.** `PATCH /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows/cells` — canon **E-066**. Request
   `UpdateCellsRequest` `{ edits: CellEdit[]; baseRevisions?: Record<rowId, number> }`, matching
   `UpdateCellsInput` (`src/services/board-service.ts:472-477`). Response `UpdateCellsResponse`
   `{ rows, conflicts }` (canon §5.5).
2. **Permission checked.** `row.update`, resolved on `boards.node_id` — a Member key
   (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:22-35`). It is in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`, so gate 5's lock check
   applies (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:36-49`).
3. **A transition rule is not a permission, and the two are never combined.** The frontend states it
   twice: "Permission answers 'may this person edit Status at all'; a transition rule answers 'may
   Status go from here to there'. Both are checked, separately, before a drop is written"
   (`src/lib/transition-rules.ts:22-25`), and `guardCellEdits` repeats it
   (`src/lib/board-write-rules.ts:14-18`). The server must keep them apart too: gate 4 produces
   `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, the rule produces `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` 409.
4. **The evaluation the server must reproduce exactly** (`evaluateTransition`,
   `src/lib/transition-rules.ts:102-133`): rules that are `enabled: false` pass; a move where
   `from === to` passes; **a move touching a key the table does not govern passes** — adding a
   status must never freeze it; otherwise the target must appear in `transitions[from]`. The empty
   bucket is the reserved key `"__empty__"` (`:28`), which must be rejected as a user-authored
   option id (`OPTION_ID_RESERVED` 400).
5. **The server is stricter than the client, deliberately.** The client evaluates `from` against
   `rowsById`, read once; the server evaluates it against the row it just locked
   `FOR UPDATE`. A batch that moves the same row twice therefore evaluates the second edit against
   the first edit's result. That difference must not be softened.
6. **Tables touched.** `boards` (T-10), `nodes` (T-06), `access_rules` (T-08) — read, for the gates.
   `board_columns` (T-11) — read, `config.transitionRules` and `config.options[].availability` live
   in the JSONB (canon §1.3.3, there is no `select_options` table). `board_rows` (T-12) —
   `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` **ordered by `id`** so two concurrent batches cannot deadlock, then
   `UPDATE` only on the allowed path. `row_activity` (T-14) — insert only on the allowed path.
7. **Transaction boundary.** One transaction, `READ COMMITTED`, covering the gate reads, the rule
   evaluation, the updates and the activity inserts (part 17 §36.4). **A rule refusal aborts the
   whole batch**: `UpdateCellsResponse` carries exactly `rows` and `conflicts` and has no channel for
   a per-edit rejection. The bulk endpoints do have that channel — E-074 skips the refused records
   and applies the rest through `BulkSkip`, because "refusing the whole batch because one record
   cannot make the move would be worse than telling the user which ones could not"
   (`src/store/board-store.ts:557-564`).
8. **The one thing that is *not* a 409.** Canon's "E-066 is always `200`, never `409`" governs
   **staleness**. A stale `baseRevisions[rowId]` is applied last-write-wins, the revision is bumped,
   and the collision is reported as a `ConflictNotice` in the `200` body — at most one notice per row
   per call, raised by the first edit that touches it, and a missing `baseRevisions[rowId]` never
   conflicts (`src/services/board-service.ts:504-512`). `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` exists in the registry
   and is explicitly never used here.
9. **Which frontend calls it.** `useBoardStore.editCells` (`src/store/board-store.ts:315-354`) —
   from the Kanban drop (`src/components/board/views/kanban-board.tsx:79`), the cell editor, the row
   drawer and a grid paste. All four write through the same action, which is what stops the Kanban
   rule being bypassable by opening the same record's Status cell in the table.
10. **Realtime event.** On success, **RT-07** `row.updated` `{ boardId, rowId, revision }`, ids only,
    published after commit. On refusal, **nothing** — no frame, and **no audit row**: a refused
    business-rule write is not a governance event; `audit_events.outcome` records `denied` for
    permission, not for record rules (`src/types/audit.ts:20`).
11. **Errors.** `TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED` 409 and `OPTION_UNAVAILABLE` 409 (record rules);
    `ROW_ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY` 409; `CELL_VALUE_KIND_INVALID` 400; `DATE_VALUE_INVALID` 400;
    `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` 404; `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403. `message` is the rule's own sentence
    **verbatim** — the API returns the prose because the UI renders `error.message` unchanged
    (canon §4.4 rule 1).

#### 39.1.4 Create a subtask

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · SubtaskPanel + board-store.createSubtask
    participant API as API · boards
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant RT as Realtime

    FE->>FE: optimistic row · displayId "TASK-…" · sequence 0 · revision 0 · isPending
    FE->>API: POST /boards/{boardId}/rows { parentRowId, cells }

    API->>DB: SELECT boards JOIN nodes · ancestor chain · access_rules
    Note over API,DB: GATES 1-4 · membership, visibility, effective role, row.create<br/>GATE 5 · trashed, frozen, locked

    rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
    Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION · READ COMMITTED
    API->>DB: BEGIN
    API->>DB: SELECT board_rows WHERE id = parentRowId FOR SHARE
    alt parent missing
        API->>DB: ROLLBACK
        API-->>FE: 404 PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND · "That parent record could not be found"
    else parent on another board
        API->>DB: ROLLBACK
        API-->>FE: 409 ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD
    else parent already at the depth cap
        API->>DB: ROLLBACK
        API-->>FE: 409 ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP
    else ok
        API->>DB: UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1 RETURNING next_sequence
        API->>API: custom_id = formatRowId(prefix, sequence) · position after the parent's last descendant
        API->>DB: INSERT board_rows · cells dense with emptyCellFor per column · revision 1
        API->>DB: INSERT board_row_relations for any relation cells supplied
        API->>DB: INSERT row_activity · "created TASK-042 under TASK-041" on the CHILD
        API->>DB: INSERT row_activity · "added subtask TASK-042" on the PARENT
        API->>DB: COMMIT
    end
    end

    API-->>FE: 201 BoardRow · authoritative id, displayId, sequence, revision 1
    FE->>FE: replaceRow(tempId, created) · the placeholder becomes the real record
    API->>RT: RT-06 row.created { boardId, rowId, revision }
```

**Participants not shown:** Storage.

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoint.** `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/rows` — canon **E-062**, with `parentRowId` set.
   **There is no separate subtask endpoint**: "a subtask is a full board record — its own display id,
   status, assignee, attachments, comments and history — so the parent stores a pointer, never a
   nested copy" (`src/types/board.ts:257-263`). Request `CreateRowRequest`
   `{ afterRowId?: string | null; cells?: Record<columnId, CellValue>; parentRowId?: string | null }`
   (`CreateRowInput`, `src/services/board-service.ts:277-288`). Response is the bare `BoardRow`.
2. **Permission checked.** `row.create` on `boards.node_id` — a Member key. Nothing about the child
   is gated differently from a top-level record.
3. **Tables touched.** `boards` (T-10) — `UPDATE next_sequence … RETURNING`, which is both the
   allocation and the lock. `board_rows` (T-12) — one `SELECT … FOR SHARE` on the parent, one
   `INSERT`. `board_row_relations` (T-13) — inserts, only if the supplied `cells` carry relation
   values. `row_activity` (T-14) — **two** inserts.
4. **Columns and cardinality.** `board_rows.parent_row_id UUID NULL REFERENCES board_rows(id) ON
   DELETE SET NULL`, indexed. A parent has 0..N direct children; a child has 0..1 parent. `ON DELETE
   SET NULL` is the schema expressing a product rule: "children of a deleted parent are lifted to the
   top level rather than removed with it. Deleting a container must not silently delete work nobody
   asked about" (`src/services/board-service.ts:460-470`).
5. **The counter is the server's and only ever increases.** `UPDATE boards SET next_sequence =
   next_sequence + 1 … RETURNING` in one statement — never `MAX(sequence) + 1`. "Deleting `TASK-005`
   does not hand `005` to the next record" (`src/services/board-service.ts:290-293`). The optimistic
   row the client shows carries `` `${prefix}-…` `` precisely because the display id is not the
   client's to invent (`src/store/board-store.ts:363-367`).
6. **Placement.** The child is filed directly after its parent's **last descendant** in board order —
   `lastDescendantOf` (`src/services/board-service.ts:342-352`) — "so the board's own order already
   reads as the tree even before a view nests it" (`:320-321`). `parentRowId` overrides `afterRowId`.
   With `board_rows.position NUMERIC` as a fractional index (canon OQ-34 position), that is a midpoint
   between the last descendant and whatever follows it.
7. **Bounds.** Canon OQ-33 position: same board, depth cap 5, cycles rejected by a recursive CTE,
   archiving a parent does not cascade, deleting a parent lifts its children. A create cannot produce
   a cycle; `PUT /rows/{rowId}/parent` (E-067) can, and reproduces the client's guard
   (`isDescendant`, `src/services/board-service.ts:354-365`).
8. **Two activity entries, one write.** `created {child.displayId} under {parent.displayId}` with
   kind `created` on the child, and `added subtask {child.displayId}` with kind `updated` on the
   parent (`src/services/board-service.ts:327-336`). The **parent's `revision` is not bumped** — a
   parent takes no write because of its children beyond that one history line, and progress is
   computed on read (`subtaskProgress`, `src/lib/board-hierarchy.ts:182-199`), never stored.
9. **Do not run the transition gate on a create.** The composer offers statuses with
   `ignoreTransitions: true` because no record exists yet to transition *from*
   (`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-composer.tsx:60-73`). The server must still gate an initial
   `select` value on `isDisabled` and `availability`, and must not evaluate `transitionRules`.
10. **Transaction boundary.** One transaction, `READ COMMITTED`, covering the allocation, the insert,
    the relation projection and both activity rows (part 17 §36.3). The `custom_id` and the row are
    one fact; an activity entry for a row that does not exist is a lie.
11. **Which frontend calls it.** `useBoardStore.createSubtask`
    (`src/store/board-store.ts:464-515`), from `SubtaskPanel`'s composer
    (`src/components/board/drawer/subtask-panel.tsx:206`) and the row actions menu's "Add subtask".
12. **Realtime event.** **RT-06** `row.created` `{ boardId, rowId, revision }` after commit — ids
    only, no cell content (canon §7.2).
13. **Errors.** `BOARD_NOT_FOUND` 404, `PARENT_ROW_NOT_FOUND` 404, `ROW_PARENT_CROSS_BOARD` 409,
    `ROW_PARENT_TOO_DEEP` 409, `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` 409, `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403.
    **Forbidden by construction:** no endpoint may accept or return a nested `subtasks: BoardRow[]`
    array on a `BoardRow`, and `board_rows.cells` may never hold a child's data.

#### 39.1.5 Upload an attachment to a board row cell

Three calls, and the third is the one that makes the file *belong* to anything.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · useAttachmentField + upload-store
    participant API as API · files, then boards
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant S3 as Object storage
    participant RT as Realtime

    FE->>FE: partitionUploads · size, extension · re-read the CURRENT cell for maxFiles headroom
    FE->>API: 1. POST /workspaces/{id}/uploads { fileName, sizeBytes, mimeType, folderId, createDriveNode false }
    Note over API,DB: GATES 1-5 on the destination · file.upload
    API->>DB: validate size, extension, and workspaces.used_bytes against the plan
    API->>DB: INSERT uploads · state pending · expires_at now + 30 min
    API->>S3: presign PUT bound to storage_key, content-type and a max length
    API-->>FE: 201 { uploadId, uploadUrl, headers, expiresAt, maxBytes }

    FE->>S3: 2. PUT bytes · XHR progress 0..1 · AbortSignal
    S3-->>FE: 200

    FE->>API: 3. POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete { sizeBytes, checksum }
    API->>S3: HEAD object · real Content-Length · sniff the first bytes
    rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
    Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION
    API->>DB: SELECT workspaces FOR UPDATE · quota re-check
    API->>DB: INSERT file_assets · size from the HEAD, never the declared value
    API->>DB: UPDATE workspaces SET used_bytes = used_bytes + size_bytes
    API->>DB: UPDATE uploads SET state completed, asset_id
    API->>DB: COMMIT
    end
    API-->>FE: 201 FileAsset · no drive node, because createDriveNode was false

    Note over FE,API: The asset is an orphan until the cell references it
    FE->>API: 4. PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells<br/>[{ rowId, columnId, value: { kind attachment, attachments } }]
    Note over API,DB: GATES 1-5 on the board's node · row.update
    rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
    Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION
    API->>DB: SELECT board_rows FOR UPDATE · SELECT board_columns for AttachmentConfig.maxFiles
    API->>DB: UPDATE board_rows SET cells storing assetId ONLY, revision + 1
    API->>DB: DELETE then INSERT cell_attachments (row_id, column_id, asset_id)
    API->>DB: INSERT row_activity · kind attached
    API->>DB: COMMIT
    end
    API->>API: mint short-lived signed url and thumbnailUrl per attachment
    API-->>FE: 200 UpdateCellsResponse · rows carry resolved urls
    API->>RT: RT-07 row.updated { boardId, rowId, revision }
```

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoints.** **E-110** `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/uploads` → `CreateUploadResponse`;
   the client's `PUT` straight at object storage; **E-111** `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete` →
   `FileAsset`; then **E-066** `PATCH /boards/{boardId}/rows/cells`. **E-117**
   `GET /assets/{assetId}/url` resolves an attachment reference later, on any surface.
2. **Permissions checked.** E-110 and E-111: `file.upload`, gate 4, on the destination node — the
   frontend funnels every upload path through one place for exactly this reason ("dropzone, toolbar,
   drag onto a folder, editor block — funnels through here, so the permission check belongs here
   too", `src/store/upload-store.ts:102-107`). E-066: `row.update` on `boards.node_id`. The two are
   different keys on different nodes and both are required.
3. **`createDriveNode` is `false` for a board cell.** Canon OQ-74 position. Today every upload
   funnels through `addUploadedAsset` and *does* create a drive node
   (`src/store/upload-store.ts:76`), which nobody chose per-surface — it falls out of the shared
   funnel. The request field makes it a decision: `true` for the drive, the files view and document
   blocks; `false` for board cells and comments, "where a folder full of screenshots named
   `Screenshot 2026-08-27.png` is noise".
4. **Tables touched.** `uploads` (T-32) — insert then update. `workspaces` (T-03) —
   `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` then `UPDATE used_bytes`; the counter is maintained transactionally, never
   recomputed by aggregate (canon §1.4). `file_assets` (T-27) — insert; `size_bytes` is the **HEAD**
   value, not the client's declaration. `board_rows` (T-12) — `UPDATE cells`, `revision + 1`.
   `cell_attachments` (T-29) — `(row_id, column_id, asset_id)` plus `uploaded_by` and `created_at`.
   `row_activity` (T-14) — one entry, kind `attached`.
5. **The cell *is* the storage.** "The board record's attachment cell **is** the storage. The table
   cell, the drawer section and the viewer all read and write that one value, so there is no
   `tableAttachments` and no `drawerAttachments` to keep in step" (`src/lib/attachments.ts:5-12`).
   `cell_attachments` is a **projection** of that value, written in the same transaction, and exists
   so orphan collection and quota are one query rather than a scan of every board's JSONB.
6. **What is persisted, and what is not.** Only `assetId`. `url` and `thumbnailUrl` are minted per
   response as short-lived signed URLs and are **never accepted on write** — `CellAttachment.url` is
   documented as a "session URL for the real bytes; null once the session that made it ends"
   (`src/types/board.ts:206-207`; canon OQ-75). A client-supplied `blob:` string means nothing to
   anyone else and must be rejected.
7. **The cap.** `AttachmentConfig.maxFiles` (`src/types/board.ts:148-150`), enforced server-side on
   the resulting list length. The client enforces it too, and does so by re-reading the *current*
   cell value at call time "so two drops in quick succession must not both start from the same stale
   list and lose one another's files" (`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:63-96`) — the server's
   `FOR UPDATE` on the row is the authoritative version of that same care.
8. **Transaction boundaries — there are two, and one thing outside both.** E-111 is one transaction
   (asset row, quota increment, upload state). E-066 is a second (cell value, `cell_attachments`,
   activity). The `PUT` to object storage is outside both, and deliberately: S3 has no rollback, so
   the order is always **object first, database second** — an object with no row is garbage the
   reaper collects; a row with no object is a broken link the product cannot repair (part 17 §36,
   T-03). Between E-111 and E-066 the asset is an orphan; the sweep's grace window is what keeps it
   alive.
9. **Which frontend calls it.** `useAttachmentField` (`src/hooks/use-attachment-field.ts:37-115`),
   used by **both** `AttachmentCell` (`src/components/board/cells/attachment-cell.tsx:78`) and
   `AttachmentPanel` (`src/components/board/drawer/attachment-panel.tsx:61`) with the same
   `(rowId, columnId)`, writing through the same `editCells`. Uploads are tagged
   `cell:<rowId>:<columnId>` so progress survives the drawer closing and reopening (`:50`).
10. **Realtime events.** **RT-07** `row.updated` after E-066's commit. **No frame from E-111** when
    `createDriveNode` is false — a cell attachment announces itself through the referencing write, not
    through the upload (part 10 §21.2). When a drive node *is* created, E-111 emits **RT-11**
    `node.changed` (`created`).
11. **Errors.** E-110: `FILE_EMPTY` 400, `FILE_TOO_LARGE` 400, `FILE_TYPE_REJECTED` 400,
    `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` 507, `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403. E-111: `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` 404,
    `UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` 422, `FILE_CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH` 400, `UPLOAD_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` 502.
    E-066: as §39.1.3, plus `ASSET_NOT_FOUND` 404 when the cell names an asset the caller cannot
    reach.
12. **One security rule that belongs to this flow.** SVG, HTML and XHTML are never rendered inline —
    "rendering uploaded markup in the app's own origin is how an upload becomes stored XSS"
    (`src/lib/attachments.ts:24-29`). The server must serve attachments with
    `Content-Disposition: attachment` and a non-executable content type for those, whatever the
    extension claims, and must sniff rather than trust the declared MIME (canon OQ-70).

#### 39.1.6 Import a QA/QC spreadsheet

The board came from the `qa` built-in — `Test case`, `Result`, `Suite`, `Environment`, `Tester`,
`Planned on`, `Executed on`, `Expected result`, `Evidence`, `Related bug`, prefix `QA`
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:281-339`). The chapter-level worked example with the wizard's own steps
is §24.10; this one shows the gates and the transaction boundary.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · useImportWizard
    participant API as API · system
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant RT as Realtime

    Note over FE: The file never leaves the browser. Nothing is written yet.
    FE->>FE: extension must be xlsx, csv or tsv · validateUpload
    FE->>FE: parseXlsx or parseDelimited · readImportSource numbers every row BEFORE the header is split
    FE->>FE: autoMapColumns against the board's 10 columns · one create target for "Browser"

    FE->>API: POST /boards/{boardId}/import/plan { source, mappings, policy }
    Note over API,DB: GATES 1-5 on boards.node_id · board.import
    API->>DB: SELECT boards, board_columns, directory, relation targets · READ ONLY
    API->>API: re-parse every mapped cell against the CURRENT schema · number every finding by its file row
    API-->>FE: 200 ImportPlan · valid, invalid, blank, issues, conflicts
    FE-->>FE: the user reads the issues and picks skip or blank · nothing has been written

    FE->>API: POST /boards/{boardId}/import { source, mappings, policy, removeUnmappedColumns }
    Note over API,DB: GATES re-checked · board.import + board.column.create + board.column.delete
    API->>API: IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED if conflicts is non-empty · IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED past 5000

    rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
    Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION · create, then delete, then insert
    API->>DB: BEGIN
    API->>DB: INSERT import_jobs ON CONFLICT (board_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
    API->>DB: SELECT boards FOR UPDATE · the board's schema lock and its counter lock
    API->>API: re-run the mapping conflicts against the locked schema
    API->>DB: INSERT board_columns · Browser, appended densely
    API->>DB: DELETE board_columns · Story points · never the primary column
    API->>DB: UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 47 RETURNING
    API->>DB: INSERT board_rows x47 · QA-118 to QA-164, in the file's order, no gaps
    API->>DB: INSERT board_row_relations for resolved Related bug cells
    API->>DB: INSERT row_activity x47 · kind imported
    API->>DB: UPDATE import_jobs · counts, issues, policy, the serialised outcome
    API->>DB: INSERT audit_events · board.import · info · allowed
    API->>DB: COMMIT
    end

    API-->>FE: 200 ImportOutcome · created, skipped, issues, rowIds, removedColumns
    API->>RT: RT-10 board.schema.changed { boardId }
    API->>RT: RT-06 row.created { boardId, rowIds } · ONE batched frame, not 47
```

**Participants not shown:** Storage — the spreadsheet is never uploaded. `ExportJob` is the only
half of this module that touches object storage, and only for whole-board scope (canon E-086).

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoints.** **E-084** `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/import/plan` → `ImportPlan`, computed
   before anything is written and **not persisted**. **E-085**
   `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/import` → `ImportOutcome`. E-085 does not require E-084 to have
   been called and does not trust a plan the client computed — it re-derives one against the locked
   schema.
2. **Permission checked.** `board.import` (gate 4) on `boards.node_id` — a Manager key
   (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:38-63`), and it is in `CONTENT_WRITE_KEYS`, so a locked or frozen
   node refuses it at gate 5. When the mapping creates or removes columns, `board.column.create` and
   `board.column.delete` are checked as well — all three are Manager keys, so in practice one role
   answers all of them, but the composition must be explicit because a future rule could separate
   them.
3. **What crosses the wire.** Not the file. The browser parses `.xlsx` with a hand-rolled
   single-sheet reader (`src/lib/xlsx.ts`) and `.csv`/`.tsv` per RFC 4180 (`src/lib/csv.ts:1-49`),
   and posts an `ImportSource` — `{ fileName, sheetName, headers, rows: ImportSourceRow[] }` — plus
   `ColumnMapping[]`. Canon and part 1 §2.4 keep it that way: the user gets errors while the mapping
   is still fixable, and the server needs no spreadsheet parser.
4. **The invariant this flow exists to protect.** `ImportSourceRow.sourceRowNumber` is 1-based
   **counting the header** — "what Excel shows" (`src/types/system.ts:62-66`) — and it travels *with*
   the cells, never in a parallel array. Numbering happens before the header is removed and before the
   5 000-row cap is applied. A row is dropped only when the **whole source row** is empty, because
   deciding it per mapped column "made a row that carried data the user chose not to import
   disappear, taking its row number with it" (`src/lib/import-mapping.ts:344-350`). Row 7 is row 7 in
   the plan, in the outcome and in the audit trail.
5. **Tables touched.** `import_jobs` (T-38) — insert then update; the `ON CONFLICT (board_id,
   idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id` is the replay guard, and zero rows returned means read
   back the stored outcome and return it with `200`, doing nothing else. `boards` (T-10) —
   `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, then the block allocation on `next_sequence`. `board_columns` (T-11) —
   inserts then deletes. `board_rows` (T-12) — bulk insert, and a rewrite of `cells` on every
   pre-existing row when a column is deleted. `board_views` (T-15) — references to a deleted column
   are pruned by the `SET NULL` foreign keys. `board_row_relations` (T-13), `row_activity` (T-14),
   `audit_events` (T-36) — inserts.
6. **Order inside the transaction matters.** Create columns → delete columns → allocate the sequence
   block → insert rows. Creating first means a value mapped to a new column has a column to land in;
   deleting before inserting means the removed columns' keys are never written into `cells` at all.
   The frontend does it in the opposite order for a different reason — it deletes **last, and only
   once the records are in**, because "a failed import must never be the thing that emptied the
   board's schema" (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:273-275`) — and the single transaction makes both
   orderings safe, which is precisely why canon requires one.
7. **One sequence allocation for the whole file.** `UPDATE boards SET next_sequence = next_sequence +
   :n RETURNING next_sequence`, so the import lands as `QA-118 … QA-164` with no gaps and no
   client-invented identifiers (`src/services/board-service.ts:1196-1204`).
8. **Removing a column is off by default and never touches the primary.** `isRemovingUnmapped`
   defaults to `false` — "dropping a column takes its value off every record already on the board.
   That is a reasonable thing to want when a file defines the real schema, and never a reasonable
   thing to do because nobody said otherwise" (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:88-95`). The primary
   column is never offered and the endpoint refuses it: `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED` 409.
9. **Transaction boundary.** One transaction, `READ COMMITTED`, under the board's `FOR UPDATE` —
   which is also what makes E-085 and a concurrent column create, delete or reorder mutually
   exclusive (part 17 §36.7). Parsing and planning happen before `BEGIN` and persist nothing.
10. **Which frontend calls it.** `useImportWizard.confirm`
    (`src/hooks/use-import-wizard.ts:224-290`) via `useBoardStore.importRows`; the wizard's four
    steps are `ImportUploadStep`, `ImportMappingStep`, `ImportValidationStep`, `ImportResultStep`.
    `ImportStep` is UI-only and never crosses the wire (canon §2.7).
11. **Realtime events.** **RT-10** `board.schema.changed { boardId }` first — the schema moved, so
    every open client refetches it wholesale, matching C-11 ("a schema response is a complete array,
    never a delta"). Then **RT-06** `row.created` as **one batched frame carrying `rowIds`**, not 47
    frames.
12. **Audit.** One `audit_events` row, `module: 'board'`, `action: 'board.import'`,
    `severity: 'info'`, in the shape the seed already uses: *"48 records imported from
    sprint-backlog.xlsx, 3 rows left out."* (`src/services/audit-service.ts:86-95`).
13. **Errors.** `IMPORT_MAPPING_UNRESOLVED` 400 (`ImportPlan.conflicts` is non-empty, so the mapping
    is not runnable), `IMPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` 400 (`IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 5000`,
    `src/config/app.ts:48`), `IMPORT_FILE_UNPARSEABLE` 400, `COLUMN_PRIMARY_PROTECTED` 409,
    `BOARD_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` 409, `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403.
14. **A rule the create path shares with §39.1.4.** Imported records are being born, so
    `transitionRules` are **not** evaluated — "a transition presumes a prior state, and a record being
    born has none". Option `isDisabled` and `availability` still apply, and every incoming `CellValue`
    is validated against its column's type: a client could otherwise post a `select` value naming an
    option that does not exist, or a `relation` value naming a row on a board it cannot read.

#### 39.1.7 Reveal a secret

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FE as Frontend · SecretList reveal button
    participant API as API · devtools
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant KMS as KMS · envelope unwrap

    FE->>API: POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/{secretId}/reveal { action: "reveal" }

    API->>API: per-user throttle in Redis, BEFORE the transaction
    alt over the limit
        Note over API,DB: still audited · steps below run in their own transaction
        API-->>FE: 429 SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED
    end

    API->>DB: SELECT secret_documents JOIN nodes · ancestor chain · access_rules · workspace_members
    Note over API,DB: GATE 1 membership · GATE 2 visibility · GATE 3 effective role<br/>GATE 4 secret.reveal · Admin only · GATE 5 does not narrow it,<br/>secret.reveal is in READ_ONLY_KEYS
    API->>API: mayUnlock = roleHas(clientRole, key) AND serverResolvedCan(nodeId, key)

    alt DENIED
        rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
        Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION · the refusal is audited BEFORE it is returned
        API->>DB: BEGIN
        API->>DB: INSERT secret_access_events · action reveal · key · actor · ip from the socket
        API->>DB: INSERT audit_events · secret.reveal · severity error · outcome denied
        API->>DB: COMMIT
        end
        API-->>FE: 403 SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED · "Revealing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY needs the Admin role"
    else ALLOWED
        rect rgb(240, 244, 250)
        Note over API,DB: ONE TRANSACTION · the audit rows COMMIT before the plaintext moves
        API->>DB: BEGIN
        API->>DB: SELECT id, key, environment_id, value_encrypted FROM secrets WHERE id
        API->>DB: INSERT secret_access_events · action reveal
        API->>DB: INSERT audit_events · secret.reveal · severity warn · outcome allowed
        API->>DB: COMMIT
        end
        API->>KMS: Decrypt the workspace data key
        KMS-->>API: plaintext DEK
        API->>API: AES-256-GCM decrypt ciphertext with iv and tag
        API-->>FE: 200 RevealSecretResponse { value }
        FE->>FE: component state only · auto-hide after 30 s · never storage, url or log
    end
```

**Participants not shown:** Storage (a secret has no object) and Realtime — **deliberately**. A frame
announcing a reveal would put the key name on every socket in the workspace.

**Walkthrough.**

1. **Endpoint.** `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/{secretId}/reveal` — canon **E-103**. Body
   `RevealSecretRequest { action: "reveal" | "copy" }`. Response `RevealSecretResponse`. The bulk
   sibling is **E-104** `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets/copy` → `CopySecretsResponse { text, keys }`,
   one permission check and **one audit entry per key**, with `secretIds` requiring
   `minItems: 1` (canon OQ-66 — the frontend's "empty means every secret" is an unsafe wire default).
   The trail is read back with **E-105**.
2. **Permission checked.** `secret.reveal` — an Admin key (`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:66-75`),
   canon OQ-23 position. `copy` has **no permission key of its own**: it is gated by `secret.reveal`
   and audited as a reveal, because "copying is a read of plaintext… only an actual write to the
   stored value is a rotation" (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:384-386`).
3. **Two questions, both must say yes.** `mayUnlock(nodeId, role, key)` =
   `roleHas(role, key) && callerCan(nodeId, key)` (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:315-317`). The
   `role` in the request is the role the *client* is previewing as and **can only ever narrow** — a
   workspace admin reading the app as a member has to be refused, or the preview is a demo rather
   than a check. The authoritative answer is the server-resolved effective role. "A role arriving in
   a call is a claim, and an endpoint that trusts one is asking the caller how much access they would
   like" (`:301-314`). A `previewAs` that outranks the caller's real role is
   `PREVIEW_ROLE_ESCALATES` 400 (canon OQ-21).
4. **Gate 5 does not apply.** `secret.reveal` is one of the three `READ_ONLY_KEYS` — with
   `board.export` and `workspace.audit.view` — that pass through the trashed, frozen and locked
   layers (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:28-33, 67`).
5. **Tables touched.** `nodes` (T-06), `access_rules` (T-08), `workspace_members` (T-04) — read, for
   the gates. `secret_documents` (T-22) — read. `secrets` (T-23) — the **only** query in the system
   that selects `value_encrypted`; never `SELECT *` on this table. `secret_access_events` (T-25) —
   insert, on both paths. `audit_events` (T-36) — insert, on both paths.
6. **Columns.** `secrets`: `id`, `node_id`, `key`, `value_encrypted BYTEA`, `iv`, `tag`,
   `environment_id`, `note`, `position`, `rotated_by`, `updated_at`. `secret_access_events`:
   `action` (`reveal` | `copy` | `rotate`), `secret_id`, `key`, `actor_id`, `at`, `ip`.
   `SecretAuditEntry.ip` is documented as "recorded by the server — the client never sources this"
   (`src/types/devtools.ts:99-108`); the mock's placeholder says the same
   (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:369-370`). **Never accept an IP from the body.**
7. **Two sinks, one transaction.** The document's own trail (`secret_access_events`, what
   `SecretAuditPanel` renders) **and** the workspace audit log (`audit_events`, SY-AUD-41), written
   together (canon OQ-68 position). Severity `warn` when allowed, `error` when denied; `outcome`
   `allowed` / `denied`; `target` is the **key name only** and `detail` is one of four fixed,
   value-free sentences (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:566-571`). **No audit record ever contains
   a secret value.**
8. **Transaction boundary, and what is outside it.** The `SELECT` of the ciphertext and both audit
   inserts are one transaction, and **it commits before the plaintext moves** — a reveal whose audit
   row was lost is an unlogged disclosure, which is the one failure this endpoint exists to prevent.
   The KMS `Decrypt` and the AES-256-GCM unwrap are network and CPU work and must be **outside**
   `BEGIN` (part 17 §36, T-04). If decryption fails after the audit committed, the log records an
   attempt that returned an error — the honest record. The denied path is audited **before** the
   refusal is returned: "a refusal nobody can see is not a control"
   (`src/services/devtools-service.ts:342-349, 358-361`).
9. **The read path never returns a value.** `GET /nodes/{nodeId}/secrets` (E-101) returns masks only,
   and `maskedValue` is a constant twelve `U+2022` bullets — **never derived from the real length**
   (canon E-101). There is no code path from the list read to a plaintext value.
10. **Which frontend calls it.** The reveal and copy controls in `SecretList` /
    `SecretEditorPanel`, through `devtoolsService.revealSecret`. A revealed value lives in component
    state only — never `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, a cache, a URL or a log — auto-hides after
    `AUTO_HIDE_MS = 30_000`, is cleared on unmount, and is dropped entirely when a save is applied,
    because a save can rename or replace any of them. A **single copy** goes through the same
    endpoint with `action: "copy"`, writes to the clipboard, and leaves the screen masked.
11. **Realtime event.** None, on either path, by design.
12. **Errors.** `SECRET_NOT_FOUND` 404, `SECRET_REVEAL_DENIED` 403 (message
    `Revealing {key} needs the Admin role`, detail `Ask a workspace admin to share it with you.`),
    `SECRET_REVEAL_RATE_LIMITED` 429 with `retryAfterSeconds` and `isRetryable: true`,
    `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 for the generic gate-4 refusal.
13. **The one asymmetry with §39.1.2's gates.** A reveal refusal names the key
    (`Revealing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY needs the Admin role`). That is not a leak: the caller can already
    see the key list from E-101, which is masks-only and gated on visibility alone. The rule canon
    §4.4 states — "a refusal must not leak the name of something the caller was denied" — is about
    things the caller could not otherwise see, and a secret's *name* is not one of them. Its
    **value** is, and no refusal, audit row or frame ever carries it.
