#### OQ-90 — How do the four `NotificationTab` values map onto the five `NotificationReason` values?

**Severity** low · **Module** collab · **Status** Position taken (canon §8.8)

**Current evidence** — Tabs are `all | mentions | assigned | following`
(`src/types/collab.ts:99`); reasons are `mention | assigned | comment | watch | system`
(`src/types/collab.ts:97`). Three tabs map obviously; `comment` and `system` belong to no tab except
`all`.

**Unclear** — Where do `comment` and `system` notifications appear?

**Recommendation** — `all` → everything; `mentions` → `mention`; `assigned` → `assigned`;
`following` → `watch` **and** `comment`. **The API filters by `reason`, never by tab name**
(`GET /me/notifications?reason=watch&reason=comment`), so the mapping lives in the frontend where the
tabs are and can change without a backend release. `system` appears only in `all`.

**Impact if wrong** — Comment notifications land in the wrong tab — trivial to change precisely
because the backend does not know about tabs.

**Blocks** — Nothing.

---

#### OQ-91 — Notification retention, dedupe, digest and inbox paging; the badge is derived client-side

**Severity** high · **Module** collab · **Status** Position taken here (paging/badge: canon §6.3)

**Current evidence** — `notificationService.list(userId)` returns the whole inbox newest-first with
no limit, no cursor and no retention rule (`src/services/notification-service.ts:28-34`).
`notification-store.load()` is load-once and the unread badge is counted from the loaded array
(`src/store/notification-store.ts`, `countUnread`). There is no dedupe anywhere: `emit` appends
unconditionally (`src/services/notification-service.ts:88-110`).

**Unclear** — Retention window, and whether repeated events on one target collapse into one
notification.

**Recommendation** — Four rules. **Paging:** cursor on `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` (E-129).
**Badge:** server-computed, `GET /me/notifications/unread-count` (E-132), so it is not "unread among
the ones we loaded". **Dedupe:** collapse within a **15-minute window** on
`(recipient_id, reason, target_key, actor_id)` by updating the existing unread row's `created_at` and
body rather than inserting — so ten edits by one person on one row are one notification. A **read**
notification never absorbs a new event. **Retention:** purge read notifications after 90 days,
unread after 180. Digest (an email summary) is out of scope for v1 — there is no email channel.

**Impact if wrong** — Without dedupe, one busy row buries an inbox. Without server-side counting the
badge silently becomes wrong the moment the inbox is larger than a page. Without retention the table
grows forever, and it is the highest-insert-rate table in the system.

**Blocks** — **P3 Collaboration, §4 (`notifications`), §25 (E-129, E-132).**

---

#### OQ-92 — Which timezone defines "today" and "overdue" for My Work and the deadline dashboard?

**Severity** critical · **Module** insights · **Status** Answer required

**Current evidence** — **Everything is UTC, and it is not an accident — it is an unexamined
default.** `dayKey(iso)` is `new Date(at).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`
(`src/lib/board-dates.ts:6-10`) — the UTC day. `isSameCalendarDay` and `isBeforeDay` compare day keys
*"both read in UTC"* (`src/lib/my-work.ts:151-163`). My Work buckets `dueToday` and `overdue` against
`nowIso` through those helpers (`src/services/my-work-service.ts:109-110`), and the dashboard's
deadline widget does the same (`src/lib/dashboard.ts:104-118`). The reference instant is a parameter
— *"Reference instant — the frozen clock in fixtures, `now` in production"*
(`src/services/my-work-service.ts:55-56`) — so the *instant* is injectable and the *zone* is not.
Meanwhile `src/lib/calendar.ts:1-16` argues at length that a due date has no zone at all.

**Unclear** — Whose midnight ends "today": UTC, the workspace's configured zone, or the viewer's
browser zone?

**Recommendation** — **The viewer's zone**, supplied per request. The client already knows it
(`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`); send it as a query parameter on E-134 and
E-135, validate it against the IANA database, and default to `UTC` when absent. The server computes
the reference day key in that zone and compares day keys — never instants. A workspace-wide zone is
the wrong unit: a distributed team does not share a midnight, and "overdue" is a statement about the
reader's day, not the workspace's. This is "answer required" because it adds a parameter the frontend
does not send today and because a product owner may reasonably prefer a workspace zone.

**Impact if wrong** — Pure UTC means a user in UTC+7 sees a task due today marked overdue for the
first seven hours of their morning, every day — and a user in UTC−8 sees tomorrow's tasks in "Due
today" all evening. It is not a rounding error; it is wrong for most of the world for most of the
day, and it looks like a data bug rather than a timezone bug, so it will be reported as one.

**Blocks** — **P3 Collaboration, §27 (E-134, E-135).**

#### OQ-93 — Search pagination, and whether document bodies are indexed at all

**Severity** high · **Module** search · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — **Document bodies are not searched.** `nodeResult` matches a document on its
`name` and, at a lower weight, on `node.excerpt` — a short summary field, not the blocks
(`src/services/search-service.ts:135-160`, `BODY_WEIGHT = 0.4` at `:36`). Board rows match on the
title column and the display id (`:88-96`); comments match on `plainBody`
(`:113-131`). Results are capped per group at `SEARCH_GROUP_LIMIT = 5`
(`src/config/app.ts:30`) and there is no cursor.

**Unclear** — Must the full text of document blocks be searchable, and is deep paging of ranked
results required?

**Recommendation** — **Index the bodies.** A `documents.search_vector tsvector` maintained from the
concatenated text of the block array, with a GIN index (§35) — the frontend's excerpt-only matching
is a limitation of a store that holds documents in memory, not a product decision, and "find the page
that mentions X" is the thing global search is for. **No deep paging in v1**: keep the per-group cap,
returning the top 5 per `SearchResultKind` in the fixed group order, `score DESC, title ASC`. Deep
paging a ranked search is a different feature with a different UI. On a **dedicated search engine**:
PostgreSQL `tsvector` + GIN, plus `pg_trgm` for the `TASK-001` id path, is the whole of v1 — no
Elasticsearch, no OpenSearch (ground rule 8). Revisit only when a measured query on real data fails
its latency budget, and note that the permission funnel (a visible-node-id set) is the hard part to
port to an external engine, not the ranking.

**Impact if wrong** — Without body indexing, search finds titles and misses content, which users read
as "search is broken". If deep paging is required, `SearchGroup` grows a per-group cursor — additive.
If an external engine turns out to be necessary, the funnel has to be reproduced there, and getting
it wrong there is a cross-tenant leak.

**Blocks** — **P3 Collaboration, §27 (E-133)** and §35's `tsvector` columns.

#### OQ-94 — Two search surfaces (`SearchHit` vs `SearchResult`) — one endpoint or two?

**Severity** low · **Module** search · **Status** Position taken (canon §8.8)

**Current evidence** — `SearchHit` is nodes-only with a `path` and an `href`
(`src/types/view.ts:42-47`); `SearchResult`/`SearchGroup` covers eight kinds including records,
comments and places, with a `score` and a `snippet` (`src/types/collab.ts:153-180`). They share
nothing structurally and have different latency budgets — one backs a sidebar filter, the other a
command palette.

**Unclear** — Nothing contentious.

**Recommendation** — Two endpoints: E-035 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/nodes/search?q=` (drive
quick-find, name match only, cheap) and E-133 `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/search?q=` (global
full-text, grouped). Both filter through node visibility.

**Impact if wrong** — Serving the quick-find from the global index makes the sidebar sluggish for no
benefit. Merging them later is a client change.

**Blocks** — Nothing.

#### OQ-95 — Do `TASK-001`-style inline record references in comment bodies resolve, and are prefixes unique?

**Severity** med · **Module** search · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — The token is parsed but **not resolved**. `ROW_REFERENCE_SOURCE =
"\\b([A-Z]{2,6})-(\\d{1,6})\\b"` (`src/lib/row-id.ts:29`) is shared by the comment parser and search
so they tokenise identically (`src/lib/mentions.ts:15-16`), `parseBody` emits
`{ kind: "record", displayId }` (`src/lib/mentions.ts:122`), and the renderer draws it as a **static
chip with no link** (`src/components/comments/comment-body.tsx:23-32`). Nothing looks the id up.
Crucially, **`rowIdPrefix` is not unique across boards**: it comes from the template
(`src/lib/board-templates.ts:134`, `:211`, `:285`, `:349`), so every board made from the `task`
template has prefix `TASK`, and `TASK-007` is ambiguous the moment a workspace has two of them.

**Unclear** — Should `TASK-007` in a comment become a link, and if so which board's TASK-007?

**Recommendation** — Resolve **within the comment's own board first**: a `row` -targeted comment
resolves the reference against its own `board_id`, which is unambiguous and covers the overwhelming
majority of real uses. Outside that scope, resolve across the workspace and return **all** matches;
the client renders a chip that is a link when there is exactly one and a disambiguating popover when
there are several. Return the resolution as a side-channel on the comment response
(`resolvedReferences: { displayId, boardId, rowId, title }[]`) rather than rewriting the body — the
body is the user's text and must stay as typed. Do **not** make `row_id_prefix` unique per workspace:
it comes from templates, existing data already collides, and enforcing it would break board creation.

**Impact if wrong** — Linking to the wrong board's TASK-007 is worse than not linking at all. Not
resolving leaves a feature that looks like a link and is not, which the renderer already ships.

**Blocks** — Sign-off on **§20 (E-119, E-120)**.

#### OQ-96 — Should Recent become cross-device server state?

**Severity** low · **Module** collab · **Status** Position taken (canon §1.2, §8.8)

**Current evidence** — `recent-store.ts:9-18` calls it *"a navigation convenience, kept in this
browser only"*, backed by `localStorage` under `nexdrop-recent` with best-effort writes. It is an LRU
of `RECENT_LIMIT = 10` (`src/config/app.ts:36`) with **no time window** — while `SMART_VIEWS`
advertises Recent as *"Items you touched in the last 7 days"* (`src/config/app.ts`), which is a time
window. So the description and the implementation already disagree.

**Unclear** — Is Recent per-device or per-account?

**Recommendation** — Keep it client-side. It is per-device by nature, it is already access-filtered
on read because it renders through the visible tree, and `useAccessSync` can wipe it on revocation —
none of which a server-side list gets for free. Fix the `SMART_VIEWS` description to match the LRU
rather than the reverse.

**Impact if wrong** — If cross-device is required, `RECENT_LIMIT` and the LRU semantics move to the
server, `useTrackRecent` becomes a fire-and-forget write on **every navigation** — the highest-write-
rate endpoint in the product — and the access filter has to be reproduced at read time.

**Blocks** — Nothing.

#### OQ-97 — Should comment drafts become server state?

**Severity** low · **Module** collab · **Status** Position taken (canon §1.2, §8.8)

**Current evidence** — `use-comment-draft.ts:5-17` cites the PRD directly — *"closing the drawer must
not lose what you were typing"* — and satisfies it with `localStorage` under
`nexdrop-comment-draft:<key>` plus an in-memory map.

**Unclear** — Is a draft expected to follow the user to another device?

**Recommendation** — Leave it client-side. A draft is per-device by nature, and syncing it means

question out of all proportion to the feature.

**Impact if wrong** — If cross-device drafts are required, this needs a debounced upsert keyed by
`(user_id, draft_key)` and a delete on successful post.

#### OQ-98 — Which per-viewer UI preferences persist, and where?

**Severity** low · **Module** identity · **Status** Position taken (canon T-37)

**Current evidence** — Collapsed groups and collapsed subtask parents are kept in `grid-store` keyed
by view id *"so switching views restores them"* (`src/store/grid-store.ts:49-56`) — but
`grid-store.reset()` runs on every board change (`src/hooks/use-board.ts:26`), so they do not survive
navigating away. Sidebar collapse, drive `viewMode` and `sort` live in `workspace-store` and survive
nothing.

**Unclear** — Which of these are worth persisting, and at what scope?

**Recommendation** — One `user_ui_preferences (user_id, scope, prefs JSONB)` table, written debounced,
covering: sidebar collapsed, drive view mode and sort. **Per-view** column widths, collapsed groups
and collapsed parents go to `board_view_preferences` instead (OQ-46), because they are keyed by view,
not by user alone. Every JSONB payload is documented as a named TypeScript interface (canon C-06).

**Impact if wrong** — Low individually, but every one of these silently resets on reload, which reads
as the app forgetting what you did.

**Blocks** — Nothing.

### 40.7 Realtime

#### OQ-99 — Realtime covers comments, notifications and permissions — but not boards at all

**Severity** high · **Module** realtime · **Status** Position taken (canon §7.2, §8.8)

**Current evidence** — `RealtimePayload` has exactly five variants: `comment.created`,
`comment.updated`, `notification.created`, `notification.read`, `permission.changed`
(`src/types/realtime.ts:15-32`). There is **no** `row.created`, `row.updated`, `column.*` or presence
frame — yet `BoardRow.revision` is *"the optimistic-concurrency token"* (`src/types/board.ts:248-249`)
and `ConflictNotice` exists specifically to report a lost race
(`src/types/board.ts:462-467`). The file says plainly that *"the backend does not expose a realtime
endpoint yet"* (`src/types/realtime.ts:5-9`), and `REALTIME_ENDPOINT` is `null`
(`src/config/app.ts:69`), which is what keeps the transport on the in-process bus
(`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:53-60`).

**Unclear** — Are board frames wanted in v1, and does a second person's edit appear without a
refresh?

**Recommendation** — Ship RT-06 … RT-11 (`row.created`, `row.updated`, `row.archived`,
`row.deleted`, `board.schema.changed`, `node.changed`), each carrying **ids only** — no cell content —
following the `permission.changed` precedent, where the frame's own comment says *"a frame announcing
a revocation must not be the thing that leaks what was revoked"* (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`). The
receiver refetches. **Do not build RT-12 `presence.changed`** until a surface asks for it: no frontend
component consumes presence today, and presence is the one frame with a continuous write rate. Unknown
frame types are ignored by the client (`src/types/realtime.ts:14`), so all of this ships without a
frontend release.

**Impact if wrong** — Without row frames, two people on one board discover a collision only when a
write returns a `ConflictNotice` — degraded, not broken, because last-write-wins means nothing is
lost. Sending cell content in a frame, by contrast, leaks values across a permission boundary and
cannot be walked back.

**Blocks** — **P4 System, §30 (Realtime Events).**

---

#### OQ-100 — Frame scoping and authorisation: who receives which frame, and how is that proved?

**Severity** security · **Module** realtime · **Status** Answer required

**Current evidence** — There is no server, so there is no scoping. The local transport delivers every
published frame to **every subscriber in the tab**
(`src/lib/realtime/transport.ts:41-44`), and filtering is done by the receiving store:
`notification-store` drops frames whose `recipientId` is not the current user
(`src/store/notification-store.ts:112`). The frontend's own model is therefore "broadcast then
filter", which is exactly what a server must not do. The one frame designed with scoping in mind is
`permission.changed`, which carries ids only and no content (`src/types/realtime.ts:20-25`).

**Unclear** — Is the subscription unit the workspace, the node, or the target key; and is
authorisation checked at subscribe time, at publish time, or both?

**Recommendation** — **One socket per workspace** (E-138), authorised at connect against
`workspace_members`. Within it, the client subscribes to **topics** — `node:{nodeId}`,
`board:{boardId}`, `comments:{targetKey}`, and an implicit `user:{selfId}` — and the server checks
node visibility **at subscribe time** and **re-checks at publish time** for anything content-bearing.
`notification.created` is delivered **only to its `recipientId`**; the server must not send it to
anyone else and rely on the client's filter. On a `permission.changed` affecting a subscriber, the
server **drops their affected topic subscriptions** rather than waiting for the client to unsubscribe
— the whole point of RT-05 is that a revoked user must not keep receiving. This is "answer required"
because subscribe-time-only checking is cheaper and may be judged sufficient, and that is a security
trade-off somebody has to sign.

**Impact if wrong** — Broadcast-then-filter puts every workspace event on every member's socket, and
the filter is client code. A revocation that does not tear down subscriptions leaves a stream open
to somebody who has just lost access — which is the exact failure RT-05 exists to prevent.

**Blocks** — **P4 System, §30, §38 (Security).**

---

#### OQ-101 — Reconnect and replay: does a client that missed frames get a backlog, or refetch?

**Severity** med · **Module** realtime · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — The client is built for **at-least-once** delivery: every frame carries an id
and a repeat is dropped, with `SEEN_LIMIT = 512` remembered ids — *"Well past any reconnect replay
window"* (`src/lib/realtime/client.ts:11-21`, `:50-62`). So the frontend anticipates a replay. But
nothing produces one: the local transport has no buffer, and `RealtimeStatus` is
`idle | connecting | open | closed` with no "resyncing" state (`src/types/realtime.ts:12`).

**Unclear** — Does the server buffer frames per connection and replay on reconnect, or does the
client refetch on reconnect?

**Recommendation** — **Refetch, do not replay.** On reconnect the client re-reads what it has open —
the board snapshot, the comment page, the notification page — and the server sends nothing
retrospective. Reasons: every recommended frame carries ids only (OQ-99), so a missed frame costs a
refetch and nothing else; a replay buffer is per-connection state that has to survive an instance
restart, which means Redis streams and a retention decision; and the dedup window the client already
has (512 ids) makes an *overlapping* refetch safe. The server sends a `resync` hint on connect
carrying the workspace's current access epoch, so a client that reconnects after a permission change
knows to re-resolve rather than trusting what it holds.

**Impact if wrong** — Without replay, a client that misses frames during a 30-second network blip
shows stale data until it refetches — bounded by the refetch, which the reconnect triggers. With a
replay buffer, the cost is a Redis stream per workspace and a retention window that is wrong in one
direction or the other. If a surface later needs true continuity (a collaborative editor), that is a
different transport with a different consistency model, not an extension of this one.

**Blocks** — Sign-off on **§30**.

---

### 40.8 Questions the audits raised for which canon reserved no id

These seven are real, they came out of the audit fact sheets or out of the frontend directly, and
**canon §8 has no id for any of them**. Canon forbids inventing an id "without appending it to this
file", so the ids below are **proposed**: they are written in the same format so they can be triaged
now, and the note at the end of this file asks the editor to append them to canon §8 before any
chapter cites one. Until then, cite them as *"§40.8, proposed OQ-102"*, never as a settled id.

#### OQ-102 — Can node ownership be transferred, and what happens when the owner leaves?

**Severity** high (proposed) · **Module** governance · **Status** Answer required

**Current evidence** — `owner` is embedded on every node as a `UserSummary`
(`src/types/node.ts:55`) and is set at creation by the node factories
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:529`, `:767`, `:818`) and **never written again** — there is no
transfer path anywhere in `src/`. Ownership is load-bearing in two places: it escalates five keys
(`OWNER_ESCALATIONS = { node.rename, node.delete, node.archive, file.delete, document.lock }`,
`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:98-108`) from `member` upward, and it is an unconditional grant on the
**access** axis — `if (subject.kind === "user" && node.owner.id === subject.userId) return true;`
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:93`). The directory keeps departed users resolvable
(`isActive: false`, `src/mock/users.ts:38-58`), so `node.owner.id` still renders a name after they
leave — but membership gate 1 refuses them (`nodeVisibility` returns `isVisible: false` when
`!isMember`, `src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:161`), so the owner-is-always-in safety net silently
stops protecting the node.

**Unclear** — Is ownership transferable, and on member removal are their owned nodes reassigned,
left dangling, or flagged?

**Recommendation** — Add `POST /nodes/{nodeId}/owner`, gated on `workspace.permission.manage`
(or `node.access.manage` **plus** current ownership), audited at `warn` in the `node` module. On
member removal, **reassign** every node they owned to the actor performing the removal, in the same
transaction, and record one audit row per reassignment batch. Do not leave nodes owned by a
non-member: the resulting node is reachable only through the admin recovery console (E-046), and that
is an unstated invariant nobody will remember.

**Impact if wrong** — If ownership must not transfer, a restricted node whose owner has left and
whose grants were revoked is recoverable only by an admin who knows the console exists. If it
transfers automatically to the wrong person, five escalated keys move with it.

**Blocks** — **P0 Foundation, §9 (member removal), §28 (ownership axis).**

---

#### OQ-103 — Workspace deletion: hard delete, or retained for a window?

**Severity** high (proposed) · **Module** workspace · **Status** Answer required

**Current evidence** — The frontend deletes immediately and irreversibly. The danger zone requires
typing the workspace name and says *"Every folder, board, page and file in {name} goes with it, for
everybody. This cannot be undone."* (`src/components/workspace/workspace-danger-zone.tsx:45-49`), and
the store drops the workspace, its whole tree and its trash bin in one `set`
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:338-360`). The action is gated on `workspace.delete`, an Admin key
(`src/lib/permissions/roles.ts:72`), surfaced as its own tab
(`src/components/workspace/workspace-settings-dialog.tsx:34`). Canon has E-011
`DELETE /workspaces/{workspaceId}` returning `204` and says nothing about retention. Trash, by
contrast, has a documented 30-day window (OQ-14) — so the product retains a deleted *folder* for a
month and destroys a deleted *workspace* instantly.

**Unclear** — Does deleting a workspace destroy the data immediately, or soft-delete it with a
retention window and a restore path?

**Recommendation** — **Soft delete with a 30-day window, no user-facing restore.**
`workspaces.deleted_at` + `deleted_by`; every read filters it out, every membership stops resolving,
and the workspace disappears exactly as the copy promises. A scheduled job purges the whole tenant —
nodes, boards, rows, documents, secrets, assets and the objects behind them — after 30 days. Restore
is an **operator** action, not an endpoint. The reason not to hard-delete: this is the only action in
the product that destroys a whole tenant, it is reachable by any Admin, and the confirmation is a
typed name — which stops a misclick, not a bad afternoon. `secrets` are the exception: purge
`value_encrypted` **immediately** on delete, because retaining credentials for a workspace somebody
asked to destroy is the wrong trade in the other direction.

**Impact if wrong** — Immediate hard delete means a mistaken deletion is unrecoverable, and the
`used_bytes` and object-store cleanup have to be transactional with a very large cascade. Retaining
when the product promised destruction is a data-protection problem, which is why the copy must change
if the recommendation is adopted — "This cannot be undone" would become "This cannot be undone from
here."

**Blocks** — **P0 Foundation, §9 (E-011)** and **P4 (§36, the purge transaction).**

---

#### OQ-104 — Cross-workspace relations and multi-workspace membership

**Severity** high (proposed) · **Module** relations · **Status** Answer required

**Current evidence** — A user is genuinely in many workspaces: `visibleWorkspaces` filters the full
list by membership (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:44-49`) and the switcher renders the result, with a
per-workspace role. Nothing constrains a **relation** to one workspace: `RelationConfig.boardId` is a
bare board id with no workspace scoping (`src/types/board.ts:156-159`), and `relationIndex` resolves
target rows without checking which workspace the target board is in
(`src/services/board-service.ts:1299-1340`). The same is true of `EmbedBlock.boardNodeId` in documents.
Search, My Work and the dashboard, by contrast, are all explicitly workspace-scoped — they read
`getActiveTree()` (`src/services/search-service.ts:59`).

**Unclear** — May a relation column, or a document embed, point at a board in a **different**
workspace?

**Recommendation** — **No.** Enforce it structurally: `board_row_relations` carries a
`workspace_id` and a `CHECK` that source and target share it, and E-071 refuses a target board in
another workspace with `BULK_TARGET_NOT_A_BOARD`'s sibling (`validation`). Reasons: the permission
model resolves access through **one workspace's** tree and membership gate
(`nodeVisibility` starts with `if (!input.isMember) return { isVisible: false }`,
`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:161`), so a cross-workspace chip would have to resolve a second
membership check that no code path performs; and `workspaces.used_bytes`, the audit trail and the
realtime socket are all per-workspace, so a cross-workspace edge has no home in any of them.
Multi-workspace **membership** stays fully supported — that is a property of the user, not of the
data.

**Impact if wrong** — If cross-workspace relations are a product requirement, the permission
resolution, the realtime scoping (OQ-100) and the search funnel all need a second workspace context,
and the `access_rules` chain query stops being answerable in one index probe. That is a design, not a
setting.

**Blocks** — **P1 Boards, §17 (E-071, E-072)** and §4 (`board_row_relations`).

---

#### OQ-105 — Access rules naming a person who has left the workspace

**Severity** med (proposed) · **Module** governance · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — `withoutMember` removes the membership row and touches **no**
`access_rules` (`src/lib/workspace-access.ts:260-262`). A **role**-scoped rule stops matching them
immediately, because `roleOf` returns `null` for a non-member. A **user**-scoped rule still matches
by id — `hasGrantOn` would admit them (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:87-96`) — but
`nodeVisibility` refuses first because `isMember` is false
(`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:161`). Net effect today: harmless, and the orphaned rows persist.
`docs/GOVERNANCE.md:336-337` lists this as unresolved.

**Unclear** — Are the rules deleted on removal, or kept?

**Recommendation** — **Keep the rows.** They are audit evidence of who was granted what and when, and
they make a re-invite predictable. Two conditions make keeping them safe: (a) the membership gate is
**authoritative and first**, so a rule can never be the thing that lets somebody back in; and (b)
`resolveAccess` filters non-members out of the rows it returns, so the access dialog does not list
ghosts. Both are already how the frontend behaves; the API must not lose either.

**Impact if wrong** — Deleting the rows loses the record of a grant. Keeping them **without** gate 1
being authoritative silently restores access on re-invite to a folder nobody re-shared — which is the
failure mode worth writing down.

**Blocks** — Sign-off on **§28 (E-040)** and §9 (member removal).

---

#### OQ-106 — A Viewer who owns a page can lock it

**Severity** med (proposed) · **Module** governance · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — The two functions disagree. `can("document.lock", ctx)` requires the owner
escalation to clear a rank floor — `owns && OWNER_ESCALATIONS.has(key) && roleRank(role) >=
roleRank("member")` (`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:73-74`). `canToggleLock` has **no floor**:
`resolve("document.lock") || document.owner.id === user.id`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:147-153`). `tests/permissions.test.ts:147-154` covers Member and
Manager only, so the Viewer-owner case is untested.

**Unclear** — Is the unconditional owner clause intentional?

**Recommendation** — Follow `can`, not `canToggleLock`: require `roleRank >= member` for the owner
escalation on `document.lock`. A Viewer holds zero permission keys by design, and locking is the one
action in the product that stops *other people* writing — no other Viewer capability does that.
Report the frontend inconsistency so `canToggleLock` can be brought in line.

**Impact if wrong** — If the backend copies `canToggleLock` literally, a Viewer who owns a page can
freeze editing for the whole workspace and only they (or a `document.lock` holder) can undo it. If
the floor is applied and the unconditional clause was intended, a Viewer-owner loses an action they
had — visible and easy to grant back.

**Blocks** — Sign-off on **§12 (E-094), §28.**

---

#### OQ-107 — Who may purge one item, and who may empty the whole bin?

**Severity** med (proposed) · **Module** system · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — The two actions are gated **differently, and one is not gated at all.** A
single item's Restore and Delete-permanently are resolved against the node —
`const can = usePermissions(row.entry.node); const canRestore = can("node.delete");`
(`src/components/collections/trash-page.tsx:141-143`), with the comment that *"Restore and permanent
deletion are gated on the node's own permissions, which is why the row is a component rather than
markup in a map"* (`:127-129`). **Empty trash** is rendered whenever the bin is non-empty, with no
permission test at all (`src/components/collections/trash-page.tsx:51-61`), and calls
`emptyTrash()` which drops every entry in the workspace
(`src/store/workspace-store.ts:705`). Its confirmation says *"All N items will be deleted for good,
along with everything inside them."*

**Unclear** — Is emptying the bin a per-node operation repeated, or a workspace-level one; and does
`node.delete` cover both?

**Recommendation** — Per item (E-038): `node.delete` **on that node**, exactly as the row does today.
Empty trash (E-039): a **workspace-level** action that purges only the entries the caller holds
`node.delete` on, and reports what it skipped in `EmptyTrashResponse` — never a silent partial. A
Member emptying the bin must not destroy an Admin's restricted folder that happens to be in it, and
gating the whole button on `workspace.delete` would make the ordinary case unusable.

**Impact if wrong** — Ungated, one Member permanently destroys everything anyone deleted in the last
30 days. Over-gated, the button is invisible to the people who use it most.

**Blocks** — **P4 System, §11/§36 (E-038, E-039).**

---

#### OQ-108 — Access resolution for a detached (trashed) subtree

**Severity** med (proposed) · **Module** governance · **Status** Position taken here

**Current evidence** — Deleting **detaches**: `trashNodeFrom` lifts the node and its subtree out of
the tree into the bin (`trashNodeFrom`, `src/lib/trash.ts`, called at `src/store/workspace-store.ts:620`), so a
trashed node has **no ancestor chain** in the live tree. But access resolution is entirely
chain-based: `chainFor` is `findPathToId(tree, nodeId)` and returns `[]` for a node not in the tree
(`src/lib/permissions/inheritance.ts:40-43`), and `nodeVisibility` returns `VISIBLE` when the chain
is empty (`src/lib/permissions/visibility.ts:164-165`). So a trashed restricted folder resolves to
*visible* — it is only kept out of surfaces because the trash view filters and the permission
evaluator refuses every key but `node.delete`
(`src/lib/permissions/evaluate.ts:79-81`).

**Unclear** — Whose access governs a trashed subtree: the rules that applied before deletion, or
nothing at all?

**Recommendation** — The rules that applied before deletion. `trash_entries` already stores
`originalAncestorIds` for the restore walk (canon T-09); resolve a trashed node's access against
**that stored chain**, not against the live tree. Concretely: the trash listing (E-036) returns only
entries whose stored chain the caller could see, and E-037/E-038 re-resolve against it. Without this,
a restricted folder becomes visible to everyone the moment somebody deletes it — which is a way to
leak a folder's existence by destroying it.

**Impact if wrong** — Resolving against the empty chain means the bin is the one place access does
not apply. Resolving against the stored chain has one cost: a rule written **after** the deletion is
not seen by the trashed node, which is correct — it was not there when the rule was written.

**Blocks** — **P4 System, §11 (E-036–E-039), §28.**

---

### 40.9 Decisions canon closed — recorded so no chapter reopens them

These came up during the audit and are **not** open questions. Canon settled them with reasoning, and
a chapter that re-litigates one is a defect. They are listed here because a reader arriving at "Open
Questions" looking for one of them should find the answer, not silence.

| Question | Decision | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Cell storage: `cells JSONB` on the row, or a `cell_values` table?** | **`cells JSONB` on `board_rows`.** The row is always read whole and always written whole; a cell's `kind` may legitimately disagree with its column's `type` after a conversion, which a typed EAV column cannot represent; N edits on one row must produce **one** revision bump. Column delete is the one axis EAV wins, and it is a per-row rewrite the frontend already performs. Four **generated columns** (`due_date`, `due_at`, `status_option_id`, `assignee_ids`) carry the indexed projections. | canon §1.3.2; §4 reproduces the full trade-off table |
| One `nodes` table or five per kind? | **One**, discriminated by `kind`, with five 1:1 side tables. `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug)` must hold **across** kinds, which a split schema cannot express. | canon §1.3.1 |
| A `select_options` table? | **No.** Options live in `board_columns.config`, because `completedOptionIds`, `transitionRules` and `options[].availability` all reference option ids by value inside the same document. | canon §1.3.3 |
| `tasks` / `bugs` / `qa_cases` / `api_endpoints` tables? | **No.** They are rows in `board_templates`. The dashboard reads a board as QA **by what it became**, not by its template id. | canon §1.3.5 |
| A response envelope (`{ data: … }`)? | **No.** The body *is* the resource. Errors are `{ "error": AppError }`, grounded in `BoardError` (`src/types/board.ts:507-509`). | canon §6.2 |
| Offset pagination anywhere? | **No.** Keyset (`?cursor=&limit=`) everywhere it is paginated at all. | canon §6.3 |
| A `RelationType` enum or a typed dependency edge? | **Reserved and deliberately not defined.** See OQ-45. | canon §2.9 |
| Cell-write concurrency | **Last-write-wins plus `ConflictNotice[]`, always `200`, never `409`.** | canon §6.4 |
| A write endpoint for the audit log | **Does not exist and may not be added.** The log is append-only by construction. | canon §3.23 |

---

### 40.10 The blocking set

Twelve rows below — fourteen ids — must be answered before the phase they gate can be **finished**.
Everything else can proceed on the position this document takes.

| id | Question | Phase | Why it cannot wait |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OQ-01 | Authentication mechanism | P0 | Nothing downstream has a caller. |
| OQ-03 | Four roles or five | P0 | The role `ENUM`'s **order** is load-bearing; inserting a rank later changes the meaning of every stored rule. |
| OQ-09 / OQ-10 | Slug minting and re-uniquification | P0 | One coherent rule, and the `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug)` index depends on it. |
| OQ-16 | Is the matrix the policy | P0 | Every write endpoint's gate. |
| OQ-22 | Deepest wins vs union | P0 | Changing it later changes the meaning of every `access_rules` row. |
| OQ-32 | Day key vs instant | P1 | A wrong conversion is written into the stored value and is unrecoverable. |
| OQ-36 | Row pagination vs client-side filtering | P1 | Paginating without server-side filtering makes every count silently wrong. |
| OQ-46 | Shared view vs per-viewer preferences | P1 | Two tables or one, decided before the first view is written. |
| OQ-57 / OQ-59 | Document concurrency and version policy | P2 | Both destroy work silently, and the fold rule cannot be retrofitted onto unfolded history. |
| OQ-65 | Secret encryption | P2 | Not recoverable after the fact — the secrets have to be rotated by their owners. |
| OQ-69 | 25 MB or 100 MB | P2 | Proxy limits, multipart strategy and object-store part size all follow from it. |
| OQ-92 | Which timezone is "today" | P3 | Wrong for most of the world for most of the day, and it reads as a data bug. |

Two more are **security** rather than blocking, and must be closed before the surface they concern is
exposed to real data: **OQ-70** (extension allow-list and MIME sniffing — stored XSS via upload) and
**OQ-100** (realtime frame scoping — broadcast-then-filter puts every workspace event on every
member's socket). **OQ-73** (comment attachments bypass validation and permissions) is the third, and
it is closed by routing comment uploads through the ordinary pipeline.

## 41. Backend Readiness Checklist

Marked honestly against the assembled document as it stands, not against the intent. **Complete**
means a backend developer can build the item without asking a question. **Partial** means something
real is missing and the gap is named. **Blocked** means an open question has to be answered first,
and the OQ is named. Where an item is complete *except* for a branch an OQ gates, it says so — a
green tick that hides an OQ is worse than an amber one.

| Item | Status | Where in this document |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Database schema complete** | ⚠️ **Partial** — 39 tables are registered (canon §1.1) and **35** carry a full column specification. Four do not: `environments` (T-26) is deferred by §4 to the devtools reference data and is then never given a column table — it exists only as an FK target and an `is_production`/`slug` recommendation (OQ-63); `trash_entries` (T-09) has its column set enumerated inside §10's E-032 (`DELETE /nodes/{nodeId}`) write plan but no table block of its own; `board_view_preferences` (T-16) is specified by its unique index and its write plan rather than by a column table (OQ-46); `user_ui_preferences` (T-37) is registered, indexed, and has **no endpoint and no writer** — build it only when OQ-98 is answered. | §4 (parts covering `users` … `secret_access_events`, §4.10–§4.20 for the board engine); `import_jobs` / `export_jobs` in §24; `uploads` in §21; `boards` / `board_columns` / `board_rows` / `board_row_relations` in §4.11–§4.18 |
| **Relationships defined** | ✅ **Complete** — every FK, its cardinality and its `ON DELETE` behaviour, including the two that are deliberately **not** cascades: `secrets.environment_id` and `config_documents.environment_id` are `RESTRICT` so E-109 refuses a referenced environment, and `audit_events.workspace_id` is `SET NULL` so the trail outlives the workspace it describes. | §5, plus the per-table Relationships blocks in §4 and the write plans in §33 |
| **Indexes defined** | ✅ **Complete** — per table, with the query each one serves, including the partial indexes (`nodes_parent_idx WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, `workspace_members_admin_idx WHERE role = 'admin'`, `nodes_restricted_idx`), the four `tsvector` GIN indexes, the single JSONB GIN (`board_rows.cells`), and the two deferrable uniques on `(board_id, position)`. | §35 |
| **Constraints defined** | ✅ **Complete** — PKs, uniques, `CHECK`s and the `EXCLUDE`-free design are stated per table, including the three that carry business rules rather than data hygiene: `UNIQUE (parent_id, slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` across node kinds (OQ-09/OQ-10), `UNIQUE (board_id, sequence)` including soft-deleted rows (a number that has been issued is spent), and the deferrable `UNIQUE (board_id, position)` on columns and views. | §4 (per table), §35 (the index-backed ones), §37.9 (why the two are deferrable) |
| **Enums defined** | ✅ **Complete** — native Postgres `ENUM` per stored enum, values verbatim from the frontend literals including `longText`, `apiDocs` and `into-self`; the three documented exceptions to the native-enum policy; `workspace_role`'s declaration order as the rank; and the `GanttZoom` legacy `'day'` coercion. 68 registered enums, 60 on the wire. | §6, catalogued against canon §2 |
| **API contracts defined** | ✅ **Complete** — all 140 endpoints (E-001 … E-140), each with method, path, request, response, permission key, transaction, frontend caller, realtime frame and error set. | §7 (conventions), §9–§27 (per module), §33 (endpoint → tables) |
| **DTOs defined** | ✅ **Complete** — every domain interface, request DTO and response DTO as TypeScript, no `any`, every JSONB payload as a named interface, `readonly` throughout, optional vs nullable kept distinct (canon C-08). | §32, with the JSONB structures also inline in §4 |
| **Auth defined** | ⚠️ **Partial — by design, and it is the one blocking gap.** The session model, token lifetimes, refresh rotation, `user_sessions`, the login/refresh/logout endpoints and the downgrade-takes-effect-on-open-screens rule are fully specified. But the *mechanism* is a recommendation, not a requirement: the frontend has a hardcoded `CURRENT_USER` and no auth of any kind, so **OQ-01** must be answered before this section can be signed off. Nothing in the domain schema depends on the answer. | §8; OQ-01 in §40.1 |

### What a reviewer should do with this

1. Answer the **fourteen blocking ids** listed in §40.10. Thirteen of them cannot be worked around
   once data exists; OQ-01 blocks starting rather than rewriting, so it is the one to answer first.
2. Close the **three security items** — OQ-70, OQ-73, OQ-100 — before any of those surfaces touches
   real data.
3. Fill the **four schema gaps** named in the first row: `environments`, `trash_entries`,
   `board_view_preferences` and `user_ui_preferences`. The first three are small; the fourth should
   not be built at all until OQ-98 is answered.
4. Append the **seven proposed ids** in §40.8 to canon §8 so chapters can cite them.

Everything else in the document can be built as written.

### Chapter notes — divergences, decisions and traps

1. **Canon §8 has no id for seven questions the audits raised.** They are written in §40.8 as
   proposed `OQ-102` … `OQ-108`. Canon says an id may not be invented "without appending it to this
   file", and this chapter cannot edit canon, so they are marked proposed and italicised in the
   index. Please append these seven rows to canon §8 (§8.1 for OQ-103, §8.3 for OQ-102/105/106/108,
   §8.4 for OQ-104, §8.2 or §8.3 for OQ-107) and drop the "proposed" wording here. They are:
   OQ-102 node ownership transfer (governance, from `governance.md` OQ-04);
   OQ-103 workspace deletion retention (workspace, from `src/components/workspace/workspace-danger-zone.tsx`);
   OQ-104 cross-workspace relations (relations, raised by the brief's "multi-workspace membership");
   OQ-105 access rules naming a departed person (governance, from `governance.md` OQ-02);
   OQ-106 a Viewer-owner can lock a page (governance, from `governance.md` OQ-03);
   OQ-107 who may purge and who may empty the bin (system, from `governance.md` OQ-10);
   OQ-108 access resolution for a detached subtree (governance, from `governance.md` OQ-11).

2. **The brief asked this section to cover "cell storage: JSONB vs cell table (if canon left it
   open)". Canon did not leave it open** — §1.3.2 decides `cells JSONB` with a full trade-off table,
   and §4 reproduces it. It is recorded in §40.9 as a closed decision rather than as an open
   question, so a reader looking for it finds the answer.

3. **Two `Blocks` targets name sections by number that a reader may not find under that name.**
   §40 cites §29 as *Audit Logs* (part-13), §33 as *API ↔ Database Mapping* and §34 as
   *Frontend ↔ API Mapping* (part-16), and §39 as *Backend Implementation Order* (part-18). Those
   titles were read off the drafted parts, not off canon — canon does not name the section list.
   If the assembled titles change, the cross-references in §40 and §41 need one pass.

4. **`OQ-45` is the only block where this chapter takes a position that a reader may find
   surprising: BLOCKED_BY cycles are *allowed*, while `parentRowId` cycles are *rejected*.** The
   asymmetry is deliberate and grounded (containment defines a tree; a relation column is a generic
   edge that any board may use for any meaning), but it is the kind of thing an implementer will
   read twice. If §17 wants to reject relation cycles instead, that changes §37's lock plan for
   every relation cell write, and canon §8.8's position on OQ-44/OQ-45 would need to change first.

5. **`OQ-08` deliberately diverges from canon §8.8.** Canon says pinning "follows the same shape
   once confirmed" as favourites, i.e. per user. This chapter recommends **global on the node**,
   because the frontend evidence for pins (no actor anywhere, a page-level menu action, no "your
   pinned pages" copy) points the other way, and canon's own wording defers to a confirmation that
   has not happened. If canon means the per-user shape to be binding rather than provisional, change
   §40.2's OQ-08 recommendation and the `nodes.is_pinned` column in §4 together — not one of them.

6. **Two frontend inconsistencies are reported here rather than fixed silently, and both need a
   frontend ticket:** `renameNode` re-slugs while `applyDocumentSummary` refuses to (OQ-09), and
   `canToggleLock` has no rank floor while `can("document.lock", …)` does (OQ-106). The backend
   follows the safer branch in each case; the frontend should be brought in line so the UI gate and
   the server refusal do not disagree.
